The Cuenellis Special is a big plate with a little bit of everything: steak, chicken, rice, beans, fried yucca, fried plantain, and all topped with a fried egg. I mean how can you go wrong with that?   The grilled chicken is their specialty.  The taste is unique like you would expect if you grilled it in the backyard.  KFC and Boston Market can't come close to this true grilled flavor. 

Desserts are few but great.  The flan is among the best I've ever tasted, and the churros are delicious.  They even have unadvertised homemade ice cream from some exotic Peruvian fruit that is amazing. 

The place is small, and it looks like it used to be a fast food place before.   It is very clean and nicely decorated, but it lacks the ambiance of a full fledged restaurant.  But I don't eat ambiance. What I did eat was delicious and I highly recommend this place.
Quality food at great prices. Try their Crepes, they are awesome. They also serve La Columbe coffee which is my favorite.

Back in my college years, before being able to afford a bonafide dining budget, parents' weekend was an occasion to be celebrated with weeks of anticipation about the big dinner out.  For me, the winner tended to be Ruth's Chris Steakhouse.  There's something about the old school feel of the Philadelphia outpost that is luxe and comfortable at the same time.  While not a fan of the hunting trophy collection on the walls, it somehow works, like eating at twilight in a mysteriously high class jungle.

Now, after nearly a decade of enjoying the steaks, I can honestly say that Ruth's Chris is amazingly and consistently good across a multitude of locations.  The filet is nearly always perfectly cooked and served sizzling on the hot plate with ample (and amazingly fragrant) butter.  Any issues with degree of doneness are handled extremely professionally and graciously.

In addition to the steaks, here are some other things I've tried and really enjoyed (I've pretty much tried everything on the menu, but these are my favorites):
1. Sizzlin Blue Crab Cakes - very little filler and seared in a generous portion of excellent butter
2. Shoestring Potatoes - my favorite of the three types of french fries, these are the thinnest and therefore the fries with the best crispy to potato ratio
3. French Fried Onion Rings - perfectly crispy and juicy all at the same time
4. Bread Pudding with Whiskey Sauce - I've tried all the deserts and this is the best one!

PARTING THOUGHT: As a bonus, if you sign up for the mailing list, there are often special deals for restaurant milestones and seasonal deals (e.g., $99 dinner for two, holiday gift card bonuses, etc.).

The meat was cooked perfectly & you're given fairly generous, nice cuts of meat. My ex ordered a Pittsburgh rare (RED center, burnt-ish outside) and got it served to him very well done, the complete opposite! The Chef realized his mistake after we got our meals and came out to apologize, giving us a whole new order. Minus that little mistake, the service and food is excellent.
Great food . Huge selection. The chicken parmesan is my favorite, two nice pieces of chicken with all that cheese n sauce. Also my son loves the banana pudding

On the drive from the airport we stopped in and got several to go platters and each were good. Jambalaya is different each place you eat it and this is a real good version.  It is nice to find that people in another city appreciate our home cooking. The key is the flavor is great and the presentation even in the to go plate is pleasing. Stop in and see for yourself as they let you sample too.

F'ing fabulous. Room was ready for me, with dog bed and bowls set up, although I arrived two hours early. Scored a gorgeous corner room on 10th floor. 

All staff was professional, friendly, and went out of their way for us. 

Architecture and design of the building and rooms fantastic and visually interesting. 

As a Kimpton member, you get free wifi and a minibar credit, which is neat. I love kimptons and have been to many of their locations.  This one may be a new fave...location cannot be beat. 

Only complaint is the Stratus (hotels roof lounge) drink prices are insane.     Two long island iced teas with tip was 38 bucks. Ridiculous. And they weren't very good either. The lounge itself is gorgeous. As was the crowd. ;)

Cute little café on a lovely sunny street. Amazing brunch choices. Definitely something to look forward to on a Sunday morning.

[ vibe ]
Sunny, wood tables, ikea-joyful. The bar at the window is definitely the place to be. Cute touches: a large framed map of Sydney on the wall and a neat basket of British chocolates near the checkout counter.

[ food ]
We ordered the dill scrambled eggs and eggs benedict. Scrambled eggs came with fruit and toast, and your choice of fresh, real apricot or raspberry jam (none of that Smuckers business). Everything was delicious, freshly cooked, and well-flavoured.

Orange juice is pulpy-fresh and the coffee is strong.

Portion sizes are very generous - you will walk out food-coma full.

[ conclusion ]
Add this to your brunch list. Grab someone you like, take a lazy Sunday morning, and start the day off right!

This is hands down my favorite spot in town, and it's hard to stop me from eating there at least once a week! The service is always a wonderful experience, and the food and coffee are amazing.

All of their sweet crepes are delicious, but I would recommend caramel ricotta, au sucre with strawberries, or apricot jam. Their savory crepes are lovely as well, however there are not many vegetarian options. However, their honeybee crepe is lovely! It's also worth noting that there are no vegan crepe options called out on the menu.
I love Spanish food and this place sucks. Their chicken was so dry. Barely anything on the menus is good. I expected better !

Cajun food in Philadelphia???
Believe it or not, my wife (who is from Louisiana) and I had some of the best Cajun food here than what we could find in SOME places in Louisiana. 

The alligator sausage was the best I have ever had and my wife agreed, even though she normally won't eat gator. She even sent me back for more.

The chicken, sausage and shrimp gumbo was surprisingly good.
As per other reviews, the service is pretty bad so get ready for a long wait with "not so friendly" help.
But, you come to Reading Terminal for food, not service.

Left my credit card here, got stolen by one of the workers, spent around 400$ on it. Skuzzy place, terrible staff. It's got a funky smell to, I wouldn't eat here. I can only hope that the owners sees this review and has a talk with his workers... bad establishment

This is a place to eat rice and french fries
"Peruvian" sauces were very thin and the peruvian chicken tasted like any other. The lunch I had was very greasy....

We ordered one of their mini chocolate mousse cakes to share and it was pretty good. We couldn't wait to try it so we had it right at Reading which was packed that day. Unlike other places the line here was pretty short but don't be fooled as they have a huge selection of sweet treats. Ive had to many cannolis living in Boston so the mousse cake was what caught my attention and I'm glad I tried it.
H3 wings are probably in my top 5 favorite across AZ and NV. Everyone was very friendly. Place was packed but wait was not bad. Going back next week

George is great!
We were out to celebrate and we fortunate to have George as our waiter. My husband got the bone in filet and I got the poultry dish. But who cares about the food? The sides ranged from delicious to mildly crisp. But again, who cares? The main point is that George is amazing. He is an old fashioned soul with a pep in his step. He is friendly, makes small talk, and shakes hands with his patrons. When you call to make your next reservation, plan your night around George's work schedule. You won't regret it. We will never again eat here without George as our waiter.

This place has DoorDash. So I would highly recommend this restaurant for that fact! Technology is a win! I ordered the famous sopa de tortilla (No. 1) and the Enchiladas with Green Chile Verde Sauce. The way they packaged this was extremely kind. I got to mix my own soup with all the ingredients and the enchiladas were nicely wrapped so the sauce doesn't spill during transport. I would highly recommend the soup on a rainy day, stomach ailment, or cold/flu! You have to try, genius idea to mix avocado with broth, cheese and tortillas. I added a bit of lime juice from my home kitchen and it was amazing! Try this place for some good authentic food. The prices are reasonable $10-15
1/4 chicken, cilantro rice, spicy beans. Comes with the green and yellow sauce.. just amazing...

I ate lunch here a couple of months back and ordered the fish and chips. First off, I'm disappointed that I am unable to find a single place here in Tucson that uses Halibut for their fish...everything is cod.  I decided to go with the the fish and chips anyway. BIG Mistake! When the meal was delivered the fish hadn't been cooked all the way and was still frozen in the middle...totally gross. I ended up having a sub-par burger instead. I will never be returning.

The burgers...sweet mother Mary the burgers are perfect. We hit up the Trident for lunch and it was just what we needed. Fair warning: the burgers are pretty huge. Couple that with a mountain of fries (I'd go for the sweet potato fries, personally speaking) and you've got a pretty giant meal on your hands. As we were in uniform and on the clock, we chose to pass on beers...but there was a really great selection of local beers on the menu. It's a shame we didn't make it back!

As of this writing the food at the Trident on Speedway has gotten much better than it had been over the previous five years.  I had the Asian Chicken Salad, and instead of the previous anemic chucks of old chicken, it is now served with several huge freshly grilled skewers of chicken over an even better equally huge bed of greens ... all with a yummy ginger dressing.  Mazel Tov! to whom ever the new chef is.  Servers are the same third rate UA college types ... but hey, this ain't Harvard Square.  Great food makes up for the overly cute bimbettes serving it.  And the overly loud sound of crowds yelling at sport teams on the far too many TVs is made up for by the genuinely hot college guys rubbing up against their equally hot bros.

I ate here just yesterday, and had a small falafel sandwich and a bottle of water - both together cost less than 5 bucks - pretty cheap.  I wished I had room for some shwarma or a chicken kabob, or even some hummus and pita b/c it all smelled and looked fantastic.  

The only drawback to my experience was the cold (it was seriously freezing in there, like the windows weren't sealed or something) and there were some fairly rowdy regular-looking dudes sitting at the counter, yelling at each other and basically being douchebags.  I heard the word 'retard' at least 30 times over the time it took me to eat a small falafel sandwich, which was not that long at all.

In fact, I only went in to Chickpea's to check out the biggest fatty douchebag of them all  - he ran out of the restaurant to get into a smackdown with a PPA ticketing person.  The dude totally deserved a ticket and he was acting like a loon so I decided to follow him back in and grab some lunch....I had some time to kill, so why not?

Food: 3.5 stars
Service: 3.5 stars
Locations: 3.5 stars
Ambiance: 3 stars
Price: 3 stars

I had been to a Ruth's Chris in San Diego once before and this experience was completely different.  They were 30 minutes delayed in getting us seated from the time of our reservations.  Strange enough, the restaurant was pretty empty.  The filet was good but not "earth shattering, yelp immediately so everyone can try it" good.  The mashed potatoes were mediocre, similar to out of the box mashed potatoes.  The onion rings were well done though.

Overall: 3 stars
Ruth's Chris wants to be a fine dining establishment but is just an upgrade from Outback or other chain steakhouses.  It was worth the price with the Living Social deal but I would recommend one of the many other spectacular restaurants in the city for the same price range instead of Ruth's Chris

I stopped by Cuenelli's earlier this afternoon for a quick afternoon lunch. I work late, so I generally take my break around 6:00 or so. Cuenelli's usually closes at 5:00, though. I decided to take an early break and made a special trip down Hillsborough to try this place out, since I'd seen the great Yelp reviews.

The place was mostly deserted. The only sound was a futbol game on Univision. I was getting a little nervous, but a lady came to give me a glossy menu, and a couple of minutes later, I was delivered a tasty, juicy leg and thigh served hot off the rotisserie, a steaming hot cup of spicy beans, and a bowl of cilantro-infused rice with little bits of vegetables mixed in. All piping hot and all delicious. I washed it down with an Inca Kola, which I highly recommend to you international soda connoisseurs out there. Grand total: slightly over $8.00. I can whine about their hours, but I can't complain about the food or the price.

The location looks like a chain restaurant from the outside, but don't let that deter you. Cuenelli's is worth your time.

NO NO NO!

Sure, if you lived in some landlocked area of our country where fresh fish would be practically impossible to come by, then by all means, Sushi Tsu would be an excellent choice BUT only under those specific conditions.

In a city such as Tampa which invites the warm, tropical stream of the Gulf of Mexico, the fish is so fresh and so good, that this is the least of your concerns for Sushi options in the city.

When the fish is fine, then the attention is placed on the craftsmen that create the art of sushi and Sushi Tsu takes a back seat to the likes of Kaisen on Dale Mabry, and even Bonsai on Bears. Tsu is lacking in technical quality  and technical quality is as big, not bigger, but as big as the freshness of seafood. It's one of a few principles that sushi rests its foundation on. 

Amen.

If you're looking for good Mexican food this is not the place to go. We have not been to this restaurant for quite some time and right now we wish that we hadn't gone back. Some of the food had no flavor and some   of it tasted bad. We had a combination plate that came with two tacos and enchiladas. The tacos were just meat thrown on top of a corn tortilla nothing else and the enchiladas were just plain bad tasting. After eating we went into the restrooms and they were disgusting they were not clean and in need of major repair.

When I first got here 2 years ago this place didn't even accept credit cards! My oh My the changes made since then!    If I had rated them back then it would have been 1 star all the way. But now - Much improved!    and we frequent the establishment alsmost always 2-3 times per week!  Great job on improving!

The food is good but it isn't as good as it use to be.  I liked the food better when it was at the smaller location.  I think it suffered some when it went to the larger location.  The rolls are done well but the flavor kinda lacks that umph.  I haven't had the hibachi... but I am not a big fan of bland food cooked on a hot metal sheet.  The food gets 2 stars.

The service is good here.  The staff is attentive.  The bigger location is more comfortable. The service gives it 1 more star.

I'm sure there are lots of people who say that because it's a chain, it cannot be good.  Admittedly, I have not been to other non-chain steak houses in Philadelphia.  That said, Ruth's Chris is damn good.  It is good in other cities, and it is good in Philadelphia.

The wait staff is unbelievably professional and attentive.  You will never wait for water, because your glass will never be empty.  Service is fast, but it's never overbearing - you don't feel as though you can't enjoy your meal.

We had creamed spinach (always my favorite at Ruth's Chris) and mashed potatoes for our sides.  And filet mignon (so so so tender) and NY strip (very juicy and tasty).  All of the food was amazing.

Of course it's expensive, but every steak house is, and I believe Ruth's Chris is comparable to others in the city.  It's worth it.

This place is rad. I came for the first time (finally) for the first UofA football game and it was packed. We sat in one of the booths and had our choice of view of multiple TVs playing various games. 
I ordered the Tucson burger and it was reallllly good - I would definitely recommend it. Pitchers of beer were relatively cheap as well, I believe it was $10 for Coors Light. 
I would definitely come here again, maybe on a less busy night but it was still fun to see everyone there wearing red!
If you like clams. I mean if you really like clams, come to Trident. Thanks for bringing good seafood to Tucson.

I had a hard time deciding what to order because the menue had so many good options.    I tried the crab cakes appetizer and they were the best I had in years.    True to the Maryland recipe they had minimal amount of bread crumbs and large chunks of crab.   Not cheap but well worth it.   I also had the steak salad with spinach, blue cheese, egg, tomatoes and a sliced sirloin with an amazing balsamic reduction.    Both dishes were excellent!   I was going to take some pictures but started eating as soon as they arrived.
What a gem of a place in the francisville neighborhood! I had a skim chai latte and a sucre crepe. The staff was very friendly and the downstairs dining area was very welcoming. We will be back.

After receiving two, unrelated suggestions to try the Train Wreck Po Boy here within a week, I knew I had to try it.  In fact, the suggestions weren't even for Beck's, but rather the Reading Terminal Market so not only was it an incredible sandwich within the eatery, but of the entire place!  When it comes to Cajun/New Orleans style food, I'm a beginner, but what a first impression.  The look of it seemed like a long lost cousin of the Philly Cheesesteak, with the chopped up meat.  It has a trio of meats that blends each's flavors together perfectly: Andouille sausage, steak and salami.  It also is accompanied with onions and topped off with cheese.  They use a French bread which is the perfect choice to hold it all together (there's nothing more annoying than a delicious sandwich that breaks apart because the bread is too soft.  I also tried the Cajun fries and to my surprise were not fries at all, but potatoes with jalapenos, onions, and peppers all flavored with Louisiana spices.  My two recommendations came through with this one and I'll certainly be going back, and working 3 blocks from it definitely helps!

White Rice and black beans - SO GOOD! Deep fried hot dogs and fries - how could this be bad? It wasn't ... It was good! Rotisserie chicken - descent. But I'll come back to try the beef! Very clean inside and nice wait staff.
Great Peruvian chicken.  Healthy, juicy, meaty, lacking fat.  And the rice and beans, special sauce, yuca were great too.  I will come back from time to time.

Love this place- great place, great food, great drinks. 

I had the crab cake Benedict- fantastic. The Bloody Mary comes with a soft shell crab on top!!! 

Go Navy, beat Army.

We were rushing to Terminal market to get my daughter a bday cake and got there a few minutes before closing time. We saw Termini and ordered their Tiramisu cake. The lady at the counter who also personalized the cake was really nice and even gave us a free candle to take with us. Cakes are pricey but their service is great!!

Excellent place for a Pub Type Lunch.  Fish and Chips are great here.  Fresh and a huge 3 piece order for $11.00 with sides.   Had a retired guys group of 7 people for lunch.  Service by Baily was top notch.  Very attentive to customer needs and very friendly.
     A very fun place !!!!
Our favorite sports bar in Tucson. Great food and service, lots of tvs, not too drunk of an atmosphere. They do it all right.

It's not exactly rave-worthy, but the food at the Villagio is somewhat akin to a diner experience. In exchange for a wide selection, you settle for food that ranges from merely adequate to excellent. The surroundings are nice, and the staff is very friendly, if occasionally amateurish. But it's really nice to have an attractive sit-down place in the neighborhood that offers something other than cheesesteaks and pizza, and the prices are pretty reasonable -- I really like their daily dinner specials.

The food was ok not the best but ok. On the other hand the service was horrible not a refill on our drinks that were brought out way before our meal so half way thru the meal we ate with nothing to drink. Kinda disappointed with our experience. No plans on going back!

Forsake the fancy donuts (ok, I woke up too late) and dive right for the cinnamon. This is perfection - sweet, a bit salty, fresh. Pair it with a cup of Federal's great coffee. 

Service here is friendly and knowledgable, and I love the design of the place too, from the rube goldberg cold brew drip system to the stowable counter seating. 

It's rare to see a restaurant get all the elements right, especially a fast food place, but Federal is respectful to donuts while operating in a class by itself.

Oh, and the chicken? Yes, also great. 

The crowd here is happy too - who wouldn't be, eating delicious donuts and fresh fried chicken?

First time in Tucson, and came here based on the recommendation of a friend. It was the perfect place to have some good and beer before the Wildcats basketball game, as many fans filled the place. The menu has a ton of nice selections and everything I tried was superb. My friendly and knowledgeable waitress suggested the brawt sliders and the bruschetta (it was the best I've ever had!). Can't wait to return!!

This is a great spot. Good drinks, food, and atmosphere. The inside of Trident is very typical of a sports bar with lots of televisions, etc. It's comfortable. The drinks are good. I think their selection is decent and I like the mixed drink I always get (I believe it's called keep a float, might be wrong on that!). For me what really makes this place stand out (as far as sports bars go) is the food. The food is better than an average sports bar. They've got your classic wings and such but then they have dishes like crab stuffed mushrooms and green chile mac n cheese that's amazing. The mac n cheese is probably my favorite thing to get.

Definitely would recommend Trident for watching a game or hanging out with friends.

#1 - the pignoli cookie
#2 - the canoli
#3 - everything else!!!

That is the order in which I pig out at Termini's.

Their pignoli/pine nut cookie is unbelievable. It is always moist in the center with a strong flavor of almond paste. My in-laws in Brasil go crazy for them. My mom recently sent us a batch in our new house in LA, and they didn't even last 24 hours.

The canoli... Forgive the spelling, I'm not Italian. :) my boyfriend has never had one. I hadn't had one since I had the best one in Quincy Market, MA. Well boo to Quincy, because the ricotta one here at Termini's blew them out of the water! And recently I had a canoli at my new local bakery, and my boyfriend and I pretentiously joked about how it doesn't even compare to Termini's.

All of the other things i've had on different occasions, and they are always amazing, but I like to stick to my #1 and #2!

I've been here 3 times and always had a good experience - I've also always ordered the same thing 'cuz it's so good I can't stray away! I had the chicken andouille gumbo and i love it! So flavorful, so good! The service is always fast and friendly and they let you have little tastings of the gumbo if you'd like before you order. I've heard great things about the mac and cheese and can't wait to try those next.

I was first attracted to this place from a Yelp search promising great local cuisine at good prices and boy did it deliver. First of all, super easy to find and great parking. You can smell that chicken roasting from the outside and it pulls you right in. Our waitress Yvette was absolutely wonderful and answered all our detailed questions, as none of us knew what Peruvian food was. 

Basically it's rotisserie chicken-- succulent and delish chicken. Choose either dark or white meat and it comes with spicy beans, cilantro rice (AMAZING), salad with a cilantro sauce (surprisingly tasty house salad) or french fries (don't be lame, people). The dipping sauce that accompanied the chicken was some type of spicy mustard and I slathered it on everything. 

For a sit down restaurant they were very quick, we were in and out in easily 30 minutes. We even got a military discount. 

Pro tip: Please note, your credit card purchase must be over $8 or bring cash.

This review is for the zeppole aka St Joseph cake. The shell is dry and the filling is basically the same as cannolis. Frangelli's is much better because the shell is more moist and overflows with amazing filling. However other pastries are great including the ricotta cannoli.

The ricotta cannoli is not watery, perfect sweetness with mini chocolate chip filled for your order so that you can taste the crunchiness of the shell. Best eaten right away to avoid sogginess.

The chocolate covered banana is their specialty too. It's banana on an almond pastry with some cream and banana fillings.

Their shoe horn is great too. It's basically an almond pastry with some almond paste. Its a must for almond lovers.

The fig bar is filled with fig covered in a thin pastry.

Another Italian pastry to try is sfogiatelle. The shell i a crunchy and layered pastry filled with ricotta andd a hint of citrus flavor that brings a fresh taste.

For cookies, my favorite is the amaretti and pignoli. The cookie is very moist with almond paste.

As much as it hurts me to say this, I've experienced better which is why I had a hard time deciding what to give. However, the place looks really cool inside and I can tell our server was still a bit new. So we had to harmlessly tease her because she was cute. She was nice about it.

I went with a small group and we waited for a hibachi grill for about 15 min. when it wasn't even that busy. But we didn't mind waiting because it gave us the chance to mosey around. The decor is really well laid out and creative. They even have like a zen like waterfall in the lobby.

The menu is average and have decent choices for tappenyaki (grilled food cooked in front of you) and small choices of sushi. My date and I were not that hungry so we just ordered the Seafood Grill Iron Skillet with the choice of scallops and a volcano roll. The scallops tasted interesting cooked in a white wine sauce. But when the food was complete I was kind of disappointed. The server told me that I'd be getting rice with noodles and vegetables, only one person out of the group had it. So I had little amounts of noodles and vegetables. And I was disappointed that they didn't have yummy yummy or goody goody sauce like Kobe or Arigato's (miss so much), BUT I was pleasantly surprised we were graced with an actual Japanese chef. I may sound like a giddy school girl, but that is rare to have one here. When the volcano roll arrived, I was stunned. It looked nothing like a volcano roll I've ever seen. Most places I've had it from it normally looked like a volcano erupted, but instead the presentation looked like a sad roll made of regular California roll with a glob of light orange mush on each piece. It wasn't even that spicy! I love spicy so we packed on the wasabi in the soy sauce until if finally reached my level of comfort. 

For such small portions, our bill was surprising. For just 5 people, we were still charged for an 18% gratuity. We were feeling nice so we didn't complain about anything so we just let everything slide. I probably won't come back anytime soon.

Very disappointing! Flys are flying around. Chips were smashed mostly crumbs! Salsa had no flavor, and we were offered 3. My mom found a piece of green plastic in her beans and the waitress said "I don't know where that came from!" It has been maybe 10 years since I've been here and it will be the last. I'd rather go to Nico's Taco Shop for this quality of food at a better price. I read the review about the sopa de tortilla and how it was good:/ I don't know if maybe they came on a good day but if you consider bland broth, soggy chips and melted cheese then by all means get this soup! ;)

We went here during dinner at the reading terminal market.  We order the short rib po boy and the gator gumbo. They were both good and very filling.  Gator is in a sausage did not realize it until my wife mentioned this. Anyways they do give out samples which was nice as well.  Everything was good and highly recommend.

This place is also in the Reading Terminal Market. I got my gumbo from there and it was swangin!! Nice and spicy. They had 2 different ones. Either the gator gumbo or the chicken and sausage. I wasn't ready for the gator so I did the chicken and sausage. The jambalaya was damn good also with the spicy Louisiana taste I look for. I was surprised at the taste as it was prepared here in Philly and no one had a Louisiana background but it tasted so authentic. I had to give them 5 stars on the strength of that alone.

Updating and upgrading to 5 stars. Cuenelli's continually serves up some of the most flavorful moist chicken in town. Wonderful sides and the waitresses here are the best. Worth a visit no matter where you live in this area.

Beck's has a great selection of southern favorites.. super hearty, comforting food that explode with flavors in your mouth. Definitely stop by and try as many samples across their buffet as you like. The staff here is incredibly friendly and helpful. My favorites are the chicken and andouille gumbo, the crawfish etouffee and their renowned jambalaya. You can mix and match any of the soups on top of an order of rice or have them separately.. the world is now in your hands.

Still hungry and feeling a bit dare devilish? Their gator on a stick/gator gumbo is always a great way to add a little pizazz to a lunch date.

The salsa was salty, while the pork and nopalitos combined overcooking and underseasoning to a rather mediocre effect.  The chicken enchiladas in molé sauce were fine, but not especially memorable.  La Parrilla Suiza does earn a few points for tasty beans and pico de gallo.  The service was friendly and the atmosphere was not unpleasantly generic.

Overall, a bland and unmemorable experience.

This bb  was our first visit to Reading Terminal Market.  With all the choices in food to select from, we decided to try Beck's Cajun Cafe.  Our server, Grace, was very hospitable and made recommendations as we were having a hard time deciding what to eat.  The menu has all the traditional Cajun foods - catfish, gumbo, jambalaya, po-boy's, Mac and cheese, and red beans and rice.  I had the shrimp po-boy and my husband had the catfish platter.  The shrimp was crispy, the remoulade had a good flavor, and the bread was soft with a chewy crust.  The catfish platter was a good size plate with 6 catfish fillets and enough red beans and rice that is certain to fill any empty spots in one's stomach.  As for food and our server, I would give a rating of 5.  

I am giving a reduced rating due to one employee.  During our 30 minutes at this establishment, we watched one employee (female, thin. long dark brown hair, nose ring, in shorts and black boots) sit on her butt and on her phone the entire time.  Other staff had to maneuver around this employee and she appeared to be disinterested in moving a muscle.  The rest of the staff, servers and kitchen staff were moving non-stop while this one employee did nothing. Every employee is a representative of the organization to which they work. This employee is certainly lacking in a positive representation for your company.

I've only tried the cannoli here, but wow! First of all, it's very refreshing to see a bakery that does not pre-fill a ton of cannoli and have them sitting in the display case. They look pretty, yes, but who wants a soggy cannolo? 

Anyway, this was exactly what it should be like: that perfect contrast of the crispy fried shell with the creamy ricotta filling. Simple but pretty much perfect. On par or better than the cannoli I've had at many highly-touted bakeries.

I'll definitely be back!

The service was good, but we were there early and the place was half empty.  The meat is very good, but I only give them three stars because I feel for the prices we paid the meat should be out of this world.  It was not.  We went there after a show which was right around the corner from this restaurant so it was convenient at the time.  Glad we went because it was a special occasion and we did enjoy ourselves, but am not sure if we would go again.

I enjoy the food at this place a lot. Hands down the best deal for your money. The everyday deal of two large fries, two cheese steaks and two cans of soda for $16 is pretty amazing. This is my go to if I'm getting takeout. Excellent place with kind and friendly staff.

Ate in tonight and the serving size was huge! Really enjoyed the quality of the food and the price was amazing! Again the staff was friendly, welcoming and accommodating. Will return!

I bought a dim sum cooking class for my brother and I to do together for christmas. I sure am glad I didn't look at the Yelp reviews before I bought the class, because otherwise I might have missed out on a great experience. There were 8 people in our class, which was the perfect size. Chef Poon started by showing us around the kitchen. We then went back to the cooking tables and learned to make all different types of won-tons and dumplings. Throughout the class Chef Poon tells lots of funny stories. I noticed some of the reviews below talked about his arrogance, but I think that is an unfortunate take on a man who just has a very outspoken character. Chef Poon is a showman and an entertainer, who also happens to be a master chef. The dumplings and wontons were then cooked and brought out to us - they were all delicious! Way too much food to eat, but we were allowed to take home leftovers. Then we learned to roll some noodles and make a quail egg dumpling. At the end of the program, Chef Poon and his helpers prepared a meal for us with general "joe's" chicken, shanghai noodles (yum!), string beans, the noodles we made, some sauteed vegetables. It was all delicious. My only complaint is that the class got started late and so there was less time at the end to enjoy the dinner. We had to get going because we were trying to catch a train, so I wish we had more time for dinner. All in all though, a really fun experience with a friend or family member!

I ordered a couple of mini-cakes as a birthday gift for someone who's not exactly a "cake person" so in these small doses they were great and were well received. I bought the tiramasu (which I tried) and the strawberry one (which I didn't). It was surprisingly smooth and light. I'm inclined to try the vanilla crunch cake (I think that's it) when it's in season. Eh, not sure what vanilla season is... but they said it wasn't in season when I asked. The mini-cakes are pricy too so I think they're better served as little gifts anyway.

We like to try new eateries.  Last night, I was trying to think of someplace unique to grub down at, and I saw the review for Cuenelli's. We have driven past this spot 5 or 6 times, but never when we  are actually hungry, so I made sure we were hungry tonight. 

We can throw my knowledge of authentic Peruvian recipes out the window. Other than knowing that the potato originated in the geographical region of Inca Empire, I don't know Jack crap about the food, and have never had it. That being said, what I can tell you is that the food was magical. We throw down at a lot of Latin spots, but this was completely different. The flavors were not what you'd get from a Caribbean Latin restaurant at all, and that was a pleasant change.

I had the LOMO SALTADO, which I believe roughly translates to "this dish will make you wanna slap ur momma." (I've added a pic for visual assistance.) This was a sirloin or flank-type steak cut into thin strips and stir fried in a soy-vinegar sauce with tomatoes and onions. It was served on a bed of french fries and with what seemed like an endless supply of white rice. (I thought only Puerto Ricans served dishes on top of fries.)

La Chica had the BISTEC A LO POBRE, which roughly translates to "poor people's steak." This was a palomilla steak served with fries, white rice, black beans, amarillos and topped with a fried egg. This dish is actually pretty common in Latin America. Hell, you can get the American version at IHOP. The whole world probably eats some variation of this dish. Either way, it was really good.

We did order some chicken since that's their staple item, and it was really good. It came with CILANTRO RICE (a-freaking-mazing) and SPICY BEANS. The chicken was moist, tender and cooked to perfection. It came with 2 dipping sauces that accented the flavor of the chicken beautifully.

We will definitely go back.

The owner came back in and turned the place around. It is back to one of the best bars and grills in the neighborhood. Great selection of beers. Good bar keep. Good food. Great service. Good happy hour prices. Damn. I better go tonight....
Fast, friendly service and very good food! I recommend the gator gumbo with white rice and lemonade for a quick and tasty lunch. Yum!

Cuenelli's is one of my favorite spots in Tampa and every time I ask someone if they've been, they say, "no what is that?" And I'm totally flabbergasted! 

Let's start with my favorite- the yuca. So delicious and perfectly cooked. They have an appetizer of yuca with a spicy cheese sauce, it's incredible! You MUST order the cilantro rice and spicy beans. They aren't that spicy, but it's a nice switch up from black beans. Omg- the tres leches is to die for! Make sure you save room. 

The service is always prompt and friendly. The only reason I'm only giving 4 stars is because albeit the chicken being delicious, it's often dry. While you can drown it in yummy "yellow sauce", I prefer juicy chicken!
Caught me with a sample of jambalaya as I walked by, which I've never had, and it was so good I bought a side with cornbread! Yum!

Read about a NEW Trident opening up @ old Grimaldi's.  Never even heard of the Trident in over a decade of living and noshing in the area.  So today the Misses & I made it a point to attend.  Had the menu in our head so choosing a meal was easy.
WHAT A TREAT!!!!
A non-descript venue in a professional suite, it was tough to find, save for the little sign out front.  Parking is precious and some is reserved so be careful where to park.
Upon entry, I thought the worst.  The place looked crowded but a quick look for the bar showed IT nearly empty.  Great!  Love to eat at the bar, anywhere!
Very quick service for an adult beverage and menus.  Time to scope the place out.  'Twas lunch time so there were tables full of well dressed adults, normal conversation level and massive quantities of food.
A naval motif, replete with period photos, dominated the main dining area and SEAL trident pins were embedded into the bar.  There were unit and professional service patches tacked over the bar.
I ordered a pound of steamed clams and a Reuben, my Wife ordered the fish & chips.
The clams were done to a "T."  Not rubbery or fishy tasting; means they were fresh and cooked correctly.  My Wife's Alaskan cod was very lightly batter fried, moist, meaty and sweet.  My Reuben was probably the best I have ever had.  Lots of tender meat, large pieces of marbled rye, 'slaw to die for, melted cheese and dressing.  Served piping hot!
We couldn't ask for anything more!
The price was nominal for the amount of food and the area.
We're very hesitant to try new places of late as they mostly turn out flat.
The Trident didn't disappoint and we cannot wait for Trident Pizza!!!!
"Keep an even strain, Trident!"
P.S:    Not ONE screaming, yelping, gurgling or out of control child.  In fact, not a child in the place!  Made for a GREAT dining experience!

Ah yes another steakhouse...

The meals are fairly pricey, but for a quality steak, not unreasonable. However, the steak I ordered was very tender and flavorful, but I could only eat about a half of it. Imagine my surprise when the second half turned out to be 96% fat. There was a very thin layer of meat along the cut line, but the remainder was nothing but fat. 

It is very high class place but it is all show. Try Sullivan's instead.
Quite large dish amount for me. Service is good. Food is delicious. We ordered Wildcat, Philly cheese steak (side dish: onion ring)

Flew into Tucson around 10pm tonight (Wednesday), all the restaurants were calling it a day. I'm from Vegas, where nothing ever closes, so I forget to consider that when traveling! Anyway, I found Trident Grill on Yelp, and had a great meal there. Cody was at the bar, recommended a great burger and ale, and it was delicious, came out fast, and was cheap, too! Nice job to Cody, I'll be back.

The train wreck is my top 3 sandwiches of all time. Holy shit it's good! If you like big flavor eat this...if you don't then don't! I can't stand bland food and this is faaaaar from that :) it punches your taste buds with every bite lol

Without question, Ruth's Chris will never leave you disappointed. In addition to their steaks, their southern-minded seafood and tuna is excellent. Moreover, it's the many choices of starches that get people talking (I've always found the Shoestring french fries to be far more memorable than any cut of beef here).

Still, as others have duly pointed out, there are homegrown options to eat better steaks, or on par steaks in Philadelphia, without resorting to a chain. The Starr Report packs some local flavor, for around the same money.

Ruth's makes sense if you're in Vegas, or in Orlando (which actually has better local steakhouses) or some other concrete, franchise hell... but in Philly, we have better offerings that when I want to take someone out for a steak, I pass right by Ruth's and Morton's just knowing that somebody else is eating the same thing somewhere else at the exact moment.

OK so it's not real Cajun. But real Cajun is pretty damn hard to find outside of Louisiana. I'd say Beck's does a decent job. My biggest complaint is that they really tone down the spices, which I know they do because most people can't handle spiciness but that's where a portion of the flavor comes from. Overall it's a good choice if you need your fix and you can't make your own.

I can't get enough of their Rotisserie chicken... I eat here at least twice a week cause it's so close to my work...the cilantro rice is amazing as well. More than fair prices. You gotta try this spot it's on point every time.

This place rocks. I just had nachos with ground beef- amazing. A green chile burger cooked perfectly medium rare with French fries lettuce tomato red onion. Best burger ever in a long time. Best nachos ever.  My boyfriend got the Chesapeake bay burger with Munster grilled onions and old bay seasoning. If I could give more stars I would. Murphy was our waitress she was awesome.

Good bagel and coffee.. but went at 11am on a Sunday morning and they didn't have eggs?? What kind of breakfast cafe doesn't have eggs when it's over half their menu? There was only one other customer in there and three people standing around "working"... send someone to the store?? Service wasn't overly welcoming.

Amazing service, amazing food!!! Environment is great. Got a West Coast BLT and was seriously impressed with it. Massive amounts of bacon and avacado. My son's burger was huge. Husband got oysters on the half and said they were great (which for Tucson is impressive). Can't wait to come back!
The food was very tasty, service was excellent. The guacamole  salsa was excellent. Wiil definitely  come back again

Yes, they have a great beer list. Plus, the nachos were piping hot and had just the right chip-to-topping ratio.

But the best thing about Trident is the bar staff! I sat mid-bar in the middle of a UA basketball game when the place was packed. But even in all the commotion, the two bartenders were so attentive that I was astonished. I never had to wait more than a few seconds for fast and friendly service. I was totally impressed.

I've been having cravings for falafel for weeks now. No joke. Its been awful, and no (decent) place even relatively nearby delivers. So one night while out on South Street I walked past Chickpeas and stopped dead in my tracks. YES. FALAFEL. I had no idea what this place would be like but it didn't matter because I had to satisfy this craving that's driven me to contemplate making my own falafel.

It was kind of on the late side, possibly around 8:15pm, so no other customers were in there. The server was really nice and waited patiently as I contemplated my options, finally opting for the falafel platter because dinner had really only been cocktails (damn fine cocktails, which on an empty stomach only makes me feel, well, happy and eager for alot of good food). And wow is that platter worth it. He just kept doling out more and more food - I got a choice of three different salads, opting for the classic tomato-cucumber, roasted beets, and eggplant, either rice or fries (got the fries - more than enough for me, my bf, and any random stranger or two who might decide to ask for a handful), hummus, pita, and of course all the falafel, which numbered like ten. It was obscene how much food I walked away with for less than $9. 

Once home, I dug in with gusto and boy was I surprised - that's pretty darn good falafel! The salads were also relatively good, but the hummus was a bit of a disappointment for me; it was rather watery and had no salt whatsoever. Thank goodness I had some Tribe hummus in my fridge. The pita was terrific, I got the whole wheat one and it was warm and soft and just freaking awesome. There really was no reason for the fries, and they weren't exactly my kind of fries: more soft overall, not crispy and crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. But for so much food, and really rather fantastic at that, I couldn't complain about some measly fries that I couldn't even eat anyway. This place is great! If my homemade falafel doesn't meet standards, I know where to go instead.

A cute little place on 16th street, nice and cozy! A group of us went here for breakfast and the food/service was delicious. I got the honey bee and my girlfriend got a sweet crepe and they were both awesome. The iced coffee was awesome too. I would come back here for sure, very awesome low key spot.

This is the bomb!!!!
Becks is the best thing next to Cafe du Monde and more!
Sundays- The Beignets are outstanding, but arrive before 11am because they always sell out. 
The food is just as good, and better, as what you can get in Louisiana. 
We will always look forward to Becks while in Philly.

Today was my 3rd visit at European Wax Center and I must say they now have a client for life thanks to Tyisha! She's literally amazing each time I've been here she's made me feel so comfortable while I was super  nervous lol. I also love how pleasant the  receptionist are at the front desks. They greet you as soon as you walk in with a friendly smile. I never have to wait always in and out!! Overall I'm satisfied and will be back for sure !! I can't forget to thank my Best-friend for the referral!!

My  husband and I are go here all the time  our favorite meal  our salads   I  like  the spinach  salad   which  is so good  and my husband likes the chicken  salad  which is good  we love the friendly  staff  their  the  bar tenders   Sarah,  Bethanie     ,  and   Ashley   are very  sweet and nice  !  As  well as Grant  and Danny  the managers   are very nice and friendly  Jason  also  who is a manager  very friendly  the wait staff there also very nice!

Very very cute cafe! I think their crepes and teas are good. Not quite I-NEED-THIS-A-FEW-TIMES-A-WEEK good, but I'd-be-happy-to-come-back kinda good. My friend and I split a honey bee and the nutella strawberry one.

3/31/2011  Shockingly unsafe food handling practices.  After paying for my food, I noticed the sandwhich maker was not wearing gloves when he started making my sandwhiches.  Mid-stream he placed gloves on and opened a package of raw meat.  After placing the meat on the grill, he used the same gloved hand to dip into the tomatoes that he placed on my sandwhich.  I watched in horror and then asked if I coudl cancel my order.  It's also surprising to see a large number of  folks behind the counter with long hair and no nets to cover them.   I can only imagine what happens when the customers are not watching.

LL

I always go to Ruth's Chris in King Of Prussia , I guess it's convenient for me to go after shopping at the mall. 

This is my first time at this location, it was so hard to find a parking in the city! This isn't their fault but $15 for valet park, that could have been an extra cocktail coming to me . 

The service was good just like usual, our server was really patient with us and making suggestions. For appetizer we ordered shrimp cocktail and a Caesar salad to share. For entrees we ordered rib eye,  petite filet and  lamb chop. The shrimp and caesar salad were good but nothing special. The lamb chop was extremely dry , what a mistake. The rib eye and filet were also so so . 

we also ordered three cocktail, one of them was their special, I forgot the name of it but it was basically raspberry martini.

While in Tucson, I searched online for places where we might find my husband's favorite beer, Kilkenny. Trident Grill was the place!

Our service was excellent and the atmosphere was pleasant on a Saturday evening. My husband had his Kilkenny, and I had a margarita that was quite delicious. We ordered tortilla chips for our son.

I had the roast chicken salad. Mind you, I was starving and emotionally drained after a full day at the book festival, and this salad seriously hit the spot. Lovely, big chunks of chicken breast and a good blend of flavors and textures.

My husband had the Hatch burger and fries and thought it was all quite good. 

We'd come here again when we are visiting Tucson--especially if they continue to serve Kilkenny!

I remember the first time I came to DK Sushi and ordered a really overpriced shrimp tempura roll and was very unimpressed. I came back a year or two later after being recommended the Omakase and was B L O W N away. Filling, fresh, authentic, for only $35 - woweee. Yes, it's assumed you wouldn't come to Franklin Table for its ambience - it's a college dining hall for heaven's sake, but are you really a foodie if you're not willing to sacrifice ambience for hidden gems? 

I came to DK Sushi for omakase a week after I went to Sakana which was $58/pp and left so hungry I went and got a full Italian meal after. After DK's omakase, I was so full I could barely walk home. Despite being in a college dining hall, DK makes an effort to serve each dish on a stone platter with impeccable plating. Also, no one's rushing you so you really have the true opportunity to focus on the food and whoever you're dining with. 10/10 would recommend. Great for the experience, poor on the ambience, you'll leave happy if you're into sushi :)

Staying in the Hilton Garden Inn so the market is right next door.  How do you choose where to get your dessert for the day?  Well the Termini Bros Bakery was the right choice.  We ordered a small red velvet and a small chocolate mousse cake to take back to our room.  They did not disappoint.  Moist and delicious!  I'm so glad we will be here tomorrow again.  Can't wait to see what to order tomorrow!

Watching the whole season of Treme in a two week span gave me a serious hankering for some cajun/creole food.  

We split the etouffee of the day (shrimp and crawfish) and a po boy.  At the server's suggestion, we got oyster & shrimp, which was a good call on her part.

The etouffe was great.  The po boy was pretty good, could have used more remoulade and pickles.  The po boy's at 10th St Pourhouse were better (at least as I remember them; haven't had one there since I moved out of the neighborhood).

Our server gave us a sample of the bread pudding, which was just enough to top off a great meal.  $20 (not including tip) for the two entrees and 2 sodas.  Awesome.

PS.  Made me miss that New Orleans restaurant that used to be in the space Tequila's currently occupies -- anyone remember it from a million years ago?  They used to let people throw beads up into the tree in front... I can't remember the name of it.  If you know, pls message me, it's driving me nuts.
The food was very good and authentic!  Also very reasonably price!  I would recommend this place.

I can't believe only one other person has reviewed this place.  People, what are you doing with your LIVES?  Beck's is truly Delicioustown, USA.  Consider moving there.

I was down for life with the first bite of Gator Gumbo.  I don't know anything about Cajun food, so I don't have a comparison point, but damn that shit was gooooood.  It was just so....deep and smoky.  The flavors went straight to my (non-existent) soul.  The love continued upon sampling the pumpkin cinnamon bisque and also the black eyed pea soup.  Damn, that bisque.  The consistency made me so happy, to say nothing of richness.  

Seriously.  Put down that shitty slice of pizza and go here now.  But watch out for me, since I may steal your food...

If you haven't tried Peruvian food, then this is a great place to start. Try the Peruvian style rotisserie chicken. It is absolutely delicious! The service is fantastic with a smile. It never hurts to have beautiful Peruvian servers to add to the experience. 
This place is cheap and not far from Tampa's airport. Buen Provecho!

I simply don't like anything about Ruth's Chris.  I love steak houses and I've given this place the proverbial three strikes.  Actually....four now that I think about it and in multiple cities.  Let me be clear; I don't like the name, the drinks, the appetizers, entrees, I don't like the way they prepare steaks, deserts, I don't like the room(s), service, clientele.  I don't even like the damned carpet!

Thank you very much.
What a delight to find authentic New Orleans cuisine n the Reading Terminal Market! I had the shrimp and crawfish etoufee. Perfection!!!

This is a must stop for me every time I get to Philly. Thank goodness it's almost always a weekend trip so I can get a couple meals here, because it's so hard to choose what to get. 

I recommend the shrimp po boy, but the real money is the snapper turtle soup. Thick and spicy it's out of this world. Another great sandwich is the gator sausage.

Morale of the story, you can't go wrong with any of it. Just get there.

In town after a long weekend of hiking and camping. The burgers were well seasoned and cooked as ordered with lots of flavor! 
Waitresses were super friendly and attentive. Was expecting more of a bar a scene but was pleasantly surprised for a relaxing dinner with locals.

Trident is where it happens...magic that is...I once saw a unicorn...twice

They use unicorn blood on their wings, they call it H-1, I'm not sure if that violates any endangered species law....but it's worth it.

They're missing a bald eagle omelet, name it "Merica!"

Take that Denny's! boom

I didn't know what to order and haven't been in reading terminal market in awhile...they gave me a sample of the gumbo. it was flavorful and a l ittle spicy. yum i ended up ordering the Jambalaya. it had a mixture of the Andouille Sausage, chicken and shrimp with veggies and , of course, rice. It was a little spicy and had a nice cajun flavor/spice I will come back and bring friends who enjoy spice.
The BEST chicken I've ever tasted! Great sides, clean atmosphere and friendly staff!!!
Fantastic bar!  Especially if your are Redskins fan!!! Great grub and drink selection. Definitely will become a regular here!!!  Been here twice and, the calamari and Nachos are on spot!

This is the second time I have returned to Termini Brothers Bakery inside the Reading Terminal Market. Their best seller which is the cannoli is worth the 1 & 1/2 hr. drive from where I live. This time, aside from the customary order of cannoli, we tried some of their other offerings i.e. - their mini cakes 1) Limoncello cake & 2) Red Velvet cake. They were heavenly! The cakes were moist, decadent & not overly sweet. Needless to say, you cannot just stop at one bite (they were history before we even got out of the Reading Terminal Market). This review however is for the "pecan bar". Had to make sure I had to get some this visit. It did not disappoint. This pecan bar was heavenly, just the right amount of sweetness, texture & moistness. I am so glad I got more than one. I will most surely try other pastries they offer next visit. Definitely in my must visit list when traveling back to Philly. This place is highly recommended.

It's my spot when I go to Tucson. Food is pretty good for a bar, always has games on, very friendly staff. Wish they had whiskey cubes instead of a glass full of ice machine ice but I'm just nit picking at this point. Burgers are good, clam chowder is good.
One of the most salty food items (gumbos) i have ever had. Talk about a overhyped place. Nope!

I was surprised I liked Trident so much considering its a Seal bar and I'm an Army fan :) Love their all day happy hour on Sunday. Most 22oz draft beers are $3 during and they have some $3, $4 and $5 appetizers. The canteen is awesome... I love the horseradish dipping sauce! Their salads are really good as well. Every time I go I just end up getting a bunch of appetizers because there are so many tasty ones to choose from! Definitely a great menu, lots of drafts to choose from and a neat dive bar feel to it. Its a good place to go to before or after UA sporting events because you can walk to and from most of the games.

Do you like mariachi music? I mean do you really like mariachi music? If not, don't go here. They start off far away sounding enticing, I take another sip of my delicious margarita and then they start moving closer towards my table and all I wanted to do was stick my fingers in my ears! It was blasting and remained that way until they started blasting some other poor folks in the next room. I fessed up the margarita were delicious, the ribs I ordered were the best I have had anywhere, and the chips and three tasty salsas as good as it gets, but I will not go back until the place is clear of horns!  But if you like mariachi music, if you really like mariachi music, I would recommend this place.

Ordered the gumbo.. it's was just ok.. 
They need two cash registers because the line is slower than necessary. . Food is made with limitations. . Gumbo either u select chicken and shrimp OR chicken and sausage.. 
I come from new Orleans so we put all of that in one pot.. average experience. .
Good price for good crepes. I had the savory Philly crepe. Came with smoked salmon, cream cheese, and spinach. Generous amount of smoked salmon evenly spread out in the crepe. Well worth the $9.

Was very impressed with the service and they even let me sample a few dishes to help me choose. I never thought Philly was the place for gumbo, but man on man! The alligator gumbo was so so good! If I wasn't headed back to Chicago that day, I would've gotten a bowl to go! Will be visiting Philly again just to get another taste!

Context: Weekend Lunch
Time of Visit: Saturday, 12:30PM

As a fan of cajun food, it doesn't get much better than Beck's.

They have many cajun/creole favorites: red beans and rice, jambalaya, gumbo, and po-boys.  If you are looking for more standard fare with a cajun attitude, they have blackened chicken alfredo, bread pudding, and awesome cornbread.  

They also have an interesting version of a Philly Cheesesteak called the "Train Wreck"; it is huge.  Also, most of their dishes do have a spicy kick, so sensitive palates should definitely sample before ordering.

If you are unsure about what to get, ask the staff for a sample: they will be more than happy to oblige (I didn't ask, but was given a sample anyway).  They are very friendly and can also help you pair dishes if you would like to mix-and-match.  I sampled the Gator Gumbo, and while it sounded like something I would shy away from, it ended up being my order for the day.

Portion sizes are very generous, with most entrees coming in at just under $10.

Delicious food at great price! We tried the family chicken meal and lomo with rice and fries. The lomo plate was my favorite. 
Atmosphere and service were great. Just at the end she was awkwardly hasty in clearing out table. We were about to leave and the place was half empty. We enjoyed it anyway!
Currently typing this from my bed with violent food poisoning. Order at your own risk.

I have to tell you I have not been since college and just moved back n everything was pretty good. Green salsa was smoky n a lil too limey but tasty. Mole good as well could have used a touch of sweetness n it would have been awesome. They didn't wanna take my freebie coupon which brought us in because I ordered a lunch special not a "regular" meal huh where it say that? They ended up taking it n were pleasant about it.

I like this place - it's not bad. It's just $$$ for students - which are their primary clientele. I'd come here if I want to splurge on a sushi box or a spicy scallop roll.

Generally fresh - I've had a few of their items like their salmon-based chef box (cute presentation/unnecessary for extra cost though), a few of their rolls, their bowls and more. 

Maybe because I am not a big fan of Double Knot so I don't find it super special but I think if you're looking for a quick sushi fix but don't mind spending the money, then it's the place to go.

Decided to branch out from my usual roast pork at DiNic's and try a place I haven't been to before at Reading Terminal.  I am so glad we ended up here!  Since it was around 11 in the morning, my boyfriend was in the mood for something breakfast-y and the "Rise & Shine" menu at Beck's was calling ("beck"-oning?) us.

We both got the Bourbon Street Breakfast (red beans & rice topped with a fried egg, melted cheese, & grilled cornbread) but subbed the rice and beans: I subbed mine for jambalaya, he subbed his for the andouille & chicken gumbo.

People.  Get this breakfast bowl.  It's simple, I'll admit.  But it's such a nice change from your typical breakfast menu options.  First of all, the jambalaya was delicious.  It was a hearty base with chunks of shrimp, chicken, and sausage.  Just the right amount of heat, too.  Next up we have the fried egg.  It was cooked perfectly over medium which is my preference, even though I didn't mention that when ordering.  A slice of American cheese is melted on top, which is the only thing I didn't like.  I don't think it added anything to the dish and would recommend skipping it.

The bowl is topped with two pieces of perfect cornbread.  It's slightly sweet which is a nice counter to the spice of the jambalaya.  I also love how they grill it which adds a little bit of crunch.  Nice detail to elevate it.

Service was kind and quick.  I would definitely come here again for breakfast and to try their other offerings as well.

Took a walk down memory lane during a recent trip to philly. Staying right across the street from Reading terminal and HAD to sneak out of my conference at the convention center  for 2 amazing treats to keep in my hotel room! When o was a little girl, birthday celebrations included an Italian cream cake ( or Italian rum cake) to some from terminis. I asked and they delivered one delicious slice. One bite of this rich cake and I was transported back to birthdays with my Italian grandpop!  This cake is layers of delicious thick sponge like cake, layered with both chocolate and vanilla rum infused cream, generously iced then coated with crushed peanuts. Too rich to eat in one sitting! The other treat was sfigliatelle: crunchy layer upon layer of pastry shaped like a lobster tail  and inside sweetened ricotta cheese delicately flavored with orange peel. Omg. Heaven  the staff were accommodating, the store is spotless! A bit pricey but worth it for size and quality. Only complaint was I went back the next day for another slice and they were SOLD OUT! Waaahhh

Found this restaurant on Yelp by searching on rotisserie chicken & decided to try because of the excellent reviews.  Picked up the Family Dinner Combo for around $24 to feed three adults.  It included a whole chicken and I got to pick three sides.  I chose black beans, plantains and french fries.  Everything was delicious!  The chicken was mouthwatering delicious, the black beans flavorful, the plantains plump and tasty, and the french fries very plentiful to say the least. There were enough fries to fill a large bowl!  Will definitely be returning.  The only reason I gave four instead of five stars is that I've only been there once.  I save five stars for repeated excellence and have confidence this place will earn that distinction...

I go to this place every time I'm in town (which is not enough). My favorite dish is the pesto sandwich. It's pesto, mozzarella, tomatoes, and avocado on a perfectly toasted baguette. It's served with a side salad drizzled with a balsamic vinaigrette that pairs so well with the sandwich. Reminds me of Italy!

I ordered its sfogliatelles. very disappointed. The shape did not look like lobster tail, which  is a quiet big disappointment. The taste was OK, not fantastic.Honestly I think I should get a refund for them!
I cannot speak for other items. jst like the review said :"Meh. I've experienced better.
 "

Wow, after reading all of those terrible reviews, I think it's safe to say that the best bang for your buck is attending the cooking class Chef Poon offers. Perhaps this distracts from his ability to offend the sensitive types? 

All I know is that my hubby and I had a great time learning to cook Peking duck, learned a lot in general, got to cook in his kitchen, eat the food we cooked, scored a free wok that Poon fired for us at the end, got a quick tour of Chinatown's underground grocery store, and were otherwise happy, even at the more-than-I-care-to-pay price! 

He is probably not politically correct, but I don't care. The food is good and he's a hoot. Very high-energy! I'm only adding this review because I feel he's getting a bad rap for those new year dinners (and it sounds like he deserves it) but he really does shine in the cooking classes.
The service was terribly rude as well as not helpful at all. Foods alright. Not coming back.

I love this place, especially in dirty Philly, this place is an oasis of class and service. Sometimes I feel like Ferris Bueller in the Abe Froeman restaurant. I always get two things: Fried Calamari and the Cowboy Ribeye. 2/3 of the time, the steak is succulent and cooked to perfection and I leave happier than Fred Flinstone at a Dinosaur BBQ. But, 1/3 of the time the steak is just ok, but not worth the price. So, I endure through the 33% to enjoy the 67% of the time that the food is amazing.

We came here for our 5th anniversary. There is no dress code on their website.  When we walked in with reservations preset they made us wait. When they sat us all they said to us was for my fiance to remove his hat before the food arrived. Every table around us was asked what brought them to the restaurant,  if they said for an anniversary they then had rose petals sprinkled on their table. It's sad that they judged us based my fiancé's  overalls as our money spends the same as the rest. $150 we could of spent somewhere that appreciated our money.

I can't attest to the authenticity of this place,  but as a sandwich lover I have to recommend the train wreck po' boy. It struck me as a cajun flavored schmitter. Steak, salami, andouille sausage, cheese, and onions on a nice roll. It was awesome. The cajun fries are good as well. Everything else looked pretty good, so I will have to go back and check it out.
Great atmosphere and the food was outstanding. The pork chop was juicy with great flavor.

There comes a time when you have to do something outside your job description. No, really, it happens. Take this as an example: finding cupcakes decorated to honor the current World Series champs to help make the next work day, uh, well, more entertaining. Now, where the hell do I find such cupcakes at the last minute in an unfamiliar territory? Well, you would think Yelp, right? Right. That's exactly what I did. Fortunately for me, Termini had been selling cupcakes with "P" in red icing, and I planned on getting here as soon as they opened the next morning. The women working there that morning were very friendly and surprisingly bright-eyed (late night game/late night celebrations) getting what looked like a million "P" cupcakes ready for the day. They were very careful in packing up 36 cupcakes for me, tying up nicely each box and giving me a ton of plastic bags to carry. Thanks to them, I was able to get such a random request at the last minute. In addition to cupcakes, they have quite a selection of biscotti, cheesecake, cookies, and other delicious looking pastries. I didn't have time to get anything else, but I bookmarked it to remind me to come back. Oh yeah...the cupcakes were a hit!

I have eaten at the Trident grill since it opened and my experience has been absolutely top notch in every way. This is a bar restaurant that serves dishes that are over the top. 

Let's today's visit the service was great, Kellen was my server and a true pro, everything is easy, personable and with a smile. I needed gift certificates, deletions to dishes because of diabetes and nothing was a problem. My saying is that there are ducks and there are Eagles & this is an Eagles only kinda employer, Kellen being a fine example.

I had the calamari and this was not deep fried either so I could have it, then I had the Sautéed Calamari and the Grilled Filet Medallions. Just the fact that I as a diabetic could have them was over the top but they were incredible as the filet was. 

I will continue to be a customer but my frequency will definitely be increased because of that sautéed calamari.

Great service...

Really surprised by the negative early reviews of this spot. The sushi rice is the signature delicious rice from Double Knot in Center City that sets it apart from all other sushi places in Philly. Everything is packaged beautifully, & the sauces on the side are delicious. I've literally had lunch here 3 days in a row since realizing they were open. I highly recommend the "Over Rice" bowls. The tuna over rice is basically the tuna tartare from Double Knot & a great amount of food for $9 & the sauce it comes with is stellar. Compare the prices to the other mediocre sushi places in UCity (Ochatto does a 2 sushi roll lunch special for $10, Pod is WAY overpriced because it's a Starr restaurant, Hai Street sushi burritos are $10+) & you'll see you're really only paying $1/$2 more for food that is better quality. Or, split a chef box with someone & you're golden. There are only a couple places in Philly that really do sushi right & this is now one of them.

Update: Since opening this is still a go-to every week for lunch but there have been instances where the sushi quality was subpar. At worst, it's still better than everywhere you can get sushi in UCity but it's important to distinguish between the unmatched quality of the OG Double Knot.
Fabulous food, good friendly service and a great atmosphere.  The food is very consistent, have never had a bad meal.

I tried this location once before it went Peruvian. Anyhow, the place has improved since it looks busier. The location is a bit awkward on a busy through street. There are not many other restaurants near it. It's also next to a gas station.

I understand that they mostly serve chicken, steak and one fish dish, but it was difficult to find much variety. But they do also serve side items like fried yuca ($3.89). I don't eat meat so I opted for the tilapia ceviche (Ceviche Peruano) ($11.99). It was really good but after awhile the citrus sauce became overpowering. Luckily, my friend ordered a combo platter that had 1/2 chicken, cilantro rice and spicy baked beans all for $8.99. I helped devour all the vegetarian sides. The cilantro rice was so tasty, especially when mixed with their curry dipping sauce. For dessert, I tried their fried plantains. It took awhile to come out, but it was so worth it because it was nice and hot. 

Overall, I liked everything that I tried. The only downside is that they don't allow you to substitute any sides. My tilapis ceviche was served as diced raw tilapia, red onions, cilantro, one sweet potato and lemon citrus sauce topped with fried large corn kernels. I wanted to substitute the corn for something else because it sounded odd. But they couldn't allow it. So when I tried them, it was like chewing crunchy chalky brittle. 

I also ordered their mango drink without milk. It tasted like an icy mango smoothie. It tasted pretty sweet.

Overall, had a good experience in terms of food and service. Just wish there were more seafood and vegetarian options.

In Tucson for the weekend and walked over to this place because its right across from our hotel. Great fish and chips, fish tacos and fried pickles. Raspberry cheesecake and coffee were very good for a bar and I'm a coffee snob.....our waitress was very attentive and always around when needed. Would recommend this place for food and drinks. Might even go back tonight to try something else off the menu......

Located in reading terminal... they give you samples to see which one you'll enjoy... I opted for the sausage gumbo and gator gumbo..and it was delicious.. had the perfect amount of flavor and spice.. I will definitely be returning when I come back to town.

hand-filled cannolis to order!  i also ordered a few basic vanilla cupcakes, and was pleasantly surprised to find a surprise filling in the middle.  The carrot cake looked pretty, but didn't taste up to par.
This is the best pancake place in a city. Cozy atmosphere and incredibly friendly staff.

Our first day in Philly we decided we'd hit Reading Terminal Market for a late lunch early dinner.  We condensed our list of places we definitely wanted to eat at from all of them LOL to our top 5...Becks was on the list.  Unfortunately we were disappointed w/ Becks.  After reading all the reviews I was expecting their food to be so much more flavorful.  It was kind of a letdown.  We got the red beans & rice, it had a nice smoky spicy bite but there was no flavor other than that.  I literally had to add 2 packets of salt just so it was somewhat tasty and edible.  We had planned to get a few of their muffellettas to take back to the hotel for later but opted not too after having the red beans & rice.  Maybe next time we're in town we'll come back and give them another try...I just expected Cajun cooking that the red beans & rice would have been so much more.  Popeye's was better than what we had from Becks.

Eh.  For some reason my husband's friends really enjoy going here - something about the cute but terribly incompetent waitresses - so I've found myself waiting for a menu, waiting for my drink, waiting for my bill too many times. According to other reviewers, I'm in the minority here with my two-star, but it is consistently terrible service every time I walk in here. 

I will say that their food and drinks really are great, (I love the potato skins) but the ambiance (bright lights and crowded tables) is sadly unappealing. It is nice that they have their own parking lot and I've always been able to find a spot. I can't wait for football season and maybe we'll wind up here and try their all day Sunday happy hour-perhaps it's a different bar in the middle of the day. Oh well.

Like eating at Coop's or Central Grocery. Actually much better than a lot of other tourist traps in the Quarter. If I can be particular, they prep the muffs ahead and the bread can dry out a bit. I'd leave them as wrapped boules and half or quarter them as they're ordered. But overall the sandwiches, gumbo, RBR, jambalaya, beignets are outstanding. You're not likely to eat like this outside of Nola. I can always find room for more Beck's.

I made a grave mistake and accidentally told the waiter i didn't want the food to be taken away. there were leftovers to be had and instead of going without the waiter went into the kitchen and got me a taco to take home. That's fucking class. la parilla is a place I've eaten at over the years but that small act of kindness made my night. wonderful menu and service. thanks for a great experience. the waiter's name was David. so... thanks David for making a night out a very wonderful experience.

Let me preface the review with this: the two stars did not mean the food was terrible. Actually, the food was the best part; the service and condition of the restaurant are why this location got less favorable of a review. With that said, let's get started! For what they charge people, I don't think its too much to ask to have great food, consistent service, and a clean environment. The Ina location nails every last one of those points. This location, only nails the good food part. For starters, the service at this La Parilla Suiza, is very inconsistent. One day, you could get a very attentive waiter, another day you could get a waiter, that is away from the table for approximately 25 minutes until he takes your order, rarely comes to the table for drink refills, and forgets that someone in your party ordered coffee (that actually happened yesterday). Did I mention we were practically the only people in the restaurant at that point? And then there's the cleanliness, and general condition of the restaurant. We sat in an area of the restaurant with booths separated by walls covered in boulders. 5-6 feet from the floor, of the wall, were completely dust free. Higher up on the wall, the more and more dust you'll see. Some parts look like the boulders are covered in fur. The restrooms.... Oh the restrooms.... A worn, grungy, toilet that barely flushed, calcium build-up on the floor around the toilet, broken stall latch, grungy sink, no "employee's must wash hands" sign to be seen, there are beer ads instead, etc... I've seen restrooms in better condition at gas stations. If this is how they take care of the stuff you CAN see, I'd hate to see how they take of stuff you CAN'T see... Go to the Ina location, and thank me later.

Waited a few weeks to write a review to see if my impression would change......it didn't! 
They simply have the best oyster po-boy I have ever had and I've had quite a few.   I just had one this past weekend at a very good water front place on the Chesapeake and Becks wins hands down, no real comparison.
 We also ordered gumbo and sampled the etoufee...both were outstanding to the point of us taking an order of each home along with an order of insanely good bread pudding. You must try the bread pudding for yourself since I can't possible describe how good this stuff really is.
Service was fast and friendly even though the place was mobbed on a Sunday afternoon.
It's nice to see food of this quality at the market.
