Very poor decision on our part and felt embarrassed for the experience. We had visited Guadalajara Grill yesterday and paid the same amount with double the food quality/quantity, drinks, and hospitality. Tonight, we had 2 appetizers, 2 margaritas (we had to order extra tequila shots since they tasted like pure margarita mix originally and then we found out later that well tequila was $7 per shot) and one fried ice cream for $61 and this included $2 off each app/marg (only one marg, that we later found out, was discounted when it was confirmed all were). Most expensive meal of the weekend considering it wasn't full entrees. We had to grab napkins from the bar, ask for more water, and the quesadilla was awful. The most disappointing part was we were up-charged when we received our bill. It was very apparent we were upset and addressed this to our server. Nothing was done to rectify our concern. As locals, we will never return or recommend this restaurant in the future. There are so many more choices in Tucson that provide better quality and service for what we paid.

A lot of gorgeous waitresses but that was not the reason I gave this such a low rating. The many times I've been here, I have tried a variety of items from their menu and I just can't really say that I've found anything to write home about. The food is mediocre to subpar for the price. The chorizo burger, for example, tastes like it went straight from freezer to hot plate. The cod fish and chips is nothing but breading. The Philly cheese steak is chinsy with the beef. I also don't think I've ever seen a waiter here at all which seems kind of sexist which doesn't matter to me but it might to some.
The trainwreck is a amazing sandwich that gives you the satisfaction of eating a cheesesteak and cajun food simultaneously.  It easily measures up to the best of sandwiches in Philly
Good food, ok service. Not bad for lunch

I had breakfast there yesterday.  I won't go into much detail on this since I don't think I tried anything that's really indicative of their menu. But I'll say this.

The Bourbon Street Breakfast is a great deal at $5.95. The cornbread they serve with it is out of this world. The rice and beans they serve will please anyone that enjoys Cajun food. 

On top of that, the staff is very friendly. They offered me a sample of the bread pudding, and it tasted like I was getting a shot of bourbon. Not a bad thing. 

And even on top of that, they serve a pretty bold coffee.  They don't just throw you that Ellis restaurant coffee. No, they give you coffee with a bite. The server even offered me a free refill to go without me asking. 

Very good experience overall. I even topped it off with one of the King Cakes which did not disappoint. All of the above came out to just over 10 bucks.
Great food. Very reasonable prices, and always good service. The cilantro rice is super delicious. We have never had to wait long for food. Really appreciate the clean and open kitchen.

Wow very delicious. Everything was seasoned perfectly. Steak was moist and juicy . Rice was absolutely flavorful and the passion fruit drink is amazing . The Staff is very helpful and sweet . Food didn't take long at all to come out . And I love the sauce that they had to go along with the food . All I can say is wow amazing .

Vineyards cafe is one of the coolest coffee shops I have visited in the US. Welcoming atmosphere, coffee and food are very delicious. The prices are great either, spend 10-12$ for the best in the city savory crepe(it tastes incredible) and cup of freshly brewed coffee. If you have some spare time, grab a good book and enjoy yourself in a cozy and comfortable setting. 
A truly great coffee shop has to feel special, THIS ONE DOES.

Fantastic! The best Mexican food I've had in Tucson yet! The only down side was the queso we ordered was not what we thought it was. We were expecting a dip but it was a giant thing of skillet fried cheese. It was still good! Everything we had was amazing!

We go to Trident every week for Geeks who Drink trivia and love it. I'd say they have some of the best bar food in Tucson. I enjoy the chicken tenders and the shrimp tacos. My husband loves their H3 chicken wings - nice and spicy! As a group, we love sharing the fried pickles and loaded fries. The $3 beer special is also great. The service is always great - keeping the drinks flowing but not intrusive. We were extremely disappointed this week however when they no longer had our favorite drink - Float Your Boat - a delicious mix of citrus vodka, lime juice, muddled raspberries and a sparkling wine float. Please bring it back!
Cannoli cannoli cannoli... (nothing else).

No, Becks.... Shrimp Po' Boys are definitely not your specialty. Not at all. Mine had entirely too much bread, my sauce was mediocre, and my shrimp kept falling awkwardly out of my roll.  I won't get this again here.

Now, the Shrimp Etouffee? THAT is definitely your thing! Yours is DELICIOUS!!!! I'm not sure why I didn't order that or the jambalaya in the first place. Actually, I do know. It was 95 degrees outside and I just didn't want anything that hot or heavy in my stomach. Luckily, my fiance' ordered it and was gracious enough to share his. Damn, it was GOOD, and I was immediately jealous because I knew he had the better entree.  Also enjoyed the cornbread- it complemented the etouffee nicely.  

Most importantly, the staff is exceptionally friendly. In fact, they were the reason we stopped there in the first place. They invited us to sample a few of their entrees and once we tasted them, it was a done deal.  I just wish I had ordered one of THOSE entrees instead of the Po' Boy.
The cheese ravioli is great I've been looking everywhere in that would deliver to my house and this is the first time I've ever liked it

Located inside the Reading Terminal is a authentic cajun stand.
I seen it for many years and I never really was into cajun but I just 
found out they serve made to order beignets. 

They only serve them Monday, Wednesday, Friday,& Sunday, so lucky for us we were at
the terminal early on a Sunday morning. I don't know about you but 
on Sunday's fried sweet pockets of sugar sounds ball tingling good to me.

They came out hot and light with a melting coating of powdered sugar
to ease them down the gobbler hole. Down they went. They were very
tasty for the brief moments as I inhaled my share. 

I did notice they have a unique cheesesteak that next time I will have to try, so back I shall be.

Sort of a mix between fast food and sit down restaurant. Good food and friendly service. Very clean and bright. Unique and I will be back to try other menu items. Really a unique restaurant with nice people and interesting food from Peru.

This place lives up to the reviews. Wonderful coffee (my favortite latte place), nice music, friendly staff, cozy atmosphere to chat or study/work, fast internet, reasonable prices. What's not to like?  I'll be a regular here from here on out.

Excellent place to start your day! The place was extremely clean and the employees were very polite.

Highly recommended!
We tried the carrot cake and it was pretty delicious! Will go back for their famous cannoli.

I don't know why but it is hard not to miss this place when visiting Reading Terminal Market. 
A. It's close to the middle of the bustling market.
B. Cajun place in cheesteak and hoagie heaven Philadelphia.  
C. There is a good vibe from the guests around the table(recreation of Southern hospitality?)

The chicken and shrimp gumbo was good comfort food. I don't know how authentic it is.  It is a good choice when you are on the road and missing home cooking, i.e. not another cheeseteak. Looking to try the gator gumbo one day.

Everyone comes for their cannolis, which are freshly filled with pastry cream. The cream is surprisingly light and not overly sweet, and the shells are made well.  It's nice to be able to watch them assemble the cannolis there.  I wish they had other flavors (chocolate dipped??  I'm thinking Mike's and Modern in Boston.)

Other bakery items looked more like generic Italian pastries and cookies, but cannolis are worth trying.

Overall the service was very good, and the food was decent too.  The Speedway location is better for sure. 

I was at the Oracle location last week and there were fly's buzzing around the table.  One landed in the cheese queso and I had to point it out to the guests I had brought so they did not eat it.  They all lost their appetite.

This cafe at Reading Terminal had amazing and authentic Cajun food!  We sat down at the booth and ordered the étouffée and alligator sausage po' boy, both of which were tasty and quite flavorful.  I washed it down with a delicious sweet tea, and left quite satisfied.  I'd definitely come back here again in the future.

I love this place! The food is awesome and I love that they let you try before you buy. The shrimp bisque is one of the best soups I have ever had. The jambalaya, étouffée, and corn bread are all phenomenal. Very true to New Orleans food and just plain great!

Best Breakfast sandwich i have ever had (Breakfast Po Boy... $4.75). It is filing and the bread is so soft.  It's the best breakfast choice and it's one of their more popular items.  

I've also had their Jambalaya (chicken, sausage, and shrimp in it). Their cornbread is made fresh daily.  You really cant go wrong with this place.  I love it!

I used to live in Tampa.  Now I visit for work a few times a year.  This is a place I visit, without exception, every single time.

Half chicken, plantains, lots and lots of verde sauce.  

Service is always impeccable.

I just started frequenting Trident a couple months ago, and I'm in love. I went for my first time on a Thursday night, expecting it not to be busy, but it was packed! It was about a 20 minute wait for a table. As someone who works in the industry, I love seeing this. The place was crowded with regulars, so I knew the food must be good. I started with a beer and some potato skins. The skins were perfectly cooked and now overly cheesy. I then ordered a Philly cheesesteak, and when it arrived, I was in heaven. It was perfectly cooked, had just the right amount of cheese, and lots of mushrooms, which I loved. The beer was perfectly cold and the service was great as well! Our server, Eden, was friendly and accommodating. We will continue to return to Trident and we can't wait to watch some football here!

Super busy for a Wednesday, but amazingly efficient.

I can't say enough about this place ... happy hour loaded fries delicious ... Mac and cheese baked and fresh ... burger perfect cook and amazingly fresh flavor.

Add to this the fact they split our plate and baked each of our Mac and cheese separate AND gave us each a pickle spear.  The spent cents to make is feel like we will come here at least once a week ... and we live 45 min away!!

Beer ... fresh, amazing and dark.

Service ... bartender knew what she was doing, suggested the perfect beer, kept us smiling and was funny as an extra bonus! She knew what she was the best we've had in awhile.

I wish I could give them 10 stars! Keep it up!
Lunch with some golf buddies awhile ago. Great Burgers...according to some of the guys.  I had the Reuben and creamy cole slaw.  One of the best ever.  Gonna go back again soon

Since I'm not big fan of Cajun food, I wasn't expecting too much from this place. But surprisingly they have pretty good spiced rice and it probably goes well with anything (like curry, stew, soup), or just by itself too! We had this sausage, chicken, shrimp "Gumbo" on the rice, and the gumbo was actually pretty spicy then I thought. If you like spicy food, try their spicy gumbo. I probably will come back to get their rice!

Great bar food, drink specials and environment. The cheesesteaks and buffalo chicken pizza are very good. Drink specials are great during games and still very fair during the off-season. The owner of the bar/restaurant is extremely friendly. He always makes it a point to greet you when you walk in. Tables on the sides, a very large bar and TV's all over the walls. It is a great local neighborhood bar.
Best. Crepes. Ever. This is a little pricey but you really can't beat it. The employees were great too

Went in today to get a septum piercing had a great experience. My wife also got her nose pierced the young lady was extremely professional and knowledgeable, although I did not catch her name. If I ever need another piercing I will definitely be returning here.

Beck's Cajun Cafe is one of the many wonderful and delicious options available at Reading Terminal Market. The food is filling and portions are generous, which is always appreciated after an exhausting walk around the city. The shrimp po' boy is flavorful, with a bit of a kick. The line and service at Beck's really varies based on when you come. On a very busy day, you may have to wait quite a while before receiving your order, but on less crowded days the wait is much much shorter. Limited seating is available in the area.

Another tasty eatery at the Reading Terminal Market. Only ate here once since I wanted to try the other places there, but I enjoyed it. Beck's has all sorts of southern comfort food including po boy sandwiches, gumbo, jambalaya, and beignets. I followed what the other Yelpers recommended and ordered the gator gumbo ($7) since it sounded really interesting. I had originally wanted to try a po boy based on the other Yelp reviews, but I needed a change from all of the sandwiches I had already eaten the past few days!

You get a hearty portion of gumbo over white rice and it was delicious as well. The gumbo had good flavor with a bit of a kick to it. Loved the sausage but I would've never guessed it was alligator meat. You'll be comfortably full with just an order of this, but I almost wished I had ordered a side of corn bread just to soak up all that extra gumbo goodness. That might've been too filling though. I also wanted to try their fried mac and cheese balls ($4.50) that everybody mentioned, but thought that might be too much food.

Bottom line, definitely worth a try. Next time I'll be ordering one of their po boy sandwiches!

Love this place! This is my #1 pick on most dinner dates. Menu has a large selection and drink menu has a great selection for patrons who drink. Food is outstanding!  Always plated beautifully, served hot and fresh. Service is always friendly and inviting. Servers are always knowledgable of the menu and can make outstanding recommendations if you're unsure of what you want to eat. Restaurant is clean, quiet and has plenty of seating. Large parties and meetings welcome. Catering available. Remains a Cyrus family favorite! We have family of every age and everyone is accomodated at La Parilla! Thank you!

This place is super cute. I came here for breakfast before work and ate in. I had a savory crepe, the Americano I believe, and a macchiato. It was ready pretty quickly, and was very good. The crepe is on the larger side; I managed to eat most of it but probably shouldn't have. The space is well-lit because of the windows, and on the smaller side. I'm not sure if there's another floor with more seating.

We enjoyed the Gumbo & a Short Rib Po Boy at Beck's Cajun Cafe in the Reading Terminal Market. The counter service is friendly & fast served, with reasonable prices for the amount of great food provided. Highly recommend.

My boyfriend and I were completely ignored after we were seated even when I made eye contact with 2 waitresses. After sitting there for 10 minutes  we left. Told the couple coming in they were welcome to our table! Seems you need to be a regular here to get service.

I had the oyster po-boy. Not great, a little mushy. However, after I ordered I decided to sample the gator gumbo... awesome. I wish I had eaten that. Really really good. The rest of what they have is as authentic as I have found outside of Louisiana (and I lived there for a few years). Good gator gumbo. Good prices. However, stay away from the Oyster Po-Boy. I usually love them, this was not good.
This is my favorite bakery in reading terminal market. I love their rum cake and cannoli cake.
Packed as always.  Atmosphere is pretty cool with the Navel decor and history behind the place.   Food is good but not great.  Beer selection makes up for it.

I will start by saying I must go back and try something's else on the menu. I had the chicken with rice and sweet plantains. I got two sauces with my order and I have no idea what they were but I really liked the "spicy" one. I order to go and it didn't take as long as I thought it would during lunch hours.
The best Po Boys in the city are at Beck's Cajun. The fried shrimp is my favorite but you can't go wrong with any of them!

This location used to serve Taco Bell tacos but now it is expensive sushi. Cash is not allowed at this location now which I am told discriminates against poor people. Taco Bell was 5 stars but had very sticky edges on the tables. DK has nicer tables that don't get sticky when cleaned, but still one star for not offering a $5 box that includes a drink.

I've had many a falafel, and I must say Chickpeas does a darn good job. The falafel are made fresh and the extras always look and taste great. I always get falafel with hummus or yogurt sauce, not tahini (too bitter for my taste) and they never charge me extra for it, which has happened at other places. The serving size is generous for the price.  I personally think the falafel are fresher and tastier than Maoz and the salad selections are better  quality.  

 The only downside  is they aren't open on Saturdays ;(

I'm getting hungry just thinking about the place. I think I'm going to head over now for a cheap dinner!

Not as good as double knot but definitely delicious for the location it is at.

The price is pretty hefty $$$ (big complaint brought up from previous reviewers) but it's reasonable. You are paying for the brand and also the location. Prices are comparable to the other stands in the food hall. I always assume I'm going to spend around $12-16 going into that cafeteria regardless of which stand I eat at.

Anyway, my sushi was good but the amount I got was so little I'm not sure if it was worth it. 

I didn't go too crazy in ordering. I just wanted a test try. I got a toro scallion roll and also an eel roll. 

The order came in a nice box, I attached a picture. It's pretty cute: arranged neatly and colorful. 

Some people complained about the stuffing:rice ratio. I thought it was pretty half and half - not too much rice (attached some close ups). 

The toro scallion roll was average 3/5. But the eel roll was so good- still warm when I ate it 5/5! But ...not sure if 2 pieces was worth the $6. 

I want to try the eat your own fish boxes and one of the rice bowls next time. It may be worth more for your buck.

Came here for happy hour and recieved prompt service. We ordered the beer battered fried pickles which were amazing! And the loaded fried, also tasty and fries were crispy. I will definitely be coming back for more!

I ordered the turkey n stuffing. platter ..it came with a big side salad garlic bread n 2 sides ..$11 n change with tax ..it arrived quickly n hot  potatoes n spinach were both good 
 ..sturdy container .not Styrofoam junk 
Phone girl Riannan(Sp ?)  was most professional and engaging 
Delivery driver was nice n presentable as well ..so much better then many other places.
I have eaten there many times in the past ..always been happy n what a bargain ..thanks guys

Not impressed.  We came from out of town and relied on the reviews from yelp.  Not sure where 4 stars came from......service was soooo slow, didnt get our food  for 45 minutes after order.  Drinks were horrible unless you are looking for straight fruit juice!  Not impressed. no atmosphere either.  Wont b returning....

Dessert heaven!! I love termini brothers! They have a variety of sweet treats to choose from. I got the tiramisu cake from here and it did not disappoint. The desserts taste as good as they look!! Definitely a must try!!
Went looking for good seafood left wondering why I keep looking for good seafood in a desert.
Love love love Peruvian chicken and the yellow sauce!  Very clean, fun atmosphere, friendly atmosphere. Very reasonable and unbelievably delicious!  You've gotta try this place!

Some friends and I went down to Villagio a couple of weeks ago, because we had planned to go to the place that was previously there.  With all of us still having a mad pizza craving, we went in.  This BYOB establishment is very similar to the previous establishment...with the addition of more menu items and a flat screen TV.  With that being said, it feels like it has lost a bit of its romantic feel.  

The food that we ordered was excellent and the portions were huge! The house pizza, which is named after the establishment, was delicious...so were the white pizza and the salads that were ordered.  


In lieu of our previous experience my wife and I decided to order a Stromboli and Mega Fry (not sure what they call it here...fries covered in cheese and bacon and baked). The food took about an hour to get to our house; for a Saturday night this was acceptable.

The Stromboli was large in size, but lacking in flavor.  It consisted primarily of chicken with very little cheese.  The chicken consisted of pretty big chunks of random pieces of chicken (we even got some gristle) and what little cheese there was wasn't even melted.  I had to microwave pieces of the Stromboli to get the cheese melted.  

The Mega Fry was very large in size, but didn't have many fries.  The item consisted primarily  of  cheese sauce and a layer of mozzarella on top. Few fries, covered with lots of mucky orange sauce and one uniform layer of baked cheese on top.  Finally, the Diet Coke that we ordered showed up as being a regular Coke. 

While I can say that I'm not likely to order the Stromboli or Mega Fry again, I can say that I will definitely be back to their dinning room for dinner.  For us the dinning room is what will keep us coming back to this establishment.  It serves as a great place to take friends and enjoy some moderately priced food.

I LOVE Cajun/Creole cuisine. I would say Beck's is probably one of the better options in the area if you're craving some food from New Orleans, but it just doesn't compare to the food down south. We had the jambalaya, shrimp po' boy and a small side of their blackened chicken alfredo. The jambalaya was well seasoned and we doused our bowl with their special hot sauce (so good - definitely going to buy a few bottles the next time I visit), which really kicked things up a bit. My only complaint was how DRY the chicken was - very chewy. The shrimp po' boy was a decent size and came halved. The blackened chicken alfredo reminded me of something you see at an Applebee's. Not bad, but the similarity is there. Once again, the chicken was really dry.

Thank you for amazing spot in Philly. Cozy atmosphere, food is delicious, service is so good. All flavors of syrups for coffee that you ever wanted (thanks for the amazing pumpkin spice). Highly recommended! Unbelievably low prices!

We stopped by Beck's for breakfast on a Sunday morning. It was perfect timing. The market was pretty empty compared to when we normally have been there. We got a seat at their bar area and ordered their Bourbon Street breakfast which is red beans & rice, fried egg, cheese and grilled corn bread. 

The portion was actually bigger than I expected but that isn't important. The food was full of flavor. The corn bread was nice and sweet, frying it was a great touch. I could definitely get this item again!
Great food and great prices. They give you a lot for what you pay for. Atmosphere is great, nice family restaurant. Staff is super friendly, definitely worth a try.

We always try to stop in at the trident grill when in Tucson. We love the food, the service, and the atmosphere. I was there last week on business and stopped in for lunch. Like a knucklehead, I left my visa on the table. I had a business trip and needed my card but live in Phoenix, and trying to get to Tucson before I left was proving to be difficult. T.K. stepped in and saved the day! She took time out of her busy schedule to overnight my card which arrived today, just in time for my trip. Thank you, T.K.!! I will make it up to you next time I'm in.

-Shane

This is literally as good as it gets for me. I have never once eaten here and been dissapointed. I usually come here with my best friend and we get the chicken and rice soup, queso and a side of rice and beans to share. Then we roll all of the ingredients up into a few tortillas with some green salsa and, YUM!! Also, the Alambre tacos, or No. 48, is SERIOUSLY THE BOMB! If you doubted this place before, these tacos will change your mind! They are tacos made from either beef or chicken sauteed with bacon, onions and green peppers- my mouth is watering just thinking about them!

Also, It is very important to me to mention the green salsa... This salsa holds a place near and dear to my heart. It is by far the best there is! I used to order this stuff by the pint-full to -go after class when I was in high school. I still crave it to this day. It is creamy and spicy- a perfect combo. 

I have never once had bad service here and I have been quite a bit. So, I feel it is safe to say that you most likely will not have bad service either. 

If you are looking for some traditional sonoran mexican food, this is not your place. This place is known for its authentic Mexico City cuisine- quite different from the other mexican food places in town. Enjoy!

The last place I stopped by at Reading Terminal Market during my last trip to Philly was Beck's Cajun Cafe.  What can I say?  They had their signature sandwich, The Train Wreck Po' Boy, on display and after walking by it several times, I couldn't resist ordering it.

The Train Wreck Po' Boy -- http://bit.ly/2vnDKbf
andouille, salami, steak, cheese, onions
The Train Wreck is a great Nawlin's take on the classic cheesesteak.  It had a bit of everything inside and had that spicy kick from the andouille.  In a way, it was almost like a jambalaya in a roll with a meaty surprise in every bite.  It definitely worth the try if you're craving a cheesesteak but with a little more kick.

I'm glad I got to stop by Beck's Cajun Cafe before leaving Reading Terminal Market and ending on a high note with the Train Wreck Po' Boy.  I hope I get another chance to come back again and try their other menu items such as their famous Jambalaya, Fried Mac & Cheese, Gumbo-topped Cajun Fries, and their Muffaletta.  They all sound so good!

This review is long overdue. Vineyards Cafe has swiftly become my home away from home. Perfect for studying or just enjoying a nice morning by myself. Super dog friendly, which I love because I can get my dogs out of the house while enjoying some perfectly crafted coffee. Interestingly, my fiancée and I frequent this place, so much so that they allowed me to host our engagement party there. Great staff, great food, and most importantly great coffee.

Can't go wrong with this chicken. Maybe the best chicken I've ever had and consistently good. The price is reasonable for the amount of food although maybe it was just the last few times I ordered but it seems like they're getting smaller with the portions of rice and beans. But wow is it all good. My go to order is : 

1/4 chicken, black beans, cilantro rice, and extra green sauce!! Winner winner.
Service always with a smile. Sometimes crowded. When a place is popular, you'll have that. Great 'bar fare'.  Convenient location. And great looking bartenders!
First time here and not only are the employees friendly but the customers are!  Had their fish sticks and fish tacos, very good!  Loved the memorabilia on the walls and a honor wall to those we lost

La parrilla suiza  this restaurant was a nicer place, ordered #30.
Waiter that serve party of three was good no problem at all.
The Good.....food was tasty,flavor and like there plates.

The Bad....nada

The Ugly....what,dang me.

Have not check out there restroom.

It's been pretty good in the past but this last time we came was a disaster. All the food was cold, we hardly ever got refills and had to send food back multiple times. We came at 3:00 and it was not busy at all, not sure if we will be back.

Everything about Cuenelli's Peruvian Restaurant is great. Excellent mood, and service is quick. Cuenelli's Peruvian Restaurant has an incredible Pollo a La Brasa, that was my first time giving it a try here, and I was surprised with how good it was. Service was amazing and everyone working here was very nice and helpful. Cuenelli's Peruvian Restaurant, If you haven't been here before, you're definitely missing out.
Only thing good here is the salsa sometimes everything else has truly went DOWN HILL. Sad used to love this place

I dare you to walk past their bakery case and resist wanting all of the things. A stop at Termini Bros Bakery is a must when visiting Reading Terminal Market. All of their baked goods look delicious but I'm only after one item: cannoli! A nice crunch to the shell and plenty of filling (and mini chocolate chips!). You will notice a couple of small pieces of candied citron in the filling which I could do without but doesn't affect the overall taste too much. 

I received great service from the staff. I just wish that I was able to buy the cannoli unfilled so that I could bring home cannoli for days without them getting soggy.

I've given this place so many chances. The crepes are not good and they've messed up my order multiple times. They are also out of everything all the time and they take a very long time to get orders ready. The bagels are subpar as well and they are always either burnt or under toasted.

It's not possible to give this place zero stars, but ZERO stars is what it deserves. Slow service on a Monday slow night. Terrible food. Slow drinks. It's safe to say I will never recommend this place to anybody nor will I ever eat here again. 

We were the only table for one server. We had to ask multiple times for items. The waitress cashed out my table incorrectly and when I asked to speak to the manager so the manager can fix it she told me it wasn't possible ti fix. 

The restaurant is DIRTY and OLD. I sat in a chair that had an exposed nail.  The greasy floor is dangerous. 

I'm really disappointed with my experience.

Always have a great experience at Trident.  Have been to all three and they all serve great food.  Not fond of number 3, however 1 and 2 are great.  This time we were at the OG location.  Service was great. The sautéed calamari was tender and the caper sauce with garlic was excellent.  The peel and eat shrimp were good size and being from the east coast, the Old Bay was key.  My father was with us and loved the fish tacos.  Always love the happy hour food and drink specials.  Keep up the good work.  Next stop....the pizza pub

While foraging via Yelp for a tasty and inexpensive dinner, we were initially disappointed in being bombarded by all the sandwich places that came up in our search.  We were excited to try Cuenelli's because the photos divulged food that looked far more satisfying and dinner-like than sandwiches.

We started off with the ceviche ($13) that was highlighted in several reviews.  There was a good balance of fish and lime surpassing n00by ceviche that almost exclusively tastes like lime.  The crunchy shreds of red onion added a nice texture to complement the soft chunks of sashimi.  The portions were surprisingly generous, along with traditional Latin American sides of roasted corn nuts and yam (be warned that the yam is chilled!  I was not expecting that).  Overall the ceviche at this almost-fast-food-like place turned out to be better in quality and quantity than the ceviche that we got at a classy Japanese restaurant.

I got the 1/2 roast chicken ($9), which is a lot of meat but at just $1 more from the 1/4 roast chicken, who can say no?  The rotisserie chicken was quite good, well roasted with spices to make it quite flavorful--while not mind-blowing, you can definitely taste the difference compared to grocery market roast chicken.  It comes with 2 sides, and I chose the cilantro rice and black beans.  Nothing special about the black beans, but the cilantro rice was tasty and went well with the chicken.  In fact, I would recommend the cilantro rice especially for Asian people who are used to eating meat with rice.

Although the name of the restaurant features rotisserie chicken, I tried a bit of the steak with fried egg and it was delicious, though it does seem like it would induce massive food coma.

Located in a plaza, the storefront is admittedly mundane.  The BBQ themed interior, punctuated by the classic red checkered tablecloth, if fun and casual but in my opinion a Latin theme would have enhanced the South American-ness of Peruvian style rotisserie chicken.
Great little cafe. I had a goat cheese turkey and dog jam crepe and it was delicious. Good prices and good service.

It was really hard to settle on a place to grab a late breakfast with all the options that Reading Terminal had to offer. But, I'm happy we decided on Beck's! The ladies behind the counter were so kind and patient, and let my husband I sample the gator gumbo, etouffe and chowder before we decided on our orders.
My husband loved his oyster po boy and shrimp and corn chowder. I had the bayou breakfast: white rice topped with gator gumbo, a fried egg, cheese and cornbread. Phenomenal! Highly recommended!

Looking for a nice pub to enjoy a good meal and some brew? This is the place, with a super cool atmosphere with a Naval/USA  themed decor and friendly staff. 

We heard they had great margaritas, but they apparently changed the mix recently, which wasn't so great. The server was quick to correct the issue by replacing one margarita with a different drink and providing additional mix for the other. 

I enjoyed the buffalo chicken sandwich! If you like spice, ask for the H2 sauce.

I'm in love with this place! If you have sweet tooth & love pastry like me, you will love this place. It was my first time to try the Italian dessert "Cannoli" and the experience was amazing! Their must try signature/original cannoli with ricotta cheese filling was so delicious (not too sugary sweet like other American desserts)! I will 3000% coming back here to try all their other Italian desserts!! I will also visit the other locations of this bakery to try out their cannoli if there is difference :)

For most updated hours, check their FB page. Their website isn't as updated.

Be sure to go early (before 3pm) to ensure they have their signature dish, Peruvian chicken.

The chicken was alright. Not the greatest Peruvian chicken, but far from the worst. Flesh was tender, flavor was skin deep only. Size of the chicken was closer to cornish hen.

Cilantro rice, spicy beans, and yucca are incredible!!

It's really closer 3.5 stars but I won't round down.

I know that you're probably thinking that going for a po boy in Philly is insanity but their oyster and shrimp po boy was one of the best I have ever eaten.  I'm a total foodie junky and love cajun food and was thrilled to find this little slice of heaven right in Reading Terminal Market.

Stopped in at Trident OG location for a lunch around 2:00 PM.  Place was pretty busy for being mid day.  Treated myself to a pint of Modern Times, the tap list has a few craft options on it which is a plus.  Started out with the pretzel app, which was real tasty with its salt and butter.  It came with a big bowl of cheap tasting cheese dip.  For entree I came to try the burger, so I went with what seems like the classic--the Wildcat, a BBQ bacon cheeseburger.  All the ingredients were nice here, from fresh veg, tasty BBQ sauce, fresh bakery bun, and tasty half pound of beef.  Overall the burger was a little dry and overcooked despite my order of medium.  The fries are super tasty here though.  The service was okay.  The environment is definitely that of a pub with kitschy bar stuff all over the walls, definitely nothing cool or modern.  Kind of charming in a way, but kind of claustrophobic.  This place is overall solid, but it didn't really excel in any area.

Be prepared to stand in a huge line in this place. They have a variety of desserts ranging from tarts to pastries to cookies to cakes to meringue to canoli and the list goes on. Two things stood out for me in this place, canolis and biscotti. I took the canoli with vanilla custard filling instead of ricotta cheese. The custard was light and not very sweet and canoli shell was crispy. There was a good proportion of filling  as well.

This is by far my favorite place to eat for lunches etc. it's a family owned restaurant with delicious food! My favorite is the 1/4 chicken with cilantro rice and beans (yum)! They also have house made sauces, get the yellow one it's so good! They get busy for lunches but staff handles it well, will continue to come back to Cuenellis for sure!

I ordered a cowboy steak and baked potato to go. I asked 3x gor ketchup and was told it was in the bag. When I got to my hotel, no ketchup, steak was all fat and bread like rubber .the waiter is an idiot and the food was lousy hardly with $73.00!
Would recommend Palm or Capital grill over this over rated snob whole!

They need to change the menu ,  its main forte is rotisserie chicken they didn't have ceviche and they didn't have papa a la huancaina , she told me that they don't serve ceviche and they want to take out of the menu so... what are you waiting for ??? 
they offered yuca a la huancaina but i wasn't in the  mood for fried yuca , the place overall is an everyday fast food place nothing formal or fancy, plastic table cloth, no glass for the drinks just a straw, prices were reasonable but they need to change the menu

It almost hurts me to write this, but I think my days of patronizing this business have come to an end. Today my friend called me to tell me about his experience here with the young lady at the counter speaking rudely to him. Ironically, a few months ago I had a negative experience with this same young lady as well. I had ordered a Vanilla Iced Chai and was handed a warm chai (in the middle of the summer). When I told her that I wanted ice in it she told me that I didn't ask for ice. I know for sure that i asked for ice, I wouldn't drink a hot drink on a hot summer day. Anyhow, I assured her that I did ask for it and perhaps she did not hear me. She insisted that I did not ask for ice, I sensed her attitude and decided not to go any further because I did not feel like arguing about a drink. Today, he saw a notice that they were not serving eggs and asked her about it, she responded in a rude tone "We just don't?" It was unnecessary and unprofessional for her to give him attitude for asking a simple question. Well, this prompted us to find out on our own. Come to find out they were in violation of code and had to cease cooking eggs immediately. That was no big deal for me, but when I read that there was no backflow prevention on the sink water supply lines, that made the decision for me. I would think that a business who's been cited with various violations would be more humble when dealing with customers. It was a nice run while it lasted and it's sad to remove them from my list of favs but with the violations and the attitude, I'm good love, enjoy!

Yoooooo this place is scary as hell. You wanna feel uncomfortable??? Just make your way to Vineyards Cafe and make sure you are specifically non-caucasian!
I am writing this review on behalf of a friend who felt so uncomfortable at this establishment. 
The coffee she had was not made well at all. It tasted like soap. 
The workers were unfriendly and felt hassled by my friend and even annoyed when she wanted to stay in the cafe to do her work like everyone else and have her nasty ass drink. They were unwelcoming.

The Peruvian style rotisserie chicken is definitely the highlight here and the item to order at this restaurant. The chicken is flavorful and the green sauce that comes with the chicken meal is just mildly spicy and really good, much better than the mayo based yellow sauce. The half chicken portion, served with two sides, was a good amount of food for one person. 

We also decided to try a classic Peruvian dish aside from the rotisserie chicken but unfortunately they no longer make ceviche, although this item remains listed on their menu. Instead we had the lomo saltado which was kinda disappointing as it was definitely missing that smokiness that you get when the meat is cooked on a wok, an important and traditional flavor component of this dish. The cilantro rice was good though, and worth trying since it's not usually served anywhere else. 

The prices are so reasonable (~$10 for the half chicken meal) which make this a good place for a healthier lunch option.

We came in on a Sun. Afternoon, it was pretty empty, so we were a little apprehensive... But this place has a very nice DR, and it has amazing pizza, it has thin crust, it is delicious, the sauce is just right. One of us was gluten-free and ordered a salad and it was amazing (Cobb salad) with a half of beautiful sliced fresh avocado, huge serving of chicken (grilled), hard-boiled egg, bacon, etc. they have an extra large pizza special , 2 for $16.99, and we had enough to bring home w/ 5 people! so I would highly recommend Villagio cafe, the staff was also very nice!! Thank you Villagio!!

You know what's the worst? 

...when your cannoli pastry gets soft and soggy because the too-liquidy ricotta cream has sat inside of it for too long.

You know what's the best?

...when your cannoli is filled to order with the creamiest, thickest most subtly sweet ricotta and chocolate chip cream that you've ever had the pleasure of indulging in.

It's a deceptively small when you first walk in but there's more seating downstairs. Very chill and friendly environment. Super cute and aesthetic. Coffee is very authentic and staff is so helpful and attentive.

If you are at the Reading Terminal, you NEED to make a stop at Beck's Cafe and treat yourself to some Cajun lovin'. I visit this place several times a month, usually on a weekly basis, and I am never disappointed. You can eat in or take out, but why wouldn't you want to sit down and relax while eating some delicious hot and fresh gator gumbo? The girls who work there are also awesome and they know how to make you feel appreciated. This place gets 5 out of 5 stars from me. Go to Beck's!

So I have to do an hour 6 Hour Dr. to Philadelphia on a road trip we stopped to grab something to eat before we can check in so we're walking around trying to find a place to eat with somebody tells us to go to the marketplace so we get there all types of food places to eat including all types of delis in meats and fish steak and cheese places and then there's this place Beck's Cajun Café
No matter where I go for my trips I'm always trying to search a place for Cajun food or crawfish and I just so happen to run into this place that has all that
There's a little place in the center of the marketplace the food is excellent and they have a little bar you can sit and eat but have to say I got the étouffée along with Banana bread pudding which was out of this world‼ 
So if you're ever in the area this is deafly worth the the visit

So, I was on my way back to Pittsburgh after spending the weekend with one of my cousins in New Jersey. I had a packed bag of food to eat on the journey back home. While my cousin and I are unloading the car, she notices that I'm missing my food bag. Oh Lord, I'm starving and there's no food in the bus terminal that I want.  What to do???

She tells me that she can take me quickly to Reading Terminal and off we go. I run into Reading Terminal looking for a stall that I can get something to eat quickly. I see Beck's Cajun Cafe and order their Shrimp and Egg Po Boy with an order of Crawfish Etoufee. (I know that shrimp and eggs together may not sound too good, but I was starving.)

Let me tell you something, that fried shrimp and eggs po'boy was fire! The eggs were softly scrambled and not overcooked. The shrimp were nicely seasoned and well cooked and they added a spicy remoulade sauce with chopped scallions. Yes Lawd! Where has this sandwich been all of my life? At Beck's along with their delicious crawfish Etoufee.

I know that this may sound like it's a heavy meal at 10:00 on a Sunday morning, but you must eat these! And I didn't have a hangover, but I instinctively know that this combo could cure whatever your previous night dealt you.  Go run and pick this sandwich up now for breakfast.
I come here for Happy Hour quite a lot- they make strong drinks, serve them with a smile, and offer affordable bites to eat.

I freaking love this place. The falafel pita is FAT, and the small is more than sufficient to satisfy my hunger and deep desire for delicious falafel.  The price is so reasonable ($4), and the salad bar is stocked with healthy and fresh ingredients. The yogurt sauce makes me happy too. Whee!!

Touristing in Philly- stopped at Reading Market and found Beck's Cajun.  This place is deeelish!  The seasonings are on point, food is delish from the etouffé to the jambalaya.  Outside of New Orleans this is the beat Cajun I've had. Will definitely come back!

Whenever my friends ask to meet up mid-afternoon for a snack, this spot comes to mind. The atmosphere is clean and calm so if you want a place to study with free WiFi, stop by! 

I'm partial to their sweet crepes. Personally I like the simplicity of their confiture crepe which offers your choice of jam and powdered sugar. I like the blackberry jam the best. Their savory crepes are good too, but if you're not a fan of cheese that is on the stronger side, you might not like their gouda crepes. I like them a lot, but I had one friend who didn't like it at all. It's up to your tastebuds I guess!

This Cajun spot is unique and adds to the diverse amount of options available in The Reading Terminal Market. They allow you to try a few items that are displayed such as the gumbo, jambalaya, and etouffee. I liked the etouffee which had a slight kick of heat to it.

I ended up getting the jambalaya with had shrimp, andouille sausage, chicken, and some vegetables. The chicken was a bit dry and not as tasty as the sausage and shrimp. The rice was cooked in a tomato-based sauce and actually not bad for cajun food. I also got their alligator sausage on a stick. It was very unique and the wrapping gave it a nice chew. Their cornbreads were decent.

It's nice that The Reading Terminal Market has different types of cuisines. This spot in particular brought me nostalgic NOLA vibes. I would definitely want to try their po boys in the future.
Anytime I come here I get the steak and chicken combo and it is always delicious. Not the most comfortable place to sit in but the folks make up for it with their amazing food!

I will not return to this place. How stupid does a cook have to be to totally mess up a $10 Impossible burger, by serving it only partially cooked; such a stupid inept clown in a cook's costume. Never ever will let my shadow darken their threshold again. I just asked for a box and brought the half-cooked sandwich home to finish cooking; I didn't send it back because it took that clown forever to only partially cook one vegan patty, in the first place. Another reason to never go into a bar for a meal; cook was probably drinking at 10:30am.

Such a wonderful dinning experience!! Went into Trident Grill after a musical at Centennial Hall... The service was spot on and the food was great! Both my daughter and I had the fish and chips, but weren't expecting much.... We were pleasantly surprised!! The food and drinks were exceptional and the prices were amazing. So looking forward to another visit to this restaurant ‼

On February 29th of 2008 I organized a small group of friends of mine to to be charged an enormous amount of money for possibly the worst dining experience of Chinatowns history!  Woo Hoo!

Someone sent me a link to what sounded like the dinner of a lifetime: Join Chef Poon for a traditional 10-course Chinese New Year Banquet featuring dishes from 8 nations. It sure wasn't difficult to convince some friends to join me since the menu sounded absolutely wonderful.

When we arrived at 1010 Arch street in Chinatown we found ourselves ascending a flight of dirty carpeted stairs that rewarded us with what looked like a wood-panelled storage room turned into emergency shelter/Chinese banquet room.  You see, there was an abundance of personal items and restaurant supplies such as old chairs, lamps and boxes of Christmas decorations piled up along the front part of the 2nd floor space.  There was no pretentious covering this stuff up.  No, it was there it was flavor!  The tables set up for our party and the other groups of victims were actually stainless steel work bench tables you might see in an industrial kitchen.  But of course these were covered with white table covers that were bleached, and yet still stained, so often they were holy.  Folding chairs were covered with images of Chef Poon, which would be creepy if not for the striking resemblance and level of class that one would see at Buddakan.  Steven Starr, eat your hear out.  Also, my group being fortunate, we were placed at the much sought after tables with the best views.  We were actually in the space deemed "the kitchen"  The equipment and sinks were only a mere 5 feet from our table!

Nonetheless the mood was one of anticipation.  If the place was THIS humble, imagine how great the food must be!  So we began with ordering a round of drinks.  We had a choice of generic Chinese beer or a glass of cheep box wine for a bargain $6. 
We had no idea what was in store for us.  The meal was over in less than 40 minutes and perhaps that's a good thing.  I wish you were there....
Oh.. let me walk you through it! No, no, it will be my pleasure to share this!

The first 2 "courses" were some mouthful-sized appetizer tastes that were actually pretty decent though tiny.  (Try and read the following as if you're training for the speed reading championships.)  These first courses were brought out at a leisurely pace of one per every... oh let's say 2.5 minutes.  It's a good thing though, since each of us had such supermarket-sample-sized portions we often were able to consume each before the next part of the feast arrived creating a sense of pride and accomplishment.  Honestly, there's no finer dining atmosphere better than that of  a pie eating contest and this was damn close to it.

So, as each dish was delivered to our work-bench table we found ourselves slowing down.  It was similar to when a child discovers something that causes pain and is reluctant try it again.

Larger dishes to be shared were brought out and and presentation occurred all at once so it really started feeling like a feast.  The presentation of some seemed aesthetically pleasing, while others were a bit scary.
Mostly though the seafood was fishy.  The Bass was greasy and the salmon tasted old, like "honey we should've thrown this out a week ago" old.  The Fried rice dish was sweet and unpleasant while perhaps the lowest point of the meal was the Lobster dish. A large dish of linguine was covered by pieces of lobster broken to hard chunks still in their shell.  They were delivered with no tools to crack the shells or retrieve the lobster meat.  Digging with a fork seemed useless but in a way I was glad the lobster was till in it's impenetrable  shell; it protected it from being contaminated by the tangy-sour and glowingly artificial red BBQ sauce which stung the eye as much as the tongue. 

And being Chinatown, we certainly were treated to our well deserved happy ending.  The sumptuous dessert consisted of a half-inch square of still mostly frozen cheescake/cookie pierced with a toothpick which held the single white grape on.  MMMmmmmhmmm. 
And then, the generosity flowed when Chef Poons staff rushed out to clank onto our table a half glass of Cook's sparkling wine. 

So in the end we each paid $54 per person (in Chinatown!) for what we all agreed was our worst culinary experience to date. 

*Please note, the delay of this review is partially because this event predated my Yelp awareness and I had tried to suppress these memories.  Forgetting is hard though since  lately when my friends and I experience unpleasant meals or find ourselves greatly ripped off, we say we've been "Pooned".  It's become a handy verb.

DAYUM that's a good crepe. I've had some good crepes in my day, but DAYUM. Got the Goat Bacon, amazing decision. Menu has savory crepes, sweet crepes, sandwiches and omlettes. The folks running the joint had a french accent which inspired great confidence in their crepe making ability and it lived up to the billing.

The crepe was huge and the goat cheese/mushroom/bacon filling was plentiful. Mark this on your GPS as a go-to spot in Philly.

If you look up lists of things to not miss at Reading the Train Wreck Po Boy is always on that list so decided to give it a try. For $10 its full of meat so a pretty good value, also one of the very few places in Reading that has counter seating which is a plus! Their signature hot sauce is really good, highly recommend adding that to the sandwich though it only has meat, onions and sauce, no other veggies! Overall still a heavy, filling sandwich with a little bit of spice and pretty good flavor. And service was FAST so good if you are trying to eat and get out and explore quickly
Nothing like some amazing pub grub with a heaping side of free breathing FREEDOM.  I never turn down a platter of fish and chips!

I was very happy with the hard work that Chris and his associate put into taming my unruly yard. They were professional and very communicative about their availability during the hurricane scare we had with Dorian. Chris quoted me a great price and did a great job. I highly recommend them to those looking for hard working businessmen who give fair prices and provide great service.

Saturday nights @ Trident I have become less than a place I want to visit. The manager sits at the end of the bar and drinks.  Puts UFC on just about every TV in the place when he knows my wife doesn't like it.  We were just about the only two in the place.  There was a PPV that night but not for another 2 hrs.   Food still good. We will just visit a different Trident for our Saturday nights out.

We came in for a late lunch and found the place pretty busy. We told the waitress we were first timers and she was kind enough to explain the menu and let us know her favorite items on the menu. She made everything sound so delicious. I love when the staff feels passionate about the food they are serving. We started with some delicious Yucca fries. We ordered a side of the cilantro rice as it was raved about - all true excellent combo of flavors. My husband opted for the steak and chicken with rice and finished it off with a smile. I ordered a salad with chopped chicken and it was awesome - they have several different sauces and I opted for the sauce vs regular salad dressing. I wish we saved room for dessert as the next table was enjoying it. Would highly recommend

Affordable, tasty Peruvian food! The service was great- our waitress didn't speak much English but she was quick to grab another waitress to help when needed. I ordered the steak with an egg- it was so good and only $13!! My friends ordered the chicken sandwich and they both liked it and said they would come here again. Great food and great service- especially for the reasonable prices !

I went here on a date. They had live music playing. I liked the inside of the restaurant and the sushi was really good. My date enjoyed the place a lot. The sushi was really good and reasonably priced to make me want to go again.

Service: the service was quick and friendly which is always good inside a busy market. 

Food: the menu offers multiple different items in a wide array of classic Cajun food. The fried catfish was overbreaded and had very little meat inside. The fried Mac and cheese was good but it deff could of used a better sauce to go with it to make it take the extra step. The blackened chicken po-boy would have been completely elevated if they used better bread. The chicken was also slightly over cooked and tough

We were visiting Philly during COVID, and luckily Reading Market was considered an essentail business. Even with said, sadly, some places were still closed.

Luckily Termini Brothers was open. My husband and I stopped by for a late breakfast. There was so such to choose from. My husband loves pastries. He got a wide assortment. I went with their cannoli. It was so good!! 

Also the person behind the counter was friendly and personable!!

READ BEFORE YOU PAY! Went in for a consult for my neck,  she made me feel like I was being so cheap for daring to bring down price.  She compared her self to ideal image.  Went to Arviv Medical, where they actually use the latest version of the laser that Ideal Image has and they gave me a much better price without even asking.  Don't feel pressured to sign up here!!! Trying to get a fair price is normal! Like Kelly who wrote a review, I do question if all the other reviews are by actual clients!

I ordered red beans and rice. The attendant asked if I want jambalaya rice or plain rice. I said jambalaya and when I went to pay I was told there was a three dollar up charge for that special rice. It's something that the attendant should've told me or just not offered It's a tricky move to generate another three dollars in revenue. Watch out!

Stopped in this morning for breakfast.  My favorite server was there and the morning cook is great!  This place just keeps on getting better.  My machaca burrito was so good I just can't say enough about it - it's got to be the best in Tucson.  For sure I'll keep stopping by!

Trivia night is why we started going here and that can be fun if you go with some friends. However, every time I have gotten a jack and coke, the soda has been flat. Even the replacement drink was flat. We went there last night again for drinks before the UofA vs NAU game and the coke was flat again, it was terrible. We ordered two whisky sours and they were just as bad, watered down whisky with no sour mix. The service is always slow, so order two drinks at a time. They have got to get some better soda and better bartenders. The food, is typical bar food, nothing special.
Delicious spicy Cajun shrimp & ettouffee over jambalaya rice with corn bread and sweet tea!   Reading Terminal Market has a hit on its hands.

I had the fish and chips and fried pickles here, a bit overpriced.
The waitress was nice, too nice I don't know why I didn't tell her my water tasted like metal.

It definitely has culture, with lots of memorabilia hanging on the walls. I'd come here again to try out other stuff. We'll see about the water.

It's perfect for the neighborhood. It's very cute and quaint, the owners are nice and I love the simple yet contemporary decor. The basement lounge area is really cool and not too tight. The food is pretty good, I'm a fan of the tarts and the fresh squeezed orange juice is awesome. I had the vegetarian omelette and it comes with a side salad that is pretty tasty. My friend seems to love the Hazelnut latte. I am looking forward to trying a crepe and enjoying the pleasant service again very soon.

I've had a Po'boy here, but let's not talk about a meal I've eaten here...  Let's discuss me ordering King Cake's every year.  I have a King Cake shipped from the New Orleans area every year.  Okay, almost every year...  My wife is going to read this and tell me I didn't order one when I was two years old... Back to the King Cakes... I wasn't fully feeling them in recent years, so I've tried some other places and even made my own last year.  This year, I was talking to co-workers and thought about local places.  I knew a place in Reading Terminal Market, didn't recall the name, but after some quick yelp searches, remembered it was Beck's...  I reached out to them and inquired about the King Cake on Instagram.  After a small conversation, I placed an order.  On the day to pickup, there were a lot of King Cakes there.  I was given mine and I got a quick peek before paying.  

"Wow" was seriously my first thought.  I think every company from New Orleans ships with FedEx, along with special FedEx boxes.  They're almost all the same...  None, that I've found, were this large.  Those are smaller, I'm sure for shipping reasons, and sometimes filled with custard, but this was so much larger.  

I personally loved the flavors so much more.  The sugar topping, which is usually too much for me, was more balanced on the Beck's King Cake.  I enjoyed the more brioche like center.   The only complaint I received, was that someone said theirs didn't have a filling in it...  I think they wanted custard...  Which another co-worker won't eat, because he doesn't eat cream cheese...  Even though I don't think there is cream cheese in the Bavarian custard we sometimes get?  I don't like people...  Why do I get these things for everyone?  

Forgetting the "extras" that goes inside, this was a fantastic King Cake and probably the best value I've gotten.  These cakes were decorated nicely too.  You can do that when you aren't depending on FedEx to ship...  I can baby, get it, this cake filled with a baby, all the way back to the office in my car.  I wouldn't be surprised if this is the place I go for now on...  It's more work on my behalf, but I think it's worth it.  I'll just get a tub of custard and fruit fillings and let people dip in the future...  Just to shut them up...

Beck's is pretty good.  I had a chance to check out the jambalaya, oyster po'boy and Cajun fries.

It seemed the jambalaya was a little skimpy in the meat category.  It took me at least 3 or 4 forkfuls before I found my first shrimp.  

When I eat jambalaya, the shrimp should be an unhidden part of the mix and not a joyful surprise when I finally find one.  Don't get me wrong - I like surprises.  I just don't like when the surprise happens to be "less shrimp than I'd hoped in my jambalaya."  It is a very crappy surprise.  Same goes for the sausage.  That being said, the flavor of the rice was good and the tomatoes from the sauce had a great texture.

The cajun fries were A-OK.

The Oyster po'boy was tasty but the roll could be a little softer.  I hate, hate, hate, hate struggling with my sandwich to rend pieces from it.  This is supposed to be lunch and not a test of the torque-resilience of my maxillary incisors.

On the action-movie-parallel-satisfaction-scale, this establishment is Collateral Damage.
This place is heavily! Never had one bad thing to eat here and the staff is excellent. Seating is limited and "first come first serve" but worth the wait. You can also order to go.

Omg!  Why haven't I been here before?  What took me so long?!?!  

This place is incredible. Moist, flavorful rotisserie chicken full of flavor. I do like YaYas but I'd take Cuenelli's any day. 

And the spicy yellow sauce served with it?  Out of this world. 

This restaurant is extremely clean and brightly decorated inside. The waitress was extremely helpful and gave me some guidance when ordering. I appreciate that I was allowed to sub my French fries for the cilantro rice. 

Now I know what all the yelp hype is regarding this place....I've experienced it and will def be back.
This is a very cozy place and has really good coffee. The coffee here was so perfect, the bitterness of the coffee was not overpowred by the flavoring.

Got the shrimp platter with bread pudding for dessert. The dessert and the cornbread are the only reason this is getting stars. The shrimp her like rubber and the red beans and rice were way too salty. A bit let down because I really wanted to like this place as New Orleans is one of my favorite places in the country. The cornbread is really good though.

Perhaps the best Po Boy I've had. Ordered the Blackened Catfish Po Boy with Cajun fries, and was not disappointed with either.  As previous have stated, it's a great spot in the Market and I will come back to try the other items. The Trainwreck was displayed in the case and looked amazing.

I've always liked Beck's a lot. I hadn't been here for several years. But today I decided to give them a shot. 

Now, at the risk of coming off as a complete snob here, I was a little let down today. Since the last time I had Beck's I've been to New Orleans. I've tasted the real deal. They're playing on a different culinary level down there. 

I now know why Beck's is considered really good for Philadelphia. But in New Orleans I sense they wouldn't quite cut it. And maybe that's not a fair comparison. But I believe it's true now. 

I went with a catfish finger platter with red beans and rice. My biggest complaint was the catfish. They came off a little chewy and overdone. The seasoning was way more salty than anything. Not bad, but far from great. 

I will say that the beans and rice were tremendous. That flavor was on point with more spice than salt. And I still like the cornbread. 

It's quite possible I just didn't get their best dish. I still have love for them. But I'm calling this one as I see it, or in this case taste it.
This little out-of-the-way restaurant a nice atmosphere. The service was very courteous and fast. The food is cooked fresh. And The Taste is awesome. I would come back here again.
Great service, food and atmosphere...especially when watching football .  Had the Captain's Platters & Chicken Salad...both delicious.  Good selection of beers and everything reasonably priced.

This is related to Double Knot in center city which is a super popular sushi / asian cuisine restaurant.

This DK Sushi is located in a new and more modern type food court. The organization is a little messy but it's all on a kiosk so once you're ready to order go up to the computer and order.

The food is a little pricey but it's definitely worth a try. I got the tempura shrimp over rice and it was super tasty and the perfect lunch amount. The sauce that it comes with is delicious. It's super fresh and made to order. 

The line may be intimidating but it goes by quickly! Be sure to stop by and grab an option over rice with a side of spicy edamame. You won't regret it!

Do Ya know the intro to duck tales ? The part where scrooge Mcduck does a swan dive into a pile of coins ? 
Well, substitute coins for cannoli filling and that's me if I'm a Millionaire. 
I'm not sure how it'll be done or if it's even possible but hey, I can dream. 

You know you have a food problem ... or eating disorder when you find yourself using a spoon to steal the filling from the extra cannoli's that you didn't need in the first place. Less calories if you don't eat the shell right ? F me. I have issues. 

Like the location on 8th Street in South Philly, Termini's gets it right. 
I've had several visits to Termini's over the years and never had anything bad. 
Definitely my favorite bakery in Philly
(Stocks for pound cake)

Cheesecake,cookies,cupcakes and their cannolis are literally the best in Philly (in my opinion) 

Pricey ? Yes. Worth it ? Yes. 

Side note : I ran into my cousin while waiting in line (It's a small world) When asked what she recommends, she said everything. 

So go ahead and pick anything.
Great food, great service fish and shrimp tacos are amazing I will definitely be back and recommend to others  .. Great Moscow mules !!
Beyond meat vegan pizza was super good and service was good even though it was super busy. We had a long wait time but eventually were seated and taken care of!

Lunch today was really good. The hot appetizer sampler was well executed and very tasty. The fried mozzarella was tender and the sauce fresh. The calamari was tender and light.   The special caponata bruschetta was "meaty" and flavorful. The seafood in my salad was fresh, tender & plentiful and the greens were fresh and well composed. The dressing was a good match of vinegar & oil. My husband's penne alla vodka was well executed, served hot & tasty.     The bread served was okay but nothing special and the server was aloof. He left the check by tossing it on the table while heading to another table.   We'd return because the food was very good.

I dream about their cannolis and they never let me down!  I love the reading terminal and this is one of the stars in the terminal. They are usually always busy and although they are usually fast it is such a small little congested area.  

They can be pricey but I think the price is totally worth it. The cannoli cream is the best ever and the shell has the right firmness without being to firm. They fill the cannolis with the ricotta mixture to order. The other desserts look divine.  I bought my grandmother a cream puff and she enjoyed it. 

If you are in the reading terminal you must check them out.

This place is pretty good.  I don't usually eat the skin of the chicken because it's typically not crispy enough for me and slimy, but here, you could literally give me a whole plate of it! (I am gross, I know).  It was just that good.  The chicken was fall-off-the-bone and their plantains were perfectly caramelized and sweet.  I ended up using their delicious home made sauces for my fries, which were also very tasty.  This place is pretty cheap for a sit-down, and you will leave feeling stuffed without breaking the bank.

Being that I had to run a race tomorrow, I opted to not totally wreak havoc on my system entirely... and just had a quick order of the macaroni and cheese balls.  They come with a delish, spicy marinara-style sauce and you can add hot sauce or old bay seasoning to it too!  
Just bellied up to the counter at Reading Terminal. Service was quick and fast.
Definitely coming back... as it was affordable for the portion and convenience.  
As chaotic as RT can be... it's worth taking a spin thru the mayhem to try this place.

Best spot in town for unbelievably tasty Rotisserie Chicken and many other mouth-watering options with a Peruvian twist - be it the green or yellow sauce, the lomo saltado, or simply the salad dressing with a touch of cilantro.

Whether you've lived here all your life or you're just passing through, check out Cuenellis!

Short:

Tasty, stick with the chicken.  Good portion sizes.  If you have a big group, get the family meal.  

Long:

Great small restuarant.  A few of my Peruvian friends actually recommended this place.  Went to give it a shot.  The chicken here is cooked perfectly and the portions are large.  The beans here are delicious.  Its not just straight out of the can tasting, they actually season it here.  The sauces they offer with the chicken is great, I recommend just sticking with the chicken, that's what they specialize in.  I've heard mixed reviews of the other types of meat.

They have a family meal here, I've seen people order that and it looks like an enormous amount of food, more than enough for a family of four.  

Staff are friendly, decor is unique.

Been hearing about this place for quite some time. A friend wanted the Three Devil's hot sauce they sell. Got the Gator Gumbo over the Jambalaya. It was bold and hearty. Definitely a good choice all around. Can't wait to try their hot sauce too
The fried oyster po' boy and shrimp 'n crawfish etouffee brought me right back to New Orleans. This is the real deal cajun spot. Awesome y'all!
The food was bland, tasteless, and cold. I was really sad. I got a pricky pear cactus margarita didn't taste like the fruit at all

Let me start off with the food was killer. I got the paleo bowl and my boyfriend got the half order of nachos. The paleo bowl had the perfect combo of shredded carrots, sweet potatoes, lettuce, chicken, and some salsa. The nachos were heavenly, of course. Can't go wrong with cheese on top of chips!

My only complaints are that the beer list wasn't fantastic. I was expecting more local items and all that stood out to me was  Barrio blonde and the Trident brew. I saw beers like blue moon and bud but would have appreciated more local options. 

This is a true local spot. Hence my want for more local beers. We went on a Wednesday when Geeks who drink was about to start. The restaurant itself was friendly however the crowd was not. I can only assume that most people go here regularly and are used to the same faces. 

I would probably avoid here on Wednesday's around 6:30-8pm. Truly, I've never felt more unwelcome by a crowd then here. as mentioned the staff was great, the food was great but the crowd was unfriendly.

In the interest of disclosure, this restaurant probably deserves 4.5 stars because I've had some pretty mediocre service before. However, I went last night and the service was on point so I bumped it up to five.

I went because someone told me they have the best fish and chips in Tucson. It's funny because I've never actually tried the fish and chips, but I haven't gone wrong yet!

It's a large, single room pub. Very loud, so you won't want to come if you're looking for a romantic outing. As others have mentioned, lots of military memorabilia everywhere. I like it and I'm happy to support the business of a local Tucson veteran as my husband is also a veteran.

I'm impressed at the appeal this place has to a large variety of demographics. I came here one night and felt very out of place because it was loaded with college students (my college days are behind me), but come another night and you'll see mostly folks in their 40s, or groups of older ladies, or groups of veterans, or mid 20s people like me looking for some good food. I like that because it feels very inclusive. Excellent atmosphere to have at a pub and I wonder how they do it - I bet a lot of people would pay the owners for their secrets on how to appeal to everybody like that. I could absolutely see myself becoming a regular here.

Now, onto the food, the most important part! The first time I came here I had the Chesapeake Bay burger because I am an Old Bay freak. Big, stuffed with goodies, and excellent flavor. However, they have lighter dishes that will actually appeal to you rather than forcing you to feel like, "Crap, I'm on a diet, I guess I'll have this nasty wilted salad."

I came here the other night and wanted to try their famous clam chowder. I had a soup and sandwich combo with the chicken salad sandwich. Now, I still think that my grandma's chowder is better, but I won't say that I didn't enjoy that chowder immensely. At request they top it with a generous bit of bacon and green onions. Yum! The sandwich impressed me a lot as well because you don't see chicken salad everywhere, but it's one of my favorites. It comes on toasted bread with the perfect amount of chicken salad. And it's not an overly sweet salad either. You know I liked it because I came back the next night and had the exact same thing.

Ok, so, the service. Last night it was out of the park. Jason noticed me at the door looking for a table and used his immense height to locate one for me in the nearly-full house. He was very pleasant and even checked on me later to see how I was doing. Janelle was my server and she was amazing. I order coffee when I come here rather than a beer because as much as I love beer, I work graveyards and need to wake up before my shift. This usually means that they have to brew a new pot because I don't know who else comes there for coffee at 9pm on a Friday night except me. However, she did so without complaint. She was always prompt and had a smile on her face the whole time. She knew what the soup of the day was without having to go check (other servers at this place sometimes don't...) and I just adored her. Never once felt ignored - and I was a one top taking up a table on a busy night. Thank you, Janelle!

As for other service I've had, it would echo what countless other reviewers have mentioned. Young, pretty college girls who have a little trouble paying attention to their tables. Like I said, they often don't know the specials, and you might have to chase them across the restaurant for the check, where you'll probably find them sitting at the bar, chatting with their friends. I don't get worked up about it because I know what restaurant work is like, it can be a grind, and they will go get my check if asked. It is sort of irksome that I have to go find them, though. It's also a little annoying that this is my usual experience with the service here, rather than Janelle the rockstar.

A note to the restaurant: if half your yelp reviews echo this experience with the service (which they do), maybe work on a little server training. It's ok to socialize, restaurants are social places, but you also need to do your job while on the clock.

Like I said, though, I'm still giving this place five stars because I love it. Come here and you won't be disappointed.
Came here for the cannoli and I was not disappointed! The shell was crispy and the filling was rich. Probably can't eat it too often tho haha.

I love Termini Brothers... 

This bakery is awesome..

However I didnt like the dirty look she shot after someone of "color" asked for a job application...  Im not a shallow person and I know what I saw we not in the 1960's grow up lady

This wont affect me not coming here but I think I'll skip and go to Comcast Center....

Legit Cajun in Philly!

Honestly, Cajun is the last thing I expected to have in Philadelphia, but I was in Reading Terminal Market and wanted something with a little kick.

Sure I had my doubts.  Most of the foods were sitting in double boilers and sandwiches were already made.  Beck's is more of a fast food type joint and unless you order a po'boy sandwich or fried items, most items are ready to go.  However, I was surprised by how good everything tasted!

They have these lunch platters but I decided to order a la carte.  Went for the jambalaya and the quarter muffaletta.  I love the jambalaya!  I've always been a huge fan of jambalaya cause it has so much flavor.  Beck's got that part down.  The Cajun Creole seasoning goes great with andouille sausage, chicken, shrimp, peppers, and onions.  It's also moist, not dry like some places.  As for the muffaletta, it's on a sesame bun and if you order a quarter, you'll get a quarter but the quarter-portion is HUGE.  It's bigger than most sandwiches actually.  The marinated olive salad is good with the usual suspects of a muffaletta: salami, ham, and mortadella.

Red beans with rice, gumbo, po'boy, catfish, and beignets are few others that caught my attention.  Unfortunately I found out about this gem on my last day in Philly so couldn't try a few more items.  Sad.

I was there about two hours ago.  I am sick in bed now.  This was the second time I've visited La Parrilla Suiza, and I really liked it the first time.  The guacamole was grey this time, and even against my better judgement I decided to eat some of it.  I will never go back.
Omg so good ! I got the Norwegian with smoked salmon goat cheese and aVocado .... sooo good I could eat another one ! Parking is a little rough , coffee is strong . I highly recommend !
Awesome shop, great artist, clean shop, walkins harder to get on the weekend but usually available during the week
