So this Southern Cajun boy needed some good ol' cajun fare and a Po'boy just sounded like what I needed at the time. Its been a hot second since I've had one and walking by this little store front gave me pretty good vibes.

I ordered the fried shrimp po'boy and I was thoroughly impressed. The pricing was good, about $10 for a large sandwich. I literally split it into two meals, maybe I wasn't super hungry as I'd eaten my way through Philly but its definitely a hearty meal if you eat the full sandwich. The shrimp was fried well, good crunch, good shrimp flavor, a bit overfried so a little dry. However, the sauce made up for it and really brought the po'boy together. The bread held up very well too, this wasn't one of those sandwiches that just fall apart the second you take a bite!

I'll definitely have to come back some day and try their other fare. They have your menu of NOLA classics like jambalaya, gumbo, etoufee so there's plenty of options for anyone trying to fill a cajun itch.

Every time I pay a visit to Reading Terminal Market, I make sure to stop by Beck's. This stall serves some of the best Cajun food I've ever had. Their gumbo is one of their more popular items offered here and it's truly delicious. They offer a variety of different gumbos including chicken/shrimp and even gator gumbo. 

For those that are a bit hesitant about trying out gator, its surprisingly delicious. It has the aftertaste of chicken and does not have an fishy taste to it...as one may have expected. My recommendation would be to order the gator gumbo with jambalaya, even if it's $2 more. The jambalaya has a nice kick of spiciness to it and it makes the overall dish much more enjoyable. 

Overall, I've had pretty decent experiences at Beck's. I look forward to trying out their fried Mac and cheese balls with gumbo and fried catfish the next time i visit.

Termini Bros is a Philadelphia classic. Whenever I'm looking for a meal topper in Reading Terminal, I always turn to them for a quality cannoli. 

Recently, I picked up a tirimisu cake for a friend's birthday. The staff was very patient throughout the decision making process, and offered good insight when I asked. She also wrote a message on the cake for free! The whole cake came out to only $25! The cake itself was absolutely delicious. Light and fluffy, yet rich in flavor. I would definitely recommend it! I will definitely be returning for cakes in the future!

I'm going to tell you, if you like bland this is the spot for you. I was so unimpressed but understood that not even enjoys flavor of food. After my over watered down mayo drenched seafood pasta, I promised myself that I would fully enjoy the real thing if I ever went to New Orleans.
I had the Gator Gumbo. I am glad they are not too close to me, because I would never cook again! Delicious. Spicy! I cannot wait to go back and sample more off the menu.

My husband and I & our friends ate at Chef Joseph Poon on Jan. 25, 2010 for restaurant week & thought the food was amazing!  Every course was delicious, especially the lobster course. I would definitely recommend this restaurant, especially during restaurant week! And it was only $35 per person for several courses!

The customer service is terrible. It is so bad that they make u feel uncomfortable instead of welcome. Rude servers. Food is ok but service is terrible.  Terra sur is not so different but the food is better.
Trident has a great atmosphere! Their food is delicious, and it's a short walk from the UofA. They also have a nice selection of local beers.
Updated review to add picture of this delicious food. The green sauce is a delicious  addition!

With all the outstanding reviews from my fellow Yelpers, I knew I had to try this place.  I am huge fan of rotisserie chicken done right and WOW does this place do it right.  The chicken has crisp, luscious skin and a mouthwatering blend of herbs and spices rubbed between skin and meat.  I have no clue if it's 'authentic' or not, but it's so delicious my husband briefly accused me of being a pod person, having never, EVER seen me gleefully gnaw at chicken bones anywhere else.  It used to be a running joke in my family that I left an entire 2nd meal still on the bone, but here?  I was nibbling off every last bit of meat and seasoned skin.  I've been a few times at lunch and done the 1/4 chicken (white) with the cilantro rice (delicious), but for the visit with the hubby we shared a  1/2 chicken and some of his Bistec a lo Pobre. Note - I said some.  Frankly, I think the only reason I got any of his steak is that he cut off a portion for me before he tried it.  Really flavorful steak that had an almost mojo-like marinade on top of a mountain of beans and rice with fries and ripe plantains on the side for those that need more starches.  And that plate was shiny clean by the time he was done.  His only complaint?  His fried egg was completely solid - no runniness to the yolk at all.  I have my eye on the pasta topped with steak for our next visit, whereas he is in line for the same thing again, but we are in absolute agreement - there will be a next time

Food is FANTASTIC but service is not that great. If dinning in, you might have to repeat yourself more than once you want ketchup, lemons slices, etc. If you order pick up make sure you specify you need utensils, sauces and napkins!!! Oh, and make sure they repeat the order to you before you pay because if they messed up and they charged you already, for example I ordered two meals and TWO drinks and only charge me for one drink they can't charge you again (credit card, low amount) and won't accommodate them messing up. They just give you attitude and say "sorry, you can pay in cash" if I had cash I wouldn't have paid with a credit card, right? Or maybe the person taking the orders on the phone needs training.

This is my first review on Yelp. Vineyards cafe is such an amazing addition to my neighborhood. The food is delicious!!! The staff and atmosphere make eating here even more enjoyable. Another bonus is they are super kid friendly!!!!!

what a cafe should be by definition!!!
Awsome food, great coffee prepared right, friendly service!

Awesome!! I've never been disappointed here with a dessert from here. Their cake, biscotti, and cupcakes are all awesome. The best thing here is their homemade cannoli. It is the best cannoli I have ever had. The center is filled with a creamy ricotta and chocolate chip filling. Anytime I am near Reading Terminal I make a special trip for it.
Never had a bad experience here.  Never even had a single bad dish. Chicken is great. Cilantro rice is great.  Spicy beans great.  Fried Yuca great.  Salchipapas great.

WOW... just wow!! I'm visiting for the week and came across this place on yelp. Just finished my meal, and my only disappointment is that I didn't try this place earlier into my trip. I've only got 1.5 days left, but totally thinking I might be able to come back 2 more times. 

I had the chargrilled oysters, raw oysters, oyster tacos, and the nori fries. Couldn't resist ordering all of that just for myself, and yes, I finished every last bite. They were all so good!!!

If you like oysters, this place is a must!

Love eating lunch here and its a really good spot for BBQ chicken done over coal. The french fries and sauces are so good as well when you feel like letting your hair down on carbs. The original servers are the best, id ask for one of them as they are top notch servers as well.
A must stop when in Tucson. Always a good time with great food, huge portions, and a wonderful atmosphere.

5 stars to the pecan square. It cost $5 for a 7/8" thick, 2.75" x 3.5" rectangle of dessert. 5 bucks is 5 bucks but WORTH it. It is an excellent rich  square. I am a glutton and I couldn't finish it but I will tomorrow. It is like a merge of Twix and a dense Turtle chocolate with 5x more pecans. The caramel is also gooey but not loose. It's beautiful. I think I want a slab of this as my birthday cake. The fig bar is good, not sweet, it's perfect for tea time kind of a thing....The other philo layered scallop thing was meh. It was hard and I was expecting the flakiness to break apart but it didn't. It was chewy and I had to make an effort to bite it off. I am also not sure what the filling is. It's a a little bit creamy but more on the stiff side and slightly orangy (very veeery mild orange) ...it's beautiful looking but it doesn't talk the talk. It just walks the walk. All of these items were $5 a pop.

Edit: The owner (I think) responded, he explained they do not have direct contact with Postmates so the menu was not up-to-date; hence, items not being available. They also shared they typically do not recommend crepes for delivery, as they should be eaten within a few minutes of being prepared. All that said, I respect him reaching out and respectfully adding context. Kudos for good customer service. 

We ordered delivery this morning, we are so so so disappointed. First, we found out they were out of 3 of the 6 items we ordered - blackberry jam for a crepe, fresh OJ, and one of the other crepes. In the end, we picked the sucre crepe, Norwegian crepe, crepe with apricot jam, everything bagel with fig jam, and an iced coffee drink. The only thing that was good was the bagel and coffee. I don't understand all the reviews praising these crepes as special. I know this will sound super pretentious, but I have had crepes in France and at many places in CA - none of them have tasted as poorly as these. All 3 were lacking flavor and the consistency/style of crepe was  not appetizing, plain, not crispy, more brown colored, and lacking. The Norwegian has salmon, goat cheese, and avocado - the salmon was overpowering, while a good quantity of protein is usually welcome, this was super fishy and with a lack of flavor/spices, it was as if rating straight salmon, not a crepe with other ingredients. The plain with apricot jam was like soaking up apricot syrup with a plain piece of bread and the sucre one didn't even taste of sugar, I couldn't even see the sugar inside.I dislike giving low reviews, but I am confused why this has high reviews which misled us and was why we ordered here. We all have different taste buds and preferences, this was our experience, hopefully others enjoy this place.

I work very hard to find black owned companies to support so I was very happy to find Bella locs.  I ordered locs for my trip and eventhough we are going thru pandemic circumstances I found them not to very professional and a little rude.  On the site it states 2 to 5 days for delivery but after the 5th day I called for a status and was rushed off the phone and told that my hair didn't even leave the facility.   I called because I wasn't sent a tracking which I thought was odd.  There were only 2 black owned companies that I was able to find and I will definitely try the other company.  Hopefully they will value my business a little bit more or at least provide up to date information.   My goal is to stay clear of Chinese companies due to what is happening in China with black people but I must say this experience was very disappointing.
The staff should be wearing masks.  I was very uncomfortable knowing staff were not wearing masks.  Food is always good but will be a longtime before I return to Trent grill

Amazing service!!! Not only was he able to detect the problem but he went out of his way to make sure it doesn't happen again!!! Highly recommended and on top of it a super nice guy!!! Very impressed!!!

Trident overall, is so amazing and unbeatable. I wish they would even expand to other places! I've been dozens of times, to all locations and mostly had a good experience. The portions are always huge but this time my salad had barely any chicken on it. Other than that the drinks were great and everyone seemed to love their food. One strange part, after 5 minutes or so of the server dropping the check on our tables she came back and preceded to tell us that "she wants to check out now so she can go" but the way she phrased it was kind of strange and impolite. It was sort of implying that we need to leave. I'm a server too, so I understand when you're cut you want to go home, but she could have said it in a much better way. This is my only gripe with trident thus far, overall the place is absolutely stellar and the food is great!
Place is hot inside. The owner or manager (chubby lady with black hair) always has an attitude, even towards servers sometimes. Today was the last straw.

It was so hard choosing a place to get food at the Reading Terminal because they are just so many options, but I was glad that I decided to get food from this place. I got the chicken and shrimp jambalaya. It was fairly spicy and very flavorful. I couldn't make a dent into the jambalaya, so I ended up taking most of it home. For some reason, I liked the jambalaya a lot better when I got home and when it was cold. I thought it was a lot more spicier when I got it piping hot.  This is a good option if you are confused about what to eat at Reading Terminal.

Being that I don't get to Reading Terminal Market as frequently as I used to, it's been awhile since I've visited Beck's.  However, the sandwiches I recently had there definitely made up for the fact that I haven't eaten there in some time.  I've been hearing about the train wreck po boy and being a cheesesteak lover, I was very intrigued by this sandwich.  It was awesome!  The steak itself was very good, high quality, finely chopped meat, just the way I like it.  The addition of the cheese, andouille sausage, salami, onions, and creole mayo make it over the top delicious.  While it's certainly an untraditional cheesesteak, at the moment, I'd consider it one of my absolute favorites in the city.  In addition to the train wreck, we got a 1/4 of the muffaletta to share for dinner (yes, it was a gluttonous day!).  It was also quite yummy!  Olive salad on a sandwich=awesomeness.  If you're in the mood for a hot sandwich, get the train wreck, if you want something cold, get the muffaletta.  Trust this confessed sandwich lover, you will not be disappointed either way.
This is the only restaurant I will even bother to order from. The food is always good, and the owner is a gem of a human being.

I ordered their chicken parm dinner which came with two huge chicken cutlets, choice of pasta (I picked ravoli) salad or soup (I got chicken noodle) and garlic bread for like $15. It was SO good. The soup was homemade, chicken parm was perfect. I will order again for sure.

Came based on ratings, left disappointed.  My wife and I ordered jerk chicken wings and each had the jerk chicken platter.   By the time we got home, we both had upset stomachs.  The food was ok, nothing to rate 5 stars.  We also each had coconut waters and my wife had a bottle of Perrier, with tip it came to $88.   All the food must have been pre-made because it came out super fast and they only offer dark meat.  Nothing tasted fresh.  The rice and peas was mostly rice, they could definitely could have added more peas or even had a side of peas or beans available.  The owner was very nice and helpful.  the server was missing most of the time even though there was just three tables seated; the most disappointing part was my wife asked the server does she recommend the chicken curry or the jerk chicken, she wasn't helpful rather just suggested to order a platter with both.  The correct thing she should have done is let us know that the jerk chicken is very spicy and the curry chicken is mild.
Great fish mediocre fries. Burger decent but wouldn't go out of my way. But the fish is PERFECT!!

We showed up late and I was worried they were out of food.  We're seated quickly and given menus to look over.   We never been to a Peruvian restaurant before.   I knew about the chicken and I wanted to try the steak.   The waitress was so helpful.   The food came out quickly.

The chicken was moist and tasted wonderful.   The steak was seasoned well but not my favorite cut.  The plaintain chips app was good. I enjoyed my meal.

Good falafel, very large portions.
The chickpea falafels were fresh and very tasty.
The weird thing is...I asked for yogurt, and they didn't have it?
What the hell is that?
Anyways...decent dinner for one, reasonably priced

I ran into this place the last time I was in Philidelphia at the Reading Terminal. I asked for a sample of the gumbo. I make gumbo myself and I was ready to play a joke on these poor fools because they were not cooking authentic gumbo. One sip and I was hooked. This is as good as my own. I was starting to think did someone steal my recipe or what. I was very impressed but I was in a rush and could not come back for a real sample.  Well, today I had that chance and I did not want to waste it. 

I got the chicken and shrimp gumbo small portion and I was very delighted with it. Deep rich gumbo flavor with a good portion of chicken and shrimp.  Very good and Traditional presentation. 

Overall. I am a big fan. I am coming back.

Great Peruvian food. For the price especially. This is conveniently located by the gym I go to, Powerhouse so it's great for post workout meals. They provide a special for $15 that includes steak, chicken, rice, plantains, fries and some salad. Great service. Waiters will usually check on you to see how your meal is. I highly recommend this place.
Good food, atmosphere, and staff. Nachos are awesome!  Good drinks and a decent price.  A good go-to sports bar or place to hang out solo or in a group.  Lots of military folks frequent Trident.

Have to give it 5/5!

What really set this place apart (aside from the wildly out of place Cajun food) was their awesome staff! They were there whenever we needed something and made sure we enjoyed our meal.

We came around lunch time on a Monday and both had the Trainwreck sandwich, which was excellent! For around $9 it was a decently large sandwich with plenty of meat, cheese and a lot of smoky delicious flavor. There are plenty of really cool vendors in Reading Terminal Market but this place stood out!
Had lunch here with a friend. The crepe, potatoes, and coffee were perfect. The atmosphere is so elegant- I love their plants! I'll definitely come back.

Let me start with this...$4 for 5 slices of fried yucca. 

Besides that ridiculous price/yucca metric and the inability to swap fries with yucca for the combination deal, I was underwhelmed with the execution of the chicken and ambiance.  

I'm used to walking into these joints and seeing the Smokey charcoal rotisserie ripping with dozens of chickens turning, a buffet line of sides, and the ever present BANG of fresh off the spit, charred, crispy chicken being hacked into quarters and halves.  The experience here is much more docile and I was left questioning if charcoal was being used. If you dine in it is full service, which again is unusual in my experience for pollo ala brasa ("PaB",) which further drives up the price for the consumer.  

The chicken lacked the crispy skin I expect and the breast meat was dry. Their yellow and green sauces were ok, with the yellow having more mustard and less mayonnaise than I've encountered in the past. 

I must've been spoiled living near Washington DC with the local purveyors of PaB, Sardis and Crisp & Juicy, because Cuenellis falls far short in terms of ambiance, value, flavor and texture.  Maybe it's as good as Tampa can muster. 

My personal search for my go to spot for PaB continues...

Pizza tasted like roller rink pizza.

Workers were dishonest and unprofessional.

It's a cozy place with more room in the basement. 
Their crepes menu is perfect, has sweet and savory options. Plus serve La Colombe Coffee. 

Is a great morning breakfast cafe. And the workers are also very nice and very helpful. 
Coming back for sure!

We have been here three times, but this is the first time that I had a chance to review the location, food, and service. This location and menu is relatively well hidden because it's not on their main menu signage. In fact, you would only see it if you sat on the row and saw the modest card with the price and menu. At $35, yes $35, you can have the chef prepare you a delightful omakase. The meal varies each time based on ingredient availability and also the chef. Prior to this meal, we had come about 6 months ago, and had a phenomenal experience. The manager, Mindy, curated the meal for us. She let us know what was available and what was not. She also interacted with us throughout the meal and gave us some insight about each of the Dishes she was serving. She also asked about how we were doing throughout the meal. One of the really great highlights of that meal was a soft shell crab hand roll. Unfortunately, on this experience it was nearly the complete opposite. The chef interacted with us only to let us know about what was being served. Although he asked about our food allergies, he did not let us know that some of the items that were on the menu were not available including the uni. Fortunately, we did not want that uni but we expected to have something equivalent to that. We were taken aback when the final dish was a standard California roll. It was nice that some of the other nigiri dishes were doubled up to make up for what was lacking, but so many dishes were served at once that the Experience was lackluster, and felt rushed. I guess the secret is out now, but we don't plan on returning. We also asked the cashier about our previous experience with the manager Mindy, and were told that she, sadly, no longer work for the business.

Really disappointed with everything. Came in and it was very busy but was seated quickly. Getting our food on the other hand took almost an hour. I understand that it was busy, but for a party of three to order quickly and still have to wait that long is ridiculous. Then, when we got our food it wasn't what we expected. I got the chuleta tacos with cheese and substituted beans for rice. When it finally came, my tacos had nothing but pork on them and the rice  was undercooked and crunchy. I then asked where my cheese was and they took it back, added cheese and put it in the microwave because my plate came out hotter than it left. Was really excited to have good authentic Mexican food but considering your in Tucson, go somewhere else.
i love this place!! they have the best service and the best food! i've been going here for years and never EVER had a SINGLE problem with anything.

Love it here. The crepes are absolutely perfect. I have the Philadelphia sandwich (lox) close to once a week. And they serve la colombe coffee.  Great space with outdoor seating and a dining area in the basement. Such a good spot.

So glad I found this place! The service is great and friendly. However the food is amazing. I'm staying in a near by hotel so I've gone a few times and have loved everything I've tried. The tacos are good, as was the Wildcat Burger. What I really enjoyed was the nachos and shrimp cocktail. The full order of nachos was HUGE!! I'm glad my friend and I shared them. There would have been no way I could have finished them alone. The shrimp cocktail was a little pricey but the shrimp are large so that helped take the "sting" off of the price. Whenever I have business by the university I am for sure going to make this my must hit place.

This place has unreasonably good food. I don't get it. You walk in, see a divey-bar looking kinda place and expect greasy fries and frozen pizza. What you get is anything BUT. Everything on the menu is great and demonstrates the care they take into making something even as predictable as chicken skewers taste really great. The happy hour is great and I recommend the nachos, hummus, chicken wings, and/or bruschetta. But really you cannot go wrong with anything on the menu. Give them a try and don't be turned off by the appearance. Looks can be deceiving!!!

Food is very good here. Not sure it's the best in Tampa, but that doesn't matter, it's worth visiting. Ideal for lunch, if you find yourself starving to the max, go for the Cuenelli Special consisting of a Palomilla Steak, Rotisserie Chicken, Fried Yuca, Plantains, your choice of white rice or cilantro with a side of beans a salad and of course a fried egg on top. Needless to say, this dish should surely satisfy. You may need a nap afterwards.

The sauces are a nice bonus, don't think you can go wrong with most of the items on the menu. Prices are reasonable. Check em out.

Reading Terminal Market is always a fun place to visit. I was looking forward to having something good to eat and I have found it. 
My first go round I had the jambalaya with chicken, shrimp, & andouille sausage and topped with shrimp and crawfish etouffee. I took a walk and came back for more. This time I had Jambalaya with chicken, shrimp, & andouille sausage and topped with shrimp and chicken gumbo. Pretty spicy, very good

I love Latin food and Peruvian food is no exception. I came in with a friend for lunch and only one other table was occupied which had me a bit concerned. The overall feel of place was fast-food-esque but it was far from anything I've ever had at a fast-food joint. We ordered the Tilapia Ceviche and Cuenelli's Special (Palomilla Steak, Rotisserie Chicken, Fried Yuca, Fried Plantains, Fried Egg, Rice & Black Beans with a Side Salad).

The Ceviche had a great balance of acidity, spicy heat, and freshness. I felt that it was slightly overloaded with red onions, but still very good. The Special certainly was special. Both the steak and the chicken were tender and exploding with flavor. The yuca and plantains were fried perfectly. The egg's yolk was runny deliciousness and the salad had a uniquely tasty greenish dressing. The only small criticism I have is that the rice was a little on the dry side. Otherwise, the service was great and it was an overall great experience with food that I'll definitely be back for.

this is some serious southern cajun NOLA style food.

the beignets are little fluffy sugary pillows of heavenly warm dough! come here for these yumms on wednesday and sunday, the only days they serve them.

hidden in the middle of the bustle of reading terminal, this is a great fast, different foodery.
Great customer service the girls were really nice! the downstairs is the cutest seating ever. I got the honeybee crepe and my bf got the honey ham sandwich and both were amazing

Went here tonight with a couple of friends as part of a going-away for one of them. One of the guys in our group had mentioned the owner was prior military and it was a cool place to go chill. I only ordered the oysters on a half shell before the kitchen closed so I can't speak to the rest of the menu but the drinks were good and service was great. The staff was very personable and on top of stuff. They didn't seem to even be bothered by the fact that we were literally there till closing, which is good because they could've been complete jerks if they wanted to! When I got home, I told my husband we had to go back because it seemed like a place he would enjoy.

I didn't know rotisserie chicken could taste so good!! 

I ordered the 1/4 chicken (dark meat) with rice and added a side of plantains.  The chicken and cilantro rice both have amazing flavor!  I mix them together and add the sauce they give you and it's perfect!  The restaurant is modern and well decorated and the staff is always friendly.

We stop her for deserts to bring home. My favorite is the pigs ears pastry. So delicious and big. It will last a couple days.
Yummy

my roommate and i went to ruth's chris last night to use up a livingsocial coupon. $50 for $100 worth of food+drinks. you'd think it'd be easy to hit $100 at a top-ranked steakhouse right? so not true! this was my first time at a ruth's chris (mostly cuz i've been deterred by what friends have told me over the years) and i found it surprisingly affordable.

between the two of us, we ordered an appetizer, two steaks, and a side to share. and we were just UNDER $100 AND we were stuffed to the gills.

the crabmeat stuffed mushrooms were just fine as an appetizer. four generous sized mushroom caps stuffed full of crab and topped with romano cheese. a bit too cheesy, but good. i've definitely had better though.

i ordered the ribeye, and for the first time, i ordered my steak rare-plus instead of medium rare. a HUGE slab of meat came out within 15 minutes, and i swear, literally a third of it was marbled fat. and it came out RED. like the color of yelp RED. i was ecstatic! what can i say, i'm a carnivore ;)

the ribeye came well-seasoned, but still allowed the natural flavor of the raw meat to shine through. the taste was a bit overwhelming though, and while i like chewy meat, i was kind of tired of the taste and texture by halfway through. guess i'm going back to medium rare.

the best part of our meal was the side: sweet potato casserole topped with pecans and brown sugar. SO SWEET but sooo delicious. we didn't even want dessert after that side.

everything came piping hot and visually appealing, but the entire meal left me with just an "ehh" ambivalent feeling. the service was attentive -- our waitress, jessica, was so nice, in fact, that it was like congeniality on crack.

while i enjoyed my meal, i prefer other steakhouses with a larger selection of cuts, better ambiance and better service. not to say i didn't like ruth's chris. i've just had much better.

Cuenelli's is the spot!!! The fries are always extra crispy lightly dusted with a sugar and salt combo. The rotisserie isn't like we're used to. It's cooked all the way through. The beans are to die for and let's not start with the cilantro rice!

great to have a korean spa in these parts. men's area is small, so be advised when the cruisey types are around to keep watch. 
also, know that the food services are down on Tuesdays. I've been told from friends in the area that their food is great, but I unfortunately did not get to try it.
i came here two separate times several weeks apart, and the same toilet was out of order, and the glass between the clay and salt rooms was still not replaced. not to mention i found a bandaid laying near the hot tub. nice people that work here make these upkeep fails semi-forgivable.

We went to the Reading Terminal Market to look around and found this bakery tucked away in here.  They had a great selection of bakery items.  We got a good variety of small cakes.  The one pictured is the tiramisu.  It was really good.  We got biscotti but it wasn't that good at all.   Too airy and disintegrated instantly in coffee.  I didn't think that was the case with a bakery of this scale.  Besides that this was a successful visit.  The staff at this location was really nice and friendly.  They wrap the box of cakes in string which was really neat.  

If you're in the area and see one of these bakeries which there are others in the area. This is not the original location.  Well worth a stop.

I come here on a Sunday for lunch. The line wasn't extremely long and the food was ready pretty quickly so we didn't have to wait a crazy amount of time. 

The food was good for the most part. I actually didn't like the Jambalaya personally but my boyfriend. The shrimp and crawfish Etouffee was delicious! The shrimp po boy and the oyster po boy are a must have for sure. I definitely want to go back and try some other things on the menu.
Best bakery in Reading Market cannolis we're better than any of the ones I had in Italy! Lemon poppy seed biscotti were ok probably would have been better if I had coffee to eat them with.
Best canolli ever.  And I don't even like canollis.  Just buy and eat it. And buy me one too!

Was in town for a conference.  Great place to watch an NFL game, any one!  The food was a step above bar food and the portions were big.  Service was great (Thanks Maxi).  Bar managers were very helpful and even had a free give away at halftime!

Helpful hint:  Get there at 10am on Sunday to get a seat and take advantage of the Sunday specials.
Ordered nachos. Never assume that beans will be in them lol. If you like cheese theta plenty of that lol. Tried the calamari chewy. Needless to say, I won't be back.
I used to love this place but on this visit I was not to pleased. Soups where bland and chimichanga was dry and over cooked. Definitely won't eat here again.

Just had lunch from there and was thoroughly impressed. The Trainwreck was a great swap instead of another cheese steak from Carmen's (not knocking Carmen's, just wanted something a bit different). The gumbo was ridiculously good - best roux I've had in a while! Bread pudding also super tasty. I would wait for this again in a heartbeat.
Best fricken burger place in town!! I always tell people about this place. They have great fish and chips and amazing burgers. You definitely get what you pay for!

I got the shrimp po boy & it was great, EXCEPT for the bread! It was way too hard! It just made eating the sandwich difficult. They need to use a different type of bread. The beignets also tasted more like Italian Zeppoles & not Beignets. Beignets are soft & moist. They ARE fried doughnuts. The ones here were def not Beignets. They were too dry & over cooked, but from flavor alone, I already knew they weren't beignets. I'd def go back if they got new bread for their po boys & learned how to properly make beignets.
Being half peruvian.I know what good food is suppose to taste like.this is it get the dam Lomo saltado or the pollo.please don't forget the green and yellow sauce.

"Holy cannoli" is about all I can use to describe the best cannoli I've had in years! I was traveling to Philadelphia on business and knew that the only logical thing to eat after a cheese steak would be a cannoli and my fellow Yelp-ers did not let me down with the reviews on Termini Bros. Highly recommend.

We love their food so when we heard they were doing Sunday Brunch we had to try it. It was delish! Large menu with something for everyone, I saw several things I will go back to try. Hubby had Dented Chicken and I had Jasons...something I cant remember the name, but it was excellent. Bloody Mary was just right spicy. Overall a very enjoyable morning.
Great food for a great price. I'd recommend checking them out if you're in the area. I got the French toast

I wanted to book a hands-on cooking class for my friend's birthday, I wasn't able to do the reservation online and it was harder by phone, since no one was answering, I even went to their location and it was always closed. Finally they responded to my email and I booked the only available date for the Double Happiness Class. On the day of, we waited outside until someone opened the door for us, then we waited again inside for the rest of the group to gather. Chef Joseph Poon showed up,he was very funny and enthusiastic. while they were setting up- they were NOT ready- Chef Poon realized that no one cooked the rice, so he had to asked his assistant to go and buy some!!!!!!! The class itself was energetic and fun, we learned how to make sushi and sum, then we had a nice dinner prepared by Chef Poon, However, it is not worth $120 per person and overrated.
Two Yelps!

I was charged and my food was NOT delivered. 

Cuenelli's did NOT take responsibility, and said it was not their fault. 

Order at your own risk.

The food is good, unfortunately one of the only places in town to get Peruvian rotisserie chicken also doesn't have beer or air conditioning. The last time we came about a year ago the AC wasn't working. No big deal, but we came again a year later and guess what? The AC isn't working... again. More like the owner doesn't want to pay the electric bill. A beer and wine license is not regulated like a liquor license, it's easily obtained and very affordable in Florida. Maybe if they added beer and wine, they could afford to pay the AC bill, or at least I could enjoy my meal with a nice cold beer - just sayin. The food is great though, especially for carry out. The fried yuca is great also, but it's like $4 for about 5 sticks, almost a dollar per stick of yuca, which is absurd - and the order doesn't even come with sauce so you have to buy it separate. The salad is huge but they drizzle very little dressing, then they charge you for extra dressing! Lol.
This place is so much better than Bert Smith in St Pete. Service department was informative and extremely helpful. Nice waiting area with good coffee, drinks, and snacks.

WHOO-HOO, finally found a proper cajun New Orleans restaurant that delivers that awesome cajun flavor.  No surprise finding it in a major city but in the smack middle of crazy busy Reading Terminal in Philly; too funny and way too crowded.  But for food and flavor like this, it is so worth it.

It took us a while to finally locate Becks among the crazies of Reading Terminal, but when we did the good times started.  From a sample tasting to actually getting two counter stools during Christmas week. 

After a quick Q&A about menus items and spice levels, we landed on what was to be an awesome late lunch consisting of Shrimp and crawfish etouffee- which was delightful and packed a nice flavor over white rice plus my wife ordered the Chicken & Andouille Gumbo with Dirty Rice which packed a fantastic flavor that hung on.  Nice kick.  The two dishes together complemented one another as we enjoyed sharing each overs dish along with an order of cornbread-- perfect for the soul.  Washed down with sweet tea.  There is a time and place and this was it.

Glad we didn't have to die to go to food cajun heaven.  

We will be back with an appetite.
You must try their chocolate cheese cake! It is total chocolate heaven!

Came here for lunch on Sunday. When we walked up they offered us a sample of the Gator Gumbo, my friend and I both liked it, so we each ordered a cup of it. I also ordered the Fried Shrimp Platter and he ordered the Blackened Chicken Platter. I chose red beans and rice as my side and he chose the Cajun Fries. We each ordered the root beer and we also got an order of beignets. All of this came up to about $40. The gumbo was ready right away but we had to wait for our platters. Neither one of us finished our food....it was sooo much food! The gumbo was good, but I didnt care for the fried shrimp and the red beans and rice were not that great either. I didnt taste his Blackened chicken, but he said it was okay. I tasted his cajun fries and they were more like potato wedges. They forgot to give us our beignets, so we had to go back to request them and luckily they remembered us. The Beignets were good as well, but we didnt finish them either. I would come back for the gator gumbo, but I would pass on the platters. Also, the line and ordering is a little disorganized, so that was a little frustrating in the crowded Reading Terminal Market.

Beck's really hit the spot yesterday. The Terminal Market was nuts, you could barely walk through, the lines were extra long, and it wasn't easy to find a quick spot to grab lunch. Somehow Beck's seemed to move customers right in and out unlike the other lunch options. They were very quick and efficient. 

I had the Alligator Sausage Po Boy for $8.95. It was grilled alligator sausage topped with caramelized onions, peppers, and creole mustard. Delicious!! I also took Jambalaya home for my boyfriend (his favorite) topped with Gator Gumbo for $10.45. He said it was one of the best he's ever had. Very pleased with my lunch from Beck's!

There are so many delicious food options at Reading Terminal, but it's worth snaking through back to Beck's!

The alligator po'boy is delicious and has a unique cajun mustard for the perfect amount of spice. Also got the fried bacon mac&cheese with chicken and shrimp gumbo on top. It's a great way to try all the best Beck's has to offer, but the gumbo does take away from the crunch of the fried mac&cheese. Especially if ordering take-out, consider asking for the gumbo wrapped separately. The bacon also made it a bit too rich for my taste, but that's what I get for ordering while starving!

The servers are super friendly and you should definitely take them up on samples of the gumbo!

I stopped in for a quick breakfast during my Saturday morning shopping at Reading Terminal. Ordered the smoky andouille Po Boy. The food was tasty and loved the fresh bread. Cool seating area in the middle of the terminal makes for a nice touch.

Double Knot is wonderful, so when I saw this spot I had to try. Sushi rolls are tiny and overpriced. Not freshly made. I ordered spicy tuna rolls and received dried out tuna with no spicy sauce. The spicy cucumbers leave much to be desired. Better off elsewhere!
I liked the place. I took my friend because he wanted to come for 3 years. he enjoyed his self. loved the meal and service was great wonderful

You would never know you're walking into such a delight! Good specious booths, ample room for four. Many televisions, which show different shows and games playing. Arrived just after 11am and by 11:30 all tables were taken. Very cool mugs and many of them, hanging around the bar area.  Great music plays, not too loud though and with it, great atmosphere.  Now for the best part, ordered the Philly Cheesesteak with fries. I was blown away from first bite. The steak and veggies were done to perfection and the amount of cheese added into the equation made for the right amount, not over powerful. The overall texture was very scrumptious. The service was 10+ I had half of the sandwich left and before I could even ask for a to-go container the waitress came to the table with one. I will be back!!!!

I decided to do lunch at reading terminal with my sister and we decided to stop here after tasting the chicken Alfredo

it was good over all having been in new Orleans a few times a bit different from what I expected but it was good

good enough that I would go back to try another dish

Philly is not actually where I would expect to find a spot touting the best Cajun around, so it was definitely worth a try.  I ordered the shrimp po boy and Cajun fries.  The sandwich had plenty of succulent fried shrimp that were nicely seasoned. The fries?  Absolutely no idea how they came up with their Cajun concept for these, but drowning potato chunks with an onion/pepper gravy (?) is not delicious. At all.

i can only review their cannoli's and mini cakes. 

their cannoli's are not only affordable and HUGE, but they are rated the best in the city.  Rightfully so. Their mini cakes ($5 each) are made fresh as well.  I have tried their tiramisu one and it was not too sweet and/or soggy as tiramisu tends to be.  

 Located in the Reading Terminal Market. i love this place!
Love the food and drink. One of my favorite restaurants to go  been going there for years with my wife

K was my first time at Cunellisa Peruvian chicken. They feel much more than chicken they also serve turkey, meat, and various other accompaniments.
Its a plain restaurant with just the basics. The wait staff was friendly. The menu is somewhat limited and its choices were meager.

I had just the chicken quarter of white meat. The chicken was very moist and juicy and super flavorful to include a lot of garlic. Did I say they use an abundance of garlic?The thing that disappointed me was the wing attached to the chicken breast was, just there with NO meat on it and basically was just a garnish. I know it's not an expensive restaurant by any means & it was only $4.99. I think I could have gotten more food than just the  plain garlic chicken breast for that price at just about any small restaurant.
Oh I know I might get a chicken to go and take it home. But I don't believe I would come back for lunch or dinner due to this initial experience. 
What's a girl to do? You have to kiss a lot of frogs to find a prince.

Would you be surprised to hear that a sports bar in Tucson is known for their delicious salads and seafood? As the wise Julie Chen always says, "expect the unexpected" (yeah that's a reality TV show reference and I apologize). Trident Grill's owner hails from Maryland and brought some very decent seafood with him, a rarity in the desert. However, if you are a normal person and didn't come to a sports bar for food with low cholesterol, have no fear! The burgers and other typical sports bar snacks were all great. Our waitress was very friendly and helpful, and made some food suggestions for us that were once again, impressive. My personal suggestion is the fried pickles. Yes, it's a simple snack but we all know simplicity is the ultimate sophistication (use that line next time you want to justify ordering fried food). 

A small footnote that might interest some: trivia is held here every Wednesday at 8 PM. So taking a trip to Trident Grill can be a positive experience for the body, and the mind.

I was in Philadelphia for a weekend with friends and after we toured the Eastern State Penitentiary I left it up to them to find a nearby lunch spot. I was pleasantly surprised at the variety of menu choices and quality of food - had the salmon/avocado/goat cheese crepe and an iced latte, and probably would have eaten there every day if we stayed in the area (the cafe is sort of hidden).

Note: they have a nicely decorated lower level that offers more dining space.

I have never been disappointed here.  How CAN you be?  You want seafood?  They have creamy clam chowder, sautéed or fried calamari, crab cakes.  All delicious and fresh.  You want interesting apps?  Try the fried pickles or the Irish egg rolls.  Burgers?? Huge burgers cooked they way YOU want them.  Oh, don't forget the Super Reuben.  We drive from Sahuarita for this place.  The fish tacos themselves are worth the trip.

I've been to Trina B at Bella Locs twice, she's awesome! The first time I went I received the Basic Mermaid Locs (they are individual faux locs on the perimeter and crotchet in the center) I loved them they were perfect for me because I like feminine locs. I loved them so much that the next time I booked her Ultra Mermaid Locs service (all individual wrapped locs) I decided to spent the extra coins because I wanted more versatility in the style being as though I workout and prefer high buns over wearing my hair down. Not only is it pain free BUT her hands and her Hair Greed Serum products have grown my hair exponentially. I am grateful to have found Trina and I would highly recommend her.
Phenomenal crepes, great coffee and an even greater ambiance to work or hangout in. The staff has always been nothing but friendly and accommodating. Glad they are a staple in this neighborhood!

I love this neighborhood cafe! The coffee is great and their crepes are delicious and hearty! I normally get the one with egg ham and cheese, and I've tried one with bacon that was tasty as well. I especially love the downstairs area; it is a great place to relax and read a book when there are not many customers. The staff is always friendly and the decor is beautiful, but I wish there were more vents because it can get smokey in there sometimes.

I am a big fan of this place. Peruvian chicken is delicious! Typically we will dine out but have dined in before. The restaurant itself is very clean and and has a pretty chill vibe. The servers (all female) are not always the friendliest but whatever I'm here for the chicken (typically why we will do carry out). Their prices are very fair considering the amount of food you get. Believe me when I say you will not regret trying the chicken here, it is simply delicious!

We will typically order the family package to go. This includes a whole chicken, cilantro rice, a salad (with some sort of garlicky yummy dressing), and an extra side. We will typically get the Yucca fries as the extra side. Once in a while I will also order a side of sweet plantains. I know Tampa is big on Cuban food, this is much more flavorful than that, I am telling you go try it now!

*Disclaimer: I cannot vouch for anything else on the menu since we always get the chicken.

This place has great coffee and great crepes! they are always a special mid-day treat. It is just a walk-up window, so do not plan on sitting down. Additionally, you can call and order ahead for pick-up.

Visited Reading Terminal with my eye on Termini's. It did not disappoint. The cannoli is my favorite. Ricotta was creamy and not too sweet. Crispy cone and the entire cannoli was flavorful. I also tried  the raspberry chocolate covered banana. This was good, but not my favorite. The anise biscotti was delicious. Nothing like the "bricks" we get in California. Staff was great and patient.  Everything looks tempting. Packaged my products very well for the trip back to the hotel. Recommend everyone to visit Termini's.

We headed to Trident on a beautiful Saturday evening, May 5th. Everybody we mentioned this place to said: "You gotta go! The food's great, the atmosphere is friendly and the staff is awesome. All of the above praise was absolutely true. The floor plan is open and welcoming. Over the bar area, rows of tankards are customized with patron's names to use when they come for their favorite tipple. We added our names to the waiting list for a tankard for both my husband and me. I started with a Jack & Coke which was mixed perfectly. After perusing the menu for a bit (there's a LOT to choose from) my hubby and I decided to start with the Nelson's Love Plate. I'm told that it's named for the owner, Nelson Miller, a retired Navy Seal.  The description was intriguing: "Cheese, fruits, nuts, olives, this and that." It was very tasty with the assorted flavors of all the little bites on the plate, and there's plenty to share. We also got an order of fried pickles to see how this establishment did theirs and we LOVED them! Those pickles were done beautifully. Somebody knows precisely what they're doing on the fryer. Mike ordered the Fish & Chips, and pronounced it "Excellent." The batter was almost Tempura-like in texture, and the fries were crunchy on the outside, moist on the inside. I ordered the Maryland Blue Crab Cake Sandwich. It was pan-fried, drizzled with aioli, served on a Kaiser roll. Man, was IT tasty. I love crab, and this was done right. On the side, I ordered the mac & cheese instead of fries for a change. The rich, creamy cheese and shells were flavorful and gooey...a decadent little side, I must say!  We decided to skip dessert, just this once, as we were stuffed, to say the least. Plus, we had a clamshell of fried pickles to take home. 
    Trident is a great place to watch a variety of sports, as they have 9 HD Flat Screen TV's and one giant screen and it's close-by the University of Arizona's basketball and football stadiums. Our wonderful server, Skye, tells us there are 24 draft beers available as well as nightly specials. Ahh...our server Skye. What a nice person and excellent staff member! This bubbly lady truly enjoys what she does, and it shows. Something else we noticed about Trident...teamwork. Skye was busy taking another patron's order, as the dinner rush was progressing. Our order appeared in the window, ready to come to our table. The two other wait staff members each grabbed the waiting plates and brought them immediately to our table, served with a smile! Skye told us that teamwork is of utmost importance here.
   We felt very comfortable at Trident, and want to come back as soon as we can...and often! This is the kind of neighborhood place that we've been looking for and now, we've found it. It's only about 15 minutes from our house, and well worth the short trip. The interior walls are decorated with items that, over time, the patrons have gifted to the, establishment, "just because." What a great place this is! Our friends and associates were right! They also tell us that it can be packed on certain evenings.  Clearly, Trident knows how to take care of their customers and now, they have two new ones.

Trident is a solid choice. The first time I came here, I was expecting something other than just a bar. Something a bit more elevated. With items like scallops and filet on their menu, I'm not sure you could blame me. I had known that a few friends had come here to watch MMA fights before, but I'm not sure what I was thinking. When we walked in, I saw that it is, in fact, just a bar. 

We were still a bit jaded, however, and started our order with scallops topped with blue cheese. I liked these better than my wife did, but we both felt they were completely not worth the price. Roughly 5 scallops each about the size of a quarter, for about $16. I would agree on that price provided the scallops were of a normal size. 

After that, my original thought of filet for a main course slid back slightly into reality and I decided that maybe a gourmet burger would be a better choice. With the waitress's endorsement, my decision was sealed and I got the brawt. This is a pork-patty burger with sauerkraut and maple dijon mustard. The burger as a whole was disappointingly dry, although that maple mustard was fantastic. We both left feeling as though we had ordered the wrong thing, and figured we'd be back again with a more late-night bar feel in mind.

Its a good thing we did, because that's exactly what this place is really good at. In fact, I have found what is so far my favorite burger in Tucson (which was tough to say since Red Garter has a close second), but the Voodoo Daddy is just one incredible burger and right up my alley. Andouille sausage on a standard burger with american cheese, cajun mustard, and slaw comes together in a wonderfully messy bite of deliciousness. I've had it twice and tried the mac and cheese for a side last time. I've had better mac, but you can never go wrong with fries instead. 

My wife likes the veggie burgers here because they're fresh, not stale like you may get at other places, and they are cooked right. We both like that you can order beer by the pint, mug (BIG mug) or pitcher. Last time we both had snake bite mugs-- a good choice. 

The fact that this place has a kitchen open until midnight, makes this an easy decision for people like me who don't get off work until 10pm. I also look forward to their seasonal crabcakes, which I have heard are really awesome. Can't wait!
Best falafel and hummus I've had in Philly. I'm Israeli and I've eaten there with other Israelis. The food is just as good here as it is back in Israel.

We wanted some latin food and our normal favorite was packed with a 20 minute wait so we decided to try something new.  Yelp reviews for this place were pretty good so we decided to give it a shot.  It looks like a strip mall from the outside but the interior was unique and well done.  The service was a little lacking because the waitress had to deal with a large takeout order but not too bad especially once we received our appetizer, papa's a la huancaina.  All I can say is wow.  I've had this dish many places but they did it to perfection.  I tried a little bit of everything from the steak to the chicken, it was amazing.  The cilantro rice was super tasty, the chicken requires no knife and is wonderfully flavorful.  We even had dessert and the tres leches and churros were a home run.  All this for a really good price. This place is now added to my list of favorite latin restaurants.

Great chicken, great customer service, the cilantro rice is my favorite. I mean, this is my go to place when I'm too lazy to cook and I want to eat something semi-healthy. You can't go wrong here. They have different food options in the menu and even though I mainly order the grilled chicken, everything else is also pretty tasty. Try one of the their desserts, the tres leches is to die for.

I too was part of Foodie M's group of diners who got Pooned.  In a city that has so many great choices of affordable ethnic food, it's rare that I'll shell out $50 for dinner, let alone Chinese food, but the menu sounded fantastic.  I have never experienced such a disconnect between a printed menu and my actual taste buds as this.

Since Foodie M did a pretty thorough job of describing the dismal decor, and the range of off beat (not in a good way) to just plain inedible dishes I'll try to keep my review brief (brief isn't my specialty though...).  As we sat down at the table I noticed a kind of funk wafting up my nose which I soon realized was a take out box of a previous diner's leftovers (From that day? From last week?  I'm not sure) they had wisely chosen not to take home with them, and had shoved in the shelf under the table.  (The tables aren't actual dining tables, but are kitchen prep tables).  This should have been the first sign.  Actually it was the first sign.  The meal progressed from dishes that were OK to dishes that were horrible. 

A few examples-
Second Course
Peking Duck with Jicama and Spring Onion with Steamed Lotus Leaf Bun

Translation - A bite of duck in a bun that is chewy in the center, and so hard on the side you can hardly bite through it.

Sixth Course
Double Happiness Lobster with Lemon Pepper Linguini in Homemade Chili Tomato Mirin Essence

Translation - Lobster claws that are impossible to get out of the shell so forget about actually eating any, on a bed of linguini with BBQ sauce.

Tenth Course
Dessert: Ice Cream Cheesecake and Fresh Fruit Sculpture with Green Tea

Translation - A 1" square of frozen cheesecake with a grape on a toothpick

OK, so I guess a grape on a toothpick may qualify as a sculpture to some, but in my imagination it would be something slightly more.

So I realized that Joseph Poon the brand is really much more about the wacky persona than the food. Oh well.  I just wish I knew that before I blew so much money.

Beck's is a favorite of mine, it offers a taste of Cajun cooking with some Philly flair added to the mix. The gumbo is delicious, the jambalaya is tasty, but this time I ordered the fried catfish platter. It's served with your choice of side and corn bread which appeared to be heated up on a griddle or pan. The catfish itself is very crispy yet and not overcooked, the remoulade compliments is very well. I'm typically not a fan of corn bread, but theirs is very well done and hard to resist. I used order the jambalaya with gumbo on top and found out they now offer it, so you're welcome for that idea :) Overall Beck's is an excellent place for those seeking the savory and spicy food of Louisiana, but not looking to fly down.

OK, repeat after me.....

Kelleigh was right
Kelleigh was right
Kelleigh was right
Kelleigh was right
Kelleigh was right.....

Whew, I think that should serve as enough penance for one review!

I admit it, I have driven past Cuenelli's Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken on Hillsborough Avenue for months thinking that it was just another fast-food chicken joint.....and yes, I was wr-wr-wr-wrong.

Cuenelli's sits in a dinky little strip mall at the intersection of Hillsborough and Andersen Road. From the outside there's not much to see, but inside the place is spotlessly clean and decorated with a lot of Peruvian culture and pride. The waiter was super friendly, and gave me a lot of suggestions.

The menu is small, but packed with a lot of flavorful choices. In addition to the charcoal rotisserie chicken, they also have several appetizers, steak options, seafood, sandwiches, and vegetarian specials. 

My server recommended an outstanding House Special called Lomo Saltado which was tender grilled sirloin, sliced on the diagonal and served with grilled onions and tomatoes, and on top of French fries. Amazing flavors, and it came with cilantro rice and a bowl of black beans. He suggested that I try their two homemade sauces so that I'd know about them for next time. The first was made with cilantro, and it was perfect on the rice & beans. The spicy yellow sauce is designed to go with the grilled chicken, but it also tasted great with the sirloin. 

I'm anxious to go back and try the rotisserie chicken on my next visit.

Thanks Kelleigh for the suggestion!

I stopped here as my second restaurant of the night inside the market (I have a big stomach, okay?), and was not left disappointed. The shrimp and crawfish etouffee was dreamy and creamy and it was hard to eat it by myself as all of my friends wanted in on the action. We reigned it as our favorite meal of the rainy night. I'll be back whenever I'm in Philly again.

Love love love their tortilla soup and their chips and 3 salas are addicting! The staff is very friendly. We usually order the "parilla mixta" which is a small table grill with Carne asada, chorizo, queso fondido, and it comes with charro beans and tortillas. I've had both dine in and take out. Usually one worries that the take out will not be as good once you get home, but the taste stays the same.  They even separate all the soup mix ins from the broth, so the tortillas don't get soggy and you can easily put it all together when you get home :)

In saw some people were complaining about the loud mariachi music, but that's only on Fridays.

I went in on my lunch break used the restroom went to the order counter and right away the lady behind the counter had the rudest attitude with me and when I tried to see what they had she didn't want to answer any questions I had. I finally got sick of her attitude and was going to leave when she flipped out and said " I knew you weren't going to buy anything you're wasting my time get out. The whole place smelled like sewer anyway I probably just save myself from a night of painful diarrhea!
Love this bar and always come here for the great atmosphere, food and drinks.  Cheyenne is the best even when currently handicapped with a sprained ankle.  :)
Such great service. Brit, our waitress was just awesome. The burgers were tasty and the sweet potato fries were the best.

I really love the food here but we went there during happy hour, clearly marked. We had a couple beers, some burgers, nothing too extravagant and the waitress told us because there was a game on TV it wasn't happy hour AFTER ALL. Would have been nice if they told us that when we were ordering apps. Long story short, our bill was $95 bucks!! We felt totally ripped off and we won't be going back. If you go there be careful!
My favorite besides the ricotta cannoli is the chocolate covered banana. Really refreshing and delicious. Definitely get this. The amaretti cookies are delicious with almond paste.

I was in town for the weekend and had been advised to visit the terminal. Beck's Cajun Cafe was the first thing that caught my eye when I went into the building. I had the catfish, Red beans and rice, and cornbread and it was really good ! The fish had an amazing flavor and was cooked perfectly. The red beans and rice were good but extremely spicy(to me ) and also contained meat so beware if you don't eat meat. The cornbread wasn't spectacular but it
Was pretty straight. The coolest part was being able to watch one of the employees preparing the Mac n cheese balls !
Best etouffe and gumbo I have ever had I would highly recommend  this place.It has really good sweet tea and food please try it you wont regret it

My first experience at Trident on Ina was not great. (LUNCH)Ordered the Kalua pork tacos and when they arrived at the table they were barely warm. Would have liked them to be hot. And the first bite was a big gob of fatty grissle. Yuck. Chef might want to check pork a bit better. Hate to think i might have to "disect" my tacos.  Might try again but not the kalua pork tacos. Waitress asked if i want to replace them. My eating guest was satisfied with her food.

We  the Trident! Consistently good food and great service. Drinks are strong and decent variety. One of the things I like best about the Trident is the diversity of the menu. So many different things to try!

While perusing Reading Terminal Market on a surprisingly quiet Sunday afternoon, I was lured by Beck's Cajun Cafe with their massive menu and delicious-looking tomato Creole sauce (spoiler alert: it was as good as it looked).

I wanted literally all of the options, but my greedy stomach settled for a blackened catfish platter with grilled cornbread and red beans and rice. Plus, I just had to get some tomato Creole sauce on the side. The catfish was perfectly cooked and very flavorful, and the dish as a whole was delightful.

A very comforting and affordable meal for $12, and I look forward to returning for more.

On a recent visit to Reading Terminal I stopped here to get a drink. The cakes look amazing but I was appalled when our server laughed in my wife's face when she asked if they had milk for her tea. So incredibly rude.
Worth it! The poboy sandwiches are delicious! All I'd want is a little more Cajun sauce, but still really great!

It's a deceptively small when you first walk in but there's more seating downstairs. Very chill and friendly environment. Super cute and aesthetic. Coffee is very authentic and staff is so helpful and attentive.

Good crepes. GOOD coffee. Great atmosphere. The kind of place I'd spend an afternoon sipping coffee and getting some work done. 10:30am on a Sunday I was worried about getting a seat but it wasn't a problem at all. For sure my new spot. I can only say I wish they had MORE crepe options so I can try them all.

Not a good example of Mexican food. The waiter was nice, but had a hard time understanding that what I ordered was actually what I wanted. That being said, the Hornitos margarita was awesome! 
The rest of the meal was not. The  alambre tacos were dry and the bacon non-existent. Save your money. The chilaquillas were a massive heap of melted chips, indiscriminate cheese, and I'm sure some kind of meat product, it may have been shredded beef. Anyway, my suggestion would be, save your money and go to an actual Mexican restaurant that will serve authentic Mexican food in such a way that you appreciate Mexican food. I would say this is like literally one step above Taco Bell.

To review La Parilla Suiza fairly, you have to understand that this is Mexico City style Mexican food, not the traditional Sonoran style that you'll typically find in the Tucson area. 
As former Tucson residents who recently visited the Old Pueblo on our vacation, we knew this would be a solid choice for lunch, so we stopped in.
We were well-treated by the staff and the place looked clean to us, so I disagree with some of the negative reviews I've read.
The food was good and the service was timely -- so again.....I disagree with the naysayers.
This is worth a try.
The food may or may not be to your taste, given that it's a different style. But you won't know until you go there.
I recommend asking your server for suggestions/explanations before ordering.

Blackened Catfish Po Boy was perfection at Beck's Cajun Cafe. First let me start off at the bones of this sandwich, the baguette. It was toasted to perfection. Just the right amount of crunch and texture. Then the sauce...oh that sauce! Its not overly specific in flavor but it is so creamy and just right to buffer the spicy cajun flavors. It drips everywhere, so tons of napkins and even a bib if you are a messy eater like me. Then lettuce and tomato, gives a fresh flavor. But the main star?, 2nd to that, the sauce of course,the blackened catfish. Now let me tell you, if you think you've enjoyed flaky buttery fish before, you really haven't until you try this! This fish just melts in your mouth and the cajun spices add just the right amount of heat!
Get the Trainwreck sandwich and slip into a cheesesteak, salami, sausage coma. So delicious, meats are all seasoned well and delicious. Roll is soft and the perfect vehicle for this meat bomb.

Love this place.  I usually get the jambalaya bowl,very good, and then get a bowl of gator gumbo to take home.  We need one on Long Island.  There is no good place for good Cajun/Creole here. They will let you sample a lot of their food, so sample before you buy, but be careful, you may want to order one of everything!

I've had two more pizzas from here since my last post and I have to update because eat pizza has been better than the last!  Last week I got the chicken club pizza with chicken, bacon, tomato and I substituted onion for the mushrooms.  After baking, I put a little ranch on each slice and I was seriously in heaven!  Let's just say when my fiance got home from work there were only two slices left.

Tonight I picked up their Greek pizza with spinach, olives, tomato, onion, white sauce and I also added chicken.  This too was just amazing. 

I haven't had the standard take-out pizza since trying Mom's Bake At Home.  It's a really nice alternative.  I'm super anxious to try the rest of their interesting specialty options!

Probably the worst sushi I've ever had, and that's saying something because I'm originally from Idaho. I ordered a spicy tuna roll - how can you mess something so simple up? The rice was HOT, which was disgusting and careless of the chefs and not how I expect my sushi to be. I don't want to eat warm raw fish. The rolls were so carelessly put together, only 1/3 of them were dressed with the proper spicy mayo topping. Double knot, DKs parent store downtown, is such an amazing restaurant that always serves food of the utmost quality - it was very disappointing to see this from their subsidiary.

My fiance and I dined there for dinner during restaurant week. Here are the low lights:
     - Our waitress disappeared a lot,
     - My steak, ordered medium, came out raw (it was purple, not even close),
     - When my steak came back it was extremely seared (burnt on outside, still raw),
     - My wine glass was dirty: food bits and particles on the outside
     - The lobster bisque was really, really bland
     - Crème brûlée wasn't caramelized on top

The mashed potatoes we had were really, really good. The suggested wine paring with my fiance's filet mignon was perfect. We dined on a Monday so it was quiet and more intimate.

I went with 2 stars because it wasn't awful, I was just really disappointed. If I had paid full price instead of the restaurant week prices I would be more upset. If you really want to do Ruth's Chris, hop on the train or AC Expressway and eat at the one in Atlantic City. Check out my review of that location if you want.

Good value restaurant!

We had dinner there for business. This is not an upscale restaurant by any means, but the food is still pretty good. I had the chicken, which was delicious. I also had the ceviche which I really enjoy it a lot. My friend had steak and rice and beans and french fries.

If you want Peruvian food that's not really expensive and still decent, this is the place.

I went on a really crazy busy weekend when I was in town for a convention, so I'm gonna give them the benefit of the doubt. The jambalaya was amazing, can't say enough good things. The po boy was hard and dry. I think I caught them on a rough weekend though.

We recently visited and had such a wonderful experience at @BecksCajunCafe in the Reading Terminal! We were very appreciative of the caring and super friendly service! In addition, the food was truly Amazing! The Trainwreck  Cheese Steak was outstanding! From the roll to the Steak, Andouille, Salami, Cheese & Onions! I also had the Cajun Fries with Alligator Gumbo which was excellent and extremely tasty! 
My wife really enjoyed the Fried Oyster Po-Boy and Fried Mac! 
Kimber was our server, she was so friendly and personable plus she provided prompted and courteous service!
We actually had the honor of meeting  Chef Bill Beck! What a great person he is! 
We are looking forward to our next visit to "Beck's Cajun Cafe" and bringing our Friends! I highly recommend Beck's Cajun Cafe!!!

Trident Grill is the best place to go for a burger in the University area. 

There are many different burgers on the menu to chose from, and they have no problem accommodating to your preferences pertaining to adding or subtracting items on their sandwiches. The service is friendly and the atmosphere is good for watching games at, as they have many TV's around the place.

For weekends, particularly Friday nights, this place turns into a pretty fun college bar. They run karaoke all night long, which is pretty entertaining. Check it out.

Really glad I found this place.  They have the seafood dishes I've been looking for (i.e. mussels, clams, oysters)...for a reasonable price.  When we went it was not too busy so service went fast.  I just got the mussels which came in a curry broth.  I switched the sweet potato fries for the garlic bread and it was really good.  It was a pound of mussels in a great tasting broth with a very large piece of garlic bread.  I almost got oysters too but I was too full.  My partner got the philly cheesesteak, which he really liked.  We'll definitely be going back.  The location is close to our home so it's convenient.

I went during restaurant week... what a disappointment. The place is located on a second floor. All the chairs had the chef's face plastered on the cheap chair covers. The food was over cooked, over fried, and left me irritated that  I wasted $50. The chef is very full of himself and rambles on and on about how he is the top chef in the city, and country. Seriously.. if you are that great, you would not have moved to a space that is located on a second floor of a seedy alley, nor would the restaurant be empty during restaurant week, The kicker is that you have to walk through the kitchen to use the restrooms, which do not have a sink inside. You have to use the SAME sink as the cooks, which I thought was very unsanitary. I saw one of the cooks walk out of the restroom, and bypass using the sink to wash his hands. UGH! There are a hundred other places that I can think of to go to in this city for good chinese.  Would never return.  Please don't waste your money or your time.
This place is fantastic!!  Staff is always friendly, food is absolutely bomb. Will definitely be back often
Dessert crepe was great! The salty crepe had no sauce and was a pretty bland but the ingredients were very fresh

Ahhhh Trident. If there is a better place for happy hour in Tucson I don't want to know about it. It has to be one of the friendliest bars to sit at in Tucson. I cant recall the number of times I have grabbed a bar stool and immediately been included in the conversation by complete strangers and their awesome bar tenders. In fact when the bar is full it can often be engaged in one giant conversation the entire length of it.

The food is good bar food. I like the burgers and their wings the best but I am resolved to try the fish and chips soon as I hear great things. I have NEVER had an error in my food service while dinning there. Lots of good beers at good prices on tap. Variety of beers as well, not just IPA and lagers. 

Sometimes the table service can be lacking but not often.

It looks like there is a lot of good reviews for this site. But I did NOT have a good or decent experience there. My coworkers and I made a reservation to eat there during our lunch hour. We specifically asked for a table and when we got there it's a booth. Ok, that's fine now the waitress took our drink orders and brought them to us and took our menu order and that was the Last time we saw her. This Trident site is not a large building and not that many tables. There were at least 6 waitresses working, yet somehow it was impossible for our waitress to come check on us. To see if maybe we needed more drinks or to let us know the food was running a little late, but nothing. Mind you like most places we only get a hour lunch. It's 45 after now still no food no waitress. We asked another waitress if she could please get our waitress for us. The manager came to our table and said he would have our food right out. We no longer have time to eat it so we asked to take it with us and asked for the check, which again we specified we were all on separate checks. He comes back with the food and says no worries one of the meals will be deducted. Well who's meal, since we're all on separate checks. He had no idea we weren't on the same check. It's 50 after now still no check, so we left and left the food there. That was the worst experience I had. Maybe the food is good there but the service from that one waitress was Horrible!!! She made the restaurant look bad with her bad service. Maybe the restaurant is usually a good place to go but this day with that waitress it was ridiculous.

We make a monthly trip to visit to Philly because Reading Terminal is  STAPLE... and MUST GO... and MUST GO AGAIN... AND AGAIN. I absolutely love Reading Terminal and every time I visit, there are just a few items you cannot leave without. For one, I recommend Beck's Cajun and please get a few items from here before you leave. 

We always order the Jambalaya as it is packed with flavor. The rice is fluffy and just perfectly seasoned, with sausages, vegetables, and spices. It also packs a good kick, but just the right amount. I always order the jambalaya with the Chicken Gumbo. This combination is 100% heavenly and def. a must get. The Gumbo is spicy, but it gives off a good heat and is also packed with a lot of ingredients, which goes really good over rice. 

Please come here !!
First time being here, My wife and me like the pastry so much. The price is reasonable, quality is good. We definitely will visit again.

Yesterday was my first time at DK Sushi. Mindy and crew were awesome and the food was delicious! I ordered the Eat Your Fish box, the sushi was extremely fresh and tasty, the Edamame was piping hot, and the best part, everything needed (e.g. chopsticks, soy sauce, napkins), was all included in the box, making it easy to get it to go and eat anywhere. I'll definitely be back soon!!!
It is so hard to find shoes in my size without having to order online. They had a good selection and good prices. Staff was friendly and helpful.

I had a great evening relaxing Sunday night watching the Cowboys and Saints go at it.  The staff was excellent, Shana, I think was her name.

The fish and chips were delicious, washed down by a few craft beers. Glad they were open!
Best freaking chicken I ever tasted!!!!! Putting pollo tropical to shame... Strongly suggest checking this place out to those who haven't tried it yet

The food was amazing.  I ordered the chicken and the meat was falling off the bones but still intact.  It was cooked perfectly.  Their cilantro rice is also amazing.  The sauces are really unique and tasty.

It is great place to pick up a quick dinner for friends or family.  It is very affordable as well.  

The decor was nothing to rave about but nothing to complain about either.  It was very clean.

Service was very attentive and warm.  

I will back.  Only complaint is location is in the middle of nowhere.

I tried them for lunch, very normal food but I until that point it was ok... guess what I got a stone on the beans almost break my teeth and the cooker told me go F myself when I told them about it, honestly it doesn't worth is filthy and bad service there is way better places in the area for Peruvian and/or Latin food

Amazing brunch place at Reading Terminal Market. We tried the alligator sausage, fried catfish and fried shrimp po'boys. The alligator sausage was mildly spicy, juicy and almost pork-ish. It came with fried eggs, cheese, onions and peppers. A very unique way to try alligator!

The fried catfish and shrimp po'boys were excellent too. The sandwiches are filled generously with lettuce, tomato and pickles. The creole mayo pulled everything together - we ordered an extra side of mayo as dip for the bacon mac n cheese balls.
