With all the fried food, we couldn't finish the bread, which was of terrific quality. Crusty on the outside, soft and chewy on the inside.

Highly recommend this restaurant with the counter seating!!

Best. Cannoli. Ever.
'Nuff said....

But I'll say more: Very crunchy crust, and delicious inside. $4/each, so be prepared.
This will be my new breakfast spot! Just moved down the street and went to breakfast here! It is such a chill atmosphere and the crepes are delicious! Especially the caramel ricotta one!!! Delish!

We love Ruths Chris on Broad St! Delicious melt in your mouth steaks perfectly butterflied and served sizzling on the plate, large 4-5lb size lobsters cooked to perfection dipped in melted butter, and great sides too. Excellent service and food!!

This was not only a great dining experience, but a learning experience also.  The Peruvian cuisine is derived from a multi culture influence from all over the world, using local ingredients (from Peru) while creating a unique taste. The result is a delicious blend of spices flavoring different excellently prepared meats, vegetables, and rice.  

My favorites of the evening were the Pollo, tostones, and the cilantro rice; Mmmm, good!  Everything else was delicious also, but those three dishes stand out in my mind. 

This restaurant is nice inside and out, and conveniently located with plenty of parking. The food came out really fast, and like I mentioned before, all great!  We were served two sauces, and both were outstanding.  The thing that pushed this place over the 4 star mark was the stellar service.  Okay, the food would still get this place a 5 star rating, but great service is the "cherry on top".

The only complaint I can think of is, I wish the menu was bigger.  Not bigger physically, or bigger lettering...  bigger as in more delicious foods to try.

The food is delicious. However, when I go to restaurants, the most important thing to me is the atmosphere. At Beck's, the atmosphere is both tense,  chaotic, and unenjoyable. The only reason for this is the negative energy by which the owner creates by his incessant criticism and mistreatment of his staff. I have been to this restaurant several times and every time the male owner Bill is there, I see him yelling at his workers, and them looking quite frankly like they'd rather be anywhere else but there. I would say, if you're looking for some food, something like fast food- get in get out and get away from the negative energy that the boss creates- this is the place for you. However, if you're looking to enjoy yourself, have some conversation at this dining establishment, the atmosphere created by management is far too tense for something like that.

This place used to be AWESOME. My girlfriend and I ordered usually at least once a week, but over the past few months, they changed owners and both the food quality and customer service has gone drastically downhill. The old owner was a super friendly guy, knew his customers by name, and always made amazing food. I've tried to give them several chances over the past few months but they've continually disappointed. Today, I ordered on GrubHub; they called and told me they ran out of all of their breakfast foods, and asked if I wanted a different sandwich instead. I got a cheesesteak, but wasn't told I was going to get a several dollar upcharge for doing so. When I went to pick up the food, I was told that a driver had mistakenly left with it, but that they would remake it and call when it was ready. Since I only live about a block from the store, this wasn't the end of the world. Unfortunately, I didn't get a call for half an hour. Eventually I called them, and they told me that the food was ready. When I picked it up, it was cold. They were clearly understaffed and very busy today, so had I not already had several bad experiences I wouldn't have thought too much of it. At this point, though, I'm done with ordering from them. If Moe ever takes it back over I'll go back in a heartbeat though!

Just leaving and I will never return!!! I ordered the chilaquiles. Not only was the presentation sloppy but it tasted like plain tomato sauce on cold chicken and soggy chips. Needless to say the picture I posted was taken at the end of our meal. At the very least they did remove the item from my check without having to ask. That is the only reason for the second star.

Orist and Zoriana are sweet and hospitable owners. Their friendliness puts this place over-the-top for me. I was happy with the coffee and the service otherwise, and impressed with the hard work they've done to make their cafe beautifully lit and warm. Recommended. My favorite coffee shop in Francisville.

Took advantage of the emptiness during the Pope-apalooza to try something new at Reading Terminal. Thankfully there was no wait on Sunday!

I had the Étouffée of the Day. That day it was a mixture of shrimp, crawfish, corn, and okra. There was definitely not enough étouffée to the amount of rice. The flavoring was decent, but I was a bit turned off by the sliminess in the texture. To be fair, I should have known what I was getting myself into with the okra. Also, the shrimp was not fresh. Had a bite of my friend's trainwreck po boy - that was the better choice.

I would be curious  to come back and try the gator.

I came by on my most recent visit to RTM last weekend.  I'd heard the cannoli was a must-try here, so I picked one up.  Specifically, I ordered one with ricotta filling with chocolate chips, since several other reviewers said this was the one to get.

I ate the cannoli while standing in line for Beiler's to get a dozen donuts for my family.  From the first bite, the cannoli made the wait not only tolerable, but worthwhile!  The outer shell was crispier than any cannoli I've ever had before, and the filling was silky smooth and rich, with just the right amount of chocolate chips mixed in.  Also, the cannoli was larger than I'd expected (about 6" x 2.5").  This was, by far, the best cannoli I've ever eaten!  I think the fact that they're filled on order makes a huge difference, but it's more than just that, since I've had other cannolis that were filled on site before that weren't as good.  The quality and freshness of ingredients sets these cannolis apart in deliciousness!

Service was a bit slower than I'd like, but this was no doubt due to the fact that only one woman was working the counter at the time that I stopped by (4pm on a Sat.).  Sure, the cannoli was a bit pricy at $4, but unlike at least one other cannoli I've eaten at that price, it was well worth it.  It's definitely a must-try item at RTM!

Quite an exciting menu.  I ended up having the shrimp and crawfish etouffee and the shrimp and crawfish pasta salad.  I liked both , especially the big chunks of okra in the etouffee.  One of the people with me had the catfish po'boy.  I had a bite, and it was amazing.  Another person had the Trainwreck sandwich, and he was very happy with that choice.  The service was quick and friendly (you order at the counter and then wander off to find a seat in the open area).

Great bar/pub/grill. A decent menu with a lot of variety.  Decent parking outside which is nice in Tucson. The inside is cool and inviting, with a nice bar, fun walk art and plenty of seating. There are hanging tv's though so it can get a bit loud.  I had the Wildcat burger which is huge, has excellent flavor and filled me up to be sure. Loved the Trident sauce. Worth the ride down from Florence.

Finally a great Indian place in south Tampa!!! A hole in the wall but with great food under a new look. If you haven't been here recently go back. They make great made to order Indian food and should have a meat market and grocery store in the back. 
A hidden gem!!
Great place for a lunch break. Speedy service, good prices, and really really really good chicken. Oh, and those sauces?? Omg haha

Delicious Crepes! I got the Norwegian which had goat cheese avocado and Salmon. It was soft and delish. I wish they brought syrup out. Didn't see it on the counter until after.

My wife got the Strudel Crepe with apples and cinnamon. It was pretty basic.

Would go back again. What a hidden gem!

I was in town for a conference and stopped here for lunch.

Having gone to school in Louisiana, my standards are pretty high for cajun cuisine. This place met my expectations, just barely.

I had their breakfast bowl featuring andouille sausage, egg, and some other things I now forgot (memories do not age well). The food was spicy, but not overwhelmingly so. There's a decent amount of salt, but does not overpower the taste of the ingredients.

I had a good conversation with one of the workers there. So the service is fast and friendly.
The nicest and friendliest owners. Great food and great selections of cafe beverages.
Muffalata from this location was pretty delicious. It takes such a long time to get if you want it toasted so please be forewarned and prepared. I did enjoy the sandwich though.

Place is drab and depressing. Sticky unsanitary and stinky. Yuck. Food is about the same. So is the service. What a downer. The checkout/host counter had an unlined trash can that looked like it hadn't been emptied in a couple days. Used toothpicks near the cash register. No pride. Gross.

I've been visiting La Parrilla for many years. Only recently the food quality has taken a severe turn for the worse. The original Speedway location is still good but the Oracle location is just flat terrible. I'm not sure why there's such a difference in quality but the owners need to intervene. I work nearby and all my co-workers say the same thing.

We are Trident regulars and are here or at one of their locations at least once a week (just throwing that out there). I love the atmosphere and when they host Geeks Who Drink. I normally don't like sitting at tables so we will wait for a booth to open because they're so comfy and add to the whole Trident experience. 

For starters make sure you order the Calamari (make sure you ask for extra sauce and lemons) and hot wings! Then proceed to either a burger, BLT, Mac and cheese or salmon. The fries are so good and seasoned perfectly. 

As for drinks, I stick to my good ol' iced tea. 

p.s don't forget the fries. 

Keep it saucy,
megggs44

Love this place! We stopped off here on our way to TX- if you like a place that offers HEALTHY options but ALSO has bar food this is ur spot. We are traveling with a group of people who all have diff tastes, I personally wanted a good salad and that's exactly what I got- the paleo salad is amazing! I got it with grilled shrimp but it typically comes with grilled chicken. Others in the group are typical meat and potato/American food types so they were happy as well. It's Reasonably priced and a cool atmosphere - it's like a bar/diner with quality food. The servers were friendly as well. Def recommend!

I love the vegan-ish food at this restaurant, but at this location the night I ate there my waiter was too busy, his fingernails had what appeared to be dirt underneath them and there was a pesky fly around my food. I will not go back to the Oracle store.

Math and science department are lacking incredibly in quality teachers. Freshman year Mr. Yeiter teaches algebra I and miserably fails to set a strong base for more math education. It shows when sophomore year geometry teacher, Mrs. Higgins, piles on geometry with the assumption that the girls already learned some of the much needed skills in algebra I. Next, Mrs. Zolk, the junior algebra II teachers does not teach, instead simply demands the students know how to do something, then fails the majority of them with ridiculous quizzes and tests accompanied by her unesesarily nit picky grading. Finally, Mrs. Boland, the senior pre calculus teacher struggles to put the pieces back together of a shattered math education that was allowed to fester for three years. The science department may be even worse off, with teachers like Mrs. Cornwall, who do not teach at all, or Mrs. Pisacano, who take joy in failing their students. Mrs. Dauerbach is just the host of a memorization game, and Sr. Fran stands alone in her skill and desire of helping students understand biology, but is not allowed to teach the AP class. There is room for serious improvement in these departments, not only because the students want to learn it, but because science and math are becoming vital skills in the career oriented society.

If you're looking for the best cannoli ever.. search no more .. they're made right here at Termini Bros! 

On my visit I had their cannoli of course.. (it would be a sin to visit and not get one) and I also had their Chocolate Covered Banana that comes covered in an amaretto cookie base and stuffed with raspberry preserve and French buttercream .. and let me tell you.. that thing is AMAZING as well!! 

I live a bit of a drive away from Philly.. but all of their desserts look so amazing! And I can't wait for my next visit so that I can get more of that cannoli goodness and taste a couple more of their delicious looking treats!
Generally quite good though not always awesome. Highly recommend a chef's box. $16 for salmon one is huge.

We love BOLD!!  We are coffee SNOBS and these gals are crushing it!!  Kelly and Lisa (I hope I spelled your names correctly) are beautiful wonderful souls aiming to do a great job.  AND THEY DELIVER! Best coffee I've had. Seriously, move over Seattle, there are new BOLD Bad Ass Baristas in town! Best coffee in Philly. Worth the trip if you are not close to Francisville/Fairmount.

I walked past this stall and could not pass up the delicious looking jambalaya. I've never had jambalaya before, so this is my first time, and it did not disappoint! I got the chicken and shrimp jambalaya. My picky eater sister also really liked it!

The hibachi itself is not bad, but the sauces were a little funky tasting. I did not like their sushi at all -- it was gross and did not taste fresh at all. If you want good sushi in North Tampa, go to Soho Sushi on Bearss.
Perfect place for passport photos!   If you're looking for passport photos come here; about same price as Walgreens, CVS and others but much better quality!  100000 x better quality!

I order for delivery and The Chile relleno  tasted like the batter was tamale masa and not egg batter we were very unhappy with it, The queso fundido tasted like edible puddy, it was blop. Unsatisfactory for us...
You sell cake and literally don't have forks. ‍ I'm not sure why I need to keep writing but this sentence is only here cuz yelp is requiring additional writing to post this post.

Loved this place and wish we were locals because we would definitely be regulars.  The place had a great vibe, the food coming out of the kitchen was that of a top quality restaurant.  The staff and the "regular" bar patrons were very friendly and service was excellent.  What an amazing experience.

Who goes to Trident and gets a salad? Apparently I do. I wasn't quite feeling up for a burger and thought I'd give their chicken and walnut salad a shot while we watched the Olympics for a bit. The reality was that I was rather unimpressed by a salad that somehow managed to taste exactly like a bunch of ingredients thrown into a bowl. Nothing mixed well together or complemented another flavor. I might as well have made it at home. My friends seemed to enjoy their burgers though, so I'm willing to give this place a shot again. 

The best part about this place is the collegiate-sportslike atmosphere that makes you KNOW that this would be a great place to watch a game with friends. We were there for the Women's Olympic soccer game and enjoyed it, but were rather put off by the slow service. Great place that I'll go to again, I'm just taking away a star for service and another for mediocre food.

Whenever I go to Reading Terminal Market, I usually always resort to Beck's. 
Their gator gumbo is good, but i feel like their fried mac and cheese was just eh the last time I had it. Was cold and tasted worst than the 4 times I've had it. 
The service was also not great at all. I get it, it's a Saturday and there's lots of people going in and out, but don't be rude to customers.

This is the worst Los Betos on planet earth  I highly recommend no one ever eat here in their lifetime I would give this place a half star if I could I have literally been food poisoned by this place I am going to get the health department definitely involved it is a disgrace that this place is still open I have literally been throwing up all night long and I literally can not wait till this place opens to give these people a piece of my mind I paid over 35$ for three burritos two California burrito and  a chorizo egg and cheese and I was very disappointed not only was there something wrong with the meat it smelled like it had been marinading outside in the middle of 110% weather DO NOT GO HERE PLEASE TRUST ME VERY BAD HEALTH DEPARTMENT WILL BE NOTIFIED...

Excellent dipping sauce with Cilantro rice . Chicken was tasty


Good value .. Wish they would stay open just a little later . They close at 8:00pm

I ordered from here through Doordash on a hot afternoon when i really didn't want to go anywhere or do anything. Being that I lost my sense of taste and smell, my options were fairly limited, but I knew I had to eat something. I was feeling like something light along with something starchy, so I thought this was a good choice. I went with their chicken salad due to my coworker having gotten this a long time ago,   raving about their homemade dressing. So i went with that. I've also had their fried Yuca sticks with spicy cheese sauce. Both items were delicious despite my lack of taste, i could appreciate the texture that came through. I actually did taste the cheese sauce, though mildly, and i could appreciate the spiciness and the rich, creamy texture. The salad itself was quite a sight to behold as it was a rather large size, though not unbearably filling. There was ample chicken sitting on a bed of lettuce, and their thick cilantro dressing was on the bottom. It made for a really good quarantine meal, and I was glad I had the opportunity to try it.

I've always been a big fan of Peruvian chicken since I first had it when I lived in south Florida. This restaurant does it with similar fashion - good chicken and generous portions. For the sodium sensitive, ask for less salty, typically there is salt in the beans, rice, and of course the chicken. The flavors were great and you definitely need the sauces with the chicken! Prices were reasonable and service was good.

Really good Cajun food!  Especially the etoufee special of the day over Jambalaya. The line is usually long but today it was perfect and gave me an opportunity to try it.  Definitely coming back when I come to town!
Good selection of tasty bar food.  We had Buffalo wings, breaded chicken and fish tacos. I've also visited other trident locations.  Good customer service

**avoid**
Coffee was the best part, waited over 40 mins for food with no apology. I ordered the train wreck omelet, it was small, no seasoning, the corn bread was terrible and the sweet potato fries were soggy and cold. 
I would not recommend this place.  1) staffing/management issues- they need to figure out the people waiting at the bar and not other orders. I was about to go make it myself. 2) food was not good and portion was lacking. 
**avoid**

Was studying here with a friend a few weekends back. The café is a cozy little space located in a rapidly developing niche in Fairmount.
I'm big on studying in cafés so ambience matters to me a lot. I wasn't a big fan of the interior space, it was rather lackluster, though it let in a lot of sunlight. There was seating out front and downstairs but the main area itself (which is where we were situated) was rather small and had one outlet on the other end of the room. If you're going to come here to work, I advise grabbing the one seat by the outlet or bringing a fully-charged laptop. 
There's free wifi and it's pw-protected, which is great.
Vineyards offers lots of different beverages, baked goods, and sweet and savory crepes. My friend and I only ordered two chai lattes, which tasted like your typical coffeeshop chai latte, so nothing really mind-blowing. The owners were very polite, which was nice. Overall, a pretty ordinary café with crepes and nice people. I'd come here again, but mainly because my friend lives in the area and we'd most likely be doing our work here.
I used to love this restaurant but the last two times I have eaten here, I have gotten very sick.  I will not be back.
Fun Atmosphere! Football games going all over. Very good food! Love the decor of old naval stuff!
Reading Terminal Market is a bustling place! Tucked away near the entrance is Termini Bros. Delicious cannolis which are also fun to watch them make!

I had never been to Ruth's Chris until recently on Broad and I really liked it.  It's much more cozy than its meaty competition Capital Grille and Del Frisco's.  I liked the ambiance a lot.  I actually sat at the bar, and had a great experience with Chris, the bartender/waiter.  

To start, I tried the BBQ Shrimp dish that they're known for (gluten-free too) and it was nothing like I thought it would be judging from its name.  5 big shrimp in a garlicy-buttery-amazing sauce.  If I ate bread, I would've asked for a loaf to dip into that sauce for the rest of the meal!

Had a NY Strip Steak and Garlic Mashed Potatoes - how could I go wrong?  My entree was delicious.  Came sizzling on a hot plate to me - and was cooked to medium rare perfection.  My friend had the filet.  Judging from the clean-plate club status, I believe he enjoyed it.  :)

Gluten free friendly - Chris was well-equipped with a list of what I could and could not eat.  I look forward to going back and trying my steakhouse favorite - lamb chops!

What a fun place. I went on a saturday night thinking it was going to be packed full of people but it wasn't.  I had heard the that the burgers were the best thing to order there, and so I had ordered the wildcat burger.  IT was so good! the BBQ sauce and the onion ring with a side of sweet potato fries YUM!  I also ordered a dark and stormy and every bite was perfection!

Located this gem simply by mistake, but it was a great one. On arrival greeted and seated. Scanned menu it's not long and complicated, but short simple straight to point. I ordered 1/4 white with cilantro rice and house salad with house salad dressing, Mr ordered half white same sides . Fork and knife stayed in formation. The salad was really good with the house specialty dressing it light and tasty. Cilantro rice was delicious and that could have been a meal alone. The chicken was moist and seasoned to perfection , every bite was a experience. Also your given 2 small condiments of green sauce one is spicy and the other mild both good. Overall this was a good meal and affordable. Noted they have a number of regulars which mean this is not just a business but a family among the community.

Had an oyster po boy today and the rolls seem smaller and they skimped on the sauce. The lack of sauce was really noticeable.

I expect better from a $15 sandwich.

I had been to the first location once(only once) and not because the food was bad, the beer menu small or the service terrible. It was a pretty good pub. but....I HATE BRIGHT pubs. Seriously???? Brighter then a Safeway. So disappointed. 

Word was there was a new location coming!!! We popped down to the new location just before they opened and I actually asked the owners if it would be as bright as location #1.... "No, the lights will be dim". Well.... Stopped the other evening in great anticipation as I am dying for a local and much to my dismay, I needed sunglasses to approach the place. I definitely won't go back. I have no desire to see the pores on your face while drinking a cocktail at the end of the day. No atmosphere at all. 

BTW, when it's as bright as it is it makes it very easy to see anything and everything that may be dirty, run down, and just ugly....

I came here for the canoli and I was not disappointed! I don't always love canolis because I think the end bites are great, but everything in the middle falls short. This place didn't really make me feel that way. The filling was fantastic all the way through and the crunch and flavors of the wrapping was great and consistent. 

I highly recommend grabbing a canoli here if you're visiting. Let's be honest. It's Readding Market and you're going to be here anyways!

Dined here for lunch recently, pretty cool little sports bar! Close to the university and downtown. We only had beers and appetizers but they were all super tasty, and our server was really friendly I never caught her name though! Cute little dive sports bar feel to it.
I was very pleased with the menu. The crepes are delicious and the coffee is amazing. There is free WiFi too and it's a great place to study.

The fish tacos are a must have!!! They are cooked to perfection, are bursting with flavor and have the perfect amount of spice. TK is always pleasant on the phone when I place my order and then she's just as friendly in person when picking it up.

YES I love Beck's! Located in Reading Terminal Market, there is always a line. You can find New Orleans gumbo, po boys, friend shrimp, cornbread, and cat fish. The Mac and Cheese balls with spicy remoulade are heavenly.

Best cannoli, ever. I had their chocolate chip cannoli and would advise you to order that, too. The cannoli cream is whipped and has a lot of ricotta flavor. Most times I've had cannoli, the cream is too thick and there is so much granulated sugar, I can barely taste the ricotta. The shell is light, but does not easily fall apart once a bite is taken. I also had their sfogliatelle for the novelty factor. It's a flakey shell-shaped pastry with ricotta and citrus fruit filling. Unique textures, but I did not truly appreciate the citrus flavor. I think I would've ordered many cannoli in retrospect.  You live, you learn. 

Everything totaled to $9, so I am assuming each pastry is roughly $3-4.50. They take credit cards.

When you find yourself standing in front of Termini Bros Bakery, you can't help but stare.  Well lit displays slammed full of pastries and treats make your mouth ready to be stuffed.

Staff know the drill and many posed for the camera when you're taking pics of their displays...needless to say, it's a friendly bunch.  

They make their cannolis right in front of you, filling the empty shell with cream that looked great.  Sadly I didn't buy one of these.  We instead shared their Lemon cream cake.  

Geez this thing was popping with citrus flavors and sweetness that made me sad that we didn't buy more!  Located near the rear of Reading Terminal, Termini Bros Bakery seems to have a crowd always, and while there's no seating at the bakery, there's plenty of places to sit in the Terminal.

Really enjoyed my Time at Termini Bros Bakery, and my only gripe is that we didn't buy more.  Do me a favor and buy some of their treats and enjoy!
Amazing... some of the best food that I've had in quite some time! The staff was attentive and friendly. Food was sizzling hot when brought out and never had to ask for a refill.

they did a brilliant job on my septum it was so quick and not very painful. Bradley did my piercing he was very chill and got the job done quick and easy i've also gotten my industrial their last year same stuff quick and easy and it never got infected.

Overall, I was very disappointed with Ruth's Chris. I will say this, the valet was great, the host staff were pleasant and our server was very friendly. However, my husband and I had been waiting to go there for our first time, on our anniversary. I made reservations in advance and even put in our reservation that we were coming to celebrate our anniversary. We are brought to our table and they initially had us a booth right in front at the bar..people's butts would have been in our faces all night long. We couldn't believe they would seat anyone there, let alone someone who made reservations and had indicated it was a special evening. We asked them to change our table and they did, so that did work out ok..it was just very off putting that they would even seat us there in the first place.
We ordered our food and my husband did like his meal. I however spent $45 on a filet that was inedible. I know in the steak world, they think your steak should be medium rare or medium at the most, but I like my steak well done..to each their own, right? And if you're a good chef, a chef at one of the areas top steak houses no less, you should be able to cook a steak any way the customer wants. I can do it great at home. Well apparently not at Ruth's Chris. They sent me a charred, burned, over cooked piece of meat. Well done does not mean burnt! I have never seen a filet be so tough in my life and I have ordered filet well done at other restaurants and still have it cut like butter. I ate 4 bites then had to spit the last one out because I couldn't even break it down it was so charred. Our server did come to ask how everything was, but it was right after our food was brought out and I hadn't even cut into my steak yet..didn't see him again until after the plates were cleared but the runner.
We had been looking forward to that night for months, and now I can honestly say I would never go to Ruth's Chris again. And that chef should seriously be ashamed of themselves to send food out of their kitchen that was like that. The only reason I'm giving 2 stars instead of 1 is because my husband did like his food. But he even said he would never go back after that.

Purchased vanilla confetti buttercream mini cake and chocolate mousse mini cake.  Both went in the trash after a bite.  Cakes were flavorless.  Frostings were subpar.  And they tasted stale. $12 wasted.

Hands-down best cheesecake of my life. I usually find cheesecake too rich and cloying for me to eat a whole slice of, so I split a slice of the plain with my friend. Boy was I regretting that a few minutes later. This is the lightest, fluffiest cheesecake I've had and the sweetness is beautifully balanced. We were just downing it like air. My friend ordered the chocolate marble cheesecake and it was also very good, though I'm a purist and prefer the plain/original. This was our favorite store in Reading Terminal. Definitely stop by and pick up some cheesecake.

BEST CANNOLI EVER!

*Clouds in the sky parted, sun beams rays directly down on Termini, heavenly angels sing, and this cannoli appeared to bring joy and delight to all those on earth.*

Choice of fillings: Chocolate, Vanilla, Cheese & Chocolate Chips.  The later of which is what I had.  

$3.00 for one and worth every penny!  Perfectly crunchy pastry shell, smooth, sweet, cream with chocolate chips, powdered sugar sprinkled on top. Thank God for the local Philadelphian who send me here for one.  WOW!  I nearly fainted with delight.

(They have other items too... candy, sfogliatelle - baked ricotta cheese, orange peel. and cinnamon, fig bars, cookies, coconut macaroons, cakes of all kinds,)

This stuff is so good that you can order it and have it shipped anywhere in the US.  6 cannoli for $40, 12 for $60.  Order them for a party and you won't be sorry!  You can also call their 800 number - 800-882-7650.

The best cannolis I've had in Philadelphia.  Unlike some other pasty shops (yeah, I'm talking to you, Isgro's), they do not have pre-made cannolis that sit around letting the moisture of the creamy cheese filling seep into what is supposed to be a crunchy shell.  Every cannoli is only made when you order it so that you get that crunch you want and expect with every bite.  And the expertly made filling is freshly squeezed into your cannoli shell, so it has no chance to oxidize and get stale.

The other pastries I've tried, however, have not been all that impressive.  There are probably some that are also awesome, but after a few only-okay experiences, I usually stick with the cannolis.

@NommingNomad Approved!

Beck's Cajun cafe, which is at the heart of my beloved Reading Terminal Market is one of the places that I take everyone who visits me in Philly to. All their food is so delicious and flavorful, I've never once had a bad experience here. With all their delicious food one is instantly  transported to the streets of NoLa and I personally love that feeling!  I've had their jambalaya which is bomb as well as their corn bread  and Mac and cheese. They also have king cake as a whole or in slices during specific times of the year!

They recently  started serving breakfast and boy oh boy is their brioche French toast bake good. When I think of Beck's I don't think brunch but man did this french toast change that. It is topped with pecan pralines and fresh berries and whipped cream and is also served with cajun fries with an amazing creole mayo dipping sauce and a choice of meat on the side. They do not skimp on the toppings or the sides and I guarantee that you will go home a happy camper. 

They also have specials during weekends like this peanut butter and fluff French toast that I enjoyed. It is perfectly executed French toast with generous helping of peanut butter and fluff in the middle and topped with a chocolate anglaise and a homemade  peanut butter cookie crumble. Doesn't that just want to make you run over there right now and demand it. 

Anyway, when you're at the Reading Terminal Market. You just have to stop by Becks and try their New Orleans food and go home feeling happy in your heart and your tum! You can thank me later!

Was in town for work. Wanted to try some cheesesteaks. Heard this place had the best one in the Reading Terminal Market. Pretty girls at the counter suggested the Trainwreck: steak, salami, andouille sausage, cheese and onion on a roll. I almost died. Was a great Italian/Cajun twist on a Philly classic. Needless to say, I got the Trainwreck multiple times during my trip. Wish I could get one in my neck of the woods!
The food is very good, unless you have been to Louisana.  I spent more than ten years as a judge for a Cajun Cook-off, and I can definitely say the food, though good, is not award winning.
Outstanding!! Being from New Orleans, this place was pretty damn close! Everything we had was tasty and delicious!

The fifteen minute wait was worth it.

After making a few laps through Reading Terminal Market, my friend decided she wanted a po' boy. The counter-seats were taken and the line wrapped around the stand, so I was weary. After taking a peak at the menu, everything looks fairly lackluster and standard. Luckily I waiting in line long enough to see other's orders being made. The Train Wreck Po Boy looked the most interesting; it was.

A little spicy, a little tangy, it was short of amazing. The andouille sausage added a peppery smoky flavor while the salami was surprisingly tangy. The bulk of the sandwich was the steak, generously creole seasoned. All three meats were finely chopped, mixed, and 'glued' together with diced onion and white cheese. The onion and cheese were essentially the brick and mortar, holding everything together tightly. A solid, unexcitingly good po' boy.

My friend got the Fried Shrimp Po Boy. It came with freshly friend shrimp with creole seasonings, lettuce, tomato, pickles, and smoky creole mayo. She didn't seem too impressed with it and I agreed with her after I tried it. 

Overall, not a bad meal for under $10. Well done for Philly.

I'm not leaving this review because I'm upset. I'm only doing this because I wish someone had left a review for me. 

1. The "mermaid locs" that she installs are 300$ for 40 locs + some synthetic hair 

2. They're PRE-DONE locs. Your hair is not actually being wrapped. 

3.  Essentially your paying $300 or $100 dollars an hour for crotchet locs. 

4. Trina doesn't respect your (the customer's) time. She said out loud where I could hear her, "only the 1st appointment of th day is on time everyone else's is going to be pushed back. And talked bad about a customer who said that she had a problem with her appointment being pushed an hour because she had things to do that day. Trina said, if a person has something else to do other than get their hair done they just shouldn't schedule on that day. 

5. Now let's get into the quality. I was charged extra money because my hair was longer than 10$ inches. She said if I wanted it braided all the way down which I obviously did. It would be extra so I paid. It was NOT braided all the way down 

6. I got home that night and saw my hair peaking through the bottom of the locs. To which she responded it's "not a big deal" and sent me a video on how to fix it. 

No one should have to fix 1st day hair. 

7. Now I'm less than a week into this install and the root of my braids are beginning to show and require constant fixing. 

No girl who has natural hair pays 300$ to be fixing things less than a week in. 

8.  The hair can't be submerged in water so if you're think about going on vacation with a cute style. THINK AGAIN 

I mean honestly if you're thinking about waking up the next day with a nice style think again. 

9. Trina is very nice and her gets the job done quick. Albeit, not on time for any client scheduling through her mandatory calendar that has open bookings every 2hrs even tho her work takes a minimum of 2.5. And also, it's not the perfect and neat job you would hope for at the 300$ price tag. 

10. I think her prices are based more upon what her competition who produce a higher quality of work are charging more than what she is actually delivering to customers.

Solid little cafe serving crepes and coffee 

Crepes were huge, with fresh fillings and a great batter. 

The coffees looked great though I didn't have one.

Only has coffee here, can't comment on the food! 

Coffee was very watery and not that flavourful

Absolutely phenomenal Cajun food.  As good or better than anything in New Orleans.  I'm from Southern CA and I wish this place would open a restaurant there.  People were friendly and service was great too.  Can't wait to come back here someday.  I got two bowls of chicken-shrimp gumbo + fried oyster P.O.-Boy (I ate 1/2 before taking the photo)

Cute little spot in francisville for delicious crepes! just a note though, there are some photos on this yelp page from a previous menu - they do not serve any eggs anymore. I love the nutella crepe, the philly crepe, and I've also had a few sandwiches that were good as well. 

My favorite drink here is an iced mochaccino- it will keep you up to get work done. I wish they had oat milk as a non-dairy option though. 

Pre-covid they were also pet friendly in the upstairs portion!

Had the pleasure of starting my day's adventure here. We were mesmerized by a single taste of the gumbo. Light in broth, yet bold, BOLD in flavor, and every piece had chicken and veggies. Immediately we knew this was the real deal and we went for it.

We started off backwards, with sweet amazing beignets. Super flaky and delicate, it was unbelievable the way it came together with just a little powdered sugar. I have yet to travel to Lousiana, but this has been what I believe to be the closest I have been thus far.

Now to start, my wife has never had a real po' boy sandwich. Plenty times she has come across imitations, sandwiches that were fairly cllose but nothing compared to this. One bite in, she drew back from a hearty bite of catfish and aioli, amazed, and dazzled by the intense difference in texture and spice from what she has had previously. She had finally had a po' boy and Beck's I appreciate you for it.

We wind up around these parts again and I will be sure to visit!

Came here for lunch and the food itself did not disappoint. Food was the same as the speedway restaurant so that was good. My guest tried the chicken poblano and it was very tasty. 
The only bummer was that are order wasn't correct and we ran out of tea and water but the waiter never came back. So we were out of luck on getting it fixed.

This place is a quaint breakfast place with a basement lounge perfect for any hipster. The one time I went they ran out of bagels, and I went at a normal breakfast time, but to be fair, you go for the crepes. These are BOMB. They have a lot of unique combinations but they also let you tweak them. This is a great local breakfast stop to pickup or to grab a bite and hang out.

I don't want to seem too generous with my rating but I have very good reasoning. They have wonderful customer service on top of their amazin cajun. In the city of brotherly love we can often be very mean people. When I went to Beck's Cajun Cafe they for one thing love giving me samples, which I in turn also love. 
    One time, I ordered a train wreck sandwich and after opening the paper wrapping realized I did not have enough napkins. So I get up and in doing so knock the whole sandwich off the table into my chair then on to the floor. My chin dropped, tears about to come rushing down. Then when I turn to the Cajun stand to order another the manager looks at me and says, don't worry about it, I got you covered. Out comes a brand new sandwich (which I hold on to tightly) and I discover there is a meat god.
   The train wreck is a definite notch above the philly cheesesteak. (Yes, I was born and raised here). It has more meat, better quality meat, a variety of meat, better bread (sorry amoroso) and this wonderful cajun mayo spread on the bottom.  My boyfriend got the gumbo that was just spicy enough while still able to taste all the other flavors. It was a little lacking in chunkiness but it might have been a bad scoop and the fact that I was eating it too.
   I would like to get their desserts but they are a little on the expensive side for the items that you are getting. However, I was so full off their wonderful food, I didn't save room for dessert. Though, I could probably live off whiskey sauce on bread pudding so I might have to make an exception next time.

I absolutely love this place. The food is great the servers are awesome! And what's better, is I can see their faces and actually understand what they're saying! No masks? You're darn tootin'! Let's get Tucson back to normal

The staff is very friendly. There's not a ton of seating. There is a 45 minute seating limit, so this place isn't really student friendly. It's mainly for a quick conversation with a friend or a business meeting. Besides that, I enjoyed my coffee and the tea latte I had later in the week.  Neither of those drinks really tasted like the flavors I asked for, but I feel like that's true for every coffee shop. Overall, it's a nice place to go for a short time. I'm sure whatever you order will taste good. And it's always a good thing to shop local, so I encourage you to give them a visit.
Great food and great service. Awesome place to eat and drink! Staff is solid, food is delicious and service is outstanding.
This play is well ran and consistently good. Never have been disappointed in my 12 visits

A Philly friend hand-delivered Termini cannoli to me when I was in NYC over July 4th - what a sweet, indulgent gift. Crisp pastry, creamy, custard: Heaven. There was chocolate, custard with chocolate chip, and ricotta filling. Not too sweet, but so rich.

a haiku: 
Termini's baked goods
hold a sweet place in my heart
 leave the gun, take these

Y'all. Y-'-A-L-L.

This bakery is so great.

When you are at Reading Terminal Market, it is really hard to pick from all the tasty options for your sweet tooth. But make no mistake: You can't go wrong at Termini Bros Bakery. 

I went 3 days in a row. Whoops. 

They have basically all the sweet options you could want. My favorite was the Almond Horn. I did not know a dessert could be that awesome until I tried that horn shaped almond cookie dipped into chocolate with almond paste inside. OMG.

And my second favorite was the Zwieback biscotti. I tried just one piece, and then I came back the next day to take a half pound home for my partner and me. It has cherries, walnuts, and vanilla. Are you reading this thinking biscotti is dry and boring and can only be eaten when dipper into a hot beverage? You are wrong. Try this immediately and experience what biscotti is supposed to taste like. 

The only "miss" I tried was the vanilla cupcake. The cake was tasty, but the icing was not my favorite. 

Lastly, the staff is wonderful and handles all the people at the market with skill. They also have great smelling coffee, and they fill cannoli when you order them. 

Termini Bros Bakery is a total gem. Don't miss it.
The selection of bakery items are to cause your brain to think about longer than your visit. The Canoli is freshly made $5 a piece I highly recommend.
This place has some very wonderful and magical healthy food for the soul! Some vegan options too! HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

Okay, after searching Google, Yelp, and their own website, it was clearly stated that Beck's close at 6 pm. I was in CC today so I hustled to get there with an hour to spare (on a hot 95 degree day mind you) arrived at 5:01 just to hear "sorry, we're closing at 5". 
Welp, you've lost my support Beck's. I kindly took my business over to Maggiano's.

This family owned and operated bakery has been a Philadelphia staple for 95 years. They specialize in great Italian desserts and pastries which range from zeppole, cannoli, cookies, confections and wedding cakes. Everything is fresh and looks mouthwatering and their signature cannolis are filled to order. Today we tried their cannoli and the shells were fresh and crispy and the filling was flavorful and silky. If your walking through Reading Terminal Market and need something sweet they have plenty to offer.

Mom's Bake at Home Pizza is super! Their pizza is delicious, and tastes fresh every time.  It's also super easy to take home and bake and store.  I hear their cookies and stromboli's are equally awesome.  Additionally, they have a LOT of different options to take home and prepare.  Double additionally, we used them for a fundraiser, and they are super helpful / kind about it.  

BIG fan!

Cannoli!

Located inside the Reading Terminal Market, this place is offering some delicious baked goods. Employees are friendly and quick. Our order was wrapped neatly. Their cannoli is made to order and super fresh. They also offer mini cakes, larger cakes, cookies, cheesecakes, etc. Everything we tried was excellent and you can taste the quality ingredients used. 

So glad we got to try this place out.

Fish and chips were kinda greasy. Nm better than a good Gordons fish stick dad said. The tap beer tasted skunky and warmish so we asked for a bottle of bud instead. gotta keep taps clean. The distributors know that but not always the people servicing the taps. Fingerprints on the window. Nice ambiance ig if you wanted to hangout for drinks with friends near the u of a.

Very tasty food!  The clam chowder is amazing but very filling.  It's more like a meal then a starter. We also tried the fish and chips and a burger. Both were great. The fish and chips were cooked to perfection and I wish I could have finished them but I was full from the chowder. 
It's pretty busy there and doesn't have a lot of room for parties larger then 4 people.  Also I saw no kids menu but I could have missed it. We'll be back for sure!

Termini Bros makes delicious & fresh Italian pastries! Their cannolis are my favorite and probably the best I've had in Philly! The cannoli shell is perfectly fried and adds a nice crunch with each bite! The ricotta filling is subtlety sweet and creamy. There's enough chocolate chips in the filling that you get little in each bite! The desserts at Termini Bros are definitely a purchase when you walk by a location!

What a great surprise!  We ordered the Train wreck Po' Boy and it was one of the top 3 items that we ate in Philly.  Who knew? Although the combination sounded irresistible - cheesesteak, salami, andouille sausage, cheese and onions..  Why not?  

And thankfully, we tried it and it was off the charts.   The steak was tender and the cheese melded all the flavors of the andouille, salami, and steak together.  I think they added some Cajun spice to it too.  

We also ordered the fried oysters which everyone enjoyed..  there was just the right amount of crunch outside while protecting a large juicy tender oyster inside.  My husband, who's a tough critic, said it's one of the best fried oysters he's had..  

It's one of the must visit places I would go to in the Reading Terminal Market  ..

As far as creole Cajun cuisine in Philly goes, Becks might just be the best (still have to try some Khyber po'boys). Its only real downfall is that you can only get and enjoyment during Reading Terminal hours and oftentimes have to stand in a pressure inducing line as a result (have never had it as bad as Eva has though). but getting the chance to chow down on some legit gumbo and po'boys almost always makes it worth it.

From the etouffees of the day and red beans & rice, to corn meal catfish and blackened chicken, Becks definitely has plenty to add a little heat to your palate. But the stand outs are definitely po'boys! whether you go traditional with the likes of fried shrimp or fried oyster, or go all out with their specialty alligator sausage po'boy that's smothered in creole mustard; you're guaranteed to experience true lunch satisfaction.

Bonus points for the incredible cornbread, and the fact that you can pick up Louisiana staples like Zapp's Chips and Abita root beer!
This place is very cute. The people who work here are always so nice. They have the best iced lattes with almond milk!

From what I've heard I was super excited about trying these donuts. I was very disappointed in what I got. I don't mind spending the money for quality but these things did not live up to the hype. The were dry and lacked flavor in the donut it self. All the taste came from the topping and icing. On top of theta when I went I store on a Saturday afternoon they only had 4 donuts in stock to try. I would not recommend stopping here. They've lost there luster from what they used to be.

Decided to stop on by Beck's Cajun Cafe on a weekend trip to Philly and I was really disappointed. My friend and I ordered the Jambalaya and the Blackened Chicken and it all was just so disappointing. For starters, our dishes took incredibly long to make and by the time we got them, they were cold. My blackend chicken was very overcooked, dry, and unseasonsed. It was like biting into a hockey puck and it was very clear to me that they simply reheated the chicken in a microwave. The corn bread came pre-made in plastic wrap and the sides were additionally very bland. The jambalaya was warm, but also incredibly bland. There was nothing special at all about anything we ate. The girls serving us showed us a lot of attitude and were kind of rude to us. I wouldn't recommend this place if you're deciding on stopping by. Wait to eat real Cajun food in New Orleans and save your coins.

When we arrived we were told to sit where we liked.  It was several minutes before we were given menus and didn't receive silverware.  The waitress came back a few minutes later for our drink order.  My husband ordered a tea, I ordered a plain margarita.  After our drinks arrived I took a sip of mine then noticed a black hair floating in it, I have long red hair.  We mentioned it to her, she didn't seem too concerned but offered me a fresh one.  We received our food from another waiter, probably not too uncommon.  My burger was missing the bacon I requested.  At this point we still hadn't received silverware.  When we were almost done with our food is when she finally checked on us, it was more of an afterthought as she was on her way to the back and then turned around to ask us how our food was.  The only positive was that the food tasted good.  She handed us our bill without asking about refills or if I wanted another margarita.  Probably won't be back, do like that they're mask free.

Natalia and her partner Tommy were amazing. All 8 of my bridesmaids were extremely pleased with the outcome of their hair and makeup and we all had an enjoyable experience. Natalia's precision and attention to detail really separates her from the rest. I would 100% recommend Natalia for her services. She has such a warm presence and makes you feel like a queen but still look like yourself ! Tommy was also exceptional for his hair services. Thank you both so much for such an amazing experience !

So much better than Maoz, but nowhere near as good as Alyan's. Chickpea's offers up a fully loaded falafel on the go. and the heaping of helpings inside the pita definitely put Maoz and their unnecessary fixings bar to shame. As Marisa says Chickpea's is owned by the same people who own Mama's Grill, so they definitely know their veggies.

Beyond the falafel and the occasional Baklava I haven't had the desire to try anything else that Chickpea's has to offer. It could just be that awesome places like Saad's make the expectations a little higher for me. But I might cave in and try the shawarma so I can find out how they do meat. The Baklava is mighty tasty, but pretty far from what I'm used to.

Little over priced but they do have some pretty good Italian desserts.   I enjoy the chocolate covered banana with raspberry sauce on top of a short bread cookie.  You really can't go wrong but be prepared for the cost $6

We stopped here with two other couples before a U of AZ Basketball game. Great server. Good was excellent. I had the Gumbo and my wife had pork tacos. I have nothing to say but good. The noise level was elevated which made it hard for one of our friends who has hearing difficult. We plan to return!

Came here and got the classic cannoli to split, and it was the best cannoli We've had in a long time! The shells are piped to order, so they stay nice and crispy. The filling was dense and super creamy, it had just the right amount of sweetness, and the chocolate chips and candies  citrus throughout were perfect pops of flavor throughout. Definitely stop by and get a cannoli, you won't be disappointed!
The crepes are always spot on. I normally get the Nutella crepe w/ strawberries & bananas, but last time I switched it up and got the Philly crepe. It was amazing!! This place is a gem!

I'm so happy that they're now successful enough to have opened multiple locations around town! I'm still biased the most toward their original location as I have so many good memories of birthdays and celebrations there! You can't beat their buffalo chicken salad with the bleu cheese crumbles, I promise you that!

Reading Terminal Market was the second stop my boyfriend and I made on our first day at Philadelphia. We were starving and it was lunch time so we decided to grab lunch from Beck's Cajun Cafe. 

The women behind the counter were very nice and were willing to let you sample some of their foods. I sampled the Blackened Chicken Alfredo which I really liked so I decided to order that. The Blackened Chicken Alfredo was creamy and tasted like your usual pasta with Alfredo sauce. Half way through the Alfredo, it became spicy because they sprinkled a tad of red pepper powder. I couldn't handle the spice.

My boyfriend really liked the sample of Jambalaya so he ordered the a Cajun Meatloaf Platter with Jambalaya, and Corn bread, I was able to try a little bit of everything. The Jambalaya was quite spicy, couldn't handle it. The meatloaf was moist and tasty. I really liked the corn bread because it was moist, not too sweet, and had a great taste to it.

I didn't feel too well throughout the day after having the food. I'm sure the other foods here are very good, but maybe Cajun food isn't for me.

Awful.  Just awful. Food was horribly prepared. We asked for a medium steak, we got blue. Asked for them to cook more, we got well done. 

Overall,  the service was very over bearing,  asking every two minutes how the food was. 

There are better steak houses in Philadelphia. Stay away

I visited for the first time today and had a horrible experience. I placed my order and as I was going to sit down I stopped to look at all the different food and how they were making it just because it all lookEd so good. woman that had taken my to go order,  approached me and started pushing me along by my arm. I said I was just stopping to see what all they were making she said you can't do that. I left the restaurant without my food I am so upset. You don't put your hands on other people. Especially during Covid but really never.  I've also never seen an open restaurant that doesn't want you to look at what they are doing there was a glass partition there. Lastly, when I was paying, before the incident, she asked me if I tipped. I actually had tipped but wish I didn't I left without my food and without getting my money back I was so upset

I've been dying to try this place and am so glad I did. I pass by Vineyards Cafe during my commute to work in the morning. It's usually not open yet since I get in so early, but one day, I was running late and thought f*** it, I'm getting myself a cappuccino! 

Small, quaint, and cozy, this little neighborhood cafe is such a treat. I'll definitely be back to try a crepe next time.

I've been wanted to go here for so long & I am so glad I finally did! We started with wings & fried pickles which were both delicious. They make some of their own wing sauces, H1,2,&3 which are all so good! Also the shrimp tacos were delicious you need to try!

Finally got the time to stand in line today. Stood in line for 10 minutes. Got a tiramisu and fig bar (not cannoli because most cannolis taste the same to me). Tiramisu looked beautiful, moist and creamy before eating it. Disappointment was real. Tiramisu was dry, could not taste any La Colombe espresso. Cream was heavy and thick. Definitely not so traditional tiramisu that I've tasted before. I recommend this tiramisu to those who prefer very light coffee flavor and heavy cream tiramisu. Fig bar is also far from a traditional fig bar. I enjoyed this dense fig bar much more than tiramisu.

5 star for their bomb a**, creamy, cannolis!!! Their ricotta cheese filling was rich and not too creamy. The chocolate chips and I believe I tasted pistachio were the perfect combination! Not too many pieces so you weren't overwhelmed with each bite. 
I found this place watching an episode of PHANTOM GOURMET (the Philly travel episode)... This recommendation did not disappoint!

Trident hit the trifecta for me on this visit:

Cold beer.

The best fish and chips in Tucson.

Super service even though the place was PACKED with all kinds of crazy fans like me gearing up to head to Arizona Stadium to cheer on the Cats.

Just when I thought finding good fish and chips in Tucson was like finding a leprechaun riding a unicorn, Trident makes a believer out of me.

I love all of the Trident Grills. Great atmosphere, excellent food, awesome staff. As a veteran, I also love that the owners are ex military as well. Support this business and support our veteran owned businesses!
The food was delicious. Limited menu and tiny restaurant but worth the trip.

I owe this place a long over due review, I'm really not sure how I haven't reviewed this place, yet!
Every time I go to the Reading Terminal Market, I keep browsing, and most of the time, I end up getting something from Beck's Cajun Cafe. It has to be my absolute favorite.

I believe I have tried just about every delicious item on their menu, except the Train Wreck and the Gator. Two legit reasons : The Train Wreck has pork and I don't eat it, and and about that Gator...I can't eat something that could have eaten me in different circumstances!!!  Otherwise, I was happy with every item I have had, and usually a nap would be needed.  

- Heavenly beignets, served four days a week, made to order. Oh boy! 
- Rich and creamy Blackened Chicken Alfredo, with a spicy kick.
- Fancy some Shrimp and Chicken Gumbo? Mind-blewing! 
- Pepper, eggs with provolone breakfast wrap. Its good.
- Blackened Chicken Po' Boy. Not my fav.
- Don't miss the Fried shrimps.  Uh, yeah.
- Fried mac n' cheese balls, they were a little bland and not as good as they sound. 
- Craving king cake, Beck's serves it during Mardi Gras season. I had it for my birthday! Oh, so good...
- Golden Sweet Cornbread. I usually don't like cornbread, but this one is so sweet and moist. 
- Bread Pudding. Okish!

Beck's Cajun Cafe staff is extremely friendly. They always greet everyone with a huge smile, and offer samples of their food. 

Want to try some of spice blends from Beck's pantry? Take some home, they have several: Devil Dust, Angel's Kiss, Rub-a-Dub, Creole Mayo, BBQ Onion Relish and 3 Devils Hot Sauce. 

Four solid Yelps.

I have frequented Trident several times. Great food and service, love the fish and chips. We decided to take my parents last night for their first time. We went to the Speedway location since we were by the U of A. Our waitress just walked up and said, "drinks?" Apparently we were supposed to order our drinks and we did. Once they were dropped off we were not asked to order, she just dropped and ran. When she returned about 15 minutes later, we asked of we could order and it this point get refills since we were hot and thirsty. With her eyes rolling, she took our order and walked away never returning with the refills. Once we flagged down the manager we finally got our drinks. Food came and was delicious, but the terrible service continued through out our meal. After 15 years in the restaurant industry I never complain when I go out, but this wasn't a busy waitress in the weeds or a new girl on her first night, she was beyond rude. Rolling her eyes and walking away as we were speaking. $90 dinner should come with at least decent service.  We will just return to the one on Broadway and Craycroft and avoid this location.

To make this short - I've never had a better cannoli! The filling is to die for and the shell is the perfect crunch. I will go to Termini's anytime I'm in Philadelphia. If you can't decide what to get at Reading Terminal - make this a must! I don't think you'll regret it.

As I write this I'm sitting in a booth at what has got to be the worst restaurant I've been to in Tucson. Service is horrendously slow (lost my order twice) steak ultra dry, supposed to come with guacamole, but no.  I'd have been better off going to Taco Bell.  To top it all off they screwed up the bill and I had to wait over 30 minutes for them to correct it!

Beck's Cajun Cafe in 30th Street Station has the same great food as its sister foodstand in Reading Terminal Market. I finally got to try the gator gumbo with white rice. It was really good! I think their chicken and andouille sausage gumbo is still the best, but it was nice to be able to finally try gator sausage in Cajun spices. I also like their jambalaya, red beans and rice, and praline cookies. The jambalaya bowl is the best value because it has huge chunks of chicken and sausage and the servers really fill the takeout container with it. The crab and shrimp etouffée is a big miss. I tried samples of it here and at Reading Terminal and both had hardly any seafood in it.

Just moved to Tampa in March, decided to stop for lunch on our way to the DMV last week and was pleasantly surprised of how good the food was!
They were being safe and social distancing tables and togo customers.
We ordered the half chicken and the beef dish not sure if the name?
So good we had to go back again this week!
I LOVE THE GREEN SAUCE! The salad is so good too!

Honestly I can't believe I paid almost 250
For the hair I received....2-5
Business days is what the page said when I order the hair after a week a reached out didn't get a response back for 2 days only to be told after the 8th business day due to covid... okay fine I'm patience the 11th day I reach out again asking for a refund no response when the messages was finally read on the 13th day she finally ships my hair...
My hair literally came in 2 day's....
Now my hair is here I open it only to be disappointed for one I could have bought this hair from a hair store or amazon for half the price... I didn't realize the locs was synthetic smh but beside that the loc packs on her page are advertised as 20 a pack i got the oceana human hair kit the only thing human in that kit is the bundle... when you break down the math 20 a pack 3x because 3 packs come in the kit that's 90 plus the bundle you pretty much are paying 150 for a bundle of 18 inch hair smh never again........ I just 3 months ago bought human hair to wrap  and human hair for the braids and leave out only cost me 210 total.... I just didn't want to go thru the whole twisting process but I wish I did... this hair is not worth 247 but I'll take my lost because of course once shipped no refundsgo figure!! Ladies you can order this hair off amazon or at the hair store trust me not worth the money or waiting 2 weeks for nothing extra special about this hair at all.... over charging

A friend and I visited Philly and at the end of a long day and driving around Reading Terminal Market several times trying to find parking, we landed on Beck's after a short stroll through the building. The staff were super friendly and although it was close to closing, encouraged us to sample different dishes and gave us a lot of detail.

I ordered a blackened chicken po'boy and chicken and corn chowder, and my friend ordered gumbo and fried mac and cheese. I scarfed down my po'boy before we departed for home, and it was very good - the chicken was tender and juicy, but for someone who loves spice, would have loved more spice and flavor in there. The fried mac and cheese smackedddd!!! (it's a good thing). My friend and I ate our chowder and gumbo at home and we both thoroughly enjoyed both. 

All in all, I would definitely come back and try more of their food!!

We love our neighborhood bar and grill. There's nothing pretentious about this place. Trident is like home to lots of military folks, local EMS personnel and of course, UA students after hours. You can catch UFC flights and all the important sporting games here. 

Food is consistently good although all Tridents share the same menu (except pizza pub). Try the wings, their Cobb salad, fish and chips, any burger selection. You can't go wrong. The drinks are always cold and the service is consistently good.

I don't know about anyone else but when I travel I make a list...not what to pack, I wing that like a pro on the go! I make a list of places I wanna see, where I want to photograph (shameless plug: CHECK ME OUT ON IG: HudsonFinch), and most importantly WHAT I WANT TO EAT! 
Philly especially falls into this last list category because it is a food paradise and BECKS is always the top of our list. 

Located inside Reading Terminal Market, Becks is a RTM institution and the place to get some of the best Gumbo I've ever had (yes, I've been to New Orleans and I like it too). So step up, fight ur way through the RTM Saturday crowd, grab a stool at the bar, and let me tell u about this place. 

There are about 10 stools at the bar and most of the time they are full because the food is out of this Cajun world. I'm pretty sure anything on the menu is amazing but I can never not order the Gumbo. Prices are great and the menu has a lot of exciting options. 

I always get the Shrimp & Chicken Gumbo and my husband literally craves the Alligator Gumbo. It comes with white rice but u have the option to get the jambalaya rice...DOOOOO ITTTTT! The flavor is outstanding! The spice is just right, not too spicy but just the right amount of heat that makes u grab for a sip of water because u at lest wanna be prepared for the fury.  Tip: add a side of grilled cornbread...the cornbread is great but put some butter on it and have it grilled and u better hope u know the person beside u because they are gonna get slapped. Lol. (Today I stayed under control because there was a baby beside me with an unusually loud Jingle Bell rattle and well, that's a whole other review!) But anyway, that cornbread...melt in ur mouth, the sweet with the heat of the Gumbo is a combination u just never forget. 

I always tell people that the Gumbo with the rice is a large portion so if ur with someone that doesn't mind sharing maybe order a couple of things off the menu and do a halftime swap so u can try more. That's the advice I give but never take myself. Lol. 

And for those that think Reading Terminal Market is a little intimidating...make Becks ur reason to get into the Philly frame of mind! "No one likes us and we don't care!" So push through the crowd with purpose, stand ur ground, get that stool at the bar, and always sprinkle it with a little charm like "excuse me", it will be worth it when u taste that first bite of Becks! Happy Eating! I hope u leave loving Philly as much as I do!!

This was my first visit to this place in a long time. I went there with a buddy for happy hour. He was looking for someplace that had a little life to it and, me, I was just good and ready for a high quality beer. Trident fit the bill perfectly.

They have a real nice selection of beers on tap, with a couple of good IPA's. It's a better selection than you find at a lot of other places around town. You can score any beer on their menu for three bucks at happy hour. 

They also have a less-than-impressive five dollar food menu for happy hour. I say less-than-impressive because, looking at the regular menu, most (but not all) of the five dollar happy hour offerings are six dollars. So, basically, you get a buck off. There are better happy hour food deals around town. We tried the clam strips, which were good and crispy but all I really tasted was breading. I assume they were fresh, but being from Arizona, I wouldn't know a fresh clam if it jumped off the plate and bit me. The cocktail sauce was good and seemed to be house made. 

A glance at the regular menu piqued my curiosity with things like fish and chips, crab cakes, burgers and sandwiches - Enough so that a return visit will be warranted soon. Expect an update.

Tangent: Speaking of the menu... their menus are printed on a metal backed board and carries the weight of a street sign. I mean, these things could easily be turned into a weapon. Seems kinda risky when the alcohol may be flowing... just sayin'.
Cannoli made to order, very nice. Vanilla, chocolate or ricotta fillings.  Staff is friendly.  Nice selection of Italian pastries. Might be the best reason to stop by RTM.

Calimari, fish tacos, best clam chowder in town!!! Decent happy hour - except on game nights. No happy hour. Always a fun crowd and usually busy any night of the week. They have an awesome blue crab day in august/September that you should definitely check out.

Location: convenient in Reading terminal. Went on a Sunday and it was very crowded. 

Service: pick up your order and go. Pretty fast and no issues there. 

Food: Cheesecake was too sweet. It did not meet my standards. They definitely should not call it a NY cheesecake. There was no base or crust. It just tasted like vanilla cream. Tiramisu cake was solid. Enjoyed the flavor, but the cake could have been a bit thicker. The cannoli was my favorite. Classic cannoli and the size is quite big. Love the piping bag attached to the ceiling!

whole chicken was flavorless. I am peruvian and I was disappointed with our order. We also tried the cilantro rice and it didn't impressed me to be honest. I'm not sure if they are better at other dishes because we didn't come back. my review is on the pollo a la brasa.

There are two items that will keep me coming back to Termini Bros Bakery at Reading Terminal Market in Philadelphia, PA.  

Their Cannolis are DELICIOUS!!!!  Perfect balance of yummy Ricotta filling in a fresh crispy shell!!  Best I've had outside of Boston!
 
Their Pecan Diamond is so Sinfully Fantastic!!  This bar shaped treat is packed with yummyness, and it is worth every single calorie!!

Termini Bros is absolutely one of my "Must Visit" destinations at Reading Terminal Market.  They should be yours as well!

This place is everything you want out of a sports tavern and not a single thing more. Their menu has enough options to entertain a variety of preferences, their drink list is long enough for everyone to find something and they have enough Tv's for your game to find its place.
The absolute best cannolis EVER! I wish they had a location near where we live because they are to die for!! Every thing else they had on display looked delicious. Will definitely be back to try more

During a trip to Philly I stopped at Reading Terminal market for a quick lunch.  I'm from New Orleans so was excited to see a Cajun Cafe, though I rarely get my hopes up for Cajun food since it rarely meets my expectations outside of New Orleans.  However, I was pleasantly surprised that this place was fantastic.  I had an oyster poboy which had a great selection of good sized fried oysters on it and fresh bread.  They have a special sauce of their own creation they put on it which is less traditional, but still tasty.  It looked like a mayonnaise base with some spice in it but had a bit more vinegar flavor than I was expecting.  They also gave me a sample of their vanilla rum bread pudding and it was amazing.  I wish I had room to buy a piece of it but I was quite full after my sandwich. The person next to me ordered the gumbo and it also looked perfect, nice and thick with a traditional roux.   The server was also quite friendly and service was prompt.  I would definitely go back again next time I'm in Philly.

If this is the tattoo spot inside the mall, Tattoo Artist JOSH FRANKLIN IS A GENIUS...that's all. The atmosphere is clean; the staff, friendly; the work, AMAZING. Josh was patient with my idea and knocked it out the park with the speed and attention to detail that only a 1st Place winner has (he won 1st place at an event in Monterrey, CA)...
 
As i was getting my tattoo a female client was getting her and the female Tattoo Artist was very attentive and quick... 

If you feel the itch for ink, this is the only place...

Yelp suggested this cafe for me. So decided to try it! It was located on this cute little corner midst a residential area. The cafe has seating downstairs too. Though it looks super tiny, it can seat a lot of people.

The menu was huge- it was all squeezed onto a blackboard but surprisingly legible! They offered savory and sweet crepes, sandwiches and freshly baked choco-chip and oatmeal raisin cookies (which were not made in house).  They were ginormous and oh so soft!! 

Coffee was given to you plain, and you can walk up to the little coffee maker corner and add whatever you please.

We ordered-
Maple Ham crepe: pretty large size, over-drizzled with syrup. It was pretty tasty if you like all sweet things. But half way in, it was a little too much of the same taste.

Pesto Sandwich: has pesto, mozzarella, tomatoes and avocado. The baguette was a little too hard for my taste. Was difficult to actually bite it.

Maybe we just had bad selection of food this time, but it looked like a pretty busy little cafe on a saturday.  I would definitely return to give it another chance! But the cookies- yum yum for sure! I'd probably go back at least for one of those!

I have been hooked on Termini's cannolis since I was a child. Even in my 30's, I continue to pick up those crunchy shells filled with ricotta cheese, mini choc chips, topped with powdered sugar. Today I decided to add the mini limoncello cake to my cannoli order. I took a taste of this cake as soon as I made it home from my TB trip. The layers of cake, lemon curd and lemon cream cheese mousse are such a sweet indulgence. I will be picking this treat up more often.

First time at Termini bros, got an assortment of things. The Italian cream cake must have been stale, it smelled and tasted off, was inedible. The fig bar was hard, couldn't bite into it. Seems they might be having quality control issues during covid. The cannolis were fantastic, but I can't recommend anything else.

4.25 to be exact.

Are you a fan of spicy food? Are you walking around Reading Terminal looking for a place to eat? If you are, then I definitely suggest coming by Beck's Cajun Cafe! Having a tolerance for spicy food will definitely allow you to try some of their best dishes and have a great experience eating here.  It's good to experience some nice Southern Comfort food!  Are you skeptical on how the spiciness is?  Well the nice thing is that the employees typically give out some free samples of their dishes, so you can see for yourself before ordering one.

I was able to try three great dishes here that are all spicy and delicious:

Jambalaya Bowl:  Sausage, chicken, and shrimp with rice, peppers and Creole spices.  A very flavorful dish with a lot going on in it.  Make sure you can tolerate it's spiciness since it is present all over the dish.

Blacked Chicken Alfredo:  I personally love alfredo pasta, so I was already biased upon tasting this and really enjoyed the dish.  For the size of the dish, they give you an appropriate amount of chicken.  The Cajun seasoning on top are what gives the kick in this dish, so I would say this is a good option for people who cannot handle heavy spiciness since it is not present all around.

Gator Gumbo: This is my favorite dish here! You get a good amount of meat and rice in here, and the spiciness is all over!  You can taste the smokiness in this thick dish. Definitely make sure you try a sample of this and be ready to eat that reptile!

As a side, also try their cornbread, this is pretty good as well.

Overall, spicy faces should be all over this place! You cannot go wrong with the prices here too, so enjoy!

#1 cannoli/dessert in Reading Terminal.

My husband and I came to Reading Terminal and got a little of this and a little of that.  We both agreed the cannoli was hands-down the best food we ate.  I don't know enough about cannolis to know why.  They just are.

Eat one.  You will not be disappointed.

I was referred here by a gal at one of my companies offices. Coming from out of town I am always looking for the best Mexican restaurants! I live in California so I'm picky! We only had time for appetizers. The guacamole was good but needed salt and the queso fundido with chorizo was AMAZING! The tables salsa were delicious too but could use just a touch of salt. Service was kind of slow but I imagine the rest of their food is delicious too! I'll be back for sure next time I'm in town!
I've been coming here for years and I definitely recommend the Trident. The food is always great and they have friendly staff. Definitely worth checking out if you haven't been.

I stumbled across this place when I was standing in a 30-minute line for Dinic's, when someone working at Beck's asked my friends and I if we wanted a sample of gator. Not only was the gator cooked perfectly, but the sauce was to die for. Way to win over some customers!

This Cajun grub is as good as it gets outside of New Orleans. The fried mac & cheese balls in creole sauce are a personal favorite! The muffalettas are huge and also delicious. Anything with gator in it is good, especially the gumbo. A personal favorite is actually the vegetarian po boy, which has fried eggplant, melty ooey-gooey cheese, and an assortment of sauteed vegetables. Another favorite is the bread pudding. It has the best cinnamon flavor and comes with raisins and sliced pear bakes into it.
