Given the crowds that can line up outside of this place, food comes out pretty quickly. The staff members are always super friendly, no matter how busy they are. This is definitely worth a visit if you're in Reading Terminal!!
This was the cheapest place to get my phone fixed and they did an AMAZING job. Not only that, but the employees are kind!

I ordered a cookie tray for my daughter's wedding to be delivered to the reception hall the morning of the wedding. I was told that the driver was too busy to deliver on a Friday and that it would cost me an extra 30.00 to have them delivered the day before at a specified time. Bothe the bakery and the reception are within miles of each other. very poor customer service ! The cookies are good, but that's where it ends

I got the Ricotta Cheese Cannoli from here and it was DIVINE. Easily the best cannoli I've ever had in my life. The shell was crispy and ultra thin. It was very well fried and not oily at all. The ricotta filling was one of the best substance I have ever tasted. It was creamy and smooth, with small chunks of chocolate chips. The flavor was well-balanced and complex. The cannoli was dusted with icing powder as the finishing touch.
I loved everything about the cannoli and couldn't help but be sad when I finished it.

Had i written this review on my first visit here it would have been 5 stars. Ive been to two other Trident locations and have never had a problem. Yesterday my gf wasnt feeling well and needed to raise her blood sugar. We were shopping next door so i called in a Pick Up order for two Cod tacos. When i arrived i was in a hurry so i paid and rushed to get the food to her. The bag was given to me tied tightly so i didnt smell it but when she opened it the smell hit us like a sledge. It was bad. However, because she was in a pinch and we had eaten there before, she took a chance and ate it anyways. She got food poisoning and skin signs of elevated toxin levels. I was shaking with how upset i was. Will never return to this location. How can a chef knowingly serve that?

This place is not run well. The manager, Fred, has no respect for his employees. I witnessed him cussing out one of his teen girl employees. Not ok! The manager sits around all day not doing anything, least he could do is clean the bar while he's at it. There are better pubs around town.

Nice out post of the original in South Philly. Nothing beats the main location with samples galore, South Phiily charm and amazing products. Love this place in the terminal for all of the favorites....fresh cannolis, cookies and the outrageous chocolate covered banana with raspberry and custard creme. Pretty much one of the top five desserts in the world.

I have passed this eatery over dozens of times and my wife reminds me each time that she had eaten at this location a number of years ago and it was real bad. She said it was fast food Mexican place she had gone with her mother to.

Well of course, every time I passed this place, even though it said Peruvian chicken, I associated it with her past comments. 

Last year we had gone to VA Cuba to arrange our travel to Cuba, and since there located in the same shopping plaza she again reminded me of her past experience. So I didn't eat there. 

Shame on me and shame on my wife. Hope she doesn't get wind of this comment . Haha. OMG thank you yelpers. Based on all your great reviews, I went there for a take out order. The wife is out of town. Lucky me. Only kidding. 

I ordered the chicken with a double side of black beans. Yummy. In case the wife reads this we're  cutting down on carbs, hence no rice. Proud of me honey!

I can't wait to go back and have a sit down meal and order the lomo saltado. Of course with the wife.

The woman that completed my order, told me they have been here 3 years. They are right on point.

Run don't walk to this place. You will not be disappointed.

The cannolis were to die for - the outer shell was very crispy, the ricotta cheese filling was completely pumped into the cannoli shell and was heavenly. Also tried their red belt cake - blissful. The pecan diamond bars went great with the coffee in the Reading Terminal.

Came to reading terminal last weekend. We walked around and decided on coming to Beck's. We drove up from NYC for the day and wanted to get a cheese steak from Dallesandro's later on so we opted to share the food so were weren't busting at the seams. We shared the gator gumbo and both had a bacon, mac & cheese ball each. They gave us a sample of the gator gumbo and I was SO surprised at how bangin' it was! It does have a kick, (for people that don't like spice) but I'm assuming if you are eating Cajun you aren't worrying about that..lol. They served it over white rice. We didn't see the seats at first so we were going to find a place to eat but the girl told us to sit. The service we experienced was great that day. Everyone was friendly. While we eating, the girl gave us corn bread and said "trust me you need this" ...and boy was she right! I loveeeed the combination of the spice from the gumbo with the sweetness from the corn bread. I highly suggest getting cornbread if you like that combination! We really enjoyed our bacon, mac & cheese balls as well! I loved it and am glad we had a positive experience trying a unique food with friendly service.

 I'll be back, Beck's!!!

I have found my cannoli happy place, and it is at Termini Bros Bakery at Reading Terminal Market. When walking around Reading Terminal, Termini Bros caught my eye because they were filling fresh cannolis to order. I previously tried Isgro Pastries, marketed as the "best cannoli," but Termini Bros is where it's at.

$4 for one cannoli and they accept credit cards! (Let's just say I spent all my cash in Chinatown.) When you order, they ask if you want chocolate chips (of course!) and powdered sugar (go big or go home). Perfectly creamy, not overly sweet ricotta filling, sprinkled with chocolate chips, and in a crisp shell that holds up. Add this to my "usuals" at Reading Terminal Market!

Looking for a great budget omakase in Philadelphia? Look no further than DK Sushi in the Franklin's Table Food Hall on the Penn campus! For just $35, the meal changes slightly every day and allows the different chefs assigned to particular days to express their vision and creativity. My dinner companion, Ken, was hesitant at first on trying all the different fishes, but was open-minded enough to dive right in. Our chef, Zion, started our meals with two tried and true omakase courses - tuna tartare and hamachi ceviché - along with a special miso soup with shrimp tempura. From there, our chef churned out plates of traditional sushi, two or three pieces at a time. The sea urchin and scallops were delightful, light, and refreshing. The toro, really a chu-toro, and yellowtail toro had good flavors. I prefer fatty cuts of fish over lean cuts. The Kobe and ikura were the chef's play on "surf and turf" and were melt in your mouth good and squishy bubbles of salty delight! The toro scallion roll almost served as a palate cleanser for the intense flavors of the final dish, a miso foi gras mini hand roll and eel sushi. I could eat ten of the foie gras sushi! The incredible thing about all of the sushi is the sushi rice was warm and perfectly seasoned. Warm rice is the only way to eat sushi! Big kudos to Chef Zion for using the available ingredients to craft a very nice omakase meal.
It's in the neighborhood and very easy to access even during COVID. I think they are opened from 8 am-1 pm but their window is opened and you can order, grab, and go. Contactless, of course.

Chai tea latte had good flavor at first but very watery
Cinnamon raisin bagel has good flavor but it isn't a good bagel at all it's so thin and dense 
I like the location though and will try other things
We like the lively and casual atmosphere of this place. Food was good. I liked the fish and chips the most. Prices were reasonable.

Why 4 stars? Because this is another solid Latin eatery in West Tampa.

   ---   ---   ---

Cuenelli's was on my list for quite a while, but I was finally able to make it out. I normally order steak over chicken, but I wanted to try both since the name of the business includes "Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken" in it. 

I enjoyed my meal. It wasn't the best I've had in Tampa Bay, but it was a job well done. I thoroughly enjoy anytime I have the chance to gobble up some South or Central American goodness, and this was no exception.

Cuenelli's was my first experience
With Peruvian roasted chicken. 
For not having tried it sooner,
Myself, I'm now kickin!

I can't decide which sauce I favor
The yellow one or the green. 
I know that I wanna pour it 
All over my everything.

I get it with a side of spicy beans
Served over cilantro rice. 
So far, I've only tried their chicken
But I've only been here twice. 

The service is fast and friendly 
When I call in my order Togo. 
And now I'm craving that chicken!
I know where I must go!

This place was good, but it wasn't as good as I thought it would be. The Sides were salty. Chicken was very moist , fall off the bone, but the sauces that are very important for dipping, were a disappointing. The yellow one that I'm use to being creamier, was watery, didn't have much flavor, it just tasted salty. The cilantro rice was decent , but like I said, just a tad salty , and even the French Fries were a bit overly salted. Hey! I like salt don't get me wrong, it's a very important ingredient used to bring out the spice in food, but in this case I felt salted to death. 
Another thing that bugged me is that they are very stingy with choice of sides. I didn't want fries so why couldn't I have fried yucca instead? I did order some on the side which raised my bill another 4 bucks. Thumbs down for that. Another thing I would not have chosen is rice , but they don't offer other options with the combo meals like my favorite place Pico Rojo. If you want the good sides, you have to order them separate. Blah. 
I should have never cheated on my Pico Rojo. Oh, I loved my Passion Fruit juice, almost forgot about that. Wrapping it up, I would try this place again if I was in the area and a friend wanted to eat here, but I will not come out of my way because I wasn't very impressed. My lunch was too expensive for sides i didn't want

Sunday brunch in the city... I find it almost impossible to find a place without a wait. Thank god for Vineyard!! 
When you enter it looks like a small coffee joint, but they have seating downstairs. I love the vibe that this place has. 
Chai latte: being Indian, I'm picky about my chai. And this beats EVERYONES chai latte (even Starbucks). 
Eggs, bacon, gouda on a baguette. Light savory dish , just enough to fill you up without that heavy brunch feeling. And the baguette is soft, so you're not tearing it apart like most places! 
Nutella, strawberry crepe: one of the best crepes I've had in this city. 
The owner even came down to check if everything was okay. The food is delicious, The place is clean And the staff is friendly. What a wonderful place in Philly to grab a bite!

I have been to Trident now about 5-6 times. Here are my thoughts: 

- I like the atmosphere in here, it's very homey, comfortable, and friendly in here! 
- They have a solid beer selection 
- They always have the UA games/football on, so it's a great place to watch a game 
- From what I hear, they have great trivia! 
- the service is very good! The staff have always been very attentive. 
- Real Maryland crab served here! My Dad, a native, confirmed this with the waitress :) 

- I've had better good meals here than not, but I have had an under cooked burger and mac and cheese that was sub-par. I would recommend the stuffed mushrooms, mozzarella sticks, and chicken tenders. 

Overall, for a bar, the food here is awesome!
Everything I have ordered here to include the chicken, cilantro rice and beans have been flavourful and delicious! Customer service is great and take out takes less than 5 minutes.
My favorite spot in reading terminal market. If you like cajun food, there is a lot to love here. My personal fave is the blackened cajun chicken alfredo.

It's always fun to visit your old college stomping grounds and the bars that surrounded your adolescence. Trident Grill is exactly that for me and I hadn't been back in over a decade. I was surprised to find the place still lively, in fact it looked better than I remembered. 

A few of us mid 2000 grads bellies up to the bar and started right where we left off. How you ask? With the 10 minute challenge of course. A shot, beer and mixed drink in 10 minutes was the game over a decade ago, so why not now?! 

We also ordered a bunch of bar bites that were a lot better than I thought they'd be! I especially liked the buffalo chicken sliders, fried pickles and soft pretzel. Yum. 

If you're looking for a great little sports bar with way above average bar food, this is a no brained.

This place was due for another trip and this time it did not disappoint. The Mac and cheese was much better than previous experience and had plenty of goodness inside which is hard to achieve as most get dried out. The jumbo was delicious had plenty of spice and flavor and was overall a very good meal.

Cute cafe in the Francisville/Fairmount area that provided an awesome place for me to hole up for several hours and have lunch, take a couple meetings, and get some work done. Seating is outside or downstairs, and on a Monday afternoon, I had my choice of tables as there was only one gentleman in the entire place (nice to meet you, Andre!). 

My café au lait was perfect, and I love the help-yourself water station with large glasses. I was excited to see crêpes on the menu and went for the goat bacon with goat cheese, bacon, mushrooms, and tomatoes. The crêpe was good but I would have enjoyed it a lot more if the bacon inside was crunchy. My dining companion's pesto sandwich looked incredible and I had a bit of lunch envy. I'm definitely going to try a sandwich or omelet next time. 

The staff was really friendly and the wifi was complimentary. Definitely adding Vineyards to my rotation of spots to get some work done, and looking forward to trying more from the menu.

I've seen this place growing in Tucson for some time now and finally stopped and ate there. Well I can definitely see why they are expanding so well. It was busy and the wait time for food is a little long, but it was easy to see what took the extra few minutes to get food. It was so well made! Every detail was covered with excellence. I dont remember our server's name, but she was the best server I have ever had. The serving sizes were huge. Normally, I always finish my plate, but not this time. I had the super Reuben and it was excellent. We had a side bowl of mac and cheese that was outstanding. The prices were good and the menu is very extensive. I can see making this restaurant one of my new favorites. Truly sets the standard for how restaurants should be run.

This is my least favorite of all the Trident locations. The bartender was terrible. She was more focused on the men at the bar then the restaurant full of people. Our server was cut in the middle of a busy rush during nfl playoffs and college basketball games. We will visit the other locations for better service.

Interesting fact: Trident's owner, Nelson Miller, is a retired U.S. Navy Seal and still trains Seals at the Pinal Air Park in Marana. In fact, he knows and helped train the same Seals that tracked down bin Laden.

Trident has been proudly serving Tucson since 2001. With a pub like atmosphere and an absolutely fantastic menu, it has a full bar and 24 draughts! 

We ordered a Cuban Grilled Cheese, a Philly Cheesestake, wings and a grilled chicken pesto sandwich.  Everything was very good! Please support local businesses!

There are 4 different locations in Tucson, AZ

Folloe my instagram "jackiefrompr" for more suggestions!!!

Walked in with my 16 year year old to take advantage of the Fri the 13th special. We were shocked to see ALL ARTISTS were not wearing masks, during a pandemic. After we promptly walked out, I looked back and found one lone employee wearing a mask.

Everything here is delicious. The cannoli and chocolate mousse pastry are my favorite. The cookies are delicious. I also want to give a shout out to the clerk who was working when I went today. It was very busy and she was the ONLY employee manning the fort. She did an excellent job, despite the long line and with a super friendly attitude and smile on her face - perfect model of excellent customer service. I didn't get her name but she was tall, skinny, African American and just stellar customer service.

I was impressed with their selection of pastries and cakes that they have to offer. Strawberry shortcake, carott cake, cookies, canolis... but I was the most excited for the sfogliatelle. It made me remember the times I would eat them while visiting my grandfathers in NJ. I can't find good ones in Boston so I figured I would try here since it can't get worse than Boston. Well the sfogliatelle was great! Flaky layered crust, dense ricotta filling packed with candied citrus. Places in Boston don't get it... never enough citrus. This was great, brought me back to my childhood with my poppy :-)

5 stars for the cannoli, which is one of the best I've had since my honeymoon in Italy 3 years ago!! Perfectly crisp shell, light but luscious ricotta filling -- just glorious. Hubby went the simple route and got a cupcake and I really appreciated that they didn't drown it in frosting; I always take that as a sign that they are confident in the quality of their actual cake and that holds true here. This is a moist cupcake with a fine crumb and the right amount
Of sweetness and vanilla flavor. Perfect sweet treat while walking around Reading Terminal Market, if you are in the area grab a cannoli for sure!

I popped in here for lunch one day because I didn't want to drive far but still wanted something yummy. Cuenelli's is located in a kinda random strip center so it's definitely not located in an area where you would expect it. I say this because it might give you a bit of trouble to find it or you might think, "Is this place gonna be good? It's next to a random cell phone place (or whatever is next to it). Do yourself a favor. Go in and try it.

I ordered chicken and it came with french fries and a salad. When I say this is probably the best rotisserie chicken I've ever had in my life please don't think I'm exaggerating. This rotisserie chicken is amazing. So flavorful and moist, even the white meat (which is great because most places tend to serve dry white meat). The dressing that was with the salad was delicious also.

My only issue was that they seemed to be annoyed when they had to sit parties of 1. I mean it has to be OK for someone to just want to get away from the office on a solo mission for great food. Right? Outside of that I'm putting this place on my list for when I visit Tampa.

Honestly I dread bikini waxes (even though it's so worth it) BUT not anymore. Karen was simply the best. She was friendly and quick. She talked through what she was doing and made nice conversation . Will definitely return for her services

Went here to check out the world-famous cannolis--the line can be long sometimes, but everything moves so efficiently.

Definitely a must stop at the Reading Market as they are very tasty and only $3 a pop.

Four stars for the wonderful food and good prices! I usually get the half chicken meal with cilantro rice. Delish! The place would have 5 stars if they had better servers. One of the girls messed up my coworkers pick up order and instead of fixing it, she gave him a really hard time. It's not the first time I deal with their incompetence and lack of hospitality.

The best cannoli I ever ate. 

The best cannoli I ever ate. 

The best cannoli I ever ate. 

The best cannoli I ever ate.
Best decision I've made on food in a long time. I got 1/4 white chicken with cilantro rice and about 5 yellow sauces. It was so good I did not want it to end. Highly recommend!

Shrimp Tacos with Green Chili Mac n cheese. Food was great, service was fine, beer was cold. Can't go wrong. There was quite a variety to choose from on the menu. I was recommended to try this place for their seafood, Shrimp Tacos didn't disappoint.

Daughter-in-law and her partner took us here after our day at the Arizona Sonora desert museum (another review for that in a minute: long story short -just go! So worth it) we walked the whole place so we were hungry to say the least. We shared a couple appetizers and it was perfect. The bruschetta was good, lots of tomatoes, thin slice of mozzarella, sprinkle of basil and a good amount of balsamic glaze. Would order again. Nashville hot sliders were good, but no where near Nashville hot. Maybe Nashville Luke warm. That being said pickles were amazing. Fish tacos were fresh and great balance of fish to tortilla to toppings. Pretzels were homemade. Cheese sauce was from a can (which always has it's place next to a pretzel) mustard was nose heat spicy which hubby loved. Only odd thing was it had pepper and not salt on it. Wasn't bad, but a little weird. The girls loved the Mac n cheese. Hubby and I weren't too keen. Liquid sauce and over cooked pasta. But hey, we all have our own opinions. Lastly, Maryland crab cakes. True Maryland style in the shape of a cookie scoop with large chunks of crab. Must order if you like crab cakes.
After loving the place, they now warn you that the chickens they serve are now smaller.  It used to be great, now it's just okay.

Snagged some fried shrimp here at the end of the night while they were closing up. Super friendly staff, should've grabbed an extra corn bread. Would check it out again for the other dishes, but honestly would go back just for the cornbread!
Best fish tacos and fish and chips in town. They have an excellent beer selection as well. We love this place!

Best creperie I've come across in Philly. It's a small cafe, located on the ground floor in a new development. My first observations were that it's very clean, and that it has a neat wood decor.

They feature a tantalizing variety of savory and sweet crepes. I opted for the Honeybee
(mozzarella, scrambled egg, and spinach - finished with a honey drizzle) and then took home a Nutella/banana for dessert. Both crepes were super appetizing, well portioned, and priced appropriately.

I'll also mention the service was very friendly (two women behind the counter). And they offer free wifi!

I've been going to Trident at Williams Center since it's opening.  My Wife and I have always enjoyed the food and service that is provided by the restaurant.  The staff is generally very friendly and welcoming whenever we arrive.  There are a few members of the staff that usually recognize us and stop by the table to say hello whether or not they are servicing our table.  
But on recent visit with friends I was very disappointed in the service and attitude of our server, Marissa.  From start to finish, she gave me the impression that she wasn't at all interested in taking care of us.  Her greeting was abrupt and without even a smile.  Approaching a table with the line "can I get you something to drink" is a poor way to start a dining experience.  I took the initiative to say hello to her since she didn't even say hello first.
Next step was receiving our drinks.  Two people at the table ordered Pellegrino, both asked for lemon and one asked for very light ice.  What was delivered to the table were two plastic cups filled with ice and Pellegrino without any sign of a lemon.  She also placed the single bottle of the remaining amount on the table.  Before we were able to ask about the second bottle, she was gone in a flash.  It was a while before she returned to take orders.  Again, I got the impression that she had no desire to take care of us by her rapid order taking.  Normally I'd look around the room to see if she was weeded, but there were two other servers on the floor with a total count of about 8 tables in the room.  I'm not certain what the policy is on taking an order at Trident, but she didn't write down any of the orders (which always makes me a bit nervous).  One reason I know that the order wasn't input properly is because my Wife's special request of her food was not accommodated. 
When our food was delivered, I asked the runner for another drink which did not seem to be messaged to our server.  After a first few bites of our meal, I became impatient for my beverage.  So I excused myself from the table to go the the hostess stand and ask for my drink and extra napkins.
The napkins arrived right away, but I still had not received my drink.  Finally, my drink was delivered and I was told that "the keg ran out so here's a fresh glass of cider for you" (no apology for the delay).
This is where I should mention that I was in the restaurant business for 40 years, so I have a clear concept of good service in any style of restaurant.
I mention all of this so that my observations can hopefully be used as a training tool.  Out of the many visits to your restaurant, we've only experienced poor service on two occasions, so as I said in the beginning, we've generally enjoyed the food and service.
I'd like to mention one more thing before closing.  One constant whenever we visit is the outstanding service provided by George.  This guy never stops moving, always smiles, and is always very gracious with us when we dine there.  I've never seen a male server in your establishment, but if you ever decide to use male servers, George should be at the top of your list.
We will certainly continue to patronize Trident because we truly like it there.  So please don't think of this as a loss of business, but a tool to raise the bar of service.
Thank you.

My boyfriend and I managed to come here twice over the course of a tight weekend because we loved it so much! Got the shrimp and crawfish etouffee, various poboys, and some eggs. The red beans and rice are really just sausage + rice and some beans - they're delicious! Cornbread comes out hot and buttery (a wee sweet) so eat those before they get cold!

The portions are enormous and the staff are super friendly. I seriously don't know how they make money on those poboys, but maybe I'm just thinking of West coast prices. I could only finish half at a time! The best part of coming here for early breakfast was the conversation. With food so good, and the environment so casual, we met folks from all walks of life. And if you're not into chatting with folks, it makes for perfect people watching. 

Great vibe, food, people - what's not to like?

We stopped by Reading Terminal Market for a bite before heading to the convention center and we weren't disappointed! With all the choices of places to eat we were hooked on Beck's after sampling their gator gumbo. We took a seat at the counter. Our server Kimber was very friendly and quick with our orders. The shrimp po boy was phenomenal. My friend, who frequented NOLA to visit family, said it was one of the best po boys he had ever eaten. The gator gumbo and fresh brewed iced tea were also exceptional.

They don't allow service animals, even if you show them state Certified proof. Rude hostess and waitress. 

Disrespectful establishment. Another time we tried food and it was extremely salty

I actually used to come here all the time. I left and moved back to Tucson. When the pandemic hit, my wife and I were quickly on the look out for restaurants that could do good take out. We love to go out to eat! I remembered this Trident location from back in the day. So, we decided to order. Since then we've ordered take out at least 5 times! Why? Because they do an awesome job. Here's some of the things we've had:

Awesome,  huge cheeseburger with fries. 9/10. Cooked perfectly every time with fresh hot fries.

Fried calamari 8/10. It would be better if it was served with something other than cocktail sauce. It's still awesome for take out!

Boiled shrimp 9/10. Tasty and always served with sauce and lemons.

Seafood platter (captains platter?) 10/10. Ton of seafood all fresh and crunchy.

Cake 8/10.

We've had mixed experiences with takeout at other places. These folks are incredibly consistent with high quality and great service!

Parking is decent around 11am for lunch. They are located right across from Tampa International airport.

Inside they have 16-18 tables about 8 or so are booth the rest traditional table and chairs.  Bathrooms are clean.

This restaurant is very clean and organized, they have background music and 2 wall mounted tv's. The decor is really nice, very high ceilings, the kitchen is wide open  so you can see everything that they're doing. Smart design, the way it should be.

You come in and sit anywhere you like and the waitresses are very attentive.  They are quick to bring you a menu and your drink.

Ordered the Lomo Saltado (beef tenderloins) with white rice, french fries and a coke.  It took about 15 minutes to get the food and it was hot fresh tasted really good and it looked just like it did in the menu.  Came with grilled onions and with green/red peppers.

My only complaint is the price.  Its on the expensive side.  For just a plate of lomo, fries and rice with a drink I spent $16 (plus tips).  That's why I knocked off a star.

I do recommend if you don't mind paying higher prices.

Pricy, but you get what you pay for, which is outstanding quality.  Best cannolis.  Excellent carrot cake.  Torrone candy tastes too sweet, but cheese cake is so good.  Friendly service and easy check out.

Been here twice, the first time I got two tattoos from Adrian and the second time I had my nose pierced by Brad. Adrian is spectacular! I told him one of my tattoos was going to be Kylo Ren's mask and this man put on Star Wars for me. Quality work and overall great dude! I've had my nose pierced twice before but had to remove it for work and I can honestly say this was the worst experience I've ever had with a piercer. There was no greeting or any attempt at conversation, which is fine, but then he asked what side I'd like my piercing on and I'd told him my left since it's already been pierced. He tells me that placement is all wrong and he shows me where he would put it and all of a sudden I'm extremely unsure of what to do. So he just lets me sit there and debate the two options, without adding any additional commentary. I feel like any other piercer would make an attempt to find some middle ground or just be able to reassure me one of the placements is the right way to go. So I end up telling him if that's what he thinks is best then we should go for it. Now the actual piercing was extremely painful. He was not gentle in any way and I've had my nose pierced TWICE without nearly as much pain or blood. I ended up going back a few hours later to have it removed and hopefully repierced so it wasn't so far back on my nose. He was not thrilled to say the least and all but yanked the piercing out. There was no way I could go through having that guy pierce my nose again and I've sat through a six-hour tattoo session. 0/10. Not to mention I didn't get a full refund. They only gave me the money back on the piercing itself and not the jewelry. So I asked to have the stud since I'm paying for it and Brad said he already threw it away.
The po boys are much better since they changed to a lighter roll. Good job!

I love this place. Great food, fantastic service, great vibe, and really a unique atmosphere. I went with a staple of fish and chips and it never disappoints. You get three huge pieces of lightly buttered fish, coleslaw, and lightly seasoned old bay French fries. If you are in Tucson you have to stop in Trident Grill and get a taste of this great joint.

We found Vista thru a car we where looking at on Autotrader online. I inquired about the car for my daughter.who was purchasing her first vehicle.  
We where contacted br Chris one of the salespeople (excellent and professional and pretty honest guy). The car we wanted initially was sold the day before.  He called me twice with different options and we liked one of the cars, we went in and we had our mechanic look at the car it was a good car. Everyone we dealt with represented the company well, from Sony who gave us the history on the vehicle and what they had done to it to get ready to be sold,  to reassuring us of some minor concerns we had that the dealership would handle them. To Zully who was through and very informed about the motor vehicle process to management who made the deal happen. The whole team was solid and wanted the deal to happen and so did we. It was refreshing experience buying a car without getting a headache. Thanks Vista Auto we will come see you first for our next vehicle.

In the mood for something with a spicy kick? A little southern twang? Who's your crawdaddy? Look no further than Beck's Cajun Cafe, housed at Reading Terminal Market. 

It's smack dab in the middle of the market.

They've got a variety of menu items - the oft proclaimed Muffaletta, po' boys, étouffée, gumbo - the list goes on and on.

Curious as to what exactly I'm talking about?

Beck's personable servers will help you out there! They will give you samples of their grub. Make sure to try the gumbo and jambalaya while you order and wait - both dishes will impart you a spicy kick to the back your throat. In fact - got a cold? Go get yourself some Beck's gumbo!  

Fried Mac and Cheese ($3.95)

The GF and I started off with two ginormous-sized balls (that's what she said). Crisply fried with lightly seasoned panko and a creamy mac n cheese within - this was great. It came accompanied with a sweet tomato dipping sauce with roasted chunks of tomato. Hard to get the huge chunks of fried mac and cheese in there though!

1/4 Muffaletta ($5.95)

A muffaletta is both a round Sicilian sesame bread and the popular sub from New Orleans (uses the Sicilian bread of course!). Cut into quarter slices, these things are immense. Stuffed with salami, ham, and mortadella, you've got a meaty bite to look forward to. Be prepared though - the olive salad within is expectedly salty. The sharp nutty, funky provolone tries to assuage the saltiness, but just barely fails. The bread is the perfect vehicle to house everything though.  

Blackened Chicken Po Boy Wrap ($7.25)

The GF opted for the po boy in wrap form. The chicken was nicely seasoned and the mayo had a nice spicky kick. The pickles helped to elevate the wrap with a vinegary tang and crunch.

Train Wreck Po Boy ($7.95)

But the real reason I came to Beck's? To get a bite of their Train Wreck, a cheese steak on crack. Andouille sausage, steak, salami, cheese, and fried onions are all stuffed into this monstrosity. This iteration of a Philly cheese steak actually integrates the cheese really well (apparently hard to do for most Philly institutions). It's got a nice spicy kick on the tip of your tongue, rather than on the back of your throat. It's coma-inducing (in a good way!) and a definite re-order (not just a must order)! That's right - you may as well order two. The one fault? The bread is quite airy so might benefit from being toasted or grilled on the outside.

Overall, Beck's is a sure-fire bet for good, spicy food that will leave you filled and asking for more. I love Tommy Dinic's but if you're looking for something outside of the box with some kick - check out Beck's Cajun Cafe.

Waitress that served us at 2:00pm was great. Pretty much got ignored after shift change. (4pm) Asked the waitress with the long curly blond hair to send our server over and she just said "sure" expected her to see our empty glasses and take care of us. But no, we waited another 20 minutes and just left. Empty glasses still on the table.
Love this little neighborhood spot!  Food is great (good quality and prices), their outdoor area is so cute, and the staff are always extremely friendly.  Lucky to have them in the 'hood!

this is now the second time I've dined here while in town. The first time was awful. The waitress was nice but a little ditsy. Not really her fault but the kitchen under cooked our burgers. Asked for medium well, came back medium rare at best. Not really what i'm looking for in ground beef.
Okay, it was a fluke, so i tried it again.
Went in to the bar, last night. Had two friends with me. We ordered beers after having to wait for the waitress to finish eating and telling the other employees "i don't give a F***" 
We were starving so we asked for menus, then after another ten minutes of them serving 3 other people we paid for our beers and left. No one took our order, even though I tried to get the bartenders attention. I've tried this place, I wanted to like it. Not coming back... sorry mr. gallegos.

Interesting market to go visit
Fun to walk around and try/eat the delicious diversity of food!

I'm not sure how the situation is now but before the pandemic it was crowded and fun to explore the market. 

Be safe y'all
Love this spot. Our new 'regular spot' while we are in town. Super kind staff. Love the bar/restaurant environment and how relax the vibe is.

If I could leave less than 1 star, I would. Yelp says they are open until10, but apparently they close at 830 when we came in. The hostess had to check to make sure it was ok to seat us. We apologized and said it was ok if it was too late. She said it was fine. We sat down and ordered an appetizer, 2 alcoholic beverages as well as our meal for 4 people. The jerk servers slammed my water down before we even had a chance to order. They blatantly told us that they close at 830 and we were basically a problem for them. Once I said to cancel our order so we can leave (why the F am I going to pay for a waiter to be a jerk to us?!) the manager came over to ask what was wrong. I explained the situation to him, which he apologized for. Overall, the staff were complete jerks and hated that we were there. That's what you're getting paid for!!! To serve your customers. But we were immediately felt like we were a burden and a chore. I don't care if we were coming in at closing (which we didn't know, get your hours right on your website), you should still treat your customers better than that
Fantastic cannolis that are arguably the best in the city (the other being Isgro). However, everything else they sell is honestly average.  Bottom line - come for the cannolis and forget the rest.

I have not gotten anything here besides the Cannoli with Ricotta Cheese and Chocolate Chips. I have not felt the need to get anything besides the Cannoli with Ricotta Cheese and Chocolate Chips. It's one of the best cannoli's I've ever eaten, and although pricey at $4 a pop, is quite large and has a taste and texture that's worth every penny. Filled to order, you can tell that the ricotta is fresh from every bite. The outer shell is perfectly crispy, while the filling is rich but not overpoweringly sweet. Most likely to please anybody, whether your sugar tooth is large or small. Maybe I'll try one of the vast variety of small cakes and pastries they have to offer next time. Maybe...

My boyfriend and I ordered the Train Wreck Po Boy at the recommendation of someone sitting at the counter.  He said he had ordered this sandwich several times in the past and just couldn't say enough about it.  We decided to take his word for it.  We ordered one and split it and got a small side of the Jambalaya to share as well (we had to save room for Bassetts ice cream).  The patron that recommended it got his and ate half of it and took the other half to go before ours came out, so I didn't get the opportunity to thank him for steering us in the right direction.  This sandwich was AMAZING!  It packs a lot of flavor and I swear every bite is better than one before it.  The Jambalaya was also very good.  We have been to a lot of the eateries at the RTM and so far this one is the best hands down.  We will definitely go back, and SOON!
Worst coffee I ever tasted. The coffee tasted like dirt and she had an attitude and the inside is closed because of covid.

A great bakery with some definite 5 star items.

The cannoli - 5/5. One of the best I have had in Philadelphia. The shell was nice and crispy and the ricotta filling was the perfect texture, and the chocolate chips were a nice touch. Worth the price in my opinion.

Tiramisu cake - 5/5. Perfect layers to the cake in just the right proportion. One of the best tiramisus I have ever had. Also worth the price.

Other desserts - 3/5. I have tried the cheesecake and the limoncello desserts here, and was a little disappointed. The cheesecake was a touch too sweet and the limoncello was a little underflavored and stale. These items were also a little pricey for what you get.

The South Philly location is a little better, but this location is just so convenient. Overall though, definitely worth coming for a cannoli or to get the tiramisu cake. Would be 5 stars for just those 2 items.

Burger was juicy and their most popular dish (fish and chips) would put the British to shame. The service was great and the servers were very friendly. We inquired about the $27 challenge burger (which has to be finished in 15 mins for it to be on the House) but there weren't any pictures on the menu to gauge the size. My only recommendation would be to include the pic so it attracts more of a fanfare.

The food was great. Fish & chips was delicious. Very large portions. I saw on a yelp review to try the mozzarella sticks, they were average out of the box. Clam chowder was amazing. My son tried the food challenge and failed but it was fun. We were all very happy with our experience and will be back!
Awesome staff, great food. Love the bloody Mary and wings.  Have visited several of their locations and always great service and tasty food.
Best red velvet cake I've had. They accommodated a last minute order from my husband... which we really appreciated!

This is a great place to hang out with friends and catch whatever sports thing is on. My sister introduced me to this place since the owner is affiliated with the Navy. We have always had great food and really good beer. I am not a beer drinker but their selection of ciders and beer plus cider mixes is fantastic! It can get crowded on the weekends but the wait is well worth it.

Every single time I go to Philadelphia, Termini Bros is a must go to spot. Their cheesecakes are truly heaven sent and the pricing is very reasonable. I typically go to the location in the Reading Terminal Market. It's always buzzing with excitement. If ever in Philly, you must check them out!

Paid $8 for a salmon bowl the size of the yoghurt cup. It would've been more acceptable if the quality was absolutely mind blowing, but it was just alright. The salmon itself wasn't terribly fresh. It's comparable to the quality of the salmon in the dining halls in the salmon bowls there. 

The packaging was really fancy though and I'm sure that's where most of the value comes from.

AMAZING!!

i really wanted to try out the Gumbo from Beck's- so even after a huge breakfast, i sat down at the booth and asked for a bowl. the lady behind the corner was soooooo adorable and sweet. she asked if i wanted cornbread and had me try the crawfish rice. the cornbread was a little dry and dense, but it was nice of her to give it to me for no charge. 

the Gumbo was perfect. chunky, soothing and spicy. every sip and nibble i had of that stuff was pure electric heaven. i have dreams about this Gumbo every time i think of Philly. 

despite the FAIL in cornbread (which they really should improve on pronto!), the genuine sweetness of the lady and deliciousness of the entrees makes it worth while.
Trident Grill is simply amazing. The pricing is reasonable. Every thing was terrific and tasty. The crew was really pleasant and service is wonderful. Trident Grill - So good!

If this is Mexico City type food, we're in trouble. I ordered two soft carne asada tacos. As basic as it gets. The meat was tough and full of gristle.  The beans were tasteless and the service was meh. The waiter didn't want to be bothered even though the place was basically empty. Nothing memorable here. Look elsewhere for good Mexican food and better service in Tucson.

A long, long time ago, in a land far, far away, lived three men who dispite hailling from three different kingdoms, became brothers in their quest for neverending adventures and explorations in an island kindom called Hawaii. First there was Col. Bruce, a stout but devilishly handsome fellow from the kingdom of Cheesesteakville on the eastcoast area of the American Kingdom. 
Then there was Herr Bernhardt, a daring cliff diver from the Bavarian Kingdom. And last but not least there was E'lan, a carefree soldier from the army of the Kingdom of Israel. The three men met while each one were pursuing the hand of the same fair Hawaiian Princess, the lovely Frances Pulawa of Popakoleia. 
Col. Bruce struck first with lyrics from legendary singers and poets from his land like the Duke named Barry White and Sir Marvin of Motown and a young Prince from the Purple Regions. Herr  Bernhardt interupted with a promise to name his next death defiying leap from the cliffs of the Kingdom of Molokai to be dedicated to the fair Princess. 
Not to be undone, E'lan promised to forgoe his life as a soldier to spend it in her arms. But  alas, the three men's efforts were wasted, because the fair Princess Frances chose the hand of a man who had great political ambitions in tha Kingdom of Hawaii.  His name was Prince Mufee, and he appears later on after being crowned Mayor of his kingdom in a photo diplayed by Col. Bruce on his Yelp page.
  The three men became instant  friends and shared many fantastic adventures in the Kingdom of Hawaii for a while. When it was time for each man to return to his kingdom, they made a blood oath to meet again on the milliniun in the Kingdom of America in the parish of New Orleans during the festival honoring the return of the Zulu King and Queen called Mardi Gras. 
Sadly, this promise was never kept and they never saw one another again. so I never got to go to New Orleans and experience the food, but yesterday I got a chance to have a cajun meal at where else? The Reading Terminal Market.  
Beck's Cajun Cafe is located in the rear of the terminal where a lot of business's fail. That's why i always enter the Reading Terminal thru the rear sevice entrance, it makes me feel part of the place. I walked up to the counter and a nice lady with a sharp, short haircut greeted me nicely and offered some samples of their food. Everything I tasted was great and I ordered a bowl pf the Black Eyed Pea vegetable soup and a big, triangle shaped sandwich called a Muffaletta and a dessert called a Beignet. 
The soup was delicious and hearty, spiced just right. The Muffaletta was good if you don't try to compare it to a Hoagie and the Beignet was powdery shot of heaven. Next week I want to try out some more Cajun dishes here and I can hardly wait until i finally reach New Orleans.

My friend and I happened upon Ruth Chris and decided to try it, as both of us heard of the great reviews. She had a chicken dish and raved about the tenderness. I had salmon and mashed potatoes, which were tasty, but nothing special. My biggest compliments involve the lobster bisque and service. The bisque was by far the best I've EVER tasted. I raved about it for the entire night and have thought about it sereral times, since leaving the restaurant. I've searched the net to see if it's sold in stores, with no luck. The service was exceptional. Looking forward to again tasting the lobster bisque.

Let me start by saying I am from the pacific North West so I have very high standards on seafood. Sorry but this place did not make the grade for me. Started out with the clam chowder, so bland, no clam flavor here just tasted like potato soup. On to the seafood platter, everything was over fried. Tough calamari and super tough shrimp. Fish was OK but way to much breading for me. The plate was covered with to many fries, not enough  seafood for the $20. they charged. I doubt if I will be back.

I had a delicious cannoli from here and it was perfect! SO good, wish I could have another one right now. However, giving it 4 stars and not 5 because the girls working behind the counter were not very good. They both had awful faces on and acted like it was a true chore to get me the cannoli. But damn was that cannoli amazing!

My previous chicken rotisserie eating experience was at Pico Rojo in the clearwater area and I absolutely enjoyed it. Was in the west tampa area, driving past Cuenellis and decided to stop by and I am glad I did. Had to order the chicken and got a side of the fried green plantain and cilantro rice. The chicken was flavorful and moist which is a very difficult combination to maintain. Finished off my meal with a very well made flan. Will definitely be back to try out the ceviche.

This is closer to four stars.  When I eat a full meal, I will re-review.

We went in for Happy Hour.  They have an amazing happy hour.  $2.50 drafts.  Awesome.  

They also have select amount of appetizers for $5.  We tried the wings, the canteen, and the calamari.  The wings were good, decent size.  The canteen is filet on bread with a horseradish sauce.  The filet was cooked as asked, but the bites were put into a large amount of bread.  Too much bread.  But the horseradish sauce made up for it.  That was delish.  The calamari were good as well.  The breading was surprisingly light, and they were not over cooked. 

 I will probably be returning.

Always been a fan of La Parilla.  From the trio of salsas that come with the free chips to the margaritas, everything here has been the same year after year (and I've been coming here for 10+ years).

We prefer the Speedway location.  The last time we came to this Oracle location, our food wasn't very hot or seasoned well.  Rather than dock another star I'll let it slide...off day maybe.

Both restaurants offer plenty of parking and great food.  I recommend the #39 Parrillada Mixta.  One of my favorite entrees to order from any restaurant I have *ever* been to.  Carne asada, chorizo, grilled green onions, mini cheese quesadilla and pinto beans...ugh!  I want some right now but I live in Cali (sob).

Have had multiple things here at the Reading Terminal location: jambalaya, gumbo, Train Wreck, breakfast po' boy. Have not yet tried the famed Mac n cheese balls, but you better believe it's next on my list. 

Train Wreck is the highlight, with sausage and cheesesteak and many other yummy toppings. Pretty darn good. 

Also the breakfast po' boy is a solid value at 4 bucks and change for a hefty 'wich.

Both the muffaletta and the train wreck po boy were out of this world delicious. The cajun fries were slamming and the bread pudding was magnificent. So glad they are in the terminal as I am tired of the Amish food and the roast pork sandwiches.

I've only been to Trident on Friday's during their infamous karaoke nights. The bar is small, and when I've been it gets super busy. If you're not into some accidental hand grazing, then this place is not for you. However, if you are, then it's a blast. It's pretty fratastic on a Friday night, which was really no problem for me- but may be annoying for a local. Drunky monkeys sing their fave songs via the karaoke lady, and everyone gets down and in on the fun. The drinks are moderately priced. $4 for a vodka/soda/lime. However, the service is slow and if you're a girl do not goto the girl bartender. Always opt for the guys. The one time I went to the girl that's always there, I waited for what seemed like hours (but obvi wasn't) to get one cocktail. This provoked me to order 2 at a time, which may be your best bet on a busy Friday if you're trying to get the job done, anyways. The weird thing about this place is that it's always lit up. There is no dimmed light, no soft light, but instead bright bulbs in your face at all hours of the night. This was awkward for me the first couple of times I went, but then I realized it was a blessing in disguise... (there's never an excuse for hooking up with a skeezer) I liked the crowd and the karaoke, but the service and space could be better.

I have only ever visited Trident Grill for late night drinks. I had no idea how popular this location was for dinner. 

They have classic bar food options but now they also offer healthier alternatives. I was very pleased with my variety of fish tacos. Someone at my table ordered a Paleo bowl. It was colorful and plenty of food. I will definitely be back to try a Paleo bowl myself. The warm pretzel appetizer was a must try. 

Overall, the servers were polite and knowledgeable. Go check out Trident Grill for more than just drinks!

Judging from other reviews, we must have really hit them on an "off" night. To set the scene, it was a Tuesday night in a college town with no real games on TV and the restaurant was about 50% full with business. We thought we were off to a good start coming here... 4-star Yelp reviews, a spunky greeting from the waitress and prompt beer delivery. The positive experience stops there. We ordered the chicken skewers and mozzarella sticks to start... but apparently they thought we were ending with our starter too. It took 30 min. for the appetizers to reach our table. When they finally came out, we were given the sticks but also pickle spears (not what we ordered) so they took those back. The chicken skewers were finally delivered in another 15 min. but by then were hangry and wanting to leave. We concluded our dining experience at the Trident as soon as we could and headed over for some ice cream to soothe the remaining hunger pangs.

Yum! My friend who used to live in Philly swore by Termini's cheesecakes and pastries. I had to bring my friend here before we left the market to get some treats for his train ride back to NY later that day. He got the cheesecake, and tried a piece (couldn't wait!) and loved it. I opted for a lobster tail and a piece of the pecan bar. The pecan bar is super rich and I could only eat a quarter before tucking the rest away for later. The lobster tail is yummy, crisp, creamy, and sweet. 

I do wish they had their cannolis at this location- they were not visible at all in their bakery case. The case itself is so much fun to look at, since everything looks so good! My two treats were 8.00, a little pricy, but yummy and a nice treat to bring home.

Excellent coffee. The pastries are terrific and the owner is a joy to deal with. A truly neighborhood type of place. 

Did I mention the coffee was great! I'll be back. No pretense here.

I wanted to hate Philly Dawgz.  

I loathe the utilization of the letter "z" to replace my beloved "s" when pluralizing a word.  I despise restaurants that can't seem to get some coherence to the menu(Philly Dawgz boasts a diverse menu whose sections include: hot dogs, Italian beef sandwiches, Austin BBQ, and Latin Flavors).  

Needless to say, my first impression of the establishment was not good.  

I tried the Chicago Style Fully Dressed Philly hot dog, described as a "100% Vienna Beef Dawg stuffed in a poppy seed bun topped with yellow mustard, neon green relish, diced onions, tomato wedges, pickle wedge, sport peppers and a dash of celery salt."

It sounds great until you take a bite out of it.  I was ridiculously underwhelmed.

That being said, I decided to give them another shot and try their bbq beef sandwich.  They offered to put any of their toppings on it, which was very cool.  My chosen toppings were onion, tomato, and jalapeno pepper.  It was pretty darn good and earned this establishment a 3-star review.  The spicy rice side was OK.

on the action-movie-parallel-satisfaction-scale, this establishment is Romeo Must Die.

After trying the cheesteaks and roast beef sandwiches at the market, make a stop here for the Trainwreck. We preferred it's meaty, spicy, greasy goodness to the iconic cheesesteak sandwich because it was packed with flavor.     The portion size was good enough for two of us to share for lunch. Try to down the sandwich quickly because the grease can make it soggy if it is sitting out a long time. We also got the beignets which are served on Sunday. I felt the doughnuts were a bit chewy because of the dough but my dining partner loved them. The sweet tea rounded everything off nicely and was a good way to wash down the lunch. Cajun is not a cuisine that instantly comes to mind when you are visiting Reading Terminal Market, but the wonderful flavors in the sandwiches served at this place is worth giving it a shot.

Went out to trident grill for the first time last night. It's a cozy sports bar with well sized menu. I was so impressed by the good and services we had a lovely waitress named Aida that went out of her way to make sure we were happy. The food was delicious. The drinks were fantastic. I would definitely recommend and will be returning!

One of the best Bars in town!  I don't think I've ever met anyone who hasn't liked Trident! 

Great location and close to the UofA.  During the school year you get a ton of College kids, but there is still a great mix of people that end up at Trident.  Fun atmosphere.

You can purchase your own stein, leave it at the bar, and drink from it every time you are there!  :)

After looking over some other reviews...I feel as though I may have gone to another steakhouse!  

I've been to Ruth's Chris twice, both times ordering the same meal; the porterhouse for two with the sweet potato casserole.  The first time I went was during Restaurant Week but decided to order off of the normal menu, which ended up being the best food choice I've made in my life.  We ordered the steak medium rare and it came out bloody red and cut into individual serving sizes.  The server then selected a piece for each of us and served it on plates that were heated to around 450 degrees.  

We were able to watch our steak cook before our eyes... there is almost nothing quite as beautiful as watching a piece of perfect steak cooking.  The steak was so tender that I was able to cut through it with the side of my fork and it literally melted in my mouth.  I wish I were exaggerating because then I wouldn't have such a high standard for the steakhouses I go to!

The sweet potato casserole is practically a dessert.  Whipped sweet potato's mixed with walnuts and caramelized.  Well worth the ala carte price!  

Perhaps the porterhouse is the only good steak they have?  I don't know and I'm not sure if I'll ever find out otherwise!

The only reason I'm not giving this a 5 is because I haven't been to every steakhouse the city has to offer yet... but I'm getting there.

Terrific, cozy neighborhood cafe that looks very unassuming but has much to offer. The coffee is from la Colombe, so you know it's good, and the food is desirable as well. The menu is rather expansive for the size of the shop and they manage to do everything well from the sandwiches to the crepes. I highly recommend checking it out. Don't forget to check out the extra seating in the basement, but the outdoor seating is just perfect for the season!

Best Cajun food I've had outside New Orleans!

Gumbo is just right with good flavor and spice.  A lot of people told me to try the trainwreck po boy, and the Muffalatta looked great.

Simple, quick service. Beignets only available select days...Sunday being one of them, but they were all gone by the time we got there at 2pm. Next time we'll have to come for breakfast.  Very curious to see if they're even close to Cafe du Monde.

I was, you know, semi-impressed. Great beer selection, interesting menu items for a bar. Crab night, oysters. Tucson really does have it going on!

Then I was neutral, then pissed off (SCREAMING BABY! SCREAMING BABY IN MY EAR! MAIM THE BABY! KICK THE BABY!), then WaY happy. It was a rocky ride, but it ended up oh-so-smooth. 

My friends had won two gift cards, to total $30, but the register would only take one at the end (the little one, I think: $20 and $10. I THINK.). Manager came over and Applebees'ed (you know, sat down, shot the ... poo ... made us feel part of the fam. No me gusta.). 

My friends were just going to swallow it, but GIFT CARDS ARE GIFTS. THEY DON'T EXPIRE. IT'S LIKE, "HERE. I BOUGHT YOU THIS!" and then TAKING IT BACK. I got a little pissy, but this is my friends' hangout, and I just moved here, so I didn't want to be "that girl." Which I am. But I shut up. I'm a good friend!

I mean, without the gift card, we were only missing like $11, and we had feasted. 
(Oh, L.A., how I love you, but man, I'm so not broke here.)

Anyway, my friends were coughing it up, and I was grumbling but digging in my pockets. 

Then, it happened. The server (sweet blonde chica) came over and said they had reissued us a new card. 

They did the right thing! How cool is that? It's cool. It's right. It's tight. Way to go, Trident. I shall return.
Great place for men to get eyebrow threading! Ruby is fantastic and does a great job! So glad I found this place in citrus park.  Highly recommend her!

The 5-star rating is solely for the bread pudding. I've never had anything else from here, although I am meaning to. Words cannot express the love I have for this bread pudding (always with the whiskey sauce!!!). I actually seriously considered just getting a tray of it for my bday. The times that I have come here, everyone has been really sweet. I like that they offer samples of the various entrees.

I have never eaten poboys and am glad that Beck's was the place I had them. I had the shrimp poboy and cajun fries and the shrimp was crisp . It was great. Husband had the Jambalaya and could not stop raving about it.  Next time, I am back in Philadelphia, will definitely make sure to stop at Beck's. Please open a location in NJ please :) 

Definite try : Jambalaya, Poboys

I am not quite sure why there are always such rave reviews for this place....I have never found that their cakes match the reviews.

Taste:  I got one of their classic layer cakes and was sorely disappointed with its taste.  The frosting was crunchy and grainy - not smooth and delicious as I would have hoped.  The cake itself was a little dry and overall flavorless.  I have gotten a few other cakes in the past and do not remember the exact type, but I do remember always being disappointed and wishing I had spent my money somewhere else.

Price:  Don't get me wrong, I am happy to pay a decedent dime for a delicious treat - but here you will pay a decent dime for something not good at all.  I thought that the price and reputation show a quality cake is made here - but I have tried at least three cakes here and never found it to be a good deal.

Service:  It is sometimes difficult to get the attention of the people behind the counter - they like to chat with each other.  They are nice enough when you know what you want to order, but they are not too helpful in providing recommendations.  When I asked for help the woman responded with a very lackadaisical attitude - she wasn't excited about making a sale nor the cakes she is selling.  Additionally I asked her to write something on the cake and once I got it home I realized that she had written on the cake upside down - the writing on the cake and the flowers on the cake were facing different directions so that something was always upside down.

Overall:  Too expensive for being untasty.  Go somewhere else.

Food: 3.5
Service: 3
Value: 3.5 

Good cajun cuisine seems difficult to come by in Philly. Their po'boys are good, but I'm not sure I can put them above other offerings in the Philly area. It's a worthwhile enough stop if you are trying to eat your way across Reading Terminal, and they certainly beat out the cheesesteak offerings in that regard.

EVERYTHING I have ever ordered is delicious, no BS.

I am a weekly lunch regular here. I am a huge Redskins fan and I have never been here during a game, hopefully one day. 

I would recommend the Buffalo Chicken Salad, The Voo Doo Daddy Burger, The BLT, and the Cheesesteak. Sometimes they make a Cajun Philly and that is just stupid, it's so damn good.

The food is excellent
It's a Redskins fan hangout
It's owned by a local armed forces veteran
The service is usually good

So GO eat there!!

The girls who work there started cleaning up well before the closing time turning chairs upside down on tables to be unwelcoming. We came in about 15-20 mins before closing and they declined us. Why? Because they already cleaned up. 
It's bad business practice to clean up before the store is closed. To be open but appear completely closed. The owner should really reconsider who he hires.

I've been in love with this place for years. Haven't been in for a while and was afraid they had updated their menu. But they hadn't. I had my all time fave, peel-n-eat shrimp steamed in Old Bay with a side salad. Washed down with a Black n Tan. 

The service was quick, friendly and efficient.
Family was stopped at the door due to wearing shorts and sneakers.  No problem with that.  But the man of the couple behind us was admitted wearing shorts and sneakers.  Double standard?

Ate at the new location on swan today.  Decor was nice and modern. Food was okay, but nothing special. Had the green chili turkey melt.  It was good, but wasn't impressed. The irish egg rolls were a pleasant surprise. Pretty good, but overpriced considering you only get 4 for 8$. This location just opened I believe yesterday. Service was great, but took approx. 40 minutes to get our food and they were only moderatly busy.  Overall, I'd go again, but probably wouldn't be my first choice in Tucson.

The philly cheesesteak is amazing. The girls are always amazing with the service. All the food we have ever had there is good. When in town, I always come here. Great food, beers, lots of TV's for watching sports.
This place features superior rotisserie chicken and other Latin specialities. Great service and good prices complete the story. Recommended on all counts.

I agree with Joy G.  The cannolli are filled to order, the taralli are the real deal, sfolliatelle,  EVERYTHING is delicious and amazing.  Be sure to order in advance for holidays like Xmas and Easter - they get BUSY.

Can't wait to visit the original location.

The food here is great. I had jambalaya and chicken gumbo, plus a collard green on the side to go on the train. They are really good. Even better is their service. I left my credit card at their counter, and found out after 2hrs train ride from Philly. I called, they found my card and the director of catering personally sent my card out that day. I received it after 2 working days! I will definitely go back there next time I take train to Philly and thank them personally.

Every person has their own special story about this institution. My personal favorite is when a baker sexually assaulted a sales girl in the basement. When word got back to thenowners, they tried to ship her off to another location so they could keep the baker because he was a good worker. When she said she didn't want to be transferred, they put the decision on whether or not to let him go on HER (probably hoping she'd say no). When they fired him, they victim-shamed her and forbade her from speaking to any male employee. She moved away a few months later and when she did, they IMMEDIATELY rehired the pervert who assaulted her in her workplace. If you want the best cannolis you'll ever have made by the worst people you'll ever meet, Termini Bros is your spot!

What a surprise! Great food service and drinks. Established very mature Mexican food. Cost efficient; great price to value. The sauces and moles are show their experience. Not in the most upscale areas of Tucson. But if you like great Mexican food, this is the place.

I have visited this restaurant several times but last Sunday was my last time. I had  ordered take out and when I got home I discovered that two orders of cilantro rice were severely undercooked. When I called the restaurant, they said they couldn't do anything about it unless I brought it back and that the manager would call me.  I waited for 3 days and never got a call back.  Another annoying policy they have is regarding which sides you can pick when you order any combo dinner.  God forbid you get two orders of maduros on a family combo!  They have lost me as a customer.

Yes!! So good! Cuenellis is near my work and it's such a great place to get lunch. I always get their 1/4 chicken with two sides. They have other items on the menu but not a whole lot. I wouldn't come here if I was craving a Peruvian food because of that- but if you're looking for rotisserie chicken, this is IT. Service can be really hit or miss depending how busy they get. During a rush you may wait a while to flag down a server.

Being from the north, this was my first time trying cajun food. I got the chicken and shrimp gumbo with jambalaya. Since I've never tried either, I figured why not try them together? And a cornbread. I'm a lover of spice so I added a decent amount of hot sauce to it (which is really good) and that made it perfect. My favorite meal I've had in Philly so far (yes, even more than the cheesesteak). It seemed a tad high in sodium, but other than that I have no complaints. The cornbread was also great. I'm going to try the gator next time.
Love this place! Super fresh food, excellently prepared. The hot sauce rocks! Definitely pick up a bottle. Had breakfast and lunch here several days in a row, never disappointed. I will be back.

After reading mouth watering reviews of the train wreck PO boy I had to try it and it did not disappoint. Full of meat paired perfectly with the sauce and fresh bread. I kept saying mmmm after every bite!
Been a weekly visitor for the past 3 months, always a great go to for wings and fries. Conveniently located, great bartenders, and always have sports on.

Chalk this up as yet another deeply satisfying gem in The Reading Terminal Market. I give the above rating even without having tried their signatures like the near-legendary Trainwreck Po Boi, and the idea that I have so much more to explore is exciting. 

What have I had? My first time there, I just got a basic order of jambalaya with tomato Creole sauce to test the waters, and it was delicious. The portions of shrimp, andouille, and chicken were all balanced and generous, and each was the exact texture I'd have hoped for it to be, while the peppers, onions, and celery all left distinct imprints on the overall flavor, which was not lacking. 

More recently, I returned and ordered a blackened catfish platter and that was even better. I got mine with red beans and rice, and it default came with two slices of cornbread. Everything about it nailed the landing, as it were. The catfish was tender and bursting with flavor. It started off feeling pretty spicy (not to excess, but noticeable) and then my palette adjusted to it and it became a tad less noticeable, while no less flavorful. The beans and rice were hearty and savory, with tasty bits of pork mixed in, while the cornbread as fantastic - on the sweet side, but also perfect for sopping up additional blackened juices from the main event. 

I've been a bit less impressed by the service, but keep in mind I've only ever gotten taken (unfortunately). The first time I went I felt like it ruined the employee who served me's day by simply being there - a very aloof vibe was given off. But things are trending in the right direction for me now - the second time the service left me feeling neutral, with even nods to friendliness. 

All told, I'm mostly just eager to keep exploring that menu.

Oh Beck's, I like you. I really, really like you. I like you so much that you're one of my top 3 favorite RTM vendors thus far.

FOOD:
Gator Gumbo w/ Jambalaya Base ($7.95): Damn good. The texture of the rice was perfect, there was plenty of meat (especially shrimp and sausage), and in every creamy spoonful, you could taste the bold flavors and spices come together. I have no complaints and would order it again for sure.

Gator Sausage ($8.50/ea): Spicy, tender, and flavorful. The casing has a nice "snap" to it when you take a bite, while the spices are well balanced. It came on a stick and with a container of mustard that, in my opinion, only overpowers the sausage. It's good as is.

Train Wreck Po Boy ($9.95): We were thinking of ordering a cheesesteak from another vendor, but I'm glad we opted for this po boy instead. It's packed with plenty of chopped steak, salami, andouille sausage, onions, and melted cheese that binds and makes everything creamy. The bread they use is soft and the perfect vessel for the meaty filling of this nicely sized po boy.

VERDICT:
So, so close to being a 5-star rating. However, Beck's loses a star for the gator sausage. As much as I like it, I don't think one link is worth $8.50. If I only knew the sausage on its own (on a stick) costs the same as the Gator Sausage Po Boy, then I would have ordered the po boy instead. Nonetheless, I'll be back.

We have grown to like this place - even with it being a Redskins bar.  Food has been for the most part good but the service is consistently great.  We've stopped in a few times before UA football games and even when they're very packed we can always get a beer while we wait for a seat.  We went in last week for dinner and again the place was full as everyone was rooting for the Cardinals game.  I misread an item on the menu and accidentally got the Diablo Calamari thinking it was a spicy fried calamari, it wasn't.  The calamari was sauteed in a spicy sauce and very off-putting to me.  I apologized to the server and without batting an eye she quickly had it replaced with the fried calamari.  The spicy sauce turned out to be bland anyway but we moved on to a burger and it was delicious.  I asked for a side of jalapenos and I got a bowl of them!  Even better.  They have a good selection of beers and wings are good too, we'll be in Sunday in our Philly gear lol

The food was very well prepared!  Everything had great flavor and the Cajun fries were so good!  The staff was very pleasant and made sure all the food met our expectations!  A must try if you enjoy food Cajun food
Can never go wrong with Termini Bro's! Bought some tiramisu this last weekend and was so happy to see that they were busy with customers. Great and classic bakery!

This food stall in the Reading Terminal serves up one delectable oyster po' boy, a large sandwich stuffed with lettuce and pickles and a spicy tartar sauce. On top of it all are the plump, fried oysters of the name. The sandwich bread is way better than the authentic Nola bread that always tastes stale and has the texture of mothballs. Beck's bread has a nice crust and soft interior, perfect to sop up the tartar sauce. Unlike the gumbo and some of the other foodstuffs sold in the heated trays, the po boy is done fresh and tastes like it. My only complaint would be that for $12.95, they could have thrown on more oysters--hey, you ain't fooling this gal with all that stuffing of lettuce and pickles, however delicious the whole combo was. However, the four large ones on the po' boy were definitely plump and juicy. Becks has other Cajun and Creole foods like gator po boys and mac and cheese, which I didn't try. I tasted the gumbo and thought it was a mite too salty. Becks sells takeout on one side and has a retro looking ounter on the other if you want to sit and eat your meal in the frenetic environment of the market.

I have pasted the following past review of another restaurant experience relating to this owner. Come to your own conclusions. After reading from other YELPERS what seems to be a habitual disregard of the public.
 
See Bottom of review for a received message from another Yelper...

The original review was from another of Poon's past disasters, SINCE CLOSED.

UPDATE** Never received any reply...AWFUL PLACE -  BAD CUSTOMER SERVICE. What a shame that the owner must think he is too important to reply to a bad experience a paying customer had in his house. Oh well. Live and learn. Spend your money in some other Chinese Restaurant. Personally, in my humble and unimportant opinion, I hope this other place of his closes as well. Eventually people may tire of such behavior and charlatan. Does the following experience ring true today?

I sent this email to, "Chef Poon" and to this day NO REPLY has been received. This is his newer place on Chestnut Street.

SAVE YOUR MONEY - This establishment is a RIP OFF!! There are far better places in Center City Philadelphia for Chinese Food.

I made reservations for your New Years Banquet for Two. I was led to believe that this would be not just a Chinese food meal but rather a real experience. I talked my partner into coming with me to enjoy such an, "experience."

We arrived at 7:30pm. My original reservations, I spoke to, "Tommy" who at that time explained that because it is only a party of 2, the "Lobster" course would be substituted. Ok, fine.

Upon us being sat, they brought over the News Years Banquet Menu. Nothing was explained to us. The advertisement(s) stated it is a 10 Course meal. Served Family Style.

We were brought the first course (which was not served family style but each, myself and my partner received one plate) Its was excellent. However later after the meal, it was explained your staff combined many courses for the first course, so the reality is that I think the first plate combined 3-4 courses?

Next plate arrived, (we felt rushed) This plate was also served not what your advertisement communicated but again many "courses" combined. Your head of the staff came over, rushed and explained that because we are a party of two and not a party of 5-6 Lobster was substituted. There was other substitutions in which today, we still don't know what we had and NEVER agreed to upon our reservation. The food was good but we paid 36.50, the same as a larger party and the "experience" was beginning to feel like a touristy disappointment.

Again, the head of the staff comes over (rushed) and stated ok, dessert will now be brought over. Dessert? What happened to the 10 courses? What happened to the Banquet?

I called over the gentleman and asked him if I heard him correctly about that the dinner was complete and now we are going to be served dessert? He came over and explained very quickly what was substituted throughout our meal? We paid $36.50 the same as anyone else and this is what is sold to us as a Chinese Banquet?

The Dessert was served. I was taken aback, what I saw on the dessert plate was ridicules and insulting to anybody spending $45 (tax and tip).

We were given 1 blue berry, 1 Raspberry, A small Dixie cup of Tapioca, one almond cookie, and here is the real kicker as if the meal wasn't already on the side of silliness, a Sugar Cube Size of Chocolate Cheese cake. Come on now, $36.50 do you think you could have been less insulting regarding the tiny, less than child portion?

I would like to know, instead of the Lobster course what did we receive? There were so many other "substitutions" that we feel like we were taken. We paid for a 10 course Chinese Banquet yet we received 3 plates.  Let me remind you what your advertisement stated,
Extraordinary Price: $36.50 per guest plus tax and gratuity. Join Chef Poon for a traditional 10-course Chinese New Year Banquet to ring in the year of the Ox.

We feel we were sold something and was not given what we paid for.
