Thank you for your time.

I thought you would like to know about the experience a customer received last night.

This Restauranter now seems have very soiled reputation in the city,

RECEIVED from a YELPER...

For your review of: Chef Joseph Poon

so sorry you went to the Poon Banquet... in Philly he is so famously bad that yelpers refer to any awful experience in any restaurant  (like your experience) as being "pooned" ... but don't feel bad-- i almost planned a UYE but was saved by some timely input from other, more experienced, yelpers...

If only I could find something this good in CA... I've been to Philly twice to visit my fiancée, and I've spent at least half that time at Reading Terminal Market.  First time I had Beck's I only had their Mac and cheese balls which were delicious.  But let's be honest, it's hard to screw up Mac and cheese balls.  BUT the train wreck, jambalaya, and blackened chicken pasta were perfect.  I'm no Bobby Flay but I like to think I know tasty food, and Beck's is the SH*T!!!  No more need to be said but there's a minimum I have to type according to Yelp.

The husband was in need of a cannoli and Termini Bros. was offering Gold Medal Italian pastries. After we placed our order, the manager rounded up three new employees for a lesson in filling cannoli shells. I asked if I could watch; I am here to tell you that was a fun and educational experience. A huge bag of ricotta cheese with chocolate chip filling (the original as I was told and no marscopone as someone in Denver had said) was hung from a hook to make piping the filling in the shell easier. So, you pipe in one side, starting in the center and bring to the edge and end with a curl. Repeat on the other side, sprinkle with powdered sugar and viola! a delicious Italian pastry. Just perfect for an afternoon treat and large enough to split.

COVID PROTOCOL NOT ADHERED . Have been going here with my family for years and enjoyed it immensely.  Today 12/29/21-Iwas alarmed to find that they don't enforce a Covid protocol. They have in the past. My waitress wore a tiny mask that covered only her mouth. I am a senior and lack of Covid precaution is alarming. Especially now with Omicron traveling around. I spoke to a  Very nice waiter and asked him if he could ask her to use a mask  that fit appropriately, he laughed but  he did tell her.  She immediately came back time and time again with her nose hanging out of her mask as if to show me she didn't have to listen. She made me extremely uncomfortable and I WILL NOT GO BACK AGAIN. She'd walked all around the restaurant without covering her nose and no other employee said anything . All others wore a mask properly.

Got the jambalaya and chicken and shrimp gumbo because I saw someone else eating it at the counter, and it looked good. They also gave a sample, which tasted good! However I got it to go, and the portions seemed way smaller than the one they give on the counter, and it was WAAAAAY too salty. Like so much that it was almost unbearable. If I were to get it again, I would just opt for the gumbo with plain white rice. Also, the corn bread was way too dry. It seemed like a waste of calories, really. Was a huge disappointment.

3.5 stars: tried the chicken ban mi. The chicken was very well seasoned but they add soy sauce to the bread which makes the sandwich taste very salty. They also do not add any butter (or a lack of)...which is something I prefer on my sandwiches...and they don't have the the pickled veggies which is something that I must have. Will give the other dishes a try in the future.
Best banh mi in the city. Their bread and pate sets them above the rest.  I always get the cha lua dac biet. Loaded with meat for only $0.50 more

Know what really sucks about this movie theatre? You have to be 17 to get in without a parent, read: "All children 16 and under must have an adult accompany them in the theatre" right above the ticket booth. Considering the fact that this is an indie movie house, you would think they would be more lenient (seriously, if I'm a young person going to see an indie movie you can assume that I'm apart of a certain "crowd" so i really shouldn't be a problem).

Back to my review.

The movie theatre is clean and they have a good selection of snacks and treats in the lobby (overpriced, but not too overpriced). The bathrooms are clean and the screen in the theatre is small. They have all of the popular indie movies/documentaries here. Seats are comfy and the floors are clean.

Just wish I didn't have to LIE to get in here.
Great choice of a movie theater no complaints at all.  I would definitely recommend specially for that film that know the theaters shows.  All round great place

I came here after searching on Yelp for "Gluten Free bakeries" but they had only one type of crusty muffin available. She forgot about my son's ice cream and when I went up to ask about it she stopped mopping, 
didn't wash her hands and put it In a to-go cup because I guess she wanted to leave right at closing. I was too stunned to say anything. The furniture is also really threadbare and gross.
adorable place to catch a flick! lower prices than the big cinemas around here. no lines. very clean! nice staff and nice movie selection! coming back again soon for sure.

I had an appointment at the Temple Hospital. I was fasting for 12 hours and looking for a decent meal after the appointment. I was so glad to trust other people's review! This is new place so there were only 2 reviews. 
I ordered an Eggroll Vermicelli and Vietnamese espresso. They were so good!!! I forgot to take pictures because I was too hungry... I have tried many Vietnamese restaurants in NY and Philly and this place is probably in my top 3 (including tastes, staff, prices, clean). I need to go back to try their pho! The staff are very nice and friendly. I highly recommend this place!!!

My fiance and I wanted to get prewedding pictures done and stumbled upon Only You Wedding; because there aren't a lot of choices in Philly we decided to go with them and just hoped that they would be "decent." Turns out, they are AMAZING! 

We worked with a small team. Annie, the manager; Johnny, the photographer; and Ling, the make up artist. Annie was extremely easy to work with and was flexible when we had to reschedule our photo shoot due to weather reason multiple times. She was so attentive during the session and fixed my hair, dress, jewelry, etc. Ling was SO knowledgeable about Asian makeup and took great pride in her work; in fact, she spent about half an hour on ONE of my eyes just to make sure that I looked as good as I could. Very rarely do I say this, (other than when I had my makeup done in Hong Kong) but I was 100% satisfied with my makeup and I had such trust in her. In fact, I am soooo sad that I don't get to book her for my actual wedding because we decided on our wedding date too late. 

The actual photo shoot was a ton of fun. We did the indoor/outdoor package and my fiance and I were both worried that they wouldn't turn out well. He always said that he didn't know how to smile, and I was self conscious about my chubby face. Johnny knew exactly how to pose us in the most flattering way possible. We did our shooting on 2 different days and when we got there for our outdoor portion, Johnny sat down and reviewed with us what we did not like about our indoor photos (there weren't a lot) and he took everything we said into account. The result: gorgeous outdoor photos that looked like they came out of a magazine. 

We only did the prewedding photos with Only You so my experience is based on this one service only. But they do EVERYTHING from wedding planning to decoration, DJing, wedding day photos and makeup. I would totally recommend checking these guys out if you're planning a wedding. Seriously, if I could give these guys 20 stars, I would.

Slow, staff was overworked, they didn't assign names to order which made it really difficult to know what food was which. This led to people taking orders that didn't belong to them and awkward conversations. Apparently it's really good but this experience was subpar. Maybe just avoid them in the early morning?

Breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi... Why WOULDN'T you go to Epic?
Breakfast menu is pretty great. They have all the regular stuff and it's made to order pretty quickly.

Lunch, they mostly have sandwhiches and cafe sort of foods which have yet to disappoint!

LOTS of different kinds of coffee and tea drinks. Their espresso shots are very high quality, so it's all good.

Mostly, this place is just fun and quirky. They encourage people to write on the walls in the bathroom, and it shows. There's a TON of stuff on every surface of the bathroom. Most of it benevolent.

If you're in downtown Tucson, first I'm sorry you're stuck in such an awful town. But secondly, good news; epic is right off Euclid!
I went to Epic Cafe for lunch with my family and was served by Skyler. Skyler was very helpful and polite. She not only took our order, but made the food, which was great. Good job Skyler!
Excellent place if you want to see an indie film or documentary without be bombarded by teenage hooligans or screaming babies. Very classy.

After ages of meaning to, finally made my way to Epic and am so very happy I did. 
Four specific things I can rate:

- Snappy service with a hip little smile.
- Funky old couches and clever bathroom graffiti that made me miss Seattle.
- Crazy delicious Chai!
- Even crazier delicious carrot cake - a slice of which is THE SIZE OF A FAT CHIHUAHUA!

And now I know, that if it ever came down to it, I can eat a whole Chihuahua. I can also try to make may way back to this epicness as often as possible.

I had more fun hanging here and meeting people than anywhere ever. The open mike was good, the drinks were good, I like the staff, I like a little attitude, keeps the stupid people away. The smoking section on 4th Ave and University is a priceless hang. On my travels I measure every cafe coffee etc joint by comparing it to Epic!

I love this La Fitness in South Dale Mabry. The staff is exceptionally helpful and friendly. They know me and I feel very welcome whenever I walk in. Any concerns or requests  I have are met in a reasonably time. The trainers are excellent and I can ask other trainers for help if my trainer is away. The equipment is available even at busy times, it's clean, and in working order.

Cafe Cuong has fantastic and affordable banh mi. I always get the chicken banh mi without pate, and while the fillings are all on point, I can't say enough about how much I love this bread. It's probably the perfect banh mi baguette, because it's pillowy soft inside and but has a crackly crust outside. 

I have eaten two of these in one sitting, and, if I were very hungry, could probably eat a third.
I've tried banh everywhere from New York down to Virginia. None compares to this place and I will be forever devastated if this shop ever closes.

The atmosphere is nice, the food/coffee is decent, and the crowd is pleasantly quirky as they always are in such places- but the staff is undeniably cold. Never any smiles or hint of chatter. The kind of thing where the employee acts as if all the customers are just a bunch of nuisances. For some people that aspect (service) isn't as important as others, but because of the consistent unfriendliness of the staff at Epic I have found other cafés to frequent (you really have a nice selection to choose from around that area). So yeah, it's a pretty sweet place if you don't mind interacting with the cold staff behind the counter when you have to.

I prefer this place over the other two Indian restaurants on Girard. I think the quality / taste of the food is great, and their delivery time is about 3 times faster. Usually when I call the other two its 1-1.5 hour wait for deliver, Sahara is usually 30 minutes. I've converted several friends in the neighborhood too!

Everyone is welcome at the Epic Cafe.  This place is the heartbeat of Tucson, Ariz., which boasts a wide diversity of people and cultures.  Close to the University of Arizona and downtown Tucson, the Epic has a wide array of freshly baked goods and numerous coffee options.  LET IT BE SAID,  I have never met a more conscientious staff--the owner could moonlight as a headhunter for Tucson corporations as he only hires the best.  I am a vegan, and the staff has gone out of the way to make sure that the items I receive are vegan.  I have never had one staff member say, "Do you want me to check if it's vegan?"  They just simply do it.  I spend a good part of the year on the road with my work, and know cafes from coast to coast.  The Epic Cafe is without parallel.

I visit Tucson occassionally having gone to college there but I live in San Diego. I really love the scene at the Epic.  Before I get into that let me just say that the coffee and treats at the Epic are awesome but the vibe is what keeps me coming back. Talk about an eclectic clientel. Where can you see students, professors, desert rats, Rastafarians, political leaders, Buddhists, intellectuals, old hippies, and lap top jockeys under one  roof? The Epic. Nothing like this in "very Republican" San Diego. The few that did exist have been gobbled up by Starbucks. This place is not the fanciest spot in town but it is certainly the coolest and the food is good as well.

Went here on a whim yesterday for breakfast.
The little lady behind the counter was very sweet and very nice. As it was our first time there, she was very helpful in explaining the menu and was patient with us.
We ordered two breakfast burritos, one with bacon and one with turkey and a strawberry scone.
We took the scone and went to go sit someplace but here, that is hard to do.  Most of the folks in here looked as though they had been here for a very long time.  Laptops, papers scattered everywhere, dirty dishes, etc.  The one table that was available was littered with crumbs and a sticky top.  Cleanliness doesn't seem to be high priority here.
We ate our scone and was thrown by the peanut butter. We thought it was just strawberry. So the pb ruined the scone for us.  It would have been so much better without it.
Our burritos came and these get very high praise! Both were very flavorful, full of meat, cheese, potatoes, etc.  They were also very filling, carrying us into dinner time.
This place was interesting. I didn't hate it but I didn't love it. It would help if they'd clean up after people and make the place more presentable to those who just want to eat. Most of the clientele looked like they had been there for weeks.  Too us, that was a turn off.

The End.

The service in this place is terrible. The people behind the counter were all attitude. I was asking their opinion between two things and the girl roller her eyes at me and sighed that she had to answer my question.
I felt rushed. The food didn't look very nice in the display cabinet either.
I asked if I could buy a whole cake and she just about bit my head off! 
What the heck is the difference if I buy all 12 slices individually or you sell me the whole cake?! MONEY is MONEY?!

I ended up ordering a cake slice and my friend ordered spinach pie.
The cake was tasty and moist and totally worth it! My friend said the spinach pie tasted great, but would have been better without the hair she found in it.- downer and gross.

It was also a little loud, hard to have conversation without feeling like I should yell.

In the mid '00s I lived here. This was our go to place to work on our art homework, drink coffee and people watch. They also had an awesome open mic night that we would attend religiously until it went down hill. I haven't been back in years till recently. The place has changed a lot, but the staff is still courteous and  I still love the peanut butter mocha and the Rosemary Almond Chicken Salad. Oh and they're cake is amazing and the slices they give you are huge. It's something you really need to plan on sharing.
We ordered the green chili quiche and breakfast burrito and both were fab! Customer service was excellent and the environment was chill. Great art and hot sauce selection.

One extra item of note- it didn't occur to me until my last visit to see Black Swan a little while ago. Unlike Ritz Five's large screen theater, both Ritz East theaters are divided into two seating areas separated by an aisle running horizontally across the middle. If you're sitting in the seats in front of the aisle (closer to the screen), this isn't an issue. If, however, you are sitting with the aisle in front of you, you have to deal with the glare from the lights illuminating the path.

Usually this isn't a problem for me, as I tend to sit in front of it by way of preference. But the last time I went there the lights were a distraction from the movie. I eventually put it out of mind (the movie was just that good), but it's bothersome when you like a nice, darkened theater to lose yourself in the film.

Otherwise I'm happy with the Ritz East.

My favorite place to go for Vietnamese hoagies. I have tried a few different sandwiches and they were all delicious. There are tables in there for you to sit and eat but I feel like its more for their friends who stop by. The only issue is for me is the parking.

Never let your customers butt in front of other customers that are waiting in line. Never. Especially when the one that is waiting in line is buying three times more then the guy that butted in front of him.

This is probably my favorite bánh mì in the city. You walk in they have a huge TV and they are playing MTV concerts on a Saturday. It's a very small place but they make the best chicken banh mi. I like Ba Le but this blows it out of the water. If you've never had one of these I would consider it a must hit

Amazing. Professional. Quality. This pretty much sums it all up.

Johnny and Annie were so easy to work with. It's all about keeping the customer happy. That's the impression I got from the start =)

I learned about this place through my friend's wedding...mainly for the MC. But then I saw their decoration portfolio and decided to get a package with them.  After talking to Annie about the package details for the decoration, she basically said she can do anything as long as she doesn't need to spend too much out of pocket.  Weeks later, I went back to her and said I want my cake table to look like it is floating on a bed of flowers. This would require a custom order of an acrylic table to match the restaurant's table.  Johnny was there that day too and gave a lot of inputs on if I needed a cake stand, how the flowers should be placed, what kind of flowers would look nice in an affordable way, etc. In the end, they said they can do it and will not charge me extra for the custom made acrylic table. Awesome!

Then weeks later, I went back with my stage backdrop ideas. I gave them several pictures because I couldn't find ONE picture with everything I want. They sketched out the backdrop from the things I want from every picture and then gave me inputs on what they think looks better. I thought that was especially helpful because I was pretty clueless when it comes to visualizing things I never seen before.  Lastly, I told them I would like to have two pillars wrapped with flowers to frame the stage so it doesn't look too plain. I told them silk flowers would do. However, two days before my wedding, Annie said she couldn't get the silk flowers to look nice on the pillar so she bought real flowers for the pillar to look better. NO CHARGE! This place is all about quality and making sure it looks THE BEST for you even if it means they have to eat some of the expense. I was extremely impress by their professionalism on this. 

Another awesome thing they did for me was...making my husband tear (almost) during our first dance. Our wedding date happened to be my husband's birthday. Being as shy as I am, I couldn't perform anything for him. I asked Annie and Johnny if they have any ideas to surprise him. Johnny gave me an awesome idea which would require some work on his end.  I took his idea and Johnny went right to work. Two days later, he sent me what he did and it was very touching. Johnny's work was put into action during our first dance and it totally touched my husband ^^ Thank you so much for the idea.  And again, no charge.

Some places would just do as you request without giving you much advice. Only You did what I requested AND MUCH MORE! 

If i were to do this all over, I would choose Only You again.

I had a latte and it was good... but they need more help so you can stay open later than midnight.  There were some people sitting inside that smelled bad.  My picky friend thought it was nice.  It was at least different but I don't know if I'd describe it as nice.  Maybe my olfactory sensitivity was involved.  The menu is big for a coffee place and it's decently comfortable.  It's very 4th ave I guess.

Yet one more Tucson cafe that's open til midnight, in irritating contrast to Phoenix which has barely any.

Three of us sat on chairs on the sidewalk sipping on peanut butter mochas and chatting for an entire afternoon, last Sunday. It was a pleasure.

It's a decent place to bring children for a cheap and fun activity.  If you want to go ice skating for the thrill and holiday cheer, I'd recommend going somewhere else.  It costs $4 for skate rentals and no admissions cost.  However, you get what you pay.  During my hour and a half there, the ice was not clean, which made skating difficult for me, a slightly less than average skater.  That is my only issue with Rizzo Rink.

I like going in here when it is really hot the thick adobe walls and dark interior makes it really comfortable to sink into a cushy both and lose myself on line. THE tasty morsels and lattes are just the thing to help me me comfortable in Tucson

BANH MI THIT NGUOI:  FOUR STARS

I believe Cafe Cuong makes the best banh mi in Philly so far.  I've tried QT's and Ba Le, among other places and haven't quite enjoyed the banh mis much after the fifth or sixth visit.

The boyfriend and I have had the banh mi thit nguoi here and it has been consistently delicious each time.  My boyfriend is even totally tempted to 'buy 10, get 1 free,' the deal that Cafe Cuong offers.

Also, I suggest fellow Yelpers to call ahead and order - that way, you don't have to wait, but more importantly to make sure they're open (as they were closed at random days and times a few months ago).

Food City is what it is and it's good at what it does. It's not Whole Foods and doesn't pretend to be. My family gets a lot of produce there (4-6 avocados for a 1$, 3 lbs of lime for 1$! etc., etc). Their selection of dried chiles and spices is great and the prices are out of this world.  I've always found the staff to be friendly and helpful. And the music they play is pretty cool.

I've lived near this Food City for over two years and finally made a visit. Food City is known for their low prices produce, carnicerias and Mexican products. This location is particularly small, the produce selection was a little on the sad side and there's no carniceria, bummer! I'd return to this one in a bind, but this location doesn't offer any of the awesome things that Food City is known for.
The Ritzes are the best places to see a movie in Philadelphia.

Not to be confused with Ritz Five, which is right around the corner! 

All of the Ritz are great. Their movie selection, concessions selection, service- everything is top-notch. There are only two movies playing at this particular location. 

If you're looking to grub somewhere, Positano Coast is great for drinks and apps but can get kinda pricey beyond that and the food can be hit or miss (more hit than miss). There's also a Chinese restaurant right next door. 

Special Note: Wednesdays are cheaper than other days!

Not stadium seating, but what it lacks in the impact factor -- more than makes up for in the quaint, homey atmosphere -- which is better for a more intimate, date-like environment.  I'd definitely recommend it for NON-action packed blockbusters, but for more storyline-driven movies.

Smallest of the Ritz theatres downtown but, like the others, it's an art house film venue. We come here for free movie screenings, which attracts an odd crowd that must wait outside. Floors are sticky and seats are broken and cramped, but for free screenings it's fine.

Added bonus: parking lot at the Ritz Bourse is $9 after 5p and 2 blocks away from the East.

My old roommate used to work here. After she ran off to Hawaii with a regular I began to wonder about Epic. It's got this mix of hobos, artists, hippies and students that are there pretty much all day. Essentially they accept all kinds. 

Their coffee is very yummy, but I'd have to say I'm more into the cold mate or the mango smoothies. They also have very good food, cakes, sandwiches, cookies, etc.

Let me start by saying I've had Sahara before, and it was awesome. I got it delivered tonight, and it was horrible. First of all, it took an hour and a half for delivery and when I got it, I received an extremely small portion of the shrimp dish i ordered (which was almost $8) and the food was not hot anymore. I called them back and was given $5 off of my next order. But honestly, I don't know if I'm going back. 
As for the food itself, the okra dish I got was extremely oily. I couldn't eat more than a few bites before feeling sick. The shrimp was ok, but also seemed to be on the oily side. I spend $20 for this meal and ended up throwing most of it away. 
:/

Friendly service. Lady kinda sneezed right before making my coffee haha so I was a little grossed out. Iced latte was ok! Good coffee, little weak for 3 shots of espresso though. Wasn't too big on interior decor.
This is a must visit place. I've had a great strawberry fanta float and tea latte. There coffee is great and they don't mind specialty orders.

I've always enjoyed this cafe. It is a diverse crowed, comfortable seating, great coffee and baked goods. I've never tried the Vegas stuff, but it is there if you want it.

Also, they have free wifi that works very well.

Ritz East is better than the 5! It has the best screens and audio in town. Petition Landmark to play the better movies that the 5 gets to play in the superior theaters at the East. The East gets the crummy movies due to a fluke in how they pay their bills with the Parking Authority. The 5 has shifty audio, and the screens are too high. The East, the Bourse and the 5, though, all employ really fun staff. They're great places to hang out and write and read and flirt with your date before your flick. But if you don't have a date, go alone. These movies are great. Quit feeling sorry for yourself.

Spunky atmosphere, lots of seating, mostly friendly staff, decent variety. Baristas are hit or miss: some are outstanding, some have their heads on backward. Food is eh. I'm happy they have gluten free muffins, though, like the baristas, they are hit or miss; they are sometimes of poor consistency or taste and other times downright scrumptious.

We have only ever once had to throw away take out food in Phila, and unfortunately it was from this restaurant.  I do love Indian food generally, including New Delhi, Ekta, Tiffin, King of Tandoor.  This food was so bad.    The sauces were pureed like they had been put through a Cuisinart (nothing recognizable in them except the meat & potatoes), and tasted really off.   Possibly just a bad night??  I have no idea, but the excellent reviews of this place really puzzle me.   Beware if you order from here...

This is very old school building. It could use some updates. But I'm not here for the new stuff. They have the Movies that are considered risky, Non-traditional etc. who knows why. I like how they have their lobby set up. Cookies, popcorn if course but Tea, Coffee etc. on a Sunday it's nice and quiet downtown.

Heard this place had great .ban min, so after brunch my brunch buddy & I searched for it!!!
Simple & small menu, its tiny with couple tables.
I ordered 2 & lady made them to order!!
I ended giving 1/2 to her since she never had one!!
 Yum!!!
Return factor: Absolutely!!
Can't wait- they bread & everything just so much elevated!!!!

i went to this theater for the philadelphia film fest so my review is specific to this event. it's a very cute space and not all space age with reclining massage chairs like some of the newer theaters. the audio was played at a completely appropriate level so i didn't leave with my eardrums ringing. 

but, omg, this experience made me realize that i'm on the way to the senior citizens' seats in the back. i made the mistake of not arriving early to line up for the show so i had to sit in the front section of seats. i sat about 8 rows from the screen and within 5 minutes of the start of the movie wished i had brought some dramamine. i'm too young for this shit. damn vestibular system.

Given the options of places to see movies in the city, this place, and the Ritz 5, and the Bourse are my favs.  The employees are efficient and kind, the concessions are always open, and serving fresh, good options at reasonable prices in quantities that won't make you feel like a total fat-ass, and the theaters are clean.  The seats are REALLY comfy and the backs recline a bit.  Previews aren't ad nauseum, and picture quality is clear.  Theater size is reasonable, and patrons are respectful generally.  These theaters typically show indie flicks, so you might have to do a bit of legwork to find a movie you want to see, but it is always always worth it.  I went to see the Philly Film Fest preview of McCanick last night, and had an incredibly pleasant experience.  Always do!

I used to frequent this cafe and wanted to go back recently after reading a recent review on tucsonfoodie.com citing Epic as "a vegan scone-lovers paradise" and Yelp reviews that they had lots of vegan items.  The only vegan pastries they have there are some cookies.   I did get an incredibly good vegan pesto on a bagel however.  While there aren't "a ton" of vegan options, as another reviewer mentioned and as there were in many years past, you can get a small bite to eat and a coffee made vegan, just don't expect many options

I first discovered this place in 2007. I've been coming here ever since. I love their Vietnamese chicken hoagie/banh mi ga. It's shredded chicken and they stuff your sandwich with it. Great quality and taste is wonderful.

*Insert snobby hipster comment about mainstream movies here*  In all seriousness though, this is a nice space.  I do like that unlike Ritz at the Bourse, I can use my cell phone in here without losing a signal.  (I have an attention span problem ok?)

I've been here but never ate anything here, since they don't have a vegetarian banh mi.  Still, the BF likes it here just fine and so do my Viet friends who sometimes drive from New Jersey to get some.  Guess that says something!  I always end up going next door to Café NhuY though, since they do have vegetarian ones.

Once, the boyfriend got some from NhuY and some from Saigon and said that he liked NhuY's better.  But maybe he was trying to humor me so we could just make 1 stop instead of two, although they're right next to each other.
As good as it gets for Vietnamese hoagies. The right bread, pate and meats finished with the veggies. No bells and whistles with this sandwich just done right.

Nice central location for a Friday night
High end prices, but some sushi selections have generous portions
No hot towel service
No daily specials or delicacies like a whole fresh pompano fish, prepared and served 4-5 different ways for 2
No complimentary miso soup or edamame beans served at the sushi bar
octopus salad ***
sea urchin ** not fresh and daily? 'market' priced $2 over $7 on menu for $9-two pieces
yellow tail *****
tuna ****
octopus *****
baked green mussels ***
scallops *****
baked scallops ***
mango roll **** preparation was not consistent between at least 2 chefs. 1 roll enough dess
rainbow roll **** and looked good, salmon is farm raised
bottled cold sake ***** for selection, but one * satisfaction, overpriced at $14 per small bottle.
Late Happy Hour started during my dinner, but I was charged full price for one bottle.
Employees not very knowledgeable about extensive sake menu.
Sushi bar *** chefs don't take orders and chefs other than the one working at station in sight of sushi bar customer are preparing food.
To GO packaging excellent, including chop sticks,  soy, and special mango sauce. This sweet mango dessert sushi roll is enough for 3-4 people to share, too much for 1 person.
Clean sushi prep stations ****
Attention from staff and speed of order delivery *****
Very friendly and attentive sushi chefs and staff *****
Restrooms ****
Not my favorite sushi spot, but pleasant enough. High noise level (sports bar atmosphere).
Patio dining looked nice for pleasant evenings.
Good place to get your basic sushi fix and perhaps consider the sushi buffet.

To echo what many have said, this is my favorite theater in the Philly area too.  Just a different experience than the AMCs and Regals we get so accustomed to.  Every movie i've seen there I've enjoyed.  They really choose some great ones.  Seats are the nicest, but they are surprisingly comfortable.  The snack bar is amazing.  So many cool and different options.  Staff is really kind and helpful with the customers.  Also, they have some amazing deals on weekdays, like $6.50 Wednesdays.  Hope to be back sooner rather than later!
Typically a go to for me for iced toddy.  I enjoy the funky flavor and company found around 4th ave

This is a great place to grab coffee and surf the web. I was out on a quest to find internet in the city and stumbled upon Epic. It was a little crowded but I was happy to see that they had places to plug in your computers everywhere. After getting a cup of joe from the excellent staff and asking for the password, I was up and running.

Part of the difficulty of reviewing all three Ritz theaters is that it becomes hard to come up with new and interesting things to say about each one. They all carry the same great elements: Quality movies, quality snacks, great staff, and convenience to Old City bars and restaurants. How much is there left to say after you cover two?

The most notable aspect of Ritz East is sheer size of the screens- two large theaters as opposed to the five apiece at the other locations. This means that you get only one or two options at best, but it also means that your getting the best presentation.

Ritz East also has, without doubt, the best parking option: a mammoth, multi-level structure that you can always find space in, and get your ticket validated as well.

A small point, but a notable one: it also has the biggest lobby of the three, so it feels far less crowded when you're lining up for the new Coens feature.

I stopped in after staying late at work. The food was delicious. The staff was friendly. The price was right. 
This is my new "go to" Indian place! Yum!
Great super fresh Vietnamese food. Meat is excellent quality. Just what Temple Hospital area needs. Wish they had a venue on the health sciences campus.

I really enjoy their delicious ice cream and beautiful artwork. I'm a big fan of their coffee, as well. Free wifi allows you to browse the Internet, work on homework, or anything of the like. A cozy little, hole in the wall place that makes Tucson feel like home.

This place brings nothing but good memories. I have been here several times and each one has been for a special occasion. The first was for the debut of a documentary that I worked on back in college a few years ago. The seats are comfy, not to big, not to small, just right. The theater itself has a lot of character and is a good mix of old and new school. I just recently came back here to shoot part of a commercial which should be airing on Valentine's day, that was real cool as well. The best part about this place though is the movie selection, they only play good movies, for someone with my voracious appetite for quality film, its the perfect cinema experience.

I'm really reviewing this for the Ritz theater in VOORHEES, NJ. I loved that theater. It's the best movie theater I've been to, and was fortunate enough to go there often. Some asshole bought out the chain and is now turning it into the same shitty ghetto theaters as everywhere else now. What made the Ritz Theaters so great was there was a great coffee shop in them, before the previews they had slide shows of art exhibits on display in the tri-state area, or other ARTS related events, and things. This theater had class, which was the last of it's kind. I feel bad for the guy who owned it since he died and his family pawned it off to the highest shitty bidder. I'm a little pissed.
Hahhaha that's some south philly goodness right there. Save for the patches of wet ice, we enjoyed it! Please do fix that though - really not safe.

Whenever an Indian take-out restaurant opens, I critique it by the quality of vindaloo they make.  Chicken vindaloo, to be specific, as control.  What I'm looking for is a deep red color from the depths of hell and the heat to match.  I'm looking for sweet and sour notes with the other spice notes to be bright and pungent.

A butter chicken and vindaloo is ordered.  As I remove them from the bag, I look and cannot tell which one is which.  They're both a pale peachy-orange.  Neither was spicy and tasted vaguely similar, so that made it relatively hard to deduce which was which.  Oh boy, this is a problem.  Delivery is faster than most.  That's it, really.

This place is a no-frills place. I mean, honestly, you're better off with taking your banh mi to go instead of eating it there. There are 2 tables, but one of them is usually taken up by a family friend who's there hanging out. 

If you're going to order anything, definitely order the Banh Mi Dac Biet (deluxe Vietnamese hoagie). Cafe Cuong has the best one in Philly; this statement comes from many Vietnamese friends. I do have to admit that there isn't a strong consistency on the amount of ingredients on a Banh Mi Dac Biet, but I have never questioned the quality of the ingredients. I have also now gone there enough times where the owners recognize me. My Banh Mi Dac Biet is stuffed with meats and veggies. 

And yes, this place is cash only.

PS - Another sign that this place is known for its Banh Mi's. I see many Vietnamese-speaking customers mass order (anywhere from 20-50 of these).

Ordered delivery and they completely messed up the order. There were no tomatoes in the BLT, there was no avocado in the TBA, and I did not get the white chocolate mocha I ordered. I have been trying to call the store for an hour and they still haven't picked up the phone. I do not understand how hard it is for this place to make sure that everything that someone paid for is given to the customer. Extremely disappointed.

Update: just tried to reorder the white chocolate mocha and they delivered THE WRONG THING AGAIN
This place was AWESOME. Amazing bahn Mi and what sealed the deal was the Vietnamese iced coffee. Hands down the best cup I ever had.

Awful customer service. Have been trying to resolve an issue with Craig, via email, since August. Ive been very patient, but this is ridiculous.  Promises made, not kept. Shady and dishonest to me... Will be filing with BBB.

I always thought I'd never find a banh mi place in South Philly that would compare/be better than Cafe Saigon in Northeast Philly, which is my OG favorite banh mi place. 

I was definitely proven wrong at Cafe Cuong. It's amazing! I absolutely love it and I think I actually prefer Cafe Cuong over Cafe Saigon [note: I've been going to Cafe Saigon ever since I was a little kid...so over 10+ years!]. 

The storefront itself looks pretty shabby and the workers are pretty terse in responses, but it's because the place itself is just meant to be a quick grab & go type of establishment. So don't be deterred! 

As for the banh mi, the bread, mayo, pate, cold cuts...everything is perfect! I usually get the "banh mi thit nguoi," which has only the pink cold cuts. But if you like cha [the white Vietnamese pork roll cold cut], then order the "banh mi dac biet," which is only $0.50 more.

The only downside to this place is that they don't accept card...so bring cash!!!

Food and drinks are very expensive. Food I might be able to say is good enough to pay for, but the drinks definitely aren't. The coffee is very weak and the chai is dry mix with milk (also weak). Sorry to burst your bubble, but Tucson coffee so far is pretty bad. I've had to go to Starbucks to get anything that is flavorful and will keep me awake (I know, the idea is preposterous). 

That said, it's a GREAT space to hang out or study. The staff is very friendly and won't make you rush to leave. If the exorbitant prices are keeping this place afloat while still giving free wifi and alone-time, it's ok by me.

My only complain I that the entrance was a little hard to find as my friend and I parked on another side of the road. 

But other than that, friendly staff and tons of space in the theatre. Personally I prefer a emptier theatre. If you're like me, Ritz East is perfect for you!!
The owner of the business reached out and personally promised that he would make changes. Really great customer service.

I came here to have studio pictures for my wedding done, since on the day it was just a simple city hall event; when I walked in and started looking at the pictures on the wall I almost drooled! Amazing. I started by having my makeup done there and asides from super nice, Annie was very carefull and thorough.. it's all about you, and she made sure to have u feeling that way :) once again I was astonished! She also did my hair, and I loved it. 
I didn't need a dress but I actually forgot my necklace, so she just told me to pick from several beautiful jewelry they have on display and I borrowed one :)
Then we went to take the pictures, the photographer made us feel very comfortable, helped by telling us what / how to do and pose, or adjusting our own posing, and in the end he even made us take some funny type wedding pictures, which we all had a good laugh out of! 

I know I can't comment on the whole wedding planning side of the service, but just for this experience alone I'd dare to say I wish I had more weddings just so I could go back there! Heheh

Epic Cafe gets an easy four stars because its the only place I've been able to get a coffee after 11pm on 4th. After walking to the end of downtown, and up to University, we realized that we completely missed Epic Cafe and promptly stopped in. Surprisingly (at the time) they were open, still making coffee, and there were plenty of other people in the shop.

As for the coffee itself, I realize I'm making my assumptions based on what is probably half-day old coffee so I'll go easy, its solid. Even after what might have been 8/12 hours of sitting, the cold toddy was still delicious. I don't know if I'd call it the best I've ever had but certainly more than acceptable for late at night. I also had a shot of espresso which was delicious, perfectly well made. 

Epic Cafe has a great assortment of seating arrangements, and is pretty quiet. I assume it'd be great for studying or reading a book. Overall its a your pretty average, hip little coffee shop except for the fact that they stay open waay later than all the others which I'm very appreciative of. 

I'll be dropping in at reasonable hours sometime to get a better feel for what everything is like when its still fresh.

I love the Ritz. They play films that I actually want to see. At this theater they only usually play one or two films, whereas the other locations (close by) play more films. They have vegan cookies for sale at this location, which are fantastic. I also like that the sodas have free refills. The theater is always clean and I like the mix of people who attend this theater. I will keep coming back to the Ritz East theater.

Cafe Cuong makes awesome Vietnamese hoagies!

The bread is so fresh and crispy! Portions are smaller than what you would get at other places, such as Ba Le. It's not going to stop me from coming here! It's not always about quantity over quality. I would need to eat at least two hoagies to fill myself up. Money well spent. :)

Daily special: Buy 10, get 1 FREE.

I've always ordered my banh mi thit nguoi from Cafe Cuong. They always come out with toasty baguettes with the right amount of lunch meat, pate and butter every single time. I always ask for the pickled vegetables and fresh vegetables to be separate since I usually order about 10 sandwiches to bring back to Jersey. My go to banh mi in Philadelphia is definitely Cafe Cuong.

That's it Epic, you are getting another star! Today I had lunch--a rosemary chicken sandwich on a wheat roll with a bag o chips. I don't know what else to say, but yum! Not too heavy on the mayo, but big on flavor, I dug the big chunk chicken although probably a bit messier than a traditional chicken sandwich. Why have I never eaten at Epic before? More importantly, what should I eat at Epic next time I go?

I come here every Sunday morning with my boyfriend, I get a soy mocha, he gets a regular mocha. We bring our own drinks and because of that we get an amazing discount! For example, it's a 16 ounce cup and a 16 ounce mocha is normally $4.25, but because we brought our own cups they ring it in as the smaller size, which is $3.95. And since I can't do dairy I normally do soy milk, and this is one of the only places that doesn't charge extra for soy. We also indulge in a scone or muffin, they have on top of the display case the day-old bakery, which is discounted. Always amazing staff. By far our favorite coffee shop in town

Aw, c'mon, Brian, how am I a shill for "a coffee shop down the street" by providing readers information that $1.91 for a cup of coffee in a toxic styrofoam cup and 75c refills are ridiculous; and, that all-you-can drink coffee, comfortable, safe seating and privacy from street bums and   dogs is available down the street. Down University Boulevard at the University of Arizona Main Gate  and down North Fourth Avenue toward the railroad underpass.

The pastries are to kill for...literally.  All the artery clogging ingredients your doctor warned you to avoid.

Readers would benefit knowing that the contaminated unsanitized key to the Epic's toilet (used by the filthy homeless and drugsters that wander through along with unleashed and unmuzzled dogs, and people who refuse to use soap and water to wash up), dangling off the grimy metal spoon or plastic chicken that serves as a key-ring, reeks of pathogens waiting to explode. The toilet is consistently dirty.

Would you eat, drink, in a restaurant with a dirty toilet? If the public toilet's dirty, how committed is the owner, reputed to be a thug in the Hell's Angels, to assuring that the less-public food-preparation area is clean and safe?

As for the employees currently wrecking havoc at the Epic, since long-time, customer-centric barista Chelsea and her excellent chick baristas quit or were fired by the new owners, the service at the Epic has simply gone to hell.

Best advice is, stay away.

I've ordered from here, delivery, some 5 times total or so, and they do generally have good food. They're very fast and really nice people. So far, we've had their vegetarian curries and a chickpea dish, and samosas. These were good the first two times we got them. Then the third and fourth time they were a little bit lacking in flavor. Then the last time, despiting asking for mild we got two scaldingly spicy dishes that nearly made my eyes fall out.

I apologize, Sahara Indian, you were really good at the beginning but went downhill in only a matter of two months. Your delivery time was always superb though, but isn't enough for me to want to try again after the over-spiced eyeball sauna you gave me.

I've lived in Philadelphia for six years and honestly, this is the best place for banh mi. I found this place by mistake. Right next door is a tailor/dry cleaner place that i always go to... 

I'll admit that there are off days, but I rarely had that experience with this place. The banh bi here uses the real baguette, not those subway bun POS. The pate is nothing to complain about...I have learned that you have to ask for extra veggie when you're ordering from here or else they will skim on that stuff. 

I love this place and honestly, for a mom and pop shop that's well hidden... you can't beat it's value nor it's price. 

LOVE LOVE LOVE!

I'm a reluctant, ambivalent Epic regular. A recent move places Epic as the closest cafe, and rapidly approaching finals coupled with an uncanny caffeine addiction drag me into this oddly eclectic and contradictory place.

Hours: Open until midnight every night. Awesome.

WIFI: The internet is more consistent and faster than at either Bentley's or Caffe Luce. It's less reliable but faster than Starbucks. It's less reliable and slower than Crave, UMC cafeteria, Raging Sage, Cartel, etc.  

Staff: I've interacted with nearly every staff member at this point. I haven't been the overly-friendly, open person I typically am - but even with that, all of the staff have been quite friendly. I'm a fairly observant individual and occasionally I'm here for 10 hours at a time -  I've never observed them treat anyone poorly. I have observed them go out of their way to help people though. I like them.

Coffee: The price is about the same as most other coffee shops, as is the quality. In my biased opinion, nothing has come close to matching Ike's in quality or price, and I lament daily over this tragic loss.

Food: Over-priced, but tasty. It's on par with Bentley's ridiculous prices. They have a wide variety of freshly baked goods that vary by the day. As another reviewer has attested, the breakfast burrito is phenomenal - but again, paying $6.00 for a tortilla, potatoes and eggs is absurd - but hey, I'm an absurd person, so bring on some more egregiously priced burritos.

Cleanliness: Many have commented on unsanitary conditions. There are flies buzzing about on occasion, sure; and the bathrooms - although I wouldn't call them a disaster - are vile in an aesthetic sense. I wouldn't consider them any less sanitary than any other coffee shop bathroom - it's just the aesthetics. Personally, I derive some grotesque sort of solace from the witty, inappropriate commentary scribbled over the bathroom walls. The furniture...it does seem a bit dingy, but that's what gives this place character. You want sterile? Go to Starbucks, you drone. 

Patrons: Diverse. College students, professors, graduate students, hipsters, yuppies, retired folk, indigents, etc. Unlike my vast experiences at Coffee Xchange, I've never witnessed an "event" here where shit gets cray cray. No bums throwing chairs and screaming about murdering everyone. No methed out college kids trying to guzzle down 6 red-eyes in one go while loudly shouting about how dark it is outside when it's 2am in the morning. No heavy drug use in the bathrooms (that I'm aware of, although it's likely, because people are awesome like that). Overall, it's safe here. If you're afraid of being exposed to peculiar individuals, crawl back into your hole or stick to Starbucks drive-thrus.

On a personal note, I find it exceptionally odd that they so heavily push "gluten-free" foods, are a certified "green business," etc., yet they sell cigarettes here. This hipster element fills me with contempt. Further, the little spiritual / meditation / new age / snake oil pamphlet/books they have for sale near the window makes me shudder in disdain. 

Overall, I love and hate this place. It's comfortable in an uncomfortable way. The staff is great, the food is good, and the coffee is average. The prices can go jump off a bridge and die.

Ultimately, I mourn the loss of Ike's. Epic is a necessary supplement. If Ike's or its functional equivalent were to open anywhere in Tucson, I'd instantly abandon ship and find residence elsewhere, regardless of the bicycling mileage involved.

Yes this is definitely a great theatre in Philadelphia probably because it is located the ritzy Olde City. They show independent films. I'm not much of a movie theatre person until someone drags with me with. The last time I was here was to see to see Slum Dog millionaire, which wasn't available in all theaters so it was good it was shown here. Great movie, great experience. I recommend Ritz East if you are a movie buff.

Why does the staff have to be so mean?  I was in line the other day and the poor girl in front of me was reamed out by the ticket seller!  She told her the film she wanted to see was sold out (but really RUDELY) then said "YOU SHOULD HAVE BOUGHT YOUR TICKET EARLIER!!! Yes, she said the entire sentence in capital letters.  Just because she has a shitty job she has to take it out on us poor schlubs?  Pffft.

They're damn lucky they have the market cornered on decent flicks.

Mediocre cafe would be a much more apt description. I've come here 4 times, twice for a sandwich at lunch and twice for studying and coffee. 

I'll start with the good, Epic's peanut butter mocha and desserts are VERY good, and if you can find a couch it's a decent study spot.

Now, the two times I've gotten sandwiches here have been VERY frustrating. Both times the staff forgot my order and was whipping out other sandwiches and hummus plates while I sat and watched hungrily. Each time I had to approach the staff and ask for my sandwich. Today the girl that took my order apologized several times after I talked to her, however when the sandwich came I found that I had paid $8.67 for an oily, over basiled, pesto sandwich on lackluster bread which was billed as "Herb Parmesan", and a little bag of salt and vinegar chips.

I won't be coming back here again for lunch, although I might for a mocha or dessert. Stick to the premade stuff and coffee, if you want a meal head further down 4th.

I sit at Epic on Tuesdays and Thursdays while the significant other attends class up the street. Each time I come in I'm reminded of the awesome cafes in Portland. The gals behind the counter usually have a tattoo, or 12, which makes me itch to get more. I usually settle on a comfortable spot and drink a flavored Mocha and eat a muffin. It also thrills me that there is Vegan fare here. The atmosphere is inviting, the people are friendly and the free wifi is an added perk. It's also definitely worthy of 5 stars.

The guy at the front was pretty disrespectful in letting us know the kitchen was closed already....

Instead of verbally telling us... he points to the sign he was standing in front of (which is obviously blocking our view of it anyway) as if we were unintelligent and incapable of understanding a kitchen close time.. 
He then proceeds to "explain" to me as if I was a 5 year old that the kitchen was closed.

No thanks..

Great place, love the AM witch (bagel, egg, tomato and cheese.)
Good free internet.

Tried to go to Nhu Y (not Nhuy as spelled on here), but it was closed so went to this nearby place. Got 3 sandwiches (dac biet and fancy pork). The sandwiches were small and light on fillings. The bread was hard (like it was yesterday's baguettes). The pate was good, but just in one smear in the middle, and there were few pickled carrots/radishes, making the sandwiches dry overall. I've only had worse in Montreal

A bit far form center city but in a cool area and still offers film viewing at a reasonable price.  The seats are fine but the screens are small (compared to the multiplexes that everyone goes to nowadays) but you wouldn't come here to see a major blockbuster action movie.  I've watched Slumdog Millionaire and Conviction here and both times, the place was just perfect.  The student discount and matinee pricing are awesome too!

I love the Ritz East! It's always clean, the staff is always friendly, and it's NEVER overcrowded. I enjoy being able to see a movie without feeling stuffed into the theater! They serve coffee & tea as well, for those of us that enjoy a hot beverage with our movies. I will continue to see movies here as long as I live in Philly.
This is probably my favorite place to get a Vietnamese hoagie ! I normally get the cold cut special with a can of soy bean ! The bread warm, crispy, the pate and meat is !

My fave coffee shop in Tucson. Extremely friendly staff and the owner treats us like family. Savory breakfast favorite is the AM-Wich (croissant with egg, cheese, meat). Sweet breakfast favorites are the scones and muffins, handmade in the kitchen. So delicious! LOTS of gluten-free and vegan options. Also lots of space to sit with groups and bring kids in.

tried sahara again tonight (the 3rd time i've ordered from them).  i live around the corner and like to support the local businesses but i think i'm done with sahara.  the food isn't aweful but it's not great (some items are average, others below average).  i eat at tiffin and ekta a lot and this does not compare.  tiffin and ekta are much better.  sahara is a few dollars cheaper than ekta or tiffin but i'd rather spend the extra $2/entree for much better food.  sorry sahara but the local competition is just too good for me to return...

i think i just came on a bad day. my friend and i ordered tea, but they were out of teabags and assured us it would be fine loose. it was...not so fine. the flavor was great, but we periodically were sticking our tongues out at eachother coated with bits of rooibus.
THEN. as we were sitting outside with our leafy tongues, a "regular" (or so it seemed) walked ALL the way outside to LET ME KNOW that i have horrible posture, and she didn't want to be rude, but i would look much better if i didn't. if you didn't want to be rude, then you shouldn't have! i am very well aware of the way i sit to deal with how much my back hurts!!!!!!! 

ANYWAYS. the tea, though leafy, was very good. the cakes looked like i would love to live inside one, and i would've loved to try their sandwiches. and for the record, i thought the rubber chicken was hilarious.
Just a killer local coffee shop with excellent espresso and homemade goodness like banana cream pie- delectable!

Our impromptu tour of Old City ended with plans to see a movie here. Street parking for the two-hour spots around here is pretty cutthroat so we ended up using the automated multi-story parking garage attached to the theatre. I was all psyched to use my old uni ID but the impatient lady at the ticket counter was hollering, "No student discounts on Saturdays!" Oh well. Not like I hadn't wanted to see Black Swan anyways.

Interesting that they rotate a lineup of two showings at this location. The concessions staff were an efficient lot, even though the non-fountain beverages didn't call to me. A very long booth facing the bathrooms/concessions makes for comfortable seating for waiting friends. Everyone respected the rules during the movie; no one left their phone off vibrate, no one made loud obnoxious commentary. Not even a crying baby in our crowded lot. I was a little embarrassed when my hyena laughter rang out like a gunshot and sank a little lower in my tippy seat.
Service pleasant. Bagel good. Drinks fine. My son drink order took forever. Flies awful.

I could not resist stopping by and checking out desserts while on my walk.  I knew I was in trouble when I say the chocolate cream pie.  Without hesitation,  I ordered a slice.  It was a generous serving and had a good chocolate flavor.  The crust was well made flaky and not soggy.
I like the atmosphere ar Epic.  Very casual with scattered tables around the dinning room to accommodate a single up to a group of eight.  The back area has some couches arranged to encourage conversations.  Food is ordered at the counter and picked up at the window.  Menu is limited to some breakfast items, salads, or sandwiches plus coffees, ice drinks and desserts. 
I like the dessert section and would highly recommend something from their sweet list.  Overall, a nice experience if you need a place to kick back.

Ended up here instead when I realized that today was Thursday so Nhuy was closed. Even though I always say that the bread is a vessel for the meat, it is a very important vessel.  Here the bread was crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside...check.  There were plenty of meat, cucumber, pickled carrots, cilantro, and pepper.  Overall the sandwich tastes good but I definitely have had better.  I'm pretty picky about my banh mi.  Also, there is not a lot of variety here.  Where is the xui mai?

IMHO, one of the best places to come in this city for a house baked good. Everything is just fantastic and, if you're a vegan, this is your baked goods heaven.
As a coffee shop though? Maybe not.
When I first moved out here this was one of the first coffee shops I found so I came here quite a bit. It's an old building, so plugs are hot commodities and, even in the summer, the place is pretty busy all the time. Lots of people there just to be seen, but a lot of people also working. Quite a bit of loud conversation too (the high ceilings don't help) so, if you're going to work, bring headphones.
Bathroom's an issue. There's only one and it requires a key from the front.
Wifi never really worked very well. Probably because of the sheer number of people using it.
Seating's an issue. Even if you don't need/want a plug, it's tough to get a seat in there many times, especially during the school year. 
So, now, honestly, it's one of my last choices for a coffee shop in town. However, if I'm on 4th and want something sweet, or with some friends and we're looking for a place to sit for a while and eat or drink something good and non-alcoholic, Epic is first on my list. I just LOVE their food and it's a great place to come for breakfast.
I also noticed this time that they've put up a bunch of ultra-passive aggressive signs regarding, for instance, use of the wifi, leaning on glass cases while in line (the line gets really long, another minus for this place), the use of nuts in their cooking, etc.
But how about the coffee? It's not bad but it's not great. They seem to like to burn the beans sometimes. Typical price, $0.50 refills. Large sizes are served in regular glasses, which is a little annoying. Mediums are in a mug though.
The weird crowd can partially be explained by the neighborhood but also by the fact that there are an abnormally large number of halfway houses and rehab centers within a few blocks, in addition to a methadone clinic. I mean, I've never had problems, but it seems to freak some people out.
Parking is free and there's a big bike rack right outside. Definitely a plus.
$7 minimum on credit cards.
Beautiful, inviting temple with an awesome marketplace to boot. Thai food was good; outdoor seating on the river was even better.

Fogo De Chao is an awesome place for dinner and wine. I recently just had dinner here for Valentin's day with my wife. Before that I hadn't been here in a few years but they didn't disappoint from how I rendered them. The side were great compliments to the meat and the sear on the meats were perfect. The season was spot on. Good place for a night out in center city. The waiting staff was polite and very helpful explaining how the flow of the restaurant worked. As well as checking in with our table they didn't hover but were very punctual on checking in with us. Definitely recommend.

Needing iced coffee, and wanting to support local businesses, we stopped in here before venturing further into 4th. A large sunny bustly cafe, there were clusters of people sitting outside under umbrellas smoking and going over books and papers (UofA is right there!). There was a long line snaking the counter when we first went in, so I peered in the bakery case and saw huge doughy scones and other gooey dessert pleasures. And then I saw one of the scones was vegan. Then I saw almost ALL of the pastries were vegan! I almost squealed (I think maybe I did) since they all looked so good and vegans are used to being denied pastries due to egg, cream, etc. Although I wasn't hungry, I can't stop seeing the visually stimulating displays of szones, bars, cakes, pies, brownies, cookies...mmmmm. The line moved pretty quickly, the coffee was a good price and I was happy to see they had soy milk on the counter (I hate when places charge extra for soy milk). The cafe had people who looked like lifers-and some had their shoes off on chairs (a lil ewwww) but most were academic like intent in conversations, books or laptops. Pretty great atmosphere with lots of seating. We took our drinks outside and sat on the side of the building with more seating (although the white plastic chairs were kind of dirty), I would def. go to this cafe if I had schoolwork to do...

Ritz East is one of 3 Ritz theaters all in walking distance. Like its counter parts, Ritz East is arts sort of house. It carries smaller indie movies, which includes some of the major Oscar contending movies.

The other two Ritz theaters carry 5 movies a piece. Ritz East, however, has only two movies. That said, it has much more seating and larger screens. Though, the screens considering the size of the theaters could be a little bigger. But hey, it is an arts house.

Ritz East is kept up very well. It's clean and about as modern as you'd expect an arts house to be. Since it's not pulling in the big bucks of a major theater, you should not expect it to be state of the arts.

The service is very good. And, the prices are always better than a major theater. And to be honest, the quality of movies is better too! Good spot to see those less popular, but clearly better, movies.

I went here on Sunday night with my girlfriend and had a mix of dishes, everything great. Restaurant was clean and comfortable along with quick service. We ordered the rice vermicelli with bbq pork, rice plate with bbq beef and spring rolls which were all really good. Both of us are excited to finally have an authentic Vietnamese restaurant in the area! The avocado shake was also a must try.
I love everything about this place.. From the food to services... I got "com tam dac biet" $8.25

I am so glad a friend had recommended this place for my wedding.  Johnny and Annie were very professional from the very start.  I had so many questions and they were very patient with me.  I was not an easy bride to work with but they kept their focus on us the whole time.  They offer many services and specialized in American and Chinese Weddings but by the time I reached them I only needed a DJ and MC.  They went above and beyond to help make my vision come true and also share many new and creative ideas for the wedding. Their price were very inexpensive considering the stellar service we received.  It's worth checking out.

I used Only You MC and DJ service for my wedding. James (MC) and Joe (DJ) did a wonderful job at my wedding. Both of them were professional and made sure my wedding went smoothly according to my timeline. My wedding was a huge success thanks to the both of them. I would definitely recommend everyone to use them for future service. You can't beat great service for a awesome price.

Ever have an Epic moment?  You will here, maybe even many!  This place is awesome, the coffee is great, menu selection is good but the best part are the baristas, particularly the morning baristas.  Alex, Mike and Char - they rock!  Always greet you with a cheery smile, offer a great sense of humor, and do their best to get that coffee to you ASAP, because after all, that's what is most necessary in the early morning!  

The baked-on-premises goodies are divine - they have a delicious gluten-free selection nearly every day, and you need to try the seeded cookie or one of the fresh scones and muffins, which come in several different varieties each day; my favorite is the savory rosemary, honey walnut scone.  

I love that they display local artists' works on the walls and that on occasion one can even observe a local artist at work there.  I also love that when I am out for an early morning walk with my dog, Mia, I can pop in with her and grab a cup of coffee without having to tie her up outside! Often they even have a treat for her!  

The cafe itself could use a makeover and some deep cleaning.  The couches should be thrown out and replaced or at minimum, re-upholstered with something washable, and the plants in the front windows need major TLC.  

But, all being said, I love that it's LOCAL, and that I can hang out there any day and will be rewarded with good coffee, good conversation and interesting sights!

GO EPIC!!

When my fiancé and I got engaged in 2015, we knew who we wanted to provide entertainment for our wedding, so we scheduled an appointment with Only You Wedding store. We met with Annie, and immediately felt like we were in good hands. She offered thoughtful and creative ideas to align with our vision for the wedding, and balanced modern (Millennial generation) concepts with traditional Asian customs (as we wanted to incorporate aspects of our Chinese heritage). We kept in touch with Annie throughout the wedding planning process to bounce ideas with her, and she was always quick to respond. My fiancé also decided to rent a Chinese Qipao dress from Only You, and Annie worked closely with her to ensure it matched my fiance's style, taste, and figure.

As our big day finally came upon us, Annie took it upon herself to be there at our event to coordinate the DJ and MC services. Her team arrived early to ensure they were set up in time for the ceremony, and provided great sound and music (we decided to go with our own custom playlist) for the procession. Annie's team then seamlessly transitioned over to the ballroom to begin the reception activities. 

From the beginning, we knew we wanted to work with her MC partner, James. We had attended two weddings before that James had serviced, and were impressed by his energy and vigor. He kept the crowd enthused through the evening as a host, and made sure the music aligned with the mood of dinner and dancing. When speaking of James to others, I describe him as an "Asian Ryan Seacrest. He's that good! Plus he speaks fluent English, Cantonese, and Mandarin."

We can't thank Annie, James, and the whole Only You Wedding team enough for helping us make our wedding the most memorable day of our lives!

as a visitor, brightly colored coffeeshops, with coffee- and city-knowledgeable baristas, a wide assortment of both consumable offerings and inhabitants, are a nice respite from driving through towns and cities where one must struggle to find somewhere decent to sit for a while. 

in other words, the coffee is good, the food is good, the selection is even better. and coming from a place with good coffeeshops, i like it here.

If you frequent Starbucks regularly, don't bother coming here, and shame on you. 

Epic Cafe is the quintessential Tucson Coffee shop. It is always a really good place to study and get work done, mostly because it is one of the few places open until midnight everyday. The coffee is pretty good, and the one time I tried their Breakfast Burrito was delightful. It is usually pretty busy but I've rarely had trouble finding somewhere to sit. 

Here's where the pleasantries end, and the quintessential Tucson bit begins. It is far from the cleanest place, the furniture looks worn down and dirty, the tables are rarely cleaned, the bathrooms are also not that clean and a lot of (for lack of a better word) dirty people like to frequent this place and hang around all day. I know that last bit sounds really terrible and judgmental on my part, but when you can smell a person from the other side of the room... that's what I'm referring to when I say dirty people. Service ranges from either amazing to not that great. There's been a few times when the person behind the counter forgot to even make my drink. 

All in all though, Epic is a coffee shop with a lot of soul. If you need to study, this is the place to come. If you're the type of person that would let the few negative aspects to get to you, then you don't deserve a place like Epic anyways, and should go back to your shitty Starbucks coffee and stay there.

This restaurant was hands down the best experience I've had in Philly in a long time. Such a gem. We had the tasting menu and every dish was absolutely phenomenal. The specialty drinks were made to perfection as well. Our waiter, Jeff, took the time to give us the best recommendations based on our taste and he truly made our experience even better, which we appreciated. I encourage everyone reading this to try this restaurant as it's my #1 favorite place in philly now, and it will soon to be yours! Thanks to the chef, bartender and Jeff for making our night impeccable!

I think this place has a lot of potential but the customer service was the worst I have ever seen. I have never left a bad review and I'm too kind to even put one star which is what I would truly rate this place. I had a few people ask me about this place and I simply told them your experience might be better but they don't want to go now. No so epic is how I would describe it. Nevertheless I hope they work it out and I wish them all the best. My suggestion hire Grant Cardone.
Clean, comfortable, and well-maintained. Watched Ex Machina and the crowd was a lot better in terms of theater etiquette. Small but worth the visit.

Epic seems to be one of the popular cafes of Tucson, and it seems to be an important part of the community.  I'm sure its size and proximity to the university campus contribute to its popularity.  It is also open late at night, which is an advantage over other cafes in the neighborhood.

They have a variety of good coffees and loose-leaf tea, as well as cakes and other desserts.  The wireless internet is free, as usual.  They also have outdoor tables, which are nice except when it is hotter than 40 C.

This is a great little movie theater. The surrounding area is beautiful, if you have some time to kill and want to walk around a bit. They usually show just a few movies, geared more to the artsy/independent film snob crowd, of which I hesitantly consider myself member. Tickets could be cheaper (and no student discounts on Saturdays- when else do students have time to go to the movies?) but I guess we will never see the $5 movie days of my youth again.

Nice quaint restaurant near the university in Tucson. Staff are super friendly!  Good food with great service!  Had a delicious veggie melt sandwich with multi grain  foccaccia bread.  Simply marvelous!  For dessert, had a homemade flan sitting on a bed of caramelized sugar sprinkled with silvered almonds.  Hmm... To die for!!!  Most tasty!  This place would be ideal for a vegetarian as they have a wide choice of salads, veggie sandwiches, hummus.

Um It is free with $3 skate rentals. So I shouldn't even complain. However, it is definitely what skating under I-95 should be like.

SKETCH.

In all seriousness, this place is a good if you have your own skates, are 13 trying to pick up one of the boys that works here, or 5 years old. I am a bigger fan of the RIver Rink for the romantic ice skating adventures. Even though you have to pay major $$ (in comparison to here).

Expect great quality tasting banh mi here. Don't expect great customer service. Don't expect your typical American run establishment with a clean environment. Expect this to be a small hole in the wall authentic Vietnam restaurant as if you were in Vietnam itself. The banh mi are delicious.

I was contacted by someone telling me that the back of the PF Chang gift card says airports are excluded because i complained in my last review that they didn't take it.  I'm assuming they work there and it was pretty comical. Check out my pick of the back of the gift card, I can read two lines past 20/20 and I can assure you that neither myself or anyone buying or receiving the gift card would take the time to read that.

This is the best spot in life. 

My only draw back is that the staff is not always nice. Now how im grading this is the fact that when I speak, you should speak back and not just nod your head in acknowledgement.

I love Epic and will continue to come regardless but I really wish I could have a good report from people I refer...because so far this place is making me look like I enjoy having people be rude to  me when I want a cup of coffee.

What Epic lacks in service they make up for in their amazing drinks, teas, foods and overall environment (once you step away from the counter). Not to mention I love the booths now..

Epic

An urban theater that only plays really good movies.  They don't do big ticket blockbusters, they show good stories, and only two at a time if that.  They also have a wide variety of snacks, from your usual popcorn and soda to the non-standard cookies and coffee.  

Absolutely get your parking validated when you buy your ticket, and if you have a student ID, use it!  Movies are about $2 cheaper with ID.  Wednesdays are half price ticket too, so if you're looking for a weeknight date, this can be a cheap escape!
Love this place!! BEST viet hoagies!!!! Been eating their hoagies since I was little...that's over 20 years

A really great independent movie theatre located in old city.

The ritz is fairly small (with only two screens), but it has a great feel, decently large theatre spaces, and a fully stocked concession stand. The first time I came was to see a Japanese language film, "Like Father Like Son," during the Philadelphia film festival three years back. The Ritz was the only theatre showing it in Philly I believe. 

I went for the second time yesterday for a free early screening of "Criminal." The movie was definitely not on par with the last I'd seen, but it was still a fun time, and I still stand by the Ritz and its mission!
Amazing theater. I forget how large the cinemas are. Hope to go back again some day.
great drinks and desserts, open till late. love this place!

This is a  great bakery and having it right in our Old City neighborhood makes it really convenient.  Service is great, too.  They have a wide variety of pastries, including some not commonly found in the U.S. but found in Switzerland and France.  They hit a home run in my book when I called at noon to see if they could have a white cake with buttercream frosting and a Happy Birthday message ready for me by 6:00.  They said the could meet my request and they delivered.  The staff is always very friendly, too.  The selection of baked goods is a bit smaller than in some of the other bakeries in town (or in the bakeries I have seen in Europe), and for that reason only I am giving them 4 stars.  For the things they do they are a 5 star bakery.

We had an enjoyable time at the theatre last night. The movie was great, but we also enjoyed it because it was at the Ritz East.

Thanks to the Ritz East for having hot tea for those of us who are not on a soda fix. Thanks for making it with boiled water rather than lukewarm stuff from a canister.  I had a tasty cup of Earl Gray, which seemed right given that I was about to see Anna Karenina.  

Thanks to the Ritz East for having Jill, who served me the tea. Jill was totally nonplussed with my unusual tea requests (one bag, but large cup) and accommodated other family members' individualized food and drink preferences.

Thanks to the Ritz East manager.
