Before the movie started, he came to the front of the theatre, welcomed all the viewers, described us as part of the "family," and advised us to go out to the lobby if we had any issues, concerns or questions during the film. I have never been greeted in any theatre, let alone with such a sincere and warm introduction.  

We highly recommend the Ritz. The selection of movies is always good. The cost is in line with other theatres. It offers student and senior discounts. You can order tickets online.  It has good food and drinks. The staff is warm and friendly.

On the downside, parking is difficult in that area. Go early if you don't have tickets beforehand.  Like other theatres, you will sit through a half hour of prequels.  Of course, you might learn about other films you will want to see at Ritz East..

Outstanding food and decor!! Was really taken back with the amazing atmosphere comfortable chairs and amazing wait staff. The food was out of this world authentic, I recommend being adventurous or you can play it safe but you won't be let down. Your taste buds may not be use to the taste but you will be able to taste the quality in every dish.

One of, if not the best coffee house in town. Apart from the *ahem* bathroom key situation (see other reviews), Epic is the bees knees. 

I've taken several out-of-towners here for a quick cup and haven't had 1 disappointment yet. The coffee is stellar, the foodstuffs are great, and the wifi is FREE! Stop by for lunch (sandwich and an iced tea) with your laptop and get some work done, you won't want to leave. The atmosphere is a pleasant mix of hippie-gone-yuppie, with more weight on the former.

Huge fan of this place for a quick, fresh, cheap, and delicious lunch.  The chicken hoagie is magnificent (tell them to go easy on the butter).  If you like pate, they will gladly put some on the bread for you.  I prefer it the way it comes and love the combination of chicken, jalapenos, and cilantro on french bread.  The coffee is also very good and a nice way to finish lunch.  They only have two tables inside so getting lunch to go is usually the way to do it.

The best Indian food. 100 times better than Tiffin (ick) or Ekta. Prices are slightly better.

They use quality ingredients, and their flavors are excellent.

I live a block and a half away, and the guys here have come to know me and my housemate well. I love that the cook runs to the window to wave hello when he sees me walk by!

I recommend the lamb biryani and of course, their excellent chicken tikka masala.

Better than saigon cafe. Best hoagie I've ever eaten in my life. Place is traditional and may be best for take out. I'm seriously still thinking about the hoagie I ate. (I had the cold cut special - Dac biet) My aunt came back to visit Philly and she took back 15+ hoagies for her family and friends. She dedicated a carry on suitcase for this.

Absolutely LOVE this place! Is by far my favorite cafe in town. My favorites include their iced chai (with soy), anything with their cold-brewed coffee which is super concentrated and strong, and their delicious white chocolate raspberry scones. They usually have a variety of tasty treats in their glass case, like pecan pie or chocolate cake to go with your beverage. The people here are friendly. I love going here to study or just swinging by to get coffee.
Also, another bonus is if you bring in your own cup, they will charge you at a lower price (for example if my cup I bring in is a medium drink, they will fill it, but charge me for a small drink).
Only negative is that it gets so cold in there sometimes! Just bring a jacket. A nice escape from the broiling Tucson sun though :)

This review is strictly based on service, or lack thereof .

I won tickets here for an advanced screening of a movie and I was very excited because of the movie and my chance to try out a new theater, as I've never been to this particular space. Now I've been to an advanced screening at the Pearl at Temple, so I was expecting it to be much like that. Nope. 

Now at the Pearl, my friend and I had gotten to the theater at least a half hour before the show start time, since we wanted seats and the ticket said they overbook the show. Low and behold it was packed and we got one of the last seats at the very front. So I figured this time it would work out the same, more or less. 

Showing up 45 minutes early (all I could manage with work) to the Ritz gave us a huge surprise. Instead of being able to go right in and find a seat there was a huge line that wrapped around the building. Womp. 

That's all well and good. My friend and I had no problem waiting in the line, and slowly but surely around 6:50 or so they began letting people in. Slowly. Around 7:10 we stopped moving. They had stopped letting people in and at 7:20 people began getting a bit grumpy, us included. If the show was supposed to start at 7:30, why were so many of us still outside with no notification of when we would be let in or if we even would. Many people in front of us began leaving the line to check out what was happening and reported that 1)staff were just standing around inside doing nothing/arguing with people who were waiting to get in 2) they were letting the people who were already inside buy concessions 3) some of the seats were taken by employees who were allowed to watch the movie. Only the first two made me pissy.

I can totally understand that seating is first come first serve. That's all well and good. But the Ritz had at least 70 of us just standing outside with no information whatsoever. We had been waiting at least an hour, and those in front of us definitely longer, and they had just stopped letting people in and told us nothing. Apparently they had begun counting seats so they could begin letting people in, but they were waiting until the people buying concessions sat back down. Um, how about you should know how many seats the theater has and initially keep count of the people coming in. Or do like the Pearl theater did and just let people come in and grab a seat. With over a 100 people waiting in line in the cold, at least give us some info. They could have let us in at 6:30 and then when everyone is seated and waiting for the movie to begin, allow people to go in and out to buy concessions. That's what the Pearl did and it worked extremely well. Shrug. 

By the time 7:40 rolled around (the movie was supposed to begin at 7:30) my friend and I decided to just leave. There were at least 40 people in front of us and 30 behind us, and if they had that many seats open they wouldn't need to count, so we figured our chances of getting in where slim. I'm sure the movie theater in general is awesome, but this experience and lack of service just left a bad taste in my mouth.

Really cool looking place.  

Came here for breakfast ordered two breakfast burritos one for my friend and one for me yay but they effed up our order we still ate it anyways because we were hungry and they would have taken long  but that was one of the issues  another was that the employees didn't seen happy I didn't get a good vibe wish they smiled or said welcome to our cafe they just looked tired I get it it's 8am but common act at least a little happy. 

This is our first time in Arizona and the first place we stopped at for breakfast so it would have been nice for this place to be woahhh but it was meh due to them messing up both of our orders and the energy of the employees but the three stars is for the place not being so busy and the food coming out to us in a timely manner also for the location of the place and for the artsy vibe I loved how it looked inside and out :) look forward to coming here in the future and perhaps leaving with a great smiling face if you're ever in Tucson you should try this place :) tootles

This was our first time in this movie theater. It was very clean and comfy. Got to watch Chuck..(it was great!) which is only available at this location. I wanna return because I saw a bunch of preview I was interested in.
Very cool coffee shop. The have a breakfast and lunch menu too. Lots of homemade stuff and also vegan stuff. Just a great place to go. Been going there since place opened about 1998.

Funky artsy little cafe. Very friendly staff. Delicious bakery selection. I had the peanut butter mocha which was not too sweet but just perfect in every way. They serve it hot or cold or blended with ice cream. I will be back! Yum.
Intimate theater, good for indie fans.

I'm sitting in Epic Cafe right now, using their free wifi, eating a gluten free raspberry muffin, and drinking the recommended iced toddy-with cream and sugar (in the form of simple syrup-these people are my heroes, just for understanding that sugar doesn't dissolve properly in cold drinks).  

It's late on a Sunday morning; there is a crowd, but it's not crowded, and there is plenty of seating (including more than one couch).  The air conditioning is keeping the place delightfully cool.  There is only one barista working, so he's a little busy, but he was quick, efficient, and helpful. The place is colorful, clean, and interesting.

The pastry case is PACKED.  Seriously.  There's something for everyone.  I am gluten intolerant, so I was really stoked to see gluten free baked goods, and not just one but THREE-the aforementioned muffin, a 
chocolate chip cookie, and huge pieces of cookies and cream cake.  The muffin actually tastes good too, and doesn't have the texture of cardboard.  It looks, tastes, smells, and feels like a "real" muffin.

It's easy to find too.  In fact, I was looking for a different coffee shop and ended up here.  It was meant to be, it seems.  And it only cost me about $7, plus tip.  That's about right, I think.

Excellent food.
Plus the famous Aaron Abbott worked there.
Best Vietnamese hoagies in the area. My family and I have been going here for years. It's $4 per hoagie, it's delicious! Get the classic.

Epic is a great spot to get together for a quick meeting or to catch up with a friend. The vibe is not of this state! Feels like I'm up in the bay area here. Staff is all very friendly and the service is efficient. While we only had a few drinks here, coffee and tea related ;), but the food looked mighty good. I'll have to go back and experience Epic in its entirety!

Came here last night for an early screening of Don't Think Twice and some of the cast came by at the end for a Q&A! Great experience - this theater is super comfy and big and there's a good amount of available parking in the area. It's also right next to Penn's Landing so you can take a nice stroll next to the water and contemplate whatever indie or artsy movie you've just seen afterwards.

This place is kind of what you would expect for an independent movie house.  It has the Ritz name, but isn't exactly of that quality I think.  Yes, they have a ton of specialty items in the concession stand, but the place is kind of dingy.  It's only a two theater place with a tiny waiting area.  They were only playing one movie the time we were there.  As the movie was letting out, people were openly talking about the movie as patrons (such as myself) were waiting to get into the theater.  Like....why on earth would you do that?  The size of this place only heightens this dilemma, but I'm not going to blame this on the theater.  No stadium seating? Kind of sucks.  I understand it's an older theater, but I am too used to this and will always hold theaters to this standard.    I did like the theater's appreciation for history.  In the lobby they feature tons of old pictures from Philadelphia and have even more when you are waiting in the theater as preview screens.

The staff is friendly and will validate your parking.  What allotted to a $17 parking came down to $8...score!

My summary: "Healthnut without being healthnazi."

The sign on the door reads: "Not closed (usually) between 6am and 12midnight." My brother and I were sure to test out the full length of those hours on one of our three days we had in Tucson... but all three of the days would include at least one stop in at Epic.

Let me quickly just say that the name of the place is no lie. This place is mythos. The people who hang out here, the environment, the workers, the drinks and the food could truly be copied down to legend solely on the basis of crossing boundaries of believability. Yet it's pretty down to earth, rugged and quite real while you're there.

Unlike Starbucks and some of the more Nazi-esque indies, Epic still has a smoking section outside of the building. One side, where the main entrance is found, is smoke free. The other side of the building is for smoking. You can pick up WiFi just about anywhere outside, although there's no power outlets... so juice up while inside o' the place.

Crazy shout out in thanks to all the Yelpers who'd previously rated and reviewed the place, as that's what lead my brother and I here on our way thru Tucson. With how much in-depth knowledge has already been posted here, I'll cut this short and just say: "So long, much love, and thanks for all the caffeinated WiFi!"

Staff, wi-fi, hot tea and breakfast burritos have been great! I yet to try a the pastries but they look amazing, no idea how much they cost. I like the seeing musicians playing outside, artist, politicians, bums and students all gathering here. My 2 dogs enjoy chillin with me inside to take a break from the heat. Love that Tucson vibe!

We love this place! very reasonable! If you enter the door of the rink they will give you tickets you dont have to pay for the skating rentals! BUT You have to give the tickets to the worker who works there

I really miss great breakfast & diners the city use to have. It is refreshing to find a place with great tasting breakfast for a fair price. 

I don't know what their lunch taste like because the breakfast is what sold me on becoming a repeat customer. 

Their food is actually seasoned to taste. Not too salty nor bland.  The portions are nicely sized. I particularly like their pancakes & french toast. The way I judge good pancakes/french toast is when you can eat them without using maple syrup & it tastes good. 

The only thing I recommend improvement is the appearance of some of the cashiers.  Some are sloppily dressed and/or wearing hair scarves/bonnets. Its very unprofessional looking especially being the first person customers see when ordering their food.

A funky vibe, lots of students sitting around on their laptops or reading, some nice sidewalk seating, good food and excellent coffee. But it's a little pricey for what you get, the service can be hit or miss, and they play the worst music whenever I've been here in the afternoons/evenings. 

I just sit outside where I won't have to be subjected to the godawful night club music they play here all the time. I know it's a college crowd, but it really messes up the cool hippie vibe they seem to want to have.
DOES NOT ACCEPT GIFT CARDS!  I was so disappointed that they don't accept gift cards; it completely doesn't make sense. They told me it's a franchise, how are you supposed to know this?

The staff is friendly and consists completely of the epitome of movie dorkdom.  The theatre is clean enough.  I've seen better, I've seen worse.  Prices on eats?  Who knows.  Only a sucker actually buys food and drink at a movie theatre.  

There was an old man sitting in the back row that seemed to be mumbling to himself or perhaps breathing oddly.  I changed my seat as to not be distracted by aforementioned breathing and talking to one's self.  He made a slight outburst near the beginning of the picture when four late comers that were being hoes turned on their flashlight app in order to see where they were going and many patrons sent angry outbursts and he exclaimed "what is wrong with you?!" but to the flashlight hoes or to the disgruntled patrons?  One will never know.  This man is likely deceased by now.

Then again, we were there to see "Nymphomaniac"

One of my top 5 places in Tucson! Located on the edge of 4th and University (street is currently under construction 5-5-12) it is a fantastic breakfast/lunch/dinner/late night choice for food and drinks.  Free Wi-Fi and a "hipster," vibe makes this a hotspot for students and others.  Prices are fair and the menu is extensive.  A new after midnight menu Thursday-Saturday is my favorite newest addition.

I think this is a great theater, especially for a find in the middle of Olde City.  It's definitely small with, i think, just two theatres, but the employees were nice, the amenities were all there with a stocked snackbar, stadium seating, cup holders, and clean bathrooms.  There's actually nothing all that noteworthy, but I think thats the best kind of setup when the theater isn't the attraction, but the movie is.  The movie played without a hitch, and the old timey pictures of Philadelphia showing before the movie were great!  We'll definitely be back!  Oh, and $9 for a Sunday show is pretty good in my book.

when anyone asks me where to get a vietnamese hoagie, i tell them to come here.  

i may not be a vietnamese hoagie expert  (heck, i couldn't even tell you what is in one besides the pate)  but i've had my share of them and cafe cuong is the best i've had. 

Its a small, no frills shop, owned by a really nice couple.  They have one table (but everytime I'm there I feel like the people sitting there are always people they know)  

the hoagies are made to order with baguettes that are fresh and crunchy, and they def don't skimp on the meat.  For a $3.50 sandwich, I couldnt ask for anything better!   You should def check this place out!

I really enjoy watching flicks at this place. It's a small theater and one of the only ones in the city that play indie films. I've seen my fair share of small and large produced films there, most recently, Lincoln. A lot of the papers usually have contests for movies being shown here. My favorite things about Ritz East: Big comfy seats, convenient location and italian sodas (make sure you get the cream soda flavor)!

I've been going to Epic Cafe occasionally for more than 5 years. Recently, I've just been very disappointed. I ordered a salad for lunch a few weeks ago, and it was amazing. I was so excited to come back. But when I came back and ordered the same salad, it came out completely differently. Different toppings, lower quality. I ordered takeout, so I didn't look at it before I took it away, but was completely disappointed when I did. I came back for breakfast a few weeks later and although the breakfast burrito was delicious, I was completely shocked by the price. $13 for a breakfast burrito and an iced tea. Apparently, although there were no prices listed on the menu board at the time, I was charged $8.62 for the burrito, plus $1.87 since I ordered a bacon burrito - no indication on the board that there was an extra charge for bacon. And although I just said I wanted an iced tea, I was charged $0.50 extra for a large without any notice. I regret not saying anything at the time I was told the price. I work just a block away, and wish that I could rely on Epic as a good lunch and breakfast option, but the inconsistencies just make it not worth going.

Went there for a pre-wedding photo. Johnny and Ming were extremely patient and professional. The makeup artist is amazing, and they offer lots of beautiful gowns for you to try on. Great service for a even greater prize! Definitely recommend them!

Terrific theater with super comfortable seats. Looks deceptively small until you go into the screening rooms. Nice size size but not too big. Sound was perfect. We were there for a private screening recently and the two guys in suits checking tickets looked very Secret Service. I expected to see surveillance mics in their ears. Right before the screening, one of them came in and pretty much threatened the room about turning off electronic devices - going so far as to say if he sees a glow, you will be escorted out. Yikes! But I was glad - last thing I want is to listen to some dickwad talking or texting. 
(Now if they could just eliminate popcorn and noisy candy bags. Heaven.)

Where-oh-where would Philly be without its beloved Ritzes? Dunno and don't wanna know!

The necessary antidote for decades to corporate multiplexes like the frightening Riverview, the Ritz "chain" is far more satisfying than your typical art-house Cinema.  Every great film, regardless of country of origin, that isn't being foisted on the public via mass-market release is introduced to Philadelphians at a Ritz, and I like countless others have memories not only of the movies themselves, but of having seen them, specifically, at a Ritz.

An unfortunate one-star deduction must be applied as a direct result of the acquisition of the Ritzes by Landmark, which was followed by the demise of the book-length Ritz program we all loved, and has introduced unwelcome corporate corruptions like long, schmaltzy, saccharine-filled commercials that precede each show.  But if suffering through those minor losses is what it takes to keep the Ritzes alive, so be it.

Seriously excellent.

- The staff are fast and good at what they do. I came early for my takeout and watched them cook and prep... artful, these guys.

- Possibly the best biryani I've ever had in my life. Also possibly the best garlic naan I've ever had, slid straight out of the tandoor for me. The saag paneer got incredible reviews from my compatriot. The korma was devoured and fast.

- I ordered a lassi at the last minute. The owner went into the back and *chopped up fresh mangoes* for it. Just... wow. That, too, best I've ever had.

1 app, 2 meaty mains (w/rice), a chicken biryani, naan, a big lassi = $39. Very very nice.

This might replace TIffin as our go-to.

Great little hole in the wall hippy art kind of place to study, meet up w/ someone or use the free wifi. Food is pretty good & they offer food for omnivores, vegetarians & vegans! They're desserts are my favorite as well as their unique teas & coffees that they offer.

This gem of a movie theater is my favorite in the entire U.S.A.! There's always a great selection of independent films screening for a low price. As a college student I get to pay $7.25 for any showing (except on Saturdays).  Better yet, all movies are $7 for everybody on Wednesdays.  

The two theaters themselves are perfectly sized and have this cozy, homey vibe. I've had the pleasure of seeing so many great movies here over the years such as Chef, Her, Fantastic Mr. Fox, The Tree Of Life, and Wish I Was Here (the midnight premiere to boot).  Philadelphia is truly blessed to have the Ritz East for its viewing pleasure.

Coffee was ok, service was terrible. The barista was a jerk- my friend and I were next in line, right behind the customer being served, barista told us the girl who had just walked in was next in line, since she was standing 6 inches to the left of us and was "in line."

I like this Ritz the best. I just like it. When there's a good movie showing here, it's great. The num nums are inexpensive, the popcorn is tasty, the guys working behind the counter move relatively fast (rather than the snail-like pace at every other movie theater I've ever been to in my lifetime). they serve delicious hot chocolate, and if you go at just the right time, the crowd of people always looks like a sea of parents, which is better than high school students. And one time I stood behind Marc Summers in line here. 

I want a hot chocolate.

Not impressed by this place.
One time, I arrived to move out, and the staffperson was over 30 minutes late, causing me to be charged another full hour.

I call and emailed management- and followed up- but they said they wouldn't reimburse me for the extra hour I spent there.
Great old city theater and location. Everyone was very friendly. Comfortable seats and enjoyable screen and audio.  Looking forward to our next visit!
The espresso at this funky artsy fartsy cafe is better than you'd expect based off its appearance.

This cafe is great. We are from out of town and we stopped in to ask the employees about vegan options. Immediately we had a support team of 3+ people searching for vegan options around the city. We ended up eating here as they do have plenty of vegan options and they offered to cook a meal to fit exactly what we wanted. It was inexpensive, came out pretty much instantly and was delicious.

Epic Cafe-- ::sigh:: this place hits the sweet spot. I don't know if it's because I'm a caffeine junkie or just a big Epic groupie. This place spells love in my heart. Their vegan cookies and cakes are super yummy. I've had better in other cities-- but for a honky tonk town (yikes! this is where half of Tucson gets bitter)... the food aint bad. A little on the dry side, but when it's the only place out of like 2 that offer vegan delights, you realize quickly its the best.

People watching... more like swooning. Such a variety, such an awesome time. I once saw a man with a beret on his head made out of foil. Jealousy ensued and I came home wondering why I didn't ask him to marry me.

Don't try to flirt with the cute staff. They'll just want to quiz you on your hipsterness and proceed to tell you that you're not "hip" enough for your super hip Chrome messenger bag straight from hipster SF. (I wont get into what Tucson even knows about hipsterness). But that's probably what attracts me to this place even more... it has TONS of sub-culture character. 

Back to the coffee rather than Tucson bashing, I love their choices of loose tea. The cherry one was my favorite for probably half a year, until I couldn't refrain from their delicious coffee. Never burnt.. never watered down. 

Sometimes finding seats outside is hard... but finding a lighter to borrow is never an issue (the important things in life... I'll sit on the sidewalk as long as my ciggarette is lit). I can't really do homework in here. The music is too loud and the people are too weird or too damn cute.... I just stare and stare, getting absolutely nothing done.

Prices are written on a chalk board, which only screams at my inner repressed childhood youth. Something about smoking outside, people watching, streaming youtube off their free wi-fi.... and a DAMN good cup of coffee.... you can't beat Epic at ALL.

Epic Cafe is my second choice for coffee and free wi-fi in Tucson. However, I don't live close to Tucson anymore so some of my views may be out of date. (My last visit was October 2011 ... but I will update in September 2012 when I get back to Tucson.) 

GREAT location if you are interested in the 4th Ave scene or walking around downtown Tucson. Their food and coffee is very good, and the menu is surprisingly varied. (Compare this to the crappy generic pastries you get at the chains such as Starbucks or Peet's -- and there is no comparison.)

Very arty and sort of a punk noire ambiance. Great place to observe tattoos (I have none) on both staff and customers. So edgy I feel like a middle-aged accountant when I visit, and I am considered a bit eccentric by friends and family. 

Your grandmother, I suspect, may feel more comfortable over at Bentley's. (I don't believe I have ever seen a child in there although I am sure they are not banned.)

Old odd collection of sofas, chairs, and tables. Quite a bit of space but often tough to find a seat with a table.  Incredible hours! 6 AM to midnight! How can you beat that short of a Denny's? And who wants to be found dead or alive at a Denny's at any hour?

Wi-fi can be a bit sluggish when you get hordes of users. Staff is generally fine & friendly although I had a couple of mildly grainy experiences. (Sort of a ... "I am way too cool to be concerned about your order" kind of attitude.) Bathroom is on the down funky side.

I would give them a 5 star review for food, coffee, location, hours, & arty edginess... 4 stars for the wi-fi... & 2 stars for the bathroom experience.

I really like this place... I was in Tucson to explore coffee shops and ran into this place. I think it's more food than coffee however.. I walked in the line was quite long, but there are enough interesting people and signs on the wall to keep yourself occupied for days. 

For example "Epic Internet is faster than a hooker to the clinic" I mean how can you not love this place.

The coffee was okay.. a lil too sweet for me, but out of all the people who ordered ahead of me, no one ordered espresso drinks.. so I can't ding them for that. 

Everyone, I mean everyone working there was so effing nice, I almost want to give them 5 stars.
Fun, funky and artsy spot! Great loose leaf teas and baked goods! Excellent customer service makes it a great find in the 4th St. area!
Great pho and great service. I got the brisket pho and the spring rolls. Both were great. I'm looking forward to another chance to come back.

I always make it a point to visit this place whenever I'm in Tampa. I love Jamaican food, and sadly, there just aren't enough Jamaican restaurants around. This place always hits the spot. My go-to tends to be the jerk chicken with rice+peas and cabbage. The curry goat and oxtail are also phenomenal. The red sauce is an absolute MUST. I like to smother it all over my plate and could probably drink it up lol :) Always looking forward to the next time I'm in Tampa so I can eat here again.

I use this place as one of my go to coffee meet-up spots. Not your usual Tucson feel. pastries and baked goods are a great addition to a coffee or espresso.

I'm not big into vegan or vegetarian food (as in I NEVER eat it) although some have caught my eye, so thats saying a lot, have not had the time for a meal here yet but I will be coming back soon to investigate.
Epic Cafe is just alright. I love their hot chocolate and iced teas. Sometimes the staff is friendly and sometimes rude. The baked goods are usually dry and don't seem fresh. Kind of a hit and miss.

These banh mi are delicious!  Don't be discouraged when you walk in and see no other customers and only one table.  Just get a chicken banh mi to go, and I promise you won't be sorry.  The bread is fresh, crispy and chewy, lots of cilantro, just the right amount of mayo and marinade on the chicken.  I have to admit that I think the banh mi here are better than at Nhuy, which is just down the street and gets high ratings here on Yelp.  The owners at Cafe Cuong are really friendly, as well.  Overall -- love it!

Called Epic because it is Epic. The best cafe in town--best people, best environment, best location, best baristas, best music free-est wifi. The open mic nights are often fun, often hilarious. The baristas will know your name. Eight thumbs up.

The coffee is to die for! This is the farthest thing from Starbucks you can get, in all the best ways! They are very veg & vegan friendly too! Such a unique atmosphere! The staff is very knowledgeable about coffee.  

This is a great place to hang out on those awkward 1st dates or studying for midterms.  I love coming to read and have a treat on my child free days. 

The decor is constantly changing with fresh local art and the amount of indoor plants takes you to a mini oasis in Tucson.

I really want to like this place because they have fantastic breakfast, but their lunch is terrible.  

Also, I'd be more inclined to order breakfast more often if they could get on the same page with the prices.  When you call to order and ask about pricing, they aren't quoting what's in the menu.  $7.65 for a single waffle and 3 strips of bacon?  Really?

SUMMARY
Best Indian food on campus, great value and portion sizes, slow service. Still my favourite Indian place near Penn - just be prepared to wait up to 30 minutes for food during busy times.

FOOD
Plethora of choices. Fresh and flavourful - the waiters will ask you for spice level, but YMMV so you'll have to figure this one out yourself. Higher quality than Sitar and the other Indian places on campus. Everything here is delicious that I've tried so far.

OVERALL VALUE (for those of us who are poor college students)
Buffet would not be good value for vegetarians since the big ticket items are mostly meat, but the à la carte menu has many veggie choices for amazing value. Can spend $12 here on a dish with naan and rice and have leftovers for a whole second meal.

SERVICE
Waiters are friendly but a little slow, and you have to struggle to get their attention sometimes during the dinner rush. I've never found their accents to be a problem but some people find it hard to understand. Biggest complaint is the wait time for food - they will wait until every item is ready and bring the food out all at once, which is terrible when you are starving. An empty plate will be placed in front of you about 10-15 minutes after your order, and food will follow another 15 minutes later. Waiting half an hour is not fun if you are hungry - they should bring the naan and other small appetizer items out first.

Cheque also takes forever to come and process for some reason. Usually have to pester the waiter a few times. Don't come here if you need to get in and out in a rush.

The food is always fresh and delicious, paired with great customer service! The wait time for food is generally short- usually less than 10 minutes. The portions are generous considering the price. There are menu options for vegetarians as well. The owner is especially friendly and remembers his customers.

Kim and her staff are always so nice when I come into visit the cafe. I work at the Garage on 4th across the street and they are always so welcoming and supportive of our new business. Awesome to have great neighbors on this side of 4th ave. Oh and their chocolate chip banana muffins....SO BOMB!

Is that germ factory of a rubber chicken still swinging from the bathroom key?

I'm not hip enough to go here anymore.  

Two stars for the memories.

Love Love Love the Ritz!  Always interesting independent films are shown here.

I've seen "Waiting For Superman",  "Vicky Cristina Barcelona", and "Convicted" here just to name a few.  

This place is so cool that one day I did the unthinkable in the movie theater....get your mind out the gutter!  I saw a flick ALONE.  This is the type of movie theater you can do this in though because you can be deemed as an intellectual and not a looser with no friends or date lol.

The concession stand has all of your typical snacks plus some eats for the yuppies (ie flavored coffees, muffins, and scones).  

I like that this theater has an old-school vibe to it too.  It's just so nice to get away from mainstream Blockbusters once in a while and see raw and intellectually stimulating movies.

Out of the trinity of Ritzes, this is probably my favorite. That isn't to say I don't love the Bourse & 5, but East is generally quieter, less crowded than the other two, and tucked away under dappled shade next to Pagoda, where you can enjoy an inexpensive bowl of noodles pre or post movie. Yes, the others have a wider (relatively speaking) selection, but if a film that catches my eye plays here, I'm all the happier for it. 
Unlike Valerie T, I have always had good experiences with the staff- most notably the occasion when I went batty over a huge brilliant cardboard stand-up ad for The Fall, and asked the manager what I had to do/fork over to be the proud owner of such a beauty. With a slightly bemused smile he told me that they give them for free to whoever calls dibs first, and they promised to notify me the moment they changed promo materials in the lobby. I gleefully (and awkwardly) carted the monstrosity off after the movie finished its run. 

Oh, and as with the other Ritzes, parking validation is niiiice.

Fantastic location.  Excellent peanut butter mocha.  Fantastic Avocado, Sun dried tomato and swiss omelet.  My sweetheart had the parfait.  Fruit was ok but not as fresh as a sunday morning would hope for.  Loved the protest walls in the bathrooms.  Very good food and local ambiance.  Felt like getting a tattoo after...

I visit Epic once a year, (almost) every year when I visit Tucson to order a peanut butter mocha.  No coffee shop in Chicago (or anywhere I've travelled, for that matter) has ever offered to put peanut butter in my espresso drink - and make it taste sooo good.

This Ritz Theatre plays the most Popular, mainstream and houses film festivals (LGBT and the other International film fest). Two theatres, both have stadium seating and they are bigger than the other two Ritz Theatres (Bourse and Five).

Epic is a chill spot to get your caffeine fix, some free wifi and acclimate to the Tucson collegy beat. Come here and you'll basically get the lowdown on the 4th ave scene culture. Close to the university, corner spots like this one are often colorful with character and characters.

Had some rare beef pho and spring rolls here tonight. Would definitely recommend. The portions were generous and priced fair.  The restaurant was super clean and the owner and staff were friendly. I'm happy there's a pho place close to me now. Will go back. Curious how their banh mi is.

Every graduate student knows about Epic, and it was even popular before they got AC a few years ago. Now it's just heaven in the summer-time.

Good coffee, good food, good pastries and desserts... you can literally set up camp here all day, and many a student does.
Pad thai is amazing for the price! The roti cani isn't that good. If you want to get good roti go to Penang or banana leaf. I would only highly recommend the pad thai.

try everything!  all baked goods are so yummy!  had a coconut peach muffin and a seed cookie along with my cafe mocha.  best breakfast ever!  barrista was friendly, coffees were made with love, and seating is funky and eclectic.  really enjoyed my breakfast date I had here - definitely will keep this on the radar!

I'm just sitting here waiting for my Hoagies (Banh Mi) and I decided to write a review. I've been going here ever since I was a toddler and it is still bomb dot com. Though it use to be $2 or something but Life. Don't hesitant to come and order yourself some OG goodness. The rules look old AF but the quality is all there. Legit the best Banh mi in Philly.

I love all my Philly Ritzes. I can always count on at least one of them to be showing a film that I want to see. More often than not Ritz East, Ritz at the Bourse and Ritz 5 are ALL featuring films on my "wanna see" list.

I love independent films the most. I love foreign films and art joints. Here's where you find em in Filmadelphia (I'm the worst). Ritz East is well-maintained, clean and comfortable. I am a fan.

 I love going to see films and then being able to ramble incessantly with friends willing or otherwise about what we've seen. Judging by the thin-lipped smiles and glazed over expressions on their faces, I'm sure that I take it to an insufferable level; as is my way. Maybe it's just that I keep repeating the word, "film," over and over. I really geek over this stuff. 

One of my favorite things in Philly life is to hatch a plan where we go catch what's playing at one of the Ritzes, then go for a drink/meal/bite along our walking way to another nearby Ritz, another movie. 

How bout a movie-meal crawl? For when you're feelin like you deserve some fun and special treatment. It's a nice little movie-meal-movie-meal cycle. Double double feature, get me?

I do love all my Ritzes, and this one is a beaute.
Excellent chicken banh mi. The bread is nice and crusty, the chicken is cooked in house. Lots of crunch from the vegetables and spice from the peppers. The owner is very friendly.

The guys can be a little rude but it's not bad compared to the racism we used to experience when we were kids. I'm now in my late 20's and I've brought my children and nieces and nephews here they loved it. Well most of them LOL. They have little fat food choices and of course hot cocoa. $4 for skate rental and admission is free
Yay. Movies. Digital. Fun staff. The ladies room is beautiful.
Lots of fun even for non-golfers... adults and kids. Besides golf:  food, drinks, pool tables, foosball, and corn hole.

Epic reminds of a place on the Lower Haight in San Francisco.  A little too expensive.  Sure.  Attitude?  Damn straight.  People busting through the front door and shouting semi-coherent rants?  Occasionally.  Everything I've ordered has been "ok".  The cashier jeered me when I tried to order decaf.  As well he should.  Sometimes when I'm in the mood for a little gritty 4th Ave action or just a little quiet time among the post-scene kids and their 4 gauge earrings, this is the place I get my tea.  The art there is pretty good, too.  Whatever.  It's Epic, ferchissakes.
The best bahn mi I've had in the city. Bread is perfectly soft fresh with nice crisp. Worth coming back to again and again and again ...
Pretty cool place.  Aesome breakfast burrito.  I wouldn't get sides in it - very expensive... $1 per veggie?  WHOA there.  Pretty good espresso.  I'd hang out there again.

This place used to be ok when I was in college but seems to have gone down hill...

-unfriendly staff
-terrible, chemical tasting, prickly pear lemonade
-'lemon meringue cake', served rudely and slowly missing half the meringue cause it was haphazardly dished and very dry/old tasting
-I've seen cleaner port-o-potties than their bathroom

Hard to support local businesses when they don't maintain quality or cleanliness

SKIP THE TRIP

We've visited a couple times and had takeout once, it was always good. Hard to find tasty Vietnamese food so far away from South Philly so we're grateful to have this place.

BBQ plates are generous and tasty. The pho is especially good-- broth is beefy and complex, noodles aren't over cooked, and they are generous with the toppings.

If you're craving chicken wings, those are really good too! 

They also have smoothies and fruit juices. I recommend the watermelon juice. All the prices are affordable and fair.

They have a pretty big delivery radius, but it's nice to stop in and see the people working there-- they care a lot about customer service and the interior is clean and comfortable. Worth it 100%

This was actually the 1st of the ritz theaters we came to . We haven't seen a movie here since then but the highly reviewed devils double opened friday so we planned a matinee after brunch. We snagged a sweet spot on 2nd St . Like all the others comfy chairs, organic popcorn and hoards of seniors wanting their discounts .

Quick review, this place has amazing breakfast especially the Belgium waffles, I think I'm from Belgium after I ate them jawns! They might have the best home fries in the bity too but hey that's just me! I might better ones but that's for Another time! S/o to them! 4/5! Woulda got a 5 if the chick that took our order didn't make me feel dumb as shit wen I asked for a 3 stack waffle so 4 STARS!! Lol
Great customer service food is ok good place to grab quick breakfast the waiter bibi is really nice
Chicken banh  mi....best one in the city. Love this place.

Seriously, this place is awesome!  The food is better than Tiffin and Ekta.  The service is impeccable!  The owners are so helpful and courteous and will make your food the way you want it!!!  And they have fast delivery, where not only is Tiffin more expensive you have to wait an hour and 45 to get your food delivered.  Try it out!!!

Pros: It's locally owned (I'm pretty sure); it's got crazy, funky decor (although they recently painted over the 'Bob' quote over the door); and they have a great big corner window that's nice to check out the passers by.

Cons: Depending on when you go you could get the barista with a really lousy attitude, and their attempt at gluten free fair is not much of an attempt - at least when it comes to baked goods. 

We have been in there 3 times total and each time there was a totally different attitude from each of the different baristas. The first one was a very friendly young woman who was very excited about what items on the menu were GF, the second time the guy was pretty pretentious but efficient but seemed more interested in waiting on the next person who he seemed to know (perhaps a regular), this last time was a young brunette woman who A) gave my fiance a 12oz drink in a 16oz cup when he asked and paid for a 16oz. When he asked her about it she said basically, "so what." When he asked again she said she could put more milk in it but that was all. Boy did she have a tone.

I bought a GF muffin and sat down to eat in at it was amazingly disgusting. A total dried out brick. I took it back to ask for my money back. She huffed, tried to give a line about that's just how GF stuff is (it's not), gave me a look as if I'd just asked her to wash my car for free and then tried to do a refund on the register. She couldn't get it to work then asked if I wanted something else for $3. I didn't so she tried to do a refund again, asked another employee if they have ever had to do a refund and he said no. She went in the back for several minutes while the other person began waiting on other customers. When she finally came out he told her to just give me the $3 back and they could figure out the refund later.

Here is the kicker. When she gave me the money she flicked it at me. I kid you not.  I don't recall the last time I'd been treated so rudely. I hope for the sake of Epic her behavior was a one time thing because if she acts like that to others Epic will loose more customers.

This happened on Thursday, January 27th, 2011 (today) late afternoon.

So their non-vegetarian food didn't impress me. I ordered it the first time and found it lacking but since then I have ordered the vegetarians entrees and they seemed better than their competitor Tiffin(right down the street).

Horrible!
Bad service, bad food and portion sizes are horrible.
You get what you pay for.

I love Epic's atmosphere and tasty drinks. However, they get a three star review for a lack of friendly service. I have had great customer service during the day, but the younger evening/night crew is just plain off-putting. The young woman who "helped" me tonight was rude from the get go, never smiled and only seemed interested in flirting with the guys from the tattoo shop next door. It only takes one bad employee to ruin a customer's experience and unfortunately, I will be taking my business elsewhere in the evening.

I've been to this theater a dozen times since I've lived here, and it has pretty much always been the same, whether I'm there on a job to review a film or just there for fun. The theater is always clean, the staff is helpful if you need them, and as usual with a Ritz theater, the food in the lobby is a lot better than any place else. I also love the fact that there's a garage right next-door and they validate. :)

For the most part, you'll find the flicks here are on the indie-side, but this is also the theater where WMMR holds their "VIP" screenings, so you can catch more regular movies here then. If you do go to a screening, though, watch out -- the crowd there is pretty rowdy and loud.

Setting is gorgeous. Drink prices insane. If 2 long islands are going to cost me $38, make them good...  But they weren't.  

If you're staying in the hotel, it's worth checking out and maybe having a beer. Make it a jump off spot, or end of night wrap up. 

It really is beautiful. So was the crowd.

Not sure why I didn't know this place existed. Really delicious and crazy inexpensive. We had a chicken hoagie and a shredded pork hoagie. The chicken was absolutely delicious, and the shredded pork was very good. Will need to get back and continue to work through the [short] menu.

Our favorite movie theater in the city. It's very clean, the seats recline and are generally very comfortable, the screen is huge, and the movies they show are mostly Oscar-nominated films. It's always a pleasant experience to see a movie at the Ritz.

Agreed, something must be done about the typhoidial rubber chicken that acts as the bathroom keychain.  Communicable diseases aside, this is my favorite coffee house in Tucson.  The drinks are super, the wifi is free, and the food is yums.  I don't know why I crave the egg salad sandwich, but I do and I want some right now.  

Plus, there's always one or another dog outside that looks cleaner than their owner.  Not to mention that older fellow in the yellow hat.  I think he may have an eye patch.  It's a cultural experience really.

Good coffee and a relaxed atmosphere. Friendly baristas and an interesting aesthetic. The only con is that some of the seating is far too low for the height of the tables, this makes typing almost impossible you put your computer in your lap.
This food city has nothing . Don't expect a bakery , or butcher area like the other food city's . It's cramped and the aisles can barely fit your cart . Very unorganized .

My fiancé and I have purchased a customized wedding package from Only You Wedding. This package consists of pre-wedding service (studio+outdoor photo shots) and wedding day service (photo shoots, entertainment, decoration and bridal hair and make up service). We just had our studio picture taken recently and we were so pleased with the service and how fast these photos turned around. The entire photo shooting took more than 8 hours but Annie and her entire team were very helpful, professional and super patient the whole time. Their make up artist did a marvelous job and I had a different hair and make up style to fit each of the 4 outfits I choose. More surprisingly is they have all 70+ photos edited and ready for view in less than 4 days!!!!!!! We are so looking forward to our outdoor photo shoot and wedding day. We are certain that we will have more comments to post once everything is completed.

Def the best Banh Mi place I've ever had and have been coming here for at least 10 years.  Just ordered 20 sandwiches that came with 2 extra free of charge for myself and my family.  I recommend getting the sandwiches to go cause it can feel uncomfortable eating in a little place but their sandwiches are def the best.  Great option for lunch cause they are so cheap and easy to eat.

I usually get the Banh Mi Dac Biet and the Banh Mi with Shredded Pork.  The bread is toasted and crispy as well as soft on the inside.  They give a lot of different slices of meat which is a plus from my experience at other places.  The veges give a great crunch and freshness.  The pate and butter mayonnaise have a rich and creamy texture and ooze out in every bite.  Put that all together and you have a great sandwich.  Same goes for the Shredded Pork.  For me, one isn't enough and I usually end up eating north of 2.  

If your a Banh Mi fan or new to it, I def recommend giving this place a shot.  It might be your new go to spot or at least you can cross it off your list of places to try.  For me, this is the place to beat.

The kind of atmosphere you would expect on 4th ave, they're open late, and usually serve a clientele of graduate students.  A change from the Starbucks, with a 90's kids twist to it. I come for the iced coffee during the middle of the night, and they never disappoint. They have wifi . I've asked for a usb charger several times as my phone is on the brink of death. 

The service is some of the best I've had, always help, and they keep it very casual and genuine. Come here for coffee, tea, or just a lovely slice of pie!

Pay in cash, I think they charge a little more if you pay with card; not certain.

I had the best vegan chimichanga of my life here about a year ago. Came here on a recent Thursday night with my boyfriend for my birthday. Our driver dropped us off at 7:48PM, we were seated, given chips/water, and although the place was not at all full and we saw servers walking past us many times, no one introduced themselves as our server, or even took our drink orders for a full half hour. We were wasting time sitting there, so my boyfriend and I left at 8:20PM for another nearby restaurant. Dissappointed, will not return.

First off, I am not the type of person who goes to these shops. I have a few hipster friends, so I went in with one of them (in my polo shirt and jeans of course) and got an arnold palmer - wasn't in the coffee mood. Even in my outsider attire, everyone was very friendly and welcoming. It was pretty good, and I enjoyed the atmosphere. It is very laid back, the lounge type. I came back with another friend, and I asked for a lemonade, but was suggested the "prickly pear lemonade" by the cashier, and boy, I'm so glad she did! It was honestly one of the best drinks I have ever tasted! It is VERY sweet! I was smiling the whole time. I now know that I will be getting that drink every time in the future! I guess I need to try out their sandwiches too after looking at the other reviews on here. Prickly Pear Lemonade, get it! Especially if you like sweet drinks!

The staff is always friendly and the patrons are interesting and friendly.

This is definitely a fun place to hang out and meet interesting people :)

First time here. Maybe we caught them on an off day. Food was very bland. Service was underwhelming. Order was not completed correctly and we never did get that cup of pasta salad. Wife's earl gray tasted burned. Two stars because my tea was alright.

My father loves their banh mi here. Their banh mi is good here. My favorite is the chicken banh mi. The only reason why I didn't give them a five star is because I had a couple of bones in my chicken banh mi.

I ordered tea instead of coffee for the first time. I received a gorgeously massive bag of green tea, so much that I was able to reuse the tea bag at home for another strong brew. They also have really cheap organic tobacco selections. 
Epic has always been a favorite for me, but nowadays it's a bit difficult for productivity and workflow, but that's how it is when students flood for caffeine to do their homework!
One of the best places to get a Banh mi thit nguoi  in Philly.  Everything here is good. Its not commercialized like other places.

Solid, quick airport option. Clean design. Lots of complimentary sauce - Thai ketchup, Cajun, ranch,chipotle to name a few.

We both had burgers without buns, they were very accommodating. The staff was happy and helpful, even for it being later in the day.

My burger was the bacon cheesy, wife's was the shroom. Both were tasty and we would eat here again.
The pork vermicelli was awesome! Great portion size too. The restaurant is very clean and the staff are very friendly.

Ok, I have to say this upfront.  I did not eat/drink or do anything here.  I have to say that my experience here is nill.  I walked in, looked around and saw that it's not a place to be if you are not a true local.  All the patrons look like they belong there.  I came in wearing my shorts and polo shirt and I looked like I didn't belong there, so I walked out.  Even the cashier took a weird glance at me and they look in her eyes was "what the hell are you doing here".  I decided that there must be more casual coffee shops around.  So I left.

Yum! I have to be honest, I didn't have a meal here cause it was too early for lunch to late for bfast. But the smell alone was enough to make me believe that the food is amazing. 

I had an Americano with soy. Good. My partner had chai and ice cream with some mexican wedding cookies. And apparently really good stuff. 

The ambience was good. Decor was fun, mood was light, somewhat hipstery but from what I could tell a strong enough mix (college profs/students, transients, queer boys/girls, middle aged white folks, and a few tribal folks) that it took away from the angsty/annoying hipster vibe. 

I definitely would give epic four stars, I'm hoping five if I choose to eat there sometime soon. Good location so I'm sure it gets crazy busy. But when I was there, good amount of people, great smells, strong coffee, plenty of lesbians. Four stars any day!

one of the best banh mi spots in philly.  one of my close pals recommended me this gem located in south philly. bread was toasted to perfection (i hate toasted bread), meats were fresh and the service was good. can't complain for only $4!

After watching every episode of No Reservations (with chef Anthony Bourdain) on India, I was left famished for curry.   

A while back I read a good number of positive reviews for Sahara on Yelp, so I decided to give them a shot.  With only one hour to eat dinner between arriving home from work and having to leave to go to a night class, I wasn't sure of the logistics of ordering food.  

My wife called Sahara around 4:30 and asked what time she should call back to place the order.  It was important for us that our food arrived at 6:00 P.M.  The person she spoke with (who was very friendly) said we could give them our order now and they would make sure it was delivered at 6:00 P.M. 

We ordered the Paneer Masala (spicy).  When my wife put in the order she was asked what level of spiciness she wanted the food to be.  This is a very nice touch, seeing as I have never been asked this by any of the other Indian Take Out/ Delivery places on Girard.  We also ordered a Green Chili Naan and a Garlic Naan.  

The food was wonderful.  The Masala was bursting with fresh tomato flavor and had the perfect amount of spice.  The tomato and cream created a smooth velvety Masala (kind of like a Italian vodka sauce, but much better).  The paneer was definitely homemade and had a very rich and firm texture.  

I was so please with the food (after I finished eating) I called Sahara to tell them how happy I was with everything.  As a former cook, I know how nice and unexpected it is to receive complements. 

The cherry on this sundae is that the food arrived at exactly 6:00 P.M.

BTW...Sahara is only a delivery and take out place...they don't have a dining room.

Let me say...I (used to) love EPIC!  I come here often to study and for the comfy couches and desserts.  Plus, they have a lot of yummy vegan cookies.

BUT...over the past around 6 months, they have been using Styrofoam cups and today plates and you don't even get an option...WTF?  PLUS, the worst thing is that they are saying that styrofoam (polystyrene) is completely recyclable.   Styrofoam is 1) bad for your health because of the chemicals that leech into your food  and 2) bad for the environment. 

http://greenliving.lovetoknow.com/How_Styrofoam_is_Bad_for_the_Environment

great people watching place with a decent cup of coffee, a great naughty toddy and an amazing cold pressed ice coffee.  the scones are good as are the sandwiches and omelets.  they are known for their baked goods but i'm not a fan of them at all.  i think the flavors all sort of run the same, like there isn't enough circulation in the case.  but those seed cookies...they are heavy enough to satisfy like a full meal and are a tasty vegan treat.

As with the other Ritz theaters, they feature smaller, independent films. This one has the larger theaters though, so if a bigger film hits, it's more likely to come here. Otherwise, pretty standard as well. They also have a parking lot and it's right across the street from Ritz Five. I like that they post movie times for each other so if one is sold out, you know what's playing across the road. Good, mature crowds and right in Old Towne so plenty to do after (or before) the movie.

Funky little corner cafe to sit and get some work done! They have some comfy couches and tables to work at, as well, plus wifi. In addition to coffee and tea, they have a pretty large food menu and quite a few baked goods, too! They were rearranging when I went, so I'm sure it's looking really good now! All I had when I was here was an iced dirty chai (with I think soy milk and a shot of espresso) and it was great! The guy behind the counter was very nice and quick, too.

Overall rating: 9/10
Price: $2-$10
Quality: I only had the flan and the ice cream, so I can't comment much about their other food. But the ice cream is amazing, creamy and not too sweet. Judging from the look of the dish other customers ordered, I think it's safe to say that they serve good food. You can get soup and salad along with pastry and side dishes anytime during the day except 12am to 6am.
Service: I always appreciate a cafe that has free drinkable water. There are no servers. You just order and go.
Ambient Environment: It's really clean and full of characters. I like the fact that they display local artists' work. They have comfy couches and small tables. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available. Plus they have bike racks outside.
Parking/Direction: street parking
Pros: clean, local's favorite, good ice cream
Cons: there might be weird strangers.
Note: I really liked this place but since that one time when a weird dude tried to hit on me while I was studying, I decided not to go there anymore. He complained that all the people in Epic Cafe were weird and then he kept talking to me even though I told him I needed to study and put on my earphones. I recommend order to go.

The atmosphere is really cool, very artistic and representative of Tucson.  When you first step foot into the coffee shop, you are bombarded with a wide variety of delectables: cakes, pies, cookies, granola bars, brownies, whatever your sweet tooth desires.  I definitely ordered a chocolate cream pi (yea, they're cool enough to use pi) late one night to satisfy a terrible chocolate craving.

However, my rating is still average for this place because I can't get over their styrofoam cups.  Other people have complained about this too, and I think it's an incredibly simple switch.  The drinks are pretty good (really yummy iced chai latte), but they need to serve them in better, more eco-friendly containers.
I don't care about the hipsters and the "They're too hip!!!" wah wah wah shit in all the other reviews because I go for the Arnold Palmers. You should too. Before you go, remember: with hibiscus.

I dig this place. Really comfortable to hang out for a really really long time, surf the web, drink way too much coffee (refills are only a buck!). What more can one ask for. And the food is pretty good too!
Cozy little theatre, old style feel, cheap tickets, big screen, great sound. Very enjoyable. I will definitely be coming here again

If you're coming here for the food and coffee, you'll love it! If you're coming here to do homework, make sure you can handle a higher noise level, the possibility of seating with limited light, and a charged computer because outlets are scarce.

Mr. Wonderful and I saw Cedar Rapids ( which BTW is hilarious) here last Friday night.  The theatre and bathrooms are super clean, staff was very friendly and parking is right next door!  I have children and I love them, but I really love the Ritz no kids under 6 policy.  The seating is very comfortable and the sound level was just right.  It's the perfect date night theatre.
Was in here for the first time. Cute theater with comfy seats and lots of leg room. The popcorn was ok. I went there on feb 8th for a private screening. Very organized and executed.

Used to be a great place, now a bit down in the heels.  I like a mixed crowd, but you here feel a bit out of place without dreads, a sleeve of tats, and at least 5 piercings.  Oh, and a good splosh of patchouli.  I still go now and then, but I miss the more mixed crowd of prior years.  These days I usually end up at Time Market or Bentley's.

Funky little corner cafe to sit and get some work done! They have some comfy couches and tables to work at, as well, plus wifi. In addition to coffee and tea, they have a pretty large food menu and quite a few baked goods, too! They were rearranging when I went, so I'm sure it's looking really good now! All I had when I was here was an iced dirty chai and it was great! The guy behind the counter was very nice and quick, too.

This is the BEST Indian food in Philadelphia. I thought I had found the perfect spot in West Philly, but one night I didn't feel like traveling and wanted take outs. I decided to give it a try because it was reasonably prices and had delivery. When we ordered online it said it could take up to 45 minutes, but came in 15!! The food arrived hot and looked amazing! BUT tasted even better. We got Spicy chicken tikki marsala with naan and it was amazing. Two orders was plenty for both of us and there was still a little left over. I also got an order of samosas, which were very good. I was very happy that the food came hot and fast. I will definitely be ordering from here again!!

It's been ages since I've been back to Epic cafe. Last time, was a good experience. Daughter had an allergic reaction to one of their cookies. Completely our responsibility to find out if there are certain ingredients in what we order. Thank God that one of the employees actually had some liquid Benadryl on hand!  What a relief and how unique.  Grateful for creative out of the box thinking.

super cute cafe with the nicest staff and really tasty food! I got the zucchini quiche and my friend got the bagel with lox- both were delicious, reasonably priced, and piping hot. the ambience is really nice in the shop, and the people who helped us were really kind and gave us some of their old stickers for free when we were disappointed that their new stock hadn't come yet. we'll be back soon
Great little spot for breakfast, enjoyed the breakfast burrito with potatoes inside, should have added the bacon. My cappuccino was made correctly. Locals are eating here and you can see why.

Very cool vibe to this place, very Tucson. Their coffee is always good and their baked goods are amazing. I'm always happy withy the food I get

However, the problem is getting the food. The service is so slow and the kitchen regularly runs out of things (today it was lettuce, so no salads and no gluten free option for my mom.) I understand that is part of supporting small business, but if I wanted an unstocked kitchen I would stay home.

This was by far the best movie watching experience I've had in Philadelphia.  Not because of some grand sound system or because the chairs were super comfortable.  Nope, it's because there were no children running around in the lobby nor in the theater like it was their own little Romper Room.  Plus, nobody was yapping on their cell phones during the movie.  After suffering through the disgrace that is The Bridge, I almost felt like I should've given a hug to the GM of the Ritz East on the way out.

Don't know why I haven't reviewed this theater , yet. Been there couple last couple years. Once to see Pans Labyrinth , another time after. I like this theater, only reason I gave it 4-stars is parking . If you are from across the bridge ,Parking is a Bitch!!! I hate it. Locals you're good, walk or get a cab. But other then that, nice.., go downstairs, different theaters are designated, looks are deceiving but the inside bigger then it looks. Surprisingly clean & the crowd it draws is predominantly more mature, not alot rift raft, independent movies, etc tend to do that-Yippy!!

This was my first Vietnamese hoagie. The first- of MANY!

$3.75 for an amazing, outrageously tasty hoagie unlike anything you've ever had in the city or outside of it. The crunchy bread, the pickled veggies, the spicy jalas, and the intoxicating, unique mayo spread make this a lunch keeper. 

Cant beat this unimposing yet remarkable little cafe.
They had banana leaves for Peruvian tamales. The staff was so helpful in finding one last box in the back for us. Also great queso fresco and spices.

Now I think I am reviewing the right place - I saw a movie last night at the "Landmark East" theatre on 2nd Street between Chestnut & Walnut.  It was clean and there were no ticket lines.  Hardly anybody there - which made it nice.

Restrooms were clean - but I bet if it were crowded that it would not have been.  Concession area offered hot & cold beferages, popcorn, candy and snacks - plus you could purchase DVDs to take home.  The staff was friendly.

All in all we had an excellent viewing experience

What is wrong with this place. They dropped the f bomb to my friends waiting outside. And told them to get the f out. Said something about how they don't call the police and they will call the hells angels. He wanted to kick them off the sidewalk.

You know you're eating in a bad Vietnamese establishment, when there is no comfortable seating with clean tables, customer service is nonexistent as the entire staff is in the kitchen squabbling about their sons' MCAT scores, and the banh mi is poorly thrown together, with the greens carelessly topped on a stale, crumbly baguette with dry white chicken.
Sorry to say, but I was disappointed with Sahara.  Their prices are good, and they give generous portions, but the food was bland.

I'm always on the look out for a good local coffee house with atmosphere.  Epic Cafe fits the bill.  They offer a wide selection of coffee and pastries for breakfast.  If you need to do some internet there WiFI is, according to their sign, "faster than a hooker to the clinic."

So far I've had their house coffee, peanut butter latte, and vanilla lattes.  All quite tasty.  If you have the peanut butter, be prepared for a unique consistency with great flavor.  I got mine iced but each sip gave me a taste of warm peanut butter with that iced latte.  Wonderful for a day when you need a little something extra to get you moving.

Bad Coffee: Not Epic
Too-sweet Muffins: Not Epic
Cappuccino Foam that looked like a bubble bath: Not Epic
Baristas/employees who seemed to never have made any espresso drinks before: Not Epic
Very Strange Music: Not Epic

Friendly, attentive service.  Baristas accommodate variations and personal preferences with a smile!  Variety of sweets including gluten-free options.  Also, a small variety of ice cream and sherbet available.  Sammies and soup - not a large selection but well-rounded options including gluten-free and vegan options.  Atmosphere is relaxed and comfortable.  A great place to causally meet up for good conversation or come solo and curl up on the couch with a good read.  See you at Epic!
Deluxe soup was enough for 2, or 2 meals for me. So good! Fresh bean sprouts, basil leaves. Cilantro. Mmm. Yummy broth! Definitely ordering from here again. To go was ready super quick.

When I saw that Ritz East was a Landmark theater I knew I was in good hands. I've been a huge fan of their Tivoli and Plaza Frontenac locations in St. Louis for years, so I know they are pretty much synonymous with quality independent and foreign films in a nice atmosphere. 

As far as I know they are the only theater showing Moonrise Kingdom anywhere in the city, which is a major plus. The ticket prices, too, are extremely reasonable for the location--$9.50 for Saturday evening shows, $6.50 for shows on Wednesdays, and $7.25 for matinees are pretty stellar prices if you ask me. 

My only advice, which is less of a downside and more of a peak-time reality, is to show up a bit early on weekends. When we went for our 8:45 p.m. show yesterday (Saturday) the theater did get very crowded, and a sign posted said that the 7:45 p.m. show had actually sold out. We ended up buying our tickets about half an hour early and walking around for a bit beforehand, which worked out really well because when we came back the ticket line had gotten really long and the theater was starting to fill up. So, be prepared to come early if you want your pick of seats.

Not impressed and not much else to say.  First time in my life that I went into a grocery store with coffee on the shopping list and came out with it still on the list.  
I will say this, it fit perfectly with my level of expectations considering the strip mall it is in.  What a depressing misuse of space... .

Nice theater. Less commercial and crowded than the one on Columbus. They usually have higher profile movies here. Oscar worthy, etc. Concession prices are actually reasonable too.

Come a little before showtime and sit in the back section so you're not straining your neck in the front section.

Delivery service not reliable at all!  Estimate of 25 minutes turned into 1 hour; had to keep calling back and the manager blamed the taxi driver who was bringing my food.  2 hours later still no food, no answer on either number at restaurant.  My credit card was charged with no problem yet no food, no answer, no help.

This is a great Vietnamese restaurant located near Temple hospital.  They offer take out and dine-in options. Generous portions and it's not too expensive.   They're extremely welcoming and make great recommendations.  I was looking for a place to grab food while I was visiting someone at nearby Temple Hospital and the options are limited. I was super happy not only find a walk-able option but with such quality food.  We had a BBQ platter and the brisket pho both were delicious.  Highly reccomend.

Okay Tucson lets get a couple things straight.  I love me some coffee shops oh good golly do I love coffee shops.  I have lived in Portland and my parents live in Washington so I know great coffee shops.  First off if this is the so-called hipster young coffee shop this is sad.  I am all for artistic coffee shops but how bout clean ones?
Seriously the girls behind the counters were rude-I loved all the choices they  had for food and when I asked a question about it since it was my first time going they acted irritated because people were starting to pile up. 
Perhaps you should just answer my question and be polite.  On top of it one of the them wiped her nose and then started making my coffee....eeew!
Seriously, I wanted to like this place so much and it really bums me out to have this experience.
I seriously think that they are just playing on the fact that they are on 4th Ave because seriously that was the worst customer service that I have had in a long time.
No more Epic Cafe for me and if I do go hopefully it'll be a great experience so I can update this review.
Ugh

A real coffeehouse experience.  Totally local and non-corporate. A good place to sit on a sofa and look out on 4th Avenue will enjoying good coffee and food. Our daughter enjoyed a hearty breakfast burrito. I enjoyed a flan with almond flakes on it, different but tasty..

Cafe Cuong is the BEST Banh Mi place in town HANDS DOWN. My family has been buying their Banh Mi Thit Nguoi for many years, and even though we try other places here and there, they all pale in comparison. The pate and homemade mayo is creamy, rich, and the ratio is perfect. The bread is always fresh and with a crisp crust, and the owners are super nice.

I was there today and asked for a coffee shake.. SHAKE but what the server made was watery shit which dint even taste good. Worst part was that she dint even offer to make it again. She was like "Oh sorry I don't know how it turned out to be so watery" and left. That piece of shit cost us $5. If she did it out of spite cos we dint add a tip to the already overpriced piece of crap, Epic Cafe needs to go back to customer 101 again. 
It would have made more sense for her to screw up if the place was filled with people and a lot of people were waiting. But it wasn't. It was empty. Just 4 people behind us, who clearly were in a group and were in the process of deciding what to get. No wonder the place is so empty these days
 I wanted to say something to her right there and then but there were like 4 more people at the counter, it was very quite so everyone could hear what I was saying, and just out of respect for someone's business , I did not create a scene. 
I used to go to Epic Cafe a lot when I was in freshmen year (2010) but clearly they have dropped their standards since then, and hired a bunch of noobs who think tipping is directly related to the quality of service you get. Is it ? If it is then correct me.
Oh and of course we trashed the piece of shit shake she gave us. 

Come on Epic Cafe. You have seen much better days. Don't lose your charm and definitely teach your servers a thing or two about making shakes. Please and Thank you!

The Ritz East, or as Elizabeth B so memorably put it, the "Ritz Pagoda" is my heavy crush of the three RItz theaters just blocks apart in Old City.  These fraternal triplets show the artsy, indie and otherwise unknown flicks you must see, plus the occasional big-budget studio picture.  

Big reclining seats, icy cold A/C and not much of a crowd means you can get as comfortable here as on your own couch.  But don't take your shoes off, please; that's just weird.

Ummmm... who the fuck serves to-go coffee in styrofoam cups? MAJOR RATING LOSS.

Otherwise, I'm a big fan of the coffee, the staff and the foods. 

C'mon Epic, lose the foam. Nobody enjoys drinking hot coffee out of that shit.
Big fan of the Ritz cinemas. They offer intelligent, entertaining films and have something for everyone! Good location and friendly staff. I'll be back!

I'm very glad to have yet another Indian restaurant so close to my NoLibs home. I think they all have their strong points. One of Sahara's strengths is their bhindi masala. Whether you have ever had okra before, whether you have ever liked it before, you should try this dish. The chili paneer, a fusion dish, is also worth trying. I do wish they carried gulab jamun.

The staff/owners are also very nice.

I attended the last in a series of late night horror classics playing at this theater (last night's was Evil Dead) and it was a great experience.  The audience was well behaved, which seems to be a lot to ask for in Philly, yet everyone was laughing and screaming together throughout the film.  A staffer gave an intro to the movie, letting us know that it was an original reel of film and might have scratches or pops.

All in all a fun experience, as were my other earlier trips to the theater.
Marshmallow fluff =/= Foamed milk. Apart from the measly amount of espresso due to the insane amount of fluffed milk, the art on the walls made an impression on me and was a nice store.
love epic.  great place to hang out, study, sit.  great chicken salad sandwich, awesome cakes and cookies, goooodddd milkshakes

The Ritz sets itself apart from other movie theaters with large, clean, mostly empty theaters with big, plush, rocking seats and a thoughtful snack bar including items like Pennysticks pretzels, a variety of teas and the regular theater fare.

I also really enjoy the Filmbill, which I noticed, sadly, as a result of poor economic times, will no longer be published. They  kept me occupied prior to the start of the movie.

And, obviously, the Ritz shows films less mainstream than those at the Riverview or other huge cineplexes., which continues to be a big draw.

Hipster and non-hipster alike will enjoy it here. It's great for just chilling and reading or getting work done, or pop in for a coffee, tea, dessert, or meal. 
I recently got the vegan blueberry almond bar which was fantastic. 
The prices are very reasonable.

Stopped by based on a few reviews.  I wish I had something positive to say.  The place was disgusting & looked like it had never been cleaned.  To top it off the Rice Krispie treat I bought was clearly way past the stale point, despite the stoner (that's being nice) chick behind the bar saying how fresh it was.  She was as frightening as the rest of the place.   Yikes.

We decided to try this tonight because it is new and up the road. We are glad we did they offer 3 spicy varieties , the masala was great and prices were more affordable then ETKA or Tiffin. YUMMY! Also they have more of a naan variety. The manager was very nice and helpful.
