Dinner has yet to be had, but I'm sure I'll be supping on feta-stuffed Hungarian peppers and other night-time offerings soon enough.
great coffee and waffle brunch dishes. me gusta mucho :)

I can't say enough GOOD things about Dr. Balzer and this clinic. We recently moved to the area, and took our dog there because they were close and, we heard, very affordable. The people are friendly and very respectful of us and our dog.

They helped us through a very difficult time as our dog had developed Cushings disease. We discussed treatment alternatives, how to keep him comfortable, and finally, they were very compassionate as we made the painful decision to have him euthanised.

Overall, they are kind, knowledgeable, compassionate people.

My one complaint is that it is sometimes hard to coordinate a return call. They are a nonprofit, I believe, and a bit understaffed. We found it was easier to just stop in for feedback on test results and such.

The brunch here is super-tasty, the coffee is pretty much perfect. I'm surprised to read other reviews critical of the service because I've never had a bad experience. Quite the opposite, I feel everyone there has gone out of their way to be friendly on the times I've visited, even when they were extremely busy.

There are a few things to know before you go: 1) the space is tiny. 2) the portions are reasonable. I like their size. I feel like I can finish my plate feeling satisfied instead of feeling like an overstuffed pig that needs to be rolled away from the table. If you need a serving like they offer at Sabrina's then this isn't the place for you. 3) Street parking in S Philly can be a challenge. 

So glad to have this little place in the neighborhood!
Excellent pizza, salad, homemade lemonade and friendly staff. If you liked Grimaldi's give Pizza Luna a try. You won't be disappointed.

Had a great experience on Christmas Eve... after a mixup about our reservation (probably our fault not the restaurants), the staff was super accommodating and let us sit and have drinks even though the restaurant was not officially open. Eventually we ordered food, which was excellent and again, the staff was attentive and welcoming to the young children in our party. The scenery and ambience of the restaurant cannot be beat- highly recommend!!
Perfect crust texture.  Extremely flavorful sauce.  Wonderful selection of toppings.  Great "salad and a slice" lunch option.  We will definitely be back!

I wasn't a huge fan of the margarita pizza. :/ 
The lettuce was good, had a little kick, maybe a little smaller?

Cute place in Passyunk square.  

I had really high expectations for this cafe because reviews and word of mouth.  The food I would say was decent and creative.  My husband and I tried the cornbread waffle and egg truffle toast.  I think the food could of been better but both dishes were cold.  The egg truffle toast was delicate and light, which I liked.  But I felt that the toast was extra hard and difficult to eat.  The cornbread waffle had some different flavors but the whole dish was cold.  It was not a busy Sunday morning bc we got there before the rush.  

The coffee was great which is why I gave this place 3 stars.  The service was mediocre..... We kept having to flag the staff by the coffee bar for our orders and refill of coffee.   Maybe because they sat us in the little window seating, we were forgotten? 

So, I wouldn't choose this place when I craving brunch food.  I would come back for coffee.

A co-worker and I had a fantastic experience here!  I loved it the moment I walked in.  The place has a very urban and Italian vibe.  It's feng shui.  I asked if they did a lunch special with a slice of pizza and salad, and they said yes!!  It's exactly what I wanted!  I had a great radicchio salad dressed lightly and a salami pizza that was covered in salami - every inch!  The crust was perfect - absolutely one of the best pizza's in Tucson!  I had a homemade blackberry lemonade that was perfect with this lunch.  The staff were super accommodating.  They said this is the first Pizza Luna, but more will come!  It's a perfect lunch stop!  They also have a nice wine and beer selection.  I love the table decorations too - cactus and a tiny bowl of sea salt!  Our work group will be back next week and I want to try the Brussel sprout, pancetta, goat cheese salad!  Great, great, new place!!  It's where Cup it Up was before in the Trader Joes shopping center!

Got delivery for dinner with my family earlier. Good sushi. but, mediocre Chinese food.  The mixed veggies didn't even come with a sauce. The woman on the phone who we placed the order with also had a hard time understanding English. Would get sushi again, but, definitely sticking with South Garden for our usuals.

Let me tell you about one of the most difficult decisions of my life. I am a rat owner, and came home from a two week work trip to find that my baby Stew was having serious issues with his eyes (popping out of his head). While my roommate could have done something about it if a more experienced rat owner, I know they feel incredible guilt that they did not do more. This was not purposefully done and I hold no blame for them. They noticed a minor scratch, informed me, but as Stew was always rather timid they didn't notice it get worse.
I did a walk in right at opening, and despite being the 5th in, the assistant noticed my crying, took a look at Stew, and immediately brought me into the back.
The small animal vet (I forget her name, I was very emotional) was amazing. Very caring and understanding. I was provided the option of surgery to remove his eyes or euthanizing. Sadly I do not make enough to afford surgery, and came in knowing that he would most likely put down. I just wanted Stew no longer in pain. It was very hard, but again the vet was wonderful. She was very kind, empathetic, and verily calmly talked me though it. And she was very loving to Stew. She gave me a lot of time with Stew after the process, andthe receptionist was also very kind.
These peiple care about your pets. While I hope the next time I go to the vet it is for something less tragic, I have definitely found my vet. 
Thank you to the vet who helped my baby cross the rainbow bridge. I only wise I could remember your name to give you proper recognition.

My wife and I came here after a quick walk around the trail.  We were here for Sunday Brunch, which is a pre-fixe set at the base of $19.95 and a surcharge for anything outside the pre-fixe.  My wife ordered the parfait and waffles with pecans.  I ordered the soup of the day (butternut squash with roasted pumpkin seeds) and the chicken and waffles ($5 surcharge).  
My wife's parfait was well layered and tasty.  My soup was very good.  The roasted pumpkin seeds gave a nutty, smoky flavor to the soup.  
My wife said her waffles with pecans was actually too sweet.  I fell to the ground and got back up because I never hear her say anything is too sweet.  My chicken and waffles were good, but I wish there were a little more chicken than they served.  The chicken portion was puny.
So here's the problem - the service.  While friendly, it was very disjointed and inefficient.  I felt like I was watching the Keystone Cops operate.  Like I said, it was friendly, but just slow and lacking simple things like refilling your water in a timely fashion or how they clear the table.
The view, if you sit outside, is really nice because there is plenty of people watching.
But overall, it was okay.  If you are there and want a place close by to eat, this would do.

I have mixed feelings in regards to this place. I love the Pizza, atmosphere and the buffet. In fact, it is because of the buffet u can find us here almost weekly eating our money's worth. Usually I have very little complaints but this time I was rubbed the wrong way. One of the employee's was cussing like a sailor dropping "f" bombs very loudly near the buffet area. It made me very uncomfortable. Be more professional! 

Also, the buffet uses pie server's which requires a lot more work to pick up a slice and u can usually see more then one person struggling with it. They should have tongs.

Lastly, this is more food for thought, but the buffet area is not wheel chair accessible and the lady in front of me had a very hard time. "Everything is in the back and I can't reach it," I heard her saying sadly.
This pizza was soggy!!! Got the Proscuitto. Won't eat here again. Unfortunate!!!   I will stay with other locally owned pizza places.

If you're a pizza lover, this is a must!  Every single ingredient on this pizza blends in like a fine masterpiece.... from the crust to the cheese and whatever else you have chosen to eat on yours.  Ended up ordering 4 different types of slices just so I could sample. I will definitely come back over and over!
Excellent crust! Fresh ingredients! Delicious pizza !! The salad was very good too! Friendly service. I like that they have pizza by the slice until 5:00.
Food is flavorless and vastly overpriced.  Avoid at all costs.  I found it sickening.  They are awful people to top it off.  Do yourself a favor and never patronize this establishment.

Sorry, there is no way this pizza deserves the ratings Yelp is showing. I will give them a 4 on service. Friendly and prompt but the pepperoni pizza was a 2 at best. If you choose to visit Pizza Luna I would suggest something other than the pepperoni pizza.
Went for a Birthday get together. The service was friendly but the Pizza was so delicious! Will definitely return.

The GVC saved my dog's life! At the age of 12 my dog developed a serious illness.  We took her to two different clinics and as much as I love my dog, I knew I couldn't afford the prices they were saying her surgery would be.  I called the GVC and the next morning I was waiting outside their door as a walk-in.  Dr. Balzer took my dog first because of how serious her condition was.  A few hours later I went to pick up my dog and she was out of surgery- a little groggy but fine.  I think I only paid a little over a hundred for it.  I'm so grateful my dog is healed and still alive.

After having a pleasant first experience at my dog's check-up a few months ago, he needed to go in for X-rays.  The vet (which has seriously un-accommodating hours) told us we could drop him off in the morning for the x-ray and either wait until done (around noon), or board him & pick him up between 4 and 5.  We opted to wait, but then were told to leave.  After several calls throughout the morning & afternoon, we were told he had not been sedated or x-rayed, to THEN get a call that they wanted to reschedule his appointment.  When I refused to reschedule because I had worked from home and dropped him off HOURS earlier, they other option they offered me was to take my 130lb dog out of their clinic in a partially sedated, "wobbly" state, instead of honoring the appointment we had made by extending their office hours.  This mishap was attributed to "emergency visits," and as a person in healthcare, I do understand the urgency of emergency situations, but this office clearly lacks a system comprehensive enough to meet the needs of their animals & customers.  Needless to say, we will not be going back. 0 out of 5 in my opinion.
Is it fair to review a business based on the clientele? How about choice of locale? Probably not. C'est la vie. I guess I've got nothing then.

Once was enough.  
The service was meh- okay.  Not too friendly or helpful.  
Took forever to get water, bread, and have our order taken.  We were there on a weekend night & the place was not full, and there was no wedding going on, so it's unclear what the slow service was about.  
The french onion soup was too potent to enjoy.  The risotto was not enjoyable either; I've had better out of the frozen section at Trader Joe's!  
The saving grace was the creme brule.  Best I've had in years, but still not enough to make me want to go back.
Food is amazing people are very attentive and generous. Dominican food to the next level. The stars they have received are definitely a reflection of the good food and service.
I ordered the spicy version, so good! I'm very pleased with this find! It's definitely a very flavorful bowl of ramen. I ordered the low sodium version- it was perfect!

This place was really good both times I ate it. I mean I was pretty drunk both times but I remember really liking it . I love the big thin NY slices that you can fold . Good sauce to cheese ratio which is important to me because I cannot stand when I get pizza that's liek all cheese and no sauce . I like this place .

Omg....so good !!! It smells and taste like NYC good!!!
Great staff and surprisingly great variety of wine! So glad I tried this place. I will be back
They left a flyer in our hotel, but then when we called they said they wouldn't deliver. Very annoying.
I love the food here. Their chicken Alfredo is really good. They also offer delivery through UberEats. Download the UberEats app and use code UE-uaduw for $10 off first order!

I hate Cav's. 
Everything is coated in a thin layer of...grease? Can't really be sure, but it's definitely not clean.
The food blows, the beers on tap usually blow. I think. (Miller Light? Ew. Yuengling? Ok!).

I used to come here after work with a friend because they never carded me (this was pre-21). Until they did. So I stopped coming up until earlier this week when I went with a few friends for a birthday. It was a $5 cover for 75 cent drinks all night. I was only planning to have one drink, so FANTASTIC FOR ME.
Amazingly, my friend and I got hit on TOGETHER, and our cans weren't even out for the world to see. I was wearing a scarf! The guy was nice enough, save for the fact that he interrupted our conversation and then ended the one he had with us with "So, do you guys have boyfriends?"
Yes, buddy, we do. Your dress shirt is tucked into belted light denim jeans. Go away.

They also have free pizza that's pretty solid pizza for being free and served at Cav's.

Really cute store!!! The staff/owner (?) was very courteous and helpful and they carry almost anything you could ever need or want for needlepoint.  The prices are a bit high, however; but I kind of expected it to be considering it's location.  Would probably only go back if I needed specialty items.

Chhaya, located in the East Passyunk District was pretty decent for our first go. Our party of 5 came on a weekday for girls brunch. We quarter meter parked immediately right out front and had no wait whatsoever. There were many people typing away on laptops and a bunch of folks just sipping coffee and chatting so it's definitely just a chill spot also. 

I remember being impressed with their single origin coffees, espresso offerings and unique teas. 

I had no issue finding something on the menu to suit my vegan needs. The black bean gazpacho serve cold with a crostini and a side of veg chorizo priced a la carte was very satisfying. It was just the right amount of food for me to leave without being stuffed, which is a good thing first thing in the morning. 

We all tasted one another's dishes. Cinnamon waffles with fresh berries and the truffle oil toasts with arugula were the most well liked choices. The Nutella and strawberry waffles were a huge hit with the littles! 

Prices were fairly standard and service was fine, nothing extraordinary. 

The place was bright, a tad earthy and inviting. 

I would give it another go for sure. 

There's a few bistro tables outside, which looked like a lovely option on a nice day and certainly great for people watching in this ever flourishing neighborhood. 

 I also saw a sign for open mic night too. Look into it if that's your type of thing.
Quaint, cozy, lovely and delicious! A true treasure nestled among the protective cover of the Wissahickon!

My friend Priti and I stopped by here yesterday after reading some of the reviews on Yelp. We're new fans! Not only did yelp lead us to a new gem, but also a new up and coming neighborhood. The stroll after brunch down the block was great and refreshing. The shops are all small, quaint, and cute with lots of character.

Chhaya fit perfectly on this row. The space has a cozy and comfortable feel to it. The breakfast was good. My friend Priti loved the potatoes/home fries, and she's very picky-so this is rare! I loved their variety of drinks, looking forward to going back and trying other items.

If you are not from the area and using a GPS, make sure to include East Passyunk, and not just Passyunk, we had a hard time finding it initially and ended up on the opposite side on West Passyunk, but after we called the restaurant-they guided us in the right direction!

Went there today for the lunch buffet today and couldn't be more pleased. Super clean and really good pizza and salad. The games and game staff were just as good, the young man operating the roller coaster ride was very professional and my son had a blast on it. The young lady operating the prize booth was just as good and very nice to my son too. We will be definitely be coming back this Peter Piper is rockin!!
How long bay sells really good Vietnamese food I had Thai tea and it was excellent and I had pho and can't tell you how good it was

I don't want to write a review about Chhaya. Mostly because I don't want you (yes, you reading this) to come and spoil my fun. I want to keep Chhaya all to myself, and only share it with close friends, because it's got this great feel of not being one of the major 'brunch oclock' places in Philadelphia- and I don't want you to ruin it. OK? so if you go, seriously, keep it under your hat? deal?

All joking aside, Chhaya truly is the perfect atmosphere I'm looking for in a brunch spot. It's just an small coffee house with perfect coffees and teas, foods, and free wifi. The waitresses are super attentive and fun to talk to- like fully fleshed out characters not just interested in taking your order, but actually having a human conversation- what what? 

As for the food, dear lord, where to start. My friend had the heuvros rancheros waffles- maybe I ate like 1/4 of his plate, my bad. Let's talk about his entree first- heuvros rancheros is a delicious meal but to me I always feel like when it comes it's just beans, and that's not what I want in breakfast. Theirs is served atop cornbread waffles, with eggs, black beans, salsa,  and practically a whole avocado and it's just perfect. It's filling yet the waffles manage to maintain a pleasant lightness and the portion size isn't overwhelming, it's exactly enough food to satiate- I love a place that doesn't think they need to have HUGE food in order to have GREAT food. There's definitely a difference, and this place has got it.

As for me I had the savory crepe of the day, it was filled with gouda, fennel, roasted tomatoes, arugula, and topped with an egg, all for only 7.50 I think- How is that even possible? It was simply the best, melt in your mouth, delightful brunch I have had in awhile- and I brunch constantly so how did they top the others? I have no idea, they just did. I think the atmosphere of the place certainly made everything just jive for the perfect brunch experience. The place is small, but it wasn't packed when I was there which was really lovely. Basically I eating here made me want to break my lease and move to East Passyunk. no big deal. Just an awesome life changing, mood lifting brunch. You have definitely created a repeat customer Chhaya- much thanks!
We are full time rv'ers and get to sample pizza in a variety of locations. The pizzas we had at Luna's were among the best we've had. I would highly recommend.

Really good BBQ - very consistent, reasonably priced. My favorite are the Baby back ribs with mac and cheese and sweet potatoes. Corn bread is great too. One of the better options for BBQ in the NE (right up there with Rib Rack, and 10x's better than Little Dave's BBQ.)
Perfection. Best brunch and coffee in town. waffles, sandwiches all of the food is wonderful. Don't come here though because I don't want to have to wait to get in (very small)
Quick delivery of deeeeelicious orange crispy beef and of course a cheesesteak egg roll!!!  Always my go to for Chinese delivery

Been looking forward to trying out Chhaya cafe but were pretty disappointed.

Food: ok, nothing we would come back for, especially with so many better options in the area. I got a pastrami sandwich, but the meat was sliced so thick that it was still cold in the middle (Pastrami is supposed to be nice thin layers). Couldn't taste the cheese because the rye bread was also cut so thick, and it was grilled in the waffle iron, so it was dry and just wrong. I would have sent it back to get cooked longer but nobody bothered to check on our table.

Drinks: I got the siphon coffee with Chiapas beans, but it was also just meh. My friend's plain old drip coffee tasted better. And then the check came - $8! Funny, they're too embarrassed to print the price on the menu so they slap you with a surprise on the check. They probably figure you'd be too well-mannered to question it.

Lunch for two came to $40. Way too much for just ok food, drink and slack service. Two of the workers were pretty nice, but two others made us feel like they were doing us a favor by waiting on us.

It's sorta cute inside, but they really need to focus on customer service and the product or they're goners. We won't be back.

PS - We just looked at the photos and our food didn't look like any of them. We noticed that they moved, maybe Chhaya was better at their old location.

This is my go-to for breakfast or brunch in my neighborhood. They always have my favorites: chorizo waffle, truffle egg toast. Excellent service. Very kid (and dog) friendly. BYO champagne for mimosas. Lots of seating so don't ever need reservations!

Hands down the best pizza in Tucson with high quality ingredients! Try the Fig, Pig, Goat pizza, you won't regret it.  They make a triple berry lemonade that you can get spiked that is delicious too.  Staff is always very helpful.
Good eats! Make sure if you dine in Monday's to get the $15 deal: a large pizza and wings special.

don't do it!! I went there for the first time because I dint know where else to go. first of all I was just there for the regular pedi and the tech insisted that I get the one above it which was 10 dollars more expensive.. he didn't want to trim my toe nails and just filed them ugh! told him I wanted glitter on just one nail and did all of them because he thought it would look better ... really??! told me to sit under the fan thing to dry for 12 min and I did but my big toe nail was not dry and when I asked nicely if he could fix it he got upset and said "I'm just going to put glitter over it no one will notice" and left it all lumpy ... not cool!!!! oh and I'm pretty sure he gave me used slippers gross!! and didn't even clean the tub where we all put our feet in. never going there again.

First off, I have to say this isn't a review of their shearing skills and colorist know-how. I am actually writing a review about the customer service I received when I went in yesterday to try to redeem a Living Social deal for a dry cut + highlights. 

Due to a misunderstanding with the appointment time and finding parking in Center City, I was already late to my appointment by 20 minutes, yet the girls were still willing to take me in. Already I was grateful for that.

Then, when I sat down for my initial consultation, I mentioned to them that I had previously permed my hair 6 months ago. As soon as I said that, my colorist Maggie kindly explained to me that she wouldn't feel comfortable putting bleach in my hair because my hair was already pretty chemically damaged. I was actually disappointed because I was really looking forward to a new set of highlights, but then I realized what she was saying totally made sense and it was for my benefit that we not proceed. She said she would be happy to see me in another 6 months after it had grown out. I explained to her my concerns that my LS promotion was going to expire next month and she reassured me that I could just call them, explain what happened, and that she would vouch for me. 

I thanked them for their selfless honesty and for looking out on my hair's behalf. Soon afterwards I called LS, they called the salon to confirm, and I got my money back. It was a pain-free transaction that put $70 back in my pocket and saved me from salon suicide. Thanks Maggie!

After reading all the rave reviews we decided to have a late lunch here.  I arrived a little after 2, it was pretty dead. The place was small but looked fresh and clean.  It's a semi self serv system where you order your food at the counter and they bring it out to you and you get your own drinks.  My friend had already ordered and there was one other person in line ordering. The pizza slice specials were not very clear on pricing (due to time of day there was a discount which I had to ask to clarify).  We each ordered 2 slices, I, the New York/Traditional and the Bianca both with spicy sausage and mushroom, my friend, the Puttanesca and New York plain (she didn't know she could add toppings for the slices since none were offered or prompted when she ordered), she got a glass of wine as well.  The food came out fast but I was disappointed in the pizza itself since I had such high expectations due to the high reviews.  Maybe because we ordered the slices instead of a whole fresh pie, the pizza was pretty dry and bland.  Both of us doused the pizza in the chili oil to give it some flavor.  I would maybe come and try it again by ordering a whole fresh pizza, but, by the slice I won't again.

Absolutely perfect setting. If weather is good sit out on the patio. Food is pretty good. Pan seared salmon and crab cake were both fresh and well prepared. But the selling point is definitely the location.

I was in Philly for a wedding this past weekend and made an appt at AMS Salon for the braid bar with Tasha. She did an amazing job on my french braid and had me out of the salon in 10 minutes. The price was great and service was perfect. I will be back next time I'm in town.

I came here soley for the discounted services, and got what I deserved.  The doctor was very short and rude with me, my cat, who has never sounded as upset as he was when he was there simply needed a rabies vaccine.  She didn't ask me anything about why I was there or for his history, she just grabbed him and threw a blanket over his head.  I offered to calm him down a little and she ignored me.  I asked if she thought that he was getting overweight, which I was geniunely concerned about and wanted a preofessional opinion, she again ignored me.  The only thing she talked to me about was if he used a litter box (what cat doesnt???) and how often I cleaned it, which I felt she was implying that I didn't know how to take care of him.. She then gave him shots that he didn't need (after I had his records faxed to them twice, once a week before my apt and then when I got there again..)  Overall, I would never go back (which I wanted to get him declawed, but have since let him tear my couch to peices because I didn't have the heart to subject him to her again)  I would NOT reccommend this place ever to anybody, pay the extra money and be treated like you and your pet are welcomed.

I enjoy the location and the atmosphere of this cafe. I like that there is a variety of menu options for food and beverage. I have been to this place twice and both times have enjoyed myself as well as did the people i had with me. The prices are great. The service is great as well. I definitely recommend Chhaya Cafe.

Decidedly not gourmet pizza, decidedly not an all-adults establishment, so with hesitation we had the lunch buffet there. We were desperate and nothing else appealing was within close distance and we were on our bikes. We had low expectations after an unpleasant experience at the other kiddie's birthday party hang-out. 

But you know what? For $4.99 each for all-you-can-eat salad and pizza, it is not so bad. Skip the overpriced and unhealthy sodas, focus on the unhealthy pizza, and it is a reasonable deal. Quality? Salad, of which there were three to choose from, were just fine, pizza, of which there were at least a half-dozen from which to choose, was about the same as frozen pizzas. Lots of salt, okay ingredients, unremarkable sauce and cheese, and pretty good crust. But this is under $10 to fill up two hungry bikers. What else can I say but "it works." Having an area away from the kiddie toys that is less appealing to children but more appealing to adults helped a lot as well.

What a disappointment
$120 for lunch for 4, and all meals were bad. The Thai shrimp noodles was bland and flavorless. The Greek salad was wilted and too salty to eat with a weird non Greek dressing with strange crumbly dried olives. The crab cakes tasted like old crab meat, worst I've ever had. The miso salad was over salted and inedible. The salad with salmon was undercooked with a very small piece of salmon.

I've been here about 10 times over the past few years and on those visits we got nice food in such a nice setting. 

Something has changed here, I'm not going back

Outstanding pizza. We went bianca with lamb sausage,onion, and artichoke. Yum. The take on a Caesar salad with rediccio was nice and anchovy flavored. Even the iced tea stood out. Not a fancy place but really good. They know what they want to serve and that confidence shines through.

Ugh, not a fan. I ordered lunch here today because I wanted to try a new place. The hot and sour soup only made it one bite before I tossed it. Bizarre sweet flavour to it - total opposite of sour. The "chicken satay" is really just the same as chicken teriyaki from any other place, except really flavourless. I ate one piece. The beef with mixed vegetable combo was not offensive, but nothing exciting. Tons of cabbage. I won't be ordering here again.

Saturday night, 8 pm reservation, three of us.  Decided to take a table on the porch.  Beer list was a little disappointing. House wines were fine.  Place was busy so service a little slow, to be expected.  Onion soup, a little pricey but very good.  Catfish (not from the Wissahickon!) with cous cous, very, very good.  Appy size crab cake, very good.  Red snapper special, excellent.  We were very impressed with this version of an old fave, hope they keep up the good work, cause we'll be back.

Being that i have a business on this strip CHHAYA should have been a convience  to get a quick bite...NOTTTT,, waited as the waitress pointed out 18 minutes even though i said 20 min...ok kill me for 2...Yogurt parfait. took again 18 min...i could have made 8 courses...all that being said the staff is what annoyed me mostly...like i was bothering them,, seriously when an Italian  girl is hungry there is no waiting that long...

Not thrilled after Dr. Balzer sold business. I've been going there at least 15 years. The new vets perform tests with out reviewing what the options are and then you get the bill with items/tests you did not agree to.  They assume too much.
Best.. Waffles... Ever!!! Nice coffee, homey atmosphere, chill staff... The list could go on. Can I live here..?
Their sauce is awesome and crust is so good I'd eat it plain. Staff was friendly and helpful too. The place was empty when we got there but by the time we left nearly every table was full.

We are frequent walkers and hikers on this trail so we've been meaning to try this restaurant for years. Finally when the hubs birthday rolled around this year and we were looking for a place to go, we thought.... Valley Green Inn. 

The first thing I noticed inside was that, in this freezing cold winter, they have to work hard to heat the old building. We were sat in a room with a roaring fireplace that made it very cozy. 

Our waitress wasn't exceptionally friendly. Maybe she's shy? I always felt badly asking her for things. I feel like a bubbly wait staff can really make a difference at a restaurant. 

I ordered the filet with a french onion soup. Both were exceptional. The filet came with Asiago mashed potatoes (delicious) and prosciutto wrapped bone marrow (which I gave to my husband....I'm not a dog!) 

He ordered the meatloaf and the mushroom soup. He raved about both. 

We will definitely visit again, maybe in the summer when the weather is nicer. The food was delicious and you can't beat the remote location.
Dirty. Just get take-out if you go to school in the area and are on a budget. But you'll most likely stumble in here if you are drunk.

I went to AMS for a Keratin Treatment and will not be returning ever again.  I found the staff to be impersonal (read: not nice) and was actually uncomfortable as I sat there waiting for my ride to pick me up once my treatment was done.  Oh, I should mention that my treatment was done WAY ahead of time because it was so rushed.  Should have taken at least an hour - sometimes more...  took less than 45 minutes.  And I should add that this $300 treatment DIDN'T WORK VERY WELL and I'm extremely disappointed.  When I called to complain about the treatment and ask what could be done, it was suggested that, for a refund, I call Groupon (which is why I went here in the first place).  Otherwise, I could go in for them to tell me what happened...  I already know what happened.  It was a rushed, poorly done treatment.  

Going elsewhere from now on.  You should, too.

Asian Fusion & Steak just opened up a bit ago and let me tell you it is GREAT! They deliver quickly, the food is fresh, and delicious. Seriously, I think they might have some of the best chinese/japanese food in the city especially when you look at their prices. 

They have these great deals so if you spend $20 bucks you get free chicken satay or a free soda and if you spend $30 bu you get free general Tso's or sesame chicken.

Their sushi rolls are a good quality and they are generous with your sides (soy sauce, wasabi, ginger). I order them delivery frequently since they opened and I have yet to be disappointed at all. 

I'll admit the first time I looked at their address I was doubtful, but I am so thankful I got over my doubt and tried them because they provide really excellent Asian cuisine in a timely fashion that wows me every time!
We had the very best pizza here. There was a wait due to busy college graduation. The staff was very polite and kept us informed of wait times. The gelato & Sorbetto were delicious as well.

Waited 25 minutes only to get the wrong order and an eye roll when I said just give me the money back.     Because I wadding waiting a total of 50 minutes for  an egg sandwich. What were they doing? Driving to a farm to get the eggs?  When they're good they're great but when they're bad they're ridiculous.

SUCH A CUUUUUUUTE PLACE!!!! The berries waffle was so heavenly and soft topped with whipped cream and 3 kinds of berries. My bf got the truffle egg toast with arugula salad in a citrus vinaigrette. That was also delicious. It had just enough truffle and lemon taste to balance each other.

My iced latte was creamy and full of aroma. I liked sitting there and reading the board with all of their drinks. I wish I lived closer, so I could try a different coffee each day.

agree.  place was never great, but new guy seems to be particularly greedy.  and they don't keep you informed of what they're doing to your animal so ask questions and keep asking them; ask about costs, too.  i went there the other day for one particular procedure for my dog.  before i knew it, they were giving him vaccines and drawing blood without asking my permission or even telling me what they were drawing blood for.

This place has wonderful atmosphere, like an old country inn, and the food is excellent as well.  Definitely recommend the pork chop.  Portions are sizable, but not overwhelming.  

Only problem - it's hard to find!  DON'T BELIEVE GOOGLE MAPS - call and get directions - it's actually inside Fairmount Park.  There are a few roads named Valley Green, so it's really important to get specific directions on how to get there, or you could end up on the wrong Valley Green Road, as we did.  It's well worth the journey, though - great atmosphere, nice and attentive staff, and most importantly delicious food.
Incredible and unique small plates. Great coffee, but you'd expect that, definitely try the eggplant relish and the hummus.

Dr Cindy is amazing -- we LOVE her. She cares for our three cats and was very sensitive during our hardship with losing our pitbull to lymphoma. The prices are very affordable and the staff is very pleasant. I would recommend this vet to anyone -- adults, college students, whatever! Thank you Girard!

This bar sucks. Management thinks that they are somehow better than a mediocre sports bar, which is what they actually are. Also virtually impossible to see whatever game you want bc their TV setup was designed by a drunk guy. Don't come here unless you have no other choice

It was a total impulse but we saw the diners on the patio and the food smelled and looked so good, we walked in! We were not disappointed! Our pizza was great, the salad was amazing and our wine went beautifully with our meal per the suggestion of their staff who took our order! A very fun night with excellent food was had at Pizza Luna!

Ordered a bagel with cream cheese and a bacon, egg, and cheese on a bagel for pickup.
The bagel had an embarrassing amount of cream cheese on it and the sandwich had no cheese with 1 slice of bacon.

I would like to say the ladies at the cash register was wonderful and was quick. The line cook or food preparation team not so much. If you trying to get food before you get to work they will cause you to be late as they have no care how long it takes to make the food. They get it done when they get your food done.

I try to keep my order simple at this particular Wawa cause they always messing up my order. I am trying to grab breakfast quickly and head to work. I don't have time for them to remake my order and I needed my breakfast so I ate it.

I had brunch here today for the second time. I brought a friend whom had never been.  Before we arrived, I told her how perfect the food was the first time I visited and that the whole experience had really been outstanding. 

Today, the food again was  great... but the service was awful! I had to make sad faces and point to my empty glass so that we could get more water. My friend only had cheese on one half of her sandwich (which she still loved!), but we decided against complaining to our server because she barely said a word to us and kind of threw things on our table, never smiling. Upon requesting a to-go container for some left over veggie chili (yum!), our server roughly shoved one in my friends face, without saying a word. Maybe she was having a bad day. We also said, "Thank you!" numerous times to Brittany S. (our server) and smiled at her, but she would not make eye contact and she never once said, "You are welcome." I could tell that other guests around us were also turned off by this server and did hear the table next to us complaining. My friend and I were in lovely moods on a nice Saturday afternoon and were so looking forward to brunching.  It is a shame that we had to experience the negativity of Brittany S. I wanted dessert after our meal, but opted to leave and get something sweet elsewhere as I felt very uncomfortable staying any longer. I saw Brittany by herself in a corner, texting/doing something on her iphone as we rushed out. 

I like your food, Chhaya, but I do not like your service.
Cute vet tech was especially cute and neutered my unruly husky with professionalism. Ghost is much happier now...I'm pretty sure

My boo saw this place on Yelp and we decided to check it out.  It was really tight inside and it felt a lot like Tetris as we moved around trying to not be in the way while servers were rushing around.  

The tables feel really small even for just two people.  I was a bit overwhelmed by the coffee menu, since I'm a Dunkin' Donuts kind of girl.  I asked if they had caramel for iced coffee and she said their caramel syrup wouldn't dissolve in iced coffee, so I wanted a regular iced and a water.  She brought the coffees with cream and I asked for simple syrup....and she gave me a look and said she'd have to check on that.    I never got simple syrup and it took 3 asks to get iced water.  

Two beverages each made our table extremely cramped and it was kind of difficult to manage my food when i was wedged between a wall and a very-close other table of patrons who didn't have a lot of spacial awareness.

I ordered the sausage gravy cornbread waffle and a side of bacon.  Boo ordered the pumpkin waffles special.  I was expecting my cornbread waffles to be a bit sweater for that sweet/savory situation...but that plate was all savory.  It was delicious, though!  And the bacon was really good too.  They were perfect portions at the perfect price, I was perfectly full.

The ambiance is a little too hipstery/coffeesnobby and cramped for my tastes, but the food was pretty good and moderately priced.

Came here today with my coworkers and a friend that is half Dominican so it was her recommendation to try this place. Glad we did! The staff is super friendly and the food was so authentic and flavorful. You walk up and order off of the buffet of food. They have lunch specials for $5.99 which includes rice, beans and a meat. I also added some potato to mine and was not charged extra. I absolutely love rice and beans and thee were so full of flavor. The chicken was AMAZING! Fall off the bone tender and wow so flavorful!!! I may be back here soon! Highly recommend if you're looking for authentic Dominican food.
Nothing less than five stars for these guys. Best sushi in the area by far. Very clean inside and I saw gloves on everyone handling food. Support your local businesses and try them out.

Absolutely fantastic food and staff! I was a little confused as to how the whole operation worked with seating and ordering, but who cares?? The food and staff are that good! The Luna Lemonade May be the best I've ever had!

Husband and I came here for a birthday party on a Saturday. It was crowded and very NOISY. But then again, I really hope you don't expect a quiet ambiance when going to Peter Piper. The pizza was actually pretty good. I admit, I was starving so I could be somewhat jaded. But, for the sake of the review, the pizza had a nice crust and tasted freshly made. The kids had a fun time playing games and the adults just sat at the table and talked. 
At the end of the night, we got on their merry go round type ride and it was actually a lot of fun! I was surprised but it put everyone in a good mood and it was like we were kids again.

Went for Sunday brunch. Great location.
Go for the location not the brunch.
Kitchen is not careful enough to poach an egg for Benedict. Eggs over cooked, English muffin under toasted. Best part of trip is walking around Valley Green trails.

Chhaya is my favorite breakfast haven in all of Philadelphia. The coffee is great, the atmosphere is warm and the plates are always fantastic. I live in Providence now (sadly) and every time I come back I will end up here. 

.:. Extra bonus if you are lucky enough to get the comfy window seat .:.
Fast friendly delivery and the food always arrives hot. And the cheesesteak egg rolls are my absolute guilty pleasure!!!

A fun little place located in the Trader Joe's strip mall.  This location has been cursed as many previous restaurants have failed.  I think the curse may be broken as Pizza Luna is quite good.  We've become big fans of Napoli style pizza since returning from a trip to southern Italy this past summer and have been sampling all the similar places around town.  While we've yet to find an equal to some of the places in Italy, Pizza Luna comes close.  Order at the counter and 10-15 minutes later, out comes hot fresh tasty pizza!  The Luna meat and cheese board was good too.
These guys from Oregon came to Tucson with a great idea for delicious pizza.  Really love the white pizza.  You have to try it.  It is our favorite place to go or carry out.

Ordered a large cheese pizza today, very nice people but the pizza is garbage. The dough tastes like it's frozen, doesn't taste like fresh homemade dough from a pizzeria, the sauce is lacking and the cheese doesn't taste like 100% mozzarella. Save your money, this place is not worth it
Not a bad slice at all. I ordered the white pizza and a soda. Will probably return in the near future to try other of their other offerings.

I had a cup of cider and the berry waffle and substituted the whipped cream for Nutella. Absolutely delicious! The ambiance is very cosy and the staff was great. The wait wasn't too long for 3, as others have said, much much shorter than Sabrina's. Overall, excellent food, great staff, and decent prices.

This location is conveniently located and easy to get to the only problem is that you have to fight through a wall of homeless people begging for money and cigarettes on your way in the store and out of the store. And God save your soul if you have to pump gas because you will be around the entire time you are at the pump.

This place is a shit show. The OWNER has zero personality and hospitality! DO NOT GO HERE. AMELIA sets her clock for 8 minutes and that's all the time she will a lot for coloring your hair, and that was reflected in the final product. I went here for two years because it was so cheap, but the quality of the work reflects it. She could barely cover my grays and they would grow back in 2.5 weeks because she didn't paint the color close enough to the root. My sister had left more than six months before I did for the same reasons. I had a family emergency and was a "no show" (ie I wasn't able to pick up their calls bc of the family emergency) and they told me they can no longer accommodate me when I called back. This was shocking and an example of the WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE. Also it feels like everyone in there is on Prozac, and they wondered why I fell asleep while waiting for my hair to process.

This is one of those places that reminds you that you live in a neighborhood.  By that, I mean there are real people with real lives and individual stories to tell.  How that is conveyed through the experience of doing business here, I'm unsure, but every time I go there, I leave feeling like I love where I live.

Excellent pie. I got a slice and a draft Dragoon Ipa. I chose the puttanesca, per recommendation from the staff. He said he usually gets meat but this one has curated olives, artichokes, cherry tomatoes, feta and on their white sauce. The order was easy, the staff is so pleasant and professional, really comfortable feel inside (patio outside is shaded but i dont have a/c in my car so I opted inside) the food and beer came out quick and the pizza - solid. Oh, when you are finishing up that crust you have to use their olive oil or you are missing the exclamation point. 

Only small draw back is you have to get a key for the restroom, which is shared with the complex. Not big enough for me to take a star off but worth mentioning. 

For under 8 bucks and a bigger smile on my face than I had coming in, I will be back.

I went here today and the service was wonderful. The staff were all very kind and helpful. The interior was a little tight but nicely decorated. This place allows animals as well. A lot of people with pets and babies seemed to stop by. A friend of mine ordered the chicken and waffles and it came undercooked. Overall, the staff was lovely the food was good although the portions are a bit on the smaller side.

I've been to Valley Green many times to hike. In my younger years I would grab a hot dog from the snack stand at the Inn. Now being a responsible adult, two friends and I went to dine at the restaurant at the Inn. We came for lunch on a Saturday around noon in early April. We were seated in the front room to the left of the entrance. It was not near the door, but the place was very drafty. We ended up keeping our coats on while they lit a fire in the fireplace. Myself and one of my companions opted for the French Onion soup while the other had the Roast Turkey Breast Sandwich. The food was good, and the dining space has a cozy old-world feel. Nice place if you're in the area or looking for an escape from the bustling city.

Stopped in for lunch. The Cesar salad was unusual. Croutons were so hard they were not edible. Dressing was not great. Pizza was very pricey for what you get.  The pizza tasted okay but nothing to write home about.

such a nice retreat from the city! beautiful building, beautiful scenery.
had a really nice cup of french onion soup. its a little bit pricey. the food's good but not great..
mostly take the trip out for the environment.

This place has the best coffee on Passyunk Ave.  I don't know what they do, but the cold brew is the stuff of dreams.  If it's cold, get the dulce de leche latte which is made with actual dulce de leche, not flavored syrup. The food is also really, really good, the wifi is great, there are outlets everywhere and the staff is so nice.  My favorite coffee shop in the city.

This is by far the best pizza I have ever eaten. My husband loves pizza while I can take it or leave it, until today. We stopped by at lunch and I ordered the slice and salad special. The Merguez pizza was amazing. Great pesto, housemade sausage and a thin crisp crust makes this the best slice in all of Tucson. The homemade salad dressing was delicious. My husband ordered the 12 inch sausage rosa and says it is real pizza, best in Tucson and I think he has visited every pizza place in the city. Located in the Trader Joe's plaza on Speedway and Wilmot it is very easy to park.
irony doesn't get much more tragic than watching a beefy security guard prod and probe little old grannies in line to see the liberty bell

Food was delicious, very flavorful, and the crust was amazing! We had the Puttanesca pizza and Caesar salad. The service was great with friendly staff and the food was brought to us quickly despite the crowd.

I just ordered from here for the first time. Thanks to some clients at work talking about sushi, I was craving sushi for dinner for delivery. My husband is not a fan of sushi, so I needed to also find a place that would have other options. 

My selection was limited when I searched on Yelp, since a lot of places don't deliver to my neighborhood (Pennsport). However, thanks to some positive reviews, I found Asian Fusion & Steak Inc.

While I'm not really sure where the "Steak" part comes in, the menu is pretty well defined by the name. The selection of sushi isn't vast and creative, but if you just want simple sushi they have all the basics (and some weird things like Shrimp Tempura, Cucumber, and mayo... MAYO- ew)....  Anyway. They have a menu through Allmenus(dot)com, and you can even order online. After debating what we wanted for nearly 15 minutes, we made and paid for our order online and awaited confirmation. Peking Duck, Sushi Combo w/ Miso soup, and Dumplings here we go! The description for the Sushi Combo was somewhat cryptic as 6pc Sushi + California Roll; I figured I could choose what kind of sushi I wanted so I wrote a note that I wanted Spicy Tuna. 

I quickly got an email, followed by a phone call letting us know that they were out of Peking Duck. While we were disappointed that they'd run out, we changed the order to Sesame Chicken with an Egg Roll. 

About 32min later (the wait is ranged 30-45min according to our email, so no problems there), our food came and I brought it up to our apartment. 

To our pleasant surprise, not only did I get a Spicy Tuna Roll to replace the California Roll (and got 6pc of Salmon, Tuna, and a fish I cannot remember what it is but it's tasty!), but we also got a free order of Sweet and Sour Chicken with "free, sorry" written on it, and two pint boxes of white rice. Wow! It was really nice of them to give us extra food for not having what we originally ordered. 

So, their customer service is great. How is the food?

Pretty awesome. The sushi is solid. It tasted fresh and wasn't creepy or slimey and didn't have a fishy smell (the mark of poor sushi in my opinion). It was pretty much just as good as if it were prepared right in front of you.. and it was in a separate bag than the hot food we ordered. Major plus. The Sesame Chicken was above average - not the BEST but it's a challenge to find knock-your-socks-off chinese food in the city that is reasonably priced. It IS far better than many other places we've tried though! The dumplings were awesome and very large, with 8 to go around. I'm not a huge fan of sweet and sour chicken anyway, but I'm so impressed by their service that I don't even care. We only took a little bite each, and are saving the rest because we had so much food!

If they lose a point for above average chinese food, they earn it back a million times for the awesome customer service. I wouldn't mind going there and seeing how everything is at the restaurant sometime! Definitely worth it.
We went to try it because it had 5 stars. I don't think it's worth the price. The pizza was fair but not 5 stars and we did not like the caesar salad.

My coworker had a craving for burgers and fries, and I happily jumped on the bandwagon-- I was getting a little tired of the three places I frequent for lunch. 

So a cheeseburger from Cavanaugh's with a side of Old Bay fries it was! 

The fries were great. The cheeseburger was on the dry side, although I had ordered it medium well. I would actually love to come here during a game, where okay food is permissible when you're buzzed/drunk!
I will never understand why pizza places call their Pizza New York Pizza, when it is nothing like the real thing.

I am the luckiest girl in the world. Great pizza just moved into the neighborhood. The crust is perfect. The meats and vegetables are perfect. The house made cheese perfect. The Caesar dressing was garlicky perfection. 

The staff was kind and attentive. Thank you Travis for your helpful advice and your PERFECT housemade lemonade. 

You get the drift. If you haven't been there GO!

I had my dog spayed at GVC and they were very helpful and supportive of all my questions when I brought my dog in for the procedure. I had gone to Morris Animal Rescue and purchased discounted spay coupons that were accepted here in order to get my dog spayed but not break the bank. Regardless of this I was treated just like any pet parent and My dog made it through with flying colors. The scar from the procedure is barely even visible today. 

I would definitely recommend this clinic to other dog owners, the only reason I don't use them full time is because it is so far from my house in south Philly and traffic gets pretty bad up in that area when I can usually get my dog in.

Broadway location may be the largest. Haven't seen 22nd st location. Better selection of games than Ina PPP. Staff are friendly and want to help with whatever you need. Love the TVs on sports channels.

I live right around the corner and am glad I finally tried Chhaya! We went in for Sunday brunch and it was full but the wait was only 15 minutes. Everyone was very nice and friendly and I felt the service was well paced. I got the bagel sandwich - it was tasty and the perfect portion. The dulce de leche iced latte wasn't as good as I had hoped - I felt like I paid $5 for chocolate milk. My boyfriend got the white chocolate waffles and liked them but noted the regular chocolate chips they add really take away from the white chocolate flavor. It also seems like a cute place to come and enjoy the coffee bar. I'll be back!

I am such a fan of Chhaya, especially the elixirs the owner concocts for her hot and cold tea blends.   A blue lady hot tea with the added heaven sent elixir, which consistes of honey, lemon, ginger and black pepper is divine, and a perfect after a Yoga session at Wake Up Yoga.  I brought my son in this week and we had a beautiful cheese plate and baguette.  I got to try the Sage Mint Lime-ade that is hand made to order, so refreshing, clean and delicious.... now that I've written this review, I think its time for a little something something.  Don't miss the coffees eithers, fresh brewed, Chemex, French pressed or Siphoned, they are all outstanding.

The lack of service was unbelievable. I was introduced to this place at least 5 years ago due to their 25 cent wings. It holds a very special place in my heart but it's really nose-dived. I sat at the bar and waited and waited and waited for the bartender. There were less than 15 patrons in the bar yet there were 4 bartenders who were too involved with taking selfies or eating candy to notice my empty glass. I have had some great nights here in the past but my service on Halloween has convinced me to never come back.  The only saving grace was the bar manager must have recognized the look of sheer disgust on face  so he gave me my last 2 shots for free.
Yum!  Well balanced sauce on the pizza.  Great charcuterie board.  Local beers on tap.  Friendly staff.  We will be back!

My first few visits here were definitely 4-5 stars but my last visit here with my sister left a taste so sour I don't think it's worth going back to again. EVER.

We didn't even dine there. It was the service that was absolutely horrible.

My sister and I walked down the trail Saturday morning and noticed that there along the river in front of the restaurant, was set up for a wedding. We weren't sure if the restaurant was closed for it so we went up and yes, there was a sign. We were looking forward to their sandwiches which are pretty good. And as we turned around and started to walk away, a waitress burst through and told us, very rudely, that she had already said that they were closed. 

We were in shock. And as soon as she stormed out, she started back in and my sister replied that we had just arrived there. We thought that maybe would've cleared it up for her but then she turned around and retorted, "NO THIS IS THE SECOND TIME I'VE COME OUT TO TELL YOU THIS."

WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE EVER. I don't know what it was. But we had literally just gotten there and was on the property for less than a minute and no one had come out to tell us anything. We were walking on our way out.

Maybe there was another Asian couple that just was there and was told that it was closed, maybe this particular waitress is blind and couldn't tell that we were not the same couple she told to go away. Maybe she just got dumped by her boyfriend. Whatever the case, it is absolutely unacceptable. I'm writing here first then I'm going to make a call tomorrow to talk to the manager. I refuse to go back even though it's one of my mom's favorite places to dine at until I hear a honest apology from the waitress in person.

In all honesty, the service at the other times were pretty good but this is just over the top. She might as well have come out and talked in a Chinese accent (even though we're not Chinese) and did the squinty eyes for how ignorant and rude she acted as potential customers.

Parking: None, must park before entering trail
Price: $11+ per person but not worth it even if it's free if the customer service is beyond horrible
Wait: Not too long once you order (if you get that far)

Just want to thank the folks at Pizza Luna.  I live near Chicago and I ordered grub hub delivery from for my ailing father and his wife in the Tucson hospital.  I forgot to order drinks and when I called to try to add them on I was told that they would take care of the drinks and they hoped my father had a speedy recovery.  Thank you so much for your kindness, and I can't wait to eat at your place next time I'm in Tuscon.

This was probably the worst experience I have ever had in a restaurant. Not because of the food quality, but because of the unprofessional behavior of the General Manager named Pat. After we had been seated for 30 min, he came out and told us that we were at a reserved table. When I pointed out that we had bussed our own table, and there were no "reserved" signs on the table, he became irate and started screaming. I think he may have been intoxicated on the job. It was easily the worst professional behavior I have ever experienced. Aside from him, everybody else working there was very nice and even apologized for his behavior. Be careful with this one!!!

Amazing brunch menu with delicious tea and coffee selection. The service was good even on a busy day and the wait is usually not long. This is my favorite cafe in the Passyunk area, and they always display interesting local art as well. Try their berry pancakes and truffle toast!

I came here after my friend suggested it as a great late night spot to eat at. I went on a Friday night and they had Absolut drinks for $5 and a Jameson and ginger only cost 6.50 so that isn't bad. I ordered motts sticks and they weren't my favorite, but my cousin got medium wings and enjoyed them. What I really like however was the place! It is really chill, very diverse and had a cool DJ playing some nice hits. Great spot to pre-game, watch sports, go on a date, or simply just grab a bite to eat. i would definitely come here again!

This place is incredible! I woke up this morning and wanted a strawberry Belgian waffle. I found Chhaya on yelp and decided to try it since they specialize in waffles - so happy I did! I had the strawberry nutella waffle and my boyfriend tried the sausage gravy and cornbread waffle: simply amazing! I highly recommend it, we'll definitely be going back for brunch.

Hands down the best service and pizza I've had in a long time!!! We had the Cesar salad, cauliflower crust pizza. The Entire staff was friendly and helpful. This isn't just a pizza joint to these guys......it's their passion and it shows in  the product they provide. You won't be disappointed!!

I am from Brooklyn, and I know pizza!!! This is unbelieveable! I was visiting the University of Arizona in Tucson and happened to hear about it from a friend, and wow. The crust is light and cruncy. Extremely flavorful. 
The margarita pizza with homemade fresh mozzarella and San Marzano tomatoes, was sublime!!! Dont miss this little gem!

Amazing everything!! Had the traditional pepperoni small (plenty for 2 people). Great sauce, pepperoni slices were huge, and the crust (72 hour process to make) was perfect thickness. Service was amazing too. Very attentive staff and the pizza was made soo fast! We can't wait to go back to try another pizza.

This place is delicious! I love it. We ordered the pepperoni pizza and the salami pizza. They were both really good. My favorite part was the crust. You could tell that it was made fresh. The pizzas came out pretty quick too. We didn't have to wait very long even though it was Friday night. The location is also super convenient for us since we live on the east side. I like the feel of this place too. It's small and cozy. If you are thinking about checking this place out, I recommend it. 10/10. I will eat there again.
Best breakfast ever! Coffee was also fantastic. Very small and quaint but I loved tge feel of the place. Planning on going back tomorrow before we leave philly.

Terrible!  Went for Mothers Day Brunch, what they had was spartan and needed to be refilled.  There was Prime Ribe which was good, but the rest was chicken, mashed potatoes, pasta, etc.  Not nearly worth the money.  There were 7 of us, our bill was almost $400 AND they added a 20% gratuity on top!!!!  Thats right 20% for a buffet!  So we got our own food, the waitress got us water, 3 glasses of wine, an ice tea and 3 cups of coffee total - and she got over $80.  Really?!!!  We got our own food and deserts!  Not good food and way expensive, I don't know if they've changed hands, but never again

Definitely a college-level sports bar, with TVs hung everywhere, a little karaoke station for the adventurous on some days (most days spotting a DJ there or a jukebox spitting out tunes), and drinks. Nothing special about the beer selection or bar, here.

The food was actually pretty good. In the booths, you sit down and face a TV pretty much no matter which direction you're facing. The fries and onion rings are delicious, but the burgers, chicken, and full meals like the eggplant parm special were surprisingly not too bad, just not the place I'd normally get each... plenty of bar food selections, basically, the appetizers and snacks are the better part of Cav's.

Wandering around East Passayunk we found ourselves in Chhaya Cafe after a quick search on Yelp! We got seated by the glass windows looking out to the street and ordered their seasonal special drinks - Ash and Elixir Iced Tea. the coffee was Vietnamese style poured over ice and was delicious. For food we ordered the scrambled egg and the special veggie Chilli waffle. 
The scramble was really good and came with delicious home fries but the waffle was meh and the topping tasted like canned food. It was disappointing as it was a special and more expensive than other brunch items on the menu. The special drinks were $4.5 each but not called out on the menu. I think it's a good place for brunch if you order the right things.
Quality problems seem to have been resolved. Pizza was very good while salads are excellent. They're now running some attractive lunch specials.

I just visited this clinic yesterday on a whim. I am a first time kitten owner and have never taken a pet to the vet so I wasn't sure where to begin. The lady on the phone was kind and helpful and even was able to take my kitty by appt the same day. Within 2hrs I was in their waiting room. Relatively small for what I was expecting. I was attended not long after. Rebecca took my girls temp and did her bloodwork and vaccines in such a sort time. She was so kind and my kitty seemed to really like her. The doctor only spent maybe 10mins max w my girl and really didn't engage with us so that was kind of a bummer. Nonetheless Rebecca really made our experience worthwhile. My only really complaint was how much I spent. I left there spending over $300 but I guess that's normal for a first time visit? I think in order for this to be 4 stars, I would need more attention from the doctor
AWESOME little hidden cafe!! The food is fantastic and I love the homey, local feel to this cafe.  Next time I go to Philly I will be back at Chhaya for sure!

Always a great place to grab a sandwich! I came for breakfast and got an egg and cheese sandwich on their Cuban bread.  Be sure to try their cafe con Leche and ask them to extra press the sandwhich :-)

We have brought our 12yr. old Lab, Ed,to the Girard clinic for the past 4 years.. Ed has had oral surgery, lumps removed and the usual health check ups. Each time the staff has accommodated our schedules,the Dr.'s have been excellent and all have shown genuine love for our boy! As a side note in the past 12 yrs. We have used other vets prior to moving to the city,none can compare. We have since moved out of the city but continue to drive back for the great care.

The first thing I said when I walked in the door of Chhaya Cafe was "OMG, this place is so cute!" Ok, actually I think the first thing I said was "Hang on, lovely hostess, I'm sorry for being rude but I need to finish this episode of Serial," but the "cute" comment was a close second. 

I met a friend here after Googling breakfast places near Passyunk and was so pleasantly surprised. First of all, it was a Sunday morning at prime brunch time and I was seated immediately, so that was great. Chhaya has a standard brunch menu that's, well, standard fare like waffles, breakfast sandwiches, granola, oatmeal, and then a Specials menu with more inventive offerings. On the Very Cool front, they have a really extensive coffee menu - you can choose whether you want a pour over, French press or siphon brew, and with which variety of bean sounds good, so whether you're a wannabe coffee snob, or an actual coffee snob, you'll feel right at home here. 

The food was delish. I was in my Thanksgiving detox mode, so I had an egg white sandwich with tomato, avocado and cheddar on multigrain bread, and my friend, who was in another kind of detox mode, had a bagel sandwich. Both were so fresh and tasty - my only hang up was that sides are separate, so if you like bacon or hash browns with your breakfast, it's a bit extra cash money. Getting my sandwich with egg whites was also an up-charge, but that's more standard. (Side note - they offer vegan chorizo as a side, which, although I didn't get, is always a great bonus in my book. Veggies want breakfast meat too! I mean...you know what I mean.) And really, the sandwich was something like $6.00, so who's really complaining.

I also loved that we were able to hang out and drink our coffee long after we were done eating. Even on a Sunday morning, there was no pressure to give up our table, which I always appreciate - plus, it gave me more time to feel like one of those wannabe coffee snobs I mentioned. Chhaya, I will be back, and probably not when I'm trying to eat healthy because girl, your veggie chili and cornbread waffle thing looks fabulous!
Loved everything!  My friends got some awesome out of the world coffee that they raved about.  I highly recommend their waffles!

Eat  there today. Some of the best crust and pizza I have had and I was raised on the East Coast. The comment below that this "run of the mill" is
complete nonsense. Maybe one of the best if not the best pizza in Tucson.And let me add that the staff is the best.
I stopped to pump the gas and grab a sandwich but lost all appetite because of excessive amount of homeless people hanging out and eating around, grooosssss

Review as a WEDDING VENUE:

I attended a brunch wedding here a few weeks ago and it was beautiful! 

CEREMONY
-The ceremony was by the water, with chairs facing the water set out on the grass and an "aisle" rolled out across the gravel. 
- Flowers in mason jars were tied to chairs on the end of the aisle, sunscreen, tissues and sunglasses were available (and necessary). The whole thing was very pinteresty and adorable.
-Sound carried well from the mics and music from the speakers. 
- Awkward factor: runners running/walking/doing that weird jogging in place thing they do at stop lights as the bride is walking down the aisle...

RECEPTION
-There were some tall tables and chairs set out outside during the cocktail hour and cornhole and giant jenga for people to play.
-The area inside comfortably fit 50 or so guests and allowed for a dance floor.
- Bar service during cocktail hour (ok it was kinda weird to order wine at 11am) and throughout the afternoon was hit or miss as far as wait, but always friendly.
-The room was decorated beautifully with some large paper lanterns, strung up lights, and other DIY pinteresty things. 
-Food was a brunch buffet and was good, but nothing to write home about. There were muffin baskets on the tables, fruit bowls brought out as appetizers and breakfast burritos, home fries, bacon, pancakes, and steak and eggs at the buffet.

WARNINGS: 
-It was hot. Like not-cute-sweaty-photos-hot. The area was covered with air flowing through, but the air was warm. (This was late June). 
-There is no cell reception. Your live instagramming of your friend's wedding will have to wait. Ubering home may be difficult.
-There will be other people brunching, running, walking by.

COST:
I'm pretty sure the happy couple paid for this themselves and did a lot of DIY so I'm guessing it was very affordable. That being said it was still a great time and a beautiful venue.

RECAP: Lovely lovely spot for a half indoor half outdoor brunch wedding!

I am very very fidgety.  To qualm my fidgeting tendencies, I needlepoint.  I have been to needlepoint shops around the country (as a native Texan, grew up going to the French Knot in Ft. Worth and then a different shop in STL during college.)  With considerable exposure to needlepoint shops, I must say that I was floored by the fantastic selection of designs and canvasses.  If they don't have what you are looking for, you can also commission something to suit you!


They also offer beginner classes and are very helpful with all of your selections from start to finish.  Speaking of selections, I have never seen such a multitude of colors!!! 

Whether or not you are needlepointer or not, drop in and check out this marvelous gem on Chestnut!

Dr. Balzer is great. She is friendly, energetic, and gets the job done quickly (without making you feel run over).  She doesn't have  the most gentle bedside manner, but she definitely cares. What I like best is that she has stayed in the neighborhood for so long and offers more affordable care than anywhere in Philly.  She works long, hard hours and isn't just looking to make a buck. That shows heart. 

However, I haven't had good experiences with the other doctors and Dr. Balzer herself misdiagnosed my pooch a few months ago. Since the misdiagnosis, I've been going to a different vet--world of animals: so far, so good, but I don't have too much to say about it yet.

In the end, I recommend Girard for basic healthcare (shots, blood work, maybe dental), but would go somewhere else if looking for a diagnosis or more serious surgery.

If I could, I would give Girard a 3.5--that seems more fair than a 3, but a 4 might misguide people.

This place is really awesome, our favorite breakfast/brunch in the area. It's kind of small, BUT because of that they're expanding... And because of THAT, they're currently CLOSED UNTIL 8/21/2014 when they'll open a much bigger place right next to the old one. 

When they reopen, get the sausage gravy and Nutella strawberry waffles with a scone on the side. They're all great.

Excellent! Had grown nervous after so many negative reviews but our experience couldn't have been better. Party of 14 on a Saturday night, service was excellent, everyone seemed happy with their food especially me and the wife. I had the arugula salad and catfish and would have both again. Good selection of craft beers and specialty cocktails. We will be back.

This was my first experience on Passyunk and I'm grateful this was my first stop. The staff are friendly, the place is convenient and clean, the atmosphere is comforting and the food is delicious. I had their Blue Lady tea which is now one of my favorites and now will forever crave their home fries. There is something on their menu for everybody and the prices are reasonable.

Only food truck I eat from in Philly. Their food is the best, fresh, and clean. I've never had such amazing food and service. So many different options in foods as well. So when I'm feeling indecisive I can choose a healthy option or some fried wings if I want. They always have a large crowd and we always order more for later (dinner). Lol what can I say we can't get enough.

So update to my last review which was five stars.  Dr. Weiner is no longer with the practice (only part time) had a new vet and our experience was less than stellar.  We waited 45 minutes until we were seen (fine - it happens) The doctor that we had (woman with short hair) did not introduce herself to us (fine).  She then asked me what type of food I feed my pets so I mentioned I could look up the name on Amazon where I purchase.  She said she would prefer that I didn't use my phone (thought that this was strange).  Then we spoke about the pets for a bit.  She gave the pets shots and told me that she was now going to update the information in the computer while we were sitting there (ok).  So when she went to do that I went to check and respond to a text message I received inquiring where I was since we were not expecting to wait 45 minutes before being seen.  She then saw me on my phone while she was updating the records in the computer and told me and my husband that she was going to leave the room and come back when I was done using my phone.  What? I told her that she was updating the records with her back to me so I did not think that I was doing anything wrong.  She then said that she likes to have conversations with clients which are hard to do with cell phones present.  I felt like I was being scolded like a ten year old child while we were being charged $90 for two exams that took less than ten minutes each.  The reason why I am giving two stars is based on the always kind and always friendly women who work the front desk and our past experiences with Dr. Weiner.

In the past, I loved taking my 2 cats here. The vet and vet assistants were kind and would explain everything to me (a new cat owner at the time). Recently, however, I haven't been able to get through the front door. My cat was sick with a very mild eye infection last week (which he has had in the past) and when trying to make an appointment, the receptionist told me that they are closing in an hour and to go to the ER. When I asked to make an appointment again, she told me to wait at the door at 730 am because there's a line during walk in hours. Again, I just wanted to make an appointment! I knew my cat just had a little cold and was going to be ok if I waited an extra day or two for more eye drops!

I took my services elsewhere (the cat doctor) but will miss the vet and vet assistants there. I will also miss the 2 other other receptionists I have dealt with in the past who were friendly.

Absolutely love this place and they have amazingggg sushi I don't like eating in there however because the same person who waits on u seems like the owner,cook,and front desk.. The service is like eating at a regular Chinese corner spot... But to go is awesome fast cheap for 2 orders of sushi and shrimp pad Thai came to 22$ plus don't  forget free soda or free crab Rangoon unless u order more money worth of food then u get more free stuff!! I order here once a week and I love it :)

I'm not a fan. This place is a one trick pony in my opinion...and the one trick isn't the best: Mangu, salami, fried cheese breakfast. My husband who's Dominican is very happy with the mangu breakfast combo but I wasn't impressed because I can do better and I've had better from non-Dominican cooks. 

If anyone knows Dominicans or Dominican food then you know that platano (plantains) is life. I got maduro and baked chicken (an abnormally big chicken thigh which leads me to believe it was pumped with GMO's) and the maduro tasted completely off. The chicken wasn't very good and flavorful enough for me to down the hormones. 

I also asked for a tostada con mantequilla (pressed Cuban bread with butter) and they didn't even press it right. I had to go home and put it in my toaster for a bit so it wasn't so soggy. 

I usually try Sancocho if it's available, but it just didn't look good. 

This place has been the home to a lot of different Dominican joints. We liked it best when it was Salsarengue as the shrimp ceviche and San cocho was decent. This new business needs a lot of work.

This pizza was so good it convinced me to leave a yelp review. I had one New York slice and one Bianca slice. They were both fantastic, plus it was happy hour so together it was $5. Luna is tied for the best pizza I've tried in Tucson. Serial grillers is the other but they're experimental and Luna is more classic style. Light, airy crust, well seasoned sauce, and an A1 cheese pull. I will definitely be back!
