Okay, I haven't done a review in a hot minute... but holy hell.   First bite and I nearly died.   Best. Pizza. In. Southern Arizona.  Hands down.  Sauce is on point, in house sausage is to die for. And the crust.... good lawd!    Yes yes and more yes!

You know those aspects of your life that you keep around because they're JUST good enough? Maybe it's that streaming service that you pay for every month with the annoying buffering and obscene amount of commercials, just because it's the only place that has your favorite series. Maybe it's that POS car that you're been driving for ten years that is more reliable than your mom's anxious phone calls, but is one mechanical problem away from being sold for scraps. Or maybe it's that significant other who you've been drifting apart from, who is starting to annoy the crap out of you, and is one smart-ass comment away from ending up in the pile of lovers past. 

Well, Valley Green Inn is the complete embodiment of all of those things in your life that you like just BARELY enough not to kick it to the curb. It is just charming enough that you'll overlook the $18 fried cauliflower, absurdly priced glasses of wine, and the too-good-for-you atmosphere. The food is overpriced and underwhelming, and the only reason that they can charge what they do is because they have no competition. 

I have frequented this establishment for years, willing to overlook this fact, just because it's convenient and charming. Today, I had horrible service, and that was all that I needed to kick this restaurant off of my "good enough" list for good. Never. Going. Back.

Gluten free pizza with figs, pancetta, Humboldt farm goat cheese, garlic, Fior do Latte (house made fresh mozzarella) & olive oil... otherwise it is called their "fig, pig, and goat" pizza was absolutely delicious! All of this on a cauliflower crust so it would be gluten-free. I loved the figs and the balsamic reduction on it too! Surprisingly I also loved their iced tea because it tasted like iced tea! Good service once you order at the counter. All delivered to you in a reasonable amount of time to make a pizza. The gluten-free size is a personal size and yes. I ate it all! Yum!

Wow!  Pizza crust is crispy and chewy, the red sauce is perfectly seasoned, the white is packed full of flavor, fresh ingredients, great house made sausage, the wait staff is friendly and knowledgeable about the products.  The atmosphere is upbeat, relaxed, and sophisticated.  We will be returning to try all the pizzas!

Hands down best  in Tucson! I had 4 or 5 mouth orgasms eating the pesto and lamb sausage pizza. I got 3 x 10" pizzas and 2 bottles of coke for $40. For this level of quality, that's a reasonable amount. Heading this weekend for a second round of pizza!

I was initially kicked out of this place because I have a service dog. Then, after informing them of the law, the "host" threw a huge amount of attitude because he just didn't want us there. I wasn't going to give them my money after all that!

Three of us went to Pizza Luna this afternoon around 4:30 pm. We were greeted by a super friendly guy named Travis who explained the menu and told us that on Tuesday, and bottle of wine is 1/2 off. So we got a really great bottle of Pinot Noir from Oregon and then ordered our pizza. We got Sausage Rosso and plain cheese - both traditional, and a simple green salad with tomatoes added. James made the pizza - the crust is perfection.  Everything was delicious. Kyle was working behind the counter also - three friendly guys who seemed to like their jobs and their boss Caleb. We were so eager to dig into the pizza and salad that I forgot to take any photos until we were finished, so I took photos of the place. Notice how exceptionally shiny clean it is!  Thanks guys - now we have a new, great pizza place :)

This review is mostly for the cheese board, atmosphere, price, and awesome service! I wasn't crazy about the pizza but the cheese board was soo amazing. One of the best I've had in Tucson! Super low key and relaxed atmosphere which I loved.

The pizza here is delicious. We got the pizza Bianca and sausage rossa. Both are great. The sausage on the rossa pizza has really good zest to it along with a great red sauce. The Bianca pizza has chunks yummy ricotta cheese. We liked it better than scordattos and serial grillers pizza. I have also had the Cesar salad which was really good too. It's our new favorite pizza place.

Foods alright but godawful seriously horrible service. Like seriously guys? Is it that beneath you to serve me coffee...? After all a job is a job...and everyone has to make their hustle we're all struggling out here, but a smile won't kill you... the entitled atmosphere behind this place ruins everything. But it's east passyunk Plenty of other great places. Skip this place and walk over to Plenty Cafe or B2!!

Small place, crowded for lunch but very quick lines. Cash only. Falafel and middle eastern pita sandwiches. I personally love the sabich sandwich with is eggplant, hummus and salad. They have great fries and a few pickled items on the side which are served buffet style. This place is definitely worth the try!

Valley Green Inn is a classic and historic landmark in the Chestnut Hill section of Philadelphia.  I've been going there when I've been in Philly since I was a little kid so in some ways it feels like home.  The setting is ideal ... deep in the Vale of the Wissahickon looking out on the rustic Wissahickon Creek. The dining rooms are furnished in old Philadelphia style.  There is a scenic porch in front, a great event space on the south side, and an ice cream and light snack stand on the north side.  If you arrive by horse there is a sheltered hitching post for your four-legged friends. Last night I was there for one of their summer beer tastings. (Sly Fox Brewery).  On a perfect summer evening, Valley Green Inn was a perfect host for this event.

Dr. Wilkerson and his staff are amazing! I've now taken 2 dogs to them. First was my Lab, and now my newfiedoodle. They have always taken amazing care of my puppers! Dr. W treats them like they're his own. Telling me what he would do, if the dog was his! 
I was there recently for the neutering and gastroplexy (prevent bloat), of my 13 month old newfiedoodle. He's a giant breed dog. They treated Ollie amazingly! 
We highly recommend and now we actually travel from NY to use them! That's how much we love them and trust them!

WOW WOW WOW!! I want to complement on the food and the great service. I now know why they have so many 5 stars. Absolutely DELICIOUS!! Fresh hand cut ingredients, delicious cheeses, hand made dough, and they baked just like I asked... a little well done. Sausage, mozzarella, wild mushrooms and fresh basil.

valley green inn is blessed with a beautiful location but comes up a bit short on food and service.

my girlfriend and i decided to ride our bikes up the river to vgi for lunch this saturday.  and while the weather and the view from the porch were great, the lunch itself turned out to be merely mediocre.

we ordered a course of soup and some sandwiches.
the soup arrived in a timely manner, but my choice, the du-jour lentil soup, garnished with prosciutto and asiago, had a poor texture (gritty) and tasted heavily of bacon.  what does it take to pass a soup through a chinois? our other soup was the everyday french onion which seemed to be topped, generously, with mozzarella cheese, but was otherwise good.

if we were a bit underwhelmed by the soup, the sandwiches didn't improve on things.  the individual elements of my girlfriend's grilled salmon club were fresh and tasty, but the sandwich was overloaded with, in her words, "blah bread."  minus one slice of the chiabata, it was actually very nice, but as served, no. 

i really wanted to like the catfish po boy. it had a nice coleslaw topping and looked good on my plate. but again, the bread overwhelmed the fillings and to add to its troubled existence, the catfish itself was, well, a bit fishy and bland. i wasn't that impressed with their side of iceberg, red cabbage, and carrot salad. this is the kind of salad you get from a bag at the supermarket

finally there were the yam fries. while they are tasty, the preparation and presentation on this offering is problematic. the fries are of a shoestring cut and served in a big bird's nest, which makes them almost impossible to pick up or eat without making a mess. and why they served them with ketchup is beyond either of us.

we weren't up for dessert when our server returned.

the service itself was good, but not very hospitable. plates were bused in a timely manner, but in a perfunctory fashion, and glasses were refilled with water, but not iced tea (nor was iced tea even offered again). a woman behind us complained about an undercooked piece of food to her server, who dismissively agreed to get the manager for her.  the manager was civil, and certainly didn't contradict her in any way, but was not exceptionally gracious in hearing her complaint either.

go if you're stuck in the park on a nice day. otherwise, skip it, or just go to the ice cream stand on the side of the building.

This place is ok my sis and I went here for the very first time we stood and waited for about 10 mins before any came over to seat us, we were the only two in the line Anyway once we got seated, in the front section where we sat lights was off and we had to repeatedly ask them to turn the lights on ugh. After we finally got settled n placed our order the evening started going a lil better the waitress was very nice but the service was slow. The crowd was mellow, there's a lot of tvs to watch sport, entertainment ect. the wine tasty and The food was really good, but...I Won't be returning anytime soon.

Ok... I was sceptical.  The only reviews were 6 five star reviews.

I was around the corner and gave it a test taste.

Ordered a 16" white sauce meat pizza.

I am NOT even close to upset!

The crust is awesome. Nice bite, crispy yet not stiff, and flavorful. The whole bite is amazing!

If the rest of the servings they have to offer are as good as the random white sauce meat with mushroom pie I had, then they are totally worth all five stars from others. They absolutely get 5 from me!

Food ROCKED!

Service ROCKED!

Experience ROCKED!

As of now, there are 7 five star reviews.

It's an instant pizza party! Not the best pizza ever, but not as bad as i thought. We normally get a medium thick crust and they accommodate any number of pre-schooler driven topping requests.  Best thing about the menu? A beer selection on tap, which makes collecting endless strips of tickets a bit more tolerable.  Wings and family size salads flush the offerings out enough to make it enjoyable for everyone in the family. 

But the food isn't why you come here.  It's the atmosphere of being at a party. Even if it isn't your party (which we never have had a big party of our own here), the kids think they are at a party. It makes it a great way to have a small birthday seem a bit more special, or to do for some other special celebration. 

This location on Broadway is HUGE, though. And if you are going to leave your table to play games, make sure to leave signs that you are coming back, as unattended tables can either be bussed or possibly pilfered. I foolishly left my sunglasses on our table on one visit and they were missing when we returned.  I told the manager and he offered a free pizza coupon, so props to management for smoothing over a case of customer blindness.  

and they have beer.

We have a serious Pizza Luna problem, we end up ordering it almost every week- there is not another pizza joint as good in Tucson, in my opinion, unless maybe you count Anello downtown, which has a different style. I like it because it's delicious, obviously, but also very fresh tasting and the ingredients are high quality. It's not pretentious at all, but nice inside, and it's priced very well for the size and quality!

Walked into smell of "burnt toast". Very friendly counter person. No chicken topping available :( but they do have LAMB topping choice. 
First bite was good then i trued to pick up my slice of pizza and it fell apart from sogginess. 
Oh well not a big lose since their prices are very reasonable. I'd come back n give 2nd chance if i happened to be in this stripmall again but definately wldNOT make special trip here.

Do not be fooled by the location in a strip mall.  What it lacks in square footage, it makes up for in taste and service.  There was a line to the door and we were apologized to for the really minimal wait. A+ for manners.  We could see the cooks tossing the dough, putting them together, throwing it the oven.  We got our pizza fast.  And when I say this pizza is good, I mean fantastic.  We had a Blanca with artichokes and mushrooms, topped with arugula.  I still have left overs and I'm excited about that.  The guys asked if we enjoyed it, if we need anything, they were appropriately attentive.  They also do Grubhub, DoorDash, and uber eats. Definitely recommended. Go!
Good food, great crust, great variety of toppings. The toppings were plentiful and tasty.  The crust was flavorful and the staff made sure each half pizza had the requested toppings.
This place has good prices, friendly people and convenient service. I would recommend this place to anyone who needs extra storage, a mail box or moving materials

The chips are really crunchy and taste great. The salsa is light and fresh and the chicken nachos are some of the best I've ever had!! Definitely worth a visit!!!

The interior is ok, but the food is worth it.

I just moved from California, and literally driving the U-Haul down starting coughing. Friday, I had the chills, body aches, congested and a really sore throat. I thought it was the flu and went here Saturday night an hour and a half before they closed. They took me in, the intaking nurse was really nice as was the nurse who took my temp (102.7) and other vitals. She immediately noticed I had trouble swallowing and took a strep test. 
After that things kind of went downhill. 
A nurse practitioner came in sort of checked me out and said it couldn't be the flu because it wasn't the season. She noticed my left ear was slightly irritated and had the doctor come in to tell me I couldn't have the flu and that I needed to get a nasal spray to help clear out fluid. He also drew a picture to help explain. Alright, I can live with all that but it took 2 hours to tell me that. In the end, essentially I was told to take some aspirin, nose spray and gargle with salt water. If it doesn't clear up in a few days go back.
My throat continued to hurt and my cough got worse. 2 days later, I finally got put on my husbands insurance and went to see my parent's doctor. Once there he took a look in my throat, felt my lymph nods (which the nurse practitioner didn't do) and said I had acute tonsillitis. And was a little annoyed that they didn't diagnose me sooner and weren't concerned about a 102 fever for 2 days. However, my ears looked great!
So, I don't know how well they do with treating and diagnosis but they know how to prevent ear infections?

This quaint, clean, and bright little pizza joint has easily become one of my favorites in Tucson! The menu is easy to navigate, the quality to value balance is excellent, and overall just great food! Both their red and white pizzas are something to talk about, but their red sauce has a lot going on in it. All of which is superb. Highly recommended!

Visited for brunch this morning and nothing was out of the ordinary, it was moderately crowded so I recommend being aware of a possible wait (you may be able to reserve but I may be wrong); the food selection was nothing big and everything was priced reasonably and cheaply (+plus!) and the service was on time, not any long wait. Lastly, the food was alright--I think chhaya is a better choice for their sweet foods (nutella & strawberry waffle) rather than what I ordered, the scramble (a bit bland, couldn't finish) I enjoyed my visit, but most likely wouldn't revisit if given the choice.

This place is fantastic and a local favorite. The food was delicious and my waitress was sweet and prompt. The decor in the other hand needs a major facelift, but with the view right by the water is stunning.

We actually ordered Pizza Luna for our wedding "dinner." We eloped, and it was just our family joining us. It was seriously delicious. They aren't stingy with toppings, and the crust is crunchy perfection!
Delicious pizza. Great customer service! They accommodated food allergy issues without any hesitation. Will be back!

I'm from Brooklyn and this is my newest favorite real Deal New York style Neapolitan pizza place ! The menu is extensive and I can't wait to get back and try something new. Restaurant was very clean and the staff very friendly. Go there! You'll love it!

If I could give this place a 0, I would. Ordered Crab Tempura, Chicken Noodle Soup, and Chicken Udon Noodles. I don't know how this place has 4 stars. 

4 small pieces of crab tempura - did not clean the crab, no meat, super bland.
Both of the soups were bland, bland, bland. They pretty much sold plain noodles in boiling water. Never again. This place should not be in business. 

The only good thing I can mention is that they were pretty quick to deliver. But it's probably because they don't even cook.

mmm waffles!

i like this cute little place that's sort of on the other end of east passyunk. waffles, coffee, intimate relaxing space with armchairs in the window area, wifi, waiter service, brunch, etc.

came here for brunch and we could sit wherever we wanted to. we had a couple servers (i think one was training) who were very attentive and kind. the food is here is really good but watch out, i thought the waffles would be a bit bigger for $8 a pop. the strawberry nutella one that i got was bangin' and my boyfriends chocolate chip one was great and came with whipped cream all over the top. i also saw the veggie chili waffle being brought to someone else's table and immediately regretted not getting that instead. it's like chili and egg and all this good stuff on the waffle. 

so basically if you don't mind spending $8 for a waffle, this place is a cute great treat.

Ordered delivery on Eat24 to satisfy a Chinese craving. Delivery was about 45 minutes and we ordered a wide variety- steamed pork dumplings, crab Rangoon, chicken and broccoli, chicken lo mein, shrimp and mixed vegetables, and hot/sour soup. Everything, aside from the crab Rangoon (very disappointing, very small and barley any filling) was incredible. Potentially the best Chinese I've had in the city and look forward to ordering again!

I attended a birthday party at your Tucson Broadway location today that began at 2:30.  The party hosts weren't aware that their time slot was from 2:30 to 4:15 and apparently your staff wasn't aware either.  I didn't arrive at the party until 3:30 and the pizza, hot wings and drinks for 2 tables full of people didn't start coming out until at least 10 or 15 minutes after I got there.  So I was shocked when the server handed one of the hosts a receipt and advised that they needed to settle the bill and vacate the tables so that they could prepare for another party.  I thought to myself, even if there was a misunderstanding about the time when the reservation was made by phone, there was still ample opportunity to get this party back on track.  Shouldn't the server have noticed that this party was over an hour into their time slot before food was served?  Didn't they notice the giant unopened cake box or the presents sprawled everywhere?  What about the fact that they took ice cream back to the freezer, but never brought it back out for the Happy Birthday celebration?  All of these were clues that the host either forgot about their time slot, they were never made aware of their time slot, or at the very least they were moving at a pace that meant they would go over their time slot.   Resolving this misunderstanding would have been as easy as pulling the host aside and saying, "Your food won't be out until about 30 minutes before your time slot ends.  Because we have 46 parties booked, we are unable to extend your time slot.  However, we can bring out your ice cream now, as I have found that cake and ice cream is a great way to gather the kids.  You can sing Happy Birthday and open presents, and by the time you are done the pizza and wings should be out.  You will have 30 minutes or so to eat before it's time to clear the tables.  And, for those guests that decide to stick around, they can look for any empty booth or table not reserved for partiers or I've found that after the party is a great time for kids and parents to enjoy the arcade area".  And just like that, everything is back on track.  Instead, the entire situation got completely out of control.  To make matters worse, Pat, the general manager escalated the situation by having a complete breakdown.  It was the worst display of management I have ever seen in my life.  He yelled, he screamed and he got aggressively confrontational with paying customers - and he did it in front of other customers.  What's really scary is not what happened, but what could have happened.  This group walked away.  They walked away with unused tokens, paid for undelivered food, to go boxes with food in them and they even left their ice cream.  The next group might not just walk away.  That situation could have turned volatile, putting employees, customers and countless children in grave danger.   De-escalating a situation is a basic management skill that Pat has no grasp of.  He either needs to be re-trained or terminated, because as long as he is the leader of the team at that location, you have a violent scene just waiting to happen.
La mejor comida Dominicana en Tampa y el servicio es excelente, las cervezas siempre frías y el Mangú  lo único que puedo decir es que es un orgasmo al paladar!!!

I really do not like writing bad reviews (everyone has a bad day, I get that) but sometimes they are just necessary. I went here in November, desperate for a hair fix before my wedding. I had previously been "over-blonded" by another salon and wanted to have my hair returned to a more natural state. I scheduled an appointment after explaining this. It was very clear that I was the last appointment of the day based on the treatment I received here. I was told by the colorist that there was "nothing she could really do" to fix my hair except give partial highlights on the regrowth. When I asked if I could just get lowlights and then a toner to take out the brassiness, I was told that my hair was too damaged to do this and I would need to come back in a month. None of this sounded right and I explained that coming back in a month would put me the week before my wedding...kind of late to fix a disaster. It didn't matter, I was told I had no other options.

Well, I had read tons of great reviews on here so I trusted her. Big mistake. I left with the tiniest bit of highlights on the roots only...the line of demarcation was so obvious and my hair was still yellow from the previous highlights.

I immediately went to another salon to get this fixed and they were perplexed as to what this stylist was talking about. Luckily, the new place gave me a bunch of lowlights and great highlights to make my hair more natural and used a toner to make my hair look healthy and shiny and completely got rid of the brassiness. I asked that stylist if my hair was particularly difficult and they assured me that it was not...it was a pretty basic fix of toning and adding lowlights. Will NEVER return to AMS salon again since this was supposedly one of their best people. So unprofessional...I could have spent $20 at a beauty school and had a better experience.
Unfortunately it seems to be slipping. A slice of pizza here recently was 4.50 and had clearly been sitting there for a while.

This pizza was really tasty!  We ordered a 16" 1/2 cheese 1/2 pepperoni, and a 16" 1/2 hot Italian sausage and onion and 1/2 meatball on napoleon.  Every single one was delicious.  The two pizzas were plenty for our family of 5, with leftovers for tomorrow.  The staff was extremely friendly, the place was clean and the atmosphere was lovely!  I highly recommend!

Had a great time!! They were able to accommodate our large group of 26 people (we did make a reservation). Wings were awesome with many options for sauce!! I tried 4 different kinds and they all were good! Nice, cozy, relaxed atmosphere. Within walking distance from our hotel (Homewood Suites Hilton), which was another bonus!! Staff was very nice and attentive. Would definitely go back!

I've ordered from here quite a few times, but have never eaten in, so this review is for delivery only.  Their delivery is quick, the food is always hot when it arrives, and they always get our order right.  

One of my favorite things on their menu is the chicken satay appetizer.  It's smoky,  tender, and almost sweet, and it usually serves as the main portion of my meal.  I've also enjoyed the cheesesteak roll, the sweet and sour chicken, and the crab rangoon.  There's still plenty of stuff left on the menu that I haven't tried... yet.

I agree with a previous reviewer about their dumplings being too thick skinned and flavorless.  I also had an issue with their chicken fried rice being flavorless and ho-hum.  Neither of these two issues is going to stop me from ordering from here again and again and again.

This is without a doubt the BEST pizza in Tucson! Made-to-order, fresh ingredients, and killer flavor! The staff is always really friendly and helpful with making suggestions. I've run into the owner a couple of times while dining and he made a point to check on every table and ask about our food/experience- one time he was in the middle of a wine tasting and offered for my husband and I to join in :) The prices are worth it- its quality food and a quality experience.

I've definitely experienced better.
Had a new patient visit and waited more than 60 minutes in the waiting room. Ended up with a parking ticket because of this. 
Also was charged $70 for dewormer, and I looked online and I can get the same medication from Chewy for $5.  SERIOUSLY?
My new patient visit for my dog was more than $250 with two vaccines. Absolutely ridiculous! I was told this place was affordable. It is NOT.

I have been to ChhayA a few times now, and while I love the atmosphere, especially when I'm trying to get work done, the food just isn't that great. The waffle and more Carby dishes are tasty, but the savory dishes are not good. I had the quiche a few days ago and it was dry, tasteless, and terrible. I have had their omelette before and that was pretty tasteless as well. The waffles and muffins are pretty good, and the coffee is some of the best I've ever had, which is why I have them 2 stars. I got an iced Americano and it was delicious, and strong just the way I like it!
If you are looking for a good cup of coffee and a hip atmosphere then this place is great. If you want a really good meal then perhaps go elsewhere.
Said they take care of rabbits, but I called and they don't. Please update your website.

Wow. Walk here if you need to. It's the best Neapolitan style pizza we've had in Tucson in a long time. The highlight is the CRUST!  Omg it was amazing. 
We ordered the Neapolitan Meatball Pizza, and we added Ricotta. The ricotta and meatballs were extraordinary.
I've been here twice and every time it's been excellent. The Caesar salad is amazing and the pizza is amazing as well I can't wait to come back and try other types

After bringing my cats here for over 20 yrs.Under the loving and total professional care of DR.Balzar I can only say now R.I.P. your through.You folks have practialy destroyed her years of dedicated hard work she so meticulously crafted.Your arrogance,greed.and most of all 'your lack of genuine love for these animals is apparent.I was planning to bring my cat in for her distemper shots'but after going on line to see if they had improved(following their progress for over year) its gotten worse.For those of you there who honestly do not deserve this criticism I do apologize.Remember the SPCA ,their dedicated,reasonalby priced.not as glam.for you glam.hounds but whats more important your pets or how comfortable you sit for a while.Your suppo .sed to be doctors professionals'well start looking the part' these people bringin their precious little ones to you for help,treat them with honesty and respece.Their not your weekend drinking buddies. Girard clinic Auf Wiederseheh und gute Befreiung.
Ended 2010 with a fabulous lunch here.  The snow looked beautiful in the woods and the food was great as usual.  Cabbage Borscht and salads.  Very nice atmosphere.  I recommend this place.

I ended up taking him as I needed his medicine and didn't want wait. I was 10 minutes late and they did not take me.   I truly hate this business and hope they go out of business.  Albert is an ignorant person!  He's horrible !  

My 18 year old  took him for nail trimming.  Wanted to fill the nexgat flea and tick for my dogs.  They wouldn't fill it because my 18 year old is behind 1 month for annual.  18 years old. The one doctor told me last year to let him just enjoy the rest of his life.  These fools want me to put him through shots to rack up money I guess!  Bye bye Girard  finding another vet!   

Btw took my English bulldog there three times in the last 3 months spent close to 1000 dollars and they did NOTHING for her.  She now goes to UPENN!    Frustrated as all hell!!!  To add to this. It took 5 phone calls to get her information faxed!

I recently bought a few new shirts from Indochino. I have bought shirts from them in the past, and my measurements were set exactly how I liked them. Since it had been a while since my last purchase, I had to go in and get measured. No problem. The staff was friendly and courteous. However, after I ordered and received my shirts, they never really fit quite right. I had them re-done, and they still have a tight fit despite explaining the problem to them in detail. Evidently, they switched over to a new manufacturer. Customer service is friendly, but they should have stuck with the original manufacturer. It's supposed to be a custom fit... They were helpful, but I likely won't be ordering from them in the future.

I have tried a couple salons in Philly over the years and I've finally found one I love! Gail is so sweet and I really love how she colors and styles my hair. I had a few hair cuts prior to getting color and each time it turns out exactly how I envisioned.

We met the owner at a local resort while we were in town for a few days. We really enjoyed getting to know him & learning about his restaurants. We decided to check out Pizza Luna with our teenage son who is a die hard pizza lover, but a very picky one. I have to say all of us were very impressed with this little pizza shop. We have had great pizza all over the world & Pizza Luna held its own. The crust was light & crispy, the marinara sauce was very flavorful, the cheese was deliciously gooey, and the toppings were very generous. We also had the garlic knots & Little Gems salad - both were very good. The salad looked & tasted like something that would come from a higher end type of restaurant, not a pizza joint in a strip mall. Very impressive. We were pleasantly surprised with this elevated pizzeria. The staff was also great! 
If you haven't been here yet, I highly recommend you give it a try.

Terrible, terrible, looking for a not
Overpriced Chinese food, near the airport. Fried Rice was greasy, undercooked and tasted literally like dirt. Shrimp roll was greasy and seemed to be reheated. Would not recommend.

I brought my lovely lady friend here for her birthday dinner this past Thursday. I found this place after a Yelp search for "romantic dinner," having never heard of it even once before. My lady had, though, and started freaking out as we approached the parking lot. As it happens, this was the same parking lot where, throughout her high school days, she and all her friends would park their cars before dragging a keg into the woods across the creek, into the woods and drinking next to a bonfire, like every single weekend. Small world.

So we're the only two people in the restaurant, at 7 pm on a Thursday. We were sitting in a remodeled living room, with a fireplace nearby and no music playing, which was weird at first but we got used to it. Besides for us, our server and a chef who eventually made her way out to the floor, there was nobody else there for at least a half hour, when a single person came in for dinner and made the atmosphere a little weirder for us.

But whatever, I can get over that if the meal is worth it. And for the most part, it was - it was our mistake ordering mussels so far out of season. Otherwise, they had these good BBQ pulled pork dumplings as another appetizer, and a handful of others on the menu which sounded very nice as well. Our entrees were both awesome, my mid-rare filet was just perfect, and my lady loved her duck two ways. She learned that she's a big fan of duck confit. And when our server got hung up with a party in a room on the other side of the restaurant, the chef came out and gave us a free dessert, this delicious thing that i can barely even begin to describe - like chocolate cake with something like gelato inside. Really effing good.

Definitely fits the bill for a romantic dinner, with great service and an elegant setting. Just be prepared for a very unique experience, mostly for better.

I went to this salon after purchasing a groupon and had a similar experience to Randi M. I decided to get a haircut after reading good reviews but was VERY disappointed. I was at the salon for less than an hour for a haircut and keratin treatment. Last time I had a Keratin and haircut it took 3-4 hours total, and I received extensive instructions on how to care for my hair. She rushed the treatment, and when she went to cut my hair, she spent 5 minutes. She basically cut my longest layer straight across in the back and then told me my haircut before was a bad haircut and that I best just let it grow out with no suggestion on how to fix it (all I wanted was for my hair to look better than when I walked in!). She was rude, insulting, and even laughed as she said, "and what exactly were you going for with these bangs." She then proceeded to charge me for the haircut after basically telling me she couldn't help fix the bad haircut. I had high expectations for this place and am very disappointed. I was looking for a new salon in the area and will go back to the drawing board. I ended up tipping for the groupon service but am wishing I hadn't. My message to AMS: if you don't want groupon customers, don't sign up for the service! It is a great way to gain new customers, so I suggest you treat us with a little respect if you want us to return.

My softball team is sponsored by Cavs West and we love it!  They have great specials almost every night of the week, but we go there on Thursdays.  They have now added karaoke to Thursday nights, and it is a blast!  Be sure to order wings and pizza, the "honey hot" wings are purrrrrfect!  Karaoke starts at 9pm, draws a really interesting crowd, from penn students to west philly residents to the glee club.  Cavs is also a great place to watch sports, they have tons of tv's on both levels of the restaurant and bar!
This is a small cafe. Good for working and maybe even some girls talk. My food was tasty. I would go back if I'm in the area

I would say this is the best pizza in town! The crust and the flavors are absolutely amazing. If you've been to Italy then you know this is the real deal! Prices are ok for that kind of quality but I wish the prices for wine would be more reasonable. Also, they close at 8 pm which is a bit early and seating is also very limited.

We were in Tampa and wanted a dinner delivered to our hotel.  The desk person recommended Pizza Famiglia.  Although the only review on Yelp was so so,  we tried it anyway. It was terrific.  Food was delivered to our door,  on time as promised  and was very tasty, fresh and hot.  And a lot too . The calzone was hugh  4 people could eat it and not be hungry.   So glad we tried it.

I made an appt for four cats. It was an hours appt. I missed it accidentally, thinking it was the next day. They didn't call me until 4:30 and said they were charging me full price for the missed appointment and would not work with me, saying I cost them an hours billing, and it was policy. 

YET saying they were so busy they could not call me to ask where I was at any point during my HOURS appt and saying that if I HAD CALLED EVEN FIVE MINUTES BEFORE the appointment I would NOT have been charged.  I've spent plenty of my money there and was totally apologetic and horrified I missed this appt. I called back and explained this would really hurt me, and could we work something out...and the receptionist kept stating "the policy for no show is full cost vs. FIVE Minutes notice call from me=no charge.  I was getting me REALLY upset at this splitting of hairs. She didn't care and was very cold.

I realize I made a mistake, and anyone could tell it was an honest one - I didn't blow them off on purpose.  I would have been there in fifteen minutes, and we all would have been happy. 

This especially irks me because previously, I've gone a couple times in the mornings and spent HOURS of my time, and stressing my animals in their waiting room hoping they would have time for me , only to continuously run out of my available time and/or carshare rental time or cabs to get there since I have no car. 

Like I told them, they are losing my business and I don't want to see that teeny tiny always crowded waiting room ever again. If being an inexpensive vet means this, I'll go somewhere else.

I was at Chhaya this weekend and sampled a number of the dishes and beverages.  I'm not a coffee geek but I think I learned enough over the weekend in conversation with the staff and the people who have seemed to already become regulars to hold my own in conversation.  Chhaya offers a variety of beans and brew styles, from the rare-for-Philadelphia (siphoned coffee - you have to go see it to know) to ones I have never heard of but that were wonderful surprises (South Indian decoction coffee).  I agree with the previous poster - I definitely felt a bit "hopped up" after about two cups of the standard brew, which is my norm.  High caffeine, strong flavor, very smooth if you get the siphoned brew.  The South Indian decoction is sweetened slightly but so well blended that it's less a sweetened coffee and more a flavor of its own.  Highly recommend that for anyone who likes flavored coffee.  Which brings me to one warning: the chef likes to make her own, well, everything, down to the chocolate sauce used on the dessert waffles.  There are no flavor shots from bottled syrups so if that's your thing you might consider the decoction.

The coffee is all good but most important to me, as I am a food-lover, is the menu.  The small plates are indeed small but pack powerful flavor and do much for an adventurous palate, even if they, individually, fall short of satiating a rumbling belly.  The first night I started by sampling the Hungarian peppers (roasted, stuffed with feta and served with prosciutto).  They were spicy enough to give you a kick when you first bite, but your tongue is then cooled by the creamy feta inside.  A perfect way to stimulate an appetite.  At the suggestion of a staff member I next tried the eggplant relish, which was a surprise.  It was served cold, somewhat on the sweet side and spiced with something I couldn't put my finger on but we deducted might be an Indian spice.  The flavors were complex and unusual, not your average baba ganoush or the Trader Joes version of eggplant spread (not that I'm knocking either of those).  The peppers and eggplant plates were enough to satisfy me, but if I was especially hungry I might have ordered a third - probably the bacon wrapped cheese.  I'm sure it's a specific cheese meant to be paired with bacon in a specifically delicious way, but I'm not sure that matters to me.  Because it's bacon wrapped cheese.  What more do I need to know.

The next morning I tried the eggs benedict waffle.  This, I think, is so far my favorite.  Chhaya has a sweet and a savory batter for the waffles and the eggs benedict is served on a sweet waffle.  The waffle itself is, as a previous poster said, fluffy and right on its own but served with ham the benedict waffle has a wonderful salty-sweet flavor, which is only enhanced by the hollandaise's buttery touch. This is in my eyes a perfect brunch dish.  The following morning I had the chili waffle, which is served on a savory waffle and topped with a poached egg.  The chili is full of flavor, slightly spicy and sports a variety of beans and just enough beef and tomatoes to make it hearty without weighing the waffle down.  The poached egg balances the dish and makes it proper for brunch.  My guess is this one will be a favorite in the fall for the discerning sports fan.

I also enjoyed the muffins and scones and, as the previous poster indicated, they are moist and treat-filled.  Great for a grab-and-go.  If you are lucky enough to be there when they are just from the oven the warm berries of the blueberry muffins are outstanding.

Chhaya is new and so of course the menu is going grow organically.  V, the proprietor and chef, has said that it will be changing every week.  As it stands now I think Facebook is the best way to keep an eye on the menu, and I will be going back to sample more as they grow and try new things.  It's possible, though, that I'm already addicted to the eggs benedict waffle.  

I think I just made myself hungry.

As soon as I walked in, it felt like home. (I'm Dominican.) The bachata music was the perfect touch. 

I went on a Saturday afternoon after a hangover so I was in need of some good food! 

They had a variety of things out to choose from. But we ended up ordering sancocho with rice and Mangu, salami and queso frito. 

The man who was there was so friendly and pleasant. He  literally did everything! He greeted us when we walked in, he served the food, he cooked the food, he cleaned the tables, he got our drinks and was the cashier as well! I was quite impressed on how he held it down all by himself! 

The food was great, and they gave a good amount for the price. I will definitely be back whenever I'm in town again.

Order here if you want to wait 50 minutes only to find out that your food has not even started to cook. Asked to cancel my order and employees did not now how to refund online order. Had to call the customer service line and they said the store should have did it so who knows if I will be refunded. Will never return again.

I am a crust girl. Thin in the middle, crispy yet thick and tender on the edges. Extra points for wood fired. All boxes ticked at Cafe Luna. I had the Fig and Goat, my husband had pepperoni. His had a nice, bright, slightly spicy sauce, and loads of pepperoni. But mine - mine.  Mine was sweet and salty (prosciutto!!) with creamy goat cheese and that amazing chewy crust. Sweet place, too. In a strip mall but cute. You walk in and they greet you warmly and everyone is happy and cheerful. Def will go back!!

The food here was tasty - I had some decent crab cakes and a gazpacho soup that wasn't bad. My main gripe here is the pricing. Far too expensive for the portion sizes and quality. The staff at the restaurant were very friendly but seemed unprepared for us to come in with a reservation we had made days in advance, seating walk-ins well before us while we waited 15-20 mins.

Delicious pizza, friendly staff, loved the small but appealing menu of pizzas, salads and wine. ALSO - their slice and a salad lunch special - yesssssss!! What a great addition to this part of town, real true neo-Neopolitan pizza. Sorely needed.

My sister and I brought my father here for a birthday dinner. Love the location. We grew up coming to Valley Green all the time to feed the ducks and walk the drive. 

It was a Monday night. Small crowd. Four tables at one point. Cozy. The service was great and the food delicious. Sean, our server, was personable and attentive. So was the host. We got the Catfish Etoufee. Delicious. Apparently that's their most popular dish for dinner. My sister had a grilled chicken sandwich which looked great. Served on thick toasted bread. We had the crab cakes for appetizer. We each had one crab cake. Dessert was cheesecake and a tiramisu, which was served as a slice of cake. My fathers had a candle, and we didn't need to ask. Just mentioned why we were there. 

Great quiet location, at least on a rainy Monday night. Prices felt fair for a nice place. I left full and plan on coming back some day.

Really chill, Southern diner/sports bar kind of vibes. Big plus is that they're open late at night, but their food is pretty over priced for what you get. The one thing that my friends and I come to Cavanaugh's for though are the FRIES. Their three cheese fries are honestly so great, comforting, and sometimes are just what you need. PRO TIP: ask for a cup of gravy on the side with the three cheese fries. Dip the fries into the gravy and you've got yourself a winner. This is what we come to Cavanaugh's for: three cheese fries + gravy + good vibes and late night conversations

Had pizza For the first time from this place and it comes the closest to real Neapolitan pizza and puts the other places here in Tucson to shame. I've lived all over Europe and have craved real pizza so much. Thank you

Great pizza. Crispy but fluffy crust, good sauce, great pepperoni (lots of them). You can get slices from 11-5 for around 4 bucks, beer and wine, some kind of happy hour from 2-5. My wife and I will definitely be coming back.

The worst management company ever!!! We have had countless issues in our community particularly with the landscaping. Brian Howell is our property manager. The problem is, he doesn't MANAGE!!! Our property has declined in 2 years UNDER Meritus Association. Brian Howell makes up one excuse after another for why things are the way they are. One star is way too many for this company. Don't waste your time or money with them.

Cauliflower crust was spot on. I honestly couldn't tell the difference from the regular crust. The pizza was superb.... and when combined with the Toole IPA on tap..... delish! Oh...and not to mention the staff was so courteous and the place is super cute. Will be back... often.

I had to report this as apparently, its been removed.... 

I just came here this morning for my mini poodle's rabies vaccine. I told the receptionist at the first desk what I was here for and then was taken to the back to have what I thought was the vaccine... Nope, they preformed an annual exam WITHOUT MY PERMISSION(not due for one yet) and gave her a distemperment vaccine WITHOUT MY PERMISSION and then the doctor had the nerve to talk to me in a condescending fashion, pushing me to get my 3 year old mini poodle neutered... Charged me 90 dollars when I was only supposed to be spending $25. I like 2 blocks away and will NEVER be back.
The service was great and the Pizza was amazingly delicious.  The spicy sausage actually had some real kick which was a pleasant surprise.

My cat was diagnosed with urinary crystals and it was recommended that he start a prescription diet. I was buying the food directly from Girard's website until I found out it's way cheaper and more convenient to order from Chewy. The thing is, Girard is refusing to release the prescription because they want me to keep buying it through them. It's a difference of $30 PER ORDER on food that is already very expensive. They said it's standard practice for vets not to release the prescription for a third-party purchase but I asked around and not only is that completely untrue, it's actually illegal in most states for vets to refuse to give out a prescription (PA is one of a few exceptions). I'm very disappointed in this, up until this experience I was pretty happy with this practice but now I'm moving on.

Went here for a quick coffee and breakfast during the weekday. Atmosphere is very chill with a feel of a community learning center that serves craft coffee. We sat in the front window where the chairs were vintage and the area was open air. The comfortable ambience was perfect for the mission of the cafe-to serve the community. Staff was friendly and prompt. The only downer I experienced was that they had a special breakfast burrito on for the day but ran out of tortillas?! Ayeee, for the special at 10am? It was ok. I recovered and ordered the scramble which was splendid. House coffee was superb and overall enjoyed the experience. This is a place where I can enjoy great coffee and get work done.

Chemicals  WHAT???

We ventured in this place as we infrequently do. We asked for water, which they give you the clear cups slightly larger than a "shot" as the cost for the clear cups at a larger size is not financially feasible (corporate office). Water shamming 

I asked for a pitcher in order to fill it with ice water to prevent overly accessive trips back to the fountain, based on the small cups. The manager (from Ohio) told me they do not give out pitchers as the clemical they use to clean the pitchers makes the water taste bad.

WHAT... what chemicals?  "Are they safe for consumption", I'm confused? I ask the manager who fed this to me (no boots on).

What's going on?

it was absolutely delicious and I am now way too full! Let's just say it's a good thing we walked there and back otherwise, I would not be moving for the rest of the day! The brunch came with a soup, salad or fresh fruit ALONG with bread and pastries AND choice of coffee, juice or tea. I had the croque madame and my husband had the egg white strata. Both came out to be mind blowing. The staff was extremely friendly and everything is beautiful and cozy! Plus you get a nice relaxing walk if you want one :). There is plenty of parking if you do want to drive

. I am So completely and utterly disappointed in this salon! I have been a loyal patron for about a year getting my hair colored by Meghan, every few months. I even referred two of my friends to this salon. Unfortunately I recently had an appointment last month that I was unable to make bc I was away on business. The salon decided to charge my card with out my knowledge for $215 without my permission for services I never received. I called twice to dispute the charges, the receptionist told me it's their policy to charge full price for missed appointments. I told her that I did cancel my appointment the week before. To make matters worse, I was never made aware of this policy at any point in time, and I asked that the money be refunded or that at least I be able to come in and receive the services I was charged for. The receptionist who was nasty and rude told me she would have to ask Meghan, and the owner if they would honor the payment they already charged me for!!! So completely ridiculous ! It took a whole other day for her to call me back, in which she informed me that both Meghan and the owner refused to credit me the money they took. They could care less about their clients or their reputation. They clearly abuse their customers privacy. I have never been treated so poorly, especially not by a salon. Therefore, I have to let other customers know about this "policy" that was never pre-disclosed to me. Beware!!  Do not risk going there and giving them ur personal information you don't know what they are going to do with it.

Rittenhouse Needlepoint is the best shop around!! I used to use a shop half way across the country from where I live and had to give that up even though I loved some of the canvas' they carried. At Rittenhouse, they have it all, canvas', threads, finishing and classes!! Stephen and Russell are great and even bring their Poodle to work with them! (A big plus from me as I grew up with standard poodles!! :D ) This has become my go to store and I make a point of going there every time I visit my parents. The staff is so friendly and every time I want to have something designed, the design team is so easy to work with and will do just about anything your heart desires!! I will be visiting them again soon when we go up to visit my parents in about a week or so!! Love this place!!

First time at Cav's with a group of friends. Some of my female friends get up on the platform next to the DJ to dance - all good. There are several women just dancing on the stage. My male friend gets on the stage to start dancing, and then security comes over to tell him that he has to get down. Security would not answer him when he asked why he is forced off the platform, but not the women. Management came over and physically dragged him off the platform and out of the club. Management explicitly stated that "men are not allowed to dance on stage, and if you don't like it, get out". 

The truth is, Cavanaugh's can't profit off of the sexualization of male bodies. It's appalling that this establishment can hold such archaic views, especially in a college town and in the 21st century. This unfair treatment of men is unacceptable in today's society, and your hard-earned money should not support establishments that seek to undermine basic gender equality. 

That, and Cavanaugh's is careless when it comes to permitting underage drinking and fake licenses. In this bar, money speaks, not morals.
Came here for brunch with some friends! It was great, great coffee, wonderful waffles and friendly staff. I can't wait to try their dinner!
This place is amazing this is food that makes your taste buds explode nothing frozen or reheated this is cooked on the spot I love it

We were regular customers, until tonight. The bouncers treated us extremely disrespectfully and turned us away, even though we just wanted a meal in the restaurant portion of their establishment. This is a shame because the wings are usually quite good. We proceeded to later call the establishment, and spoke to the manager, Brian. The call started off well and I just wanted to better understand the situation and why we were turned away. About halfway through the conversation, he lost his cool and treated us extremely disrespectfully. No Brian, I was not drunk like you claimed I was when I called. I do not appreciate you hanging up on me either. The bar wasn't even half full tonight. Take your business elsewhere. We went to City Tap House and had a much better meal and Thursday Night Football experience. Brian, I can't wait to see how you decide to disrespectfully respond to this review like you did with other patrons who had negative things to say on Yelp. You might want to consider taking some basic classes to learn how to properly treat customers and effectively run a business.

I'm feeling conspiracy theory levels of confused that this place is so highly reviewed. Incredibly rude and pretentious employees who seemed to go out of their way to be condescending and looked perpetually put out. Had to beg at the counter for our check after waiting 20 minutes, and got curtly told to go sit back down and wait some more. Excuse me?

Overpriced menu too, imho. I don't mind paying $14 for a nice meal. But their Huevo (just one) Ranchero was $14 for 3 dry, cold little sections of corn waffle, a tablespoon each of black beans and pico, 4 little chunks of avocado, and one fried egg. Aside from a drizzle of hollandaise, it was bone dry and hard to eat.

It's a no from me!

This pizza is legit. If you like a little bit of charred crust, plenty of toppings, and good sauce, I would definitely recommend. 

Have gotten a large pepperoni each of the last three weeks, and the consistency is also good. The garlic knots are not garlicky on top, but twisted into the knot. Would also suggest some extra marinara with those. 

Thank you guys, keep up the good work!

There are certain things I straight up hate about coffee shops. They're always so cramped, to the point where you're basically sharing s table with some stranger. The food is always gross and old like it came from the food museum. Service is always slow and comes with a scoff and a scowl. 

Chayya is huge and has tons of seating. Definitely feel free to go out for brunch with friends and even bring the kids. The menu is more imaginative than coffee shop pastries and wraps. It won't get a Michelin star, but it's still good. Service is super slow. But hey, at least they check their scowls at the door.

It's like having a bodega, something I miss when I'm away from NYC. Great little store that has everything you need from snacks to drinks, and even a few grocery items. Friendly people, no complaints!

We found this place on Yelp. Otherwise we'd never known it exists. Located off Broad St on a small local road, it is barely visible to those driving by. The interior is also very small, yet cozy. But when it comes to flavors, there's nothing minimal there. The flavor palette is grant as is the  decor of the food on the plate. It slightly reminds me of those famous LA caffees - exotic approach to traditional food. Highly recommend for brunch!

My husband and I had a post-elopement party out on the Wissahickon patio and could not be more pleased with the beauty of the site, the service, the food, and the preparation and care put into our event by staff (Catie and Amber in particular). Catie was our contact person and was so helpful throughout the process, letting us know our options and following our wishes to a tee. We wanted to relaxed event that felt more like a summer garden party than a wedding reception, and Catie organized a lovely low-key event that still managed to be elegant and memorable. From the time we arrived (they reserved the closest parking lot for our party!), the patio looked stunning with white tablecloths and lavender napkins, candles on every table, and the gorgeous backdrop of Valley Green and the surrounding foliage all around us. Everyone congregated at the bar where we had a Mimosa and Bloody Mary station with everything from fresh fruit to olives and even bacon, plus local beers on tap. The buffet lunch was delicious with standouts being the sage ravioli and sesame salmon--people also raved over the French fries! The setting was so idyllic, and Amber (on-site coordinator that day) was so professional and catered to our every need. The day was so seamless and magical; I would highly recommend the Valley Green Inn for special events, especially if the weather allows you to be outside on the patio. It is a stunningly beautiful yet simple and rustic locale that suited our personalities perfectly. Highly recommend!
Really great service and excellent pizza and salads. This definitely is not your average pizza joint. Highly recommended!

Four of us geezer techies just had delicious pizza, sandwich, and salad today for early lunch. Food was great. Staff are outstanding. Location is good, right next to Trader Joe's. I created a white garlic, goat cheese, onion pizza that was super yummy from crust to topping to mouth to tummy. Will definitely return. See two photos.

I came here a couple months back for a quick drink and bite to eat. For $15 you got a large one topping pizza and I believe it was like 10 or 12 wings (don't quote me). 

Dang, I was actually very pleasantly surprised. They might be one of my favorite places to go for wings. The pizza was okay, not the best not not the worst. It was a little too much dough for my taste. 

Drinks, well, I got my usual... Patron on ice. It was a little more pricey than other places and the bartender had me switch over to a cheaper tequila. I hated the cheaper tequila so he didn't charge me for the bad tequila and poured me a new Patron, which I thought was super nice.

I have never written a yelp review before. I work in the restaurant infistry and have my own issues with guest publicly reviewing businesses, especially given the fact that often their experiences are taken out of context, but I am making an exception for this disgraced business.

I have held my tongue until now because I like to give everything a second chance if possible. A few months ago I was at Cav's on a thursdsy night with one of my friends who happens to be gay. The two of us were dancing, and we decided to go up on the platform below the DJ booth. A bouncer grabbed my friend's arm and told him that no males were allowed on the platform. I obviously got down with him, and asked why. He said something along the lines of, "I'm protecting you. I don't want you to be touched and grabbed." (As if he has any discretion over what makes me feel comfortable) A severe issue in its own right, but my friend proceeded to ask, "Would it make a difference if I were strait?" Two bouncers then proceeded to pick us both up, and drag us out of the bar, spilling drinks in our faces, gragging our feet on the floor, grabbing us as tight as they could. 

I just got off the phone with another one of my friends (who also happens to be gay) who is currently outside of the bar speaking to the police about a discrimination case based on an identical experience that he had there tonight. I left out many of the details of these encounters for the sake of length and to avoid using profanity, but I have never been so angry nor so motivated to let a business die. I have informed absolutely everybody that I know about these incidents, including very prominent people in the Philadelphia restaurant industry, as well as am in the process of filing a report with the police, as well as the ACLU.

It disgusts me that in a city that I love, people such as those who work at and run this bar still exist. It sickens me and I hope that they are faced with the most severe consequences for what they have done.

Mondongo Mondays! 
I'm soo happy I came here! The food is amazing and the customer service was exceptional! 
The small mondongo plate is the perfect serving for one person and so flavorful and fresh! 

Definitely will be!

I took my 13 y old furbaby to get blood work  at Girard Veterinary on 11/30/2017. She needed a new prescription for her thyroid. She was diagnosed over 6yrs ago with hypothyroidism. They do her blood work and tell me they see no sign of an issue with her thyroid. My baby has been on meds for years and by 3 other Vets her blood work also shows that. I sent all her medical records over. On 12/15 I contacted them, via email and by telephone, speaking to the receptionist 3 times & expressing that I know my dog has a thyroid and needs her meds! I never received a call back after the receptionist stressed that Dr. Wilkerson is busy but will contact me before days end! I never heard from Dr. Mooney or Dr. Wilkerson! I even expressed my dog mood, eyes and attitude has changed and she was off balance! The email I received was, they believe is a neurology problem and she needs x-rays! I just spent $400 for a CBC & a THYROID PANEL & I know she has Thyroid medicine and they have yet to contact mean whole 24hours later! I wouldn't recommend this Vet at all! No compassion or anything humane about this place. Only want money! And I have ano problem with paying for my furbaby! I have a problem with them ripping me off and not doing their job!
Yummy! The chicken trips are so juicy and the Mac and cheese is delicious! Reasonably priced

I cross-stitch as a hobby (when I have the time, anyway) but inconvenient trips to craft stores has been holding me back.

I finally stumbled upon Rittenhouse Needlepoint after doing a Google search and realized I walk by the store to and from work every day. Convenient! 

Being buzzed into shops makes me nervous but once I was inside the building I went right up the steps and into the shop. This store really caters to needlepoint fans. I like needlepoint but I was really just in for thread and cross-stitching fabric.

The staff were all friendly as could be and made themselves available to help but didn't stalk me the whole time I was in the store. 

I walked out with a bunch of thread, some fabric, and some needles. Oh, and a bumper sticker that says 'Save Needlepoint: Kill a Knitter." Win. 

The needlepoint projects, and the rest of the items at the store, are a teensy bit on the expensive side.

You get what you pay for. Be warned.

My dog needed some blood tests after starting new meds to be sure that they weren't affecting his kidney and liver. The specialist who had prescribed them said that Girard would probably have good pricing on the blood panel. We go to Society Hill and although they are great, they are pricey. So I had planned to make an appointment to get the tests done and try Girard out. Before I got around to the appointment, my dog got a bad upset stomach and was vomiting and had diarrhea so I took him in figuring I'd just get the blood work done while I was there. So I called to tell them the story and they said I could do a walk-in for both problems that day, which was cool.

The staff was really great. everything was good until we saw Dr. Balzer. She was weird with my dog off the bat, almost afraid of him, but at the same time really rough with him, like she was rushing us the whole time. She scared the crap out of my big teddy bear of a dog by practically throwing him on the rickety outdated metal scales that she then raised up without warning, making a loud noise. This, while being oddly manhandled, made my dog really uncomfortable. Even still, I could deal with all this. So, not the best bedside manner or nicest facility, ok, maybe that's par for the less expensive course. 

She wants to discuss why my dog is on meds, so I tell her about his hip and knee issues. She tells me, without running any tests, that the meds are the reason for my dog's stomach issues. Since my dog has been on these meds a while and has been doing great with them, I ask if they are still going to run tests, just to be sure that's what is actually wrong with him. She says that they will do tests and sent me out of the room. I come back in and she starts talking about his knee and hip issues, which I didn't come there for and how I should be getting a second opinion from another specialist, the one she takes her dog to, because she thinks my dog should have some surgery, which I was already told by the specialist my dog wasn't a good candidate for, and which I also didn't ask her for. I tried to ask about the issue at hand, my dog's stomach problem and how to treat him, but she didn't really listen at all. She rushed us out and told me she'll call with the results tomorrow. She didn't give me any recommendations other than to give him chicken and rice and stop his meds, which I had already started doing before we came in. I was looking for more of ... you can give him this to soothe his stomach, or just something more than the nonexistent advice I was given. But I still had hope at this point, for there were still test results to discuss the next day.

The next day I wait and wait and wait. No call. I call around closing to leave a message, asking that someone please call me back with the results, only because it's a Friday and they aren't open on the weekends and my dog wasn't any better. They called me back around 6:15. I had expected a call earlier in the day. There had really been no diagnosis for him the day before, I kind of expected one with the test results. She called and said, "your dog's blood tests came back fine." and I said great. She said okay then, like she was hanging up. I was like, wait wait. My dog isn't any better. And she just acted like, oh well, sorry. She was eager to get off the phone and she was eating food while talking to me. So I said, can you maybe tell me what to do about his stomach problem, since the tests came back fine, or tell me what I might be able to do for him. She told me I could give him Maalox and I could come back Monday (and pay for another visit) and they could check for parasites. I told her, very politely, that was why I brought him in yesterday and I guess I was confused as to why they didn't do that when I was there. She told me, almost in an accusing tone, that I should have brought in a stool sample. I told her, again politely, that no one told me to bring in a stool sample when I called before I came in or I would have been happy to do that. She told me that she would send me the blood results and I should take my dog somewhere else. I'm not making this up. Completely unacceptable. She was that unprofessional. 

I guess I will be sticking with Society Hill. Where overpriced care gets you a diagnosis, a treatment and a piece of mind. It's worth the money.

Always enjoyed breakfast here until today when a customer sat in the restaurant with her large dog sitting on the floor. I asked the waitress if they usually allowed dogs in there and she said yes if the customer is waiting for take out. I asked if she knew that dogs were not allowed in places where food is served and she said she did not. I will be looking for a different place to eat.

Couldn't really tell you about the quality of the food, but I can tell you whoever the lady was that answered the phone is probably costing this business plenty of money. She was rude to a point that my wife and I simply hung up and ordered elsewhere, I'd save yourself the time and not even bother calling in the first place.

So I went to this establishment tonight. My friend, who is ACTUALLY 22 years old got his ID snapped in half. Staff and cops and literally everyone were no help. Even though he is of legal age. Absolute bull****. Why should people of legal age get their ID snapped in half and then be subsequently forced to buy a new ID for 49 dollars. Also, I (and 3 friends) got into the bar before he got his ID snapped so we had to pay cover even though we spent 5 minutes there. Awful experience. Bounces are awful do not go.

Ordered delivery, it was pretty late so maybe that had something to do with it, but that's still not an excuse for how gross our food was. Grilled cheese was burnt to a blackened crisp, to a point that it was inedible. The fries were soggy. The mac and cheese could only be described as a heart attack in a bowl. The closed container was actually covered in grease when I received it, so you can imagine what the mac itself was like. This was my first and last time ordering from here -- wouldn't risk it again.
The food was good and the service was also good, they let dogs on here just incase you came with one. The food did take a while to come out but it was good.

Stopped in with a friend a couple of times this week. It's a beautiful restaurant and very clean. The restroom is in the plaza but not in the restaurant, you'll need a key. We ordered a couple of beers, wine, Luna Board, and two slices. Help yourself to water at the front. 
The food was as delicious as it was visually appealing. Perfect meats and cheeses, fig jam, mustard. The cracker bread was very crunchy. Like, you can't hear anything but yourself crunching and you also go slow so you don't break a tooth off. My friend had some plain bread knots added the second time we ate here because she couldn't do the super hard cracker bread. They also have peppered oil in the table- this stuff is amazing! Pour it on everything!
My only complaint is a personal one: music. The first time we were here, it was quiet either Italian or classical music. But the second trip was some kind of loud techno that was so jumpy, I thought my hearing was going out. It sounded like transformers throwing up. Maybe people like that but it wasn't for me. 
Anyway, the food is very much worth a stop in to this cute place. Excellent pizza crusts, great topping choices, a slice is filling, the Luna Board! Get it! Flavorful food with a friendly atmosphere.

I'm updating last year's review, because after yet another New Year's Day visit, I can't recommend their brunch highly enough. This restaurant is truly a gem. In our case, I booked for the 10:00 AM opening on New Year's Day 2016, which may sound crazy, but turned out to be a great way to start the new year. So great, in fact, that I repeated the visit again for New Year's Day 2017. If you want to do brunch (or even lunch) I recommend that you don't drive in and park in the lot at the Inn; instead, park at one of the more distant lots (the Kitchens Lane lot for example), then take a walk along the Wissahickon on Forbidden Drive. (On the way back, take the trail on the other side of the creek - there's a great view of the restaurant from across the creek, especially in winter when the trees are bare - plus you get to walk through the Finger Bridge.) There's something really special about taking the time to walk, and then arrive at this restaurant, which is so evocative of the pre-automobile era. During our New Year's visit, the Inn was decorated for the holidays, which was charming, and with the wood fireplace actually providing the heat for the dining room. (I wouldn't sit too close.) 

I was sorry to see that this year, they didn't offer the hot buttered rum, but their spiced cider made up for it. The new year's brunch was a $30 prix fixe two-course menu - a truly excellent value. Their house salad was excellent, and the 2016 lobster frittata was gone, but the 2017 crab Eggs Benedict was outstanding, eggs perfectly poached. I don't think you could go wrong with anything on the menu. We'll definitely be walking back again for brunch before long.

Get on their email list - this past December they offered gift cards that were basically 50% off. Incredible bargain.

Straight up, this place gets it. Affordable artisan style pizza, really great beer for a cheap price, and the employees are so laid back and just love their jobs. I highly recommend the caesar salad paired with either a simple pepperoni slice or a slice of the margarita pizza!

The location and ambience (especially if sitting outside on a nice day) are really great. The food is unfortunately only mediocre to good (at its best), and service in my experience is often fairly slow. It is not a place you go for the food itself and not if you are in a hurry. However, it is enjoyable if you just want to relax along the Wissahickon trail and enjoy nature.

My boyfriend and I wanted to quick bite and some drinks last night so we decided to try Cavanaugh's because they had a pretty decent score on Google. We got there and walked in and the vibe was okay. We did notice how many TV's were there and pointed out that the bar would be amazing to watch sports at. We found seats at the bar pretty quickly because it was a Tuesday night. We sit. About 3 minutes later we are given menus ... and then we are totally ignored by the two bartenders who seems less than thrilled to be working. They continued to wait on patrons who had already been served and ignore my boyfriend and I who hadn't even been given water yet. They bartenders moved very slow and didn't have a sense of urgency at all. I won't be back.

We had a very nice lunch here. Clearly the appeal is the view not the food, but we had 3 different sandwiches and they were all decent. Our server was polite friendly and attentive. We arrived right when they opened, filled up quickly. Set your expectations right and try it for a great change.

Always love to try new pizza restaurants. Pizza Luna isn't a 'create-your-own' place but would be better served if it was. Had a couple pizzas, a couple beers, and a glass of wine and our bill was $54 before tax. Seems a bit much for a run-of-the-mill pizza joint. 

Given the proximity to the Trader Joe's store, I feel they are feeding off of that customer base right now. Eventually people will realize that it is just not worth it.

The first time I came to Pizza Luna, I was pleasantly surprised by the ambience inside. On the outside, it looks mediocre as it is located in a mall strip near Trader Joe's. No, it was clean, bright, and quaintly small when we came inside! My husband and I ordered their speciality pizza with the sausage in it. It was so good that we ate all of it up in one sitting! Ingredients are fresh. Pizza sauce is fresh and not as acidic usually found in many pizza joints. 

We weren't disappointed when we came back a second time on a Friday night. Pizza is fantastic and wonderfully cooked each time. The only downside is the waiting time because too many people found out about this gem and ordered in. We had to wait our turn to get handsy with our customized pies. It was kind-of worth the wait and but not so easy on the wallet. I say come to this place and see for yourself!

Probably one of the best places to bring a guest visiting Philly, if you can get there.  The brunch was really good - $18.95 set price, and there wasn't a thing that we tried that disappointed us.  

It's a good idea to incorporate a run/hike in the area, since you'll be eating a lot of food.
Food is good, place is nice, and has a cool hipster vibe to it!  Unfortunately, the hipsters that work there have very bad attitudes- taking off a star for the moody tudes'

Great place to watch sports. Food is overall pretty good. I really like their cheesesteak! I've tried a burger and it was a little over cooked. Chicken tenders are great as well. The staff Is very nice and and attentive.

I ordered the Gyro pizza and a Greek salad. It was really really phenomenal food. The potato salad on the Greek salad was actually very tasty. And the pizza was extra cheesy and the meat was seasoned well. I would recommend to anyone. I ordered delivery, and it was on time and fresh. My only suggestion... offer a side cup of marinara to dunk the pizza crust in. That's my favorite 'extra'. Great food!! Will definitely order again.

Always understaffed.   I waited 17 min for a breakfast sandwich today.  One person serving everyone.   Just not cool how this place is miss managed.   Every mornin it's like this. Not enough people working for a quick in and out
The guys at Pizza Luna are stand up gents. Always visit my beer bar after work to support fellow local businesses. The food is AMAZBALLS

If I could give 10 stars, I would.

The people who work here are kindhearted, enthusiastic individuals who set the standard for vets everywhere--and I truly mean this. 

My two kittens (a male and a female) were spayed/neutered this past Thursday, and they came back to me healthy, happy, and unstressed. If anything, I was a bigger wreck than they! An emergency led me to being late in picking them up, and I called the office at Girard in tears asking for them to stay fifteen minutes past the hour so I could take my kittens home. This was an unreasonable request on my part, but the vets there didn't miss a beat. One particular young woman who I neglected to get the name of waited for me to reach the hospital, and calmed me down as I ran in, all flustered. I almost wanted to stay and hang out--they were THAT kind!

I applaud these people for their dedication, their promptness, and their kindness. I am very grateful for their work, my kittens are healing up perfectly, and I will be returning from now on. :)

I'm so pleased about this place! The location is great and I'm glad cute places are spreading farther down East Passyunk. The cafe is clean and bright and welcoming. The staff was all friendly. It was your usual East Passyunk brunch crowd.
