I asked them, which is what AAVSB said to do, ask them for their insurance so I can inform their insurance company that I will be going forward with a lawsuit with Girard Veterinary Clinic. Girard Veterinary Clinic has yet to return 1 phone call!! They duck my calls and WILL NOT CALL ME BACK!! I pray that all who have furbabies please think twice before walking into that place! Because they sure have no live for furbabies! Wrong answers and over charging is what they are about!!

This is the best pizza I have had in Tampa! I keep asking them what do they put in their pizza and they always say the same thing, they use the best ingredients out here to make their pizzas. The customer service is extraordinary and I always feel like I am family when I dine in. The place is always clean and they have TVs playing local sports and National Sports and at night they play really good music for the night crew to enjoy the late night crowd because they stay open till 4am! Love Jason too!!!!

I was looking for the top yelp ranked pizza in Tucson since im visiting here I love pizza. 

I gotta say I did not disappoint one the best pizzas I had in a while I ordered pepperoni pizza and prosciutto pizza which it was my favorite. 

Even tho it was to go delivery it was still hot and fresh when I got it delicious if I could give them 10+ stars I would. 

During this difficult times businesses are trying their best to keep their doors open for us consumers and the best way I can do to give back its writing reviews I encourage other do the same. 

Cheers

I don't know what is Boston-style pizza is, so I cannot comment on their authenticity, but Palazzo Pizza offers up fast pizza for carryout via their website and porch window that is easy to eat.

I ordered two pizzas online, and I was told to give them 15 minutes. That kind of turnaround time is impressive. I requested to pick up in 30 minutes, and when I arrived on time, I could see them putting the pizza into boxes. The restaurant has a large deck, and there is an ordering/pick up window on the deck, so I did not have to enter the restaurant. That's super handy in these COVID days, and it probably is a great convenience for people showing up at 3am for after bar pizza (they have very late hours on weekends). 

The pizzas were fine. I appreciated the crispy bottom crust. My husband and kids shared a large pepperoni pizza (half mushroom). My husband commented that he suspected the mushrooms were canned. I ordered a small sausage pizza since they mentioned on the website that they used a locally sourced Italian sausage supplier. I found the sausage to be tasty but not very remarkable. 

There is a small private lot next to the restaurant, so pick up was easy.

I found the pizza to be fine if not extraordinary. I'm glad that there's another locally owned pizza place in South Tampa.

We came here for lunch last week. There were 4 of us. And we ordered right away in the front. The guy taking the orders was so patient in explaining everything since most of us hadn't been there. We ordered the lunch special where you receive a slice of pizza and a side salad. Everything came out fresh and fast. I ordered the margherita pizza and the radicchio salad. So good! The food was out quickly and the salad was crunchy. It had lots of garlicky salad dressing which I didn't mind. I want to come back again for dinner to try some of the wine options, but overall a great experience!

Read the other reviews if you want atmosphere comments.  This review is only for things I felt were out of the ordinary.
It was generally clean, but the service so soooo slow.  We had to ask for our waitress twice.  Only about half the tables in her section were occupied.  It just seemed a little off.  Not to mention I felt she was dressed inappropriately; maybe that's how she makes her big tips, but it seemed like more of her chest area was showing than covered, I know most guys wouldn't mind, but I felt it made things sort of awkward midafternoon.  In her defense it was St. Paddy's Day and I'm sure things were going to get crazy later.  The DJ, however, thought things were crazy now.  The music was just plain too loud.  He had a playlist going and was probably around the bar or somewhere, i.e. not on the decks.  Overall, I'd go back to Cavanaugh's.

Very disappointed.  I had the Frenched Chicken Breast.  The chicken was burned, dry and extremely small.  There were 3 brussel sprouts sliced in half and I think maybe 6 small pieces of roasted potatoes on the plate.  The server was very pleasant and service itself was quite good.  Drinks were refilled quickly and she was attentive to our table.  The others in my party were pleased with their meals which is why I went with three stars. I am usually not very hard to please but this chicken left much to be desired.

I have no PPP aged kids anymore, so I won't speak to the games or frivolity that goes on in this place so huge that it should have it's own zip code.

Sheer curiosity about the lunch buffet brought me here. Maybe it's just me but Peter Piper Picked a Peck of Pretty Pathetic Pizzas to Provide People... at least in the buffet.

I don't care if it's less than six bucks for the buffet.. not going back.

First, I am a pizza lover. If pizza is not my favorite food, that is only because lobster edged it out. I am very particular about my pizza and would choose something else if the pizza available is subpar. Hence, I avoid chain pizza and supermarket pizza,  both frozen and fresh. I am not interested in pizza that is "not bad" and won't give it a second chance. 

After a hair appointment that ran late and still needing to grocery shop at Trader Joe's, I decided to try Pizza Luna for a quick bite in the Joe's shopping center at Speedway and Wilmot. 

The restaurant had been a Cup It Up. The scuttlebutt was that they closed due to politics, but likely it was because the food wasn't great. I tried it once, deemed it okay, and that was that. 

Walking into Luna, the first Impression was olfactory: The garlicky tomatoey fragrance could bring any pizza lover to his knees. I was enthusiastically welcomed at the order counter and was asked if this was my first time. Since it was, I was handed a menu and offered a very helpful guide to ordering. Three different styles of pizza are offered and each can be tailored with the toppings of choice. My guide raved about the fig, but I opted to go the more traditional route of house-made fennel sausage and onion. Advised that my pizza would be ready in seven minutes., I was thrilled; it was now 2:00 and I was starving. 

Seven minutes later, my pizza was ceremoniously delivered to my table along with its intoxicating aroma. I picked up the first piece, dripping molten cheese, burned my tongue, and didn't care. The crust is perfect: thin - but not at all cardboardy - with a delightfully chewy edge. The sauce is faintly sweet and deliciously present but not dominating. The fennel sausage is, frankly, scrumptious. I'd take credit for amazing ordering, but the young man at the counter deserves a nod and Pizza Luna deserves the rest of the credit. 

If someone in your party is not a pizza lover (what?!), lovely salads and an antipasto board are available. A lunch special offers a slice with a salad. Beers and wines are on menu as well. 

Tucson had two pizzas I will eat; then there are three.

HANDS DOWN BEST PIZZA IN TOWN!!!!!!
Flavor is off the charts! Super crispy! 
Loveeeee the white pizza!!!!!  
The steak sandwich that is ONLY available on Wednesday's is sooo yummyyy! I'll be back soon!

Meritus is the company placed in charge of the Community Development District that we live at in Manatee County. 

We have a beautiful home on a lake, but there has been a problem this summer with fish dying to the point where there is a stench. 

We have complained several times in the past few weeks to Nicole Chamberlain. She is slow to respond and sometimes not at all. 

Today, we left a voicemail to her boss Brian Howell. He emailed a response that was snippy and condescending. He thinks we are the only ones that have this issue since nobody shows up at their meetings. Well, when you hold meetings at 1pm on a Tuesday, people are unlikely to show up since we have to work for a living. But, it is setup like that on purpose so they can say they "met" and collect the community's money without much accountability. 

If you are moving to Tampa Bay, I urge you to look carefully at whether or not you will be dealing with a CDD. Investigate it and make sure they actually work for the residents.

I was very pleased with this vet!! I am in grad school and don't have a lot of money so I wanted a 1) inexpensive vet who would be 2) very knowledgable so I wouldn't need many tests to figure out what was wrong. I was disappointed with all other vets in center city but I read many great reviews of this place. I did the walk in service. 

The woman on the phone recommended I get there early (walk in hrs start at 8 so she recommended 7:45, even 7:30). I was the second person there at 7:20 and while only 4 people were there by 8, I would not have recommended going anytime after that because the place filled quickly. It did take a while for them to bring me back but it was worth it. 

I saw Dr. Balzer. She was great with my cat: had good bedside manner, immediately knew what was wrong and didn't waste time in doing what needed to be done. She was firm but kind to me about what I needed to change in my cat's diet and was very helpful in answering any questions. 

I was expecting a high bill (as I was under the impression that most vets are overpriced) but their exam fee is only $40 and $10 for the antibiotics. 

Overall I was very pleased and will visit them again!

I'm always looking for a good pizza spot and came upon this new addition to the Hyde Park area.  I ended up ordering online and despite having a carryout order, there is still a convenience fee assessed, which was a bit puzzling.  Wait time for a Friday night wasn't bad at 25 minutes and paying for my order upon arrival was easy as they have a walk up window outside.  

I had ordered the Meaty Meat pizza, which has sausage, meatballs, pepperoni, and bacon toppings on the normal sauce and cheese pie.  Size and taste was great.  The icing on the cake for me was that the crust had a buttery flavor so it didn't have that normal cardboardy taste.  The crust was also chewy and a good consistency.

Went there with my best friend...love the area...I live in this part of philly and it just doesnt even seem like its philly...anyhoo I digress...I cannot stand this place..the service was bad, its like the waitstaff had some kind of problem in serving us...smug attitudes...and the food was so beyond subpar it was ridiculous...and the restrooms were beyond unsanitary...i love the trails that are in front of this place but I will never step back into that joint again...it gives joints a bad name.

My mom and I stopped by for a late lunch last weekend. This was our first time here as we don't live in Tucson. We each ordered a different kind of pizza and sat on the patio. The workers there were very friendly and the food didn't take long to make. We both loved our pizza choices! The Neapolitan and a white pizza. My mom said this was her favorite White Pizza she's ever had! I also really enjoyed mine, it tasted very fresh. When we are back in Tucson we will definitely come eat here again!

I see why this place gets such good ratings..sometimes it's for the customer service.. sometimes it's fir the actual food..well I'm giving 5 stars for both! You can get really good pizza anywhere but most places don't have an amazing crust, fresh mozzarella and drum roll please! SAN MARZANO TOMATOES! 

We were here for a few days so I was on a search to find the best pizza I could find.. I found some places closer but I kept going back to pizza luna's Yelp page because nobody had this pizza. They may have looked like it but a true Neapolitan pizza does not have pizza sauce as other places were trying to sell..they use San marzano tomato's! So my decision was easy..yesterday I came in for just their slices to try..ordered the margherita (only difference was basil), their cheese pizza with pizza sauce as usual and their Neapolitan. Margherita was super good..not too different than the Neapolitan ..but my suggestion would be ..not to cook the basil..leave it fresh on top torn into pieces...still super good but the Neapolitan just seemed tastier to me..today with the large size I came back for I felt there wasn't any garlic like I tasted yesterday but that was the only bummer..and the cheese pizza was good..not the best I had but good..come here and try the San marzano pizza's..maybe even get some fresh arugula on it..wish I would have tried the bianca pizza..

Now for the customer service..these guys are all sooooo nice! They are friendly, polite and accommodating as I had some requests fir our long drive. They gave me a smaller box too so we don't have to keep the huge box in our car with us for our 7hr drive back home with a dog. Next time I'm in Tucson..I will be back! Neapolitan Pizza

We ate here for Valentine's Day 2016.  Prefixed menu for $70/person so pricey, but definitely up to the par.  She had lobster bisque and I had a goat cheese beet salad.  both were really good and plenty of it.  followed it up with a crab cake and a pork belly with pickled radishes (which might have been my favorite).  she had the duck and I had the lobster tail.  the duck was great with a really nice sauce and the lobster tail was cooked very well (and I was complicated and asked for the truffle mash potatoes rather than the rice, and it was so worth it).  So very accommodating and very pleasant meal even though pricier than expected.  full bar selection with some house made stuff that we should've tried.  will definitely go back.

service was also great.  a little too quiet for our liking so maybe in the future they could have a little background music.  just a thought.  I hear great things about brunch so looking forward to enjoying that.

We were having trouble finding anything open passed 10 pm and ended up here, so happy we did. As long as you're  not a drunk mess you can go inside.  Every single person that worked there was so nice and friendly, our server was great and the owner even came over to say hi. The service was absolutely incredible. Being from Jersey we know pizza and this place is top notch. Don't hesitate to come here!!!! Ps F you Jason

This place is an absolute gem. 
I went to eat lunch here on a beautiful summer day. It was a wonderful break from the hustle and bustle of the city! They give great portion sizes. 
The only downside was slow service and quite a few bugs flying around while we tried to dine outside. 
The food is delicious. I highly recommend the grilled salmon and especially the creme brulee. 
This place is a hidden gem. Its definitely worth trying to find!

I have been to this Wawa several times and it seems to always be busy anytime of the day or night. Yet you still get in and out quickly. They have about 10 Tesla supercharger stations you can plug into as needed. 
They have their fresh made sandwich shop inside, and a huge selection of drinks and snacks. Wawa's are at the top of my list of favorite gas stations. They are always clean, well lit, and even their washer fluid to clean your car windows when getting fuel, is blue and cleans your car windows very well. Some cheap places use dirty plain water, not Wawa, they use real glass cleaner, very nice touch! 
All types of healthy pre-made snacks are also a choice for those in a hurry.

Great pizza spot in soho! Located next to HPC there is limited parking on the street but an empty lot across the street. Feel free to seat yourself (we chose the patio.) we started the night with a few appetizers-empanadas, sausage + peppers, Greek salad and wings. You wouldn't expect empanadas at a pizza joint but they were actually really good! The salad was our least favorite of the bunch. It had quite the block of feta but overall the dressing wasn't your typical Greek we were expecting but more so of a vinegar and olive oil type dressing. The sausage and peppers weren't my choice while ordering but they were surprisingly delicious. Now these wings were the highlight of the night. Crispy fried outside but juicy inside. The garlic parm dry rub was intensified with the garlic sauce we just poured all over them. Honestly, some of the best wings I've ever had! Pizza was also great! Buffalo chicken could've used more Buffalo sauce for my liking but a side for dunking will suffice as well.

Love, Love, Love Pizza Luna. I'm from the north east, and have had more than my share of NY pizza, this is as close as you'll get outside of NYC. We order fairly regularly, and have never been disappointed. We get the Take-and-Bake - set oven to 500 degrees, put pizza in for 4 1/2 minutes, it's perfection. 

Every time I go in everyone is working away, they're super friendly, take the time to say hello and look like they're enjoying what they're doing. Can't say enough great things about the people and the food, a MUST have if you're in Tucson and it's great to support local businesses!

I'm glad I finally took the time out one Sunday morning to take a stroll and have brunch here.

I started my mid day ramble with a friend, driving down Bells Mill road and parking in one of the lots right off the creek. From there it was a walk of a mile and a half, perhaps even two, reminiscing about days gone by and speaking about days to come. 

The lime-green canopy of freshly sprung leaves put a glow in the air that was just... happy. The sound of shallow water rushing over rocks massaged our ear drums, and made us forget how far we would actually have to go just to eat - a journey that only existed because I felt that if one were to take the road directly into the Valley Green Inn as opposed to walking Forbidden Drive, one would also be missing half the experience. No matter.

We got to the inn in just under 30 minutes, to find a guitar and violin duo playing "What a Wonderful World," as a wedding party made final preparations for their ceremony outside the inn. At this point, could the scene manage to get any more idyllic? Actually, it did - two angels descended from heaven and gave me a happy ending. You can't put a price on that, though my friend tried by throwing dollars coins at the seraphs. All kidding aside, the atmosphere leading up to the inn was pretty awesome.

And then we walked inside. Brunch service was in full swing at 12:30 pm, so we asked the hostess how long it would be given that I'd neglected to call ahead for reservations - a habit I'd picked up over time as other places in Philly don't play that.

"It should just be 15 minutes."

Nice. And you know what? It was. We went outside to watch the ducks, and the children that were running around the wading waters chasing the ducks. I remember when it was acceptable for me to behave that way. Now they say I have a "developmental disorder" and give me pills. All kidding aside, again, and we checked up on our table. It had just gotten set, and the hostess seated us.

Service was excellent, and food was tasty. Not exactly a heavenly hand-jo as described above, but definitely on par with any respectable purveyor of brunch items. My friend and I ordered, and we started with black coffee and scones, and then fruit salad and Caesar, respectively. Afterwards, she got the wild mushroom frittata. I went with the brie french toast. It was insanely sweet because of the candied walnuts on top - I shoved those aside and found the rest to be perfect.

Having gorged ourselves and restocked our tissue supply (allergies), we went outside and puddle jumped our way back. And that was that.

Pro-tip:
If you decide to walk to the inn, as I did, be sure to time your bathroom stops, because it's a pretty long walk. Manageable, but not exactly two blocks to the corner store.

I give them no stars. I only chose one because I had to. They have been horrible to deal with. Our community has complained countlessly about certain things with no change.  They couldnt even decide on a budget or send us payment books until the middle of the year. Try calling them! You can't get through to talk to anyone unless you know specifically who you are calling and can use the dial by name directory.  Otherwise, you have no other options and no matter who you call no one answers their phone or returns calls. This has been my experience. Now I am selling my house and was supposed to close tomorrow but the title company has been trying for weeks to get in touch with them but has just gotten the run around. They didn't know where my account was then they said it was in collections  (which it is not). The attorney they said had my account has nothing in my name. It's just a run around because they don't know what they are doing!! Now I've spent money and made moving arrangements for nothing. DO NOT USE THEM!
Wonderful ambiance, delicious food, congenital wait staff.  It's a lovely venue for brunch, lunch or dinner.

I actually liked this place more than Sabrina's and Green Eggs Cafe... 

Like most of the Yelpers had mentioned., it is a small and cozy place.. The staff was nice... I did read up on some prior comments about some rude waitress.. Kept my fingers crossed as we walked in that we won't see her.. We were greeted with a warm smile... Phewwww... 

The food was excellent.. We got the Brunch Burger and Truffle Egg Toast... with a side of sausage... Machiatto and Chai Tea... The burger tends to get a bit messy as your eating because it's filled with such goodies!!! The truffle toast had perfect tasting, I'm speechless.. Food came out in a fair amount of time too!  I would definitely be back for more goodies =)

MmmMmm, Passyunk knows how to do brunch! If asked to make a snap decision on where to go, however -- I will always suggest Chhaya!

If you arrive when its crowded, be sure to make your way to the counter inside, ask the wait time and give them your name! You can probably slouch down to the Bottle Shop if its after 11 to waste a few minutes - but you'll be seated within the time they tell you (it seems they've got it down to a science!)

Always always always read the specials. The only bad thing is that sometimes the specials are so enticing, they keep you from enjoying delicious menu staples!
Anything they do with waffles is always incredible and decadent. 
And of course - there's the coffee. Dolche de Leche Lattes? Incredible South American coffee offerings? Behind that aforementioned counter lies a mechanical wonderland of coffee prep tools. The staff is very knowledgeable about their coffee (and very friendly as well.)

Service can be a little slow towards the end of the brunch rush, but they aren't rushing to kick you out either - and I'd prefer that in a brunch any day!

If you're planning on brunching in Passyunk, or need a hot cup to pick you up in the morning, check them out!

This was my first time ordering delivery from Pizza Luna through door dash.  For $77 (tip included), we enjoyed one large prosciutto pizza, one small pepperoni pizza, radicchio Ceasar salad, and garlic knots.  This is somewhat pricey for a couple of pies, but you can taste the difference from chain pizza.  My favorite was the pepperoni pizza.  The 72 hour dough was soft and chewy on the inside and crunchy on the outside.  Their Neapolitan pizzas are made with caputo Italian flour and baked in a 700 degree oven.  After trying their pizza I would have to list them in my top 5 pizza spots for Tucson. Cheers!

Cavanaugh's... Cav's for short is a cool little bar with plenty of TV's to watch EVERY game out there.  I do not stay late as I am usually popping in before a softball game or after a victory.  Wings are good but 3 alarm fire, is more like kinda hot.  Beer selection is great, the staff is awesome.  Prices can be a little hit or miss.  Most of the specials are great but check the price before getting a pitcher of beer that your wallet can't handle.    Yay! I'm a fan.

Had to try Cavanaughs "award winning" wings and they lived up to the hype!! Best wings in Philly I've had so far. The bar has an awesome sports college bar type feel and I can't wait to go back! We went for an early dinner and got two large orders of wings with CAVs and mild buffalo sauce.  The CAVs sauce was amazing.  It was a little sweet but also tangy and had a spice to it.  The wings were crispy, the meat fell of the bone, and they were perfectly sauced.  We also got an order of nachos with shredded chicken.  The nachos come with a lot of nacho cheese and sour cream so they were not my favorite but were still good.  The tater tots were the best I've ever had.  Both the fries and tots came with a chipotle ranch sauce that was very tasty.  All in all, great place, great prices, lots of beers, and a good vibe.  I would recommend this local place to anyone especially if they like wings!!

I wonder how many restaurants named China King are there in Philadelphia?  Probably a lot.  China King is a neighborhood takeout spot that delivers.  Sometimes only Chinese food can scratch the itch,  I give them a call.  I usually order egg rolls,  pot stickers,  boneless spare ribs, pepper steak,  chicken wings and egg foo young. So with dishes like spare ribs, pork yat and egg foo young,  you only order in the neighborhood and if you order them in Chinatown you'll be disappointed. 
Delivery is fast and courteous and the prices are reasonable.

To start off it is difficult to get an appointment unless you show up in the morning and wait literally hours for their open clinic  or you are willing to wait weeks for an open slot.  I went to the Girard Clinic for paperwork to take my cat overseas which basically required a blood test and filling out forms and sending them to government agencies....not the most difficult thing I would think (although it cost close to $400).. At any rate all I got was a lot of misinformation about the process (even when I had all of the papers in order to begin with), I had to wait weeks for the blood work (which in reality was finished in three days), and in the end they messed up the filing of the paperwork (the vet forgot to sign it) forcing me to miss a flight costing me hundreds of dollars and for me to make a trip to Harrisburg to do everything myself which I was paying them hundreds of dollars to avoid.  When I made a complaint to the manager  and the vet trying to be proactive and rectify the situation, all I received was a lot of grief and outright lies on their part, threatening to not to give me my cat's  bloodwork results (which I had already paid for). I strongly do not recommend this clinic. Maybe this was a fluke, maybe they are better with surgeries than filling and signing a simple form...but there are enough vet's in Philly....choose someone else

I recently moved to Tucson from the Bay Area. I am a pizza lover to the core and extremely picky when it comes to my pizza. I needed to find my new go to pizza spot. Pizza Luna does not disappoint! The pizza is absolutely delicious. Quality is outstanding! The service and staff always greet you with a smile and a positive attitude. I always leave smiling. This is my third time here and now my weekly habit . It's worth every penny. Thanks Pizza Luna!

This 3-star rating is salvages because I got some really comfortable cotton shirts (I have some skin problems when I where synthetic fabrics for many days in a row) for a very reasonable fit and price.  Since I live close by, this is kind of the first store I see besides Burlington Coat Factory, so I stop by to see if I can get something for a good price.  It's all very hit or miss because as of late, I've seen some weird threads at the store.  And how can I not say how I adore fleece to keep me warm in the winter.  Just be sure to take care of your clothes because multiple washed may bring them closer to the grave than you think.

Old Navy has gone down hill since they've moved the Fat Girls' clothes to online only sales.  

That said, I really like this old navy because it's easy for me to get to (within walking distance) and doesn't involve me going to the suburbs

How can I even give this hole one star.  Lex. D is too generous.  My daughter stayed her on January 17th.  Was to be 2 nights and we arrived very late after being at the Brandon Hospital to treat a broken foot (daughters).  First room had roaches on the walls and the floors, appliances and walls were filthy.  My daughter freaked.  We were given the only other ground floor room (remember the broken foot) which was just as run down but at least did not have roaches.  The fridge door and exterior door were both blistered with rust.  They had simply painted over the blisters.
Told them we would not be staying the second night and when we went to check out in the morning no one was at the front desk for the full 20 minutes I stood there.  Left the key and guess what?  When I received my credit card bill we were charged for the second night.  The woman at the desk when I called to complain said that I had checked out with her the morning after we had left the motel.
They refuse to reimburse the second night, reply to a letter explaining the issue or call my cell that I left on the letter.  
This motel should be condemned.  I have contacted the BBB and the corporate headquarters.  My next step is to contact the Tampa Health Department.
Amazing!!  What a little Gem in Tampa. Perfect breakfast and perfect price. We will definitely be back. Thanks Dylan.

I read the reviews and had to see what fuss was about. It was worth the try! Here's the deal- the food is good but the service is BETTER and that's rare these days. A friend and I showed up about 2 minutes before closing and Dylan not only accommodated is without hesitation, but he also used his personal truck to provide shade for us from the sun while we waited. He could have easily hurried us along. He deserves 10 stars but 5 is all they would let me do. I'm in Tampa for a week and I can't get enough of this place!
The sandwich I ordered was good, but for the $8 price there was hardly any proscuitto or other Italian meats in the panini - it was a bit overpriced.

I try shopping at thrift stores & feel good about that. Clothing is so disposable- why not grab inexpensive hand me downs?

But I confess, I also shop at Old Navy and cringe every time I see a made in Cambodia (with notoriously bad labor practices) label.

But I got a pair of pants for $20 that are freaking amazing in color, cut and fit. I'm thinking of paying $20 to have them taken in now that I've shrunk from working out. These pants are my dream come true. 

It seems like the people of Old Navy get that women come in all sort of shapes and sizes and celebrates them all. I like that.

One of the few places I've let just "bring me something, I'm too tired to think about it" and it was great.

A favorite lunch and "sit outside & watch the world go by" place in good weather.

Owner Lynn keeps the staff hopping and totally professional.

The Old Navy Experience is rarely any fun, no matter where you go. So I shop online. This generally works out, as I know what I like - you know cheap t shirts and such - and they have great sales that they send to my email. The rub is when I try something new that just won't work and attempt to return it at the store. Generally, the folks in Chelsea are just fine (the lines, though. Ugh) but the Philadelphia store?

Dirty, unorganized and some of the angriest retail workers I've had the displeasure of encountering. And the lines? Made all the longer by the pick and choose policy of who's next. (hint: it wasn't me. The mean girl vibe in the whole mall is appalling)

What a great find! This little food truck pushes out some great eats! Had the Cajun eggs and it was great - perfect amount of spice and very flavorful. 
Coffee is self serve and tasted good and you can either sit by the truck or take it to go and eat along the Riverwalk.
Inexpensive but the quality of the food is the reason to stop by. Make sure to bring cash as credit cards are not accepted.

This was my second dining experience at Paradiso and it was just as good as the first visit. We went for a friends b-day dinner. We had the scallops for an appitezer which were cooked perfectly. Sometimes restaurants tend to over cook them. My girlfriend had the Duck which was presented beautiful which she totally enjoyed. Our friend had the special rib-eye steak which was a huge portion which she loved. I had the filet. It was a nice size with a crusted top and cooked to perfection. It is upscale and expect to be about a $50+ a person if your order a bottle of wine. All in all a great spot for upscale dining on Passyumk.

The cashier was friendly and pleasant to deal with. The frosties were on sale for half price!!! Which was TOTALLY AWESOME in the middle of one of the worst heat waves Tucson has seen since the 90s! The frosties came out quick and cool dust down and they're clean air conditioned lobby.

I loved this food cart. Food was fresh m, delicious and owner couldn't be nicer. 
Let's talk grits! BEST GRITS WVER!!!
Oh and his coffee....you must try.

Stopped by for dinner with the family last night , and sorry to say we were greeted by the women who would be our waitress , she was informative but dry and very pushy 
seemed she wanted to up the the check amount. the food was tasty but if you are hungry this is not the place to go ,for the portions are small, the initial bread basket was served (size of a small roll) and never refilled again..nor was there an offer to not form the bus boy or our waitress there were only a few table's at the time. over priced for the size of the dishes!!  ordered a pizza afterwords! ONE AND DONE!

I love love love this restaurant!  The Passyunk Avenue district is a great place to hang out, the atmosphere inside is cozy, the service is excellent and the food is delicious.  The chefs name is Lynn.. I can't remember her last name... and I've been told she's one of the best in the country (she's also the owner).  Oh.... there's also outside seating if you like "people watching" and I believe there is also seating upstairs.  My personal preference is the tripe.  If you've ever had it before, I dare you to try it here, it's the best ever.  The prices are just slightly on the high side but considering all the above it's definitely a bargain.

Service was sooooo SLOW!!! I did a take out order (mind you the food is already cooked) took them 45 min to put it in a to-go tray. The girl at the counter tells me "your pork chop will be done soon" I told her "I ordered chicken."... had to wait another 10 min to fix this error. Finally got the chicken and it was tasteless not enough seasoning. The workers are way too laid back and bring their kids in to work. They are juggling between babysitting and serving. I don't recommend this place. Poor service and the food is blah!

This is a food truck in the park, not the office building cafeteria.  Best omelette I have had in my life.  The grits are very good, they are stone ground.  It's just one guy and a tiny grill.  Cash only.  Mostly omelette, frittatas or eggs.  If you need meat or pancakes, this might not be for you today.  If you need eggs, go here now.  Downtown street parking is 75 cents per hour, limit two hours.

When i walked in the front desk ladies were very nice. However, I told both the front desk lady who went over my paperwork with me and my massage therapist Tina that my lower back was the most painful and tight and needed the most work and my shoulders were a little tight as well. During my massage Tina only worked on my shoulders and didnt even touch my lower back. I have never had a massage where they didn't massage the whole back, especially when i specified that my lower back was the major problem area. With that said, Tina had great pressure on the shoulders and did relieve some tension. I just wish she would have listened to me more because I left feeling disappointed. I also felt the front desk woman was very pushy in trying to get me to buy the package even after I said I would think about it... she asked me why I had to think about it?

Definitely agree that this is the most upscale restaurant in South Philly.  This and Le Virtu get my vote.

The food flavors and quality here are stupendous.  Many options to choose from, which makes this a date place, a parent place, a group place, you name it!

LOVE that they aren't byob.  Adds classiness for sure.

Very disappointed based on the reviews.  I ordered a single on wheat; the bread was dry and tasted like it's been on the shelf a while.  The meat was decent but rather small.  Not worth a second visit for me. Tip: order a double on regular bread, hopefully you'll have a better experience.

Paradiso is an upscale Italian restaurant on Passyunk and I enjoyed my meal there. They have impressive and tempting list of specials. We had a vegetarian antipasti and I had the gnocchi. The service was great and we were able to walk in for Saturday dinner at an early hour 6pm. 

I look forward to returing, as there were multiple appetizers and entrees that I was interested in trying (esp the sweetbread ravioli).

Awful experience in every way. They are extremely rude and curt, they didn't have my stuff ready when they said they would, they are expensive ($16 for two basic shirts and a pair of regular pants), and they wouldn't accept a credit card for an order under $20. I will never go back here.

Needed to find a hotel/motel that accepted dogs quickly around the location I was in at the time. I came across this place and decided to check in because of the cheap rates. Sadly, you get what you pay for. This motel is for if you can not find anything else.

It's "working girls" everywhere, so much that it's a sign or something to tell with room is "working." This motel is full of roaches, one of the rooms they gave me was infested with roaches. The furniture is very old, stink inside, and falls apart with one touch.

The receptionists are rude, forgetful and annoying. One woman receptionist called my room everyday asking when I was paying when I paid for a week already. Another woman receptionist flirted with ny husband everyday since the first day. She hated seeing me around my own husband. The housekeepers are also rude, forgetful and annoying. They take a loooong time just to bring fresh linen and towels.


The structure of the motel is not stable, it's on the verge of collapsing. The pool never look clean to get in. One very small grill on the premises. 

I do not recommended this motel!

This is my go to location! There is outstanding service. They are always accomidable. I had a misunderstanding on my account and a woman named Kelly went above and beyond to help me out! It's so nice when a place really just wants to help you out and make you as comfortable and worry free as possible. Many thanks to the staff especially Kelly! Keep doing what you're doing
The lamb and sausage dish was nice, so was the pork chop and very creamy gnocchi.

Top notch Italian restaurant. Upscale and great for a special occasion. I've always heard great things and it did not disappoint. 

I came here for my girlfriends birthday with a large group and we had a blast. There was nothing that was ordered that was just okay. Everyone was happy with their meal. The wine was amazing and the service was excellent. This is the kind of place where you can put your meal in the hands of the server and you'll be happy.

Reservations are necessary, but not as difficult as you might think.

I was a little skeptical when I looked at the menu for Noord online, but it is an absolute gem. The food was delicious and the service was perfect - not intrusive but we were not ignored. The restaurant is cozy but they don't jam the tables in so that you can't move around. We will be back!
Delicious, affordable, and fast. It is worth taking a longer way to my office to pick up a yummy omelette. Dylan is always willing to make you whatever you'd like and its always so good!

We arrived for our reservation at 7:30.  After a slight wait, with excellent communication, we were seated inside.  Reviews had warned us that the room is loud. The staff opened the windows about halfway through our meal which helped the noise level, but don't let that distract you.  

  Our server described the menu and style, and then suggested the tasting menu offered to parties of 4 or more.  This was a perfect suggestion, as we got to taste much of the menu.  My only critique is that we were served 2 of the crudo.  It was delicious, but a different dish would  have been appreciated.  

   The pasta course was the overwhelming favorite, and while the Bronzino and Pork Shank were delicious, the Chicken entree was the favorite of the table.  We were pleasantly surprised.   

   More importantly, the service was flawless.  Our sever(s) were unobtrusive, professional, and accommodating.  Food was thoughtfully served, prepped for 4 people to share before it left the kitchen.  Our wine glasses were never empty, which is a touch often missed in a byob.  

Thank you for a memorable night

Not your ordinary breakfast spot. It's actually a small cart in the middle of downtown Tampa with the view of tall buildings and the bay. The food was delicious especially their egg sandwich and grits. Perfect blend between great breakfast dishes at a low cost. Highly recommend checking this place out to start your day right.
The employees here are always pleasant and they take care to make sure my order is correct and never appears thrown together in a mess. Love Wendy's chili and the taco salads!!

This is my new neighborhood dry cleaner. Someone spilled beer on me big time at a Blonde Redhead show last week while I was wearing my winter jacket (they at least picked up the tab). So, despite reading some off-putting yelp reviews, off to Kim's I went! 

In 3 days, the beer smell was gone and the fabric had that nice, even dry-cleaning texture that is super nice. The price was better than any self-proclaimed organic cleaner I've ever been to and the lady who helped me was very pleasant. 

Thanks, Kim, (whoever you are)! I'll be back!
Fresh cracked pepper, delicious white cheddar, ripe tomatoes and added poblano peppers-- all melted over sizzling fresh eggs-- honestly the best frittata I have ever had. Thank you!!!

I came here with my cousin. We were just walking by and the sales person had no problem letting her try on some dresses. They had exactly what she wanted. It was nice for the rest of us, while she tried on stuff, we got water and were allowed to look around. We had gone to David's Bridal earlier and she was in tears. While the dresses are probably twice as expensive but 100 times better quality and exactly what she was looking for.
5 Stars for BEST Mall burger I've ever had.  Locally owned and friendly staff.  Don't just try the burgers.  Their other sandwiches and real ice cream shakes are awesome too!

Awesome

What a gem!

The egg sandwiches are great

Omelets and grits rock

Yelp sucks but this place is awesome!!!
Omg these grits are to die for and get resuscitated and come back for more! And the omelettes are terrific like you wouldn't believe! Get there early or get left out !
Stumbled upon this while we were visiting tampa. It's a food truck and it's easy to miss. Very friendly and the egg breakfast sandwich was fresh and delicious!

I don't even like grits but I would eat a tub full of the cheesy grits from here. The frittata is amazing too. This place makes magical food from a tiny little kitchen. If I could, I would go every day!
Easy to get to! Massages are great and worth the price... Facials, well I'll just say wash your own face for the price.

We have been coming here for over 3 years now. 

What have always gotten the Well Done Beef Brisket Pho which is exceptional and the Fresh Basil Rolls. You can't go wrong with any of these two options. We jump between a lot of entrees but our favorites seem to be "Shaken Beef/Chicken" or the Beef Vermicelli. The customer service is great however it will lack during busy times. Wether it be not refilling water to not taking your initial order for awhile. The food here is great - we have scoured Buford Highway looking for a good combo of pho and entrees. Usually you'll find one or the other, but Nam Phuong is great for both.
Breakfast here is fantastic!  Fresh ingredients are prepared on the spot, and the results are great.

Food was overpriced and hit or miss. The escargot entree was good and the burrata was okay too ( though small portions). The two entrees we ordered were terrible. The gnocchi was underdone, the peas were still hard, the pancetta non existent. My husband had the duck which was overcooked and accompanied by maple thick farro. The service also was not great. Will not return

You have seldom eaten breakfast of this exquisite order. The ingredients are expensive, the taste artfully composed with the sort of care seldom seen in today's "diners." You will have to wait a bit for the food to be prepared, and you will not regret it. No less important: while the food tastes twice as good as any diner in Tampa, it will cost you half. What a godsend is Yolk, White & Associates.

This hidden gem is outstanding. Hours are limited during the weekday mornings, but the food is outstanding. It's a one man show over the stove with a typical line for the great food. The Dylan with a cup of coffee is 5 stars! Go see for yourself!
Best breakfast in Tampa in a great location. Highly recommend the Cajun frittata and freshly ground Guatemalan coffee.
Can't beat an bagel and egg sammich like the one Dylan makes. For $6 you're getting fresh and delicious. Just look at the pic and decide for yourself. He is a cash only vendor.

Serves $9 omelettes for $6. 
Solid, fast, handmade, reasonably priced.
High quality egg based breakfasts served from a food truck for those of us Americans on the constant go. 
Dylan a.k.a "Eggman" serves a quality product with good conversations whilst he works. He actually really cares and is especially appreciative of food allergies. He doesn't make you feel awkward and makes sure to review the ingredients so you won't get sick. Delicious and filling. Gluteneers rejoice!

Delicious and quick, my wife and I both had the Opener. Perfectly cooked eggs were complimented by cheese, fresh spinach and tomatoes to make a yummy hot breakfast sandwich. Conveniently located on the river walk to fit right into our morning stroll. Dylan was very friendly and we will definitely be making a return visit.

By far the best massage envy I've ever stepped foot in. I'm from Scottsdale so I was blown away that this Tucson one was even better. Dani for my massage was absolutely astounding with great deep pressure. Cecelia was also outstanding with customer service. Kudos to the management here for overall running such an amazing spa. Gorgeous spa / environment!
The Cajun was as delicious as many reviews have posted before. As a bonus the coffee was good as well.

Full disclosure - I've only eaten breakfast in Tampa twice in my entire life. Both times were here. That said, this was some of the best brekky I've ever had, period. My fiancee and I found this spot on yelp, not knowing it was a food truck. When we pulled up to the spot, I saw the sign for Yolk, White, and Associates and we were a little disappointed but were in a rush so we said screw it and walked up.

My fiancee got a bagel sandwich - I forgot the name. I got the cajun fritatta. The food took a little longer than expected, but it's because the owner makes everything fresh. He cracks the eggs fresh, he grates the cheese fresh, he seasons the grits fresh (I think) - he cuts the bagels fresh and even brews the coffee fresh. Dylan is a guy that truly loves cooking and this is so deliciously apparent in his food. 

"The Opener" bagel sandwich was amazing, stacked perfectly high with tomato, spinach, and chedda. My fiancee added bacon because bacon. Combined on an onion bagel, this was apparently the best breakfast sanguich that my fiancee has ever had. The best part - mine, the Cajun Fritatta. Lord have mercy, this was the bomb. While Dylan freshly prepared the ingredients, I asked him, "what differentiates an omelette from a fritatta?" He explained it to me while he made the beginnings of the fritatta in cast iron, then finished it off in the broiler. 

Seasoned up with whatever he used, this was one of the best breakfasts I've ever had in my life. Side note, it also came with cheesy grits. As a disclaimer, I don't like grits. At all. I just don't mess with grits. These grits however were life-changing. Cheesy, thick, and with the right amount of spices. Eat them while they are hot! 

All in all, Dylan is a guy who has mastered his craft. If you are in Tampa and want a quality breakfast, don't let the food truck appearance fool you. This spot is gold. We went back again before we flew home out of Tampa Airport. Take my advice and go get you some Yolk, White, and Associates.

Review of the bar only.

Stopped in on a Friday night for some wine since we were at Townsend and their wine list BLOWS! They have a very good wine list at very good prices. The bartender was social and super cool. I do want to eat here but I'll certainly be back for some casual drinking.

I love this place, I am not only a client I am also a front desk sales associate here at Massage Envy. The moment you walk in to our clinic its pampering time from start to finish. Youre offered a beverage, water, hot tea, ect.. the sessions are customized to your needs, whether it be that you like hot towels under your neck, back or feet you'll also love one the many different enhancements that they offer, which are aromatherapy, sugar foot scrub or enhance Muscle Therapy. The therapist are all very knowledgeable and very talented, each one of them have special unique techniques that they use, every therapist does full body massage and each one of them specialized in different areas of the body. Massage Envy also offers Hot stone massage, prenatal massage, Heathy skin facials, back facials, and chemical peels. Its so wonderful to come in, relax and take care of yourself, give your body what it needs and loves. Love, Love, Love Massage Envy.

Had some dry cleaning here, nothing special. They do a good job and it takes normal amount of time.

The real gem about this place is the tailoring. This is the best place hands down to get alterations in the Rittenhouse square area. They worked miracles with a couple suit jackets that needed the lapel adjusted. I went to 3 separate places that all said it couldnt be done until i went to Kim's and the job they did was spectacular. I get all my alterations done here. I've had about 3 suit jackets altered, an innumerable amount of pants hemmed, and a couple other quick tweaks on other stuff, and not a complaint on one article  of clothing they've worked on.

It's not often I want to write a review before even getting the check...

Dinner at 6:15 PM on Sunday evening....Paradiso was dead empty with the exception of one table, some people at the bar who seemed to be regulars, and my fiancé and I. This place is obviously empty for a reason. The service was adequate, and the prices seemed fair at first glance. Just wait until you see the portion sizes...minuscule is the perfect word. So tiny my fiancé and I laughed when we saw them. Sad part is I enjoyed what I ate...garden salad was dressed nicely, and the entree was flavorful. BUT, nowhere near good enough to justify $20 for five small tortellini. My fiancés fish portion was even tinier and more expensive. We skipped dessert because we each wanted more than one tiny spoonful of chocolate.

We read reviews prior and some indicated good portion sizes. Perhaps they're skimping because business is slow? Who knows... Bottom line is I'm headed home to cook another dinner and we won't be going back. There are too many other fabulous restaurants in Philly (Modomio if you want great Italian).

If you're looking for great food and want to feel like you got your money's worth, don't bother with Paradiso. 

Two stars because the food was tasty and service was good. The rest was laughable.

Everytime I come to this massage envy, the staff remembers me and my life story, they are so calm and soothing and really create a great experience. The masseuses are always so great as well. I enjoy that the staff lets me know the masseuses specialities so I can make a decision based on how I'm currently feeling. I finally signed up for a membership and will definitely be a repeat customer.

Fresh salads and tasty soups. I haven't tried the sandwiches but they look good. Service is good, considering this is a lunch spot. Lines get very long (testament to the food) during the lunch rush hour, otherwise it's very quick to get what you want.

Where do I start? I'm STILL thinking about all the excellent food we had at Paradiso for dinner last weekend.
We were in town visiting family and we tried this place. What a beautiful ambiance but most importantly, the food was excellent.
We got to meet the owner and chef and after trying all the delicious plates we got, you can tell she LOVES what she does because it shows. 

As appetizers we had the warm octopus with potatoes. I'm used to eating octopus as I'm from Spain and it's very common back home and let me tell you this was cooked to perfection. The potatoes were excellent too. It's not easy to cook a potato, believe it or not, they're either too mushy or too hard. PERFECTION, trust me. The veggie board and the escargot were also to die for. Also, the olive oil that comes with the bread... Let me repeat this, I'm from Spain, I know good olive oil when I taste it and this may be one of the best (if not the best one) I've ever had.

The ricotta gnocchi had this lemon zesty flavor... I wish I had taken pictures of all the goodness we were served but I didn't want to be THAT annoying person pulling my cell phone out in the middle of a very nice dinner. The boys ordered the whole branzino and I heard nothing but great things about it too.

And of course we had to have dessert. Homemade cinnamon ice cream? Have you ever had it? I hadn't either and let me tell you, I don't care for sweets that much but EVERY single dessert we ordered was excellent. I even told everyone at the table if the owner was my mom I'd be fat because it's impossible not to eat what she cooks and it's all so good.

If you're in Philly, stop by. The ambiance's beautiful, the servers are extremely attentive and professional and everyone there including the chef and cooks in the kitchen are worth their weight in gold!
This place is impossibly good for a little food truck. The owner made some fresh, incredible food from his small menu and oh yeah, best grits ever made!

Hubby and I headed to Passyunk Avenue for "Flavors on the Avenue". Ended up shopping the craft vendors and neglecting the food (and freezing out buns off). Decided it was time to eat and thaw out. Happened to be standing in front of Paradiso, looked at the menu and was excited to see some great sounding meals on the menu. Walked in and were immediately seated. Aaron, our server came over quickly, greeted us, and gave us water and menus. When it came time for drink orders, my hubby couldn't decide between 2 wine. Aaron was able to provide beautiful descriptions of both wines, making the decision much easier as one sounded perfect for his taste. Another indecisive moment where I couldn't decide between several entrees, Aaron was able to offer 2 half pastas rather than choosing between two. I'm so glad I was able to do this because both were incredible! The one was pappardelle with mushrooms and the other was a pasta with wild boar ragu. My husband's Branzino was perfectly prepared. All portions were perfect. I saved some pasta for tomorrow's lunch and had room for dessert. Desserts did not disappoint ether! Both the Budino and the Bomboloni were quite yummy! Can't wait to go again! Thanks Paradiso and Aaron for helping make our meal one to remember!
This is a one man shop with many customers. The food is pretty good and tasty. I would've given it five stars if they start hiring more people so the waiting line is reduced.
Delicious, cheap real food. After days of corporate catering downtown, this was a wonderful find. Friendly service and a nice place to eat by the river.

If you are even mildly interested in the electric bike experience, this shoppe is well worth a visit. In a lovely area (parking in front of the store).  I spent an hour or so test driving several models before buying a fabulous ebike.  Staff is TOP NOTCH all the way. Plenty of selections, all quality!  So glad I shopped here. A real pleasure.
Amazing food and Dylan is a great guy. I once forgot my wallet and he trusted me to drop off the money the next day!

First rate in my experience. I am not particularly sophisticated but their organic cleaning far superior to the other cleaning methods I am used to. The owners are Korean and therefore a bit gruff or distant, but they warm up when they know you. I have used them for years for my daily work shirt, and they have not ruined a single one, which is a pretty good record for shirts.

update 2/17: ha ha I read some of the most recent reviews. While some of the negativity is likely overstated Mrs Kim is definitely no politician and extremely cool. I could easily see some people taking her cool responses as challenging. That said, I have continued to use Kim for my cleaning since I initially wrote my review at least one shirt washed per work day and his record is...still perfect. Many many shirts have failed but Kim has never stained or damaged a shirt (or any other garment). The only people who understand this are those men who get their shirts washed on a daily basis like I do. Kim maintains that quality by doing the shirts himself (and charging more as a result).

The only reason for 1 star is because they won't let you give no stars.
Let's start by saying that the waiter Norman was excellent. Next my Wife got the Halibut which looked like it would be 2 bites and done for me. My wife said it was good but very small. ( she does not like to criticize). Now for my meal. I got the ( Special ) Short ribs, wow, there was NO meat on this short rib. All fat and when I say All fat, I mean nothing but Fat !!! I had to send the meal back which I never do. The Waiter was very apologetic but the Manager/ Chef never came over. There is NO way that the Chef/ Manager did not know this Short Rib was all fat while cooking it and still sent that piece of FAT out to a customer (Me)...The Chef/ Cook / Manager or whatever never came out to apologize. I was so angry that I had to get up and leave My wife, Son and Daughter In- Law in theRestarauntI. I did not want to chance eating anything else after that mess.

We dined outdoors but when it started to get a bit windy, they informed us that if we started to get cold, we can move indoors. We toughed it out though and enjoyed our food. Awesome authentic Italian food with stellar service and fantastic decor.

Great little spot by the riverwalk for breakfast.  Strong selection with several ingredients I did not expect from a food 'cart'.  The food was delicious and the coffee, which I expected to be an afterthought, was full of flavor and well-prepared.  I stumbled across the place on work, but will definitely visit whenever I'm in town again.

Great new place....in the north east corner of the park by the river. 

Big fan, very friendly owner and extremely reasonable prices.

Definitely will come back, ingredients are fresh and coffee is high quality.

I used to love shopping at Old Navy - about 10/15 years ago. In the past few years, I've been getting more discouraged by this brand, and my most recent visit to the Gallery takes the cake.

To begin, most shelves and racks are disheveled. It seems like the workers there don't do much refolding or sorting - but rather stand around and gossip amongst themselves for most of their shifts instead.

The quality of clothing at Old Navy continues to get worse over the years as well. I realize that these articles all come from third-world countries, where each $10 shirt  probably actually cost Old Navy $2 to produce and transport to retail. I could barely find anything here now that wasn't 100% paper-thin cotton that was already wrinkling on the shelf.

To summarize my thoughts of Old Navy (in general) as well as this store at the Gallery: THUMBS DOWN! I went here yesterday to use my Groupon ($20 for $10) - and now I realize why such a well-established nationwide chain actually had to resort to Groupon!!
Complete deliciousness!!!!!! What an amazing find right on the Riverwalk! Best egg sandwich on earth!!!

Delicious, quick, and cost effective. What's better?! Don't let the simplicity fool you, Dylan packs a ton of flavor into his food. The classic omelet is full of fresh spinach and tomatoes and every single bite is tasty. The grits have so much flavor and a little spice to keep you wanting more. (Looking for a healthier option, asked for sliced tomatoes in place of the grits) Great pairing for a filling and lovely breakfast overlooking the river. Go get an omelet, a coffee, and grab a bench on the river walk...then take a little stroll along the water for a great morning any day of the week.

This is our go to Italian dining restaurant...nice little tip...you can order half servings at a reduced price...pasta always al dente...calamari sautéed not breaded and fried!  That's always a bonus!  Escargot and sauce with crostini a meal itself...drinks masterly mixed and served.
During the week they are open for lunch...their cheese steak is suburb as is their hamburger...wish they had lunch on the weekends!!!

This restaurant and it's staff make up the worst dining experience I have ever had. Essentially, we were not happy with the quality of the food and mentioned it to our server. After a tense encounter with the manager, both chefs came out and yelled at my family and I in front of the other guests saying they had never been so insulted and telling us to never come back to their restaurant. As a longtime employee in the hospitality industry, I was appalled at their behavior and recommend that people do not try this place. Or at least be sure not to complain when you don't enjoy your food as they will not take it well. I had to give it one star per yelp rules, however I would give it none if I could.
I dined here with a large group.  The food was excellent.  The service was top notch.  Decor lovely. Enjoyment was diminished by the noise level which left me with a headache.

NOTE: this is a food truck/cart not a restaurant. That being said, the best dang breakfast I had in Tampa. Puts those overpriced, so-called hotel breakfasts to shame. Was in town for a conference and did the yelp thing looking for a breakfast place and Yolk and Associates came up as #1. It did not disappoint. If in the area, skip the hotel breakfast and take a walk down and visit Dylan. I'm glad I did.

Seeing this place open up right next to my place of employment was a godsend, since normally I eat little or nothing at all for breakfast before this.  This food truck serves nothing but breakfast, but mainly focusing on egg products. The variations of eggs include egg sandwiches(eggs however you like them), omelettes and frittatas.  I have thus far tried several of the omelette variations, and all of them taste (obviously) home cooked, since they're cooked fresh as you order them.  The eggs are always fluffy and delicious, and each time I've ordered over-medium for my sandwiches, they came out perfect.  I also tried their "The English" english muffin with one over-medium egg, goat cheese, bacon spread and arugula, and it was downright incredible.  Other food choices offer the staples of bananas, yogurt, granola, bagels and donuts.

They also serve great coffee, drip only, all of which is either organic or specialty blends.  I really appreciated it since all I have is bulk brewed starbucks, or instant hotel swill coffee to choose from where I work, and that is just not acceptable.  The Sumatran coffee is fantastic if you like a good, bold cup.

Dylan, the owner, is very personable and friendly, and easy to talk to, and I'm more than happy to try and drum up visitors to his establishment and to support his endeavors myself by purchasing his tasty food.  If you're looking for completely non-pretentious, good, "simple food done well" type of breakfast for very affordable prices(CASH ONLY!) to get your day started off right, you can't make a better choice than to check this gem out.

Loved this place!  Stopped by on our way to Busch gardens based on the reviews and were shocked that it was just a cart in the square by the convention center.  Apprehensively approached but decided to give it a try.  SO GLAD WE DID!! Dylan was very friendly and very accommodating.  His suggestions were perfect and he happily chatted to us as we waited for our freshly cooked to order items.  I had the Dylan Frittata and my husband and son had the egg sandwiches.  The smell coming from the cart was heavenly as we happily read the daily newspaper articles that Dylan tapes to the cart windows to occupy his customers!  Totally worth waiting for-my husband proclaimed the bagel the best he had ever eaten and the frittata with the grits is a MUST.  Thanks Dylan-we will be back!!!

In a town filled with Italian restaurants, Paradiso stands out as one of the best. --Just don't expect the typical red-sauce menu. It is our go-to place for special celebrations. We have tried a variety of appetizers, pastas, and the one main we can't get enough of, the Pork Chop Milanese. We have never been disappointed. (except the night the pork chop was not on the menu!)

My parents (including my Italian mom) and I found Paradiso last year while celebrating a birthday. After that meal, we came back several weeks in a row - mostly, for the pork chop. Everything at Paradiso is outstanding but OMG that pork chop! We usually all order pasta entrees and then get a pork chop for the table to split. Last night, the waiter told us we ordered too much food, but we cleaned our plates. For pasta, the gnocchi and black spaghetti are outstanding. Make sure you also start with the frito misto and burrata. In a city full of great restaurants, Paradiso is one that should not be missed!!
If had know this place was that good I would have been here sooner. But now that I know i will make this my everyday breakfast spot. If you are a foodie, you would love this place.

Awesome breakfast frittata & sandwiches.  Great coffee, location, and cook.   

Two coffee, two large breakfasts, generous tips, $17....true awesomeness.

I was in town for just a couple of days, but I wish I had discovered this spot my first day.  I read about the grits and wanted to try it.  I was not disappointed.  The owner was very friendly, and the Cajun breakfast with grits were hot and delicious.  Along with coffee, my breakfast was $8 and twice as good as my $8 coffee and yogurt from Starbucks (in the Hilton and one block away) the day before.

This was place was fine. Not great, not terrible. Weird comments from the server, but I ate there too long ago to remember exactly what they were. Not sure I'll go back, with Fond right nearby- their food was far superior to anything I ate at Paradiso (gazpacho to start, fish for the main course). I probably won't go back.

During my second visit to Paradiso since May, I was pleased to find the food as good if not better. The service was excellent. Out server - Melissa, I think - consulted on all selections as asked without being overly solicitious. When asked her opinion it was as if she would take us in to her confidence to lend an opinion.

Two of my friends had the heirloom tomato salad and the fruit delivered a local, seasonal tart freshness. Another diner had the squash blossoms, delicately stuffed with cheese and fried. They were light and delicious with a hint of rich cheese flavor. I had the fazzoletti; al dente and perfectly dressed. 

Our entrees were short ribs, calf's liver and scallops. The short ribs and calf's liver were served over a marscapone polenta. It was creamy and savory-sweet, without a hint of graininess. The scallops were seared with the slightest hint of crunch at the corners, and tender and delicately chewy throughout. It was fantastic. 

I didn't sample all of the wines served at the table, but Melissa cheerfully brought  a few samples before a bottle was selected and I had a glass of a sauvignon blanc that was fresh and bright with a nice grapefruit nose and a lovely crisp, citrus finish. We finished with cheese.

This place is reasonably priced for the premium ingredients, preparation and presentation making it a bargain, and parking was a breeze. I would suggest this restaurant to any local foodie or out-of-towner.

Really nice place, relaxed ambiance, courteous service.

The food was very good, escargot was amazing, awesome cheese trays.

 The only issue is that the portion size was a bit smaller than I would have liked.
At first I thought it was a restaurant but to my surprise it turned out to be a food truck.   The owner was very gracious and the frittata was delicious.   A great way to start the day.

I accompanied my spouse who was in Tampa for a conference. I ate here three days in a row - did not see any reason to switch! I tried different omelets every day, asked the owner for suggestions. He was very nice, and made a great hot meal to start the day. Check it out and enjoy the nice Florida weather in the morning!

We live in the neighborhood and, after tonight, are sad we have not visited Paradisio sooner and more often.  We typically find at ourselves at BYOBs but, for no particular reason, we decided to go to Paradisio tonight and we couldn't be happier. The service was excellent - Anthony was knowledgeable & personable.  We had a tough time ordering as there were so many tempting options, but he guided us through the menu with confidence.  We ordered a great, affordable bottle of wine to accompany our meals and the bill wasn't much more than many meals we've had at BYOBs.  We are already planning our next meal there.  Definitively try the veal pappardelle.  Ridiculous.

I didn't remember to review when i first ate here-- earlier this year.  However, from then on every time I've had grits or heard the mention of grits i thought to myself "Well, Dylan has the best grits."  So i'm going to let you finish reading this review, but Dylan made me the best grits of all time!  

The mark of something worthwhile is when it clings on to memory.  Now i remember:

It was a chilly morning, strange for April in Florida.  The location is on a small patch of park, facing the water with the tall city buildings behind you.  My friend had the english, which was a small bite in my opinion, but packed a delicious punch.  My egg was delightful and well executed, but something about those grits.  It was slightly spicy which was welcomed in the morning breeze.  It was a picturesque start to a beautiful day.

Ok do Not let the fact this is not a inside restaurant defer you from eating here. Is a 11 minute walk from Marriott hotel along river walk. This is a food trailer with great food. Had frittata  andbreakfast sandwich, dark roast coffee, and a great everything bagel. All excellent. Eat here .prices very reasonable.

This place is pretty incredible! If you enjoy horses, this will be heaven for you! We came for a couple nights but could stay a week without getting bored. There are various riding options for your morning or afternoon rides, a heated pool, hot tub, game room, theater and more. The food is great and the staff members are fantastic. We came here with our ten year old and he didn't want to leave! Don't bring fancy clothes...just jeans and boots are all you need!

An unexpected find in downtown Tampa's mini concrete jungle. Thanks, Yelpers, for directing us here! It's the cutest little food stand near the river by the park, so you can sit on the benches facing the river or at one of their two cute cafe tables and enjoy a fresh breakfast and coffee, or take your breakfast to work.  

The menu is simple and simply good. There are fritatta, omelette and sandwich options with eggs, cheeses, spinach, arugula, tomatoes, and different breads: Cuban, wheat, white, bagel, onion roll. My husband got the cajun omelette that he really liked. It was nice and spicy from the sausage. I got the Opener on Cuban bread. The grits had a nice spice to it. 

Everything is fresh and freshly made, so don't expect to walk up and get a meal handed to you after you order. Take a seat and enjoy the scenery or play with your phone :)

Tips: There's parking in front and in a lot on the same block if you're not walking/working from the buildings. Everything is affordable. Only $3-4.50 for a breakfast!

Excellent breakfast and coffee.  My wife had the open sandwich and I had the English sandwich.  Great ingredients, excellent chef and good conversation.   Customer service rules at this venue.  Great place to grab breakfast on Riverwalk.

I was walked in and was asked by a cashier what do I need very rudely because I was walk toward the side of the store I asked for a plastic bag so I could put my smaller ones in it and she said their only for paying customers which I was planning on being once I could carry my things easier but she certainly changed my mind
Great location... Been in business just over two years... Friendly demeanor... Kool place...yummy

One of the best egg sandwiches I've ever had. So good, I was tempted to go back to get another one. The English muffin was toasted to perfection and buttered and that goat cheese/bacon spread is heavenly. The owner was a super friendly and cool guy. Grab a sandwich and sit on one of the benches at the river walk.

I had dinner here with my girlfriend during our weekend in Philadelphia.  We didnt plan on going here but we stumbled upoin it after our original plan was smashed.  We were glad we found it.  I NEVER order pasta when in a restaurant.  However for some reason I had the homemade gnocchi and it was unlike anything I have ever tasted.  So soft and fluffy.  Not that hard, chewy stuff you normally get.  We left very happy.  Fantastic place.  Great service as well.  I can't remember what my girlfriend had but she evern said best gnocchi ever.
Stayed in Tampa at the Sheraton for a week. $7.50 for a frittata, amazing grits and a nice cup of coffee. Small business owner doing things right, and Dylan is super friendly. Great place.
Simple, no frills, but absolutely delicious. Best egg sandwich that I have had in a long time.
On a business trip and this place was great- fast, friendly, fresh and a great value. I hope this is the start of a high quality food truck culture in Tampa.

Not that good but the beer is ok. We tried the grilled corned beef Rueben which was unremarkable and served on soggy bread. My upgrade of sweet potato fries was a bad idea. The fries were cooked in the same fryer as the fish they serve and remnants of beer batter were throughout the dish-uggghhh. We also shared a Thai chicken lettuce wrap dish. It was full of sugar and served on wilted lettuce. I asked the waitress if indeed the fries were cooked in the same fryer as the fish. She asked the kitchen and confirmed that it was so. It was not a place I would return to even though this was our second visit. The first visit was ok, not great, but ok.
Decent, but not the "WOW" I was expecting. The food was just "ok". Our waitstaff was over-attentive. Checking in with us was appreciated, but every few minutes seemed excessive.

This was our second visit to this restaurant, but it will, unfortunately, be our last. If we had just come for appetizers, then perhaps 4 stars. However, when 3 out of 4 entrees are subpar, then a 2 star rating is sufficient. The only entree up to standard was the branzino. The pasta with crab, the pasta with sausage, and the gnocchi were under-sauced with mush for pasta. Service was fine, but the waiter insisted that the chef does not willingly change the contents of a dish so choose another option. Next time we will choose another restaurant.

I was part of a group that went there for our Holiday lunch and the food was terrific!  The restaurant was absolutely lovely.  I don't think they are generally busy for lunch because we were the only ones in there for a good part of our meal.  Our server was really helpful and informative.  

Out lunch started with an appetizer of tomato, mozzarella and prosciutto- how can you go wrong with that?  The order of entrees were mixed.  I got the streak sand which and it was very good.  Some ladies went for the scallop wrapped in bacon and the comment that was made the most was that they were a bit on the salty side.  

And of course, who can go out for a holiday lunch and not get dessert?  Most of us chose the pumpkin cheesecake and it was spot on.  It was an Italian style cheesecake so it wasn't heavy at all.  It was the perfect ending to a lovely meal.  It was a bit on the pricey side but if you don't go out often, its well worth the extra cash.
John is absolutely amazing. I had the best massage I've ever had in my life.  I definitely recommend asking for him he gives the best massage.

Oh my god! This place is amazing! I wish I had discovered this place earlier-- it has the best omelets in all of Tampa! The omelet was fluffy, very simply seasoned, and with fresh ingredients! I got the classic omelet with the grits and it was filling. The grits were great too! Furthermore, the owner is super friendly, great to talk to, and accommodating. If you are looking for an amazing breakfast/ brunch experience, definetly go here. And the view is great too!

After the place I was planning on eating birthday dinner at had a 45 minute wait for no good reason (uh, no thank you!), we wandered down Passyunk until we came across this gem. Though I lived in Philly for probably ten years, I had never even heard of Paradiso (ahem, maybe it's new?). Since there was plenty of available seating, we scooted right in and made ourselves comfortable. Unfortunately, the 4th person in our party was late meeting us and the "Please refrain from using cell phones in the dining area," while a nice touch, made me a little wary of checking in with her even when I needed to. Apparently they don't really enforce the rule, but I still felt bad so I erected a menu barricade to hide behind. Ok, now the good stuff. Our servers name was Anthony and he was SO MUCH FUN! We laughed through the whole meal, which was amazing... AMAZING! I got the wagu beef (am I making that up?) which was a special. One of my best friends had the black noodles (also delicious) and my other best friend haaaaddddd..... you know, I can't remember what she had, but ALL our plates were bone dry at the end of the meal, so you know it was good! Top it all off with an apple tart with some ice cream (what the hell kind of ice cream is that? It actually tasted like apple pie ice cream, is that real life?!) and a birthday candle and I was one satisfied birthday girl!! I plan to be back many, many times.
