Service is not too bad for a busy location. Staff is nice to deal with pretty attentive. It's not 5 star but who really is? Good job guys

With so many great Chinese restaurants in Tucson, this one I won't return to. I ordered takeout tofu with vegetables. This is one of my favorite dishes to order but I was amazed at how bad it could be prepared. The tofu was broken up into little pieces,  the sauce was slimy and tasteless. My husband ordered Mongolian beef. The beef was sparse and the sauce was congealed and also without much flavor. The food was ready when promised but the server was not friendly.

I went here for dinner on a weeknight and overall it was a pleasant experience. 
We ordered the pan-fried dumplings to start, which were very good. 
As someone who usually is limited to what they can order (because I am vegetarian), the menu was a little overwhelming!  There are pages upon pages of options, so you are bound to find something that you like.

I explained to the owner that it was my first time there and asked him what I should order and without hesitation he said the Herbal Duck.
And the herbal duck I had.  It was pretty good.  

I wouldn't say that this place is the best asian food I have ever had, but I will probably go back to this place if I have a vegetarian friend visit from out of town.

Have eaten here a half dozen times over many years but only because there are very few places to order in the neighborhood. I wish I could rave about the food but it's always below average. The basic beef and veggie entrees are so void of flavor. There should be a nice rich flavorful 'gravy' but it is consistently bland and watery. The lemon and sweet and sour chicken are done as whole breast pieces which isn't as good as when they are cut up in pieces and individually breaded and fried.  Won tons are weird in that they are completely flat.  Hot and sour soup is so bland, BUT what is really weird is that the Golden Dragon on Wilmot/Speedway has KICK ASS hot and sour soup and this locations' soup  is the best in Tucson. It is obvious that the chain is   not keeping the recipes consistent around town.   My recommendation for the best overall chinese food is Ba-Dar on east Broadway.  Prices are much more reasonable too.

Really enjoyed the dim sum experience here! This restaurant is not as crazy or frenetic as the dim sum places in Orlando and boy oh boy is the food tasty!  Lots of variety and a fun time for the family.  

Leave your inhibitions as the door and try everything!  My favorites were the jelly fish salad,  the taro pastry and the tofu wrapped dumpling.  The chicken feet were yummy too! 

The service is as you would expect going to a dim sum house. Cart after cart will come to your table, just let your server know which dishes you'd like to try.  English most likely will be their second language, but that will be no impediment to enjoying tasty treats.

Great Chinese food. 

I haven't ever been disappointed by anything I have ordered from Golden Dragon. The dishes have always tasted fresh and flavorful. Great takeout chinese food!
I have been a customer for over 10 years! Always happy and love the new location!  Bill and Andrea are both very knowledgeable and are great hairstylists. I'm so happy that they are still
The hot and sour soup is the best I have had in a long time. The food is great, the restaurant is very clean and nicely decorated. My whole family was happy (which is hard to do). We will return!!
Miso soup and vegetable delight with brown rice was sooo good.
No time to write a huge review right now but best food, atmosphere, and view! in La Encantada
Good food. Good price. Always polite and helpful. Been a family favorite since we moved to Tucson in 1994.

I had dinner here on a weeknight with a large group of both vegetarians and meat eaters, and everybody enjoyed it. I actually didn't realize until I went to write this review that the restaurant is entirely vegetarian. This should tell you two things: (1) the fake meat is pretty good, and (2) I'm not good at reading signs.

Our server, who I assume is the owner, was quite the comedian. He was very entertaining, as well as accommodating of our group of about 20. I'm not sure why he didn't seat us in the upstairs dining room, which we would have filled comfortably, instead of crowding us at a bunch of tables pushed together in the downstairs dining area, but oh well. Not a big deal.

The bill was VERY reasonable.

You might not be aware that Singapore Chinese has a karaoke room. We didn't end up taking advantage of it that night, but I would definitely go back to check it out. Considering the place is BYO, it might just be the cheapest karaoke option around. Bring some friends, some bottles, and go to town.

I drove in to get the chili and cheese hot dog which were on special via my received text. The service was quick and my order accurate. The staff was very friendly. The dogs were very tasty and I would buy them again. Keep up the great work.

I've had Singapore a few times and love the place on principle, but their food doesn't really stand out. I love the fact that I can order anything on the menu without hesitation, its all vegetarian, but most of the dishes would come out taking the same.

My favorite from Singapore is the the General Tso's, but I'd probably eat my shoe in General Tso sauce if I was hungry enough. On my latest trip I had the Dim Sum and although a great bargain at $10 per person, many items were over-fried (most notably the latke/hockey puck) or just bland. You'll leave full and happy because of it, but don't go expecting anything outstanding.

Vegetarian warning: they ironically cook their tofu entrees in chicken broth, and you can taste every bite. Only complaint.  

Other than that, great service, great food, and they even cooked my pick-up order while closed. If a disgruntled vegetarian can give this place three stars, what's wrong with everyone else's reviews?

I don't understand why this place has such low reviews...but anyways my experience here and with other pet supermarkets have been superb. Have I have to choose between petsmart, petco and pet supermarket, I would choose pet supermarket all the way. 

Pet Supermarket is more high end compared to other pet stores. Reason is because they have a wide selection of premium quality dog food...and we go here to get food for our Kuma, the shiba inu. Compared to petco, who also carries Kuma's food brand, pet supermarket has it as a lower price. Other than dog food, they have a wide selection of premium cat food and an assortment of food for all of your furry/scaly/swimming/flying friends. Don't forget the assortment of toys and bones and bully sticks they have! However instead of getting toys here, its best to get toys from the dollar store as we all know they will be ripped up regardless.  

The perk about pet supermarket is that if you join their free VIP program, once you buy 10 bags of food within the year, you will get 1 bag of food for free. For us that means a saving of atleast $60 for a bag of food. And to save a bit more money, you should sign up for their email subscriptions as there are $4 off coupons or free nail trim coupons you can get.

Another perk is that they have an affordable rotational vaccination clinic. So you can immunize your companion really cheap. 

As for cleanliness, pet supermarket is really clean. There is no foul odor when you walk in, and the hardwood floors are spotless.  

I have had no issue with the staff, and whenever I bring the doge (hehe) there has been no problem whatsoever.

We went to Singapore for my birthday because of the room they had upstairs and recommendations from friends and I could not have been happier. The room was perfect for a party, complete with karaoke. They brought us so much food and it was delicious. Even the meat eaters were saying how impressed they were. The best thing about this place though are the staff and the owners. They were so accommodating to our large party and really made the night because of their great service. And it was so reasonably price for everything we received. There is no doubt that I will be back.

Ordered this for take out. Quick and fast and easy to order. Had gotten 2 Bahn Mi and an order of fresh basil rolls. Everything was exceptional. Order was ready in  less than 15 minutes and the flavors were on the money. I loved the tight packed rolls but most of all the Beef Bahn Mi had the perfect amount of sauce and the bread tasted very fresh.

Small little busy shop! They've got great Stromboli's!
I had once placed an order over the phone and when I stopped in they were quick and great at replacing me what I wanted. They have good speedy service!

This was amazing! I went with two friends and we ordered one of each, pizza, pasta, and salad. We all loved everything we ordered, but each had our individual favorites.  I have been craving that pasta again ever since I finished my very generous leftovers.  Favorite pasta in Tucson so far!
Place is very clean they have a nice selection for dogs. The staff is helpful when your not sure about something. Also they give some great tips!

PORTION SIZE IS POOR: 
This restaurant is located in the elite/upscale Catalina Foothills sector of Tucson therefore they should know not to skimp on the portion size. If you're big on portion sizes don't eat at this restaurant

It surprises me that I haven't written a review for this place when I've eaten here countless times. I've always liked Golden Dragon, it's your average Chinese food take-out joint when you're just too lazy to make dinner. My husband and I usually get ho fun, which is a very delicious noodle dish. We accompany it with kuo-teh, which is in fact just pan fried gyoza/dumplings. They're very tasty and the sauce that comes with them is delicious. I usually pour the left over on my noodles. I had just recently ventured outside of my noodle comfort zone and tried some walnut shrimp. Though pricey, I would buy it again. It's so good! The candied walnuts were perfect. We've only dined in once so I can't really comment on their restaurant service, but take out is the way to go. If you're feeling lazy, I say hit this place up for some good ol' white box.

I loved this restaurant!  Although I'm admittedly biased *towards* fake meats since I'm an omnivore who hates the texture of beef.

My boyfriend and I came here based on reviews on Yelp.  We got the dinner special and ordered mango shakes, which was way too much food for us.  The shakes were delicious and tasted really fresh.  Dinner was only $12.50 per person and came with crispy noodles, soup, and three pieces of dim sum.

We went out at an odd time in the afternoon, so the restaurant was pretty quiet and empty, but the guy I chatted with briefly (owner?  manager?) was really friendly.  Can't say I understand what all the little paper hearts are about, but the decor is adorable =)
The holy grail of food truck pizza! Stumbled upon it and my husband and I couldn't be happier. We will be strolling back around very soon!

Went there this morning and was very disappointed.  Had to ask for a straw for my drink, and upon checking my bag to see if everything was there, I noticed that half of my food was missing.  Then to top it off they gave me three small bags.  Why?  Couldn't they just give me a bigger bag.

My boys favorite place very family friendly we eat chicken lo mein, orange peel chicken, Mongolian Beef, fried duck, General Tao, kun poa chicken or shrimp
All entres cooked fresh

Okay to put it out there, I'm a huge meat eater.

You know how they say that 1/3 of your plate should be meat?  Well, it's usually the opposite on mine.

So my friend, who hates the thought of meat, thought that it would be fun to try dim sum.  She was ecstatic.  And then she found out that her dim sum options were quite limited.  She was sad.  Then she found this kosher restaurant.  She was happy again.

The service was really good and the chef explained everything in laymen terms for our party of three.  We took her advice and got the dim sum platter.  The food wasn't that good.  Everything left a pasty feeling in my mouth and the tea was pretty bad too.  My vegetarian friend didn't like the food either..

This place should get five stars for its service (but that may have been because we were the only customers there) but I personally thought the food was terrible.

I ate a pork bun after we left.
This place has forgotten part of my order 3 times in a row...this is the last time it happens to me....Do yourselves a favor...Don't go to this place...It's a joke.

I would give this Sonic five stars, but they're just so slow.  They are always friendly and the food is usually top-notch.  I only got a pair of old jerkey dogs one time, but that kid was new and probably didn't realize he was supposed to change those out.  Other than the one time, my order has always been fresh, hot, and delicious.  Also, they hired one extra person who comes out and serves people in the drive-through line now, so it no longer takes ten or fifteen minutes of waiting behind that lady with the ten kids.

first off, the food here is delicious and relatively cheap. the owner is always here and he is a real joker. seriously! my friends and i have knocked on the door after they just closed and he opened the restaurant up for us! totally awesome. the birds nest is good and the spicy "chicken" and dumplings are always a good bet. 

second, which people don't know is that this place has KARAOKE! yes!!! it's true kiddies. i have been to many parties upstairs where there is a private room so your peeps can eat and SING KARAOKE!  good food and depending on the pipes on your friends, good tunes! :)

also, for the upstairs room, it is BYOB. they supply the stem wear and ice, bring the soda pop, etc. it is always a fun nite and a good party place. just call and book in advance. that way you can feel so VIP. if it is a bday party, they have the video/karaoke machine that the owner will set up to have the bday songs play so everyone can sing along. also during the songs, it has on the screen "have a good time." lovely. instructions to have a good time. ah, asian culture. gotta love it. also, the pictures do not match the songs. so be prepared to see scenes of fish while singing songs from mamas and the papas. 

also, while there, the owner will tell you all if you have a chance on american idol.

with this wicked cold windy weather, what better way to warm than with some hot won ton soup, crispy noodles and your friends cranking out the lines to sappy ballads or robert palmer all done beautifully to Muzak and casio notes. it is unbelievable on so many levels. i always have fun here and my power pellets are always restored to full due to the large portions. uh-huh.
I'll probably try again, but I've been twice and I can't say I've yet to enjoy their menu. Maybe a shake or two of salt would help their tuna salad and mac and cheese.

I've never dined in here -- always take out, but they've got the best hot and sour soup I've had in town. They're super fast and I've never had to wait at all. We've tried a variety of their entrees and everything has been good. They're our go to for Chinese.

Yuck!  We ordered a staff lunch.  Which included a variety of menu choices.  The consensus was that the food was not good.  My Mongolian Beef was so watery, poor quality beef, full of grizzle fat.  The beef was not your typical crispy texture.  The sauce was watered down.  Lacking flavor.  Not only was I disappointed, but order placed for most of us was lacking on quality and flavor.  No more orders for us.   I hope!!!

Heard that this place closed!  IT was a bastion very old school kosher place in Philly.  It wasn't accepted by the strictest holders of kosher laws but I enjoyed it.  Pretty sure it's closed......you should call them!

I organized a work Holiday party here and the owner was SO helpful! We took the big room upstairs and managed to squeeze in over 20 people. We did all-you-can-eat dim sum and the food just kept coming! We had brought our own beer and wine the staff was AWESOME about providing glasses, clearing dishes and just generally being helpful. 

While I think that some of my workmates were a bit freaked out about fake meat (especially the chicken leg that has a fake bone in it) we had a great time. AND we blasted out some karaoke hits after lunch!

We pick up from this place all the time and eat there. Occasionally we get delivery. Delivery had said 90 min so we called and the phone number is now disconnected. 90 minutes at this point had passed. My boyfriend had to go there and the food was not even sent out. This is on a Tuesday night. This place although the food is okay service is terrible. Last time we ate there service took way to . I NEVER write reviews but people should definitely be aware of their poor service.

Too much soya sauce in mangolian chicken
Only spice was the salt itself.

Veg low mein and chicken fried rice too bland

I would say flavorless food

Ah, pet stores... I am a sucker for all of them. This is not my favorite pet store in town, but I tend to pass it frequently,  thus I stop by.
It is smaller than many pet stores, which has advantages and disadvantages. 
One major advantage is you can run in and pick something up quickly and usually exit quickly. Convince is a definite plus.
I have found some staff very knowledgeable and other that can't tell me why the same product varries dramatically in price.  There is a somewhere limited inventory and usually only 1 cashier. Your pick convince or time lost?
What's a girl to do? I prefer convince & sales, so it is hit or miss for me.

This was the 2nd time we ordered take out since it's the closest in our area.  This was the 2nd time we were disappointed.  EVERYTHING is bland!  It's monochromatic bland slime.  The beef is colorless, the pork almost looked like tofu, the chicken was dry & tough, the Lo Mein was as thick as a straw.  Mix in some higher prices & you're in for a disappointment.  Never again.  You've been warned.
This place is amazing!! One of my top 10 restaurants in Tucson because of the amazing server, Phuoc!! Always delivers the best customer service and makes me look forward to going back!!

Very good food.  I've been several times.  One of the first times I went, I got the $10 dim sum sampler, and I haven't gotten anything else there since.  It is such a good deal, and the dishes included are so tasty.  I can never finish all the food, which means I get to enjoy it later.  I give it 4 stars because it doesn't blow me away, but it is really good and affordable.

Food tasted fine but I got the worst food poisoning of my life after eating here a few days ago. I am sure it wasn't from anywhere else as I hadn't eaten in a while since, and my friend who I ate with also got sick. I went to the ER and was vomiting blood for about two days. My stomach is still weak and I am just getting back to eating solid food again. Just be careful eating here.

The people here are nice always helpful but they take forever for the smallest things, especially at night! They can't even fix the volume problem with the speakers. Every time the talk it sounds like they are screaming at us. 

Even though they aren't the best, I still tip them because they all work very long hours. Not a lot of people apply to Sonic which makes it harder on them. Tip your waiter or waitress. They will be very grateful!

I haven't eaten here in years. And to be honest I couldn't really remember the experience. But today we decided to go here again. The lunch menu is wonderful. Quite a few options, with soup, entire and what they called fried rice. So much food for under $6.00 that we both needed boxes. Staff was very nice as well. We will definitely come back soon.

Rated on a scale of fast food or course. My order is always accurate and the food is occasionally transcendent with everything being perfectly hot, delivered quickly, etc. It is always at least pretty good and 2 times out of 3 you will get everything hot and cooked to order. Note to Sonic: just cook everything to order and synchronize it to be served correctly and hot for any customer that isn't hurrying through the drive through. Don't make the customer ask, just do it right every time. You may waste a small amount of food but you will have better repeat business... don't be unpredictable.

Singapore is great! For me, it is a very close second to Kingdom in terms of food. Very similiar.
I like the Moo-Shoo dishes the best, however, at Singapore, you can't go wrong with what you order. The lunch specials are dirt cheap. Cheaper than McDonalds, just about.
The owner is a very nice man. 
The only small negative is their credit card policy. They have a $10 minimum. This is in strict violation of the agreement/contract they signed with Visa/MasterCard. Minimums are not allowed. Got dinner there once and had to buy like three cans of soda to make it up to $10. Lame. Bad business practice. Unethical. I understand, but...

I've waited almost 20 minutes for one cup of French Vanilla Coffee and when i finely said something about it the manager said everybody is called in order. I've watched several people get coffee that was in line behind me. I do give props to the cashier she spoke up and said she forgot.

Here's what I liked; 154, golden lions head. Ask for spicy. They're really light on spice. Potato latke is amazing if you like fried food. I didn't like the scallion pancake, but niece did. Try crispy noodle in chill bean, singapore fried rice noodle and spicy bean curd. DON'tGET FAKE DUCK! PLEASE. Trust me. Fried rice not so good--oily! I liked the staff. Family. Really nice. And good prices still. Clean as a whistle..hard to find in chinatown....trust me on this. I've seen truly remarkable things that would make you stop eating food prepared by restaurants.

Am so excited about the new Starbucks at 3400 Civic Center Blvd.  It is truly like a coffee shoppe that is independently owned, not part of a major corporation.  The staff are incredibly service oriented.  It must be the test they pass to get hired!!!  One of the women asked me to call her ahead of time so she could save a pumpkin scone for me!!!!  And I plan to do that!  Friday after I see the doctor, my treat is to go to Starbucks, have the pumpkin she saved for me  along with a café ole!!  Could not be happier!!!!!

I've heard people rave about this place for months, so I was pretty excited to eat here.

Walk in:  icky atmosphere.  pink plush, stuffy, cluttered, eww.

Sit down:  pobrecita de la mesera no hablaba ingles.

Eat:  I asked the owner? to recommend something good off of the lunch menu, which ended up being some tofu concoction.  I'm a vegetarian, so I've had a lot of tofu done many ways.  what ended up on my plate was tofu and vegetables smothered in the most foul tasting, eu-de-dirty-socks sauce i have probably EVER had.  frown face.

my expectations were so high.

maybe i should've ordered one of their mystery "meat" dishes.

i won't be back anytime soon.
AWFUL!! Was quoted 45 mins for delivery and it took over an hour and it was cold!! The orange chicken is basically a blob of orange goo!!! DONT GO HERE!! Awful!!!

please. look no further.
if you want to die happy, or at least pretend to indulge in your last meal, Singapore is the place to go.
after eating here, i find it hard to imagine ever going to any other chinese/dim sun restaurant in philly.  ..ever.

Highlights: 
All Vegan, All Kosher, BYOB, Family-owned, two paintings of young jewish boys, Karaoke, Efficient & Witty Servers, and if that wasn't enough, it's Cheap!

My Experience: 
we celebrated my friend's birthday upstairs where the karaoke set awaited us. poorly translated songs like "pet your pussy" were, well, hilarious.  Here, $10 is a curse and a blessing.  it gets you a savory soup to start and endless rounds of ridiculously delicious dim sun.  the plates just kept coming and coming--trust me, i tried, you can't finish.

Favorite Moment: 
a tie between seeing the look of ecstasy on my meat-eating friend's face while biting into a "chicken" drumstick AND owner Peter Fong singing along to classic rock karaoke with us.


i still don't understand why there weren't more vegan hipsters bowing before the singapore steps.
Fast food, but good fast food. Service has gotten much better. Very friendly and timely.

Andrea continues to impress me with her ability to transform my look! I have baby fine hair that is almost see through!!! Andrea doesn't judge me for having the whitest of white people hair and when I leave, it appears that I have actual grown up hair. She is a great colorist and stylist! Check her out!
Sonic is always my go-to when I want a late night snack. However with the new hours, I guess I won't be able to make my midnight runs to Sonic anymore :(

Worst customer service. We used to come to this okay often for brunch, but our most recent experience was very unpleasant. My fiancé went in to pick up a to go order. He ordered us both croissant sandwiches and asked for Swiss cheeses on top which they charged him for but did not do. When he got home half way through his sandwich he tasted something funny  turns out the styrofoam box had melted into his sandwich. When I looked at mine it was the same thing. He went back to ask them for his money back and they refused to work with. They didn't even apologize. I'm sorry but when I spend $40 on two breakfast sandwiches I expect a much higher quality in my food. The owner was extremely rude as well as all the employees in there. For someone operating a local business that is not the way to run it. I will never recommend this business to anyone, but instead will warm people to stay away from terrible customer service.

The restaurant I went to (there are 3 of them) is in a shopping mall at Swan and Sunrise near the Safeway but a bit south of it.  They do a lot of takeout but we dined in.  I've eaten here a few times and it is decent food.  I like their egg rolls that have a nice crispy outside.  I've had a few different dishes including cashew chicken and the chef's recommendation of pork with satay sauce.  They will prepare it mild, medium or very spicy.  I think medium is best as the mild doesn't have a lot of flavor.  The interior is dated and the seats in the booth are lumpy but service is always quite good.

I love this place. I eat often here either at the restaurant, as pick up or delivery. They always have great service and the food is delicious. I have order pretty much 60% of the menu but my favorite is beef lo mein.  Also a good tip if you go online to their website they sometimes have coupons for take out.

Never had anyone be so detailed and take their time to get it right. Andrea is great to talk to, really good at cutting hair, and gives a fantastic shampoo massage. Hard to beat considering the price point

Ever since this Starbucks opened next to The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia and the Perelman Center for Advanced Medicine, I have been utilizing it as equally as the other coffee options nearby (Dr. Coffee in CHOP, Gia, etc.). Overall, this Starbucks has been both a blessing and a curse for coffee lovers. Here's why:

The blessings:
-It's Starbucks! You can use your Starbucks card and get your favorite drinks (and get rewards) without walking all the way to 34th and Walnut (next nearest location). Great for people working in the hospital system.
-Great ambiance--a decently sized seating area in typical Starbucks-style decor (dark wood chairs/benches, artful coffee-referencing wall art) which I have never seen full, meaning that if you were not working in the hospitals, this would also be a decent place to get work done or meet up with people

The curses:
-It's Starbucks! Bad for your wallet and other coffee places with the good old fashioned punch cards probably have a better rewards system for loyal customers
-It is exceptionally busy, service is decent but mistakes are made on orders occasionally (mobile or in-person)
-Did I say that it is exceptionally busy? Service is slow because of the huge influx of mobile and in-person orders (the line can be out the door literally during peak hours)
-Even when it's not exceptionally busy, the service is occaisonally slow (barista dependent)
-From a coffee quality standpoint, it is pretty much on par with all other Starbucks'; you could probably find better coffee elsewhere, but there aren't that many other options in the area

Overall impressions:
-Avoid peak times (6-8 AM) and sometimes afternoon shift change
-Mobile order unless your drink is complicated (saves you the wait and you actually inadvertently "skip" people in line based on when your mobile order is put in)
-Be prepared for some drink mismatches and mishaps no matter how you order and either roll with it or be prepared to wait some more for a re-made drink

I've ordered from them countless times before because they are always quick to deliver and the food doesn't disappoint. This time I ordered for pick up and it was ready in 15 minutes. I got home and realized it was the wrong order. I called and they said they would deliver the right order ASAP. It was true, in 15 minutes they were at my door with the correct item. I am so impressed! I will continue to order from here! Also their shrimp fried rice and Kung Pao Shrimp are my favorite....

Location- Convenient to Penn hospital
Service- Slow, do NOT go here if you are in a rush! 
The store is fairly clean, some of the staff is nice. 
Product- Not the best Starbucks I've ever been to but standard!

Visited Singapore Kosher Vegetarian the other day, Im a first timer. We were in the area and needed some lunch, This wasnt our first choice, but my wife had said it had been years since she was there. So we decided to try it. When we first came in the waitress greeted us and sat us down with menus. A few minutes later she came back and took our orders. There was a lunch special for 7.50 Your choice of soup: wonton, shark fin or miso, white or brown rice and an entree. Entrees were all vegetarian, so we tried the following: (faux) General Tso's Chicken and (faux) Peking Spare Ribs. 

The soup arrived first, the miso was so-so, the shark fin tasted better. It had long translucent noodles and a thick hearty broth. A few minutes later the food came out. We thoroughly enjoyed it, pretty decent sized portions, great taste, and it wasnt overflowing with sauces. We ended up taking a to-go box, to be honest I was stuffed. 

Several other groups of people came, and there was a take out order. I thought the food wasnt bad at all. It said it was certified Kosher, and there were Hebrew documents hanging on the wall, along with pictures of famous philiadelphians, including Governor (then mayor) Ed Rendell.

I went here with my girlfriend and we left stuffed, happy, and no less poor than we were when we walked in. I got mock chicken and beef in a bowl made of crispy noodles and, as a relatively recent convert to the meatless ways of life, I can say that I gave the tofu creations a double-take. 

The seasoning is the key here, along with some crafty tofu cooking. Nothing is overcooked, as is often the case with tofu and mock-meat dishes, and the atmosphere was cozy, with a mix of families, friends and couples. 

My girlfriend had the "shrimp", which, incidentally, tasted inexplicably like shrimp. The mango shake is awesome, although it could have been a bit colder.

The service was very friendly and very fast, and we're excited to return soon to sample more of the selections available on their mind-bogglingly massive menu.

Peter, the owner, is lovely and there is a private dining room upstairs for larger parties, but all the food taste the same. Xu Xing (sp?) on Samson and 15th doesn't have supervision, but it is vegan and sooooooooooooo much better!

I just got back into town from NY,  I'm looking forward to getting another hair cut from Andrea.  The cut, conversation and shampoo all made for a great experience .  I dig hair cuts that look more like I got a haircut a week or two ago.  Not many other stylists (that I've been to) can really pull that off with wavy somewhat crazy hair like mine

Ordered a vegetarian Lunch Special to go.  By the time I arrived less than 10 minutes later, the food was packaged and ready!  Vegetables were cooked perfectly (a bit firm, not soggy) and the sauce was delicious, not too salty nor smothered in soy sauce.  

For $7 my lunch included egg flower soup, lightly fried rice and a vegetable mix.  The reason I gave 4 stars is because there are only two choices for non meat eaters (mixed vegetables or bean curd ... I would have liked garlic broccoli).

I like the ambience as the restaurant is always clean and nicely decorated in a modern style. I've eaten here a few times and the food has been consistently delicious and the service has been professional, quick and efficient.

This place continues to make great food! The prices aren't actually too much higher than other Chinese restaurants, that is unless you decide to order the duck. Everyone that works here is very polite and friendly. When I make special requests, they honor them. The owner (who works from this location out of the three they have) has a unique life background so if you see him be sure to ask him about it The noodles they use for their lo mien dishes is very tasty and filling. The string beans with garlic is dynamite! Add a little bit of sauce to your rice and you get a decent kick. I don't use soy sauce but use some of the leftover sauce-gravy on it. They can still hash out a decent egg foo yong with gravy and mushrooms. The cashew chicken can use a little more flavor, and the soup is a little too bland. 

They definitely give you a lot for you buck. As with many other Chinese take-out, they pack so much into those boxes. Don't feel like you need to eat it all in one sitting; this food makes for great leftovers. 

This establishment recently was rated 'excellent' by the Pima County Department of Health, and I can see why. A caring staff combined with fresh food makes getting food here an enjoyable experience.

A-freaking-mazing!
The "New Year" soup is the best, when they have it.
Gen Tso and dim sum are very good as well.
This is the only place I'll eat Chinese food from. The food is very good, large portions, decent prices and you can call in your order and have it ready by the time you get there!

Definite YUM.  I'm not a vegetarian, but I love my veggies and tofu.  Singapore Vegetarian is dirt cheap, has an incredibly vast menu, and service was good.

Highlights were the broccoli w/ golden needle mushrooms (I was expecting lots of broccoli, few mushrooms...  But we got clusters and clusters of the delicious stewed mushrooms) and the taro duck (crispy, great texture and taste).  We got a few other dishes that paled in comparison (mostly sweet + sour stuff).

Veggies, veggies, veggies...and seitan and tofu...

That's what you get here in so many different ways it makes one dizzy. The SG and I stopped in for the first time and spent a good 15 minutes looking through the menu, as for him- the true vegetarian- the choices were endless. I'm just along for the ride.

And a good ride it was- fake chicken satay, fake chicken szechuan, and pekan golden fish ( that is not a misspelling- right off the menu). The fake fish thing was my choice- the "fish" were shaped like tiny goldfish made of taro, potato, water chestnuts and fried. A pea made the fish eye and carrots for the tail. At the very least, the food is fun.

It was truly, basic chinese with the same flavors, just without any kind of meat. 


I would go again.

The staff as a whole isn't bad but there's one rotten apple. Maybe 2 at this Starbucks. I'm new to the Starbucks world so it's pretty inconvenient when I don't know the name of an item and I'm confronted with an attitude by the cashier. Another incident with the same girl happened when I told her I wanted my cookie warmed and she turns around and throws my cookie in a frisbee motion into the warmer. She then take the cookie out and puts it with the mobile orders. Meanwhile I'm sitting there for ten minutes waiting for my cookie, running late for work. I ask her is it done, again with attitude she tells me "I been out that cookie over there." So now it's no longer warm. Fast forward. I come in a week later. She loudly tells her co worker she thought I was gay. I call corporate at this point, they've done nothing. I message them weeks later to see what's going on, they wrote back saying they didn't forget about me. This girl still runs the register. Just two days ago I go to buy a green tea lemonade with a co worker who's new to our site. She gets into an argument with him. She then says she's gonna get her brother to come up to the location for us but sends her giant son out to our table 30m later who tried to fight me on the side walk! I call corporate again. Still waiting for a reply and I've gotten nothing yet. Today this same girl takes a picture of my coworker while he sits on a bench at work. I'm guessing to send to whoever she getting to come up to the location. I feel as though I have to carry my firearm to work now because of a bad seed at a Starbucks. Starbucks obviously doesn't care about complaints. I've tried to do the right thing. But who knows! She may have already taken my picture! I don't know what's in stored for me. But I have a family I have to see everyday and night and I'm going to do what I have to to make sure I make it home. Starbucks should be ashamed of themselves for allowing a mother and son to work together and for them to have this kind of character behind their registers.

My wife and I had not been to Victor for more than 21 years, before we were married. We have lived in DC for the last 16 years. We went to celebrate our 21st anniversary and our visit exceeded our expectations. We knew that the staff all sang opera (or in one case a selection from My Fair Lady), and they were all terrific. Our server, whose name I don't have in front of me (but who comes from Havertown and went to Temple University) was terrific. She was attentive but not intrusive and genuinely seemed to enjoy making our visit memorable. The icing on the cake was our dessert that we ordered, an awesome zambaglione, she topped with a candle, called the room's attention to our anniversary, and played an Al Jolson waltz, inviting us to take the floor, which we did. 

My experience with Victor both past and present as to cuisine is mixed. My wife had a seafood picante which she really liked. We enjoyed an excellent Italian wine, wonderful caprese, and the incredible dessert. My veal picante had a bit less flavor than I would have liked but was still very good. Another nice touch was lots of Italian bread with the requisite oil with basil for dipping, but also butter for the oddballs like me who prefer it.

All in all it was a very memorable evening, thanks to our wonderful server and the overall ambience. We look forward to returning. Another note is that prices were reasonable. Most entrees were in the low $20's and even the best steak was only about $36. We appreciated the specials, which included our dessert. This is a wonderful place to let your thoughts wander across the sea to Italy, to enjoy your meal slowly in the Italian way, and if you just happen to go on your anniversary, drop a hint and enjoy an anniversary waltz.

This is the worst Starbucks I have ever frequented. On average it takes 15mins to receive your order. The preparation of the drinks are inconsistent. You can order the same drink everyday & get a different drink. They do not respect people with allergies. The manager took my order and not properly ring it up or prepare it. They staff except for  two individuals have poor customer service skills and are rude.

Their appetizers and dim sum are great. My favorites include the Singapore potato latkes and Singapore satay. With entrees, it's hit or miss. 

Definitely skip the Spicy Chicken Curry and Pork strips with spicy garlic sauce. It's a pile of gross mess disguised as vegetarian food. All I can say is it's all yuck. Something you might consider dressing up as for Halloween. What's good was the sweet and sour spare ribs. The gluten ribs also have fake bones (made from taro), fried in a crispy batter and finished in a bed of sweet and sour sauce.

I think next time when I do come back, I'm gonna stick with ordering a few appetizers instead of their entrees.

Szechuan duck was beyond awful.  sauce didn't resemble any szechuan sauce I have ever had -- more like a bottled watery sweet and sour sauce.  
i threw it down the disposal, inedible and quite expensive.

We came here mainly for the dim sum and were expecting cart-style dim sum. This is not the place for this. The dim sum sampler is just a bunch of appetizers already chosen for you.

Even though we didn't get what we were expecting, all the dishes were delicious! They have some Singaporean home made hot sauce which was also different and amazing too! 

Ordered General Tso's chicken (fake meat), Eggplant and 2 dim sums. We had four people and 2 dim sums was a lot. All the meat is made of tofu. I thought the chicken drumsticks were so cute in design. 

Also, service was great! (which is rare in Philly Chinatown restaurants). 

The only bad thing was the dumpling sauce tasted bad. But seriously never went to a Philly chinatown restaurant that had one great tasting thing after another! 

Would definitely come here again and again and again even though I live an hour away from Philly. Definitely recommend!

I was very anxious about trying acupuncture for the first time and Chris really put me at ease. He takes the time to listen to your needs and address both physical and psychological issues. I was experiencing muscle pain and SO much stress so I decided to give acupuncture a try. I am amazed by the results! It has changed my life. Chris is patient and gives his full attention to you and bases his practice on a unique individual level. His office is relaxing and I always look forward to each session with him!
Excellent food and great delivery. If youre in the area and looking for chinese, this is your place.

I've been traveling a lot lately, and this was the very best shuttle service anywhere!! Requesting the ride from the airport to the hotel was super easy (as was requesting the return trip), and they were even early to pick me up from the hotel. Very affordable and reliable option, but beyond that, the driver was SUPER friendly (even remembered that i was in town for an interview when he picked me up for the return trip), and the rides were really enjoyable.  I highly recommend this shuttle service!

We order take out here on occasion and the food is fresh.  There is typically a wait so plan to order an hour in advance of when you want to eat.  They are very conscious of our food allergies, which many places are not even when informed.  They have brown rice as a healthier, which you can substitute in rice dishes.  A great choice for the whole family.

Super busy location right next to CHOP and HUP. Often packed between shifts at both hospitals, so be prepared to wait 5-15 minutes. A few times, I have bypassed this location based on the snaking line inside and nearly outside. When I have ordered, the coffee-based drinks and offerings are pretty much on par with other Starbucks locations. With such high-traffic, the cleanliness of this store suffers as well. Not sure how the employees can really address this. They have seemed super busy when I have been there. I think most people who go here love Starbucks products and are willing to put up with the lines and lack of cleanliness around the store. As a plus, sells the Starbucks Reserve brand coffee.

I really like the selection and variety here for my cat and my dog. I never have an issue finding what I need and they even carry raw food for my dog which is a plus. I frecuente this store and am in their rewards program which is so helpful with discounts, coupons and freebies. They have a grooming salon and have shot clinics which they post about in front of the store. My only concern is customer service. I go in once a month and stock up on items and food for my cat and dog and the last few times as I'm checking out, there seems to have been few employees or none checking the front register, but I've been left waiting to pay and having to track someone down to ring me up. Other then that, I still visit, just hope the customer service improves or I come on a day with more employees to help me.
Wonderful. Steamed options at request. Dining Out for Life Regular.

i am skeptical of these chinese veg places where the menu is almost all fake meat.  so when I went to singapore, i imagined that it would be very difficult to explain that i wanted vegetables and no fake meat.  but the owner understood right away and when we told him that we wanted spicy noodles and vegetables, he brought us two delicious dishes that fit the bill and spicy sauce on the side.  food was a bit oily, but delicious.

i was shocked to see a pizza truck turn the corner, i havnt seen one since i was a boy in the 70's ,i stopped ordered a fresh one, which he put in the oven, he drove around the neighborhood to sell slices and 10 minutes late he came back with mine fresh out the oven.And boy was it good !! it brought back so many good memories too !! i wish we had one here in Mayfair.

Wasn't awful but also lacked flavor. We got the vegetable lo mein, which only appeared to have mushrooms and onions in it (and had huge noodles which I was not a fan of); chicken and broccoli, which was in a thick white sauce that had no flavor; and vegetable egg rolls, which were actually tasty. And I thought for portions we received it was very expensive at $25. The following morning my stomach was upset from the food. We won't be back and will drive to Chengs Beijing or just buy a PF Changs frozen meal next time we are craving Chinese (as the portion size would be the same and it has more flavor).

I eat here often and love the food.  We always get the chicken lettuce wraps to start, which can feed one person easily by itself.  We also love the sczechuan shrimp and Mongolian beef.    They have several TVs and sports are on so you can still watch the late game on a lazy Sunday night.   I have read several reviews on here and I have never had a bad experience.   I would have given five stars, however, I am a Chinese food snob so I reserve five stars on Chinese for truly exceptional Chinese food.   Golden Dragon is a bright spot in the restaurant starved foothills area.

The food was convenient, but, they charge you to deliver. I am a great tipper, but, get irritated at nickel and diming.  The food was good, but, pricey. We ordered for dinner and I didn't realize how large the portions were, so, the portions were commiserate with price, but, I wasn't told over the phone that I wasn't ordering a combo, so I was a bit surprised when everything was priced separately. I.e, rice, egg roll, etc. I wouldn't have ordered it all if I hadn't been asked....hence, thinking it was a combo. 

It is convenient location wise, so, I will likely order again.  The food is good, but, not great.

Had a yen for good old-fashioned Chinese and decided to try the Golden Dragon on Sunrise based mostly on proximity. Became suspicious when the bag of takeout smelled so bad on the way home I had to open the windows. Downhill from there. Fried shrimp were really greasy and tough (yes, tough...) Broccoli and bok choy looked diseased. Rice was gray. Sauce for shrimp was like fruit punch thickened with cornstarch. We put it all down the garbage disposal and five hours later I'm still spraying the kitchen with air freshener. Fortune cookie said I have a good sense of humor. Didn't think that was funny.

The order person answered & I literally thought it was a robot because the person who answered was so perky. Nope, just a guy named Gabriel, that seemed like he enjoyed what he did. He brought out the order & was just as pleasant & conversational. Just wanted to leave a review about the great job he did.

My boyfriend pushed for this place, after I wanted to go back to New Harmony. I should listen to him more often. Shh. Don't tell him.

We ordered a bunch of appetizers (Dim sum?) and split an order of sweet and sour pork. Also, I had a mysterious coughing fit, so we ordered green tea.

I loved that there was no mock meat in the veggie buns, and they were still delicious. Also, the homemade hoisin sauce was pretty awesome. (The duck sauce was homemade too and great!) The Singapore latkes were also a stand out for me, and are something worth trying. The curry dumplings reminded me of samosa. The only disappointing dish was the scallion pancakes, which were too doughy and tasted like oil.

The sweet and sour pork freaked me out. It was so realistic that I was certain they were lying about the meat content. After a few minutes, and some reassurance, I was able to get past it, and simply enjoy the deliciousness. We were full from the many appetizers, so we ended up taking most of the pork home. I ate all the leftovers and didn't share a bite. 

I loved the loose leaf green tea, and entertained/embarrassed my boyfriend by claiming I could read my tea leaves. 

The server, who I think was an owner, was so sweet. When a young boy asked where the bathroom was, she jokingly told him it was outside. I think he believed her for a second. The cook (also owner?) hand delivered all of the food to our table, which was a nice touch.

PS- The tablecloths look like bed sheets. Something worth noting.

These guys are awful.  Their "managers" are worse. And their prices are almost double compared to amazon. 

I would recommend ANY other pet shop.

If you like Starbucks drinks then there is no issues since they almost always take the same no matter the location. 

This location is smaller but has excellent use of space. 
The staff is extremely helpful. 
I find the wifi to not be very good here but that is the only downside. 

Also usually very crowded

I get really irritated with stupid little fees.. Extra delivery charges when it's not that far away or the coupon is only for dine in..or print out the coupon? Really... That's annoying. There are 2 other Chinese restaurants in the vicinity that WANT my business. I'm a working professional and sometimes carry out and delivery is a priority. Stop nickel and diming and telling people to print out a coupon..you're supposed to be easy and convenient. They almost always forget the fried rice upgrade. But don't worry they won't forget to charge you for it.   But the Food is good. Not anything crazy.. id prefer panda express if they'd deliver

My boyfriend is getting chemo at Penn so I ate some meals here. I was surprised the breakfast sandwich I ate (egg, gouda and bacon) was actually pretty yummy. The chicken artichoke flatbread on the other hand was awful. I took one bite and threw it out. It had a fridge off-taste. I also ordered a peach green with lemonade and this wasn't good. I don't like the mint taste in the peach green and what was I thinking adding lemonade when I really dislike Arnold Palmers. I spilled it all over myself and she was nice enough to make me a new one. She also let me sample a mango iced tea. I do think better customer service would mean that if I said I didn't like the tea, that she should have taken it back and given me a large size of something else instead of the sample. Because she didn't offer to replace it, I felt uncomfortable complaining about the sandwich. I spent good money here over the weekend and the service should have matched the money I spent. Plus if I'm going here on a weekend and not dressed like a medical personnel, most likely I've got a family member in the hospital and need some extra kindness.

I ordered the following: 

Pad Thai    $8.95+
Pan fried rice noodles, bean sprouts and green onion in a sweet tamarind sauce. Topped with crushed peanuts. It was so spicy. It had more chill and jalapeno. This is not a hot dish I was sick my mouth is burning. I call them and they said it comes like that. I said no read your menu. So I ordered beef with Brockley. It smelt like my dog's food. the taste was awful. I never Had food that bad ever.  I gave a star to the delivery person :)

Delicious fried faux meat products here. The menu never specified exactly what it is as far as I could tell, but it seemed like seitan to me. Very difficult to tell the difference between their mock meat and the real thing; after all, it's deep fried and doused in flavorful sauce. The texture is right on, though. 

Veggie lo mein was pretty average, unfortunately, leaving me wishing I'd gone for one of the mock meat dishes instead, which were all outstanding. Service was quick and totally adequate, if not exactly warm and bubbly. Atmosphere is kind of weird and hard to describe, very, uh... soft?

It's going to be hard to decide between Sang Kee for duck and Singapore for, well, not-duck when I'm in town and craving Chinese next.

this is a great little gem in chinatown. 
went here for the first time last night with a friend. 
the service was prompt and SUPER DUPER (almost too much) attentive. filled up our water every few minutes even when we didn't need it. which i mean...atleast you don't have to worry about ever having to track down your waitress if you need something. they also give you hot tea. i hate when chinese restaurants don't do this. so i was happy!

everything is vegetarian. i had the spicy chicken curry and it was so delicious. i wish it was more spicy, though. i can take the heat! they asked if i wanted brown rice with my meal and i said yes figuring it came with it. turns out it was an extra $1. so beware of the extra charge. it obviously isn't a lot to spend and i was fine with it, but i didn't bother to ask and was a little surprised.

the food came out pretty quickly. we got a nice little plate with sesame balls and oranges and fortune cookies at the end of our meal which was a delight. they also bring out warm washcloths for each person at the table to wipe your hands with and they smell so good.

i would definitely come back here again. only bad thing was they seemed so concerned with making sure all of our needs were met that they were a little overwhelming at times. but i can deal.

The synagogue felt like home from the first day I entered. I have gone alone to services many times over the years, and I have never once worried where I would sit or with whom. Everyone is always so welcoming and friendly. Once a month on Friday night we celebrate a magical evening called TGI Shabbat, where we have guest musicians play during the service and a wonderful meal after the service. Rabbi Avi and Cantor Jesse are amazing. Our playschool and Hebrew School are thriving. Our Adult Ed has exposed me to new adventures in learning and conversations with interesting Life-long learners of all ages. We are independent, egalitarian, diverse, socially active and vibrant.

This place was very average, the only really good thing about the restaurant was the service was pretty good.  Things came out quickly, and my drink was always filled.  The food was very bland unfortunately, and I wish I could give it more stars for the friendly staff, but really, it should always come down to the taste of the food.

This Starbucks is pretty clean with a couple of tables to the side. It located at a very convenient location next to HUP and CHOP. They are pretty fast with completing orders, with 3 people working on drinks. The ambiance is pretty nice. However it's pretty busy with people coming in and out. If you are looking for a place to complete some work, this is also a good location because the tables are off to the side away from the crowd of people flowing in and out.

After a recommendation from a fellow Yelper, a buddy and I went to Bain's for a quick, relatively cheap dinner. 

I was trying to figure out why I knew the name, and realized that it was from EVERY MALL FOOD COURT EVER. For some reason, I equate restaurants in mall food courts with being bad, (except for Yanagi [R.I.P] in the Oxford Valley Mall FC), so I was skeptical about Bain's.

But! It was pretty good. It is a bit pricey, but we came in during opening week and everything was 20% off. 

Also, they have Stewart's Orange Creamsicle and Cream Soda, FTW.

I love that this starbucks is soo close to work! I get a grande hot chocolate and everything bagel with cream cheese almost every morning (I know super unhealthy, right?) Anyway the point is - This place gives me my breakfast and I like the baristas here.. they are super friendly and nice :)

I must say the service here is amazing. Right from the start, a friendly waitress came over and alerted us of the specials. It was a nice buy an appetizer and get a free beer. We quickly ordered and even received a complementary cocktail. Great! The ramen I would say is very average. Nothing too special. Comming from famous ramen places in new york... this place is just "eh". Fortunately, the service is what keeps this place going. Would reccommend it just for a try.

I LOVE Singapore.  My family has loved this restaurant for so many years.  Ever since I can remember, this has been the place we would drive up to 2 hours to go to (we live in Maryland) for birthdays, special occasions, and just an amazing meal.  Peter is awesome, and always takes such good care of us.  We are all vegetarians, and it feels so good to be in a place that takes it as seriously as we do.  We have always recommended it to our friends and family, and even our non-vegetarian friends have loved it.  We are a little weirded-out by some of the seafood things, though we're crazy about the black bean fish, but I think it's just our own preference that causes that- I'm sure everything here is superbly-made and delicious if you like seafood.  The orange beef is super, as is the sesame chicken, and the.... everything.  Everything is awesome.  Excuse me, I think I need to go back there, right now- bye!

I can't review on their hair services because I never got far enough on the phone to even make an appointment. The guy on the phone was super snotty and I was immediately turned off. He made me feel like I was a pain in his ass for bothering him. 
Sorry guy, I assumed you wanted business.

I have to say I'm slightly disappointed... We went here after attending a game in the area.. Chinese sounded good and based on the reviews we decided this would be our spot for dinner.  

We were greeted and sat as soon as we got in.. The place is small but cozy. Our drink orders were taken and after about 15 mins our server finally came over to take our order. 

We ordered several soups as well as orange chicken,  teriyaki chicken,  Mongolian beef and almond chicken.. We like having leftovers for lunches or other dinners and therefore ordered a variety of things. 

Everything was so good with the exception of the teriyaki chicken.. The chicken was so hard.. Even cutting into it with a fork was challenging. As a result of the hardened chicken no one touched it.. It was literally inedible. 

I typically don't complain at restaurants.. Especially because when it comes to the food it really falls on the cook,  not the server.  I decided to let our server know that the chicken was inedible and that it was super hard,  even demonstrating the fact that it could not be cut into. 

The server asked if we wanted anything else.. I replied  no and he brought our bill.. 

The teriyaki chicken was actually on the bill!   I was so frustrated at this point that we paid the bill and left.  

I would not go back here.. Ever.. Very disappointing

I was so excited when I saw the "coming soon" signs this summer for this Starbucks next to Gia and Jimmy Johns! I always wished for a closer coffee shop on my way into work, and now there is! This Starbucks is clean and bright, with plenty of outdoor seating and some indoor seating as well. It's great for anyone working in the hospital or research centers around the area because of its central location and quick service! As for the quality, it's what you would expect of any starbucks - reliable! Definitely going to be a new staple of mine :)
Good food at great price!  The remodel has vastly improved the interior.

I am not the biggest fan of Vegetarian Chinese food, I'll say that right off the bat. But, as is always the case, I was with a vegetarian who swears by the place and in we went.  

As far as the food is concerned it's standard veg chinese fare: Gluten shaped in different forms. I found the food here to be better than kingdom of vegs, however, and the service is friendly indeed! 

The highlights of our meal were the soups- the curry soup was awesome, and the dumplings were way better than the ones I've had at kingdom of vegs. for sure. The general tsos mock meat dish was standard. 

Overall one of the better Chinese Veg places I've been to, bonus points for the yummy curry soup. I'd put this place in the top half of vegetarian chinese places I've eaten at in Philly.

Ordered delivery via GrubHub and Golden Dragon marked the order as delivered almost two hours after ordering even though it was never received. Upon troubleshooting with GrubHub it turned out that the order was not even prepared and that they would not be delivering at all. It would have been nice to know prior to having our entire staff wait until 2:00pm to make backup plans for lunch.

Ok. Maybe not quite a 4, but it was ok. Been a long time since I was at this location. It has completely changed!  Modernized. Clean. Smaller. Better service. 

Menu hasn't changed in decades. Order house noodles. Tastes the same. Comes with soup. Nothing special. But solid. I asked for them to make it spicy. They did. 

This place is so consistent. The flavors have not changed in years. So if you want reliable, here it is. You always know what you are getting.

Excellent, delicious food. Their thin crust wagon wheel pizza is out of this world. The counter girls are not very courteous or helpful. Stood at the counter for 10 minutes before I was asked what I needed. Their phone answering skills are sub-par also. Answering just saying please hold is not appealing. How do I know I called the right number

When i first lived in Fishtown it took me a while to figure out the origins of that bell that rang all the time, and when I saw the pizza truck drive by my place I was shocked and delighted.  

However, I'm more of a fan of this truck for the novelty rather than the actual pizza.  As awesome as it is to have unsolicited pizza delivered to one's door, its not as awesome when said pizza tastes like Ellios.  Regardless, sometimes it really hits the spot.

Nice addition to South Broad Street and the neighborhood in general.  Tasty sandwiches. Affordable. A variety of meats and cheeses and breads.  Salads look good but I have not had any yet.  Plan to soon.

The guys in the picture no longer own it...and you can tell. Everything is half of the amount that you use to get! And the price is higher. 
I am writing this out of frustration.  I ordered and specified NO seeds. (I am diverticulitis) after 2 nice bites....I realized it had small sesame seeds in it. 
I will never go there again!

Food is ok. I had the fried chicken, my friend had the lamb and my husband had the burger. We all agreed our meals were not worth the hype and a bit over priced . Gave it a two star because the atmosphere and staff are nice. Overall, ok.

I haven't been to this place in 5 years (don't worry, I just don't live in Philly), but perhaps if I write a review where I recall that incredible vegetarian crab I will remember to come back. It was dim and comfortable, big and exciting, and probably far more up my alley than the authoritarian capitalist city-state it is named after (and perhaps the owners are from).

We walked around philly's amazing chinatown and saw 2 vegetarian restaurants and figured why not try some fake meat.  They had a holiday special another dinner special and we ordered them. The food was good but definitely needed the extra spice from the chili sauce. The pricing was good and we actually got orange slices and fortune cookies :)

Ok, so for anyone keeping tabs on my reviews, I am no chef, or foodie. I can only comment as an innocent bystander in this crazy world of flavor and food. So from the outside, this place looks run down, and the inside is tiny and- you guessed it, run down. The staff is very quite and I wonder if they employe mute people only; although I have heard them mutter things on occasion. They do their job though.
Let's talk about Peter. He is the owner and he is very friendly. He is one of those guys that will make you feel as if you were friends for a long long time. Very charming guy. 
Food: I warned you, I'm no expert but this place is freaking good. I agree with some of these posts that say you can't taste the difference in the faux-meat with real meat. I went twice, to make sure the heavenly first time I went wasn't a fluke. The second time, my guests were die-hard meat eaters and they couldn't tell they were eating fake meat. The shrimp did not pass the test but for me, it tasted like it was right out of the ocean, fishy taste covered in seasoning. There are lots of veggies on all the plates and they are very well cooked, I am very picky with my veggies and here they are always neither too crunchy or too soft, never lacking flavor. Everything you put in your mouth you will find trying to decipher as there are spices floating in your mouth the entire time. Make sure you try the fruit juices as it will taste as if you put a straw in the actual fruit! The juice is not from concentrate, powder or syrup, it is the actual fruit. Make sure you don't choke on the sweet and sour chicken as you shovel it down your mouth like I did, stuff that delicious should be illegal.
Summary: Excellent place for a chill meal if you want something delicious and cheap. Terrible place if you are looking for something nice for a date and I suspect critical people of food may find this stuff too simple. 

FYI: apparently they have a secret karaoke machine upstairs that you have to call in advance to book for your party.
Food's cheap and delicious, and the service is excellent. I usually get the same server, Ha, who is just fantastic and always remembers me and what I like.

Haven't been able to hit the bank so I decided to jump on Uber Eats to get dinner. Out of all the places in my area, this had the best rating for the most affordable price. Seeing an average of 4-5 stars across multiple platforms, I expected something like a Tacconelli's or Beddia pie so I was a little disappointed when I received a pizza that looked fairly ordinary. The smell was familiar and when I took a bite, I realized it's the same recipe as Non Stop Pizza & Grille on Hegerman. It's a good pie, I've ordered consistently from Non Stop in the past, but the rating threw me a bit. I'd give it 3 1/2 stars if I could, it's better than average.

I'm a vegetarian because I don't like eating meat, it's not just a matter of taste, but more so the idea of chewing on flesh.  Anyway, this place is totally vegetarian, so it's perfect for someone like me, right?  Well, actually, no.  Singapore substitutes meat in almost every dish with wheat-gluten.  So, everything on the menu read ,"Chicken, this" or "Duck, that," etc, etc.  This is probably great for most vegetarians, but for me, I prefer not to chew on anything tough and flesh-like, even if it isn't actually meat.  

For starters, I ordered the Steamed Vegetable Dumplings, expecting to get just that, vegetables - diced up and wrapped in a thin wonton.  Instead, they were thick, ravioli-looking pieces filled with brown stuff (wheat-gluten again, perhaps).  Yuck.  I ordered the Steamed Tofu with Vegetables in a spicy Schezuan Sauce for my entree.  This, I was able to partially consume, but it was far less than tasty and the "spicy" was left out altogether.

If you're a meat-eater, or a vegetarian that welcomes imitation meat-like products, please read Joe M's review, as he has a slightly different perspective.

Best of Chinese food in tucson after Lucky. I mean this place was good, pricier than Lucky, but way nicer atmosphere. 

Went here a bunch of times with my buddies in college when we were feeling like Chinese food and lucky was too far away. 

Pricing is pretty reasonable, $30 for two people for a really good amount of food. Highly recommend it if you are in the area and want something nicer than Lucky.
Terrible food, I believe they also stole my credit card number for fraudulent use.  Stay away!!
I am regular and the food is consistently good and the service is excellent.  The owner and his staff are very friendly.

Cool place to hang out with a couple friends. Hookah bar with smoking inside (don't see many places like this anymore). casual with outside tables during the warmer months. Above average service and decent variety on the menu.

Nice atmosphere and popular right now. The margarita was very good.  I got tacos in a lettuce wrap instead of tortilla, which did not hold together at all. Still tasty but you need to use a fork to eat them. Maybe they will triple wrap the lettuce or use something stronger than Bibb lettuce.  I thought the table side guacamole was boring.

Food is good but their wait times are ridiculous. I ordered delivery online. They said the food should be here approx. 5:45 pm. It is now 6:15 pm and still no food. Carry out is worse. They'll tell you 25 min from your phone order. You show up and you end up waiting another 30-35 minutes. If you don't mind the wait time this is the place for you. I will no longer be ordering from here. This has been an ongoing issue for over 2 1/2 years now

This place is very middle of the road when it comes to Chinese places in Tucson. They have all the usual dishes you'd expect, and for the most part they're pretty good. The vegetable egg foo young is my favorite.

The biggest drawback is that the chicken in the chicken dishes is always super over cooked and rubbery. Every time. So even though this place is super close to my house, I drive an extra 10 minutes to get Chinese food somewhere else.

I moved into town and was looking for a good chinese delivery.  I called this location and they told me delivery would be an hour or so wait. So I ordered take out. I was told 15min and It was 45min wait. When I got the food I was very dissapointed at the lack of seasoning and quality of the food. Maybe in Tucson the elder population try to cutt down on salt, i was just so disgusted I couldn't even eat the meal. Beef and Broccoli was ok but the General Tsao chicken and the noodles were sub par.

This place has now become my favorite all vegetarian Chinese place (even beating Veggie Heaven in NJ). During a recent 2 days trip to Philly, my family got food from Singapore twice- it's that good.
  Those who suggested the General Tao's chicken were right- it's amazing! Plus the chicken drumsticks are the best. The curry fried dumpling are also really good (like chinese versions of samosas). Needless to say, everything we had was very good- some we liked better only because of our tastes. The only caution would be that if you want to somehow minimize your intake of fried foods, you'll need to ask which items are not fried because it's hard to tell until you get the item. 
  They also have amazing little sweet potato / sesame seed balls for dessert (they're free).

After blowing our NYE budget on dinner the night before, my man and I came here for some cheap eats before going dancing.  We started with the scallion pancake.  It was too doughy and the scallion flavor was really lacking.  Then, we got a mock duck dish and mushrooms with broccoli.  The duck was pretty tasty; my boyfriend said if fake meats tasting like that were available all over, then he'd be a vegetarian no problem.  (I am, of course, skeptical).  The mushrooms tasted like they were from a can.  

Although the variety on this menu is superb, and I am still curious to go back and try something else, I have been more successful just ordering vegetarian options from meat-serving Chinese restaurants. 

Service, though, was excellent.  It seemed like there were regulars in the restaurant that the staff knew.  That's always a nice touch.

I went to 4th Avenue Hair for the first time today and had a great experience. I usually go to Style America, sadly because it is the cheapest, however I have never been impressed by the attitude I've received. Today the line was long so I figured it was time to seek greener (and nicer) pastures. I went to 4th Ave and saw the salon and the experience was great. Free wifi, the style was wonderful (he added in curls which made my hair look awesome) and it had a great feeling.

So, I'm deciding to go on this review-writing marathon. Please bear with me :P

If you happen to live in this neck of the woods, you know very well that delivery options are limited. Fortunately/unfortunately, I'm not the biggest pizza fan(yessss, I know I'm weird) and always end up calling Golden Dragon. I mostly do pick-ups and I feel as if the food tastes better when I do take out rather than dine in at the restaurant.

They're always super efficient and the food is fair for its price. They always pack the boxes and never skimp on anything. 

One time, they forgot one of my orders and when I called back, they immediately delivered it to my place and apologized. Don't you wish all restaurants did that? It's the worst when you finally get home and realize they forgot something in the bag and it was a huge relief when they said they would drop it off ASAP. 

I think their food is good despite what some people say and this place will always be my go-to place when I don't feel like cooking.
Anyone know WHY Singapore Kitchen closed? I miss Peter and his awesome food. Wondering (HOPING!!) if maybe they're reopening somewhere else? Can't find any info about it anywhere.

Hard to find but definitely worth the search.  I like the laid back atmosphere and all of the girls are really nice.  It's fun to go to a club and not feel rushed or badgered for tips.  Best lap dance I've ever had!  Raven is an awesome girl.  Super fun to talk to.

Cool place for your pet supplies but kind of small. I've seen bigger and better ones for sure but overall a nice place. Never once had a problem with staff their always friendly and knowledgeable. They have tons of cat / dog toys and treats. Basically this isn't the best Pet store I've been in but will get the job done.

This is a cozy little restaurant in Chinatown that serves some pretty good vegetarian dishes.  I'm the first to admit that I am a carnivore, but I do like coming here for the dishes made with golden mushrooms and mock meat.  In particular, I like the Golden Lion's Head, which is made with many inds of tofu and golden mushrooms and cooked in a spicy sauce.  The bean curd skin knots with ham is just okay (I make this quite often at home so I am extremely picky) but this is the only place in the area that offers it.  The family style spicy bean curd is quite good and pretty authentic, not to mention very spicy.  They also have sticky rice dumplings wrapped in bamboo leaves, which are nice, but I kinda wish that they have a small piece of marinated Chinese bacon in them for that extra flavor punch (that's what I put in mine along with egg, etc.).  

Service is always great and very friendly, not to mention efficient.  Overall, a good vegetarian pick in Chinatown.

Introduced to me by one friend as "The most mediocre of all of Tucson's mediocre Chinese Food Restaurants"... I went last night because someone else said it was pretty good.

The atmosphere is the most standard you will ever see in a Chinese food restaurant, uncomfortable booths and all. 

The food is overly sweet and quite flat in the flavor department.

Servers were attentive and the cost was pretty standard.

Mediocrity at its best!

Yesterday I made my first visit to Singapore for some quick and cheap take-out.  Hot & Sour soup is my litmus test for Chinese Restaurants and Singapore's is great.  Its slightly sweeter than average balanced nicely by a mild spicyness.  This soup tends to be thinner than average, which I believe is more authentic.  

I ate mine with some tender steamed brown rice and pan-fried curry dumplings.   I looke forward to exploring the rest of their menu!
They invented a Yoo-Hoo shake!!!  Next time I hear anything that sounds like a fire station's alarm I'm gonna start hunting.

A bit of a mind warp considering that most of the items are listed as "chicken," "beef," or "pork," but that they're all made from different forms of gluten. I came with a vegetarian friend and it was generally a pleasant experience. Their hot pots are in between stews and soups....not a pleasant consistency, but my dining partner's faux meat was delicious. Still, neither of us could finish all of our dishes as it tasted a bit cheap and we got tired of it easily.

Service, on the other hand, was great! The tiny older woman was very attentive and pleasant.

Ordered the Singapore Rendang, it is okay. It is more like curry instead of rendang. To be honest, it is abit weird to me because this dish actually taste abit sweet. Anyhow, I would go back to try out other dishes and hope they will satisfy my crave for southeast asia vegetarian dishes ^^

Had some wonton soup and mongolian beef delivered via grubhub. Wonton soup was decent, especially with the crispy wonton flakes. I specified spicy for the beef on my order but the only flavor I could taste was cornstarch and a faint taste of beef. Maybe they got it backward?

Tonight we fly ... in hell!

Due to a US Air error, they didn't have a seat for me on the last flight out of Philadelphia, even though I had paid over $1200 for the roundtrip just days before. Willing to take my money, unable to get me to my destination. They put me on the first flight out ... the next day!

And don't get me started about the hotel they put me up in. 30 minutes from the airport. In New Jersey. With 20 other disgruntled US Air passengers.

On my four-leg roundtrip, two of the legs were overbooked.

The customer service agents at the gate, the ticketing counter, and the phone ranged from incompetent (miscounting passengers at the gate, waving the bump volunteers on board only to then deny the rest of us seats) to rude. The ticketing agent looked at me like I had horns when I asked for an upgrade to first class for my troubles.

Worst. Airline, customer service, and staff. Ever. Negative stars. Avoid at all costs.

Ice cream truck? Water Ice truck? Psshhhh, boring.

PIZZA TRUCK, now that's what its all about.

Fishtown/East Kenzo exclusive, you hear the ringing bell like someone just robbed a bank, you run outta your house and grab a slice, or two, maybe a shake, and whatever else they got on the paper menu taped to the window. 

Far from the best pizza, but for a buck fitty a slice, and the chance to relive childhood by chasing after trucks for edible goods, it can't be beat. 

Unpredictable, sketchy, dirt cheap, and a lil comical, what the neighborhood is all about.

The bo ssam appetizer is extraordinary. Perfectly cooked pork bites plus oysters, wrapped in lettuce.

An excellent prelude to the sushi. But nothing, nothing tops that bo ssam.
