RICHARD

Such a fun place. Very cool vintage clothes and so many other items. Great MCM furniture. If you are looking for Pyrex and other kitchen items this is your place. The staff is very helpful and friendly.

I have been known to go to pet stores with my dog and spend wayyyy too much time and money shopping.... it's practically a pastime for us. Here, that wasn't the case. I really didn't feel like my dog was really welcome by the employees or other shoppers. Like another reviewer said, meh.

Pet Supermarket carries my dog's special food, which is why I usually go here, but they didn't have the flavor she likes in the right size. I don't know if they were low in stock or just didn't carry it? At least the prices are decent.

For now, I'll stick to the location on Fowler.

With all due respect to my friends in North Tampa, maybe the suburbs just don't understand the 5-star rating.  That's not to say you can't find great restaurants in the burbs, but 5 stars in the burbs sometimes doesn't seem to be the same thing as 5 stars in the city, even when talking about Tampa vs. the Tampa suburbs.  This place had such great reviews, but oh lordy lord lord lord, there are so much better sushi restaurants in the Tampa area.  Again, maybe this is 5-stars for Carrollwood, but if so, I'm really sorry Carrollwood.

Anyway, standard COVID stuff - staff was in masks, but I didn't notice gloves.  They kept tables separated but it was slow, so I don't know if they fill every table when busy or if they leave some empty. 

For a mediocre meal, we certainly ate a lot.  My love started with crab rangoons. I think she liked them, but for details, you'll have to read her works.  I started with the pork and shrimp dumplings, which were okay but probably the best part of the meal, so lets say, okay+.  We then moved on to sharing a spicy tuna roll, california roll, and a ceviche roll.  Taste wise, they were in that order from least tasty to most, but overall, still mediocre.  Some of the rolls had way too much rice, but it was inconsistent and there was a proper amount of rice (in my less then humble opinion) on other parts of the rolls.  Ceviche roll (made with yellowtail) definitely had the most flavor.  Upon finishing the rolls, and being constantly hungry, we then both got soup.  For my part, I got the wonton soup, which was just weird.  Standard broth and dumplings, but it also had large chunks of vegetables, which just don't belong in wonton soup.  It wasn't bad, but like everything else, it was just okay.

I guess if you're going to carrollwood and really want sushi then this is a place to come to, but I did see some other well reviewed spots on yelp and you should probably try those first.  This place happened to be in the most convenient location for where we were hanging out that night and the best looking menu.  However, they kinda failed on the delivery.

The family and I stopped here this weekend to get a quick bite to eat. Excellent service excellent food, good bunch of people work there  and they are very friendly. Definitely going to be back again.

Sooo good! Service was excellent! Would come here all the time if I lived closer. The decor is cool, with a new mural and modern lighting. We had Cashew Nut with Tofu, Rice Soup, and edamame. Wouldn't write home about the edamame--a bit over cooked and over salted. But it was all very tasty otherwise. Would recommend to anyone.

We just visited again tonight for the second time for takeout.  Let's start with the phone service....so important during this time! Whoever answers, she's a gem! Polite, friendly, helpful and not rushed.  We've had both Thai and sushi now and it's totally worth the drive for us as so many places are closed in our neighborhood on Sundays. We've had the fresh rolls two times now, just veggie and with shrimp.  Fresh, well-made and just the right size.  The peanut sauce is different...I can't tell you what makes it different but it is. It's a little spicy and unlike most places, the color is almost orange/pink. But still good.  My daughter loves the bubble tea and the Tom kha soup; she asks for it not to be spicy and it's been that way both times.  This order, we had a bagel roll and the citrus roll.  I would get the citrus roll every visit...it's one of the few that is in the healthy side and an interesting combination of tastes. I loved it. Last time, we ordered a Thai main dish - eggplant basil.  I like to order dishes I would never make myself and this fit the bill.  Ltd of veggies and enough for lunch the next day.  I love this place.  Give it a try!

So good! Me and my fiancé did not want to leave the house on New Year's Day. So we ordered in and they did not disappoint! Everything we ordered was so good and still hot when it got to our house. Definitely will be dining in soon!

We've enjoyed the Golden Dragon on Sunrise and Swan for decades.  But lately, and as of tonight, I am really concerned about their chicken dishes.  
I ordered a vegetable chicken dinner months ago and the chicken was so shoe leather weird and tough I couldn't eat it.  
Recently I ordered the Sesame Chicken, a pretty predictable dish just about anywhere we go, and it was also strange.  Tough, too tough to eat --wiry, stringy, tough, thin,  as if it wasn't chicken at all.   Kinda spooked me.   I couldn't eat it, though I tried.   
I'm afraid to imagine what it actually is, but if you told me it was chicken feet tendons or pork anus I might believe it.   But it's NOT chicken breast or thighs.   And it's NOT edible, even at $11.95 in delicious sauce.  
Don't let the sauce fool you, you could eat cardboard with their sauces.   

Look, I love this restaurant.   Some of their dishes are the best in all of Tucson.  
But now I'm concerned and frightened by their chicken dishes.   
I hope they read this and listen:  don't destroy your great reputation by doing creepy stuff to your chicken dishes.   Raise the prices, do whatever, just don't serve what you are selling as chicken anymore:  it's NOT chicken, even if in generous portions.  
Please.

Sushi fans rejoice! A great new Thai and Japanese restaurant. The Lama roll is totally unique -- so many layers of flavor. Daughter said the pad thai is among the best she has had anywhere. Will be back!

This was just a short order. Almond Chicken n white rice  and enough vege egg rolls. I did the pickup. Ready in 20 min. 
There was a line for Take out. 
No inside dining yet.  
Very nice guy helped me. 
It was bagged and ready
When I came to the desk. 

Delish!

4.5 stars... This is center city's greatest walk-up delicatessen stand, offering numerous delicious options made fresh daily (closed Sundays). I like the egg salad and the seafood salad, but my personal favorite here is the tuna on kaiser or the chicken salad which must contain a secret differential ingredient that makes it better than any chicken salad you'll get anywhere else in Philadelphia Proper. There are wide varieties of rolls, sandwiches, and other fresh deli offerings (many cheeses, salads, pickles, slaw, various shades of peppers, bacon, etc). 

A slight detraction could be the ambient temperature on some of the food items. I like an item to be hot enough to practically burn the palate, but Bains does not always deliver in that regard. No problem, as I always order a cold sandwich or platter, and just avoid the rather lukewarm soups and sides (by my standard of temperature). 

The Bains family and other employees here personally strive to make the lunch ordering experience unique to everyone's tastes and yet consistent. If ordering platters for groups they recommend a call ahead to be ready for pick-up and not have to wait.  The savviness of the employees generates a cult repeat business although they have provided plenty of first time visitors with a wonderful meal as well.

This place used to be okay. They have some decent looking dancers, but there are too many mediocre girls walking around; too many girls with huge guts. It's very small, so the best time to go would be in the afternoon/early evening. The major downfall of this place is that all the dances are $30; I found that out the hard way.

This Chinatown vegetarian eatery is cozy, and has room to serve groups of any size. Service is friendly. The place isn't bad for a date, especially if you and/or your date are vegetarian. I'm not, but I can appreciate a good vegetarian restaurant.

Last I was here, two of us shared a dim sum sampler ($10/person; minimum two people), where we had a choice of soup and various dim sum plates. We tried:
- hot and sour soup, sweeter than expected, but quite tasty
- "chicken" drumsticks, not bad for a faux chicken
- pan-fried scallion pancakes
- Singapore satay
- spring rolls, they were okay
- cold sesame noodles
- pan fried curry dumplings - one of the better fried items
- steamed vegetable buns, "chicken" dumplings, and leek dumplings

Most items were okay, but I'll try their regular entrees next time; vegetarian dim sum doesn't seem to agree with me.

Decided to give this place a try but prob won't be coming here again. Their lunch special indicates a bowl of soup for dine in but due to covid I asked since we're taking out we can get that to go and the answer was "no" with no decent rationale for why. I showed up to pick up my order and asked for chili sauce, the girl says that they "have to make it," so she gives me one and then I asked for another since I ordered a fairly large amount of food and her answer was, "we have to make it again then." Ummm okay?? So, just based on poor customer service alone I will probably take my business elsewhere.

This place is pretty good! You can taste the quality of the ingredients of the food for the price. The service was golden and they are nice for a great conversation. On this side of town, it's probably the better Asian food you'll get. I got carry out for some dumplings and it was delicious and fresh! They give it to you in a cute paper bag. Would come back next time to eat in.

That shit was good vro 
Domino's is better than every other pizza place

I be eating this pizza like damn dominos cheese so good dog

We're done. This Sonic, like the rest of the Sonic Drive-ins in Tucson is complete trash. Time and time again we are given grotesques variants of their advertised menu items. The staff is always rude and incompetent. The staff appears to hates their job and hates doing business with their consumers and the business is always filthy. And now this, the Coney dog footlong meal with extra chili and cheeseI "missing" just purchased has part of the bun missing, the hot dog is broke in the middle and when I took the first bite I had to "literally" spit the bite out to keep from gagging. The hot dog is so old it has a metallic chemical spoiled taste. I really don't know how to explain it any better than that. I should have listened to my eyes and never attempted to push this vile crap into my mouth. My advice,  DO NOT EAT HERE!

This Starbucks has always been there for me whenever I need a little pick-me-up in the morning before I start my shift. Its the fastest mobile ordering Starbucks around University City area. I can place a mobile order while I'm on the way to work, and bam 5'-10' later, my drink is ready for sippy sippy. Regular morning staffs are amazing and super efficient. They're giving out orders like boom boom boom, super fast UNLESS they have a new hire that requires training or something goes wrong with the mobile order system. Other than that, my coffee is always ready whenever I'm in the store to pick it up.

After morning rush hours slows down, the amount of staffs are also reduced, everything is going with a slower pace. The weekend also has fewer staffs compared to the weekdays.

The disadvantage here is that there's no parking on the street, so its very challenging for customers to stop by or even pick up with mobile order. It's only more convenient if you're visitors from the hospital or employees from the hospitals. 

Staffs are friendly. They remember your name if you're one of the frequent customers. They also make me happy whenever they greet me by name and ask how I am doing.

I am so happy that gold is back open! The staff was amazing. I was especially pleased with Scarlett. She was so talented, enticing, and nice. All of the girls are so pretty, but I will especially be looking out for her again the next time I am there.

Place is exactly what you would expect from an alley way strip club. Size is perfect. The dancers aren't hot but that means they will go that extra mile to "satisfy" their clientele. The one thing that definitely sucks here is the dancers or whatever you call then hound you for money. Probably because they are all pill heads. Beer and drink prices aren't bad. Good spot to hang for an hour and sink some suds. Recommend going good and drunk so the "performers" look better.

The only strip club I've been to and I appreciate that it's topless only.  Situated right next to an Applebees (in case you've got to take a dump) Gold Club is a carpeted, couchy, topless club with A-B cup dancers.  Seriously, every time I've gone I haven't seen juggable jugs or hoot-worthy hooters.

There are two (maybe three?  maybe I was seeing triple?) poles on stage that get wiped down with the 'nasty rag' right before dancers launch themselves on and twirl around.  Spoiler alert, all dances end with boobs and a g-string.

Immediately afterwards the girls walk around and smush their boobs together in front of you asking in a whispered baby voice "will you tip me for my dance?".  Out of guilt and pity accompanied by sheepish giggling, you always do.

I've been in NYC and LA this place would compare with any Japanese restaurant in those cities. A real pleasure to find such a wonderful restaurant in Tampa. Beautiful ambience and no sports on TV, but they show development of their menu items with classical background music. Reasonable price and beautiful presentation with typical Sushi items, very fresh fish. Best in Tampa bay! Really clear the staff enjoys their job, cordial and friendly.
Excellent and I can't say that enough volcano rolls. The staff was very friendly with my me and my family while still maintaining social distance
This place tasted Marvelous! I had the Pad Thai during lunch hours and also added the crispy chicken cashew nut! Wonderful selection!

Awful !!
Tasteless food regardless of what you order. 
I've sampled several dishes   Not one was memorable.

Wholesome family run sushi and Thai restaurant. The owner and chefs made an effort to get to know their customers and ensure top notch food. This is the best Thai food I have had since coming back from Thailand. The owners wife is the amazing Thai chef and the sushi was amazing!!

I know for a fact that these people use real shady marketing practices to lure in potential buyers. 
I called on a great looking used RV, for a great price, which I saw on their website. The response was that they sold it already and hadn't had time to take it off the site but  would I be interested in another RV? I wasn't.
Two days later I saw a brand new Craigslist posting (posted that day by Pedata) for the very same RV they told me they sold.
That's about as low as it gets in the marketing business. Shady.

I had the calamine, crab cake and the snapper.  Truly disappointed with the main dish, it was average at best.  On a positive note the crab cake is excellent.  I would highly recommend this place for a date and sit near the piano bar.  Would recommend the crab cakes and not sure about anything else.

New favorite spot to get Thai! It seems like sushi is the main draw here for most folks, but I got a bunch of Thai to go and it was all so good. I called in my order, pulled up front and a nice young guy quickly brought it all out to my car. My top favorites were the papaya salad and the pad see ew. Really can't recommend this spot enough and I can't wait to check out the rest of the menu next time I'm craving sushi!
All of the electronic ordering boards are broken and the posted menus are not accurate. Maddening.

I went there to grab some sushi rolls for myself and the family. I could not be anymore pleased. In addition got the lunch special Panang Curry with Salmon ?!? Delicious! Great Service, Great food -come out and support your local businesses!!!
I think I'm gonna need a bigger boat!?!

Went for a special event. Sophie Dee feature dancing.  That night there was a $10 cover.  I'm assuming this is a typical cover for this club on a Wednesday though I could be wrong.  I have not been to a lot of strip clubs but this one seems to be on the small side.  Small stage with two poles and dancers.  Seating was tight at small tables in front of the stage and seats along the walls.  The girls come out after their dances and work their way through the crowd for tips.  Seemed less rushed than other club where they make a round behind the bar collecting.  $20 for a couch dance.  Main complaint is that the couch dance room is way too dark.  This was made up for by the fact that the girl giving me a lap dance had a more liberal touching policy than any previous experience. I cannot say if this is typical of all the girls at this club.  I would say everything else is typical of a Philly strip joint.  Expensive drinks, at least one lady who is too old to be dancing, etc

Noon-2am  Mon-Sat

So I'm reading these reviews for this place, and they're a bit mixed. I decided to check it out for myself, especially Wednesday's with Megan. Turns out she's amazing. Its 9:15 & its closed. 2/21/2021. The site says they close at 10. Smh i drove a about 32 minutes to get here for something quick to eat. They shouldn't deceive customers with the time that they close:

Was at Michael's and decided to give this place a try.  It was DELICIOUS and the service excellent. My server Alex was super polite and attentive, and knew the menu really well. Bad expirience and not honest or reliable, they do not care for the people just the sale. Did not even keep their end of the deal on what was signed

[ production - Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf ]
We got free tickets from the Philly Yelp Elite squad to see "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf", which was an amazing experience. I don't often go to plays - usually only when I am given free tickets - and the last thing I saw in Philly was some awful Samuel Beckett thing that I didn't understand, probably because I'm not highbrow enough for that sort of thing, so I've been rather turned off theatre for most of my life.

This production redeemed it! A touching, intelligent, and fantastically impactful story with four phenomenal actors. There were occasional line slipups, which they recovered from with dignity and actually added to the charm of the whole thing.

[ venue ]
The theatre itself is rather small and intimate, tucked away on a residental section of Delancy Street. Friendly and casually dressed staff will meet you at the door to collect tickets and hand out playbills. The theatre is pretty old and worn, but comfortable. You'll be able to see and hear comfortably from anywhere within the room.

Downstairs has bathrooms, a water fountain, and a small concession stand which sells tea, coffee, hot chocolate, candy bars, and small snacks. There appears to be some kind of bar upstairs, which I did not check out.

There are only two stalls in the women's bathroom, so make a point of rushing out there to avoid the line during intermissions.

[ website and pricing ]
Tickets seem super affordable - the tickets for Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf were selling online for $10, which is amazing for the production value and quality of the play.

The website is a bit messy and counterintuitive - there's a link for a credit score calculator at the top of the page, which is odd - might be a sponsorship thing. 

**PROTIP for online ticket buyers: The "buy tickets" page doesn't seem to work - If you want to order tickets you have to find the event in the calendar on the right hand side of the page and copy-paste the http://boxoffice.printtixusa.com/ link into your browser.

[ conclusion ]
Lovely little place to absord some culture which is well-run and managed enough. Not polished, but that might be a part of its charm. Take an evening and check it out.
The sushi is excellent as well their other dishes. Be sure to order the boneless curry duck. Absolutely fantastic.  Also try tnt mussels for a extra kick
Not awful just not anything special. The fried rice was kind of bland and the crab rangoons were basically just cream cheese.

So happy (my wallet disagrees) this Starbucks exists so close to my work! 

Yes, the line can be long during the busy morning hours and it maaay take awhile to get your order. BUT just download the Starbucks app, pre-order your complicated venti soy double shot extra foam extra hot sugar free cinnamon dolce caffe misto and it'll be ready for pick up in about 5 minutes (skipping the line!). The best part, aside from avoiding the dirty looks people behind you give when you start rattling off your drink order, is prancing from the door straight to the counter past the uninformed in line (VIP style) to pick up your perfectly made drink. 

You're welcome.
Basil fried rice was okay. Amazing eggplant stirfry was definitely not amazing. Very bland and underwhelming. Mangos and sticky rice were pretty dry. Won't be ordering again.

5 stars for the overall experience and price. 

Met my friend tonight for dinner and we were looking for a geographically mutual, new experience- which is how I found this place. Fantastic dinner for the  price. Their HH is amazing. Fish is delicious and fresh! Service was super! Would gladly go back.

I'm so sad to see this place have bad reviews! My husband and I have been ordering from here for over two years. The food takes 45-60 mins, but there's always a lot in those tiny boxes. Average pricing, but food is always great. We've sampled all over the menu and haven't found anything disappointing yet. Green bean meals are my favorite, the brown sauce is amazing. Also, our delivery guy is the sweetest and we always hope he's the one who brings our food.
Manager is awesome. They always deliver on time and their garlic knots are amazing!

Had the opportunity to go for lunch and so pleased with the many specials. I love the panang curry with tofu. The tofu is made in house and so creamy. The curry is smooth with such a pleasant taste. The lunch special comes with soup and a fried spring roll, and again comes hot and fresh. Alex was my server and is fantastic. He is knowledgeable and makes sure that all Covid processes are adhered to. Always a please to eat here.

Better than a pizza shop. My wife says to buy one every time Dieter is around, if we ate dinner or not. Great food, great guy. Love it.

I found them to be honest,  professional and very easy to deal with.  If they do not have the RV you are looking for they will find it. Jerry sent us updated emails every week on new inventory.  I would highly recommend them.  Best RV dealer in Tucson.

Let me just say. I love this place!!! I love the papaya salad. I tend to come here often enough and allow me to order chicken with my papaya salad instead of shrimp. The chicken satay. Amazing too!! Food is served quickly!

It had a sweet lime mixture that tasted really good. We also ordered pot stickers and  crab Rangoon. The pot stickers were my daughters favorite. I enjoyed the crab Rangoon personally. The food was still warm when it arrived and I have left overs  for later.

Such a fun divey strip club! If you want class and a-class dancers, then head up to NYC. But for $10 cover and some surely entertaining hangover memories to laugh about the next day, go here. PS- if you buy a $6 shot from the shot girl, it comes with a free mini lap dance ;)

Meh.  Seemed like the perfect place to go for social distancing - you order from your car, wait for your food and eat right there.  All under a nice canopy to keep the sun off your vehicle.
Everyone else had the same brilliant idea, the place was packed and they were clearly overwhelmed.  Took about 10 minutes to place our order and maybe another 25 minutes for the food to come.  Long time for a cheeseburger (see photo) and a hot dog.
The bright spot was the cherry limeade - pretty good!  I don't know what they did to my cheeseburger, but as is visible from the photo it looks like it got cooked in the wrapper, the way the foil got all burned.  The lettuce got pretty cooked too.  Maybe too long under a warming light?
The hot dog was pretty good, tons of pickle relish.  It would have been nice for them to provide extra napkins or something for the diners to prevent their lunches from plopping into their laps.  I hogged the empty bag for a tray, but my wife's hot dog...oh well.
Oh, and the credit card reader on the ordering stand (see photo) didn't work.  I tried repeatedly, no go.  Paid cash, which fortunately I had on hand.
Maybe we'll try again when they are not so crowded - some of their ice cream deserts look pretty good.

Three stars, not because it's bad, but because yelp defines four stars as "Yay! I'm a fan" and it's not quite there. I didn't actually go myself, but sent my dad as he was looking for a synagogue for the Saturday we were visiting Philadelphia, and this one seemed like it would do the trick.

He said the service was fine, but was mostly women. Being conservative in the more literal sense (that is, stuck in his ways), he was amused that the service was led by a female rabbi, and that they wouldn't have been able to make a minyan without the women present. I suppose he was a little rattled by the break in tradition, but when pressed, he said that the rabbi was passionate and professional and took her duties very seriously. 

So, in all, I'd say it was a positive experience for the old man, who had never seen a female rabbi in action before. I guess I am a fan after all.

I placed an order yesterday through grub hub. Luckily they soles v my issue with a full refund. The dood was odd and both hung llike the photos on their yelp site. When I opened the containers. A rank smell came out. We both  got super sick. That's the last tile I will ever go o there.

Was searching for Thai food delivery and came across this place and decided to give it a try. Most Thai places near us we've tried and even though were decent at one point, quality and service have sadly gone down. This is not near our neighborhood so we have never been before. 
Pleasantly surprised! Opening the takeout boxes and seeing the presentation of each dish we already knew this place was a winner. Everything was packed properly. We ordered pot stickers and bbq skewer appetizers, chicken pad Thai, chicken basil fried rice and the red snapper with Penang curry. Delicious flavors!!! Authentic Thai spice. Our favorite sauce was the dip that came with the skewers. Fish sauce with peppers I think. 
We will definitely be ordering again when we need our Thai cravings satisfied. I only wish this COVID-19 was over so we could dine in and try even more. Thank you for such wonderful service!

I only have had takeout from this restaurant, but what I did have was great. The total experience has been wonderful. This place is the real deal. 10/10! I stopped in yesterday for a late lunch . The staff was super friendly and helpful. I also had the Remix Sandwich which was delicious as well. I forgot to take a pic because I couldn't stop eating but trust that it was the bomb.com. I'm excited to try more items off the menu

Hubby and I went here last week. We wanted to try something new so he ordered the duck and I was intrigued by the shrimp and tamarind sauce. They did not disappoint. The duck was sautéed so it was a bit crispy but not dry. And if I could lick the plate after eating the shrimp in tamarind sauce, I would've. Maybe next time...lol

This is a nice little shop with a good variety of items.  When you drive you, there are some items outside to look at.  Inside there is one big room and three smaller rooms.  There were a number of lamps, small tables, pots and pans, tools, books, CDs and DVDs, collectible items, jewelry and more.

Although I didn't buy anything this time, it is interesting enough that I'll go back again to see what is new.  It was fun to browse and glad I made the stop.

Great cozy sushi restaurant.  Service was excellent, we were both greeted immediately after walking in.  Place looked clean and tables were well organized.  Lots of great choices on the menu.  Server made great suggestions and she was right! Sushi was spot on and we will definetely come back.  Thank you!

I passed by & thought I'd sit for a few minutes & have a drink but I was immediately informed that I, as a female, was not welcome w/o an "escort". Unfortunately, I have a Jeep...lol. Jokes aside, they just missed out on a good tipper.

If I could give less than 1 star I would. I bought a 'coach' from Pedata. Flew in from Mn. 2 days after my mom died and purchased the 'coach' and started driving home. The check engine light came on after approx 400 miles. We continued on as it was not an option to stop due to covid. 
We made it home to MN. It was taken into the local mechanic to have the check engine light fixed and ended up replacing the ignition coil to the tune of $400.00
 1 week later we loaded up to travel to Kansas City Mo. to drop my moms belongings to my sister and we made it to South of Des. Moines when the entire rear end blew out. We were forced to sleep on an exit ramp then have a wrecker tow us to the next town. We stayed in the mechanics parking lot for 4 days while it was repaired. We were told the rear end had so much fine sand in it that they thought maybe the 'coach' had been in a flood. The bill for that breakdown was almost $7000.00. The mechanic took pictures and kept the parts because he recommended a reimbursement from the dealer. 
 After we were on out way again to home, The check engine light came on, the automatic step quit working and it began vibrating enough to run you off the road.....
Back to the mechanic we went....This time all ignition coils failed and 3 of the 10 spark plugs had no spark at all! ANDDDDD....another 500.00 in repairs, we still have not been able to fix the step (it is stuck halfway out). 
  When I sent the info to Pedata, they were kind enough to send me a letter through their attorney saying I cannot contact them anymore. 

I will warn you right now, they made all kinds of promises and assured me the 'coach' was so good, safe and trustworthy. 

Pedata will sell you junk and laugh at you when you leave. I am a hard working nurse and a ranchers wife. This was my first big venture in buying on my own. I bought this so I could travel with my grandchildren and enjoy family camping. 
It is a shame that Pedata hurts the American family and will not stand behind their 'coaches' they sell.
PLEASE be warned.

Visited on a Thursday night for some happy hour snacks. The restaurant has a beautiful ambiance & inviting decor. I was greeted upon entry & my server was friendly & professional. I started off with the spring roll & a Sapporo beer. Then, I moved on to the Boston roll & vegetable roll - both were filling & tasty. I thoroughly enjoyed my first experience & look forward to visiting again.

Excellent service, clean atmosphere!  We were very impressed with the fresh sushi and their specialty rolls, we also ordered some Thai food and hibachi steak which it was delicious.  Roger and the rest of the staff are very personable and friendly. Our family loved it and we highly recommend it. Definitely will be back

The. Best. Quality. Pizza. I have ever had in Philly. Ever. 
Small hole in the wall spot but the pizza is baked to perfection. I really appreciate the effort these guys put into making pizza because almost every other pizzeria seems to make the same mediocre pies.

I am writing this review in reference to a Motor Home I purchased from this dealership. I saw it online and we decided to make a deal on the unit. After making the deal with Don Lewis . We just popped in and the sushi was amazing. The chef asked us what kind of sushi we wanted off the menu and he made it for us. I am vegetarian which makes ordering sushi tough. He made some suggestions and the outcome was perfect. The owner said that he can make most things on the menu vegan and vegetarian.  This is our go-to for sushi from now on.

Although the sign outside the door said please be patient due to staffing shortage, the time my friend and I waited was within acceptable limits for any restaurant. There was only 1 wait staff, Roger, who as it turns out, is also the owner. Roger was very personable and funny. We had a few laughs with him as we decided on our meals. We both decided on lunch specials. I had the Hawaiian Fried Rice and my friend had Green Curry. I was hoping for some good miso soup and I was not disappointed. They do ask that you mask up when not eating which is a good idea if you can manage it. We both certainly enjoyed our meals and will be returning to sample some of the other sushi and tempura dishes. I can't wait. Sorry, no pictures. I'll try to remember next time.
Very efficient and clean. They are particularly good with the mobile ordering. My order is always ready by the time I get there!

I was waiting to finish my first trip with my new coach before writing a review. I recently purchased a 2007 Fleetwood Bounder 38L Diesel Pusher. We traveled 1200 miles round trip and had no issues.
I had nothing but a great experience with the Pedata Team, since I first saw it on their website through the time of walk through before delivery.
The Team went beyond to make sure everything was properly working, made minor repairs to items I found during final inspection and replaced my awning motor onsite. Their goal was complete Customer Satisfaction and they totally succeeded. 
I live in Las Vegas and we drove to Tucson to get Coach, no regrets.
I must mention all the Team Members without their diligence and hard work I would not be a Happy "Camper"...
Carlos, Jim, Taylor and Cindy
Also must mention Mr Gerard Pedata (owner) was always available to answer any questions and provide full support.
Thank You to All of You - Now let's Travel :-)

This VERY GOOD eclectic eatery opened in 2018, & is opened 7 days a week. The Thai/Japanese/Hibachi chef (& owner) has 20+ years experience, while the sushi chef has 30.

I will definitely return to try many more offerings! The Eel ($7) & Yellowtail ($8) Sashimi was EXCELLENT, as was the Pineapple Fried Rice w/ shrimp; there was a $2 uncharge for brown rice. (The standard lunch portion w/ white rice is $10.) The Crab Rangoon ($5) was VERY GOOD, as well as unique w/ regard to the shape (calzone-like) & the actual crab inside-- it was deliciously stringy in texture rather than finely chopped. I didn't enjoy the Mackerel Sashimi, but it was my first time trying Mackerel; I believe it was just me:)

The Miso Soup (which accompanied the Pineapple Fried Rice) was average, as was the fried spring roll that accompanied it. (With check-in, we received an additional one.) My lunch date said the Shrimp Tempura Sushi Roll ($8) w/ cucumber & cream cheese was very good; it can be ordered mild, medium, or spicy. (We substituted brown rice for white-- another upcharge.)

The menu is extensive, even for lunch. There are 28 Sushi Specialty Rolls, 8 Sushi & Sashimi Dinners, 23 Traditional Sushi Rolls, 7 Vegetarian Sushi Rolls, 22 two-piece Sushi & Sashimi rolls for smaller eaters, as well as 6 Sushi & Sashimi Lunch Specials--  weekdays (11 AM - 3 PM).

There's also a separate menu for Japanese & Thai foods-- hibachi, noodles, curries, stir fry, appetizers, soups, salads, & desserts. It, too, is extensive. There is something on the menu for everyone. 

The restaurant was clean, the booth was comfortable, & our service was stellar-- Ethan was EXCELLENT! He was fast, friendly, so helpful, & it was all genuine-- just a very nice young man. Multiple times he made suggestions & explained menu items in detail. He also indicated that management works hard to please guests, so if we ever want something special, we should just ask-- the chefs do their best to accommodate, if at all possible.  

There's plenty of parking out front of this strip mall, & I believe I saw a couple of small metal dining tables near the entrance. I'll know for sure the next time I'm in the area...  because I definitely want to return. (Ethan highly recommends the hibachi, which the chef/owner once specialized in as a Kobe chef.)
my bat, we entered the wrong place. i only saw singapore/chinese. once inside, i thought i could be adventurous w/ veggie.

I ordered to go food by calling. They were polite when I called and when I arrived to pick up my food. It was ready on time and the payment process went quickly.

I would rate the food about 3.5 so I rounded the total review up to 4 stars because I enjoyed my food and I would go back here. 

Red curry chicken- I chose the middle level of spice & I probably could have gone up to the next level. It wasn't as spicy as I expected from other Thai food places where I've selected the same level of spice. But it was still really good. They give you big pieces of chicken and plenty of it. 

Fried rice- The rice was a bit more sticky than I would have liked it to be, but still tasty with fresh vegetables including cucumbers and tomatoes.

Why 5 stars? Because the menu is giant and the quality is great.

   ---   ---   ---

I booked this spot a while ago because it had a very strong 4.5 star rating and is close to my house. But recently, I noticed that 4.5 upticked to 5 stars overall, so I knew I had to make it a priority to stop in. We did so today and were very impressed.

We started off with wanting one sushi roll. I couldn't decide which one to go with when our server suggested an off-menu roll called the Roger Roll (named after the owner.) All I really remember from her description was crab with a bunch of other stuff that sounded good, so I was sold. It came out with a bunch of thin, fried... tentacles on top? Not sure how else you'd describe them, but they were delicious and added a nice crunch.

We tried to fatty tuna sashimi next and this was the only unfortunate miss for us. When we visited Tokyo, we loved getting fatty tuna as much as possible, but this was nothing like it. It was warmed and I guess pretty cooked? It didn't really even taste like tuna. I'd avoid this in the future.

Both of our main courses were excellent: pad thai and crispy chicken cashew nut. The pad Thai was a tad sweeter than normal. Our server said she doesn't normally like pad Thai but does like their version - I could understand why. It wasn't wildly different than normal pad Thai, but just a couple ticks tastier than usual. And the crispy chicken cashew nut was also very enjoyable. 

We finished with coconut ice cream and mango with sticky rice for dessert. The mango stick rice was fine, but the coconut ice cream stole the show. Also, our 15 month old acted as if it was the best thing he'd ever had in his young life. 

For the majority of the time, we were the only customers in here, but we did arrive about 2 minutes after they opened on a Sunday afternoon. I hope they have a steady rush of customers because they certainly deserve it!

****BUYER BEWARE**** This outfit of clowns are not to be trusted. I was quoted a price on 10/4/18, decided to keep looking. Came back to this deal on 10/9/18 with the intent to buy. Now all of a sudden the quote goes up $1500 dollars. I can only assume this is "the boss" throwing a tantrum that I didn't purchase 5 days earlier. Seriously, what kind of business operates like this, one run by a 10 year old? I guess if your selling used RVs for a living though, enough is said. This actually turned out to be a blessing, as there is no telling what their "prep" would include. Probably stealing/breaking everything they could that was valuable and would not be noticed. I have no doubt I would have been stranded with some issue on my return home. So in hindsight, thanks Pedata RV for being complete idiots. I'm am confident your lack of professionalism on the front end saved me endless hours of pain and trouble on the backend had I actually bought something from you tools. **RUN WHILE YOU CAN IF YOUR LOOKING AT BUYING FROM THESE IDIOTS**

Looking for sushi in the area and were recommended Ahi. The food was great and the staff was awesome. We were the only people eating in the restaurant although others did pick up to go orders while we were there. The sushi was super fresh and delicious. We had a limited wait which was nice. It was the night of a hockey game and they did have a tv to watch on which was nice. Bathrooms were clean. Parking was easy. We will definitely be back!
Convenient location, however, there are always flies swarming in the pastry display case and around the store. Does not make for a very appetizing experience.

The duck drunken noodle was delicious!! I had it Thai hot  it was so spicy yet so flavorful I loved it. I highly recommend this place. The food was very tasty, the thai tea was really good also. I wish the crab Rangoon had more filling, it tastes good as well but it's just not enough. The ambiance of the restaurant was so cute! Next time I'd love to sit there and eat now that they are also allowing dine in services. (Side note the man who paid out my order then went back into the kitchen was handsome also lol) all around 5/5! I can't wait to get more! Finally found another really good Thai place to go to.

The website says they deliver, but when I called the restaurant the pot-smoking-sounding-guy on the phone said they don't deliver.

How can you run a business where you WANT to SELL stuff to PEOPLE who will PAY YOU and refuse to do exactly that?

Bye bye, Golden Dragon.

We had a great dinner here, including both sushi and Thai.  There were many sushi specials of fresh and unique fish.  This restaurant is low-key, friendly and very tasty.  The staff take pride in their food and restaurant.  We would definitely dine here again.

Super Fratellis has Amazing pie. We have only ordered from here so I can not speak about anything but the food. It is delicious. Everything we have ever gotten from here was perfect. We order from here quite often and the y have never flubbed an order. The prices are quite reasonable and the delivery time has always been super quick. The drivers are always on point.

The first two visits were great! I needed a root canal and that was a joke. I was in this surgery for three hours. The doctor had other appointments going on, leaving my room often explaining the three hours. Horrible experience! I've had to go back a few times because the crown didn't sit right. It's a different doctor adjusting my crown who is nice but I'm still having issues with this. Alot of money for a horrible job.

I honestly thought this place was DE-LICIOUS!

Was on Yelp looking for a different place, a different experience, and found this gem (while running on the treadmill, no less)!

There's a Chinese Vegetarian place I LOVE in Jersey City, and I am haunted by the faux General Gau's chicken from there. For reals. I haven't had it in YEARS, and I have been craving it. So, saw this place and started hoping for the best!

I convinced one of my buddies to come with me, and we walked in together on a blustery evening. And it was like being transported to 1990! Pink tablecloths, fried noodles with duck sauce and mustard on the tables, and old menus. Regardless, we ordered the Dinner Specials for the both of us - New Year soup, trio of dumplings, and Orange Beef for her, and General Tso's chicken for me!

Yum. We were honestly full after the soup and dumplings. And the Shanghai (I think??) dumplings the friendly guy at the next table recommended we get (thanks for the tip friendly stranger! Would love to pick your brain regarding marathons by the way if you're reading this). So when our entrees arrived we were only able to pick at them, but they were really good! My choice of the two was definitely the Orange Beef. Deliciously crunchy!

We received impeccable service, and we were actually really surprised at how good the food was!

Definitely worth a visit.

I once went to Golden Dragon for lunch about 20 years ago.  I remember not caring for the meal.  With that said, I stayed away for 20 years.  That is just how I am. Burn me once and I'm history.  Weird, because it is so close to my house. It could have been a good deal for me.   Fast forward to last week.  I was suffering from a respiratory ailment and couldn't breathe with both nostrils stuffed up.  Head felt like it weighed a ton.  Just miserable.  It was Christmas Eve and as tradition goes, we usually go out for Chinese Food.  It's a law when you are from N.Y.  I absolutely did not feel like dragging this sick body to go to our favorite Chinese Restaurant.  A light bulb lit up and I suggested bringing home some nice hot Won Ton Soup and some Chow Fun from the very convenient Golden Dragon.   Let me first start with the Won Ton soup.  Plain broth, little taste, lots of won tons that we like mush, tons of torn cabbage, tough grisstly pork.  The Chow Fun followed suit with noodles like they had been cooked for an hour.  No white rice, no noodles for the soup.  I hate writing bad reviews but maybe someone will wake up.

Delicious food and the best staff! So patient and polite. I would definitely go back just because of how awesome the guy who took our order was. He also sort of created a pizza for us to accommodate the fact that I couldn't have meat. :)

They steal.  All the girls are gross and they try to scam you.  STAY AWAYY.  They add drinks on your tab and then pretend that someone else said they were with you and were on your tab but it's all a scam.  Gross.  Stay away!
Just stay in your black hole, no need to go outside and waste your time whining at a place like this, your wife hates you? Kids hate you maybe? Idk. Just stay in your black hole of a life.

I didn't know much about Ahi and I was invited here for lunch. I'm so picky about the places I eat because if they don't have the proper stars on Yelp... ‍ We ordered shrimp rolls and I had the crawfish (craw) sushi. The shrimp rolls were nice. The Thai basil REALLY came through I'm with each bite. It looks/tastes like they used the base for the Penang Curry as the "peanut sauce." It didn't taste too peanutty - instead it was more like curry. The craw was the absolute BEST roll I've ever tasted! It was REALLY well flavored. Our waiter was definitely not a very good one, but it wasn't enough for me to say I'd never come back again. All-in-all, great food, service needs work.

I was somewhat hesitant about eating here after seeing the 3 star rating on Yelp. But we had been driving around Tucson for sometime and couldn't agree on anything else, so Chinese at Golden Dragon it was.

 The restaurant is quite small with about 9 or 10 tables, but a friendly and cozy atmosphere with lots of takeout customers coming and going. Our  server tried so hard to balance our initial table that was wobbly, but eventually reseated us at the larger table next to us, the only other available.

We ordered oolong tea to have with our meal, and then their chicken foo young, sesame beef, crunchy rice with vegetables and chicken, and chicken chop suey. Steamed rice was also included. Total before tip: $52.84. I enjoyed everything but as for my wife; the chicken foo young and chop suey, not so much. She thought the chicken was too salty and the chop suey veggies overcooked. But plenty of leftovers for a meal the following day in our hotel room, before heading off to see Hamilton at Centennial Hall.

Not great Chinese food here but definitely above average.

When your looking for veggies in Chinatown your either going to be faithful to Singapore, or roll with the Harmony/Kingdom combo. I like Singapore, but Harmony is how I roll just because it's pretty hard to beat their all you can eat dim sum deal and BYOness.

But Singapore does offer plenty of tasty treats and is the better spot to go to for take out. I also dig their ambiance a little more. And Chrissy R. is right about their General Tso's bringing the hottness!

5 star pricing if you ask me!! A hidden gem of sushi! My friends and I really enjoyed it this restaurant and man do they feed you! For $15 you get to pick three rolls (8 pieces each)! I will be returning!

In an age of covid where employees don't show up to work and companies run out of things constantly, this place does a great job. I typically come in the morning and they treat me like family. 
Always efficient and friendly. If they are out of something they are always cool about it and offer other things. They seem to care about their customers which I find pretty rare. Love this place!

Worst place ever called and ordered they went to the wrong house then told me they would give me credits to call back another night and when I did they said I had none was 36$ I'm getting my money back one way or another!!!!!!
Horrible! I frequently order here from work and love the sandwiches. Today I went to get one myself and was treated to the worst service ever! The woman behind the counter is incredible nasty!

Best RV Dealer in the South West!

After both purchasing a Class C from Pedata RV Center and having it maintained by Pedata's service department for the past few years, I am satisfied that they do indeed live up to their commitment to provide affordable RV sales and service that meet customer needs and expectations.

The used RV I purchased was priced literally thousands of dollars under what any other dealer was asking for the same and similar coach. The sales staff was polite and helpful without being pushy.

I've had engine maintenance and oil changes, air conditioner and generator maintenance, interior equipment replaced (Kitchen faucet), and exterior painting. All were done in a timely, workmanlike manner and in every instance, met my expectations at a VERY AFFORDABLE price.

Pedata RV Center should be the first stop in your search for your next Motor Home.

Had been wanting to come here for a while, since I won't pay Vetri prices for food, and loved the pizza at Osteria. We were a bit diappointed, though. This was New Year's Day at 6pm, so the place was pretty empty. Service was fast and courteous and helpful. Somehow though, it was loud. And though the music wasn't loud, it was classic rock. I'm a fan, but it in no way fits here. Perhaps it's the play between the bar and the restaurant atmosphere mixing in a small space?

Anyway, the food:
Swordfish meatballs - excellent
Striped bass crudo - good
Rotini with wild boar ragu and pears - very good
squid ink linguine - good

We expected excellent all aorund, but the prices were in line with the quality. We'll have to try again to give it another chance.

We live next door, just moved here and thought we would give Ami's a try for Sunday brunch. I had the hazelnut, maple waffle and my husband had the scrapple with sunny side up eggs. We also had a Bloody Mary and mimosa. Every bite was delicious and the cocktails were superb! We enjoyed the sidewalk table and had excellent service. Looking forward to bringing our friends here!

Amis was possibly the best meal ive had in the city in a very long time. It was so good because every aspect of the experience was spectacular. We wanted to try everything because it was so hard to choose just one or two things. So we got about three different appetizers, three anit-pastas, two pasta dishes and two desserts.  That's the way to go!  The veal tongue and octopus were incredible. The papparadell was aldente and melted in your mouth. We got two caraffes of red wine and I topped the night off with a hazelnut chocolate tartufo and a macchiato.  Our bill was so reasonable. I got out of there well under $75 with tip per person.... $75 for all that food!  Our only complaint was our server rushed us a bit. We sat at 8:00 or so and we wanted to sit and relax and enjoy. We let her know we'd be ordering a little at a time because we wanted taste, then decide on our next dish. She was a little put off by that and told us they were busy and we should order all at once. She was very nice about it however, we weren't going to be rushed.  To her dismay we ignored that suggestion and ordered bits at a time anyway.  All in all it was sinfully delicious food and wine, great friends and perfect ambiance to enjoy the perfect company in.

Great knowledge and advice for our pool. Thank you guys so much for all you help. Great to have a local pool store nearby with competitive rates. 

The first time we came in it was just to ask questions and get our water tested and they were still very helpful and didn't try to sell us a bunch of chemicals we didn't need. 

We have since been back a couple times and all the staff are super friendly as well as knowledgable.

I really can't complain about any of the food I had or service I got on the night I came here. When I saw that the average rating was only four stars, I was expecting a good but not great meal. Luckily, I can say I truly did get a great meal. 

To start they have a small but well curated selection of local craft beer, so I indulged in a brew from Free Will brewing, which I rarely see on tap. The restaurant was also taking part in Negroni Week when I went, so I snagged some sips of my fiance's drink. It was stiff and very well made made. Honestly based on the ambiance I would say you could come here just for a drink, but you should definitely stay for the food. 

For a starter I had one of their meatballs (Sal's old school meatballs that is), and it was quite tasty. The texture was interesting and the flavors cohesive. When it came to picking a main course I was a bit stumped, since everything sounded good, but their special sounded like a good choice. It was a beef cheek ragu, and let me tell you, it was amazing. The beef cheek was cooked to perfection and nearly melted in my mouth. There were cherries in the ragu which added a lovely tart note to the whole dish, and gave it a somewhat less heavy flavor. I wish it were not a special because I might order it every time! In addition I also got to sample some cacio e pepe, which was equally flavorful despite it's simple ingredients. All the pasta was nicely cooked, a true treat and something you can't always take for granted at Italian restaurants. 

This is the point where I talk about what was possibly the best part of the meal; desserts. I ordered the tartufo al bacio and was not disappointed. It was extremely rich but very enjoyable. While the overwhelming flavor of the dish was chocolate the cherries and hazelnuts were what turned this into a phenomenal dish. The taste was perfect, the texture was perfect and the fact that I wanted more was a good sign. Another one of my dining partners raved about his dish, the olive oil cake, and I snagged a taste of it. Let me tell you, this olive oil cake is unique and delicious. The cake itself has a nice chew to it, and the sauces and cream combine nicely to make one perfect bite. It's not too sweet, so those who don't like desserts might actually really like this dish.

Overall I was impressed with my trip to Amis. There was nothing to be left desired and I enjoyed every bit of food placed in front of me. With my closing thoughts I will say that the uniforms the servers wear are a bit odd; their car mechanic shirts are more reminiscent of a gas station than an upscale restaurant. I would implore management to reconsider this choice. Then again, it is just a uniform, and neither the service nor food suffered because of it. I hope to be back.

Food: 3.5 stars
Service: 4 stars
Ambiance: 4 stars
Location: 3.5 stars
Price: 3.5 stars

Recommendations:  I would recommend starting off with a combination of the bruschetta and salumi for appetizer. The 'imported bufala ricotta and black pepper' is a must have.  The whipped ricotta is so smooth and creamy; it literally melts in your mouth.   The 'mixed salumi' plate is a great addition to the ricotta.  The variety and quality of the salumi is excellent.

The main courses unfortunately did not match the quality of the appetizers.  The initial pasta we ordered was the 'spinach pasta with sausage'.  It definitely was the better of the 3 main courses.  The pasta was very fresh but the sauce was a little flat. The 'gnocchi alla romana with oxtail ragu' was far too salty as was the "mixed seafood grill' secondi.  My girlfriend who enjoys food on the saltier side was overwhelmed by the amount of salt used in the dishes.

Overall, we had a great time at the restaurant.  The ambiance is great and the service is wonderful too.  The general consensus was that the food did not meet all the initial hype and expectations.  I'm not sure if we will return for another dining experience.

Overall: 3.5 stars

Man, I saw Steve E.'s photo and made it a point to get up to Strudelking. Pulled into the parking lot, wandered in, and chatted with the owner a bit about Germany and Europe as a whole. This guy is the go-to man if you plan on traveling to Germany; he pointed out so many little places to check out that no one really knows about and so many bits of history. I wish my review was just on how awesome of a guy he is.

It seems since everyone else has reviewed this place, Strudelking has started selling their goodies online. I'm not sure if this is why my experience differed or what, but my strudel definitely didn't have the same kind of flake I see in Steve's photo. I picked up an apple and a blueberry cheese one and followed the owners recommended heating instructions (45sec for apple, 30 for the other in the microwave). I guess I should note that they are refrigerated before buying them, and I don't know if they're put into the containers while warm (causing the heat to be trapped as steam), but there wasn't much flake or texture. I feel like they would blow my f'n mind straight from the oven though. Is there a secret on when to get these bad boys or am I just destined to only have them from the fridge? On my second try, I put a piece in the toaster oven on a lower heat for a longer period of time to try and dry out the top crust, and it turned out better than the microwave. I definitely liked the apple more than the cheese, but I've never been big on cheese pastries.

Amis is quickly becoming my favorite Italian in the city.  I need to keep coming back to try new things, as well as revisit my old favorites.  The cacio e pepe is outstanding. Swordfish meatballs are as good as everyone says.  Squid ink pasta? Yes!  

Service is always spot on.

I have been to Amis twice now and was disappointed both times. While the atmosphere and service are great, they can't make up for the obscenely small portions and obscenely high prices. The menu is deceiving because everything is priced $10-25; but it takes about 2 of their "entree-sized" dishes or 4 of their "lighter bite" dishes per person to give you the sense of having actually eaten dinner. Add on a few drinks, and there is no way you're having dinner for two for under $130 there (and you'll still probably go home and break out the cereal). I hate leaving a restaurant feeling ripped off, but that's exactly how I felt both times I left Amis.

Very unhealthy menu and very unaccommodating
in response to a request for healthier versions of
their entrees or vegetarian selections generally.

Great addition to the Tampa Restaurant scene.  
You have to try one of the bowls when you come!
Outstanding food and service. Depending on where you sit you could be very cramped.  Very loud the evening we were there.

Very disappointed. Swung in for my usual Billy Barou and the tall kid behind the counter with awful teeth jipped me. He out barely any chicken or Queso. The chips were so dry I asked for more Queso and he said he have to charge me

The $.50 or $1 he was worried about = no more $ ever from this customer...

I was really looking forward to our meal here, especially after they were rated so highly in Philadelphia magazine.  Unfortunately, it was a complete disappointment.  The only positive thing I can say is that the restaurant has a good vibe.  But I've had much better italian food at our local bar.  For our entrees, we had the gnocchi with ox tail and the papardelle with veal ragu.  Both were fairly bland stew over a bland starch.  Honestly, nothing stood out here.  And they rushed us through the entire meal.  Apps through dessert in 75 minutes.  When I tried to slow down, they just brought another course.  One last bit of annoyance - the waitstaff had obviously all been instructed to recite the same cheesey lines such as "the artichoke sells out by 8:30" and "the tiramisu has been haunting my dreams" which we heard repeatedly from several servers.  This isn't Fridays people.

EXTREMLEY DISAPPOINTED IN THIS LOCATION'S CUSTOMER SERVICE. I come to chick 3-5 times a week on average for breakfast/lun/ din and this is the second time in 3 days that you've cut off breakfast when I've waited in line for 15 minutes and still arrive At the box to order at 10:29 and 10:30. Other locations are superior to this one. Don't waste your time sitting in this line SMH

I've been here a few times and always had a wonderful meal.  The things they do with cauliflower and brussels sprouts!  Fantastic atmosphere.  Good beer selection.  The staff are friendly and informed on all the menu items.

My girlfriend and I returned to Amis for a second time after a late summer dinner that we enjoyed heartily. Our server, knowing that I was vegetarian, and my girlfriend was vegetarian-leaning, suggested we return for a Meatless Monday tasting menu. 

After securing a reservation on OpenTable (100 points, y'all!) we returned this past Monday evening. Soon after being seated, we found out that they have stopped their Meatless Monday promotion. We were saddened to hear this, but our waiter kindly offered to check with the Chef to see if he could accommodate; luckily, Chef was more than happy to help. 

We received imaginative, off-menu items that were delicious. We received 3 courses -- an appetizer, a pasta dish and a dessert. This was the best meal we have eaten in a while and would return again. Amis took care of us (Chef/Server[s]/etc.). We'll be more than happy when it is time to return for another wonderful meal.

I've been coming to Amis for 7yrs. It's been one of my all time favorite philly restaurants. I moved two years ago but when even I travel back I come straight here for a granita and their delicious small plates. I've never had anything less than excellent. Everything has always been executed perfectly...until today. Sadly I was so disappointed. First they no longer had my beloved granita, the icy mulled wine in prosecco that I crave, then the pecorino with honey wasn't nearly the quality, nor was it gooey and melted the same with the crispy edges it had always had previously. Even their signature pasta didn't taste the same.  I had a great time and the service was suburb....But in a city where food is excellent you can't have less than  average nights especially at these prices.

Terrible service, the gentleman that took my order acted annoyed that I ordered a salad & he had to get more lettuce from the back.  In addition the portions are not standard to any Chipotle I've been to, they hardly gave me any meat & when I asked for more they threw a huge piece of fat on top. The guy behind me had to ask for more cheese. Really? Tighten it up people, you're down the street from where I live but I'll drive twice as far to go to a less convenient location with better service & portions.

SO Good! Julianna and I had one of the better meals of our lives tonight! The rabbit antipasti was absolutely amazing! We also had the fresh mozza, sweet bread, mortadella moose, strip steak, lamb ragu, and jalapeño pasta. We finished it off with the Belgium waffle, Nutella, and ice cream. Everything was absolutely perfect! The service was especially great too. We really enjoyed donating $ towards helping kids eat healthy, and Amis matched which is really cool!

The food, atmosphere and service were all great at Amis but even at a late dinner (9:30 on a Friday) the restaurant was just too loud. I could barely hear the person I was with or the waiter. If they figured out a way to better the acoustics, this place would definitely get a 5 as the swordfish meatballs, duck and peach special, flank steak and tiramisu were all delicious.

This is my favorite Vetri experience to date.
Prices aren't bad, food tastes great, mostly smaller sized plates for sharing and trying multiple dishes.
Amis is on my list for a return trip.

Contrary to the negative review in the Tampa Bay Times, our experience on two occasions at Bar Asia was great.  The food - bowls and sushi -  was very fresh and expertly prepared and the service was just attentive enough.  The restaurant itself is attractive and conveniently located, with its own parking lot.Do give it a try!

The employees at Moe's are always in an awesome mood!  I love how they greet everyone with an enthusiastic "Welcome to Moe's" as you walk in the door... it's like everyone is so excited that you came to the party!

The food isn't authentic Mexican cuisine, but the burritos are cheap and very tasty.  My one gripe is that the menu is way more confusing than it should be.  Say I want sour cream and guacamole on my burrito... do I order the Homewrecker or the Joey Bag of Donuts? I'm not a regular at Moe's so I always have to ask the employees to decipher the menu for me. Why can't they all just be called burritos and I'll pay for my extra toppings?!?!

Good food at cheap prices with friendly service... How can you not like that?

When the waiter was cleaning the crumbs from our table I asked him to put them in a to go box. Another fabulous restaurant by Mark Vetri. Great service and fantastic food. Olive oil bread basket was incredible. Tuna croquettes were these wonderful little balls of savory delicious tuna. The pecorino and pepper pasta....NEEDED MORE! Savored EVERY bite! Bucatini with jalapeno and almond pesto is as good as it gets!  No dessert since we were stuffed by all the food we ate!

Meh is what it says when you give a restaurant a two star rating here, and meh is exactly how I felt upon walking out after my meal.  Don't get me wrong, the food was wonderful, a real treat and a luscious throw back to the best trattorias of southern Italy. And I'm really not a complainer when it comes to restaurants, but my experience made me want to take the time and sit to write a review. 

The overall experience fell well short of the expectations we have of the the top restauranteurs in this city.  The service was mediocre at best.  Most of the staff left me with the feeling they were "overtrained" to be nice.  I like a more relaxed natural discourse with the staff than that especially in this type setting.  The waiter was confusing in explaining the menu, eventually admitting there were no special.  It was just that the menu had recently and completely changed.  The bus boy whisked a dish away without first asking.  I really wanted some more of that sauce on my arancina oopss...too late.  He never bothered asking if I was done before grabbing the dish.  

Also Marc, and I know you and your staff read these reviews, would it kill you to put more than one amarena cherry in the tartufo?  I know they're a little pricey, but often people want to share desserts.  It would be nice for each person to get a full effect of the flavors the  chef intended.  Especially since the menu says cherries (plural). After touting the flavorgasm of amarena cherries to my significant other, upon finally finding one and digging through the rest of my tartufo  it was "Oh sorry honey, I had the only one they put in the dessert.  And jury's still out on that bread.  I'm pretty sure I can bake the same thing in my bread baker and the recipe that came with it now that I know to just add sea salt on top.  And salt does seem to be a common flavor which stands out in most of the dishes.  Particularly the pasta.

The ambiance was very nice, but rather loud if you like conversation that's especially personal in nature given the next tables are five inches away from your elbow.  I did enjoy hearing about the sex life of the two energetic young ladies at the table next to ours though.  The four of us decided we're going out together next week to try a Garcas restaurant.  Thanks Marc!

Seriously, it's quite a shame when the food is this good that so many other things seemingly have fallen through the cracks.

I've been doing massage for 20+ years...all over the world (retired USN)  and the massage that Sam provided today was exceptional!  I keep a lot of stress built up plus I am beginning to exhibit more stiffness and flexibility loss due to 12-hour days in meetings or at the desk (old man syndrome, I fear).  My usual therapists have all been good, but the session often leaves me sore for several days due to intense deep tissue.  On the other hand, this was much more focused on stretching, with the warm compresses and great aromatherapy too.  It was an amazinly restful experience and a great value, especially coming from San Diego where a 90-minute session can easily run over $120.

This place was fine. In my opinion, the sushi/meals were overpriced; however,customer service was amazing . I loved the warehouse interior which was chic and trendy.  The tables were a little wobbly but once we mentioned it, they were fixed right away. The food and cocktail were fine but nothing earth shattering. Maybe I need to try some different meals to capture a complete opinion. They have recently opened so I will be interested to see the development.

Very good food and reasonably priced for quality of food. Friendly, knowledgeable staff. Pasta dishes were impressive and swordfish meatballs were nice treat. Not sure food lives up to acclaim of restaurant, but still a good dining experience. Only real complaint was the LOUD rock music playing in background. No idea why it's necessary.

We have had Luke come out three times now.  One for a general bug spray, a whole house termite treatment and then a spot treatment for termites.  I like everything about the company and their service. At a really good price.

Giving 3 stars to a Vetri restaurant seems like sacrilege, but I had an equal amount of hits and amísses.  

The olive oil bread basket is absolutely ridiculous (if you typically skip the bread, try this and try to each just one - good luck).  After analyzing the menu and pointing out all of the recommendations, we went with the following:

- chicken liver toscani: ever since I had and loved the chicken liver at The Spotted Pig (NYC), I haven't been able to find it as good anywhere else.  The streak continues....

- baked pecorino with almond honey: absolutely amazing.  I took more than more portion, ordered it again, and took more than my portion again (it was so good, I didn't care about the social repercussions). 

- Sal's old school meatballs with tomato potato: all parts of this appetizer were delicious - the meatballs, the sauce, and the 'tomato potato'. 

- grilled veal tongue with pepper mostarda: I had high hopes and it was just ok (nothing memorable). 

- tonnarelli "cacio e pepe" with pecorino and black pepper: I was distracted by the overcooked pasta (I didn't finish my plate which is rare)

- polenta with brown butter: it was bland. I was expecting sweetness from the brown butter, but all it seemed to do was make a brown ring around the polenta.  

- spagetti squash with pork jowl and pecorino: I was strategically taking spoonfuls of the pork jowl (and you'll do the same) - wow.
We've had dinner and brunch here. Very creative menu with offerings made from fresh ingredients that taste great. Highly recommend this place!

Went here for valentine's day.  Had a lot of small dishes, including:

Baked pecorino cheese with almond honey (appetizer) - really really good, lots of melted cheese

Root vegetable salad - so so, probably should have skipped it

Mussels - in Romanesco sauce, with awesome bread for soaking up the sauce

Rotini with black trumpet mushrooms - Amazing.

Salted butter gelato waffle pizzele - enormous and worth going back just for that.  Best thing we had.

Bottle of Cava - always good

Service was pretty attentive and professional.  They also have chef's table style seats facing the kitchen, which  might be cool to check out next time.

Came here on a freezing Thursday night with two friends and it did not disappoint. Perfect night for a hot pot. Service was good and the food was good as well.  Nice big selection of items. Overall nothing ground breaking but definitely nothing bad either. Very modern and in a good part of university city Penn campus.  I will probably come back the next time I'm back in Philly.

We went here last Wednesday evening when we couldn't get a reservation anywhere else close to our hotel. We sat at the "chef's table," which was similar to a table you would find at a sushi bar, where we watched the incredible kitchen crew rapidly prepare and plate complex dishes for the entire restaurant. The restaurant was incredibly loud, and entertainment from the kitchen staff was key to allowing us to enjoy dinner without feeling the need to scream at each other to be heard. Do -not- go here if you're looking for a nice place to eat and have a quiet conversation! The music in the restaurant is booming, and so all the diners have to take it up a notch to talk.

Our food was good, but not outstanding, but what really made our evening was the amazing waiter who was, by far, the best waiter I've ever encountered. I wish I could remember his name, but what made him so great is that he was extremely attentive, very friendly, casual when the situation warranted, and knew the menu inside and out. I noted that he should quit his job and develop a school for waiters because this guy was top notch.

Summary: Good food, LOUD atmosphere, outstanding service.

My expectations were high and they were not  met. I ordered the polenta and it was BLAND. I also had  2 pasta dishes the gnocchi and cannelloni, both were very average. For dessert the waffle w ice cream was good, that was probably the best dish. The service was great  but the food was very average and overpriced. I dont think I would go back to eat .

Had the bucatini pasta with jalapeno and almond pesto. fantastic! Well worth the price. 

I have now been here three times and the restaurant has never disappointed.  My wife said the pork chop parmesan was 'to die for'.

Tonight we actually had some space for dessert and the chocolate tartufo. amazing! even if you come just for this dessert, it is well worth it.

Awesome food. Well prepared with fresh ingredients. 

Mortadella with Hazelnut and Honey was awesome, a great combination of flavors.

Bucatini with cheese was very good, pasta is fresh and cooked perfectly. 

My only regret is I wasn't hungrier so I could have eaten more

Had a great meal with the family at Amis. If you're looking for a more quiet & relaxing experience, definitely choose a table outside! It was nice to be able to hear each other talk. All of the food we had was delicious -- the eggplant caponata, pecorino with almond honey, duck pasta special, and Mom Mom's rice pudding being a few standouts. Beer is reasonably priced and they have a good variety on draft. My mom and brother really loved the peach cocktail. Service is friendly and Mr. Marc Vetri himself even stopped by to refill our waters and make sure we were having a nice time.

On a quiet part of 13th Street, Amis is bustling once you arrive inside. I came as a part of Philly Wine Week. Even with a reservation, our table wasn't ready right away. (I saw a couple people being seated with drinks already, and I'm pretty sure that's just what they say to get you to wait at the bar first.)

After looking at the wine flight on special: four 3oz pours of limited/bottle-only wines for $55, we decided to split a tasting to see if any of them stood out enough to order a full glass. That was definitely the way to go because we ended up liking two, indifferent on one, and really disliked one; so we were glad to not be stuck with expensive wines we didn't love. We ended up just ordering a carafe of the house wine instead of something fancy after that.

For dinner, we started with swordfish meatballs and calamari. Both appetizers were delicious. The meatballs were so tender and flavorful, served atop creamy polenta. The calamari was also tender, not chewy, fried with jalapenos. For the main dishes, I got the chicken alla diablo with a chili oil and spicy cherry peppers. The chicken was cooked very nicely and was juicy. I usually don't get chicken at restaurants but it's just what I was in the mood for, and I wasn't disappointed. My date got the lamb shoulder, which was served an odd fashion. It was pressed flat and thing with a crisp crust on it. While my bite was fine, I felt like it tasted drier than it needed to. Served with cubes of potatoes, it was just a slightly underwhelming dish. 

On that note, we decided to skip dessert. Plus, nothing really stood out. There were a lot of other appetizers and the pastas that definitely seemed worth coming back to try. Someone also mentioned a good brunch menu.

So I had quite the unique experience here. I'm contemplating on changing this review to a 3 star (I decided 4 star because I'm feeling generous right now)

My friend and I went on a walk on Sunday morning and passed this place and decided to have brunch - it had only opened a couple of minutes before we decided so we were literally the first customers of the day. They were setting up inside so we decided to eat outside (they have about 4-5 tables outside) to stay out of their way - we thought we were being nice and doing them a favor. I ordered orange juice to drink and it came out right away (as expected).Since we were on a walk, I had to use the restroom before ordering my meal so I went inside. I was in the stall doing my business (sorry, too much information maybe) when two frustrated waitresses came into the bathroom talking about how annoying my friend and I were because we showed up to eat right when they opened. One of the girls literally verbalized, "What bitches! How rude to just show up like 5 minutes after this place opens! No one does that! I'm so annoyed and I want them to leave!" 
I had never felt so awkward in my life!! I literally sat in the stall until they left - it was terrible!  Now that I think about it, I should have walked out and been like I heard that!! 
I ran outside and told my friend what had happened to contemplate if we should leave or not and she said she had just ordered for us. We decided to stay and eat - we didn't want to be even more of a burden than we were (apparently). 

So back to my rating of this place - the ONLY reason I rated this place a 4 star is because of the food. The hazelnut waffle was AMAZING. I would eat it for breakfast every single day if I could. My friend didn't enjoy her breakfast chorizo though. 

Overall, I didn't enjoy my experience here because of the awkward and unwanted feelings my friend and I had. If a restaurant says its open, they should be happily serving... even if it is 5- 10 minutes right after. I don't know if I would come back here again - depends on how much I am craving that waffle and on how confident I am to go back hahah
