I've also gone to a certain pub in Fishtown known for their high-caliber Italian chef serving at pub-fare prices, so I'm probably a bit spoiled as well. 

As a result of all these things, when I ordered some of their popular items, like the almond & jalapeno bucatini, cacio e pepe, and swordfish meatballs, I was sort of underwhelmed.  However, the service was excellent and very friendly. That, the ambiance, and its nice location in Center City are definitely part of the equation.

Wonderful food, inconsistent service bordering on the inattentive.

Paul
The most delicious cookies I ever ate. They literally melt in your mouth. Everything is so clean and fresh.

I popped in here for  an awareness rate deal and received an amazing massage from Marcella.  Thai Massage is completely different than what I expected, but I felt much more flexible for weeks after the experience and I am a tight puppy.  In fact, it's time for a tune up!   If you are a runner, cyclist, athlete, or just have a lot of kinks you owe it to yourself.  Try them out.  They have a lot of specials.
The pasta dish literally defined "al dente" and the veal tongue is not to be missed. Thank you fellow Yelpers for the tip on the Baked Pecorino w/ Almond Honey which is a real winner.

Do this is by far one of the busier locations. Skip the drive through, which I've waited up to 30 mins more than once and my co-workers have too during lunch. Inside is much faster. An even better option is to download their mobile app and do a carryout order ahead of time with the mobike pick up.  Plus the app will give you great perks like free food nust for signing up and you can earn points to redeem how you like as well! Chic fil a has a great reputation for consistent food, great customer service and clean stores. This store also meets their high standards and there is a reason they are consistently busy. If their drive through was faster I would've given 5 stars as it is a fast food restaurant.

Done coming to this location.  Consistently has issues with quality and inventory. 30 minutes after the store opens they have no chicken,  scarce amount of steak, not to mention everything looked dried up. So I wait 5 minutes for them to finish cooking the chicken while my food is partially made dying on the line (seriously stop making until everything is done..) get my food, drive back home so my wife and I can eat lunch super undercooked chicken. Drive back to chipotle,  inform them of what happened, no issues and they replaced my food... drive back home for round 2 of my lunch, some lovely medium rare chicken... You were just told that you gave someone undercooked chicken and don't quality check it a second time around? Very poor management.

Brunch'ed it at Amis for my mother's birthday celebration.  We were a group of 5 and were seated at a round table.  Because of said seating at round table, we decided to play a game.  A Food Ordering Game.  We started with my mother, who picked one item to order off of the menu.  We worked clockwise around this round table, with each person ordering a different item off of the menu.  The only Rule of this Ordering Game: no duplicate items can be ordered.  This allowed for our party to try almost the entire menu, as we made it about 5 times around the table.  Our server thought we were both funny and nuts at the same time.  

The cichetti-like plates (italian tapas) made this ordering game a success.  The highlights for me were definately the Sunny Side Up Duck Egg with Grilled Guanciale and Pecorino Fondue.  Anything with guanciale and I'm in...I could eat this dish for breakfast every day.  If breakfast  (and eggs!) were actually a relevant meal in Italy, i could see this being served all over the country.  The mortadella mousse was equally amazing.

The Italian cocktails worked perfectly with this brunch menu and are much more interesting than your standard Bloody Mary/ Mimosa brunch boredom. A good cappuccino is hard to find in America, let alone Philly.  The cappuccino at Amis is as authentic as it gets and will hit tyour cappuccino fix.

Overall, I give Amis 4 Stars.  Only 4 because I gave 5 Stars to Amis' big brother Osteria.  And the big borther is always better, right?!?  I need to return to Amis for dinner soon.  The Belgian Waffles with Nutella are calling my name.

OK, I get the whole Amis is owned or related to the restaurant Vetri... BLA BLA BLA... 

Both are over-priced over-rated places that serve mediocre food. Both are more concerned with their "fancy" ingredients they add rather than looking at the greater picture of things and asking... "Is this good?" 

I ordered pasta that was supposed to have a touch of mint in it. Cool, I get it, mint in pasta, different, unique... Not for me and I am sure NOT for several others.

After eating my breath was minty fresh because he added way too much.

Service was good, food was pricey, looked nice (I guess) but was lacking some sort of soul in it... Maybe Jose Garces and Marc Vetri can open up a restaurant together...


M-E-D-I-O-C-R-E   !!!

Overall for my first Verti experience I was sorely disappointed.  I was highly disappointed and will not return.  Most everything was disappointing from uninterested bartender, overcharged at the bar, failure to transfer bar tab to table check, (we were honest though!), seated 26 minutes after our reservation in the bar area not in the dining area, the first 2 desserts I asked for were sold out.  There were 2 saving graces, lovely table service and the food was pretty good.  We had high hopes and after all the bells and great reviews we read the expectation was that they could deliver on that and for us they most certainly didn't.

In preparation for our recent trip to Philadelphia, my partner and I attentively watched Anthony Bourdain's "The Layover" on Netflix. Right off the bat, Bourdain makes it clear that  cheesesteaks have no place in his trip, nor did they have a place in ours. Bourdain mentioned Amis offhandedly and I am forever grateful we'd watched and paid attention to his show. 

We made our way here on a Friday night, with no reservation. There were plenty of open bar seats- of which we grabbed 2 and made ourselves comfortable. The bartender, Kate, was very friendly and helped us with ordering. 

I had the Ugo to drink, and together we shared the Porchetta, Brussel Sprouts, and Pasta with Duck Meat dishes. We also indulged in the Belgian waffle with Nutella. Everything was delicious and I would go back in a second. I personally found the pasta to be quite rich, and the brusells to be the real star of the meal. Even the complimentary bread was mouthwatering. Do yourself a favor and try as many different plates here as you can!

After hearing so many great things we were very disappointed. Everything was so salty...so very very salty. 
Our table was ready when we arrived and our server came right around.
We got swordfish meatballs, pecorino and honey, roasted cauliflower, brusselsprouts, monk fish and fagioli bolognese.The cauliflower and brusselsprouts were too salty to eat.
I was surprised that the waiter didn't offer the specials until I asked after overhearing it from another table. When we asked for a recommendation he was unable to really explain any of the dishes...like the whole fish, "It's sea bass stuffed with lemon and dill and dropped in the fryer. Served with a spring salad". That certainly didn't sound very inspired.
He was clearly trying to hurry us up and out. It was as if he was eyeing the folks waiting at the bar trying to squeeze another seating in.
Unfortunately, this was a disappointing meal. 
Did I mention how salty everything was? I need a glass of water.

For me, this is as good as it gets. It may have been the kitchen counter corner seats  allowing for a great view of the cooking and plating operation leading to fun conversations with the sous. Intelligent inquiries and buying a round for the kitchen staff resulted in some special attention and food we would have otherwise never tried.  The staff was quite attentive and the menu has a lot to choose from. We were there on a Sunday evening when they featured their " Sal's Sunday Supper" which looked great (Spaghetti with Sunday Gravy, meatballs, sausage and a hardboiled egg) but since I was an Amis virgin, we decided to order a la carte from the many menu items that were offered. There were too many to get through on a single visit. Great starters included house made terrine, headcheese croquettes, and fantastic olives. A simple escarole and apple salad was really refreshing. The tripe stew was earthy and very cassoulet-like. It was outstanding by itself and could have served as the meal but the total stars of the night were the homemade pasta dishes we had: Tonarelli Cacio e Pepe and Buccatini with Jalapeño. I actually had dreams about those dishes afterwards because they were that good. A final recommendation would be the homemade rice pudding. . .apparently a secret recipe from the owner's grandfather. There was nothing bad that came out of the kitchen during my visit and so many things on the menu I would love to go back to try. Of the 3 nights in Philly, this was the best meal we had and one of the best I've had in my life in terms of great food execution. . .it was plain good cooking.

Fujianese is one dialect that I don't understand and it's so frustrating because I have so many questions about the menu and dishes.

We are hooked on their soup - ones w/ Chinese herbs w/ different kinds of meat.  Here, we chose with pig feet and stomach.  While it looked disappointing- it was rich and flavorful.  Loved that two pieces of the pig feet were of the toes!  

Also had the stir fried rice noodle w/ pig intestines - again, looks blah but simple and delicious with Napa cabbage and eggs.

Very very disappointing. I took my family here for dinner for the feast of seven fishes. Supposed to be great according to other posts. Then, I realized that you all lied to me!! Well I'm here to tell you the truth. The start was so promising - the swordfish meatballs and baccala spread were delicious, unique dishes. Next came the scallop and shrimp risotto, which was also very tasty but with undercooked rice.

The crab pasta was really just pasta. Could not even taste the crab and there was still shell. 

At this point in the meal, I would have left with a "eh, probably 4 stars despite the ridiculous price". But alas (or shall I say amis), the entrees we're truly inedible. The octopus was bombarded with salt, over-cooked, and oily. The monkfish was its slightly less salty counterpart bae.

At this point it's safe to say that I was a bit salty myself. But a memory is what you are left with - on to desert.

Tiramisu and sesame cookies were very good! However, If you are prediabetic, or just become cranky on sugar highs, don't even smell the lemon cookies - although their consistency was great. The other desert cut in the shape of a biscotti that was supposed to be a biscotti was definitely not. Consistency was closer to shortbread.

If it's not clear - I don't recommend. Happy new year from your friendly yelp krampus.

My girlfriend and I had a wondeful experience from the second we walked in the door. The ambiance of the restaurant was romantic and intimate yet fun and funky.  

The food came quickly and everything was cooked to perfection. You could tell everything, down to the bread, was homeade with their own flare.

Having lived in Italy, my girlfriend is pretty particular about her espresso. For the first time, she was blown away at how similar the espresso was to her experiences in Italy.

Awesome customer service; WILL BE GOING BACK!

It's been a few years since the GF & I were last at Amis. And that's completely on us - we no longer live at 10th and Spruce. Still, we fondly remember some of our best first dates at Amis, which were always coupled with great food and hospitality. Based on  a recent visit back, I'm happy to say that nothing's changed on that front. But it's clear I need to get my butt back out here more often. 

Clockwise from Top Left: Negroni Fresco [$12] | Sangiovese [$12] | House-baked Olive Oil Foccacia

After a fairly busy work-week, drinks were needed. The Negroni Fresco hit the spot for me, with the gin balanced by Atxa Blanco vermouth and the sweetness of Ramazotti amaro. The GF enjoyed a glass of Sangiovese. FYI - the wine list at Amis has always allowed us to find some real gems! House-baked olive oil foccacia was easily enjoyed while waiting for starters. 

Baked Pecorino [$12]
Almond honey

Baked pecorino was pretty perfect - hitting the salty and sweet notes that were just right for the grilled bread. Nice texture from the almonds as well. 

Bass Crudo [$14]
Fava beans, preserved Meyer lemon

Chef Brad Spence and company dropped the bass nicely with the crudo. Hits of salt and citrus made each bite, with the hearty heft of the favas incorporating bits of spring. 

Charred Octopus [$12]
New potato, ramps

Octo was meaty and tender, with lovely charred bits that were accented nicely with garlicky ramps and creamy new potatoes. 

Cacio e Pepe [$18]

Cacio e Pepe is always a must order. Perfect tonnarelli noods were tossed in plenty of butter and Pecorino Romano, with the hits of black pepper providing that bracing bite that makes the dish so memorable. 

Pork Chop Parmigiana [$29]

Beast of Amis is what this restaurant is known for. With whole animal cookery in mind, there are usually a few dishes centered around a specific protein. On this particular night, the "Beast of Amis" was rabbit and normally that's the route I would have taken. But I couldn't help but opt for the massive pork chop parmigiana. Nicely pan-fried, this thick-cut pork chop was juicy on its own, but made even better dressed in tomato sauce, olive oil, ricotta, and plenty of basil. Delicious. 

Creamy Polenta [$6]
Brown butter, sage 

As a side, the glutton in me couldn't help but order the brown butter polenta. And by brown butter, I mean drowned in browned butter and crispy sage. Nutty, rich, and creamy, this was the perfect side for the belly of this pig. 

The kitchen also sent out a delightful strawberry ice cream and chocolate sundae, knowing that we recently got engaged. A nice touch and a wonderful way to cap off a great meal.  

Chef Brad Spence and his kitchen continue to knock it out of the park at Amis Trattoria. But the evening wouldn't have been as memorable without the exceptional service we received throughout the meal. Yes, blogger's bias, but this sentiment has held true since back to 2012. Already looking forward to returning for our next meal!

Hello, swordfish meatballs.  I want you inside me.

^They're lovely fellas, perfectly offering something new (a fish "meatball", wut?) while still retaining their delicate, distinct swordfishiness.^

The Standouts:
- Service.  Excellent, comfortable, omnipresent.
- Cacio e pepe. Maybe a bit too heavy, but all the comfortable flavors were there with a quality that makes you want the dish to never end.
- Bufala ricotta.  Is this ever bad?
- Eggplant fries (in the pacchieri). I don't know why, I just really liked 'em.

The Things I Wish Would Change But Never Will:
- It's loud in there.
- Close quarters.

Tried a few other dishes that were certainly nice, but didn't blow me away as much as I'd expected them to.  Nothing at all bad here and some dishes are among the city's best so overall a solid dining option that will consistently range from very good to exceptional.  Basically a more comfortable, Italian, less pretentious Barbuzzo.

Had the Bucatini Carbonara for brunch. Out of this world.  Best pasta I've tasted in a long time. The muffins that came with the bread basket were also awesome. Cold beer and great service. I'll be back. Five stars for me. And I don't give them out too easily.

!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
bippity boppity boo, the food is kinda gucci
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Went here the night before the Philadelphia Marathon so my husband could have his pasta dinner.  It was delicious!  We ordered several appetizers, all of which were gone immediately, including the extra artichoke they brought to our table.  I had the papardelle with meat sauce.  The homemade pasta makes all the difference, so wonderful!  Next time we're visiting family in Philly, we'll have to take another trip to Amis.

I've visited Amis a number of times over the years since it originally opened.  Often we sit at the chefs counter.  It was fun watching Marc Vetri pop in at some point during the meal and wander through the kitchen.  Indeed it was one of my favorite restaurants in Philly, if not one of my favorites period.  All good things unfortunately do come to an end.  

My most recent visit was in April of 2019.  Again no reservations but the chefs counter is usually first come first serve. The first change I noticed was how dark it was, unnecessarily so.   Since my girlfriend doesn't drink I usually order a carafe, but it wasn't listed.  Fortunately it is still offered if you ask, since the prices on the wine list have continued to rise.   It's hard to justify paying $60 for the least expensive red on the wine menu when you are the only one drinking.   Especially when it's a $16 bottle of Dolcetto, and a glass is $13 or $14.  Terrible value.  

The real disappointment came with the meal.  We ordered the Beef Cheek Saltimbocca.  It was literally a chunk of fat wrapped in Prosciutto.  Barely edible, and really left me scratching my head in disbelief that it made it out to the table.  The Octopus was good as was the Escarole Salad, pretty hard to screw up.   The Bucatini that has been on the menu for a long time was dry and not up to the usual standards.  

In all I feel like I have lost a good friend, and shame on the new owners.

My wife gave me a gift certificate to Bloke's so this was my first visit.  What a wonderful experience.  When I arrived, I was invited to relax on the sofa to wait for my stylist Kayla.  To my surprise I was offered a beer--which hit the spot.  I had a haircut and a razor trim and shaping of my beard.  The haircut and beard trim was great.  

I would like to try some of the other staff.  It appears that haircuts and beard shaping at Bloke's is really an artistic and creative endeavor so it would be interesting to try a few of the staff.

Bloke's is not inexpensive, but it is reasonable all things considered.  I must say I have long wondered why there are few, if any, salons for men, where getting a haircut and perhaps a shave or beard trim is a pleasant experience, and not just a necessity.  I was invited to browse the shop after my haircut.  I want to return with more time, as Bloke's is an interesting place to explore

Great Mini Cream Puffs, Apple Pie Is Good, But The Crust Falls Apart Very Easily.....
The Canoli .... I was Not To my liking ...
Their Fresh Made Italian Bread ... Delicioso!
Will Be Coming Back....
I would Want To Know , If They Use High Fructose
And How Much Artificial Flavors They Use

We had a great lunch here today! We were a group of 3 moms and 4 toddlers - great play area for the kids and we were asked multiple times by staff if we needed a refill on drinks. The food was great as always ... nice place for families!

Making an appointment was extremely easy. My email was responded to quickly. Very friendly and knowledgeable staff. They understand what I wanted and took the time to explain my options. The business came highly recommended to me by a friend. I will return in the future. Great product and value. Comfortable waiting area.
Excellent service. Our server John was great. Very knowledgeable and personable. The food was amazing as well. I ordered the lemon grass chicken bowl, not too pricey. Five stars!

I really liked this place. Great food, great wait staff and owner checked in to see if everything came out ok. Will define come back here. We tried the sticky chicken wings, spring rolls, sizzling beef tacos and 2 kinds of sushi.
Good Vietnamese food.  Recommended to all my friends.  The owner is extremely friendly and nice too.

Strawberry Shortcake, made by many mastered by few.   Schenk's is nearly perfect and I would like to give it 4.75 stars out of 5, here's why; the writing used in the name, the sugar crystallized so maybe a gel writing would have been better.  That's it, that is the only thing "wrong" with the cake.  

The strawberries that topped the cake were sweet and delicious.  Most places use strawberries that are past their prime and lack flavor but not at Schenk's.  Can we talk about price?  I am posting a picture of this massive 10 inch cake that was only $34.  I was expecting $75, talk about reasonable. 

If you need a good, no, great strawberry shortcake, come to Schenk's, you will not be disappointed.

Me and my husband really love Moe's. Especially on Monday. I have nothing to say about the quality of the food, it just taste like a Moe's. 

However, Service is terrible and not consistent. I just wish they will a little bit more about my food. It seems like there is a lot of interns conflict among the staff. 

Come on! In this location, you guys could make so much more money if you had a GOOD service.

oh this place is LEGIT! had no idea it was IN the pour house so fyi to the tourists and out-of-towners!
as for the coffee...i am a nitro connoisseur back in LA la land, and I am so impressed with the stark differences with each nitro on tap. Josh hooked up samples of each of their coffees and teas on tap, and I am in heaven.

Amis has been on my list ever since I moved to center city, and the bf and I finally made it there last Friday night! I was a little last-minute with our reservations so we got a lovely table early at 6:15. We were one of the first few tables seated for the night. 

The ambiance of the restaurant is really nice, very cozy with a beautiful bar and I loved the open kitchen with chefs table overlooking it. The decor was lovely and gave a great feel just walking in the door, very authentic rustic Italian.

We were greeted with fresh olive oil infused focaccia bread at the table. Drink menu has some good options, and the wine list is very Italian so you're safe there! You can taste the wine as well to make sure you like it, and I love when restaurants let you do this, it makes life so much easier! To start we shared the Sal's old school meatballs with tomato & potato, and my boyfriend got the octopus as well. Both were delish, and I've heard the baked pecorino is really good too so I'll have to try that next time!

For our meals, we couldn't pass up the fresh house-made pastas! I got the tonnarelli with cacio e pepe, a square-spaghetti with a creamy, cheesy olive oil sauce that was totally outstanding! My boyfriend got the bucatini with jalapeño and almond pesto which was phenomenal as well, and definitely has a KICK! We were also lucky enough to land a small extra pasta gratis, which was the sopressini with wild boar and pears - so unique and delicious! All the pastas are good portions, hearty enough to fill you up but small enough that if you wanted a meat entree as well you could do that too. We also shared the polenta with brown butter, which was very good but a little rich in combination with all our pasta. Great nonetheless!

We hadn't been on a date night in a while so we splurged and shared the Belgian waffle with Nutella, vanilla semifreddo, and walnuts which was awesome. We were stuffed but managed to finish it anyway - the waffle was so light and crispy it was too good to leave on the plate! Needless to say, we are already antsy to get back to Amis, and it deserves all 5 stars! Grazié!

I felt compelled to write a review because I had such an unusually good experience.  First let me put it out there that I have dietary restrictions.  I am lactose intolerant and gluten sensitive.  Anyone who needs to watch their food intake for medical reasons knows how difficult it is to feel comfortable with the service in a restaurant.  If you are watching your weight and you ask for no butter, you may never know if they serve you butter.  If you are severely lactose intolerant and they serve you butter you know and it's not pleasant.  The server made me feel completely comfortable that she and the kitchen could serve me food that was both dairy and gluten free.  They have a gluten free menu.  Many of their dishes are dairy free or are easily changed.  If I'm paying for a meal, I don't like it when restaurants want to serve me a plain piece of meat with salt and pepper.  I want an interesting meal that has nice flavor.  If it is supposed to come with a sauce, then I want sauce.  I had the lamb shank with risotto.  I was pleasantly surprised that I could even have risotto.  It was an amazing meal.  My husband was jealous, and he can eat both dairy and gluten.  I highly recommend this restaurant for quality of food and service.  I even more highly recommend it for accommodating dietary restrictions.

We came here for NYE, excited to try the spot that Anthony Bourdain raved about on his recent show, The Layover. As a New Yorker, I'm pretty well versed in good food and service and looked forward to Amis given what I had read & heard. 

When your New Years plans revolve around a meal, you're clearly serious about good food and looking for an experience vs just a dinner. We had a 10pm reservation for 4 that had been made weeks in advance; we had called ahead to confirm and were told there'd be a champagne toast at midnight. We were planning to spend the time enjoying a nice & leisurely spaced out meal and drinking until the clock struck 12. 

We specifically asked our waiter to space the meal out, that we weren't in a rush and wanted to take time between courses. We even had requested to put the appetizer order in first and the pasta and entrees later in order to take our time. Instead, he pushed us to put it all in at once, claiming that the pastas would take a lot of time and that we wouldn't be rushed at all. 

Our appetizers were delish, but came all at once. When we'd finished the plates were quickly cleared...and not 5 minutes later we found BOTH our secondi pasta dishes AND our main course entrees laid out in front of us. On top of this, the 2 side dishes we'd ordered with the main courses never showed up! I wasn't happy, it was only 10:30 at this point, a half hour from when we'd started. 

Again our plates were quickly cleared when we'd finished and we ordered dessert which was popped down in front of us quickly. Our meal had been completely rushed-we were done at 11pm, in just one hour! Despite this, our group agreed that we would take our time with dessert & order more cocktails in effort to ring in the new year at 12am. That's when without being asked if we wanted another round and WITHOUT ASKING FOR IT, our check arrived on the table. Mind you, no one was waiting for our table-so what was their rush?

At this point I'd had enough. It was NYE and I felt like they were trying to push us out the door before midnight, while the restaurant still had plenty of seated tables. I went to the manager and explained everything to him-that we had specifically asked the server to space our dinner out, and that not only had we been rushed but our check had come without request when we'd planned to stay. He brusquely told me that he encourages the waitstaff to put in orders at one time and barely acknowledged my points. He told me he'd be happy to bring us another round of drinks, which I accepted.

We rang in the new year, but without a champagne toast-the restaurant had offered NONE. And if that wasn't enough, they didn't even comp us that last round of cocktails-we paid for them! What a gross way to treat customers who paid a fortune for dinner, especially on New Years!! And to add insult to injury, the manager sarcastically stopped us on the way out to wish us a happy new year and to add that he hoped we'd enjoyed the rest of our experience. 

It's a shame that this place is managed by such a terrible staff, because the food was delicious. But if I lived in Philly this would be the LAST freaking place I'd give my money to ever again! Go to a Steven Starr restaurant instead, he knows how to run things!

Excellent food, quick service. I'm usually not impressed by Italian food because pasta just doesn't do it for me. But since we're talking about a Vetri establishment, I thought I'd give it a shot. 

We shared the baked honey almond pecorino, swordfish meatballs, octopus, veal tongue, cacio e pepe pasta, monkfish with San marzano tomatoes, tiramisu for dessert. I'd have to say each dish was masterfully executed. The meatballs were surprisingly moist, the veal tongue and octopus were very tender. The pasta was unlike any I'd had before because it was so dense, but it was cooked perfectly and I enjoyed it. It was a very rich meal. Come hungry.
This location was a disappointment.  We arrived a few minutes after opening. Every booth, except one, was dirty. The ceiling is leaking. The chips were stale. No consistency between the chains.

We came for a holiday event and were able to sample almost the entire menu!

LOVES:
-the meatballs! Melt in your mouth
-grilled octopus-perfectly cooked with a great hit of saltiness
-arancini-something i typically don't eat that was quite tasty
-cauliflower app-who knee this mix of flavors could be so flavorful??
-the service: attentive friendly and amazing!

LIKES
-chicken entree
-eggplant 
-crispy potatoes
-Brussel sprouts-very very crispy

NOT SO GREAT
-bufala ricotta bruschetta -compared to others on 13th street, it was dismal.

Will be back soon!

SERVICE
The waiter was knowledgeable about the food and was very friendly. Each table is given its own bottle of water. They are definitely very efficient with the food prep and delivery. 

FOOD
The bread wasn't that impressive. We didn't even get EVOO. Definitely the worst bread I've had. If you're going to serve flavorless bread then they really should provide very good EVOO and balsamic to have with it. 

We got complimentary bruschetta so we were able to try both. Surprisingly I think we could all agree that the eggplant was the best of the two. 

Everyone at the table got meatballs to start. We each got 3 very large very seasoned and perfectly cooked meatballs. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

It seems as though most of the dishes were vegetarian but with a twist? So they don't use the traditional basil pesto but almond. It wasn't bad but... honestly everything was delicious but one can appreciate old-fashion simple ingredients. 

I'm not sure if these selections they chose for restaurant week wasn't a proper representation but... It seems as though the only thing worth getting would be Cacio e Pepe which is a traditional Roman dish. They seem to be using the correct pasta and they stick true to the ingredients. 

Either way I do think you should go because the food is actually very good but I don't think it captured the simplicity of the Italian cuisine in the restaurant week menu. 

The Tiramisu was definitely sweeter than what I had when I was in Venice but still yummy!

Uneven, hit & amis

I finally experienced the third Vetri restaurant, Amis.  After reading through yelp I wasnt sure what to expect.  I can say now though, it makes more sense to consider the 2 or 3 star feedback for this place.  As a table of five foodies, we shared everything and critiqued each bite as we normally would.  The key word, I think, is uneven.  There were very delicious highs and there were surprisingly disappointing lows or "meh"s.

The appetizers (or smaller dishes from the first few sections of the menu) were clearly the most adventurous payoffs.  The eggplant capanota, the melon-mint-pistachio salad and the swordfish meatballs on creamy polenta were delicious and among high-points.  The spaghetti with pecorino and pepper with a cheese sauce was blah.  Really, it could've used a tiny more cooking and a bit more flavor.  Closing my eyes, I wouldn't distinguish this dish from a corner diner experience (ouch, right?).  

The Mussels were tasty but as quite a lot of our meal, they were way too salty.  In fact, as the meal progressed we accumulated our week's budget of sodium intake.  As we spoke up about it, we shared the opinion that just about all the dishes were noticeably too salted and this is not typically something we've noted at other restaurants.   That's not our usual complaint, so you can imagine our surprise to be in a Marc Vetri restaurant admitting this to each other!

We ordered two main dishes, a grilled rib-eye which was very tasty and tender, though a little bit more raw than we would've ordered.  However, our server never asked us how we'd like our steak.  Even the nice aruguala salad on the side of this dish was a  bit too salted, though a nice balance of the bitter greens to balance the rich fatty and tender meat.  The other "larger" plate was the seafood platter which was sparse and less than seeming $24 worth. I had a 3" square of toasted polenta filling a third the plate even.    

Desserts and coffee were wonderful.  We had a good ricotta crumble cake.  The Baci Tartufo,  however, was divine.  The coffee was very good but my friends that had espresso drinks were super impressed with the cappuccino and decaf espresso, going on and on about how great they were.  

I do not predict any of us heading back to Amis for dinner, though we admitted it might be smart to go for cocktail hr nearby, and stop in for an appetizer and dessert after.
Went back last week...ordered the same dishes and more this time and the food was extremely average.  very disappointing.

Never again. Went there years ago not impressed. Went two days ago. Very disappointed. The employees are good. The food just barely average. The cost way too much. Extra for their crummy queso. It's like Elmer's glue with a couple jalapeños. 
           Qdoba so much better with more choices of queso and more with no upcharge. Don't waste your time or money!!!

The new location is not all that. I'm sure that the inside was nice but the outside patio is not great. They need to add some plants and greenery.  It's going to be hot out there in the summer. As for the food, the pork chop had a heavy sauce that was not very palatable. The old location was my go to space. I am hoping this is just growing pains and that they improve the wine list, the food and the outdoor ambiance.
Food are not extremely fresh. Hotpot soup was not very authentic. Just a convenient location for lunch with fast dishes.
This Chick-fil-A is awful. Asked for an 8 piece and looks like I got someone else's left overs.

Was visiting Philly for the weekend for a conference and decided to come to Amis Trattoria for dinner last night. WOW! My colleague and I were absolutely blown away. Everything about this restaurant is fantastic. The ambiance is very nice, the couple next to us was celebrating their anniversary! Our server, Rob, went above and beyond for us. He was incredibly attentive - from bringing out our drinks immediately, to cleaning off our table after each appetizer, and he even gave us a free pasta dish!! The food was absolutely delicious. The brussel sprouts were zesty and perfectly cooked. All of the pasta was flavorful and the ingredients were fresh. I cannot recommend this restaurant enough if you are in Philly. I will definitely come again the next time I am in town.

Had the veal chop, fennel as recommended by the waitress. Best steak(?) dish ever had. 

Service was fantastic, very knowledgable of the menu. We even had the opportunity to meet the owners of the restaurant. Great people, great food. Will be coming back!

My girlfriend and I went to Amis a couple of weeks ago.  It was our first Vetri restaurant, and we came with high hopes, though not much of an idea of what to order.

The atmosphere was great--nice tasteful, not too pretentious.  The menu was unnecessarily opaque for a country bumpkin like myself.  No descriptions of the menu items, and lots of long Italian words in the titles (for example the ice creamy dessert is called "semifreddo" instead of gelato).  Still, our young waiter was quite happy to oblige or requests for explanations of half of the words on the menu.

We appreciated the availability of an affordable carafe of house red.  For an undiscerning palate like my own, it hit the spot.

For appetizers, we went for the Ricotta with Black Pepper Bruscetta and the Escarole Salad with Apples and Radishes.  Both were absolutely, deliciously simple.  Couldn't have been happier.

The entree is where things got dicier.  We went for the Strozzapreti with Clam Cockles and Muscles and the Guinea Hen Leg Saltimbucca with Prosciutto and Sage.  I liked the guinea hen better, but both were disappointments.  I'm a chronic over-salter, but these went above and beyond even my salty tastes.  Too much.  And the strozzapreti didn't even have that much taste beyond the salt.

For dessert, we went with the Waffles Amis and the Pear Almond Tart (forget the exact name of the pear/almond dessert).  The waffles were wonderful, the pear almond dessert not so much--dry and tasteless.

Overall, not a bad experience, but Amis did not live up to my expectations, and I can't give it more than 3*'s.  I may go back sometime to do a better job of picking those entrees.

So happy to see this Chick-fil-A open in my neighborhood on the site of a former Sonny's BBQ restaurant.

My visit came in the evening for dinner and I had no issues accessing the building or parking my vehicle or any "Chick E Cheese" atmosphere with kids wreaking havoc as is usually the case at the South Dale Mabry location.

Once inside, I enjoyed the expected high level of customer service from CFA. Employees are clearly trained very well at this new location and enthusiastic to have jobs here.

My food seemed to take a little longer than desired considering they were not busy, but I appreciated the taste of my items and how perfectly they were prepared and packaged for a takeout order.

The dining room is better than other CFA's that I have visited around Tampa Bay, although I'm not sold that this "communal table" is a good idea. It is sort of the "waiting room" for CFA customers and none of us like waiting rooms. 

For others here on Yelp complaining about getting in and out of their parking lot, may I point out that this CFA is located in front of a large plaza with plenty of spaces. Park to the left of Moe's or out in front of Winn Dixie and walk 75-150 feet to enter the restaurant. This is not a big deal at all.

Now if CFA corporate would just admit they made an error when they replaced the previous version of the Chicken Salad sandwich and bring it back, we'd have a five star review. 

Must be an Atlanta thing when it comes to these types of big failures:

Coca-Cola rolls out New Coke

Not one but TWO professional hockey teams leave town for Canada

And there's that blown 28-3 lead in Super Bowl LI
Glad they did away with the sidewalk bar as outdoor seating.

Hit or miss. I've been to this place a few times and generally enjoyed it. The service is good and atmosphere nice, but the food (what counts the most) ranges from meh to pretty good. 

Take last week when I went with some friends on a visit for brunch. The bread basket was terrific and carbonara (they generally do good pasta), outstanding, but the frittata dry and bland, and the "soft scramble" not at all soft and watery (gross). The scrapple (yes, scrapple) was  excellent but bacon underdone in half of it and extra crispy the other. 

It's a perfectly decent place, just remember to order wisely!

One of the first great things about Amis is that it's only a few blocks away from me. If a place is close by and has great food, they're already on my good list. The first time I was here, my wife and I sat down in a very busy and loud corner of the restaurant. I was a little worried that our experience wouldn't be so great due to both of these factors, but boy (and girl and everyone in between) was I wrong!

Our waitress, who was all smiles and energy, came by right away and took our drink orders. She was back in under 5 minutes with them! She then, very excitedly told us the specials and explained a few things on the menu. We decided on the Brussels sprouts for a side dish and then I got the Bronzino and the wife got a pasta dish. The pasta dish came out first, and then a few seconds later, someone delivered a side order of crispy potatoes. We told the server that we were actually waiting on Brussels, and before he could even respond, those were set down on the table by another person. The potato guy said it was on the house, and if some dude comes at you with free potatoes, you smile and say thank you. As the side order servers walked away, our waitress was back profusely apologizing that I didn't receive my Bronzino yet. Within 1 minute (or less) the Bronzino made it's way over. No apology was ever necessary as all the food, including the free potatoes were served within 25 minutes of arrival. 

EVERYTHING was soooo delicious. The sides were super crispy on the outside and buttery soft on the inside. The fish was filling and well seasoned even though I omitted the spicy sauce. The pasta was "creamy and super yummy" based on my wife who always has the most descriptive words for my reviews. We were 100% satisfied, but still craving a little something sweet. We ordered the pavlova, which was huge and so damn sweet, and because my dish arrived so late (3 seconds), we got another dessert on the house!! It was the very hazelnutty and very creamy tartufo. Holy sweet tooth Batman. This place delivered and then delivered some more, and then delivered on top of their 2 deliveries. So much yes!

I'll also add that we came back a few weeks later and had another very delicious meal. This time we sat outside and though the service was not quite on it as the first time around, the beautiful quiet night made our delicious meal just perfect! We can't wait to return.

The more I think about this place the less I like it. I really wanted to like it given the rapturous applause of anything Vetri on this site. Giorgio's on Pine is better and cheaper. Also, why would you give an Italian restaurant a French name?

I've been wanting to try Amis since it opened a few months ago. I live two blocks away and it always sounds loud and lively when I walk by. 

Last night did not disappoint! Reservations seem necessary, but I made mine only one or two days before and it was fine. I was there with three others, and we shared 8 plates total.

the baked pecorino with honey was to die for. to. die. for. except they should give you a little more bread to go with it...
fritto misto was great, except the shrimps still had heads...never seen that before. but the zucchini chips were amazing.
and the stuffed figs (something i order whenever i see them on a menu) were just ok. tria has better ones. 
however, the larger dishes were amazing. we had the fettucini with pork ragu, which practically melted in my mouth it was so delicious. the eggplant lasagna was amazing and not too overwhelming. and the lamb with potatoes was made to perfection. grilled veggies topped it off just right.

for dessert we split a fruit crisp that was so good i wanted to lick the bowl. we also had the waffle with nutella, but i wasn't as crazy about it (and i love nutella, so that's saying something). 

i definitely suggest anything with local in season fruits and veggies. 
and if you want a cocktail instead of wine, go with any of their fun prosecco drinks! the granita is my new favorite beverage. 

oh, and the staff was great, very helpful and on point- even when it got super busy later in the evening.

Overall, the food and service were terrific here.  We sat outside and thus did not get a great sense of the ambiance indoors, but I would certainly be willing to come back and try indoor seating when the weather isn't quite as nice.  We split two pastas, one entree, and one vegetable side dish between two people and felt that was the right amount of food (though we went hungry!).  Our server was knowledgeable and helpful.

Very pleasant restaurant with amazing food and wine choices. We started with the eggplant bruschetta after reading the reviews from here, and it is was definitely worth it. For the pasta dish, we chose the jalapeño dish with a delicious almond butter sauce. My favorite part of the meal was the dessert. We ordered the last pavlova to try something new, and it was one of the most delicious flavor combinations I've ever had!

In short: eat everything and anything here and leave happy.

It's all good. The quality of the food, to the presentation, to that AMAZING olive oil bread basket. The service is spot on, and the atmosphere is classic and not at all stuffy or pretentious. 

This has been a favorite of mine for quite some time, but my last visit this past weekend really sealed the deal for me. Each and every small dish is to die for: We've had the swordfish meatballs a few times, the scallops were perfectly cooked, and the pumpkin and fresh mozzarella salad was perfectly dressed with a peppery sauce complete with pistachios. 

The fresh pasta... you cannot pass this up. It is the sole purpose of this restaurant. Get one or more pasta dishes. If you are eating a small plate or two, a pasta dish is the perfect portion to finish up your meal. 

Our waitress was sweet and knowledgeable, and easily able to point out some menu standouts. She was kind enough to remove a drink from our bill that was perfectly made but simply not to the liking of my dining partner. She really didn't have to do that.

The ONLY downside happened during this past visit. The "special" truffle fettuccine dish with "special truffles imported from Italy" was an $85 dish. While it was delicious, it came as a surprise at the end of the night when we got our bill, and maybe should have been mentioned during the special offerings. "We have a very special truffle fettuccine tonight for $85" We probably still would've ordered it, but it was necessary to bring it up beforehand in my opinion.

I had high expectations for this place but my experience was not great. The place was packed on a Saturday night but the service was pretty quick. If you are here with a large group they wont sit you unless your entire party is there (even though you are ordering drinks at the bar). The menu is tapas type dishes and they have a really good wine list. If you order the same wine as another person at your table they give you an extra little jug of wine as a refill and you're suppose to split it evenly by yourselves (which i thought it was a little weird to have to split the wine on your own, make sure your friend doesn't finish your share! lol). The brussels sprouts i ordered were delicious as well as the swordfish meatballs. The main entree i got was swordfish pasta with eggplant fries. The dish was a little tasteless. The fish and eggplant were ok but the pasta was really dry and tasted a bit like cardboard.
First time I came here I had Veal for the first time. It was amazing. I loved the butternut squash. The sauce was very rich

Absolutely delish!! There's really not much to like about Amis, this flagship spot of the Vetri chain. They hand roll all of their pasta,  hand bake all of their bread, and use locally sourced ingredients! The ambiance is on point, with darker vibes, tons of candles, an open kitchen and outdoor seating. Service was impeccable, cocktails were stiff, and uber creative, and the food was such an elevated modern twist on the Italian classic you love...

Think bucatini with jalapeños and almond pesto and a white crab lasagne with béchamel and basil pesto. Wowza! Both were ordered by our crew, and both were very much well liked, with the bucatini being a fan favorite! So much flavor and it's definitely unmistakable homemade fresh pasta, cooked perfectly and properly al dente'. 

To start, we were given a basket of hot, crisp, thick load with incredible olive oil and offered more. (Love that!) We were all starving and jumped in with an order of their rosemary fried potatoes, which were perfectly cooked, crisp on the edges and seasoned well, as well as the baked pecorino with sticky, icky good almond honey. What a nice blend of the salty and the sweet. 

While they don't officially have a kids menu, they were kind enough to make our girls just a plate of pasta red, which they enjoyed. 

For cocktails we tried the 'Fumoso', which was comprised of mezcal, lime and curaçao with Calabrian chili. It was incredible! Think tropical with a spicy twist. Perfect balance of flavors. 

We were able to sneak in without reservations of a Friday around 9pm, and in the city, we consider that quite a win. 

Unfortunately, I did hear they're closing and the end of the summer, so definitely try to make it in before then. It was really a wonderful meal all around. 

They do serve brunch also, which I can imagine would be lovely on a gorgeous Sunday morning outside in the city. I personally want to hit up their Navy Yard location for their fried avocado dish!

We moved to Philly 3 months ago and hadn't had a bad meal until now. I left hungry. I usually take tons of photos of food. I was so disappointed that I didn't take any. And I regret not to be able to show you. First, this place is about the scene. Seen and to be seen. Not food. I got a martini it was fine. Husband had a glass of red, it was maaaybe 3 or 4 ounces at its best. Then onto the food. We always start with a salad so we asked for recommendation from our waitress- she said the Escarole salad is leafy, refreshing and a great start. We got the salad, it was again, maybe total of 3 or 4 ounces. It was composed of some butter lettuce, couple pieces of apples. A little bit of the pecorino cheese. For $12, I was expecting at least a full plate... It tastes just okay. Then I got the squid ink risotto $20. Husband got the braised goat $30. The risotto came on like a flat plate that looked like a side dish plate. On there, a think layer of the risotto. A few pieces of crab. It almost instantly got cold because there was basically nothing on the plate! I ate it, it was good enough in taste. It was just gone in maybe 8 bites lol. I laughed because I usually NEVER finish my food. The goat was tender. And that was the only thing about the dish. The butternut squash was so sweet and rich. He couldn't finish it. We also keep finding small firm sticks. I think they were some herbs that used to flavor but didn't all get removed. So with drinks and tips, our bill was around 100 bucks. I think I will take Benny elsewhere next time.
The slowest service  it took us 20 minutes to get a frozen coffee from the drive thru...
The staff was nice. The food portions got way smaller. I'm giving this specific location 3 stars because it was so hot inside that we boxed up our stuff and ate in the car. WTF?!
Loud, loud, loud, tables waaayyyy too close together. food is good, service is great!+

I love this place! The food is imaginative and delicious - always a treat. I recently had the clams, which were delightful. The beet salad and risotto were excellent as well, just a couple of many good options for vegetarians. The service and atmosphere were also impeccable. The building is truly representative of Tucson, and the history well preserved. Check out the patio on a nice evening - can't be beat!

Good service, horrible food. Our waiter was the only shining star of our experience, earning Amis two stars instead of one. 

My partner and I took her mother out for her birthday here, and quickly regretted it. All the dishes are laden with salt and dripping in oil. The swordfish meatballs that everyone raves about? Mostly breadcrumbs, Kraft-brand grated Parmesan, and the tiniest hint of swordfish imaginable. My partner's mother and I both ordered the lamb with potatoes, which was described on the menu as "roast lamb coated in spices with oven baked potatoes." Sounds tasty, right? Not at all what we received. The lamb had been pulled from the bone, smashed flat, deep fried, then coated in salt. The potatoes had been mashed, reshaped into cubes, frozen, then deep fried as well. There was nary a vegetable to be found, just a plate full of fried, over salted food. Not at all what the menu made the dish out to be. 

My partner ordered the roast pork with polenta. The polenta was the consistency of day old jello, and the pork had been cooked "medium rare like steak" (not food safe). Absolutely appalling, and for such high prices! Would never recommend this restaurant to anyone - not even my enemies.

Amis is a wonderful place for quality small-plate dishes and entrees. Your server will most likely suggest 2-3 small plates for a couple, as well as one entree each.  Do yourself a big favor and get the bufala ricotta with olive oil, black pepper and grilled bread. It's simplicity is what makes it so delectable.  Also, the sweetbreads, if you don't mind organ meat, was the best I've ever had.  For small-plates, we also had the swordfish meatball with polenta and pignoli.  Of the entrees, the lamb shank with creamy polenta was amazing, though my girlfriend's pasta dish (oxtail cannelloni with roasted mushrooms) was a bit dense. Lastly, since it was our anniversary, they gave up a highball of vanilla bean semifreddo. Very nice overall.

Oh my. I just tasted my first cake from this bakery at the American Cancer Society Relay for Life event. I am SO bummed that living all the way in NJ will make it difficult for me to eat here every day. 
Absolutely delicious sheet cake! And I am a self-proclaimed sheet cake snob.
Highly, highly recommended. 
Many thanks to this bakery for their generous support of a good cause.  I am a new avid fan!  Perhaps even their biggest fan. I even dreamed about the cake last night! I kid you not.

OK, went back over a year later and well, things haven't changed.  If I'm setting the bar too high, well, that's what a national reputation brings.  Marc Vetri has been hyped out the wazu, and I just don't taste it, folks.  The meatballs were so pedestrian, I feel like I've had them a million times around the world, including my own kitchen.  You shouldn't feel that way for the price point.  Everything is smothered in cream and cheese, so of course it tastes good at first, and then you realize you feel nauseated and get sick of the one trick the pony is doing.  Sadly, I'm over it.

Fun P.S.:  I'm on a flight to San Francisco the very next day and sit next to a guy who coincidentally dined at the restaurant the night before as well!  We compared notes and started finishing each other's sentences about the disappointment we felt.  Sigh.

As a regular patron of the Philly restaurant scene, both fine dining and otherwise, I have to admit that I was excited to try the latest Vetri endeavor.  I was sadly disappointed.  Maybe I went on an off night (a Tuesday in December)...but everything - the food, service, ambiance- was a let down.  I started with the shaved fall vegetable salad, which was good, but certainly didn't meet my expectations as to flavor or presentation.  I ordered the bucatini with braised oyster mushrooms as an entree.  It was oily/greasy and overseasoned, with cheese that overwhelmed the flavor of the mushrooms.  Honestly, I have had better pasta dishes at  certain inexpensive, chain Italian restaurants I patronized occasionally in college.  It simply was nothing special, and definitely did not live up to our expectations.  One of my friends ordered the gnocchi, which was also a greasy disappointment.  The octopus appetizer was alright, but again, nothing special. 

The worst thing about Amis was the atmosphere, however.  It was so loud that we literally had to shout to hold a conversation.  There were 6 of us at the table, and we were celebrating a friend's birthday.  Luckily, I sat next to the friend with the birthday, because otherwise I wouldn't have been able to communicate with him at all- it was that noisy.  Our waiter was no help - he practically mouthed the specials and when we asked questions, his attitude fluctuated between smarmy and condescending (to a crowd of fairly discerning diners, mind you - we are not rookies of fine dining) and brusque and unhelpful.  At first we thought it was one table of loud diners ruining the ambiance for everyone, but even after they left, there was a din that couldn't be overcome.  It was unpleasant.  It's really a shame, since I've had several, much better experiences at Osteria, another Vetri restaurant.  It seems that Amis needs to be reworked.

The other night I went to Chic-fil-A at Kirkman and Conroy in Orlando for some soup, I have a cold and went through the drive to get soup and go home to bed. I was in the right lane waiting to order and as I sat I saw 3 other cars go through the left lane and be served. So I figured something was wrong and went inside to get the soup. I asked for a manager to report the problem with the left lane and Celeste came to the counter. When I told her what happened, she said to get in line and order the soup. I told her I had just waited in line outside and could I order from her. She said , if I wanted to order I had to get in line behind many other people and wait my turn or I could leave . I was very surprised  because this is very bad customer, especially from Cick-fil-A because of the professional way they conduct themselves at their other stores. Apparently, Celeste, whom I found out later is not a manager, even though she represented herself as one, has not had the proper training to work at Chik-fil-A. 

Gary Gordon- Orlando

This little restaurant is really special.   The atmosphere was so nice and the food was delicious.   The staff made us feel like we were in their home.  Would definitely come again next time we visit Tucson.
honestly i've had better hot pots in bathrooms. the worst part of the experience was the way the waiter HIT MY SON, i demanded a REFUND but they wouldn't GIVE IT TO ME

Amis is a well run place with excellent preparations of wonderful ingredients. We started with baked young pecorino cheese covered with almonds and honey. The pastas were fresh with seasonal accents including a pappardelle with fresh corn and scallions. The best dessert was an olive oil cake with fresh blackberries. Our server was professional and efficient.

Arrived without reservations so we sat at the table in front of the chefs. Got to watch them prepare the meals and drool over (from a distance) the dishes. ;-)
Got the fresh mackerel, sweetbreads, veal tongue, and tripe stew.  Loved them all!!!

The place is crazy loud so be prepared to nearly shout to carry a conversation.

So glad I finally tried this. The menu looked incredible, the food was excellent and the service superb!
I got the pappardelle with oxtail, it was delicious but I did find a couple of bones. I casually mentioned it to the waitress who was so sweet, she brought our table free dessert because of it!
I will most definitely be back!

Don't you hate it when an unexpected surprise on your bill spoils an otherwise amazing meal?! That's exactly what happened when I came here this past weekend. I had been wanting to try Ming River for the longest time after my dad raved about how this was the best Fuzhou food he's had outside of China.

Our group ordered a ton of items from the Fuzhou Specials section of the menu and thoroughly enjoyed everything. My absolute favorite was the guo bian hu, which I haven't had in years and totally brought me back to eating it growing up. I also really enjoyed the peanut butter noodles and meat dumpling soup. The flavors are delicate, simple, and homey, and it's exactly the type of food you want when your taste buds have been overwhelmed by the oilier and saltier foods other restaurants serve. And what's even better is that everything is super affordable. Nearly all the items from the Fuzhou Specials are under $5, which means you can try a little bit of everything without feeling guilty.

So why 3 stars? Because we were completely overcharged and given the worst reason for it. When we asked for the bill, our server told us the amount without actually bringing a bill over, which isn't that unusual for such a small place. However, $38 was higher than expected so we asked for an itemized bill. The hand-written bill she gave us had no prices next to the items, so we then cross-checked everything we ordered against the menu prices and totaled it ourselves. The bill was in fact too high, and I waved her over again to tell her there must be a mistake. She proceeded to tell us in an annoyed and impatient tone that their prices recently went up and there was no mistake in the bill she gave us. SAY WHAT? First of all, why would you not tell us this when we spent 10 mins looking up the menu prices and adding up the bill in an attempt to double check the math? Secondly, how are YOU annoyed at US when we were clearly misinformed by YOUR menu? And finally, shouldn't any decent business honor their menu prices, especially if they gave no indication that prices have since changed?

At that point, we were all so irritated we just paid and left as quickly as we could. Would I come back though? Probably, actually, because the food really was that good, and you really can't find this type of Chinese food easily here. Would just make sure to ask about prices upfront next time and know exactly what to expect on the service front.

Stumbled across this place, figured we would give it a try on a cold rainy day (perfect for hot pot). And here is what I walked away thinking:

- Food = good overall, nothing special but nothing bad
- Prices = decently priced but not worth, they charge you for every little thing and the portions are small, not ideal for sharing if you have to order multiple of the same dish 
- Service = awful

Which brings me to the main point of my review, the service was extremely disappointing. From the looks of the restaurant, they are certainly overstaffed. Only about 3-4 tables were occupied when I came to eat, yet there was waiters and hosts and bartenders all over the place. You would think that they would take good care of us having all these people...we were ignored basically the entire time. We had to keep trying to get their attention to ask for the bare essentials, which I think is unnecessary. All on separate occasions, we had to ask them for water, for spoons, for napkins, for bowls, meanwhile the entire staff were just sitting around on their phones and iPads during our meal. They probably thought we were asking for too much and being too troublesome for the amount of service we had to ASK for. When I asked for bowls, the guy just pointed and said "they're over there". Idk maybe it's me, but good service would have just gotten for the customers, I had to get up, walk all the way to the back of the restaurant mid meal just so I could get bowls for my table since my guy went back to playing on his phone after he pointed it out to me. 

Won't be returning, solely because I was not impressed and I felt like I served myself the entire time and that's not what we pay for.

The meal starts out with complementary bread that's cake like. The ricotta with black pepper is a must try! It's been days and I'm still thinking about this dish. If you're feeling adventurous order the grill veal tongue. It was my first time having veal tongue and not my last time. For the main entree we ordered the spring pea tortelli in a lamb ragu. It has to be one of the best tortelli in the city. 

The service was good nothing over the top. 

Overall, the food is great. So if you are looking to over load on delicious carbs give this place a try!

This place was a stunner! OMG! Start to finish, all
aspects were incredible! The pastas were out of control. That cacio e Pepe had the perfect al dente bite you want from a homemade pasta. Oh my god I don't think I can eat anything but homemade pastas after having that dish. Basically ruined me it was that tasty. The beef cheek saltimbocca was melt in your mouth. The combo of the beef with the crispy prosciutto and that sage was an unreal combo. Mmmmm. The desserts were lovely too! Rice pudding wowza! And the pistachio cream with the pavlova was one of my fav moments in the meal. I left here so happy. And it was a place that both gluten fans and enemies can enjoy! All will leave with a smile :)

Hands down the worst Chick Fil A in Tampa. They've been open for like 2 years now and have had 0 improvement. They always take forever to bring you your order and shits wrong a lot of the time. Curbside pickup takes longer than going through the line, how does this make sense?? They suck. All of the employees look like they hate their lives and are incompetent. Management is even worse. Please don't waste your time coming here and just drive to the South Tampa location.

Great food.  We are displaced New Yorkers and Amis delivered last week as well as any of our favorite restaurants in Tribeca or Brooklyn.  All of the plates we had were delicious and all had great flavors + seasonings and well put together seasonal vegetables integrated into the dishes.  didn't seem like the chef was trying overly hard on the local point (which is starting to get ridiculous at times these days).

Couple of points which really sets Philadelphia restaurants apart from the best in NYC and Los Angeles (and I'd throw Chicago in there) are small touches like the fact Amis uses Dial pump soap in the bathrooms (Dial, really?)  At least throw down $2.50 for Method at Costco.  And the waiters outfits just seems like someone had thought too hard about making a statement.  

GREAT food

Went for the Cacio e Pepe and it was beyond amazing. Great little quaint place with food and drinks to die for. We saw chef Brad Spence on tv and originally went for him (and his cacio e Pepe). We will definitely spread the word and will be back.
The best chocolate cream filled donut in Foxchase! This place is great and is always clean. Love the hours, 7:00pm on weekdays!

All time favorite restaurant in Philly. Nice enough to feel like you are having a nice night out but not too fancy to make you uncomfortable. Menu is always changing and definitely never disappoints. Service is great. Food even better.

Amis has become a favorite go-to for a date or dinner/drink with friends. I love the atmosphere and the food and the service is usually excellent. They do get quite crowded on weekends, so make a reservation for dinner!

For drinks, they have a great selection of beer, wine, and cocktails. My favorite is the prosecco - seems to go with everything and if you're craving something a little more fun, order a granita! They'll serve you a prosecco with a little dish of semi-frozen berry deliciousness to add to it and it's just so yummy!

We usually go with the small plates to get a nice variety, and who doesn't like sharing? A couple of the stand-outs: warm pecorino with almond honey (divine), quail with bitter greens and kumquat marmalade (great complementation of flavors), fried brussels sprouts with lemon (perfectly seasoned and a great portion). I have a pretty specific diet, and can always find something tasty!

I've had to wait for a few times when we didn't have a reservation and ran into friends there the other night that waited even WITH a reservation, but they were quite busy and make it up to you with their friendly waitstaff and oftentimes even some complimentary small plates from the kitchen. 

Highly recommend! Have taken out of town visitors and they loved it just as much as I do.

There are no stars for this over priced, loud, mediocre meal restaurant. The best part was the sparkling water. The items on the menu were so obscure they had to be googled. The simplest dish, spaghetti and meatballs had to be ordered off menu and it was overpriced and underwhelming. 
Avoid this place.
Have never been in and out for an order under 15 min, even when they aren't busy. Transaction times are wayyyyy to long for customers.

I love Chick-fil-A all across the country, great food and great service. This Chick-fil-A and the other one on Dale Mabry are not good at all. No matter what time of day, busy or not, you will wait in the drive-thru for 25 min at the very least. The service is bad, the people are not kind and welcoming. Also, my order has been wrong 3 times.

I didn't expect to like this place - after all, I don't like the overpoweringly smelly soaps at Lush - but I loved it. 

They had a wonderful range of natural smelling products for bath and body, including shampoos, scrubs, moisturizers, conditioners, soaps, washes, face masks, and deodorants. The main display table held piles of glowing and translucent soaps that were hand cut and priced by weight. They smelled enticing and included such skin-friendly ingredients as shea butter, sea salt, olive oil, black clay and aloe. 

One of the soap-makers was standing by the table ready to answer questions about the soap-making process, or about the ingredients, or to cut a bar to specified size. After some deliberation I chose one bar that contained goatsmilk, oatmeal, honey, calendula and slippery elm and another that contained strawberry seeds, aloe, and champagne. Both smelled heavenly and didn't burn my nose. I also picked up a bitter almond shower gel with cherry blossom extracts  that smells so good that I pause when scrubbing just to breathe in the scent. 

Although I didn't buy any I was really intrigued by the aluminum-free deodorants, which are made of a vegetable protein base and come in such scents as moroccan cedar, sandalwood lavender, violet and spiced lime. If they'd only had one in bitter almond I would have snatched it up.  

I have to say I was impressed by the customer service - everyone working there was knowledgeable, friendly, and efficient. The line moved quickly and items were nicely wrapped in tissue. I came away oddly excited to get home from Philly and treat myself to a soapy shower.

HORRIBLE customer service!! I have made an appointment with them and they have rescheduled me TWICE with this last time saying "we will call you back when we can see you". So now I'm waiting for a call next week to find out when they can do me the "favor". I am so disappointed in this business and always try to support local owned businesses but this one is horrible! I don't recommend them to anyone. Spend your money somewhere else.
This place is super delicious and the staff is all very nice! The Beef Balls with Pork are particularly delicious.

My boyfriend was meeting me and another couple there, but was delayed by the snow. So I had to keep pushing back our reservation. They were super accommodating, on a Friday night no less, which definitely won me over. The food, though, was not all that remarkable. Don't get me wrong, everything was tasty, but nothing stands out upon reflection. Except the "semifreddo," but that's only because it was more like a custard than a real semifreddo. It had a nice flavor profile, but the texture and consistency were off.

Anyway, having never been to Vetri, I could be wrong about this, but this seems like the perfect place for people who love Mark Vetri, can't afford his flagship enterprise on a regular basis, but want to get as close to that experience as possible without setting all their money on fire to do it again.

Ordered 2 of the exact same orders, a chick fil a sandwich no pickles combo, the first sandwich was fine no pickles but the fries lacked the "sprinkling of sea salt" the fries were not seasoned what so ever, I was able to move past that but my 2nd sandwich I ordered came with pickles and that's where my foot goes down. Only 3 things come on the sandwich. Bread, chicken and pickles. Now when I ask for no pickles and somehow pickles still ends up on the sandwich when there's only 3 things that come on it anyhow that's just ridiculous. Also need a larger lot or something because the drive thru is all out of whack with so many cars being in it and no room to leave the parking lot it.

Edit; decided to order 2 meals exactly the same .. number 1 add Colby jack cheese. I receive my order and head home to eat my lunch with my girlfriend before I have to get ready for work. Once I get home I open my sandwich and instead of Colby jack I received pepper jack.. The cheese by then was practically stuck to the chicken and I couldn't get it off without ruining my food so With that being said I didn't have much time to go back and have it replaced so my lunch was pretty much ruined with me only being able to eat fries and a soda. I called and was hoping they could offer superior customer service by replacing my meals since I could not enjoy my lunch and I had to go to work rather hungry. They informed me they could only replace the sandwiches rather than the whole meals.. (Even though it wouldn't have costed them much to just replace the whole meals) While I was rather irritated they couldn't replace the whole meal I accepted the remakes and they gave me a 48hr time period to come back so they could fix their mistake. I went in and after a lengthy wait (1 employee on register and another employee just standing around) I finally was able to talk to a manager and she put my orders in. I received my food but this time before leaving I checked my sandwiches and once again I received pepper jack rather than Colby jack. At this point I was expecting to receive some sort of voucher for their continuous screw ups .. instead I received nothing. By the way, the managers position was "Hospitality director" she wasn't nice at all.. and while she wasn't mean either it's not what you'd expect from a "Hospitality Director" ... Carlos Brito, I don't know what your standards are.. but these are not the chick fil a standards I am accustomed to.

It's just not the same ....

We are long time Coronet visitors and were excited to go to the new location. 

The food arrived cold, the chocolate mousse wasn't a mousse, the soup was a thick enchilada sauce not a soup, the menu descriptions seemed off from what arrived....

The cocktails were fine...

The service was lacking.... took multiple requests to get simple things like bread, cocktails and water.  

The order numbers were backwards for every serving... cocktails, appetizers, and main.  It got old having to repeat ourselves. 

We made the reservation more than a month ago for the holidays and we were seated next to the door with cold air and people standing over us.  Like we had made the reservation that morning and we were being squeezed in. 

Not what we hoped for... sadly, we won't be back and we won't recommend to others.

This location is just ok. For some reason they like to give extra small portions compared to other locations I have been to. I find myself constantly telling them put more lettuce in my bowl. Why they skimp on lettuce? I'm honestly not sure. The workers aren't the friendliest but hey, it's Chipotle. 

I will say the parking is horrendous at this location. It's hardly packed inside but the parking lot is too small for the shopping center because there are hardly any parking spots that are ever open right in front.
After several bad experiences and a complaint to corporate, this chipotle has come around and redeemed itself.

Impersonal, unfriendly, and constantly trying rush me. They unapologetically skimp on ingredients like no tomorrow, and they will give you a glare if you object. I never have complaints about Chipotle, but this location needs a serious retraining of its staff.

This is the most authentic shop I've found in the US for their Fu Jian wonton soup.  The wontons are suppose to be tiny with just a little bit of meat.  Add some hot oil and it's perfect.  The meat wonton soup and Guo Bian Hu are delicious as well.

They need to be trained pertaining to service dogs.  The server thought it was odd that we asked for water for the dog.  The service dog always gets water when you go out to eat.  This dog is with me at all times, and per the ADA law written into law under former President Bush.   The food was good quality.  The staff overall was friendly.
I've been here 3 years and never had chick-Fil-a and omg am I in love! One the best "fast food" places to go down here. Forget McDonald's and Burger King come get this fresh chicken!

Roman Italian at its best! 

Mark Vetri is a fixture in, what is becoming, the nationally recognized Philadelphia restaurant scene and he's certainly outdone himself. My boyfriend and I came here the Monday of the week of Thanksgiving for a 7:15pm reservation and we were seated promptly upon our arrival. The ambiance of the restaurant is really comforting. The decor is lovely and gave a great feel just walking in the door, very authentic rustic Italian. The warm colors made the restaurant feel cozy and inviting - perfect for a date night. 

After being seated, we were warmly greeted by our waiter who was well-versed in the menu and attentive, without being overbearing, throughout the entire meal. The drink menu has some great options and the wine list is very Italian! To kick things off, we ordered two glasses of nice Italian wines and were offered fresh olive oil infused focaccia bread at the table.

To start we shared the eggplant caponata, semolina crusted shrimp with parsley sauce and baked pecorino with almond honey. The caponata was a good balance of sweet and sour. The shrimp were unique with their crunchy semolina exterior but could have been seasoned a little more. As for the baked pecorino? To die for! I'm putting it down of as one of my top "eats" for 2015. Absolutely delectable. 

We ordered another round of wine and some more plates to share. My wonderful dining partner and I went with the quail with charred polenta & cherry agrodolce, fried brussels sprouts & lemon and rigatoni with swordfish and eggplant fries. The quail was cooked well; tender with a nice seasoning and sauce that complimented it nicely. The brussels sprouts were salty and acidic - in a good way. The leaves were nicely caramelized and crispy (almost chip like), yet still airy and light in texture. It was a nice refreshing twist on a winter vegetable staple. The paccheri with swordfish is a genius plate of pasta filled with fresh, unexpected flavors. The eggplant fries added a crisp, salty element that complements the pasta in a satisfying way. My only qualm here is that there could have been a bit more swordfish in the dish. 

To end our experience on an extra sweet note, we shared the Belgian waffle with nutella, vanilla semifreddo and walnuts. It was light, fluffy and absolutely divine. 

Needless to say we enjoyed our date night and I highly recommend the restaurant to anyone - local or not. 5 stars Amis! Grazié!

I used to love Amis and was a regular until they blocked me on Instagram and removed me from their email list because I pointed out that they used "edition" instead of "addition" in an post, and questioned them when they sent me a calendar of December events in January. Plenty of other places to eat that don't immaturely block their customers on social media. I'll never give them another dollar.

This is the most incompetent Chick-fil-A I have ever been to! Charged my card wrong and wanted to do a total refund and re enter the order, they still could not seem to get a simple order right between 3 employees. The "manager" Melissa was rude and refused to serve me and my friend. Literally this location is shit and If I could give it negative stars I would.

Amis, I miss you and the smell of funky cheese in the air already!!
