We went here for a work year-end dinner and it did not disappoint. We ordered several appetizers. table favorites were: cauliflower and eggplant burrata. All were good portions and sharable for 5 people. 

Main entree was the bucatini jalapeño and pesto. The noodles were perfectly al dente. I ordered it because the waitress said the jalapeños pack it with lots of flavor. I liked the dish but it was definitely missing a punch or wow factor.

Ambiance was nice. Definitely a good date spot!

Horrible!  After all the hype and the FYI Philly segment, I decided to give this place a try.  Everything I bought, a variety of things, was stale, dry and tasteless.  The icing on the cake tasted like grease.  I've been to some of the best bakeries and was hoping to add this to my list.  No way!  I threw everything out.  I'm happy I taste tested before I gave it to my company.  I would never go back nor give this place a verbal thumbs up.  Sorry, FYI Philly got this one all wrong.

I ordered Togo at moes today the lady making orders was all over the place and slow I ordered 5 tacos they where good but I also ordered chips and queso when I got home I had chips but no queso what's up with Mexican restaurants and chips and queso I quit going to tiajuana flats because I would get either my chips or my queso but never both maybe  fast food restaurants should hire people that pay attention when you order and check your order before it goes out

I went to this place for drinks with friends. The ambiance and location are great. The music selection was on point. The service was slow. Sooooooo sloooow. They had one waitress working. I get it. Not a lot of customers inside, but she took so long to bring my drink, I started looking for her. The margaritas are WEAK! I basically had $12 juice. And I made the mistake of ordering the second before finishing the first because of how slow she was moving. Just order beer or shots and save yourself the disappointment. Oh wait. The only beers they had in the whole place were Carona, Miller Lite, and Bud Light. They had cups over all the other taps. 

They could be great if they kept all of the alcohol stocked. You can't have bar as part of your name and not have beer.

This place rocks! Generous portions and delicious thai food! My wife and I have been trying many my wife and I have been Trying just about all the time restaurants in Tampa LOL; the food here is delicious and they serve generous portions, you will leave full and happy. The service was prompt and the staff is friendly; highly recommend this place!

Chick fil a is supposed to be ran swiftly & quickly. But not this one. Always takes me 20 minutes just to get my one entree that I ordered.   It's in a good location but could definitely be a little faster.  Luckily it's not my first time at chick fil a or I probably wouldn't be back. It's supposed to be a version of fast food and there's NOTHING fast about this location.


After waiting in the drive thru with the rudest cashier I've ever met at chick fil a ( I don't know her name as she didn't give me a receipt ) I get my food and this it what it looks like.  Chick fil a has never been such a disappointment to me before. I can tell you I will not be back at this location.

13th street, Philly
With friends who are foodies (who don't even do yelp but always seem to know where to go), they brought me here, and we had a magical night! Loved the atmosphere in here-good for groups. Food was pretty good! They ordered; I ate! It is has been some time since I was here, but I would come back. Don't expect me to know what Im eating; all I ask them is: any allergens Im allergic to in these dishes? Friends approve the food or warn me by moving the dishes I can't eat away from my reach; I eat. Lol. Life is great when ur friends order and you never have to read the menu , but I also never know what the heck I'm eating in the menu. As I result I am terrible orderer. And I "eeny meeny miney mo" a lot on menus. But hey when friends are foodies/chefs they know exactly what tastes great! And it is yummy at this reataurant! So come for the food and stay longer for the ambience!

Super good. Can be a romantic dinner spot if you secure a proper table. There are some tables that are a foot from the table next to you. Those tables aren't that romantic only because you'll be privy to other conversations. 

But the food is superb. Cacio y pepe and the rotini w/ bolognese was poppin. Calamari is an interesting and delicious presentation. The wine list is above average as well. Do try the elizabet Prosecco. You'll impress your date. Just don't over do it. The sugar will give you a headache later on. 

Haven't had a chance to try any desserts but I'll be back for sure. Great neighborhood spot and destination for celebrations. Be sure to make your reservation ahead of time so you don't miss out on the culinary treats. 

Ciao...
These folk are delightful.  They are quick and funny.  They engage the audience and kept us all laughing out loud

One of the best two meals of my life! I've come here on vacation twice in the last two years and both times I was met with world class service and food. Most recently, I had the Sea Bass and the Lobster Lasagnette. Both were perfectly done and flavorful. Definitely recommend those along with the lemoncello cocktail and the tiramisu. Waitress was Liz and she was amazingly polite, funny and non intrusive. Easy 5 stars.

Very disappointing visit to Bar Asia today.  When we arrived it became clear that the place had only one person acting as server and bartender.  But three people in the kitchen and the menu is bowls and sushi, etc so how long could the food possibly take?  Well, it took over an hour and we had to ask for ours to go because we were late to an appointment.  The table behind us was about to leave but right as they were deciding, an appetizer came out so they didn't have to go hungry forever. 
I will note that the bartender/server, Krystal, was great.  She was quick with refills and kept apologizing for the slowness of the food.  Not her fault and I appreciate her service. 
While sitting and waiting, I saw a post on the Bar Asia Facebook page advertising to come have brunch/lunch today.  I commented on the post that they should have another server as we had been waiting for food for nearly an hour.  The restaurant DELETED my post.  So I posted again with a screenshot of the original post.  DELETED again!  I tried to review them on Facebook and they even blocked me from their page.  Seriously?  A simple message to me would have made all the difference in the world.  Explain what happened, apologize, invite me back. 

So I took to my own Facebook page.  Within minutes people were telling of similar experiences and several sent me the link from the Times review last week.  A terrible review, highlighting many of the issues we experienced.  You'd think on the tail of that kind of a review they would be prepared for a South Tampa Sunday lunch.  No. 
Once we were finally able to eat our food, it was just average.  Mine was white rice and vegetables.  Nothing special.  They only gave me a spoonful of sauce so it was very bland.  I was hopeful that the food would at least have made the awful experience a little better.  Also, sushi prices were outrageous.  Almost all of the rolls were $15 and over.  What?!?!  Go to Soho Sushi, Yoko's, Matoi or Kelp before Bar Asia. 
Don't waste your time here.  South Tampa has a million great restaurants with more opening weekly.  You shouldn't have to tolerate bad service and mediocre food.

Awesome massage, despite it being hard to find (it was in an office park upstairs, a little confusing). Anyway, I get a lot of massages and this one was incredible. She really went deep tissue, how I like it. And she was super nice - we talked about life the whole time!

Went to diner here on Saturday night.    This is my 4th or 5th time at Amis.

Started off with an Amis punch which wasn't too sweet and pretty good though a little small (with lots of ice).

Had a Deep Fried Pork balls special which had great flavor but the texture was too mushy for my liking.

Had the Melon & Cucumber Salad.  AWESOME!

Corn & Tomato salad was very good.

Enjoyed the Baked Cheese and almond honey very much.

Had the Spaghetti with Chiles.   Good but a little hot and not much flavor going on.

Overall very good.  I didn't care much for their Sunday brunch on a prior visit but still Amis is a SOLID 4.5 star experience.
I've shopped here for several years, I've never been disappointed! I've ordered birthday cakes, cookies, cupcakes and I've always been satisfied!

My wife and I had Valentine's Day dinner at the Coronet on Feb. 14th at 5:30pm.  The ambiance was striking when you enter the historic building but the noise level was loud.  Albeit, that not only was it Valentine's Day but it was also during happy hour--which ended at 6pm and it did quiet down a bit after that.  For an appetizer, we ordered the liver toast which was excellent.  My wife had the Valentine's Day Special of seared scallop and poached shrimp, which she said was excellent.  I had the blueberry, kiwi and pear salad,  which was also excellent along with the duck breast.  I thought the duck was a bit tough but it was very tasty.  I prefer my duck in a sweeter sauce than my duck was served in; I probably wouldn't order it again.  For dessert, we had the jamica and rose bread pudding, which was very good but not distinctive.  I felt the service was slow but efficient.  Overall, it was a solid 3+ experience.  We would return and give it another try for a during-the-week normal dinner.
Great restaurant with friendly staff. Always clean. Great lunch deal I recommend the #1 traditional chicken sandwich fries and drink die well under $10

Four of us went before theater and we all agreed that our entrees were bland at best. The place was so dim that we truly had difficulty seeing our own plates, and, as others have noted, it is a bit crowded and noisy. But worst was the indifferent service, bordering on downright rudeness. We explained that we had a time constraint (although we had allotted 90 minutes for dinner with a 5:30 reservation, hardly prime time), but watched our drinks sit at the end of the bar for over 10 minutes before someone deigned to bring them to the table. When we expressed concern after nearly 50 minutes had passed and still no entrees, our server poo-pooed us and said we would have plenty of time. Finally, we had to go get a host/hostess to bring us our bill after waiting another 10 minutes after we finished eating. There are too many other good restaurant choices downtown to go back.

I can't attest to the effectiveness of their work, but can tell you to stay away purely because of their customer service. I reached out to the company to schedule a pest control treatment on June 6th. I got redirected to their secretary who was to schedule me for June 20th. She told me on June 11th that she was working on scheduling the next day. I followed up 4 times with her what time they were coming - no response. I work M-F 8-5, so for me I need to give my employer enough notice when I need to take off. Finally two days before hand (6/18), after another email and voicemail, this time copying the owners, I finally get a response telling me 10-2. But then the owner tells me 12-3. So again I ask them to clarify what time, in which case the owner of the company accidentally responded to me saying "This woman is nuts". WOW. All i was doing was trying to find out the time of my appointment, and I'm nuts? I shouldn't have to reach out multiple times over the course of two weeks to find out what time they're coming. She tried to blow it off by saying "this woman is nutes" was in relation to the weather being nuts lately, which had nothing to do with our conversation, haha. Needless to say, very poor customer service.

Unique and Delicious dinner!

Pros: 
cocktails!!
homemade bread
homemade pasta (bolognese!)
pistashio cake
service
ambiance 

Cons:
brussel sprout salad

Had a fabulous lavender&lemon cocktail to start. They're homemade olive oil infused loaf bread with more oil drizzled on top and salt... omg wow! Octopus appetizer was superb! It was a unique combo with a cold potato salad. Little disappointed by the brussel sprout salad. It was raw. I should have checked before I ordered but forgot. It was dry and lacking in flavor and dressing. I think a cooked and then chilled salad with more dressing would be better. Homemade pasta in the lamb bolognese was TO DIE FOR! Nothing beats fresh pasta. Way less starchy and chewy than regular pasta. It was so light and al dente. The bolognese sauce was amazing and had no cream/milk in it (this lactose intolerance person appreciates!!) Instead they use pork fat. YUMMY!  Seriously one of the best pasta dishes I have ever had, and I've had plenty of pasta in Italy. Hanger steak was good/average, nothing amazing. This cut is a little chewy by nature. The whole grilled onions that came with it were great though! My boyfriend FREAKED over the pistachio cake! We said we would walk back to Phily every week for that cake (and we live 2hrs away). Alternating layers of plain vanilla cake with a dense/thick chilled pistachio butter cream! Paired with an amazing negroni. Fabulous dinner!!! Server Aliecia was so sweet and helpful. In reading other reviews below I see they will be closing soon?! WHY??? SOO SAD. Get here before you miss it :(

I come here a few times a month and I'm never disappointed with the great quality chick fil a has to offer. I'm plain and simple and I always order a chicken sandwich plain with a medium fries, CFA sauce and a half&half tea. Drive thru can be busy while no one is inside so I recommend going inside during lunch.

Placed an order for our office online.  Website does not allow for special instructions i.e. lite beans, sauce on the side etc... We put names with each item ordered.  Nothing was identified in the bags and it all looked the same.  The person making quesadillas either they have never made a quesadilla before or they need more training.   The flavor is good but ordering process and presentation need work.
Much better when ordering in person.
Consistent quality and great inexpensive alternative to fast food joints out there.  Food always cooked well and very fresh.  This is my standby when nothing for dinner comes to mind.

This Chicfila is convenient and much needed in the area, but the workers frequently mess up our order. We've gotten good about checking before we depart, but several times we didn't and realized it when we were already at home. The sides (fries, side salad, and mac n cheese) are the most commonly forgotten item. It's very. busy, long waits and also seems it's run in a disorganized manner. I hope this improves as this location hasn't been around that long. I wish PDQ were closer...

Disappointed because I was in the chick fil a with enough time to get breakfast but the service took so long that by the time I got to the counter, I missed breakfast by 3 minutes. 3 minutes!! I asked if there was any way I could still get a breakfast item and they basically shouted no more breakfast. Like come on man, I was in the chick fil a before breakfast closed and they still wouldn't serve it once I got to the counter. Leaving this review was my pleasure.

Slow customer service...
They are poorly staffed and usually under staffed.
Make sure you have time to hang out...
This is for the inside counter.
I have not gone through the drive through....
Probably will not.

This is probably the worst Chick-Fil-A in Tampa which is unfortunate because it's the closest one to my house. I just got home from what I call a nightmare of an experience with them. Just to get in the parking lot is a pain in itself. I usually do drive thru but considering how busy it was I decided to order inside. I placed my order in less than a minute and the young girl that took my order was very nice. She instructs me to wait in the "Pick up" area. Once there I see at least 6 people waiting for their food. I actually get my food in less than 3 minutes which wasn't too bad but I waited for my milkshake for at least 7 minutes. I would've waited longer if I hadn't said anything. I was super annoyed at that point and left. When I got home my order was wrong. I go to Chik-Fil-A quite often and I've never gotten my order wrong. I was pissed. I thought about going back to say something but they never gave me a receipt and I was hungry and decided to eat what they gave me; 4 count chicken minis meal instead of 12 count nugget meal. In addition, the thought of having to return to that mess of a parking lot is what made me decide to just leave it be. My advice, go the extra few miles down the street to on S. Dale Mabry near Swann Ave.

It was really nice of my bf to surprise me with a reservation here on NYE.
Unfortunately though it seemed as if we found the Philadelphia Olive Garden.

Holy disappointment this turned out to be. 
The star is for the excellent service from our very nice waiter.

Eggplant caponata app -- Nice price of $6.  This is usually a fave of mine but found it to be much too oily and lacked the true flavor it should have.  Served with super thick slices of not good tasting bread which were all terribly charred.

Okay..so the 3 pasta dishes should be better..After all we were told to only order the pasta here and from the looks of our dining neighbors next to us they left almost all of their food on both their plates and sort of shook their heads (looked as if they had some sort of fried filet with a salad?)  So of course we were lucky enough to know to order the right things!

Wrong.

I have never had heavier sauced pasta dishes in my life.  Normally I am a salt-aholic and put salt on everything.  This was the first time I didn't want to.  Everything was so completely OVER salted it was barely edible.
The pastas all so overcooked you couldn't tell if you were eating fresh pasta - In fact it could have very well been a store brand.

Squash lasagna- an oily mess with what tasted like cheap cheddar cheese melted over the entire thing.  Overcooked mushy lasagne with a tiny amount of squash, which gave it really no squash flavor - just salt and cheese.

Tonnarelli cacio e pepe - thought I was going to choke to death on a peppercorn.  The tonnarelli was wayyy too overcooked.
The most overly creamy/buttery/salty dish I have ever had in my life.  Olive Garden could do it much better than this - and that's not saying much - at half the price.

Pappardelle with oyster mushroom ragu  - the dish I was dying to get after seeing it on the online menu.   This was the best one of the night.  Again- too much oil and salt but the mushrooms gave it some actual flavor.  Noodles were again too overcooked, but not as badly as the other 2 dishes.

Once again my theory proves right!  If I don't like the bread at a restaurant I end up not liking the meal.  The bread looked like focaccia but tasted like some stale sourdough.    

This isn't good cooking.  If it were the pasta would have been cooked al dente to perfection, the sauces would be light to compliment the pasta, half a salt shaker wouldn't be poured into the food.  

I'm a tough critic, I know.. But this food left me with Italian food nightmares and perhaps a few pounds.
Not sure if I will ever try Italian outside of my family's home again!
Two stars because I didn't get E. coli. Yet. If you order online, treat the register like a crowded bar and assert yourself, or you'll wait indefinitely.

SERVICE
The waiter was knowledgeable about the food and was very friendly. Each table is given its own bottle of water. They are definitely very efficient with the food prep and delivery. 

FOOD
The bread wasn't that impressive. We didn't even get EVOO. Definitely the worst bread I've had. If you're going to serve flavorless bread then they really should provide very good EVOO and balsamic to have with it. 

We got complimentary bruschetta so we were able to try both. Surprisingly I think we could all agree that the eggplant was the best of the two. 

Everyone at the table got meatballs to start. We each got 3 very large very seasoned and perfectly cooked meatballs. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

It seems as though most of the dishes were vegetarian but with a twist? So they don't use the traditional basil pesto but almond. It wasn't bad but... honestly everything was delicious but one can appreciate old-fashion simple ingredients. 

I'm not sure if these selections they chose for restaurant week wasn't a proper representation but... It seems as though the only thing worth getting would be Cacio e Pepe which is a traditional Roman dish. They seem to be using the correct pasta and they stick true to the ingredients. 

Either way I do think you should go because the food is actually very good but I don't think it captured the simplicity of the Italian cuisine in the restaurant week menu. 

The Tiramisu was definitely sweeter than what I had when I was in Venice but still yummy!

A small group of us came here for hotpot & had a pretty good time. However, a major problem with the service is that, for the All You Can Eat meal, staff repeatedly gave us worse food than what we had ordered.

THE GOOD:
Food is good. Hotpot ingredients seem fresh. I like that they have an option to have up to 3 soup bases.

Sauce bar has a good selection.

The spicy Szechuan buttery soup was tasty, but I'm not sure it's worth the $9.95 surcharge. There are other broths that taste good too.

PROBLEMS:
An ongoing problem was that the staff consistently failed to give us what we ordered. We ordered Fish Balls with Fish Roe several times, but they kept giving us a mix: some fish balls had roe like we asked, but half of the balls were some random other kind. It seemed like they were purposefully giving us fish balls we didn't want so that we'd fill up on eating foods we hadn't ordered. (Fish balls with Roe have a pointy shape & look very different from the random ones they gave us.) This seems sneaky and dishonest -- for the AYCE deal, they claim we can order what we like for $24 per person, but then they repeatedly gave us items we didn't order instead of giving us what we did order.

SUMMARY:
Staff was friendly, but service was not good, since they did not bring us everything we ordered. 

Food (the items we ordered) was around 4 stars. The food items we received but didn't order were around 2+ stars.

Without the service problem of passing off worse food on us than what we ordered, I would have rated Ochatto Hotpot more highly.

This is the worst chick fil a I've been to. SLOOOOOOW service in the drive through for two chicken biscuits and an iced coffee... then we drive away and realized the order was wrong too. So we stopped back on the way home to get the drink I actually wanted, and the drive through took 20 minutes! I don't know what this place is, but it's not a Chick Fil A, that's for sure. I think this is a Burger King with the wrong sign out front.
I love the food but don't eat here as often because they don't clean the tables regularly. This pic is typical at Chipotle, especially this location.
Food is okay - nothing to rave about. Their are better places for Italian food in Philadelphia. Their crab lasagna was dry and burnt - no real flavor. However service and dessert was excellent.
This place still is terrible. I thought it got better but it was temporarily good but now its bad again. :(

Another uninteresting overly rich Vetri jawn. Can't get why these places are getting the traffic they are getting. There is absolutely no attention to detail in terms of flavor combinations and if the food is going to be this soulless I don't want to spend this kind of money. Plenty of other places that will give me way more satisfaction for my hard earned dollar. 

I'll dwell on one thing: the salumi. Please tell me why these already pretty uninspired meat products need horrible sweet "jams" to go with them. Whatever little flavor they have (serious, again, completely uninspired--someone is just going through the motions) goes out the window in this hideous fashion that has everyone sticking jam (sorry, fruit preserve) with cheese, with meat, with whatever. It's OK if it's Manchego and quince paste, you know, a classic. But it gets really old really fast, and when you are getting an incredibly bland mortadella smothered in honey or a liver pate smothered in marmalade it's just gross (bet Vetri loves the 8% food cost on that plate, though). 
Anyway, as you may have noted, I really wasn't impressed with this meal...not for the price or for anything else. Vetri is now a machine producing the same kind of crap in every one of his places. It isn't inspired, it isn't good, and most importantly, it isn't fun. 
Why did I go? Someone else suggested it. Believe me, I'm done with Vetri if it's my choice.

I love love LOVED Amis. We attended their recent "Feast of the Seven Fishes" dinner on Christmas Eve (eve) and had the best time.

The set menu involved 7+ small plates, 2 pasta dishes (incredible), and monk fish piccata with fingerling potatoes and mushrooms. Did I mention that there was also dessert? A huge piece of tiramisu, chocolate ice cream, and a plate of cookies. 

I would recommend this dinner experience to anyone. There was a huge variety of fish used in each of the plates (monkfish, clams, shrimp, crab, cod, swordfish,tuna, etc)

The restaurant is cozy and warm although a bit small. There was some claustrophobic seating options (climbing over other patrons to get out of your table) but we got lucky with a two-top near the bar. (However even this resulted in people standing right on top of you while they were waiting to be seated. We got lucky but this can ruin a meal for me so make sure you are prepared for this.

All in all, I am very excited to go back for a normal dinner but may opt for the bar to avoid the awkward seating situations.
Food is yummy and fairly priced for the portion size. Definitely recommend if you want authentic Mexican!

I enjoy the food. I really do. I typically get the Homewrecker but have also tried several other things. While it doesn't knock my socks off, it hits the spot.

I hate the freaking salsa bar. The cups are so small that I typically need 3 for my chips. Plus, the set up seems so unhygienic. 

Finally, there are always so many kids. I realize there is little Moe's can do about this but it really, really ruins the whole experience. Perhaps make kids meals more expensive? I realize this is petty but it the the biggest reason I typically avoid going there.

Ordered my food. Payed for it with debit. Got up to the lady standing outside before 2nd window and told her my name which was "Manny" (my husbands name) she then told me someone else came and got the order. Something about the names sounding alike which that happens. What really upset me is the fact it took 3 employees to just sit out there and talk to each other and continue to figure out where our receipt was. We told them what we ordered, we paid, I had a bank statement but we still sat there waiting for I don't even know what. It was embarrassing. If we already paid and repeated our order back, why couldn't I have pulled up at least to the 2nd window to eventually gather the food I paid for? Forget my about my receipt. Our a/c doesn't work and it made no sense of us sitting there for well over 10 minutes when there was 0 cars in front of us. Left and noticed our large coke was a diet. I honestly wish we would have just gotten an apology for the wait. Extremely disappointed with the customer service I got today.

This place is delicious. We ordered the crispy cauliflower and charred octopus as an appetizer and they were amazing, I defiantly recommend the octopus its a must try.  I ordered the tonarelli which was great, I have never had pasta so thick and I really enjoyed it. The people I was with ordered the cocoa pasta, ricotta ravioli, and the shells and they all enjoyed their meal.
Stopped here without knowing anything about it.  What a fortunate find!  Great chef, great bartender (Jesse), great atmosphere.  Best food I've had in awhile. You won't be disappointed.

This particular Chipotle is definitely not my favorite. Once again, I am disappointed with my order. I ordered online and when I got home the food was not even warm. Mind you, I arrived before my pickup time. Both bowls did not have sour cream and they were very small. It is almost like they used the last of certain ingredients like MEAT. I ordered half chicken and half steak which we got very little of. I will not waste my time anymore with this restaurant because all of the employees do not follow the same standard. They could learn a few things Wawa's and  Chick-fil-A where I will be taking my business.

Not what it used to be... We have not been there for a while and were disappointed. I ordered a miso soup and a tuna sashimi salad. My husband ordered a bento box. The waiter brought the bowl of soup by hand. His thumb was a millimeter away from touching the soup. Yikes! - A tray would have helped. Anyhow, I decided to ignore that. Then, it took more than 15 minutes for my salad to arrive. My husband's got to the table much earlier, and that was a bento (?). The salad I got was more like an appetizer size presented in a large dish. On the Menu, the dish it was described as "8 pieces of sashimi over mixed greens". I got 8 small and thin pieces of sashimi around a handful of iceberg lettuce! When I mentioned this to the waiter, he said that they did not have mixed greens (?). I think he should have mentioned that at the time I placed my order. The waiter did nothing to correct this neither offer an alternative. The price of the salad was $12. The price of the bento was $11. A rip off.

Not sure why people go to chick fil a. Their chicken isnt seasoned.  Bland people with a taste for bland food.  Flavor should not come from just the sauce. The drive thru does provide good quick service.  At least the chicken is fried in peanut oil which provides SOME flavor,  but not much.

The first time I went here, I wasn't very impressed. I went again recently and not only was the service great, but the food was wonderful. I would definitely recommend any of the appetizers since they were all fantastic and each of the pastas were such a treat. I will definitely be back here soon!

Bought a chocolate chip pound cake for a birthday. The cake was as dry as biscuits. If I wanted biscuits I could of bought milk bone. The owner asked me to bring it in for him to look at. I brought it back three days later the owner called me back. He said that's how their pound cake tastes! How embarrassing to your guest!

We came here for dinner on Valentine's Day. My husband originally wanted to go to the location in Devon because of less traffic and better parking, but I was worried it wouldn't be as good as the Philly location. 

We had a plan of exactly what we were going to order  ahead of time, but after hearing the specials we had to change it slightly. We were originally going to order the cacio e Pepe tonnarelli and the meatballs as our appetizers. But I ordered the lobster tonnarelli special as my entree and didn't want 2 of almost the same thing. So we ordered the pumpkin ravioli and meatballs as our appetizers.  


I'm glad we got the ravioli, it was delicious and my favorite part of the meal. The pasta melted in your mouth and had great flavor with a brown butter type of sauce. The meatballs were good but I could have done without them. My husband wanted them he's the meatball fanatic. I enjoyed my entree, the lobster was perfectly cooked. It could  have had a little more lobster or something else in it though for the price it was. And the pasta had a wine sauce, I wish it came with the cacio e pepe instead. My husband's slow braised goat was great. The goat was very tender and the butternut squash complimented it well. Both entrees were a little on the salty side, but not so salty that it ruined the dish. 

Our drinks were also fantastic. I really liked my husband's negroni drink and we tried to re create it at home with the same ingredients they used, but it doesn't taste quite the same. For dessert we ordered the warm chocolate tart for 2 but we wanted ice cream to go with it. Our server offered to put a scoop of semifredo on top so we got the butter semifredo. It was a great way to end the meal.

Sitting here today at the Tampa Stadium Location (#03838) and just received my food.
I placed an order in the drive thru and was told to pull up to the VIP spot.
Waited waited and waited so more. 
Business for this location was extremely slower than normal today (assuming due to the local events and festivities this weekend ) - SO NO REASON TO WAIT AS LONG AS I DID!
I had to walk in and ask about my order
At that time the manager on duty somewhat disappeared behind the wall (gotcha!) and everyone looked around as though they had never received an order at all never mind that the VIP 1 spot is in OPEN VIEW. 
So today you receive an - UNPROFESSIONAL POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE RATING SMH
(Nothing is free..... this was a PAID order and I am a CUSTOMER )

There is always something missing from my order here. Unreal. Whether it's a sauce, portion size, something, odds are your order will be screwed up. 

Update: came here again about a week later thinking to myself, there's no way they mess up my order again. So I ordered the same thing and yes they messed it up again. No sauce. No almonds for the kale crunch salad. Terrible portion size. It's embarrassing. Not trying to be rude. I love chick fil a, but this location is absolutely terrible.

Oh Marc Vetri, you maestro of pasta, guru of Italian cooking, can you do any wrong? I moved away from Philadelphia right around the time that Amis opened. I had been to Vetri and Osteria but never had the chance to go to Amis. This is a great place to come in and experience Vetri's cooking without having to order the fixed menu at Vetri. I was very impressed with everything but the star of the evening was the squash lasagna. This is not your mother's lasagna, it's thin and delicate, not overly cheesy. I also really enjoyed the swordfish with eggplant fries but thought that the eggplant fries were much better than the accompanying fish.

Had one of the most amazing meal of my life here. Must order sal's old school meatballs! I'm not really into meatballs so it says a lot that they're a must order in my book. Also had the fried cauliflower which was very good as well. I ordered the Rigatoni and it was sooo freaking good. My family members ordered the Bucatini and Paccheri. Both were so flavorful and also very delicious. I was just so pleased with my meal. This is a must visit place. I cannot wait till I can dine here again!

After much fanfare, Susi and Mike Jacobi (former owners of the Schnitzelhaus restaurant on Waters Avenue) have opened a brand-new German take-out bakery called Strudelking. This place opened at the beginning of July, so expect a few quirks in the system until they get everything sorted out.

The storefront is a little tricky to find as it is tucked into a small shopping plaza just south of the traffic light at Casey Road along Gunn Highway. Signage isn't the best right now, so watch for the marquee with The Magic Emporium, and you'll find Strudelking right next door.

If you were a patron of Schnitzelhaus then you'll recognize Mike immediately. He's a very delightful guy with a thick German accent and a hearty laugh. He's also one heck of a great baker!

The menu is quite simple: Apple Strudel, Cheese Strudel, Cheese Strudel with Blueberries or Raspberries, Black Forest Cake, or a German Ice Cream Cake. The strudels are sold whole and the cakes can be purchased whole, or by the slice.

The strudels run $12 - 14, and they are heavy, dense pastries filled with fruit and / or cheese. This thing is about the size of a loaf of Cuban bread, but surprisingly light and flakey. I picked up an apple strudel to serve at a client meeting tomorrow and couldn't resist sneaking a thin slice after dinner tonight. 

Wow, I'm glad that it was just a thin slice because I was stuffed after the first few mouthfuls. The pastry is quite filling and really delicious.

Remember that this is a carryout bakery, and also remember to invite over the entire neighborhood, church group, or college dormitory to help you eat the dessert!

Cash only!!!

I went rose gold/pink with Allison and couldn't be happier with the results. My dark brown hair is on the curly/frizzy and thick side, but Allison knew exactly what she was doing. She was so friendly and just as excited about my hair as I was. Thank you again for the best hair experience of my life

The Coronet moved and somehow the food got... Even better?? Is this possible?!

I've always been a huge fan of The Coronet. Their patio was my favorite on 4th Ave. When I heard they were moving, I was worried about what that meant for the restaurant.

Well, what that meant was room for growth - literally and figuratively! Upon walking in I immediately felt that vintage charm the old location delivered. Wood furnishings, dim lighting.... My partner and I wanted to sit outside so we got a table in the back patio. It's just as lovely as ever, and much more spacious!

Now for the food - the food blew our minds. We ordered mussels as an appetizer and enjoyed eating the bread at the bottom (which was soaked up in delicious broth). For dinner I got a salmon with pumpkin puree. The dish had tons of depth. The pumpkin was slightly sweet but had a slight spiciness to it that gradually built up as you ate. The salmon was perfectly cooked; the skin was light and crispy, the fish soft and succulent. It came with some other sautéed green which was very delicious. Drinks were also perfectly made each and every time. 

Overall my partner and I were very impressed with The Coronet at its new location. A charming gem in Tucson!

I travel the country every week.  This gives me the opportunity to visit a lot of restaurants.  Recently I brought a group of eight customers to The Coronet.  I regularly look for local restaurants not chains to patronize.   I don't have much to say that is good about this restaurant.  In fact I was truly embarrassed to have brought my customers here.   The service was not bad they accommodated us when the weather was cold by moving our tables inside which I recognize as a true act of good service.  Some of the food we ordered was very good like the octopus.  But most of our entrees were delivered cold.  This matches other reviews.  I am just not sure why this restaurant has gotten so many good reviews.  It just is not good.   Look else where for fine dining in Tucson.
Just received excellent service from Destiny in drive thru!  Warm, hospitable, and efficient.
Great location and the employees were great! Definitely one of the best Moe's restaurants I've visited in Florida.

This location brings shame to the chick fil a brand. Consistently super slow moving line. Most employees are less than friendly. I feel bad because whenever I dine here they always seem to have new trainees at the registers. They constantly lose employees. Unlike most chick fil a locations employees at this location ignore you when you go up to ask for a refill. They will walk by you over and over. Always a less than stellar experience

We've been to the Coronet twice now and have enjoyed it both times.  The menu has some interesting, unique items that you won't find at many other places in Tucson.  Or maybe at *any* other places in Tucson...  The interior is cozy and inviting, and the courtyard is a nice place to sit and listen to music - there are plenty of heaters when it's cold out.  The cocktail menu is also not to be missed, and the happy menu too!

After waiting in line for 20 minutes, I finally got to order and was being very rushed. When I went to eat my bowl, the rice was barely cooked at all almost as if they had rinsed it and put it out and it all together sucked. This is the worst Chipotle in Tampa and I refuse to come back to this location.

It's difficult for me to justify Italian food in the city at high price points, and this place was no exception. I think I've just given in to the fact that I probably have overly high standards for entrees when dining out though, since I cook so much at home (Italian included). I've also gone to a certain pub in Fishtown known for their high-caliber Italian chef serving at pub-fare prices, so I'm probably a bit spoiled as well. 

As a result of all these things, when I ordered some of their popular items, like the almond & jalapeno bucatini, cacio e pepe, and swordfish meatballs, I was sort of underwhelmed.  However, the service was excellent and very friendly. That, the ambiance, and its nice location in Center City are definitely part of the equation.

"Welcome to Moe's!" is what we always hear when we come to Moe's Southwest Grill! Moe's is a friendly casual Southwest or Mexican eatery where you can customize your burrito, taco, quesadilla, rice bowl, or stacks by asking for toppings as you go down the line, subway style. I've been coming to Moe's ever since college.  What keeps me coming back to Moe's Southwest Grill is their delicious free salsa and unlimited chips, unlike Chipotle.  My favorite of the salsas offered is the Kaiser Salsa which is a medium-heat salsa made with all-natural diced tomatoes, onions and fresh cilantro that goes well on everything- except pants lol. El Guapo Salsa is a  medium-heat salsa made with all-natural fire-roasted tomatoes brings out the man in you, even if you're a 77-year-old grandma.  The Green Tomatillo salsa mild-heat salsa is filled with surprises like its citrus, jalapeño and cilantro taste. Their is also a corn salsa and a bean salsa which are all pretty good. I usually get two cups of each of the salsas for dipping my chips into. Moe's Southwest Grill's meats are well marinated and pretty tasty. Moe's chicken is cage-free, their steak is grass-fed, and their pork is grain-fed, and all the meats have no added hormones which is nice. I usually get the steak Joey Bag of Donuts burrito or the John Coctostan Steak Quesadillas and they are always really big and delicious.  Their burritos are so big that I used to get the kids meal burrito, the Moo Moo Mr. Cow, and that was more than enough to fill me up.  Since then, they've made their kids meal burrito smaller. Perhaps this make me seem old but every time I go in here, the prices go up. I remember back in the good ol days when the burritos were only $3 lol. Often I am unable to finish their big burritos. Sometimes I even split their burritos because they are so big. There are many funny menu item names like the John Coctostan, Ear Muffs, Band Camp, Art Vandalay, Homewrecker, Close Talker, and Wrong Doug. A cool fact about Moes is that they only play music of people that have died and have posters up of artists that have died. I wish there was a Moes closer to where I lived or I'd come more often. Moes is located off South South Dale Mabry next to Publix in a plaza off Neptune next to Gigi's Cupcakes and Tropical Smoothie cafe. There is plenty of parking available in a shared private lot for the plaza. There are 2 TV's and they will put whatever football game or channel on you'd like if you ask. While my new favorite casual Mexican eatery is now the Lime off Westshore blvd, I still am looking forward to my next visit!
Cold, hard rice, chip bag had the napkins and utensils which I did not request. Will not be ordering here again

Had a yummy and very filling meal at Amis during restaurant week. Went with a friend and got the Brussels and cauliflower to start, followed by the fish and Cacio e pepe pasta and finished with the olive oil cake and tiramisu. The fish was nice and light and the best dessert was definitely the tiramisu. Would recommend but come hungry!!

Came here a few weeks ago for my friend's birthday with his wife and two children. We ordered a whole bunch of appetizers, pastas, side dishes and desserts, but what stood out the most were the meatballs (courtesy of the house), duck sausage and pork chop (one of the best pork dishes I have ever eaten).

However extraordinary the food, the service was even better. The staff at Amis went above and beyond to serve us and make my friend's night special. I was sincerely touched by the consideration and concern the restaurant showed towards us, in a way that I rarely ever see.  Thank you, Amis.
Poor management. I have a few favorites workers though. Bad location getting in and out of parking lot and drive through.

Stopped by with a group of friends last night because of the nice decor and hot pot sounded like a great idea in this cold weather. The atmosphere is awesome due to the music and the friendly staff. They give you a menu and a pen and you check off on all the things you want to get. I was surprised that they had other things on the menu besides hotpot; skewers and customizable mixed spicy bowls that remind me of Asia!! 

Compared to Nine Ting and Hippot, the prices are a little higher because this is not an all you can eat, but the quality of food you get is incomparable. Everything is fresh, clean, and beautifully arranged. The interior is pretty modern and so is the music. After you get your filling of food and if you still have room in your stomach (which you probably won't, but your eyes tell you otherwise) you can take a walk to Caffe Bene, which is right around the corner, and get some drinks or dessert and digest. 

All in all, I will definitely be coming back again!

Went to Amis for a last minute date night and had the most wonderful evening on one of the outside tables. I enjoyed the Amis punch, the most perfect summer cocktail, and we started with the brussel sprouts, buffalo mozzarella and charred octopus. The brussel sprouts were delicious, the charred octopus was okay and the mozzarella was simply perfect. 

We decided to share the special - a crab salad - and the swordfish pasta. The pasta was very flavorful similar to a ragu but the crab salad stood out as a favorite of the night. If they are still offering it you have to order it. 

The service was outstanding. The only minor negative is that we forgot our leftovers which we were looking forward to!

I stopped in here on Easter. There were a lot of restaurants closed, so my first choice wasn't available. Upon arrival, the host greeted us warmly and we were sat immediately. There were about 8 or more empty tables, probably because it was a holiday, but the host attempted to sit us right next to an occupied table, which was spaced about 1 foot away. My friend stopped her and asked for the table 1 away, which should have been the first move by the host, since it was a quiet night. Our server came over, introduced himself and poured our water, then asked if we knew what we wanted to drink. We ordered drinks  then food. After placing our order, the food started coming out very quickly, which was great, because I was very hungry. Started with the tuna and white bean bruschetta. The bread on this was grilled and thick and yummy, but the tuna tasted like it was from a can, so I didn't finish it. Next, the Pecorino with honey and chopped almonds, excellent! Again, it had the same bread as the bruschetta, lucky for me I really liked that bread. Then the swordfish meatballs, very strong flavor, but good. My friend had the rigatoni with beef bolognese as her entree, it too was good. I had the jalapeño pasta, which I thought was very good! Overall, I thought the food here was good, but some of the products being used taste of lower quality. The service was ok, but I think I was disappointed with the appearance of the server. I'm not trying to insult, but a wrinkled dingy shirt and at least 3 days unshaven shouldn't be ok.

Best hot pot in philadelphia hands down. I'm from central jersey where there is a ton of options for hot pot. 

Until this place came along, there hasn't been a decent hot pot place to write home about. 

Fresh ingredients, clean, very affordable price, and nice incentive for those who pay cash
I've been here 3 years and never had chick-Fil-a and omg am I in love! One the best fast food places to go forget McDonald's and Burger King come get this fresh chicken!

As I'm typing this review, i am eating my burrito and the rice is falling to the plate raw as can be.  Customer service was awful. They tried to charge me for queso. The guy who served me looked like he just came out of jail. Did not look professional as wearing sweatpants and angry as can be at work.
Eggplant caponata, bucatini with jalapeños & almond pesto... two amazing dishes that we order every time we go to Amis, along with other delicious dishes!

Honestly don't waste a time with this place. There's 0 organization around mobile orders. It's too busy to deal with inefficiency. They should have taken a note from the location on Waters what has an efficient drive through experience. I also don't understand why mobile orders are prepared when you are in close proximity.
Overall I won't visit this location again unless there are major improvements.

Feel free to check out the blog for some more deetz on Amis and the Chef, but I'm sure we're here for the food. So let's get on with it!  

The restaurants features something called Beast of Amis, a nightly round of specials that showcases different parts of an animal in a variety of dishes. Tonight's special was pork three ways. Unfortunately, in an effort to showcase some a la carte dishes, the GF and I decided to pass. Still, if there was a pork belly special on hand, I'm sure I would have been tempted.

Blood and Soda [$11]

Famous Grouse, cherry herring, vermouth

I started off the night with this scotch-based drink. For those that are interested in entering into the realm of whiskey, this is a great entry course. Light, refreshing, and bright, the cherry liqueur came through on the finish nicely. Easy drinking.

Mandoria [$11]
Tito's handmade vodka, amaretto, pineapple

The GF's drink offered even easier drinking. The amaretto brought forth soothing undertones of sweetness with the pineapple providing brightness. The vodka was easily masked, but definitely there.

Bread Service

Our night's indulgence started off with incredible olive oil focaccia. Light and airy within, the exterior had a crispy crust laden with sea salt. It took all I had not to get up and attack the whole house-made loaf being portioned out for the evening's diners by the server's station. Come for the bread alone. Seriously - it's that good. No accoutrements needed here.

Eggplant Caponata [$8]

In line with our eggplant kick (at least one of our weekly dinners involves l'aubergine), we had to get the caponata. It came with four slices of grilled, buttery sesame-crusted bread. A perfect vehicle for the smooth, savory eggplant. Certainly a contrast in textures as well as temperatures, with the caponata being served appropriately cold.

Bufala Mozzarella [$12]
Charred asparagus, mint, pickled red onions

The mozz was expectedly creamy and rich, with the charred asparagus offering a bit of texture. The pickled onion and vinegary base provided the necessary hit of acid. It's clear that the quality of the ingredients are there, but it truly is the sum of the parts that make each bite perfect.

Salami del Giorno [$8]
Onion marmalade

House-made salumi (crafted over in a room at Vetri Ristorante no less!) came complimentary from the kitchen. And I'm glad it did - mainly because it's now a must-order. The salumi were sliced gossamer thin - cleanly flavored and nicely complimented by the sweet onion marmalade. The quality is evident here, unadulterated by much else. I couldn't help but think about the next Vetri-Spence-Michaud venture however. Vetri-wich anyone? (Craftwich ... Grahamwich ... you get the drift). 

Fried Cauliflower [$9]
Pecorino, salsa rossa

The GF has really been in the mood for cauliflower so we decided to get this dish. The cauliflower were crispy, yet incredibly meaty and not greasy at all. It's definitely well-seasoned with the salty pecorino and salsa rossa adding extra layers of flavors. It was a good dish to alternate with the sweetness of the salumi and onion marmalade or the creamy-vinegar juxtaposition of the bufala mozz.

Arancini [$12]
Short rib ragu, truffle pecorino

Starting to make our way into some of the pastas, we had to get the arancini. These were deftly made - crispy on the outside, yielding to a creamy interior filled a surprisingly mild pit of cheese.

In fact, at first I thought it was a bit bland, but it completely made sense when paired with the bed of well-seasoned short rib ragu.

Pappardelle [$16]
Smoked guanciale, parsnips

For our first pasta proper, we went with the pappardelle. The GF was sold on the parsnips and for me, how can I say no to guanciale? The fresh pasta had bite and was not drenched, but perfectly coated in the sauce. While the GF was begging for more of the parsnip, the pork jowl/cheeks were incredibly smoky and offered the heft and salt that each bite richly deserved.

Spinach Lasagna [$16]
Veal bolognese

We were getting full at this point, but this next dish came out, compliments of the kitchen again. While the previous pasta was great, clearly the chefs know how to order better than I. In fact, I may just have the kitchen order up my entire next meal. Basically, if you see spinach-pasta dish on a Vetri menu, you should probably just order it. I mean, we all know about the incredible spinach gnocchi at Vetri Ristorante, but this lasagna certainly holds its own. In fact, you could taste each individual layer that at one point I thought I was eating a large raviolo, infused with delicate spinach flavors. The exterior was so deftly crisped that it was like eating well-seasoned fried cheese with the veal bolognese adding an extra layer of sweet savoriness. Definitely a favorite of the night.

*** TO BE CONTINUED ***

If I could give 0 stars I would. This chic fil a is horrible. I will never come back to this location. The wait time is horrible and the employees attitudes are unacceptable. I ordered breakfast and my order was canceled.

Excellent selection of fine spirits and mixed drinks.  The food was a creative mix of classic American favorites with a North African mix of herbs and spices. The restaurant and patio had great style and ambiance.

This is hands down the worst Chipotle I've ever been to... by far. I've visited 3 times and I actually think they may have gotten worse. After my first visit, I wrote to Chipotle HQ about it, recommending a visit to perhaps provide remedial training to the managers and employees.  I have been a patron at Chipotle restaurants all over the US and I think I have a reasonable sense of expectations: clean areas, efficient employees, fresh and available ingredients. They fail on all three counts. Our portions were tiny. The employees were slow, lazy, and/or annoyed. The checkout counter was filthy. They were out of sour cream (?) and the drink fridge was half empty.  This Chipotle is more Taco Bell than Taqueria. I'll just drive the extra 10-15 mins to a different place.

I dined here last night and was completely disappointed and embarrassed I suggested this restaurant. We were greeted by the hostess who was kind and friendly and seated us immediately. Seating is so jammed together they have to move your table so you can turn sideways and slide your way into the booth. I could hear the conversation to the right and left of me clearly and could rub elbows with fellow diners making me feel uncomfortable and trapped in. I asked the hostess to seat us elsewhere and she was accommodating and understanding.  However, I did think to myself, if I were to need to use the restroom while food was on the table, would I have to raise my hand to have the waitress move my table? 
So let's talk about the food..
After we ordered we were given complimentary almost frozen bread...it was very cold.
We had the traditional meatballs which were good, although a little flavorless. And for the main dishes, the bucatini and lasagna. The eggplant lasagna is completely disappointing and sad looking. The eggplant was tough and hard to chew not sure how that's possible but apparently it is! Who knew! It was also only slightly warm and the portion size looks like it should belong on a kids menu.
I did enjoy the Bucatini and ate that up quickly !

I suggested this restaurant because I came here two years ago and enjoyed every dish I had. Sad to see Amis go downhill and needless to say I will not be returning. The only reason I am giving this review one stars is because the service the hostess gave was great was and that she was  accommodating..

Worst Chick Fil A I have even been to and I was in sales all over Florida. Many times I've come here, the employees have been rude or unpersonable. My orders are wrong around 25% of the time. The drive-thru layout is horrific.... and not an employee or manager to be seen to direct traffic during busy times. Avoid this location and drive the extra 4 minutes to the South Tampa location...they are amazing. You'll spend those extra 4 minutes waiting in this line anyway at this location so just do it.
Worst restaurant in the chain!!!! Wrong orders, missing items, the female manager is useless and rude. Wht a horrible place!!!! She does nothing to fix the conplaints and instead walks away!!!

Came here for Valentines dinner and was thoroughly impressed.  This is my first Marc Vetri restaurant and it did not disappoint.  I yelped some of the more popular selections before coming here.  

We ended up ordering the fried cauliflower and the swordfish meatballs for appetizers.  The swordfish meatballs were perfectly cooked, but my mom makes her own fish balls and I couldn't distinguish the difference in meatballs made with white fish and this swordfish - nonetheless, it was delicious.  The fried cauliflower was great as well, didn't really taste fried to me, more like baked?  

For our main course we had the Cacio E Pepe and Paccheri with Swordfish and Eggplant fries.  I can't speak much for the Cacio E Pepe, but the Paccheri was delicious and a very interesting looking dish.  Slightly salty, but savory nonetheless.  It's definitely a foreign idea to me - paccheri in tomato sauce with basil, swordfish bites, and topped with a few eggplant fries.  Somehow it worked, kudos Vetri.

For dessert I had seen the Belgian waffles with nutella on here, so we had to have it.  It did not disappoint.  We were so stuffed at that point - the portion sizes were larger than I had anticipated.

Mike was very helpful !! Needed a recliner for my husbands birthday 
was a smooth process and a fast delivery   Was included 
Delivery guys was very professional!!! Definitely coming back again!!

It was love at first bite here! My bf took me here to celebrate my PhD proposal being approved. It was a last minute date, but it was great! The staff were very friendly and accommodating. 

We had the meatballs for an appetizer and can I tell you, they were so good, I thought we might have to fight over who would get the last one (of course, he is a gentleman, so he offered the last one to me). The bread was light and fresh, served with warm butter as I like and the food was fresh. Our dishes were flavorful and well seasoned. We didn't have to wait long for our food and the seating, lighting and ambiance were perfect. 

The dessert was heavenly! We had the Belgian style waffle with nutella and hazelnuts - can you say DELICIOUS! This place is off the beaten path and is not located in restaurant row and because of such, may not get as much play. However, this restaurant is 5 stars all the way. 

Did I mention the ambiance is wonderful. This is definitely a place where you can go to have a nice evening with the one you love and share the love of food :).

We just tried Moe's. We usually go to Qdoba. Qdoba has bigger portions and no upcharges. Qdoba queso has much better flavor. We also use Qdoba' rewards program and easily earn free entrees. We won't be going back to Moes.

Amazing happy hour! Cheap drinks ($3.50 for beers) and cheap but delicious food (neat Asian choices like edamame and Shanghai chicken). Just don't get the red wine flight, it's $5 but it's horrible.

Really friendly and attentive servers. Nice place to get cheap drinks and good food.

Went there with some friends hoping for another lucky strike of good food.

I started with the Bufala Mozzarella with Clementines and Walnuts, nothing exceptional to brag about! My friend, however, had the Baked Pecorino with almond honey, It was Warm, melted and looked amazing and I knew I had to try it. The saltiness of the gooey cheese and the sweetness of the almond honey drizzle was divine. I totally regret not getting it! 

Rigatoni with skirt rib ragu was my entree. The home-made rigatoni was okay, not the best I ever had. Besides the tough texture, the chef was so generous with salt! 
Seriously, my pasta was extra salty that I thought either my blood pressure will be elevated or I will dehydrate. I think I did drink more than five glasses of water to compensate the highly-salt dish.

After the disappointing appetizer and entree, I was hoping that my dessert at least will be the "icing on the cake,"I believed that it will be hard to go wrong with the Belgian Style Waffle with nutella, vanilla semifreddo and toasted hazelnuts, it sounded as the winning combination. Again, it was decent, not really memorable. I had a bite of my friend's Mom-Mom's Rice Pudding looking for some comfort, I was dissatisfied. The chef complementary tiramisu was average! 

Nothing was memorable except the Baked Pecorino with almond honey, I will go again just to have it for myself!

Disappointing highlights: 
1/ We weren't seated until the rest of our party showed up- we waited at the bar.
2/ Food took forever to come out, with long gap between courses 
3/ I'm even more disappointed because its part of Vetri's family!

Three Yelps!

Not the best location around. Used app to order dine in and had to wait 15 minutes for the order with only two other customers inside. Hash browns were 'warm' and soggy. I ordered a chicken filet without the biscuit and I got what looked to be a nugget. Small potion and not even hot. Quality control is lacking.

Once the weather starts turning colder, I start to consistently crave warm bowls of pasta in all forms. And that is how I found my way to Amis. 

Inside, Amis is cozy and warm, with dark lighting and close tables, lending an intimate vibe to diners. The menu is elevated italian, with all of your favorites, many with a twist. 

We started with the BUFALA MOZZARELLA - a gorgeous white dream with a fluffy consistency, topped with sweet and crunchy apples and a drizzle of honey oil. I didn't find that the apples paired well with the mozz, but regardless the cheese was delicious on it's own. 

I'm not sure who "Sal" is, though I'd like to meet him because SAL'S OLD SCHOOL MEATBALLS were some of the best I've had. The order comes with 3 decadent and luscious meatballs that exceeded any expectations I have. The meatballs were incredibly moist and flavorful. If you even remotely like meatballs, you should definitely order these to start!

After finishing our starters and enjoying our bottle of wine, we didn't even notice that our pasta was taking a little long to come - really, we didn't. Without even the slightest complaint, we were brought crispy cauliflower, courtesy of the chef, because he didn't like how our pastas turned out and he was remaking them. That is some quality service right there - he was attentive to both our food and us, and to that I am thankful. 

The CRISPY CAULIFLOWER is a large portion, covered in pecorino cheese and a spicy red sauce drizzling on top. 

Now, the moment we had been waiting for - the pastas. And honestly, we were a bit disappointed. Everything was good, but nothing was as good as I hoped it would be. 

The COCOA FETTUCCINE had an earthy flavor but an unpleasant brown color. The wide-cut noodles are thick enough to stand up to the heavy flavors of the mushrooms and parmesan cheese. It was good, but I think I would have preffered another pasta. 

The TONNARELLI was your classic cacio e pepe, but was too peppery. I liked the bite from the pepper, but it could have been a little more subtle.

Amis is a cozy place for warming up on these cold nights with comforting pastas and meatballs better than your Italian mama can make.

It's a new hot pot restaurant in University City with nice decor. Since I'm a hot pot fan, I give this place four stars. The hot pot bases are good in general, and I like their three-base large pot that can be shared by groups, so you can try different hot pot bases with your friends.

I usually have my hot pot with spicy base because I'm from Chengdu. The spicy base is around the same level as Nine Ting in Chinatown. It's okay, probably at an acceptable level offered outside Sichuan/Chongqing areas, but not authentic enough from my point of view.

The biggest problem here is service & management. The waiters seem not well-trained and the restaurant management is quite messy, which definitely can be improved.

Nice ambience and locale. Reservations needed. Food was above average, quick service. Sometimes way too quick, the waitress hardly gave us time to dig in to our dishes and she was already asking us how it was! Starters of meatball and fried cauliflower were great. Seconds pasta with jalapeño and almond pesto had an awesome al dente texture but the sauce was a little meh (couldn't tell what the flavor was). Scallops were good and the chocolate dessert was delicious. I would repeat!

The drive-thru at this location is awful, it doesn't matter what time of day it is I have had to wait 15-20 in line at this location on multiple occasions, which is unheard of at Chick-fil-A. They also have bad card readers being used by the staff walking along the drive-thru, they had to take my card to three different machines because they weren't syncing to the i-pads. Then I finally got my meal and the fries are rock hard and inedible. This location is just a headache, avoid at all costs.

I clearly got this place on an off night.   Had a bad experience top to bottom.

Had reservations at 9 for 3 people for a friends birthday.  Showed up around 8:45 and was told it would just be a few minutes.  We got drinks at the bar.  Pretty tasty.  Checked in around 9:10 on the table - was told just a few more minutes.  Checked back in at 9:20...was told "they were clearing the table".   9:30...still not seated.   Checked in again and the hostess said she would send over the manager.  He came over and explained that they were only 15 minutes behind and were just waiting for a few tables to finish.   I was confused and said our reservation was for 9:00....He didnt say "Oh, I apologize we have you down for 9:15"  he literally said "No, your reservation is 9:15".    While he was standing there I pulled up the email confirmation (hoping I had it right) and of course my email confirmation showed 9:00.   Upon showing him the email....he said nothing.  Walked away to the host station.   Strangely we were seated within 30 seconds....without apology or explanation.   I know it might seem annoying or simple but we didnt get seated until 9:40.   I am fine waiting...just want to be treated properly.  A simple apology would have made the whole night better

The food?  Well it was solid but not great my favorite two items of the night....the sweetbreads and the mortadella (my favorite) mousse.    Squash lasagna was just very average to me...nothing great, nothing awful.   The Swordfish meatballs seemed very fishy ( I realize it was fish).    I would give the Food a 3 1/2 stars.   Again....I am guessing our palettes were off due to being in a pissy mood.
Super good fry rice (huge plate for $8), amazing fried dumplings (8 for $5).  This is the place I always come to eat whenever I am in Philly!

Schenk's has great pastries and the most amazing lemon meringue pie and apple pie. But, I ordered a Blueberry pie for my mother's birthday and it was terrible.  There weren't any blueberries in the pie, it was like a goopy jelly. My dad said it was the worst pie he ever had.
WORST CHIPOTLE IN TAMPA. They have the worst customer service! You wouldn't even think you're a paying customer. The way we were treated made me completely lose my appetite :/

Really great food - Great service - All around 5 stars

Went with friends before an event at TCC - got their early but a lot of other folks had the same idea so there was a line out the door. Luckily we had reservations and got seated and served right away. We were expecting things to back up but actually, everything was served on time and to perfection. They've got a really diverse menu - something for everyone. Sally, the owner, was very friendly and wish I'd gotten the server's name but he was really on top of everything. Top choice for Tucson for sure.

These folks are absolutely fabulous! I initially used their Groupon for 1 time service and now I'm a quarterly customer. The owner communicated very very well with me and my needs. The tech we worked with, Larry, IS THE FRIGGIN MAN! I loved working with this guy! It was easy to tell how much experience he had. He was really a delight to work with and I've requested him again for my next appointment with absolutely no issues. 

Get some dry wall and spackle cause the customer service here will flip your wig so hard it will leave a hole in the wall! I'm absolutely thrilled to leave Terry and her team a 5 star review. They definitely deserve it.

Really good strawberry shortcakes as another reviewer mentioned. I've gotten a few of them for various birthdays for coworkers and all have been really delicious. I've also had their chocolate cake with chocolate buttercream icing. I'mnot a big fan of chocolate on chocolate but this was pretty, very moist, just didn't love the jimmies on the outside of the cake. I've also recently tried the carrot cake, which was very rich almost more like a coffee cake than carrot cake, but good.The cakes are also reasonably priced (i think around $12 for the strawberry shortcake). It's worth a visit if you're in the neighborhood.

Truly a sad day. This has been my go to bakery forever but I must move on. The makeover has brought minimal improvements (counter staff attitudes) and doubtful improvements (decor) but also major problems. The best decorator in the area is gone, replaced with someone just average but even worse than that the products are poor. A $125 birthday cake dry as toast. I'm needing the exact same cake in a few weeks and am heartbroken to have to take my business elsewhere.

I was here about 2 years ago and loved it.  Raved about the food to everyone.  Went back last night.  The atmosphere and the service were good.  The menu appeared to be much the same so I was excited.  Then I was disappointed when the food was served.  It wasn't terrible but certainly want neatly as good as on my previous visit.  With so many good restaurants in town don't think
I'll be back.

NOT FOR DINNER! Didn't expect to spend $55 (not including drinks or tip) and leave hungry! I ordered the Chicken Tandoori dinner expecting to get half a chicken, well they brought out two drumsticks, a though and two pieces of bone lol.  Also ordered a chicken tikka massalla, very little chicken in it; I think they took the meat of the the breast in the tandoori, gave us the bones, sold us the meat in the tikka and had enough left over they made a second tikka massalla for another customer lol! we order a chick pea veggie dish, great portion and delicious; I think that just because chic peas were cheap for them to buy so they splurged.  Bottom line is don't come here for dinner, waste of money.   I won't even go into the awkwardness they make you feel if you walk in with a sleeping baby in a stroller.  But hey the food tastes great!

This location is PERFECT.. with that being said.. the LAYOUT if horrific. Clearly none of the 5 stars have gone during lunch peak hours where you only have one way in and that same way out! Good LAWRD! I feel like they had so much time to lay out the restaurants aesthetics properly; especially being right off of Dale Mabry. So Ironically I wanted Chick-Fil-A for lunch and was like 'Oh let's try out the new one'. It was already too late to turn around as the drive thru and the entrance ... AND THE EXIT is all in one spot! It's an accident waiting to happen. 

OK enough about that part (which is like a major part about this location) If you really want to come here go at a totally OFF PEAK time... like anything before 11am and after 7pm. I walked in and there was NO one in LINE?! I thought to myself where the.. why the.. there are SO MANY CARS in the parking LOT..coz it's a small lot. I ordered my food and then walked to the side and realized that's where everyone was.. they had taken over the communal table and half were using it to wait for there to go orders. 

The inside is impeccable.. it's beautiful inside. I would love to come here ALL THE TIME but that will not be happening unless it is off peak hours or we can convince the intern at work to go get our food (which you're not allowed to tell millennial's to do because it's below their pay grade---this is a whole other subject) back to my review...Its so pretty inside, the staff is so friendly as EVERY Chick-Fil-A has ever been. I would love to see how they train their employees because the other chains can take a note out of their play books on niceness. 

OK-- i had it at 2 stars but changed it to 3 stars--considering the other horrible element of this place... the inside experience is nice. People were drinking their drinks while they waited for food and the staff was always quick to say 'If anyone needs a refill come on up'. =)

Exceptional service, by far one of the most hospitable staff I have ever encountered by a restaurant, from being accommodating to knowledge of the menu. Delicious food, highly recommend the fettuccine main and the truffle dessert. A bit loud for such a beautiful restaurant, but not enough for me to give 4 stars

WORST CHIPOTLE EVER!!! I ordered via the chipotle app at and received an order confirmation email at 12:57pm saying my order would be ready at 1:30pm. I arrived at 1:30 and saw the pick up order shelf to be empty and approximately 8 people standing around waiting for pick up orders. I have the girl at the cashier my name and order pick up time and I was met with an attitude far from that of good customer service. About 10 minutes later I reminded her of my order and she finally printed out the order receipt and gave it to the two guys making orders. I finally received my order at 1:50pm and did not receive any apology or kind gesture regarding the wait and horrible customer service. I got home and opened up my order, BOTH orders were WRONG. I was missing items on both orders and both orders had items on them we did not order. To add this fiasco, my food was not even room temperature warm, no napkins and not eating utensils. I WILL NOT return to this location. This location gives chipotle a bad look and I strongly hope chipotle comes in and does an overhaul. Lost my business permanently.
Delicious and unique food - a proper reflection of the Tucson community.

This chipotle is consistently terrible. I went in at 8:15pm on a Tuesday to a long line that was barely moving. I stood in line for 15 minutes and watched the people working start orders then leaving to go in the back. They all opened refrigerators and went in the back with the gloves on they wore to grab food without changing them when they got back. The line was messy with food all over the surfaces. They were out of black beans and steak, both of which I generally order, and said they wouldn't be making more even though they had over an hour before closing and a line of people. The lettuce for the salad was almost empty and what was left did not look fresh. The staff was slow, and seemed uninterested in anyone they were serving, and there wasn't a manager of any sort in sight. Needless to say I didn't stick around to eat, and after many disappointments I doubt I will again. 

Do yourself a favor and go across the street to Qdoba where the staff is always friendly and fast and the food's always fresh.

This chick fil a is consistently the worst one out there people! I usually come only because of the convenient location but I will drive out of my way from now on... everyone treats you like they don't care about their job and forget about doing aNy kjnd of mobile orders they always take WAY longer than going through linee... and  I ALWAYS ask for lemon  with my tea and 90% of the time they say "I don't have any cut up" or just straight up say they don't have any.... and it will be 7 AM.. I know you lying!  And the worst part of this morning's trip was getting a long ass piece of hair FRIED into my chicken biscuit... absolutely disgusting. Do yourself a favor and go to McDonald's, honestly you would get treated better there anyways.

37 minutes and counting!  I'm still in line for "fast" food!  Completely unacceptable, I want to drive over the landscaping just to escape but I'm blocked in.  This is 2nd worst place in Tampa, behind Popeyes.  Stay away from this place if you have any plans for your day!

The worst service I have experienced at a Moe's franchise. The workers are rude and incompetent. After multiple errors with deliveries (three of my deliveries - taco packs - contained only sides and no protein), I decided to take my daughter to order in person because she loves the chicken. The workers were incredibly rude. At first they wouldn't take her order and implied she could not pay for it. They skipped over her to the next customer even after she said she knew the cost of a taco pack.  When I went in to see what the problem was, they continued to ignore us. There where three people behind the line and two of them just stood there doing nothing while the line got longer. After 15 minutes of waiting (for them to finish the orders of the customers who had been behind my daughter), I ordered the taco pack. I got home and discovered they had left out the sides. I am never returning, and I'll be happy to see it fail so a reliable business can take its place.

Based on the reviews on the strawberry shortcake I decided to make to trek to this bakery from far northeast .. Nice clean place... Bought cake home ... Both my wife and I did not like it... The icing was not what we expected and not enough strawberry throughout... Sad to say ended up in the trash... But the cinnamon buns were good

I don't know why I give them more chances. I'm better off driving a little farther to the south tampa chic fil a. Every time I order they miss something. This time I had a pretty big order (my bad for not checking) they forgot to put an entire meal in my 3 bags!! The time before I did a delivery straight from the app and they forgot fries and a cookie... the time before they didn't give me a sandwich! Get it together. This time out of principal I won't be back.

The best & most authentic wanton I've ever had in US! Even better than those authentic Chinese restaurants in California. The taste is very alike the wanton I had back in my hometown. The childhood memories all came after drinking the soup. Love it so much!
