Worse CFA experience. Sad that even one of the shift manager Erika was just as rude. Got my order wrong and had a horrible attitude when I came back to get my correct order. Not typical of a CFA, this one is the worst.

Thai mama is a nice food truck and seating area in the lot of comfort in. I ordered the shrimp Pad thai, it was too saucy and the noodles were too soft, basically mush, but they had a decent amount of shrimp, which saved it. My husband, who is a shrimp fried rice connoisseur, loved his entree. It was nicely seasoned and good amount of shrimp.  Might come back to try their curry.

This has got to be the worst chipotle I've been to, and I've been to many. The rice is always either over or undercooked, the meat is too salty, the vegetables have either been sitting out or are underripe, the staff is disjointed, with no leadership. Corporate, if you're listening- you've got a major problem here.

How can you possibly hire the slowest people ever. This is consistent I refuse to go to this location again. Most of my friends who love Chick Fil A also have started to avoid this location. I just amazed the company allows this to continue. I'm done.

I've been here twice and had the $20 all you can eat option (once on Saturday lunch and the other on Sunday lunch). I would suggest getting the hotpot split with spicy and the mild normal one (sorry can't remember the name). When we just got the mild one, I don't think the flavor is as concentrated so it definitely tastes water downed. We got two rounds of vegetables and meats for 5-6 of us. 

The service was fast and relatively attentive. There was never too much of crowd when I came so we never had to wait. 

There are also other family style options I saw, including a giant lobster and this giant rice stove dish.

The food is good, but the menu is misleading. We ordered all you can eat but the menu shows all you can eat and other food with extra price on the same page. When we ordered, the waitress didn't remind us that some food we ordered is not included in the all you can eat list and charged us almost twice the price. I think they are misleading, deceiving and cheating consumers. Though the taste of hot pot is reasonable, I don't think I'll ever come again.

What's worse, the plates and soup bowls are not clean. The servers are not well trained and one of them even stopped us from eating more. As long as you do not only focus on the taste of food but also food quality, service and whole experience, please do not come.
New bar in soho! Pretty nice from what I've seen. They have tables inside for dining and an inside/outside bar area. They have pretty good music too!

Knowing that I had a project from October that would be completing Valentine's day weekend, I wanted to ensure that I could take my wife somewhere enjoyable, before I ditched her for a long time...  I really wanted to travel to the Devon location, but then my wife wanted to go to the city.  I placed my reservation and received a follow-up phone call confirmation a few days before our night out.  

The day of, we left a bit earlier, expecting traffic and didn't hit any.  I made it to the city with quite a lot of time to spare.  We found street parking right away and walked to the restaurant about a half hour early.  Fortunately they were able to seat us that early and we were in for a fantastic evening.  

We wanted a lot of food.  Starting off, we went with Sal's Old School Meatballs and some pumpkin ravioli.  Honestly, the pumpkin ravioli was some of the best food we had the entire evening!  Brown butter sauce and pumpkin, but not pumpkin spice flavor.  

As a Valentine's day special, my wife went with the Tonnarelli and lobster, while I tackled the slow braised Goat.  Each bite was better than the previous one.  I didn't want to share, but of course I had to.  Kind of...  

For dessert, a chocolate tart with some butter semifreddo.  We enjoyed the fresh pastas and the great service.  They really made out night special.

Amis may or may not be my favorite restaurant in Philly. Okay, fine, it is. I can't help but recommend this place to everyone that visits Philly. AMIS, YOU WIN, YOU HAVE MY HEART, OKAY? Amis is even better than my favorite Italian restaurant in New York (Giano).

I love Italian food, and I only love it as much as I do today because of Amis. This place is amazing delicious beautiful intimate and have I mentioned amazing? A good friend of mine took me here before I graduated college and I regret not having discovered Amis before then.

We started with the salami del giorno with onion marmalade ($8), which was delicious. The salami comes in slices that are quite thick, and the marmalade balances the saltiness of the salami perfectly. The plate comes with around 5 slices of salami but it was a great appetizer.

For entree, I got the tonnarelli "cacio e pepe" with pecorino and black pepper. Oh my goodness, I loved this so much. The pecorino sauce with black pepper is rich, but not heavy in a way that made me feel too full from flavor. An extremely simple dish, but it's what I imagine a pasta dish would be like from Italy. The pasta was cooked to perfection and I am literally salivating as I type this.

For dessert, my friend and I split the belgian waffle with nutella and ice cream. UGH I WANT TO EAT THIS EVERY DAY. The belgian waffle was fluffy, but still had a nice crunch. The ice cream was perfect and I could just eat a jar of nutella myself normally so there's that.

I left Amis so full and so satisfied. Like, never been happier in my life. I recommended a couple of friends to go to Amis when they visited Philly for the first time and they loved it too.

Definitely a great restaurant for a date, as it is very intimate, with dim lighting and very cute decor.

Amis, I love you. So much. So so much.

Ordered a cookie tray for work the day before Thanksgiving. The staff had no problem putting this together for me at the last minute and had it ready at the time promised over the phone. People in work raved about the cookies. A huge tray lasted less than 2 hours. (I work with vultures) If you like crunchy chocolate chip cookies, these are my absolute favorite. Even though the bakery was super busy, the staff was really nice.

Ate at bar with my buddy Jules. Good stiff drink. It was some type of house special old fashioned. Nice dining room. I like Vetri restaurants for the most part and was excited to try this place. A bit of a letdown. Good "foo foo" food. Nice presentation but just ok.  Tried a bunch of small plates and a couple of pastas. The pasta dishes were the best part. Nice staff. Nice vibe. Expensive food. I prefer Osteria and Vetri ala carte menu.
This place is good but I won't rush back.

Ordered 2 of the exact same orders, a chick fil a sandwich no pickles combo, the first sandwich was fine no pickles but the fries lacked the "sprinkling of sea salt" the fries were not seasoned what so ever, I was able to move past that but my 2nd sandwich I ordered came with pickles and that's where my foot goes down. Only 3 things come on the sandwich. Bread, chicken and pickles. Now when I ask for no pickles and somehow pickles still ends up on the sandwich when there's only 3 things that come on it anyhow that's just ridiculous. Also need a larger lot or something because the drive thru is all out of whack with so many cars being in it and no room to leave the parking lot it was a mess

There are some good employees here but the bad outweighs the good. This place is so hit and miss that you never know if you're going to get good service that day or not. 85% of the employees are rude and jip you on food. I shouldn't have to ask for more, just put the proper amount! It's not difficult. They're ALWAYS out of something.. Whether it's guac, peppers/onions, if it's not one thing it's another.

The westshore & north Dale mabry locations are 20% better. I'm not brave enough to try Qudoba but Ill probably venture to chik fil a or westshore chipotle

This location needs work!  When we arrived at lunch time. 1:20.  No chicken no beef no brown rice.   no forks.   We waited for the chicken and brown rice (about 5 mins) but were told  steak would take forever so didnt wait for that.  Thus, my son got a burrito he didnt want.    Anyways, the "general manager" sensed my frustration and was gracious enough to offer me a BOGO card.  So..... if i come back and spend more money (after my $40 family lunch) they will give me one free.  no thanks. I will be driving to  the westshore location.   One last thing.  the gentleman cutting the chicken gave us all a dirty look when we asked for steak.  It was cooked but he was cutting chicken and would not stop to offer us steak.  

This location will not survive with this type of service.  And , there is enough negativity surrounding Chipolte that at least their workers should be  trained on customer care!

I decided to spring a date night on my wife. She chose this spot because.... well neither us had ever been! So I agreed because it's her night and I'm always up to the challenge. 
So your meal starts with bread while you wait. The bread didn't taste like anything and you don't get any butter or olive oil for it. Unless maybe you were supposed to ask? Either way we got the happy hour bruschetta so it wasn't important. 
I got the swordfish special. It was beets and swordfish on top of arugula with olive oil vinaigrette. Not a lot of food. I was planning on going light tonight anyway. The fish was pretty dry. I think it was cooked a little too long. I just tried to soak up the oil with my fish. She got some noodle dish that I had a taste of. Yum! Overall my dish was good but She won this round! 
We shared a rice pudding. We've been desperate for rice pudding since going to the Pineville a few weeks back. This did not disappoint. It was very good! 
No complaints about service. No real complaints about anything. It was a nice surprise night out. The bill came out to about $70 something after tip. So that's for a happy hour appetizer, one happy hour drink, two meals and desert. Oh also a hot tea!

At the risk of sounding a little picky but, I KNOW Amis can do better.  Now please allow me to explain because we had a very good meal but I've been to Amis once prior for brunch and was blown away but this time there was some inconsistency in the preparation of our meals.  

Our evening started very promisingly with the bufala ricotta bruschetta, and the charred octopus.  The octopus was amazing, perfectly cooked with the right amount of crisp on the outside without compromising on the tenderness of the flesh, excellent, my wife even said after the meal that she would have been happy just eating a few portions of that alone.  I also wanted to try the veal tongue.  It was cooked with some kind of cranberry reduction and green onions, it was a little greasy but that didn't detract from the flavor at all.

My wife and I each had an entree, the fried branzino and lamb loin respectively and shared 1 order of the cacio de pepe.  We were especially looking forward to our pasta because the last time we had that preparation was in rome itself next to the pantheon and absolutely loved it.  Our dinner companions had the bucatini with jalapeno, almond pesto, and paccheri, alla norma, swordfish.  

Unfortunately this is where I thought our pasta fell a little flat.  I appriciate that the hardness of the pasta is often a personal preference but I thought our cacio de pepe was a little too soft but the paccheri alla norma was a little too al dente.  Again how done a pasta should be is up to the individual person but personally I thought it would have been better if the various pasta had the same consistency.  I also thought the cacio de pepe was lacking in pepper so I asked for some extra.  All in all, I was slighlty underwhelmed with our pasta, still very good in flavor but need to tighten up the execution.  

Our entrees though were excellent.  The lamb was cooked perfectly and the fried branzio was very good.  I never had fried branzio but it was very good, not overly greasy.  However, there was one slight issue and that was the sauce for the branzio and lamb was very similar, I believe they both had a pesto base and maybe some other embellishments but basically the same sauce.  For those of you who have read my review of Terrain, you know this is a pet peve of mine.  No restaurant worth their salt should reuse a sauce for a different dish. That is just lazy.  Again good flavors but just not quiet the level I was hoping for.

Finally, we had a rice putting with pistachio and mint.  I like the dessert but one of our companions didn't care for the mint but I thought it was good.  What would have been even better probably is if they had some kind of Gelato or sorbeto as a dessert option. if you've been to Rome you'd know that nothing beats a good gelato after a great meal.  

So in conclusion.  Amis is definitely a great Italian restaurant.  In my opinion, they had some issues with execution tonight.  If you are used your local macoroni grill or olive garden this place will blow you away, and even for any one who has had "real" roman cuisine, this is still a very good choice short of flying to Rome for dinner.

PS, the brussels sprouts were a fantastic side.

We use to eat here all the time but This location has gone downhill.  Each visit gets more disappointing. Overpriced, cold and skimpy amount of ingredients.  Never order online - they will really mess up the order or pile on the lettuce to compensate for the lacking meat/rice/beans.  Better off at chipotle or taco bus...

Litterally always out of stuff.
Tonight we ordered a Salad and Bowl on the App.  They were out of the Salad Dressing and Salsa.  Luckily we were planning on getting chicken as they were out of steak as well.

Last time, they were out of cheese and lettuce.  They ended up just giving people queso for free since they were out of cheese.  Its hit or miss if they have steak, id call ahead

I love this place! The food is imaginative and delicious - always a treat. I recently had the clams, which were delightful. The beet salad and risotto were excellent as well, just a couple of many good options for vegetarians. The service and atmosphere were also impeccable. The building is truly representative of Tucson, and the history well preserved. Check out the patio on a nice evening - can't be beat!

First visit here- it's a block from my office but seems like the opening bugs have finally gone away. The menu is now pretty much all available- which added the Salmon bowl- it's a LARGE bowl of food. It's got greens, some Asian slaw, a good portion of salmon and lots of sticky noodles. It all works together- but needs some more sauce then what comes from the kitchen- the noodles all kind of stick to themselves and make it a little messy to eat. I added some sirachi which acted as lube and I like the heat so it works- adding a bit more sauce right from the kitchen is badly needed. Could use more Asian flavor it was sorta bland but I admit I like bold and interesting stuff this seems to be catered more towards the masses then fancy palates like mine ;) service was good she kept the waters filled- my coworker got the Pork Banh Mi and for the $$ I wouldn't order that personally, but hard to compete with Saigon Deli which is my go to for Banh Mi- overall a nice atmosphere with the super high ceilings and very nice lighting and ambience. Will go back for more off the menu in future :)

Usually a good time. The cakes are consistently yummy  and the hours are reasonable. The location is great and the staff is always friendly.

One time I visited and wanted a standard poundcake or cupcake with chocolate but they didn't have any on display. That wasn't a big deal until they told me that they usually don't have that stocked. Not okay but what do I know.

Love me some chipotle, but came out unimpressed with this one.

Ordered the chicken and it was probably the saltiest chicken I had from a chipotle.
The guy on the grill cooking the meat, was on his cell phone talking while cooking.  No one seemed to know that salad dressing comes with salads.  They kept telling me "youll get it at the register".  Then I get to the register and they didnt even know they had salad dressing.

This place is just as old tucson Pueblo as you get I've been twice and I must tell you the more people want to dine here the loader it gets. It's like spend some money on installation.  The potential for this space is over the top. Decor is splendid the food is alright at best and the staff are entitled servers . The price point is expensive. We had high hope for this place and I'm sure it will get better but for this moment in time . Why ? They do have one saving grace the 5.00 $ glass of pretty good wine. This is my last visiT the first on sept 25 which I felt oh well another tasteless dish.  Adding salt and spices does not make a dish.  The owner a real Tucsonian should know the equation having other gem Resterante under her belt.  In short if you are going to open a Swanky looking place make the food better than the place then people will rave about the food . Anyway cool m once oh well jokes on me fool me twice I'll kick myself in the back side and there won't b a third time . Sorry

This is my absolute go to place for Chick-fil-a! I come here all the time after my classes and my food is always one point! I always mobile order and my food is always one time and cooked to perfection! Costumer service is great and everyone is really nice there :)

How the heck have I not been back more often for dinners and industry nights?! Alas, regret is setting in too late as Amis will close their doors tonight. 

We landed last minute reservations at the Chef's counter - where we got to see all the dishes go out. Everything looked fantastic, and the pastas were incredible (of course)

I wish we could have ordered more, but our bellies could only hold so much.

The other locations will remain open, but the glory of 13th St is no more. :(

Stopped by to get a quick drink. We didn't have time to grab a bite on this trip, but we will definitely be back. The location and the atmosphere is great. The hostess and servers were so quick and accommodating. They assured us right away and found us a seat at the bar. Bar tender came over right away and asked for our order and also had a couple of recommendations for specials of the day. 

We grabbed a quick beer and a old fashioned.  Beer was nice and cold, and the mixed drink was nice and strong and perfectly made. As we sat and enjoyed our drinks we had the opportunity to see a lot of the dishes come out. The one that stood out the most was definitely the pork chop with mashed potatoes. Looked and smelled fantastic. The couple next to us couldn't stop raving about it. Definitely will order that on our next visit. 

They do have a great drink menu with lots of specialty drinks available. The place itself was so quaint/retro side it was as if you stepped back in time to the 30s or 40s era. (Not a bad thing) very warm and inviting. 

The hostess was very nice and informative. Told us about the dishes and also recommended reservations if you wanted a table. At least 2-3 days in advanced. They can accommodate parties, and they do have a area where you can have a private area for 14+ people.  If you haven't been, it's a must go for a drink or a nice dinner!

I quite enjoyed my recent visit to The Coronet. The food is very good; the ambience is lively and fun, though the noise could be a little overwhelming. 

My companions began with the Dinner Salad, while I selected the Beet & Halloumi Salad. Theirs was a simple green salad, but nothing special. The beet salad was excellent, though! Large slabs of salty halloumi cheese are paired with chopped beets, hazelnuts, and shallot, and drizzled with a lemon vinaigrette. This salad hits all the right notes: salty, rich, zesty, bright, and earthy. I'd honestly love an entree-sized portion! 

For our entrees, we selected the Salmon, the Roast Chicken, and the Roast Eggplant. The salmon was topped with a butter citrus sauce and served with a spiced pumpkin puree and creamy leeks and rutabagas. It was a delicious dish -- subtle and appropriately wintery-feeling. The portion was small, but was sufficient when following a salad. The chicken was on the other end of the spectrum in that it was a very large portion of chicken served with shrimp and a heaping plate of grits. The flavors were bright, bold, and punchy; it felt like a fun twist on both shrimp and grits and southern-style chicken with okra and greens. The peanuts added a great textural element as well. The eggplant was a very interesting dish. It's large eggplant steak with a creamy couscous and accompanying squash, radish, and greens, and the flavors strongly reminded me of Thai food. It was good, but only for serious lovers of eggplant. 

We were excited to see the new location, which is charming, and were happy to see the restaurant happily bustling. This did mean, however, that it was quite loud. Between the live music and the way the patrons' conversations echo loudly in the space, it was difficult to hold a conversation. It's also quite dimly-lit, so I'd recommend against taking anyone with vision or hearing impairments unless you're able to make accomodations for their needs.
Worst chick fil a I've ever been to. Drive thru is a mess. Waited 30 minutes and the workers couldn't care less. Tear it down

baked pecorino with almond honey $10
- delicious! one of my favorites from the menu. perfect balance of sweet from the almond honey and salt from the pecorino. 100% would order again.

grilled veal tongue with pepper mostarda $11
- my friend and i wanted to like this one. we wanted to try something a little different than our usual italian selections, but it ended up backfiring on us. we just couldn't get over the fact that we were eating tongue. if you're into offal, go for it!

rigatoni with beef bolognese and spinach  $16
for $16, i wish the portions were a little bigger. this is a decent rendition of the italian staple of a hearty pasta in meat sauce.

bucatini with jalapeno and almond pesto $16
- a creamy, nutty pasta with a little kick. i enjoyed it.

fried brussels sprouts and lemon $8
- i feel like you see roasted/fried sprouts on every menu these days, but they're there for a reason! super crispy with great texture.

I have heard so many times that Vetri's restaurants are A. expensive for what you get, B. crowded.  Neither was the case at Amis.  We came for brunch and it was surprisingly inexpensive and very good.  The trick I think is to order things that aren't so breakfasty.  In fact, you can mostly avoid anything to do with breakfast if you want to.

Amis is supposed to be very casual and the food is simple but extremely well done.

We did the charcuterie plate, the escarole salad, and some pasta dishes.  Mine was the carbonara.  A great rendition, everything about it was well done.  The escarole salad is not easy to find first of all, and this one had some parmesan on it, and it was just bitterly delightful because of course escarole is so bitter.  The charcuterie was three different meats with three different sauces/mustards, all very good.  One was a chicken liver.  I love it when a restaurant has the guts to do chicken liver, it has such great flavor.

We had a verdicchio and a valpolicella, two great inexpensive wines that just work so well with simple Italian cuisine.

Service was very professional, and staff knowledgeable.  All in all a great experience and inexpensive to boot, even though three people split two bottles of wine.  And one of us was my mother in law.  Now that says something, I think....

This probably is the worst experience I've ever had at a chic flila. Upon arrival through the drive thru I had asked to order spicy chicken biscuit. The cashier informed me that they were out I even stated I could wait she informed me no we are completely out. I would also say the level of service was horrible with no smile or excitement. They even forgot my drinks least to say I will never go back to this location. Management needs to do a better job of managing there people. I would rank a 0 because they have completely lost my business.

We were in town recently for a swim meet and we were told to go to Champion for a swimming Tech Suit for my daughter.  I was nervous when we pulled up because it just looked like your average pool supply store. To my surprise they had several kinds of competition swim suits (very reasonably priced) as well as Tech Suits. Eric was a huge help for our first time purchasing such an expensive suit. Honestly when my daughter needs another suit when this one wears out, I would make the drive from Phoenix down to Champion.

What happened?! I brought back like 10 co workers to a place I thought would deliver based on last years experience. This time around, (Tuesday evening) the waitresses bringing the food to our table looked super inconvenienced, annoyed and pissed. Food was super salty and orders screwed up. Music loud as heck. Have a feeling management changed. Not coming back. Please train your employees on hospitality and keeping their fingers and long hair out of food while putting it on tables. Ugh
Third time here and its been great every time! Darla, my bartender today, was awesome! Very friendly and attentive. Great rolls and drinks as well! Great addition to SoHo!

This used to be my favorite easy Mexican restaurant to pick up- but the service this past weekend was replaced with a bunch of young ladies (teenagers) that couldn't care about an ounce of customer service let alone a decent attitude. This time the food was probably cut in half portion size. They ran out of stuff early this Friday evening so just gave us what was left and charged the usual price. Probably won't be coming back until staff is changed.

What a gem!!  The Coronet's patio is a very special place,  and Tucson is lucky to have such a great outdoor dining experience available to us.  Delicious food, beautifully lit patios, and some of the best heaters around:  the Coronet offers all this and more.
We have been there for both happy hour and dinner, and we're already making plans to go back.

Schenk's Family Bakery on Veree Avenue in the Fox Chase neighborhood of Philadelphia, has been in the flour, water and yeast business since the early twentieth century when their first generation started baking in Germany before immigrating to Germantown  and opening their shop in 1938. Both the family and the bakery have moved around, but always remained Philly centric. Their recipes travelled well.

Today, their storefront is small and lined with glass display cases and shelved walls, all full of their classic cookies, doughnuts, cupcakes, custom iced cakes and amazing pound cake. My small sample of half dozen doughnuts (glazed, vanilla iced, cinnamon sugar and powdered sugar) were all fresh, lightly yeasty and full of sweet flavor. They were perfect for accompaniment with hot coffee. 

The vanilla pound cake was dense, moist and was solidly superior to any commercial effort I have eaten. Better even than Starbucks, which has been on my pedestal for a long while. It would have been great heated with a scoop of ice cream, but stood unapologetically on its own. Why they loaded it up on three sides with copious amounts of white icing is a mystery. It was truly an amazing sugar coating, but unnecessary given the quality of what it covered. Diabetic overkill. 

That shelf of large Eagles playoff cakes looked great and gave comfort that they would be the hit of any party or cold afternoon tailgate at the Linc. Unfortunately, the sweetness would not be enough to change the outcome of the game to come.

We had dinner with friends at the Coronet last night and we were not disappointed. Our friends had just been seated, and the hostess unerringly brought us to them. Our server immediately asked if there were any immediate needs, then a few minutes later, after we had a chance to peruse the uniquely exotic menu, she was back to help us one by one by explaining menu items as well as the off-menu special. Service was quiet and unobtrusive, but by standing next to each diner in turn, conflict with the music of the pianist two tables away was really not a bother.

I had the East African lamb dish, redolent with herbs and spices and delicious, with a fresh flavor bomb in each bite. My wife enjoyed her chicken dish down to the last crumb off the bone. Our friends similarly enjoyed their dishes so much that conversation almost stopped while we were tending to business on the plates. 

Dessert was not a relic, but a legacy from the past: the Tack Room chocolate mousse dressed with creme fraiche, rich and aromatic. 

The decor, with antique miniatures and bottles, suggests a restaurant from another era, and is worth a walk around the periphery of the restaurant while supper begins to digest.

We will definitely be back.

The slowest chick fil a ever. Sad it's the closest one to me. I once sat in the drive thru for an exact hour, and because there's no exit once u drive thru, I had no choice but to wait. Fries are always cold and half filled. Chicken sandwiches have double the bread than the chicken. And it's more often than not that they mess up the order.

If there was ever a restaurant to change my perception about Philly, I would have to look no further than Amis.

Not sure if my boyfriend, Danny, and I would have stumbled upon this place during our visit to Philly if I hadn't won a raffle for the annual charity event, "The Dude Hates Cancer."  

Amis had generously donated a gift certificate to this raffle which I had won back in August 2010.

The Maitre D seated myself and Danny directly in front of the open kitchen.  Total win!

I think our eyes were bigger than our stomachs when we first ordered the appetizers.  No regrets.  Everything was absolutely delish.  From the bruchetta of imported bufala ricotta and black pepper to the swordfish meatballs accompanied by one of the best polentas I've ever had.  Underscore the word, "ever."

Oh but appetizers didn't stop there, we received a house plate of a grilled veal tongue with pepper mostarda.    Danny and I smiled brightly at first and then had a "oh shit moment" of sorts.  Of course, I had wrongly assumed Danny (a classically trained chef) was well versed already in cooked tongue.

Me: "So..you've had tongue before, right?  How is it?"  His response, "Nope, but I'm about to find out."

Now, as much as I do enjoy food, I am quite PICKY.  Yes, there are people who have special diets....the gluten-free, low sodium, vegan....yeah, then there's me...the picky.

Yet, I decided to ignore my diet this one instance and politely picked up a piece of tongue labeled with grill marks and coated with what appeared to be a glaze (this would be the pepper mostarda).

Immediately took my first bite...looked at Danny.  "So umm...are you gonna eat the rest of that?"  

My only regret is that the pasta dish of ravioli was absolutely heaven and I wish I had ordered more of it.  So tender and the sauce perfectly complimented the pasta.

Dinner was good, but I think we were stuffed by the time it even came around.  Danny had the duck which was plated beautifully.

Of course, there is always room for dessert.  The tartufo was delicious and we also had  "mom mom's rice pudding."  To be honest, I'm not a rice pudding fan at all, but this dish was so creamy and filled with so many different fruit flavors.  I highly recommend it if you're at all into rice pudding.  Absolute lip-smacking heaven.

Thank you so so much, Amis, for your wonderful food and hospitality.  Exceeded our expectations tri-fold.  Danny and I will be visiting Philly soon again!

I will never order from this chipotle ever again. I ordered off Uber Eats, and they were so late to get the order ready.. took an hour to get the food. I paid extra for chicken and got what felt like a half of a scoop. So frustrated! That service there is horrible. They are lucky that they are getting 1 Star, because they are so bad. I'll stick with my Qdoba from here on out.

After reading many of the reviews, the two of us decided to get hot pot on our first day in Philadelphia. Many choices of broth that's  $3.99 per person per broth. You can get up to three. Then you get to choose your toppings or the meats, seafood, noodles, and vegetables you would like to be put into the hot pot. It's actually a pretty hard decision. 

We went with snowflake beef(so so), shrimp pork balls (very yummy), combination vegetable(came with cabbage, lots of kelp knots, spinach, potato(strange), and mushrooms, and mussels(so so).  Not sure if we 'll try this place out again. It was good bit overpriced for hot pot. We ended up spending about $80 with about 3 beers on the menu. I think I prefer the all you can eat option because the quality wasn't comparable to the price. Service is a bit on the bad side but not the worst I've ever had in an authentic Chinese restaurant.

Oh yeah! Don't forget to make your dipping sauces and don't try to eat one of the Thai chillies.

Tried this after seeing a fb ad for $10 lunch special. Honestly, without the special, I wouldn't have eaten here...the food is just way overpriced for what it is, especially the sushi. There are too many asian/sushi restaurants around here for their prices to be that high. The service was great and that's literally why I'm giving this place stars. The food wasn't bad either, just can get the same thing elsewhere for wayyyy cheaper.

This is a fantastic hotpot spot, with a ton of variety in their selections. The ribs here are absolutely amazing and definitely my favorite protein. All the standard hotpot meats and veggies are present too. 

The sauce bar has a great mix as well, with some homemade garnishes and at least a dozen choices to mix and match. There are also 9 different broths available for your base soup stock. I'll definitely be back again to try all of them out; I haven't even began to scratch the surface of all of the treat combinations here yet.
Wonderful outdoor seating and food options. We especially enjoyed some Austrian wine (grüner Veltliner) and had a great time. Ordering several smaller plates and sharing it all was fun.

Went for Valentine's Day. We got a charred octopus small plate and for entrees ordered the moqueca (fish stew) and one of the V-Day specials (a steak with garlic potatoes and roasted carrots).  

Firstly, the food was DELICIOUS. The octopus in particular was amazing-- I had no idea that octopus could have a soft texture like this one. I thought it always had to be chewy. Honestly, that was probably my favorite bite there (the entrees were good, but that was just stand out). The four stars is because the desert had a weirdly burnt taste. It was a special bread pudding, but neither of us liked it. Very bitter taste. 

The aesthetic was very dark, with a live musician singing French music. I ended up having to wear a blanket because the patio is very cold at night-- but, I kind of expected that! Just keep it in mind before you sit outside.
TERRIBLE TERRIBLE DRIVE THRU. Super slow and delayed worst location ever. They should redo parking lot

We were looking forward to dinner at Coronet, eager to find a quality eatery so close to the Symphony.  But we were bitterly disappointed.

The initial turn off was the room's acoustics.  Although we arrived early to a half full dining room, the room noise had already reached at a pitch that made conversation challenging.  As the room filled, the noise became almost intolerable.  It's not as though there was a loud roudy table causing the elevated noise level.  The reverberating acoustics slowly forces the otherwise quiet diners to speak more loudly which in turn raises the noise level necessitating a still louder conversation.

All is not lost yet.  If the food was exceptional there was the option in a return visit of dining in the patio, away from the interior acoustics.  But disappointment again.  The halibut entree looked appealing to three diners in our party.  All three of our halibut dishes came overcooked and underseasoned.  The sauce, an interesting sounding 'pistachio yuzu emulsion' was bland.  The addition of salt helped.  And the 'glazed celery stalks' and celeriac puree were quite pleasant.  But overall it was a very unsatifying meal for the three of us.  On the other hand, the Beet & Halloumi Salad was enjoyed by the 4th member of our party.

Dessert did not salvage the  evening.  Panna Cotta should be a delicate dessert with a custard-like consistency.  But their Fig Panna Cotta had the consistency of a Greek yogurt with no hint of figs.  The 'figs' come from a few tiny pieces of dried figs lumped on top of the not-very-flavorful 'yogurt'.  A poached pear dessert was also not distinguishing with the pear lacking much flavor beyond the pear.  An order of coffee to accompany dessert was served lukewarm and returned.  By the time the replacement arrived, we were through with the dessert course.

Amid all these disappointments, we must commend the service which was very good.  Jared, our server, was congenial, informative and attentive without being overbearing.  Our complaints were handled politely and efficiently.  Service was the silver lining to a storm cloud of a dinning experience.
Has to be the slowest Chick Fil A I have ever been too! To top it off they removed the Curbside Ordering from their mobile app! I wish there was a different location on my way home from work.

Father's Day surprise was awesome- great cookies, cinnamon buns, pound cake, and mini danish! Love the mini servings especially so that everyone could have a little bit of everything. Service is wonderful and it feels like family here!

Something was definitely amiss when my wife and I went here.  I thought this restaurant was going to hit the mark, but alas it was a miss.  

Ok, enough of the Tom Foolery.  I did not like this restaurant.  

I thought I'd order the salami sampler plate because it was a big night out, and heck what's $16 in the grand scheme of things?  It turns out to be a lot when all the salami plate consists of is a few thin cuts of bologna, liverwurst, and salami.  I'm talking about like an 1/10 of a lb. total on the plate.  It was OK, but not anything to speak highly about.

The oil infused bread was pretty good, but it came in tiny portions.  Ask for three refills throughout dinner, tiny.  No deal breaker here.

Then came the entree, Pasta with Wild Boar Ragu.  Sounds exotic!  Well it, in the words of my wife, "tastes like hamburger helper".  She asked for salt (not at the table and is offered in a small bowl and spoon) which helped add a bit of taste.  

Unimpressed with the appetizer and entree, we saw where this meal was going and decided to head over to Max Brenner for dessert (which was delicious).

P.S.  Not that this affects my quantitative rating at all, since I like to rate based on food and not on the experience, we had 7pm reservations and were told that we needed to wait.  We finally sat down 25 minutes later.  It wasn't the end of the world.  However, it added a sense of urgency to dinner, since we had a finite amount of time left on the parking meter.  

Then, at the end of dinner, the hostess asked for our coat tag, when they hadn't given us one in the first place.  I offered to help find the coats, but she said "actually, I'd rather you didn't" in a curt tone.  For the next few minutes we were treated very poorly & given attitudes by both her and her coworker.  I don't care to go into trying to describe their demeanor, as I am no Hemingway, but let it suffice to say that it was a very un-customer-friendly experience.
This bakery never disappoints me! Custom designed birthday cake that tastes absolutely amazing, only $65!! Thanks Schenk's!

NO MORE CURBSIDE SERVICE? What happened? That was the saving grace to battle the abnormally long wait times at this location. Curbside Service used to be available on the Chick-fil-A app but it has since been removed - while still available everywhere else. This is a real shame and will make me choose the location south even though it is further away. Probably the biggest issue this location has is not its fault... but the way the parking lot is configured slows down everything and makes it difficult for parking or using the drive through. This compounds the longer wait times.
Very disappointed in the grill white chicken combo, just terrible, food was cold not fresh coffee was water down couldn't drink it, traveling doing expediting in the Tampa area.

We don't usually get dessert with dinner and wine, but here, it's a MUST, and I'm talking about the Belgium waffle dessert! They make it fluffy, so it's not as thick and filling as a regular Belgium waffle, but has the same great taste topped with delicious ice cream! 

The menu does not have descriptions, so definitely ask the wait staff about anything you want! Our waitress was extremely knowledgeable and explained several of the appetizers and entrees to us in order to make a decision. The extensive wine list is also in Italian, and I usually drink Napa Valley Cabernets, so the waitress recommended one of the best wines I've ever had! 

They serve a variety of salad, pasta, seafood, and meat entrees along with a large selection of bruschetta, meat, and cheese appetizers. 

Appetizer must: Sal's famous meatballs with tomato covered potato. You get three juicy meatballs with a little potato underneath them, and the flavors were impeccable!

We were looking for pasta and had the ricotta and tonnarelli dishes. Both were outstanding. While other reviews mentioned "generous" portions, I would categorize them as below average for what we usually receive at high-end Italian restaurants. We both finished our plates and could have eaten more, whereas usually I cannot finish an entire pasta entree. This was even after consuming one appetizer, fresh bread (provided to all patrons but with no dipping oil), and our complimentary side (described below).

The service was top notch! Besides our waitress being attentive and knowledgeable with everything, we were offered a complimentary side that we shared while waiting for our meals because the chef was not happy with how the entrees resulted. Therefore, he started over while we enjoyed the side. We greatly appreciated this level of service! 

I'm surprised it's rated $$$ because most entrees were $16-20 a piece minus a few exceptions. We got a bottle of wine, two entrees, one appetizer, and one dessert for $115 plus tip! The ambiance was upscale, yet we saw people wearing anything from t-shirts and flip flops to dressy. 

They have $18 valet that is the best option unless you want to park and walk quite a bit. They had outdoor tables, but we opted for inside as outside seating is on the sidewalk by where everyone arrives, walks by, and valet.

We enjoyed our date night and would definitely go back as we are huge fans of the Vetri restaurants!

I am very particular about pastas and this place never failed me! We had the ricotta and veal tongue as starters and they are heaven! The pastas, there is nothing more to say about them, simply divine. And the services! They just keep getting better. When we ordered the ricotta, they also gave us an extra mousse on the house for the bruschetta. The Jalapeno and almond pesto bucatini was a bit salty at first and they re-made it for us and gave us a plate of fried brussel sprouts while we wait for the pasta to remade! Excellent service and very attentive! Overall great food and great service and very very impressed!! Highly recommend!

Ordered on the app for food to be ready at 8:45. At 9 when the food was finally ready it sat behind the register for 5-10 minutes while team members complain about their day and I am trying to get their attention to give me my order or place on the to go bag rack... then my chips n salsa is missing chips... key ingredient in chips n salsa. Stay away from this location!!!!

By far the worst chik fil a In Tampa. There is always an issue everytime I try and come here. Tonight was the last time. I ordered 4 meals, one was a salad. I got up to the window, waited a minute and watched as all the employees were chit chatting then the girl at the window said she would check on my order another lady with a different colored shirt on, so I'm assuming higher up started talking saying "park the salad order" "just park hylaree" which is me, she was being very rude her customer service was way below standard. So the girl at the window says ok we have to park you we are waiting on your salad. So I asked how long? The other "higher up" lady said it should be two minutes. Ok, have to go park. 5 minutes later I see a girl delivering someone else's order I ask her what the hold up is, tell her my name and how this chik fil a never has service like any others and she apologizes but then tells me how they are low on things. Ok well if they are low on things they should've said that before letting me order and pay for it. A team lead  "Daniel" later comes out with the food and I ask for a refund he goes inside and 5 minutes later comes out with a receipt. No apologies nothing. This chik fil a just likes to waste your time!! They are always "low and out of things". Someone here isn't doing their job!!!

This is an absolutely lovely little restaurant - warm and inviting with delicious food and friendly staff.  Wherever I live, I can only hope that I have a neighborhood place like Amis nearby, I would wear out one of the seats.

As soon as you walk into Amis you'll experience a wave of warmth and hospitality wash over you.  We had a drink at the bar before getting seated.  The bartender greeted us warmly (almost feeling like a regular already) and got me a lovely Negroni Fresco - lighter and less sweet than a regular Negroni it was delightful.  

We got seated and were provided with some delicious warm bread and the menu was explained.  So many good choices. We did Baked Pecorino, Bufala Mozzarella and Spinach Ricotta "Meatballs."  All were exceptional, but the Mozzarella was perfect - light and airy with just enough bite, perfectly complimented by the sweet apple slices and chili oil - so good.

Pork Chop Parmigiana was outstanding.  This was not your Grandma's Pork Chop Parm, it was kind of a hipster deconstructed dish with fresh mozzarella, splashes of delish sauce, and super crispy yet juicy Pork chop.  Terrific.  And Whole Roasted Branzino was so moist and flavorful it turned my wife who usually only eats raw fish into a Branzino lover, no small accomplishment.  

I love the warmth, scale, friendliness, and amazing food at this restaurant.  It was the perfect place for a cool autumn evening and I can't wait to come back.

Ordered a steak bowl with guacamole. Delivered timely but order didn't have steak OR guacamole. Called restaurant 4 times, think someone picked up once and then let the line sit and then hung up. Drove to restaurant and asked what happened and see 4 people working there sitting and laughing. Not one picked up the phone, all I was offered was a new bowl. Not even a sorry or gift card or anything. I expect to be contacted. I have been very loyal chipotle customer and even was an intern for chipotle in tampa during college. This location has consistently messed up delivery orders and cares nothing about the customer. I also expect a refund as it defeated the purpose of delivery I had to drive there to get it fixed. Unacceptable.

Hello yes I know I'm black lol, walking into this establishment all eyes were on me and my 7yo sdaughter... not a cruel evil feel just an awkward "are you sure you're in the right place" look.. after 10 long seconds an older woman asked did I need "help" i wasn't sure if this was strike 1 or 2 at this point. I asked for a menu and to be seated and she just pointed... (that was definitely a strike) the restaurant screamed Chinese store and that's exactly the prices I was looking for. 

I ordered chicken lomein for my daughter,(we both shared it... it was good the noodles seemed to literally soak up all the seasonings perfectly, at first glance you'd think they are dry)

the fried pancake thing everyone else seemed to have(I thought it would be like a scallion pancake... not at all, that was awful) 

a duck soup (which I thought was a pho but they use a different type of noodle still good)

 and pork dumplings(juiciest dumplings I've ever had, fried just right) 

They only took cash so I went across the street to the gift shop... nothing was wrong with the bill it added up just right with 8% tax and I gave them a $5 tip... 

The second time I returned it was a lunch break I remembered it was cash only and only had their magnificent dumplings again can't beat it st $10! Still those awkward looks though.. this time the customer service was much better from the older woman.

Ummmm....I don't think the 'Save my Bakery' advice took. Just bought a small vanilla cake topped with "buttercream" icing. The cake was good. The buttercream tasted like Royal icing...and I have tasted better Royal icings. It was way too sweet with no flavor. The chocolate cupcake was dry with no real chocolate flavor. Tasted like a little Debbie cake. And the chocolate buttercream icing had no flavor at all. The people are very nice. I am a long time Fox-Rock resident. We have several bakeries in the area and I don't seem to want to patronize any of them.

I'm originally from Tucson but have lived in SF for the past 20 plus years. I came back to the original Cushing Street location to find it amazingly restored, complete with a beautifully lit Mexican tile courtyard (traditional blankets with the heat lamps, nice touch.) Do yourself a favor and peek in at the private rooms with the cozy benches and cholla cactus ceilings. The ambience was superb, I loved the attention to detail with the romantic lighting and the (Buffalo School?) seating. And the menu; Seriously, when they refer to Tucson as a UNESCO gastronomy site I think the Coronet would be top of mind. There were solid choices on the menu but they took chances as well. It was exciting to see the ancho bisque next to the grilled octopus with tiny heirloom tomato with chilies. I had a Brazilian seafood stew with anchovies from the Sea of Cortez. Amazing execution with a delicate touch. My dining companion had more traditional choices, but again, perfect execution on the meat with a deft hand on the accoutrements. And there was a tasteful jazz trio playing romantic standards in the corner, (How my Heart Sings!) What an amazing experience that rivals any in SF or Napa.

Seriously Chick Fil A....in Drive thru at 10:22 with a very long line. I'm  finally next to order when it turns 10:30 and I am told that I can no longer order the breakfast I came for??? Really? Brian, the manager, basically said tough luck. May I have suggested that someone could have come out to the line with the mobile order pad used at lunch to give all the customers waiting for breakfast a chance to complete our orders? You've lost a long time customer.

I had dinner here last night with a friend. I ordered the soup of the day (octopus in salmon consomme) ($6), the two hearted ale and cheddar toast happy-hour special ($9), and the seasonal-offering dessert ($11). Everything was terrific: the food, service, atmosphere, even the background music.

The first time I cleaned my plate at a restaurant in a long time. The pork chop was medium well, as requested. The whipped sweet potatoes were light and fluffy. The egg and bacon and parsley brought out the flavor of the pork chop and  the fruits, blackberries and a date enhanced the flavor of the pork chop so well.  This place's atmosphere is beautiful. The old fashion I drank with #4rosesbourbon was amazing. I would come again.... if only Tucson was closer.

I am hoping they do well in this location, I have not seen many incarnations of the Cushing Street location, I can't even count the times of opening and closing.  This time it is exactly the same interior and patio as all the other restaurants, right down to the uncomfortable ice cream parlor chairs on the patio.  We sat inside for a moment and it was super loud, so we found a table outside.  The patio has never lived up to any real potential, it remains again a great space with no clear vision.  I had the happy hour price steamed clams ( clams are way smaller than mussels) and a small bowel of the soup of the day, a piece of bread,  a non-alcoholic hops drink, and split the Tack Room Mouse slice of cake.  Out the door with tax  and tip around $40.00, while the food was not bad, it was not that good for the price.  The service was ok but not great, it took a long time to get water at the table, and the food came out randomly not at the same time .
I think the Coronet left something significant behind in the move from 4th avenue to Cushing, because I really liked it back there, this not so much.  
There are too many good places open now to just be ok, and expensive.

Amazing location, brand new restaurant, yet i have never had a good experience. Incredibly slow service every time. Have been to this location a handful of times to give it time to improve and always an unreasonable wait.

hark to me knave, i hath said thanketh thy f'r thy patronage.  the n'rve of that gent to just standeth th're liketh yond aloof as that gent returns mine own f'rm of payment.  i believeth t is thy duty to sayeth "my pleasure".  4 shilling f'r days fusty chicken and a did fry potato, the n'rve of t all.  driveth home in silence, wast t those nuggos i shouldst has't gotten? dont rememb'r yond those streetlights fusty one with bags ov'r those folk new ones directeth traffic on the second, receiveth wh're thee wanteth to beest at which hour t lets thee.  and the n'rve of yond knave.  i hadst did thank thee and i am to nay longeth'r expecteth thy kindness once the food hast been given f'r its owneth means to englut.  i sitteth h're eating in mine own owneth senseth of ruin'd identity.  wast t a pleasure to s'rve me? bland and ineffectual the days fusty chicken is, down to liketh lasteth piece of bread which f'rms a p'rtion of its whole but in itself is nay longeth'r a sandwich.  finish t whole into the abyss of pleasure did bury und'rneath the sup'rficial principles of humility yond i des'rve, yond i hest as univ'rsal law.  2 shilling f'r days fusty chicken, the n'rve

After many recommendations to this place, we finally ventured to this place since we were craving Italian food and celebrating a birthday. We were nestled between two other tables. Tight squeeze, so not a place to dish out your secrets. Despite the frigid weather, there were many diners to keep this lively place buzzing!

The wine list was very impressive, and equally very delicious. I tried the Pinot Noir and sadly, I forgot the name of the other one. The menu had much to offer, but we settled on three appetizers and two pastas: octopus, swordfish meatballs, sweetbreads, beef bolognese rigatoni, and the soppressini with wild boar and pears! However, I do want to add that their olive oil-infused bread was so soft and unique bread basket, different than all the other Italian restaurants we've tried. Our appetizers surprisingly came out all at once and shortly after we ordered. I've never tried sweetbreads, so I got out of my comfort zone, and found to be quite tasty. Dusted with almond powder, topped with fennel, and a sweet jam that pulled this appetizer together! Octopus was also lovely and not chewy, but standard to other octopus dishes I've had. Swordfish meatballs! Very nice flavor, and the polenta made it not boring. I'd order this again! Three appetizers for the win!

And then we waited.

And waited.

And waited.

The wait between appetizers and entrees was quite long, but when they finally arrived, we were both disappointed. His beef bolognese had little bits of meat, and mine just had a tad bit more. Thought there would be more meat for both of the dishes. Nevertheless, the portion was the right size, and the pasta did taste great despite it being less meaty. 

Two wines, three apps, two pastas totaled to be about $100 for two. Not bad at all!

Despite the long wait, the meal itself was pretty good and on par to the other Vetri restaurants. I'd come again to explore the other options on the menu.

Amazing meal with amazing service to match. Restaurant was packed and our server managed to make us feel like we were her only table. And the food....oh the food, how incredible!!! From delectable crumbly pecorino cheeses to hearty plates of pastas and finally to our meats, mine, a deliciousy glazed pork chop, his a citrus tuna with fennel pasta...I will definitely be going back! Not a good atmosphere for a romantic dinner, very open layout, so it tends to get rather loud...

The food was fabulous.  We got there early for happy hour and started with green bean/ potatoes salad. We had the sardines too. Then we followed with grilled lamb it was fantastic. 
The service was very slow which was offset by live music that was worth waiting for.
The ambiance was nice a European feel

This is the worst Chick-Fil-A in the area which is a shame because it is the closest to my house.  Maybe I'm just partial to the other ones in Tampa, I'm not sure.

The Food: Every Chick-Fil-A tastes the same.

The Service: Absolutely NOT up to par with other Chick-Fil-A's I've visited. I sat there and watched the person behind the counter double charge a customer during rush hour in the drive thru. On top of having to hold everyone up to sort out the issue, the manager seemed unfazed and completely unapologetic to the customer. There was no apology from the manager (only the worker) and no coupon on them for messing up or anything. Definitely not what I would expect from a Chick-Fil-A.

The Parking: Is horrendous and horribly designed. Whoever designed that parking lot did a terrible job. It isn't designed for the traffic from the drive thru to get out effectively and efficiently without running into the people coming off of Dale Mabry. 

If I'm home and want something to eat I'll more than likely still eat here however if I am already out I will likely stop at another Chick-Fil-A instead of coming here. I just can't get past the service and the poorly designed parking lot.

My friend and I came here for brunch last Sunday not really knowing what to expect. You can get the buffet for $20 or order off of the menu so we opted for the buffet and bottomless mimosas. All together our total was about $30 which isn't bad at all.

I am writing this review keeping in mind that they just opened up so here goes:

THE LOCATION:
You really can't beat this location as it's on S. Howard close to Kennedy. I also really appreciated how they have their own parking lot as we all know how parking in SOHO can be a nightmare. The restaurant itself is an open kitchen concept which seems and looks cool. I do have to wonder how this will work in the summer and if that will make the restaurant extremely hot. 

THE SERVICE:
We had the most adorable waitress and since we sat outside by the bar the bartender was also checking on us to make sure that we were ok. We never had to really ask for refills on our mimosas. One of the two ladies would usually refill them for us which was appreciated. I will say that since the restaurant is new I picked up on some discrepancies when asking questions about the restaurant and their offerings. Maybe that will change once they are open a while.

THE FOOD:
For a buffet, I didn't have any complaints. They had a good variety of food choices from traditional brunch offerings like chicken and waffles to sweet chili chicken wings to sushi. We tried literally a little bit of everything and there wasn't anything that we didn't necessarily like. Everything was tasty. I did get a glance at the menu and it definitely looks like the brunch buffet offerings aren't on the normal menu so I do want to come back for lunch or dinner one day.

All in all it was a positive experience and I will most likely return at least for brunch.
This place is horrible, disorganized, never got what I ordered.  Waited an hour and they said it could take up to two more, what?  Don't go here, go somewhere reputable
They always forget the sauce and aren't that polite here. Traffic is also horrible getting in here.

Let's be clear, I love chik fil a--JUST NOT STADIUM CHIK FIL A in Tampa, FL. I live closest to this one BUT I will drive past it now just to go to Int'l mall or the one further down in South Tampa. Stadium chik fil a always gets something WRONG, traffic getting in and out is a MESS, and their managers DON'T CARE--they asked for my email and never even reached out to me.  The last time I was there, instead of getting a sandwich meal they put 3 fruit bowls in my bag, NOT EVEN CLOSE to what I ordered. They don't answer their phones and the waffle fries here are always broken stale pieces--THIS LOCATION MUST BE THE IGNORED MIDDLE CHILD OF ALL CHIK FIL A'S...don't waste your time or money here--go the little bit of way to another one!!!

Amis is a very well respected Philly foodie destination and for good reason.  Ate there in December and I'm looking forward to a return trip in the near future.  Staff was very attentive and friendly (no issue with moving our table in the middle of the dining room over to one by the window, also allowed us to pull up a fifth chair when a colleague came to join for post dinner cocktails).  Pretty nondescript, chill ambiance and loved that the kitchen is open to the dining room.

For food, shared the mako shark bruschetta with the table, WOW!  Perfect marriage of taste with the sea and the grill combining for probably the best take on bruschetta I can remember eating.  For my entree decided to get something I would normally not order because I felt like a switch from my normal fish routine and I just had a steak at Ocean Prime, so ordered the Pork Chop with polenta.  I was very pleased with my choice, excellent cut of meat, very juicy with notable taste.  Not much polenta, but what was there was creamy and delicious.

This is one of the coolest new spots in SOHO/South Howard! It has an open concept that incorporates an outside bar and an open dining room. The decor is top notch with the coolest lighting fixtures. I had a sexy roll and my friend has two tacos. I've been told their bowls are pretty good as well. This was my first visit but it will not be my last. The roll was delicious and the atmosphere was awesome. I will look forward to visiting for brunch on Sunday, I've heard they have a live DJ!

My dad stopped in and ordered a Turkey for thanksgiving. It's a family tradition. When he came to pick up the turkey the day before Thanksgiving, they told him they never got any turkeys in. No phone call, nothing. Luckily we were able to stop and get one at Boston Market but it wasn't the same. Never going back to this location.

One of the managers called me back and apologized--she told me why things were perhaps a bit in disarray. She offered me a credit for my incorrect meals and upon return they did get it right! Also, they have finally improved their waffle fries, they actually look like waffles and not burnt ends and pieces! I appreciate the sincere response and will stop by if I am close-by.

Preety bad experience. I wss expecting from this company called Chick fill a!!! I dont know why the called your name when the order is "ready" well, thats what I assumed! For a carry-out! After a 30 mins drive, I got home and half of my order is missing (sure, I should it checked it)  good job! (Are these the people who wants $15 min wage that cannot complete an order???) Called the supervisor on duty and cannot do anything! Her best answer was to go back (30 mins drive (1 hr total)) and get the remaining items SMH!!! then she hang on me because she cant do anything else! I called back 3 more times and she would not pick up the phone and then last time I called she lifted the phone and put it right back down! Is this what the BIG CHICK-FILL-A us about??? I tried to called later from a different phone number and the other employee would not give me her name! So I would called her the UNKOWN SUP!!! Hope Corporate reads this and they can improve your customer service

Starting with cocktails at the bar, seemed to be the way to start the evening, they were running behind with reservations.  Not a problem, knowing that guest that linger when having a great time that can happen.  Cocktails were put together well and would recommend the New York Sour, Rye with a splash of red wine to finish it off.  Once seated, menus were dropped quickly and the server introduced himself and shared the specials.  One of the guests at my table recognized quickly that the server was "in the weeds."  Not a problem again for us, we were out to have a good time and cocktails would keep us happy.  After coming over three times, we got the idea that the waiter wanted that order.   Asked for recommendations for appetizers, which he gave us, then the problems started, when ordering entrees, he told us that two of us were out of luck, they were no longer serving that item this evening.  Then he stood and waited while two of us had to find another entree.  Once we ordered the appetizers showed up quickly, delicious except for the meatball app. which was raw in all put one of the meatballs.  Gentleman brought over the wine we ordered and we showed him the raw meatballs. His response was classic, I don't know what the fudge I am saying.  "They are pink inside because of the pink salt we use."  Jaws dropped, at the table, there were folks that are great cooks and one that owned a restaurant. The raw meatballs were taken away, and right as the entrees were close to being delivered, a properly cooked meatball app was dropped on the table, without a word.  Entrees were quickly dropped at the table and we quickly went into sharing.  Overall entrees were good, some a bit confusing as to the execution and a couple extremely small for the price, but overall, not bad. As folks finished an entree, someone swooped in and grabbed a plate as if it was closing time.  This continued right up to the presentation of the check. The credit card  was given and the receipt was dropped off with the credit card. Without checking a few minutes later the waiter grabbed the credit card holder and disappeared.  Don't know about you but when I have paid with a credit card that holder usually stays until the guests leave.  It continued, every once in a while someone would swoop down to the table and grab what they could to clean if off.....and honestly give us the impression it was time to leave, though there was still wine on the table. We finally got the idea and got up to leave, thinking they needed the table, only to find the place 3/4 empty.  Food, OK, Service, Poor.

We were thrilled to see Coronet posted a new takeout menu during the Covid takeout/delivery only orders. This is one of the best takeout menus we've enjoyed thus far...why? Because it's a heat and serve menu. So, the meal  is cooked but light refrigerated so you are prompted to warm it back up in the oven at 350 degrees. We did just that and the food was still perfect and super flavorful. You can enjoy 20% off with curbside pickup too! The entrees each come with a choice of salad. We didn't expect such large portions so we had left over the next day! We ordered the Sirloin with chimichurri sauce and asparagus. The pork tenderloin with honey chile rub and sweet potatoes. We chose the lentil salad and the freekeh cashew salad with our entrees. We also added the mediterranean potatoes. We didn't really need them but they were super yummy. I love this menu because it's delicious and there's something for everyone (carnivores, vegetarians, vegan). The ordering process was super easy and pick up was even easier. The food was ready at the time they said it would be ready. We'll order from Coronet again for sure!

DO NOT ORDER takeout from this location. I ordered and paid for 2 kids meals and a quesadilla. When I got home they had ONE KIDS meal in the bag and that's it. 

When I arrived at the restaurant to pick up the food, it was bagged up and tied so tightly. There's no way I could have looked through it without causing a big scene and having to have an employee repack everything. I trusted they had all our food in the bag and left. 

Big mistake!  This is the second time this has happened to us from the same location. I paid for 3 meals and got 1.  So frustrating.

I'm still dreaming about this place.  I came here with my sister, brother in law, and boyfriend to carb load before a race.  Best.  Decision. Ever.  We started with the marinated olives, and then sampled the squid salad, old school meatballs, fried cauliflower, bucatini with jalapeno and almond pesto, chicken al mattone (perfectly cooked), one of the pasta specials for the evening- a chicken ragu pasta, and finished with a chocolate semifreddo and the tartufo al bacio.  Everything was amazing, amazing, amazing.  The wine list was also fabulous, and yes, even before our run the next day, we couldn't help but sample several of the selections (if you enjoy a very dry wine, the Petra Zingari is to die for, but my favorite paired with the meal was the Casolare Rosso).  The highlights of the meal for me were the squid salad and the jalapeno bucatini (surprisingly spicier than I anticipated!)  The best part? The price!  I was actually amazed at the final bill- expecting the meal to be far more expensive than it was. I would love to come back here the next time I'm in Philly, but my guess is that the wait for a reserve is long!

This is the second time we have used champion pools and spas for parts and service. First time they did not carry a simple pool filter gasket that I bought up the street from there competition. The second time they came out to work on my older pool spa heater. They claimed it needed a new electrical part which they ordered and installed. After installation of new part they claimed that new part still didn't fix it and I should just replace the heater with a new 2,500 unit. Ya right!! What a bunch of BS!! 

Here is where it gets good! I had a heating and air conditioning friend come look at the unit and he discovered the part was wired completely incorrectly and they had also bypassed a built in safety fuse. These guys are hacks! They are a joke! Bonus!!!! They left there dirty rubber gloves on the ground near my unit which blew into my pool!! Stay away!!! They are small time! Order your parts online and go to Leslie's pool supply in Rita Ranch for quality service!

Good Evening,

I just want to say I had a wonderful time at your restaurant and the food was absolutely delicious. This was my 1st time eating at your restaurant and I must say I will return. When I made the reservation I just mentioned in passing it was my mother's birthday.  Can I just tell you when we walked in the hostess greeted us warmly and said Happy Birthday, my waitress was WONDERFUL, the maitre D was absolutely AMAZING and everything was just impeccable. I'm not sure how you train your staff but whatever you do it's absolutely amazing. Each and every person met every need we had and we never had to ask for anything. There are so many restaurants  someone can choose from just in a 5 block radius but I must say your service was absolutely 5 star. One thing my mother said when we left your restaurant and it was so key, she said it was as if they were expecting us. Not that we were just another reservation or even just people who were going to sit at a table but truly you wanted us and everyone who walked in your restaurant to have a great experience.  From the linen to even how the glasses shined. It truly shows that you have an amazing staff. Thank you for making my mother's 68th birthday one to remember!

Usually pretty fast service but not genuine service. Went to grab a fountain drink , nothing but carbonated water ( no problem). Let the cashier know and was barely acknowledged. He said they would take care of it, 10 minutes later and being seen by atleast 3 employees waiting, nothing. I work on base and have limited time so decided to leave with no drink than  bring up the issue again and be ignored.

I patronize Chick-fil-A's throughout the state of Florida in my travels. This Chick-fil-A on North Dale Mabry by the stadium in Tampa has the absolute worst customer service Of any Chic-Fil-A I have ever been at.

The employees do not know the first thing about customer service. The service is horrible. When they make a mistake they refuse to take responsibility and correct the mistake. They refused to identify who the owner is and they refused to give you a telephone number where you can file a complaint regarding any issues at the restaurant.

The owner of the restaurant is Carlos Brito. After speaking with Mr. Brito I can understand why his employees act the way they do. He himself does not know the meaning of customer service. I obtained Mr. Brito email and telephone number. . I emailed him and asked him to call me to discuss my experience at his restaurant. He replied by saying I had the wrong Carlos Brito in the email. I then proceeded to contact him on his personal cell phone he didn't give a hoot about my experience. He was only concerned how I had gotten his phone number. He spoke over over me, argued with me, lectured me on how I got his number. He did everything except show a concern or desire to hear my experience at his restaurant. 

Mr. Brito claims to be this Christian protestant former pastor but believe me his Christian values are as fake as the president he currently worships.

The night of my unpleasant experience at this restaurant I went up the street to the Chick-fil-A at South Dale Mabry. This location is runs  like a true Chick-fil-A, unbelievable customer service and satisfaction, excellent food quality and true customer loyalty. I can say the same thing about the one in Brandon. While I was at the South Dale Maybry location one of the customers in line waiting to pick up an order expressed the same sentiments that I did about Mr. Brito and the lack of customer service at his location. One of the employees remarked that they hear these same sentiments on a regular basis.

Mr. Carlos Brito needs to be given a refresher course on customer relations 101. He needs to be retrained by Corporate Chic Fil A on how a Chic Fil A franchise should be operated. He rude and unapologetic demeanor is well reflected in several of his employees

I had the best experience at Schenk's Family Bakery! they are so great to work with and very patient. They spent time with me so I could stay within my budget. I wanted a Game of thrones themed cake for my husbands 30th, the results exceeded my expectations. Not only did the cake look amazing but it tasted delicious! Thank you and I can't wait to order again!
Laura was very helpful and nice! She helped us fix our order at the payment station and was happy to help. Great customer service (:
Winnie is a great stylist at Tim's Salon! She has helped my hair to grow in very healthy, and the prices are reasonable.

Rather I'm going in or sitting in line; this location has yet to fail me. Line could be wrapped around the parking lot and you would still be out in twenty minutes!  Food is great. People are great! Service is great!
I love me some chic fil a. The chicken of course is amazing. The unlimited amount of dipping sauces are my favorite. And the cookies are better than mom's homemade. No offense ma.

BEST BUY FURNITURE EXPERIENCE WAS THE BEST!! From the ordering all the way through delivery was the best experience,  very highly recommend it!

I ordered a Beautiful trundle sofa bed for my guests,  when I came to the store everyone treated me kindly and were very helpful.  They warned me in advance regarding Covid delivery from the manufacture but of course I wanted that piece and no other.... The delivery arrived much earlier then promised which I appreciate greatly.. The delivery men were very respectful they were on time,  Assembled the sofa bed and took the trash with them.
IM DEFINITELY GOING BACK FOR LIVING ROOM FURNITURE and I can't wait!

Awful management here.  Consistently gets customer orders wrong.  Never provides any sauce or a fork for breakfast bowls.  I'm surprised that corporate hasn't shut this location down as it's entirely inconsistent with their brand and the usual good experience you get at nearly every other location.  I've given this location a second and third chance and it didn't get any better.  Don't go here.

I had some reservations about coming here because of the UO takeover, but I was pleasantly surprised.

We started off with an Amis punch and a beer (I ordered the Amis punch). It was refreshing, not too sweet, and very drinkable. Aperol reminds me of Campari, so I knew what I was in for, but if you're not used to Italian aperitifs you may find the drink slightly bitter.

The house-made ricotta, grilled squid with artichokes, and Sal's meatballs were our appetizers. We shared everything, and loved it all. Contrary to other reviews, I didn't find that any of the dishes were over salted. The grilled squid was cooked perfectly, and the housemade ricotta was deliciously creamy. The meatballs were perfectly executed, and I felt that the potatoes were a great addition to the tomato sauce.

We ordered the bucatini with jalapenos and almond pesto as well as the salmon with grilled ramps for our shared mains. The salmon was PHENOMENAL and perfectly cooked, with a crispy skin that was to die for. We'd never tried ramps before, and I'm glad that we chose this dish because I will actively seek out dishes with ramps in the future. Almost like a grilled spring onion, they were deliciously smoky and garlicky and pungent yet extremely fresh. I was surprised at the size of the bucatini- it was definitely a larger portion than I thought. The pastas are great dishes to share! By the time I sampled the pasta, I was getting really full and I wasn't able to appreciate the nuanced flavors as much as I would have liked, but the texture was amazing with the crunchy bits of almonds.

I would have liked to try some of the crab specials that were featured, but my husband isn't overly fond of seafood so the shared salmon was a nice compromise. Pay attention to the evening's specials- they all sounded incredible.

The service was also amazing- servers share tables and waitstaff works cohesively to provide exceptional service... our main server even remembered my name from our reservation when she asked if I'd like another drink!

I recommend ordering 2-3 tasting plates and 2 mains to share if you come with a dining partner. It was the perfect amount of food, though we were a little too stuffed to sample the delicious looking desserts. I'll definitely return to sample more dishes.

Just had to add a short note about brunch at Amis.  Terrific!  Would have rated a 5 star if it wasn't so noisy. I had the omelet parmesan with a side of bacon, and we all shared the bread basket. Delicious!  And I didn't need to eat anything more the rest of the day. Can't wait to go back.

Cyndy's Bottom Line:  High expectations low execution. 
Between 2.5 and 3 stars.
