Excited to dine at Amis only to be disappointed with the food. We were phoned to confirm our reservation a few days ahead then phoned again enroute to the restaurant.  The front of the house is on their game to keep up with reservations. 

We were seated in front of the kitchen and you notice the activity and the plates going by.  Then you discover the music and how loud it is playing.  Is that the trend in dining or I'm I just a traditionalist and would like to enjoy the food and have a conversation when dining out.  

This is what we drank/ate:
I ordered a prosecco which was served in a white wine glass.  That was the first star lost.

*Complimentary focaccia bread.
The bread was very good and tasty but there were pieces that were burnt.  2nd star lost.

*Swordfish meatballs with creamy polenta with pine nuts.
Excellently prepared meatballs so flavorful and moist.  The polenta very creamy with pine nuts.  

*Mortadella with hazelnut honey
Texture is a bit rubbery, sparse amounts of pistachio.

*Cacio e Pepe
The black peppercorns were too coarse and did not compliment the dish.   I avoided eating the pepper because it was overpowering the pasta.  The pasta was ok and served al dente.  The cheese was light handed and the sauce runny and did not bind to the pasta.  
3rd star lost.  

*Pork chop Parmesan
The pork chop crust was overcooked but at least it was still tender.  Nothing exciting.  The tomato sauce was bland and tasteless.  Hubby was bored with it.
Another star lost.  :(

*Lemon cookies
The cookies were complimentary and especially good.

Dirty. Not at all up to the Chick-fil-A name. I'm not a Chick-fil-A groupie like the rest of the planet but honestly, this place is dirty!

Upon our visit: Bathroom sink didn't work, smashed sauces on the floor throughout, food under the tables throughout. Paper products on the seats and floor. 

Yet both drive through lines are full and there were 6 people in front of us inside to order.  Simply amazing. Maybe its because the employees say, "welcome to Chick-fil-A, How may I serve you?" while McDonalds down the road says, "Yo, what do you want?" 

Still, overpriced chicken and dirty facility means no more for me.

I love chipotle, but this location is really dirty. Concerning in general, but especially considering there is a pandemic, yikes! The floors and tables were dirty and the food didn't look fresh, whoever is running the place needs to better direct their staff and hold better sanitation standards.

First of all, it had plenty of outdoor seating. We had reservations and were quickly seated. The staff was great and appreciative of our presence. The food was served family style which gave us an opportunity to try many of the delicious appetizers and main dishes. This was our first time visiting and we will be making a return real soon.

Tried the carry out reheat thing and it was a big success. We got the pork and the steak and both were great. They heated up nice and slow at 275 degree oven and didn't overcook. The pork in particular was super tender and delicious. Easy contactless pickup in 15 minutes and enough food to be lunch the next day too.

So disappointed in this place. My husband ordered online and had a pick-up time of 10:45. When he got there, they hadn't even started making our food. 15 minutes later, when our food is finally ready, they say they have to make the salad dressing still, which will take another 5 minutes... Seriously 20 minutes late getting one burrito and one salad ready? And every time we go, we have to make sure they put salad dressing in their because they are so cheap that they never do! 
Awful customer service! We won't be going back to this location.

My most favorite coffee shop near USF. My favorite drink to order is the honey bear latte. The staff is always so nice. This location is less busy than the one on 42nd, too. Either one serves great coffee, though!

No point in doing curbside ordering. The drive thru will cycle ten times over before you ever get your food. Once you type in your space number, expect at least another 20min before you get your order...even if the drive thru is dead.

A lovely dinner by another spawn of the Vetri collection.  I've eaten at Vetri before and absolutely was blown away by the food.  However, I've been curious about their larger and more relaxed option, Amis, and finally had the joy of dining here tonight.
Great service. Wonderful food. Impressive wine and cocktails.  Nothing to shake your finger at here!  Had the arancini (SO GOOD) & beet salad to share, and then the rigatoni with black pepper sausage special (perfect preparation and lots of flavor, but not too heavy),  and pork shank (which was HUGE, but just as the server said...so tender that it feel right off the bone).  My client has an aversion to meat on the bone, but LOVED this dish and it didn't bother them one bit!  
Definitely will try to return and putting it in my arsenal for client go-to places!
Looking forward to coming back to try desserts!!! The belgian waffle with nutella looked INCREDIBLE.

My husband and I went to Amis last night and sat at the kitchen bar. Our first time here and definitely not our last.  A great choice. Put your phone down and watch the orchestrated chaos- a great/fun kitchen to watch. The food they put out was incredibly flavorful, well seasoned and cooked to perfection. 
What we ate: Salmon crudo with fresh julienned beets (amazing-highly recommend)
Baked Pecorino with almond honey (very good, sweet, would have had as a dessert with tart apple slices)
Swordfish meatballs (go for it, trust me you'll love them, maybe even more than the traditional meatball)
Sams- traditional meatball ( a very good meatball- looking for a little more crispness to the outside)
Casarecce  with a light and spicy san marzano tomato sauce with salmon and toasted bread crumbs (a special that night and delish!)
Bucatini with jalapeno and almond pesto (perfect amount of heat)
Spring pea Tortelli with lamb ragu and mint


Overall a great dining experience.
We'll be back!

This is as good as it gets.... I think everybody in their Lifetime should experience this Heavenly massage. Zona was simply awesome.
The Living Social Deal really helped...looking forward to some more of those deals!!
Wow this place was amazing! From start to finish! We enjoyed the galette, gravlax toast and fernet cafe. It was all delicious and the staff was really friendly and nice.

This restaurant tries, but misses the mark at this price point in Tucson. Recent visit for an early seating (5:30) on a weeknight.  Venue is classic Old Pueblo, but it's tight and LOUD when the live music plays. Service was efficient, but seemingly intent on turning the table. Only one cocktail was ordered pre-dinner - a fine Manhattan up, but properly chilled drink was served in a room temp glass - a miss off the bat. The cheese platter app was uninspired with stale crackers. The server pressed for entree orders and they arrived in record speed.  My pork chop was a B at best. My dining companions' pasta and vegan entrees rated the same. Nobody felt the meal was worthy of the tab.  Given the speed of service - more worthy of In-n-Out than fine dining  - and the looks from the service staff, we turned the table and finished our conversation on the sidewalk.  Highly doubtful we'll feel a need to return.

Terrible Chick-fil-A! They have forgotten items in my order multiple times after waiting in the drive thru for 30+ minutes. I've had to leave the line a few times because of how long it is taking. They almost always mess something up. This location is definitely not the usual Chick-fil-A experience. If I didn't work right by here, I probably would never go.

I was very happy that The Coronet had reopened. I went this morning to get breakfast around 8:30. I came with my wife and 1 year old daughter. We were greeted very unpleasantly and not welcoming. We tired to brush it off but after trying to order the lady told us our daughter couldn't come inside that only one of us could order. It was about 50 degrees or colder and when we told the lady we would leave because it was to cold for us she rudely said she could have turned on the warmers.

Ugh, rude. I would never come back here. Their doors were open, so we walked in. An employee yelled, "OUR STORE ISN'T OPEN YET". Like dang, you couldn't say good morning first and then politely tell us to come back in? We waited in the car a few minutes past their "opening" time and looked around. As we started to get towards the middle of the store, we were asked to stop because the lights in the back were not turned on yet. Not our problem that YOUR employees are LATE. Even if the customer service was polite, I wouldn't have purchased any furniture. In my personal opinion, the furniture looks like it would be used in music videos and the very back was not clean. Highly disappointed because I have a few friends and family members who have purchased great couches from Best Buy at other locations.
Absolutely the worst chipotle in Tampa bay. Been going for months because it's right next to my house and nobody they hire can roll a burrito correctly. Food always tastes different every time.

I love love love love chic fil a, it is my favorite fast food restaurant. This location, the stadium location by Raymond James should be shut down. It's the worst chic fil a I have ever seen, the employees are often underwhelmed to serve you, and you'll probably get into a car accident trying to get around the line to enter a restaurant. This is easily the worst designed chic fil a I have ever seen. When they see how it functions at capacity, they should be embarrassed.

This is the worst chick fil a I've ever been to. In my life. I've only been twice but on the first occasion my food took 20 minutes to be ready after I had already went through the drive through and was told to wait in curbside. The second time they gave me a teaspoon of chicken on a regular sized salad. Just close at this point because you guys are tarnishing the whole brand.

Ordered on the app & when I arrived at my pick up time I waited another 30 minutes to be handed my food. Not busy inside, food was cold, & noticed my order was wrong after I got home. If this was the first time I would understand but this has happened multiple times. Not going back.

Well this place was a first for me. It was very nice, but not quite my style. Great for a romantic dinner type of place. Very nicely decorated and dimly lit. Nice live music in the background. What really stood out about it was the food. These meals were definitely prepared by professional chefs. I had the pork chop which was cooked to perfection. Some tobacco cream sauce on the side and honey with a little piece of honey comb on top of the pork chop. It was delicious! This place is definitely a good choice when the time calls for it. Not my regular type of restaurant, but I am very happy that I was able to experience it.

Had an awesome NYE / belated birthday dinner for my boyfriend here. This is how you do Italian food! We ordered swordfish meatballs on a bed of polenta and the almond dusted sweetbreads with fennel marmalade to start. All were delicious, highly recommend both. For our entree we split the fettuccine with duck bolognese and the roasted lamb shoulder. I have been dreaming about the fettuccine since! The pasta is super fresh, hand made, and so delicate. The lamb was crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. For dessert, we had the tartufo as a birthday dessert. Rich and decadent chocolate with hazelnut. The space feels like a trattoria, energetic with delicious smells coming from the kitchen. The lighting is soft and perfect for a date. Can't wait to come back again!

Whatever you do, do NOT let them paint your pool.  Within a few months paint started cracking and of course they blamed it on water conditions...which happened to be perfect since the refill.  All my research indicates poor prep.  Thankfully we did not pay for a repair in the spring because now the pool is peeling in several spots.  It's total redo time...again and several 1000's down the drain for nothing.

I've had a couple of items from Schenk's over the years and they've all tasted good.  The pound cake is a little dry for my taste but the icing is delish!  The strawberry Shortcake is much better than their standard pound cake.  I'll have to venture in again soon to try some of their other menu items.

This Moe's pales in comparison to the one further up north on Dale Mabry. I ate here on a weeknight and it was after the dinner rush. There was no one in the restaurant really, but there were tons of tables dirty and messy. The manager was at the end of the line talking to several people in a group. The group was loud an annoying...also everyone who was buying food had to dance around their oblivious group. A wee bit annoying given the fact that place could've been much cleaner.

The Coca-Cola Freestyle fountain they have there is awesome and has over 100 combinations of Coke products. You want some Coke Zero Vanilla and some Grape Fanta...together in one cup? No problem! This does cause a problem however...not everyone knows how to use it, or they take a ton of time figuring out what they're going to get. Mind you there is ONE HOLE the drinks come out of. So, you're at the mercy of the person in front of you. It reminds me of when you're standing behind a CLUELESS person at the ATM. All-in-all it's very cool but it's also a kid magnet.

This Moe's left me wanting for more. I got the Chicken Bowl and it was just OK. The chicken was barely warm. They asked me if I wanted chips. I did, and I got around 11 of them. Pathetic.

I'll probably eat at Moe's again, but it won't be at this one. If I'm eating this type of food in South Tampa - It'll be from Chipotle.

In need of a massage to ease my muscle pain, I searched for spas in Tucson. That's when I came across Treehouse. Never experienced Thai massages before, I wasn't sure what to expect. But Jason who answered the phone was very helpful, he explained the different styles of massages to me and what I needed to bring.

Unlike other spas with individual massage rooms, Treehouse has a big open massage room with padded floor mats. The place was very clean and very "Thai", with the bamboo curtain and bamboo floor mats. 

I went to the herbal steamroom first. It was a single person steamroom. The room was big enough for you to sit, but the smell of the herb and the steam itself were so soothing and relaxing that I didn't want to come out after the 15 minutes. 

Jason was my masseuse, he was very attentive and brought me cold water. The massage itself was so heavenly! It's basically getting Yoga done to you. So all you need to do was sit back and relax. I had some muscle pain from moving and exercise, but I can't handle the deep tissue or sports massages that are usually offered at regular spas. I often become more sore than when i went in, so I always asked for Swedish even though I needed more pressure than that. The Thai massage gave me exactly what I needed without hurting me, it helped me stretch out my sore muscle while relaxing me. I felt rejuvenated. 

I had such a great experience there I will go back again on a regular basis. I highly recommend this place to everyone!

I realized I have written many reviews but have never written a review on my favorite bakery. This bakery is a neighborhood gem!! The counter staff are always pleasant and their baker is very talented, no matter what custom cake I ask for they always manage to create exactly what I want. From my wedding, many many birthday's, to my husband's retirement cakes. Not only eye catching but delicious, I don't know about you but the cake is always the focal point & centerpiece at all of my parties. Schenk's does not disappoint, I usually get yellow cake with lemon but I have had yellow cake with other flavors and their Black Forrest with cherry filling as well pound cake with butter cream filling. Look at some of the cakes they have done for me, they are not only works of art they are also delicious.

The WORST chic fil a.  If I could give zero stars I would. Went to this location and they refused to serve me. Spoke to the manager and she offered an apology but that was it. No service no nothing. Do not Reccomend

Wow, what can I say about this restaurant. Simply that it's amazing. Everything about this restaurant from the food to the service was an incredible experience. It was everything I hope for and some more. This is a truly a wonderful Italian restaurant. Our waiter was great, since this was our first time he explained everything. The way he said everything he did it with great detail. The food was delicious, thank you so much to the Chef. We ordered a lot but my favorite had to be the veal tongue, the cacio e pepe and the butterscotch ice cream. Wow the flavor and the love that is in the food is unbelievable. I cannot wait to go back. This restaurant was a real pleasure. I will go back.
Great pastries! I love their italian cookies and canolis!

Ordered my food, used PayPal to pay.  Got confirmation from PayPal that the money was authorized, but got no text from Chick-Fil-A that my order was received. Called the store at least 8 times, always told to leave a message.  If you don't have time to answer the phone as a business, you're not checking messages "regularly" as you claim.

Called "Chick-Fil-A Cares" (hahaha).  On hold first time for a long time.  At least the guy apologized and said he would reach out to the store and have them contact me very quickly.  Over 30 minutes later, PayPal still showing my money as out the door, and no contact from Stadium store.  Called the store again several times - you guessed it - no answer.  Called "Chick-Fil-A Cares" (hahaha) again, got a woman who just kept repeating "We ask that you give them 3 business days to respond."  Asked for supervisor to see if they could at least refund the PayPal money asap.  Nope.  Gotta deal with the store and they have three days to get back to me.  

What?

You have my money for the order, your delivery fee, the tip for the driver.  I have no food, and you want me to wait 3 days to talk to someone?  I literally just wanted them to call me back so I could tell them what the order was so they could deliver it.  I won't need it in 3 days.  I have other plans for Thanksgiving.  

tl:dr  Ordered, they took my money through PayPal, store apparently never received order, won't answer phone, Chick-Fil-A Cares doesn't actually care, they're keeping my money and asking me to wait 3 days for someone to call me back.  

To paraphrase a Seinfeld character, "No more orders from me!"  See ya CFA, you just lost a LONG time customer.  No more platters for celebrations with my students when we get over this pandemic, no more platters for potlucks, and no more Saturday afternoons after shopping.  Your customer service is HORRIBLE.

We were refused service. Walked in at 6:40pm on Saturday, August 14th. There were at least 3 groups inside waiting on food, as well as a nice young man running food out to cars. It had been raining for a while that afternoon, but had stopped before 6:30pm. I pulled up the app to order as they didn't let people order inside. I was refused the opportunity to order "due to inclement weather". Since this was obviously not true, I asked the guy running pickup orders out how I could order nuggets and fries for my son. He asked a manager, who refused to speak to me, but rather snapped at the employee "YOU KNOW BETTER THAN TO ASK ME THAT!"

The poor guy suggested I could do drive thru, but after that experience and seeing as though we were walking to the Bucs game, that wasn't an option. 

That's OK, I'm done with this place. They may close on Sunday in honor of Christianity, but their manager's behavior towards me and her employee shows that here it's a blatant lie.

Overall, I thought this was a cool place - industrial chic atmosphere, with extremely diligent servers, and pretty good food.  My husband and I started with Sals meatballs -  very flavorful, but rare in the center (sent them back....came back less rare but still underdone), the baked pecorino with honey and almonds - this was the best dish I had, the buffalo mozzarella with candied pears, and the escarole salad with Granny Smith apples.  I need to say it again, the baked pecorino was amazing.  The cheese was warm, gooey and salty, the honey, sweet, the almonds gave a great crunchy texture and the slightly burnt toast gave a great smokey flavor and more texture.  Before ordering this dish, I thought how good could cheese with honey be?  It's that good.  Everything else only had aspects that were good.  The pears were expertly caramelized and were delicious, and the mozzarella had a great soft creamy texture, but was bland.  The escarole salad was well dressed, but pretty bitter.  I think if the apples were in smaller pieces and were able to be eaten with every bite it would have been better.  I then had the bucatini with jalapeño almond pesto.  This was pretty good as well.  The pasta was a great chewy texture and was perfectly cooked and the pesto was spicy, but not overly and the almonds again gave a great texture and butteriness.  My husband had the skate and was underwhelmed.  We then shared an apple bread pudding.  It was pretty good - light with a nice custardy texture.  But the highlight of this dish was the zabaglione - amazingly light and smooth.
Great food, great staff and great environment.  Definitely worth every penny. Pro tip: make a reservation ahead of time.

Quite honestly, when I heard about Vetri selling out to Urban Outfitters, I was kind of bummed. The food used to be amazing at Amis, and I was scared to go back. However, we snagged a late reservation and were pleasantly surprised. 
The food was exceptional. We ricotta starter was delicious, the almond jalepeno pasta was to die for, and the tiramisu, as usual, was the best I've had in this city. 
The staff was great. The service was on point. The food was fantastic. I'm glad to see nothing much has changed.

Younger female didn't seem to really care about anyone walking in the door. Handled my girlfriend and I with a rushed and unpleasant attitude. This was my first time going to a Moe's. I hope others are better. The food was nice.

Same great quality I expect from Chipotle but extra kudos for the staff. My colleagues and I are in the military and in our service uniform - which isn't permitted to be worn in public - but the staff came out and delivered our order to the car without question. Order was accurate and they were generous with the guac. 5 stars.

Amis will you be my Amis?

First you must go here with friends or people who you like and know how often they wash their hands. I say this because we all have sketchy office-mates. 

Order lots of small dishes like the amazing fried baby artichokes. If you came to me and sad I could only have eat these and nothing else for the rest of my life...I wouldn't even balk or raise or an eyebrow. 

The salami with honey and hazelnuts! A must! The salami is perfect. Thinly shaved, smoky yet almost sweet. The honey ( yes I am a honey fiend) perfectly complements this ever so perfectly without being cloying. The hazelnuts round out this plate giving it a bit of crunch.  Vetri you are a genius!!!!

The onion focaccia that comes out in a tin.......sublime. Oniony without being overbearing. 

The saffron honey that comes with the cheese plate? Could he start a vetri-trading company like Jose and sell it?

Hmm what else did we nosh on?

The olives. Don't get them. You are expecting Amada-y olives. These are olives drowing in a bowl of oil without any vinegar. It's the only thing I would pass up.

The ricotta is also not worthy of getting the next time I go. It's not as sweet and lovely as the ricotta at Village Whiskey that comes with the pickles. The eggplant spread is nice, but I'm not such a fan. The girls enjoyed it.

The gnocchi with oxtail ragu is heavenly a cloud of potato cheese love drapped in a tender ragu of oxtail. Sara was not so in love, but I have dreams of this dish every now and then. 

The girls had the pasta in the cheese/blackpepper sauce that was also earthshattering simplicity done ever so well.

We had the olive torta, tiramisu and waffle with marscapone semifreddo. 

The girls dug the olive torta, I'm just not into this whole olive oil cake movement. I loved the deconstructed tiramisu and the waffle.....heaven.

It was a dreary dismal rainy night, but Kyle( our delightful waiter) and Amis made it the most wonderful dining experience I have had in Philly in a very long time.

Did I mention I met Marc Vetri outside the loo?

Two stars for the food only. Understaffed, mismanaged, or a combination of both is the only reason I can come up with as to why the service at this location is abysmally slow every time I have come. Every now and then I forget and decide to swing by and pick up food. Quickly, I am reminded as to why I typically drive further to other locations to avoid wasting my life away in a line that fails to move. 
Please, someone at this location visit ANY other location and take notes as to how to successfully manage/staff a restaurant.

I never thought I'd have to do this, but I have to leave Chick-fil-A a negative review. Not it's not about the food but the set up. The ONLY option to order food is the drive thru. This location is situated in a plaza parking lot so if the have a line of more than 8 cars it impedes traffic, people are coming in from several directions which causes confusion. Luckily there is another location a few short miles away so we left and went there. They provided drive through or carry out. Traffic wasn't bad at all we were in and out. I think this location should rethink their traffic pattern and rethink either opening carry out or offer curbside. They are falling short of the expected  chick-fil-a experience. This is not my opinion from 1 visit but my last 3, which is why I'm now sharing my review. If you decided to stop here please know it may not be what you expected, I'm all for giving a chance so please do but know if you have a similar experience just pop out of line and drive a few miles south and visit the other one.

This review is for restaurant week. I've been to Amis for dinner before and absolutely loved the cacio e pepe and craft cocktails. When I saw they were on the restaurant week list, I knew I had to come back.

Our server, Rob, was extremely nice and knowledgeable about the menu. I have a tree nut allergy, so I always appreciate a server who is well informed on the contents of each dish, as well as what can be adjusted to my dietary concerns.

I was pleasantly surprised to learn that Amis' restaurant week menu is four courses! We started with bruschetta-I was lucky to double up on the stracciatella due to my allergy. Next, I had the meatballs and my friend had the brussels. Meatballs were good, in an interesting, thick, non-traditional sauce... it could've used a little more salt (which I rarely say about a dish). I'm told the brussels were delicious and crispy.

For the entree, we couldn't help but order two cacio e pepe dishes. They were good, but again my friend and I both thought there could've been a little more salt. For the finale, we both ordered the flourless chocolate cake which were yummy, fudgey, slices of heaven!

Overall a solid meal and definitely a great choice for restaurant week. The portions seemed to be the same as the regular menu which I appreciate, as many restaurants downsize their dishes during promotions like this.

Amis has been on my "To Try" list for a long time and this week I got around to trying it. My only regret is that I didn't come sooner. Everything was awesome from the service to the food to the ambiance. Restaurant week meals can be hit or miss but at Amis it was a total hit! 

First and foremost the service is some of the best I've had in Philly and I have had some stellar service. The server (Javar or Javas or something to that effect) was on top of everything, even as the restaurant got progressively busier. He even kept my water glass full in spite of the fact that I had a whole bottle I could pour myself sitting right at the table. 

My dining partner and I shared everything so we didn't miss out on any of the amazing flavors. 

Appetizers:  
Stracciatella, rosemary bruschetta: This burratta on bread with Rosemary was to die for. So creamy and salty. Perfection served on generously sliced rustic bread. 
Eggplant caponata bruschetta: Yum. I am not big into Eggplant but had no issue finishing off my portion of this plate. 
Fried Cauliflower: This was pretty good. Not the best I've had but pretty good. I would have liked a hint of spiciness to balance the flavors a bit.
Meatballs: Solid meatballs. Big portion. No complaints here!

Dinner: 
Pork Chop Parm: HUGE portion. Like, 3 meals worth of food. Although no one is complaining about left overs of this tasty entree. This was delicious. 
Trout: Very generous portion size. Perfectly cooked and bursting with Lemon and Garlic flavors. Still good the next day (a rarity for seafood leftovers).

Dessert: 
Tiramisu: This was a traditional tiramisu by all accounts. You can't really go wrong here. I liked it a lot... but my favorite was the, 
Olive Oil Cake: Still thinking about it. The perfect balance of flavors. Not too sweet. Perfect density. I could have eaten the whole thing but alas, I promised to share.  

Such a fantastic experience. I am looking forward to coming back. In the future I'll recommend Amis to out of town visitors looking for a great meal, especially if they are willing to bring me along.

Amis is a beautiful, dimly lit restaurant that will probably get you laid if your date likes Italian food. It will probably also get you laid if your date does not like Italian food. It has great lighting and an interesting ambiance that is simultaneously chill and exciting.

The baked pecorino with almond honey rules. It has multiple layers of sweet, salty, and cheesy flavors. Amongst the items I tried here, this was the winner.

The roasted squash with vincotto and walnuts had an amazing texture. Protip: if you order this, eat it without the bread. The bread distracts from the discipline of the squash.

The gnocchi with oxtail ragu is pretty darn good. It isn't anything transcendent, but it does the job. It is served basically like a hunk of gnocchi with the ragu on it, as opposed to the little gnocchi balls that you are used to.

Now, onto dessert. They were offering tiramisu on special and so I had it. I'm not usually one to harp on presentation, but it literally looked like someone threw it onto the plate from across the room. You know how a pizza looks when you return home from doing 90 on winding mountain roads? All pushed to one side? Well that's pretty much what this looked like, but instead of pizza it was tiramisu.

That being said, the tiramisu is very good. It did not blow me away but I was very happy with the result.

I went to Amis for the first time during Restaurant week for dinner.  The menu looked really good, and overall, I enjoyed my experience.  I started with the Ugo cocktail, which was mainly prosecco and elderflower (with other herbs).  It was really delicious!  

When we ordered our courses, we all shared, so I got to try a few more dishes.  We got the ricotta and eggplant bruschetta.  I was surprised, because I liked the eggplant bruschetta much more than the ricotta.  The ricotta was slightly bland and they didn't put a lot on the bread piece. 
 We then all shared the brussel sprouts, cauliflower, and meatballs.  I definitely recommend the cauliflower and meatballs.  Probably one of the best cauliflower sides I've had and the meatballs were so delicious! Well-seasoned and a great texture! The brussel sprouts were just mediocre. Since so many places offer brussel sprouts, you really have to wow with this dish.  They put a lot of citrus in their dish, which was slightly over-done. But the nice thing about the dish was that it wasn't over-salted, which I feel like a lot of restaurants tend to do.  

For my entree, I switched to wine and ordered the chianti.  It was delicious and paired well with my bucatini dish.  Their pasta was really well made.  The pasta dish could have been salted just a little more, but overall it was really good.  

Finally, the tiramisu was so, so good! They give you a HUGE piece, and it was so good that since I couldn't finish it, I packed it up and took it home.  

The restaurant's interior is on the smaller side and cozy.  I like how they take reservations online.  We had five people, and it ended up being a great restaurant week experience!

Wish we had more places like this near home.  Great vibe and food.  Hostess, bartender and waitstaff all very professional and responsive.  Tried the baked pecorino with almond honey, mozzarella with squash and grapes and fried cauliflower for apps and all were excellent.  I had the bucatini with jalapeno and almond pesto - also excellent, as were the fried brussel sprouts we ordered as a side.  And the bread is great too.

Only one issue - we didn't order dessert (given my aggressiveness in ordering the earlier courses), but they dropped off a small bag with the check.  How nice, I thought - a little take-home sweet.  When I opened it later, however, it was someone else's leftover meatballs.  Oh well, still a five-star.

This location is just not it! 
Order online and can only pass through the drive through to pick up. 
Drive thru is soo long it's trouble to get in and out! 
They need to do something quick!

I do not know why I continue to make the mistake of coming here. If you order a mobile order it will be 30-50 minutes later than the time you are "promised." Every time, every day. Do not come to this location unless you want to sit and wait.

Sadly, this Chipotle has gone downhill. I used to come here at least once a week (maybe twice) and they had the friendliest workers and the freshest food. Now the workers are so unfriendly, unprofessional, and constantly skimping on ingredients. The last two times I've ordered sour cream on my bowls the employees have literally drowned the bowl in it, to the point where it is inedible. I've also ordered online for pickup and they have lost my order at least two times, unacceptable. Parking is horrendous as well since its in a big plaza with a Chick-Fil-A, Jersey Mikes, nail salon, and a pizza place.

This place has not been good in awhile, but we decided to give it another try because the other Moe's we went to had employees preparing food and not wearing their masks properly. I didn't even get in the door all the way and noticed that the kid making food did not have his mask covering his nose.   We quickly exited and will not be back.

Worst Chick Fil A I have ever been to and the reviews show it. How has the manager of this place not been fired? Or chick fil a not step in yet to protect their brand? Service is terrible, drive though is chaos filled with accidents and frustrated people. The most non efficient Chick Fil A in history! Please shut this place down!

What an amazing experience this was! A hot sauna ( check) great friendly staff ( check)  amazing massage ( check ) this was different than any massage I had had before ... First of all clothes are left on , and it is a mix of yoga and massage ... Almost as though the massage therapist is contorting you into yoga positions ..... Lotus flower & downward dog later ... I felt much more limber and my aches began to lessen.... Very cool experience .. Check it out!

Authentic Fujianese cuisine. Came here numerous times before. The food is good but can be a hit or a miss depending on what you order on the menu. The menu is huge. Lots of the things you may be surprised about in terms of weird eats. Also, lots of variety in terms of taste... The restaurant is very small and located around the middle of 10th street towards Race. 

Check the place out for yourself.

We came to Amis coz of Marc Vetri and Brad Spence, with high expectations, but left a bit disappointed. The interiors are classy even the noise level is over the top. The house made rhubarb strawberry soda was pretty good. The salami platter was good but it was a lot of sweet accompanying the meats with no piece of crunchy toast (maybe an in house bread). The Cacio e Pepe was, unfortunately, a travesty. The pasta, which was pretty good, was ladled in some cheese sauce which had a very grainy texture and grated Parmesan. 

I'm afraid to say we might not be back soon.

I have enjoyed Moe's Southwest Grill in many other locations, so when I tried this location for the first time, I was expecting the same consistent experience. Unfortunately, I instead noticed some food safety issues while my food was being prepped:

Issue 1: bearded employee did not have a hair net for his large beard while preparing my food.
Issue 2: same worker pulled his phone out from his pocket to turn off a call or something, then proceeded to continue handling my food without changing gloves. Gross.
Issue 3: As I left the line, several employees were laughing because one of them kept getting caught "eating on the line." I don't know if that meant eating her own food out in the assembly area or eating food from the assembly area, but either way, it doesn't sound great.

I informed the management here about these issues, but the staff response was rather nonchalant, even the manager's. This location is a little out of my way anyhow so I don't think I'll be returning to this particular location.

I had heard of Amis years ago after making Marc Vetri's parchment paper pasta with clams sauce, which turned out brilliantly by the way. So I finally got a chance to make it in after missing them my previous trip to Philly. I made reservations in advance, which I recommend, and sat at the bar. The setting is chic, but in a comfortable kind of way.

Definite standouts on the menu are their Baked Pecorino with Almond Honey, which was superb, and their Porchetta. Sal's Old School Meatballs were pretty good as was their Veal Tongue dish that my bar neighbor let me try. My main dish was their Bucatini with Jalapeños and Almond Pesto. That, was disgusting and not at all on par with the rest of the food and dining experience. It tasted like bad Chinese food, that was a week old. I was surprised it came from the same kitchen as the other items.

For drinks I had their New York Sour, which I did not like at all. I did like the service. All in all it was a bit of a mixed experience. The good outweighed the bad though so I would return in the future.

I didn't enjoy the "old" Coronet.  The service didn't match the prices and the menu was odd at times.
The new Coronet is promising.  I've been three times now and aside from the gift of gorgeous location and setting, sometimes it's heightened with lovely Brazilian live bossa nova music, which complements the old new-world décor and ambience.
The menu has great standards for meat eaters, and if you get the steak, it's a great value at about $30, with a lovely hunk of melty cheese on top. The pork is a monochromatic but lovely tasting dish, and the lamb has a lovely spice that if one didn't enjoy, might feel it pervaded the dish too successfully.  There are several others dishes worthy of a try, which is good -- the menu isn't too grand; there are no pages to turn.  But it's varied enough to go back several times and try something new.  
One of my favorite aspects of the menu is the happy hour.  I've had delicious soups for the happy hour appetizer, and each time different.  They also have some lovely traditional handcrafted cocktails for happy hour so it's as though one is enjoying a little meal, before the meal if one partakes in some drink and nibbles before the main fare.
I would also suggest even on chilly evenings the outdoor patio.  It's in a lovely courtyard, with heatlamps if needed, and outside the din of the interior.  Unfortunately "good" seating limited.  There is a long corridor where one party must face the wall and focus intently on the dining partner, while the other will have the captain's view and be able to soak up the ambience, while your dining partner drones on.  Another daquiri, please!

If you don't have cash on hand, and who does nowadays, then be prepared to eat somewhere else. Twice in two weeks I've been to this location after 6pm and they will yell "no longer accepting cards, cash only!" This time I stuck around instead of leaving and saw people were STILL using the card.

Also with COVID going on you think they would clean the tables. NOPE. Tables are disgusting. Looks like kids came in and threw food all over the tables and sat in it. Twice over two weeks it's been this way. If your customer service sucks I mean at least clean the tables and seats at least!
This has been the second time I've had bad experience in this location where they don't give the right order which I thought it was one time type of thing but seems like is constant now

Very disappointed so that I decide to register yelp to speak out and let people know how awful their service is as many people have already stated!!! If there is other choice, DO NOT go to this restaurant. 

My wife and I went to this rest this evening, and were immediately surprised that there seemed more waiters than customers. while, it doesn't matter too much for us. We ordered 5 types of meat, and 3 types of vegetables for the hot pot. After we ordered, we realized that there are combos for 6 types of meat and 3 types of vegetables with cheaper prices than separated ones. So we asked the waiter is it ok to add one type of meat and change them to meat combo and vegetable combo. The waiter told me actually the prices are similar that there was no need to change, but finally agreed. Actually price for combo is cheaper than separated ones. I double confirmed with the waiter regarding the price for the two combos in case there is any problem.

When we eat a while, the problem came: the same waiter came to our table, and told us we need to pay the price for separate ones because the portions is less for combo and they just served larger portion for separated ones(actually quite small portion). At the same time, another male waiter come, and also insisted I need to pay the price for separated ones for their own mistakes. I refused and asked them to show me the description regarding the portion difference on their menu, otherwise I wouldn't agree. 

Then their manager(another male) came with a rude and aggressive question in Chinese: 你们有什么问题 (what problem you have?) I told him I don't get a problem. He replied: no, you got a problem, and I would like to hear what problem you have. Can you image three people in front of you when you are having you dinner and trouble me due to their own mistake? Fine, I told him the issue between the waiters and us. He told us there is description outside of the restaurant regarding the price and portion, and that "I believe I don't need to iterate that to you again." Actually I was a little scared at that time and felt I might be attacked at any time due to his super aggressive attitude even though I am Chinese. Ridiculous, right? A Chinese customer worried about being attached by a Chinese restaurant manager in US. But I still told him I double confirmed with the waiter before the dishes were served, and that if there is any problem it's not my fault. OK. This manager started to say "OK, your order is counted as combos this time", and then rebuked to the waiter in front of me. I had no appetite at all since that. 


The manager harassed us later again when our lamb was served. "why you have 7 types of meats instead of 6?" I had to count and told him we only have 6! Then he told the waiter to change the lamb to a smaller combo portion. Fine! I just wanted to leave this fucking restaurant as soon as possible.

I was wondering the reason the manager didn't care how aggressively and rudely he spoke with me might be we were talking in Chinese. Other customers cannot understand. I feel I have to speak out and let people how awful their service is: three waiters bully their Chinese customer! And their customer feel their safety is threatened.
absoluletly fantastic.

If you're unbothered by obnoxious attitude and, at times, conspicuous prejudices this place is a'right! Always noted how black patrons are treated there until it became a pattern of how my family and I were treated.

Food was so flavorful and service was good and relatively quick. We started off with some olive oil and salt infused bread which was delicious. We also got the swordfish meatballs, regular meatballs, eggplant, baked cheese, salumi mixed plate, brussel sprouts and a couple of pasta dishes to share. 

All were delicious but I highly recommend the meatballs. Another favorite is the bucatini pasta with jalapeno and almond pesto. It has just the right amount of heat!

Would definitely come back if I'm in Philly again!

I'm a huge chick fil a fan. But what's going on at this location? The only way to get food is through the drive thru or Grubhub. I'm from out of town, staying at the Hilton and had to walk. I ordered in the app and asked if I couldn't pick it up inside like the grub hub guys - if I could have it brought outside for me, and one of the stalls. No luck. Very frustrating. Please use some common sense. Instead of forcing everyone into the drive thru - and idling our cars, open up some way to walk in. And help out the person that doesn't have a car- and doesn't want to pay double by ordering through grub hub. I really don't know what's going on at this location. What's happened to all of the friendly workers? What's happened to common sense? But maybe you don't care because the money rolls in regardless of how everyone is treated.

We stopped in for lunch and thank goodness I didn't allow the reviews to deter me! The service was great and the food was incredibly flavorful! 

Lunch is Monday-Friday 11-3 and for $10! What does that get you? Vietnamese spring roll, a drink, and your choice of Banh Mi, fresh bowl, 3 taco or any specialty sushi roll under $17. First the spring rolls knocked my socks off!! They were soooo good!! Crispy, flaky, light, and full of flavor and the vinegar based sauce that should be packaged and sold!! Next course, sushi...more specifically the Ultimate Mexican Roll...omgosh y'all... it's amazing! It has everything I LOVE in a roll. Shrimp Tempura, cream cheese, avocado, cucumber, masago (skipped) and spicy mayo. If I had to critique something here, I would say remove the tail of the shrimp. Most restaurants don't, and I don't understand why. Extra points for fast service. I was able to get in and out on my lunch. Yay

Ambiance, is open style dining. Which was fine during lunch since is wasn't crowded but I would imagine it's pretty loud at night. May not be the best place for a romantic dinner. It seems to be the perfect spot with friends or family. 

I have to give a very special shout out to the owner Aldo & our server Maggie. Aldo came over and introduced himself and genuinely cared about our opinion & dining experience. It was nice to see a young owner interacting with his guest. I can't forget Maggie. Her service was on fire!! She promptly refilled drinks, cleared the table right away and was very patient as we took our time to order! She's a star in this establishment. 

All and all, this place is a gem. Give them a try, I hope you have the same experience I did xoxo

This place was amazing! The outdoor patio was so cute and such a vibe. Our waiter Isaac was great and gave great suggestions since it was our first time. We tried so many things.. my favorites were the Leek Fritters (I wanted to lick the beet purée off the plate) and the Chimichurri potatoes!! I got a Paloma and it was perfect! The dessert... I have 2 words... CREME BRÛLÉE!!!!!!! It was soooooo delicious!! Overall everything was great; food was amazing, service was outstanding and the vibe was unmatched!!

Check out more of my reviews on Yelp as well as my IG page @jenjonesinthecity for reviews and pics of stuff to do in Atlanta!

My friend and I try a new restaurant every week and this was by far the best experience and food. The level of professionalism from the servers to the guests was impeccable. Sitting at the chefs table was also a great experience in itself. Each meal was timed perfectly and I never felt rushed once. I pulled chef aside and let her know that everything was absolutely amazing and her kitchen staff was very talented. Lastly I loved that the manager was frequently walking the floor and checking on tables. Highly recommend this restaurant! I will be back soon for sure! Thanks for the amazing service and food!

I write this review with a few things in mind: 
1. They just opened.
2. They hired waitstaff with no serving experience.
3. Yelp is blasting their business by pushing notifications to regular Yelp users.

Atmosphere - 5/5 
Atmosphere - A for Awesome. Modern lighting, high, airy ceilings - it almost seems like they should have planned a two-story venue or added a second story to house local businesses - there is definitely a lot of space in this establishment! The bar is double-sided (you can sit indoors or outside) but I can see the outdoor elements becoming a hindrance to the open kitchen concept. The open kitchen adds an eclectic flair and is a nice touch...but the minute Florida bugs and outdoor elements come inside, I will probably bail.

FOOD - 5/5
The food was GREAT and the prices were perfectly appropriate for the portions we were served. We started with the Vietnamese Crispy Spring Rolls. This dish came with 6 halves, which made it easy to split with an odd number of people. The rolls contained ingredients that tasted very fresh and the dipping sauce was sweet and not too powerful. 

I ordered the shaking beef entree which the kitchen presented as an ornately decorated dish. The dish consisted of a tender, not too chewy stir-fry or flank style steak, cooked medium well, atop a bed of watercress salad with tomatoes, (pickled?) onions, and a side of rice. This dish was very good - I would have liked more rice but our server did not stop by after she dropped off the food so I didn't really have a chance to ask for more until the end - at which point I decided that I had eaten enough. 

My two friends ordered the bowls - one with shaking beef, the other with chicken. Both of them devoured every bite and reported that they would order the bowl on a regular basis. Definitely recommending the bowl on their behalf. They are also appropriately priced at $12 (chicken) and $14 (shaking beef). You can also add a fried egg to the bowl for an extra dollar, which one of my friends did.

SERVICE - 2/5
Our server was a very pleasant young lady but she was definitely new to serving and it seems that Bar Asia still has some kinks to work out with that regard. Some of the qualms fell on the restaurant itself - like not having a drink menu or wine list at all printed. I appreciated the bartender's willingness to come to our table and assist with our drink selections, but one person in my party had to go to the bar himself to figure out what kind of drinks they had to offer.  The bartender came to our table and let us sample a few wines - she explained that all of the wines are on tap and they include a Lambrusco, a Pinot noir and a Cabernet. I didn't love the Cabernet so I went with the slightly sweet Lambrusco. It was palatable but none of the tapped wines tasted very good to me. The only other shortcoming worth noting is that after our food was dropped off, the server did not return until it was time for us to pay the bill. Typically servers check back after two bites to make sure that all is well. She was new to serving so with some more experience this should improve.

Overall, I give this place 4/5 stars and I hope that Yelpers take it easy on them for the first few weeks...and I also hope that Bar Asia's management reads these reviews and accepts AND considers the feedback as constructive commentary. Best of luck Bar Asia and welcome to the South Tampa foodie scene!

Recently visited Amis for brunch over the weekend. Overall, the food was decent for the price tag that came along with it. From an ambiance standpoint, Amis surely wins with the open kitchen vibe, modern trendy bar, and the friendly attentive staff. For me, the hype didn't live up to the expectations when it came to the food. My friend and I ordered the crispy cinnamon bun with cream ($12) and the omelet a la parmigiana ($14). The cinnamon bun didn't meet my expectations since it was served cold vs. warm. Could've been my own fault for imaging a warm oozy cinnamon bun to the the table. Secondly, the omelet itself was very good, but from a portion size thought you could get a little bit more for the value. 

All in all, I would give this restaurant another try for dinner with the pasta reviews. Just missed the mark in my book for the brunch aspect.

My go-to spot for lunch. Even though the drive-thru can be pretty slammed, the line goes pretty quick. Everything is always fresh when I go. #2 spicy chicken sandwich meal w/ lemonade and 4 pc chicken tenders are my go-to . If you want to skip the line, you can always use the app to order ahead and wait for your food parked. But usually the quickest way to get the food is to just go in.
Without a doubt, this is the worst run and managed Chick Fil A in the United States of America. Customer service is a nightmare and an embarrassment to Chick Fil A.

I've been to this chick fil a a couple times after just moving to tampa. The first time they forgot part of my order & told me the would email me a comp meal but never did. That was fine. I just went the other day & ordered online with three meals needing biscuits. Waited at the chick fil a for 20 minutes for them to say they ran out of biscuits & replace the meals with bagels. I called to say this isn't what I wanted for them to not answer the phone & never call me back.

Rude. My chips were soggy. I asked for fresh chips and was informed that they are all cooked in the morning and they are all the same. The place was dirty. The staff acted as though they were doing me a favor by waiting on me. I won't be back

MUST ASK FOR YOUR BILL! The lady would add up some additional charge to your total price!

This is the only place I could find my hometown taste which is closest to where I live, yes, 3.5 hours driving without traffic. Whenever I come to PA, or pass PA, I would always stop by here. 

The price on the menu was good(if she didn't added some "additional charge" on your bill). The food was very tasty and it's transitional Fuzhou style food. 

This time I ordered several dish and was told the total was $26, I gave her $30 and told her to keep the charge. I never thought the bill was wrong until later I added up all the amount together when I was driving. 

I know I would still come back whenever I go to or pass PA. But I will definitely ask for bill or calculate it before I pay. 

Oh, do not expect any customer service. The lady has some attitudes, really impatient and get annoyed at whatever you ask her.

My friend and I came here for restaurant week and had a great meal. My friend and I shared Sal's meatballs, the pig head croquettes, the fried brussel sprouts, the polenta in brown butter, the jalapeno bucatini, the linguine with pork ragu, and we each got tiramisu. 

The meatballs, croquettes, and brussel sprouts were all delicious. They give you a lot of brussel sprouts, so it's a filling appetizer. I do wish the croquettes were filled with more meat. I split mine in half and it was mostly air with a little slab of the meat, but it was still tasty.

Neither of us really enjoyed the polenta. It relied too much on the brown butter for flavor, as it was swimming in butter. There wasn't much seasoning otherwise, so it was a little bland. Both the bucatini and linguine were delicious. I would have preferred the pasta to have a little more bite to them (they were pretty soft), but the sauces were delicious. The tiramisu was great and a pretty big slice. 

Our waitress was a little terse and not very warm, but other than that, the service was good. Our waters were constantly being refilled, and they were kind enough to give us another plate of focaccia when we requested it.

If you like overly peppery food - this is the place.  They put white pepper in Everything.  The "Open Kitchen" is deafeningly noisy.  Our meal was delayed for an unexplained reason.  Waiter was quite indifferent as we had complained about the white pepper.

Came here for restaurant week with friends and had an incredible Italian meal. The star of the show was definitely the super rich and moist tiramisu. The eggplant bruschetta was also incredible and full of flavor. The pasta itself was pretty filling and had the noodles had great texture. 

We came in a little late at 9:15 pm so we had most of the restaurant to ourselves. The waiter kindly walked us through the menu and we took his recommendations. Overall, I remember all the dishes being one of the best Italian dishes I've had so definitely will be back!

I had such high expectations! Unfortunately, most fell short. We felt very rushed the entire time. We arrived at 6:30. By 6:45 our food was already arriving at our table. The "best selling" crispy cauliflower was nothing special - plain, undercooked, and poorly seasoned. Pastas were good but Americanized. The bread was served alone without any sort of oil which, in my Italian opinion, is one of the most important aspects! The only saving grace were our cocktails and desserts. The "Alto" was quite tasty. The flourless chocolate cake very rich.

Worst chick-fil-A in the country. I just stood at counter for over 10 minutes. Never greeted never even an attempt to take my order. At least 4 employees walked by me. What a terrible example of how Chick-fil-A typically run their stores. I came here today specifically because I had heard 2 bad experiences from others in the last couple weeks that I did not believe. Boy was I wrong. This store is successful only based on location. Get it together Chick-fil-A

Hey the pandemic has been over for 6 months maybe you should open your dining room. Drove all the way here just to see a drive through line of 60 cars and 20 waiting for mobile orders. Not a good chickfila either. If i could give 0 stars i would

Overall a descent place to get food. They are not skimpy on meat like some other locations are and will get service done at a good pace. Customer service is good, location could be a lot cleaner. On my good list

STALE !!!!!! 
 I tried to support the local small business but too many times they sold me stale doughnuts. The final straw was when I paid at least $2.50 each for two cookie monster cupcakes and one of them was HALF THE SIZE of the other, yet there were at least a dozen more proportioned of equal size to the bigger one remaining in the case ! Why on earth would you give anyone a cupcake that small and its clear to see that its abnormal. This neighborhood has predominately white folks living here. Being African American I can't help but feel like this was intentional. If the majority of your customers are white why should you care if I return ?
You saw an opportunity to get rid of the ugly duckling cupcake and if that wasn't your intent it would not have been sold to me or in the case to begin with .
The salesperson was not blind .

This location is terribly disorganized and poorly managed.   The employees are ill-trained, lack knowledge about processes and problem solving skills. Additionally, I ordered the mac-n-cheese and it was awful. Never have I ever had such a disturbing experience with a Chick-fil-A before. They shouldn't be allowed to claim that they are part of the Chick-fil-A family.

I eat here regularly, not anymore!!! I am allergic to cilantro, its impossible to get tomatos without cilantro in it. Usually an employee will find some somewhere. Tonight i had an extremely rude emplloyee ask me if i was deaf, because she told me once before there was no tomatos without cilantro. She was extremely rude. Does Chipotle thinks everyone likes cilantro??? How about tomatoes without it!!!!! That would be to smart an idea for them, i used to eat there 3-4 times a week!!! Never again!!! Not after the extremely rude customer service, and not till management gets their heads out of there butts and make a side of tomatos without cilantro. This place sucks!!

Given the fact that Amis opened on Thursday and I ate there today (Monday) I'm very impressed with how well and smoothly the restaurant is running. All the major players were on site supervising service, including Marc Vetri, who popped in and out the kitchen several times while we were there.

The atmosphere is warm, fairly loud (both the acoustics and the rock music), and a mix of high-end and casual. 

Service overall was excellent and so was the food. Any kinks they still have to work out are minor and the caliber of the food makes up for any shortcomings.

This is a small plates restaurant so don't go in expecting heaping portions of Olive Garden slop. Do get the oxtail ragu gnocchi. It's exceptional. The sweatbreads are tender and delicious. The drink menu (we had the alto and the ginginber) is well put together and the desserts are very good.

Overall you get a well rounded high quality meal for about $40-$65 per person. This will easily be one of the best restaurants in the city from what I've experienced so far.

Ordered a gallon of lemonade for crew at job site. Got to the window and was told the needed to make a new batch and would be 10 minutes and to park. Waited 15 minutes went inside told it would be right out. Waited ten more minutes and went inside to wait more minutes. Told it was a shift change this time. Horrible Communcation and service. Thinking it was a one time deal I went back today to get a milkshake for my wife and I just left rather than deal with their horrible service. Two bad experiences of probably a hundred at Chick-fil-A, but none good at this location.

If this app let me put 0 stars I would. My boyfriend and I have been going to this chick fil a for the past like 10 months. We have never once had a good or even decent experience here. Constantly missing food, giving the wrong food, charging for the wrongs meals. Staff is extremely rude, none of them pay attention or care, they talk over you with an attitude while you're trying to order. Worst of all is how terribly slow the service is. It took us nearly 35 minutes to get my food today. By the time it got to me my food was not even worth the wait. The fries and chicken were both cold and very clearly not fresh. The point of having a drive through is for it to be fast food and that has never been possible here. I understand things get busy, but every other chick fil a in the area is able to handle busy except for this location. I honestly have no idea how this location has lasted so long with such terrible service. It's more worth your time to go to the location inside the nearby international mall than to waste your time and money here.

What in the world are they doing??? In the not too long drive they line for over 20 minutes!!!! And you can't get out of the line to go inside. They need a better system here!!! People are turning off their vehicles for the wait. Do not go through the drive thru unless you see someone outside. Maybe the manager is home with the flu but things are falling apart tonight !!!!

A lot of ppl are saying negative things, but hands down even if this location has it's downfalls when compared, its still amazing service, fast service, great customer service, & they get the orders in & out & ppl taken care of. Mistakes happen & yet it's still rare here. The negative reviews are just from a bunch of hoity toity people. This place does not deserve 2 stars. That's a McD's rating.
Worst chipotle I've ever been to. It's online only and the service is awful. Won't ever be going back to this location.
I got a cake here for a party. It was delicious! They did a great job decorating it too.

Amis-tery Story:  The Case of the Wet Feather-Vest
I first dined at Amis on opening night, where I tasted Ricotta imported from an alpine town, a succulent appetizer whose subtle flavors would continue to haunt me for months to come.  My desires in full force, I convinced my boyfriend to celebrate our anniversary at Amis.    Little did we know that the unspeakable, gastronomical pleasures (tuna steak to die for) were ill-fated to conflict with the horrible service we experienced.  Though we made the reservation a couple of months ahead of time, when we arrived, there was no table for us, and we had to wait about 20 minutes before we were seated.  Finally, when we went to the hostess to retrieve our coats, my vest was missing from the hanger.  When I asked the hostess where it was, she whispered to one of the managers and he went into the back office.  When he returned, he brought back my vest which was soaked through with what I hope was water.  It was dripping and I had to carry it home in a bag.  We still muse over possible explanations, but none are so sensible as to tempt me to re-cross the sharp divide of Broad Street.

Food was good except the burnt bread served in the beginning. Entire meal was so rushed. I arrived on time for 5:00 reservation but husband had to park car. They would not allow me to sit at the table until he came. He came within 5 minutes.The entire restaurant was empty except for tables of 2 all bunched together. They proceeded to try to seat us between these two couples already bunched together. I asked to be moved to one of the tables a little space away. From then on the service went so quick we couldn't even enjoy our dinner. The waiter told us the specials and asked us about drinks as we were sitting down. We were celebrating something special and we were out of there very quickly. It is great to have prompt service but you can feel when you are rushed. We were done and out the door before the other the couples who were there before us were done. I think by then we had had it as well.Maybe we should have stayed at the table squeezed between the others . I guess the waiter wanted to turn our table.  If you really want to enjoy a meal and the entire dining experience I recommend Fork, Fitler's Diner or Zavinos. It wasn't worth it to us to go back. I would rather have time to enjoy our meal and feel welcome.

They do not have prices on any items and will scan single items for questionably high prices. Be careful when buying a soda. They will scan a single can but charge you for the full pack unless you say something.

I was enjoying my CFA chicken wrap for lunch when I noticed that my wrap had an extra ingredient.. CFA's produce is so fresh, they still have lady bugs on them! I find this repulsive and completely out of character for CFA. I just want everyone to be aware of what you might find in CFA's chicken wraps or any of their meals that have lettuce. Be careful out there or you might be munching on some extra protein.

One of my favorite Italian restaurants in the city. Black pepper pasta, short rib, wine and cocktails spot on. It's fairly loud and busy, not many large tables, but if you are looking for Italian food in a trendy, cozy environment you can't do much better.

Just sublime. Went last night for maybe my 100th time? Took a vegetarian, which means I got to eats lots of CHEESE and desserts! 

Excellent swordfish meatballs, Sal's meatballs, baked pecorino, veggies, and desserts. Yum. The house white wine is a bargain.

Outdoor seating on a warm Wed night was chill. Service is impeccable, as always. Danielle, Arturo, Ned, and the rest of the staff rock.

I was in town visiting a friend who is moving back to NYC next week and this was on her list of restaurants to try before leaving Philly.  

When we first got there we were told we would have to wait for a short while so we ordered drinks at the bar.  But by the time we placed our drink order, our table was ready and the hostess was not too pleased to have to wait for us to get our drinks.  She was the one who told us to wait at the bar so come on!

Also, first the hostess asked us if we wouldn't mind being seated at the area where the chefs are cooking.  We considered it but the restaurant was really loud and we thought conversation would be difficult so we declined and said we would wait for a table.  A table opened up for us pretty immediately so that was good.  Or perhaps they knew they would have free tables but wanted them for other reservations.  Who knows.

Our waitress was super nice although she never told us her name so I can't pass that info on to you.  She told us most tables order a few appetizers to share and then a pasta and a main dish depending on the hunger level.  I was with two friends so we decided to order 4 appetizers and to split 1 pasta and 1 main dish and to save room for dessert (always my main focus).  For us that was the perfect amount of food.  None of us are super tiny/non-eater types so I think you can trust our opinion when going yourself.  We also ordered a carafe of the house red wine which was quite tasty.  

My favorite appetizer we ordered was the eggplant caponata that goes on the slightly too hard bread.  We also ordered a pasta that was really simple and a bit creamy with black pepper as the main flavoring.  It was amazing.  Delicious.  We ordered the duck and in reality duck isn't my favorite so I didn't eat that much of it.  I thought I would like it but then I remembered how fatty duck is and how much I dislike chewing it!  

For dessert we got THREE things because I was so excited for dessert.  We wanted the tiramisu but the QUITE rowdy table next to us ordered about 15 pieces and so they were out.  Instead we got the waffle with nutella and ice cream, the  blueberry tart and the polenta shortcake which was hands down my favorite dessert of those three.  

Each of us ended up spending about $50 which really isn't too bad.  I thought the prices were reasonable, I liked the ambiance and the food itself was fresh and delicious.  I would definitely go back here if I am in Philly again.

The employees were great and welcoming. The food was horrible. I have never been to this location until today.  

Queso was extremely watered down. Beans mushy, meat and the rice were burned.
Slowest Chick-fil-A. For being Drive thru only you'd think they'd have it more together. Staff was not familiar with menu.

The Coronet is a great spot if you like the food of Europe.  I'm a little shocked at the 4 star Yelp.  I went before 5pm during their snack menu, and everything was excellent.  I had the frites and a salmon plate with baguette.  Pro tip: the coffee here is very good.  Just as good as any specialty coffee location.  I recommend you sit outside on the sunny patio with a couple cortados.
bro whoever's reading this review that's in charge get urself together, train ur staff, get new management, and do better
Their drive through is an absolute disaster, blocks traffic for the entire shopping center. Fix it.

Great location! My wife the Patriots fan & I (the Bucs fan) came to dinner here before the game. Actually, I grabbed some Chinese, she got Chick-fil-A. The cow kept coming over to give her a hard time for being a Patriots fan. My wife deflected the cow by pointing out I wasn't eating their food. I defended myself saying I WAS eating chicken (and mooching off her delicious dinner too). Haha, cow took my side! It was all in good fun. Fun cow, good food I mooched off the wife. Nice, new, clean location. Friendly staff! That line was almost out the door and moooved very quickly too!

Haven't been to this Chipotle in awhile since the one by my office never disappoints. Decided to get takeout since I'm working from home. Ordered my usual which always includes *light* sour cream. I'm not normally picky, and I'm perfectly fine eating Mexican food with a regular portion of sour cream on it, i just am not a fan of too much. I opened my bowl and I have legitimately never seen this much sour cream on a chipotle bowl. It's almost laughable lol. I'm assuming they misread my *light* SC as *extra* but cmon man. This thing is damp.
I really enjoyed my coffee and my husband and I both loved our bagel sandwiches. Love the atmosphere. The staff was very friendly.

This location has gone down hill FAST! No longer offering curbside, counter pick up or delivery which makes there drive through A MESS!!! Not only are you waiting in line for the drive-through for 20 minutes but then you're also waiting for your food for another 5 to 10 once you're at the window because it's not ready.

I was looking forward to my brunch meal at Amis and based on the reviews and menu I saw online had high hopes.

The meal started out fine - we were seated, offered still (bottled) water, etc. But then our waitress disappeared for about 15 minutes only to come back to inform us of some changes to the menu, including some items which we planned to order. So on to plan B - which can be difficult when your dining partner has a few food allergies. We asked if they could make slight alterations to some items on the menu and they said NO. This left the only item on the menu which my wife would eat - a ribeye steak. She wanted to try a few other items but was disappointed at the lack of flexibility in the kitchen. The steak was flavorful and well cooked. Wish it came with a sunny side up egg.

I ordered the pasta with roasted squash and walnuts, which was filling but not as flavorful. Also had a cornetti stuffed with apricots which was good, but not sure I would pay $5/piece if it were served at a bakery.

Fresh squeezed blood orange juice was a nice touch.

Overall, the good was food, but I deducted 1 star for the lack of flexibility in the kitchen, slow service and very high noise level,

We left a little less than impressed or full, so stopped at a Garces place on the way home.

Check your cake BEFORE you leave the store. Brought home a cake and there were dead ants baked all on the bottom of the cake. Returned the cake in less than 20 minutes from buying it and was told perhaps it came from my house. The cake went from store to car to home (a 8-10 minute drive) and I cut it as soon as I got home. So it was far fetched to say the dead ants came from my house. The ants were dead and baked into the cake. They refunded the money.

If you are looking for a place to get a good burrito that will fill you up might as well go across the street to Qdoba's. This chipotle is like the chipotle's where people trying to lose weight go to. They give small portions of rice, protein, and sides. It is like their pay is based on how much ingredients they save in each burrito. Every time I get hungry I always see Chipotle headed home and go in with a  smile on my face, but leave disappointed and still hungry. Good thing Chik-fil-A is in the same parking lot.

This place takes reservations, but may require a credit card if you have a large party.  

The food here is on point.  Service is amazing here.  This place continues to exceed my expectations.  We ordered a few appetizers:
- buffala mozzarella with beets: really fresh mozzarella- nice and light
- sals meatballs -  very tender meatballs, sauce is tasty.  The potato is ok, meatballs are definitely the star of the dish.
- calamari - really tender calamari.  Like the jalapeños that come with it.

Entrees:
Cacio e Pepe - standard Italian dish.  This is the best place to get it in the city.  I thought my pasta was slightly over cooked.  Would've wanted it more al dente.
Bucatini - great flavors and the pasta was cooked well.  Very large strands.

Good food and service!

Mixed feelings. The ambience is nice but the music a bit too loud. And of course very dark. The wine selection was good, but not great value. 

The appetizers we ordered were really good, the cauliflower was probably the best of them. I ordered the roasted chicken which turned out really to be fried chicken, just not battered, and it came drenched in a pool of butter. The seasoning was good but it felt disgusting to eat chicken from a butter plate. Luckily the accompaniments were good.

Review 1000!!!

And a birthday dinner review at that!

When I realized that the time frame of hitting my 1000th review was going to fall around the time of my birthday dinner I knew that I was going to have to pick a Philly restaurant that was worthy of both occasions. At first the task proved daunting when my first choice (A tasting menu at a restaurant beginning with a Z that I have recommended on countless occasions based on YOUR reviews) didn't have a reservation on the needed day. But then it hit me that there was still a very worthy Philly chef out there who's food I've had yet to sample. 

While I've enjoyed offerings from Garces and Starr restaurants,  food from the likes of Solomonov and McAndrews, and have shared plenty of off kilter moments with the likes of Chiang and Jacobson, the fine Italian cuisine of Marc Vetri is something that has up until this point alluded me. Of late I've found myself salivating over the thought of his pizza, pasta and homemade salumi; and had become especially fond and appreciative of the charitable efforts he does with the Vetri Foundation. So while the dilemma of choosing between Osteria and Amis was a challenge, the baked pecorino was enough of a wild card to delight the cheese monger in me and the reservation was set.

Many reviews on here go into the extra attentiveness of the staff, and our table did experience that in some ways such as having 2 different servers check on our table, and asking how everything was during our meal a few times too many. It also created a couple of "Whos on First?" style moments when one would complete the dessert order or check taking that the other started. But if anything it was done in a way that was extra accommodating and informative as opposed to being extra aggressive and overbearing. And it showed in the little details like them adding a birthday candle to my dessert when they overheard our table having a birthday discussion.

Every so very often there comes a menu that sounds so enticing that I want to order and savor one of everything on it. And with its various bruschettas, homemade salumi, classic and elevated pasta dishes, incredible sounding fish dish and meat dishes, and overall old world Italian meets new world Italian feel, it was VERY much the case at Amis. Which is especially amicable given the tripe, tongue, and liver dishes that they had. the salami del giorno was enticing with its fennel inside and rich marmalade accompaniment. the eggplant caponata  was fresh and robust in all of the right places. But the star of the appetizer show was definitely the baked pecorino with almond honey. In all my years of being a cheese monger I never thought I'd be able to see a typically hard and grate-able cheese like pecorino presented in a way that was so soft and gooey. But seeing and especially tasting is believing. And seeing experiencing it with that decadent honey made me a believer!

It is important to remember not to hit up an Indonesian noodle market for a quick lunch before going to a place that's known for its pasta for dinner.
