And since I was one to sadly make such an error (D'oh!), I wasn't up for getting the chestnut fettucine with duck ragu that I otherwise would have gotten (double D'oh!). But in the experience of trying something that I wasn't at least somewhat familiar with I ordered the grilled cobia tagliata for main. And what I gotwas an incredible swordfish style whitefish that was meaty and not overwhelmingly fishy thanks to its fennel and citrus accompaniment. One could get hooked on the potent and fruity vodka and lemon infused Amis Punch if they're not to careful. But fortunately the small yet impressionable draught list was enough to have me intrigued. And the Trubbel De Yards delivered a malty yet fruity complexion that I wasn't expecting from a dark beer. Normally dessert is another tricky thing to choose. but the prospect of a homemade salted butter ice cream sundae with blood orange and crushed chocolate biscotti was pretty damn hard to pass up.  And it was the perfect final bite to a flawless meal that already has me craving more!!!

The ambience is great, both indoor and outdoor.  Service is friendly.  The food was good, but not remarkable. The portions were very small, even for someone like me who doesn't like large volume servings. And the prices are very high for what you get.  Even something as basic as bread - which many dining establishments provide gratis -  needs to be  purchased and  is served as four small slices of baquette.   Sadly, I don't think the ambience makes up for the lack of value.

I just recently went to the new location (new for me, as I haven't been there in the last 3 years). I had the Shakshuka and the the Lil Dutch Babies. Loved both. The patio is beautiful and the staff is friendly and COVID responsible. One of the best coffees that I had in Tucson and for that matter, in US (I am European at base).

*** Please note that this review is based solely on their lunch special! ***

I went here on one of the most frigid days we've had in Philly this year. Since I was on U Penn's campus and nearly frozen, hot pot sounded like a solid choice. 

Upon entering, I saw a sign for the crazy good lunch special they had -- $9 for one item off of their menu for hot or cold dishes. Even though I had initially planned on hot pot, I couldn't pass this deal up. 

I chose to get the Shredded Pork with garlic sauce and I was very happy with my choice! The pork was tasty and the garlic sauce was very flavorful with a bit of a kick. It came with your choice of white or brown rice. I chose brown rice, but unfortunately they had just run out so I was forced to get white rice. Good to know they do offer both for further visits though!

The following things stood out to me about this place:

- Staff was very nice! They initially brought out a bowl of edamame while I browsed through the menu. After I told them I am allergic to soybeans, the gentleman profusely apologized for putting them on the table, quickly took them away, and brought out a bowl of seasoned vegetables instead. Very thoughtful and the vegetables were pretty darn good! 

- After placing my order, my server promptly warned me that the pork would take about 15 minutes to prepare and asked me if I was ok with that. I was ok with it so I kept my order and I'm glad I did! The food came out so quickly! Far less time than the 15 minutes I had been told!

- The Shredded Pork lunch special was of a decent size with a heaping bowl full of rice. Best part? It only came out to $9!!! What a great price for such a great lunch!

Would I recommend Ochatto to others? Absolutely! Their lunch special is fantastic! Would I return? For sure! I've gotta go back for hot pot!

*PRO TIP: Bring some cash with you! 10% off your order if you pay with cash!*

Loved this place! Will have to go back and try the other dishes. I took my boyfriend for his birthday. We split two aps, each had a main dish, but sadly passed on dessert. We both ate half of our main dish and took the rest home. Maybe next time we will add an ap and take away a main dish in order to have dessert. Dessert list looked great.

Swordfish meatballs, braised pork bellies, black pasta, and a duck special...I'm still drooling over you.
Service and food were quite nice. However, charging 22% for our party of 8 was outrageous. 20% maybe, but not 22%. Would not recommend for large parties.

Hello I ordered my table 4 months ago from this place I thought it was a good place. They told me it would be delayed because of COVID reasons and I understand that. But it's been 4 months now and whenever I call them they don't have manager at the location and they keep telling me we will inform you in two weeks but I never get a call back and I always have to call them for delivery. One of the furniture we received from this place was also broken. I called at different location today and he told us that he doesn't have any records on receipts? How does someone open multiple businesses and not have contact with their other business. I got everyone's name I will be seeing everyone in court soon. Adding more to it when I went to checkout the table in September their employee had wrong price tag on it and I also have picture of it this is not my fault that their employees are giving us wrong information. I paid $200 after to receive new product but I still didn't receive any information or date on when it will arrive. I paid lot of money for this furniture and will be talking with my lawyer.

I just went to Moe's for the third time in two weeks. I've been craving the food. But each time I go in, I'm confronted with employees wearing masks under their noses. Tonight was the last time I tried.

This gets a solid 4.5 at least. Have been here a couple of times. Nice on a weeknight when less busy. Memorable dishes include the mozzarella salad (they had one with squash and pistachio pesto when I went), the bucatini, lasagna, mom-mom's rice pudding, tiramisu. Really delicious.

Amis was my first Marc Vetri experience, and a fabulous one indeed.  As one could probably glean from my reviews of Jose Garces restaurants, I respect innovative chefs/restauranteurs who can make seemingly incompatible flavors blend impeccably.  The gregarious waitstaff and laid-back, unpretentious ambience made for a great evening.

On the day we'd had dinner, their catch of the week was shark, and we ordered their night's special of shark pasta (which was clearly fresh and very good).  We also ordered their signature Tonnarelli "Cacio e pepe" with pecorino and black pepper (*beyond words*), a side of polenta (too buttery and greasy for my personal taste), and the Belgian style waffle with nutella, vanilla semifreddo, and toasted hazelnuts (OUT of this world). 

Overall, we remember our experience very fondly and would recommend this place to anyone with an appreciation for Italian/innovative cuisine.

Welcome to Moe's great friendly staff but food is just so so. It's good if you just need something fast and decent on the healthy scale if you still want flavor and of you choose less toppings. My only issue is the meat is like a tables spoon of chicken or maybe maybe...2 tablespoons but they don't give much meat and of course if you want more they charge you. Very minimal on the meat though.
Chick fil a sets their standards high, so this location really missed the mark. Waited SO long for my food (on a Tuesday night), only to receive overcooked fries.

You know, I'm super conflicted about this location. I went with a friend of mine during the last weekend of Sonoran Restaurant Week and got there right when it opened. Our waitress gave us a tour of the new space and walked us through the menu items and wine pairings. She was fantastic! My friend and I each ordered different appetizers, entrees, and dessert, and watched as the restaurant quickly filled up. Before I knew it, the restaurant was at capacity. This was exciting to see, but not exciting to dine in. They definitely placed more tables and chairs in the space than should be allowed and my friend and I constantly had to scoot our chairs in to not get bumped by the service staff or other customers. We were polite, but after the fifth or so bump, it felt a bit excessive.

Finally the food arrived -- frog legs, green been salad, eggplant risotto, roast chicken, burrata & melon, and pannacotta. The presentation itself was meh, which I don't usually care about but after eating at several other restaurants for Sonoran Restaurant Week plating became an additional fun thing I enjoyed seeing considering how much we were paying. Additionally, the serving size was lacking. To be honest, most of the dishes tasted bland and under-seasoned, with the risotto being the only dish I would eat again. It was deliciously creamy and tasted fresh, which was surprising considering it looked like someone dumped a box of instant rice onto a plate. 

I would go back because the happy hour drinks look bomb and our waitress killed it, but honestly I would rather spend my money on a handful of other high-class Tucson dining experiences.

If I could rate lower I would.  Today I visited the Chipotle location on Gandy Blvd. in Tampa Florida.  I have visited this location several times since it has opened and always left in disappointment.  Today will be the last time I ever visit.  When I visited today, I stood waiting for an employee to help me, yet there was no one in the restaurant.  The man finally came over and asked what I wanted.  I explained I wanted a chicken bowl.  I had to ask for more rice since in the past the portions barely filled a quarter of the bowl.  I asked for black beans which appeared to have been sitting out all day.  I requested fajitas (peppers and onions) however the container was left with small and shriveled remnants.  I asked if there were any fresh ones being prepared and he said yes, stating it will only take a minute. I proceeded to confirm that I wanted chicken. He literally only scooped out enough chicken to only fill the tip of the spoon. This equated to approximately 7 tiny, dry, pieces of chicken in my bowl. He then proceeded to finish the rest of the bowl with the ingredients I desired, however the bowl was left open waiting for the peppers and onions to finish.  I waited for approximately 5 minutes after realizing my bowl was getting cold.  I just asked to box it up without the peppers and onions since it was probably getting cold. I asked for a side of the green salsa which he filled approximately a third of the way full in the cup. I then leave and return home. Sure enough by the time I got home (half a mile away) it was in fact ice cold.  As I sit here and type this, I feel sick to my stomach since I believe the ingredients were old and not fresh.  Based on the bad reputation Chipotle has recently received in the media by directly causing patrons to get e coli, one would think that the Chipotle experience would be rated highly in order to restore their reputation.  However, I am here now questioning if I will ever return to another Chipotle.  It is unfortunate since I have been frequenting Chipotles for over 10 years.

Kale crunch consisted of 3 pieces of kale and no crunch

Cold chicken sandwich.

No drink.

I would say your chance of success at any
 Chick-fil-A in Tampa is 50/50.

Do better.

Very frustrating to sit in drive through line for 20+ min on 2nd Chick fil a locations only to be told you did not have any ice cream for shakes and then could not get out of line for another 10 min. This is ridiculous. Tried to call but no one answers phone at location to tell if you ice cream and your app says only order drive through. Called Chick-fil-a cares and had to wait on hold for over 10 min to tell someone about experience that really lacked empathy and just said ok I will tell management.

Terrible customer service, lazy workers, and lackluster portion size.  There's no management on-site and staff runs amuck without a care in the world.  Avoid this chipotle location or drive up the street to Qdoba or Tijuana flats.

If you're looking to get shortchanged portions and overcharged, come to this Chipotle and waste your money!

I hope the owners see this review. I would like for the owners and managers to have a little more respect for their junior employees. I went in for lunch, to walk up to a door that had stated " thank you for your safety", followed by a paragraph of small text, uninviting information stating that this branch has updated mask mandates for all guests, including the vaccinated. As the manager went to the back during rush hour, the junior employees had to continuously put up with guests not coming in with a mask. The employees became enforcers, continuously having to speak up to older adults almost every single time one walk Into the door. I could see the exhaustion on these junior employees as they had to often get in back and forth talking. They shouldn't have to be enforcers and servers if your leaders could put up a clear,legible, and straight to the point sign on the door saying maybe..." Masks required".

I really liked the layout of the space. Nice mix of contemporary and rustic italian decor.  We got there for a 5pm Saturday seating, which is awesome because there were no crowds and we got the full attention of the waitstaff.  The way the tables were placed very close together, I suspect we would have felt claustrophobic it the house was packed.

As for the food, it was very satisfying. The squid ink pasta had a hint of the pier in it's aroma, which I like.  The rotini with black trumpet mushroom was out of this world. The herb butter sauce truly highlighted the texture and shape of the handmade spiral pasta.
The kale side dish and the eggplant caponata were decent and well executed, but not anything unique.
By far, the star of the meal was the sweetbreads with almond dust and fennel jam.  The breading was was light and airy, the sweetbreads themselves were unbelievably creamy, and the jam was very subtly tart, and perfectly balanced the entire dish. 
I would seriously get two orders of this dish next time around!

I am a fan of all the Marc Vetri Restaurants and can not wait for him to keep opening up more. I was at Amis on friday night and once again, it did not disappoint.

This place is always packed so reservations are necessary. Even with reservations, you may need to wait a few minutes but, for my group, it was friday and we were happy with having some cocktails at the bar. 

I was thrilled with the table they seated us at. One of my complaints has always been how close they seat you to other tables but our table was sort of off in the corner with plenty of room. 

There are a few highlights at Amis that I must mention. First, they have my favorite preparation of sweetbreads that I've ever had. They're almond dusted, fried and served with an orange fenel marmalade. They are juicy on the inside, crispy on the outside and the marmalade adds an awesome sweet flavor to a salty dish. YUM!
That aside, the pastas are always a highlight as well. My favorite pasta this time was a rigatoni with a wild mushroom ragu. The pasta was aldente and the ragu was creamy, salty and delicious...especially if you love mushrooms like me.

From here, there were two seafood dishes that blew my mind. The skate wing and the swordfish meatballs. HOLY skate wing. They dust it in this super fine flour and pan fry it just to give a little texture, serving it with a lemon butter sauce with fried brussel sprouts...very approachable. The flavors and textures in this dish were heaven. I could eat this dish all the time and be happy. After that, the swordfish meatballs. YUM! The meatballs just fell apart when you touched them and were perfectly tender and juicy, served over some creamy polenta. 

The only thing I wasn't crazy about for this meal were the desserts. They were good but not great. Honestly, I can't even remember what we had but everything else was so delicious, it doesn't even matter!

Food was good.  Great ambience, good staff and busy on a tuesday night (usually a good sign).

Had high expectations for this place and I think it fulfilled most of them.  Pasta was al dente and meats tasted fresh (Wild Boar special - brought in that morning).  Cocktails were ok, but could be a bit more exciting.  The food itself reminded me of my visit to Italy which made the meal a little more enjoyable.

I would give 4.5 stars if possible because price was great for the amount of food and service.  3 apps, 1 pasta, 1 entree and 3 cocktails = $115.  Thats a bargain for a great dining experience in the city.

Left feeling happy and complete.  That is all!

Come here ever morning for breakfast. Friendliest staff, always prompt with my order. Food is always fresh and consistent. They actually remember my order by just saying my name at the drive thru. Amazing staff!

After having been told that this is the "Jewel in the crown " of restaurants in Tucson I went expecting,at least, not to leave hungry. Not only did that not happen but I can honestly say that this was the most disappointing dining experience in my five-year experience of exploring new restaurants throughout Tucson. I was privileged to have been a restaurant reviewer in the Hamptons on Long Island and enjoyed some remarkable meals throughout that time. In all of my years I have never been so disappointed. I can only begin by mentioning that the potato leek soup was appalling. The presentation was of large chunks of potato floating in a meager amount of liquid with charred remains of cauliflower floating on top. Thinking perhaps I might be missing something I made the mistake of trying the cauliflower and found it to be nothing more than burnt remnants. The artichoke hearts were tasty but not appetizingly displayed. The extra-charge baguette was at least a day old if not older. There were no butter plates provided. In general the service was not thoughtful. They were out of the steel head that was used for their signature dish and they offered a replacement of Seabass. My husband is 6 foot two and the portion was adequate for a five-year-old. Our dining partners ordered the squab and it was unappetizingly displayed, overcooked and in general tasteless. There were no vegetables served as an accoutrement. The plates were all small plates sized even though the pricing and the description were that of a full dinner. All in all, not only will I never go back but I hope that the dining public takes note and lets the owners be aware of their shortcomings. Take this review to heart and dine elsewhere.

Arizona bug doctor is the absolute best for pest control. They have helped me multiple times in emergency situations. Terry is the sweetest and is always so quick at getting back to me to me. Matt does an awesome job and is very thorough. I've had scorpion problems and he always triple checks my house to make sure my family is good! I would most definitely recommend Arizona bag doctor

Would give this a 0 star if I could but I don't even know where to begin. Multiple times now have I had to wait over a half hour for my scheduled pick up, not to mentioned the food is dry and disgusting. They never have salad dressing for the salads which is kinda the point of ordering a salad. The best part is the carefree staff that is full of attitude. This location is an absolute joke and whoever is in charge should be ashamed, but it's definitely not the manager because he has the worst attitude of them all. Go to Qdoba down the street or even Taco Bell, this place is awful

I can't even give a star! Kyle is a manager why!????
He is the rudest most inconsiderate person ever.
Why would you have a mother of twins in a double stroller wait in line in the drive through with gas fumes blowing in their face so they can eat. 
Kids are screaming crying for food but would not get service. 
P. s. Our car was across the street at Honda getting serviced that's why we couldn't use our car. 
Very frustrated Christian mother.
Thanks for your help Kyle!!!!!

This is my local Chipotle and it is a great option for me when I need something quick and just a bit healthier. I will usually do a salad or a bowl. This location can get busy and often times it is not because of the number of people trying to get their chipotle fix, it is typically because the staff is SOOOOOOOOOO SLOWWWWWWWW! I also feel like this location does skimp on everything. The next closest Chipotle definitely gives me more food in my bowls than this location. Aside from this the food is generally good. I like the barbacoa meat! The fajita veggies are also great! 

I rarely eat in although I do not mind it as this location is pretty clean. If you are in no rush and in the mood for Americanized Mexican food then this is your place to eat!
Would have given 5 stars, but the noise level is unacceptable.  Loved the food, service was great, but too noisy.

Food is okay but most of the staff has a bad attitude. I understand nobody wants to work and keeping an establishment like chipotle staffed must be difficult but it is not an excuse for poor attitude and customer service.

We were very underwhelmed with Amis. Between 3 of us, we spent about $280, including food, drinks, tax and tip. The drinks good. The limontella was really good but very sweet so hard to drink more than one. The food was not so good. Of about 8 plates, we were happy with two. The oxtail gnocchi and the arancinis were good. We ordered the octopus and it was awful. We actually sent it back. It tasted like frozen octopus with no flavor and basically dissolved in our mouths. The snail bruschetta was way too salty. The stuffed clams lacked flavor and were too salty as well. We began talking to the table next to us when they saw us send back a plate. They too said their food wasn't good. For dessert, the server was raving about the tiramisu. It tasted like whipped cream with cinnamon on top. He also said his favorite dessert was the pear tart. It was awful. It had no flavor. The mint leat on top was completely wilted as if it had been sitting in the fridge for a week. For a $10 dessert, the garnish should never be wilted, and I think the lack of freshness in the garnish really carried over through the whole meal. I will definitely not be returning.

Messed up my order. Twice. Pulled over to wait. Took 30 minutes for a chicken wrap. What takes 30 minutes at a fast food restaurant? Manager shrugged his shoulders and said "do you still want it?". If I paid for it what type of question is that? Chicken wrap was put together sloppy and tasted stale. What is this?

We recently went to Amis to celebrate a friend's graduation.  I was so impressed with this restaurant, that it is now one of the top recommendations I give to people looking to have a lovely dinner.  We had a large party, so we had to wait for a specific table to be seated at.  Despite our reservation, the people who were at the table took a VERY long time.  The people obviously did not have diner's etiquette when eating at a restaurant during the weekend, because they took their sweet time.  Amis handled the situation delicately, and ensured us they would make it right.  Because rude diners are unfortunately out of the control of the restaurant, the Amis staff did their best to accommodate our party and the party that greatly overstayed their welcome.  We have been to many restaurants throughout the city, and any other restaurant would have taken the attitude of if you don't want to wait, then leave.  But, Amis was different.  They were caring and committed to having us as customers.  Now to the food...everything was so delicious!  The pecorino, the pasta, the bread, the desserts -- everything.  Amis did make it right, and we happily celebrated a wonderful occasion with delicious food at lovely Amis.

Consistently not providing sauces requested and salsa that comes with burritos.  Chic Fil A has become inconsistent overall and starting to become more like Burger King and others.   I expect better and if this continues I will take my business elsewhere.

The barrio bread and canned tuna pate saved the evening.  The rest of the cooked menu items were bland.  We had the burgers and the half hen.  Will more than likely not return unless they season them correctly or change the menu.  Service was average.  Social distancing norms enforced.

The cookies are prob the best thing they have here. Ive had the cake and the donuts and they are just eh. 

The cakes are too sweet, and the icing they use has a strange taste. 

My family loves this bakery, but they are so hit or miss with their baked goods.

Drive through only when they have one of the worst drive through set ups in the country. Doesn't have enough staff to support the demand. No indoor dining or curbside pick up either. What's the point of coming here if it's going to take over an hour to get a chicken sandwich?

Third time walking out. Why? Because their food is disgustingly displayed. This is by far the worst chipotle I have seen. Every time I go I want to believe it will be a different experience but every time it's progress my worse. The line is a complete disaster. It makes me want to throw up. The beans are splattered everywhere! Their cheese (queso) and sour cream is touching their not fresh shredded lettuce, fajitas, and on their chicken!!! I have a severe dairy allergy. This is NOT okay. My boyfriend has a severe avocado (Guacamole) allergy that would call for hospitalization. In this world more people have food allergies than not. 

I also filed a complaint to the Better Business Bureau for this specific location. 

Never coming back to this location. BRING THE CEO IN!!!!!

The staff here is beyond rude. You could truly tell how deeply they did not want to be here, and did not care. 

Orders were wrong - Pork instead of steak, no lettuce when asked. Fountain drinks were completely out of order. No changing table in the oddly huge bathroom.

Busy and stressed out and still Top notch service all around!  My burritos were exceptionally large and not rollable. A more seasoned vet stepped in to complete it using two shells. Great teaching moment and fun to watch. Always fantastic food for the price!!

Stay away from this place. Purchased a couch in March'21 with an expected delivery date within 4-6 weeks. Just before memorial day it was another 4 weeks. Mid-June I was told it was another 2-4 weeks. July 4th came and still nothing. I had to dispute with AMEX since they would not provide a delivery window after being pushed around. Customer service is horrible, especially Neesha, an old woman who can't speak English should never be on the phones. Thankfully I got my money back from AMEX. This place is disgusting and the people are even worse to deal with. Awful

Thankfully, the standard Chipotle.
The South Tampa area has gone downhill for almost every dining establishment over the past couple of years; but this Chipotle at the intersection of Dale Mabry and Gandy was fully staffed, and serving to the standards of other Chipotles pre-COVID.
I ordered a carnivals burrito, and it was tasty and loaded. 
The line moved fast, and the workers were professional and friendly.
Would have been five stars of the order line was a bit cleaner; but I am sure it is the norm these days, with all the online and Door Dash orders.
Always busy.

Great place for watching a game--or games! There are multiple TVs on all of the walls and they're all big screens. I also liked how big and spacious the restaurant looks while being able to seat so many people. I also liked the football helmet and framed Jerseys and picture decorations throughout the whole restaurant. Moreover, their menu is great as well. They have vegetarian and gluten sensitive options. As far as drinks they have daily specials of 2 for 1 drinks (see menu picture). I liked the grilled shrimp and if you want to spice it up a little you can ask for one of the sauces for the wings on the side. I got the honey garlic sauce and it was delicious!
Great bakery everything is always delicious! They did a great job on my granddaughters birthday cake.

As Namir S. said a few days ago, "mixed feelings". I completely agree about the ambiance and music clashing. The music said night club but the dark lighting and set up of the restaurant were attempting to keep its trattoria vibe. My family and I had 7pm reservations, which in hindsight we didn't really need. It was steady but never overly busy.

We were sat on the left side of the restaurant next to a large group celebrating a birthday. That was fine with us as it was my sister's birthday too. The service wasn't particularly great; it wasn't awful, but it definitely was apathetic and worthy of only 3 stars. Our server wasn't very helpful with the menu and seemed more worried about the other tables in the section. 

We started with the swordfish meatballs (saying that shows the date of my visit; it looks like they've changed the meatball options on the antipasti menu), mozzarella and baked pecorino because there's no such thing as too much cheese. The mozzarella was fine and dandy, but the baked pecorino was the real star. I can see why they keep it year round. The almond honey mixed with the cheese was divine. I wonder if they do anything else to it because if not I'd assuming it's easy to re-create at home. I didn't try the meatballs but my parents seemed to enjoy them. My dad said they were cooked well and he finished the majority of it.

For the entrees, we split the veal chop, rigatoni, and chestnut ravioli. All three entrees were delicious in their own right. However, none of us thought these dishes were any more of a standout than the other. I do firmly believe I could have received the same type of quality food at the modern Italian restaurants in my own city. We also ordered a side of the crispy brussels sprouts. Now those were worth writing home about! I've noticed that the items I thought were the best are the ones that stay on the menu year round. Perhaps they know what menu items really shine and keep them, then they experiment with everything else? I wouldn't be surprised if so.

Had the service been more attentive, I probably would have given Amis 4 stars. The server, as stated before, seemed more interested in the large party behind us and we fell to the way side. My mother asked for the dessert she ordered (rice pudding) to come out with the entrees as she was more keen on the dessert. That request was completely ignored and he didn't seem very apologetic when she was upset that it came out in a bag at the end of the meal. He wasn't around after our entrees came to ask where the dessert was. Also, and I know this is a bit of a personal vendetta I have, but I stated in the OpenTable reservation that we were celebrating my sister's birthday. Apparently it was a celebration for everyone in the building because multiple tables received desserts with candles. It just kind of sucked that I put it in the notes and it wasn't recognized since they were recognizing practically everyone else.

I wouldn't come here again. There are far too many nice restaurant concepts in Philadelphia to consider eating here. It doesn't seem to live up to the standards of a Marc Vetri restaurant. To be honest, I wouldn't see it lasting if it didn't have his name attached to it. I would rather spend my money at Scarpetta.

Best food ! First let's start with the atmosphere! Outside it's got a great ambiance with lights! The waiter was Steven , he was very attentive answering all questions! Even ones that didn't involve the menu ! We asked about the ice skating near by and he looked it up for us ! Next let's talk about the level of food ! 5 stars doesn't give the chef justification! The dishes are very different yet so delish ! If your looking to put your money where your mouth is then ,you should try it !

Fantastic carrot cake, desserts, soups and European style breads. Made a mid evening trip across town for dinner and loaves of bread for myself and neighbor. Had several issues with the guy at register getting my order prepared, collected, and bagged. The soup and extra sides of bread and butter were left out of bags I took home for dinner. Wait time was above average. I called about the missing and charged soup, etc. Store manager Frank said he would look into the matter. Frank called me back that same evening after speaking with the general manager and all was made whole and well in a very prompt and pleasant and professional manner. FYI - I asked for a loaf of raisin bread and received a round loaf of very rustic whole wheat raisin bread. I'll have to see if that is it for raisin bread on the menu on my next visit. Too dry and heavy for my taste. Thanks BB.

The black linguine with squid and chorizo and tartufo al bacio dessert are stellar. If you eat at Amis and don't partake in these items, then you have permanently sullied the quality of your life.

I don't really recommend the imported bufala ricotta and black pepper bruschetta.

The salami del giorno with marmalade is good. The salami is thicker than you'd expect and the marmalade adds a delightful sweetness.

The grouper is OK.

I got here at exactly 6:25am since I had to be at work no later than 6:45 (was like 7 minutes away). Three cars in front of me in line. I wanted to order a chicken biscuit for breakfast but they said they didn't have biscuits.... Lol what? The day just started. I ended up getting chicken minis, and left at 6:43am. One of my chicken minis didn't have the chicken in it. Great experience!!!! I was late to work, didn't get to order what I wanted, and what I did was missing part of it.

Not updating this review sooner has been a complete oversight.  I've actually been back four or five times since my first visit, and Amis has become one of my favorite destinations for dining and/or drinks.

There are several things on the menu that I have come to absolutely adore, starting with the strozzaprete alla vongole, its buttery flavors I have talked up to just about anyone who will listen.  Another favorite is the bufala ricotta; rich and creamy and drizzled with olive oil, it is the perfect spread for the accompanying toasted bread.  

I was once offered a bite of the turkey cutlet by a distinguished gentleman sitting next to me at the bar.  Normally, I'd pass without thinking twice, but this man insisted that the preparation changed his previous contempt for turkey to pure lust, at least, for this particular dish.  Who could pass that up?  I have to hand it to the guy, he was right on.  It sounds crazy to order something so plain-sounding, but trust Vetri and his crew to turn a plain old turkey into a Cinderella story.  A turkerella, if you will.

Make your reservations far in advance, dolls.  The tables don't come easy!
The worst customer service I have experienced on multiple occasions. The food is sub par and the staff acts as if they work at the French laundry.

My wife and I ate hotpot in Ochatto yesterday night. Let me start with telling you the good things about Ochatto. The venue is nicely decorated. Due to the high ceiling, it does not feel cramped. The food is also up to expectations. We enjoyed the soup bases in particular. We order three of them: the tomato soup, the Tom Yum soup, and mushroom soup with pork broth.

That brings us to the negative parts of the Ochatto experience. The waiters are blunt. It was quiet when we came in, but we had to wait for ten minutes for a waiter to order something. We waved at waiters that were just standing, but they were unwilling to help us because another waiter was apparently responsible for our table. I can understand that the restaurant assigns tables to waiters, but in quiet times, the personnel should be more flexible. What makes it even more ridiculous is that the assignment was suddenly ignored when it was time for us to pay. Another waiter than our assigned easier presented us the check. It was also strange that the pork broth was mentioned as vegetarian soup on the check. 

Another annoyance is that the restaurant does not have air suction above the hotpot like other restaurants. I agree that it does not look pretty, but lack thereof makes it hard for people with glasses to operate the hotpot at times as glasses tend to fog up when the steam flows in their direction. Moreover, all your clothes smell like soup after a visit. Finally, a decent hotpot restaurant should provide tongs for the raw meat. Expecting the customers to use their chopsticks to handle the meat is unhygienic. It took several times of asking to get just one tong. Well, I'm not shy to reduce my tip for lousy service. 

All in all, I have mixed feelings about this place. I might come back for the food, but not for the service.

Came for New Years. It was an expensive prix fixe and I understand a busy day for the kitchen staff.

I'm vegetarian and they had vegetarian an explicit option. But turned out I just got stale cold bread, cold fried things that were just oil cause they were fried at least hours earlier and beets. Many many beets. No sauce or preparation just boiled beets 

For dessert was a "chocolate mousse" which was at best brownie mix if you cooked the eggs in the batter. If I accidentally made that at home I wouldn't even eat it myself, it would go straight to the garbage.

And to top it off we were rushed the entire time, next course came immediately when they took away the last course. And then after 90min they told us to leave cause another party had a reservation. 

Hope they get new chefs in 2022

I have been excited to try their brunch for over a year and finally got the opportunity this weekend. 3 of us went on a Sunday at 12. There were plenty of tables if you wanted to walk-in. We started with the honey ricotta bruschetta. For our entree's we shared the waffle and ice-cream, eggs an polenta with prosciutto and the signature pasta dish with pesto and walnuts with a side of bacon. Everything was good, different I would say for brunch and I would recommend.

Bar Asia is a nice addition to the Tampa food scene.

The restaurant serves up a creative spin on Vietnamese cuisine, traditional Asian classics, and sushi.  

For our starter, we tried the Korean style sweet soy wings.  The sauce was really good and not too sweet, but the wings tasted frozen and were way too big for my liking.

For the main course, we tried the Bahn Mi and Rice Bowl.  Both dishes were really good and full of flavor.  

I also like that they have wine on tap but unfortunately the varietals are limited.

The open kitchen concept is cool.  The restaurant also has an indoor/outdoor bar and it's own parking lot that must be accessed from Cleveland Street.  

The owner was cool.

Check it out.

To start, I am a huge fan of chick-fil-a eating here 5-7 times a week for breakfast or lunch. I pass 2 other chick-fil-a on my way to work because I enjoy the morning staff at this location.  It just seems like the proprietor is making poor decisions at this location. For example, I ordered my normal breakfast this morning & asked for a large cup of water & ice (which I have done every week since they opened). The Employee at the drive thru window told me they no longer give large cups of water, only medium cups. I thought this was a corporate decision so I decided to grab lunch at another location.  Sure enough, they gave me a large cup of water & a large cup of ice without the slightest problem.   Needless to say, my money each week will now be going to another chick-fil-a, one that appreciates customer service more so than trying to cut costs. So ridiculous!!!

Okay, I am not sure if I did a review on this location. If not, I truly apologize. Its been very hectic with lifestyle lately so I am about to a lot of reviews today. 

I have been to many Chipotle Mexican Grills and always hope that my next location would be better than the first time. I think I just need to quit going to any establishment altogether. 

The tofu was very spicy, almost too spicy for me to eat with my bowl. The food was mediocre I can say the least. I will not be back to any Chipotle Mexican Grill.

Meh. The service was lovely, the food very good but the price point for the portions was lackluster. The space is beautifully done but so incredibly loud it was hard to hear our friends and there were only a total of 4 of us. My husband and I ordered the Fluke Crudo for an appetizer and while delicious the portion was absurdly light. My husband had the Wild Boar shells which he said were amazing, I had the Caccio de Pepe which was good but for $18 didnt really blow me away. Our friends, who we took there to celebrate their engagement seemed to like their food but didn't seem floored by it either. Could offer a bit more cocktail options as well. We liked it but with so many stellar Italian options in the city with better portion to price point ratio, we wont be racing back anytime soon.

This review reflects my first of what will probably be many experiences at Amis, especially if my guy has anything to do with it. We stopped in for drinks and some light bites after our recent class at Tria's Fermentation School. At 8:30 on a weeknight, mostly all the tables were full so we opted for one of the high tops near the bar. The environment of Amis is the antithesis to that of Osteria. Amis is cozier, darker and sexier. 

A basket of soft focaccia was dropped at our table. Later, it was replaced by a different type of bread. I love, love, love bread and I enjoyed the variety. 

We started with the pecorino trio, a salami (I can't recall the exact name) and the ricotta. One of the selections on the pecorino plate seemed a bit dry, as if it had been stored incorrectly, but we really enjoyed the others, particularly the softest of the three. The salami was studded with pieces of peppercorn and had a nice consistency, but the flavors were not as abundant as I expected. The ricotta was the clear winner in this first round; a heaping pile of the snow white cheese glistened with olive oil and was specked with black pepper. It was heavenly, and will certainly be ordered again on our next visit and should be a mandatory part of everyone's first visit. 

We also ordered the stuffed clams and oxtail gnocchi. The clams were very good - almost as good as my grandmother's but not quite. They had an interesting flavor which made me wonder what exactly went into the preparation. The gnocchi was delicious and extremely rich. A few delectable bites was all I could handle on top of the other splurges of the evening. 

We didn't have room for dessert but I definitely look forward to checking those options out soon. I'm going with three stars for my first experience but am looking forward to trying more of the menu.
We had delicious food, not at all an ordinary menu.  Our service was also friendly and quick.  No complaints at all.  Will be back.

The Coronet's new home is the perfect evolution for one of Tucson's top restaurants. 

Everything that I loved at the original location is even better.

My most favorite coffee shop near USF. The honey bear latte is my go-to - delicious! The staff is always really friendly. It's a little hard to find seating sometimes but it's only bc their coffee is so good!

The cuisine portions are smaller than usual but the flavor of each bite you take is exquisite! Your palette will enjoy how the chef marries the different tastes of each flavor that leaves your mouth wanting more!  The servers are kind and knowledgeable. I spent more money here than I have for anything that I would classify as an appetizer! However, I would come back in a heart beat!

This restaurant is built in a warehouse style building and looks like it could have been a nightclub before opening as Bar Asia. I did not order sushi, because they sell Krab instead of Crab (so does virtually every sushi restaurant in Tampa).

But I came here for the bowls, this restaurant recently opened, and I waited about a month hoping that the kitchen would work things out. Unfortunately, the food took a very long time, almost an hour from the time that we ordered. The waiter did not apologize for the delay and our water cups remained empty throughout our visit. 

Parking is a bit tricky, although there is a small lot behind the restaurant, I could not enter the lot from Howard. I had to drive around to park. A sign would have been nice.

I ordered the lemon grass chicken bowl and the flavors were very good, but there was not 8 ounces of chicken as advertised. It was mainly  vermicelli noodles with some pickled carrots and cucumbers. One can fill up on noodles because the other ingredients were scarce. The siracha aioli sauce was heavy on the mayonnaise. Maybe they should remove the portion size from the menus. I do think that this restaurant may improve, hence the 3 stars.  If I return I will order the Banh Mi.

Wow, just seriously wow!
Now I knew I was going to enjoy The Coronet, it has always been a fantastic spot. 
But this new space just fits them so well. It's so Tucson, yet the eclectic blend of furnishings and decor mirror the uniqueness of their menu.

I think it was the best Chicken dish I have ever had. No joke. The best. 
The wine menu actually delivers diversity! From deep dark reds, and full whites, to light zippy whites and bright reds. The cocktail program is equally as impressive.

If you are looking for one of the best dining experiences in Tucson...look no further.

I have never been so disappointed by a Chipotle. I ordered a burrito bowl and chips and guac for delivery. When my food came, it was messy, my bowl had like three pieces of lettuce on it, and my guac wasn't there. Well, I called the Chipotle to see if I could just get my money back for the guac. Not only did she tell me it was the Uber Eats delivery driver's fault for not checking and making sure the order was right, but she refused to accept responsibility for their part in the mixup and acted like I was an idiot when she was telling me that DoorDash and Uber Eats are the same thing (they're not).  She also told me the only way I could get my money back was if I came into the store (in the middle of a pandemic). Forgetting the guac wasn't a huge deal and I could look past the rest of the issues with my order, but the customer service is just terrible and I won't be back to this location. It's a bummer, too...I love Chipotle.

Last night I tried out South Howard's newest addition, Bar Asia. It was the soft opening so there were a few bumps throughout the service, but I will give them the benefit of the doubt and return once the full menu is offered.

The good: I loved my meal! I started off my meal with a glass of Italian Cabernet. It was a lighter Cabernet, very drinkable, and reasonably priced at $7 per glass. For an appetizer we selected the crispy spring rolls. The rolls were lightly fried and paired with a tangy fish sauce, cucumbers, and carrots. Once I saw several of the tacos were not yet available on the menu I decided on the Fresh Bowl with Shaking Beef and a sriracha aioli, served over vermicelli noodles. The bowl was huge and packed with flavor from the pickled onion, crushed peanuts, fresh cilantro, and crunchy vegetables.

The bad: I have a sinking feeling that the indoor/outdoor wraparound bar is going to make the restaurant miserably humid in the summer. The menu prices were all over the place ($4 tacos, $15 bowls, and $17 to $38 entrees). The sushi prices are on the high side, even by South Tampa standards. While the food was delicious I didn't feel like I was in a high-end restaurant and I think the restaurant is going to find that most diners are not looking to drop $50 for dinner in a bar like atmosphere. 

I won't dock Bar Asia a star for offering a limited menu and no printed cocktail menu, but both of these issues need to be immediately addressed if they wish to be successful. I'll give Bar Asia another chance once they are running at full capacity. This restaurant has a lot of potential.

Came in here on a Tuesday night with reservations for two.  We had to wait a LONG time (30+ minutes) because we didn't want to sit at the chef's counter.  They were very nice and apologetic, and even gave us glasses of wine and some appetizers.  The food was delicious - I'm a fan of simple dishes and loved the cacio e pepe and the mozarella with pears.  The bread pudding was the star of the meal.  I'll definitely come back - but hopefully on a night when it's a little less busy.

There are very few places like this restaurant. I have to say that its a must try. Even plates are little small, everything very tasty and charming. Frog legs is a must try for someone who never tried. Loved this place certainly will come back.

This bakery has been on the decline for years now.  I gave it four more chances in the past year.  The selection is always minimal.  Two chocolate chip pound cakes bought recently from the display case proved dry and unappealing.  One chocolate chip pound cake pre-ordered for a graduation party was delicious.  One pound cake loaf outside of the display case was dry.

I will avoid going to this bakery whenever possible.

The worst.
----------------------
$10 for some skin.
--------------------
Run!
------------------
What's the minimum character limit for a Yelp review?

After blowing our food budget for the week on a special night out last night, we were left with fast food for super tonight. This chick fil a is a bit strange and the dining room was really noisy and people seeming to move at random patterns through out the room ... it was distracting. The food was as expected, and was served quickly and our orders were accurately filled. There is a nice patio outside, but it was like 90 degrees and 85 percent humidity, so we stayed inside ... otherwise we would have been outside in a heartbeat.

This was the dirtiest Chick Fil A I've ever been to. All their empty tables were dirty, and there was trash all over the floor. I ordered the specialty tea, and by the time I got it, I was already done with my meal. This experience really turned me off to chick Fil a.

Another great Chick-fil-A. I highly recommend getting the number one which is a Chick-fil-A sandwich with a large fry and a large sweet tea don't forget to ask for Chick-fil-A sauce to dip your fries. I'm so glad to see your new location. You're still working the kinks out here I had to wait About 10 minutes longer than I should have for My Mobile order. Staff Is very courteous even though they were slammed

Very good Italian food. The pasta was fresh, not dried, so really good and chewy. The vegetables (zucchini, cauliflower, I forget what else) were pretty salty, but in a flavorful way. The fish was tender and moist. The rice pudding was good and plentiful. The only thing that neither my friend nor I liked was the olive oil cake. It's a strange flavor to get used to.

The best part about Chik-Fil-A is consistency; I've been eating here for years all over the country and yet to have a bad meal. That being said, this location has messed up my order the last THREE times I have been here thru Drive Thru. The food is still good and the staff is friendly and considering it's close to my house I keep giving it a shot but CFA prides itself on being a step above the competition on service and I think they should make some changes at this location to work on improving their service to not give a black eye to the brand. I'll give it another shot but if they don't deliver what I've ordered I'll spend my money elsewhere.
Chic Fil A PLEASE restructure the drive thru lines of traffic for this location!!!  There is not enough space in this parking lot!!  Thank you!
There is always something missing from my order here. Unreal. Whether it's a sauce, portion size, something, odds are your order will be screwed up. Go to the one nearby at the mall.

This seems to be the most chaotic Chick-Fil-A in Tampa. I don't know what's going on, but the staff always seems to be confused and totally lost. Missing items, wrong orders, and delayed wait time are just a few of the issues that consistently occur at this location. I placed a mobile order, went in 30 min later, and still had to wait ANOTHER 30 minutes. I place mobile orders every time I go to Chick-Fil-A and have never had an issue. Thankfully, Reggenae was understanding and made sure my order was fulfilled while serving  other customers. 

I used to blame their mistakes on the high volume of customers, but EVERY Chick-Fil-A is busy, so  there really is no excuse. This location is in a great spot, and I'd really like to see it become more organized and better managed.

Let me start by saying that my reservation at Amis was for 9:30pm on a Saturday night for a party of 6.  Our party strolled in a few minutes late and was told by the hostess that the party before us was running late and it would be a few minutes till our large table would be ready.  It turned out that the party before us decided not to leave...

Amis then made us a makeshift table and comped us about 4 or 5 appetizers. I thought that was really swell of them.  All the food was magnificent, especially the swordfish meatballs and salumi plate. Their carafe of house wine was also superb.  My main course meal was the pork parmesan and it was the best piece of pork I've had in a long time. 

Other reviews have mentioned spotty / rude service.  We did not receive any of that and all of our servers, waiters and even the manager were the friendliest.  I would definitely go again and highly recommend.

Please do not go here!! Everyone has additudes and noone has name tags on... I got cussed out by one of the Employees!! So of course I cuss back and I look like the bad guy!! Needless to say everyone there needs to get another job because I will not be treated the way I was!! Horrible service PLEASE DO NOT GO HERE!!

marc vetri is like, a superstar in my eyes.  my birthday experience at osteria last year with my bestie was one of my favorite meals ever.
so i came to amis with higher than high expectations, and i think that was its downfall.  

the space is cozy, cute, perfect.  really.  i walked in, promptly greeted, and was already a little bit happier.  we sat at the counter (which is how we roll) and it all started going downhill from there.
the plus was watching the every-bustling kitchen, which is always fun.
i had the fried artichokes, buccatini, seafood fritto (apparently i was on a fried kick)... my friend had the olives and seared tuna.

everything was good...  but no dish made me scream and yell and want to go back for more.

the waiter was extremely awkward, making me feel like i was somehow a nuisance or something.  he never offered tastes of wine, just so we could figure out what we wanted to drink (which i feel like is a must at this price point).

the crowning moment was the hair found among my too-soggy tiramisu, which it took prompting by the kitchen for the server to notice.  he took it away (thankfully)... but instead of asking if i wanted another, or a replacement, he just silently dropped off another bill with the dessert taken off.  really?  isn't your job to talk and be friendly?

and in the end, my bill came out to be about the same as osteria, but my experience here was not even half.  sad.

Upon hearing that ramps were in town  I made a mad dash for an early Sunday dinner to Amis. Again ensconced at the end of the bar, I had a very nice simple meal, beginning with the root vegetables served on a bed of yogurt flavored with curry. More middle eastern than Italian, but very good. The swordfish meatballs were outstanding. You got delicious fish, with punches of flavor from pignoli and raisins, served on a bed of polenta. Outstanding.  The highlight of the meal was the linguini with ramps and pecorino. Simple and flavorful, the ramps shined amid the al dente pasta and cheese. Dessert was a home made italian pumpkin ice cream. Delicious. Amis does things simply and lets flavors come through. Get there while the ramps are still rampant.
This closed curbside pickup drive thru only. Why would do that on work day. I hate coming to this location every time there's something.

If you need to do a little 'spring cleaning,' then this location is for you!  Honestly, I have never had food this bad before in my life. Beans were mushy, rice was crunchy, and practically everything else needed salsa and hot sauce to create flavor. Oh. And the sprint to the toilet in 10 mins after finishing the meal.  Not good.
Nothing adds up about this location. It's in a great spot with lots of traffic, yet they employ people who play on their phones and lack any energy to do their job.  They seemed annoyed that I was there to order a meal. I really tried to give this another try but yet again they failed. And again, their AC still doesn't work.
I always enjoy coming the this Starbucks. They make drinks in a consistent way so it doesn't taste like something totally different each time. And there's a good amount of seating.

I hate to downgrade a restaurant that I've really loved in the past, but my recent brunch experience at Amis was not at all worth the high price tag that came along with it. 

My friend and I were seated against the wall in the upper left area. Our server was polite but possibly a bit spread thin as we often had to wait longer than usual to order drinks. Speaking of drinks: the bellini is a spiced peach version that's high on flavor but low on champs. I had nary a buzz after I finished so I switched to the spicy bloody mary which was fine but didn't seem all that different from a regular bloody mary.  

For food, I opted for the san marzano tomatoes with eggs and basil. This teeny tiny portion tasted fine but, again, nothing special. The roasted potatoes were under-seasoned and Lo Spiedo's homemade smoked bacon tasted no different from store bought bacon. 

After hearing so many positive things about Amis' brunch I can honestly say I was disappointed, especially since brunch for two with tip came to somewhere around $100, give or take. I'll stick with dinner at Amis from here on out.

Two stars because it's Chick-fil-A, but omg this location has never learned "how to Chick-fil-A". This review isn't for the line workers - I know they're doing the best they can. But for the manager and operator - it feels like you need some serious training. This location was always below the Chick-fil-A expectations before the pandemic, and it just keeps getting worse. Drive thru is abysmally slow, my order frequently has been wrong, it just makes me sad. Ultimately, the drive down to the location south of Kennedy is a net wash on time. You drive further but it's a lot faster.

If you are looking for that upscale yet laidback place for dining, this is the best spot! It is just south of the hubbub of Congress Street. The whole vibe is much more chill. What a lovely atmosphere to celebrate my birthday with a friend. Our waiter was amazing and even had the perfect timing. We start it with a sangria which was wonderful. Then my girlfriend and I decided just to have four different appetizers for dinner. Both of us agreed the risotto was amazing. The flavors along with the caramelized roasted vegetables was warming and very much in season. Then we had ceviche. I told my girlfriend this was a Peruvian styles so she asked the waiter who concurred. Yellow tail-fin is marinated in lime and coconut water. Then the platter is served with various vegetables and jicama sticks. Absolutely divine. The artichoke crisped with a coating of lightly caressed seasonings along with the leek fritters it made for quite a variety of umami flavors. Towards the end of our dining experience, the owner came by to meet us and her graciousness pit the perfect bow on the whole time.

The food took way to long to be prepared. We ordered it 20 minutes in advance. Our food was supposed to be ready for pickup at 7:50, instead it was ready at 8:05. The food was mediocre and we have had better service elsewhere. On top of that they also don't allow in person orders.They make you install the app and place the order on there.

The Coronet is still Cushing St without music except Thurs and Sundays, which is unfortunate because that brings part of the ambience into it but I get it more tables means more money.  
Can't fault them for the furniture but I do wish cushions were available, it is truly unpleasant to ache from hard chairs in restaurants. *shrugs* 
Service was fine, although half way through our appetizers within 20 minutes we were asked if it's okay to serve our main meal. Indeed my husband was put off, isn't it fairly obvious we came to relax, drink our wine, enjoy our company etc.. we certainly don't want to be rushed.  
Food was good but not enough to go back to as it is there are plenty of places to eat unfortunately this won't be one of them.

We're not sure if my husband and I went to the same restaurant as everyone else?!  We had high hopes as we are huge fans of Osteria and frequent there often, not to mention the glowing reviews from the other Yelpers about Amis, we were really excited to try it!
We came here last night for our three year anniversary celebration, since it's a Vetri restaurant with a James Beard award winning chef, it automatically had to be good right? Meh.
We brought along our one month old son and had no issue getting seated at a four top to accommodate the car seat, so that was a great start to the night!
 The space was small and akin to an industrial warehouse. The staff was friendly but the service was very spotty, we really appreciated that everyone congratulated us numerous times on our anniversary which was really nice. We started off with the mixed salami plate- bland selections of meats, more like fancy pepperoni, flavorless pate and ham in a board!
Sweetbreads - undercooked which made the protein gelatinous and was overly salted, which was disappointing since the flavored were there just prepared poorly.
Pork belly- was the texture of raw bacon, I'm use to having it prepared with a crispy skin and a cooked pork, so it was very off putting, but perhaps that was just not our personal preference.
Meatballs-  again undercooked and underseasoned. Aren't meatballs the Italian staple? How we're they not phenomenal?! My husband said that he would preferred a Wawa meatball and I would have to agree with him!
Perplexed, we decided to go very conservative with our entree, in fact we lost faith In the chef and split a basic pasta dish, which we never share entrees! We just couldn't bare to spend anymore money on mediocre food!! It the duck bolognese special was actually pretty good, so at least we had one good dish during our evening out.
Our server seemed to be overwhelmed with the amount of tables he had, so perhaps that is why the service was so lacking. The bus boy started to clear our table without aaking If we were finished, we actually had to stop him a from removing one of our plates. We had to ask for
refills on our cocktails too!
We declined dessert, but to our surprise they came over with a complimentary rice pudding and some vanilla ice cream with a candle which was very tasty, so the night was redeemed somewhat, however we left feeling very disappointed with the dinner courses for our special occasion.
It's ashamed because it's literally a block from our house, it could have been our default place to eat!. Amis was a miss!! It really fell way short of our expectations.

Three of us went to dinner and two of the meals were extremely disappointing. The Culotte Steak had to be sent back to the kitchen twice because it was cold; you would think they could have solved the issue the first time.  The steak was also tough and overpriced. The Duck dish was also served cold, sent back, and was returned lukewarm.  It was overall disappointing, overpriced, and we will likely not return.

Worse experience ever.  Was trying to pickup a door dash order.  I was early and I was told it was still in process.  Came back..no order and absolutely no help with the order.  This is their 3rd strike and I will never go back.  I love their food but I cannot give money to a company who allows rude, nonexistent customer service.

The products are very good, the customer service of one individual not so good. Gave my wife attitude for her and my daughter wearing a mask inside the store. We have 2 girls 3 and 7 months old. We are vaccinated and want to keep them safe and have come to you guys during the pandemic to support your business. If this is how you treat customers for chosing to stay safe around people we don't come into contact with or know than you just lost our business
Horrible location, food wrong. Plan to wait and fight getting into the parking lot. Doesn't seem to stop anyone from coming even with all the poor reviews. I will not be back.
HOLY GOD OPEN ANOTHER REGISTER!  So crowded and so few cashiers.  3 stars only because it was clean.

Omg so awesome! Clean, courteous, and most important DELICIOUS! I drive from Land O'Lakes hut for the tofu and stay for the duck soup! I take home 3-4 boxes of rolls rice and tofu for the week. Omg delicious thank you for existing! Please don't change a thing! I'm coming in tomorrow and looking forward to it!

The best Banh Mi sandwich (BBQ pork) that I have EVER had!  The pho was nice.  I prefer tendon in my pho, which can be tricky to do well.

The service was quick and polite.  

It was a very clean space.

We also did some takeout from the adjacent shop.... and it was very good indeed.

CF Purgatory is my home away from home.  Ok, not really, but my friends there are like my family.  I had worked out alone for years and pretty much I was at a plateau.  I just couldn't get stronger, faster or any better alone.  I had a few friends going to purgatory and I decided to try it.  I LOVE CF Purgatory because it's not only helped me get stronger, but I have made friends with the melting pot of people that attend.  You don't have to be 20 years old and be in peak physical conditioning to try CF.  You can be 90 years old and there is something for you at this gym.  Next week the owners will be opening a brand new state of the art facility in the same shopping center.  If you want to get in shape, shed that gut or make some friends you should try this place out.  You have nothing to lose!

Had dinner at the Clearwater Beach location wile I was in town so, when I was in a pinch to grab a quick lunch before my flight, I decided to give the cafe a try.  I only ordered the black bean soup, but I highly recommend it!  The side of bread is just as good as what they serve in their CB location.  Obviously the atmosphere is not the same as their other locations, but for airport, it is above par.  Quick service and good food!  If you fly in or out of the E terminal, be sure to check them out!

I had to peak and as I suspected there is an army of what I assume are Vietnamese people cranking out mass amounts of authentic delicious cuisine. The front of the house staff was attentive, Min took great care of us and at least 3 other servers efficiently popped in at some point to assist. Ample portions, killer bahn mi, so many exotic desserts and dishes available in the to go area. They make tofu and soy milk on the premises and bake incredible breads and savory treats. It was like a self contained ecosystem, a tasty world of authentic fresh delicious Vietnamese cuisine that is priced a little on the low side. Definitely be back.

You want food?  You don't care about a parking impossible experience?  You don't want to have to pay something for nothing?  You don't really care about "nice" appearances?  You kind of prefer it if you're more or less the only European in the place? 

You love the taste of charred wok on your flat rice noodles? 

You sometimes fantasize about being in the world of blade runner?

Your not actually on Java.

You want to be here - D'jakarta Cafe.

You will not be disappointed.

Thank me later.
Great food, great prices and great service. My daughter had tofu pho that was humongous. I had Singapore noodles that were amazing. Really glad we took a chance on this place.

High prices, rotten produce (you can get fresher vegetables and fruit on ninth street for a fraction of the price and we all know that produce is on it's last leg but at least it's cheap), VERY miserable employees....They actually stand there with their arms crossed while you bag your own groceries. Also was in there tonight and three employees putting out produce were talking like they were on the corner of Broad Street using the F word loud and several times... where are the managers here? So unprofessional this place is a sorry excuse for a grocery store.

This place gets 1 star only coz their Bahn Mi sandwiches are good. Other than that all my visits here were a NIGHTMARE and dont get me started on the workers! Their service is a complete JOKE!!! I have been here 4x in a month and my order was always messed up and it takes a long time for your food to come out. I dont know what the hype is about their drinks when they taste really bad (honestly) , like for sure dont order the green mango tea coz it tastes like poison. 

I had ordered a bahn mi sandwich with egg on top but they gave me an egg on a plate! I told the waiter i wanted it ON my sandwich! So he takes the egg back and Then he brings out my sandwich WITHOUT the egg!!! We kept trying to get his attention and it was obvious he was ignoring us, i was super disappointed. I also ordered 2 kids soup with meatballs but instead they brought chicken! When I ordered the egg puff waffle with ice cream, it took FOREVER!!! 20-30 mins later the waiter tells me they're out of the ice cream I ordered, and didnt tell me ahead of time. She just wanted to give me the waffle with no ice cream! And i just cancelled it coz i was so upset we had to wait that long with no update. This place needs better respected workers and organizations. Very disappointing
I went there accidentally for my lunch. The food is delicious and prices are reasonable. I definitely will be back if I have chance "cuz I live in Houston".

This legendary restaurant did not disappoint! The food is amazing. The bartender recommended a combination entree that was perfect. The meat was so tender and flavorful. The yellow rice, beans, yucca and plantains were perfect and so flavorful. Can't wait to come back for a Cuban Sandwich.

Decided to try this place out and I'm so glad I did. Everything was absolutely delicious, it exceeded my expeditions with such large menu variety. It's very contemporary and they have a special shake bar with any and all sorts of shakes as well. I love the fact that they have the small buffet for pastries and snacks that you can grab in addition to or on the go. They also have things for you to buy to cook at home. The Pho was absolutely delicious with perfect flavors. Highly recommend this place and staff is excellent.

Great portion size, great service , the seating area is good , could be a bit cooler for us northern people .
Definitely worth stopping by .

Tried the curry chicken and was blown away on how tasty it was for the price.  You can't beat spending $8 on a meal, having leftovers, and it being extremely authentic.  Highly recommend, server could have spoken better English but other than that it was very satisfying!

My husband, dad, and I went to this new restaurant to try because of the 4 star Yelp review. Initial impression is good because the place has been redesigned and renovated from what used to be the Korean bbq restaurant. Table seating is very close to each other. We ordered #34: Bun Bo Hue, #28: Thinh An Special Vermicelli, and #10: Thinh An combination beef Pho soup. 
#10 was ok, no aroma of Authentic Pho. #34 tasted salty, just mediocre; #28 came out missing egg roll n grilled ground pork, told the server n she called a Vietnamese speaking server to come, who looked at the bowl and said: nothing is missing, everything is in the bowl. I then had to read each item on the menu to her before she admitted that there were items missing. Exactly what I said from the beginning! Then 1 guy who I think is the manager walked by our table eyeing my untouched bowl of vermicelli to verify if it's missing those items. After all that, he brought out my 1 egg roll and 1 strip of fried( not grilled) ground pork, and said "sorry". I said: "it's ok".
Next, I ordered for To-Go: 1 order of #10, 1 order of #74: Three Color Dessert, 3 orders of #75: Four color dessert. No ice on All desserts. The waitress wanted to check us out before she goes on her lunch break, which I said is fine. The tab had an extra order of #75, so I told her it's wrong,and she took it off. The desserts came With Ice, when I told her No Ice. And it was all 4 of the same dessert: #75. I told the server that 1 was supposed to be #74, not all #75. The Dessert Maker came and said that bc it was entered as 4 orders of #75 so she made that and that's why it came out like that. I said the server was notified of her mistake n told the dessert maker,i.e. Her. She then left n come back with the menu, telling me that #74: 3 color dessert; doesn't have the beans here: pointing at the dessert cup, and said that she gave me an extra ingredient in there for no extra charge. But if I wanted to, she can take out the beans in 1 of the cups. 
At this point, I got totally upset. I said "forget it. If I wanted 4 orders of the same thing, I would have ordered it like that. Price is not the matter here."
They have Terrible communications between staff. Do not admit their mistakes (server was blaming the dessert maker, and dessert maker was blaming server). Dis-respecting us, their customer. 
This Vietnamese restaurant and staff under-estimate their Vietnamese customer's knowledge of Viet food and taste buds. No concerns for customers. No apologies whatsoever from dessert maker.

A happy place where carnivores and vegetarians can happily coexist  As one of the later, I was excited to find a section of the menu dedicated to vegetarian meals. So many places too often have a sadly pathetic option for us non meat types. 

The place was packed at lunch time. Extra parking in the rear. Clean, contemporary and even a huge screen (silent) tv, which was great for catching glimpse of the Olympic Games. 

Very reasonably priced, my huge bowl of tofu and veggie vermicelli was more than satisfying and no big dent in pocket. Along with a yummy iced peach tea, so many flavors to choose from!  Bill came to about $7. 

Be sure to check out the market, some mighty fine foods, got me some tofu to go. They have hot foods such as egg rolls, croissants. Prepackaged soups and fresh baked bread for .50?!!  

Great addition to the area. Lots of pho being happily consumed.  Would have tried an avocado smoothie but they are made with whole milk which I don't do. The peach tea was a better choice.

I went in kind of late at night and I was so happy they were open! It's a food truck with outdoor tables with umbrellas blocking the sun. The employees have always been very nice and the food is great! I got the hamburgesa paisa/paisa burger. It's very good and tasteful, I always have a big appetite and it was very filling! (I love the white sauce!) Definitely worth trying!

One of my favorite Vietnamese restaurant in Tampa. They have ready to eat foods displayed so it was easy to see and select the ones you like. The food is average. Will come back here when I'm in the area

I dont think I have ever been to a Vietnamese restaurant this great before. It has all the qualifications for an outstanding restaurant: cheap quality food, quick service, and a large menu. This place can get pretty busy especially on the weekends, but because the service is usually quick  people are constantly leaving. On a Sunday afternoon, my party of 8 people only had to wait 15 minutes. The menu offers a wide variety of Viet foods. There are rice dishes, different soups, and of course banh mis. My favorite thing about the restaurant is their offerings of desserts. They have waffles, bubble teas and so much more. I ordered the wonton and egg noodle soup with pork. This soup is absolutely amazing. The wontons are soft and packed with flavor. Just a warning, there are A LOT of noodles in this dish so if you're just interested in a brothy soup, just ask for less noodles.

My sister suggested  this place. We kept saying ooh ahh while eating. All eight pounds of crawfish disappeared in half an hour.  Sampled the tofu made on the premises was incredible. I couldn't come to Vietnamese Restaurant and not having Pho. The broth tasted like I made at home. In the nutshell,  Pho is all about broth!
Incredible food! So fresh, great taste. Had vegetarian summer rolls - my mouth is watering for more! And tofu & veggie soup. Delish! And inexpensive. Great ready to eat food, too. Will return often.

3.5 really.

Plus: You don't need a card to take advantage of any specials.  There's a sale, you buy it, and it's automatically applied. None of this "don't have your card on hand? you don't get the sale price."

Smaller grocery store with Whole Foods a block away as its main competition.  Slightly less expensive, i.e. $6.99 for a build your own salad, less than that of WF.  Of course, the salad options are far fewer as well.

No free wifi.

Pleasant sitting space if you want to stop and eat here.

Pastries don't seem very fresh.  I picked up one of their giant pretzels and it was rock hard. No bueno.
The best Thai food I've had and the prices was very reasonable. Everyone was very friendly and welcoming. We will definitely come again.

I ordered delivery so that may be the reason I was not pleased.  Nothing seemed fresh.  The spring rolls were flabby.  The shrimp roulade tasted old.  The shrimp dish was discarded as was the beef entree.  Just seemed reheated and greasy.  I love Indonesian food but this was not very good.

I always bought to go, so i dont know hows the services there. They don't have delivery service, so you need to pick up your food. The place itself is clean and nice. 

Order 3x and feel in love with the vegetable noodles. I always love handmade noodles and dont mind to pay more. It cost 8$ but keep in mind that their portion is small. I think it needs 2 portions for male adult. Lol. The noodles came with chicken pork meat, small fish balls, 2 small fried pork dumplings, 1 egg, and2 beef balls in the soup. It more expensive than sky cafe and smaller portion, but i like the taste here more.

I tried other menus, they were good but not so spectacular . However, i give 5 stars because of noodles only. Even my son like it so much.

This is the most authentic Jakarta cuisine I found in Eastern seaboard.
Menu is simple, prices are very reasonable, friendly and very good service. Definitely my favorite Indonesian restaurant!

I use to be a customer here - all my clothes smelled like smoke when I got them back.  It was weird. I don't think they smoke in there. They have a pet in there sometimes but it wasn't the smell of pet - it was like musty smoke.

I've since switched.  Sansom is closer to me but its hard to justfy going.  I'm not a smoker and I don't believe I should pay to have my clothes smell like smoke.

Bummer.

The couple seems really nice too...

Without a doubt, the worst. Unreliable. No customer service. Today, my pre-arranged cab to the airport was more than 10 minutes late. Driver said it was dispatch's fault (naturally!). On the way to the airport, he said he had to stop and get gas! (Because I've used them before, I gave myself some extra time.
