Vietnamese is one of my favorite cuisines.   Nothing makes me happier than a bowl of Pho filled with thin slices of beef, herbs, sprouts, onions and a jalapeno or two.   I am convinced Pho is curative.  It always drives away a cold or any kind of blues.   Bun also rocks my world.   I love it with grilled pork and lots of crunchy veggies all mixed up with the vermicelli and doused with fish sauce and a little garlic chili sauce.  Or Banh Mi, the ultimate and most flavorful of all the world's sandwiches.  And don't forget refreshing boba tea or my favorite, Vietnamese Ice Coffee.   

Thinh An has all of my favorities and prepares them well.   I stop here when I am nearby.   It is always crowded with tables packed into an enclosed terrace and a smallish dining area.  Off to the side, there is an area where you can fill up take out containers with various hot items, pick up wrapped packages of everything from sticky rice to fresh spring rolls, pick up refrigerated and frozen items, and load up on all kinds of baked goods, some influenced by Vietnam's time as a French colony.  You place and pick up your orders at a long counter.  That counter is also where the teas, milks, smoothies and coffees are made and displays French-influenced desserts for purchase.

Think An is so busy and a bit on the dark side that I prefer to get everything to go. The This is not the ideal way to eat Vietnamese food but Think An does its best to package everything in a way that keeps the noodles and veggies from getting soggy,   I order online in an effort to save myself a wait.  It can take 25-40 minutes to fill an order.

The Pho is very good.  It's all about the broth of course and Thinh An's broth is very good.  Not the best ever with hints of ginger and other spices.... but very good like a great bone broth.   If I had to find a flaw, it is with the vermicelli.   I prefer it underdone so it can cook a bit in the warm broth.   Think An's vermicelli is "well-done" so the noodles are a little too soft.    That softness can spill into the Bun as well.   The pork (or chicken depending on my mood) is spiced and slightly grilled, making it quite flavorful.  I get an eggroll to provide crunch along with the veggies.   Love it.   And then there are the Banh Mi sandwiches.   I love the chicken Banh Mi sandwich.   A single bite is like a flavor explosion on my tastebuds.   The bread is so good, I buy some loaves for later.

Tampa is fortunate to have several good Vietnamese restaurants... and I am trying to work my way through all of them.

Wow. I only had a banh mi sandwich and a Vietnamese coffee. But omg so good.
Fresh bread, fresh pork. All kinds of veggies. Fish sauce. Heaven.
Only about 3.50. Seriously!?
I almost ordered two since i figured it would be small. Not really.
The coffee , though. What? Delicious!!!!
Chicory with sweet condensed milk.
My taste buds came alive.
So much pho. So many rice plates.
Everything's clean and super nice.

DO NOT GET IN THE VEHICLE. If I could give less, I would. We were really iffy about getting the cab in the first place since the car looked like it has been in some accidents (dents and cracked windshield) but had a scheduled car rental 10 minutes from the airport. The driver drove terribly and purposely took us the wrong way which made a 10 minute drive a 30 minute ride, even after we told him we had the navigation up and he was going the wrong way. Once I told him we were going to call the company, he suddenly knew where he was going and took us to our destination. A lyft would've cost less but since he was there, said he could get is there quick, and thought a 10 minute ride wouldn't be bad,  we went with him. We've traveled all over and have never experienced such treatment. Shame on you for trying to take advantage of people. I will be calling the company as well.
Simply amazing. Best pho around town. Long wait times so just call ahead but other than that it's amazing

I didn't think there would be a significant difference when Acme took over the Super Fresh location, but I was wrong.  The space is brighter (which use to be really annoying) and they have more employees which make the wait at the check out aisle much less horrendous than at SF. I must say that they are also a bit friendlier the first couple of weeks, everyone was chipper and engaging, now that time has passed they are more indifferent.  I like that the deli has more of selection of meats and produce section doesn't look as sad as it did previously.

I pop in and out of here to get cleaning supplies and odds and ends I can't get across the street. I'm glad for the facelift and I can pretty much find anything that need without humping to Target.

They have a freshness guarantee on deli meats- I've had turkey spoil within days of purchasing and was refunded and given new turkey for free!

Also- the customer service area is for 5 or less items that do NOT need to be weighed (i.e.- don't bring your apples or pears over there to pay! I'm annoyed that theyou don't advertise that- especially when there are horrendously long lines and people are standing around with a couple of things!

We visited this restaurant on a Thursday evening after a former local recommended it as their most favorite Vietnamese restaurant in the Tampa Bay area. I can confirm that this is indeed a good place to go for authentic Vietnamese food. They had a big menu with lots of selections; we even needed a little bit of extra time as it was tough to decide. The bun cha gio thit nuong (vermicelli w/ bbq pork and eggroll) was a seriously large portion but it was delicious. We also got the ca kho to (braised catfish in claypot) and com bo luc lac (shaking beef with rice) and those were also pretty good although the beef dish could've used a lot more onions, there were literally only like 3 slivers from what I could see. We also got beverages- the mango and the avocado smoothies were a little bit more on the creamy side, but the durian smoothie tasted as it should. I also liked their area on the side where you could buy some items to-go, nice to have to snack on later. I would definitely come back to eat here again.

I'm glad a place like this has opened so close to where I live. Their food here is great. You can sit and order something or you can stop I really quick to grab some pastries. They have a good selection of pastries, most that are below $2. They do sell boba, waffles and snow here. 
  If you are not sitting down to eat that be prepared to wait for your drinks or snow. Came in to order some milk tea with boba, didn't get it till 10 min later. The service here is good. Your first time here you might be a little confused about where to pay or who to talk to because there are two cashier places, but it's not too bad. They also take Apple Pay here!!! Big plus for us Apple users. 
  All in all this is a good place to eat! I'm going back.
If you want to buy expired meat or things that have been opened, or cans that are dented...then this is the perfect supermarket for you!

First off, I want to make mention, I would ordinarily give this place 5 stars as the Bah Mi sandwich and their Pho is one of the best in town; however, the experience I had as a walk-in take order left a bad experience. I arrived and placed my order 3 Pho Combo and 3 Bah Mi sandwiches. The restaurant has a separate area noted as Online Pickup (with listing of Grubhub, DoorDash, UberEats, etc) so after I placed and paid for my order I asked the young lady who took my order if  I need to pick up at the online order counter and she said no and that I was to comeback the the counter where I had placed my order. I was told it would take 20 mins. When 20 mins came and went, I asked the you lady how much longer, and she said 10 more mins (without taking the extra measure of either going back to confirm with the kitchen that in fact my order was not ready. Then 10 mins came and went and now it's about 45 mins since I placed my order. A lady from the Online Pickup counter saw I was waiting then she came over to ask what I was waiting on and I told her I had placed a takeout order 45 mins ago and gave her my order number. she went behind her Onlin Pickup counter and my order was ready and had been sitting there for 10 mins!
This was very unnecessary. Would I go back, yes but let me share my lesson, I will preorder online (even if I am in their parking lot). Foods too good to pass up because their was a break in their process. 
To all, good eats 'til I post again!

I was pleasantly surprised by visit to Thinh An Kitchen & Tofu. I visited during the week day for dinner and the restaurant was very busy. Almost every table was occupied and there were folks rushing in and out of the building with takeout orders. I had the krab Rangoon as a starter, the fried pastry was filled with cream cheese and was a tasty treat. The spicy vegetarian Pho is a must have! The soup isn't actually spicy but was flavorful. The meatless dish included noodles, veggies, tofu and a few bites of seitan. Everything was delicious and fairly priced. I can't wait to visit again and I recommend for authentic food.

I bought D'jakarta via Door Dash a few weeks ago. I got the special fried rice and beef rendang platter. The food was okay, it was missing a lot of flavor. The portion of beef I received was very small. The fried rice had a lot of seafood, which I appreciate but again, not enough flavor.

Drove all the way from St. Pete to this spot and it was definitely WORTH IT! Had the Paisa burger and it was cooked to perfection. My husband and I ordered regular fries and topped them with their Pink Sauce and Green sauce... Needless to say, we will be regulars here...

Last two times I've been there the women working checkout were incredibly rude - no eye contact, don't respond to questions.  Security guy always nice though.  Whole Foods it is on this end of town...
We ordered a beef soup. Beef was hard. Noodles were too soft and overpacked to the point where they were breaking apart. We asked for a replacement and they denied.

This was the closest grocery store on my route to my next destination. Unfortunately, they were low on products and the aisles were blocked in an unsafe way. I went to the poultry section, the meat packages were wet/slimy and not presentable.

The service was not engaging and/or comfortable.

This is a super busy thai restaurant and has a lot of options in the store that they have. 

So I ordered at 2:30pm after the lunch rush, when I walked in there was someone to help me figure out where to pick up my order etc. it was very pleasant I must say! I walked around the little area where they have their buns and prepared foods and it was pretty abundant with the labels but not that much food put out (but it was after lunch so they probably sold out.)

So I got my food and I specifically said no jalapeño, extra lime and no onions for my wonton soup... well they gave me extra jalapeño and onions with no lime... I was pretty mad about that because I can't have spicy foods.

When I ate the wontons the mixture inside was SOO peppery/ spicy it was not enjoyable. It tasted dry inside and the same with the spring rolls it was the same pork mixture they use. It's way too peppery and dry.

The wonton soup broth tasted ok, I would go back to try the pho but nothing with the pork mixture since it's over peppered.

So glad to have found yet another great, authentic, Southeast Asian restaurant today. 

Great food and good service with a smile.

The lamb and chicken satay were both excellent. Great sauce on the chicken and the lamb was tender, fresh and perfectly grilled. 

Shrimp rollade was yummy. 

Grilled pompano was the standout...spectacular. Moist, perfectly marinated. Great accompanying sauces, and crisp delicious skin. I couldn't leave a crumb and even ate the fins . So good. 

Soto Betawl was also awesome. Tripe melted in my mouth and the broth was light yet interesting with depth. 

Tamarind soup side was just like we make it at home.

Left very satisfied for a fair price. 

We'll be back!

Not sure how the layout of the kitchen is, but they seem to have trouble with dropping inedible items in food. I had a toothpick in my spicy chicken curry one time, but I didn't take a picture and figured it was just an accident. Today I ordered the Banh Mirito (a Banh Mi but wrapped in a tortilla) and one my last bite, I noticed something very chewy that seemed out of place. Well, it was a rubber band... I told the server and he took it immediately and told his manager. The manager never even came to the table. I really like this place and haven't had anything I didn't like... But c'mon man! How do you have stuff like this in your food?! It's a clean place with good service, but watch out for falling objects...in your food.

This was a very cute spot that we went to while we were in Philadelphia. The restaurant is very quaint and is good for a small group. It became very bustling around lunchtime. 

I was excited to try the many delicous dishes on the menu and decided to grab Chicken Satay and Chicken Liver as apps followed by Nasi Goreng Special, Nasi Babi Kecap, and Bakmi Goreng Djakarta. This was followed by a yummy dessert/drink, Es Cendol. We also grabbed a box of Peyek to munch on. 

Overall, everything was delicious! I'm not a huge fan of liver but the liver wasn't too bad and was around a 7/10. 

The satay was tasty although I wished it was a bit crispier. It was around an 8/10. 

Nasi Goreng is one of my favorite dishes and this did not disappoint. It was flavorful, full of chicken, sausage, and shrimp and I enjoyed it a lot. A 9/10 for me. 

The Nasi Babi Kecap was hands down my favorite and a solid 10/10. I loved how tasty the pork was and the sauce was perfect! 

The Bakmi Goreng Djakarta was also very tasty, with the perfect consistency for the noodles. This was also a 9/10. 

I enjoyed the Es Cendol and felt it was an 8/10.

Lastly was the peyek, which was also very tasty. Another 8/10.

This is a great spot that seems to be a go-to for the Indonesian community in the area. I recommended popping by for some delicious food if you're in the area!
I order the same thing and it's rarely consistent. The staff isn't very friendly to each other, although they're nice to customers. The inside could be cleaner.

THE BEST VIETNAMESE FOOD I have had in Central Florida PERIOD! Every time I have visited this establishment, I have been served quickly and efficiently - and always with a smile. Everything I have tried on the menu is absolutely delicious. My favorites are by far the curried chicken (with fresh french bread), the Vietnamese spring rolls, wonton soup, BBQ pork sandwich, and beef noodle soup. The also have a bakery with every Vietnamese baked good you can think of. This restaurant needs to expand across FL ASAP - as they will surely succeed!

I didn't know I was a juice lover until I visited sip n glo! The shop is adorable, the staff has great energy, and the juices are delicious. Every time I visit Philly I make a stop there and always get the one love - its fresh, healthy & amazing.

I was in a rush to go to school this morning. I called them at 6:58 a.m. and asked for a cab, and they told me the estimated waiting time for a cab to arrive was 10-15 minutes. I wait 15 minutes and no cab. I call again, yet another 10-15 minutes. It's been over 30 minutes and I'm already late for school..

Worst cab service ever, unreliable and disappointing.
Best restaurant in town all the server so nice and friendly,it the best place to come when visiting in Tampa thank you so much Thinh an

I experienced the worst customer service I've ever had at this location. Not only was it unprofessional from management on down to store associates but even the security guards were hostile and rude and combative I in fact the security guards was so rude I had to call corporate one of them tried to fight me as a customer. This particular store is low class and disgusting. I cannot  explain how terrible the service is at this location I even called the corporate office to express my  frustration and they were completely dismissive this whole organization is horribly flawed.

Prejudice and rude management. More than half the employees were not following CDC guidelines and preventing the spread of COVID-19 including management who also thought it was appropriate to have an employee follow my roommate and I around simply because he was African-American. Horrid establishment.

It was late instead of calling Uber I figure use United Cab I have not used them in year now I know why. POS car the guy could not speak English and my ride to South Tampa was not far enough.

Use UBER

My coffee was good and came with an adorable little icecream cone. My friend enjoyed the gelato. The atmosphere is spunky. Not super modern but fun. It's in a neat little plaza. The employee was nice.

I have frequented this restaurant to try and convince myself that it's great.  After giving it a fair shot, I have to say my overall experience from the beginning  has been average, and most recently very irritating.  While the restaurant and bakery is aesthetically appealing, the service is subpar.  I fault management for this flaw because the individual workers were generally working their tails off which is much appreciated.  In my opinion the pho broth is average, not the best or worse I've had.  The grilled pork could be better, I would say it didn't have much of a grilled flavor profile.  The spicy beef noodle soup broth is about a 3/5.  Probably my favorite item on the menu is the fried pork egg rolls which are freshly fried on a consistent basis.  Now the major flaw,  it took 22 minutes to make a small taro slushee and small yellow slushee.  The restaurant is properly equipped to handle a high customer flow, unfortunately I saw only one man the entire duration making the drinks.  This is about the second time now I've had incredibly slow service from the tea/dessert section.  This is how restaurant gradually fade, poor management.  These guys are wearing rocker bottom sketchers and they need to shape up or else they will be stomped by the competition. I will be reluctant about coming back to this restaurant.

I am stuffed! Not only is this place affordable, the portions are generous--I paid $15 for my meal and had leftovers! The food is amazing with great flavor & the service is fast. Great place for a quick & delicious lunch!

They have a large menu of dishes.  I've had the bun bo hue and my gf had broken rice combo plate and both were very good.  They also have a small market selling ready-to-eat dishes that you can take home as well as banh bao, egg rolls, and fried sausages.  They also have banh mi which is also very good.  Their flavors are a little muted fory taste buds, but still very good.  Note that parking is tight during peak hours.

Wow! My coworker told me about Thinh An because I've had a craving for banh mi. Ended up getting the banh mi to go because the soups looked so good. We tried the bun rieu and pho tai, and some BBQ pork fried rice. Everything was delicious! The banh mi were so good! They make their own bread for them, and fill them generously with whatever you choose. I was a little disappointed to get home and realize none of them had any jalapeño, but maybe you have to ask for it? Either way, the couple I tried (bbq pork and tofu) were both delicious! I have to say I preferred the tofu. 

They have a large assortment of snacks and grocery items for purchase to the left of the restaurant. Lots of yummy pastries, and also savory snacks you can take to-go.

Was searching for a quick warm meal on a cold day (Sunday, 1/16/22), and I found it here: their $10 meal deal was not only a great deal (protein + side dish + rolls), it was tasty! I got the mango habanero chicken: it was tender and juicy, and there was just the right amount of sauce -- a little sweet, a little spicy. Special thanks to the deli counter manager, a very friendly lady who helped point me to where everything was.

Wow!!! I'm so in love with this place now! I went in on a Saturday after reading all the great reviews for weeks. I knew that I would base my initial review on the croissants/pastries so this is strictly based on that!

 My husband and I used to travel 30 minutes to Brandon to get croissants at Mimi's Cafe but once they closed we were devastated. We have been on the hunt ever since. When so many of my yelper friends complimented the croissants here I KNEW I had to give them a try. I initially tried to call and order several of them ahead of time but I was told that they do not hold them. I knew by the time I made it there they would be gone because the girl on the phone told me they only had about 6 left. Bummer! 

When I was finally able to make it in I got 6 to go and one Strawberry croissant.  I'm not sure how, but they disappeared in less than 24 hrs  (hehe). Anyway I came back on Sunday and ordered 10 regular and 2 Strawberry. Needless to say, I think we have found our place!!! I also picked up a package of the summer rolls to try on the way home and they were excellent!! I can't way to try the pho. I also had the Thai milk tea and it was delicious!!

This is a favorite spot of mine in Tampa bay because their menu is not only a wide variety, but everything I've tried is really good and fresh tasting so far. On top of that, they have a little fresh food/bakery section off to the side that is always full of goodies I can't resist. Love coming here when I get the chance!

There is actually very little "social distancing" now. The tables are close together  and diners are back to back... all table in use, and 4 people per table. No one sitting down was wearing a mask... of course it would be hard to eat with a mask. And it was pretty well packed. The staff in the dining area do wear masks, but there were customer in line at the register with no masks, and some entered with no masks... and nothing was said. The kitchen staff vary... the ones you can see from the dining room usually have masks on... but a number of the staff exiting the kitchen to refill the hot bins, or delivering orders to the takeout desk... do not have masks on.

Food is excellent as usual... and the staff is friendly. I will do takeout.. but that is it. Like most Florida restaurants.... visit at your own risk, they have gotten lax.

This is a glorious oasis in a sea of culinary abominations.  This is not because the food is incredible(it isn't).  The food is standard, acceptable pizza place cuisine.  It gets 4 stars instead of 3 because all the other local choices make it look great by comparison.

It is good because you can actually sit down and have a nice lunch here.  Skip the pizza and go straight for their grinders.  The chicken parm and buffalo chicken cheesesteak grinders are their best offerings(and you get a free can of soda with one during lunch!)

This resturant is new to this area and the inside is modernized with a counter for deserts and an area to take food quickly to go. If you're going sit down and eat they make sure to get you to your table and a menu  in your hand. Very polite people working here and an extensive menu to look over. There are items X'd off with a marker on the menu like they ran out of that item or just didn't have it in the first place. I ordered the beef soup with egg rice noodles and it took almost no time at all, which good because I was at lunch. The meat was tender and very tasty with nice sweet and salty broth in sat in. There were a few vegetables to go with the soup which tasted great as well. The noodles were all a little meshed together like they were boiled a little longer than they should have been. I used a couple of the sauces at the table and they had just enough heat on them to make my soup that much more enjoyable.  The one with a strong garlic taste was my favorite. I would definitely come back to this place again and recommend it to any who has or hasn't had Vietnamese food before. This is the perfect first time experience location for anyone who hasn't because they'll make sure you get something enjoyable.

Everything on the sweeter side, but still good and of great quality. 

Spring rolls were straight up just lettuce, some basil (?) and shrimp; a very sparse spring roll, showing minimum effort. The peanut sauce was good, however, and I will admit that the spring rolls were nice as appetizers.

As my main, I had the Vermicelli bowl with grilled pork. It was exactly what I needed - a taste of home (Seattle). I was really craving the vegetables, and this bowl delivered in satisfying the longing for nutritious greens. I do wish they had put more vegetables in, but they did give a generous portion of meat and noodles. The fish sauce was very good - none of that fishy taste. Clean, simple, sweet.

This place has a larger menu than most Vietnamese places I've visited, so a definite plus there. I do think other dishes (I should have left room for dessert!) would have been just as good. And, the price was right.

Service was spot on. Great all around! For the area, yes, for sure, I'm a fan.

This is not like a lot of Vietnamese restaurants.  There's a lot going on inside.  They have a large menu selection and a beverage menu that's half the size with assorted boba teas, smoothies, and ice creams.  They have a lot of desert options and foods that can be purchased to go as well.  
I had the pho, the number 13 to be precise, and I bought some deserts on my way out because I was too stuffed to actually eat anything else.  I will definitely be coming back.

I love the set-up at this restaurant. You have a dine-in section, a bakery/snacks/tofu/pre-made food section, and a dessert drink section. I like to hit up all three sections, and yes, I have my favorites from each section! 

First, I dine-in and order my usual favorites: Shrimp Spring Rolls for appetizer and then their Pho Beef Combination Noodle Soup for my main food item. Their rice dishes are good too. The food comes out pretty quick - very good, fast service. After I'm done eating, I walk over to their dessert drink section and order a Taro smoothie with coffee jelly (the combination is just soooo on point). While I wait for my drink to be made, I hop on over to their bakery/snacks/tofu/pre-made food section and usually I like to getting: their almond pastry, ham and cheese pastry, their pork buns and the MOST IMPORTANT thing to get in this section is the TOFU. I love their Lemongrass Chili Tofu! 

This place can get super busy during lunch and dinner rush times but I never have to wait long for a table. They are organized and efficient on how they run things around here. I always look forward to coming here!

A cool Vietnamese restaurant in Town & Country!

I came here on a Wednesday night and it had heavy traffic! With a gigantic menu, there's so many ways to have your vista mess dish! There's so many pages of the menu, I can't even post it! You'll have to go on their website to look it up! 

There's a cool mini market-style area to the left as you enter as well as a bubble tea and waffle station! It's like a mini cafeteria that works together!

Fried mushroom tofu- good texture and pretty filling! Mushroom flavour was very mild! Got this at the market. Was not warm when we ate it since it was under a warmer for who knows how long. 4/5 

Fried onion tofu- good texture and filling! The fried onion taste was there and was my preferred of the two. This was at the market also and same comments on temperature. 4/5

Mango Bubble Tea with Pearls- this was delicious. It was not overly sweet and the white pearls added a good texture but I would have paired it with maybe a regular boba. 4/5

8. Grilled Ground pork rolls- the meat does not look appetizing but I'll say this tastes like a mild pepperoni! I unfortunately had it the next day so The rice paper was really dry. I can't comment if this was the texture it should have been. Definitely eat it the day of...I'll rate it 3.5/5 until I have it fresh the next time I order it. 

12A. Crab rangoons- this was my partner and friends favourite crab rangoons they've had. I'm not the biggest fan of crab rangoons in general but these were good. We air fried them for 2 minutes prior to eating and it came out very creamy! Just because my friend and partner raved about it, I'll rate it 5/5

32. Thinh Anh Special Vermicelli- this was amazing! Pretty much a taste of everything! The fresh vegetables really helped lighten the meal because there was a lot of vermicelli! The beef was delicious, the grilled shrimp was flavourful, the egg roll was amazing with this, the shrimp patty was a nice surprise in texture,  the broth/sauce added some much needed moisture for the meal! 5/5

31. Sate Beef noodle soup- this was a wonderful spicy soup! Not for the people who can't handle chili heat! The beef was pretty much raw but cooked with the hot soup! It was delicious!! The noodles were nice and soft as well and veggies added some good heartiness!

I can't comment on the shrimp fresh rolls, the lemongrass beef ans the pho because I did not try them (they were my friends dishes and we had so much food).

Tapioca Pudding- this was delicious and not sweet! The tapioca is made from sweet potato starch and the pudding tastes like coconut milk. There's a nice saltiness to it- definitely recommend! 5/5

Coconut Jelly- this was not sweet as well and was actually refreshing! It tastes like coconut water for the bottom part of the jelly, and coconut milk for the top part. 4/5

Thai Style Pudding- I was not a fan of the green jellies in this dessert- which there are a lot of. I liked the durian (which is a very controversial fruit) and the coconut milk surrounding but overall not pleased with this dessert. 2/5

Such a hidden gem. Drive too fast and you'll miss it. Authentic and delicious. Plenty of options and everything we got was good. They are willing to cater to every diet and will do almost everything vegetarian is possible. Pho was amazing and enough for 1 very hungry person and 2 slightly hungry people. Fried tofu I heard was a hit (but didn't get to try). The coffee was strong but hit the spot and the dessert waffle was just the right kinda sweet. 

Very affordable and the service was FAST! I got a coffee, pho and dessert for like less than 15 bucks. Definitely worth a stop!

The most amazing Vietnamese food you will ever have. Best vermicelli EVER. I get it every single time I come (except when I tried the beef stew)! I don't live close a good 30 miles or so but it's worth the drive! I LOVE their staff! Very kind and great at what they do. The food is beyond words. It's always fresh and SO yummy. Usually pretty quick at cooking and preparing the food! Only cons Parking is sometimes rough and the seating area isn't big but they have an indoor or outdoor(patio) option! They are usually quite busy! But ofc they are, their food is INCREDIBLE!!! Highly recommend. The Tofu Bahn Mi Sandwich is incredible whatever sauce they have on it is DELICIOUS. Food always tastes consistently amazing. I'd give them a million stars/ 5 if I could! YOU NEED TO TRY THIS PLACE, but I'm warning you... it is almost impossible to not become a regular here, you always come back! Never had a bad experience and I've been here many times over the years. Love the staff love the food love it all!

I just keep coming back to this place! As I mentioned in my first review, it can be a bit of a wait sometimes but it is always worth it. The menu is huge and so very reasonably priced. I had my first chicken bahn mi sandwich is here, it was like 8" long for $4.50! Can't beat it. It was stuffed with chicken, cilantro, pickled carrots and daikon. It's definitely one of my favorite things to order to go to eat for dinner after I've had a large bowl of soup for lunch. Awesome gem to have in this community.

We got the hekeng udang, soto betawi, and super meatball! I liked the crispness and flavor of the hekeng. The soto betawi came with a good amount of meat, and the soup was souper tasty! The super meatball was not as flavorful as I expected, but the smaller meatballs in the soup were good. Portion sizes were decent, normal.

Overall, good meal in a cute restaurant. I liked the wall decorations. Also, they take card now :)

Guided by Yelpers, I ventured away from my favorite Pho place, Pho An Hoa. Glad I did. This place is great Best Pho in Tampa for sure and I've tried the top 5. Meats and broth are better quality. Variety here is vast with good explanations and photos for novices. You're more apt to try something new if you get a good description and a photo to go by. 

Bun Xeo was excellent. Wife's Banh Mi was excellent. Bread perfectly crunchy outside and soft inside. Great pork filling.  Drinks were very good as well. Coffee and Thai tea. 

Portions are huge and I was in food coma. All for 28 bucks.  

Inside nice choice of take home products. 

Loved everything.  
Give this place a try

Same food you expect from wawa. But I was here once when a guy's eye literally fell out of his head.  Boys were on their skate boards looking for it and whatnot. Ew it was just gross.  EVERYTIME I go now, I just imagine an e floating around in my tea.  It kinda ruins it for me.

Came here many times after first review. The food is solid and very tasty. Tried their bubur (porridge), sate ayam, and mie ijo (noodles made from veggie). Highly recommended. Reminded me of my hometown food and with covid we cannot go home

This review is for horrible customer service experience. I used the checkout and noticed that I didn't get the discounted price after clipping my digital coupon. So I asked for a customer service help. She was so unfriendly, very rude. After she found out that I didn't put my phone number in, she was huffing and puffing explained it to me. I felt bad that it was my fault but she could have been nicer. I will never go to her register or self checkout if she is around.

What an AMAZING place. I wish I had this here where I live, I would probably go all the time. The food here is delicious, massive, and sooooo cheap! Oh my goodness, give me a lot of good food for super cheap and I will immediately love it. 
Anyways, there are so many options on the menu, I wish I could try it all. They also have a section of pick and serve food with a variety of different Vietnamese appetizers, desserts, bakery items, etc. Very authentic Vietnamese place and I would definitely recommend to everyone. 

Food: 
I ordered the pho, extra large bowl of course, and shared half a banh mi and I nearly finished. I do not remember but I believe it was around $12 without tax and tip for a meal that lasted me maybe the entire day. My friend could not finish and brought it home as leftovers so, in actuality, it was $12 for the entire day haha. 

-Pho Dac Biet: $10; Rate: 9/10
-Banh Mi #1: $3.50; Rate: 7/10

I love love love this place.  We always get 3lbs  of crawfish, the #13 and the Duck dish over noodles. Though the food is amazing, we came because Kyle (our server then) made us feel so special. He knew our names, our order (mmmm Tsing Tao), the order we wanted it brought out, our fav spot (patio) and even our sons allergies.  He was so great and so pleasant.  He was promoted to manager (congrats) but sucks for us.  We love overtipping those who deserve it!  Be back soon!

Visiting clearwater beach we looked up vegetarian friendly places in tampa for lunch and decided to give this  vietnamese place a try - one of the best decisions ever! We ordered the vegetarian pho, chicken loaded banh mi and chicken noodles - all of them delicious! We also got fresh sugarcane juice and honeydew bubble tea - both of them excellent. 

The restaurant was packed to capacity and masks weren't really enforced - hence the 3 star rating.

They also have a market to buy bakery items and pre-packed foods. Will probably visit again once the pandemic is over.

I'm giving this place 5 stars for a few reasons. If anyone follows me or reads my reviews they know I LOVE PHO! 
So I love the set up. It's like new meets old. Meaning they have the Bev bar with waffle ice cream etc with big lit screens then to the left you have "to go cart style" items. The bakery is AWESOME.  I love the outdoor feel seating as you first walk in then it turns into almost a cafeteria feel. Maybe because of the buffet serving they also have???  I'm glad they leave chili paste on the table. I hate having to ask for it. 

We ordered spring rolls and summer rolls and they were out super fast and still very fresh.  The next biggest reason I'm giving 5 stars is because they had fat flank.  Ben likes yellow crunchy fat and that's very hard to find. We asked for the fattiest flank they had and it was great compared to the sideways look we get when it's not a true authentic Vietnamese place. I had vegetarian pho in beef broth and the portion was so big! 

The only negative thing I could say is our waitress was def pissed at someone she worked with. Didn't take it out on us but I don't think she realized guest could hear her.  Other than that it was an awesome experience and this will be our go to Pho place now.

Wow! What a hidden gem! The green noodles were so good, had that el dente texture to it. The grilled whole fish was on point, not too expensive $20 where any where else it would have easily been $35. The shrimp I got was good too including all the sauces they give! Everything at this restaurant was on point and the prices were reasonable.

I wish I still lived in Philly so I can come back more often but can't wait to visit again later this year.

The best Vietnamese food in Tampa, hands down. Awesome service! Awesome food! After running a few errands with a friend who had a craving for pho, we decided to stop here. My friend has been here before and  raved about it.  In town and country, the restaurant is located on waters Ave and pat ave, the parking lot is small so parking can be difficult. The restaurant is divided into two sections, on the left a bakery where you can pick some yummy  Vietnamese goodies take home, and on the right it's the restaurant.  There are several big tables so smaller parties might be sitting next to each other.  It's cramped but the staff is very friendly and the food make up for the small size of the restaurant. 

Onto the food! Did I mention that it was amazing?!! I ordered the pork egg rolls and the beef combo pho. My friend ordered the chicken egg roll and the sea food pho.  The food came out quickly which was a blessing to two hungry people. The eggrolls were great, not greasy and they were extremely flavorful. I love spicy food and thankfully the table had there different type of hot sauces, siracha, chili pepper oil, and red chili paste. As soon as we were done with our egg rolls, we got our pho. My friend warned me that it was going to the huge and it was! The pho was flavorful and delicious! The pho was crystal clear like any good pho should be. The beef was perfectly cooked. Each piece of beef was large and there was a perfect amount in it..The pho came with the usual herb garnishments, Thai basil, jalapeño peppers and bean sprouts.  I spiced it the pho up with the chili pepper oil  and extra jalapeño peppers.  

Even though, I definitely did not finish my pho (had leftovers for the next day) I decided to order a taro tea with boba. The boba was a perfect way to end an amazing meal here. I recommend anyone who loves good Vietnamese food to come here. I am definitely coming back!!!
Amazing food and hands down the most authentic Vietnamese restaurant around town. Must try for a unique taste and good service- especially the snow ice!!

Love this place but it's quite far from USF area. They have a huge menu to choose from - the very few that have my favorite dish, bun rieu.  It's not the best I've ever tasted but I think it's the best in the area, probably even compared to st Pete places. If you have recs for bun tieu, please let me know :) 

Their pho is good and they're rice platters are decent sized and yummy. Banh mi is good. I like how the place is really clean. I love the market with the fresh desserts snacks and bakery! I always get the almond croissants :) Boba and dessert galore too!

Food was incredible.  Great flavors, huge selection, very generous portions, impeccable service.  Have ate here several times and regularly get take out, Always very happy will definitely be going back!
Thank You so very much BILL AD SUE!  ME MY SON AND GRANDCHILDREN WERE IN HEAVEN! Best tri tip in Arizona! Thank you again have a very blessed holiday!

This restaurant is so crowded but the wait time is not bad at all. We are party of 7 and about 10 minutes wait. Their pho is superb and meat is tender. The broth is so rich and flavorful. We also try their rice grill pork combo and it is not bad. Their tofu is so bland (wont recommend this), fried rice is not too good, and their Vietnamese coffee and avocado smoothie are good. We get their summer roll - it tastes ok but their fried spring roll with grill pork and shrimp tastes better

So excited to have a great Vietnamese place nearby. This place is outstanding and the food is very fresh. They bake their own bread so the banh mi is a must!  The Pho is off the charts. We will be back here often.

I have ordered delivery 2x through Doordash during the quarantine and it was absolutely delicious. Although I haven't been there in person, I thought the food was priced well and delicious. Highly recommend the homemade green vegetable noodle (very chewy!) and deep fried chicken (guilty pleasure). The braised pork was yummy too, though portion is a bit on the small side. 

Will definitely keep ordering from here, and hopefully will get a chance to eat there in person!

I bought heavy cream and when I poured it, it already curdled. The expiration date is about 28 days away. So the next day I went to customer service expecting a refund. Instead of apology and refund I was told that the store did not accept return. I was saving my breath from arguing. If it's Trader Joe's I bet they will refund me. I would be better off going to Whole Foods across the street or Wawa around the corner.

Went here with my family last week to have lunch as we miss indo food. Service is great and friendly. Food is generally taste close to home's taste. I ordered the Nasi Campur Rendang and Bihun Bakso that comes with vermicilli noodle & yellow noodles. Both taste great and the bakso is my favorite because it tastes like home. Plus, they also have the bakso with egg filling inside, very delicious and tasty! The only thing is that the portion is a little bit smaller and I was hoping that it came in larger portion. Prices are great and location is pretty accessible as it is located at the street corner. I wish I remember to take photos but I dont have it. I'll come again sometime & take photos!

Take this from a Vietnamese person: this place is where you want to go for authentic and delicious Vietnamese cuisine.

The menu offers an abundance of good dishes to try out with generous portions. Don't stick to pho; try some other tasty meals! I promise there's something for everyone in their menu. Hungry for an egg roll, but don't want to pay for an appetizer? Protip: Get it all by ordering my go-to dish, which is the vermicelli noodle dish with grilled pork and egg roll! When I first ordered this entree, I was incredibly surprised by the portion that arrived at my table.

The service has always been efficient and friendly even when packed. The cool thing is that they have their own bakery, which is an added bonus if you're craving for some to-go pastries. Despite the long drive, I can always count on Thinh An for a great meal.

Ordered the Bun Rieu (tomato/crab/seafood soup) and I thought it was pretty flavorful! I wasn't a fan of the crab chunks they made, but it wasn't bad- it sorta reminded me of cha, meatloaf, that you find in the rice plates.  My friend got the banh canh which he loved, and my husband got the banh cuon and the Mi Vit Tiem (duck soup with egg noodle) which he said both were ok. The broth was good but the duck wasn't. 

For dessert, we got the che 7 mau (7 color dessert) and it was the perfect amount of sweetness. We also ordered a pandan egg puff and a coconut egg puff. I wasn't a fan of them because i've had them better at other places, and for some reason it was so hard for them to get it right. First they brought out a waffle, then they brought out chocolate egg puffs...

Overall, I I liked this place and would certainly come back if I was in the area!
This place is literally amazing. Everything on the menu taste great and the staff is very friendly and will serve you with a smile

What a great little treasure with yummy food in a surprising location.  I've been driving past for sometime and decided to stop after seeing such a large crowd waiting for tables.  Glad I did, the best Vietnamese food I've had in awhile and the service is great. The noodle soups are all my fav!

Great to see many Yelper gather and enjoy the fun time together. Thanks to TJ organize it. It was fun to see who like it, who cannot stand the smell or who cannot take the durian straight. 

Durian is king of the fruit in Asia. It look very pointy at outside. To open it, find the point of crust tip and hit it the ground to crack it open slightly. Than you can peel break it. Or use screw driver penetrate to the tip and pry it open. 

Some said this fruit look like the poop and some said is a golden nuggets. This fruit is either you like it or stay away of it. When fruit ripe correctly, it has an alcohol sweet taste. The sweetness is one of the kind that you cannot imagine. 

If you have durian at home, the people who visited your home will know that since the aroma of the smell will occupy the air space of your home. When the gardener or planter walk under the durian tree, they need to wear a helmet. The ripe durian actually fall to ground and that is the signed ready to eat. You don't pick durian from the tree. You wait until it fall to ground.

Do not go here. It's hard enough for me to find parking without even more people learning of this place's awesome food!

I had the deluxe special beef pho, and oh my goodness. Purely divine. No bland broth here! When I eat soup, sometimes I eat all the good stuff out of it and pass on the rest of the broth. Not this time! It is amazingly flavorful, not overwhelmingly salty, slightly sweet, and packed full of delicious, velvety noodles. 

When my waiter brought out the bowl, I couldn't believe how massive it was. $9.50 for a bowl of pho twice the size of my head; and certainly bigger than my stomach. Who is selling these gargantuan bowls?! I didn't know if it was the real life or fantasy, but since Freddie Mercury didn't slide into the dining room singing, I had to believe my eyes.

I would take a bite of noodles and there were more noodles. Every time I lifted up a piece of beef, there was another just below it. Have you ever wanted to eat something endlessly? I think this bowl of pho is the closest you'll ever get.

I also got a milk slush to go. I made my own small one ($4) with yogurt and raspberry. It was incredibly refreshing and just the right amount of sweet! A "small" isn't even that small; more like a medium. And THIS medium sees Thinh An in your future! (Ha... ha... please laugh.)

I will DEFINITELY be going back! But you stay away. Remember, limited parking. ;)

I'm Vietnamese and I love a generous bowl of Pho. Although the quality is not top-notch, it's really good for the price. Generous portions and fast service. If you want homey, no frills, delicious food I'd go here. A normal bowl of pho is about $6.50 before tip, but that should fill you up! The large bowl is really quite large so come in hungry :)

I also had their vermicelli, pork, spring rolls, Viet sausage. The meat quality is average, but again, can't beat the price and the generous portions.

My favorite pho place! I've been coming here for Pho and Vietnamese dishes for 10+ years - consistent throughout! Cheap beers/drinks, and casual. Also much closer than 11th and Washington and the prices are also very cheap. 

The service isn't stellar, but that's not it's known for. 
Would highly recommend the clams in black bean sauce, fried spring rolls, and of course - the Pho. Must try for first-timers!

I went after the Pride Festival, so of course the place was wild. I LOVEEE that the dancing on the second floor is free! My friends and I went to Woody's before and they wanted $10 for us to go up to the second floor and dance. Some people you can wait till 1:30 to go up for free, but I'd rather just come to iCandy, where it's free to go up and dance anytime. The dance floor was cramped and hot, but if you don't mind it, it's a lot of fun. The music is blaring, guys are dancing on poles, and everyone's yelling in each others ears to hear what they're saying over the music. 
There are plenty of bars here. From the outside it seems incredibly small, but from the inside there are floors and floors and rooms and rooms. I lost count of how many bars I saw inside. All in all, great time with my friends. I'd be a little intimidated to go alone, but it's a good time with a young crowd.
Cimarron has been awesome with my Isabella.  They were upfront about each procedure and their prices are comparable.

Having had some very bad experiences with Philly food--quality, cleanliness, and so forth--I decided to not take a chance and go to Yelp for advice on best Vietnamese/Pho places. I had a cold that needed to disappear, thus I went straight for a hot bowl of beef Pho and a (very large) side of Chinese broccoli with garlic. 

I would return here again and again, given the fact that this is probably the best East Coast Pho I have ever had. San Francisco and Seattle still have a handful of places that have this place beat. Regardless, it was excellent. 

The service is friendly, quick, and all for a very decent price. I finished my meal with a mango smoothie, which was refreshing and tasty. 

Highly recommended from one visitor to another!

My prime rib was underdone. The potato was cold. The salad was really good. I think my mood was affected by the incredibly loud -- REALLY LOUD -- drunk people. That's not the restaurant's fault.

Nice waitress. Good service.  But I don't think I'll go back.

Why have pay at pump if you have to always go in and stand in line to get a receipt anyway. 

That and the store and parking lot is filthy.

Arguably the best Pho restaurant in Philadelphia's Chinatown; the Pho in Chinatown isn't great to begin with. Washington Ave is a drive away if you're looking for something slightly better.
The place itself was like any standard Pho restaurant; cheap tables, small cramped spaces, etc. I ordered a large bowl which was two dollars extra from the regular bowl at ~$6.
Food came out quickly and the servers provided refills of tea and water quickly. Overall, service was pretty good. They also listened to our request of steaming up the bean sprouts.
For the Pho itself, it was average across the board. I needed to put a good amount of "extra" ingredients to get it where I wanted. For the price and the service I couldn't complain though. I'd gladly go back again, but it may not hit the spot for some of you Pho aficionados.

I've been to Choo Choo a couple times since my initial review.

Okay, look, the food is slightly above average, but you can go with a vegan, a gluten-intolerant person, a gluten-intolerant vegan and voracious carnivores and find something satisfying.  The portions are huge, too.

Service is what you'd expect, and it can be a little crowded, but it's a solid solution to an intersection of food allergies and ethical choices.

Unlimited soup and salad is the best part of this resturant, of course the Tour of Itally wasn't bad either. My sister took part of their temporary dinner today and dinner tomorrow offer and both items (that night and the following afternoon) were Delicious.  They even offered to to-go box for the rest of our bread sticks.

This past weekend I visited Philly for the first time and Yelp sent me a notification about this hot, new restaurant called Sandler's. When I say I had two amazing experiences at this restaurant that's what I mean. Everybody working was so nice and willing to answer any questions I had. I first went for Brunch on Sunday and then back again for lunch on Monday. On Sunday, I ordered the bacon fried rice with a fried egg on top. It was STELLAR!!! Might I add, I hate eggs but it was sooooo good. I also had the Greek yogurt parfait which was so refreshing. My friend had the Nutella pancakes and something else that I can't remember but it was amazing. Next time I'm in philly I know where to find good eats.
Decent Pho. Not the best I've ever had. Service was mediocre.

Goodness has good food but HORRIBLE customer service. I am a regular customer as I go there at least once a week. My patience is running thin though. My order has been incorrect 3 times, I've waited 15 minutes for a smoothie to be made 2 times and my card was charged twice for an order. I have expressed these issues and only received an apology once. I have worked in the restaurant business and I understand it can be busy but the way goodness treats their customer is unacceptable.

My friend and I came here during a day trip. She used to live in Philly and this was one of her usual hangouts, so she was very excited to bring me!

I had the rice dish with shredded pork and grilled pork, and egg. I also had a lychee drink. Everything was super tasty! My favorite part, other than the grilled pork itself, was the bill, which on my end came to around $10 after tipping and even with the drink. Wonderful!

Really nice atmosphere at this location. Except for a small domestic argument by some patrons and some unruly kids at the next table, everything was quite nice. Food was as good (as is at normal OG's) and will be returning more and more as we can.
Fresh and delicious savory bowls, blended fruit bowls, juices, and smoothies. There's something for everyone and you can't really go wrong with any of their offerings!

This pho place is really great. As with all pho places the service is amazingly fast. The broth is really tasty. Not sure if there is MSG in it but I like it :D

I've come here twice and must say that if you want cheap eats in a casual place this hits the spot. 

Note: it is run by canto people but they do Pho right :D

I want whoever made my breakfast bowl this morning to come and cook for me every meal, everyday!  I stopped for breakfast on my way to work this morning, and I'm love!  The breakfast bowl had turkey sausage, egg, fennel, avocado, kale, greens, and pepper.  I also had a green tea.  I felt so good after eating this.  I was full until lunch which is rare for me, and it just made me FEEL good!  I'm dying to try lunch there because there were about 5 things on the lunch menu that just stood out to me.  I'll be grabbing lunch here in the very near future!

Olive Garden is my favorite restaurant. My boyfriend brought me for my 18th birthday dinner, I mostly go just for the salad and breadsticks, but had the chicken parmesan for dinner, and it was delicious! It was a Friday night, so it was crowded, with a 25-30 minute wait. We had a pretty good server, she was nice and attentive. Food took a while to come out, but like I said, it was a crowded Friday night. The restaurant was clean, and the food was amazing, as it always is.

Went on a Sunday and it was pretty busy. I ordered pho Tai and broth was good, but the rare steak is a bit thicker than usual. They had about 6 waiters and this place is pretty small. Seats about 40 and on this busy day, they always seem to hanging out at the back and never checked on me after they delivered the food. That's pretty typical of a vietnamese restaurant.

El servicio de este restaurante estaba muy malo. Estábamos con la familia y no cogimos la comida que ordenamos. No los dieron cubiertos ni vasos para la cerveza o bebidas. También, estábamos esperaron por mucho rato, casi DOS horas para recibir un appetizer. Y también cuando recibimos la cena estaba muy fría y ni recibimos todo lo que ordenamos. No voy a regresar a esta restaurante. Muy mala experiencia con el servicio y no lo recomiendo.

Love  Sundaze yogurt shop! We just moved to Tucson and were happy to find this local yogurt shop down the street from our new place. I had the salted carmel yogurt, my husband had the strawberry banana smoothie. Both were excellent. The owners are very friendly and welcoming. They are clearly people who care about their business and enjoy their customers. The shop was very clean too.

Delicious and cheap, my friends and I all know this place as "The choo choo train restaurant."

I was first introduced to this place by my chinese (now ex) girlfriend and her family a few years ago, and it has since become my favorite destination for inexpensive asian cuisine.  The restaurant isn't especially well lit, or even impeccably clean for that matter - but I love it regardless of it's lack of ambience.  The food is that good!

BTW - Is there a proper way to eat shrimp paste wrapped around sugar cane?  I've just been eating it like a drumstick.... but I always hide a little when I do, and feel like a tourist in my own city.

I LOVE THIS RESTAURANT.

I have been dining here for such a long time and it has never disappointed me. The same staff, they are all so kind and vigilant. 
It has taken me almost 6 years to sit down and write a review. Every time a friend from out of town stops by I absolutely take them here. 

THE ITEMS YOU MUST TRY!!!

Bun Cha Bio, Thit Nuong, Tom Nuong (bbq Pork SO GOOOOD, bbq shrimp, vermicelli, pickled daikon, cucumber)

Hu Tieu Do Bien (Seafood noodle soup, ask for egg noodles)

The curry fried chicken is FUCKIN BOMBBBBB

The sauteed pea leaves are delicious. 

ANY of the rice platters, especially the PORK!!

If you're in chinatown and are unsure, don't walk by this hidden gem. You can't miss it, right on Race St. It has a locomotive train neon light in the window and a glow of vietnamese goodness. Be adventurous, this is not a place you want to take someone who is on a chicken nugget and french fry diet and gets upset if you get some organs in a menu item you don't understand. GOOD LUCK
Great food very clean. They make everything in front of you. It's all wide open great shrimp egg foo young

Food and service excellent.  We HATED the very loud music and each customer's name being called on a loud speaker when their order was ready.  The restaurant is small and cozy, so blasting music and names literally shouted over speakers are both very disconcerting.  Hard to have a conversation with others at the table. We won't come back for the delicious food  because of the noise.

Choo Choo's! I've called it this since the beginning of time, never really reading the sign out front... called 411 for the phone number and I swore to the operator the name of the restaurant was Choo Choo's. lol. 

Anyway, I have many a fond college memory coming here. It's right on the edge of Chinatown, and absolutely lovely food to warm yourself up with when it is freezing outside! 

The Pho is amazing! For $6, you can get a small (really gigantic) bowl of Pho to enjoy... The Shrimp Pad Thai is delish as well. I often have trouble deciding between the two. One of my friends just gets the fried rice because it's so good. More often than not, I order Pho to eat there, and order Shrimp Pad Thai to go and I'll eat it at home for dinner. :) The restaurant is pretty small, and always busy. It is great for large parties too, and the service is really good. There's this head guy in charge who I think pretends to not recognize me, lol (I've been coming here for 8+ years!). He's very efficient and makes things run smoothly. 

I miss living in Philly more for this place than for the cheesesteaks, definitely. Sometime over the years I've even gotten my Dad to love this place as much as I do, and he always calls me when he's eating here just to piss me off. I love you Choo Choo's!

p.s. parking sucks. avoid it if you can!
Delicious, fresh and perfect for a lunch stop  if you want a comfortable spot to relax and get away.

Saw an ad in The Desert Leaf magazine and decided to check it out.  Tons of tables and space for studying, and it was the best Latte I have had yet since coming to Tucson.  I looked up the Coffee Roaster online and they really have a famous history and following in California.  It is the best tasting espresso I have tried.

Bought a scone because the baker was bringing them right out of the oven.......
Then I bought another scone because warm scones are ridiculously good!  They bake all their own stuff!

They also serve Pannins and I will return next week for that...  after I study at least one hour first.
Acai bowl was lame - half of a half of a strawberry, one slice banana - must be a fruit shortage- for the price expected more

Another excellent vegan restaurant in Tucson. I haven't had anything here which wasn't good and most of the stuff is excellent. The food is all cooked fresh and prices are about run-of-the-mill for this type of restaurant. I should add that you can have wine if you wish.

We met here for a casual get together with friends tonight. My dad is from the Mid West, and I just kept saying how much he would love this place!  The meatball appetizer had a good texture and moistness.  The flavors and spices inside weren't overwhelming.  The lasagna came with a choice of a soup or salad -  I got the salad, just a small green salad, nicely dressed. The lasagna - AWESOME!  There was a sweet flavoring in the marina that just made it.  There were a couple of cheeses, and the whole thing was covered in that lightly sweet sauce and delicious toasted cheese!  The bread that came with the meatballs and to the table was light and airy and buttery. I regret not having room for desert.  Service was good too, we had a large group of 20, and I was impressed by how well they kept up with all of us.  Very cool Western vibe.  Love the art and casual atmosphere!  I can't wait to go back!  I want to try desert!

Our meal was delicious.  I had the "everything" pho (the first pho listed on the menu) and shared a papaya salad with beef jerky as an appetizer.  It was soo good!  The papaya and veggies for the pho (basil, bean sprouts, and lime) were so fresh too!  The meal was super cheap and I was so full at the end.  I'm looking forward to going back again! :)

As a 'Miamian,' there aren't places down by me that have EXCELLENT Pho as I've encountered in the area with a large Asian population.  To me, the best we have in Miami it's mediocre when it comes to these in other parts of the nation, but its up to par for the satisfaction of my belly.

Pho Xe Lua...You have met my expectations in satisfying my belly with your Big O' Bowl of hot soupy slurpy goodness.   

As you walk in...this place is waited by predominantly 'Chinese.'  I know, because I speaky their lingo... ; )

But service is quick & efficient, hot tea is brought to you without any questions as you are sitting at the table.  Once ready and your order is placed, it doesn't take them very long but about 5-10 minutes for the waiter to walk briskly to your table with this big white bowl of hot soup filled to the brim.  The broth is where its at!  This broth was steamy and tasty with all those hours that they spend brewing up a pot of this.  The noodles were cooked to perfection, springy...just a tad past al dente.  Enough where it is not soggy and breaking apart every time you attempt to grab them with your chopsticks.  BTW...the regular large size is more that enough!  Unless you are starving and can scarve down your hatch a HUGE-R (yes, I know that word doesn't exist, but there is no other way I would describe how big their sizes are) bowl of slurpy goodness...go right ahead.

Pho here is cheap and plentiful.  You really get your bang for your buck!

...Wish there were more places like this back home.

After over a week in Chinatown, we finally made it to Pho Xe Lua and it was worth it.  We had traditional Pad Thai along with a dish of mixed veggies, tofu and bean sprouts and it was more than filling. And tasty.  I have to say that even though Pad Thai may be the beginner's Thai dish, it was delicious here, one of the best I've had.  Shrimp were plentiful, plump, and perfectly cooked.

Beers were incredibly inexpensive for a wide selection of bottles.  Service was efficient and friendly.  Also helpful.  We walked in early on a Saturday night when most of the other restaurants on the street were almost empty.  Pho Xe Lua was almost full on both floors--now I understand why.

Pho does not disappoint.  
Very generous portions, fresh fixings and a great price.
Would be nice if they added some cilantro.

After reading a blog post from the owners online, I have made it a point to come here instead of Starbucks. First of all- the drinks are a million times better. The espresso is so smooth and they draw a beautiful latte. The location is weird, but I only think that because I'm jealous I don't live in the apartments for their delivery service. I love the frappe drinks too. They're amazing
SO GOOD!  Sundaze is WAY better than BTO or Orange Leaf in Tucson.  I get it about everyday, I can't get enough!

For what it is, I can't give "Choo Choo" anything but 5 stars.  It is certainly borderline hole-in-the-wall, but it is cheap and so good!

I am always overwhelmed with what to order (and usually make my friend order the appetizers), but this place is amazing.  The portions are huge, and every single thing I have eaten has been delicious (especially the pad thai) and the raw beef dish appetizer.  On my list visit, four of us shared four appetizers and each had our own entree, and we paid about $15 each.

Definitely check this place out!

Pho in Chinatown... and some of the best Pho I've had to boot!

I could describe the service, the atmosphere, and everything other than the food, but really why bother?  You're here to eat!  Get some Pho Tai, spice it to your liking, and dig in.  While they were a bit light on the tripe, the beef was cooked (or should I say uncooked) to perfection. A regular bowl (they call them L versus XL) should be able to take care of you well until your next scheduled meal.  Try to beat the lunch crowd since it gets packed.
Good food at a good price, the pho ga hit the spot on a warm spring night.

I use to hear they have bad service, but it's great here. Maybe they used to have a lack of servers speaking a bit of English and people misunderstood it as bad customer service...? I like them, they do great. It's cheap and yummy food! Can't go wrong. Their cured raw beef with peanuts, Thai basil leaves, and fish sauce is bomb btw. So good. And it's cured enough. Great curry as well!

Dr. Cronin and her staff are absolutely wonderful. They are welcoming and put you at ease if dental work makes you nervous. Dr Cronin is an exceptional dentist and I highly recommend her skills. She is thoughtful and has your best interests in mind. I've had a few bad experiences in the past with dentists and I'm happy to have found her and the staff at Rittenhouse Smiles. Highly recommend.
Best Pad Thai (phad thai) ever! And the raw beef with lime juice is my favorite appetizer. Pho is pretty good and the drinks selection is pretty vast. You can buy alcohol here!

I've only been here 3 times in the past half year.  The first 2 times I've ordered smoothies, both of which were decent.  I liked them enough.  In general I like this place because of the healthy vibe, and when I need something to tide me over until the next meal this beats getting a latte.  

Well, I don't know what I was thinking, I guess I wasn't paying attention when I came in yesterday and I ordered the Green Bully because I wanted some greens in my drink.  First, it's a juice (so that's my bad, wanted a smoothie), and second, it has a savory flavor.  Totally not what I was expecting, and go fig I ordered the large size.  I had a hard time finishing even half of it--ended up saving it and adding it to my leftover veggie soup at home.  Weird?  Yeah, but I couldn't bear to waste a nearly $10 (w/tax) drink.  

It's not cheap here, like others have mentioned.  I feel like if the menu could be $1-2 cheaper this place would be even more appealing... But I get it, quality ingredients and using fresh entails cost.

The ambiance is fine for a place to eat, and so I guess this may or may not be fair.  But trying to get a little studying done here was a little hard (but then I'm pretty that's not what the shop's aiming for their customers). I couldn't concentrate with the type of music being played, it was horrible.  After 45 min I ended up packing my stuff and going to a coffee shop, which is prob where I should've gone in the first place.

This place is still somewhere I'd go if I need a place to pick up a healthy snack.  I won't cross it off based on one unfortunate visit.
Poc are not welcome here.  Don't waste your time or money at this establishment.  There are plenty of other options within a two block radius

Bad service poor excuse from one of the so called owners after an hour salad came not even an appetizer portion left we were not going to wait another hour for dinner when it wasn't busy when we got there.
This place needs to get out of Tucson
A local favorite and a regular spot for pho around university city/ Chinatown. Consistently great food and very authentic.

Visited Philadelphia for the first time coming from SoCal, been gone for a 1 week with no Vietnamese food, I was craving something. Happen to stumble thru Yelp and it has good reviews.

For me, it was ok. Too much MSG for my taste bud, made me kinda sick.

This is your average expensive laundry center, but it is open 24 hours, so you can wash whenever you feel like it, though I would not feel to safe in there that late. There are no workers that you can see, it is pretty much do it yourself, though there are a couple insects in there which can bother some.

Great "Mom & Pop" establishment. The frozen yogurt is amazing--I've lived all over the US and I've never had fro-yo as good as this. A lot of fro-yo places serve icy, thin yogurt but the fro-yo at Sundaze is creamy and rich. The sugar free and Wow Cow flavors are so good you'd never know they were low-cal.  I love that they rotate their flavors so there's always something new to try, yet they keep the "tried and true" for those of us attached to one or two flavors. They have amazing toppings and the best waffle cones I have ever had. Anywhere. Period. The. Best. Waffle. Cones! Their smoothies are excellent, too.
Wendy, one of the owners, knows all her regular customers and greets us by name. Whenever I come in she asks about my husband (who is frequently deployed). She knows my "usual" which is amazing in itself because I don't live close-by and am not there as often as I'd wish.  It's worth the drive from Marana.
The place is always clean. The teens who work on evenings and weekends are always friendly and attentive. Prices are fair--you get a lot of yogurt for the buck.
Wish I could give more than five stars.

WOW This pho is amazing

Get the pho special
-Its huge and cheap
-the cuts of beef are very generous
-the BROTH is the best I even had.  Just drink some of the broth before you mix in hoisin&siracha to taste how rich and beefy it is

meatballs are not included in the pho special tho :(    (extra $2 its worth it)

Also try the Snails.  When i was here i saw every oriental person order them.  they must be good.

Anyone out there like tendon in their pho?  I do!  This place offers a very generous portion of tendons with the pho, which is why they are my go-to spot in Chinatown for pho.  Their avocado and taro smoothies are good here, too.  They didn't get 5 stars bc the pork chop plate with broken rice is not the best I've had - the pork chop was a little on the greasy side and they overcooked my sunny side up egg, which is a big no-no. Also, the udon with ham hocks don't come with true Vietnamese Udon, which are translucent, but they use an opaque type, similar to ones used in Japanese/Korean food; the ham hocks had flavor, but they tasted like they had been frozen and had freezer burn/picked up weird smells from the other stuff in the freezer (does this make sense and gross anyone else out?).  

Ok, I said my piece.  I go here often, despite finding the occasional dish that I don't like.  They make tons of other things, and I'm sure I'll find lots of things I love here.  Another perk is that they are open pretty late for a Vietnamese restaurant - till 11 some nights (Friday/Saturday).
My favorite Viet restaurant. I went there on a weekly basis and never got disappointed.
I don't care for the place too much... But the dancer inside that box is pretty good ICandy. So cute!! Haha... Too bad their gay.
Killer. Love the mango shake of course. Everything is tasty and the wait-staff take good care of you.
I stop at this Wawa every Thursday after I do my grocery shopping. Always fast, friendly, and convenient. Nothing beats their coffee bar, and I've never had bad service here.

In the interest of truth in advertising, they should rename this place "Mediocrity."  The beef in the Azteca steak bowl was overcooked and had a slightly livery taste, the other ingredients were OK at best, and the portion was very small for the price.  Worst of all, the little scoop of avocado in the center of the bowl included quite a bit of brown sludge from a bruised and rotten area of the fruit.  It would have been very easy for them to cut this out of the avocado before scooping, but instead they chose to mix it in, making it very hard to avoid and rendering the entire dish fairly unappetizing.  Food like this would be OK -- even welcome -- if you were stuck in an airport or had to eat at a mall food court for some reason, but at a "real" restaurant, even a fast-casual one, it just isn't good enough.  The place is also very loud, and while the kids working there seem nice and well-meaning, they don't quite know what they're doing; the service is a bit unprofessional even by Tucson standards.

I just wanted to say the customer service is excellent. I stopped by my moms job at Jefferson's hospital to have lunch with her and she recommended this place. However, there was a slight error in my order with my onions rings and Korean wings. I was not going to say anything because I've already begin to eat the food because I was hungry. My mom still called and explained my concerns. They told me to come back and I was given an additional fresh order of onion rings and Korean wings. The cashier girl was really nice and continued to apologize for the inconvenience. Thanks ! The food was delicious and your service is all that ! I will be back to eat at your restaurant!

The concept is pretty cool, but the unremarkable service combined with mediocre food will keep us from going back. We liked the western movies playing, but continued issues on both visits with the sound system blaring off and on was jolting while trying to enjoy a dinner. Baked potatoes weren't throughly cooked or served warm, cheese was a large glob and not melted, but not cold either. Prime rib was undercooked and salmon was tough and greasy. The salads were drenched in Ceaser and lettuce was wilted. The beer was cold and the calamari was pretty good though. Overall not worth $80 plus a tip. We really wanted to like this place, the location and ambience are great.

Choo Choo's!!!

seriously one of the best Vietnamese places in Chinatown.

i love their food and theres just so many that i want to list.

writing this review is making me hungry...

this was always the hangout spot for me and my friends since forever.

i highly recommend it.

Everything you've heard about this restaurant is true. They have a wonderful cook or cooks and the entrees are superb!! The staff is so gracious and the atmosphere is very very pleasant. The smear is .......I began going there a lot since it's so classy and I need to relax after working so hard all day. So I order this wonderful dish that the taste is to die for and before I get it it was placed on the other end of the bar in the middle of all the waiters gathered there. They all get a good look at it including one who puts his face right over it and then the head waiter or I'm going to point at the very short fat one sticks a fork in it and takes a mouthful of it as my waiter has his back turned. Im disgusted at this point and when it's brought to me I can see the smear where my food has been on the plate. I mentioned something about it to my waiter but he played it off like i was mistaken. What bothers me most is that I'm paying for it and i didn't authorize this person to taste it. I don't care to go back there again. Their loss. It ought to have been brought to me directly from the kitchen like all the other times.

This has become mine and my boyfriend's favorite cheap place to go on a Sunday evening. I usually just get the same thing (veggie pad thai). He mixes it up quite a bit and has liked everything he's tried. His go to meal is chicken curry which I have to say smells amazing even though I am a vegetarian. 

I would give this place 5 stars however our last trip the beers we ordered were skunked, but even if that never happened I wouldn't give it 5 stars because the fish tanks freak me out and I can only sit in there if my back faces them. 

Two beers, two entrees, $20.40! Bam!

I really wanted to like this place. I'm a big spaghetti western fan, and this sounded like a cool concept. Some friends were in from out of town, and they wanted steaks. So I thought of this restaurant. We were disappointed. First this bills itself as a premium steakhouse, With prices in line with the premium steakhouse. If you're paying premium prices, you expect premium ambience and service. The service was good, but this restaurant is not a nice looking. There's a cheap paint job, and the bathrooms are not up to snuff. As to the food, it was fair. The calamari was rubbery, The salads were small and uninspired, the Marinara sauce had a strange sweetness to it, and the steaks were just fine. On the plus side, our waiter was so thoughtful and  friendly.  Lastly, despite the fact that the restaurant was near empty, dinner took a very long time to be served.  If the prices were lower, a lot of this could be overlooked, but for this price, I'll try one of the standard steak houses in town.
The staff is great!  Nice rotation of flavors. The kids look forward to getting treats from here. Prices are reasonable. We love this place!!
Amazing beef pho. Fast service, great (yet simple) space to dine. Definitely will be back!

So my Asian buddies tipped me off about this place when I complained about not having good Pho in Philly. I heart you Choo Choo! I thought the Pho is good but my favorite food here is the pork chops with rice, which comes with a red/orange sauce. It's so cheap and the portions are generous. The servers/waiters are very nice too.

Came here for the first time and ordered pho with chicken. It was pretty OK; it was not the best pho I have ever had nor was it the worse. I wouldn't go out of my way to come here (like I did this time) but, if I were in the neighborhood, I might be willing to stop here for a steaming bowl of pho for lunch...but I would probablly just go try the pho at one of the other nearby establishments.
