Great selection of healthy food. Their acai bowls are huge. I'm used to paying just as much for bowls that are half the size. It would have been perfect if I didn't find mold on the berries in the bowl. Such a bummer. I ordered a juice (beets, apples, ginger) and that was very good. I would definitely return here.

Really fast service and honest pricing. They don't charge an arm and a leg. Fast service and will work with you if you can't be home. Very pleased with their service. Being in property management I deal with many vendors and can say I am very impressed with gasmasters.

What an amazing gem!
Unlike most Pho restaurants in the city, this one offers a vast menu that includes not only Pho (the signature soup) but many specialty dishes. Their Pho is also amazing because it has about 20 variations and does include seafood Pho (a rarity in the city as well) 
The place itself is rather old, which gives it a dirty look but it's just the look,  I do believe that they pass their sanitary inspection with flying colors.

A nice variety on the menu. Very friendly staff, nice ambiance inside too! Ordered two smoothies and an acaì bowl. Delicious bowl and filling smoothies! The menu was a little confusing for a first timer but once you read the entire thing you figure it out. The outdoor patio and a juice would be on my list for next time!

Olive Garden is not a place to go for authentic Italian food really. But the food is nice and the price is reasonable. You get free breadsticks and chocolate. We asked for refill and have some extra so the server packed it for us.

Love going here after yoga. Very nice atmosphere as well as staff. The staff is very informative and they are good at making recommendations! I can't wait till they open one closer in my area. Hopefully sometime in the near future!

This place is not only cheap but also authentic! I couldn't believe the proportions and sizes when I first entered here. Compared to some Chinese restaurants, I argue that this is the place for bang for buck and dishes that can be catered to any taste ranging from complex flavors of thai, soothing pho soups, spicy curries, salty and savory rice dishes, sweet desserts, and fresh crisp summer rolls. 

I recommend their pho- large generous portions 8.50 for a large. You can also get their rice dishes like curry or pork chop for 7$ or less! I haven't run into anything bad on their menu but their fish fillet thai dish was a tad salty so I had to eat it with a lot of rice/

Staff is attentive and fast and the food service comes all in one go. So if you don't like wait time, this place if not early, will get least get all the dishes in one go onto your table. 

Place is clean and decor is cozy and homey. It seems all the locals come here and having been to various Viet places, this place is authentic in style and taste and ambience. Compared to other Viet places it definitely makes it to the top. There's another Viet place a bit further down, but I think its pho is mediocre and overpriced. This is a bit more secret directly across from Nineting
Absolutely fell in love with the tofu and noodle dish. The watermelon juice was also pretty good. I'd definitely comeback for the food!

Hey...if you travel solo...this is a friendly place to hang...talk ti bartender Kake...good convo
Drink soecials keep the wallet sane
Great broth and large size for Only $7 (give or take). My go-to spot for Pho since I moved here.

This has the best Pho in Philly and the best value.  One can drop by any time of the day or night for a bowl of Pho.  Great during thses frigid weather - warms your soul.   It has many other delicious dishes too (Vietnamese, Chinese,and Thai).   Enjoy!

Visiting from Northern Virginia.   It was one of best pho restaurants I've eaten recently. ..  The price was also excellent.   I would go back whenever I visit Philadelphia.   Order spring rolls with your pho...

Last night a big group of friends and I went to the lovely David Bowie tribute dance party. While we were outside smoking a unknown man started aggressively forcing his way into our conversation. We politely asked him to leave multiple times and had stopped talking but were just continually asked him to leave. A security guard got involved and took it really seriously by physically forcing him away even though he just kept coming back. I felt amazingly safe and supported and just wanted to shout out to BLK Transporter! You made the night so much better and I will definitely be back! Thanks for looking out and going above & beyond at your job! 

Btw) this isn't my 1st time here and I've never had a reason to complain so you should probably go get a Jell-O shot if your already thinking about it...

Our favorite pho place in Philly.  Owners are friendly and attentive, and staff are relatively efficient.  
Food quality is excellent, always very fresh and well balanced.
Prices are very reasonable.
Most highly recommend.

The Pho here is pretty good/standard, and our overall experience wasn't terrible but the service was pretty slow and they almost forgot my friend's ice tea order until after the food arrived even though we ordered it as soon as we sat down. 

6 hours later...I had some pretty bad food poisoning/side effects. I don't totally want to blame or discredit this place but that is the exact window/time period for food poisoning...and nothing I ate was with my hands :/

Not a terrible place but I probably will not return due to this incident.
This place was fantastic! The flavor of the food was poppin! It was so good! The wait staff was friendly and accomidating. An all around great dining experience!

A hidden gem in Chinatown. The food is affordable and delicious. Perfect for college students who want good food and cheap prices or anyone on a tight budget. This place is also a fantastic date spot. The atmosphere is great and the interior is well decorated.

There is absolutely nothing wrong with the Olive Garden. There isn't anything outstanding, either. In the restaurant rainbow from Mall Food Courts to Bern's Steakhouse, Olive Garden is the color gray. 

The staff is nice, but not engaging . The food is tasty, but not interesting. The decor is like a hotel - clean, but stale.

Do eat at Olive Garden? Sure, I just don't get excited about it.
Love this little spot. I've only had the Pho here and it has become one of my go to places. The tai iced tea is so good.

12th Air is one of the most spacious and cheapest bars in gayborhood. It is not a place to pick up a date, or to have a galmorous night out. Come here for $5 24 ounce lagers, free snacks of mysterious orgin, and bartender Tinh. 

Many peope dub this bar 12th Scare, but it really is worth a try for a low-key night with friends. Its empty dance floor, 3rd floor deck, no cover charge and no wait for drinks makes this place a common destination for my friends and I. Happy hour runs from 6-8 or 9 every night and its ridiculously cheap.

When looking to grab some pho in the city, this is always my first choice.  The chicken is always tender - not rubbery or chewy like the pho joint much closer to my house.  Definitely a no frills atmosphere, and the Thai food is not quite as good, but you will never leave hungry.  

And $2.50 Sapporo - not bad, either.

My tummy is full of the Goodness from Goodness. This place is terrific!  I met a group of girlfriends here for lunch today and was so impressed I had to come home and Yelp about it right away. 

First off, the parking situation is AWFUL during peak hours. But that didn't stop me from finding a spot after a while. 

It's a very clean, bright area.  The setup is very similar to something like Sauce, where the menus are on the wall and you order at the register. It was packed when we were in there, and the staff was doing a great job at keeping the pacing consistently quick. 

I ordered the roasted veggie salad and added chicken. This is one of the BEST salads I've had in a very long time.  Some brown rice, fresh spring mix greens, roasted carrots, broccoli, pickled red onion, butternut squash, and beets topped with a nice serving of chicken made my little tastebuds dance. All of the veggies were beautifully seasoned-I added the dressing (one tiny container is what they give you and you don't even need to add it, the veggies are seasoned that well) because I like the tang of vinaigrette however the pickled onions have basically the same effect. I ate just about half of the salad and was very comfortably full. 

Among the other things ordered at our table were the kale citrus salad, the pesto chicken sandwich, and the morning breakfast bowl and one chicken taco. Everything was presented beautifully and the girls loved all their meals. 

I also got a large iced green tea. It was delicate and floral and did not need any sweetener added!

This is what I would consider "pricey" for lunch-the salad with added chicken and the green tea set me back almost $15 however I will be able to get two meals out of the salad. I typically spend no more than $7 on lunch if I eat out BUT if this place was closer to my work I would eat here all the time-it's worth it!!

5th star will be reserved for a few visits down the road when I can try more of their menu!!

I've been going to this place since I was a child and I still love going here to eat all the time! If anyone says "Let's going to choo choo's!" you know that you're going to have awesome food for awesome prices! I always go for the seafood noodle soup and so much more! :)
Average at best. Very salty. Asked for extra spicy and they brought dressing on side.
Great deal on NYE - only $5 cover, along with reasonably priced (and strong) drinks, and go-go boys dancing all night long!  Would definitely come back for NYE or just for happy-hour.

Always my go to spot for viet food. Last night was just disappointing. I order spring rolls and a veggie dish both orders were too greasy. Service is whatever, should of known better, their Asians.  Gotta excuse that. Lol. Noodle soups are alway tasty thou.

Just learned that this place has a name other than "Choo Choo" as I have always lovingly known it. This restaurant has replaced Pho 75 (R.I.P.) as my neighborhood Pho joint. They also are great for vermicilli dishes, which are my favorite Vietnamese food! It has a hole-in-the-wall vibe, but service is quick, prices are low, and you will always leave happy and full. :)

I haven't had pho in years!!! Omg this place is awesome!!! Love the atmosphere... They seated me all the way in the back which I didn't like cause its like right by the kitchen but whatever at least the food was on point... I order two apps... papaya salad and crispy veggies spring rolls ...the papaya salad they didn't give me enough sauce so it was a little dry other then that it was fine...the crispy egg rolls was yummy ...two entrees...  Which were pho Mac and pork chop over rice...the pho mac i order had three types of beef loaded with veggies.... I order the medium but it looked like a large bowl of pho gosh ...i wonder how big the large pho would be  after seeing my pho ...yums! This place makes the best pho!! I defiantly would come back for that if i didn't live so far...The pork chop over rice was pretty good but the portion of the meat was pretty small they put imitation crab meat with eggs on the side which is kinda weird but whatever lol ...all that food cost around 15 bucks!! I think that was pretty awesome with all the food I order came out to 15 bucks!

Stellar (meaning very low) prices, generous portion sizes, and speedy service. Oh, plus $2 Thai iced tea! I got vermicelli with BBQ pork and meat on a sugar cane stick and pork balls, I think, for $6.95.  And that's if you get the "upgrade" from the standard $5.95 vermicelli, which already seems to have a lot of goodies included.  The pho is $5.95 (large) or $6.95 (x-large) - guess there's no size small for the pho.

There's additional seating upstairs.  This place was packed when we came on a Saturday night, though it was past standard dinner hour.  I would definitely come back in the future for a generous-sized meal you can get for well under $10.

This is probably my favorite place to go for Vietnamese food or pho hands down in Chinatown. Known on the streets and by my friends as Chu Chu's (cuz there's a neon-lit train with steam in the window), this place has some wonderful pho indeed, which you can order large or extra large and add extra fixings as you want for an additional charge. My go-to for pho here is usually 106, which has a nice portion of the cuts of beef I like (beef, tendon, and frank brisket), but really, you can't go wrong with any of the pho choices; it just kinda depends on your preference. The pho broth is phenomenal, savory, satisfying, and simple. Oh and did I mention how quickly the place gets your order out of the kitchen right in front of you? Prices here are more than reasonable and the place also takes card as well. Fish pho is not on the menu, but is a secret menu option (for those who like trying secret things). The spring rolls here are also pretty fresh and dope and they have a wide assortment of other foods and drinks available. It's really quite an extensive menu and well-worth your visit to come and eat here for lunch or dinner. What are you waiting for?

I was very disappointed when I tasted the food there.  Originally from SoCal, I know my vietnamese food and this restaurant is so bad.  I read the menu and wanted almost everything on it.  But I had to limit myself so I ordered 3 things. 

1) pho  2) bun thit nuong (dry rice noodles with BBG pork)  3) chao tom (shrimp on sugarcane).  

The pho broth was plain without spices, lots of MSG, and the meat was tough.  The dry noodle was okay but the BBQ pork was again plain, no seasoning/taste to it.  And the shrimp on sugarcane was the worst.  OMG, it tasted like cardboard without any flavor.  I would not recommend this place to anyone.  I don't believe people are okay with this kind of food.  It fails to represent vietnamese food.  In fact I don't think any of the vietnamese restaurants in Philly represent at all.  Sorry.  Try Southern California in Orange County.  Most restaurants there are good.

Stopped here for a lunch last week. My husband had a hamburger (his usual lunch choice) and he thought it was pretty good. I ordered a Cobb salad. Now a Cobb is nothing elaborate or complex: iceberg lettuce, bacon, hardboiled egg, blue or Roquefort cheese, chives, avocado, vinaigrette dressing. The lettuce was not iceberg -- it was mixed greens and they were nasty old. There was precious little bacon and no hard boiled egg. I complained. The staff agreed about the lettuce and offered to make it right. I told them to forget it, but they offered to make a fresh salad to go and only charge us for the hamburger. OK. Fine. I got a Cobb salad with mixed greens, albeit fresh ones. There was no egg and again precious little bacon and not much cheese. Sigh. The folks here are very friendly and accommodating, but they really have some bugs to work out. I hope they succeed, because someone needs to give Jones a run for their money and we need good lunch places in this part of town!

Came to this restaurant after many great reviews, expecting great food.

Expectations were surpassed on the food front.

HOWEVER, not so much with the staff. 

When my girlfriend and I were waiting to be served, the waiters were wandering aimlessly around the restaurant, a couple of them looking miserable and grimey, almost sickly. 

They probably were, because not a couple hours after having eaten at this restaurant, I caught the stomach flu. 

TL;DR - Good food at the price of two week's worth of fever, vomiting, and diarrhea.

The food was good; my husband had the chicken BLTA and I had the Bucatini pasta. Sadly, the service was very slow; I don't think the place has sufficient waitstaff and may have been taxed by a very large group of over 15. It wouldn't normally have been such an issue, but we almost didn't make a 7:00 PM show a block away when we were prompt for our 5:45 PM reservation. Dinner was less than relaxing as a result.

So yummy! Friendly staff, very tasty menu, with many affordable and healthy options! Very fresh options to chose from! I was so happy with my first visit! Great atmosphere and decent hours! Parking is a pain in the butt but totally worth it!

Where to begin? The Pho broth is lacking favor and is substandard. The high rating and expectations makes this place a disappointment. I highly recommend not eating Pho here as broth is king in Pho and this place don't have it. Disregard the high rating. The waitstaff here are also uncomfortably watching you eat in anticipation of serving you which creates an awkward environment.

Ok. I'm a white guy, but having traveled a great deal and the fact that I eat Pho at least once a week, makes me qualified to write this review. One of my favorite dishes is Beef and Tendon Pho, but what I was served here was bad. The tendon was overcooked and way too soft, with chunks of fat hanging off it. The the beef was tasteless and tough. The bean sprouts were yellow and stale. I could go on about this for another page, but I feel that I've said enough.
Comparable to lemonade in LA! Love their fresh juices and salads. Lots of vegan and gluten free options! The goods smoothie or beet salad with goat cheese are a must have!
I have been going here since college and still have the best pho in philly!  You just can't go wrong with XLG bowl of Pho!

This is one of my favorite Chinatown destinations--it's cheap and delicious! 

I always order the Tom Yum soup (perfect if you're craving hot and sour--esp. in the wintertime), the raw flank steak (served with fresh cilantro, crispy shallots/garlic, crushed peanuts, and a chili vinaigrette), and usually a whole steamed striped bass with ginger and scallions--and for around $20 a whole, fresh fish is a super bargain. And an avocado shake for dessert! YUM!!!

And let's get to the good part: C H E A P  A L C O H O L. Awesome.
Beers are under $3, mixed drinks are under $5. But that's everywhere in Chinatown pretty much.

Any minuses would be that it takes a long time to get a check or refills sometimes, and I think it closes pretty early--like 10pm?
Ignoring Asian customers on the top floor dance floor is not a good strategy hunty sorry blonde girl I am not having your bullsh*t

The concept is pretty cool, but the unremarkable service combined with mediocre food will keep us from going back. We liked the western movies playing, but continued issues on both visits with the sound system blaring off and on was jolting while trying to enjoy a dinner. Baked potatoes weren't throughly cooked or served warm, cheese was a large glob and not melted, but not cold either. Prime rib was undercooked and salmon was tough and greasy. The salads were drenched in Ceaser and lettuce was wilted. The beer was cold and the calamari was pretty good though. Overall not worth $80 plus a tip. We really wanted to like this place, the location and ambience are great.

The service at this particular location rocks! I'm lactose intolerant and therefore can't have their salad dressing, butter on the breadsticks, etc, but my server is always super patient in helping me. It's nice to know that your server isn't annoyed that you're physically incapable of consuming a type of food. 
Also, the food has also been awesome every time I've gone in. I've never had a "bad" order of anything.
Cheap, and Good. Not the best Pho I've had, but its good. The portions are huge.

Whenever I say Xe Lua to anyone, they look at me like some type of weirdo. But when I mention choo choo, they're like "OH, I love that place!". It's the same place...

I've been eating here since I was a kid. I remember the food quality being better from years ago. OR, I'm just a picky snob now. Who knows. Their service is still fast and rushing, though. 

My last trip to choo choo's was after a Kelly Drive run. I was starving. I ordered banh beo (rice cakes) and bo luc lac (stir fried beef cubes). My friends ordered a goi cuon (summer roll) and pad thai (stir fried rice noodles). I love their Pad Thai here. The other stuff, not so much. 

The banh beo was missing the tiny dried shrimp, which I like. The dried pork that was sprinkled on top had a funny taste (expired?). 

Bo luc lac is supposed to be stir fried filet mignon, according to their menu. The meat was so tough that I thought it was stir fried beef chuck. It also had way more peppers and onions than beef. I don't think bo luc lac is even supposed to have onions and peppers in it. 

I know their pad thai isn't very authentic, but it's still delicious! Don't forget to add the lime to the noodles. 

The only times I come here are when friends choose to. If I'm craving Vietnamese food, I go to Washington Ave. Don't forget to grab a bubble shake!

Omg y'all... just go to Applebee's. At least you can get a dollarita to wash the taste out of your mouth. 

I got:
Pretzel crusted chicken - tasted burnt and flavorless
Caesar salad with dressing on the side- dressing was not on the side and no apology came with that fact just "is that ok?" .... surrrrre
Lobster roll - not sure why this came on a hamburger bun.

Anywhooo not sure why so many people are raving about this place I'll chalk it up to them coming into the city from the burbs and eating there on their lunch break.
This place is amazing! I only wish I lived closer. My daughter had the pink dragon and I had the grilled cheese and tomato soup. Devine! I will defiantly return!

Always a great time here. I only eat fish and seafood so I have never tried Pho. They had a vegetarian version that was delicious!!! I was so pleased. I am usually turned off by the smell of the broth, but this broth was crazy good. The prices are so reasonable and it is a comfortable and casual setting. I love that all of the waiters wait on you. There is no assigned waiter so the service is quite fast and accurate. As soon as you finish, your plates are picked. Your water is constantly refilled. They do a great job in customer service. I am a big fan of the lemongrass shrimp!!! Try it out!
I've been going here since high school, and it's still one of my fave places to eat in Chinatown, I always get the house special pho and it's always delicious!!
Love this place for breakfast!  Great Cafe con leche and best Cuban bread around.  Haven't been for lunch but their Jouevos Con Queso breakfast sandwich (egg & cheese) is one of the best in town.
it's always empty here, and a bit older, but good for happy hour drinks - there is a dance floor upstairs and they have an asian night once a month there

The clouds have parted... and there at the center, is a huge bowl of Pho.

Absolutely delicious and enlightening (thus the first sentence) lunch experience at Pho Xe Lua today! I felt almost treacherous ditching my normal spot, Pho Cali, and wandered a little further away from work to this spot. What a good idea and I will absolutely be coming here again in the near future.

I got regular rare steak pho. The meat and noodle portions were large just with a regular bowl portion. What really made this pho exceptional was the broth. So savory and had the right amount of scallions and cilantro. 

My PIC (partner in crime) got the beef stir fry noodles. Also amazing! But really I'm a Pho girl and this will be my new go to spot for it.

While we thought we were getting fresh (no precooked) wings, they tasted very much precooked and quite salty. This isn't a bad place to get Chinese takeout, you just have to be selective with what you get.

I have this place on speed dial. They produce affordably priced, delicious meals. Prices are the same for lunch and dinner, so it is great if you want a dinner that costs $5-7. Here are some of my favorites from over the years:
-Lemon grass chicken over rice
-Curry chicken over rice
-Beef with bell pepper over rice
-Chicken vermicelli
-Chicken pho

Ah, the memories. The place offers efficient service, piping hot food, and complementary tea (for dining in) during the winter time. The interior is nothing fancy, but it is the perfect place to go for a casual meal. If it gets packed, they open an upstairs seating area to relieve some of the pressure.
Love this Tucson find. The food is outstanding-especially fond of the quinoa salad. Service is excellent. I could eat here every day.

I've ordered over the phone the last 2 weekends. I go in to pick up my order a good 10-15 minutes after I place my order and they tell me it will be right out. Last weekend I waited about 20 mins after paying for my meal that I ordered over the phone just to find out it was sitting next to the register since I got there. Today I go in AND THE SAME SITUATION OCCURS. Keep in mind I am not going during a particularly busy time but it was the same girl working the register so I'm hoping she's just forgetful and not representative of the business because the food was good. I just did not like the service.

Excellent attentive service, the tomato soup and grilled cheese pop and poutine were amazing. Coming from NYC, we are very used to upscale-casual americana flavors and dishes but the food here was extremely well done and the atmosphere was sophisticated but laid-back. Loved it here and will certainly return on my trip back to philly!

We came for the juice and smoothies and ended up with the hot tropic and the goods!

The lady at the cash asked what we wanted to order, I began placing my order only for her to shout across the place at another man (I guess she forgot to give him his number). My whole point with this, is it was incredibly rude and there was never a sorry or anything. Quite frankly our server had little customer service skills period. 

The smoothies took awhile, they are a little slow considering there weren't that many people in the restaurant. 

The smoothies tasted good, except for the fact the hot tropic was insanely sweet. There were also huge chunks of dates that not even the wider straw could pick up. People go for smoothies because they want something healthy, I could have gotnmy sugar rush at Starbucks. They definitely need to cut back on the dates in this one...

The Goods smoothie was just at the right sweetness, but the entire side had smoothie all over it. We didn't discover this mess until we got in the car and had to rush back in for napkins. 

We do like the consistency of these smoothies, they are nice and thick. The decor is nice, the menu is great, but they have some obvious hurdles to overcome.

All of the dishes came out at different times the potatoes were cold, prime rib was barely warm, the creamed spinach had zero flavor and was cold. They need to work on the timing in the kitchen. The marinara was good. The shrimp scampi had incredibly delicious noodles. The owner or manager was walking around in a T-shirt and a ball cap while all of the servers were dressed in a uniform of a western cowboy shirt. We thought it was inappropriate that place with $36 entrées had somebody who was managing walking around looking like a slob. Take some pride and set a good example.

I'm not an expert in Pho, but this was absolutely delicious. The service was efficient, the food was very reasonably priced and with good sized portions, and it was busy with diners - usually a good sign. I can't wait to go back and introduce all my friends to it.
I've only gotten take out but the food and prices are great. Love to bun bo heu, way more pork knuckles than some places give you.

Pretty good. A little hole in the wall place with dated decor. The pho and crispy spring rolls were both sufficent. Two of us ate here for a total of $18. Service was good and quick. After we sat down and ordered, our food came out in like 5 mins!! My steak however was really fatty but my fiancé's was better... Maybe I just got a bad cut or something. We will return here again if we are in the city and need a cheap meal... Won't go out of our way however.
This place is no joke!  Fast service and all.  The papaya/beef jerky salad is very nice.  Beef and frank brisket is a must.  Choo choo is choolicious!!

I gravitate towards this place for the food and low prices. I enjoy eating the vegetable pho and chicken fried rice. I would also enjoy eating the summer rolls if they removed the intestinal line on the shrimp. Disgusting!

Last night I went to Pho Xe Lua for dinner because the bf was craving some chao long (or rice porridge with meat and innards)- a dish that has been hard to find in Philly since moving here all those years ago. I could make it myself, but then we would be stuck with a whole pot...and sometimes you just need a bowl to be satisfied. I was wary of the "fusion" aspect of the restaurant because I typically dislike asian places that try to do multiple cuisine. A lot of the time it ends up half@$$ for both or (shudder) all three types that they try to encompass.

The restaurant was lively, and there were a lot of diners having dinner- good sign. We ordered eggrolls, they came out steaming hot and delicious, also another good sign. I ordered the the grilled pork rice platter (com suong nuong), which is a fairly typical order for me and I have tried it at many of the different vietnamese places around philly. Much to my dismay, the rice was mushy, the pork floss was bland, and the pork cut that I got was fatty and also lacking flavor. The chao long had all the essential ingredients, but also bland. When you make rice porridge, there are lots of different types (chicken, fish, etc) but when you make that type you cook the meat in the rice porridge. In this restaurant'scase, bc they had multiple types and prob to make it easier for themselves, my guess is that they made a plain porridge pot (no flavor) and add in the meat of the type you order. 

Overall, neither of us were pleased with our meal choice. I dont think I will be back here anytime soon.

Best pho in Philly! 

They have this recipe perfected for sure. The waitstaff can be kind of brusque, but I'm not there to be coddled! They bring out your pho super fast and it always hits the spot. 

Bring cash because they have a credit minimum (I think $10) and a regular size is certainly under that. I've never needed an XL because the regular is so filling. 

Complimentary green tea to boot. Can't beat it!

I just can't help myself!  This place is literally a once a week stop.
I get the same thing everytime.  The breakfast burrito and the goods smoothie.  I really should try other things but the burrito and smoothie are just so good! 
Let's start with the smoothie.   It is made up of banana, kale, vanilla, almond milk, and other goodies...i think blueberry.  Anyway, so tasty and refreshing.  I instantly feel healthy after slurping it down. 
The burrito is filled or i guess i should say stuffed with egg, quinoa, tomota, cheese, turkey sausage and spinach. It is served with a dipping sauce.  Not sure what the sauce is but it has a lil kick to it.  Anyway,  it is so tasty and flavorful.  So much flavor hits you in the mouth and it is fantastic.  I love the burrito.   It is very filling.  I will eat this and not eat again until dinner.
Price wise,  i think you get what you pay for.  Maybe even a lil more.  13 and some change for the smoothie and filling burrito.  I think that's a legit deal. 
Staff wise,  they are friendly and they serve it fast.
They also serve lunch but i haven't tried any of the options yet.  But i have to say,  today i saw their steak all sliced up and marinated and I'm pretty sure i drooled a little.  I'll need to try lunch for sure! 

The End.

Hadn't been here in awhile and happened to be at a meeting in town and ventured in for lunch.

I have never had a bad meal here.   I love trying different soups (they have an extensive menu).   Wanted spicy,  so went with the Bun Bo Hue.  Fantastic,  though you have to be forewarned:  gets its great flavor from trotters ... yup, that would be pigs feet !   The pieces of fatty brisket are yummy and abundant !  And it packs a kick.

The only reason I didn't give this place 5 stars is because I'm comparing it to a number of other favorite Viet places and it doesn't quite surpass some of the others that I rate a 5.

Service is very quick and the prices are fantastic !

Great Thai Iced Tea and Cafe Su Da !

Great space with clean airy vibe. Food is so tasty and healthy! Fast and friendly service. Only gripe was my rice bowl had some very hard and dry rice  that almost chipped my teeth. Also can be pricey.
My boyfriend and I have been coming here regularly for years. It's always our go-to spot for Pho therapy.

I think this is the best pho I've had in Philly. Better than Pho Ha. Better than Pho 75.

Why?

Clear, clean, aromatic broth. (Not cloudy or questionable). 

Tender, high-quality tasting beef. (Not chewy or gamey). 

That's really all you need to know. This place may be a diamond in the rough that is Chinatown. Check it out.
Friendly staff, great service, food is tasty, reasonable price, menu has many options. I think is best Vietnamese food in the Chinatown.
Best gay bar in the city.  Find bartender Ashley, she'll get you messed up in a hurry.

Loved this place.  Bright and friendly.  Looks like everything is very fresh.  Love that they have juice and smoothie with vegetables.   I will definitely try again.  I had the hulk and it was better than expected.
Absolutely loved this place! I got the kale salad and the green juice. It was perfect and the employees were so nice and helpful

3.5 STARS

Very good Pho. Had the Beef and Beef ball, 108. Hearty soup base, barely any 'msg', fresh bean sprouts/basil leaves on the side. The beef ball is generic, found in market. The beef is ok sliced beef. Ok portion of noodles, big bowl of 'soup' base that is very drinkable. Good price at 5.50

However, the rice plates are so-so. Had the pork chop with rice, and fish cake. Came with 2 leaves of fresh lettuce. The rice was ur plain old rice, not even broken. The pork chop was kind of dry, and only came with one piece. The fish cake was not good at all. Mushy. 

The Viet coffee was pretty good, $2.

One of my favorite places in Chinatown! Come here if you're looking for a great, filling meal that won't hurt your wallet. 

Service is incredibly fast (although it may help that my best friend and her husband are regulars here)! 

Try an XL bowl of pho - I think it was still only around $8 and I couldn't finish my bowl (and I don't EVER have a problem finishing a good bowl of pho). Broth is flavorful, and bowls are fully loaded with meat and noodles - no skimping here!

Affordable, authentic Vietnamese food with a wide variety of options.  It's not some hip, modern, fusion-y restaurant.  It's just a straight up, high-value Vietnamese restaurant that will give you a bang for your buck whether you're up for a good rice dish or bowl of pho.  

Went to lunch with a co-worker and the place was packed! Ordered the house specialty rice place with the pork chops and it came out with two incredible pieces of pork chops.  Left there soo full and satisfied.  Will be coming back again.
I've only ever had one pastry from here.  But damn, it was a memorable one!  I can't stop thinking about the cream filling.  Addictive.  Stuff fantasies are made of...  I'll be back.

Not the best pho around- that distinction belongs to Pho75- but a very close second, in my opinion. I'd actually rather go here when in Chinatown because when it comes to everything besides pho, this place is unbeatable. 

The appetizers taste incredible, and they even have stuffed grape leaves, which is very rare around here with Vietnamese joints. The jackfruit shakes- my personal favorite- are so good that I usually order 2 or 3, with plenty of rum added in for good measure. 

I can't say enough about this place. If you want more than just pho, you can't go anywhere for Vietnamese in Philly and have a better meal than at Xe Lua.
This place is still One of my favorites. I've tried several things on their menu now in the quinoa salad is amazing. I've actually never had anything bad here

I consider this to be my first time having pho. In truth, I have had it before, but the dish was unmemorable and I was so clueless in my technique that it simply did not count. So, I started fresh at Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai, and I'm glad I did. I had the Beef Pho and I instantly understood the hype. I do not have the experience to say that this is the best, as many others have, but I did enjoy the dish and trust that this could be some of Philly's best. The servers at Pho Xe Lau Viet Thai were eager to remind me that I am a newcomer. I know the reason, it's because my boyfriend is Asian and he is therefore superior in this setting. I am used to being ignored when in this situation and know that they will only address him. But when you give me the fork, you hurt my feelings. I will not hold it against you, I loved the Pho and I will be back for more. Maybe in time I can prove myself to you, servers of Pho Xe Lau Viet Thai. Looking forward to it!

Tonight we tried Classic, primarily based upon positive Yelp reviews.  Since it was Prime Rib Tuesday, we each had the 24-oz. prime rib, which comes with stuffed baked potato and garlic-basalmic green beans and soup or salad for $42.  I ordered lobster tail as an add-on, as did my friend.  I also added Dijon leeks and marrow butter.  We both opted for the house salad.  My friend had beer, and I had two glasses of Merlot.

The salad was fresh, crisp, and delicious!  it contained a nice melanage of greens and included carrot.  

Garlic bread was hot, fresh, and perfectly seasoned -- not too buttery, not too garlicky.  It was also soft rather than hard, which my older dining companion appreciated.

The prime rib was PERFECT!  It was seasoned to perfection, tender, and had some fat but wasn't too fatty.  The aus jus and horseradish were the perfect accompaniment.  The stuffed potato was good but on the small side and a bit hard (leftover?).  It included cheese, butter, and green onion (yay!), but I don't remember bacon bits or sour cream.  The garlic-basalmic young French green beans were to die for!!  Very flavorful, with just a little bit of crisp.  My plate contained two small rock lobster tails with accompanying drawn butter.  The lobster was tender and delicious!  The Dijon leeks were disappointing -- the mustard overpowered the leeks, and that comes from a mustard! LOVER!  The marrow butter was good, but I didn't think it was worth $5.

For dessert I had the tiramisu, which I was informed was house-made.  It was incredibly fresh and delicious, topped with fresh berries.  A 12 on a 1 to 10 scale!

The service was attentive but not hovering throughout the meal.  Our waiter kept us happy, checking on us periodically.  We had the opportunity to speak with the two owners, one acting as host and the other making the dining room rounds to make sure everything was copacetic.  These gentlemen were both very pleasant and seemed to be attuned to customer satisfaction. 

My cheque, with two glasses of Merlot, including tax and tip, came to $124+.  Why?  The two glasses of "house" Merlot were $11.50 each.  My friend and I were each charged $3.50 for garlic bread. Come on, guys!  BREAD IS GRATIS IN ALMOST EVERY RESTAURANT, especially of the caliber that you're trying to pull off.  Of course, I expected to be charged for my add-ons (leeks, marrow butter, lobster tail) that I had ordered but was not expecting the bread charge or the inordinately expensive Fleming's-priced wine.

I also ding Classic for not having any bottled or sparkling water whatsoever. Get a clue, guys!  Pellegrino would be perfect, 

Despite the neighborhood, the place is lovely, with a hip/sexy/nuveau Italian-western vibe and decor.  My only complaint about the ambience is the echo, not only of the patrons conversing at tables but the traffic noise on Stone.  I think hanging tapestries or perhaps even a few strategically-placed rugs or runners would help obviate the noise.

Overall, this was a very positive dining experience. Most of the food was outstanding, although I do not recommend the Dijon leeks.  Also, if you ask for bread then expect to be charged for it.  

We will be returning to Classic to check out their pasta offerings.

Super cute place with nice outdoor seating for warmer days. Was craving fresh juice and decided to try. I got the Clean It Up juice w/ orange, pineapple, parsley, cucumber & lemon. Good for headache relief, blood detox & high in fiber. It was so refreshing & delicious!

Great, fast service on an early Sunday afternoon. The food looks sooo good and there looks like plenty of vegan options. Can't wait to come back to try the some food and smoothies!

Can't go wrong with eggplant parm!  This was our go-to place when the kids were growing up, and the hubby and I still come here for some tasty, affordable food.  Breadsticks do not have as much flavor as they once did, and they seem to be putting more lettuce and less veggies in the salads, but I guess everyone is cutting back.

Went here last night with a group of 8 friends not expecting them to have room to fit us all right away considering the place isn't very large.  We were immediately sat by a friendly waiter and we all ordered a round of drinks which were extremely cheap yet satisfying.  I started off with the vegetarian spring rolls which came out quickly and were hot, steamy, and delicious! Shortly thereafter, the large Pho Ga (pho with chicken) came out.  The portion was more than enough for me, but it was hearty and delicious and exactly what I needed/wanted. Whoever said that chicken noodle soup was good for the soul obviously hasn't tried pho. I'm definitely coming back here soon. Great location, great food, great staff!

Best Thai seafood noodle soup I 've had for the lowest price. Absolutely the most delicious broth complimented by ...non-intrusive and efficient service. Hands down the best bargain in town. LOVE IT!
Great menu and bar, in terms of balancing creativity and tradition. Only cons: they don't do delivery and it can get a bit noisy-the place is always packed. Don't go: let me have it for myself:-).

I wouldn't recommend coming to this Olive Garden. I went out to eat with my father and my 5 year old. Note: we were all feeling fine before we ate here. I ordered my food which was good, they over cooked my fathers pasta and my daughter ordered kids pepperoni pizza. My father is Italian and can tell what has gone bad just by taste. My daughter offered my father a slice of pizza since she felt bad about his food. After my father had his first bite of that pizza, he said the pizza went bad. (My daughter had already eaten half of the pizza with no problem.) So I had taken the pizza from my daughter. We left after I had finished my plate. It's been a few hours since coming home from the restaurant and my daughter was complaining of stomach pains and dizziness. I had given her a bath and gave her some medicine for the stomach pain. She went to sleep after a while. At 2:00 AM she woke up crying. I went in to check on her and I see that she had vomited all over her bed. Hearing her still complaining about stomach pain ,she was also looking flushed. I had felt her head and notice some heat. I had checked her temperature and she had a high fever! Called her Dr and he said to take her to the ER. Turned out she had food poisoning! Never will I set a hair into that restaurant ever!

Not going to lie, when I walked into this restaurant for the first time I was like where am I? But it is sooo good! I have converted all my friends to going here.

First off, the menu is extensive. They pretty much have anything you can think of. And everything I have ever had is amazing. And it is sooo reasonable! I always get the shrimp pad thai, i think it is around 10 or so dollars. It is sooo big, it is enough for two people for sure. 

Also they have really cheap drinks. Like $4 wines. I love to come here before going out, or for just a random night in china town. There really is no ambiance, but with food this good and this cheap it doesnt matter!

THE best Chinese food takeout I've ever had.  Seriously, it's the perfect mix of grease and savory flavors.  I don't know how they do it, especially since there are some Mexicans there too.  Maybe that's the secret.  

I have a weird allergy to carrots which can make ordering takeout Chinese difficult.  (lots of chinese food has carrots and language barriers etc etc).  This place has NEVER put carrots in anything I've ordered.  The woman who answers the phone is ON THE BALL.  Which makes for such a pleasant experience when ordering.

They like Mario's pizza across the way, do not deliver.  But there is a blockbuster, super fresh, and rite aid in the same shopping centre.  Order your food, do your errands and end it off with a fantastic lo mein.  

PS Their Chinese Spare Ribs are to DIE for.

Absolutely love going there. Service is okay depending on how much people is there. Usually I go and it's pretty busy so I am kinda okay with their service. 

Their pho are I think the best in Chinatown. The food comes out pretty quickly so theres not much wait.  Their smallest bowl is a large bowl so I do recommend going when you can finish it all so you dont waste the  food. :] 

Prices are cheap, the large bowl is like 5.50. & it's from Chinatown?! #fellinlove lol. 

Their bubble drinks are cool too and they always put it take-out drinking containers and not in those glasses so you do not feel like you have to rush the drink and actually enjoy the goodness.

Shame the owners let this place get run down. It is a large bar, just drab and dark inside. Plus the lighting outside is horrible, unless you know where it is, you would miss it.  drinks are cheap and the bar staff nice and helpful.

We've heard great reviews from our friends who dine here frequently so we went for the tasting menu. Overall disappointing. The fois gras was stringy which didn't have a pleasant texture nor taste. The pickling of some of the vegetables was so extreme which overwhelmed the dish and taste buds. There was a lack in balance of flavors.The cheese in the final course may not have been stored properly because it tasted rank (almost fishy) and I never met a cheese I didn't like. I really hope this was an off night for them.
The pho and shrimp rolls just ok here, nothing special. I had higher expectations for the place based off of the reviews. They have a big menu of other items if you don't want pho.

I've since tried other dishes at Pho Xe Lua so I'm updating my review.

Filet Mignon with lemongrass is still tasty.
Pho is good, comforting.
Appetizer with raw beef slices is solid.
Fish dish was not as good.
Tofu with vegetables was uninspired -- I'd avoid ordering this in the future.

For $5, the mixed drinks were solid. Quite good for the price.
Solid Pho, nothing crazy. Pretty delicious. My boyfriend got a non-pho dish was a pretty disappointed with it. But the beers were only $3 so he got over it quickly.

4 1/2 Stars. So....I found my new fave place to detox! 

Don't get me wrong...I'm the kinda gal who loves her some bacon. I've defeated a 32 oz. Porter House steak like it was a 4oz. child portion. But every once in a while, you need to take a step back, and detox. You need to let your body have some wholesome nutrients. And this is the place to do it.

I walked in with the expectation that it was going to be like a Jamba Juice. Not that Jamba Juice is bad or anything, but you know....it is what it is. Wow was I pleasantly surprised! This place has an LA vibe to it. And by that, I mean that the first thing you notice are the nice and tanned people manning the juice bar. That, plus the cool decor, abundant amount of fruits and wheatgrass, and healthy looking people eating there! 

I just felt like snacking,  so I ordered the Quinoa Salad, and added turkey to it. The bf ordered the Roasted Chicken & Brie Sandwich. OMG. The salad literally came out on a lunch tray. It was huge! Not quite Cheesecake Factory salad huge, but it was quite large, and full of yummy goodness. The bf's sandwich was delicious as well, but much smaller than my salad! Haha (check out my pix) we also ordered the Daily Buzz Power Shake. It was very good as well. It had coffee, cocoa powder, almond milk, chia seeds, dates, and a banana in it. 

I wil definitely be back next time I'm in need of a detox. Or heck, just when I want some good, fresh food (and juice/smoothie)!! :)
The beef pho noodle soup is just okay here, I've had better flavor at the restaurants down on Washington Ave.

YAY for healthier options in Tucson!

++POSITIVES++
+ ACAI BOWLS!  -- It's so freaking hot in the summer that I'm surprised not a lot of places serve acai bowls!  Needless to say we always get one when we come here because my one-year old son is crazy about it.  The honey they use in it is heavenly.  
+ We've had the Big Melons juice and love it.  
+ Chicken and Brie sandwich is a favorite for my husband
+ Love all the healthy options they have
+ Nicely decorated, lofty space to enjoy a snack/meal with friends

--NEGATIVES--
- PRICEY esp for Tucson. Sandwiches are $8 and are about the size of a homemade sandwich ...with no free sides ...free side of carrots might be a nice touch.
+ Parking in this complex SUCKS.  It has to be one of the worst places to get parking in Tucson besides that Speedway/Wilmot shopping complex.

#supportlocal #shoplocal :)  I hope this place does well and stays open because we really do enjoy it!

With Miss Saigon in Jersey City as a benchmark for average Vietnamese food, I am starting to lean towards it being the best I have ever had.  Not being from Philly and not researching Asian food for this trip really had me at a disadvantage.  Most of my food adventures in Philly are sandwich based, so fortunately I had yelp to fall back on.  Sometimes it's a gamble with yelp, but more times than not, I'll find that gem.  Since I had researched on yelp mobile, this was the most reviewed restaurant in downtown Chinatown that wasn't Chinese.

We ordered plenty, Pad Thai, Beef over rice with poached egg, stew over rice, fried fish.  Pad Thai came out of the gate first, like a bolt it took off.  The future looked good.  Then I got my beef over rice, it came to a slow pace.  Stew over rice, a sudden halt.  Not good and drops to the bottom of my Vietnamese list.  The beef was bland and the poached egg?  Just didn't get that.  I'll stick to cheesesteaks when I am in Philly.

Bad yelp reference.
Awesome food and always good service plus the prices are really reasonable. Servers are on their game and just need to turn your head to get their attention.
Everything from this place is so good and the price is average. Drinks are good too, my favorite drink is their avocado smoothie. Yummm

I never want to take a pho to go. I always have it hot at the restaurant. It's just not good to eat at home. I want to savor it while it's hot. It's best when they serve it to you and you are ready to slurp the soup. It's always been my practice that if I want pho, I want it now. Pho aside, we came back to this restaurant because we really liked it's fast service and good food. My partner ordered noodles with seafood but to our surprise and disappointment, he found a big chuck of hair in his food (just like the hair you'll find in the bath tub - yuk!). It's really horrible because I don't understand why would a big chuck of hair will get in the food unless, you use to wash the seafood in the sink and the the cook showers there too. It's careless and therefore, unacceptable. I don't care if the manager thinks that it was an accident. They should be very very careful in preparing/cooking the food and should take more time to clean the food. For that matter, I got to downgrade it because all I can remember is that strands of  hair in the seafood - even a seconds won't make me eat it again. You might not see me here again because down the block is Pho 75. I'll check it out next time we are in Philly Chinatown.

A terrific new addition to Tucson steakhouse offerings!

Food:  I had the Tues., night Prime Rib Special, served with two sides in addition to soup or a salad.  The prime rib was exactly medium-rare and very good.  The vegetables were nicely prepared, one with a good quality Cheddar sauce and the 2nd with a balsamic based seasoning.  The vegetables were delicious and the salad crunchy.  My husband had the Chicken Marsala, linguini served with an Alfredo sauce, and soup.  All were tasty and more than even he could eat which is rarely the case for him.    The portions were quite generous.

Drink:  A full bar, wine & beer, with a 'happy hour' deal.

Ambiance:  QUIET!!!  My husband and I could talk easily to each other without having to raise our voices to be heard.  There was soft western movie music coming from a dining theatre for those who wish to watch spaghetti westerns with a drink or a meal.    The lighting was soft with plenty of room between tables allowing privacy.  The blue tablecloths covered with clean white paper, with the burgundy cloth napkins and table settings including wine glasses, gives the space a simple elegance, a nice subdued feeling tone.

Service:  Terrific.  The wait staff and host appear to be genuinely happy to be working there.  Everything was served timely and hot with staff checking back twice.  

Prices: Competitive with the two Tucson chains and one other locally owned steakhouse.

We'll be back, as I hope others will, providing the owners a steady clientele and a successful enterprise.

A bowl of Pho (#101) would probably make our Vice President jump out from his seat and yelp 
"This is a big f--king deal". Yes!  That was my reaction, and many yelpers too, who tried it in Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai (choo choo restaurant). It tastes so good and makes me want to yell (but obviously I didn't), instead, I yelp to you now. so let's begin:

Pho #101 (Large or Extra-Large): Even you order a large bowl; you will be amazed by its size when the bowl is actually sitting in front of you. Yes, it's HUGE in my opinion. Inside the bowl, a pile of various types of beef and beef inner parts (such as thin cuts of beef, brisket, fatty flank, tendon, tripe...etc) that covers up top. Right under them, you will find a ton (a little bit exaggeration) of white rice noodles in clear beef broth. Let me rephrase myself one more time on the last part of my sentence : CLEAR BEEF broth (many other restaurants are serving NO-CLEAR, NO-Beef, or nasty broth). If you dare to look at it again, you will probably think that you are getting an extra-large order (don't be shy about it, ladies!). A plate of fresh greens, herbs, vegetables and various others are right next to your soup and waiting for actions. Once you properly "mix" them into your soup, Da..da..da!! delicious! Yet, the price is under 7 dollar. Can't be that.

Pad Thai: Spaghetti like rice noodle mixed with red hot/sweet sauce covered up by big shrimps, dry tofu and others on top looks very nice. And of course it tastes good too. It's one of the best pad thais I have in Philly so far. Yes, it's under $10. Great deal, great taste!

Many other "Exotic" drinks such as martinis with various flavor, bubble teas, and Avocado smooth drinks are very tasty, and yet, probably the cheapest in town!

Try them yourself in this Choo choo restaurant !!

I frequent Olive Garden, and it is usually very good, but this last visit was not so great. As usual, our server was very friendly and attentive. However, the food really fell short this time. First, it was taking a while for our food to come out, and our server said it was because the steak was still cooking, even though it was ordered medium rare. When we did get our food, the steak was more like medium well to well done. I ordered the seafood alfredo, and the shrimp and the scallops were over cooked. However, I have been to Olive Garden many times, and it is almost always satisfying. I will definitely go back, because it was probably just an off day. I still gave it three stars though, because I have had more positive experiences than negative.

I came here with a friend after 5 years absence from this restaurant :)  

The Pho was the same as i remembered; bad. The broth was bland and I can't really smell any Pho scent from it and i have sensitive nose. I still like their Bo Tai Chanh (Vietnamese Beef Carpaccio) and Bo Luc Lac (Vietnamese Shaking Beef).

The best pho in the city. Outside of that, there is a huge variety of dishes that are mostly at a great price. Service is speedy and the quality of the dishes are close to perfect. Great spot for a quick bite.

This place has a good menu, but don't order eggs. The eggs are not as advertised, they use liquid eggs. Apparently, cage free liquid eggs, but not fresh cracked eggs from their shells. Eggs from a box sounds gross to me. So, go to their other location for non boxed eggs.

What can I tell you?
So, I'm eating here with my girlfriend last night- something we do often. We ordered spring rolls, shrimp rolls, a bitchin appetizer with rare beef slices topped with french fried onions, with a lime spiked fish sauce.

She wasn't very hungry so she didn't order pho. I, however, ordered the pho tai bo vien. Now, The waiter spent at least about a minute with me, teaching me how to say pho tai bo vien properly.  Cool. He's really into his job, and very attentive. One might even say that I may have felt a bit special.

A half hour later, we realized that I might not get my pho. Our appetizers were delivered. But no pho. I looked for my waiter throughout that time span and saw him sitting in the back. He then went into the kitchen, or back room, or whatever, and never came back out.

So what I'm basically trying to say is that the waiter forgot my pho, then he disappeared, so I didn't get my pho. Are you following me here? I went out to eat pho, and didn't get my pho. At a pho joint.

But, despite all of that, those appetizers (and a couple rum flooded jackfruit shakes)  were so good, and they made me so happy, that nothing else that happened that night matters.

That tells you alot about a place. Five stars, still. If I could add a star I would.

Go here, people.

We had a Holiday work party for about 20 people last night.  This place killed it.  Food, drinks and service were all on point.
My Wife and I had the shared tyhe Ribeye and Spaghetti plate.  FANTASTIC!  I am truly a fan and cannot wait to go back.

Note:  The bar in this place was built in the 70s/80s.  It is totally unique and bad ass.

DOV. 08/11/14

We never go to OG unless someone else wants to, this was the case this week. We went to an early movie then they suggested OG because he has been ill and has a special diet. 

Greeted nicely and seated right away. Waited for server and she was not the friendliest in the world, for sure.  They were not busy yet but she seemed rude about wanting to rush the man who needed extra time to see what he could eat and answer questions. 

Hubby and I both got Pasta e Fagioli and Spaghetti and meatballs. Our receipt says we got salad but we got soup. She asked if we wanted cheese in soup, three said yes one no, she still grated cheese in his, had to get another one...waited for that. 
The other lady was not pleased with her Chicken and Gnocchi soup. 

The spaghetti meat sauce was not too tasty. As I said before, not our favorite place and they did not win us back with this meal.  Hope they do not end up like Macaroni Grill.  Closed in New Tampa.

I've had every thing from drawings to thickly woven fabrics, small and wall sized, framed here as well as repairs to frame supports repaired. Always very friendly service people who add their expertise to accomplish fantastic outcomes of projects. A very positive and creative place to do business. Total satisfaction.

So for 3 Friday's in a row we have dined and dined well with a superstar of a server in Victor in the cozy bar area and the food has been prepared picture perfect. Still not sure how diners can bring kids(noisy and unruly kids at that) into a bar area. If I can't carry my handgun in a bar area you shouldn't bring kids into a bar area but that's a whole different subject. My beautiful wife and I start with wine, breadsticks and a bowl of Alfredo sauce that is nothing short of
Liquid crack rock addicting. I envision them serving it by the glass one day. Ha ha. I highly recommend the chicken and shrimp Carbonarra. Just an excellent pasta dish. Warning! Be prepared to be wheeled out in a pasta and breadstick coma with a full belly of fine italian fare. We also highly recommend our server Victor who tends graciously to your every dining and drinking need. It's been a great 3 weeks of italian atmosphere and food and hope to continue our streak.  MANGIA !!

To start off,the building is too small for the club this tries to be.   If you go on the weekend, it is hot and cramped.   Otherwise, it isn't bad, but I can't deal with the claustrophobia.   Music is modern, different areas with different decor are perky and fun.   The clients are always up for anything, so you find what you are looking for here, no problems there.   Staff is a hit or miss,  some stuck up prissy bitches who only pay attention to their friends or model hotties, and others who make you feel like Royalty to serve your every whim.  You will figure out which is which right away and make your choice appropriately.

We've had a very good experience here in the past but our most recent visit got off to a bit of a rough start.  The vet technician had that "you are the worst pet parents ever' attitude that seems to be common among the profession, at least in my experience.  While she was gentle and caring with my fur baby her underlying tone was frustrating. Dr. Bohnke to the rescue though. She was kind and compassionate with an excellent bedside manner.  She called promptly with the lab results and took the time to discuss the results and suggested plan of treatment at length. I felt that her advice was solid without any hint of tying to sell me on additional services or tests.
For kids only. Pho noodle comes with plenty of noodles which kids must love. But for a more advanced eater, the soup is very plain.

I decided I wanted pho randomly the other day even though I've only had it one time in my life.  I looked at all of the places on yelp and really wanted to try some of the places on Washington Ave but my boyfriend screeched  "not so fast!  no washington ave!  someone just got shot there recently!".. I tried to explain that it was 100000% safe in the daylight but he wasn't having it.  So we went to this place instead.  We both had the summer rolls and the beef pho as our entree which was very good.  I was really impressed with our waiter, he explained a couple items on the menu and he was easy to understand.  Sometimes there are language barriers at Asian  restaurants and I get stressed out that I'm going to order pigs balls or something like that because I don't know what I'm ordering so I was happy.  I was also pretty pumped at how clean the place was..my garnishes were healthy and looked like they had just been washed.  I'll definitely be back to this place!

Went here with a group of friends for my birthday. We arrived at 8:30 but had a party of 15 so weren't seated for over an hour even though we had a "reservation" which i dont think actually existed. Luckily they have a pretty good sized bar so we enjoyed that until we were seated. For such a large party, we received our drinks, soups/salad and entrees pretty quickly. We had 2 servers to our table and one was good and the other was ok but it could have been that it was 9:30 at night by this time and we were a large party. They were both very tentative and made sure we had fresh bread and filled glasses throughout the whole meal. They brought out a surprise dessert and sang for my birthday which was sweet. Sangria i had was good but the 5 cheese Ziti wasn't great. I should have went with a 3 course option that a couple others had that looked yummy.  Overall it was an average Olive Garden, nothing great but nothing bad.

Stormi

Oh pho train, I'm so MAD at you!  My dining companion wanted pho but I didn't because i felt like it was too hot out for soup.  

I had some deluxe vermicelli and it was the nastiest thing I've ever eaten in my life.  Gross enough to make me knock this place down a star.   The noodles were overdone, and the fried chunks of meat on top just tasted disgusting.  

I like the pho here, but I'm not going here again unless it's for pho.

Hands down the best Vietnamese/Thai food I have ever had in my life. 

First of all, the portions are HUGE. And, as if that's not enough of a selling point, the flavors are always bold and delicious. 

The pho is definitely my favorite. The 210 and 212, the chicken and beef with lemongrass and peppers/onions are amazing too. I also highly recommend the 216, the chicken and potato curry. 

On top of the deliciously flavorful  food, the staff is always so polite, friendly, fast and attentive. 

This place is so good that you will find yourself craving it weekly, my family has been going there or getting take out at least once a week for about 7 Years now. 

Give it a try, you won't regret it.

Oh my goodness (in a Minnesota accent).

Expensive but GOOD for the GOODNESS of your body. 

The Daily Buzz is the good, gooder, goodest.

Alright that was all very good and annoying.

Worth the price. Even if I feel super unhip and so very in my 30s when I'm surrounded by the kale consuming good hipsters. :D

In January I was diagnosed with diabetes, and had to make some drastic lifestyle changes.  Other than changing my unhealthy eating, I had to loose some of the 340 pounds that I weighed at the time, and reduce my 11.2, A1c.  After being on a strict non sugar/carb diet, and desperately craving something sweet, I googled "sugar free frozen yogurt."  Thankfully Sundaze came up in the results.  That was January.  Now its  October, and I have lost 155 pounds, and blood sugar has returned to normal. A1c 5.3.  I can't say enough what a blessing Sundaze is with their sugar free, fat free frozen yogurt.  I don't know what I would do with out them.  Their yogurt really hits the spot, and cures my sweet tooth, and most importantly, has no effect on my blood glucose levels.  Their tasty treat is a life saver.  While it is a 46 mile round trip from our house to their shop, it is very worth the trip, and we make it quite often.  The flavors change regularly, so there is always a variety.  Service is top notch.  When it is inconvenient to make the trip, I can call and Wendy gladly puts some aside for us.  We even celebrated my birthday with one of their yogurt pies made with delicious sugar free/fat free frozen yogurt.  Again, I can't say how grateful I am for Wendy, and Peter, and Sundaze Frozen Yogurt.  I don't think that I would have achieved the success with the weight loss, or the management of my diabetes, without the availability of Sundaze sugar free, fat free frozen yogurt.  For that I am truly grateful.   Thank you Sundaze, I hope you are here for a long, long time.

Choo choo pho is the best bang for your buck in philly, hand down.  I've been going here for years now but when I first moved to philly, my buddy and I searched for the best pho in town.  Being from the bay area in california, pho is a staple!  The portions we found here were gigantic and the food was pretty good all around, not the best but for how cheap it is and how much you get, this truly is a great deal.  Their other menu items like the curries, vermicelli bowls and spring rolls are also delicious and a good size.  I started bringing a bunch of my friends in and now we're all hooked on choo choo pho.  They know us so well when we come in that we simply raise our hands for those who want an XL-105 and the servers know what the other regulars like too, whether it be the yellow curry chicken or pad thai.  If you're on a budget, this place will spare your wallet and totally satisfy you stomach :)

Love this club always a great tim and awesome staff !!!
And the owners always make you feel like family !
A refreshing healthy place to eat. Great juice and shot options, along with sandwiches and bowls.

OK, this has been one of my favorite places in Philadelphia since I moved here almost 10 years ago. I don't think anything has changed except the lovely LCD monitors picturing a slideshow of food offerings. The pho is always good, and though I am not an expert food critic, I am told it is the best around. We get the pad thai, which is a little dry but good nonetheless. Fresh and fried spring rolls are good. I just discovered the vermicelli with spring roll combo and it is really light and delicious. We always get the avocado shake with tapioca which is delish but be careful not to fill up before your food arrives!

While trying out all the different Pho places around Philly, I find that this was mediocre. The broth was watery and had almost no flavor to it. Perhaps because it was Saturday during lunch time and it was starting to get pretty busy. But still, the broth is everything and I was let down by it. The meat was tender and delicious and the staff was very friendly. All in all, I'm glad I went here once

I only go here when I get dragged in by my friends, but honestly, this place sucks. Even with the tacky "makeover," the place is just embarrassing on every level. First of all, the name! iCandy? How dumb is that?? Secondly, the people that go here -- a bunch of anorexic underage, overdramatic twinks doused in Axe body spray with bleach blond hair, fake color contacts and wearing Amrani Exchange shirts. Thanks, but no thanks! The music sucks, unless you like listening to Beyonce and Lady Gaga remixes over and over. The showers on the second level with the guys dancing? LOL!!! Oh, and let's not forget the third floor with the cool lava lamps! Give me a break. The worst is you can't even enjoy the tiki bar in the summer because they allow people to go out there and smoke, which is actually a violation of Philly's smoking ban. Trust me, if you have any dignity, avoid this place!! Oh, and who could forget their famous Tuscan Tavern restaurant!??! hahaha Who eats dinner in a gay bar? WTF??

Always a great meal and great service.  Try the seafood Tom yum soup.   Mmmmm. Been coming here for years and have never had a bad meal.   The goi cuon is the best.    Try the no tai Chan. - raw flank steak marinated in lime juice with fresh basil, crushed roasted peanuts and a great fish based dipping sauce
This place is horrible, never a good crowd.. always empty and the bouncer at the front is an old man who gets off on giving people a hard time.. much better venues in Philly !

This review is really overdue. We came here for our daughter's birthday mid-week in January. We haven't been to Olive Garden in a really long time, but this one definitely made us question why we don't dine here more often (it's because we are always on some sort of low-carb diet...sorry). I love their bread sticks and salads. I had one too many bread sticks because they were so warm, fluffy, and delicious. Everyone's pasta dishes were supreme as well. The only minor complaint was that there seemed to have been some wait time in seating people even though there were plenty of empty tables.

Kinda nasty environment even for a pho place, but holy hell the bowls are HUGE and the summer rolls are HUGE!  Everything in this place is mamoth.  Great place to go if you're hungry.  

I felt a bit uncomfortable a few times when I went there...is there such thing as a vietnamese mafia?:-)  

Definately one to check out though, don't miss..BRING YOUR APPETITE!

Awesome food, great ambience, but we hear they're closing soon.  I hope the owners find a new location, because the food is really outstanding.  The peach cobbler makes having to buy bigger pants totally worth it.   It's a shame to see a place like this not make it.

I tried this place out for Sunday brunch last weekend and was really impressed! I literally wanted to try everything on the menu. We also went during prime brunch hours and didn't have to wait! I'll definitely be back.
the food is great. the staff is not so friendly. and i also didnt like seeing dead fish in their tank.
It is a really good place if you're craving Pho or vietnamese food without going washington ave. I really like their chicken over rice dish, their price are good and the taste is good
One of the best authentic place in the city.   The food is so good and prices are reasonable!  The service is quick, too.  Will I head back there?  If course, next week!

Acai bowls yes please. This place is super cute, fresh and fast! I think I'm in love. When I first heard the name I thought... That's a lame name... Then I walked in and my goodness it's the perfect name for this place. So thank you Katz for opening a new healthy spot in Tucson. This place will keep you coming back for more!

If you've ever seen that old skool movie The Game with Michael Douglas where he basically wakes up in some scary town uncertain of how he got there, then that replicates my experience here.

First, I was in a cool bar sipping a Stella. Then, suddenly I was at 12th Air Command. The horror.  The horror. (Read with husky Brando voice).

This places puts the fright in frightful.

Because my experience there is mostly a blur, I can only tell you what I remember.  Sweat.  Smoke.  Leather.  Basically, what my mind will allow me to recall.  If this description has given you the impression that this bar is a cross between Sing Sing, and armageddon, then that's just about right.  

Prison coutre.

Yikes.

Love coming here for their chicken curry rice with potatoes! Food here is what you would expect at a Viet Pho restaurant. Portions match their price, but one thing that could be better is service. However, it is understandable that service won't be the best considering the staff to customer ratio. Overall, I still think that it would be worth your money to check out the place, packed or not.

Reviews looks good so we tried it. The restaurant is small the paper on the tables was noisy and unappealing. We ordered steak cooked 4 different ways each game out not what we ordered. Didn't send it back because the service was so slow we didn't dare. We waited 45 minutes for the meals. Steak was good though the horseradish was more sweet than a kick. Spaghetti was over cooked and watery. Surprising no bread was served. Won't be back.

I was claustrophobic in this place. They seated me RIGHT BY THE DOOR! There's several people coming in an out at any moment. I mean damn it was busy. Had I ordered pho like I started it would've felt like eating in a bus depot. Like I want a constant stream of debris being kicked up in my food from outside every time that door opens I'm a bit of a germophobe. Not to mention the mofos at the next table were smellin RIPE! I couldn't deal. I couldn't hang. I didn't even smell any food. I would've lit a match if I had one. So i switched sides of the table. While I looked over the menu they brought out a glass of water and I have all these damn people standing around me.

I was curious about the avocado milkshake so I ordered that to go. And the second I stood up they put somebody else at my table. I didn't even get a chance push my chair in. It reminded me of mid-90's MickeyD's on Canal St. with the gypsies.  

I ain't tryna be rude dude just GIVE A PATRON SOME SPACE! I didn't even have room to think about what I wanted. In fair disclosure, this was during the Chinatown Block Party. Maybe the crowds were bigger than usual.

Ok so about the milkshake... I didn't know what to expect. It was interesting, not bad at all. I just wished it was a little sweeter. Also, the cup it came in was pretty cool, but not cool enough to get me back in here.

This place is so fun.  Jeffrey, the bartender upstairs is a doll.  It's a great place for ladies to get their dance on without having to worry about being pawed all night.  Generous drink specials + a drag show last time I was there!  I definitely sounds like it's changed a lot under this owner, since it's pretty nice inside now.

If you want the best Pho in Philly Chinatown, check out Pho Xe Lua (or the train/choo choo place). Not only is it one of the best in Philly, it also gives the most generous portion of Pho (vietnamese noodles), it's not that expensive, and service is super fast. They also have some good smoothies, like the strawberry or mango smoothie, along with other flavors. Their rice entrees are also pretty good, but their trademark dish is the pho. I've also had their thai coconut chicken soup... very awesome. I recommend this place for anyone who wants some fast cheap food in Chinatown. 

Note: they close on Wednesdays.

Yesterday I stopped by goodness juice bar and fresh food . Overall my experience was 4out of 5 stars .  The food was delicious and fresh just as expected . I got the roasted chicken and Brie sand which . It was served hot with a side of spicy mayo . The commuter juice was fresh as well . No complaints . Cucumber , basil, and like made the drink refreshing and easily drinkable in the hot heat 
My one complaint is the customer service from the front staff  and back staff could have been more pleasant . Every one there seemed to have an attitude .

This used to be one of my favorite places in Tucson for a healthy fresh meal, but I've noticed lately their quality has really declined.  My favorite for breakfast is the Cacao Warrior bowl, which when made right and when the fruit is ripe, is still very good.  But in this item, inconsistency seems to be a major problem.  Sometimes the bowl has been huge and other times extremely small and the proportions of ingredients blended into the bottom part always seems to be different.  One time this summer another customer got a bowl literally twice as big as mine at the same time as me.  I brought it up that my bowl was smaller than usual and instead of remaking it, they just added some more fruit on top.  A very nice gesture, but not the same as more acai blended in with coconut milk for the base.  I just let that slide.  Then the barkback app is never working either, except for the first time it was advertised as a frequent flyer benefit.  Today they told me to download the app on my phone and they would credit me for the visits I had missed.  When that didn't work (the app said they didn't have a loyalty card yet), the manager said he needed to talk to the upper management, but didn't offer anything in return.  

The icing on the cake was the Aztec steak bowl I ordered today.  It was a far cry from the original bowl I used to love, was not as advertised on the menu AND had a hair in it that was not mine!  YUCK! Instead of avocado was guacamole that was heavy on the cilantro, not a flavor that I like if it predominates.  Instead of cabbage was coleslaw - hello?! - not everyone enjoys mayonnaise on their fresh, healthy bowl.  Instead of bright quick pickled red onions as in the past, a ton of heavy wine (?not sure, but I'm not supposed to have alcohol) braised or poorly caramelized onions were substituted instead.  Finally, the beef did not taste like grass-fed as advertised and the quality was not as I remember it either.  All in all it just didn't go well together and felt very heavy.  Then after I found the hair, there was no turning back.
