Although I'll be bummed that I won't have their house-made salsa, which gave it a nice little kick! Definitely a hearty and filing breakfast.  And fresh squeezed OJ was refreshing too!

One of my favorite Vietnamese restaurants...i kinda mixed it up today..i had fried rice noodles and seafood, ladys and gents...let me tell you it was the bombs yo! I also had a mango smoothie different fir me since I always get the ice coofee.  I have no complaints about the service, like always fast and friend.

Yummm... cheapest and the best thai/veitnamese!

Dingy little place in china town... but the best pad thai I ever had!
Loved it, loved it, loved it!
Do not go here for the presentation or service... just the food.
Pho was pretty good to.
Lychee iced tea was really good. Surprisingly had the worst Thai Iced tea.
I am going back there again!

I really like this place. They're a little "brisk" when it comes to service, but their food makes up for it. Good portion size, good quality, good value. Will definitely repeat!

I think you have to know what to order, so for those that gave it low ratings, try ordering something else next time. I had some BBQ thing with this egg side dish that was yummy....I don't know what was in it, but it had egg and some other stuff.

I went once and people were semi nice. But they staying in one room when your under 21 was a different experience. We had to go around back into an alley to get in. It was dark and raining and the only ones back there and they wouldnt let us in for about 10 minutes. Some of the dancers couldnt dance. One dancer was kissing people. He started making out with my friend and was friend was taken by surprise.

Regardless of whether or not you are having an immense craving for Vietnamese cuisine, I would not recommend coming here for multiple reasons.

The food, menu options, and prices were on par with any other typical Vietnamese restaurant. And trust me, there are quite a decent number of better valued Vietnamese restaurants in the Philly area that are much more worth your bucks.

The spacing in the restaurant is fairly tight, most likely in an attempt to accommodate the large number of people who would come in because of its busy location. And you, my friend, should consider yourself intelligent and give yourself a nice pat on the back, for doing the appropriate research on this place prior to coming (unless you're all ready seated that is).

Both service and cleanliness need improvements, which were what brought my overall rating for this place from an average rating of 3, down to a "meh" rating of 2 stars. I mean, check out the little surprise surprise metal piecing found in one of our meals. 

Therefore, do yourself a favor and treat yourself to a proper meal. While the food and pricing are "aye okay," overall, it's just not worth the experience. There's plenty of awesome Vietnamese restaurants in the city that are well worth your time and money, even if it's a wee bit more out of your way.

I'm having a bad day, but this pho is the ultimate comfort food .Quick service. Generous portion for the xe lua.  Lots of well done beef brisket. BIG NOODLES.

Plus  my coffee is fresh, maybe too much condensed milk tho.

#legitviet

Great place for lunch. Take out only, other than one temporary table.  The food is cheap and made fresh.  The homemade egg rolls here are excellent.  The best I have had in the area.  Solid won ton soup...they give you tons of won tons and its cheap (and I actually prefer more broth).  Ive had entrees just a few times,  but the egg rolls and soup are enough for me at lunch and so good, I don't desire anything else.

Wawa is always a good place to stop, and this one happened to be the most conveniently located for a work meeting. We were able to get in and out quickly, which is the main criteria for stores like this, and the coffee was good and hot. Store was clean and easy to navigate. If I happen to be in the area again, I would stop in again
Best place in Philly for vietnamese food.  Never been disappointed. The food is alsways fresh  and I also call it the choo choo restaurant.
I LOVE their pho, but dislike the service. Stop rushing me to eat!!!!!!!!!

Disappointment. $20 for lunch. Got a chicken and Brie sandwich. All I can say is I wish I didn't. No flavor. A little greasy. A disaster. All crust. Hardly anything between the bread. Got one of their juices..healing vibes. It was good. If I want to spend $10 for a small drink. I will then return.  Parking is bad. A lot of effort. I was meeting someone there. When I got their I remembered being here before. The previous time I sent the food back. All sauce. More like a soup. Think it was the Thai chicken bowl.
This is my standard pho place in Chinatown. I love how fast and reliable their service is. Great place to come for a quick dinner/lunch with great pricing.

Don't get it twisted.
Chooch (what we tend to call it) is the best restaurant in Chinatown.
Kept it under raps for years, but I'm pretty sure everyone knows about it now. 
Pho, water spinach and fried spring rolls. Eat them.
Durian Shake and Avacodo Shake. Drink them.
The staff was friendly, the atmosphere was awesome and the food was delicious! Anything you order on the menu is a good choice!

Pho Xe Lua is not a large place, but it's bigger than it seems since it has second-floor seating. It seems like it'd be best for parties of 6 and under. Despite having small areas, the restaurant is not crowded. It has a clean, simple design, and Vietnamese pop plays quietly in the background. I was really surprised at how clean the bathrooms were, too. They were impecable, and even had those Xlerator hand dryers.

For a smaller restaurant, Xe Lua has quite a large menu. It includes a category of "Chef's Specials," which is a total mixed bag of dishes from beef, pork and shrimp to frog and lamb. It offers dinners to be shared for parties of 2, 4, 6, and 8. Alcohol is featured at the forefront of the menu as well as the store, but I just had some Thai tea ($2, cheap!) while waiting for my friend. I observed a mixed clientele, ranging from white to hispanic to Vietnamese.

I ordered Pho Tai Nam. Pho here comes in two sizes, large ($5.95) and extra large (6.95). Xe lua indeed! It came quickly, and the large was huge! I couldn't finish. My friend Michael is what he calls a picky eater and what I call crazy - he asked for his with no vegetables. Somehow, it came with onions and scallions anyway. Poor Michael! He ate it anyway.

The broth here is light, tasty, and not oily at all. Michael and I both agreed that it could use more meat flavor though. Perhaps it was a little too light; we felt it was a muted flavor. I was very happy to see pink meat, something I've missed for a while. As I separated my slices of rare steak, the ones in the middle were even more pink! Finally I could see my meat cook in the broth. Sadly, it wasn't very flavorful either, but a bit dry. I thought it was pretty good overall, but something must have been wrong with me that day. I didn't come close to finishing. Did I subconsciously think it wasn't very good, or was I just not feeling pho that day? I was definitely hungry; I'd been walking around Philly all day sightseeing. Oh well. It's probably worth coming back, but if I were to eat pho again in Philly, I'd give another restaurant a try.


Rating Breakdown:

Taste (10/14):
Broth flavor- 4/5
Noodle & meat quality- 3/5
Garnish selection- 1/2
Portion size- 2/2

Restaurant (13/16):
Service- 4/5
Cleanliness- 4/5
Atmosphere- 3/4
Speed of arrival- 2/2

Total: 23/30

Read more at www.phoacrossamerica.com

My first visit today with my daughter.  I had the Pink Dragon acai bowl, it was absolutely delicious. The only thing i would wish for was a little more fruit/nuts...other than that i loved it and am already craving more. My daughter had the breakfast burrito w turkey sausage, she really liked it and so did i (stole a few bites). We shared a smoothie and a coffee, both good and i appreciate the strength of the coffee. Woke me right up. Will definitely be back!!

Classic Spaghetti Western is Tucson's newest restaurant and it would satisfy even Clint Eastwood.  Their menu is amazing with everything from Chicken Marsala to Spaghetti and Meatballs to Spinach Manicotti to Steak, Prime Rib, and Lobster.  The decor is fun and a Spaghetti Western old movie is shown on the wall near the bar.   Waiters wear really cool black Western shirts and look really hot LOL instead of ho hum white shirts!

Our dinner opened with the perfect glass of Sauvignon Blanc.  For my first course, I chose their daily soup - which happened to be a western chili.  My mother chose Chicken Caesar Salad while Randy had the House Salad.  This chili was THE BEST western chili I have ever had in my life. Even though the restaurant was packed on a Saturday night, we were immediately seated and our entrees were hot and delicious.  Really superb!  We finished the evening with a scrumptious peach cobbler piled high with ice cream and whipped cream. Our dinner could not have been more delightful.  Classic Spaghetti Western has my highest recommendation!

This place is fantastic the prices are a smidge high but i cant blame them the products are phenomenal. Ive gotten the daily buzz 16oz the last two times and it filled me up. So good! For a quick healthy meal stop here you wont be disappointed :)
Summer Saturday night and it was quite empty.  Why is there a cover charge for the second floor?  Not impressed.

Goodness is a stylishly modern restaurant serving health-conscious hipster food.

Prices are modest.  Presentation is always colorful and immaculate.  Food is just A-OK, nothing I would crave. I ordered the Hulk shake and it tasted like blended grass, which I suppose some people like.  I also had the Thai chicken bowl for brunch, and I would recommend that to anyone looking for suggestions.  It's a fairly large portion.

The parking lot is shared with about a dozen other restaurants so parking can become scarce.  You might have to resort to street parking.

This is certainly one of the nicer olive Gardens.  I like the layout with the bar and bar tables in front and the dining room in the back.  The front of the house staff is very friendly.  Service is pretty good,  but depending on the night can be a little slow.  Lunch is usually pretty good and they get you in and out quickly.  In my opinion,  one of the better Darden restaurants,  and as a chain you know what to expect.  They usually have very tasty seasonal specials and you can't go wrong with the soup salad and breadsticks deal

boy oh boy where do i begin. let's start with the pros
the food is great and the pictures don't do it enough justice. 
the kitchen is ACTUALLY clean. OTHER THAN THAT my night came to a rapid end when the roach showed up. 
cons: the roach

it's Christmas eve, so we always go to Chinatown for dinner. this year we chose Vietnamese to get ourselves out of the box. so they are filling up the sauces on a table behind us.2/3rd into dinner. its just about closing time. (Sauces we are not using). I see this dude with a large cup of tops and nozzles and i think i see a fly near the tops. a fly is a fly. ya know just swat it away. oh nooo!!!! this sucker starts crawling across the cup of tops. the main guy knocks the cup across the table some and that thing comes creeping across the floor. i have to now grab all my stuff(and it had rained so we had stufffffff and my family was there) so it wouldn't crawl across us! 
WE kill it, get the check and bounce. I only tipped cuz my meal was almost over and well we won't be back. I'm pissed cuz my food was clearly fresh and well made. i even got a glimpse of the kitchen when i had to potty and it was decent. but if they can't keep it bug free in there why bother?

Since I cant pronounce the name, I just call this place "The Train". 

When I lived in Philly, this was my go to spot to fulfill my once, sometimes twice weekly Pho cravings.

Always ordered the same things: fried spring rolls, seafood noodle soup with egg noodles, and an avocado milkshake. Hit the spot every single time.

Great food + Fast service + Great price = Win
Also the service is unimaginable fast. By the time your server walks through the kitchen door, no more than 30 seconds goes by before you're enjoying a steaming hot bowl of delicious noodle soup. Seriously, time them.
One of the only resultants in Tucson with such a good selection of healthy and fresh food! We need more juice bars like this, the melon juice is my favorite and the teriyaki bowl is amazing!
Really big bowl and they give you an abundance of meat. The broth holds it's own.

This places is quite amazing! The food they give you is not only delicious, but the portions are quite generous; they even give you the option of an extra large bowl of pho.

Speaking of the pho, this place is spot on with their offering. I usually get either the extra large beef, brisket, and tendon, or the beef and meatballs. This comes in a giant bowl with what may be around a pound of noodles and a generous serving of beef. The noodles and soft and slurpable while the broth, while somewhat neutral, is quite appealing; if it's too neutral, add in some of the wonderful condiments at your table.

While the food is good, I have to be fair with this review and mention the cons. First, it seems that they have kept some of the bowls for a long time, as there is some wear and tear on the edges. Also, that crowded and not very clean fish tank make nervous for the people ordering seafood.

Overall, I'd recommend this place to people in a hearbeat!

My wife has been going to this place for years as she's into juicing. Even though I think juicing is such a fad they do it right here! The big melons is refreshing yet not overly sweet. The tacos are very light accompanied by delectable toppings. I would recommend the chicken and tofu tacos  over and over again! I could do without the wheat based tortilla but I know they emphasize the importance of health.

This place is great and inexpensive. Double-whammy! No, seriously, go to here.

Raw beef salad. Awesome and fresh!

Chicken curry. Amazing and cheap, like $5?! 

Love this place!

I'm a sucker for peanut butter banana smoothies.  Add in some cold brew?  You had me at hello.  

This place can get a little busy at times and you may have to wait longer than you'd think, but everything I have had has been great..........until..........I asked a question.

Me: "How many dates and how much honey are in that smoothie?"

Woman at counter not knowing what customer service is and speaking really fast so I don't ask more questions when there is a line: "I DON'T KNOW HOW MUCH SUGAR THERE IS IN IT."

It's always a bummer when someone thinks because it's busy at THAT moment they should rush the line along and get perturbed.  How dare I ask a question when I'm kicking down $7 for some frozen blended concoction?

GOODNESS- when its gets busy in there don't loose your customer service goodness.
Great time! Good atmosphere, reasonable drink prices, and great music. Only downside was the wait to get in the door.
Best Pho and Shrimp Pad Thai in Chinatown. My wife and I try to eat here about once a week and we are constantly recommending it to friends.

It's hard to find good Vietnamese food in Philly that isn't on Washington but this is pretty good! It's my go-to to find Vietnamese food when I have cravings but don't want to go farther than Chinatown (which is more accessible bc of septa). Pricing is pretty good too, as even on a date night we actually usually don't meet credit card minimum of $15. My favorite is to get either com suon nuong (rice with pork) or bun dac biet (vermicelli with everything combo) when we go but their Hu Tieu is also good. Can't speak for their pho yet as I'm a little picky/used to home cooked food and cheaper pho back in Houston but I'm sure it's good!
We paid 50/person for the drag show and it was terrible! It was a bridal shower! And the owner has no interest in feedback.
This place is good and you can feed 4 people for $40. Many variations of pho soup and bubble tea. I enjoy this quaint local eatery on a very cold day.

12th Air Command is a weird and wild place.  It reminds me of what a bar would look like if it were conceived by Maculay Culkin in "The Good Son"...fun with a liberal seasoning of danger. 
 
I've only been here once and I had a blast, however, I spent the entire night wondering if I was ever going to make it out alive. 
 
It had nothing to do with the company that I kept.  The birthday boys that I was there to celebrate aren't the most violent bunch (more inclined toward Beauty than the Beast), but I still had the nagging suspicion that if I took a wrong turn in this multi-leveled, Prague-esque, Communist-era club of a place that I may never find my way out.  

I could vividly picture falling through some long-forgotten trap door, shouting for help to no avail, crying myself to eternal sleep in a secret lair...my head resting gently on the lap of the skeleton of the last guy that foolishly decided to poke around...

I can summarize the evening in a simple list fashion:

Gays...check
Strong Drinks...check.
Friendly Bartenders...check.
Cool roof-deck...check.
Chips and M&M's Buffet...check.
Pervasive sense of dread...check.
Creepy Grab a Stuffed Animal Claw Machine...check?

Came for the Diva Royale Drag Show for a bachelorette party.  They have a small stage, fold out chairs and a private bar (that part was pretty nice) for the show area.  The host Bev, was pretty funny, but otherwise it was mostly lip syncing and some dancing (more shimmying).  If you pay for the hot seat, they stick you up on stage and give you some extra attention, but I wouldn't say it's worth the extra cash.

We definitely had fun, but I've been to better drag shows, the 'girls' didn't really do much
Best place to get freshly squeezed fruit juice in town! Also love the teriyaki veggie rice bowl!
Deep inside my cynical heart is a little Choo Choo train full of pho. Pho Xe Lua, don't ever change.

Stopped here after a hike because they have sugar free frozen yogurt. The flavor was coconut which wouldn't have been my first choice but we were hot and so I decided to give it a try. It was delicious! Nice and creamy and they have sugar free chocolate chunks!!

Wawa is the bizness. Lots of pumps and lots of space for topping off your car. Inside, the coffee bar is insane with just about every possible fixing you could want for your coffee, short of actual Irish Whiskey. Clean, tidy, efficient. And fast. Even if there's a line, it moves very quickly. And the cashier taking your money? They're actually pleased that you stopped at the Wawa. Crazy, eh?
Very nice beer selection, but the food always tends to leave me less than impressed - the wings are nothing to write home about.
Freshness at its best! The melon drink is great for a hot tucson morning. Very chill environment!

We went here about a month ago and absolutely loved it!  Friendly service and great food. Atmosphere was fun, love the pictures and music! Four of us all had steak which was actually prepared correctly!  Hope to come back soon.

This place is near and dear to my heart. I have been going here half of my life and i still order the same dishes. At least three of the servers date back to my high school choo choos days. The prices still rock i think dishes cost .50 cent to 1.50 more than 14 years ago. I should start to try new things there but why mess with a good thing?
Very sweet place, great drinks and pastries. I had the spiced chai and a very tasty cinnamon roll. The lady who helped me was really genuine and wanted me to have the very best experience.
I was pleasantly surprised with the food...really tasty stuff...good place to go....kinda smallish in size so may feel a little cramped...but definitely worth a try

Some gross girl puked on me and the bouncers/managers could not have cared less. You should not serve people to the point where they are vomiting on paying customers. This place is a disgusting trash box. The one star is for the Whitney Houston song they played, which was awesome.

Definitely one of the better pho places in Chinatown. Such an affordable price for the large bowl. Service was okay, took a while for the server to come to us, but they were super busy. Spring rolls could have been better. If you are looking for an affordable good pho place, this is it.

I've been to PYT before like most reviewers on this site. I agree that the food has been downsized but, in my opinion, nothing else has really changed. Granted I've only been a handful of times but I still really enjoy the place.

My husband had the promo Doritos burger which was delicious but definitely small. I had the veggie Calibunga burger which was a great size and really tasty. Our server was fantastic. He was friendly, outgoing, polite and checked on us often. He was super helpful and made suggestions when we ordered. Also, check into PYT on Foursquare and receive a free beer!

You have to know what you're getting into when you go to PYT. It's loud and hipster trendy. The service is not your typical restaurant-proper staff but more casual and relaxed. I've always been happy with the flavor of the food and the size, eh, is not as big as it used to be but still is plenty. It's a fun place if you're looking for a relaxed, chill place to hang out, grab some grub and have a beer.
Love this place, great food and cheap price. Service was always fast, it is the best place for pho in the Chinatown area. Great smoothies as well!

After reading reviews, I decided to come here with my boyfriend. It was such a disappointment. I ordered pot fried frog and my boyfriend filet mignon.
Place looks so nasty, dirty. Service was bad also. The price is too much for the things you get. 
We waited really long, and when we got food, it looked ok, but tasted horrible. Frog was full of fat and some weird spices. My boyfriend thought that it was not enough food at all. It was enough for me. 
NO WAY I AM COMING BACK THERE. 
Also, there a lot of weird people, some dirty workers, I was scared that my purse will be stolen.

I took a group of 15 girls to the Diva Royale Drag Show for a bachelorette party. On the whole, we all enjoyed the show a lot. I thought they did a nice job with the different celebrities, and our host was hilarious (and did a great Miley Cyrus!). And there is a bar in back just serving for the drag show, which is great.

The room at ICANDY is a bit small, with several rows of folding chairs, and a small stage, that has a pole on stage left. I had bought 15 General Admission tickets, and did know that they would be standing room. However, the bride had sprained her ankle, so she and a few others upgraded to the VIP tickets (an extra $23 a ticket) so they would have guaranteed seats. When we got there, it turned out that only the girls from our group and a couple other people had bought VIP tickets, so we all ended up being able to sit in the chairs, but up in the front 2 rows, since we had some had purchased reserved seats. It was kind of a bummer though for the girls who paid extra to sit, since we got to anyways. But definitely was first come first served seating, and getting there early was key for us all being together.

Also, small thing, but the ticket said the show was at 7:30, but it was really doors open at 7pm, show at 8pm. The show ended up starting around 8:15, and ended just before 10pm. 

You could pay extra to have someone sit in the hot seat on stage for a song and be featured, which was a nice option for those interested. 

Overall, this is a solid option for a special night out on Philly.

Affordable large portions. 3 stars because the cha goi was was not crispy... oil wasn't hot enough. Also found a hair in $3 item and they did not take the measly $3 off the bill, especially since we ordered meals and appetizers, they should have.
Great food. Enough variety but not an overwhelming amount of choices. Good price. Friendly staff.

The first time I stopped into iCandy I was with some friends, and we didn't stick around long because the place was crowded and they just weren't feeling it that night.  However, I came back another night while waiting to meet up with a friend to see Rocky Horror at the Troc, and since everything was closing, I didn't want to linger around on the streets in fear of getting accosted by some freak.  Therefore, I came into iCandy in search of a good cocktail.  At the bartender's suggestion, I settled on a Pinnacle whipped cream vodka with cranberry juice--wasn't too strong and it hit the spot! Only $4, when it would've cost $8 elsewhere.  Personally, the club portion is not my thing; I'd rather just stick to the bar...besides, the bartenders are very pretty and friendly, and a friend of mine is one of the "shot boys!"
Very pricy for what you get, but what you get is very good. Good selection of organic food and very imaginative dishes.

Thank you Philadelphia for making me well-versed enough in pho to speak on the greatness of this establishment. Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai is my new favorite place to get pho.

A friend of a friend swears by this place, so after trying many others, I tried to come here a couple weeks ago, but it was too packed to get a table. I returned a bit after 5 on a Friday, and had no trouble getting a table for two. First of all, Pho Xe Lua has the best dining atmosphere - over all other places to get pho in Philadelphia. Their menu is bigger than a lot of the other spots as well. You can also order alcoholic beverages or a bubble tea to suit your tastes.

Service is super quick and pretty friendly. The pho...great meat quality, tasty noodles, cheap, and decent size. Perfect.

This spot deserves to be my default pho restaurant!

Amazing summer rolls, amazing pho! I have dreams about the pho here. My friend brought me here over the winter for the first time and it was the perfect meal. But now that the warm weather is coming, I'm still going eat it when it's 90 degrees out and I'm sweating like an armpit

today we had two dishes: the dac biet (special) pho and the bun bo hue
these were very common vietnamese noodle soups

the pho was disappointing, the portions were good and there was a lot of meat, but the flavor had little depth (there was a nice extra hint of cinnamon but that didn't make up for the lack of other flavors), the meat was cut too thick, and the noodles were overcooked

this was the WORST bun bo hue i have ever had in my life!
1) the bowl was small, not a pho sized bowl, but a soup sized bowl - u know?
2) the broth was soooooo bland, as in, no flavor - and they did not provide the extra hit of shrimp paste on the side that is traditional of this dish to give it an extra kick
3) the meats were lacking: like where were the coagulated blood cubes that make bbh different from other soups like pho?
4) the garnishes they gave were the same as the garnishes for pho (lime, bean sprouts, basil) when bbh should come with (lime, shredded cabbage, and shredded banana flower), since the soup is different, different garnishes will highlight it

it was loud and i was annoyed by all the misbehaving kids, what has happened to the well-behaved asian child, i was one, why can't these kids sit still and eat?

Even with its limited menu, and maybe because of it, everything is made to order and fresh, fresh, fresh!
They serve freshly cooked vegetables and greens, something difficult to find in most restaurants.
I look forward to returning and trying more dishes and fresh juice combinations.
Definitely returning!
Wish they were open later... Hope we can give them enough business that they can expand into that!

This is my favorite stop in Chinatown. They're open late, they're dirt cheap, and the menu makes you want to be daring (for newbies to Pho like me). 

Honestly, what I like about Pho Xe Lua too, is it's atmosphere. Whatever time of day, this place is packed. Eaters are lively, friendly, and it's just a great example of Philadelphia at its best. 

Parking is growing more impossible by the month, so this is a better catch if you live within walking distance. But there is no way I like to end a stressful week, then heading here for some pho and appetizers. No other place in Philly makes me say, "I'll have what she's having," like this spot.

P.S. the neon train in the window will be mine if I ever win the lotto.

Without a doubt my favorite pho place in the city. Staff is friendly and very efficient, they get food out quickly, and the bowls of pho are huge, tough to finish in one sitting. My go to is the pho thai nam (brisket) and it never disappoints. It's consistent to the extent you'd expect from a comfort food restaurant. I worry sometimes with getting take out from places where I like to dine in but it still tastes incredible regardless.

Bear with me here but I'm pretty sure the pho has healing powers. This place has become my default when I'm sick and need soup, it makes me feel better (great for flu season). If I could give 6 stars...
Fabulous burger. Highly recommend the cheddar burger plus avocado. Excellent service. I highly recommend this place

This laundromat is absolutely awful.  It is filthy and  unattended during "open" hours.  The bathrooms are locked or not functioning.  Half of all the machines are out of order or not marked and you've wasted $10 on a machine.  Someone needs to shut this place down.

This place draws a crowd, but that doesn't keep them from offering speedy service. Think their noodle soups are tasty -- broth is flavorful and I like how their noodles are... chewy (for a lack of better word). Like most restaurants in Chinatown, food is cheap and the portions are big. Good place to go to if you're craving pho.

Also, if you're looking for good hangover food, I'd seek this place out.
Great place to grab some Thai and super cheap! I was surprised at the amount of food I got for under $20
We were visiting and my dad wanted some Vietnamese food, so glad we found this place.  It was a decent place for a casual dinner.  Food was good.  Service is quick.

If there is anyone else on a bland diet like me, this is a good place to get your eating out fix! It gets really hard to cook every meal at home, so it's finally nice to find a place that doesn't make their food too oily, fried, or spicy. Obviously they have those options on the menu as well (my friend said the spring rolls were really good) but I just got the simple chicken with rice noodles soup (pho ga) and it was clean and delicious! The chicken slices were tender, the broth wasn't too salty/oily, and they have plenty of sprouts and extra add ins. Hopefully my stomach problems will have improved by the time I come here again - I want to try the house special next time!

This is actually my favorite restaurant in existence. I have come here 30+ times and have tried almost every smoothie and dish on the menu. My favorite is the quinoa salad with tofu, which is always cooked perfectly. I also love the kale citrus salad, tofu tacos, and morning bowl and breakfast burrito (but I substitute tofu for the meat because I'm vegetarian). The acai and pitaya bowls are good too but not anything I couldn't make at home on my own. My favorite smoothie is the hot tropic! I've tried multiple times making it but it never tasted as good as at goodness. The solar power is second best and I'd say daily buzz third. I will always keep coming back when I'm in Tucson!

It's the typical Olive Garden...there are some in the Tampa Bay area than others. This specific location was a pleasant experience; easy in and out. The wait staff was attentive even though we didn't order much food (small bill/check). Oh when you ask for the special, the wait staff will tell you; however, ASK for the special menu that has items $10 and under listed. During my dining experience, I wanted calamari, and I wasn't disappointed.

Came here feeling sickly and wanting some pho, and got exactly that. Went come and for some reason developed a fever. Weird.

I tried the pho with beef balls and raw meat. I was curious about the beef balls but they were general meatball things sliced from a sausage looking thing. Yea, not sure what it was so I don't know if I would recommend it, but it was tasty.

Pho was pretty good, but to me, pho is how you doctor it not how it comes to you. Came pretty tasty so that's cool. 

Service was pretty good, water was constantly flowing as were napkins (so necessary with pho). But I think we had like 3 waiters at a time so it was difficult to figure out who to ask for things. 

I was a little bummed when I asked for a thai bubble tea at the end and didn't end up getting it. But the whole dinner for two was $13. I'll def come again. 

On the other hand, I've been here before (about a yr ago) and got noodles and other delicious foods and found myself suuuuuuuper satisified. I'd still try again despite the weird, but tasty beef balls o.O
Very affordable, gives big portions, i love going there. the only con is that Mexicans that work there are constantly staring at you while you are trying to enjoy your meal.
Awesome authentic food. Had Pad Thai with Shrimp and tofu & spicy pork belly. Both were very good and prices right as well. Will be back.

Decent take out Chinese-American food. Inexpensive and extremely fast (15 minutes means 15 minutes). The usual staples like General Tsao chicken and pepper steak are solid choices. Service has always been extremely friendly and courteous. I'm. It saying this food is gourmet by any stretch of the imagination, but it certainly hits the spot when looking for a quick cheap Chinese fix.

My first experience:
I ordered two smoothies and two sandwiches.
There were a few people ahead of me, so it took a while for the smoothies,
 But even longer for the food. I think I ended up waiting around 30 minutes for the food. I noticed they don't really have a habit of calling the food out, so you have to guess if this is your order or not...
 The smoothies were definitely good, as was the food.

My second experience:
 Decided to get some cold brew from here. 
They serve Cartel, which is right next door, but Goodness offers it in 16oz, which Cartel does not. And it's cheaper, so I figured why not. I was guest #1 and it still took 25 minutes to get. Something about needed to wait for the hot coffee to be finished or something. When I finally got the cold brew--it was terrible. I don't know what they do to it that Cartel doesn't, but it was bitter and very acidic. I actually had difficulty finishing it.

This is my go to place after a long day at the office or whenever my husband and I want a treat.  The yogurt is so cold and refreshing.  They have the staples like chocolate plus custom flavors rotated in. My favorite is graham cracker on their homemade waffle cone. The girls at the counter are alway pleasant.  It's a little pricey, but well worth it.  It's nice to support local family owned businesses in Tucson.

Awful!  There were only 4 tables of people in the whole restaurant, which should have told us something. We ordered two burgers and waited over an hour. We left after an hour. The glasses on our 2nd round were sticky, and the fruit in my margarita had brown spots. It smelled a little funky as well.  We went to the bar to pay our bill, it was dirty. The price of 2 domestic beers and 2 margarita was $25.00. Save your $$$
I love this local yogurt shop, I make sure to go every time I visit Tucson. It's the first place I've seen that has puppy cups.The owners Peter and Wendy are funny and always make my day when I go :)

The chu chu train!

Great soup but most of the stuff on flat plates that I've had there has been pretty generic. Their raw beef covered in peanuts is pretty good for all the raw beef & peanut enthusiasts out there and their shrimp balls on sugarcane are also good. 

The waiters are great (love that tall, skinny old guy) but if you order booze you may have to explain what whiskey is and how it's served. 

Also a friend of mine ordered something with beef balls there, and we were pretty sure that they were actually beef testicles. He made himself vomit from shame in the parking lot, so I would stay away from anything called beef ball in that place.

STOP!!!! TURN AROUND AND TRY ANOTHER PLACE.

Geez guys, I hate to be the one to complain, especially considering all the great reviews.... But I wish I had read an honest review so here we go...

When we got there we got seated. Not much was said, we were kinda pointed at a table. We sat down and ordered. Our appetizers came out and I was completely underwhelmed. I said thank you 3 different times and wasn't even acknowledged. My husband (mind you, this man HARDLY EVER complains) asked our waiter to take back his shrimp appetizer bc he didnt like it. The waiter literally stood there and argued and said he wasn't going to take it off the bill. In his words, "Its not for you to try and send back of you don't like it"- MIND YOU, its not something we tried on a whim. We've ordered it before at other Vietnamese restaurants! So my husband (being the nice guy) didn't argue. Told him thats fine. I was ready to leave and he concinced me to stay bevause we came for the pho and all the reviews said it was great.

...I had the medium rare beef pho and my husband had the pork chop pho. We were so excited because we thought it would be this AMAZING experience... Wrong.  Missed a lot of flavor and was just disappointing.

Bruh. To be honest, the food was just "ok" for such shitty service. Do yourself a favor and go somewhere else.

Service was fast. I ordered bun bo hue and it was a disappointment. The broth tasted watered down and the dish itself did not have much flavor in it either. However, the wait staff was courteous and the portions they served were bigger than most other Vietnamese restaurants. The pricing was also on par with what you expect.

A lot of bang for the buck.  I don't know that anything was EXCEPTIONAL (though my 15-year-old daughter  exclaimed the [not on the menu] Chicken Pad Thai the best she'd ever had.)  They did have SHRIMP Pad Thai, but the waiter (all spoke more than adequate English) gladly accommodated her request.

Entrees would accommodate any tastes, from vegetarian to snail and frog fans.  Veal ribs, pork chops, curries and noodle / rice / vermicelli dishes were all possibilities.

Apps (Crispy Spring Rolls and cold shredded pork rolls) came quickly along with dipping sauces and daikon/cucke/carrot. )  My son's beef satay soup was ENORMOUS.  Other entrees (Crispy fried fish w/ Thai sauce ) BBQ beef/ pork w/ Vermicelli were each more than enough for a single person.

Two apps, and five entrees came in under $45.00.  Dishes came a little spaced out, but over all service was pleasant and polite.  Place was PACKED on a Sunday at Noon with local Orientals.  Cheap parking down the street at 8 bucks for two hours beat the gouging lots hiking up for every Convention Center event.  They even gave $1.50 off the parking.

Bottom line, is they serve very good examples of standard Vietnamese and Thai dishes (over 600 items on the menu) in huge portions, where an average entree is under 10 bucks (and many huge noodle / soups are around 6.  You can stuff yourself with some pretty pleasantly seasoned dishes made with good fresh ingredients on the cheap.  Don't expect a  sommelier to fawn on you, but they do have a variety of nice Oriental beers that compliment the dishes well.

This place is always full of people!  It is primarily take out only (ie there is 1 table in there, and it's mainly for people waiting for their food).  That being said, the food is always ready within 10 minutes and it is PIPING hot.  I've had a ton of different things here and they have always been very good.  Egg rolls here are especially tasty.  I know that you should expect Chinese food to be greasy, but sometimes I do feel it is a little greasier than I'd like at New China Court.  (That's really the only reason I took a star off.)  The service is generally very nice.  The prices are more than reasonable.  THEY ARE CASH ONLY, so leave the plastic at home.  

Great place to order when ya just don't feel like cooking.  Never a disappointment!

Great mellow ambience, friendly staff, delicious food and smoothies! I love this place and sad they don't have one closer to campus. Also, would be great if there were more outlets to plug in a computer and study.  Still, one of my favorite spots for healthy feel good food! I love the cacao warrior ( an acai bowl with coconut, gogi berries, local honey) for after a run, the hot tropic smoothie for a mid day pick me up (with mango, dates, vanilla) and the Thai chicken quinoa bowl is amazing too! Make sure you show your student ID to get 10% off too!

had the quinoa salad with chicken ,tasted really good and would definitely would go there again. The only problem is that their site does not include the nutrition facts of the dishes they serve, so be sure to ask them about type of oil and stuff they are using in them.
Ordered the Pho and loved it! The meal was delicious, though the restaurant itself was fairly loud. Incredibly great value for a great meal.

I like bars of all type, but few things I like about this place are the following: 
1) Asian bartender on 2nd floor is funny, smart, and nice. 
2) There are multiple floors and space. I'd rather be in a place with breathing room
3) Upstairs on 3rd floor is a little charm. Little private yard to have a cigarette, enjoy the sky, or do briefly get away from the scene
4) I have been here multiple times, and no customers or bartenders have been rude to me. Just mind your own business and you will be just fine. 
5) Music is a hit or miss. But the DJ does play what is In and HOT. It depends on what time you go. 
6) Some may call this place too "ethnic". I have one phrase, I love it.

I have yet to order anything that isn't delicious! My go to is the breakfast burrito with quinoa and turkey sausage! Get the salsa and mix with Siracha! I used to be bothered by the speed of service but that has improved so there is nothing I can ask them to improve upon... Unless they are thinking about doing a punch card..every 6 burritos get 1 free?? I love this place and I bring all my BNI members here when we meet to discuss business!

Pretty good. I got the clean it up which has orange, pineapple, parsley, cucumber, dandelion greens and lemon. I was pleasantly surprised. I'm not a vegetable person but it had a very nice taste. The only problem was that I drank it in about 30 seconds. I'll be going again and trying out the food.

This is not just a petrol station it's actually lunch dinner and even snacks.  When I found out that they are now matching the gasoline prices at Sams Club it helped me to make a decision on if or not sams club is a really important membership for my business and home. 

Wawa Has almost everything that I need and I can always get something to eat as well as a freshly prepared drink. Just knowing that they keep the prices of petrol low means it'll be first choice from me especially since they're right around the corner from my house. 

 Convenience, prices and great service the three factors that make Wawa a must for me.

I visited Goodness for the first time today, for lunch. I had their Asian Noodle salad and it was so good I couldn't believe it. I gave it five stars for the quality, freshness and the deliciousness of the food. The ambience was what I would describe as "functional," was quite comfortable for me.  Don't be fooled by my photo. That bowl is not small!
Closed till 7/23! We walked all the way from the Independence Hall for some pho & iced coffee for lunch. Went next door instead. Check out my review of Viet... House.

The place I go for pho in Chinatown! Named the Choo Choo or the train, this is where we go. All the time. Big bowls of delicious broth, lots of noodles and meat. Number 106 for me! It's always crowded but servers (different ones taking your order, giving you water, clearing plates, and giving you the bill) do their best to make sure you get what need! 

Don't think we've ever waited any more than 5 minutes to get a table. Nice!

Oh yes, yes yes yes. This is the place to get Pho.

It's a tiny joint in chinatown, that my friend introduced me to last week and I've been thinking about it ever since.

My staples are summer rolls and beef & tripe pho. It's seriously the basis of my diet growing up and whenever I'm homesick or lost in life... I run to the nearest Pho place and chow down. I think it just grounds me, whether if it's mentally or in my tummy. The portions here are great, I got extra meat, lime and basil and they were sooo generous with it. My friend got the raw flank steak with lime juice, topped with crunchy onions, he was so excited for it because it's not a common thing to see on menus. He also got the tomyum soup and loved it. My other friend also got pho, however she got the beef + brisket variety and was really satisfied.

Also, to settle my tastebuds- I got the Avocado milkshake and it was just perfect. 

I'll probably go here tomorrow, and twice a week for forever.

Even though the name of the place is called "Xe Lua" (XL), their Large was more than enough. I ordered the pho tai sach and it really filled me up. It's so aromatic and the broth was delish! Plentiful toppings of tai and sach with enough pho to go with it. Oh, and the price is really cheap too. $7 for a large? wow

Service was consistent and quick. Really great place to go out to get some pho.
This Wawa is always mobbed and the employees are doing the best they can with the crowds, end of story. We are lucky to have a Wawa in this part of town.

I've been coming here since I was a kid. It's def my go to place when I want something cheap and quick in chinatown. The food is ok..your average vietnamese fair. They have a pretty extensive menu, much more to offer than some of the other vietnamese restaurants in Chinatown. I've tried many items on their menu, but I tend to just order their beef & tendon pho. The broth is pretty tasty and the tendon is always tender. The raw beef (beef carpaccio) is also one of my favorite things here. Service kinda sucks, but bearable, its def gotten better over the years.

Because my beloved Pho 75 closed, boyfriend and I settled for Pho Xe Lua around the corner.  If you have read my previous review of Pho Xe Lua's disastrous and inedble Com Bi (rice with shredded pork) to-go, I was hesitant in coming back here.  

The place was PACKED, but we were sat almost immediately and took only a few minutes to take a look at what we wanted to order.  Ended up ordering Pho Tai (large, $5.95) and him Pho Xe Lua (x-large, $6.95) and they came out within minutes.  The first few bites were okay, but the noodles were stuck together and the beef was blah.  The broth, in particular, didn't really meet our expectations either - maybe it's because we've been spoiled by Pho 75.  His x-large pho was ginormous, by the way.  You can probably feed like two or three people with just that bowl alone.  I guess they really mean 'xe lua' (train) when you order the x-large.  

We might possibly try the Bo Tai Chanh (Vietnamese beef carpaccio) at Pho Xe Lua next time... since a table close to us ordered it and it looked absolutely DELICIOUS.  My mouth is watering right now thinking about it!

So the three stars is solely based on the pho.  It was just eh.  The Pho Xe Lua experience itself wasn't terrible, don't get me wrong.  We'll give it another try soon.

We eat here a few times a month and always have excellent service . Food is very good for a chain Italian restaurant . We only use Lucas as our server . He is very attentive and always goes the extra mile .

I've been to a plethora of pho places, eaten many bowls of delicious pho, and I've found many that I like and would go back over to eat over again. But... this was not one of those places. As always when I first go to a pho restaurant, I get the special pho. At this place, I didn't find the broth to be very savory, and I am allllll about the broth. I found myself needing to add a lot of sriracha to make it taste a little bit saltier and sweeter. I also usually love the tendon and the tripe in the soup, but they didn't give me very much of that--it was just a lot of noodles... a little bit too much noodles and not much of real gems!

Overall, I just found the pho to be eh, one-dimensional.

Was finally able to stop by after passing by on my way to work almost everyday! Place is cute for both inside and outdoor. seating seems to accommodate a good amount of people. Menu boards are posted up a little before you get to the counter to order so that's always nice :) I tried "the cure" juice and also ordered a breakfast bowl and grabbed an R bar for later haha. The girl who took my order was very nice and asked if I would like ice in my juice but I kindly opted for none since I have never heard of such a thing ! Haha ( assuming the veggies are stored cool). Lol we both kinda agreed on how silly it was then she took my name. I paid and waited. Didn't take too long after that 5-8 mins tops and I was on my way to work. Very filling bowl that's for sure and the juice hit just the spot! Wish I lingered a bit longer to take pictures but I will be back!
The Service was good, and the portion sizes are huge. They'll be plenty leftovers for lunch tomorrow.

After dinner on a Sunday, we visited this club.  It was packed full of people, even though it was a random Sunday evening.  



The beer is cheap.  One of my friends bought some pitchers of Coors.  Later, I ordered a huge tube of beer.  It was only $10.  We also had jello shots for a dollar.  Each was topped with whipped cream.  
 


This place had multiple areas.  There was a huge bar area. There was an outside area that was my favorite.  There was also a dance floor.  I noticed that there were other areas that were not even open that day.  

We also tried the food.  They had cheesesteak egg rolls.  

This place was a lot of fun.  It was also cheap.

So, it's an Olive Garden. But it's one with fresh, hot food and great service. The hostess found the perfect table for our party, which included an elderly man in a wheelchair, and our server anticipated our needs beautifully. Food came out remarkably fast and it all hit the spot.

The Pho soup is a popular thing here!  I always get the vegetable noodle soup.  Its only 5.95, its hot, fresh, and comes out in less then 5 minutes.  The portions of all the meals are more than enough for you and another person and you are more than likely going to take it home, because its so delicious!  Parking my be a difficulty, but if you look you can park anywhere around the area  and just walk for about 10 min. The lemon grass chicken and vegetables is also very good, my family always gets it and everyone wants to try it.

I REALLY wanted to like this place. I wanted it to be one of those places that doesn't look like much it has amazing food and you tell all your friends to go because they're going to get their taste buds blown away. No such luck.

Here are the good points: our waiter was great. Personable, knowledgeable, friendly without being overbearing. I can't fault the service. The chili was really good. The Caesar salad was okay (Romain, cheese, croutons). Not mind blowing, but okay. I did like that they put the dressing on the side (I usually ask, but forgot). The shrimp scampi was....mediocre. Heavy on the butter, light on the lemon and white wine. However, when you compare it to my friend's meal, it was amazing.

Here's the bad: my friend got spaghetti and meatballs. The flavor of that dish will haunt me for the rest of my days. The "marinara" tasted like hot ketchup. And not Heinz. Like store brand ketchup. But not GOOD store brand ketchup. Like Food City ketchup. Hot Food City ketchup atop almost over cooked pasta. The meatballs tasted...odd. The first bite gave you a very strange tangy flavor that I can't quite put my finger on. It was just a very tart, unpleasant flavor. And, whooo boy, were those suckers dry. I'm guessing that they are frozen meatballs that they put in the oven during prep and are taken out as needed. Other than the weird first tangy/sharp taste you got, they were flavorless. It was disappointing. Olive Garden would have been better. Mrs. Stouffer's would have been better. Chef Boyardee would have been better.

They do have really good mints on the host stand. That's something. 

But we won't be back.

My gf and I came here for breakfast and quite enjoyed our meals. I had the mango jungle acai bowl and she had the breakfast burrito. We both agreed that our meals were winners and full of the goodness this establishment is named after. I would highly recommend trying this place out. The food is healthy and yummy and the prices aren't too had, either.

Going on five years in Philadelphia, and "Choo Choo" (affectionately named, in reference to the neon train in the window) is my most frequented restaurant in the entire city.

Why? The food is good, it is plentiful, it is cheap, and comes out at the speed of an African swallow (which if you didn't know, is pretty darn fast). This place is always teeming with locals, and they make good use of their downstairs and upstairs seating areas. Service and ambiance could always be better, but if these things are important to you, then I don't know why you came looking in Chinatown in the first place.

Definite recommendations:
- Pho - of any kind (and get the meat raw on the side). You can find better quality pho along Washington Ave, but nowhere else in Chinatown will you find it as cheap, as fresh, or as large.
- Beef carpaccio (raw flank steak with lime) - don't be intimidated by the word "raw." Just think of it as like a Vietnamese, red meat ceviche.
- Fruit smoothies - with real fresh fruit! Avocado is my personal fav, but there are plenty of other winners too.

There is an extensive menu - and I mean EXTENSIVE - with other delicious rice dishes and vermicelli. Be warned though, the summer rolls are not fantastic. They also have domestic beers available for about $3 a pop. Great for a quick lunch or late night.

Word of Advice: Even though the word "Thai" is in the title, don't come here looking for Thai, not even a little bit. Stick to the Viet stuff, and you will leave a happy, stuffed camper.

Enter an Olive Garden restaurant and you immediately smell Parmesan cheese and bolognese sauce on the stove.

Friendly service, large portions, fabulous tossed salad with delicious Italian dressing (served tossed at your table), and great tasty home-cooked fare. 

Don't expect fine dining, but diner style family food.
Love the new roof top bar. Definitely check this place out when you're in the city. It's three floors and the staff was friendly as well.

Food and Service are always on point, whether it's lunch, dinner, or brunch.   The beer list is well thought out with a great mix of styles.  There are a good amount of vegetarian options too, so it's great for groups.

Only been in philly for a week and have been here twice, the prices are good, restaurant is very clean and the staff are quick. All in all a great overall experience. I hate when people make pho complicated and this place keeps it simple and tasty!
I always make a stop into Goodness while in Tucson. Awesome menu with great healthy options.

Certainly one of my favorite spots in Philly. Very local. Frequented by Asians. So you know it's authentic and good. And it was... I only had a Phõ Gha size Large and I was stuffed. Nice fresh broth. It could be a little more spiced but nevertheless very very tasty. I will certainly come back here. I actually wanted to get some spring rolls but had no space left .. Next time ;)

I come here often, and I usually order #108, Pho Thai Bo Vien, and it's always amazing. The food is so fresh, very flavorful, and extremely well priced. I've started sampling other parts of the menu, and I'm continually impressed. The service is good, too. The waiters are attentive and very friendly, and it always impresses me that they are able to carry steaming hot bowls of soup with their bare hands. This is a great restaurant, and I highly recommend it to anyone visiting Philadelphia.

Yo son...I hate that I know live in surburbia. And I'm not too much a fan of Philly. But I think that might get better if I finally take the time to try out the food. Avocado smoothie? Oh why not? I can order one of everything on the menu and still only pay $15....oh yes please. I'm not the biggest fan of Pho but I was feeling adventurous. Don't ask which Pho I had....something with beef, lol. But that avocado smoothie? Yes ma'am and sir. It was the definitive highlight of the meal.

Not bad. The salad is really the high point of the meal. Just the right amount of dressing mixed through perfectly. 

There is nothing bad to say about the rest of the meal, just nothing outstanding either. 

About what you would expect from a chain Italian style restaurant.

Prices are reasonable and the service was really good.

Really yummy and cheap food! All kinds of pho, vermicelli, shrimp rolls and more for around $5-6. Did I mention that the portions are enormous? Somehow you could never finish the portions. Someone mentioned pho number 106 and that's what I always get! Plenty of different sauces on the side to spice up your food!

The service can be a little better though, efficient but not as friendly. My friend took a while to decide what to order and the waiter did not look too happy. Place has two stories, and there was a short line on a Saturday evening. Definitely the place to get authentic and cheap vietnamese food in Chinatown!

2.5 to 3 stars, I have mixed feelings - Ive come here many times over the years and now that I live in Chinatown, I feel I can make a better assessment because I remember feeling underwhelmed each time I go and whenever someone suggest Pho Xe Lua, I squirm and politely suggest somewhere else.

For me, Pho here is not as bad as Pho 20 down the st but is very lackluster and plain. The broken rice dishes arent bad but one time I tried to order banh canh cua and it was completely not what banh canh cua is supposed to be. It came with what looked like regular old chicken broth and didnt have that viscousness to it. I don't mind the oc in coconut basil sauce though and the bo luc lac was good. Also do enjoy the bo nuong la and bo tai chanh. 

Even though there are some things they make here that other viet places in chinatown dont have, this place is not the cleanest.. but IDK, maybe thats all restaurants?

Despite many reviews on here complaining about the staff, they haven't been too bad to me, but I can see how they can be aloof and unapologetic.

Went in with friends to chat and chew. Ordered the Shrimp Pad Thai and it was delicious. The food came out smoking hot and super flavorful! As far as options, there are so many different options available and the staff was friendly and helpful. Would 100% reccomend and return!

Cheap, large bowls of pho!! This place is always busy which is always a sign of a good restaurant. 

I wish there were more pictures on their menu... I would probably be more adventurous if I knew what I might be getting myself into.

The Bucatini pasta is delicious and a standout item. Although, I wish it was offered with a meat add-on option such as chicken. I'm not a vegetarian but didn't want to pass on this pasta just for lack of meat.  Ambiance is relaxing.

Awesome yogurt shop! I've been here a lot due to my school being just around the corner and the staff is always so nice and friendly. The yogurt is also so good and they also make specialty drinks which rock! Definitely earned my 5 stars!

This place has a great fun vibe but you have to pay $5 to go out on to their roof deck which kind of sucks. And certain drinks you can only get up on the roof deck, such as their famous cum bucket or frozen wine slushies. The service here is quite fast and everyone is friendly. The bathrooms are clean as well

The wife and I enjoyed our meal very much and had quite a nice time at dinner. The staff was super friendly and very attentive. The wife ordered the shrimp scampi and I the ribeye and spaghetti. both meals were delicious and outstanding, I am a big guy and I had to take home a good portion of mine so needless to say the portions are ample. 
I like the theme and its a fun place to have dinner I encourage everyone to take a trip here and experience it for your self.
Love this place! One of my favorite healthy breakfast stops. Breakfast bowl and fresh juice are always amazing choices.

Being a new place I decided to try It out. Very dead on a Thursday night. Awkwardly quiet made me feel like I was eating in a library. Excellent service as soon as we stepped out of the car as we were greeted by an employee in the parking lot. The amazing service continued through the entire meal. But even with this great service the food feel short of extraordinary, burnt fries , and calamari was not full of flavor. Burger was ok and the Italian sandwich  fell apart (meat is chopped and not in slices which gets messy) and sadly this meal is forgettable. I hope they have some improvements since I would like this place to succeed.

The bun bo hue is basically spicy pho (though it's still sorta tasty) and doesn't even come with any of the eponymous xe lua (unless I'm getting that totally wrong bc I don't know which accents are correct). Anyways, I was really craving BBH and I don't really feel like that craving was satisfied.

Delish.. I always get the fried rice and shrimp rolls best fried rice I've ever tasted !!! The rolls are delish I love the vegetarian and seafood soups ... I knocked a star off because of the service otherwise delish !!!!!! I'll continue to go here despite feeling ignored once they bring out the food .... Which may I add comes out astonishingly quick!!
Potent drinks and a decent dance floor. The staff should be friendlier. Would definitely come back again
These people were experts, of course I highly recommend their services. prompt, kind and knowledgeable.

Lets start w/ very great price... appetizer, 2 main dishes, 2 beverages ll for $44 which includes tip ... tasty and well worth it for 2 people

The Pho you can skip on b/c the broth is weak... but try 212 - chicken lemon grass and white rice and the pad thai .... bangin'

Also, please please please get the vietnamese coffee dripped (hot or cold), a must have here along w. the beef carpacio bathing in lime juice and friend onions and fish sauce.

For a fast in and out (40 mins top sit down venue), it gets a 4.5 stars minus 0.5 for the lack of ambience
Small dining area; quick, friendly service; lots of parking. Smoothie was great, yogurt was good. Very creamy. Will definitely go again.

So, I have returned to the almighty Choo Choo's experience once again. What is there to say about this that hasn't been said already? It's a decent place. 

Choo Choo's is relatively small and narrow place, with upstairs sitting. It is humble in its appearance, but tailors different paintings of the motherland. It is a not a place to go to relive the atmosphere of Vietnam/Thailand, but more of a "get in and get out" type of meal.

We ate lightly with the Pho Xe Lua Dac Biet and the Oc Xao Dua (Snails in Coconut and Basil). The pho is nothing special. The broth is clear and probably loaded with MSG. Although manages to still be tasty and nicely sized portions, the bowl of pho was just alright. As for the snails, they were much more appetizing, but that might be just be a personal bias because this has been my goto to place for snails my entire life. They are delicious with such great flavor, entices me to drink down the sauce. 

All in all, it is what it is. Don't expect much in this rather small pho spot in Chinatown, when you probably have better luck down on Washington. But, it probably won't be my last time here.

By the way, the smoothies with tapioca are pretty good here, so definitely go for the avocado or mango.

The food is decent, but the atmosphere is...I'm not sure...I think they're trying to capture a 90's California mall vibe? The music is kind of loud and intolerably upbeat. When an order is ready a person behind the counter shouts "healing vibes smoothy for...Lindsay" into a microphone then that person...who is only 3 feet away...from the shouter picks up their order dumped on the counter... Just kind of weird and robotic. The upside is no one stays long so there are always seats and they have wifi. You can just throw in some earbuds and get some studying done...I'll probably be back sadly.

I can see why this place has one of the best reviews for PHO in Chinatown and it's one of the reasons why I made the trip to this particular one. I got #1 and it's the normal special beef soup noodle bowl. The broth was a little less beef taste than I've had before, and I don't know if it's a good or bad thing but maybe this meant less MSG? They give a good portion of meat as well and I couldn't finish everything. For around $9, the portion size is really decent and I would definitely recommend coming here to try out their PHO soup noodles!!!

My friends and I lovingly refer to this place as "Choo-choo's" due to the large train neon light on the front. This spot is my go-to place whenever I'm craving pho in Philadelphia!

Their classic Pho Tai is ON POINT, and the price is unbeatable! $7 for a heaping bowl of delicious pho. I'd highly recommend the Pho Thai (rice noodles with thinly sliced beef). If you order the "special" Pho Thai or any of the other beef options, you'll be getting tendon, tripe, and lots of other squiggly beef cuts that aren't the most appetizing (unless you're into that!). For vegetarian friends, the "vegetable rice noodle" is the veggie/vegan option! It's LOADED with fresh veggies and really delicious, but the tofu is kind of odd and the broth isn't as flavorful as the beef broth. However, it's a great alternative. Last, I have a huge weakness for Vietnamese spring rolls, and this place does not disappoint! I like that they have both meat and vegetarian options so that everyone can enjoy these deep-fried goodies.

I generally only come to Choo-choo's to get pho, but I've come with friends who have ordered other food, and they've all loved their dishes! The staff isn't the friendliest, but they're polite enough and the service is very efficient - great for those of us who experience hanger when we have to wait too long for our food!

Tonight I had to wash my down comforter, so I went to Carrollwood laundry and had a horrible experience with the tenant. She basically told me I couldn't dry bec she was closing even though she let me come in to wash. I sent a review email which I thought was going to them, but it went to washlava...a place I didn't know of. Someone immediately emailed me back saying it was the wrong laundry, but that I should come in here and she apologized for the OTHER place. I came here and it's so nice I'm shocked!  I'm grateful for the good service and clean atmosphere! Thank you

Stopped in for lunch today with a friend.  The service was fast and friendly enough and the ambiance purely noodle house, which I like.  

We opened with a shrimp roll for an appetizer.  It came with the peanut sauce and it was refreshing and tasty.  My companion, ordered a clam soup, which she enjoyed thoroughly.  I ordered the Bun Bo Hue, which I was a little disappointed with. The broth was a little bland and lack that kick that a good bun bo hue broth should have.  The prices were very reasonable, and because of that alone, it would be worth a try. I am sure my companion would give it four stars, but because my main course was no better than average, I am resigned to give it 3.  

Give it try.  It is solid noodle house that will more than take care of your lunch or dinner needs.

This is as viet as you can get in the neighborhood of Chinatown. Most authentic viet food for a lovely price! I would recommend anything beef related, the pho is great! Something to stay away from may be the seafood dishes, choo choos aren't the best at preparing single dishes (but more like pho, noodles, vermicelli, rice dishes, etc) 

And they have very awesome beverages! Something that Americans may stay away from is avocado, but i tell you, you're missing out! 

P.S: LOL at the workers who run away from the durian milkshakes!

After a day of exploring and walking out in the rain in Philly, my friends and my stomach were calling out to us for some food. Something hot would be preferred, so we ended up here. Since my friends and I were drenched from head to toe, we've took turns and dried ourselves in the bathroom. It was awkward because the entire waitstaff likes to hangout right outside the bathroom and each of us would take about 10 minutes in the bathroom, while the hand dryer is running non-stop. The waitstaff were probably like "what the hell are these guys doing in there?" lol.

Nonetheless, we've all gotten the pho since we've heard raving reviews about the broth and they were spot on. The broth here was amazing! It definitely is better than the ones I've had tried in New York. The broth here was very rich and flavorful. The food here is pretty cheap too. I wish there was a better pho place in New York and I will become their most frequent diner =)
Delicious, fast, my go to pho place. My girlfriend and I go at least once a week. at 7 bucks for a huge bowl, it's the best deal a college kid can get

My husband and I enjoyed a fabulous dinner here. Our server Moriah was sweet as could be and absolutely amazing. The restaurant was pretty busy when we arrived but we were seated very quickly and our appetizer and entrees were lightning fast, piping hot and delicious. We were beyond pleased with our visit. We will be back for sure.

Loved the Thai Chicken rice bowl and the low-key dining area.  On a cool day the warm bowl, filled with roasted chicken, sauteed spinach and mushrooms and vegetables was excellent.  The only addition I would have liked was more sauces available.  They provide sriracha and Himalayan pink salt , but no real sauces to bring all the flavors together.
Like many local restaurants you order at the front, find your table and wait for your food to be delivered.  They also offer take-out.  A great lunch spot, a little tough to see from the road as you drive by, so slow down as your come near the intersection.

I absolutely love this place! I refer to it as the choo choo train because of the neon light train sign on the store front. I have tried various different dishes on the menu and I have never been dissatisfied. The prices are amazing and the portion sizes are appropriate. You will never leave Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai Restaurant hungry. I have treated many different picky eaters and food connoisseurs to a dinner here and they all leave happy. The service is excellent, with a wave of a hand your waiter will be there and they never leave you cups empty. It is clean and in a great location and you can never go wrong eating there.

My first trip in. I had the Vietnamese version of Carpaccio (sliced then beef raw cured with lime juice) that was Fantastic. Also had a whole live crab cooked in a very interesting way. This was messy and cumbersome to eat but had a delicious flavour.  Great service. If your server doesn't speak or understand English very well, there is always a someone helpful near.
Great place hidden gem came for birthday dinner Jerry our server was great really took care of us will come again

My friend and I were up in Philadelphia for the Chinese Lantern Festival. I went on my yelp app and I found this restaurant. We were seated, got some water and looked over the menu. I ordered one of their vermicelli dishes and some boba tea. Waiter service was prompt. 

Everything we ordered was fresh and yummy. The one thing I noticed was a bunch of the wait stuff standing by stairs in the back, watching the customers, like reading them to know when I take a plate, or to come over with water. Attentive. 

Although I'm not in the area too often, I know I will be back.

Been dying to try this place since we discovered it on Facebook! Finally went today on a Sunday evening with a rather large party.
Restaurant was cute, Western themed of course, very clean and we were quickly seated.
Service was fine, the waitress was attentive and friendly enough.
Food was just ok. I ordered a 6oz Sirloin cooked Medium with a side of Broccolini and Cheese. I aLso added Bone Marrow Compound Butter as an Enhancement. Presentation was lovely, my food was barely warm. The butter didn't melt as I put it on my steak and the cheese sauce on the broccolini was starting to separate. I prefer to not send food back, I'm sure they could have fixed it, but at this price point I expect it to be done well the first time. 
Everyone else in my party thought the food was good. No one else had issues with food temperature except my two year old niece. We ordered simple Mac and Cheese for her and it was steaming hot!! Not too big an issue, but we had to cool it down on a separate plate for her to eat.
We might be back to try again for a date night, but probably not for a such a large group again.
Very good, had 6 choices for frozen yogurt and tons of topping options. Everything was tasty and service was great. Would definitely go back.

My kids and I go to Sundaze every Wednesday after school.  It is a treat we look forward to all week long. They always have delicious new flavors to try.  Even better, we enjoy seeing Wendy the owner each week with a smile and a friendly hello.  This is a great little neighborhood place.

finally made my way over here and i would give this place 5 stars if it wasn't for the uncleanliness.

broth and pho were perfect and very hard to find pho places that give grilled porkchop on the side so that was a win for me.

the spring rolls though were disgusting, definitely frozen and old. the minced pork was so grey i almost vomitted... as well as the bathroom as well.

i think this place needs some major cleaning and revamping to do with their appetizers and floors/bathrooms.

i may be back sometime soon but i pray to baby jesus that i won't be holding my nose in the bathroom.

This place is a hole in the wall. It is not aesthetically beautiful in the slightest. 

But the service is fast, the prices are reasonable, and they're consistently good. I've been going here for over ten years. I've taken at least seven friends here and converted them to ChooChoo too.

Favorite dishes: Beef Pho #102 and TomYum.

The best frozen yogurt for taste.  I am in love with Cake Batter but there are so many that taste so terrific. The consistency is creamy and smooth and the owners get to pick their product so it all depends upon your taste buds. :)
The prices are right and the service is always with a smile. They also have the cutest young students working there who just aim to please.
Been going there more often since I learned they will call if your 'favorite' is available that weekend. 
A terrific homegrown Tucson small business. You cannot go wrong!

I stopped by here and the tofu tacos are amazing.  Very flavorful with a delicious cilantro cream dressing. The Green Bully fresh juice was very refreshing and not too sweet. Definitely a must for vegetarians!

Just another Pho house. Very large bowl for Large size ($5.50) and Ultra large bowl for their XLarge size ($6.50). Same prices with any other pho joint. Same meats. Same cold/indifference service like any other pho places.

Don't get me wrong. The food is tasty (read: edible). But.. it just like that. Nothing different with any other pho restaurant.

Oh meatballs is extra $2. I think that's a little steep, but whatever. They taste ordinary (read: edible)

Although being a pho place, Pho Xe Lua doesn't meet my expectation at all (just fyi i'm vietnamese). The broth is not there yet, it lacks a deep 'umami' flavor, thus it tasted more like pork broth rather than beef broth- you can almost see how light-colored it is. The well-done flank is more chewy than at other standard places.

Otherwise, I would give five star for other dished I have tried such as Bun Thit nuong, Bun bo hue and Hu tieu do bien Thai Lan. They were all on point especially the Bun Bo Hue. 

The service is just sufficient like other vietnamese places; and it's very cheap compared to other vietnamese places.

I would come back, but not for the pho.

best and biggest pho in the area.  also has excellent rice flake dishes and ho fun.  your food comes out furiously fast (almost too fast) and prices are cheap, cheap, cheap.  there's no atmosphere and you are squeezed into your tables.  they cram everyone in here to the gills.  i always see them blendering yummy looking drinks.  i would eat here every day if i could.

I stopped by here to see what replaced Umi.  I got the Thai Energy Bowl, which is basically chicken, quinoa, some pad thai sauce, some greens.  It was definitely tasty, but a little small for portion size.  Definitely a healthy snack / small meal.

I'll have to try the smoothies and other things on the menu.  Based on that I may add a star.

Ambiance is nice.  Good lighting, not too busy.  Servers were very nice.

Not a 5, but somewhere between a 3 or 4.  Will definitely keep an eye on to see how this place defines itself after the opening buzz.

The male host working was a lot to be desired....kinda rude when we first walked up, had nothing positive to say as we walked to the table.  Soup, salad, and breadsticks was the typical Olive Garden experience.  Service was slow and not a reason to rush back

Gotta give at least 4 stars to a restaurant that effortlessly takes on a group of 25 and does it so well.

We made reservations for 5 pm on a Saturday and were promptly seated in two large tables in the back of the restaurant. Our waiter Khalid was amazing; he was attentive, humurous and made sure everyone was pleased with their experience. Olive Garden has tablets on the tables and for $1.99 you can play an unlimited amount of games. Good idea for the kiddies and the price gets added to the bill automatically. 

I tried their tropical margarita - tasty and just the right amount of liquor in it.

The food was great. I got the buy one take one of fettuccine alfredo; this plate was super filling and delicious. With the entree I picked the chicken gnocchi soup. More like a chowder and pretty good as well. This deal runs $12.99 and they give you a cold dish to take home with this deal. Of course the endless breadsticks were great, a family member took a bag home of them lol. 

The dessert options were good and everyone who got dessert were pleased with their choice.

My one negative: this place had a weird musty smell throughout the restaurant.

I definitely recommend this place to anyone visiting or who lives in the area. Ask for Khalid as your waiter, you won't regret it!

Had the bun.  The pork was really excellent, but the shrimp was not great.  The vermicelli were also much bigger than I've had at other places and I didn't prefer it that way.  Not the greatest I've had in the city, so I wouldn't make a special trip up there when I could just go to Wash Ave.

Update: Went again. Sad dead crab floating in tank. Mushy pho noodles. Won't go again.
Espere una hora y nadie me atendio. No me trajieron ni agua. Estoy muy desepcionada con el tipo de servicio. No regresare!!
