Checked out this place for lunch and had the Turkey, Pesto & Goat Cheese sandwich - so delicious! Ingredients are fresh and I didn't feel heavy afterwards. It was super quick service as well which was great! I'm excited to try out more items off their menu!

Quite bar with friendly staff and amazing food.  Had the homemade chips and salsa, salsa was excellent!  Then we had the peanut butter burger.  I know, it doesn't sound appetizing but IT WAS AMAZING!  I split it with a friend and we are both stuffed! Delicious, filing, affordable.  Go here!

Exploring Chinatown and no clue where to eat with the only requirement from my bf was "Vietnamese food". Yelp came to the rescue which is how we discovered and tried Pho "choo choo" Xe Lua Viet Thai. 

The menu was huge, almost to the point where we were overwhelmed and had no idea where to start. I got a mango milkshake with a rice dish with lemongrass chicken and spring roll. (#219) is all I remember. My bf got a regular size bowl of Pho with beef in it. Which was HUGE. My bf's brother got a seafood dish that he said tasted like a bait shop. So I guess it was really seafoody. 

Food was extremely filling and relatively inexpensive. It was an experience but I don't think its a place that I would die to go back too.

The Train should be categorized as the best spot for Pho in Chinatown, as it does fall a bit short versus other restaurants in South Philly.  The portions are a bit smaller and the broth is on the oily side.  With that said, they do offer a decent bowl of soup and you won't be disappointed.  You can head next door for Bubble Tea afterwards.

The main issue is parking for those of us who don't live in the city.  Why fight for parking in Chinatown when you can drive up Washington and park in a lot for free.

My parents always make us go here when they are in down. The pho here is great. Everything comes out quickly. Pretty typical Chinese/Thai restaurant, but the food quality is definitely a bit better than the other chinatown places.

If you want a cheap dinner, this place has lots of $5 entrees. The portions are huge, but of course you shouldn't expect entirely choicy, lean cuts. Service is quick and decent, especially for Chinatown. The only other quibble I have is the appetizer menu, which isn't that appetizing to me.

My favorite Vietnamese restaurant in Chinatown.  
And cheap, because it only reaches my defined price range as defined by my friends' appetites (read as LARGE.)
Large enough for groups with 2/F, good drinks, huge bowls of pho, nice tanks of seafood upfront.
Me and the boyfriends go to spot! We get the curry chicken with potatoes and the sizzling veal tips with never ending bowls of rice!! Our favorite place to go!!

Coming from someone who used to love OG... This was the worst OG I've ever been to. We sat at the bar & had a few drinks & dinner. It smelled gross, the glass for my beer also smelled gross, the male bartender was unfriendly, awkward & inattentive. The food was fine, hence 2 stars. I'll probably carry out the next time, which won't be anytime soon.
Being Italian I don't really go out for it much but for a chain this is good! Sauce is just eh... Price is good for what you get especially at lunch time.

This is my spot in Chinatown! I go here a few times a month, and while I haven't explored many of the vast options on their menu, I can say for sure that the food is all superb. In particular, I love ordering their Pho in the wintertime: it's cheap, tasty, and you get 2-3 meals out of it.

For most people that know the place, it is actually referred to as the "Cho Cho Train" restaurant, fyi.

We are new to the area and have been searching for good pizza.  We have tried several pizza shops in Old City, but ultimately found Little Italy on Yelp.  We now order from them regularly.  We always order extra cheese and find the pizzas quite tasty.  The pizza is a bit saltier than we would like, but that seems to be a common trait to all pizza we have had in this area so far.  We love the fact that Little Italy will deliver to us in Old Town on Chestnut and the cost of delivery is modest and the cost of the pizza is quite reasonable.  We are happy to recommend Little Italy to others.
The staff is always super nice and they're consistently able to give you great yogurt and good prices!

It has been a while that I have been here. We finally went for lunch. Sat outside so we can feel the super warm Florida air, and enjoy our lunch with our precious pup. Olive Garden did not disappoint. Our meals were so tasty. I am one to avoid chains, but I really like Olive Garden, and honestly I am not an Italian food lover either, and never usually go, but Olive Garden is still worth it to me.

My Beef with Tortellini in Marsala sauce was tasty and was big, my husband had chicken alfredo with lots of chicken, and my mom had the pasta fagioli with breadsticks and soup. All people mostly know and have been to Olive Garden and I will definitely say, this place is still great in my book.

I braved OMGZOCTOBERSNOWSTORM2k8 to grab lunch here earlier this week and it was okay.

For my taste there was too much sauce on the General Tso's but no more than average. I just don't like a lot of sauce on my Chinese. The chicken however was nice and crisp.

Pork fried rice had a nice amount of pork but didn't really deliver on greasy flavorful goodness.

The so-called homemade pork egg roll was the best thing I got and it was pretty delicious, I'm tempted to believe it's actually homemade.
Def the most inexpensive Pho I've had in the city.. Very popular spot I think. Not much too the place itself. I highly reccommend if you're trting ro get your Pho fix

We had a weekend trip in Philly for the Made in America festival and stayed near Chinatown so we ate in the area every day.

This is a typical no frills Vietnamese joint (run by Cantonese people as always).

Our pho came piping hot with generous portions of beef and noodles, while prices still reflect what you'd expect - cheap! Throw a handful of bean sprouts, lime juice, sriracha, and hoisin sauce in there and BAM, you're golden.

It was so delicious. Their Viet iced coffee also hit the spot.
Vermincelli bowl and the Pho!   YUM YUM YUM YUM!    Top 3 favorite Pho places.

Something that is strange to me about this Olive Garden, is that you never seem to have the same waiter or waitress.  Usually when a place has been around for a while, you would possibly have repeat servers or at least see familiar faces, but it never seems to be that way.  For instance, we went to a new-ish seafood restaurant last month and when we returned this past weekend, we had the same waitress as when we had gone before.  That never happens at this OG!  And I don't mean to sound racist, but you hardly ever have someone that seems to be from the area (which could be white, black or hispanic), always foreign accents which sometimes causes uncomfortable situations when you can't understand them or they can't understand you.  I also don't like that they push that self-serve kiosk thing.  If I want to wait on myself, I will stay home.  As far as food, well, it's Olive Garden, everything is fine, but it's not as good as going to a family owned Italian place where you get huge amounts of food for the price paid.  I used to never be able to finish my entree after having salad and a breadstick or two, but that doesn't seem to be the case anymore.  They have definitely decreased the portion size in the last couple of years.

Order: 
 
501 Spring Rolls
502 Steamed Rice Flour Rolls with Vietnamese Sausage 
102 Medium Rare Beef Rice Noodle Soup
301 Bbq Pork and Spring Roll on Vermicelli


This place is amazing! Best pho in Chinatown. Good portions, fresh ingredients and decent price. Chili oil is on point. The bbq pork has a flavorful marinade and don't be fooled, there's vegetables underneath all those noodles. We always order the spring rolls because they're irresistible and our new favorite is 502. Looks strange but tastes delicious. You can never go wrong checking out this spot!
First time here. I will definitely return. The shrimp pho was excellent. We sat upstairs and the vibe/atmosphere was great. It was super cheap as well.

I'm used to being served pho quickly without any intervention in regards to waiter-service.  That's fine, I know what I'm doing with this pile of immersed food.  Just hand me my bowl and I'll take care of myself, no need to ask me how my meal was or how I'm doing.  However, I do always want a glass of never ending ice-water as soon as I take a seat.  Pho's a long, hot, and salty journey and I'd like to make it through.  Most places you have to ask for ice water and ask again once it's empty.  That's why I like Pho Xe Lua, you get the water and they'll leave you alone otherwise.

Pho here is above average, the noodles have some resiliency to the bite and the broth is aromatic.  And when you ask for tripe, they really give it to you.  Man, I love tripe.  I've also had the bun bo hue, a spicy Central-Vietnamese bowl of soup.  It was on-point.  Reddish, hot oil slicked surfaced and out of this world lemongrass-spicy notes.  Chopped pigs feet (which is key to the dish).  Don't be scurred by that, I think everyone should try out bun bo hue if you like pho.  I don't think the soup is getting its just due being overshadowed by its monolithic northern brethren.  So if you would like to try bun bo hue, go here first to give it a proper start.

There's also live tanks filled with lobsters, dungeness crabs, fish and such.  I wonder if I can get seafood pho and have them dunk a lobster in my bowl.  Mmm... opulence.
The menu and food quality are great. The employees are rude and act inappropriately in front of guests. I'd visit more often if not for that.

Great new addition to cambell street lunch options. Try there quinoa salad its one of the best.. Its about time tucson started doing concepts like these. I will go back to try there sandwiches and bowls..
Cheap, fast, and delicious. My favorite place to eat pho! I also love to get the pork vermicelli here.
Not very good at all. Soup is sweet, which is weird to me. Not exactly the cleanest of places either. Wouldn't necessarily go to Chinatown to get pho

WOW!  My husband and I just enjoyed a wonderful lunch during Sandler's soft opening.  He is a traditional eater and loved the onion soup and burger.  I am more adventurous and had asparagus, kale and corn soup and cheese steak Scotch eggs. I have rarely had anything as interesting as the eggs - deep fried cheese steak with eggs in the middle. It was amazing!  The soup was also delicious.   We look forward to trying breakfast next week when they are officially open.

A delicious and ridiculously affordable mean.
5 of us ate (with a few drinks) for about 50 bucks.
Beers were only 3 bucks which is how it should be done.
I had the Pho Ga (chicken pho) because I'm a big fatty on a diet but food everyone else had looked amazing.
It was a light pho but very tasty.
A couple across from us had a big plate of what looked like lamb chops and some greens and some sort of fish dish.
I'll be back.

Most accomodating staff around.  Wonderful drink specials.  Great shows.  Haus of Ham's Christmas Show turned my boring ass Christmas into a great memory.  

Love it here.

Julie

3 1/2 stars but i'll round up.  Excellent Viet spot in Philly's chinatown.  I've had pho here before and it was excellent.  Well prepared, and hot soup and fresh meat. 

i just stopped by and here's what I had.  Started with the Banh Cuon Cha Lua..  or steamed flour rolls with Viet sausages that you pour sauce over.  Delicious... The sausages were just ok...  I really wish they would have the same exact dish but with chinese sausages instead.   Summer or shrimp rolls are good as well.   I got the grilled chicken and pork chop combo on top of rice for $5.50...   How can you beat that.  The pork was a little fatty and not as much flavor as i like, but still good.  I liked the chicken better.  Also had a chef special "salted baked soft shell crabs".  Taste great but a little greasy.  The first few bites were delicious then the grease got to me.  They should call it deep fried soft shell crabs instead.  I got a rainbow ice with the meal which is red beans, mung beans and some jelly like stuff mixed with ice and condensed milk.  Fattening but soooo good.

It's a great place for a delicious and cheap meal.  No decor in the place but you're going there for the food....
Do not listen to the bad reviews. The juice and food here are among the best I've had, and I'm a juice head. The prices aren't cheap because the ingredients aren't cheap.

Is called Choo Choo's because of the train on their storefront signage.

Oh my gosh I love this place. Everything about it. It's legitimate, food authentic, and prices unbeatable. $5.95 vs $6.95 for a large and x-large respectively.

It has the hallmarks of any authentic Vietnamese restaurant: House special Pho, and spring (summer rolls). 

There is sriracha sauce, a bilingual menu, and asian waiters. The bowls are humongous (large vs x-large - get the x-large if you want to split with a friend). The meat is as  standard as any legit viet restaurant has.


The spring rolls are SO GOOD. They're big, and filled with shrimp and everything! The dipping sauce is generous and good. 2 for $3.00! It's a steal anywhere you go.

Just as good as Viet restaurants in LA, if not better.

Pho Xe Lua (Loosely translated as "long car special") is one of the older houses at the bottom of Race Street, and it shows its age.  The menu is extensive, particularly if you like Vietnamese dishes or Pho.  Portions are large.  Prices are low.  Very popular combination that keeps the two floors busy day and night.  Just don't spend time looking at the floor around your table, because cleanliness is an issue.  The house hasn't been inspected by L & I for a long time, and it shows. 

Still, it is mind over matter.  If you don't mind the grit around you, it doesn't matter.  Just enjoy the plentitude so light on your wallet.  

We were there for a late lunch and stayed with the soup.  My partner had the Pho Special that contained all the meats available in the kitchen, and I their Bun Bo Hue.  They label the sizes of their bowls as large and extra large, as if that was something everyone understood.  The former would be a large bowl in most establishments, and the later, a fish bowl.  We couldn't finish either.  

The Pho broth was decent; full of noodles and a load of meat.  It was tasty, but lacked some of the more subtle flavors associated with the better noodle soups.  I did not taste Anise, although it could have been in there.  My Bun Bo was stocked with three big Pig's Feet (Glad they left him one on the hoof), plus slices of Beef and shreds of Pork.  It had ample Lemongrass for the strong spiciness that makes this so distinctive, Fermented Shrimp Paste for sourness,  plus Onions, Mint, and a few unidentified floating objects.  I did not detect Coriander, Rock Sugar, nor Congealed Pig Blood (thankfully), which are part of the totally authentic mix.  The side dish accompaniments had the usual Sprouts, Thai Basil, Jalapeno Slices and Lime Wedges, but was missing the Banana Blossom Slices, and/or Red Cabbage.  

Still, it was pretty good; the first spoonful paralyzing my vocal cords so I could only whisper for about 15 minutes.  It wasn't the best BBH I have had in the City, but it wasn't the worst.  Given the complexity of the real deal, perhaps it was unfair of me to expect Pho Xe Lua to get it completely right.  

Service was fine, and our server was multilingual, making my Mandarin speaking friend happy with his descriptions in her native tongue. 

No need to run back here, but its broad non-Chinese menu makes it a reasonable alternative when in Chinatown, but not feeling like Chinese food.

For 6 months my dog has went to Cimarron animal hospital. At my dogs initial visit I purchased the puppy package which included 3 visits, DA2PPC 1 and 2 vaccination, Bordetella, and rabies. During 3 visits with my dog the staff was great and went out of their way to help in every way.  In the last week I have had issues obtaining an itemized list of shots that were given to my dog to forward to another facility. Today I went in and spoke with the receptionist and we discovered that my dog was never given the Bordetella vaccination at 11 weeks. Since Bordetella was included on the puppy package and I was told at my 3rd and final visit that my dog was up to date on shots I boarded him at a pet hotel for 3 days. Luckily my dog is well and not sick, but he was put at unnecessary risk due to an unfortunate mistake. We discontinued services with this vet.
We tried Sandler's On 9th for both lunch and breakfast. The food was good, the wait staff friendly and the atmosphere clean and relaxing. Would definitely come back.

Very good soup!

I have come here a few times with friends, and we've always left stuffed and satisfied. I usually order the Tomyum seafood noodle soup which is spicy and has a Thai flavor. It is filled to the top with shrimp, squid, fish balls, mussels, and delicious rice noodles. The bowl is huge, and it takes a lot of effort to finish it. The best part is that it's less than $6! My friends rave about the beef or beef tendon Pho (I haven't tried either, but they tell me it's delicious). 

The last time I went, I also ordered a soursop "milkshake" for dessert. I wasn't sure what to expect, but it ended up being delicious! It had a fruity taste and was the more like shaved ice than a milkshake. My friends got the Rainbow ice, which was a shaved ice with red bean, mung bean, and jello mixed in. It sounded disgusting, but I tried a sip, and it was actually sweet and pretty good (although I don't think I'll be ordering that one in the future).
Wawa is the best gas station of any i have been in,  clean, employees are helpful.  They have fantastic subs, smoothies, and pastries.  Well worth passing other gas stations to get to thisbgem.

Absolutely love this place! I usually get "The Goods" and a chicken caesar wrap and without fail its always delicious. The atmosphere and workers are pretty rad. I'd stop by more often but the prices are pretty steep so I usually only go in whenever I happen to be on that side of town. Definitely recommend the joint!

Super good super fresh and fast. A very good light and healthy option for lunch. We had a couple teas and two bowls. The thai bowl and the noodle and tofu bowl. They were really tasty. The thai bowl had a delicious white curry sauce over the chicken and the bowls veggies were cooked and seasoned perfectly. The tofu was flavorful and so were the noodles, it was a really good lunch. I feel like i have to go back to try the juices and wraps and breakfast options.

This place is good for cheap eats and super speedy service. We usually come late at night. Pho is usually a pretty good choice, #107. Beef carpaccio is you're feeling adventurous. You can pretty much point to anything on the menu and be pretty satisfied with it.

They also make pretty good shakes. Mango is my favorite flavor and it's perfect in the summertime!!!

This is a great restaurant. We ate here the other night and had great food. I got the roast chicken and my wife got a chicken dish. It was well seasoned, great flavors, and a very accommodating kitchen which is really important for us. Very friendly and knowledgeable staff! Great ambiance. Great concept!

Great coffee. If you don't like the dark roast everything at Starbucks, this is the place for you. We had a medium mocha, a medium latte, a small hot chocolate and a cranberry scone all for just over $11. Great prices and everything was seriously delicious.

The menu looked great and I was excited to try it. I had the butternut squash soup which was over spiced and the lobster roll which had no flavor. The weakest link was the service - we had a party of 7 and first he forgot to put one of our orders in, then we asked for dessert which took so long he was handing it to us in a bag as we left. Even finding him was a chore.  It took well over an hour and a half for lunch.

Several vegan options, fresh ingredients and pleasant service.  I love coming in here for lunch.  They have quinoa and tofu as options for most dishes.  Their smoothies and juices are amazing.  This is definitely somewhere I frequent.

Maybe I've been spoiled by the abundance of great quality pho joints in Philadelphia, but I just thought the pho here was a bit lacking. The most essential component of my favorite rainy day elixer is the broth and it was just so bland. It had very little favor and I found myself added extra hot oil, sriracha, and lime in an effort to bring it to life with little success. We went on a Sunday evening, perhaps we got some watered down broth? Regardless, I feel that pho flavor should be fairly standardized in a restaurant. Consistency is key, right? 

While the broth was lacking, the meats were actually pretty flavorful and very tender. Another member of my party ordered one of the vermicelli dishes and it was also passable. 

Everything we ordered was OK. We finished our meals--nothing wow'ed us. There were some other dishes that came out of the back that looked pretty yummy. If I return, I'll probably try something other than the Pho.

I had the pho with beef, tendon, and tripe (#107) in the large size (as opposed to xl) for $5.95. I also had a martini for $4.95. The broth was incredible and the beef and tendon pieces were large and plentiful. It was absolutely delicious and such a great comfort food for what was a bad day for me. It arrived in less than 5 minutes too. I will definitely be back. Delicious, super fast service, and inexpensive. What more can you ask? I have a new favorite place for pho.

Oh, Choo Choo. How we love you.

Living down the street, most of our takeout meals come from this small place on the corner of Chinatown. And they have never let us down. I've never eaten in the actual restaurant, but the takeout has always been ready in 10 minutes or less.

We usually get the Tom Yum soup, which is one of the few dishes with strong Thai flavors and just the right amount of spice. Sometimes I wish that they had a smaller portion, as the current menu option is too big for an appetizer or afternoon snack.

Any of the rice/noodle dishes with BBQ pork, lemongrass chicken, or minced shrimp are fantastic. Not a huge fan of the spring rolls, but if you get any of the combo dishes you won't be disappointed.

We've gotten the Pad Thai a couple of times, but the flavor/texture is never quite as good as it is at other Thai places in the city. The only other reason for not 5 stars is that the chicken/pork can sometimes be a little on the fattier side. A mouthful of fat overwhelms spices/flavors every time.

Solid breakfast sandwich to start the day off right.  Came here because its dogs friendly. Smoothie was great. Highly recommend the morning buzz. Yum! Sat outside with dogs but no water offered. That was the only draw back.  Great little place.

This isn't a 5 star froyo place. There were only 6 flavor choices, and none of them fruit flavors (our favorite) - they had vanilla, chocolate, coconut, brownie batter, white chocolate macadamia, and peanut butter.  They also didn't have any lactose-free choices, which all decent shops have now.  We were hoping for a bathroom for young kids, but they don't have a public bathroom.  It's a tiny shop.  The yogurt was decent, not delicious - vanilla and white choc macadamia didn't have much flavor.  Service was good and friendly.  But we wished we'd gone somewhere else.

Just opened a couple of weeks ago and I'm relieved to see that it has been taken over by the right management. Just what the place always needed. 

Came in for lunch yesterday and had a Churrasco steak with Moro rice and Tostones. It was simply the best Spanish meal I had in a while. Forget La Teresita, you must try this place. They have it all from beer to full liquor bar, outside patio and even a VIP/ Private room upstairs for meetings, etc

Will be back with some friends to try their Mojito!

This place is worth to walk up to 30 minutes for.

The prices are ridiculously cheap. I can get a full meal under $10 and that includes a beer. 

The pho, hand drawn. From my understanding, it is the only place in Philly that hand draws all of their own noodles. Every thing is quick and ready to go in. And the portions are massive!

No place else I'd go for pho.

It was good up until miss security lady wanted to push me and my sister out after asking politely if I can charge my phone for 3 to 5 minutes BEFORE being kicked out around 2:20ish BEFORE playing a Cardi B song. Miss security lady walked behind my sister to make sure she leaves and then says "do i have to do this one by one" like excuse us we're only trying to go home we cant be out on the streets. We live in a bad place in North Philly. This place needs to be closed down. If I could rate it any lower i would!
Avocado toast was soooo good! Perfectly seasoned with really nice ripe ingredients. Thanks chef! Service was good too.

Best Pho I've had in Philly. After living in SF for a year, I was hesitant to even try the Vietnamese soup in my dear Philadelphia, out of fear I'd be 1) disappointed and 2) depressed/nostalgic. But I tried this place on a recommendation from a friend and could not have been happier.

For 6 bucks all in I ordered the #102 to go. It was packaged perfectly - one of the things I love about pho is the process of making it yourself. Every single part of the soup was excellent - the broth, the meat (better quality than SF I must say), the noodles...even the sprouts!

Highly HIGHLY recommend this spot to anyone who loves Vietnamese or is looking to try. You will not be disappointed!

I was looking on Yelp for a place to get a quick bite to eat & came across this place. I wanted something light yet satisfying. The young man at the counter was very helpful. I had 3 menus items in mind & he suggested the Greek Yogurt Bowl. Turned out to be a good suggestion!!" This place has unique menus items & I would recommend it to anyone who has not been here. Thanks Goodness!!
By far the best pho I've had since I moved to Philadelphia. It's cheap, the broth is made fresh daily, service is always great, and the food always comes out so fast!. Always my to go place for pho.
Amazing find in Philly! Super delicious and creative menu, great service & city vibe! The owner couldn't have been nicer and attentive... give them a try, you won't be disappointed!

My go to pho place in Philly! Super affordable. It looks small but they also have an upstairs area that can seat larger parties. 
 I usually get the pho with rare beef and beef meatballs. The serving size is huge and while I always think I can eat a large, the medium always fills me up. Would also recommend their spring rolls and their beef carpaccio(can't remember the actual menu name)! 

And while this is not something unique to this restaurant, they have no issues splitting the bill. I find that a lot of restaurants require you to tell them beforehand, but they do it easily even when you have like 8 people. I believe they also have no issues with credit cards.

Known as "choo-choo", this restaurant is always busy and still manages to pump out quality food without making you wait very long. The wait staff is VERY helpful and knowledgeable about the menu. Portions are generous and the food is absolutely delicious. This is one of my favorites.

Mmmm cold and creamy desert.
Nice range of flavors
Friendly staff.
Shopping center is an oasis with lots of choices.

One of the better meals we've eaten in Tucson! I received a Yelp alert and we decided to try it. What a great place, service was superior,  great attitudes. Beef had great flavor and was cooked perfect.
I do love the pho here as you get great portions to what you order and it is healthy for you.  Only issue is parking in china town... urggghhh....

Talk about customer service! Speaking of supporting a great and 30-year local business. Delicious yogurt, served in immaculate conditions, by the friendly and knowledgeable owner. SunDaze is a neighborhood tradition, and we often run into friends and neighbors when visiting. Nice.

I was having a green juice craving one day and stopped by Goodness Juice Bar to satisfy it. I had the Green Bully which is packed with all things green--kale, parsley, cilantro, celery cucumber, and green apple. It was everything I could have hoped for! I would say it's a little expensive, but for 24 oz of such exceptional juice, I really got what I paid for. My only complaint is that Goodness is almost 20 minutes from my house, please open a location on the Northwest side!!
Always good food!! I usually order an acai bowl when I go to goodness. Pricey but worth it once in a while.
I was here once and it reminded me of an Atlantic City casino. Then I saw the YouTube video of the owner saying the "n word". Disgusting.

This review is based on an (rather empty) Monday evening visit (no shit Sherlock). Super friendly and nice staff, both bartenders and bouncer. Drinks (liquor+mixer) was $3, which was awesome. :) 

Would have loved to come when there's more people and go dancing here, feels like it could be a really good place to hang out at.

One of my favorite restaurants to go to... Even now after I've changed my diet plan to vegetarian with a little fish.... I know I can count on a great meal here!  Kelly Barnett, the general .... I recognized as someone who went to our high school in Missouri... It was great to see him again!!!  As usual the food was absolutely terrific... We splurged and got Alfredo sauce for the delicious bread sticks!!!! yum!!! The Tapia Piccata was absolutely amazing!!! Our waiter, Brady, was very attentive and friendly and brought our food right away!!!
This is probably my favorite restaurant in the city. Their food is good, cheap, and they have a lot of options. Also, they have $3 beers and $5 mixed drinks.
Very refreshing and tasty. Food was fresh and service was kind and patient since it was my first time coming here. I will definitely come since my kids liked it.

ICandy offers the Phila scene an energetic and Lively Club for all types to hang out in. It is considered a gay club primarily but all are welcomed & quite comfortable. The club has undergone a large renovation once again and is about to open a new set of inner clubs within the main club. The atmosphere is energetic & Alive. The patrons are respectful & open. Everyone on staff is really friendly & helpful. The drink prices are fair and the drinks are well poured & created. The bartenders are superb all around in asking what you would like and in taking care of you as a patron. You quickly become a friend! The bar is split up into separate levels. the first is a type of hang out where you can casually greet and meet, hang out with friends and just catch up, enjoy a snack and get some cocktails! As you go to the second level you are greeted with more of a high energy dance club. There are stages and dancers. The bars are always well stocked and moving with energy and people. As you approach the third floor you have a mix of the other two in that it is similar to a lounge atmosphere. It has just been redone buy one of the owners himself and it looks sensational! The colors, accents & atmosphere are perfect. There is also access to an outer area where smokers are more than welcome and it is open to the outside. It is a perfect break if you wanted to just go outside and get some air & still enjoy full bar access with atmosphere. ICandy really has improved greatly. The new ownership has done wonders in the past few years and continue to shine as a top spot to meet and greet!!
Have been coming here for 8 years, high quality delicious food and affordable. I always bring friends from town in and have had two big birthday bashes here, drinks are cheap too!

Agree with Chris L.'s Review.  I usually can inhale the whole bowl of pho easily, but the portion here is quite generous, I actually couldn't finish! Both the soup and the noodle are great!

You should also try their Vietnamese coffee! I'm so wired now!
Green bully substitute fuji and a kale ceasar and I am in HEAVEN!!! Clean, healthy, good atmosphere . One of my top 5 in The Baked Pueblo!

Arrived at Olive Garden and preparing myself to critique the meal. Keep in mind we are with a party of 20.
1st round was amazing salad, break sticks and Italian dumpling soup. Not disappointed yet. Had a bowl of pasta Fazoo (not sure how to spell it) was very good. Service and food perfect!!!

From the Yelp reviews, we decided to go. BIG MISTAKE. Service was bad, food was even worse. Uninspired summer roll, chewy filet in Bo Luc Lac, and horrible beef Foux. So overall, steer clear. Don't know how they got the four stars on Yelp, seems like they must be paying people for good reviews.

Choo choos is the place to be for some good Viet around. It has big portions, variety and does not break the bank. they accept cc which is also a plus. overall everything from pho, bun, and rice dishes are on point.

Just arrived at Olive Garden and I was troubled by the fact that my family was not allowed to sit at a booth of our choosing, however our waitress, Karlie, alleviated our disagreement with her great service. We had the Salmon Bruschetta and Chicken Primavera with Giant Fusilli which were outstanding. I cannot emphasize the level of attentiveness, professionalism and service of Karlie. We will certainly return to this establishment in the future.

One of the best steak burgers and fries! The meat was amazing and spaghetti was outstanding! Different than any steakhouse in Tucson! A definite place to try if you're in the mood for some good cooking!

Awesome mom & pop shop with amazing frozen yogurt. This little shop was a pleasant find after a hot trip to the dog park and had a delicious way to cool us down. Our puppy Cas even enjoyed a cup of their pet friendly yogurt which unfortunately for him only lasted a matter of seconds. Highly recommend this spot for anyone who loves a cool treat and who would like to surprise their fur babies as well. To conclude this little review the staff was amazing and extremely kind. We will be back!

(Cue the Good The Bad and The Ugly whistle theme)

This song was stuck in my mind the entire time my crew and I dined at Classic Spaghetti Western Steakhouse on Stone. To describe it in classical gay innuendo, the word "camp" comes to mind, then again there isn't anything more camp than a classic spaghetti western. 

For starters, there are images of classic shoot-em-up scenes plastered on the walls, along with really cool western style shirts worn by staff, they don't let the theme fade for one moment. But it's a steakhouse so let's talk about the food now. 

We start off with some wine and beer, then segeway to their house bruschetta. The salsa was good and hearty, croutons could have been a little more toasted, nonetheless I was happy. Next came salads; a problem with many house salads is that they are either too dry or too saturated. These salads, seasoned just right. Goldilocks would be at home here. 

 Now come the entrees, I had the signature ribeye and spaghetti dish, Lord almighty is there any better way to prepare a steak like how it's done here?!  Crisp edges including side fat pieces rendered just fine. Be honest, that's the best part of any ribeye steak. Then let's talk about the spaghetti with meatballs, pasta done al dente, meatballs seasoned with correct Italian spices. Savory is the word that comes to mind. 

The verdict, spaghetti westerns are definitely back in fashion, and this stand will lead the charge for fine dining and classic films emerging for a second life.  

(Cue whistle theme from The Good The Bad and The Ugly).

I hear so much good thing about Wawa. 
Always wanted to go in to check it out. 
(There are no Wawa in Jacksonville fl )
They have different type of coffee. 
Not very many selection of refrigerated food option. But they have section where they make sandwiches like subway. 
I still think it's similar to other convenience store.

Needed to stop for gas on my way home from the CYME Event. The WaWa was $0.02 more expensive than the station down the road, but with it being at the cross roads of 301 & MLK that is understandable. 

The station was neat and clean and well lit, which is important when you're 2 women traveling alone.  The pumps worked efficiently and then we went inside to get coffee. They have easy kiosks to order at, and once the order is placed, you wait.. It doesn't take long for your order to come up either.  Then you pay at the front check out. 

Their bathrooms are clean too!
Some of the best pho I've had. Spring rolls were also amazing and the workers were very friendly and helpful with suggestions.

So happy I found this place over the weekend! Finally a place in Tucson where you can get fresh food with organic ingredients. What I love about goodness is that it's fast. You order your food at the counter and in 5-10 minutes they will call your number and your food is ready! My boyfriend and I tried the breakfast burrito and the breakfast sandwich and both were extremely delicious. We also had two smoothies that were to die for and there are still a bunch of menu items that we can't wait to try. The only problem I have with this place is that it is a little overpriced. I mean $6 for a smoothie is a tad high but if you're willing to spend good money on high quality, guilt free food then it will be money well spent.

Last night was my first time here... I LOVED IT!!! The DJ was rocking it. As soon as I walked in I began to dance! The bartenders were attentive and everyone (including myself) seemed to be having a great time! I can't wait to go back!!

It's about time I reviewed this place. I ate here years ago, before I even knew what Yelp was. It did not leave much impressions then, partly because my appreciation for food were much less refined at the time.
I recently gave it another shot. The service were super fast and attentive. I ordered 3 appetizers and 2 entrees. The food came out ridiculously quick. The egg rolls were very flavorful and stuffed with meat. The shell were paper thin and crunchy. However, I do believe it was old oiled they fried it in due to the smell. I also had dry beef salad and steamed muscles. The salad were fresh and the beef not overly dried. The steamed muscles were also fresh and meaty but I was not a big fan of the sauce. For the entrees we had tom yum noodle and sate beef noodle. Tom yum noodles were a bit sour for my taste but otherwise good. In the end though, fast service and terrific prices won me over. A great stop in china town. They have a huge variety of food so make sure you try them all.

Amazing food and great service. I went in for breakfast and ordered the avocado toast with poached eggs, it was like summer on a plate. Not only was the presentation beautiful the flavors are so fresh with a hidden zest of lemon. I eat out in Philadelphia at least once a week and this by far is the best food and value I have had in a long time. Can not wait to go back with my husband.

Browsing through the reviews of various gay bars, I was surprised to find that it's predominantly by female reviewers. There's nothing wrong with that but they are gay bars and they are mainly catered towards gay men. lol. Another thing that surprised me was the nickname for 12th Air Command is "The Scare", really? That's funny. 

Well, the very first gay bar I've been in some 11 years ago was 12th Air Command, they host the only Gaysian event in the city and being a Gaysian, I went and had a pretty good time. Throughout the year, Jaded Lounge remain to be the most successful if not the only Gaysian event in town and for that I have to commend the folks at 12th Air for their commitment for hosting it. 

While Woody's have their twinks, Bike Stop has their leather crowd and Voyeur has their after 2am partiers, 12th Air has never seemed to lock down a specific clientele. The place has never managed to pack house other than some event nights like the aforementioned Jaded Lounge which only happen once a month or their porn star nights that used to happen but not anymore. 

I used to go there a whole lot some 9 years ago and enjoyed their friendly bartenders, especially John and Steve, but there seems to be a problem with retaining staff here. The owner Richard seems to be constantly firing staff which is unfortunate because as cliche as it sounds, customer like to go to a bar "where everybody knows your name." instead of some pretty boy bartender who enjoys being gawk at but with no personality. 

What 12th air has going for them is a skydeck and bartenders who knows how to make foofy interesting drinks. I particularly like the Jolly Rancher, my friend has another favorite but I don't recall the name. The skydeck is an amazing space to hang out under the night sky, too bad it's not open as often. They also have karaoke but the host is a bit obnoxious and pushy to the point to off-putting and he favors a smoke machine that irritates.

Other than the third floor, the place is not exactly inviting. Nor does their exterior makes people want to go in and check the place out. Maybe that's why they rendered the nickname "The Scare". Right now the only inviting thing other than some drinks and the single event might be the friendly bartender Paul who serves downstairs. I hope they can make it more interesting somehow, maybe someone can host a trivia night or something fun.

This is a typicaI china town restaurant and we cant expect good ambience. Always crowded. I usually give points mainly for quality and taste of food. The broth was very flavorful and the meat very tender and fresh. We love their fruit juices and bubble teas.

I've been here many times growing up as a Chinatown kid. Choo Choo's was where i first experienced the avocado smoothie which is probably one of the best fruit smoothies ever. Sounds like it would be strange but it's actually so delicious. On this last visit I was introduced to the durian avocado smoothie, surprisingly really rich and tasty despite durian's pungent smell. For the ambitious, definitely give this a try, but for others I highly recommend trying an avocado smoothie or any of their fruit drinks in general. 

On the food side, we ordered their classic pork chops. They were very flavorful but had a bit of fat on a couple of pieces. Also got clams, a vegetable dish as well as a fried crab. All of the food was pleasant and service was fairly quick for it being a Friday evening.

Every Vietnamese restaurant we venture to, the true test will be the beef cubes entree.  Once we must try the beef cube, it will determine the type of establishment we are dealing with.  We will rate the taste, texture, beef quality and how chewy it is.  I must say, it was OKAY, maybe 6.5 out of 10.  Not the best I had before.  

Vietnamese restaurant is known for the pho - vermicelli noodle soup.  It is a must have because you cannot go wrong with it.  The broth was hot enough for the raw bean sprout to cook and added mint flavor will help.  

Unbelievably, Philadelphia chinatown is quite popular out of the New York City venues.  I will go back again to try the karaoke, and hot pots that I saw when I passed by.

Constantly being on the hunt for perfect Pho, Yelp pointed me in the direction of PXLVT.  The restaurant was pretty crowded when we first entered so we had to wait about ten minutes for a table.  It kind of feels like you're standing over the people sitting closest to the door being that there is no real waiting area (other than outdoors).

Being that we were kind of in a rush, we both ordered the sliced chicken Pho and some spring rolls.  Both were great.  

The server could have been a little more friendly, but I can't complain too much being that we got delicious, inexpensive food in a short amount of time.  The tables stayed full, and the turn around was pretty amazing.

I will definitely go back.
I've been here several times and usually get good service. I'm a fan of OG so my opinion might be a little bias.

This place is perhaps below average for the selection of Vietnamese food that you find in Philly. The portions were okay so were the prices. However, you can definitely find much better food in South Philly.

Oh my gosh I want to move to Philadelphia just to eat here every night. For the prices, we probably could eat here every night and not break the bank. I had the regular beef pho - it was the best I've ever had and incredibly fresh. My husband had the pad thai, and wow, it was perfect. Not too sweet, perfect texture, fresh and hot. Oh, and the portions are huge. If you're coming from out of town, make sure your hotel room has a mini fridge!

Lunch is incredibly cheap. Our bill for two was less than $20. Portions are large. I would stick to Pho, but the Pad Thai is also very good (it's actually the closest thing I've had to street food Pad Thai in Bangkok). 
Restaurant itself could be a little cleaner. I noticed a bug crawling on the floor on our way out. I'm not the kind of person who gets super gross out by stuff like this, but it's worth mentioning.

Excellent food! Definitely my new place for when I have an unnameable craving. 

The Raw Flank Steak with lime is my new perfect food.

Although the ambiance is that of a mobile home, it could do well to change the lighting, the ugly linoleum floor and perhaps go with a moody earth tone throughout.

I give a 1/5 for the chicken pad thai.  Wasnt a fan, i dont know what sauce they used, but i had way way better. Soon as i saw it,  i knew i had a problem.  But all their other food is GREAT.  AVOID the pad thai and try other food.

I knew it was a true sign of city Asian cuisine when encountering the makeshift aquarium that held anxious lobsters and fish folk at the main entrace. The restaurant was showcased in fluorescent lights and flat screen t.v.'s that presented their dishes in high def which was a good alternative to framed pictures. The place had character and well, was kind of charming. 

We never felt rushed as attentive servers were only paces away tending to their tables and POS systems. We sat towards the back near a paradise etched mirror with a giant AC unit suspended over our heads- I could only imagine the summers there. Our waiter gave us a hot kettle of tea and small cups as we browsed through the menu. As a first time guest, I eagerly turned the pages to seek Pho and was amazed to find a variety of different bowls and a price tag that even a child could afford. I discreetly looked around to watch well seasoned customers twisting the noodles around their chopsticks followed by gulps of soup with their spoons. They looked like they were enjoying themselves and I just had to try it myself. 

And I was happy that I did. It came out piping hot, with a clear broth and substantial pieces of beef and noodles and a fresh accompaniment of sprouts, basil and limes. The other members of my party endeavored for striped bass, green curry chicken and beef with peppers over rice which they thought were satisfying. As an appetizer, we shared shrimp Pho which was both colorful and healthy. We got avocado shakes, but as a savvy Asian of Filipino descent, I knew first hand that it wasn't real avocado that they used, rather, was a mix powder blended with ice (a trick they use to entice the unknowing consumer). Bummer. And the lychee drink was practically out of the can- fruit and syrup juice together. If it's a bottle of beer you desire they have a bar, but we wanted to try their assorted juices just for giggles. 

In the end I barely made a dent in my Pho as I packed up the rest in a plastic container to bring home. I had it the second day and it was still very good. For under $6 bucks for my meal it certainly was a good value and quality- Pho show!

This place is no frills, but provides reliable, fast service. The staff has been here since forever (ok, slight exaggeration) and they are always consistent.
I usually get the green curry, broken rice & pork chop or pho when I come here. Today I decided to be adventurous and try their bun bo hue, since I'm currently obsessed with that broth.
The broth was cleaner than Pho Saigon's, but I did not enjoy the pig's feet. It was not as tender, which I was bummed. However, the broth was delicious...so I can make an exception. I also tried my friend's shrimp green curry and the beef & peppers dishes which were so, so, so tasty...wish I got that instead!

Yumyumyum. My  place to come for pho when I'm in chinatown. Seated super quickly upon arrival and order taken quickly. Had the beef pho noodle dish. The portion size is huge, and comes super quick as well.

Good food, but the service is not good. If you happen to order a sandwich instead of one of the more popular bowls everyone else in the place gets served long before you do. People that came in after us were served, ate and left before we got our order of 2 sandwiches. 

Update: Since I was called out for abusing my Yelp power I will correct my review by saying the food is mostly good. There was one good sandwich in the order and one rather sad sandwich (Mostly bread, very little content.)  Bad customer service can really ruin a meal, so when a customer is upset it might be wise to apologize and try to make it right, which did not happen.
Amazing pho.  Great prices.  Delicious broth.  All the fixings.  I have nothing else to say.  Go.  Go as much as you can and as often as you can.  Beer available.  Quick, friendly service.

My boyfriend came into town and we wanted to get Pho after visiting the museum. Naturally I hopped on yelp to see where we should have our late lunch. 

We stumbled upon Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai. We made our way to the restaurant and were seated fairly quickly. We both ordered #113 and the food came out rather quickly. I will admit that I was slightly disappointed in the pho. The meat lacked flavor and they were stingy with the noodles. I wouldn't go out of my way to come back, but if I'm in the area again I wouldn't mind stopping back.

This car wash does too quick of a job leaving behind plenty of dirt and overall a dirty car. At first glance the car looks clean from the outside but after a closer look it is still dirty. They spend some time on the inside cleaning the windows and quickly brushing off dust. However, the inside is still incredibly dirty, not even spending any time on the center console to clean the cup holders. Even after twice pointing out where I wanted them to do a better job they still didn't get the car clean. 

PS - this is the third time I've gone there and every time I am dissatisfied with the end result.

This place has tables so close to each other you feel claustrophobic. Only reason I am giving it 3 stars is because we had the world's best waitress ever  (I left her a bigger tip than I had ever given anyone. Wow!) And food was good, as usual. Sangria were way way way to sugary. Not use to having one that sweet. Tampa Palms is a great area.

The rice and noodles dishes are freaky good and hearty. Pork and spring roll w/ vermicelli, curry chicken w/ potato,  and the pad thai are tha best. The drinks are good too. I tried the pennyworth and the avacado milkshake. The Pho weren't too bad either. One of my favorite place to eat in Phily.

This is the cheapest Vietnamese joint in town. Their seemingly endless menu offers everything you'd find at the fancier places (at about half the price) and far more, including numerous Thai dishes.

The service is fast, the food is delicious. Nuff said.
good pho, the broth is nice and clear and beefy.  Best of all, the price is $6.50 for a small to go.
Excellent friendly staff reasonable prices very clean can ask for anything better great place to come and have a quick bite or snack or in my case get a great smoothie hot tropics

This place is a place that one needs to go back to, again and again. The shrimp on sugar cane was a hit with my 8 year old, and my wife and I enjoyed the mussels and summer rolls.

We all had Pho, which was wonderful. Being from Portland Oregon (with a large # of  Vietnamese/Thai restaurants that rock), we had been hard pressed to find a good Pho dish here.

We now have found it.

I promise you I was stone-cold sober when I arrived here, so my review isn't jaded due to intoxication.  I can't speak towards the end of the night, however.  I ended up at Bok Bar at 1:30 AM just to take a pic of the skyline and bounce, so let's just say the night was a blast and I have iCandy to thank for that.

Let me just say I'm really, really pissed I haven't been frequenting this place for the many years I've lived in Philly.  Perhaps one reason would be that the name/business concept has changed quite frequently (there's still 2 of the older names on the signage outside).  Hopefully this one was built to last, cause I haven't had that much fun at a bar in YEARS.

This was primarily due to the music.  No bland, press-play top 40s, no boring deep house - just pure, dancey, techno/EDM blended seamlessly with hits of today and yesterday.  The DJ was just really, really good and knew how to work the crowd.  When a remix of Missy's WTF came on, I went HAM.  I was ready to get on stage and dance with the v. hot, bearded, tattooed dancer (tons of eye candy aplenty: and OMG I just got the name of the place, holy shit).

The space/cooling system is the next bonus of iCandy.  THREE whole floors that don't feel jam-packed at all, much like those tight rowhome bars akin to Raven Lounge.  Very spacious and COOL.  I can't stress how important that is.  Don't get me wrong, I was still uber sweaty, but that was only from dancing all night in squat form and in heels (why I did that, I'll never know....#thighgameonpoint, #bootygains).

The first floor is standard and chill with TVs and seating, for mingling and warming up for the night.  The second floor is out of left field like WOAH ($5 cover-totally worth it BTW) with go-go dancers and strobe lights and that amazing music and a couple fully-stocked bars with super attentive/shirtless bartenders.  And the third floor is very trendy like some upscale Manhattan jawn, with chandeliers and shot boys who come around with whipped cream-topped strawberry jello shots for a buck (hardly any liquor in them though).  The third floor also has an outdoor deck to sneak away for a bit.

Overall, the welcoming vibe of the staff, the music and the kickass layout made me shake my friend and say, "We're coming here EVERY weekend!"  So you can bet I'll be back.

2 bowls of rare beef pho and an order of veggie spring rolls = $20. We fat Texans were stuffed for like all day, which is quite feat!
Unassuming place just around the corner from the Chinatown Mecca on 10th.
Walked in at 2:30pm on Sunday and it was packed! Waited about 10 min for a table. Tried to stare at people at tables and drool at their food so they would hurry up! 
The pho was FANTASTIC! Best broth I've ever tasted. Service was friendly and nice. 
They accept credit cards, a rarely in Chinatown. 
Worth a stop for cheap, very filling, eats!
Great spot to grab Pho in Chinatown! The brisket pho is awesome and so are their appetizers - I've had it a few times and it's never disappointed.
Same great price, same fast service, same great food, familiar faces, year after year.  This is my favorite spot in Chinatown.  Can't beat the large #1 with a side order for spring rolls.

This place is dirty! Ordered pho w/ no onions and they ended up giving me onions in it. After I told the waiter, he said he'll pick them out with his hands. After that, I refuse to eat there unless I'm asking to be on a 1000 Ways To Die.

If half stars were available I'd rate this 3.5. This place was decent. You'd definitely get a lot for a very affordable price, but taste wise, I've had better. When it comes to pho, I am very picky with the taste, quality, and quantity. Soup base was a bit bland -- even with the lemongrass and limes added. Quality of the noodles was passable. If you just want the biggest bang for your buck then this would be the venue.

Only been once while in Tucson but it was outstanding! I ordered the dragon bowl which was sweet, filling and simply delicious. I also ordered an iced green tea which was perfect for my long drive. Will be back again!

Fast seating, fast service, food was delectable!

I stopped during the lunch rush, I was seated quickly , received GREAT SERVICE....

Walked out full, and happy!

Definitely worth a look!

Tasty authentic Thai and Viet food for cheap. The portions of noodle soups are huge- way too much for one person (more suitable for two). Fast service. This is the perfect place to grab a fast bite while in the area/having a craving but wouldn't bring a date here.

I actually still love this place...probably because it's so dam cheap lol.
However comparing food wise, it's not all that compared to other restaurants.

Like their sweet and sour soup (either chicken fish or seafood) does not taste like Nam Phoung's soup (which is WAY better!).

The Pad thai...taste nothing like the authentic pad thai...cuz they cook it with ketchup lol. 

However the BEST dishes thats most popular that I LOVE! is the raw beef - you def gotta try it with the viet sauce, its so goood! but only if you like raw stuff (aka sushi lover).
The fried squid is THE BEST here! i love it! so crunchy and flavorful! lol
Thai tea is yummy! Fast service too. there's plenty of them around lol.
They have an upstairs and downstairs, but sometimes there's a wait if it gets too crowded. mostly on the weekends.  And because of the small space, they usually sit you next to someone...moving the table about 2 inches away from yours..lol..
This is definitely the spot for good cheap food. :D
Not a ton of vegan options but they do have some. The pad thai isn't bad, and it's hard to do better than $3 beer in Chinatown.

Love this place! I'm vegan so it's easy to find something delicious. It's a tad expensive, especially for drinks but everything is great! I got the Quinoa salad with tofu and it was not only delicious but beautifully presented. And the Hulk Smoothie. Both delicious. Would definitely come back! Wonder if they could switch out honey in the bowls.
Cool art work on the walls. Clean! Plenty of waiters and the nice manager at the front. Food was awesome! A really sweet hole in the wall spot.

Food was great and our server, Neil, was awesome! He did a great job keeping up with our food and drink needs as well as adding in some fun conversation. Rarely do I request a server at a chain restaurant but I will ask for him again when we return.

I got the morning bowl, super fluffy eggs, balanced fillings. Absolutely adored it. Definitely coming back for another one. 
I came with my friends, one got the roasted vegetable bowl, and had only one complaint that the vegetables were cold, but that was the main part of the dish, so she really just didn't pay attention. My other friend got the breakfast burrito, hers took a little longer than our bowls, but that's because they roll the burrito and then put it back on the flat top to make the entire outside warm, which is a GENIUS idea. 
On the service aspect, food came out quick, and the workers kept checking in on us to make sure we were enjoying our food. As we walked out, we were thanked, which was great. 
I'm not vegan, vegetarian, or gluten free, but anyone who is would have a large selection of foods to eat here. 
Overall, great food and great atmosphere. Would recommend to anyone.

After having enjoyed Umi Star, I was looking forward to giving this place a try. On the upside, the menu is creative, and they offer a few items that you won't find anywhere else. On the downside, it's pricey given the size of the portions and the taste is really nothing special. My real complaint is that my steak and gorgonzola wrap was ice cold despite the menu's promise that it is "served hot". When my friend touched it, he said "That was refrigerated". I don't know whether the entire sandwich was refrigerated and then re-heated, or if it was just the wrap, but it was quite unappealing. 

All in all, I doubt I'll be back here, despite it being across the street from my office. Frankly, I think I'd have better luck at the Eegee's next door at half the price.

I called GasMasters on my plumber's recommendation after my hot water heater died.  They were able to come out on the same day to evaluate the situation and explain my options.  The formal estimate came the next morning, at which time, they were quickly available by phone to discuss things further and schedule the installation.  Knowing that I was without hot water, they even rearranged their schedule to get someone the next day to install the new water heater.

They are fast, efficient, and considerate.  They are good about answering phone calls, although they aren't quite so fast on the email.  Their prices are very reasonable.  I think the price of our water heater + installation + inspection was not much more than the internet-advertised price of the water heater because they are able to tap into any deductions from the manufacturer and the local energy companies immediately and apply them to the price rather than charging the full amount and leaving the customer to deal with applying for rebates.

Great pho and pad thai. I have tried many asian restaurants but Pho Xe Lua is the one I coming back to. The service is great as they always have an entire staff of waiters working around all hours. The food is very inexpensive, comes in huge portions, and is as good as them come. Highly recommended!

Worst experience and Worst customer service ever
  Every employee has an attitude and they didn't want to work.
My first time having Pho and I loved it! I had tequila sunrise, my boyfriend had a Thai Iced Tea. We both had #105 Pho and LOVED it. The service was fast, friendly, and we only paid $30 after tip :)
Rosemary Chicken and Risotto Bites were very good. Our server Todd was very polite and courteous.

Reliable tasty Vietnamese restaurant in Philly's Chinatown.  We've been there twice, so far 
Fresh summer roll.  Also very much like the grape leaf wrapped beef

I wanted to try this place awhile back but they were closed for renovations.  

Coming back on Chinese New Year, I'm not exactly sure what they renovated as it looks like every other chinese food place in Chinatown except they have monitors on the wall letting you know how the Dow Jones Industrial is doing along with the weather as if stock brokers and meteorologist come in for a steaming bowl of Pho constantly.

Besides that, I had green curry chicken and my fiancee had vermicelli with bbq pork and spring roll.  We were sufficiently fed and happy with the result.  I have a little regret that I didn't try to Pho but maybe next time I have a hankering for soup and stock information, I'll give this place another whirl.

When in Chinatown do not pass by the "choo choo" restaurant that is named something I can never remember. Why? The menu is vast, including excellent pho, noodle dishes, and apps, the food is inexpensive, it's real and it's spectacular. Other pluses: Service is quick, it's byo, and you never have to wait too long. Their shredded chicken soup is my stand by when sick... Or well. Enjoy!

Anytime i go to an Asian restaurant and most of the patrons are of the restaurants nationality I get a big smile on my face. Such was the case here. To me it means they are authentic.Dined alone here tonight and it was comfortable. Kind, attentive service. 
Menu:  Sliced beef and beef balls Pho in a large bowl of broth. Took half home. 
Served with a fresh pot of free tea which helped on a dreary, rainy cold night.
Takeout was shrimp rolls.  The dine in and takeout were great. Drumroll: total bill was 9.99!!  You read that right. Liked this affordable chinatown Viet Thai place so much i bought Xmas gift cards.

It is very convenient having this place a few minutes from my home.  The food is always the same, the servers always nice.  Lunch last time was delicious, especially the salad and tortalini plate.  The dessert shots were yummy but too small.  I would always come and tell all to come too.

I have been going here for almost 8 years. It is consistently good. No Frills, large portions, very fast and priced great. I am a creature of habit and pretty much order the same thing (#107 add beef balls) almost every time. It is always piping hot,flavorful and always plenty of beef balls, tendon, tripe and brisket. The spring rolls are very good also. You can tell they are fried to order, unlike another well know vietnamese spot on 11th street. The service isnt anything to write home about but that never bothers me. They have the strongest, sweetend iced vietnamese coffee in town. Its a must after dinner. While there are plenty of great PHO spots in the city, this is my go to everytime I am craving soup.  I love the computer screens all over the walls displaying certain house specialties. The only strange thing to me is they are closed on Weds.
My favorite pho place in Philly! Great prices, size and taste! I'm a huge fan of the various pho & bun. They also do a really good salt baked squid and Seafood over Rice noodles.

If you want a wonderful dining experience I highly recommend this place, food was great, the bison burger was perfect! The wait staff was very attentive and kind. The restaurant is attached to the Franklin hotel so the atmosphere is high end without high prices. Try to stop in when you are in the area, you won't regret it!

I have only had pho one other time before this and I was not disappointed. I came with 10 people and they seated us right away. I got 102 (pho with beef) and the serving sizes are big and filling and the meat Is really good. They have a large variety on their menu and are very friendly. Prices are pretty fair.

We chose this as a Birthday/Anniversary dinner with the in-laws...this was a PERFECT choice. The food was amazing, the service impeccable and the atmosphere fun. Though it was Saturday night, it wasn't crowded or loud. The food arrived at just the right time for each course - we never felt either deprived or rushed. Our server was very helpful with our wine selection and the Tempranillo we enjoyed was delicious with our steaks and spaghetti. My mother-in-law ordered the prime rib, which was not only HUGE, but perfectly to order and delicious. The green beans and potato were delightful as well. My husband's ribeye and spaghetti was generous and perfectly cooked - which is usually very hard to find for thinner cuts of steak. My spaghetti was delicious and the meatballs had a unique flavor that made it hard to put them down even after I was bust-a-gut full.

Then we got desert...oh, my! A decadent, creamy sundae with a scoop for each of us. Made to share and heavenly good. 

The eclectic menu makes me want to come back when I'm in a sandwich mood, or maybe for a more Italian style dinner. I love that the hubby can do a steak and I can get something else that's equally good - rather than just the typical "non-carnivore's poor seconds" I get at some steak places. 

I couldn't have been happier with my experience and really hope that this place is successful. Its nice to see the downtown revival expanding into midtown as well.
I think the food there is pretty average but it is cheap so I don't mind. And it's pretty tight in there, barely any space to get up
The noodle soup is great. The Tom yum gigantic. The price is very reasonable. Large portions.
No matter how you pronounce it the Acai bowls at goodness are the best in town. The hubby and I get the mango jungle with granola yum

This is a great place for a cheap quick meal.  I was in the mood for Vietnamese but Vietnam(the best vet food on earth) was closed, we ended up here for lunch... not bad. Please note the shrimp will not be peeled or cleaned if you order it! I had tofu vermicelli... so good! I recommend the iced chi tea or avocado smoothie, yum.

This place has been open less than 2 weeks & we have already been twice. The first visit I had the Aztec Steak energy bowl. The flavor was excellent, good portion. The second visit I had the Chicken & Brie sandwich, also excellent. I love the Green Apple Chutney that is on the sandwich as well. If you're at a loss for what to order both of these are good "starters". The space is nice, I love the casual but more upscale look & feel of the place. Nice to see something like this in Tucson. You can also sit outside at the picnic tables. Service was prompt & extremely friendly. I would love to give it 5 stars, however there is no recycling...come on Tucson establishments, STOP being lazy - f**king recycle! On top of that, both times we ordered for in house, yet they package it as to go....so here I am stuck with a very recyclable container that I am eating off of, in house & yet no where to recycle it. Same goes for the glass bottles, nowhere to recycle them. 

Good food - bad for the environment.

Today was my second visit to Goodness, and it was just as perfect as last time. Super fresh, super flavorful food and juices. Today I got the breakfast burrito that was the perfect amount of food, and the flavors all worked so well together. They serve Savaya coffee that is unique and delicious too. The serve really high quality green juices without all the added sugar that most places have, which I really appreciate.
The kitchen knows what it is doing. Really good Pho, curry and BBQ. Waitstaff is prompt and efficient and the bottled beer is cold. The neon train is just an added bonus!

The concept is pretty cool, but the unremarkable service combined with mediocre food will keep us from going back. We liked the western movies playing, but continued issues on both visits with the sound system blaring off and on was jolting while trying to enjoy a dinner. Baked potatoes weren't throughly cooked or served warm, cheese was a large glob and not melted, but not cold either. Prime rib was undercooked and salmon was tough and greasy. The salads were drenched in Ceaser and lettuce was wilted. The beer was cold and the calamari was pretty good though. Overall not worth $80 plus a tip. We really wanted to like this place, the location and ambience are great.

I am sure a lot of people would love his place but I came here for the Acai Bowl and left disappointed. I ordered one Acai bowl, one yogurt bowl and their breakfast burrito. The bowls were very overwhelming due to the fact that they had way, way too many toppings. I was hoping for some fresh bananas, strawberries, and granola but instead got a ton of weird grains and some raspberries. It was overwhelmingly sweet and on top of that it had a lot of honey. I was only able to eat half. My two kids shared the yogurt bowl but I think they felt the same. Too many weird grains in it and sweet dried fruit. I so prefer Whole Foods' Acai bowl. They blend the Acai and simply top it with banana slices, strawberries, granola, and coconut shreds. The burrito was good bit it needed more flavor. It was a little bland. The food definitely looked prettier than it tasted. The blonde girl behind the counter was not the friendliest. I felt like
I was bothering her anytime I asked her for something. She didn't bother to ask if I needed anything when she dropped off our food at the table. The male cook was very friendly when I went up to the counter to get an extra spoon. Probably won't come back again but like I said, I'm sure some people will like it. I think if they simplify their bowls, they can lower the price a little and get more customers.

Went here last night. Highly impressive and also very original idea. Yes ghetto location and you may hear someone across the street say "peanut butter and crack sandwich" but do t let it stop you from heading down from the foothills to have a meal here. We sat at the bar, very friendly staff and outstanding food. I think this place is one of the most original and better restaurants in town. We had the filet and scampi. Delicious.  We had the gaja bottle, well priced wine list. The owner is a cool guy and I hope this place takes off.

Just in from New York, we were looking for breakfast on a Monday morning and drove by Goodness. Allured by its cute appearance, clean lines and welcoming energy, we flipped a u-turn and ventured inside. The food was very fresh, healthy and flavorful. The breakfast burrito with quinoa and turkey sausage was awesome, even the tortilla was flaky and fresh. We were satisfied without feeling too heavy. Might have to stop by this spot again this trip.

Plenty of these reviews must have occurred outside of a Saturday breakfast. We came in to a 30-40% full dining area. A server was hosting and running food which is never a good sign. Everything good about this place is nearly impossible to screw up (heating breakfast meats, toast, coffee) Bacon Fried Rice was incredibly salty and my GF makes better fried rice in half the time.  Our service was incredibly slow and we have a high tolerance for waiting after being on both ends of the process. Had to add 30 minutes to my parking app to get the check and a box. Hire more people for breakfast shifts ASAP
Yes to everything. Everything has been amazing especially the juice!! So happy there is a place that uses quality ingredients for fresh meal & drink options.
this is why i love chinatown.  authentic food. reasonably priced.  they're known for their pho but also try the spring rolls and thai chicken with lemongrass! yumm. owners are really cool, too =)
really good!! this is the best pho i have ever had. and it is really cheap! It worth to try agian!

This place has the worst staff I've ever encountered. I dined here once and the waiter spilled soup all over me and didn't apologize or anything. He immediately left the scene and non of the staffs responded to the mess he made. It was probably one of the worst dinning experience of my life. I will never go back to that dump.

In our current world of "Dispense your own froyo and top it yourself', Sundaze Yogurt is a nice change with really nice people. I love little local places like this, they are small and only have six flavors at any given time but i LOVE unlike a lot of other places that they are designed 'no dairy' or 'no sugar', etc. That is definitely something that is lacking in the local fro-yo scene. 

Lots of topping, prepackaged quarts you can take home, and reasonable prices. The best part? It's close to my house, so if I get a hankering I can just head over here.

This place doesn't even deserve a 1. I was there with a family of 18 celebrating a premothers day dinner with my almost 80 yr old grandmother and the service was not just horrible , but the waitress and staff was horrible . My husband and I ended up leaving after an 1 hour and 45 min wait.  They ended charging the rest of family for the items we had originally ordered and cancelled them and left the place. It was horrific, stay away.  The food also sucks and the drinks , not even worth to mention it.  THIS FACILITY NEEDS TO SHUT DOWN !!!! Thieves !!

i love you choochoo. there is a train on their front window. the chinese on the side also says train.
Good pho. Good price. Good portions. Food is ready almost instantaneously. Very accessible from the subway lines.

Decor is bland. Ambiance is lacking. Staff isn't the friendliest. But you're in chinatown. and you're eating pho. If that's what you're looking for, you're in the wrong part of the city. And probably looking for the wrong type of cuisine. So if you want to included those into the rating and compare it to all other types of restaurants, maybe choochoo gets a 4/5 stars.

ive been here often. will be back many more times.

NOTE - theyre not open on wednesdays. Even though this yelp page says they are.

This is an ok place to hang out with friend and family. The service is pretty good, the waitresses were always looking forward for anything we needed. Real good Cuban pizzas and croquettes (love them), however, we had a mamey and mango smithies and they were not good at all, similar with the the crema de queso, it was estable but not great. Prices are affordable, so that also makes them a nice place to go now and then.

I'm really glad that I stumbled upon this place on Yelp after searching for a Philly pho joint to satisfy yet another pho craving. The prices here are very affordable and the portions are a great deal for the price. This is a pretty casual restaurant and would be the perfect place to go to catch up with friends in Chinatown while enjoying asian cuisine. Service was awkward and not that great, but the food made up for it.

For an appetizer, my boyfriend and I got 3 spring rolls, which were pretty decent compared to spring rolls at other Philly restaurants. They were crispy on the outside and the pork inside was juicy and flavorful. For my main entree, I ordered the Beef & Frank Brisket Pho, while my boyfriend ordered a Rice Dish with the minced shrimp on sugarcane, BBQ pork, and spring roll. My boyfriend said that his dish was fulfilling and he really enjoyed the BBQ pork which was perfectly seasoned and cooked. Meanwhile, I was also satisfied with my pho. The broth had a lot of flavor to it and the beef was cooked the way I liked it (not overcooked or undercooked). They gave a reasonable amount of meat and noodles in proportion to the amount of broth. I ordered a large, which was $5.95, but still had to take some home to finish. This restaurant probably gets my vote on one of the top pho locations in Philly (that I've tried so far). To top everything off, I also ordered an avocado shake, which was delicious. I noticed on the menu that they had $5 cocktails and was tempted to order some, but decided to get it next time. Everything on the alcohol menu was surprisingly cheap, from cocktails to beers to wines. 

Overall, I enjoyed my experience here and for the price, this is a great deal for broke, college students who need weekly pho fixes, like myself. Looking forward to returning and trying out some of their alcoholic drinks!

I rate this place a full 5 stars. If you love Vietnamese food this is the place to go. It's the best place to go on a budget. They make the "best" avacado shake. I tried many different places and Pho Xe Lua makes the best shake there is. 

Their xtra large Pho is truely Xtra Large. if you really wanna go cheap you can buy one xtra large and split it with you and your friend. LOL.  I am sure that is frowned upon.

Love love love this place! Went on a Wednesday night where Larry was hosting games and contests all night! We had a blast. We came back two days later to meet Jujubee from RuPauls Drag Race and there were prelims for their Miss iCandy contest and the girls were great! We're going back tomorrow night to hang out with Larry and the dancers again.

Really good food, and a lot of healthy options to please many people's palate. However, they were excruciatingly slow (35 minutes wait) to make a simple pitaya bowl (just cut up fruit with a pitaya puree over top). We asked them a few times and the cashier kept saying they were understaffed even though there were 7 people on staff with only around 10 clients, 5 of whom came after us and all received their orders before us. 

I think part of the problem was just them being unorganized. They made our drink order 3 different times and kept calling it out on the intercom even though we kept telling them we already got our drinks.
