It was still really good, and if I come back through Tucson again I would be happy to go there. They just need better training / management to streamline it a bit more and a simple "I'm sorry for your wait" would have been nice.

I was a little skeptical of how the food would be from the looks of the place from the outside. However, it was amazing. 

Despite being busy, we were seated quickly.The waiter knew the menu and recommended us great options according to our preference. We ordered the Beef and tendon Pho, Chicken Green Curry , and vegetable egg rolls. All three were AMAZING!

Pho- the broth was very flavorful. You could taste each ingredient in the broth. So we knew it was freshly made. The beef was high quality beef-- good color, good scent, and tender. (5.95 for a large which we both ate and still had some left over).

Green Curry with Rice- Again, very flavorful and fresh. The curry was spicy enough to give you that zing...however, not enough to over power the other flavors of the dish. The mushrooms and green beens were fresh. 

Vegetable egg rolls: It is pretty hard to make a bad vegetable egg roll. But to make one that actually stands out from the rest is a challenge. And Xe Lua Viet Thai (also known as choo choo) has succeeded. Crispy on the outside with tender vegetables on the inside. Lovely... 

Restrooms- In the back of the restaurant. We did not visit them so I do not know if they are clean.

Parking- Street parking with meters. Hard to find but worth the fight. There are also parking lots around the area. However, these cost about 10$ per hour.

Cost: REASONABLE. All three dishes cost less than 20$. Pho Large serving is only 5.95$

Ambiance- Very casual. Crowded. Loud.

Suggestions: Have lunch or dinner there and then walk around China town and pick up a pastry and coffee from one of the many bakeries in the area. 

The only reason the place is not a 5 star is because it lacks in decor, space, and a proper bar/lounge area. You will see what I am saying if you get the chance to eat there. Bot overall, a place I would recommend.

We arrived for  a celebration lunch and had a great meal. There were 8 of us and each meal was made correctly to our expectations. The sandwichs were large and made with quality ingredients. Even the kids chicken tenders were high quality. The filet and prime rib plates were generous and cooked as requested. The peach cobbler was homemade and tasted divine. The server was friendly. We forgot to mention the 25 percent off offer that we got for checking in. Darn!

Just mediocre -- meh...
Had the new Rosemary Garlic Chicken. It was just so - so. A little too much garlic. Think 6 cloves is a bit overboard. The Zuppa Toscana was so salty I actually had to spit it out in the napkin. Can only imagine that is what a salt lick in a petting zoo might taste like? The garlic bread was old and crusty. Asked for more and the second round was even worse. As if the meal was not bad enough....the toddler behind me was screaming bloody murder. (I have two children and believe me -- they were far from perfect, however if they misbehaved when we were trying to eat a meal out at a restaurant -- my husband or I would take them outside. Let people eat in peace and quiet). Apparently the parents of this screaming toddler thought it was cute that the child was hitting notes higher than Maria Callas, We could not get out of this place any faster. I will give it two stars because our drinks were filled numerous times and our waitress was friendly. Will we be back? No thanks :(

Through word of mouth is how I found out about Goodness and I am so glad that I did! I've been twice in the last week. Tucson doesn't have anything that compares to what Goodness has to offer. It's definitely unique. It's such an inviting environment. I love the large, detailed, yet easy to read menu. 

 I had the cacao warrior today. The ingredients used in this acai bowl are delicious and the consistency was perfect. Mint leaves were sprinkled on top (didn't sound too good at first) but it ended up tasting really good with everything else. 

I recommend Goodness to everyone! Their menu has such a wide variety, you'll definitely find something you'll love!

I was craving pho after returning to Philadelphia from Orange County, CA (home of the largest Vietnamese population in America), and what a letdown Pho Xe Lua was. I ordered the pho tai, and was sorely disappointed. The "steak" meat was made of some sort of weird, processed, flat steak-like product that completely lacked flavor, and a greasy, flavorless sausage was also included. The broth was ok and the noodles were just fine. I definitely won't be returning.

Good pho, but mediocre pork over rice. The restaurant itself is well lit, clean, w a polite staff. I'm glad I tried it, but will likely go to Pho Saigon over this spot bc I sometimes would like a variety of food. The pho is very good here though.
This has got to be one of the best bowls of PHO I've had in the last two years living here in the East Coast. If you like tendon --- these folks give you the most TENDER parts. There is HOPE folks...

Great little place in Chinatown.  Have been ordering there for years.

Try any of the Pho soups, the Tom Yum soup, the Satay beef with noodles, or the shrimp rolls.  Affordable, fast and delicious.

This place is not pretentious by any means - it's a great place to go on a weeknight when you just want some quick, well-priced, satisfying food. The service is friendly and like I said, prompt. The prices are amazing, especially considering you get a huge amount of food (the pad thai was enough to feed two). I ordered the vegetarian pad thai and it was delicious with lots of good tofu in it. My friends really liked their dishes as well. I would definitely recommend this place! They also have a full bar, which is always a plus.

i like the simplicity concept...but every item in the restaurant was throw away plastic.  i ordered the turkish coffee - sweet little porcelain cup above the register...i received it and it was in cardboard...i asked for the other cup and she brought a huge plastic to go thing ~ they don't have the porcelain cups....so wasteful.  even the fork....plastic.  i order the tofu noodle bowl and it was heavily salty with tamari and very oily with...sesame oil and again, served in plastic. i might go back for one of their smoothies....but not for the "food".  most importantly, it was a shame to see such wastefulness in a restaurant that strives for "goodness".  definitely misses the mark.

What a fabulous find today! In town for a brief visit and wanting to eat clean and healthy. I could eat breakfast, lunch and dinner here. Options for gf, v and veg. I loved their wild albacore tuna salad, their turkey was fresh and delicious and the Greek yogurt bowl with housemade granola, fruit and honey was a big yum. And my green juice was on point. The space is urban comfy with indoor and outdoor seating. You may see us again tomorrow!

#117. Order it.

Pho with white meat chicken and bean thread noodles. This is just delectable. The broth is always flavorful, the meat tender, more than enough bean sprouts, lime and vietnamese basil (i think is the herb served with it). The noodles are quite good, clear because they are bean thread noodles. One of the best pho options in Philly. My friends have ordered vermicelli with all kinds of interesting things in it (shrimp, pork, sugar cane etc) and have loved it. 

This was my first Pho experience, maybe that is why I keep going back to it even after having been with many other Pho places. But I just can't resist the temptation of xe lua. it's just...so... good.

p.s. the place is lit with fluorescent lights and is far from impressive. Do not let that deceive you! it is very clean, has a verified inspection and everything. cheap prices may mean a less than gorgeous venue. I'm okay with that.

I have been to Philadephia Chinatown so many times before, but I didn't try this places. I read the reviews about this restaurant last week. And last Sunday, I ate there!
         Their Pho is awesome! My husband and I both ordered extra large special pho, and it costs $6.5 each. This thing was HUGE! This was the biggest XL  Pho that I ever had. The broth was so delicious, and lots of different meat in side. They gave us much more basil and bean sprout than any other places I've ever been. I really liked it. I love lots of fresh basil and sprout in my soup. 
        We had their Shrimp rolls too. They are larger than the ones I had before too. So even I do have big stomache, this time, I tried my best finished all the solid stuff in my pho. And this was my first time that I had lots of broth left.
        I will definitely go back there again! I will go there tomorrow again, exciting!
Me encanta el lugar buena comida ,buen servicio,buen entretenimiento y variados, les recomiendo el churrasco,la paella buenísima ,el bistec uruguayo,el pescado frito súper fresco ,les encantará
This place is the best! Everyone is super nice here and the food is always on point. Go if you want some delicious, fresh, healthy food for any meal of the day

OMG I love the shrimp scampi here so much. I've dined here 3-4 times and everyone else I'm with loves their meal but I can't bring myself to order something different because it's so good. They make the pasta for it in-house. Nice full bar as well and friendly staff

Went to the Diva Royale show for a birthday. The show was good. The host was funny and did a few good numbers. The other 2 performers were also ok. Costumes for one diva needed attention- they were dirty and ripped and it didn't do the performer any good. The show was only 6-7 songs over about a hour and 45 min with a break in the middle. I had thought there'd be at least a few more songs. We paid $45 for VIP seats but reality was there was no need for it. The room is very small so there were only about 35 people. The drinks were ok but inconsistent. I had a cosmo that was basically all vodka and a red death (drink-not shot) that was all pineapple juice. During a break, I put my drink down to use the bathroom and someone threw it out so the bartender did replace it. The gender neutral bathroom immediately off the show room was disgusting!!! It literally smelled like foul pee and there was only 1 bar of soap that had visible dirt on it. 
All in all, a fun night out but don't expect luxury.

La comida buena pero el servicio super malo yo tengo que pensarlo para ir allí las mesera lo atiende a uno con mal genio como que bueno va a pedir y son lentos la verdad yo no recomiendo estés lugar por el servicio
Very attentive staff. Excellent wings. Accommodated a decent size group of us on game day, and were excellent with my cousins kids.  Great spot to watch all the action.

Such a watered down experience of what a "gay club" should be.  Wow.. Philly really sux.  Amazing for a city so close to NYC... but doesn't come in a fraction inch close to NYC or FL clubs.  The male bartenders (with the black shirts on.. and WHY do they have shirts on, when everyone else, incl barback have to be shirtless and the place is called I candy??????) are so cocky, uninterested and indifferent.. for No reason.  They think they are models.  NO SMILES.  WEAK DRINKS.  A few of the bartenders actually have some personality.. they tend to be the more flamboyant ones.  The "shot guy" with all the leather harnesses on him is pretty cool and engaging.  Jusr really poor bartending staff.  The older (not old, but 40s+) doorman is super cool and was really nice.  Tall, dark haired bartender, VGL was just an ass all nite.. and weak drinks...   Short and short haired lesbian bartender was cool and good drinks.   Another female bartender (very light skinned black girl with curly shoulder length hair)...Never once cracked a smile during service either.  I acutally told her that the guy next to me was about to vomit (he told me so) and asked for a water for him.  She rolled her eyes, gave him the water, and charged me for it.. lol  Next time, I will let them vomit on your bar, honey.  No matter to me.  Very large crowd of underage female lesbians.  Perhaps they have ID, but I know it for a fact.  NOT a "mens club". . more of a very young gay men with their "fag-hags" and young lesbian scene.  A lot of north philly types too.   Just better places to spend your Saturday.. like home.. lol Restrooms reaked of vomit and I saw at least 2 other patrons that were out of their mind and about to puke.  IDK why.  But they were there.  Odd mixed crowd.. like new lesbians/very young gay dudes with their faghags/ then 70yr olds watching..   VERY crummy (not cummy) music!  Jello shots that are ALL jello.. plus the tip... IDK what else to say..  lol

Love this place!  I usually get the lemongrass shrimp over rice, but all of the lemongrass dishes have been very tasty. For an added twist, the 214 comes with an egg and rice noodle patty that is amazing.  I look forward to trying the pepper chicken dish, as well as the lamb that was recommended by folks at the table next to us...

Traveling from Cali and heard of this Steakhouse. My sisters and I were not disappointed! Atmosphere was very inviting. We had the steak and scampi, lasagna, & spaghetti & meatballs. Dessert was an amazing peach cobbler and the tiramisu. Outstanding entrees, dessert, and the service met my expectations! We will definitely return!!

A very disappointing experience. I had decided to stop in for lunch today with my parents and this has been without a doubt the worst food, service, etc...I have ever received. Let me elaborate: I sat down and ordered two mango shakes, a Media Noche sandwich and two frita sandwiches. (no frills regular and quick Cuban lunch typically). After 10 minutes the girl brought us a little bit of bread with garlic and no water at all to drink and ran away. After another 10 minutes, I saw her walk by and asked her to please bring me some more bread while I waited for my food along with water to drink (I feel I should never have to ask for water in a Restaurant) and the girl said "If I bring more bread, then I have to charge you for it"- so I said "No, that is okay" this is just un tasteful to say this to a paying customer. Ok, so here we are waiting for the frita and media noche sandwich, well after 45 minutes waiting I get irritated and ask for my check so I can leave, I said to another girl, forget the sandwiches just ring me up, and she talked me out of it, she said it was on its way, so I said OK let me wait another few minutes. About 5 minutes later the food comes out, the food is cold and to make matters worse, the Media Noche sandwich is totally GROSS!! I have never seen a Media Noche sandwich with mayo and ketchup before, honestly! This thing had two pickles , Ham, Cheese, and ketchup and mayonaise  and no pork, ZERO! So when the girl comes back I said to please retire my sandwich, that I really am horrified at the mere sight of it, she said OK and leaves. After five minutes, the owner comes out to ask me what was wrong, and I politely said the sandwich is terrible, that it does not even have pork, what kind of media noche is this? So she then starts to explain to me how I do not know what I am speaking about, and Blah Blah Blah...and that "if I did not like the food or place not to come back again" So, I think at this point I had enough abuse and finally left this place forever. They are very rude to their customers and the food is the worst Cuban food ever! ( I am Cuban and have eaten this food all my life). Needless to say they will not get any stars from me, I urge people to stay away from this place!! I hope my review helps

Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai Restaurant is a small quaint Vietnamese restaurant in Chinatown district of Philadelphia, that also serves Thai cuisine as well. In my unofficial quest to have Pho in all 50 States, my quest continues here in Pennsylvania. I found this place, along with a handful of other restaurants that served Pho and other Vietnamese dishes on Yelp. One of 2 off the list had a 4 star rating, so I decided to try this place after reading a few of the reviews. This place did not disappoint, clearly due to the fact of cheap Pho. Cheaper than most places that I have been to. $5.95 for a regular bowl and $6.95 for a large. Can't believe that! Only problem was that they had a $15 minimum charge for credit card payments, which sucked. 

I had to order 2 extra orders of shrimp rolls to round out over $15. It was annoying, but I had something to have for a late night snack later that night. Here I was having a late lunch here after seeing the sights of historic Philadelphia. Located on Race Street in Philadelphia Chinatown, you can tell this place was definitely the place to be. The set up was that of a Chinese / Vietnamese mixed. The servers and staff talked Chinese, so that was a dead give away for sure. I was here on a cool Thursday afternoon. Not much going on here and it wasn't busy at all. Just a few tables that were occupied. I was hurried a bit to the table and I hastily got the menu before the staff started to mingle about themselves and talk in Chinese.

I ordered the regular sized Pho, not really wanting the large size that day. Not sure why, but that's what I did. Ordered an order of shrimp rolls and a soda initially for the meal. It was insane to see that the order of shrimp rolls were $3.00!! That's cheap!! So awesome this place, although the $15 minimum credit card thing was a bummer. I realized this after getting the bill. However, the Pho was pretty good, although the flavor could have been more refined to be sure. I wished that they don't do the watered down version of the Pho. Maybe next time it will be different. The shrimp rolls were okay. Nothing great about them, although they are certainly cheap and filling. The taste, however wasn't so much. 

Overall, do try this place for the inexpensiveness and you may find this place a hidden gem, like I have done. Be aware of the $15 minimum for credit card payments, as mentioned before. The place is well kept and managed. Plenty of staff to assist you and the service was okay. Fast and expedient. All you want at the price you want. Thanks Pho Xe Lua! It was a good experience. Maybe next time, I'll come back.

Support local!

B

What a great experience. I had to take my Brittany in for an emergency. Dr Crawford was very through and explained all of his findings. I just moved from California and must say this was the best Veterinarian experience I have had and I totally like my California Veterinarian. I am glad for the reviews on yelp which helped me with my selection. The entire staff were helpful and very carrying to my Brittany. A big thanks to all at this clinic.

Food: 3.5/5.0
Service: 2.5/5.0
Value: 4.0/5.0
Decor: 2.0/5.0
Overall: 3.5/5.0

Pho-tastic value.  Been coming here for over a decade and it's still worth a stop when I'm in Philly.  Huge bowl if you go for the $9.95 XL option (normal sized if you opt for the $7.95 large/regular).  Pork dishes are good too.

It seems that no matter what I try here, it ends up being the most delicious version of that something I have ever eaten! The dishes are fresh, flavorful, packed with colorful vegetables, and the ratios of ingredients are portioned in a way that's very healthy. (I certainly appreciate having a higher proportion of vegetables on my plate, but if you are someone who orders a noodle dish expecting the entire dish to be nothing but noodles, this may not be the place for you.) Goodness is also the first place I have had a salad that could actually be considered a balanced meal by itself, and the use of three different colors of beets made the salad particularly beautiful and unique.

Ok, so I pretty much stopped coming back here after the above experience. However, I came back here when I was hungry in Chinatown and craving for some pho. Thinking I was in safe territory with Vietnamese food, I ordered a bowl of pho tai bo vien. The soup tasted and looked like chicken soup. Maybe I'm a pho-snob, but in my house, beef pho and chicken soup have no resemblance. 

All in all, I would not recommend this place for either Vietnamese or Thai food.

YUM! We came here with our teenage boys after an exhibit at the Franklin Institute (not within walking distance). Two words: lobster poutine! It was a great starter that my boys fought over. The sandwiches and Kobe dog that they ordered looked great, I had the filet (cooked medium) and it was delicious. In fact, it was better prepared than the filet I had at a fancy steak house in Connecticut last month. Great atmosphere, not too fancy, not too slouchy. I'm glad we passed the bar down the street and choose to eat here instead.

First off, I like to say for a Chinese fast food joint, they got the ordering down! Food taste good, price is reasonable, and fast (especially if u call ahead). The lady that runs the counter, is so sweet! Only downfall to this place, is location. Its easily missed and hard to spot, so keep ur eyes open when ur driving around the small shopping plaza..

So obsessed!! Their Glory juice is everything a good juice should be: healthy, refreshing, inspiring, and delicious! They also have gluten-free bakery goodies (like banana bread and blueberry muffins) that make this perrrrfect. I don't think I would ever try their dishes (they sound gross and not too many gluten free options) but their juices are on point.
Meh on the acai bowl. I got the vegan and it was more of a runny cold soup--not what I wanted for 8.50. I'll come back but not order that again!

It's known as "choo choo" to everyone I know. I think it's the place for every asian teenagers! It brings back so much memories everytime I go there. They are known for the pho. I love the pho there, especially the thin slice beef flank and tripe pho. It's favorful and you can taste all the spices they used. I usually order the papaya salad or the summer (spring) rolls. I've discovered that they don't use as much herbs as I hoped( a bit too light for my liking). On the other hand, Nam Phuong is hardcore with the herbs which I love. I think it's mostly about the location. Choo Choo have a larger population of mix audience whereas, Nam Phuong is in a Vietnamese community. It's all about customization of the tastes.

Favorite restaurant in Philly by far. It's super cheap, the waiters are really nice, you get a TON of food, and it's really yummy. They also have a lot of variety, which is good for me since I'm very picky. I love the pho, the BBQ chicken, and the stir fried chicken with rice. It's a whole lot of food for around $6 each. I also got one of the Vermicelli dishes once, and it lasted me for three full meals. The highlight of the restaurant for me are the fresh fruit smoothies. I highly recommend the coconut smoothie with bubbles. I think I've been going here at least once a week, if not more, and I haven't tired of the food yet.

Do not go here! I first walked to the bathroom which smelled as if it hadn't been cleaned in a very long time. There was no soap or paper towels. I went to sit down and the seat was sticky. That was it! I waa disgusted. I could imagine how dirty the kitchen must be.

My friend and I came here for Pho yesterday.

We started out our meals with a share of the spring rolls, which were accompanied by a tasty peanut sauce, and proved the perfect appetizer! We then continued with bowls of the seafood and special pho, respectively, and both hit the spot. From the broth to the noodles, they were among the best bowls of pho that we have had.

Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai is definitely as good as it gets!

I highly recommend this place. I always get their seafood noodle soup. Its broth is very tasty. I need to expand my food palate. However, I just can't resist but getting the same thing every time I am there! So good & it is cheap!

The door guard is rude and disrespectful.Police are right next to the bar staring at you, and they id like crazy ...i never been inside i only came to the door , and got bad vibes!! I will probably go back,but i will make  sure i carry a jar of vaseline just in case another gay guy like the rude door guard wants to step to me!!! Go to voyeur the  staff are nicer!!!
Its Olive Garden.  What else can you say.  Lol.  I have a gift card but noone ever wants to go.

I really like the selection here food and juice is great... Only reason I give it 3 stars of because not once have I Been into goodness and the staff was polite. Almost like stuck up snobby vibe... Kind of a deal breaker

Very delicious food! Can't ever really get a good read on the people that work there, can't tell if they're angry or just don't like talking to people. But it's still welcoming environment and the food tastes as good as it is healthy for you!

Mediocre. That would be the word I'd use to sum up my experience here. Certainly not worthy of the four stars Yelp has generously given them. I believe this place is simply a tourist trap for people who have not experienced better Vietnamese food elsewhere and those who do not want to venture further north of Philly where the better more authentic Vietnamese food lies. 

The food served was lukewarm. Taste was average. And service borderline bad. Our server was rude when I asked the simple question of whether they serve broken rice or not (a special way Vietnamese people prepare their rice), reprimanding me for not knowing that they do when it was not even noted on the menu. And when we needed small bowls for sharing a couple of items, we had to get up and look for a waiter who then brought big bowls though they have smaller bowls and we specifically asked for small bowls since the table was cramped enough as it was. Needless to say, there won't be a next time.

Really good neighborhood take out Chinese. Always great, friendly service. Beef and broccoli is the best. Good egg rolls. They often throw in am extra egg roll for free. Great reliable place we get food from regularly.

First time at Classic last night and it was great!  Prime rib plate and spaghetti and meatball plate for our table and they were fantastic!  Caesar salad good! Great service, full bar. We will be back!  Really really good prime rib!!

Always good food and fast service. It's all about the food here! If you want ambiance, this is not the place for you.

My favorite go to dish is shrimp with lemongrass or the seafood pho. You can't go wrong.

One more thing....very very very affordable! You can have a meal for two for about $25
I'm never disappointed with the quality of food or service. I love sitting on the deck w/drinks and enjoying multiple dishes. The menu is perfect for all. Great for a group or a romantic date.

Third visit,

Very nice time, a bit slow on the service, but very pleasant server!

Only problem I had was ordered the pork saltibuuca which I've loved before but for some reason this time it was covered a in a white cream sauce Alfredo style not a wine and butter sauce which made the dish way to rich!! 

I should have sent it back! 

Consistency is so important in this business!!!


Second visit; 

Food was so salty is was un eatable! Seems like problems with consistency ?


First visit;

Nice place that offered excellent service right off the start, decor is pleasant but low budget for sure!

I hand the 16 oz ribeye with spaghetti and meatballs $33.00, the steak was very tasty and tender a bit to much grizzle at times!
The pasta was cooked just perfect doneness and the sauce was outstanding!

A soup or salad came with my plate which I choose the Greek lemon and noodle soup that may have been the best item of all?

Garlic bread we ordered was very nice too!

We finish with a fresh baked peach cobbler that was outstanding!

My friend had the spaghetti and meatballs that he seemed to love!

I would definitely recommend this place/ the staff was friendly as well!!

Yum yum

I want to totally love everything about this place. The idea is so amazing and clever. The decor is awesome and hip, like "The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly" meets "Pulpfiction". The staff are cute hipsters that are super friendly and helpful. The food is the only part that is holding this place back. And even then, not really. It is so close to being there, but missing something. 
When we arrived, we were promptly seated and given water. We ordered the Bruscetta as an appetizer, and waited for our food while watching a western on the small TV they have in the middle of the restaurant. Meanwhile, the people behind us were sending their food back. It was the wrong thing AND it was cold. We got our Bruscetta and it was DELICIOUS. Perfect. Then, of a party of about 8 next to us sent back 5 entrees because they were cold! Then we started to worry.
We got our food (Spaghetti and meatballs and lasagna) and, surprise, it was cold. SO disappointing. The meatballs were obvi hand made, which made them delicious, but the cold just made it not good. The lasagna was burnt and cold. How does THAT happen. But it was good food. 
I will be coming back again, because i really want to LOVE this place, but I will give them about 6 months to learn how to heat their food properly.

Your experience here can vary quite a bit based on what you order.  I'm all for efforts to curb the horrible obesity epidemic in this country/state, but I draw the line when restaurants start selling food that touts some alleged health benefit at the cost of tasting good.  
 Even some of the more sinful sounding options like "The King" Sandwich suffer from a fairly lackluster wheat bread.  Then there are the dishes with "Turkey Sausage" two words that should never be that close together.  You're eating sausage either way - ground up hoofs vs. ground up beaks - whatever health benefits potentially exist with the fowl option are greatly superseded by the flavor superiority held by the swine.  Live a little.

But then there are the redeemers like the "Cocoa Warrior" or their fresh lemonade. I won't give up on Goodness, but with a name like that, they need to shift their focus a bit more toward a flavor-first mentality to live up to it.

I think I need a Vietnamese Person to explain why this place has a big neon train out front.  

The food is actually pretty good.    This may be the best tripe I've had in Pho place.  I love tripe and it was just really yummy.  I think Pho 75 up the street is better in terms of broth and noddles, but that closes early and the Train does not.

Plus, it's all about filling up on the cheap so it's a bit academic to nitpic if you don't get food poisoning.

Regardless of the owner comments on the news previously i commend the bartenders here unlike the one in UBar, special mention to the two jello shots guys who are fabulous during outfest nyt. To the apprehensive good looking straight young security guy at the patio last night he is indeed an icandy but needs a drink so he can loosen up a little and smile hahaha but it's all good we will take him as it is. Shout out to the cool security guy who called out a guy in the patio to pull up his pants lol hate it when u can see ghetto guys with their low riding pants showing ugly underwear and cant even afford a prada or armani underwear :-)
Good pho fast and friendly service. I ordered the veggie pho and you can get the soft tofu instead of the fried one!

Very homely and has very nice staff. The food is a little on the greasy side, but what else is expected when ordering a cheesesteak? Overall, it's a very nice choice if you are hungry. It is filling at a great price. 


PS, the cheesesteak and pasta is grrrrrreat!

Lunch was great here at Sandlers on 9 th street. First time coming here with my co-worker. Lobster roll was good although the roll could have been lightly toasted to make an even better experience. Co-worker had the cheddar burger it was well done and very juicy.

Best pho in Philadelphia! I'll admit I'm a little gunshy when eating in Chinatown but this place is delicious! Broth is tasty, not too salty, always piping hot and comes out super fast. The spring rolls are great too. Plus you can't beat the price. Only reason for giving a 4 is ambiance. Very cramped and in definite need of a renovation

I live by the food modo I'll try everything twice (except for durian bubble tea, good God, what the F is that S??). The first time I got the Pho Special from Xe Lua and saw the gelatin meat cube that I believe is called tendon (for any Hungarians out there it looks exactly like head cheese) in it I was visably disappointed. Either way I hid it at the bottom of the bowl and hoped that it would disinigrate into the soup. It definitely didn't and I gagged it down.

Christmas night we went back and I went for the Pho special again because I was worried I would be missing something if I gave up on the tendon after one try. I wasn't, it was gross. 

The rest of the ingrediants were very good though and I'd give the Pho 4 stars minus tendon.  The second time I got it, knowing I might not enjoy the Pho with the meat jello in it I also got the salt and pepper baked squid. It was so chewy it was like eating gigantic braces bands. The flavor was really good but it took me the entire length of Money Ball to finish it (literally). 

4 Star Pho san the jello meat / 2 Star chewy squid / 2 star movie



*In 7th grade I made a diarama of a cell in gelatin, some of you may have as well, that's exactly what the tendon looked like...mitocondria gross!!!

I was really excited to try Pho in Philly since NY pretty much has a very disappointing if nonexistent Pho culture.  Being that I'm from Cali, I've been spoiled and used to the amazing Pho broth.  Maybe I'm asking for too much to have the same wonderful Cali Pho broth in the East Coast but Pho Xu Lua Viet Thai was a big let down.  Their XL portion is huge, with a ton of meat which is a plus but the broth just didn't cut it for me.  I also tried their rice plate and thought the pork chop was pretty decent, but the steam egg wasn't.

Bun no hue is flavorful- not the best I have had but decent. Pho is ok-there are plenty of places that do it way better. The extra crispy egg rolls are some of the best I have had. The summer rolls are fresh and large. Spicy tom yum soup packs a punch and has a depth of flavor beyond the heat. The noodle dishes and curries are good but, again, there is better in Philly. I was not that impressed with the interior. Probably will not be back given the other options.
The food is bad and so is the attitude of the waiters. Don't know what is wrong with them. Probably they have a bad day. Definitely never come back.

holy pho bang, batman this place is disgustingly addicting.  the pho was amazing, the noodle was almost perfect and the broth is MSG free goodness.  i love this place with a passion...too bad i don't live around here or i'd be here all the time.  I LOVE IT!

i liked this place and am glad there are options in tucson for healthy food and drinks.  the one issue i have- which is quite a big one- is that i was told everything was organic there on the phone but when i arrived it was clear not everything is organic.  the menu on the wall listed what was organic and it was very few items actually- mostly salad greens, quinoa and a few other things.  everything else was not listed as organic- including my green juice i ordered!  a lot of restaurants these days hop on the organic bandwagon because it's popular but don't actually use all organic or they say they use it whenever possible.  due to the fact that there are 100% organic restaurants out there- i know it is definitely always possible to buy organic.  it really comes down to price point.  if i am incorrect in my thinking about this place please correct me- but based on my experience and what i read on the menu this place is not even 25% organic.  i wish i had been told the truth when i called.

Yum!

Bring a sweater it's cold.

And whatever you do, do NOT order the x-large soup for just you.  It could easily feed three of you.  Really good thai noodles, too, though not very "thai".
They have everything you need for a road trip stop. Food cooked fresh at their restaurant, and a good selection of snacks. They also accept EBT.

A good solid Vietnamese place in Chinatown.  Also a pretty big menu with dishes that I haven't seen at many of the places in NY Chinatown..not sure if that's just an indication of Philly Chinatown Vietnamese food vs. NY Chinatown Vietnamese food or just something about this restaurant.  It's one of the places I go to semi-regularly for takeout and the food is always fresh and tasty.  I tend to order the rice vermicelli dishes...nom nom  Never tried to eat in there, but it looks pretty standard and generally clean and good.  Always seems pretty full when I go and pick up food.  All in all a good option for Viet food if you're in the area.

This is my favorite Pho place in Philly right now.  The Pho is good, doesn't really WOW me but the drink menu! oh the drink menu!.  the drinks are categorized by liqueur.  Up and down for each the price is the same.  So their top shelf scotch is the same as their rail scotch.  You just can't get that anywhere else.   

Also get started with a spring role, those are great and super refreshing, especially with the peanut sauce.

Yes, 5 stars!  From beginning to end, our experience here was 1st class!  We were greeted promptly for our reservation time, and sat immediately.  Waiter appeared with water, and to explain nightly specials.  We're ordered calamari ( done just right, and half off appetizers until 6).  Went with the special- spaghetti and meatballs with a side of steak!!!  Pasta cooked perfectly with a deliciously authentic Italian sauce.  Meatballs are flavorful, a combo of beef, pork, veal, salami!  Prices are reasonable, considering how much food there is!  I agree with reader about Caesar salad.  Just the right amount of dressing.  And, the New York steak!!  Perfect temperature, with a lovely seasoning.  Service was efficient and friendly.  You have to look for the place, "CLASSIC" is the only part of the sign you can read!

We purchased general admission tickets for a bachelorette party for their Diva Royale drag show.  When we called we asked if we purchased our tickets separately, would we still be able to sit together, they replied that it's first come, first seated, so we would be seated together when we arrived.  *They specifically stated "seated", so imagine our frustration that when we got there we were told that general admission tickets were STANDING ROOM ONLY!  Now, it's fine if that's their general rule, limited table space, we understand, however, we would have certainly chosen different shoes to wear knowing we were standing for 1 1/2+ hours.  The doors opened at 7pm, show started at 8pm, so we planned on getting there at 7 to make sure to get good "seats".  Well, again, we wish we knew that since it was only standing room, we didn't need to get there an hour early and kill time (standing), we could have stayed in our party bus and drank for cheaper and comfortable.  

So, all that being said, besides the incorrect communication, we did have a good time.  Staff was personable (and easy on the eyes..lol)  Drinks were half price I believe before the show started, then full price after 8, so I think a beer was $3, mixed drink was $6.  That's what I overheard, I didn't drink, so I can't say for sure.  I did ask for a water, they gave me a bottle, no charge, which I appreciated.  

The talent was wonderful.  They were friendly as they walked around the room before the show, very entertaining and interactive with the audience.  Some of the personas portrayed were better than others, but was easily overlooked due to the entertainment and enthusiasm of the ladies!  

Another note, we were told the show went from 8-9pm, the show didn't end until around 945pm, which was great that we got longer entertainment than expected, but again, that was poor communication on their part since we had other plans afterwards and the party bus driver expected us to be done around 9pm.  Nothing that ruined our night, but an inconvenience and frustrating moment due to incorrect information that was given to us. 

All in all, a good night, would probably do it again, but would want to be aware of those things.
My favorite pho place, $6.25 for big bowl of noodles and cow parts.

Guys... get it together. Your food has great flavor. But I payed .50 extra for quinoa and y'all put brown rice in my bowl. And I'm a vegetarian asked for tofu and chicken showed up in the last two bites of my bowl. Good food. Bad and inconsistent service.

First they do not offer alcohol.  Restaurant was completely empty and they placed five of us in a four person table.  I asked to be moved.  Ordered two orders of wings to start, Korean & Buffalo, mediocre.  We left half the wings untouched.  Burger was fine, hotdog was fine, skirt steak was good, both pastas were harder than al dente. Pesto sauce was nice.  Service was good.  $140. I expect better food.

This place is great. It's nice, cozy, decorative and clean. The staff is friendly (they smile!) and give quick easy service. 
I dined with a group of friends. We ordered a variety of pho and hu tieu (clear and egg noodle).
You know a place is good when you can have a great time with your friends and the conversation of free of any complaints of service and only accolades of the food.

I've been here twice. Ordered Pho and Bun Bo Hue for 2 times. Both were unbelievably bad. The Pho soup was really plain, my friend had Bo Kho and she said it was not any better. Today we decided to give it a second try. However, it was worse than the first time. The meat of the Bun Bo Hue was rotten, making the whole thing smell. It was just terrible. I can't imagine how one can set up a restaurant with such low quality food. I'm from VN and I lived in California for 4 years so my taste can't be wrong. They just don't know how to make Vietnamese food. Can't deny it's cheap but feel like it doesnt worth a penny. Swear to myself to never go there again. There are some good places on Washington street. If you're looking for real and good vietnamese food stay away from this place!!!!!!

The Sunday football happy hours are phenomenal here...$3 pitchers and $10 towers!!!  The bartender also let us put our tower on hold while I ran home to walk my dog.  The wings were also really good...50 cents, and pretty sizeable.  It's great for football watching...not a lot of loud obnoxious people, ample tv's and a cozy environment with a faux-fireplace.  The only negative is the bar had kind of an odd smell to it.....that was masked with the scent of vanilla candles.   The bar is also kind of dark and dingy, but on a hazy Sunday evening, it serves its purpose.  I'd definitely go back.

I have eaten at this location under many different restaurants and the interior fro all of them have been about the same, this time they changed up the entry, the rest is the same funky layout.  They have added some perfunctory changes such as paint, better chairs, and a little better lighting.  The food is more of rollercoaster at times really good at other times wandering and lacking.  
My least favorite item, sadly to say is the spaghetti and meatballs, the sauce is too sweet and is missing some pep, and a viscus consistency that I was not fond of. 

What was just okay,  was the lasagna (one time with a lot of red pepper), but the next time was marginal.  I did  not finish it or take it home

The Pork Sambuca, was I thought one of the best meals here, rich and a nice sensation to the palate.

The star of the show is the Prime Rib this is the reason to go here, it's juicy, it melts in your mouth, it's pretty close to perfect.

The sides, salads, apps are all okay, but not indelible to my memory.

The service has always been good to great with a party 5 or less, 6 or more we run into problems of inertia.

So go and get the Prime Rib with a small group, and you will be happy,
I think.

I'm bummed I didn't find Goodness earlier. Goodness is a juice bar but also serve breakfast. After a yoga class down the street, I stopped here for the steak bowl and wow, it was one of the best things I had eaten. I was also very hungry. With that said, the bowl has a good portion of steak, avocado, tomatoes, and pickled onions over brown rice. Normally, I have to substitute ingredients but here, everything looks fantastic. I was between this item and their breakfast burrito. I guess I'll have to go back to Tucson!
Went there 30 minutes before closing. Had a great pho tai nam that came out in a few minutes. Inexpensive and delicious. I'll be back.
Favorite pho place, with extensive Thai and Viet menu. Service is always quick and easy and food always comes out delicious.

I think that this place is over rated.  The Pho is really cheap and you do get a lot for your money but this is about the taste.  The taste is decent and it's all that bad.  The broth was a tad tasteless, I believe it's due to all of the noodle that they toss into the bowl.  If they were to make the bowl a bit smaller, and focus on the taste rather than the sizes, it would taste a bit better.  

The spring rolls is a spring roll.  I don't care if the waiter tells me it's not a "shrimp roll" haha Spring rolls are not fried, those are egg rolls!  The service is not all that great but then again, this is about the taste of the food.  

If you're looking to cheap Pho, this is the place to go because you get a large amount of decent food for a pretty good deal.

You get what you expect from an Olive Garden. Big portions are n the pasta, small on the protein. Breadsticks are always delicious. Service is always great. You can never go wrong with Olive Garden and this one is no different.

So I found my Philly pho spot.

Really solid pho, listened to other Yelpers and stayed away from the bun bo hue. You usually want to find a place that only does bun bo hue for that soup anyway. 

I'm a pretty big eater and the normal large ($5.95) was more than adequate. Almost every other pho place, I usually pay the extra dollar for the larger size, but it's completely unnecessary here. Tons of meat too. Unless you're built like a lineman, or your nursing an extreme hangover, stick with the large, not the XL.

one more thing - they open at 11am, not 10am. And it was more like 11:05 am on this particular Friday. 

One weird thing - I went right when they opened so it was me and three other tables there. I guess the full wait staff was there and didn't have much to do, so they were just kind of standing at attention, staring at us and watching us eat. I'm sure they were just being vigilant about refilling water, but it was slightly unsettling. Not so unsettling that I didn't enjoy my soup.

Great environment, good music selection, indoor and outdoor seating
Slow service to make your food/drinks. Many healthy options!

Goodness has a very good atmosphere, with even better food. They had lots of different options, including gluten free, vegan, and vegetarian options. Really cute outside seating. The guy who took my order was super chatty and nice. Definite will go back.

Great place for whole foods and healthy eating for breakfast lunch or a quick healthy shot of energy, vegan and gluten free options available. Great vibe, I always come in to great chill music and the staff is helpful and pretty chill as well.
Fresh ingredients, good vibes. I don't think there is a single item on the menu that is bad, it's all succulent

Delicious food at this hole in the wall. All the comments about its nickname "the choo choo" are dead on. Their neon train sign helped us out of towners find the place a boy are we glad we did. Very affordably priced! My friend and I each had an entree, shared an app, she had a beer and I had a Thai tea and then I'll came in under $25! I even walked away with a nice sized portion I left overs for lunch the next day. The chicken curry was delicious and perfect texture. Peanut sauce is on point. Will return again!

After almost 300 reviews, there's probably not much I can say that hasn't already been said.

Great food for cheap is pretty much what sums it up. I am no Pho expert, but I've had my fair share of bowls. This one was very good. the shrimp rolls were also very fresh and tasty.

Service is incredibly fast so if you're looking for a quick and inexpensive dinner on a week night, this is your place

OMG do I NOT like vietnamese food? I don't know. I think I ordered some interesting things.

I went with a friend who is veggie and I was disappointed that they didn't have much veggie options for her. No appetizers. They have a small section in the back of the menu. The waitstaff recommend she get the only soup that was veggie and when it arrived (in a LARGE bowl) it looked soo tasteless and it indeed was not tasteful.

I did appreciate their large portions tho. She got an entree that was much tastier tho.

I got the shrimp (cold) spring roll appetizer. I enjoyed the peanut sauce but I must admit I lost interest in the shrimp roll when I spied the shit?/vein? of the shrimp all wrapped in the wrap and visable thru the thin skin of the roll wrapper. I mean I know shrimps have veins in them but shouldn't that be cleaned out? and should you try to NOT have it show (if u don't take the time to devein it?)

I didn't eat the second roll because I was just like ECK..I don't know what I'm eating.

I ordered vermicelli with like a mixture of stuff. But seriously after that shrimp spring roll event, I was kinda skeptical of everything after that. I felt I was eating "mystery meat" and i was not comfy. 

I don't think i would come back to order again. I'll just go to the burmese place up the block.

Noodles are eatable, but not good enough to get more stars.

I ordered beef Pho and beef was overcooked, soup base not favor enough, its cheap and serve with big bowl, just not that impressed of their food a lot.

Restaurant have two floors, very old style atmosphere, I've experienced a better one in Chicago.

I had vegetable spring rolls as an appetizer, and also pan friend noodles with shrimp and vegetables.

Presentation of the noodle dish was great--it looked like a giant bird's nest made out of crunchy noodles, with the shrimp and vegetables in the middle. The amount of shrimp was generous, which was nice. However, it was too saucy for my liking. As soon as I dug in, the sauce spread to the crunchy noodles, instantly rendering them soggy.

The vegetable spring rolls were awesome, especially with the sweet & spicy dipping sauce. Chopstick-licking good :)

I think I will give this restaurant another try, but will likely order something else, like pho or rice soup next time.
Great place awesome atmosphere... mixed guys/girls and many workers with minimal clothing... droo traxx kills it as their dj... He's the main reason I go

Screw fast food, nothing beats pho here for a cheap, fast meal. Loses points for cleanliness (the floor and the corners tend to look a little grimy) but I've never had any issues personally, so I keep coming back for more!
Icandy is a great gay club! The DJ could be better, but everyone in the club was extremely nice and it looks really nice inside.  I definitely would recommend coming here.
Everything is super yummy here. Tried there soft shell crab if you're a true seafood lover! It comes with rice too.

This place meets all my criteria for a place I will come back to again and again:

Has an eclectic menu - always something new to try  (i.e. snails or sugarcane shrimp, yum!)

Serves alcamahol - (unlike some of the other pho places near by)

Would definitely categorize it as a 'cheap eats' -  for under 30 bucks my husband 
and I stuffed ourselves plenty AND had 2 rounds of drinks!

Fast and efficient service - never had to sit and wonder when i would be getting my food even when it's been pretty crowded there

THE best PHO in town!

Love love. love this place - if you are a viet food lover, don't miss out!  

(oh yeah, and they serve thai dishes as well)

where else should a single woman in the city have cocktails after work? let's just say, i was the only one. ran into a coworker on the street. he invited me in. paul was the bartender. he was funny and sweet. made me feel comfortable. it was a wed late afternoon. it wasnt busy, but everyone in there was super friendly. i swear, the martinis are bucket sized! 
the music was great. it was music videos. i didnt see the other floors or the outside area. next time, i guess. good times, good times!

First time here. I ordered Pho and a dish.

PROS:
-Fast. Fast. Fast. I ordered it and the wait time was less than 5 minutes. The place was not crowded, but there were around 6 tables that were eating and around 3 waiting on food.
-The food was great, and for a very good price. It filled me up so quick that I was dumbfounded. 

CONS:
-None

OVERALL:
The outside may look a bit "shady" but the food inside is wonderful!

Amazing!!!!!!!!!!! 
Great price. Fast service!!! I order the tofu pho. It was perfect! They serve you hot tea. It's a hidden gem. Truly yummy
Going back each time I'm in philly

Clean, friendly local frozen yogurt place. The lady who works here is always so friendly and inviting. The flavors are great and my daughter and I love coming here for an after school or after camp treat.

This place is quantity over quality. The portion size at this place is unbelievable and the prices are so low they don't seem to correspond. When I go here, I'm thinking I want a small soup to start with. For less than $4, I order what I think will be an appetizer sized soup, but instead I am served a gigantic bowl of meat, broth and veggies. . .not that I'm complaining. 

The menu is very diverse and has things that I have never seen before, but they seem to have a way of cooking things differently here. I've tried their common Asian dishes and the flavor is just. . . .different. It is not necessarily bad, but not necessarily good either. 

The best thing on the menu is the seafood noodle soup. When I go to a restaurant, I usually like to order something different every time, but the first time I had the seafood noodle soup, I couldn't stop thinking about it. It has resulted in me ordering it at almost every subsequent visit. This probably has something to do with my soup obsession. The broth is unbelievably flavorful, topped with a combination of seafood and then finished with the traditional condiments of lime, mints, culantro, etc. Something about this dish makes it so much better than any other seafood noodle soup I've ever had. 

Despite the inconsistent quality, I have a way of returning to not so good places because they lure me in with their quantity size. I plan on going back again and again, but I probably won't like it, unless I'm there for the seafood noodle soup.
This place didn't do it for us. High ratings but both the pho or curry didn't have much flavor.
Came to Sandler's on 9th for brunch. The service was okay, and the food was good. Highly recommend trying Fat Elvis!

I came here while on a business trip and it was refreshing to find somewhere with healthy, fresh food. I stayed in a hotel right by the airport and the food options around there were slim, think fast food only. This place is a 20 minute drive out from the airport area but is so worth the drive if you're ever in the area. I recommend the Healing Vibes juice and the Thai Chicken bowl (add tofu). Oh and the staff is super sweet and friendly too!!

This Olive Garden always does so well. No matter what day or time we come, we are never dissatisfied.  The wait staff is on point. We always try and sit with our favorite server Rose, but when she isn't here, we are still taken care of well. 

My go to is always the ziti al forno, but I love trying all the seasonal seafood dishes and of course desserts! 

Friday nights and weekend parking is pretty busy, but I recommend coming before 6 pm or after 8 pm.

I love this place, it reminds me of my mom's pho which I now sorely miss. I've been here twice; first time visiting with my boyfriend because we were craving pho and after a Temple homecoming tailgate and I was drunk and craving something beyond pizza and fast food. The best idea ever tbh but I digress... I always get the Pho Tai Nam. Portions are H U G E. There are two sizes for pho: large and XL. I stupidly decided to get an XL and I could, maybe, consume half of it. The broth is tasty, you get the usual vegetable and sauce condiments, and the wait staff is super attentive! Support local businesses and come here!
the pho here is consistent and cheap. It is my go-to spot in philly, and the service is quick and efficient.

Wow, Tucson is really lucky to have a veterinary clinic like Cimarron Animal Hospital.  

I take Kitty in for her normal checkups here, but over the weekend she got really sick so I called Saturday morning and they were able to get her in right away.  I didn't even think they'd be open, let alone able to see her- I envisioned having to go to a scary 24 Hour place with a vet I didn't know, etc.

They talked me through everything they were going to do and were SO nice- they even have a special exam room for cats which is nice- they line the table with fleece so Kitty isn't sliding all over the metal table, and they have kitty treats and everything.  Small touches like that really let you know that they care about ALL animals; that they aren't dog-centric who occasionally see cats.  

We ended up taking x-rays and doing some bloodwork, and a final diagnosis couldn't be reached, but they did treat her for her dehydration and give her meds for her nausea and other symptoms.  They also sent me home with some medication and special food for her GI distress.  Talk about convenient- they had it ALL in-house.  They even cut up her pills (she was to take 1/4 pill).  Man, even MY pharmacist doesn't do that for me!

Here's the awesome part- they sent me home with her X-Rays and labwork results in case I needed to have her admitted to the Emergency Vet (they gave me a card with their info on it, too), so that they would have a heads up as to what was going on.

Thankfully, Kitty is feeling better so she didn't need a trip to the Emergency Vet, but I had peace of mind when we were home over the weekend that she'd be in excellent hands due to the legwork that Cimarron Animal Hospital did for her.  

I am so thankful for the time and effort they put in for Kitty- we were there until 1:30 (they close at 1 on Saturdays) and they all went above and beyond when they could have said "Sorry, we're closed, you need to take her somewhere else".

I highly recommend Cimarron Animal Hospital- they are so friendly and their prices are reasonable.  Give them a try if you're on the eastside- you won't regret it!

This is one of the best pho places in Chinatown and has always been regardless of the newer Vietnamese restaurants that open around the neighborhood. It's usually always busy especially around lunch time so I don't understand why they are closed on Wednesday (makes me sad). 

Their menu is vast but I usually always get their noodle soups and bubble teas. The pho comes out pretty quick and the temperature of the soup is perfect. I would always return here for a quick bite during work hours or after a long day.

I have dreams about their breakfast burrito. 

To be real though, my girlfriend moved to Tucson, Arizona for work and we have been venturing Tucson and its eateries. It wasn't till we came to Goodness, that we found our new favorite place. We've been here now a few handful of times, but there was not one time when we avoided the breakfast burrito. 

Originally, I'm from San Diego, and I've had my fair share of the occasional carne asada/carnitas/breakfast burritos from the local taco shops. But after having this breakfast burrito, filled with honest to goodness, fresh cooked quinoa, avocados, eggs, pico de gallo, and turkey sausage inside a multigrain tortilla served with their own chipotle sauce. It is the best burrito I have ever had, and have no guilt post meal. 

The atmosphere is pretty hipster, but can serve anyone, and the interior is very impressive. They also serve fresh juiced juice, smoothies, acai bowls, teryaki bowls, and you name it. Also the ingredients are fresh daily. 

I might be weird, but their water also seems very refreshing as well. The only thing I dislike is the fact that parking is pretty cramped, it would be great to go early or after lunch due to high traffic to the restaurant. But overall, quality, price, and appearance. All 5 stars from me. Great place to enjoy, and hidden gem here in Tucson, Arizona.
The Pho here was delicious. They give a lot food for the price and the service was pretty quick. I plan to come back to try some of their fried dishes in the future.

Found out about this restaurant  on Yelp and boy was I glad I tried it. The food was excellent  and the service was great! There was a musician  playing  songs in a soft tone so the music  didn't  overtake  our conversation  and the decor went with the name on the building. Over all I definitely  will go back and would  recommend this  place! A new gem in Tucson!

First of all, I'm going to start off with saying Hi to I-Candy's Management and Employees.  The Management who runs The I-Candy club care about their guests, and care about everyone having a good time.  The Bartenders are awesome very friendly and they talk to you like your  Family, Also the Front door person is so sweet, He always makes me feel so warm and welcoming, He always says Hi and gives me a Hug, when I enter the Club. I-Candy is the go-to Place to hear good music Dance and Also good bar food if you decide to eat.  The drinks here are cheap and super strong! This is the place to go to drink and dance your heart away with no worries...   They have a lot of Space to dance, space to sit and space to drink.  I truly Recommend I candy to anybody that wants to have Fun...Come on It don't get any Better!

Delicious and affordable! I threw down a pho Xe Lua sac biet for only 7.fitty! 

The soup broth was nice and sweet without being... Sweet. Its not like many places I go to where an XL is just a medium in a huge bowl. They loaded it up with meat, tripe, tendons and all the good stuff. 

This will be my goto spot for the winter.

The first time we went here it was fine - 3 or 4 stars food with acceptable service. The second time was not so good. The tea in their cups tasted like soap so off to a bad start. Then we ordered a veggie dish that I took a few bites of before seeing a piece of hair in it. We called the waiter's attention to it, and after he saw it, he took the dish, asked if we'd like a replacement (we declined) and then took it away, without another word. How hard can it be to apologize? A simple acknowledgement would have been enough.

The actual vermicelli was okay but not great - the meat was good but not a fan of the raw bean sprouts. Also, they only give you about a 1/2 cup worth of noodles. The pho (from the first time we went) was decent but not as good as the spots down on Washington Ave.

With so many other good Vietnamese options in Philly, we definitely won't be back.

Excellent breakfast spot! My husband is skeptical of all "healthy" eating but he loved Goodness too! We each had the breakfast burrito and shared the cacao nib Acai bowl. The burrito was amazing! Spicy and filling. Very well done. The bowl was also good. Smaller than most Acai bowls but great flavor and not icy at all. The granola was excellent! The coffee was light and yummy. Goodness had a great coffee shop feel with great food! Recommend for anyone looking for a healthy, fresh breakfast.
Duck leg Egg noodle soup! Seriously Vietnamese food, in Philly!?! Wowza! Thanks for the rec Alyssa!

This place is a Chinatown staple. Whenever I ask my Vietnamese friends where they like to go, this is the place they point to so I know the food is authentic. The decor may be plain, but the menu is extensive, the service is quick and the prices can't be beat.

I have been here several times growing up and the pho never fails to satisfy. Recently, I ordered the Seafood Rice Stick Noodle Soup  and my boyfriend ordered a Thai curry. I had a good variety of shrimp, squid, crab and fish balls - yum ^^ Where we live, my family's go to lunch and dinner spots are Pho places so I have had my fair share of pho and can tell the good from the okay. Tasting the soup here was a real treat - they really know how to make excellent broth!! My boyfriend wasn't too fond of his curry though. They probably specialize more in the Vietnamese food realm. Overall, it's a nice place to go for some savory, winter time warmth.

It is an average Chinese restaurant.  Prices are equivalent to other places I have been, food decent and the service quick.  I come here fairly often and while I would not say it stands out,  it is good enough for many repeat visits.  
My only criticism is in the summer it is like a sauna in there.  Waiting 10 minutes you are sweating and it grosses me out to think people are sweating while cooking my food.  Plus, I really feel bad for all those working there.  
The woman that is there often is very sweet and welcoming.  If you want some quick decent food for pickup, I would recommend stopping by!

The only reason they lose one star is because it's cash only, which isn't helpful on the go. Great food and the lady is very nice and friendly. Curry chicken with white rice and noodles, always good and filling.

Fe Fi Pho failure here.
On my last evening in Philly we decided to get full on Pho before heading be to NYC.
Using the Yelp App we chose Pho Xe Lua.

We order Pho. the first thing that came out was the extras for the Pho; bean spouts, mint leaves and lemon wedges. Lemon? Yip, No lime.
 
The bean spouts were full of the green-brown bean casing from the growing process use to grow bean spouts. Which means they did not rinsed them properly.
These casing with  leave a muddy taste in the Pho and the lemon did not go well with the Pho broth. the flavor was just not right.

The Pho in general was just OK. 
Today their broth was weak, no rich & flavorful as I was hoping for.

The service was sub standard, even thought there were about 6-8 waiters standing behind us with nothing to do but to chat. At the end of the meal I spill my tea by accident and was wiping up the mess. One waiter walk by and didn't even bother to help.  All the other ones were busy chatting.

Hope your experience is better than mine.
I was visiting today 6/30/18 from Maryland and decided to stop here for dinner. I had the chicken and waffle and it was off the hook.

There's always "that place" everyone goes to growing up as an established point of socialization. I found this place in high school and everything has been good and consistent. The name actually means "pho train" which is what they're known for. But unlike the other pho spots that dedicate themselves to just pho and a few rice dishes , this place has it all. It tends to get packed at times and you'll get quick and efficient Chinatown service, but this is a great lunch a dinner spot

Your standard American-style Chinese take out. The place is clean, the staff friendly and the food is not wonderful, but is exactly what you expect from a place like this. They get enough business that you don't need to worry too much that it old.  I was surprised to find that the steamed broccoli included almost as a garnish, was fresh and not overcooked.

They would get 5 stars but let's leave room for growth! This is a 4.5 star review. 

First off, service is great! You can definitely tell it's a team affair. We were greeted and sat promptly and although the person who sat us wasn't our server she was very helpful. The place is nice and clean and although they don't serve alcoholic beverages just yet you can grab something and BYOB 2 doors down. 

Our server, Jordayn, was very attentive. She definitely delivered service with a smile. We even saw a few managers who also came by to ensure we were having a great time and that everything was satisfactory. 

We had 2 starters, poke tacos and Korean bbq wings. Both delicious! 

For our main course we had chicken and waffles, the delirium burger and 2 cheddar burgers. All good was fresh and delicious and presented well. 

We were quite full so ended with a shared dessert because we just had to try it! I'm glad we did...Oreo creme brûlée.  I can't wait to have that again. 

I hope they maintain this level of service and quality in their food. We live in NJ but we will be back and hope we receive the same excellent service and good eats!

It was mostly inedible, but then again- i didnt really have much of an appetite after the roaches crawled by me at my table.  Many places have roaches. I guess they just don't bother to exterminate. Anyways, I wont ever go back.  Oh service was bad too. They tried to keep taking my soup and asked if i was done like three times trying to rush me out.  It's really bad.  Read the other reviews about " if you go, don't look down at the floor before your food comes out"--  unfortunately it's true.

We were very happy to get in around 6:30pm with no wait!  Our server was very nice and helpful with the kiddos pickiness for food!  Soup was a little slow coming out, but grace given because they were busy! I ordered the eggplant parmigiana with Angel haired pasta, covered in 3 cheese marinara. They only put my request over the pasta, but she kindly came out with an extra bowl of sauce to cover the eggplant. Hubby had the baked ziti and no complaints. Kids had kid portion of baked ravioli and chicken fingers w/buttered pasta and grapes.
The beef with Crunchy  noodle  is delicious, had me coming back 3 straight weekends.  Their smoothies are amazing too, just don't go for durian, strawberry is the best one we have tried.

A great place to go if you are in center city and want a delicious but inexpensive meal. Viet Thai is one of my favorite places to go. You get huge plates of food for a really small price. I like all of their spicy rice dishes. I have been so many times and have never been disappointed.
bbq beef, shredded pork, and steam egg over rice.  it was really tasty and very reasonably priced. a busy restaurant with reasonable prices and tasty food. can't beat that.

I can't help but hearkens back to the wise words of Obi-Wan Kenobi when thinking of 12th Scare Command - "You will never find a more wretched hive of scum and villainy. We must be cautious." Ok, it's not that bad... But it does have it's scary dark recessed "mugger's paradises" on the 1st and 2nd floor. The bathrooms are a mess, and quite often you'll find some kind of illicit activity being perpetrated in there. And really, what's with Philly gay bars and floor to ceiling mirrors on the dance floors?! The 70s are over and Studio 54 wants it's look back... The drinks are potent, the staff friendly, and the music okay. It's best to go as a group and stick close together... Use the buddy system and don't leave anyone behind!
friendly waiters...awesome food....5-10min for food. basically it's the best hot pho in chinatown

Owned and operated by an awesome couple who were so friendly on our late night visit. Yogurt was great but it tasted better knowing I was giving my money to a momnpop establishment. This would be my go to place if I lived in Tucson
There's a reason this place is referred to as "12th Scare".  Srsly, this place can be a nasty meat market of horridness.

5 stars for the bartender! I wasn't there for drinks, just food. He was super friendly and attentive without doing too much. Just overall a good service provider who took pride in his job. Food was so great. Lobster ravioli wasn't impressive at all but again the service was good so I'll go back

My go to pho spot whenever I'm craving. The broth here tastes really clean and their summer / spring rolls are good as well. I'm not a fan of their pad Thai, but then again I only like one place to get pad thai so i could be being a little biased  but overall it's very affordable and is filling! The  downside is that since it's located in Chinatown,  parking may be difficult at times

Coffee smooth.  I normally drink tea, however, was invited to meet a friend there recently in the middle of the day.  The location is a little off the beaten path and I hope they make it.   Staff was pleasant, courteous and serviceful.  Enjoyed the coffee and the great, fast wifi.  I will be back soon.

Our go-to place in Philly for when we are craving pho. 

We always get the summer rolls and different types of pho. Food always comes out super fast and it's really affordable. Our bill is usually only $15 for the two of us.

Newly opened restaurant that opened in my former residence, The Ben Franklin.  It replaced the overpriced Indian restaurant that was located here.  But took a colleague out for his going away lunch.  I ordered the lobster roll which came with a side of fries, no complaints there.  It's your typical lunch restaurant, well-run, clean, good service.  I wouldn't mind coming again for a work lunch.

Good pho at a great price! I usually go to Nam Phuong in South Philly but wanted to find a place closer to home My girlfriend and I had pho and shared a rice place and my boyfriend had the seafood hong kong style noodles. We were all very happy and very impressed by both the service and price! $30 for 3 people for dinner was not bad at all. The ambiance is not fancy at all so don't expect much. It has your typical vietnamese restaurant kind of ambiance. I'm definitely going to make my way back next time I need my Pho fix!

Yelp has failed me this time. I went to philly to get some authentic Vietnamese food. NOT chinese vietnamese food, that I can get anywhere in NYC. Everything was just mediocre. I only spent a day there, and am very diappointed that I chose this for my dinner.

Yum! My boyfriend & I had our first pho experience here today! It was delicious (medium rare beef pho and well done beef pho, as well as spring rolls - yum!!) and service was good! We weren't sure if we were supposed to add any sauces to the pho - probably yes  We will definitely be back!!

Holy smokes this place is the real deal! Awesome crazy staff that reach right in front of your face and deliver pounds of pad Thai that will have you stuffed for days. Shrimp, chicken, tofu it's all amazing. My favorite pad Thai in the whole city. Order 420! Smoothies here are also awesome and you can even get them to go. Really fast pick up times too, under 15minutes
I had the pho, the broth was not very complex and the noodles were overcooked.

My husband and I stopped by for lunch and had 
a delightful time. The service from Jahlil was awesome and such a friendly atmosphere. 
We both ordered the Fried Chicken and Bacon Belgian Waffles with the PA maple syrup. For a new location finding their way I was impressed coming from NY and the many American bistros we have in the city. I loved the twist on the American classic. We both agreed the chicken was moist and tendered. The waffles was light and a bit crispy, must drip the maple syrup for the finishing taste. I would certainly return to try another dish and have a few rounds of the spice jalapeño martini..

We were looking for a quick healthy meal, and that is what we got.  The restaurant was clean and neat.  The food was fresh and good.  There were gluten free options too!  I ordered the kale caesar salad with chicken it was just what I wanted.  Give them a try, they have outdoor and indoor dining.  Food was made individually and to your specifications.  Please give this new restaurant a try, they do give military and other discounts.  Casual dining with a healthy kick!
The pho was very good could use more star anise. but the chicken my husband had was tasteless. Very good for he money but like most pho restaurants little atmosphere . Good soup

One of my go to Pho spots in Chinatown. I got their house pho and it's pretty good. For under $10 and it's x large, you can't beat that deal. The broth flavor is fairly mild but the portion more than makes up for it.

The service at this place is quite quick. Quick to take your order and quick to fill your water. It seems similar to a fast food type environment. It might have been because they had all their waiters staffed that day. That is how it felt since there was alot of employees when I went around six on a weekend. 

Overall, it is a good spots for good photos at their price. Can't beat that.

Tried their lemon flavor and it tasted like nothing. Just plain yogurt with no flavor that was watered down. They were nice enough to instead give me a vanilla one, but it was still was medicore at best.

This place is alright. The food wasn't so fresh like I thought. But I think Pho might be better I ordered BBQ chicken on vermicelli. The noodle weren't so good and chicken did not taste like anything. So, I don't like it too much. And my boyfriend ordered beef something I don't rememder the name of it. Beef didn't taste anything. We might not come back.

Known to the locals simply as Choo Choo, because Xe Lua translate to train in Vietnamese and there is a neon sign of a train on the front window, Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai is one of the best Vietnamese restaurants for a college student on a budget in Philadelphia.

The pho itself isn't the absolute best pho but it is pretty good.  As well as their numerous other dishes.  Spring rolls and egg rolls are big, fresh, and delicious.  The bean sprouts and basil that come with pho and some other broth dishes can be a bit spotted but in general it's still good.

I've tried many dishes in this restaurant and most are on a scale of 3.5/5.0 to 5.0/5.0 stars for me.  And with the prices so reasonable you can afford to try different dishes.  There of course are always some more expensive dishes offered, but they are not excessive.  They also offer family style meal options which are also delicious.

Some of my staples:
Pho Dac Biet (House Special Pho)
Hu Tieu Do Bien Thai Lan (Tom Yum Seafood Soup)
Com Xao Bo Xa Ot (Lemongrass Beef with broken rice)
Com Suong (Pork Chop with broken rice)

One quick note: $15 minimum for charge.  Happy eating!

There's not a better place to get pho in Philly. Large portions, lots of meat. Their other dishes are great too, just like home made. Prices are reasonable, not expensive. Gets crowded and tight spaces but definitely worth it.

The bar is fun but stay away from bartender Kale. I was flagged after three drinks because I flirted with this straight bartender. He seems to put up with working there but does not encourage a good time. Go there and have fun but stay away from Kale the bartender- he doesn't belong there taking tips when he clearly is not friendly or service oriented. From a friendly visitor from SF.

I've been here a few times and its always been a pretty good time. I found that it was more fun and more crowded on Fridays (when they have 18+ night) as opposed to Saturdays when its only 21+. The drinks are somewhat reasonable priced, the music is good, the clientele is on the younger side (a plus for me), and the go-go boys are really hot. 

My only criticism is the size of the dance floor. Its not all that big and can get really crowded when things get going. But all in all, I enjoy my nights spent at iCandy.

Do not come here! My table ordered the bun bo hue, pho dac biet, and the banh hoi nem nuong and they were all disgusting. Everything was not flavorful and appealing at all. We couldn't finished anything and was very disappointed. 

The restaurant was pretty small and cramped. The prices were decent.
