I've been coming this place for years since I moved to Philly from Jersey.
Among those Pho restaurants I've tried, this is the best. and super  cheap, Once in a while, the flavor would be different, but understandable.
I do know how hard it is to keep the same flavor everyday.
I always get 102 & 206 for my wife and myself. And we always leave satisfied.

This review is strictly for PHO only.  I can't even conceive of ordering anything else from this venue, so please go on to the next review if you are interested in anything other than pho.

The only five star pho review I will ever give in the east coast.  I know, because I've been eating pho EVERYWHERE they have it in the east coast and the west coast (AND Vietnam, I might add) for the last 12 glorious years.

Pho is my last meal item.  I love it that much. But I'm fiendishly picky about every component of this dish.  I'm not a true carnivore, and as such, do away with the funny bits of cow (I have no problems with them flavoring my broth with it, but I don't care to chew them, thank you very much), and typically go for Pho Tai.  

So starting with the meat...this needs to be RAW, sliced THIN, and a bit on the glistening-bloody side.  The broth, therefore, needs to be piping hot so that as soon as you flip the meat underneath the mass of rice noodles, it cooks instantly.

The rice noodle, since it'll be plunged into the hot broth, cannot be overcooked. They need to be JUST barely pliable, so that it finishes cooking in the broth and becomes slurp-worthy.

Broth, aside from the temperature, is truly the soul of the dish.  I cannot abide by any broth that has little blobs of grease floating on top.  That's an individual preference, I suppose, but I think it tastes so much cleaner and deeper without the floating grease.  Xe Lua gets as close to it as I've seen, though a total elimination isn't possible--after all, it's not consomme we're consuming here.

Last, but not least, are the herbs, lime, and sauce.  Don't skimp on my basil leaves and dandelion leaves.  I cannot, simply cannot, believe people who leave any of these herbs out of their pho!  I get an insane urge to grab them off their plate when I see this.  This is what perfumes the broth and elevates pho to the "Oh my god I just died and went to culinary heaven"  level.  Also, no lemon.  It MUST be lime.  Again, Xe Lua does it right.  In my 12 years, I think they served lemon ONCE.  It shook my phaith (sorry) to the very core, but that has been a few years and they have rectified their cheapskate ways since then.

If you have not had pho ever, I think you would do yourself a great kindness by introducing yourself to it here.  This was my first, and still the best, pho experience in all of east coast.

This review is for their Chicken Pho (Pho Ga) only. 
If you're ordering chicken pho -- the honest opinion is 2/5 stars.. I've definitely experienced better. But I rounded to a 3 star, since this location isn't known for their chicken pho and I don't feel like a lower rating is fair as this is the only dish I tried.

$6.75 including tax, so your standard pho price. The broth is light, but not very flavorful at all. The chicken is not bone-in, as the menu states it is " shredded chicken". Some of the chicken was very tender -- some of the pieces were undercooked unfortunately and that's a big NO-NO for chicken.

Would not return for chicken pho. I've heard great things about their beef pho though

One of my favorite places in Philadelphia Chinatown!! It's cheap, fast and delicious. The XL Pho Combo is a great deal($9) and it lasts me at least 2 meals The soup is flavorful and they give plenty of toppings. When I have ordered Pho to go at other restaurants, a layer of oil usually precipitates out at the drop. Whenever I get it from Xe Lua, I have never had this problem. The service is fast and the waiters are attentive. They also have the AC blasting in the summer, which is perfect while eating a bowl of Pho.

I kid you not--I have been here so many times whenever I'm in town, this is my automatic go-to place. So yummy and so fresh! But the kicker is that their food actually has FLAVOR! They win the best healthy food in Tucson in my opinion.

In my opinion this is the best gay bar in Philadelphia. Woody's, around the corner on 13th Street, is more popular but also more crowded, which makes it hard to get a drink or find seating. Icandy is larger (three floors) so even on a busy Friday or Saturday night it's possible to find a place to chill.
Prices are reasonable in a fun festive atmosphere, although parts always seem to be closed for renovation. Lately a lot of straight girls have been crowding out the gays, celebrating bridal showers among the shirtless bartenders. Good for them, I guess. All are welcome. Generally it's a young hip crowd. Keep up the good work!

Best pho in the city. I know, bold claim, and tbh for food quality and price Pho 75 across town is roughly equivalent. This place wins hands down for convenience. Pho 75 regularly closes at 8 p.m., is cash only, and is reallllly out of the way. Xe Lua is right in Chinatown, takes Square, and has infinitely more workable hours. Best I've found, and my girlfriend keeps taking me to places.

I ordered delivery thru Caviar bc of the great reviews but it was terrible. The fried chicken was so heavily breaded. It was all bread and little chicken. We ordered $120 worth of food and all of it was gross.

I've been here three times so far and I'm sure I'll be back. The food is affordable, authentic, and good. My favorites so far are the special combo vermicelli and papaya salad. I'm actually not a big fan of the pho itself - the broth seemed really lacking in flavor - but it is amazing value and tastes good once you add some extra seasoning. Friendly, fast service, definitely recommended.
Great Vietnamese food. Whenever my fiance and I go to Chinatown we always stop at this restaurant to eat. It is usually always packed. Staff is very friendly.

Disappointed with this location. My husband and I ate here on a busy Friday night around 8pm; there was a 45 minute wait for 2 people. We decided to dine at the bar- which was empty aside from a few people taking advantage of the half-off wine special. With 2 bartenders, one would figure that they would remember to give us silverware with the salad and put in our appetizer (calamari). Our food arrived and was tasty, however we were never checked on during our meal.
My favorite family restaurant to eat at! Pretty delicious food wise but place gets packed fast! They have one of the best snails made here! Definitely try it out!

My daughter wanted to try this place out because of the acai bowl. We ended up sharing a Mango Jungle bowl and The Commuter juice.  Both were very good and we felt we were eating something healthy too.  Plus she showed her UA student ID and we got a discount.  We'll definitely go back here again for breakfast, maybe even for lunch.  The only downside was the terribly apathetic waitress who really gave off the vibe that she couldn't be bothered with us.
Had the granola and fruit with Almond Milk, my wife had the breakfast bowl which they modified to be vegan. Both dishes were fantastic, the atmosphere felt healthy. Great place!
Good food for a basic menu. Lots. Could have shared mine with someone. Service adequate and fast. Clean. I'd come back. Easy to find. It's the first restaurant on Race in Chinatown.

This is my regular pho place! I call it choo choo's for short (the neon sign train in their window). I love their pho and how affordable it is. Everything here is super cheap, and they don't sacrifice too much on the quality. Pho, thai green curry, pork chop over rice, pork chop vermicelli, raw beef appetizer (with peanuts, crunchy onions, lime, basil), summer rolls with peanut sauce are my faves. :) Highly recommend. 

Although I'm a huge fan of the price and the food, the service makes me a little uncomfortable. They are extremely fast and they do comply with all my requests - more limes please, meat on the side, etc. etc., but they are definitely not trying to make nice with all the customers.

I cant believe I've never been here until today! Their entire menu looked delicious - but because we came around 3pm, we went for sandwiches and fresh tea.

The girl who took our order was very friendly, smiling the entire time - and answered all of my questions. 

I ordered the veggie sandwich which had kale, hummus, roasted red pepper, balsamic and squash -and it was the bomb. Tons of flavor - and fresh bread made it perfect! 

My wife ordered the torta, which had chicken breast, cilantro, avocado and black bean spread on fresh bread. She said it was the best "healthy" sandwich she's ever had. 

I had black tea, my wife tropical green tea - both were very good - not too sweet. 

Overall - we are excited to go back and try some more menu items.

Thanks guys, see ya soon!

Fantastic burger. nice enough staff. They were slammed, yet still took care of you well, and a few were downright fun.  

Beer selection is amazing. Want to make it a life goal to get through it!
This is our go to place for pho now. Everything we've had there so far has been excellent

Our favorite place for Vietnamese food in Philly and one of the best we have ever had. Of the pho options, we generally go for the house special beef pho, and it never disappoints. We regularly get takeout from here, and our staple choices include shrimp summer roll, pork chop and chicken over rice, and special combo vermicelli. Wonderful taste and generous portions across the board. Don't save the vermicelli for the next day though, as the noodles stick together. Of the chef special dishes, the salted pepper three treasures is probably the best salted pepper dish we have had ever.
I was visiting today 6/30/18 from Maryland and decided to stop here for dinner. I had the chicken and waffle and it was off the hook

The food here is awesome 
My family like to come here lot  
Great food Vietnamese and Thai foods.

Having tried their pho multiple times, I decided to listen to some of these reviews and try their Spicy Tom Yum seafood soup with rice noodles(#126). I'm glad I ventured out because I DON'T regret getting it. If you've ever had those sour veggies that accompany hand drawn noodles, the taste resembles it. Don't let that scare you away because the flavors come together to create a tangy but savory broth which surprisingly wasn't very spicy. If you want to come for something other than Pho, I definitely recommend trying it.

I agree with most of the reviews, New China Court is a pretty typical American Chinese place. The food is good and the service quick. It's another Chinese food place.  If your in the area it's not a bad lunch stop.

I was duped. The bartender (who was very nice but still duped us) said he made a 'mean old fashioned'. When we ordered one at his recommendation - full price since happy hour doesn't start until 6pm and we arrived at 5:45 - it was pretty good. However when we got the bill it was a $17 dollar drink. The bourbon was $8 on its own and the old fashioned (which is technically just sugar and cherries) cost $9 on its own. When we brought it up to the bartender he adamantly agreed that something was wrong, only to double check and be told the price was accurate. He apologized but didn't do anything about it, leaving us in an awkward situation. 

Long story short - don't listen to recommendations from the bartenders there because it'll cost an arm and a leg. Be wary of the happy hour hours.  If you're looking to pay $20 per drink for an underwhelming experience this is your place.

I'm not much of a club person -- as a matter of fact, my venture to 12th Air was my one and only time at a club in my life. And for a club, it was basically what I expected. 

The dance floor upstairs is pretty much the bulk of this place. The bar area is SO SMALL, it's nearly impossible to get up there and get a drink or a bottle of water [neither of which is cheap]. I spent the majority of the night on the floor with my friend, dishing on cute guys and dancing until we couldn't breathe anymore. The DJ plays a pretty good selection of your obvious gay club music [Britney, Madonna, whatever is on the Top 40 list right now and remixed]. People are not afraid to makeout or show off the goods here, so it's not a place for the demure [although what gay club is?]. 

Overall an interesting experience, but I think if I ever venture back to a club, I'd like one with a little more breathing room.
The food was amazing - the service outstanding - I will definitely be going back for more! Best steak I've ever had, no exaggeration!!

This place is good for a healthy snack, and really lends itself to meet-ups with friends. I've only tried their juices/smoothies, but they also offer salads & protein bowls. They have many choices, and you can customize your own drink or go with one of their options. It smells good, they play good music - the only pitfall is the price. It's quite expensive... but if you're going to splurge on fresh juice, you should do it here!

My wife and I went to this restaurant last night for my birthday and what a FANTASTIC choice. It is located on Stone just north of Speedway so it was very easy to get to from our home in the northwest, much easier than going downtown. The concept was fun and the food was ABSOLUTELY AMAZING and reasonably priced!  Our server "Jerry" who is a level 1 sommelier and suggested the PERFECT wine to go with our meals. They give you a lot of food so we took some back home for our 12 year old to try and he said that the spaghetti and meatballs was the best he'd ever had. So now that we know this a place where we can take the family. We now have a new go to place in Tucson.
This is the best frozen yogurt place in Tucson! The staff is so nice and the yogurt awesome. Definitely recommend it

I've visited Goodness multiple times, and each time I was hoping it would be better, I was disappointed.  Consistently a hit or a miss, but more often than not an overpriced miss.  Yes they do have some good things I would recommend like their Tacos and the Tofu Noodle bowl, but other than those, their smoothies are bland and their other items just aren't up to par.  

I got the "Morning Bowl" that lists it has Kale in it, yet there was only wilted lettuce in it and barely any of the turkey sausage it claims to have.  My friend got the Azteca Steak bowl and there was such a disproportionate amount of rice and a tiny amount of steak we thought that maybe they were running out of steak and just didn't feel like making more for her meal.

I desperately wanted to like Goodness as it does look like a cute place, but the food is mediocre, the staff aren't friendly, and the wait is long.

Delicious breakfast burrito (I had the quinoa on the side and it was yummy too) and breakfast sandwich.  Great service and atmosphere.  The commuter juice was very good.  We are looking forward to going back for lunch!

This is my first yelp review. I normally don't leave comments but today's experience was really good:)
I ordered 130, noodle soup with pork feet, 620, vegetable dish and the best one 419 pork belly. Definitely too much for my appetite but I saw the pork belly picture in one review and could not resist but ordering and try.

Everything came really fast, probably due to I was there quite late, close to their closing time. I feel bad to stay long so I decided to take the pork belly to go while having the noodle soup and vegetable in the restaurant. 

Everything was really tasty and satisfying, and not too oily to my standard. The pork feet can be a bit softer but that's just my preference. Noodle was soft but not soggy and soup was flavorful. 

I am a big fan of fatty meat like pork belly and normally quite picky. The one I ordered from the restaurant was exactly what I want, the right amount of sweetness, saltiness, and the meat was soft but not losing its texture. It reminds me of my mom's home cooking and I was really surprised to feel that way. 

Will definitely come back if I come to philly again

Fast service, great food, friendly staff - what more could one ask for?

We ordered the Pho Dac Biet, and Summer Rolls. They were both delicious. 

The summer rolls were so freshly made that the rice paper was still wet! They were served with a side of peanut sauce for dipping. I have to say, this was one of the best dishes of summer rolls I have ever had the pleasure of eating. 

The pho came out and smelled and tasted fantastic. The broth was nice, hot, and just a little spicy - a nice kick. The beef and noodles were both extremely plentiful. I can't find a single bad thing to say about the pho.

I would definitely come back for more. This is absolutely a great place for a first date.

It's been a few years since i order from here.  I ordered the fried chicken wings, one shrimp roll and one house special soup.  The Chicken and shrimp roll over cooked.  As for the soup, i'm not sure if i want to eat it.

Philly became a super noodle city to me... After finding awesome Lanzhou beef noodle in Philly, I just found the best pho I have ever had - in my opinion, the broth beats the ones at that landmark hole in the wall Vietnamese place in New York Chinatown.

This place is awesome! I ordered the summer rolls and pho with beef and brisket. First off the service was super fast. The summer rolls were delicious with the peanut sauce! I highly recommend. Lastly, the pho was great. The broth had much flavor to it, which I find to be critical to a good pho. I will definitely be coming back!

Such an amazing bowl of pho! The portion size was great for the price too. I got the pho chicken and it had great flavor and a ton of chicken. I tried everything else my friends got and there wasn't one thing I didn't like! I'll definitely be returning on my next visit to Philly.
Great food, very healthy and always fresh:).  Staff is friendly and outdoor seating option is a nice touch.  Definitely recommend visiting.

I'll admit I haven't actually had juice here. I'm not sure juice bar is the most accurate moniker, but then again I don't make a habit of surveying such establishments. Next life.

I was very pleased with how fresh each component of the food was in the bowls and noodles - the sweet potato, beets, quinoa, carrot, broccoli... The greens didn't need the dressing that came with but it was tasty when I did some dipping. Maybe you like it extra saucy. You do you. The teriyaki beef with broccoli sauce wasn't as awesome, but the component ingredients of the bowl were great.

Service was nice, but it's strictly counter and it does look like there's some issues in communicating to the outside when orders are ready.

The iced tea was worth a mention, too. So here I am. Mentioning it.

Have been here twice, first visit with a friend who is vegetarian. I only returned because I was looking for a place that was close by and wanted a simple, fresh meal.

On my first visit it was a hot day and there was no indoor seating so we ate at one of the picnic tables outside.  Fortunately, they were shaded.  Not a bad spot.  Plusses:  the waiter brought our food out; my friend's "big melons" fresh juice was good; she said her salad (kale etc.) was also good.  Minuses: the menu is brief, the food comes in to-go containers even if you are eating in, my grilled cheese sandwich had two (or maybe three?) types of cheese, none of which was melted.  The sandwich was a disaster, in fact.  Dry bread, pungent tasting, and overpriced (no side came with it). Another minus is the parking, which is somewhat challenging both in front and back. 

But my second visit was really bad.  We got there around 4 in the afternoon on a rainy day.  My husband ordered the breakfast burrito and I chose the chicken and brie (hot) in a wrap.  His was just OK, although he said it wasn't filling.  For those two items, plus a green tea, it was $20.  My chicken wrap was gooey but didn't taste like it had brie in it.  Again, no sides.  I did not get my drink until after I got my wrap, and the cashier was supposed to have done it when I ordered (she didn't bother apologizing when I said I was still waiting for a green tea).  Oh, and the wrap was barely warm and certainly not hot.  Just like before, the food came in to-go boxes.  The seating was extremely limited, and outside was not an option due to weather. One of the seats had a busser's tub sitting on the table collecting water that was leaking through the roof.  On both occasions the cashiers have been indifferent and/or rude.  To tops things off, there is the usual really loud music (indoors) blasting while you are trying to talk.

Would only come back with a die-hard vegetarian or gluten-free friend who was craving wheat grass, limited seating, and small portions.

My friends and I ate here a few weekends ago because we were craving pho.  We only had to wait about ten minutes before being seated upstairs.  The service was quick, the Thai iced tea was good, and the food was delicious.  I would definitely eat here again.

I am really distraught at having to award this place three stars.

This is the kind of place I should be gushing about.  GUSHING.  It is cheap, it has an endless menu with tons of variety, it is a hole in the wall that reeks of authenticity.  This is my kind of place, in short .

Maybe it's because Choo Choo is mad hyped ... but ...

all right, so C and I ordered vegetable spring rolls to split.  I am pretty sure we were given egg rolls.  No bigs!  I am not a fan of egg rolls, so C got an extra out of the deal.  I then ordered the BBQ pork with grilled pork balls over vermicelli, remembering a review that gushed about Choo Choo's BBQ anything.

The pork was tasty; the pork balls were stellar.  But ...

I don't know!  The ratio of vermicelli to lettuce to pork was stacked heavily with vermicelli and lettuce.  The vinegar-chili sauce had no punch.  It felt like I was eating a really big bowl of mediocre salad.

For an entree that was hugely filling and pretty okay (and 5.50$!), I will be back.  Maybe I just ordered the wrong thing -- for me -- and will be giving this place an update with five stars.

I really hope so.

The bread and the chicken gnocchi soup is the best here. They also have a nice outdoor dog friendly patio which is nice when the weather is nice. That is about it! 

I ordered a chicken parmigiana which was just ok! The chicken marsala we ordered did not have a lot of marsala sauce which is the best part. It did come with heaps of roasted potatoes mixed with sweet potatoes. That was better than the chicken parmigiana with spaghetti. 

It will probably be a long while until I come back here! No biggie, and it is pricy for the quality!

So disappointed.  The bison burger was mediocre.  The Chicken BLT was terrible - chicken was cold, had been grilled at some point but was dry.  The entire sandwich was dry and there was a  tiny sliver of avocado.  The bacon was half done.  The Turkey club was totally dry, no mayo or any other spread, turkey itself was dry and tasteless.  The server seemed much more interested in a table that knew the chef or owner.
I have been coming to la Giraldilla for quite sometime. Great Latin American food. Tampa needs more of these places! Full liquor bar which makes a night out wonderful..

This place is my favorite place to eat at! I love their food so much and not only is the food really tasty but it's healthy. I like that they have many options for people who are vegan, vegetarian and gluten free. I love the grilled cheese even though it's kind of simple it's so good because of this spicyish (not really spicy at all) sauce they put inside and the dipping sauce it comes with is so good! Also I love the hot tropic smoothie it's a definite must have here! Only problem I've had here is that a few days ago they kind of messed up my smoothie and it was all banana oats and dates but none of the other ingredients. But hey I mean it was the first bad smoothie I've had there out of the 50 I've probably had. Anyway I love all the food here and I hope in the future they come up with more recipes.

This place is a hole in the wall with the best pho! Great size bowl for the price. Very flavorful and delicious! I don't come to Philly often, but when I do, I refuse to miss a trip to Pho Xe Lua! Perfect for a cold winter day!

Really cheap and delicious! $6.95 for a large bowl and $8.95 for a XL bowl. After tax, the large bowl is only $7.51. They are really good at bringing out your food fast. Service is okay; they'll refill your water when it gets low and take away plates as you finish them!

Good place to get a warm bowl of pho on a cold day!
Gluten Free Chicken Tacos will make you slap your Granny!  Great Juice Bar, Great Service!

We had a Holiday work party for about 20 people last night.  This place killed it.  Food, drinks and service were all on point.
My Wife and I had the shared tyhe Ribeye and Spaghetti plate.  FANTASTIC!  I am truly a fan and cannot wait to go back.

Note:  The bar in this place was built in the 70s/80s.  It is totally unique and bad ass.

The pho alone is definitely five star worthy. But the rest of the menu is mediocre, nothing you couldn't find elsewhere (and of better quality) but the pho is rely one of the best in the city. And it's super cheap!

Our first time at Sandler's and we were ten people deep!! That's was fine at Sandler's because they treated us so well. Great job Nicole!! Food was spectacular! The chicken And waffles was amazing and seasoned. I don't eat pork so they made it without the bacon in it and it still was amazing! My husband loved his cocktail as well. Oh the star of the show was the bbq chicken nachos. Sweet Jesus that was by far the best loaded nachos I've had so far.. A must do!!

Used the online ordering option to pick up dinner here and there seems to be a disconnect between what is on the website and what is actually available on the in-store menu.

Upon walking in to the restaurant, some wonderful options that allowed for two different entrees at one low price (Sort of like a Panera Pick Two) were staring me right in the face...yet I had no knowledge of them when ordering online.

This is too bad, because it would have been perfect for my needs that night considering who I needed to feed.

Then, making idle conversation while waiting for my order, I asked about one particular item that was available online and was told it was no longer on the menu. Good thing I didn't order that!

There's also an option online for things like utensils and napkins, and I actually was in need of bowls and plates that night so I clicked those boxes.

However, when I arrived at my destination with the food, there were no bowls or plates included.

The food was what we expect from The OG, although having a sufficient amount of salad dressing would be nice for take-out orders, as it tasted fresh and was detinitely served hot. 

Perhaps this is why I only visit Olive Garden about once every six months and almost exclusively out of convenience.

Food was good, service was absolutely awful. Our server told us we could split the unlimited pasta bowl, which his manager later told us wasn't allowed and couldn't split the cost between two checks. Also, our meals were supposed to come with salads which we weren't told or given, we wouldn't have even known except for it being on our bill. And the cherry on top of this shite show was ordering coffees when asked for our drink orders and not getting them until our bills came. Will never go back and don't recommend to anyone.

Super tasty food! Loved the western atmosphere! Service was a little slow but the wait staff was very nice about it. We had the pork saltimbocca and the steak burger and it was definitely worthy of going back for again!

Amazing pho had the mid rare beef and brisket I'm an upcoming chef in the city and have recently Learned what pho is and how to properly make it and this is great a lil of the sauces jus to take it up a notch but not only amazing food the service was great too it's a small close environment but I love that charm about China town

This one is a solid 3.5 stars. I love love love the fact that this new spot serves brunch all day, a rare find in the area! I've eaten here 3 times in the last 2 weeks (once for takeout) because I became in love with Sandlers. As a self declared eggs Benedict fanatic, I must state that this place has one of the best crab benny's in the area, yet only 3.5 stars overall and here's why:
Dine in service-on both visits our servers were fabulous! Super friendly and very knowledgeable of the menu. During a busy lunch, however, service can be very slow so don't expect to be in and out in an hour or 1.5 hours. 

Take out service-training is needed. While friendly, the person at the register decided to debate with me regarding the fact that the cheddar burger comes with bacon. She tried to charge me an additional $3.00 for bacon that is already included in the price. The manager eventually came and corrected her lack of understanding of the menu items. 

Food- On my first visit I had the crab benny...Ohhlala delish! Everything about the dish was amazing! Second visit, had the cheddar burger to go, another outstanding meal (especially for the price) Thought of ordering the creme brulee for dessert but it is severly overpriced for the portion size. Third visit, OMG what happend?? Both of my co workers had Benedict's and they both received what appeared to be hard boiled eggs! It took so long to get our food that there was no point in trying to send the dishes back. There plates also appeared to be quite skimpy. Another co worker had the salted caramel French toast and said it was only OK, and was lacking in flavor. The saving grace was my order of chicken and bacon waffles, now it was delicious! 

What happened after we made the server aware of the boiled eggs- The co worker who clearly disliked boiled eggs asked to have her left over food packed to take home and was told she would receive a credit on her bill. Unfortunately, only part of her remaining food was actually packaged to go, and two poached eggs were added to her container. It's not very easy to reheat poached eggs so she already told the waiter she did not want them. She would have liked to have kept her potatoes however, which were apparently discarded. To make things worse, they only gave her $4.00 off her check for a $14 meal that she clearly did not enjoy. They did bring ice cream cones for the table, but it would have been better to have comped her meal or at least given half off. We were all given 20% off which was very nice, however those that disliked their food were very disappointed.  

With a few changes, this place could easily be 5 stars (after all they are new). I'll try Sandlers again, but be mindful of going during the busy lunch period.
That was the best breakfast that I've had in a long time. There was so much that I saved half for lunch.

If you like to eat healthy then this is your place. Really good salads with a lot of ingredients. The smoothies are also awesome. Finally there is a spot if you want healthy food fast. You won't be disappointed.

HIDDEN GEM! Been coming to Sandler's for 6 months now. Excellent food and service. Family owned establishment - owners Paul and his daughter Ally are super friendly and great hosts. Bartenders Gina and/or Mike are there every time I come in and couldn't be nicer. Both of them have great personalities and keep the bar fun. Great place to watch a game and have a good American meal. Keep it up Sandler's!!

This place is pretty awesome. I'm a fan of their pitaya bowl and the mango jungle. We also ordered the half order each of  The Cure and The Clean it Up fresh juices. The Pitaya Bowl and the Mango Jungle bowl, in case anyone else is new to ordering things like that, are basically a smoothie with some fresh and dried fruit/nuts on top reminiscent of a parfait. (Only icey cold)  We came in on this rainy frigid day, straying from our usual greasy spoon Saturday breakfast in favor of a more healthful option. I was pleased to see vegan options clearly marked as such and most other dishes appeared to be vegan friendly with tweaks. 

My one complaint? I'd love to see a warm (Cold day and smoothie/frozen breakfast make for an even colder nose on this lady) breakfast options. I'll definitely be back for lunch one day and check out their salad to wrap transformer options or a bowl/ burrito option.
My first time and I had breakfast. The wait staff was friendly and attentive. The food was excellent and plenty. The Decor was inviting and very clean. loved the coffee !!

Went here after a day in the city with my boyfriend. We both ordered pho of course and absolutely loved it. The food came out very quickly and hot. The bean sprouts and other assorted pho additives were very fresh, which isn't always the case in restaurants.

This will be a quick review. As it's getting cold in Philly. It was appropriate and perfect for Pho.  It's pretty good and they were not skimpy with he meats. At least compared to what I'm accustomed to seeing in Vietnamese restaurants in my home town.  The service was typical, but they did pack our leftovers well. As I had a lot of pho leftover, we asked that they separate the soup, and they tried to drain as much of of it to another container. Overall good experience. If I lived close to this place, I'd be a regular here.

A great place for lunch! I have tried the Teriyaki Veggie Bowl with Tofu and Asian Noodle Salad with Tofu. Both dishes are great! The vegetables in the veggie bowl are outstanding! I love the crispiness of the broccoli. There are many vegetarian and vegan options here! The service is fast as well. Parking is the only problem I see here.  I am going to have to come here more often in order to try everything!

One of the worse "LGBTQ" place of entertainment that I have ever gone to. They do not even try to hide their Prejudices towards anyone of color. Being a African American Lesbian made it even worse. Never acknowledge my or my friends presence when we approached the bar. GLAD ITS CLOSED.

3 start is for regular drip coffee and apple cobbler. Was very exited to try their brunch, I ordered eggs Benedict with salmon. We got a misunderstanding with server,as she sought I ordered regular with meat. It took about 30 minutes to prepare it,which normally should take no more than 20 if it's busy. Wait time wasn't biggest concern,but still. Hollandaise sauce was so sour that it tastes like it was prepared 4 days ago if not more. Potatoes which comes with it on a side also wasn't great,kinda sour as well for some reason.  
Hope you will work on taste and freshness of ingredients to your dishes. Ss I understand,you are new place, so good luck in future
Wow, loved everything we ordered, but particularly the papaya and beef jerky salad! That was the best I've had, so fresh and vibrant! The soups were great, too, can't wait to be back!

We came back for a visit for old-times sake, and were ushered upstairs as the first floor was very busy. With a child and two others, it was good we were separate from most - we had a lot to handle keeping the little one happy. Service was sporadic as we were one of three groups upstairs initially... but it got better once more people were seated upstairs.

Still.. the serving bowl looked the same, but the noodle amount seemed less... and the broth was very clear compared to the past. A healthy dose of basil, pepper, and bean sprouts was good, but I guess after having pho in other cities now, I still find myself unsatisfied with the flavor here today. 

Might be too much MSG in it? Left feeling super-thirsty...

I've had takeout from here MANY times. It is good greasy American Chinese food. It is also very inexpensive, and they get the order perfectly correct every time, even when they are busy as hell.

I prefer this over Mario's across the parking lot for a quick bite anytime. 

There are slighty better chinese takeout spots nearby in Chestnut Hill, but this is by far the least expensive and fastest.

Firstly, can I say that this is economic development at its best? What a wonderful, vibrant addition to the 48th and Spruce neighbourhood. Marcus, our server, told us that he had known the owner since he was little and that this was his dream, finally realized. Nothing like a successful new small business to give me hope and optimism for the world. Kudos to these guys.

[ food ]
A friend and I split the chili glazed salmon platter, with collard greens and sweet mashed potatoes. The chef accidentally gave us normal mashed potatoes (which were delicious anyway, highly recommended) so we got a side of sweet mashed potatoes for free when Marcus realized the error, and those were great as well.

The salmon filet was perfectly cooked - just the right combination of tender and crispy, and the chili glaze was perfectly balanced. No complaints about the food at all, and we will certainly be ordering delivery if we can't make the hike out to 48th from Penn campus.

Prices are reasonable and serving sizes are huge - great value for money too!

[ decor ]
Clean, home-like, diner-style. A couple of bars and a TV, and also nice family-sized tables. Comfy, friendly, non-imposing vibe - almost reminded me of a kindergarten classroom, but in a good way. :) Oh and the fans look like palm leaves! Cute touch.

[ service ]
Marcus is so invested in his job - he worked straight through his break to make sure everyone was happy and when we asked him why, he said it was because he had known the owner since he was a child and he was so happy to see his dreams realized. I love stories like this. This is how strong businesses are born.

The chef personally came around to ask every single table how the meals were, and our plates were licked clean.

[  overall ]
Fantastic addition to West Philadelphia. Will certainly be returning. The epitome of a successful small business story! :D

Great place to grab lunch and breakfast all day. I haven't had dinner yet but that's in the near future. Fresh, hot and great portions. Hip vibe with great music to match. The interior has a very chic and comfortable feel. The bar has a very nice selection of liquors, wine and beer. Nicole, Jordy and Lisa offer top notch service and go above and beyond to insure you have a prolific experience.  That's pretty amazing. No, but seriously. This is one of my goto spots for a quick, fresh meal.  Try the wings, extra crispy. Barbecue Chicken Nachos are a slam dunk and the burgers are thick and juicy.

This establishment uses styrofoam cups which are bad for the environment. 

The frozen yogurt is good but they were greedy with the toppings. I literally only received maybe 5 miniature gummy bears.

Hands down the best cupcake / cake batter I've ever tasted, and that is coming from a froyo expert that lives in Los Angeles visiting! Great service as well, the ladies on Monday night were very friendly and helpful and answered lots of questions!

Great food horrible service let me tell you this the wait staff is rude to customers and each other. Why do I say they have horrible service you ask? Well, I came there with my family ok so first appetizers cam out very thing is fine. The. My sisters food came out. Not till 10 minutes later until my dads food comes out and then another 10 minutes past my moms food come out. Not till 15 minutes later till my food came out. Really? I'm eating with my family I expect the food to come out at the same time not each food come out one by one. And there was also this incident with another table close by where the bust boy was getting finishe bowls of soup from a table. Then a waiter walked by, bumped in to him and he spilled the food all over the hot soup all over the customer. He didn't even manage to say sorry but stood there and cursed at his co-worker which caused a little altercation. Who needs about 10 employees to run a restaurant with about 15 tables with customers? It does not make sense to me. My mom was nice enough to tip them $10, honestly I don't think they deserve anything. Don't go to this restaraunt, I don't care that their food is good go to Jade Harbor or something around there.

This was our first visit to Spaghetti Western. We ordered a couple of ribeye and spaghettis and a prime rib. 2 had clam chowder and 1 salad. The salad was fresh and crisp. The chowder was loaded with plenty of clams and bacon.

It's always fun to taste test everyone's choice at a new place. We agreed that the 2 cuts of beef were done as ordered. I thought mine was a bit over seasoned. The others thought theirs were seasoned ok. We ordered their "house-made" onion rings, they were tasty but had a bit too much better. Garlic balsamic green beans that came with the prime rib were  crunchy but cold. The spaghetti and meatballs were good and the sauce was acceptable. We enjoyed our meal and will probably return to see how this place matures. 

Interesting that they have picked this theme. In a past life as Damiano's a lot of famous people frequented this property while filming at Old Tucson. I used to see Michael Landon there often in the 1970's.

My salad is fresh in a big bowl. The dressing isn't overwhelming and add freshness to it. The salmon is perfectly cooked but small.

The pancakes are light and delicious comes in 3 with home fries. The syrup is pretty sweet so add it moderately if you aren't into sweets. The fries is greasy and mostly burnt.
 My friend's omelette is a little bit too greasy according to her.

I would recommend for sweet breakfast than the savory. They have Elvis pancake with chocolate crunch, Nutella, and tempura battered banana. Sounds yummy.

This is a great small restaurant in the heart of Chinatown in Philadelphia. Easy to miss, and you might not even notice it walking by. 

This place is very cheap and affordable. They have a pretty wide variety of food you can choose from their menu.

I always go for their vegetable noodle soup. The vegetable is fresh, it comes in huge amounts, and it is healthy, quick, and I always feel full after. I've also had their summer rolls and would say they make one of my favorite tofu summer rolls. I've also tried their green curry, definitely had better, they just don't have as much other fancy veges/ complimentary food that goes along with the dish. 

I see a lot of their customers order their sizzling dishes. They also have the fish tank with fresh fish, shrimp and lobster for consumers to pick some fresh seafood to be prepared and eaten at the restaurant. Don't be freaked out by it, that's just the Asian way of eating fresh seafood. I'm not sure if I have ever seen anyone actually order from there though.

Food is always quick, and the menu is sooooo cheap. Great place to pop in for a quick lunch if you like Asian food.

I just found this place and I love, love, love it. My fave is the cacao bowl, subbing granola for almonds to make it gluten free! It is delish with a little circle of raspberries and blackberries. So pretty! My son had the Pink Dragon twice! He is usually very leery of "healthy" food. I also had the Green Bully smoothie which is a green cleanser!

Stopped in for Sunday brunch. I had the chicken and waffles and the GF had the crab Benedict. Both were fantastic. Coffee was good as well as the classic Bloody Mary. Attentive, friendly, and quick service. Highly recommended!

Came in as they were getting close to closing. Got myself a hulk smoothie without agave. It was still perfectly sweet and very delicious. If I had had more time I would've ordered some food from here. It looks like they have some great options. Inside the ambience is very inviting
I order a cookies and creams milkshake and she didn't put cookies in the milkshake. And when I told her and she got mad at me

I love pho and I love trying new places! My friends raves about this place so I couldn't wait to get my pho on! The place is kind of hard to find so make sure you read the sign correctly. The place was pretty crowded but we got seated pretty quickly. I ordered the vegetable pho, my friends ordered the beef pho and shrimp fried rice. Our food came out pretty fast and omg the broth!!! It was so so rich and fresh. Also my friend fried rice was so freakin good. It's not your regular fried rice- I don't know how they make it but it tastes clean yet so flavorful. You add hot sauce to that rice and it's magical. If you go here- make sure you get one pho and one fried rice ( promise me).
I haven't been back to this place for a while.....but this place is still pretty good!  I would recommend this place to any pho lover!!! :)

We have been going to goodness many times over the past year and lately it has been each Saturday. I placed a Togo ord r for a full smoothie and a breakfast burrito with no tomatoes.... well this time when we got the breaskfast burrito they put tomatoes on it when I specifically said no tomatoes. I am very allergic to tomatoes and when I called to speak to a manager to discuss this I was given a vague answer and not allowed to speak to them. This is unacceptable.

I had a work lunch meeting here. 
Ordered a soup and salad combo so the salad portion was smaller. 
Their take on French onion soup - Onion Ale - was very good with a rich deep beef flavor but not overly sweet. For the second half of my l got their  Roasted Beet & Tuscan Kale salad. It was very nice with the tangy goat cheese balancing out the sweetness of the beets and candied walnuts. 
I will definitely keep them in mind when getting lunch in the future especially since they have a grab & go take out shop next door.
Stop supporting racist business!  The owner is on video making racist comments about patrons and the bouncers reinforce a racist dress code!  check out Tavern on Comac instead.

First time eating at this location and we liked it! If you're looking for a healthy place to eat, you've found it! 

We ordered their Quinoa Salad with avocado and chicken (both additions cost extra). The salad was absolutely amazing and refreshing! Exactly what I've been craving. Had choice greens, pickled onions, lots of quinoa, chicken, corn, avocados; dressing wasn't too overpowering. Would definitely order this salad again!

We also tried their Thai Peanut Bowl. Had carrots, chicken, broccoli, rice. It was great except it was way too salty! Made that bowl unenjoyable. If we order this again we will ask for no salt. 

Lastly, we ordered three drinks:
Hot Tropic: PERFECTLY REFRESHING! So much flavor! Was a mix of pineapple, mango, banana, chia seeds, honey, mint, dates and coconut milk. Absolutely delicious! 

The Hulk was also delicious! Had avocado, kale, broccoli, agave, banana, wheatgrass and almond milk.

Cold Brew was pretty good. Very strong, flavorful. 

Cashier was extremely friendly and patient. Will definitely come back.

This place is your typical, authentic Southeast Asian restaurant! I love it here. My  husband and I will walk 30 minutes to Chinatown just to have a bowl of their delicious Pho! It's the best price too! Seriously, so good it brings back good childhood moments. For me, it's like that moment when that crazy bitter critic in Ratatouille takes a bite of the best meal the rat has to offer and it triggers nostalgia? Yeah, that's what their pho does to me. Makes me cry for my momma. Ain't no shame in that.
Outstanding food.  Outstanding service.  Delicious and priced well.  Bloody Mary was fantastic.
After the show walked right in. No wait.... cocktails were over the top....service great food just okay!

Perfect. Yet 4 stars, only because I hold out hope for something comparable to west-coast-pho. That being as it may, so good. No non-sense service. I mean, you ask for 'veggie pho' and its what you get minus the snooty/ dumbfounded attitude. Also, they got booze, booze plus coursed options w/ suggestions. This is the sort of place that if I were single would bring a date AND get lucky. Not in the heart of China town, between it and the highway, so, you know, no where to run. Moreorless at the center of that whole 'north 8th - 12th' center city scene.

Date spot, great broth, booze, helpful service/menu!

While the sales people and installation staff were pleasant and helpful, their after installation service was absolutely awful. They sent someone who was young, winy, rude, confrontational and needless to say very unprofessional to our home when the system stopped working shortly after it was installed. Another major gas appliance also stopped working, both most likely due to a storm event, the company that serviced that appliance was very professional, helpful and considerate. This was the second appliance that Gas Masters installed for me and I found their customer service response one of the worst I have ever experienced when a problem happened after the install. My initial appliance never had a problem.

An amazing little hole in the wall restaurant that is one NOT to miss. Very quaint and quiet. Not too many tables but it's nice as the staff are attentive and prompt, food comes out fast and hot and delicious. The menu is massive with options galore. They serve alcohol as well which is a plus. I had the Chicken Pad Thai which was just amazing. It's not too heavy and not too saucy. The portion is large and big enough to share. Highly recommended. Friends got the Pho and that said it was one of the best they have ever had; definitely something I'll try next time. The staff is friendly and attentive. This will definitely be a regular spot for me now.

This most unassuming little place in Philly Chinatown is MY NUMBER 1 RESTAURANT IN ALL  USA!!! Now let me explain why. I am not a big fan of overly pretentious places and this  place is as unpretentious as it gets. But then it still has ambience - of the most natural  and relaxed kind. The clientele is very eclectic and the restaurant, being located smack dab  in the middle of Philly Chinatown is very accessible. But of course, none of these is the  main reason why I love it so much. It's the food, stupid!! And at a throwaway price too to  boot. My staple for several years have been number 215 - the Thai style shrimp green curry  on rice for $5.95 and number 409 - filet mignon in lemon grass sauce (Bo Luc Lac) for  
$12.95. Thai and Vietnamese food are my two most favorite types of cuisine and this place  combines both in a way that I have not found anywhere else in the US. The Pho is most  definitely the greatest I have tasted anywhere and if you're not sure of what to choose, is  a great beginner's dish here. They also have just the right sauces on the table, drinks  (alcoholic and otherwise, including those exotic Asian soft drinks) and prompt service. The  only reason I am not getting around to going there more often is the slightly iffy parking in  Philly Chinatown - but that's really a very minor quibble. Tip: Street parking there is free  after 8:00 PM.

This was such a treat to discover! Went for lunch and totally over-ordered. Nicole, our server was simply amazing and made us feel like long-lost friends. This is what other restaurants should want to replicate. The nachos were amazing and could totally be shared by a table of four. The bacon cheeseburger was perfectly cooked and juicy. The freshness of all the ingredients was apparent in the flavors. This is not like your big chain American food location, it's so much more. I strongly recommend making a point of visiting here, and ask for Nicole--you won't regret it! I wish we had a location in Miami!

I love cimarron,. I have been going for a decade . Everyone is sincerely kind to me. And my dogs. Very personable and caring. DR.B listens to what I am saying, and is warm and caring. We are not treated like just any customer.. I had to say goodbye to my Charlie, and everyone knew exactly what Charlie neede, as well what I needed to properly send him off. I was given all the time, and Kleenex needed, and it was all explained to me as my farewell was happening. They made me feel comfortable.
A special thanks to Claire., ...
Thank you for being here all these years.
I trust you and feel calm you are there.
Also, never a wait. Never.

Sandler's was nothing less than exceptional. The moment we walked in we felt at home. The bacon fried rice and chicken and waffles were nothing I've ever had and would recommend this spot to anyone looking for a great dining experience. Thank you Aly and staff for hosting us!

Great trendy restaurant. Reasonable pricing. The grilled cheese pop on a stick to dip into the tomato soup is delicious. Their burgers are very, very good here too. Can't go wrong with any choice. Lots of tables and full wall windows to look out into the streets. They let me put my bike inside behind the counter so it wouldn't get stolen, forgot my bike lock. It's kindness like that which makes it a 5star for me.

Delicious & cheap. I have been a regular customer for a decade... even though I live in Seattle now. I have even tried to replicate their yellow curry dish using TJ's yellow curry sauce, but I can't come close. I just have to wait til the next time I'm back in Philly.

p.s. I believe my friend came up with the nickname "choo choo" 10 years ago while we were in college (she discovered it)... Well, at least I like to think so. :)

Great food! Large menu so everyone is sure to find something they like. Service was a bit slow, but food was delicious and they give you large portions. Would definitely go back! Nice cozy spot for American food.
Since someone is claiming that the owner isn't racist you can google ICandy owner uses n word and see your yourself.
When we are in the city and looking for Pho and pork summer rolls, this is our place!

Went around 7:15 on a Saturday night. The place was dead but it seemed like forever before someone came to our table to take our drink order. By the time they came over we were ready to order everything. The server was not particularly knowledgeable about the menu. The drinks we ordered were yummy. The bacon app was very impressive to look at. My husband loved it. I got a burger that was definitely good. My husband got the bacon poutine. Less than impressive on that one. French fries with cheese sauce. No gravy. No cheese curds. The music kept abruptly stopping and switching to a different song. Lots of brittney spears, spice girls. Odd choices for a restaurant that's trying to be fancy The food was decent for the most part but I wouldn't go back considering the service and prices.

I eat here ever since I was 12. The pho tastes much better back then. The portion was larger back then as well. Now, their broth is bland, looks like their meat is getting lower quality ones too. However it is still my to go place when I'm in Chinatown for a quick lunch. Their service is very fast too which is a good thing.

I never had a problem here, always enjoyed it. However, recently it's been lacking in quality. Most nights are fun, I enjoy the outside part and the multiple floors. The staff is kind of rude, and also if you like partying with cockroaches, this is the place to be. I saw one crawl across the bar and walked right out. That is disgusting. The drinks are a little overpriced too.

I have enjoyed the smoothies that I tried. The tacos are good. The bowls are average.  I like the kids menu. The first time I came in, I had an attentive waitress. The next two times the service was seriously lacking and when I ordered food to go, the gentleman behind the counter seemed irritated. A couple  hipsters working there that are impressed with themselves.  I would come in for the food again but I really hope service improves. I am giving three stars bc I feel that service is a big part of eating out.

I just finished trying out both The Burger Bar in Chinatown Square and M2O burger in South Philly and didnt like either place. I have been anxiously waiting for Sandlers to open and since I just had two burger disappointments I decided to try their burger and here is the breakdown

Menu--I love how the menu has something for everyone from salads to burgers to breakfast items

Bun-- I am not a fan of the Martins potato roll bun which seems to be the new trend but Sandlers bun is perfectly nice and fluffy like a bun is supposed to be in order to contain a juicy burger 

Meat--the absolute best part because I asked for medium and it was cooked a perfect medium... The burger is so juicy there was literally a puddle of delicious burger juice on my plate which tells me the cook knows what he is doing

Toppings-- I was very happy getting the basic cheddar burger that has bacon on top

I shall return!!

I think I found my new go-to pho spot in Philly Chinatown!  I always tend to frequent Pho Cali when I'm in town because it was right around the corner from the Greyhound bus station.  But I've come to find that they're getting a bit expensive for the quantity and quality of their food.  This time around, I was determined to try out a new place.  Thumbs up, Pho Xe - a bit of a walk but totally worth it!  Ordered the banh cuon and pho for myself (clearly a fatty) but started to have second thoughts when the banh cuon (app) looked like a full meal!  Silly me, I should have known better.  But my momma taught me to never waste food and everything was fabulous.  The pho was delicious and plentiful.  I was also super glad my friend decided to join me because I needed to take a break from eating before I could finish the rest of my food.  She ended up ordering an app and a bowl of pho as well and we both ordered Coronas.  All in all, the bill only came to $30!  Gotta say that's a great deal!

Washlava pretty consistently has open washers and dryers,  so I'm not there all day waiting. The facilities are clean and stocked.  If you wanted to drop laundry off that's available also.  Overall the only complaint I've ever had is that sometimes- not all the time- the app had difficulty connecting with the washer or dryer. 
Good place,  generally quiet.  I like it.
Huge delicious portions! Great service.. Sabrina was awesome! We were stuffed! Nice atmosphere

Well doing the Race Street crawl as I spy-ed my phone as to the place with the most amount of stars this place was it. Really did not disappoint and the place was really not busy on a Friday afternoon.

Had the Spring Rolls which were cut in pieces and covered in chopped peanuts. Overall not bad could have used more lettuce and they only serve 3, at most other places they come in four pieces. 

The Pho was quite yummy very nice broth with a nice amount of meat, I had the big bowl. V V Good!

As a kicker my friend and I decided on the Iced Vietnamese Coffee it was quite good.
beautiful restaurant, decent food. large, appealing menu but strangely empty for a saturday brunch.
This was an amazing experience! The food was great and the service was impeccable. Lisa was extremely nice and thoughtful. Please support this restaurant.

Came here last night craving pho since our go-to was closed.  Like many of the places nearby in Chinatown, it's pretty much a hole in the wall, but if you can get beyond the dive-y feel, the pho is actually pretty good.

I got the beef special pho, which contains beef flank, tendon, and tripe.  I've never had tripe before, so eating it for the first time was an experience (it doesn't taste like anything, it just looks weird and knowing what it was as I was eating it didn't help either, but I still ate it). But overall, the pho here is pretty good: not too bland, not too spicy, and definitely filled with tons of ingredients.  I got a lot more beef in my bowl here than at other places.  Both of us got the XL bowl, which proved to be too much pho per person.  I also got an avocado milkshake, which was sweet, creamy, and delicious.

Overall, this is a great, cheap, and very filling dive-y spot with good Pho.  Next time I'll just stick to something with less organ meat.

One of favorite "go-to" bars in the North East. Very chill place, with great beers and food. Plus, for Frankford Ave, you get a nice, "non-douchebag" crowd, which is a real plus. They always have awesome and interesting beers on tap, plus your old stand-by's as well. Highly recommend

First trip to Philly.
Plenty to see. Plenty to taste.

I walked through many neighborhoods and considered many locations for dinner, but somehow my belly led me here...to the Pho. I thought the Pho was good, but FAR from the best I've ever had. Rating for the Pho would probably be 3.5 stars. The five stars are for the cheap liquor. Cheap, as in affordable. Not cheap, as in low quality. Asians don't drink "cheap" liquor. It's the law. Shots of Absolut were under four bucks and they pour high. I was just excited they had a bar with hard liquor. Authentic spots like this don't usually shell out for a liquor license.
Our favorite spot to grab pho on a cold winter night. The service is fast and the price can not be beat!

cheap tasty food- what's not to love! what it lacks for in ambiance and charm, it makes up for with yummy pho and super fast service. its usually packed but being seated fairly promptly is usually not an issue. the menu is extensive (and having only eaten a few things off the menu i can't speak for the hundreds of items here), but what i've had i love. the broth of the pho is very flavorful, the curry chicken with rice (a simple but hearty dish) always tastes right and we walk out of here completely satiated and satisfied, having spent only $20 for dinner and drinks. kind of divey inside, but excellent value and tasty food.

I am so happy we found this place! My family recently relocated to the area and have been on the hunt for great places to eat nearby. We found a winner! Such an awesome menu of options, great service, and the food was excellent! Will be back on the regular!

We ordered the calamari, prime rib and some drinks. Service was super friendly and the food was good. One complain was the calamari was a bit flavorless. Im not a fan of salt but I found myself drenching the calamari with loads of salt and pepper and the au jus and very oily and nothing juice about it. Other then that, we will try again in a few months when theyve gotten all the kinks out.

This place is ridiculously overpriced. I was charged $6 for a side of turkey bacon, which was two slices. The service was really bad and the food took a long time. The atmosphere isn't great, you're literally almost sitting on top of the people at the next table. I could barely get up from my table without knocking into the people next to us. Don't waste your money or time, so many better places in philly.
We asked for Vegetable Pho and received vegetables in hot water. The server was rude!
Love their fresh OJ. They're always fresh. My flavor dish is satay beef.   The brisket in pho is tender enough to melt in your tip of tongue but still has the mouth feel for bite. Well done.

I just had a very satisfying dinner here for under $10!

They offer two sizes of pho (large and extra-large). I went with the Pho with Beef and Tendon in the smaller size, and it was huge! There was plenty of soup, noodles and meat. In my bowl, I had over 10 slices of beef and several large chunks of tendon. 

I also got the Avocado Smoothie. O-M-G. SO GOOD. Super creamy, sweet and seriously amazing. At $3, it was an absolute steal. It reminded me of the avocado smoothies I used to get in boba shops in California (for no less than $5). 

Food came out within 5 minutes of ordering.

Met a friend here this morning.  Fabulous place.  Wish they still made the pizzas, would have loved to try one.  Breakfast sandwich was good and the drinks were amazing.  Starbuck's is right down the road and those who frequent it should try this place.  Only drawback, poor signage.  No one even knows it is here.  Read other reviews on other sites who agree with me.  Needs better signage and a name.  Will tell others about this place.

Giving this rating to Goodness pains me. I normally love coming here because of the fresh food and juices, but I recently ordered a to go meal and found a piece of rubber band in my food. I ordered he azteca steak bowl, so when I originally popped the rubber band piece in my mouth and started chewing, I just thought it was a rubbery piece of steak tendon or something of the sorts. After not being able to break it up, I spit it out and low and behold, I saw a bright blue-green piece of rubber band. I was so devastated that I found this in my food. Apart from that, the food was of course super tasty, but I was so put off, I couldn't even finish the food. I'm so disappointed, and I know this doesn't happen often, but it's enough that I probably won't go back for a while-until I get over the initial shock.
Love having the ability to reserve a washer/dryer. The notifications are extremely helpful. What a great experience.

Pretty standard restaurant in chinatown - portions are huge and the prices are cheap! Was craving pad thai so I opted to get that instead of pho, which is what everyone else in the restaurant seemed to be eating. It was fine but had a bit of a different flavor than other pad thai's i've had. Although this place is Vietnamese-Thai, it's definitely much more of a Vietnamese restaurant so if you're craving Thai pick a different place.

I have to start by saying I'm not related to Paul Sandler, the owner of this gem of a restaurant. I'm just one of the thousands looking for a terrific place to eat in Philly. There are countless trendy options in the City, but if you're looking for a place with a wide selection of American standards - this is it!  I found Sandler's last August when walking to my office. It had just open up on the corner of 9th and Chestnut. A few days later when the folks in my office were looking for a place to have lunch in celebration of a birthday, we decided to give Sandler's a try. We had no idea what to expect. What we found was a menu that had something for everyone, a knowledgeable waitstaff and great food.

This Saturday my husband and I celebrated our 49th anniversary and were looking for a place to have lunch with our children who live in Center City and know all the "in" places. I suggested Sandler's.

From the moment we walked in, we knew we made the right choice. The place was packed with holiday shoppers, but we were greeted immediately by Paul's daughter, who with another daughter, also runs the restaurant. To our lovely surprise we were seated in "her" special area which occupies an exquisite part of the Benjamin Franklin lobby. It felt like we were in a eating in a mansion. 

Sometimes when the setting is beautiful the food isn't. Not the case here! There is a Saturday Sunday brunch menu with lots of unique breakfast style sandwiches, eggs, pancakes, and salads. You can also order off of the regular menu. Our waitress suggested that no matter what we get, we try their special barbeque chicken nachos with a special house made cheddar cheese sauce. They were out of this world!  Everything else we got was done to perfection from the ahi tuna salad, to the burgers, omelete, and the blintz.   

But there is more. When we were walking to our table, my daughter told Paul's daughter it was our anniversary and the next thing we knew, champagne arrived! There we were sitting in an elegant room, with wonderful food, surrounded by our loving family in a restaurant owned by another loving family. 

Thinking this is the place to celebrate our 50th next year!

Probably new owners.  Watched a worker, with his bare hands, use a handheld to take a phone order, complete a counter  order, including making change; then, cook an order of of food with no hand wash/gloves. GROSS.  The place is off my list.

This is the place that I always try to get people to come to for pho in Chinatown.  The bowl is gigantic.  The amount of meat that they put in there will make your head spin and will satisfy your inner caveman.  The broth is clear and flavorful as all good pho should be.  Other food here are good too.  However it is unfortunate that my other favorite noodle soup dish, bun bo hue, is so mediocre here or this place would have warranted a five star.
The train is the bomb! Food is always fresh, quick, and fabulous. A place to go!!!

Amazing food. Loved everything! 

Service was a little rude. They should train their younger waiters to be nicer and patient.

Came here with high expectations and I have to say, they were met. My friends and I ordered the lobster poutine, crabby benny, chicken and waffles, and the classic eggs benedict. The lobster poutine was great and had chunks of lobster claw. The crabby benny had a hint of spice to it and came with a side of homies. The homies had pieces that were burnt and others that were undercooked, but overall was good. The chicken and waffles was hands down my favorite. I have nothing but good things to say about it. The chicken was crispy, the waffle had bits of bacon, and came with a side of maple syrup. The classic eggs benedict was simple, but delicious. The homies were also partially burnt and undercooked for some pieces. Nonetheless, I would like to come back to try foods from their all day menu!
When I lived in Philly, I went here often.  Cheap, quick, and I love the seafood soup.  Look for the choo choo train on the front door!

Been going to Philly  for years...never in my life heard of anything  of a rule that you cannot  go into the restroom with someone...my husband and I yes we are 2 males waited  in line for 10 minutes  to use the bathroom....  to save time for the others we went in together...well anyway  when we got out we was told we had to leave the premises! I said to the guy why? He said it's the rules....I said well we are married and if I want to go to the restroom with my husband I am he said you have to leave that's the rules....so we was with my uncle  and 4 other guys and we left and we never  will set foot in this place again....I understand  that they may do this for some reason  I was told it's because  of drugs....well your security system sucks!!

Hands down best pho in Philadelphia. Way better than Pho Saigon, Pho 75 and all the other overhyped places I've been to. The broth, meat, tendon, and noodles are all perfect and the portion is much bigger than other places for the same price. Unfortunately, I can't say the same for their other food which was decent but not amazing. We've had a grilled pork chop with rice, chicken curry, and a stir fried noodle dish but nothing stood out enough to be ordered again. BUT THE PHO! Every time we have gotten pho elsewhere since having it here we have been disappointed and swear not to cheat on Pho Xe Lua again.

This place had the Z Squad on today. And they probably always do. I met up with my wife here and asked the bartender if she has a tasty Pilsner on draft. She was somewhere in her 30s, glasses and long dark hair. And she replied "what you see is what I have." So then I found it on the draft list that's he decided to give me after sassing me. So I ordered it and had to help her find the beer. You should know everything you're selling in a restaurant. And if you don't know, you should say "not sure, but let me check." Don't make the guest feel like they're a burden on the staff. Then another staff member came behind the bar, took a two margarita order from two other bar guests and took like six minutes to make just one of them. The management needs to light a fire under these people's asses, man. They're jokers.

Welcome to this place near my office as additional options on this side of market/chestnut st.
Tried it for lunch and they were pretty busy.  The menu is interesting and lots of options.  I went for the steak nachos and the kobe hot dog.
I really liked the hot dog, the bun and the grilled onions.  The nachos could have used more steak, less cheese but still good

The raw beef (marinated in line juice and served with dry/fried onions, peanuts, basil and fish sauce) is one of my favorite dishes EVER. And I know spring rolls taste the same (if delicious) everywhere, but theirs are really something else. Pho is good/fine, I've had better, and same with the salty dry fried shrimp with head (well cooked, but a bit bland last time I had them). The grape leaves are excellent. Good, friendly no nonsense service, pretty cheap Chinatown prices.

Do not go to this office if you have a pacemaker. Mine went crazy while I was in the waiting room and rushed out before my appointment. They have a MRI machine in the office that my pacemaker reacted to. I would give it 0 stars.

Eh, not sure if tonight was an off night for them, considering all the raving reviews... But I came in here starving (so things should automatically taste 10x better) and came out with a very disappointing experience. 

I would stick with the beef noodle soup (Pho Tai) which features very tender and nicely cooked slices of beef, instead of the one with beef and brisket - which I chose today. The brisket is cooked to the point where it is dry and flavorless, and the broth is a bit on the thinner side as far as Philly pho joints go. The noodles were also over-cooked. 

I also tried the minced shrimp on sugarcane appetizer, but really regretted this choice after seeing that there was barely any shrimp wrapped around a really big sugar cane stick. Not only have I had it better elsewhere, but for some reason, this appetizer also took a really long time to arrive. 

The worst was the service, even by Chinatown standards. Most places in this neighborhood have awkward service, but it seems like most of the servers here don't even try. I had barely sat down and set down my purse when someone asked me (twice) if I was ready to order. Once I ordered, the food took a while to arrive, and the service was completely nonexistent after that. 

I may or may not return. They do, however, offer alcoholic beverages, and they do take some credit/debit cards.

Ordered the tuna poke tacos, lobster poutine, pappardelle and crabcakes sand. Here's the verdict. 

Tuna poke (4 pieces) - perfect way to start. Clean, refreshing and good amount of tuna.  Recommend

Lobster poutine -  too salty. Why call it poutine when it's just bits of lobster (not too many pieces) over cheese fries?  Call it cheese fries with minimum lobster.  Do not recommend. 

Crabcakes sand - not too impressed and was around average plain Jane.  Meh

Shrimp Pappardelle - was ok but nothing to cheer too much about. Better than average and my child ate most of it quietly which means it's good enough for me as the parent. Little above avg. 

Reminds me of a upscale but chain restaurant however; the service was good!

Had a wonderful evening and homemade meal...handcrafted cocktail...perfect ..we had the pork saltimbocca which was spot on...the spaghetti western ribeye cooked to perfection....  But the peach cobbler was mmmm... Loved this Restaurant..

I've eaten here many times and it is hands down the best Vietnamese food in Philly (at least among places I've tried, and I haven't tried them all). Their food is consistently so fresh and so full of flavor. Service is quick too. I brought one of my Chinese friends here and she loved it - she also agreed that it was so fresh and flavorful. The pho was perfect after walking more than a mile in bitterly cold and windy temperatures too. 

I've only beef pho, chicken pho, and the shrimp rolls here because they're the best I've had in the city, but everything I see others eating looks so good too! One of these days I'll venture out and try something else there. 

This isn't a place you go for ambiance. It's not a place to see and be seen, but if you just want some delicious Vietnamese food, go here. You won't be disappointed. At least, I hope you won't!

I wasn't particularly impressed with my experience here. I had high hopes, as it seems like a relatively well to do place and with the prices, I think the food would be pretty darn good. Don't get me wrong, it isn't bad. The tacos were interesting-sort of fried Chalupa type of appearance to the Shell and then some Ahi tuna inside. The choice of the mango salsa was an interesting one.

My steak was a little bit undercooked down to rare when I had asked for medium. I ended up asking them to cook it back again which they graciously did. It was decent but just didn't wow me for the price that I was paying. For your money, I think there are other establishments that Are a better option.

We came at 9 AM and at this rate we are going to leave at 11:30. There must have been 6 total tables and 2 staff members. Towards 10 AM there were no more than than 10 tables. The service was extremely slow. It took 20 minutes to get an espresso. My water bottle was never refilled even though my server said she would come back with water. There was something wrong about all the dishes we ordered. The fried rice was extremely salty. My brisket sandwich was 75% egg, 25% brisket. I asked for no peppers, but they excluded the onions, too. It tasted so dry. My partner ordered the big pauly which was supposed to come with tomatoes. I kid you not, there was a burnt half of a cherry tomato on his plate. Both our plates came with home fried type of potatoes and they tasted unseasoned. I bussed my own table as our table was so packed I couldn't eat comfortably. I will not come back. I would never normally write a post this long but I have nothing better to do as I wait for my bill. Since you have to pay for parking around here, I am going to put more time on my meter as well.

I've been here at least a dozen times and order the same thing and while it's $6.95 on the menu they charged me $10.95. I was advised to speak with the man at the front register that said "what you asked for was extra $ and You should have asked, most customers don't care about the extra $ so we don't tell them." Needless to say, I won't be going back. Terrible customer service.
The pho here is decent, but what really shines are the vermicelli bowls (bun). The chicken is my favorite -- I've been known to eat two bowls on occasion. The price isn't bad at all, either!

This place is FANTASTIC!!! From service to menu to ambiance, they hit the mark on every front. The menu reflects a balance of classic gastropub fare with current culinary trends. From what I could tell, they also have every dietary restriction covered - gluten free, vegan, etc. Their poutine section of the menu is fab. Lobster poutine is luscious!!  The best part about this place is that it's family owned and family rub. The manager takes care of you as if you are visiting her home and the staff follows her lead with warm, attentive but not intrusive service. I can't say enough good things.
Service was great, burger was amazing, menu had lots of appealing choices for adults and kids. Would absolutely eat here again.

FINALLY! Tucson has been needing a place like this.

Great location- located in the Campbell/Grant strip mall near Cartel. Open, airy, natural lighting- perfect for casual dining. 

This is definitely a location you bring health conscious people- but there ARE things in the menu that ANYONE would enjoy...classic sandwiches and salads with a bit of an upscale vibe.

I came for the acai bowl and was not disappointed! They only currently have two options, and were out of the one I wanted, but I was able to modify the option they had available (Cacao warrior). It was SO SO good. Good breakfast portion with delicious granola, coconut and fresh mint, which took it to a whole new level. I was sad when it was over! My only complaint is that I was spitting out a few ice cubes...but in house made for the win!
