The menu is moderately priced, but $8 is a little pricy for the acai bowl, especially with their other breakfast options being so cheap. However, the quality definitely makes up for the $$$.

I will definitely be back!

This place is an absolute must visit if you're in Philly. Their pountines are to die for if you're a cheesy fries lover. Bria and Allie were extremely helpful and patient with my moderately indecisive wife and me, and every thing came out quickly and fresh. I can't tell you how happy I am with Sandler's. I am not exaggerating when I say this is my favorite restaurant in Philadelphia.

All the things to try are variations of Vietnamese soups! They are really good. But the problem they don't have the pictures in their menu, so really difficult to identify how the dish would look like in reality. Try to see some yelps photos first.

This place blew my mind! My husband and I finally got a night away from our five kids. We stumbled upon this place, which ended up being the best night of our lives! To start, the bartender - Mike made us the best cocktails EVER and Lisa ... she was the icing on the cake. Not only is she beautiful- but also a great cook!! All in all, we will absolutely be back!! Thanks Lisa and Mike!

This past Friday night myself and a group were looking for a cool new place to try in the city. We happened upon this place through yelp and really liked the pictures we saw and decided to give it a shot. We were so pleasantly surprised by the experience and it exceeded our expectations. It's also very affordable, and the ambiance was amazing and a good place to catch up with friends. I had the hog burger which was about $14 and was worth every penny. If you're looking for a cool place to go for dinner look no furture.
Ordered Egg Noodles on Postmates with Vegetables and they gave me egg noodles with meat. I am vegetarian and I literally cannot have dinner now. AT LEAST SPECIFY ON THE MENU!!

I had a very terrible experience at "Sundaze". I typically really enjoy going here as it is local, and the frozen yogurt is descent. However, when I order frozen yogurt I expect to get the amount I paid for, not half the cup full. Also, there was literally five pieces of cookie dough as an "additionally charged topping". The woman working tonight was rude when I politely asked for more cookie dough (as there was clearly none), and tried to charge me even more. This place is a waste of money. Definitely not worth it.

I've never been a fan of healthy juices because it feels like they just throw oranges, carrots, and your local yoga instructor into a blender. This place is no different, every juice I've tried tastes like I'm being forced into doing a "deep-cleanse" and getting all my nutrients in one drink.

Everything else is amazing though! Especially the food. The tacos, the steak bowl, the lemonade all taste amazing while making you feel as if you've always been a healthy eater.

We had a reservation for 9, which always makes me nervous about service and quality of food (everyone getting food thats fresh)....This place delivered! 

We arrived and were immediately seated in our own room, that they closed the doors to, so we didnt disturb anyone, and we were not disturbed, which was great. 

Service was on point, they had a pretty good selection of craft beer, although there were a couple that were tapped. Either way, no shortage of beers!

Food was great, we had a few different apps, although their poutine is not what I would consider typical poutine (no brown gravy, but a ton of cheese sauce). Wings were crispy and we had the korean wings, recommended by the server and they were good, so were the traditional hot wings. 

Main course, everyone was happy, food was hot and fresh, burgers were cooked to order, and huge! Fries done perfect, good flavor and crispy!

This is your best bet for good Vietnamese food in Chinatown. They offer big portions and good quality food. The service is super fast and they let you enjoy your meal in peace for the most part. 

My favorite part about this place is that they have fresh fruit smoothies. Their durian and avocado smoothies are something I order every time I eat here! Very rarely can I say that I'm able to get a fresh durian smoothie.

I appreciate the wide variety in the menu. As much as I like Pho 20, which is probably the only other Viet restaurant I go to in Chinatown, I only go there for Pho or a rice dish whereas at Pho Xe Lua, I would be willing to order something less basic.

They have a lot of seating that stretches to a second level. Tip: the bathrooms are only 1 stall so go to the one upstairs if you're stuck waiting for one on the first floor!

Usually when I eat out, I want to indulge. I can prepare decent-tasting and healthy food at home. My friend and I wanted a light, healthy lunch before a workout, and this place fit the bill. We got in line in the nick of time, as a long line formed right after we ordered. Goodness is an order-at-the-counter joint, you take a number and your food is brought to you.

I've been into green juice lately so I ordered a Green Bully and the chicken and brie sandwich. It was hard to choose what to have for lunch. I also considered the Thai bowl and a couple of the salads. The breakfast menu (served all day) looked good too. I liked my sandwich. The juice was okay, way too much ginger, and I've had better from other juice bars. It was quite busy, so we got two seats at the bar. You can watch the juice being made and food being cooked. There is a yoga studio nearby, and it appears members come eat here in droves after their class. A VAST majority of people there looked as though they had just come from a workout or were going to one. They had a location at La Encantada that closed, and I'm surprised, because I would think this concept would do best in that area, but hey, it's clearly doing great here too.

My green juice and sandwich (with chips) was about $18. A bit spendy, but not more so than most other restaurants. They do seem to have successfully struck that sweet spot of good for you AND tasty. I will definitely return and try other things.

We've ordered catered food from Sandler's many times and unfortunately the food is bland and lacks seasoning, the chicken Parmesan was over cooked and chewy & the broccoli rabe was straight up burnt. I believe one of the managers names was Lisa and she was great! I expressed our concerns and she welcomed the feedback. She promised to make it better next time and I have faith in Sandler's! However at this time they have a little work to do. 

If you do catering, get the sandwiches. Those are great!!

Arrived at 11:30 for an early lunch with an admittedly cranky two-year-old.  Sat at the table for solid five minutes before meeting our server which was indicative of the promptness of the service throughout the meal. The waitress seem to understand the needs of a child as she offered fruit before a meal but even that took a while to show up. Inconsistency is the theme, as the cocktails were not good which with a cranky two-year-old is a must have!  The chicken fingers were amazing as was the salmon.  The flatbread pizza came out almost uncooked as the shredded cheese was still very clearly shredded cheese.

THIS PLACE IS THE MOST STRESSFUL PLACE TO LIVE!! Don't let them fool you either. As of late 2018 they got new management and the building now goes by Villa Bugambilias. THESE PEOPLE ARE WORST THAN THE LAST! Selfish and cold hearted management. Trying to change the apartments for the "better" but just making it 10x WORST!! Just moved in right before was taken over and was happy with my stay until these new rude, ignorant employees stepped foot in. I've never had so many problems in my life with an apartment!!!!
I love this place! Seriously the salads rock so do the smoothies. A peaceful zen vibe with yummy food and desserts.

Annnd the service is still so slow! Why does it take 20 minutes to get a smoothie or a fruit bowl? Also, the smoothies are icy again. Used to be creamy and well balanced but now they're using way too much ice. Gotta save money on those overpriced smoothies somehow I suppose.
I was craving Vietnamese American pho and this place definitely satisfied my taste buds. Really generous portion, too!
This is my favorite fro yo place! The owner is super nice and helpful. I love their waffle cones and variety of flavors that changes. My dog loves their puppy cups! Great price for a yummy treat!

I was in town a night early for a work meeting, so since I was solo and it was by my hotel I ordered Olive Garden online for pickup. The ordering system online was easy and friendly. The food was ready when I arrived at Olive Garden and I appreciated they double checked my order before I left. Overall, a great ordering experience with good food. I recommend the online ordering system.

Not the greatest.   Place felt dirty and it was.  Sat down in a spill of chocolate something.  No apologies was just told we could move.  Food  ehhh.  Ordered salads and the greens were all brown edges.
What can say I'm usually not into chain restaurants but you can definitely can't go wrong with this restaurant. Food is always great and prices good and a nice wine selection.

$7 for the extra large bowl of pho and when they say extra large, they really mean EXTRA LARGE! The bowl was so humongous that even the two elderly Chinese guys sitting next to us made comments to each other about how big the it was (that's what she said). It's very reassuring when your hot food greets you with a face full of steam.

I took a quick sip of the soup and discovered that it was very weak for a pho broth. It tasted more like a light broth you would typically use for chicken or seafood soups. I added my standard pho condiments: basil leaves, bean sprouts, lime juice, and extra jalapenos to make up for the weak broth. Obviously, Sriracha and hoisin sauce were added too. There were a lot of delicious cuts of meat, considering the price of the meal. Very generous with the beef tendons and brisket.

It took what seemed like forever to make even a small impact on the bowl of soup. I was there for the long run to finish this beast! Thankfully, there was enough meat, Sriracha sauce, and hoisin sauce to balance out the bland flavour of the rice noodles. I managed to finish most of the meat and noodles, leaving mostly broth in my bowl.

Service was average: it took a while to get a menu and a take-out container when we were finished. They did refill our waters regularly though. Generally with Asian restaurants, you don't go for the service, you go for the cheap eats!

I agree with the comments about portion size. The size of the food items here don't exactly match up with the high prices, especially if you consider how easily you can whip up a similar (if not identical) meal at home. My first meal here was a rice bowl, with marinated mushrooms, chicken, brown rice, veggies, and a light peanut dressing. My second meal was a smoothie I paid $8 for. Again, things I could easily make at home. 

However, they key word here is "could." Yes, I "could" easily whip up a smoothie before work. I could put stuff that's hanging out in my fridge into a tupperware to eat "al-desko" at work. But sometimes I just can't and I have to resort to eating out, which is hard to do if I want to eat healthy. For this reason, I  appreciate Goodness being so close to home and work. I know that if I'm in a pinch for time, I can rely on Goodness for a truly healthy meal with simple and wholesome ingredients. 

Despite the slightly elevated prices, this place is great, and a nice addition to the central area. I'm a fan!

They take credit card. Great service, very fast and efficient. Food came out quickly as well. There are a lot of different menu items that blend Vietnamese, Thai, and Chinese. However, if you're looking for straight up pho, there are places that do it better in the city. Broth was clean but had a lot of msg. If you want a little bit of everything like rice and noodle dishes, this is a good spot.
Summer rolls were fire. But I did get the pad Thai also and it was reaaaaaally underwhelming. I wouldn't recommend. But i'd like to try something else.

Cheap.  Fast.  Filling.  No real complaints.  4 stars!

This is my preferred pho location in Chinatown.  Bowls are $6-$7 and are quite filling.  They also have some nice beef carpaccio, and some sugarcane, minced shrimp, BBQ chicken noodle combos which are really enjoyable.  Prices are par for Chinatown.  Certainly not a particularly attractive place to eat but seems clean enough.  Service is fairly quick and food is delivered from the kitchen within 10 minutes of ordering.  I think they are closed on Tuesdays?

Pho!  Nomnomnom.  Cheers.

Best Vietnamese restaurant in Chinatown! And best price too! Rainbow(mung beans, red beans, green jelly) ice is my favorite drink. Service is fast. Really fast! Literally minutes after you order the food is here on your table. Will definitely go back when I crave pho.

Is this a chain? It's pretty much the menu and quality of an Applebee's. Sticky floors. Slow service. Inattentive bartenders. Bar prices in the Ritz-Carlton range. I doubt it will be around in a year.

I can not even begin to explain how amazing Sandler's is! My husband and I got married at the Ballroom at the Ben and asked Sandler's if they would extend their hours for our 275 person wedding after party. The owner, Pauly, and his staff did not even bat an eyelash! We partied all night long. They even made custom menus saying "Congratulations Mary Kate and Blaze." It was unbelievably thoughtful. They were AMAZING to say the least. They rearranged the seating in the restaurant to clear a space for a dance floor and asked us what type of music we wanted. I have worked in the Philadelphia area restaurant and bar industry for ten years and I have to say the service and atmosphere at Sandler's is fabulous, attentive, meticulously clean and beyond accommodating. EVERYONE was coming up to us saying how fun the after party was. I have never written a yelp review in my life but this staff deserves all the credit! They work their tails off to ensure we were 100% satisfied. 

If you are getting married anywhere in Old City, I cannot recommend Sandler's enough to be your go to location. FOOD, DRINKS, and SERVICE are beyond exceptional.  Their team really helped make our wedding the best night of our lives! 

Thank you again to Paul Sandler and his excellent team over at Sandler's you know how to provide top notch service!
This is my favorite spot for Viet food, Cheap, great food probable the best in China town.

Great spot we discovered while in Philly for the weekend. We were able to make a reservation for 630 pm on a Saturday night and were seated immediately. They were suddenly extremely busy because a large group of people came that seemed to be in Philly for a conference and kind of took over the place. It became apparent that they were short staffed and a little frazzled however, they were still very attentive to us and periodically checked in with us to make sure everything was okay. My friend and I ordered the lobster roll with sweet potato fries, which was absolutely delicious!
Service was top notch!! Food was not good at all. Quality was low and did not taste good at all.

Good pho place in Chinatown with a lot of options to choose from. Pho, rice plates, vermicelli, other entrees, you name it.

I ordered the vermicelli bowl with grilled pork, shrimp cake, and grilled pork balls (that's bun thit nuong, chao tom, and nem nuong for my fellow Vietnamese readers). It was a solid bowl of noodles. A little heavy on the lettuce and not so much the vermicelli, but the amount of grilled pork made up for it. The fish sauce was not as flavorful as I like but it still managed to add some Viet flavor to the dish. Overall, a pretty decent Vietnamese establishment in Chinatown!

Everything was fine but I didn't think it was anything super special, especially in a city rife with great brunch options. 

Went for brunch on a Sunday. Had to wait for 5-10 min for a seat even though there were tons of open seats everywhere. I believe the owner seated us, and he was very nice for sure which was cool. Then once we sat down it took at least another ten min for someone to come over to give us water and take drink orders. We were ready to order by then so we just ordered at the same time. Again it wasn't that busy so I don't know what the hold up was. 

Menu was a bit confusing as most of the things under the sandwich section weren't actually sandwiches...

I had a platter of scrapple, bacon, sausage, two eggs, home fries, and toast. The sausage was cooked very very well, so amazingly crispy on the outside. Everything else was fine...

Overall meh service, surprisingly hard to hear each other in the restaurant, and food that was fine but nothing special and for a relatively steep price for breakfast. Could do worse...but could definitely do better as well.

Good food though overpriced. Can't give more stars because of their poor customer service. One example--I placed a large phone order, went in and paid and then waited. And waited. I finally decided to walk around to the side counter only to find that the order was ready and they had not called me. Then one of the cooks starts giving me a hard time about paying, but instead of directing the question at me he keeps asking the employee standing next to me. Really awkward and rude. One of the employees apologized but the whole incident really left a bad taste in my mouth, no pun intended.

I'm on vacation in Philly this week. After walking by the Liberty Bell, we pulled up a list of restaurants to eat at that were in walking distance. The pictures from google looked really good, so we settled on Sandler's.

The restaurant wasn't very busy, so we were seated quickly. Service was fast and friendly, the atmosphere was very rustic and relaxing, and I always have an appreciation for restaurants that have glasses for water and wine ready before you are seated.

We ordered a few drinks from the bar, I had the tomato soup with the grilled cheese pop, and my boyfriend got the lobster roll with fries. The food and drinks were really good! The drinks from the bar were kinda pricey, though - two margaritas and a beer ran us about $24. Not sure if they used top shelf on my margaritas. I'm sure there were several other food items on the menu that would have been very good to try, too. 

I would definitely recommend eating here! And I wouldn't be mad to go back and dine with Sandler's again.
Excellent breakfast and service. Varied menu, extremely flavorful. Never disappoints!

Recently had lunch from Goodness and Oh My Goodness!  See what I did there? We split the Thai Chicken Bowl and the Roast Chicken and Brie Sandwich. The Thai Chicken Bowl was served with vibrant carrots and broccoli which seemed to be at their peak. But the highlight of that dish was the sliced, spiced apple. The apple was a vibrant addition to the dish. 

Both were very fresh tasting and had beautiful presentation. If you like fresh, high quality, nutritious and delicious food this is the place for you. I didn't check out their juices but one always needs a reason to go back.
This place is pretty good. I've tried the pho and bun bo hue here and have never been disappointed. This is my go to viet restaurant if I want something good and cheap.

The food is decent here. We always go for happy hour and the service is a little slow, but overall we enjoy the selection and the environment.

The breakfast is really solid actually!

Huge portions!!! The XL bowl is only $6.50-ish, so filling and hearty, and they are generous with the sliced meat. They also give lots of lime slices, basil, and bean sprouts. Broth is delicious as usual. I love that it's in the heart of chitown and I can walk right over for bubble tea afterwards (only if I get the large sized bowl will I have space for bbtea)

Only cons: unfortunately, the meat was a little thicker cut than I like it to be and the spring rolls I had last time tasted like they had been sitting out for a while.

One plus is it can fit groups. The restaurant is equipped with 2 floors so it can hold a good amount of people. The waiter we had was great and was very nice and polite.  

Based on the name you would expect the pho to be top notch but sadly it wasn't. The broth was bland. They do give a good portion of noodles. The viet coffee was your typical drip like with condensed milk. The spring rolls were decent. Overall i was disappointed in the Viet food in philly since I heard philly viet blows ny viet food out the water.

Not really a secret bar judging by the length of the line outside on any given day, but maybe that's an intentional part of the experience. Expensive ($11+) drinks. Maybe worth it, depending on why you came.

Decor: 9/10
------------------

Neat atmosphere inside - dark, chandeliers and wood tables, I didn't exist in the 20s and neither did most of the people drinking here or writing these reviews, so I don't really know what they mean when they say it feels like going back to the 20s because, well, you've never been there. The floor's probably much cleaner than it would have been.

Value proposition to your ego: 9/10
-------------------------------------------------------

There is a nice intellectual vibe - witty menu descriptions and drink names and whatnot ("I Asked Her For Water, She Brought Me Gasoline"). A distinct lack of basic people, which was nice. Though I'm fairly certain most of us can't actually afford to come here on a regular basis - I know we couldn't and we blended right in.

Service: 8/10
---------------------

I snuffed out the candle on my table by putting a glass over it and the doorman graciously offered to bring me another one when he saw me try to relight it with another candle from the bar. He looked like he was about 10 years old, but he was very gracious and polite.

Drinks: 8/10 (revised up)
-------------------

Like an above-average hooker: they taste fine and look pretty but are not worth $11 plus tax and tip. Too much ice. But at least they are strong enough to not taste like fruit juice.

EDIT: I went back to this place and ordered a drink from the last page, the one subtexted "sometimes you need a drink with teeth". Damn, there were teeth alright. +1 more point.

Overall: 8.5/10
-----------------------

The kind of place you'd take a girl if you wanted to get laid and she isn't enough of a Basic Bitch to fall for $3.50 happy hour beers at the local pub. 

If you didn't get laid, congratulations, she's probably too smart to be swayed by dark lighting and overpriced ethanol paired with witty descriptions in elegant typeface. She probably saw the movie version of The Great Gatsby and wasn't actually impressed. Better up your game.

If you did, congratulations. She's probably listening to a Lana Del Rey song and thinking about you right now. Well played, sir.

For a long time, this laundromat was falling apart; Washers were constantly broken, Dryers wouldn't dry, Service was abysmal.

Then, starting this new year, it was placed under new ownership, and the turnaround was awe-inspiring. George, the man who now works there, is always in the place. He is constantly maintenancing the machines to keep them in tip-top order, cleaning the floors, assisting those who need assistance, and breathing life into a dying business. Since his arrival, All of the machines are working perfectly, the change machines are completely reliable, the laundromat looks and smells fantastic, and there is a general lifting of spirits when he's in-shop. And if he isn't in shop, a number is posted around the place where you can always reach him - at any time for any reason. 

George has informed me that the renovations and innovations are far from over, so if you need a 24/7 laundromat, this is the place to go. Expect big things from here.

A fair and calm warning to not park here to pick up your child from Lake Magdalene Elementary would have been nice but I did not receive this treatment. I and many parents have been parking here for years before this laundry mat was transformed to Washlava. It is a short 2 min walk to the gate to pick up your child and 2 min walk back. So less than 5 mins of being in the Washlava parking lot. I was the first to be approached by the store manager with his small children following behind him like baby chicks and the conversation from him started with "Ma'am, I have a picture of your license plate. If you keep parking here I will call the sheriff." His opening sentence to me in front of my son was a threat. So my reply after his threat was "Well you are 4 years late telling parents this. I also don't see signs stating that this is parking for Washlava customers only. It takes less than 5 mins to get my child and leave." This managers response was icing on the cake, "What a great mother you are setting an example of." Now I am angry. He started to approach other parents walking up but proceeded to them in a civil way than his approach to me. So then this also made me feel singled out. So I tried to tell the parents that I knew walking up what was going on and then the manager then tells me "Lady I don't want you anywhere around here. I'm calling the sheriff and telling them your license plate." Mind you...this establishment is not reaping in 2 million a year. This is a slow if not mostly dead during the day laundry mat. I drive by here day and night as I've lived in this neighborhood for over a decade. This is unacceptable and disrespectful. If you are a parent of a child that goes to Lake Magdalene Elementary this is your fair warning from me.

We arrived at 6:20 on Saturday night and left at 7:20. WITH NO FOOD! Worst service ever! We told the waiter we had a show to make. He said he understood. We left when he apologized and said we are going to rush your order now. Lots of sorry but not an offer to make it right or a coupon etc. We spoke to the folks that waked out with us and they said they waited 45 minutes. Others who came after us were served. What a mess.

A random chat with a girl at a restaurant bar led me to this place. Highly recommended. Her recommendation did not disappoint. A wonderful atmosphere, and spot on wine and dinner recommendations by Nicole. The crab cakes are amazing. The Constantino Cab Franc was as described. Deep, and full bodied. I'd love to return to sample other offerings on the menu. Nicole was attentive and personable. So happy that a random chat guided me to a wonderful restaurant. I will definitely return on my next trip to Philadelphia.

This place is amazing. We have been there a couple of times. Tonight's experience was nothing short of fantastic. My wife and I were able to sneak away for a date night. We were both excited for Classic Spaghetti and we were both hungry. Upon arriving the service was great. The hostess was very nice and our server was great. The food?! Where to begin. My wife ordered the Chicken Marsala. I ordered prime rib. The last time we had come we tried the meatballs and it was hard not to order those again. We also wanted to try the onion rings. The food was nothing short of amazing. BEST prime rib in Tucson. Yes. Best. Amazing. My wife's chicken was also delicious. The onion rings also amazing. 

The food and the service were excellent. We would recommend CSWS to anyone and everyone. We were told that they have a great kids menu also. We will definitely be back. 5 stars for sure.

Stopped by here for a quick small lunch. Everyone was very friendly. The tuna tacos were very good not a typical flavor which was great. The lobster mac was GREAT. It had just the perfect amount of everything with a lot a lobster which places do not typically do !!! As far as drinks go although having a full bar they have no drink menu (just an FYI). Great place would 11/10 recommend

Great service! The menu was diverse enough for everyone to find something (including vegetarian options). The crab poutine was absolutely divine! I love the old bay cheese sauce!The service was quick and staff was incredibly kind and attentive. I will definitely be back.

This Vietnamese place, affectionately known as the Choo Choo Train, has been in existence for decades. Although I have been here numerous times years before, I took a 7 year hiatus due to another pho place I have been frequenting.

For a change of pace, I ordered the lemon grass pork chop with broken rice and another guest ordered the pho. The meal was under $20 which was a great deal, but I'm more experienced in Vietnamese food now and I can say that this is average.

The lemon grass pork chop was flavorful, but the effort put into this dish left something to be desired. The fish sauce was too sweet to a point of scratching at one's throat and the pork chop was not marinated enough for the flavors to seep in. I also enjoyed the chop to be slightly caramelized around the edges but this was just cooked with the tiniest bits of caramelization.

In addition, the pho broth was neither rich nor flavorful. It seems to inherit the spices and bones of a good broth, but simply wasn't simmered long enough for the delicate, savory, bone flavors to seep in.

In addition to the mediocre dishes, the restaurant itself was cramped and sticky. There was almost no breathing space between your table and your neighbors and the AC was not strong enough to accommodate the crowd we had that day on a hot summer afternoon.

Overall, this place had the potential to be better, but didn't seem like it wanted to try. It certainly could fool any tourists or pho newbie, but I'd have to pass on this one.

The absolute worst experience I have ever had at a restaurant. I picked this place because of its proximity to Walnut St. Theater. We got there a little past 6 with the show at 8. We made it clear from the start that we had a deadline but didn't really think it would be an issue. Well It was. It took forty -40-minutes for two bowls of soup to arrive. We just knew our entrees would be arriving shortly. Wrong! It was now past 7! We appealed to the waiter and hostess to no avail. Finally at almost 7:30 we were told that the kitchen was doing "a rush job." Meaning the order had never been put in! Totally disgusted we left the restaurant. Apologies galore but no offer of anything to atone for the terrible experience we had been through.

Was in the mood to try something different and Sandler's caught my eye. I should have known that when I was able to make a reservation within 15 minutes of prime time on a Saturday, 15 minutes prior, there was something wrong. The place was completely dead and we were greeted with horrible service and cold food. Was asked what order we wanted our food to come out in, and 40 minutes later all three dishes came at the same time with the temperature as if they came out in the order we requested.  Clearly somebody wasn't doing their job.  Took me another 25 minutes to order a 2nd round of drinks, nobody was around. There was two of us and we were starving and this was about all the food we could force down.  We ran out of there and got Geno's cheesesteaks, such a better value.

This is becoming a regular for me on my trips to Philly.

Taking a cue from fellow Yelpers, I had the beef carpaccio and Beef "Frank" ([sic]...that's really the way it appears on the menu) and tendon pho.  I loaded it up with the herbs and a couple of jalapeno slices.  There were several more slices provided, and looking back, I should've added one or two more jalapenos.  Mental note to self: spice it up a little on the next trip.  Still, it was tasty and very filling.

The star of the meal was the iced coffee.  Before you die, you have just GOT to try this stuff.  Made at your table, a container of super strong espresso is set atop a glass, where the contents drip down onto a layer of waiting condensed milk.  Stir it up, and pour the chocolatey brown mixture over ice.  Starbucks had better hope that this stuff doesn't find it's way out of Philly Chinatown, because if it does, the green and white is in some serious trouble.

The service was friendly and prompt.  With the dinner I described above and a 20% tip, the bill came to $23 (which, when I think about it, is about the price of Starbucks bar drink these days.)

We stopped here for brunch during a visit to Tuscon. The acai bowl and PB and banana toast were both amazing - tasty, filling, good portion sizes and good ingredients. Free parking out front, plenty of seating and we were served quickly. Definitely recommend this place!

The food looks amazing but the taste failed to wow us! for example the chicken and waffle (the waffle was amazing but the chicken had a acidic old oil after taste) change the oil for god sake! Now for the best part of the meal The brisket poutine with fried eggs was the main attraction the flavor and taste was spot on. As was the Elvis pancakes with Nutella. But the damage was done with old oil after taste as for the shrimp and crabmeat Cesar salad it was lacking flavor and the mixed bread croutons look liked recycled toast. So over all out of four plates two plates were spot on.

My GOODNESS. 
I adore this place- GOOD vibes, leave feeling GOOD! 

1. The Food: When ever I eat here I feel great afterwards, not overly full and satisfied that I ate out healthy. They have a variety of healthy smoothies and bowls. Smoothies are fresh ingredients, you can watch them prepare it in front of you. Anything that I get on the menu has not disappointed me, except once I had an overly salted bowl but it wasn't terrible. I also really appreciate the option of switching out the rice to quinoa (huge plus if you want to make your bowls extra packed with protein). I recommend trying the Goods smoothie and the Thai bowl. They also have a vegetarian option. 

2. The Ambiance/ Service: I love walking into this cute juice bar. It is small though, there are like 6 tables inside. The outside has a few benches to sit which can get really hot if there isn't shade. Parking is limited in a small shopping complex, there is parking in the back or on the side street though. It can get pretty busy during lunch time, but overall its a quick service. They give you a number at the counter after you order and pay. 

3. Recommendation - Would I go again/ what I recommend it for: Quick healthy casual breakfast, lunch or break for a smoothie. Highly recommend this place, it is definitely one of my favorites in Tucson.

My husband works near Chinatown and for ages I've been listening to him rave about the $5.95 bowl of seafood noodle soup he gets for lunch at the Viet-Thai restaurant every Friday. Finally got to test it out myself last weekend and it is just amazing!  The soup comes in a big bowl and is served with a plate of bean sprouts, herbs and slices of lime. He puts all the stuff in the bowl and squeezes in the lime... eating is a bit of a challenge but it seemed best to use a combination of the spoon plus chopsticks for fishing out the noodles and fish. There was a variety of seafood in this dish, shrimp, squid, mussels and something that looked like slices of fish cake.  While we tried some other things on the menu, I have to say this soup was the best thing we had! 

This place doesn't have much atmosphere, but hey, its cheap.  Beer is $3 a bottle. This place is a bargain.  

Most of the people around us seemed to be ordering some kind of soup...probably the pho that I saw on the menu.  I also saw quite a few people eating snails. They have some unusual stuff on the menu like frog legs.  I'm sure we'll be back to try other things, but for now I'll recommend that seafood soup!

(FYI the seafood soup is number 126 on the menu).

Love it!!!!!!!! We had breakfast here three times during our visit to Tucson. Delicious wholesome nutritious food. 

My favorites:
Breakfast burrito - normally when I think of quinoa I think bland.. but not this one! It was packed with avocado, salsa, cage free eggs, turkey sausage and a side of spicy sour cream like sauce. Absolutely delicious!

Big melon juice: tasted like a fresh cantaloupe to me! Very refreshing and hydrating in the desert climate. 

The hulk: tasted very creamy and delicious!

This place was simple, fast, and cheap so it definitely gets 4 stars in my book! They have two sizes for pho: regular and x-large. XL is huge. The people I went with were hungry, but they still only got through maybe 2/3 of the bowl and honestly could have been very happy with a large and just finishing the entire thing. I would definitely head back this place for a nice warm bowl of pho. Keep in mind the space is small so I could see there being a wait or it being too crowded during prime times.

Goodness is Greatness. I've been here many times and tried many things and have yet to be disappointed. Smoothies to Hulk out for. Breakfast burrito or bowls are top notch. Sandwiches are awesome. Tasty teriyaki to Clutch Coffees. My only wish was that they were open longer. I'd eat there more if I could. So get some goodness in your life as it not only tastes good but it's also good for you. Keep up the good work friendly staff.

Solid Vietnamese spot in Chinatown Philly. I'm glad my bf and I came here for some pho before heading home to ny. Broth was flavorful and not oily- it probably didn't w en need any hot sauce or sriracha with it. Their bowl of pho was huge and the portion is big and their Meat is tender. Excellent service and very quick.

I don't usually write reviews unless I'm really absolutely compelled to do so. I ordered the Notella waffle and it was so undercooked and underwhelming. It was the most unappetizing looking thing I've ever seen. 

Even though it didn't look appetizing, I continued to try it since I had already paid for it. The waffle was soggy and undercooked. The entire waffle was cold, as if it just gotten out of the freezer. 

The waffle was overflowing with the chocolate, nutty mixture. Almost to the point where it was overwhelming and took away from the entire waffle. 

I even went up to the workers to express my dissatisfaction. It is something I probably wouldn't ever do, but really felt the need to tell them. I told them I felt sick in my stomach and that the waffle was absolutely disgusting. The only reply I got was "I'm sorry". There was nothing done to fix this situation. This also has to be the poorest customer service I've ever received. Any decent place would have offered me a refund or at least a replacement. 

I don't know how the other locations are, but the girls at the store at this location are incompetent and do not know how to treat customers properly. They also aren't trained properly to create the products as they are advertised. 

I attached the pictures for reference. 

I would give this place 0 stars if I could.

As a Bostonian, I have to say, Tampa really needs to step up it's game. What a disappointment. Avoid this location at all costs.

Best yogurt in north Tucson!  Great variety that rotates several times a week so there is always something new and something we like.  We also enjoy the choices of nonfat and sugar free and all the toppings available.  The staff is great and very friendly and outgoing.  Great place to grab a snack and just sit, relax and talk.  We especially like supporting a small local business!

Breakfast was very good. It's off the lobby of the old Franklin Hotel. It's a very pretty space. The service was polished and professional. The owner? A young women at the front was gracious and funny. The coffee was excellent. I had the fried chicken and waffles with real PA maple syrup. My friend had Killer Irish oat meal with strawberries. The whole menu looks interesting and I never think that. My only complaint is I prefer white meat to thighs. But for value it was off the hook! Only $10 for the chic and waffles!! If you are in town it's an outstanding option for breakfast or lunch. BTY all the other food I saw looked great!

Seriously excellent eats.  Stellar service.  The thought of chicken and waffles never made sense to me....until now.  They were divine.  Our waiter was thoughtful and efficient.  We had a great brunch.  Party of 4 completely satisfied.

The Good: The best chicken and waffles ever! The chicken is boneless and the waffles are made with bacon in them. The atmosphere was nice with nice spacing in between tables. The service was very good because the staff worked together. Restrooms are private and clean.

The Bad: I can't really think of anything for this place.

Overall, I will definitely go here again and will tell others about it. Enjoy!
The trainwreck breakfast sandwich with a side of Paulie's sauce is the perfect Sunday morning cure! The bartender is so friendly and funny and makes a great Irish Coffee and Bloody Mary!

Nice atmosphere. All the food is good. I've had a good half the things. Breakfast is my favorite. Eggs and home fries, French toast. Waitress Shannon. So nice. Over the top help with my guest. Haley, savana, and Tyler, Paul the owner so nice. Can't say enough

We came here for my birthday after a day of walking around the city. After we were seated the waiter told us he'd be right with us... then never came back. We saw him waiting on other tables that had COME IN AFTER US and got increasingly annoyed. Finally we flagged down another server who went and got him, and he came back apologizing that he had, indeed, forgotten about us. What?? Isn't that your job?? We ordered and the food took a long time to get to us (again, tables who came in after us were getting their food and LEAVING before we had ours. There were only 2 of us). The bacon cheese poutine was awesome, the turkey sandwich was very dry, and the skillet cookie was amazing. However, we were running late to relieve our babysitter and before we ordered dessert we asked how long it would be to get. Answer: 7 minutes. In actuality, about 20 minutes and very late getting home. I'm not sure how good our waiter's sense of time was.

It's decent; I enjoyed my food and drinks for brunch that we had, just nothing stood out as amazing. The grilled cheese garnish on the Bloody Mary was just some cold cheese in between some slightly toasted bread. Service was acceptable as well.
Highly recommended bank with local, small-town service.  Manager Annetta Derracot arranged a commercial loan for our business at highly advantageous rates.  Great staff to work with.

This was the first spot my friend and I decided to eat at when we first arrived to Philly and it was seriously amazing. We both got the pho dishes and let me tell you, the broth was super flavorful. This is one of the best pho spots I have ever had and I've had many. The bowls were large and it was only $7! They had a lot, and I mean a lot, of noodles. I usually add quite a bit of sriracha and hoisin sauce to my food but this did not need any! It was flavorful as is and I highly recommend this to anyone who's around Chinatown in Philly. In fact, this was also the last meal that my friend and I had before heading back on the bus back home. This place made quite the impression on us and we will surely come back whenever we visit Philly!

We also got drinks, the pina colada was excellent and the salted plum drink was just salty enough, and the avocado smoothie was creamy.

I've tried the chicken and waffles, and it was very good. The ahí tuna sandwich, medium rare, has to be one of the best ahi tuna sandwiches I've had in a long time. If you like grapefruit martini was also really good. I'll be back.
Good food, fresh ingredients, great prices...  We're regulars and big fans of their pho.  Not everything on their menu is equally good, but their best dishes are outstanding.

Nice atmosphere with the local ball game on. Just ordered a few appetizers for dinner. Thought they were decent (BBQ Chicken Nachos and a few others). Had a service who just seemed to not want to be at work. Honestly would it kill a person to smile.  Would rather pass on this restaurant to not endure another episode of someone who seems to hate their job so much.  I won't mention her name in hopes she was only having a bad day. If this is her normal then it'll catch up to her soon enough. *Update* Owner reached out to me regarding our experience. He seemed genuine in his response and seemed to want to further educate and grow his staff to be better off this review. I added a star because of the owners want to create a customer service orientated environment. Thank you Paul for caring.

Big disappointment. Came for lunch during the week. Ordered a Cobb salad with steak. The dressing that came with it was disgusting so I asked for ranch. The steak was disgusting. Damn near rare and still cold in the center. I asked for medium well. The server took forever to come back. When she did I told her about the steak and she removed it from the bill. As she should. I couldn't eat it and that's not how I ordered it. 

The bill came and I paid it and left a 20% tip. The automatic alert from my credit card appeared and the approved amount was about $8 more than the bill and tip. I asked the waitress what happened. She shrugged, said talk to the manager and walked away. 

I did speak with the manager. She was very nice. She fixed the problem and refunded my money. 

Bottom line: I wouldn't return. Poor service by the waitress. And who can't get a salad right??!!

I want to be on the record here saying that Ali, the owner's daughter had told me to come back to the restaurant with my family so she could make up for a previously terrible experience I had at this restaurant, and comp us a meal. When I went back (unwisely) for my brother's birthday, she charged us for everything we ordered except a couple of appetizers. This is one of many of the reasons why this restaurant is going out of business today.

I realize that i am rating an Olive Garden with a 5 star.. but if you are resigned to dining at a chain restaurant because you are longing for a smile and predictable meal, then I am always a fan of this place. The salad is always awesome. And tonight I had baked ziti (which I doubt you could screw up), and it was really good.. filling and satisfying. But our server, Brady, was fantastic. Excellent, excellent service. The manager checked on us twice and she was very attentive... all in all, it was exactly what we were looking for after a long week on the road and overpriced meals

Wow... very disappointed in this place. While waiting to order, I overheard that two people at another table had waited over an hour for their food. One ordered her steak medium and it came out raw. She sent it back but it was brought out the exact same. They were still charged for their food. The $16 chicken fajitas consisted of microwaved chicken with onions & peppers that were obviously cooked earlier in the day, a few sprigs of salad lettuce and a bowl of watery beans. We also waited probably 40-45mins for this. The owner was around but never once went over to talk to the poor customers at the nearby table. They were also out of deserts. It's Father's Day weekend... c'mon guys!

This restaurant in china has a great selection of drinks at a happy hour price! So, definitely go there for the drinks. I ordered the green curry with tofu and vegetables, the food was okay - really not so good not so bad. But, my disappointment was the slice of chicken that I found in my vegetarian curry :( 
The host was a very nice man to apologize profusely and take the amount off my check, they still get a 3 and not a 1. For all meat eaters, please try this place and feel happy to not have to break your bank and come back tipsy, stuffed with good food.
Steak with Lobster Ravioli...steak just OK ravioli REAL BAD all for $20 bucks I think..6 oz steak...overpriced and just not very good at all.

Well, as you can tell, my breakfast burrito was terrible! All jokes aside, this was hands down the best breakfast burrito I've ever had. The burrito was made to order, hot and fresh and the ingredients were perfectly balanced and the chipotle aioli, I could drink! If you're looking for a healthier alternative to breakfast while still having the guilty eating effect, this is for you. I think I may stick around for lunch!

My favourite new spot in town! I found this place by accident, I was driving and felt like some juice, then this place showed up. From just seeing one picture on yelp I was excited.

Sure enough when I arrived I wasn't disappointed. We don't get these kinds of places in Tucson. This is the kind of place you can find in London, LA, Chicago the big cities that understand interior design and what people want. Even the parking reminded me of LA.

Everything about this place can be summarised in one word: fresh. The food was freshly prepared, the juices are freshly squeezed, and the ambience is modern with great lighting and design. Thank you for bringing places like this to Tucson! I will be a loyal customer for many months to come. They're opening a branch at the University of Arizona too.

Food was for the most part good. Prices were reasonable and competitive with other restaurants in the area. They ran out of what I had initially wanted to order. The staff was very apologetic about it. Overall, not a bad experience. I've been here several times before.

Love Wawa pretty much everytime. Stopped at this location on way home Orlando. Its exit 260. I ordered turkey - lettuce, tomato, mayo. This location was packed and they had a great staff. I had 10-15 numbers in front of me and maybe waited 3-4 min. They have lots of staff as this a very fast paced location, being off of I-75.

From the time of reservation to the time we left this wonderful restaurant, the experience we had at Sandler's on the 9th exceeded expectations.

 I had a question about the menu; when I emailed the restaurant, the owner, Paul Sandler, responded to me immediately. We were running late for our reservation - and the very friendly girl who answered the phone was super helpful and accommodating. Our server, Jamie was delightful and helpful. He gave us some great suggestions and was very attentive. 

We enjoyed the tuna poke tacos, tomato soup with grilled cheese pop, lobster poutine and the "hog" burger. I will be craving that tomato soup and lobster poutine! You have not seen the last of me - thanks to everyone there for making our dining experience a memorable one!
Online menu says breakfast served all day. Tried to order breakfast burrito at 1:07 pm and was told breakfast food wasn't available

I love this restaurant. It was a perfect one so far. I'm happy that they do refills but the only thing I'm not a fan of is the tablet itself. They are running Android with the Olive Garden Edition software. I really want Minecraft on it. 
I love the purchase and the food it comes up but there's no problem with the business itself. The design is more a wooden home style restaurant from Italy in Europe. But hey it's 2018, what about splitting up  Olive Garden in 200.9Mlion Cities across the US:

I'm giving 5 stars for the pho and beef bun! Coming from LA, I cannot believe that I had the best pho ever in Philadelphia of all places. I was visiting my best friend and she took me here for lunch. The place was very crowded on a Friday. It's pretty clean. Service is fast. Their lime soda is pretty good and is my friend's favorite drink there. The pho comes in only large and extra large! The prices are really good. Their large is usually the large bowls that my hubby gets in pho restaurants in LA. I typically get regular size bowls and can't finish them. So this was crazy big. I can't imagine who can finish their extra large bowls. The broth is super flavorful and not greasy. The meat was really tender and noodles super good and not stuck together like a giant noodle ball. I asked for no cilantro as usual and was so happy that they didn't just give me a bowl with no seasoning (since many pho restaurants mix their cilantro and green onions together). Instead they gave me lots of green onions just the way I like it!! Major points for them! My friend ordered the beef bun. I was sooo surprised at how good the beef was. It was high quality meat (more like steak) and super flavorful and tender. Yummy! I only wish they have places like that here. I'll bet there are places this good in Westminster but I didn't expect this in Philly. Well done!

I just had to put to sleep my "Boo Bear", on 5/18/16 after a very aggressive form of cancer was too much on him.  I am so very grateful for Dr. Bohnke and all she did for my baby. I just want to thank the office staff,  and a special thank you to Claire for such an awesome job on my Boos' paw print. Also with all the love and gratitude I can muster to Dr. Bohnke and Denise for the love and support while my boy was passing on and after. You will never know how much it means to me to have had those hugs of love! I would recommend this place to anybody, who wants top quality care and support in your animals needs, now and in the future. Cimarron Animal Hospital is 100% my go to place for my four legged family members...
Great options for healthy meals! My favorite is the Açaí bowls, mango jungle in particular but also the quinoa salad with tofu!

This restaurant is located in the heart of Philly Chinatown and can be quite busy. This restaurant serves Viet and Thai food dishes. We got the summer rolls which were standard but it was pretty big compared to other places. The only complaint here was that they might have overstuffed it so it wasn't rolled as tight. The crunchy spring rolls were standard as well, but I thought it could have been a little more deep fried and crunchy. For my main entree I got #312 which was vermicelli with BBQ pork, crunchy spring roll and shrimp on a sugar cane stick. This dish came with a little bit of everything so you get to try different proteins. The entree was pretty good as there was good flavor with the BBQ and the shrimp on the sugar cane stick was pretty solid. We got our food pretty quickly so the the service here is pretty fast. If you're looking for your Viet food fix while you're in Chinatown come and check it out.

Very cute setting and very spacious. Easy to get a table through Open Table for brunch. Service was very good, the staff was all very polite and friendly. 

Full bar. My friend got the bloody Mary which she said was really tasty. They did not skimp on the olives. They can make spicy or not, to your liking. 

Lots of food options, but I wasn't particularly blown away by my omelette with Kennett Sq mushrooms, spinach, and tomatoes. "Homies" were good: nice and salty and peppery. Friend got the Lox eggs benny and another got the avocado toast and another got the salted caramel french toast. No complaints. I think the salted caramel french toast was probably the best dish. 

Very pleasant experience but probably not going to rush back. Seems like a good option if you have a large group bc it wasn't too crowded (though today was rainy).

Stopped by and visited the other day! Staff was so nice and welcoming! I had a pick 2 ultimate topping bowl and it was absolutely amazing! Also all of there health shots were amazing! The recovery shot saved my day!

This little hole in the wall restaurant delivers! It's simple but to the point. The food is delicious, inexpensive, and big portions. The waiters listen and will actually make substitutions without any hassle. 
We came on a cold and rainy Philly afternoon hoping to find a delicious bowl of pho to warm our souls and we were not disappointed. We got the XL bowl of pho $8.95 (ours had different cuts of beef and meatballs). This bowl was definitely XL it fed two adults and we had leftovers. The broth was full of flavor and just perfectly cooked. They do not skimp on anything here. My favorite were the meatballs next time I'm getting extra of these.
We also got the shrimp summer roll for $3 you get two huge rolls per order. It was very fresh and satisfying. 
All around 5 stars. This place delivers what it promises at such a low price. Food is at your table in no time. And servers are attentive, I can't wait to go back and explore their menu!

This my go-to place for pho and also noodles... The food is fantastic and you cannot beat their prices!! Dinner for two with grew entrees for $20.... Doesn't get any better tasting except when you factor in the low cost

I have been to Sandler's three times for lunch.  Service and food have all been excellent.  Great menu.  
Recently I have been working with Paulie and Allie for a family
dinner and it is very easy to work with them.  They "get it".

I love this place.  Super-fast service.  Great food.  Economical.  Only issue is parking, but there are lots nearby and if you work in the city like I do, it's an easy walk.  Although, I always go for the Pho, (it's an addiction) I love the smoothies too, especially the Taro with pearls.  Durian, not so much, but hey, nobody's perfect.

Usually I get takeout from here and it's fine, but today I noticed something off. I noticed little hairs embedded within the beer tendons and it just grossed me out. Normally I never closely inspect my food but it was just gross. It doesn't seem like is it part of the cow... I'm assuming that it can only be human hair, and it definitely isn't mine since it's embedded in the food...
Today was my 1st time eating here and it was absolutely amazing! Everything was cooked to order and so tasty and fresh! This will be my new lunch spot! Love it

Price point is great but food itself is just so so. We ordered three fishes between the two of us: pork spring roll vermicelli Bun, papaya. Pork shrimp salad and the flank steak, brisket tendon pho. 

The bun lacked the requisite shredded cucumbers, daikon. The spring roll was not crispy. The bun dish was sloppily put together. 

The sprouts and basil that normally accompanied the pho was not fresh-- limp and yellow. Broth had a bit too much msg.

What a disappointment for dinner. I had seen Sandler's 4-star Yelp rating - in retrospect, I should have looked more closely at the actual reviews. I was intrigued with its historic, upscale and classy former Ben Franklin Hotel location (not to be confused with the Hotel Franklin on Independence Park).

It's rare that I give only 2 stars based on one visit, but in doing so I feel I'm being fairly generous.

We arrived early on a Tuesday evening for a 7:30 reservation, and stepping in the door, the live music (amplified blues guitarist and percussionist) was so loud that we immediately asked to be seated somewhere quieter. The host asked, "What?" because, of course, he couldn't hear us. That's when you know you're in trouble, and the instinct to leave was almost overwhelming. (Don't misunderstand, I love that music, and it was excellent - just way too loud - and the concrete floors don't help in that regard.) 

The host showed us the seating in the hotel lobby, which was empty of diners, and it seemed like being on display for the building's tenants walking through. (It is indeed a huge, beautiful space - but the website description of the "second bar and lounge in the lobby" as being "intimate" seems like sheer puffery - and the host assured us that there wasn't a bar.) He then led us to a table in the far corner of the restaurant, which was still loud, but bearably so.

Our server arrived promptly, but left us with only 1 food menu. No problem, we can share. 

Asking her to recommend the driest white wine on the list, her response, which admittedly was difficult to hear, seemed to be "I only know the liquors." (Right, I'd stay on the hard stuff myself if I had an evening ahead of me shouting in that din.) The poor server, she seemed so forlorn and unhelpful, we could only feel sorry for her. But it really says something about the way the management trains the waitstaff, that they don't know anything about the white wines and don't have anyone to turn to for help, doesn't it?

The Ferrari-Carrano we selected (served in a single glass plastic carafe) really lacked character and was notable only for its sweetness. Just what we didn't want. A second order for a red wine was much better. Okay, one for one. (Of course, the server didn't have any comment or question about the fact that the white wine remained mostly untouched.)

At this point, not one to abandon all hope, I focused on the veggie burger - at the least, this "local sourced" and "sustainable food" business might have a great plant-based burger, perhaps a runner-up, if not a winner for my "Search for the Greatest Veggie Burger" collection. Nope. 

This is an experience that I'm sure every vegetarian can relate to. That veggie burger, which always appears toward if not at the bottom of the meat burger list, shouts out that it's an afterthought - it's the obligatory "we have to have a veggie burger for those people" - even though the chef or owner would never want to eat such a thing. So it's the rather bland white bean-quinoa mush "patty" (two pieces of romaine on top) that   ends up being mostly extruded from the bun. Texture matters, people! There was a side of spiced mayo to jazz it up. Hey, don't brag about sustainability and then put a burger like this as the only veggie option alongside a variety of meat burgers. Nothing to celebrate about the chicken cutlet sandwich, either.

Seems like Sandler's can't figure out if it's a trendy, local-sourced eatery in a cool, classic old hotel location - or a sports/tourist bar. With the 3 huge TVs, high decibel level, inattention to quality service, and lack of imagination about the menu, I'd say the sports bar is winning. Yes, they use plastic bags.

In sum, I'm sitting there thinking, why am I eating dinner in this place when there are within a few blocks some incredibly great restaurants deliver service and food at such a higher level for roughly the same price?

In fairness, the Conshohocken Type A IPA on tap was excellent, and the onion rings were, too. This place does a breakfast and take-out business, and perhaps for that they deserve those four stars on Yelp. But not for the dinner experience.

I was visiting today for the second time 10/6/18 from Maryland and ordered what I had before -the chicken and waffle and it was burnt badly. Very disappointed even though they replaced it. The mere fact that they served it burnt was the reason for the 3 stars.

I was craving frozen yogurt one day when driving back from the other side of town, I was so excited to put all my toppings on and just have plain tart yogurt but to my surprise it wasn't self serve and there wasn't any good toppings, just a bunch of candy and other things. I don't go to places that are not self serve because I like to do it and I want certain toppings. I already walked in and the lady working was nice but I kinda felt obligated to order, I honestly didn't want any of their flavors I just like plain tart yogurt with strawberry and Pineapple and Boba balls and mochi. I didn't see any of that. I got the salted caramel sugar free one with some coconut on top. It was okay, it was creamy but if I wanted ice cream I should have just went and got ice cream.. This was pretty much ice cream.. I just wanted frozen yogurt. Every yogurt place should always have plain tart. I don't like the flavor ones, if I wanted a flavor I would eat ice cream I guess. I now know it's not self serve and they don't have the toppings I wanted. I didn't see any fruit at all. 
The place was kind of run down, was not very inviting, "old" is the word I would use. The lady working was nice so that's a plus but I'll get my yogurt else where from now on. I guess I'm just picky.

Cheap, fast service, good food. What more could you ask for? 
I came in on a weekend night with two girlfriends and we were seated immediately. You receive complimentary hot tea for the table, and it's pretty delish. We ordered spring rolls and three bowls of pho. Everything came up super quick. You need only look in the direction of your server and he is at your table, reading your mind, and already doing what you are about to ask. 
I ordered a large bowl of chicken. The large is pretty big and that is the smallest size. I ate maybe 1/4 of my bowl. The 1/4 I ate was very flavorful and steaming hot! I am always a fan of the "add your own" sprouts, basil, and jalapeno plate that comes on the side. 
Our grand total for all of that was about $30 with tip! Will definitely be back.

I'm not trying to hate, but I think this place is a little too hyped up. I've been to "the train" a couple times now for pho and thought it was good, but not great. The portion is generous, but my husband and I both agreed we got more beef and noodles over at Pho 75. That's where I'll be when I get my next pho craving.

The cold spring rolls were a disappointment. The shrimp roll had barely any shrimp and the pork roll was dry and hard to swallow. I also ordered a lemon soda and it had no fiz! Weird. I haven't given the Thai dishes a chance yet, but maybe they'll change my mind about this place.

The service at this location was exceptional. Micah was our server and he was very attentive polite and everything we ordered tasted fresh and was hot. Other servers food runners and even the managers checked in and made sure everything was to our liking and that our drinks were never empty.  Being in the restaurant industry as a manager I am rarely impressed when I go out to eat but this particular location did it. I'll definitely return!

ICandy has an amazing staff, an addicting menu (can someone say spicy fries with cheese sauce?), and a fun mixture of rooms and floors. Be sure to say hi to Charlotte, the best female bartender in Philly!

Who new such healthy food could taste so good. I got the Mediterranean bowl and the chicken taco. The amount of healthy ingredients that is thrown into these meals is astonishing. This may be my favorite restaurant ever. Best taco I have ever ate.

Had the tomato soup and grilled cheese squares--very good. French onion soup had meat in it--different but good. Friend had the prime rib poutine--liked it. Three of us had the chicken BLTA sandwich, sent one back. Little to no flavor, no sauce, hunk of chicken--hard to bite. Had the chocolate chip w ice cream dessert--yummy! Waitress we had didn't stop back enough once the food was delivered; not the best waitress.
Great food, great music on Saturday night and nice place to dance without it being trashy like most places to go dancing in Tampa.

Salmon was pretty good and they cooked it to order.  Served with mustard sauce and roasted vegetables.  I like the way that everything paired together. 

The chicken cutlet was gigantic and tasty, served with balsamic reduction, tomatoes, and greens.  Crispy breading, perhaps slightly over cooked, but pretty good flavors.

They serve "poutine" here, which is great, I want more poutine on more menus.  However, this wasn't really poutine, it was cheese fries.  No brown gravy, no cheese curds.  French fries with lobster and cheese sauce.  That being said, there were whole lobster claws in there, which is pretty cool.  Just stop calling it poutine.

Nothing that was too interesting on the drink menu.  

Service was a bit odd.  Our server was friendly I guess, but did not seem to listen well, was standing too close to people, and shouting to people across the dining room.

Xe Lua is not only my favorite Pho but one of my favorite restaurants. i love the papaya salad with beef jerky and the Xe Lua special Pho. it comes with plenty of beef and the tripe and tendon are always tender and delicious. their French press coffee with sweetened condensed milk is awesome but packs a caffeine punch.

make sure to get an avocado shake in the to-go cup to bring with you as you check out the cool markets and boutiques in Chinatown.

I've been exploring Philly eateries for about 10 years now, and this place has remained my absolute favorite for about the past 5 years. I've tried damn near everything on the menu at one point or another, but I usually find myself ordering my favorites; fresh pressed lemon juice, flank steak appetizer, and sauteed steak with green pepper and onion entree. Its delicious and its cheap. In a city where an entree can easily be $15 this place has consistantly low prices, around $7 for an entree.

The staff are always attentive and friendly, even when its packed and chaotic. The food has always come out quick and hot for me. Icing on the cake; they serve alcohol. Dispite this I find it difficult to run the bill up too high because of the aforementioned cheapness of the food here.

They are closed on Wednesdays, which has been very disappointing when I forget about this and try to go there on a wednesday, which I do maybe twice a year.

Doorman was old and cruddy, which is probably why we waited soooo long in a short line to get in.  Not the best welcome.  Drinks and music was okay...nothing too new and exciting.  It's sad because this spot has tons of potential to be amazing.
I have dinned here several times and always have a good experience. The waitresses are always was nice and attentive. Food is delicious. I would recommend this place.

Needed a pho fix in Philly, this place did not disappoint. 

Pros: Real pho noodles, delicious broth, various meat etc. options, excellent price, ridiculous portions, excellent service, easy to find in Philly Chinatown, bathroom was clean.

Cons: I wish I didn't sit facing the kitchen, it kinda grossed me out. Do I think it would be closed down by the health inspector...ummm I don't know. I know I was more squeamish than usual because I was nauseous from riding the SEPTA. 

Overall: I'd come here again because the food is delicious!

I had had a previous bad experience, but I went in earlier today and was blown away. The customer service was excellent. Alysa was straight up excellent and the food was delicious. Cant wait to go again.

I'll keep it simple. If you haven't been here yet: You Are Ca-razy!

This place is awesome. I would give it 5 stars if the service wasn't so hit or miss, but I love love love all the food I've had here. From the Pho to the Vermicelli to the bangin ass rice dishes. You just can't go wrong with pretty much any dish here. 

My favorites: 1. Vegatable Spring Rolls 
2.Pho Tai, Nam Gan
3. Bun Bo Nuong
4. Com Suon, Bi, Cha Chung 

Be a fatty and get them all. It's just that awesome. That ish cray!

Went here on a Saturday. Place was dead. Took almost 2 hours to get food. Waitresses were rude and snobby. I've eaten at fast food places that had better service. When our party wanted refills or some bread while waiting for food the waitresses felt like we were bothering them. Too much to list for complaints just simply go elsewhere food is subpar.

I rarely frequent this bar, and when I do it is sub-par.  Some people have been posting about he owner, the racist comments and the video capturing his racist rant: https://youtu.be/A3hOVbKGpfs  

Don't waste your time or your money at this place.

3 stars at best. The only have a few good comments about our experience. The hostess and servers were very professional and very polite. We started with potato soup  and it was delicious. We were excited at that point for our meal. Unfortunately, the rest of our food was somewhat mediocre. The spaghetti noodles were soggy the sauce was nothing exciting and the meatballs had a very strong sweet taste nothing I had tasted before. And I'm a good way. Shrimp scampi was OK and so was the chicken marsala. Out of our party of six the steak Sandwich was the best. 

Would probably not go back. Prices were reasonable but the atmosphere was not a friendly one, Service again, very polite but we didn't feel the most welcome.

This is a great first-step for someone who wants to eat better foods without spending their whole pay check or going vegan overnight. I only had a chance to try their juices, which were nice but NOT organic. Someone please correct me if I'm wrong, maybe they switched to pesticide-free since I last visited?

The atmosphere is nice, perfect for the college crowd, though I think ventilation could be improved if something is being fried. 

I really hope Goodness is successful, because Tucson definitely needs healthier options!

I was happy  to find a new place that serves healthy food with vegan options. I got the roasted veggie bowl with quinoa and it was pretty good. I did get overcharged by $2 though because apparently they just lowered the prices but did not inform the cashier nor change it in the computer. When I realized the mistake, I did get my $2 back. Good that the prices are lower, but you think the staff would know about it. Then when I was eating I saw the cashier who had been handling money putting her fingers INSIDE every cup as she was placing stickers on them that said "goodness". That is so unhygienic and just gross! All the people handling food wore gloves and so should anyone touching clean cups that people are going to drink out of!
Also, the trash and recycling bins are not well marked so everyone just threw trash in both.

I just do not understand the appeal, IMHO.  Went there in recommendation of hubby.  So disappointed!  Started out with two dirty water glasses.  Was seated right away because restaurant was not busy (Saturday afternoon).  Seated at a table with no utensils.  Followed by the water glass issue.  Only part of my order was delivered and the poor man who was assisting our waitress (who we could not find) was jumping through hoops to make up for her lack of attention.  I ended up getting utensils from a nearby table  and I finally went to the bartender to ask for part of my order (we each ordered the same meal, how is it only part of ONE meal isn't delivered).   

Three stars because my pancakes were really good (and huge) and my scrapple was cooked to perfection!  

Clearly most of my dissatisfaction was based on the service not provided by our waitress.  I also thought the dining area could be a bit cleaner....  Not sure I would try again.

We ate here Saturday evening, October 21. I had spaghetti & meatballs ($16) my wife had the lasagna ($15). The food was superb. We have a an Italian friend who is an excellent cook, and this was like eating a homemade meal in her kitchen. The meatballs are beef, sausage, veal, and salami, and the best I've ever had, and the ragu sauce was good, too. I tasted my wife's lasagna and could see why she was raving about it. We seldom eat out because restaurant food is usually just average and overpriced, but this was great food. If we lived in Tucson this would be a regular stop for us. Big portions, so bring an appetite. Good selection of wines, too. We had an opportunity to speak with the owner, very down to earth and pleasant. Don't let the atmosphere fool you, this is not one of those trendy places with exposed ceilings and TV's everywhere, it is an older building and quiet, but the food rocks.

Machines break down often, dryers out of order. No attendant on site only a phone number on a wall. Parking lot not lit well after sunset.
Pricey, compared to others.
Food was good it the check took a long time I think they forgot about us. They were busy with people going to shows. Left me disappointed

Just ate here tonight again. I think before, I was a bit too generous with the three stars. This place, really only deserves two. 

Pho. I forgot how clear the broth was. If you were one of those people who said this has the best pho in Philly, then you are limiting yourself of greatness. Save your money and go to Washington Ave.

I also had the soft shell crab tonight. I remember getting that back in the day and it being delicious, but now, it's just "good." Decent at that. A bit too much breading, fried overly crispy. Where did my crab go? 

Service was horrible tonight as well. Left us in a corner upstairs and forgot about us. Take it or leave it.

I will ONLY go here for the snails. They make it just right, and everything else is subpar.

Sorry Pho Xe Lua, I used to like you like that.

With so many burger joints and franchises, I'm very happy to see a place like this open. I popped in for lunch and didn't really know what to expect (I had read the Yelp reviews before I went). I ordered a turkey pesto sandwich and it was ready within a few minutes-very quick. It was delicious and very filling. I also ordered a juice 'commuter'; it tasted just the way that I imagined it would. To be honest, I was a little worried about the prep time and portion sizes based off the Yelp reviews that I read. But I didn't see a problem with either of them. After the juice and the sandwich, I was very full. My coworker tried their albacore sandwich and a smoothie. She liked both and couldn't finish her smoothie because she was full.

Oh yeah, the staff were very nice too :) 
I'll be back.

Staff isn't as welcoming nor friendly as they are at Woody's. Drinks were good and priced appropriately. Downstairs was comfortable to hang out around the bar and the music isn't too loud to chat over. 2nd floor was happening with a dance floor and great music. The upstairs roof was closed unfortunately because it was snowing but I hear when it's open they have slushy drinks. Would come here again.

This Olive Garden, while turning tables fast was only mediocre. The food was dry and overcooked. We like to go to Olive Garden because it is usually a sure thing with the kids, but this time was a disappointment.

I love this place!  My dog was having tummy issues and I found Cimarron online.  I travel between California and Arizona and did not yet have a vet.  They fit him in first thing the next morning.  The facilities are clean and beautiful.  The receptionist, vet tech, and doctor were the best!  They were all upbeat, welcoming and helpful.  They showed genuine concern for my dog and showered him with compliments, scratches, hugs and even kisses.  There was no long wait and pricing was reasonable.  They ran some tests and called me back within half hour of leaving with the results.  So happy I found Cimarron!  We will be customers for years to come!

This place was actually recommended to e and my boyfriend by my Vietnamese roommate. We were craving Pho and she said this was one of the best places to get it. 

The place seemed a little strange to me in the way that it was orientated to sit, but I usually feel that way when entering an unfamiliar restaurant. The person running front of house ended up seating us at a two person table, directly next to where a table of three was sitting. Which, normally wouldn't bother me, but there was about a half inch gap between tables. We were practically dining with them. I felt very invasive of their privacy considering I could hear every bit of their conversation, and majority of the time ended up being distracted by it. It would be one thing if there were no other seats available and that is where they sat us, but there was an empty table for two one row over and no people sitting at the table next to it.

Honestly, that's my only complaint. The service was quick, as was the wait for our food. We both got pho ga (chicken pho). It was delicious and the portion size was big enough for us both to split it and be full. And to top it off, the bill was only about $13 for two huge portions of food. Very delicious. Very cheap. Would definitely come back for more despite being very close to other dining patrons.

This club/bar mash up is NOT the business!  We came here one Saturday and left completely underwhelmed and sober.  It was just a drag.
