If I remember correctly, it was PRIDE weekend so we were expecting the place to be "poppin'" as the young kids would say.  There was only one server for the entire place (guess everyone else called out to party) and it literally took 17 minutes for us to get a menu.

FINALLY, we got menus.  We ordered wings and fries (I think) which were okay, but I remember getting a to-go box.  We NEVER have left over wings, so I think we were just over it and ready to go somewhere else that would give us life.

I don't think we'll be back unless bribed by a group of friends... seeing as how I know almost no one in Philadelphia, I think its safe to say we won't be back :-)

Oh, almost forgot... the ONE saving grace of the night. JELLO SHOT BOYS!!  Well, one in particular.  He was friendly, adorable and actually got me to take a jello shot with whipped cream!  I'm not a fan of jello because it reminds me of hospitals and toothless seniors, BUT, I was game that night :-)

I've had a hypothesis that if a restaurant has great neon lighting, then my experience will be wonderful. Pho Xe Lua proves my hypothesis correct.

As we entered, we were automatically seated on the first floor. Service was extremely attentive and we had our dishes within ten minutes. I ordered 101. The bowl was definitely bigger than my face and consisted of clear, delicious broth, vermicelli, and different cuts of meat. I always feel like pho places skimp out on the beef, but they went all out in my bowl. I even had a few good chunks of beef afterwards, which never happens! My partner ordered a vermicelli dish, which I can't recall right now (although I'm pretty sure it was 301). It was also very good, but looked tiny compared to my humongous pho bowl. A lot of people have criticized their cleanliness/décor. I'm not sure if they were expecting P.F Changs décor, but it seems like a typical Asian restaurant to me. Our bill totaled to $14 and some change - so if you're trying to get the bang for your buck during the winter months - definitely come here!

This restaurant provides a variety of breakfast and lunch options and is a decent pick for a "breakfast all day" place. I recently went and ordered pancakes for about $11 (not including tip and tax) and they were good. However, something I wish I knew before I went to Sandler's On 9th is that the prices of most of the dishes are over $10 and so these pancakes were one of the cheaper options on the menu. If you're looking for a cheaper breakfast/brunch/lunch option this may not be the place for you, but the quality of the food and ambiance make it a nice restaurant to eat at once in a while and it is good for groups :)
If you're looking for vegetable pho this place is without a doubt the best in the city. Their menu is enormous as well and will satisfy a wide range of what you're craving.

Visited here this weekend and met with nicest girl on Bumble Bff! It was so great to have someone to show me around the area and the food was incredible. Great atmosphere to meet and chat with someone new I would definitely recommend!
It's awesome. I love it.  Fast lunch, quick service. Always friendly.  This is now my go-to spot in Chinatown for vermicelli and pho.

People who've been going to this place as long as I have all know that it's really called CHOO CHOOs =)  I mean, with a neon train in the front window, what else could this place be called?? But name, aside, those who know Choo Choo also know that they have some of the best fruit smoothies, particularly the Avacado, Durian (for the brave) or Strawberry. 

Some of the other notable dishes from here include the Vietnamese beef carpaccio (Bo Tai Chanh) and the Bo Luc Lac (Lemongrass Beef Cubes with Watercress Salad).  A couple other of my favorites include the Thai coconut mini escargots and the beef sate stew served with wide rice noodles......yum!!!  Think I need a a Choo Choo fix right now! Haha

Went here on a Saturday. Place was dead. Took almost 2 hours to get food. Waitresses were rude and snobby. I've eaten at fast food places that had better service. When our party wanted refills or some bread while waiting for food the waitresses felt like we were bothering them. Too much to list for complaints just simply go elsewhere food is s

Visited here for early dinner on Saturday about 2 months ago. The place was almost empty. We were seated promptly by the server from the bar but when we responded we didn't want wine, he removed the wine glasses not holding them from the outside but by putting his fingers inside them. Not hygienic!
They gave us water and menus. We ordered an avocado toast with beacon and an egg breakfast. The avocados color was dark which indicates they were not fresh and very unappetizing. My companion only ate 1/3 rd of it. When we asked for our check the server didn't ask whether the food was to our liking. If the food was good I would have said the prices were ok. But given they gave us what they should have thrown in the garbage, it was over priced. But after observing how unhygienic one of the servers was, I will never go back.

I stopped in a day last week after yoga and ordered a clean it up juice with orange, pineapple, parsley, cucumber and lemon...so delicious!  The staff was warm and welcoming, the restaurant was bright and airy and the juice was so tasty.

Came in with a friend that had never been. Waitress refused to speak to me in English. I don't speak any Spanish. We ended up not getting food at all because they were so rude and dismissive. The music was so loud at 1:00pm on a Sunday it was like a club on sat night. Won't be back...
Excellent  , food , service. Chicken Marcella  very good. Thursday night  music  6-8 great country singer !

Excellent dinner. We sat at the bar and "amazing mike" was our bartender/server. He gave us his top 5 choices to pick from. He was spot on as the nachos were the best we've had and my burger  guy absolutely loved his burger with short ribs. It was so big he could finish all of it. It was cooked perfectly. Drinks were great and the brownie sundae Mike brought out for Scott's bday was super nice and delicious. Aly the owners daughter was very sweet making sure we were taken care of. We will def be back soon to try other things. This was a great recommendation from a friend who is foodie himself. 
You must give this place a try. Check out their menu you won't be disappointed. 

ENJ

Always looking for a new place to lunch around this part of town, it's the middle between me and my girlfriend for our weekly lunch meetups, and what a great find this was. This place is new and the menu is full of tasty sounding food. Sadly I am keto during the week and I got a burger with a side salad. It was a delicious burger, cooked well. But I totally want to go back and try like the whole menu. We were there at 11 on a Tuesday and the place was fairly busy. Lots people with children, so this place is very kid friendly, they have a funny kid menu even ("you pick" = chicken nuggets, "I am not hungry"= cheese burger" they also have a bar, I don't know how happening it is at happy hour, but would give it a try.

Awful. The pump stopped at 67 cents twice after I paid $20! They finally had me move to a second pump and I was completely frustrated. Staff seems incompetent and didn't seem to care I was inconvenienced at all. Food wasn't that great either. Wouldn't come back.

Apparently this place (aka Choo-choo's) recently changed owners/management. Based on our most recent visit, the taste of the pho has changed....not for the better. It had an unexpectedly sweet taste, not the deeply flavored bone taste we were looking for. The meat and accompaniments were still good. We also tried the chargrilled pork and shrimp and spring roll with fresh vegetables on vermicelli noodles. When everything is mixed together and topped with the sauce provided, it was good and very filling. The vermicelli noodles had no real flavor when tasted independently of the other ingredients, they were also a little limp and cool in temperature. Service was fast.

BEST pho in Chinatown!

The broth is one of the better broths i've ever had! AND the extra large bowl is EXTRA FREAKING LARGE. 

Also, they have so many servers standing around, you are bound to get as much attention as you ask for. I asked for extra lemons and I almost had three servers walk away to get some.
This place is amazing! I live in La but come here to see my man on the weekends.. Didn't think I could find a good healthy spot in Tucson.. So happy I did!! I will be here every weekend!

Let me start by saying the service was excellent.  That being said, the food was underwhelming.  We started with the calamari and the antipasto.  The calamari was decent but nothing to write home about, the antipasto had a good selection of meats and cheeses and was quit good, but don't believe anything on the board was actually made in-house.  I had the soup, which was albondigas, it was hot and very good.  Should have ordered a bowl, because I ordered the porterhouse and that is where things took a turn for the worst.  It was thin, like something you would get at Golden Coral.  That I can deal with but don't charge $44.00 for it and please by all means make sure it's warm.  My steak was so cold, the fat was congealed and coated the roof of my mouth as I ate it.  My wife had the Rib-eye and spaghetti, steak was the same and the spag tasted like it came from a can.  It wasn't inedible but, for $300 for a party of 4 I expected a lot more.  I think I will let them work the bugs out and give it another shot.  Until then my rating stands.

Interesting ambiance and menu. Italian bistro meets the old west. Had the clam chowder which was tasty but a bit runny. Also had the ribeye and spaghetti. Spaghetti and meatballs was better than I expected, more than an afterthought. Ribeye was very flavorful and tender. Daughter had prime rib which she enjoyed. Peach cobbler topped things off perfectly. Nice place, would return again if we lived in the area.

Solid solid pho in the heart of chinatown. 

Nothing wrong, nothing amazing. Just come for good grubbing.

I like ICandy from time to time.  It's good for a change, even tho looking for a 'change' in the Gayborhood is kind of a lost cause when it comes to clubby bars and such.  Not a fan of the club scene, I tend to stay downstairs mostly.  For some odd reason, the lower level of ICandy resembles a Mexican restaurant.. not sure why and honestly I don't want to think about it too much.
They have random drink specials, but when they're not having drink specials, expect to spend WAY too much for a drink.
There is a new bar area upstairs labeled as 'Liquid'..  Mostly white.  Prince would appreciate it.
The staff is nice, and service is usually quick.  The bar is big, so you never really feel too crowded here.

Had high expectations for this place since all my foodie friends rated it so well, but I'm going with a solid 2.5. Came for brunch. The menu items sounded amazing, but the food was mediocre and bland. I had to salt and pepper just to taste the eggs on my crabby benny. And the service was slow. They overcharged us for drinks when the menu clearly stated lower prices. With all the great brunch options in the city, I definitely won't be coming back.

They are closed on Wednesdays. This place has decent Vietnamese food if you don't want to head all the way down to South Philly. In Chinatown, this place gets packed on the weekends. The Pho was good, but I wish they had the tiny trays to put Siracha and Hoisin Sauce. I ended up having to put the sauce in my tea cup. Service was ok, my waiter looked pissed off but I'm sure he was just having a bad day.

I ordered an açaí bowl (the mango one) and a rice teriyaki veggie bowl with tofu. The açaí bowl was delicious! Fresh fruit and the perfect amount to eat with the açaí smoothie! There was a lot of honey, but who can complain about that !! 

The veggie bowl was good as well.

I wish they could have some vegan options for sandwiches!

Thanks!

Fresh and healthy ingredients is the signature of Goodness. I highly recommend their acai bowls, specifically the Cacao Warrior -- Full of berries, hemp seeds, chia seeds, cacao nibs and cool refreshing acai. Also recommend the breakfast burrito - busting with quinoa, homemade fresh salsa, eggs, turkey sausage. Honestly, one of the best breakfast burritos we've ever had and didn't make you feel gross after! Very satisfied every time I leave!
Great food, amazing customer service, the bartender recommended a French toast special that was fire!

Took my granddaughter here last week before a play at Walnut St Theatre. It was only one block away and very easy to get to. We took train to Jefferson station and walked there. We were seated in the are overlooking the lobby and it was beautiful and quiet. The menu choices were great for both an 11 year old and myself. The service was perfect and the prices were right ! Even my wine was reasonable ! I would highly recommend it and I will return again !

My wife craves a good pho and having just gone to Hop Sing Laundromat, this place was the highest rated pho place nearby. It's definitely a hole in the wall but we were seated right away and our food came out literally under five minutes. I ordered the well done beef pho and the meat had little fat on it. It was good but I definitely had to add some of the table sauces to it to make it pop more. It wasn't the best pho I've had but it wasn't bad.

Don't be fooled by the spotty decor, this is the best Vietnamese food in Philadelphia.!!!!!  I've been in love with the vietnamese cuisine for sometime now and can spot a fake by just smelling their fish sauce, and looking at the yellowish/ redish tint.  The pho train gets it right on every mark.  The food here is as authentic as can be.  It is an absolute hidden gem!!!!!

Booked this on OpenTable for a table of 12 and we were able to secure their semi-private room for our Saturday brunch. Took us forever to get seated but this is American comfort food as advertised! I had something called the Braised-N-Confused, which was very tasty. Although it says it comes on a roll, there is so much cheese and grease on it that I used a knife and fork instead. My only complaint was with the mimosa, which they forgot to add whatever it was to make it raspberry. They seemed pretty understaffed at the time and we had to ask for the check way ahead of time for it to even show up when we were done eating. My friend said that their bacon fried rice was just "okay" as well.

4.5 Btw that half a  star is coming when they get the liquor license.

Though brand new, Sandler's hits a homer on the first pitch. Staff greets you at the door and honestly are excited and attentive and seem vested in making your dining experience pleasurable.

We had the mustard pretzel chicken app and the tuna poke tacos. Ingredients were fresh and delicious. Great crunch to the chicken and the serving size could feed 3.

You have to have the bucatini pasta. If you have company, order the crab cake, one of the best in the city, and I live here, so I know. Lump crab, great spices, and crispy top.  We had the burgers and the lobster roll on another visit and they were superb. 

Dessert were chocolate dipped ice cream cone sampler and the Oreo cookie creme brûlée'.  Now they do offer breakfast all day, and when a plate of banana topped pancakes passed by, my Mother almost fell out of her seat. 

The kids will love this place. The adults will love this place.  And when the wine comes ...! I got a quick peek at the planned list, and I have enjoyed more than half the bottles on the expansive list. I said expansive not expensive. But  I will let the management tell you about that.

We visited late afternoon on Sunday my husband ordered the pork saltimbocco with a side of shrimp scampi I had the filet with a side of spaghetti and meatballs. Everything was amazing!!! My husband raved about the saltimbocco and generous side of shrimp scampi my filet was perfectly cooked. Patrick, our waiter was attentive and friendly
We will definitely be coming back!! I would have posted a pic of our amazing meal but it looked and smelled so good that I forgot to, next time for sure I will!!

I come here a lot in the morning after my first class and I enjoy it a lot. Their food is fresh and I love the pink dragon bowl! 

Tip: ask for one of the acai or pitaya  bowls in smoothie form if you don't feel like using a spoon or enjoy the smoothie portion better!

My only thing is that their plates and dishes can be a bit inconsistent, probably because of the kitchen. One salad can have little dressing then the next day it's drenched in it. The portions are small fyi. 

It's definitely a healthy alt for your lunch or meal so check it out!

My second time here.  I really like this place!

Dropped in after an appointment at Jefferson.  The place is clean and appealing.  TVs for those who want; glass walls for those (like me) who'd prefer to people watch.

Last time I sat at the bar and enjoyed great wine while doing some work on my laptop.  Today I enjoyed their all day breakfast.  Phenomenal omelette.  Coffee was great (and i am very picky; most coffee is too weak for me).  

Best of all was the server, Billy.  He was attentive and friendly without being overbearing.  One of the best servers I've had anywhere in a long time.

I know I'll be back, and soon.

This is a great spot for a quick Pho fix! The service was lightening fast and the the Pho was plentiful and super delicious. The Summer Rolls were a bit disappointing - the rice paper was too thick and the consistency was off, they were skimpy on the shrimp and they were not de-veined. Too bad because the peanut sauce was really tasty. Everything on the menu is very affordably priced, including the alcohol. They do have a full bar and most cocktails are $5 - $6. This place is definitely worth a visit if you're in the mood for Pho!

No hassle for coins! Operate the machine and pay via your smartphone. The place always clean. Free WiFi, Not to mentioned they give you 15 mins time that you can reserve the machine while you are on the way..

Excellent Mexican food in West chase! Especially their corn tacos, for gluten free diets there's are the best in town.   We ordered Asada (steak), pollo (chicken) and Barbacoa (shredded beef) tacos ($2.99 ea) and really enjoyed the steak and barbacoa; chicken was a bit dry. We also ordered quest dip ($4.25) and it was authentic and excellent.  Place is reasonably priced and defiantly hit the spot!
Everything we have ordered are good. Especially the vegetarian options are abundant. I really liked the vegetable pho and pad Thai. Would definitely recommend this place.

JUST ASK FOR NICOLE 

The only thing better than the brunch menu at Sandler's...is the service. Lead server Nicole brought our Prosecco pitcher to the table faster than I a chubby kid goes down on a see saw! 10/10 would recommend

I had a really disappointing experience here earlier today.  I've been here before and have generally had the pho/vietnamese fare.  My previous experience with the food were generally good.  I thought if this place as one of the better places in the neighborhood.  

I ordered the wide noodles with seafood (not exactly sure what it was called).  I was with a friend and our food came out FAST...like too fast.  Like, not enough time for something to be stir fried correctly.  

The noodles were in a dish a very bland, lukewarm sauce with tons of cornstarch.  Visual appearance of the dish looked much different than the picture of the menu.  Upon putting the dish down, the server looked unsure if this is what I had indeed ordered.  Ummm...he's the one who's working at the restaurant...shouldn't he be confidently presenting dishes to the tables?  

Back to the seafood noodles...the seafood was not very warm and quite slimy with absolutely no flavor.  Just odds and ends of different frozen fish products...far below the quality I was expecting.  

The noodles of this dish were REALLY overcooked...they were disintegrating into a starchy mess right in front of my while I was trying...you'd have to use a spoon for these noodles.  

It made me wonder if they had it all assembled beforehand and just heated it up...really gross food and unlikely I will be back.

Fantastic find!! Such a cool place with amazing food. The Cacao Acai Bowl was the best I've ever had!! The food came out fast and they have so many healthy options and the best thing is it's not vegan! You can get chicken, etc!! It's rare to find a super healthy place that isn't vegan or vegetarian. I will be back!
Love this place. Awesome food for great prices and amazing service. Especially love the Pad Thai with shrimp and tofu and any of the Phos.

I get the breakfast sandwich with goat cheese instead of bleu cheese and it is to die for. 
Yummmmmy!

Stopped here on a road trip from Tucson to Texas and were really happy with our stop. I got an acai bowl and my brother got the breakfast bowl. Both were healthy, light and delicious. It was a cute set up too -- easy to relax and chill at.

Consistently decent Vietnamese food for some of the cheapest prices you'll find in Philly. My friends and I go here all the time for a nice big bowl of pho and it never disappoints. Service is okay, nothing more or less than expected. A good place if you're in the area and hungry with a few bucks in your pocket.

Visited Sandler's last Wednesday for a work lunch. We tried the bacon on a stick and the Philly cheesesteak scotch egg. Both were incredible. I had never had a scotch egg before and the cheesesteak twist was delicious! The bacon was thick cut with a spicy maple dipping sauce. Delicious and great presentation. For my entree I ordered the Cobb. This thing is MASSIVE. The bowl was so big I almost needed to stand up to eat it. I would definitely go back and try some of the additional seafood options

Oh my goodness...I have to embrace all my new BFF's.... Philly yelpers, you rock.  Let me just start off by saying you saved me from myself. I was thinking...  "Well hell, I'm in Philly, I had better get myself a Philly cheese-steak."  I would still be writhing from that gut bomb ( not that I wouldn't have enjoyed every whiz filled morsel).  I almost did it, however.... with the rain a bowl of pho sounded like a good comforty idea   Being from San francisco I have to admit I have a hard time trusting ethnic food outside my seven mile by seven mile food utopia on
the west coast.  Philly yelpers steered me right....I wish I has someone to 
share this experience with.  The broth on my pork chop pho was perfectly spiced, not to salty.  My thin grilled pork chop was exactly like I dream of them...with a grilled sweet flavor that I will be craving for weeks to come.  I was so caught up in the experience that I took a take out menu.....ummmmm three thousand miles might be a little difficult.   Maybe I'll just sleep with it under my pillow and have sweet pho dreams.

It's a very simple club. 3 floors. During the summer the sky deck is open which you're able to smoke, sit and relax and enjoy the outdoors. Everyone has been friendly except for the owner, but the staff def. makes up for it. It's a nice DL location for anyone who wants to get away from the scene for a bit, but still wants to go out. It's very easy to make personal connections at 12th air.

Solid place in Chinatown for Pho. I ventured and tried the tripe here. Ive had it cooked other ways and liked it. However, I learned I dont like it in my pho.  I still prefer my favorite place in south philly but this place will do. Service here was fine.  I'm just happy they refilled my water without me asking. It's a fast casual restaurant so I don't understand people complaining about service. Staff was very friendly every time I've been here.

I saw this new restaurant pop up on Yelp so I decided to check it out.  You can guess the theme of the establishment based on the name.  In the same vein, I will attempt to describe the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly of my experience (though I'll do it in reverse order).  Ordered the Spagetti and Ribeye for dinner and Cobbler and ice cream for dessert. 

First the Ugly, the place from the outside looks like some run down diner.  The signage is poor.  I passed it 3 times thinking that can't be it and the signage wasn't clear while driving by.  All I could see what "Classic'.  I was looking for Spagetti or Steakhouse.  Oh it is there on the sign but not unless you are going slow taking your eyes off the road for too long of time to be safe.  I finally pulled in to check my phone and I accidentally was in the right place.

Next the Bad, the Spagetti was eh.  The noodles were too done for me.  They weren't mushy but they weren't al dente either.  The sauce was totally uninteresting as was the meatballs.  They meatballs were firm and had nice consistency but no real flavor.

Finally the Good, the Ribeye was great.  It was a large piece of meat cooked to perfection.  It was tender.  I really enjoyed it.  It made the meal!  It would be worth going back just for that.

Like most of my reviews, I comment about the service.  This place knows about service.  They were right on top of everything without being overbearing.  All of the servers were friendly without being overly friendly.

Though a bit pricey (Spagetti and Ribeye was $33), overall it was a good experience.  I would like to give it a try again and maybe try one of their other pasta dishes.
It is a very good restaurant, Cuban and other kinds of food are exelent, taste delicious and very well done. Family environment. I recommend it to everyone.

This group is amazing. We had a party of 20 and we were accommodated graciously! The management here welcomed us with a red carpet. No reservations but we called ahead and they had a table waiting! The birthday girl was so delighted! Thank You Olive Garden
Our food was fantastic as usual! 
Tour of Italy enough for 2 and a take home!
The chocolate mousse cake.....WOW

I've been meaning to dine here for a while, and got the chance to do so for a very late brunch on Labor Day. Seating was ample and immediate, and the restaurant did not look very busy. We ordered the chicken and bacon waffles (delicious! get!) which hit the spot. We also ordered the cheddar bacon burger with fries which was also delicious. Portion sizes were good but a little smaller than competing restaurants, especially for the price. My only major complaint was the slow service. Service was friendly but the food took a long time to come out and we had to flag down ketchup ourselves. Not sure if this was because of the holiday, but the quality of the food made up for the service. 4/5

Ordered Arugula salad without avocado because I am very very allergic to it. Received salad timely but WITH avocado. I returned it stating such and they took it to remake it. I received the same salad back w same fork, they did NOT remake it and it STILL had avocado in it. I explained that my throat would close if I eat avocado and to please remake it. I can't believe they would risk someone's health just because they didn't want to remake a simple salad. smh

Great food, especially for the health conscious.   The staff, on the other hand seem like a mostly uptight, miserable crew.   Something I'm more accustomed to back in Jersey.  In fact they often seem perturbed if you don't order and move on chop chop even if they're not busy at all.
Stood at the hostess desk for 10 minutes with no acknowledgement what so ever. We were noticed but no reaction to tty and sit us with a restaurant full of empty seats. Left highly disappointed.
Textbooks say you can't catch STDs from toilet seats but those textbooks have never been to ICandy

If anyone ever touches my Choo Choo, I will rage like the star wars kid on you! The only complaint, and its the ONLY one is that this place isn't open 24/7. Because if it was, I'd bring my toothbrush, blanket, and set up upstairs... Away from the customers... OBVIOUSLY!

I go there all the time with my wife, and each time is better than the next. Their Pho is basically a mini swimming pool, if a swimming pool was a hot steaming cauldron of fatty marrow, sublime chicken broth, and accompanied by your standard Pho fare. But what makes this place stand out to me is the variety of other good food that is on the menu, so let me start on those.

First, there is coconut snails. O sweet lord, that is ultimate beer drinking food. You get that with some 333 or Tiger beer? O man every time I'm there it reminds me of my youth. Not that I drink when I was young... at all... ever. Then there is the Papaya salad, holy crap that is just the best when accompanied with the beer. 

This is a place that defines happiness, from the families that sits around and talks about their day. To the older couple with their grandchildren enjoying each other at the round table. To the cute high school or college couple who are awkwardly trying to feel each other out on the first date. To the couple like myself and my wife who are just getting drunk in the corner, well ok I'm getting drunk and my wife is getting high off the food.

This place is the best place for everything Vietnamese.

I'm no food connoisseur nor do i claim to be one but i do know what my taste buds like and Surprisingly WAWA has the best breakfast sandwich i have had in such a long time! The fact that my favorite breakfast meal comes from a trucker rest stop makes it all the more surprising & shocking!

perhaps it is just this location who made my sandwich piping hot and fresh, but it DEF was on point. I don't think i can ever start a morning on a good note now with out one of these in my belly before i step into the office. They must have put some sort of special chemical droplets inside that i don't know about because these sandwiches are like crack, i keep coming back for more ha! I haven't yet dared to venture outside of my Sausage, egg & cheese on a crossant because everything else will fail in comparison and i don't want to start the day on a bad note. SO here i am now for the past week finding myself in WAWA to grab one of these hot treats so that i can officially start my day right.

To further confess my love for this treat: the croissant is crispy & buttery, the sausage actually is a decent size, the egg is fluffy and the white cheese in the middle combines with everything to make the sandwich a melting perfection of breakfast goodness. My only gripe here is that my breakfast wasn't bigger! Then again for $2.49 who cares!

If you want a place with no-frills, but cheap and tasty Vietnamese food, with efficient service, this is the place to go.  The grilled sirloin beef cubes (don't know the dish's actual name) and the beef wrapped in grape leaf appetizer have been consistently good.  Although the pho is not the best I've had, it is tasty and comes in huge bowls.  The grilled chicken on rice is very good too.  Generally, I've found their vegetable dishes good.  If you're a little adventurous, try their fried frog legs.  

It's also nice that the waitstaff is generally nice and efficient.

We had the beet salad and tomato soup. Salad was good, but don't expect any extras. No bread, toast, or crackers. Just a salad. As for the tomato soup, don't waste your $4. It was a very basic small bowl containing a tomato-like substance. Bland! A little on the loud side. Now we know...
This club has something for everyone in its expansive three floors. We loved the friendly and diverse crowd. It blows any bar or club in SF out of the water in terms of size and diversity.

I was initially going to try out another pho place but since it wasn't open at 11 (even though it said it would be open), I decided to try this one instead (since they open at 10:30).  Typical of most pho places this place was a no frills kind of place: decor was lacking and the service was fine.  I ordered pho with meatballs and before I put all of the other stuff in it (sriracha, hoisen sauce, herbs) I try the broth; if the broth is good, the pho is going to be good.  And it *was* pretty good.  I was satisfied.

I have been here couple of times, sits on corner, it was closed-temporarily, for remodeling, .My parents like It there. Their variety of Pho & soup dishes , amazing, actually too big...but nice assortment. The waitstaff & service is good, like the summer rolls, & soups are good, but of course, when its Hot out, not craving soup!! not just yet!!

I have been using these guys for several years specially for direct hook up for natural gas to a barbecue from my house line. I am selling my current home and leak was detected on inspection. It turned out that it was just a very simple fix and these guys did not charge me and were very honest about their repair when they could've easily charge me. 
Because of their honesty I will surely use them for my new home.

This place should disassociate itself from any reference to Thai food.  They are only good at Vietnamese food and nothing else.  We ordered two Thai dishes and they were extremely bland. We ended up giving the food to a homeless person.  Also, they took about 15 minutes to bring the margarita when we were already half way through our meal.  

The only pro is that they bring out the food really quickly.

I was hoping the Pho would be better than Pho in NYC but it wasn't in Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai Restaurant in Philly. 

I had mine plain with no bean sprouts and no basil. Part of it is allergy problems and part is bean sprouts can taste too muddy sometimes for me or tastes like it is not fresh. Not sure if that is the same taste because I don't like the taste of raw bean sprouts. 

I'll explain why...my bf took all the bean sprouts and poured it into his soup. He noticed how funny it tasted to a point where he could not finish his soup. He thought his soup was tasting odd. I told him because it's the bean sprouts. I was right. He said they didn't clean the sprouts. EUW. He said he saw the shells/hulls falling off all the sprouts when he put it into the soup. He thinks the restaurant didn't clean the sprouts by soaking them in clean water. Euw they served dirty sprouts. That is disgusting. 

I thought my soup was blah and so was my meat. I had higher expectations for Pho in Philly because everyone says Pho in NYC is bad..okay it's not that great in Philly so far either. 

I spilled tea by accident and the waiter who was standing behind me did ABSOLUTELY NOTHING. Wow. Bad service. 

If you drink alcohol, they serve alcohol at this Pho joint!
Excellent food! The green chili pot roast was delicious. Nice ambience- would recommend it

I really appreciate the menu and the concept of the restaurant, but I think it really misses the mark in execution. The food seems to be kind of slapped together and isn't prepared with any thought or care. I ordered the quinoa salad, and was disappointed to find that the lettuce was wilted and the quinoa was undercooked. For a "health food" restaurant, and an expensive one at that, I would expect more.

Snails. Lobster.  SOFT SHELL CRAB!!!  What more can you ask for?  Perhaps decent Pho at a Vietnamese restaurant.  Does Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai Restaurant deliver? 

the answer would be...a resounding YES! YES! YES!

The broth tastes as it should...FLAVORFUL!!!  The portions are huge.  The large was more than I could handle.  Order #101 if it is your first time eating Pho.

The waiters are great as well.  Your water cup will never run dry.   Very attentive staff.

Come try this joint if it's your first time trying Vietnamese food or if you are a tried and true Pho fan.   Either way, you won't be disappointed.

I always enjoy the food here and the service!  Just an FYI this is a place where you are sitting very close to your neighboring tables.  I can never remember the names of my entrees but I can recommend the spring rolls and thai iced tea.  One weird minus is the location of the bathroom (basically in the kitchen/waiter area).

Allie was amazing! We arrived with 2 kids and a 25 minute wait, not knowing we needed a reservation. We had tickets to a show, and Allie (a manager and host) totally went above and beyond to accommodate us. She sat us as quickly as possible, took our order to expedite it to the kitchen, brought us fries for our hungry little ones, and checked in multiple times to ensure we'd be able to eat and make it to the show. 

Thanks so much!  You made our day great!

Wanting lunch before the play:

Sadly this is a case of wait staff either enhancing or killing your experience.    I am sure the tables around us had a good experience.    Training isn't that hard to do.   So it's most likely more the managers fault, but it falls on the waitress.   Which is a simple fix.    Ours was a four strikes and you're out experience.   It's like everything went wrong.    Tables around us had quick, competent service while we:  waited for menus's.  Waited to order, waited 13 minutes (I timed it) for our drinks to be served.  (A beer and a Prosecco).   Waitress forgot to put in the order.    We ordered  two apps, which one was wrong and the avocado toast took 35 minutes, which we finally cancelled.    The manager came up after we cancelled the toast and said something about having two different items on the menu and was nice enough to take the toast off our bill.      I feel like I might be the most forgiving customer on the planet and wanted this to work out.   The brisket poutine with fried eggs, despite not having the eggs was still tasty.   But our service was simply a comedy of errors. Serves us right for not going back to Craftsman Row which has always been fantastic. 




The play at Walnut Street theater was awesome by the way.

Tried the "Mango Jungle," and boy was it mango-licous. The fruit toppings were extremely fresh and packed full of flavor.  However, there was a bit too much honey in the bowl for my liking. The bowl also had an amazing crunch to it, so I would def recommend for those that love texture with their foods. I also had their chocolate chunk pretzel cookie; this might not be the exact name, but anyways it was amazing. I'm not usually a fan of sweets with a salty element, but this is honestly a treat I see myself consistently ordering. 

Loved the relaxed atmosphere of the restaurant, and the food came out pretty quickly. Service was excellent...I left my wallet in the car, and by the time I returned my order was prepared and all I needed to do was pay!

It's ok, and it's certainly nice to have another option in the gayborhood. I'm a little confused as to why the drinks are small, weak and expensive on the second floor, but much larger, cheaper and stronger on floors one and three. Shouldn't the same establishment have uniform quality and pricing?

I must say this place is awesome.  I order it for a office lunch and now 3 weeks later I am sitting here enjoying my wonderful service from server Nicole D. She has been nothing bust sweet and knowledgeable.  What good on the menu and what you absolutely can't pass  up! To the point  that she has know talked me in to the OREO  Creme brulee and is toasting it in front of me table side.  I will be back.

sooo good. ive had everything from the tofu tacos, bowls, salads, and smoothies. I've never had a bad experience here. Also, the dude w/ the long hair @ the counter is super cool and friendly. He always seems like he's enjoying himself at work.
This is a great spot for brunch. Really enjoyed the salted caramel French toast. They have pitchers of mimosas. The raspberry mimosa was really good.

Came for dinner but don't think they cater to dinner. The place was empty except the bar. Wound up ordering eggs which were good but over priced. Generally the place is not clean and sits next to the gorgeous Ben Franklin Lobby.
It's obviously a breakfast brunch place. If open for dinner should pay attention to this meal and create a dinner feeling.

Very good pho, just try to avoid any of the meat varieties with copious fat-chunks in them.  To be frank, it's a bit of a turn-off to see huge mounds of cow fat floating around in your soup, especially when the other beef selections are so much tastier.  Other than that, enjoy this authentic and very tasty purveyor of Vietnamese cuisine.

I'm a fan of Goodness!

I went there two weekends ago to grab some brunch with my SO.  As a vegetarian, I really appreciate the variety of meals on the menu.  They're super filling, healthy and tasty. I ordered the breakfast burrito with quinoa, eggs, and avocado.  It made me very happy. 

Meat eaters can rejoice too!  My BF got a sandwich which left him full for the rest of the day.

Fast and excellent service at great prices :)

I wanted to try this place because I want to start eating healthy, but I LOVE EATING OUT. Being an addict to fast food I didn't LOVE this place, but, BUT I will say it was pretty good and the serving sizes are pretty good. 

My order was the Teriyaki Veggie bowl. The broccoli and carrots were cooked well and tasted fresh. The sauce was a bit on the salty side. For a drink I had the Beach Bod. This drink was very good and had a lot of flavor; it did not have an overpowering powdery taste from the protein.

I went there yesterday with a couple of ny church friends. This restaurant has over a 100 choices of food to choose from. I recommend getting one of their pho or curry rice dishes. The price is inexpensive and the waiting time is short!

Sundaze yogurt is one of the only things I miss about living in Tucson! The owners are obviously passionate about excellent customer service, and I can't think of a time I walked out without a smile. They provide a wide variety of toppings and are changing their flavors on a weekly basis. It also helps that they post their upcoming flavors on Facebook so you know exactly when your favorite yogurt is here! I make it a point to get Sundaze whenever I am back in town, and recommend it to anyone visiting or living in Tucson.

Nice little spot in Chinatown on Race Street. Given the location, if you're driving, it will only be street parking (which is fairly typical for Chinatown). We had to circle around a few times before finding a spot that was 2 blocks away from the restaurant. It was a bit chilly out so naturally the walk felt A LOT longer than it was in distance. 

The cuisine is a medley of Asian options - between Vietnamese and Thai. I think the main draw is the pho (especially on colder nights, such as the one we visited this restaurant.) 

I didn't see any vegetarian pho options on the menu, so instead ordered their Phad Thai. In hindsight, I think they may have a vegetarian/vegan broth with veggies, but I opted for the noodle dish instead. My other guests did order the pho and were very pleased with the outcome. As for me, the Phad thai was well made (and without egg and mushrooms, per my specifications :]). The dish was savory but definitely required additional spices. I drizzled in a combination of the hoisson, chili oil, and jalepenos to get to a amped up spice level. 

In addition, we all opted to try their bubble tea! I chose the soybean drink with the tapoica and was pleasantly surprised on how good it was - not too sweet, and complimented the Phad Thai pretty well!

The service was very quick (which was awesome since we were all starved!) The place was fairly busy when we arrived, so we hung out for about 10 minutes. This worked out just fine though since we were served our glasses of water and had a chance to look through menu while a table was cleared for us. The waiters were attentive and fairly knowledgeable about the menu items. It did take some reaffirmation that any modifications to the menu items were noted, but other than that the food was prepped to everyone's liking.  

I think this spot works best if you want quality food - fast, coupled with the dine in experience. Would come back and venture for vegetarian pho, and if that is not a possibility, the Phad Thai is still a solid back up plan!

i didn't notice any thai dishes on the menu, but whatever. i got the flank 'n' tripe pho...the meat was good, but the broth was much too subtly spiced for my taste, i had to dump a bunch of sriracha and hoisin in there just to give it some flavor. i can't argue with the portion size though, i got the "large" (rather than the "extra large") and i'm still full seven hours later.

This is my second time in here. The first time I had a salad and it was pretty decent. But the reason I came back today was because last time I had some really awesome juice. Today I ordered a "vibrant health" juice which came with two kinds of beets and a few other goodies. All I can tell you is it was absolutely delicious. I asked for a small glass of ice on the side so I could cool it because it come served room temperature and I didn't want to compromise any of my juice amount by adding ice to the cup at first. Juice here can be a little pricey, but it is pricey everywhere else I've gone as well. Very fresh and very tasty.

I absolutely love Goodness. They offer delicious healthy fresh eats that are hard to come by in Tucson and I love that they open early! They serve breakfast, coffee, fresh juices, salads, sammies, acai bowls (one of the few in Tucson!), and more... I really couldn't ask for much more than that especially because everything is super yummy and the staff is really nice. When I'm in the area I definitely head here for a post workout green juice rather than a coffee which makes me at least feel like I'm starting off the day like the picture of health ;) Sure the prices are higher than your average fast food place but I am a firm believer that you get what you pay for. The ingredients are fresh and high quality. Compared to purchasing a bottled cold pressed juice their prices are actually cheaper! A 16oz Suja is nearly $9 at whole foods and you can get a 16oz juice at goodness for less than $6... plus they'll customize things for you if you ask. Sounds like a no brainer decision to me! I wish they would start selling bottled juices too. As their food goes I haven't been disappointed with anything yet and I'm on a mission to try their whole menu. I would recommend the azteca steak bowl without a moment of hesitation. From reading other reviews I was expecting to still be hungry after especially since I was starving when I walked in but the bowl was the perfect size and with the carbs from the brown rice, protein from the steak and healthy fats from the avocado it was perfectly filling and had some staying power. Icing on the cake? 10% military and student discount! My only tiny complaint was I went there to work one morning and between the slow WIFI that wouldn't let my VPN work and the loud music I had to go elsewhere for a conference call I needed to be on. Clearly not a deal breaker for me though and I probably could have asked them to turn down the music since I was the only person in the restaurant at the time. Welcome to Tucson, Goodness... happy to have you!

Our first vet in Tucson operated on the "I'll have my assistant bring in the medical plan" plan -- which almost always included everything but the kitchen sink (including liberal use of his own expensive equipment). On one visit, that very same doc mixed up the files of two of my dogs he encouraged me to bring in together. Two times, he spent more time trying to sell me one of this own music CDs than he did talking about my dogs! 

When my dread of going to the vet exceeded my dogs' dread level, it was time to look elsewhere. 

Cimarron Animal Hospital is even closer to my house than the first vet. They are competent, caring, kind and efficient -- not pushy or prone to guilt me into expensive treatments my dogs don't need. 

That's all we ask, right guys? (Ears perked, tails wagging) Right.
Worst service ever. Waitress was so rude to us. She was annoyed by every question we asked. Had a really strong perfume. Food was good but it took almost am hour to get. I won't ever come back

Best bargain restaurant in town!!!

Everything is so cheap but soooooooo  good. After 3 years trying, nothing on the menu failed me so far.  

Pad thai w/shrimp and beef chow fun are my favorite.

Goodness has a nice selection of modern eclectic food, and the food itself is delicious. I give it four stars because it's quite expensive. But if you don't mind the large expense I would highly recommend it. 
Favorites: "the goods" smoothie, tuna sandwich.

Don't question it. Just get here and get some delicious frozen yogurt. I left a picture with their low prices. Mom and pop owned place.

Got a punch card, yeah I'll be back.

My first visit was exceptional! I was warmly greeted by Shannon who explained the restaurant details to me since it was my fist visit. I had the turkey, goat cheese pesto sandwich and my friend had the beet salad. Both delicious! We split a piece of banana bread for dessert. Shannon warmed it up for us and delivered it with a big smile. 

The food was so good that I forgot to take pictures! Next time! I will be back because of the exceptional service and food!!

This review is for Goodness Kitchen on 6370 N Campbell.

This place was kinda of dead for a Friday night, especially coming from Woody's and Tavern, both of which were pretty packed as always. The venue itself was decent, very spacious with lots of different areas in which to hang out. There was just hardly anyone there to hang out with. Maybe business picks up on other nights, but for 1-2am on a Friday in the G'hood, this place was pretty empty. Not a good sign.

Goodness is always amazing! I'm in love with their Açai bowls! Especially the "Cocoa Warrior!" The breakfast burrito has the perfect ingredients inside that my friends and I talk about every time we go there. They have delicious juices to top it off! I've been many times and every single time it's simply satisfying, not one bad thing on the menu!  Love this place!

I thought the 12th Air Command was a decent bar...only because it dared to be different by the others with having arcade games.  LOL!  But, hey, isn't it fun to play Ms. Pac-Man while buzzed?!?  Yeah, let's see if you can beat my high score! Mmmm-hmmm, I thought so!

Anyways, I do have to agree with the others about the patrons there.  My friends and I walked in there and everyone turned to checked us out like we were fresh meats to, at least, a little lick of taste.  Gawd, what a freaky, awkward moment that was!

But then, they soon turned away and went right back to their own worlds and dramas.  I mean, there was this guy walking around the bar really fast, chasing someone.  Ugh, high school?  And, much to my surprise, he worked there!  O......k!

And I have to agree with Erin below.  I never realized it until she mentioned it.  Yes!!!!  There are mirrors in just about every gay bars in Philly!  What. Is. Up. With. That?!?!?!?

Other than that, 12th Air Command is different by being a little fun with arcade games, mirrored decor and "youthfulness".

The food here is pretty good. Never have had a problem. Today, my coworkers and I had a work lunch and our waitress was PLASTERED. Almost blacked out drunk. We were the only people in the restaurant and she messed our order up twice, had us waiting forever for the food and then the check. It was all quite entertaining but totally not acceptable for a restaurant like that.. She was stumbling, hiccuping and slurring her words fumbling for our check, then she had to muster all her might to fish her pen out of her apron. If you're planning on having dinner there tonight, i hope she sobers up in time for dinner service. Don't drink on the job hunnies, and if you do don't get so sloppy - it's not cute.

This is not a "pet friendly" community. They claim to be, but unless it's a dog or cat. They do not allow ferrets or other animals according to their corporate services. Was told they do before signing a 1 year lease. After living here and notifying them, they tell me no ferrets. Even when the lease doesn't state only cats and dogs allowed.

Consistently great food and great service both at the bar and the tables.  Highly recommend the Tomato Soup with Grilled Cheese Pop, Chicken Nicola and the Braised Short Rib entrée.  
They have an enclosed private room that is great for business dinners or smaller parties.

Fave Philly Pho spot 
It's not-so-secret but still underrated spot in chinatown. I used to dislike pho until I ate their pho. I don't even put the hoisin or sriracha sauce because their broth already is flavorful and well-seasoned. All for lk $7-8!
Their pho is literally what I crave the most when I'm hungover or sick over my mom's home-cooked miso soup. I used to get their pho nam with but recently they changed the meat or something because it's not the brisket-ty soft texture anymore. 
The phos come out super quickly usually. Other things take a little longer. Also you can ask the bean sprouts to be steamed. 

Their grilled lemongrass porkchops is my sister's go-to when we go there (we used to have a monthly hangout at that spot before she moved away). The lemongrass beef is good but they don't give you enough to fill you up. So porkchop or chicken seem to be better bang for buck situation. 

The vermicelli are also good of course, with big portions. 

They take card (visa, mastercard) but I think the minimum  is $10 or 15.

mmmmm choo choo!
    I am not the hugest pho fan in the world, but I do love me some pad thai, and they have the best pad thai in the city, especially for vegetarians.  the #617 - spicy veg pad thai - is to die for.  they give you a ton of it so I always get to enjoy leftovers the next day.
          Also, best Thai iced tea in the city.  And mmm unfried shrimp spring rolls.  and shrimp coconut curry.
I love love the Spaghetti that's all I can say. Ribeye was kinda tough so I wasn't enjoyable for me. I will definitely come back for spaghetti though. I love the sweetness to that sauce.
Good egg rolls, liked the shrimp cracker egg/rice noodle combo, but thought the broth was just ok. Huge portions, but Nam Phuong is still my go-to for pho.

Had dinner there on Wednesday night.   Terrific Food and a warm and inviting atmosphere with most seats filled at the bar to make it festive.  Tuna Poke Tacos were fantastic with spicy mayo mango chili salsa.  The Garlic Shrimp Pappardelle  was served with large shrimp and the pasta was cooked perfectly.    I sampled my date's Braised Short Rib Flanken and that dish was prepared just the way I like it, tender with lots of seasoning and flavor but not drowning in sauce.   Excellent beer and wine selection.

Incredible new restaurant. I'd recommend to anyone and will definitely be going back. 4 of us went and every meal was incredible.  You won't be able to tell by the outside or the neighborhood, but don't let that fool you. Inside you'll find a very professional staff, subtle lighting, quiet atmosphere and no down lighting in your face. Try the pino noir for sure! Just go!!
Cheap, fast, and delicious viet fare. This place never disappoints.

Wow wow wow! Everything from our duck quesadillas, steakhouse bacon, variety of burgers and Oreo creme brûlée was absolutely delicious! We were served at the bar with amazing service and great drinks. Clean and chic environment with great music choice I might add! Definitely will be back!

I had the chicken BLT and my business partner had a bison burger. Both were very good. It was lunch so we didnt order dinners. Service was very good as well. They do take reservations but didnt need one at lunch time. I would go back

Came yesterday with my boyfriend and 2 friends and I left somewhat disappointed.  I ordered some green mussel appetizer and a bowl of vegetable noodle soup.  The mussel appetizer came out and it was dry and overcooked.  You could clearly tell that they mussels were simply steamed and then had a chili-tomato sauce poured over it.  Unflavorful and dry.

The noodle soup I had specified to be vegetarian, but yet it still came out in a beef broth.  It wasn't until we spoke to somebody higher-up (the servers are hispanic and don't seem to understand English) came out and offered to remake it.  I said that it was alright, they didn't have to, but the boyfriend insisted on it.  So they made me another one but it was just unflavorful and anyway, by that time everyone had finished eating.. at the very least, they do put a whole lot of vegetables on there unlike other vegetable noodle soups I've had elsewhere.  Yet I guess in a noodle soup, it really is the broth that makes all the difference, and this one was simply just soy sauce in water (and that is what the chef said).  I can understand if they don't specialize in vegetable noodle soup, but if you're going to offer it, at least make it decently.  Otherwise, don't offer one..

Still, I do appreciate that the chef (or, whoever that was) remade it for me.  It's the effort that counts, I guess.

It was my first time here, and it wasn't the worst place I've gone to.  It's just that everything else I sampled here off my boyfriend's order like the salt baked squid was just normal like any other place in Chinatown too.  So, that coupled with a wrong order and an unappetizing starter gives it just 2 stars.  I won't hurry to come back here anytime soon.

The Filet Mignon with Lemongrass is so delicious.  There's lots of bell peppers in there too, so you get veggies.  I want to eat up all the sauce even after I'm full.

I've tried a few other dishes here that were solid:
Satay Clams with Casino - tasty and the greens were a nice addition
Satay Fried Frog Legs - tasty, but a little difficult to eat with all the little bones
 
The salt-baked seafood was not as good.

Came here and had the tom yum with seafood noodle bowl.  LOVED IT.  Whenever I go to a Thai restaurant and order my favorite soup, I always want more after I'm done.  Here, I ordered the tom yum and, let's just say, it was plenty of food for $7.  The reason for the 1 star down is because we ordered an appetizer and it never came.  Not a big deal because the regular size portion of noodle soup was plenty of food.  All-in-all, I will go back, but I definitely want to try that raw flank next time.

Classic American food with great decor and service. I'm a simple eater, so they had great options for me!  It's was pretty quiet when we went, so it was a very relaxed experience and definitely somewhere I'll be back to.

Decent Italian food but only go during non peak hours. During peak hours the line is almost always out the door. The food is usually decent, love that you get salad and breadsticks. Servers are usually hit or mess when it comes to personality.

Love that I can bring my dog with me on the patio! Never heard of a Cuban pizza but couldn't wait to try it. The mango drink was perfectly revitalizing without being too overpowering!  The shrimp cocktail came with HUGE Shrimp and a custom sauce that beings out the flavor of the shrimp. Love the pepperoni Cuban Pizza: Its CHEEEZZZY, Creamy, Chewy and delicious.

Fantastic!!! I wish I found this place sooner! We just happened to be walking by and stopped in. The staff was very welcoming and the food was fresh and hot. The homemade ranch was amazing! If I am back in Philadelphia any time soon I will be back!

I am here to clear the slate.... I had a very frustrating experience here one day, and it took a lot for me to return. But return I have and have now been in close to a dozen times, at all hours and have ordered something off of most sections of the menu.
I have consistently had great, pleasant, knowledgeable people take my orders and prepare my food!
I am quite pleased with the options and freshness of the food.
My one piece of advice would be to cook the veggies more thoroughly, they  sometimes come off rubbery.
I am looking forward to many more returns.

My boyfriend and I have begun exploring Chinatown recently. Our friend had recommended that we try this place. They had no idea what it was called, but told us you can't miss the giant, neon train in the window and they were right!

We had a really great meal here.They have a full bar and large portions. Their menu is huge and I was tempted to order my go-to of beef pho, but decided against it.  I was a little disappointed when my rice noodle dish had fried noodles, but the flavor was great and I was glad to try something new! Will definitely go back to try the Pho sometime!
This place has the best hookah in town!  I've been to hookah lounges throughout the world and nothing compares to this one.
Great atmosphere. Very good cuts of meat at very reasonable prices. The staff is great and friendly. The atmosphere in the bar is unique and fun.

Good Pho for a great price! The atmosphere is very dated and is essentially in a what appears to be an older home. We were seated quickly and provided a menu that offers many options. We ordered the Pho with rare steak and brisket w/o onions, Pho with only rare steak, a lychee drink and a bubble jack fruit smoothie. Within only a couple minutes out Pho was at the table piping hot just as ordered. The broth tasted very good, the rice noodles were the perfect texture but the meat was a little dry. The lychee drink came out next and was packed with lychee fruit in the bottom of the glass, it was so sweet and delicious. The bubble smoothie was soon to follow and it arrived at our table in what appeared to be a to-go cup. The pictures of the smoothie in the menu and on the tv monitors throughout the restaurant represented it served in a glass, just like the lychee drink. I asked our server for one in a glass and he assured me that it was just freshly made. We ended up enjoying the smoothie but would've probably wanted to just go to the bubble tea shop around the corner. All in all, Pho was good and worth the money spent.

THAI PEANUT FOR THE WIN. This place has great quality veggies and you can taste the difference. Very unique flavors in all of their bowls, which is the only thing we tried. All of the food looks great though and it's very well decorated inside and the design and branding is appealing for the people that walk in! Try this if you are looking for healthy, delicious, and quick food in Tucson :)

I can't say enough amazing things about Sandler's! They hosted my bridal shower and every detail was executed to perfection! The owners (Paul and his daughter Aly) are absolutely wonderful and made this a beautiful day for me. The food, drinks & service were impeccable and my friends and family couldn't stop raving about it! Shannon and Danielle did a fantastic job servicing the party and Lisa, the manager pulled together every last detail. Thank you to everyone at Sandler's for making this day a dream come true!

I've been to the Olive Garden in New Tampa many times. After a few more years, I may be able to find its amazingly secluded shopping center on the first try. (If you're coming from USF, it's the last left before I-75, across from BJ's. If you're coming from I-75, it's the first right you'll see on Bruce B. Downs going southwest.)

Usually we come here for the questionable novelty (and the undeniable gluttony) of the Never-Ending Pasta Bowl, an autumnal ritual of orgiastic consumption which has its roots in the ancient Ursa Dormiens tradition of fattening everyone up before going to sleep for several months. Oh, wait, that wasn't ancient Romans, that was grizzly bears. But I still end up wanting to go to sleep for several months once the carbohydrates hit my bloodstream.

Like most restaurants, the Olive Garden probably makes most of its profits by selling drinks. Like most movie theater snack bars, they unsubtly drive drink sales by walloping you over the head with salt. Having the $7 lunch combo of salad (with salty cheese shredded on top) and soup (also salty)? Well then, help yourself to free breadsticks. I'm not going to say they taste like Lot's wife with a yeast infection, but there's a reason the Olive Garden doesn't try to charge you for them.

And yet I keep coming back. I have to take three stars off my rating of my own intelligence and award them to the Olive Garden. They earned those stars, damn it. I don't know how, but they did.

This place can be hard to find but well worth the china town trip. I come here when I am sick and need a hot bowl of pho to the face.

My favorite is the seafood tom yum soup. Its loaded with jumbo shrimp, mussels, fish patties, and imitation crab. First I load it up with all the fresh herbs and bean sprouts they provide you. I then put two spoons of spicy red sauce. Finally I try to eat it as hot in temperature as I can stand and like magic my sinuses and nasal passages are completely cleared.

I have also tried the shrimp roll appetizer, chicken vermicelli with shrimp stick, and the classic beef pho. All of which are excellent.

The time from when you place your order until your meal is ready is fast (usually within 10 minutes). The service is ok considering that only two staff members speak broken English. The rest can speak a few words. I always have to ask for extra napkins and this can be a challenge sometimes.

They also have a cheap full bar menu if you want to get your drink on.

Best of all are the prices and serving sizes. For 6 bucks you can have enough food to feel completely satisfied and have enough to bring home for another meal.

What prevents this place from a 5 star review is some cleanliness issues (like the bathroom), the cramped feel, and the fluorescent lighting inside can be unpleasant.

Overall definitely give it a try, especially during the winter or if your nasal passages are stuffed.
My favorite place to eat! The staff is always so friendly! The big melon juice is the yummiest! A must try!

TL;DR no wait for table but slow service, poor quality drinks, passive aggressive staff, awful private room, average food.

Brunch on a Sunday with a large group isn't easy to come by. This place was able to take a party of 10 fairly quick and since it had a bar and TV to watch the Eagles, we were happy. We sat at the bar while we waited for the table to be ready. There was one bartender, making on drink at a time. There was no consistency in the drinks. My friend and I bother ordered and American Glory, hers was bright pink and tasted like berries, mine was clear with a tint of pink and tasted like champagne. My friend ordered a chocolate martini, two came with a peanut chew and one didn't. Oh well, they tasted good and we just learned that we needed to order another drink the second the first was delivered or else you'd be waiting an hour between rounds.

We finally are seated and we are put into a small room with glass walls secluded from the rest of the place. But, there was no TV in the room, so we had to sit strategically to see the few TVs at the bar. We also soon realized that with the doors of this room closed, the echoing was unbearable. It was hard to hear the person sitting next to you, which makes everyone just talk louder. We opened the doors back up, but quickly realized that we were getting the stink eye from a woman at a table fairly close to the room. Oh well, if she wanted a quiet meal she could've stayed home. It's an Eagles home game during brunch, of course it's loud.

Throughout the meal two men who worked there would come over and close the doors without saying anything. Eventually I got up and told them the doors need to stay open or else it is impossible to have a conversation in that room, they said fine. I was grumpy because I wish they would have just said something to us to begin with rather than quietly closing us in hoping we didn't notice.

The food comes out. It is average. The avocado toast was drenched in lime to the point that I couldn't help but feel like it tasted like some sort of cleaning product. The toast was soggy from it. 

All in all, it was a fine experience. Nothing to write home about but not rushing back. Maybe once this place is open for a bit things will get ironed out.

In my 42 years of life I've never ever sent food back until I ate here. I got the turkey burger which presentation wise looked great but I cut it in half and went to take a bite and I smelled something was off. I let my friend smell it, decided to be brave and taste it anyway and I actually had to spit it out into a napkin, horrified. It smelled and tasted spoiled. The amazing waiter!!! Quickly replaced it with a chicken BLT, I forgot the exact name, which was decent. Nothing to rave about. The saving grace in this place is the service and the fries. The staff is awesome!! Maybe it was an off day for the kitchen, idk

Remember when I said I wouldn't come back unless bribed by friends? Well...  how about opening party with my flag football league?

So, we came back and... we had a blast!!  Not sure if it was because of the group we met or because we sat at the bar this time...  I can't quite put my finger on it, but something was different.  Different, good!  Even after the party was over, we stayed.  We shut iCandy, DOWN!  We ended up not leaving until the place closed.  The DJ was on point ALL night, drinks were flowing, we spent a lot of time playing the "What's different in this picture" game with naked ladies.  It was a really good night.

The SHOT BOYS were out all night with $1 jello shots and whipped cream :-)  There were random drink specials throughout the night ($4 Jager shots, $4 Pinnacle shots? and $6 or $7 Pinnacle drinks).

We ended up going back two more times since then and we think we'll put it on our list of pre-game spots to hit before embarking on a night of drunken debauchery!

I was glad to find that Ssndler's is open on Christmas Day. Located in the historic Franklin, this is a great spot for brunch in a casual setting that doesn't feel too laidback. 

We started with some brunch beverages - a mimosa that had a great ratio of champagne to OJ, and a bloody mary topped with a cube of grilled cheese and a slice of crispy bacon. Both were great!

I had the LOX, EGGS, AND ONIONS. The eggs were scrambled, with deliciously rich pastrami lox and sweet onion. The "homies" on the side were too similar to a dinner-style roasted potato, and I didn't care for them, but the eggs were great.

My brother's FRUITY PANCAKES were the star of the table. The fluffy pancakes had blueberry in teh batter, and were topped with more fresh fruit on top. THese were some great pancakes!

Our server, Nicole, was very sweet, despite having to work on the Holiday. Thank you Nicole and happy holidays to you! 

I can definitely see myself coming back here for an easy yet delicious breakfast or lunch.

When you look at the name and note that the restaurant is in Chinatown you know you're going to get authentic vietnamese pho for a good price. I'm from California and this pho is just on par or even better. I got the #101 (pho dac biet xe lua) Oh and I'm also Vietnamese so I eat this stuff all the time.

I went here last week because I was looking for a good pho spot downtown, and it was great!  I ended up going there for lunch two days in a row...medium-rare beef pho both times.  

The service is quick, the prices are cheap, and the bowl is huge.  Extra-large is just too big for me, but the large pho is plenty big enough.  I also had the spring rolls (delicious), and one of the best cups of coffee I've had in a long time.

Was looking for a new place to go for my birthday dinner... looked at the reviews here and thought okay looks cute let's give it a try. Boy what a huge disappointment not much to choose from and the prices very steep. Won't be back!!!

First I have to say, the restaurant has a nice atmosphere. Drinks delicious, especially the beer cocktails. 
Everything started going south once we sat at the table for dinner. cheese plate ehh..barely had enough for 2 people to enjoy more than a bite. Still trying to determine if the steak salad I ordered is truly the dinner portion or the appetizer special. It was so small with 3 thin slices of cold meat. I looked at it and wondered how this could be ever considered a dinner portion. Forget the price point..really? $18 for a thin slice of cold meat with a few greens? Oh and don't get  the homemade pretzels- wow, bland and the sauce was just terrible.

Visited Philly to see Bruno Mars. Sandler's came up as a recommendation on Yelp so we took a shot. The staff there were great. The servers are well informed and made great recommendations. I had the tartare tacos and my friend had the nachos. It was so good we went back again the next day before hitting the road. Will put them on my 'Places to Eat in Philly' list.

Came in for brunch with a group of 12 people and sat with Raffael. He was such a hustler on the run getting us everything we needed and very quickly! The food was delicious and worth every cent. Snoop hog 10 out of 10; but what put our experience over the top was the service we received from Raffael. He was awesome and very attentive! Would highly recommend to any of my friends!

The best thing about this place is that you don't have to crave pho to think that pho here is the best thing you'll ever have. This was my go-to place in college, and even though I've moved since then, it will still be my go-to place in Philly. The prices are affordable, the place is group friendly and the service is quick. And that's really all you can ask for. So if you're hungry, don't hesitate.

Honestly, this place blows every other Pho restaurant I've ever been to out of the water. To go anywhere else is a mistake.

It's hard to believe that I could ever be unable to finish a bowl of pho, but the XL bowl is so big and portions of meat so generous that I have yet to polish off an entire serving. Not much else to say.

Randomly, they are closed on Wednesdays. If you want pho on a wednesday, you should save your appetite for Thursday - don't go somewhere else.

Hands down the best Vietnamese food I've ever had. The menu is outstanding, yet I still get the same thing everytime, because why mess with perfection?? 
Spring rolls with Thai peanut sauce, a large 102 (pho with rare beef), and a pineapple smoothie. 
The food is good and good for you... well much better than any fast food crap you can shove down your throat on the run. Located @ 10th and Race in Chinatown, it's only a stonesthrow away from jersey.  I would eat there everyday if I could. Also the coffee is outstanding. Like a dessert in itself. Brewed with individual filters and made with sweetened condensed milk.  
10/10.  Go! NOW!!!!!

My boyfriend and I went here for our 2 year anniversary!

The service was fantastic, the food? SO delicious and the serving sizes are perfect, you pay and get a good amount of food. The overall atmosphere is really nice as well, and I know this a very disjointed review, but please try this place out! ( PS - Love the shrimp scampi and spaghetti! ) I will be coming back and taking my family and friends here

Had a great dinner here yesterday. Though the restaurant was full we were seated very quickly.Nick was very friendly and always made sure our cups were full. We had the 2 for $25. Plenty of food for your buck. We had the soup, Zuppa Toscana, (this was the only thing was not happy with because there was very little potato) and the my main course was a new Parmesan Crusted Tortellini with Prosciutto and my BF had the Parmesan Crusted Chicken. Delicious. And the Risotto Bites and White Bean Hummus was tastey. No long wait period for meals.

I've been here twice now, once when they first opened and last night now that they have been up and running for a few months. Both times I've been really impressed, the pasta dishes and the steaks are top notch and they make a really awesome Caesar Salad. They've also got a full bar and make a nice old fashioned, it looks like they have a pretty extensive craft beer selection as well. The staff has always been super friendly and helpful. It's a place I felt right at home in the very first time I walked in the door. Steaks are amazing and so is the art on the walls by Tucson based artist Danny Martin. Tell your date to wear cowboy boots, the parking lot is not high heels friendly. Service, food, and atmosphere are all excellent here. I don't think you'll be disappointed. The picture is the Danny Martin art on the top of the kids menus.

I often get depressed on Wednesdays when I realize that the Train is closed and I'm craving one of their dishes.  There are just so many amazing things to order, that aren't even necessarily on the menu.  When "off-road" ordering at the Train, I go for the Sate (sp?) clams or the Clam Pho in spicy broth. (Clearly I have a thing for clams).  This is also a great place to host a large family style dinner for a number of guests - in the past we've ordered the stuffed tofu, ginger/scallion lobster and crab.  Non-chinatowners are always very impressed by that selection.  They also make amazing shakes - and when dining in, just one ask from the waiter and you can turn your normally healthy and delicious strawberry shake into an even more delicious strawberry daquiri w/ a shot of rum!  Oh favorite Chinatown restaurant - what would I do w/o thee?

Healthy and delicious just not as consistent as I would hope. The first time I had the fruit granola and yogurt it was amazing and full to the brim, on subsequent visits, it was lacking.
 I like the clean feel of the space is has a nice energy, tables outside are nice and have shade, but they are street side. 
 The hot tropic smoothie is my favorite 6$ or 8.5 for a large tends to drive up the price of my breakfast but I feel so healthy.

I really love the Atmosphere at this place. When I come to Chinatown I want it to feel like I'm in Chinatown, and this place does not disappoint. And they Certainly don't disappoint with the Pho here. The broth has a good ginger taste that is almost sweet, but doesn't go overboard. The meat is good and the food comes out in minutes. I love that they have fish tanks up front with live crabs and stuff in them. Cause as I said I want to feel like I'm in Chinatown. 
My only knock against this place is the summer rolls we got. They seemed to be using really crappy pork but then again I only got them once. But Pho here is really tasty. And keeps me coming back. Which will be often this winter

Excellent customer service I was very amaze how the restaurant was connected to The Ben Franklin Residence. The food was fantastic too bad the alcohol wasn't there but I'll be back once my son Anthony tells me. ( Its always sunny at Sandler's) - Anthony (SA)

I'm a fan of this new spot. They have a nice selection with many options on their menu and a lot of them have a twist that's different from normal. Prices are super reasonable, good service. I can't find anything to complain about. Wasn't starving on the day I came in here but the flatbread I had was bomb!

It was solid. Looking for a place without reservations on a Fri night last night. No wait to get it. Soft-Pretzel Crusted Chicken Tender appetizer was 5-stars. 
Burgers and Salads were very good. Fries were were a little wiggly. Very under-staffed but the staff still had great attitudes!
It's a little pricey, but most juice places are. The food is good and the smoothies are great! The staff is super friendly. Cozy place for a post workout gab session with your pals.

I have wanted to stop here for the longest time. Choo choo did not disappoint at all. 

First off, definitely try the snails!! they were pretty tasty once you get into the rythem of eating them. The mussels were just OK, non of us were a fan of the ketchup like sauce that they ere drowned in.
