Nice looking place but nothing we ordered was as good as it sounds on the menu.  Also we possibly had the least friendly waitress I've ever encountered and she barely did anything or spoke to us despite being her only table.  I would rate as a 2.5 if I could.

I literally love everything I get. It is so worth the price! Tried the Beasley salad and teriyaki bowl and I can't wait to go back ! I got a granola bar thing that I didn't reallly like at all but otherwise great food!

My sister describes it as merely convenient. And it is that. Nice service. Fairly cute inside without any warmth or charm. Yet a simple breakfast was tasteless. Sweet waitress asked if I wanted cream for my decaf. Yes, please! Thought I was off to a good start. It was so tasteless, I added all the milk and two sweetener packets. (I normally do not add any sweetener.) Finally asked for another cup. Decaf for us shouldn't taste like hot water. It tasted fresher, but couldn't find our waitress to get more milk. Another one helped. I said more cream please, is that really cream? Answer: No, we're out of cream. I knew that wasn't even whole milk for my coffee. 9 am and you're out of coffee creamers? Sister ordered the lox, eggs, and onions. Our eyebrows went up when asked how she wanted her eggs. I ordered two soft scrambled eggs and scrapple. Gosh, those eggs tasted powdered. Scrapple was good: a big piece and fried crispy on the outside. We found our potatoes really odd. Homies were described as potatoes with a bit of onion and Cajun seasoning. Gosh again: tasteless. Oddly, sister's bland looking potatoes tasted much better than mine very dark potatoes. I don't understand where the darkness came from.

I was skeptical of this place when I first heard about it.  I was bowled over by how good the food was.  I had the ribeye with spaghetti and the ribeye was melt in my mouth good.  I look forward to going back for the food.  The building itself is dated and needs some work but the food is fantastic

Edit:  our waitress was Sabrina and she was great
Stupid policy won't let people sit inside (or even wait inside for our order) when every other restaurant in town does. It does let employees wear mask with valves.

As a celiac (I must eat gluten-free) I find it very difficult to source quality and delicious lunch during the workday. Today I sat down at Sandler's and was royally taken care of. They prepared the Lobster Poutine gluten-free for me and it was one of the best/biggest/most delicious lunches I've had in a longgg time! The rest of the menu is filled with interesting and innovative comfort food, perfect for a high-quality pig-out.

Very good Asian noodle salad. They lose one star for counter service. If you have counter service you can't get 5 stars no matter what. The other lost star is because the place looks and feels kind of dirty. The food is good and pretty healthy. I'd eat here again.

The washer/dryer combo that we have in our apartment is garbage. So we have had to start taking our laundry to a laundry mat. I found this one a while back and decided to come back. I really like the way this one works. You do have to create an account and pay for the washer and dryer through your account. Which makes it good for the fact that you don't have to go get a bunch of change and carry it around. They don't have a huge selection of machines, so you might have to wait a few minutes for one to be available. Also, the machine are all for 4 loads. They do not have single load washers. Each washer and dyer have lights on them so you know which are available. You can also reserve a machine when you are on your way up which would help not having to wait for a machine. The place is clean as well so that makes getting your laundry done better. The washers are all $6 for a 4 load wash, and the dryers are all $2. The washers take 28 mins and the dryers are 40 mins. The only issue I have seen (which I believe happens at all laundry mats) is that people start their laundry and then leave the place. So you see machines available, but people have their belongs left in them.

We took our niece out for her 14th birthday, the server Jack was extremely pleasant and attentive. His service was 5 stars. We got the Bbq chicken nachos for an appetizer and it was a hit. The kids all got cheeseburgers, our niece got a create your own omelette (pretty good) , my husband got the delirium tremor burger and I had the short ribs with mashed potatoes both of our entrees lacked flavor. The kids enjoyed their food. All in all, if you're looking for an 'okay' food experience with great service then Sandler's is the place for you.

Definitely a fan. Definitely Cheap. Definitely open pretty late (for philly). 

While Pho Ha is still my go to in terms of having parking and taste wise. This is a close second. It's kinda plain looking on an off street, but it's good. The brothe is tasty, the flank was a bit fattier than I liked, and the tripe was pretty tangled.

Definitely good though. The brothe is what makes or breaks pho for me.

Talk about a local spot that delivers. Some have tried to compete in the area and thankfully this spot continues to provide delicious froyo. As a part of a yelp thankful thursday I have to give my gratitude here. 

Great homemade flavors and toppings galore. The prices are more than reasonable to take away and keep some in the freezer for later (if you practice restraint). 

My old man is diabetic and they always have a sugar free option (and SF choc chips!) I can pick up for him too. 

Check this place out, get a sample to be sure you will enjoy and it will be tasty enough I guarantee at least one brain freeze.

this place was a let down

i came in for lunch and we waited about 5 minutes for a host to come up but it wasn't busy at all, i guess they just didn't have a lot of workers that day. i could tell by the few tables that were occupied that they were also waiting for their waiters

once we got seated i ordered the french onion soup, a breakfast sandwich w/ porkroll. my friend got sweet potato fries and the duck quesadilla

french onion soup - cheese was good but the soup itself was suuuper bland. not worth it for the price, i've had much better

breakfast sandwich w/ porkroll - this was so so, not worth it for the price again. i can get it for $5 at the deli near my apartment for better quality. the egg was not well cooked and the bread was stale. the breakfast potatoes were also bland and not warm

the sweet potato fries were probably the most decent thing i ate here. the service was mediocre and the restaurant itself was pretty small and empty, something needs to happen!

Today was my first time and last for sure. When the guy behind the counter gave me my cup, it had lipstick stain on it. When I complained about it, he took it back, held it below  the counter and wiped it with a green cloth and gave it back to me, probably hoping that I didn't notice it. Not the best experience. who are these people?

I wanted to try something simple but good while I'm in Philly & Sandler's on 9th was perfect. I order the Lobster Poutines, glass of cab & brownie cheesecake. Everything was amazing the Lobster Poutines was my 1st time trying it it was fries with cheese sauce & chucks of lobster on top. Ohhhhh so good
Really enjoyed the food. Tried the Avo toast, Mediterranean salad and an Açaí bowl. They were all fabulous. We will be back.

I can't believe a company that is in a customer service business.  Would send out a Neanderthal to customers homes.  This piece of work came to our home.  Unfortunatly while I was at work, and rattled my wife so bad she started to cry.  The high ups at gasmaster better start taking a look at the people they are sending to customers homes, before they don't have customers.

Today the service at Goodness was beyond good! Daniel helped me get my card out of the wood slotted patio area because I accidentally dropped it through the cracks. I told him I could just order a new card, but he went above and beyond and helped me out. 5 star employee!! Thank you Daniel

All aboard the Choo Choo's train whenever you're in Chinatown.

Choo Choo is one of my favorite pho places in the city. It's actually the only place in Chinatown I go to for pho. At around $6 for a xlarge bowl of pho, it's the cheapest and largest bowl of pho in the Delaware Valley.

If you do order the xlarge size (there's only large and xlarge bowl sizes here), be prepared for a bowl containing about a gallon of broth to be served to you, alongside a generous side dish containing sprouts, cilantro, thai basil, and jalapenos.

I think the broth at Choo Choo is delicious. It is always flavorful, with a very nice balanced amount of spices. No crazy throat-drying additives in my bowl (MSG). Always a must. The other thing that I like about this place is that you won't be disappointed in the amount of noodles you're served, which I've found to be lacking at other places. 

Not to mention that they have the best name in all of Philadelphia. High five for the sweet name.

Came here because the lines at Dim Sum Garden and Terakawa were too long, and we were hungry. Food is very sub-par, but the service was surprisingly good for Chinatown. 2 stars for food, 4 stars for service. 

I got the summer roll and Tom-Yum soup with rice noodles, and the latter was barely edible. The summer roll was ok but definitely not that good. The sauce didn't have enough flavor. The noodle soup dish was just plain bad. The broth didn't have the typical flavor of Tom-Yum soup but had all of the tartness. It tasted like citrus water. The seafood inside the dish was likewise not great. The noodles were fine, but rice noodles can't be hard to mess up.
I had the Tom yum seafood soup and it was the best soup I have ever heard and highly flavorful! I would recommend getting this when you come here!

We were here for brunch & it was delicious! My teens each got omelets that we're cooked perfectly. The Ugly BLTA was unique & so good. My favorite was the brisket poutine-the brisket was so tender, the gravy flavorful. I can't wait to go back for it again. The only negative was it was a bit slow getting the food out-I understand it was close to the holidays & they had several big parties in the restaurant. But the servers were very nice & kept our drinks filled while we waited. I absolutely recommend it.

Came here with peeps since pho 20 had no indoor seating. We ordered spring rolls and steamed dumplings which I wasn't a fan of, I was looking for just Pho fix. It was ok but not amazing. The broth was flat to me. Lacking the fatty umami flavor that true broth has from hours of cooking, it was most likely high in sodium or msg since I was thirsty after dinner.

This place really sucks. The staff is rude, the place feels so cold and awkward, the "bartender" didn't know what  was on draft, I've been sitting here with an empty glass just begging for a check (I was gonna get another drink but I don't have faith in these people so check it is) I had to basically yell "can we close out" because eye contact isn't a thing here. I don't know what else to say, I just came in here because it was open and now I can't wait to leave and never come back. Peace. Corporate weird nonsense miserable staff

Food is a 10/10 but the service here is a 0. I don't like leaving poor reviews at restaurants but I've had way to many disappointing visits that it has to be raised with the manager or owner. I tried giving this place a chance, in case it was just a 1 off instance, however they have failed in some way after every single visit.  Every time I come here I either wait FOREVER for the cashier to come and take my order or every time I call to place an order to go, they ALWAYS just leave me on hold for over 20 mins. This has happened at least 5 times in one month. After waiting for +20 mins on hold they forget I'm there and hang up. How I said, I've really tried to give this place a chance because I love their food (props to the cooks) but is completely offset by the service from cashiers. They need to hire more personnel or do better with their customer service because they will lose customers this way.

Nicole is hands down the best server!!! I went to Sandler's for the first time shortly after I recieved upsetting news from Jefferson hospital. I was very and visibly upset when we walked in. Nicole was compassionate and attentive and immediately made me feel better. We had the chicken salad croissant as well as the lobster shrimp sandwich! They were both delicious. Of course martinis and desserts are a good way to feel better too and we had both! In my emotional state I spilled one and it was quickly replaced by another. We ended up having a chat with Nicole about some personal things. She is a dedicated, loyal, and ambitious young lady! It is so hard to come across people like her these days and I wish her the best both at her job and with her personal endeavors.

Still delicious!!!! Words cannot describe how much I adore this Acai bowl!!! Nom nom nom delicious! The granola is so homemade and perfect...and the mint...oh, the mint. Superb! I can not recommend this enough.

don't go to these guys with any kind of timeline in mind. over 6 weeks ago i set up an appointment for them to bid a small project. i had to email them two times for the bid after they came out. i should have known, that if you have to chase someone to throw money at them, it will probably be a headache over the entire project. 
Then, i had to change something and asked for an update, and asked for an update, and called for an update, and then 11 days later i got the update. i accepted the new lower price but they were backed up for weeks to fit you in. two weeks later after accepting the new proposal, they show up to do it with the old proposal but didn't bring digging equipment. that will be another week and a day at the earliest to get someone else who can dig out. I've got something going on that i planned over six weeks ago, "what if i pay overtime"  nah they are fine. they don't want money, apparently, they just want the pride of Mastering Gas, time frames be damned.

We walk in a not a sole in sight. We didn't know if the place was open. A couple minutes later a young man came out and got us seated. The prices range from $11-$45 depending on what you get. Our waiter was not very observant. He either missed things like spoons to eat our soups to refills on our beverages. The food was cooked perfectly, the only down side is they use extremely large amounts of crushed black pepper on the food. The marsala sauce had a great sweet flavor. The kids barley touched their alfrado because of all the black pepper. The prime rib 10oz was hug for the size and a nice thick cut. The veggies had a nice balsamic glaze. Our other dishes were good just a lot of pepper. I only gave this place 4 stars because the service was bad and the excessive amounts of pepper in our food.  This place can be very well if they fix the service and the seasoning problem.

The food here is very mediocre, but service is pretty decent. The menu looks so promising, but the taste just wasn't there. With so many great places in Philly for brunch, this is a place you
can skip.

I came here for brunch with a group of 5 on a Sunday around noon and were seated quickly because the restaurant was very empty. That itself should've been a red flag about the quality of the food. The server told us about the lobster poutine, which sounded glorious, so we got that to share. The first bite was great, but the flavor just wasn't there, and the lobster tasted old and hard. I also got a breakfast sandwich that came with potatoes, and the potatoes were really bad. They were mushy and bland, and no amount of salt and pepper could rescue them from their mediocrity. I had a lot of food left over on my plate, but I couldn't bear the thought of eating those potatoes, so I basically had to let half of my plate of food go to waste.

No time to make a home made, high quality, healthy meal? Goodness has your back! No processed fast food here just Goodness that looks great and tastes divine. I am a huge fan of their Hulk Smoothie because when do we really get enough greens in such a delicious drink? And what sorcery is this: the Hulk smoothie has not only Kale but Wheat grass in it and is some how tasty?  This is a feat unto itself. 

I'm also a big fan of the bowls offered here because they are delectable and again super nutritious. My favorite is the Thai Peanut with chicken and sub out the rice for quinoa. Where do I even begin here... Thai coconut sauce is creamy and decadent and make you feel like you are clearly cheating on your fitness. The chicken is always delicious and never dry. The kale and carrots are cooked to perfect, never overdone and soggy with a good crunch to them. 

Do your health a favor and eat here instead of the fast food joint that's calling your name. Your body and taste buds will thank you!
Best Pho I've had all year! Beautiful ambiance inside, great service and all around delicious appetizer and soup! Can't wait to go back!

Please know up front this is not me blowing hot air as I rarely write reviews and the few I have, are positive. This genuinely merits a review and is not COVID related.

It pains me to write a bad review about a local business but I simply must as the service was absolutely terrible.

I first tried Goodness in October and had a rather neutral experience - while the patio was not shaded and it was rather hot, the food was overall good (although I would agree with other reviews that the açaí bowl was too runny). 

I then went back this past week with my family and left rather in shock as to how our experience unfolded. I will summarize with this statement: be prepared to work for yourself. 

1- Do not expect the tables to be clean. And when they are not, you may surprised at the response when you ask for them to be wiped down. We started at a table with jelly and crumbs all over it and moved. The new table had such a dirty film on it, it was clear they hadn't been wiped in awhile. The employee said they cleaned them each morning and they're just stained and not dirty.  IRONICALLY he stated this as he lifted the white rag and it was black from where he wiped it. Yeah, don't try to back out of being caught in a job not done; clearly the tables where not cleaned that morning as we showed up 10 minutes after it opened. Just own it, apologize and move on. It's your job at ANY time in history to wipe tables. And especially during COVID. 

2- Don't expect to get cream, sugar, utensils or anything of that sort with your food. Instead, be prepared to go in not once, not twice, but 3-5 times to ask for these things as you discover you need them. And then be prepared to have the employee get clearly annoyed at... wait for it... having to do his job.
We went back in and asked for cream and sugar, painfully he got it. We went back in and asked for a stir stick, he grabbed with bare hand in the middle of it (a napkin is what is commonly used to grab those; even in non COVID times).
We went back in and asked for a booster seat- nope, don't have them- sorry. "We used to but got rid of them."
We needed a bit more cream- he was clearly annoyed. 

To feel GUILTY as a customer for then needing a fork for my child to eat his food and not wanting to go in and ask, well, that's bad. 

3- The REDEMPTION is that the food is great. Reasonably priced, good quality. Good stuff. 

In summary- so much focus is put on the customer supporting small businesses during this time. And I agree we should; as is proven by how we spend our money. But know that when you are an EMPLOYEE of a small business, you represent that business. Do it well. You're paid for more than a transaction. Say hello when a customer enters (oh that didn't happen either). Anticipate what a customer will need and if you don't know, ask them at the table. Smile. If you make a mistake (like failing to wipe tables before opening), own it and do it with no excuses (because when you lie and say it was done as you heap black grime on your cloth where our child is eating it looks lame). And for heavens sake, don't look annoyed when the customer NICELY comes in for the 4th time to ask for something needed and basically is doing your job.

I give it two stars because the food is food.

4 stars for food. 
No stars for service. 
2 stars is the median.

I was so happy to be done with NBAZ when I walked into one of their branches on 4/22 to permanently close my account.

I happened to log in to my old NBAZ account tonight while looking for past deposit. I was shocked to see that the auto pay that I forgot to transfer to my new bank actually went through on a CLOSED account nearly a month later!

The payment was returned the next day, but a $35 insufficient funds fee still remains. The account is also now listed as 'Open.'

How do you get rid of this bank?! I filed a BBB complaint, so hopefully I can end this nightmare soon.

Very Americanized but who cares still great! Come hungry huge portion of pho. My husband was sick and he swears their pho cleared it up, he was so thankful to have it while he was sick. I had their pork hoagie was soo good when i was done it left me wanting more , cant wait to come back and try some thai dishes.

Horrible experience at this location, my food came out cold so I sent it back, my wife's food literally made her sick for days... Asked to have a manager call me but it's been over a week and nothing. Apparently this location does not care about their customers satisfaction, better choices in the area

Came here after an exam and the workers were so nice and accommodating, especially our waitress Nicole. She was very polite and quick to respond for anything we needed. 

The food was also amazing. I had the chicken and waffles and it was amazing. Great flavor, great atmosphere, definitely a place to check out

normally I really enjoy this place for the bowls.  I tried the turkey pesto sandwich.  it was a absolute joke. I should have taken a picture of how flat and no filled it was....It was amazing they sent that out for 13 bucks.  ? should have went to a place that specializes in sandwiches.  I try to stay away from chains.  and actually am friends of a family member of this restaurant but that sandwich yesterday was humiliating.  rip off. I'm mad I was so hungry I didn't take a picture.
the sandwich was flat like a chef sat on it.  2 pieces of sliced turkey flat. not rolled over like pic.  arugula was like so sparse.

The exterior might not show it, but the inside has a fairly western feel to it, complete with saloon door to the bar. The main dining area is an open area with tables in the center, booths to the sides, and a big flatscreen playing old westerns.

The hostess and server were very friendly to our party of 7. We were given suggestions and told it was happy hour (which, I might come back for). 

I wasn't hungry enough for a steak so I split the chicken Marsala, and it was plenty so I can see leftovers being taken home frequently. The chicken was cooked perfectly, juicy and tender, not dry at all. It had the right amount of sauce, though I would've liked more noodles and a few more mushrooms. 

Everything seemed moderately priced, especially for the portion sizes. It's a nice enough restaurant to take a date but casual enough for a family outing.
Steak and spaghetti is an interesting concept, so I applaud these guys for venturing out and keeping the feel fairly old west. Will have to come back and try a classic spaghetti and meatballs sometime.

Came by for lunch as I was in the area and wanted to try something new out. Tried the lobster roll and was a bit disappointed with it. Was expecting a buttery soft bread but it's served on a rather rubbery baguette and the lobster itself was on the bland side. Fries were just fine though and the service was great as usual. 
Kind of a strange situation with there being spirits and beer taps at the bar but no cocktail menu to speak of. Would have liked a beer with my entree. 
Will probably be back, but not for a lobster anything.

I would consider this place to be perfectly lunch-casual, but my boyfriend contemplates eating here anytime, everyday.  

The waiters was attentive and the service was fast.  I got chicken pho; the chicken was so tender (despite the hot broth) and the noodles were superior in texture.  The banh cuon is listed as an appetizer, but there is enough to be a meal.

Go here often.

Absolutely LOVE this place! Nicole is an amazing server - we walked in with a large group after finishing final exams and she was so sweet and made sure that we were well taken care of. The mimosas are great and the tomato soup/grilled cheese is to die for!!!

i'm so happy this place exists!  I love veggie juice and they do a great job with the varieties they offer.  it's a little pricey for veggie juice but it gives me a place to get a snack when I'm on the run and not feel guilty about it.  and my body is very happy with me when I make this healthy choice.  I haven't tried any of the menu options yet, but I've tried nearly every one of the juices and enjoy them all.

very clean (as are the bathrooms) and the staff is friendly.  has a nice vibe when you go in and i've always had seating to hang out in while waiting for my beverage.
cockroaches everywhere!! upstairs neighbours sound like elephants playing baseball with bricks.

What a rip-off place charged my friend and I $10.00 each for a short well vodka and cranberry. Not sure if it was because we were woman or non Hispanic. Won't ever go back and none of my friends either. Avoid this place!!

Met a friend here at noon on a Tuesday and the wait wasn't bad at all! This place really reminds me of Chopshop in Phoenix! 

I wanted something light, so my friend recommended the Teriyaki Veggie bowl with brown rice (the other option is quinoa) -- Super delicious but I was craving more sauce! Maybe next time I'll ask for extra sauce. I was actually surprised at how much food I got! I ate all the veggies but was left with so much rice! I think it's just because I wasn't super hungry though so I didn't eat as much rice as I probably would've. 

I also ordered a cold brew coffee which was great! But man, it was strong. I was coffee buzzed until 6 pm! I would like to go back and try more of their bowls

Price wise, expect to spend $10-15 a person depending on what you order. I spent $12 for food and drink, but my meal was veggie. I expect protein meals would bump the costs up a little.

I got a small (9oz) cloud 9 bowl. Very delicious and filling, but I felt like the smoothie wasn't worth the price that I paid for compared to the other places I've been to (mostly toppings). I could've gotten the 12oz for the place of a 9oz. I got half a banana on it with granola, strawberries, coconut flakes, and drizzled honey and blue sauce. Nice blend of mango, banana, and pineapple with coconut and almond milk. The blue algae (spirulina) wasn't over whelming didn't really taste like anything.

The pho is definitely great here, no doubt about it. I ordered the shredded chicken pho and the broth was very flavorful. The chicken wasn't really shredded in the way I had hoped but it was still pretty tender. I hadn't tried anything else so I can't really vouch for it but the environment leaves much to be desired. 

I came in pretty early on a Saturday evening and while it was busy in here, it wasn't too crazy. The waiter to customer ratio huge and since we were seated in the back I felt a little awkward because they were all standing around and staring. I would suggest to reduce the number of waiters, there's honestly no point for it because the restaurant isn't even big enough to require that many people.

Credit card minimum is $15!

Sandler's on 9th is a phenomenal establishment. One of the best restaurants in the Washington Square neighborhood. The management team is second to none - Lisa & Aly. They both work unbelievably hard for the success of their staff and the future of Sandler's. Paul is a true leader and his management team resembles that. The servers & bartenders are wonderful. The food never disappoints. They serve breakfast ALL DAY. Who in the city does that? Everyone at Sandler's truly cares about their guests! Definitely my go to spot in Philly!

love their breakfast sandwich and bowls so much! I also love buying a ginger shot with my breakfast to help my stomach digest better :) this place is awesome! some attitude with some of the workers but nothing a good meal won't fix

This is my second time in here. The first time I had a salad and it was pretty decent. But the reason I came back today was because last time I had some really awesome juice. Today I ordered a "vibrant health" juice which came with two kinds of beets and a few other goodies. All I can tell you is... it was absolutely delicious. I asked for a small glass of ice on the side so I could cool it because it came served room temperature and I didn't want to compromise any of my juice amount by adding ice to the cup at first. Juice here can be a little pricey, but it is pricey everywhere else I've gone as well. Very fresh; very tasty.

Aka as choo choo train by the locals, this place has one of the best viet foods in Chinatown. If you order the pho, it's more on the salty side of broth as compared to the traditional sweeter one. Each time I go, I get the extra large bowl that satisfies my cravings for pho. The fried spring rolls there are one of the best I've had. Durian smoothie is good too if your into that stuff...the only thing that needs work is the decor, this place seems like it hasn't been renovated since computers were invented and had floppy disk drives

Came here for lunch....so my rating is just on lunch menu.

Food was little above average.  Ordered the Cheddar burger and wife got the Bucatini Pasta.

Cheddar Burger - was tasted good and the size was on the bigger side.  It came with a side of French fries and a pickle.  

Bucatini Pasta - the taste of the pasta was good (a pesto flavored pasta) but the pasta was a little hard.  I wish it was cooked a little bit longer, then I would say this pasta dish was on point.  It came with mushrooms, which was cooked well and tasted good.

I rate based on the food, but I will mention that the service was great.  When first tasting the Bucatini, we asked if it was supposed to be a little on the hard side and she mentioned that it was and asked if we didn't like it.  We told her, oh okay and that it was fine.  When we got our bill, she didn't charge us for the pasta.....service was definitely five stars.  

Though the food was a tad bit better than average, the service makes me want to definitely come back here again.

RIP 12th Air - iCandy certainly does not do your memory justice.

iCandy is 12th Air with the following changes:
+ Cover charge
+ Extra $3-5 per drink
+ A few additional bar areas
+ Topless shot boys serving kamikazes in test tubes
+ Overcrowded dance floor
+ MANDATORY $1 coat check
- Roof deck
- Tinh
- Bowls of popcorn on bar
- Ability to control temperature inside

Too bad. I loved 12th Air and had some of my favorite nights out dancing there. Having to spend more money (by a lot) minus all of the former awesome quirks makes me think that I probably won't be going back.

Super impressed with the baked goods. Being a vegan with celiac disease really limits you on options when eating out. Super grateful for the delicious treats at Soho. I tried the lemon blueberry donut it was soooo scrumptious soft and full of flavor. We also tried the CBD infused chocolate donut, it was very good delicious. My husband doesn't have celiac and can eat gluten filled food and found these to be very tasty and rich. 
Also love that everything is certified gluten free like the granola.

Philly! I know what people think, cheesesteaks right? well yeah, but my second favorite thing to get in the city of brotherly love is.....Vietnamese food. Shocking! I know. But really, if you ever stepped food in the "chinatown" here is that there is a huge variety of vietnamese restaurants here. So I came here with my classmate from graduate school and we were starving. An order of classic spring rolls and stir-fried vermicelli later and things were great once again. 

On a saturday night, the place was not crowded. I've been here before and never waited more than 5 minutes so that always a thumbs up. The service was on point, I never had to seek out a server or did i ever reach the bottom of my water glass. Top notch. 

Onward to the food! The classic spring rolls were meh, not the best spring rolls you were hoping for but enough to get you through apps. The problem was the filling was a bit dry and unlike the traditional way of wrapping the spring roll into a large sheet of lettuce along with shredded carrots and radish, the dish that arrived did not include enough of the latter ingredients to concoct the right amount of lettuce spring roll wraps. Usually thats the best way to combat dry spring rolls, and a much better method then dumping all of the fish sauce onto it. 

The stir fried noodle was delicious, buried in the middle of the menu, it's usually not the obvious choice in viet restaurants, but lately I have taken a keen stance on ordering it every chance I get and it was a great choice. Full of flavor, the dish did not rely heavily on sauce which is a good thing. There was a good meat to carb ratio, and the portion size was enough for one hungry man. But i can totally see someone sharing this with two less hungry men, or women. 

Not in the mood for cheesesteaks? Give this place a shot.

We found this place just after Armature Works opened. We loved it! Every time our friends met us there, we insisted we finish our day downtown with one of these famous bowls. In October of 2019 everything changed. New menu. Now, Does NOT taste the same. We are VERY disappointed and will NEVER go back again.

This place is great! I've been here a few times now and have no complaints. I've had a more traditional salad, tofu tacos, a chilled Asian noodle salad, and a warp. The tacos were particularly good, but the salads were nothing to scoff at either. I do appreciate their array of vegan/vegetarian and meat options. I have yet to have a smoothie, but I plan to have one soon and I'm sure they are great as well. I think the concept of this restaurant is amazing and sets the model for new pop-up restaurants that want to cook in the same vein. I plan to return to Goodness several times for their wonderful lunch options. Oh, did I mention the prices are RIGHT as well? You can get a very filling, fresh, and delicious salad to go for $8. I think that's a great deal. Give them a try if you haven't already!
Foods good. Needs more bartenders. There seems to be a lack of them on Friday mornings.
My favorite spot for pho! Nothing better then hot pho on a cold weather with the family!!

Was the first Vietnamese restaurant I ever ate at, so there is a certain sentimental vibe that I get from here. It's really not my favorite place overall for Vietnamese (Nam Phuong, Le Viet, or Vietnam are probably there), but it has a nice selection of dishes and the pacing is very quick. I actually don't find the pho that good, although they have some other dishes that are very good, including my favorite bun bo hue in Philly. Pho ga (chicken pho) is also pretty good.

Favorite items:

Appetziers: Cha Gio (spring rolls), Goi Cuon (shrimp rolls), Papaya salad with shrimp and pork, flank steak carpaccio

Soups: Canh Chua Ga Thai Lan (chicken coconut sour soup), Bun bo hue, Hu Tieu Do Bien (Seafood Noodle soup), Pho Ga, Hu Tieu Suon Nuong (BBQ Pork Chop soup), Pho Tai Nam (beef pho with flank steak and eye round)

Noodle Dishes: Hu Tieu Xao Bo (Rice flake with beef), BBQ pork and spring roll on vermicelli, Shrimp on sugar cane and BBQ pork and spring roll on vermicelli.

Rice Dishes: Com Suon Nuong (Pork Chop on rice), Com Ga Nuong (Lemongrass Chicken on Rice), Com Ga Ca Ri Khoai Tay (Curry Chicken with potatoes on rice), House Fried Rice

Specials: Curry Chicken, Lemongrass Chicken, Bo Luc Lac (Filet in lemongrass sauce)
The BUNRIEU hit the spot, exactly what I need in a cold night. Rich crab ball, thick soupbase and pig blood. Yummy! We order to pick up and voila, 10 min everything is ready.

First time visiting since Covid-19 and we will be back.. Sunday Morning wanted Acai bowls and no one was opened yet.  Goodness had a online website way to order, so we placed our order.  When we arrived head of our timeslot, we noticed they are well set up for takeout.   Masks Required to enter the building. One door entry and plenty of physical distance marking and another door to exit.   They do have outdoor tables if you want to enjoy your meal outside.   When our food was ready, they call us and brought it to a take out "window" they have set up in one of the entry ways.   Both of our acai bowls, Mango and Cacao were reasonably priced and tasted good.   Well packaged for travel back home.

All around pretty good for the main stay pho. Definitely the best you will get in China town but be prepared to pay cash because if u don't have it, it will be trying to get on a mission to hit twenty dollars. The place could be cleaner, but it's pho is good and that's what I'm coming here for. Fried spring rolls was a no go. Regular spring rolls was a yes go, don't get the pork ones, trust me. So, dac biet and good night.
very dissatisfied here. I wanted it to be better since I know the owner. I believe this location is not a great location for any business. I wish the owner all the best.

So they didn't have the ingredients to make the first two drinks my friend ordered (negative). They felt bad and gave my friend his first drink for free (positive). Overall our waitress looked a little flustered and confused but was very nice. We both got the lobster roll which was probably the wrong choice. It was average. Loved our martini. Will I be back? Probably for breakfast over lunch!

I'm a regular at Wawa gas stations but this location unfortunately didn't meet my expectations. When I exited my car to check the pump number I had to dodge all kinds is liquid and trash that had been discarded on the ground by previous customers. The gas pumps had dust and caked on dirt as if they weren't cleaned in months and  every trash can was filled to capacity.  Wawa is a major gas station chain I would hope that they have procedures in place to make sure trash is dumped and the ground is power washed. Maybe this location had a bad day I'll give them another try.
Service was good and prompt today. Salad was terrible! The whole bowl was full of onions, I swear there was a whole onion in there. Meals were delicious and piping hot.

This place is amazing for brunch! Amazing food, amazing drinks, and most importantly amazing service from Nicole!
My boyfriend and I are visiting from Dallas and we decided to come here based in the Yelp reviews. We got the Brisket Poutine Fries, Braised n Confused, Chicken & Pancakes, and a short stack of Fruity Pancakes. Everything was amazing! The dranks! Even better! Get the Prosecco Punch! Highly recommend. You're getting the best bang for your buck and it tastes like juice! So get ready for trouble!
Nicole, thank you for your amazing service! You're funny, have great recommendations, and you were a pleasure to talk to. 
If you're reading the other reviews that rated this restaurant poorly for service, pay them no mind. If Nicole happened to not be around we were able to ask any server for help and they happily helped us in any way they could. 
Now, how do we get you guys in Dallas? Philly ain't giving' you the appreciation you deserve!

Loved the atmosphere here because of the seats by the lake. We went early in the day when it wasn't as busy. We had the flatbread, Philadelphia roll, spicy tuna roll and the chicken and shrimp lettuce wraps (not pictured) and it was all delicious. I'd definitely go back. I just wish there were other options for the lettuce wrap. I was so excited to see the lettuce wrap on the menu because they're not easy to find but the only ones they had were chicken and shrimp mixed together and I don't eat meat. I asked if I could get just shrimp but it wasn't an option.  my friend had it though, and he loved it.

I got a brazilian here and it was amazing. The first time client pricing is an extra $10 compared too returning clients but it comes with a little aftercare kit so definitely worth it. Such a great experience and Tashua was amazing. Made me feel really comfortable and was so so nice. Also love being able to support black woman owned businesses. Definitely coming back and recommending to all my friends!

Delicious! Serves breakfast all day then other food. Joe P was an amazing waiter. Drinks never empty and he remembered my husband's milk with the meal.... no one ever remembers that. I had crabby eggs benny and the home fries are tasty. We also had a turkey club looked like it was on a rustic fresh baked bread, steak with mashed potatoes and asparagus... and steak and eggs with home fries. They serve "morning libations" too. We'd definitely come back!

I ordered the tree hugger juice and a blueberry lemon donut for breakfast today on Uber eats, it got here super quickly and it is so delicious as always. I really highly recommend the juices and the bowls, to anybody who want something tasty but healthy. Thank you soho!!
Menu picture and name does not match! The picture with the thick noodles is the real satay beef with rice noodle and the other one is Xe Lua Egg and Rice Noodle Soup.

This is a local favorite and one of mine! A wide variety of dishes are available to order. Service is fine. Waitstaff don't usually win points for being particularly friendly or welcoming but they come by and fill your water glasses and bring out food without any problems.

I've ordered a bunch of dishes in the past:
- The escargot was excellent. We ordered two kinds: one with peppers and lemongrass, the other with a coconut sauce!
- Crab soup ($11 for a large bowl for sharing) was bland.
- Tangy curry chicken with lemon grass ($7), recommended.
- Vermicelli with grilled pork and a spring roll ($5), very good.
- Miniature lamb chops ($10), delicious! The filet mignon in a lemon grass sauce ($11) was a spicy treat.

Prices are reasonable, not atypical for a Chinatown restaurant. The check came quickly when it was time to go. Avoid the soup and the phad thai (it's nothing to write home about, try Siam Cuisine down the street instead). Recommended!
Very generous size vietnamese pho. Soup was delicious but a bit lacking in the meats department. The fried pork was good, crispy on the outside soft and flavorful on the inside. Overall a good meal.

This place was awesome, the brisket poutine was a LARGE portion, the cheddar bacon burger was fire, the bacon and (I assume house made) pickles were delicious. The drinks were absolutely delicious, but the real icing on the cake was our waiter Joe P. Request this man cause he's the best server I've had in years. Absolutely recommend; come hungry and come thirsty.

Good stuff!! The service was great and I love the spaghetti and steak combo. I enjoyed the spaghetti and meatballs I prefer my getti to be more saucy but this has a good taste.  The would recommend the peach cobbler as the dessert.

One of my Tucson classics. Everything on the menu is awesome. I enjoy the morning brew smoothie and the Aztec and Mediterranean bowl the most! Their avocado toast is worth the price, super different. 

Check out this spot.

Note to owners: Change up the menu sometimes. Maybe so weekly specials.
The pho broth is amazing and full of flavor. I ordered take out it was packaged perfectly, and so delicious

Located in the corner space previously occupied by Umi Star, Goodness continues to pleasantly surprise Tucson. Goodness is an excellent concept, filling the gap of healthy quick bites and meal-worthy smoothies in Tucson. The all-day breakfast menu seems to attract the entire class from nearby yoga studios, as everyone waiting for their take-out look amazingly fit in their skin-tight workout outfits.

Husband got the breakfast burrito, which had turkey sausage, quinoa, and egg bundled in a wheat wrap. It is light and delightful. I got the mango jungle acai bowl, with cut mango pieces, silvered almonds, and shredded coconut sprinkled on top. At first glance, the portion is smaller according to the normal Tucson standard, but they are real filling! The acai bowl powered me through the entire day without any sleep-induced properties. While small and balanced, the Goodness bites still feel like a huge pampering treat and a reward for being active and conscious of our body.

Such a bad place to live in!!! We had bed bugs and moved out ever since and still kept paying rent because the lease wasn't due for another 6 months and they couldn't do nothing about it! So frustrating! And let's not forget roaches are everywhere. Overall it's such a horrible apartment complex! If I could give it 0 starts I would!! Disgusting!

My favorite açaí and smoothie bowl place in Tucson. 
Nice place to brunch. Open seating outdoors. Less a star because they are on the pricier side and parking can be rough. 
Slowly but surely making my way through their offerings. Most recent bowl was the cocoa warrior: açaí, berries, coconut, chia seeds,mint, pecans, honey, cocoa nibs. It was fantastic!

If you are ever hungry and just looking for a phenomenal place to sit down and eat a good meal Sandler's on ninth is the place to be , the staff is very attentive and always one step ahead of what you need , absolutely phenomenal service , our meals were everything and more you could have asked for , definitely my favorite place to go to when I'm in the city so stop by for yourself and check it out you will not be disappointed!

This place is one of the pricier laundry mats I've been to.  For a regular sized load it's $4, for a large load it's $6.  And another $4-5 to dry.  90% of the driers are taped so you can't use them and have been like this for weeks.  Tread lightly because the ones that aren't taped, may or may not dry.  Please be sure to use the restroom because theirs doesn't always have TP, paper towels.  People in here are always complaining but nothing's changed much in the while I've been here.  At least now I've gotten to know which machines are good and which are bad.

For some reason, they feel like they have to rush you in and out.  Server took our food and beverage order at the same time.  Our salad was out in a couple of minutes...no drinks.  Then we got drinks.  I took two bites of my salad and my food came out.   My "Cosmo" was nothing but a glass of cranberry juice.   When I tried to explain this, nicely, to the manager, he just explained to me that this is how they do it.   He didn't try to make things right.   Not going back.

I had been dying to check this place out and am so happy I finally did. Decided to stop on after Christmas to meet an old friend for lunch. Was incredibly happy that they also serve breakfast all day. I ended up going for the Trainwreck, a sandwich composed of egg, cheese, longhots, and pork roll on a Kaiser roll. I originally requested to switch the cheese up (not a huge fan of American). They forgot this, but it was still incredibly good. The sandwich also came with a spicy aioli type sauce that was pretty good. The sandwich came with "homies" or homefries that were amazing. Definitely recommend. For a large portion and a coffee, my bill was under $17 including tip.. not bad at all. Definitely recommend this place!

Oh. My. Goodness! Over my 30+ years of life, I have easily eaten (at least) three times my weight in acai bowls - I don't know what it is about them; they fill me with joy. I first went to Goodness on a whim while studying, in search of a salad (which they have plenty) to break up all the carbs/coffee I consumed. The salad was great, but the Acai bowl....the acai bowl (Cacao Warrior) was delicious. First of all, the blend is amazing, and it is made to order. The base acai is smooth, creamy and cold with just the right amount of sweetness and a uniform texture without icechunks/fruit chunks. Then, the granola...oh boy! It's homemade, and is always crunchy, fresh and perfectly filled with dried fruit. Next, the toppings - coconut, chia seed....so good! They add just enough crunch, without being overpowering (usually, these cost extra at other acai establishments, but not here!) It is also topped with fresh raspberries and blackberries, then drizzled with honey - Yum! My favorite sneaky sneaky addition - mint! So refreshing, so good. So worth the trip. Side note: I'm not a fan of cacao - so I always ask for this on the side (Yes, it's a little awkward for me to order a "Cacao Warrior" bowl without cacao...but hey, what's a girl to do!). Everything is made fresh, and is delicious.

Pretty average. Granted, we only tried two items but both items were alright, but not as good as we hoped.

I got a "hot" turkey pesto sandwich, but the pesto, cheese and turkey were slapped on a toasted bread. The sandwich was cold in minutes, and the insides weren't close to being hot at all. The sandwich was over priced, I thought. I also didn't notice why it was worth so much more, when I could make the same sandwich at home, have it taste the same, and spend way less money. It wasn't bad but it wasn't something I'd pay 9 bucks for...

The other meal we got was the thai chicken bowl with quinoa. Another eh dish. The ingredients are fresh but uninspiring. Again, with a little effort and less money, we could make this dish at home.

We also got a lemmon scone. Very eh. No different than a random scone you get at Fry's... beyond bread has amaze-balls pastries. Sure, maybe they put more sugar, fat, salt etc into their pastries but hot damn is this place not worth the hipster hype.

Ambiance is great, openness is great. Food is alright, prices suck.

This is my go to for pho. The morning after drinking, when it's cold outside, or just because their pho is amazing. This place is always busy. I love their pad Thai and Vietnamese iced coffee. Their mango smoothie is also so fresh and delicious on a hot summer day. Definitely recommend and there is seating upstairs!

I have been working with Michael at Mesquite for 5 years.  Wow, is this guy knowledgeable!  He takes time to explain all the pros and cons of various options.  He has guided me with citrus, roses, bushes; plants of all types.  I tell him about a particular location in my yard, and he always has a great recommendation!  In addition, he is just a really nice guy!  Ask for him by name at the desk.  You'll be very happy you did!
Tony is awesome!! Fast great service, and best prices in Tampa!!
Love this place.    Everyone so friendly.  I dine alone her alone with my well behaved pup in this dog friendly restaurant.    Food is awesome.    It's my go to place  now!

we tried the location  at @armatureworks_tampa the waffle was burnt and the young lady that worked there was really rude about exchanging and wouldn't exchange our order....maybe another location is better! Not a great experience at all!!

You would think that a chain restaurant would have the same recipe but man was I wrong the last time I had chicken scampie I was in San Antonio it was excellent last night it was terrible dry and just plain bad   I sent it back and received a fresh plate it was even worse. Soi switched to soup and salad. So I'm finished with Olive Garden for a while

A hot bowl of pho from here definitely hits the spot! Portions are generous, food is fresh, broth is great- really can't complain about this place. The spring rolls are also very tasty- different from how other places may do it but definitely worth the try. My boyfriend and I would love to come back here if we are ever in the area again.

First off, I would like to say that of all the Vietnamese Restaurants in Chinatown, this has got to be my #1 favorite.  That being said, I frequent this place as often as I can.  I  have my boyfriend hooked on this place too.

The staff has been the same for as long as I can remember and they get the job done.  Not overly friendly but the service is quick and attentive.  Plus, whenever I order take out, the guy who works the counter never charges me tax.  They take care of their regulars, that is one aspect of many that keeps me loyal.

I have ordered a variety of different things on the menu and cannot remember a time when I was disappointed.  My boyfriend swears by their Pho and raves about it to anyone who will listen.  My favorites are: the Raw flank steak appetizer; Banh Cuon Cha Lua (Steamed rice crepe with pork sausage) any of their BBQ chicken, pork or beef with lemongrass over broken rice combos; Bun Bo Hue (Spicy beef noodle soup); any of their Rice Vermicelli combos, and either an iced cold Vietnamese coffee, or creamy avocado milkshake.  All amazing and keeps you coming back for more and more.

If you're questioning on where to go for Vietnamese food in Chinatown, look no further, you have reached your destination.

After having been to several Olive Gardens in different states, you expect a certain level of consistency in the food and service.  However, this is not the case for Olive Garden.

My entire party of 4 were not offered any grated cheese for the salad or their entrees.  I had the Make-your-own pasta and chose the angel hair, and it was not properly cooked because some of the strands were stuck together when it was served to me.  Also, the croûtons in the salad bowl were stale.  Also, the server was not friendly-looking when compared to the other servers that I observed...it seemed like he just wanted to do his job and did not seem happy working there.

Overall, I would not come back to this particular Olive Garden again.

After checking online to see if the dining room was open, I saw a "Join Wait List" option with a 1 - 15 minute wait time posted.  Driving down from Land O Lakes, I didn't want to take a chance on the dining room filing up so I filled out the form with my name, party size, phone number, & email.  It's about a 17 minute drive from my house so I figured it would be perfect timing.  When we arrived, I gave the hostess my name and told her I had "Joined the Wait List" online.  She didn't have my name and her support staff didn't have me down either.  Her associate or manager who didn't introduce herself accused me of sending it to the wrong Olive Garden.  I checked and showed the hostess that I did indeed sent it to the Tampa Palms Olive Garden, and showed her my form with my name, number and email.  She asked again for my number, and then said she added me to the list. I then went from just mad to absolutely furious when I asked her if I was on the bottom of the list or where I would have been if there system didn't have a glitch.  She said where I would have been, but then I got a text saying my wait time was 60 - 70 minutes.  Its ok to make mistakes, I understand that there are issues as they open their dining room, but don't lie to me and add insult to injury.  I told to take me off the list, and will never be back.

The bar area was nice. However the drag show was probably one of the worst I have ever seen. All the queens did was walk around and beg for money when there wasn't a drunk bride on the stage for them to lap dance with. Be ready for them to beg for money for a very half assed performance. In the beginning the host queen told everyone to get as drunk as possible. I'm sure it was to make the performance seem more tolerable. If I were really drunk, maybe it would have been.

The food was pretty good and authentic to what you order. No wait to get in. Greeted almost right away. Only catch is you have to pay additional cost if your bill is less than $15, but that's an easy solution and just add everything to one tab. Would highly recommend!!

Awesome Viet restaurant that's not far away in South Philadelphia. Great for Pho, Bun Bo Hue or broken rice and the like. Drinks are cheap too.

I'd recommend #101 from the Pho menu!

I have been going to this yogurt shop since it opened many, many years ago. When my dad was alive I always brought him there for a big chocolate cone, which he loved.  It is the best frozen yogurt I have ever had. The owner is a lovely, friendly lady, and the service is always great. In fact, Sundaze is SO good that it put the bi yogurt shop across the street out of business. It is a 5 star shop!!!!

Never a disappointing time at choo choo. Consistent pho since I was a kid to now. I always bring my frIends here if we want pho in chinatown. 

Fast service, clean establishment. Make sure your pho comes steaming hot! Tastes the best that way. 

$10-12 after tip for a big bowl of pho? Why not?

If you guys are cheap like me and are in the area and are craving pho, come to this place. I got the large $8.85 pho dac biet. It only came in 2 sizes which I was happy because it's the only 2 sizes I get when I go to pho places, large and XL. Their pho is pretty good to be honest. The broth itself had a sweet beefy flavor which is the key to a good broth. They gave you a lot of meat and noodles which satisfied me. This place is pretty small so don't take it personal if one of the staff members bumps you. In my opinion there's too much wait staff in that small restaurant and half of them is doing nothing and playing on their phones but I don't mind that. They need to shorten up the staffs with only 3 waiters. My overall rating is 5/5

This place has amazing pho! I've had pho in different places and this place was one of the good ones.

I actually came here while on vacation and unfortunately came down with a cold and I knew something warm would make me feel better. The broth had such a great flavor and made me feel a lot better.

I ordered the 101 pho bowl, which comes with everything except meatballs (but you can add them in for $2).
The pho bowls come in large and x-large. I had a hard time finishing the large, but it was so worth it! It had such great flavor and the meat was delicious! I also ordered the shrimp summer rolls. I LOVE these rolls. Their peanut sauce was yummy!! 

For dessert I ordered a Taro smoothie and it was delicious.

The environment was very nice and clean. The staff was amazing and very friendly. They were very attentive. Our food came out within 10-15 minutes at most. 

If you're craving some pho while you're in Philly, you have to come here!

We dropped by this place for brunch last weekend. We were somewhat overly aggressive with the lyfting because bae automatically thought we were somewhere far away like old city but in actuality we were probably less than half a mile away lmao.

No reservations are required for brunch mid-afternoon on Saturdays. We came here for BRUNCH. At 2pm on SATURDAY. When we were first seated we were given like a dinner menu? I'm not tryna eat dinner at 2pm. I had some juicy eggs on the mind and I panicked. Luckily brunch menus were provided upon our request and brunch is available all day! Phew.

The bloody mary was a no-brainer but this place also has other good selections for brunch drinkage. The bloody marys themselves have unique variety: CHEESEBURGER bloody, GRILLED CHEESE AND BACON?!?!? bloody. We went with the classic bloody mary which had an overwhelming horseradish flavor and spice. 

I was eyeing the chop chop salad which has salad classics in addition to avocado, egg, quinoa, and green goddess dressing. I ultimately am an egg brunch bitch and ordered a 3-egg omelette with cheddar, peppers, and spinach. Omelette and all egg items are served with a side of "homies" and toast. Omelette was cooked well without me having to request it "almost on fire". Fillings were adequate in their quantity.

My beau had to make me JELLY and order the chop chop salad. Luckily for me she was unable to consume it in its entirety so I took one for the team and finished it off. Unfortunately the salad literally did not come with dressing, which was odd. We requested a side and had to toss it ourselves. The salad was really quite good and multidimensional. 

Also had I known they were playing the GIANTS game I might have requested to sit in the bar area, they have a few large TVs for sports viewing.

Looked it up on yelp and tried it for the first time. We started off with the lobster poutine for the appetizer. The server was spot on with her recommendation. I had the French Dip, my wife had the Crab Cake Sandwich and my daughter had the Kobe Dog. The food was fresh, hot and delicious. The service was great. As we left there was a small band starting to play Frank Sinatra music, we missed out. I'll definitely eat here again.

Yesterday's lunch devours lead me to one of my favorite Phó  spots in Chinatown. Pho Xe Lua is a Vietnamese restaurant dialing up traditional soups and noodles in a basic setting. Yesterday, I ordered the traditional Seafood pho with no noodles and side of white rice . I also ordered the snails  in lemongrass which were absolutely delicious . If you ever find yourself in Chinatown, and wanting traditional Vietnamese foods? Check out Pho Xe Lua! #philadelphia #seafood #philly #crab #shrimp #food #foodporn #foodie #foodstagram #foodphotography #foodblogger #lemongrass #water #ginger
Very comfortable and clean place with caring staff. LeeAnn and Dr B are always so wonderful with my animals. Thanks! :-)

Ok, I didn't like this place and won't be back. Here's why:

1. This may seem trivial to some, but I HATED having my name called on a loudspeaker to pick up my order. Embarrassing, LOUD, and I don't need every patron knowing my name/ order. Why the heck is this necessary in a tiny smoothie shop is beyond me. PLEASE, at least assign customer numbers Five Guys style so the world doesn't have to hear my name at 82938283 decibels.

2. My smoothie was not properly blended whatsoever. When I started drinking it I just thought it was bland, but I discovered the bananas/chocolate all caked at the bottom. No thank you. If you can invest in loudspeakers, you can invest in a Vitamix or at least a decent blender.

3. I don't want to sound like a snob but I will anyway... all of the employees were dressed lke ex-cons in dirty outfits with the attitudes to go along with it. The guy taking my order was unfriendly, did not educate me about how the process worked even though I told him It was my first time here, and continued conversations with his coworkers while taking my order. 
Not really my kind of customer service. Smoothie shops are kind of a niche - well dressed and friendly employees, large selection with a level of customer education, and caring about pleasing your customer. I Implore management to work on this obvious issue.

On the flip side, the guy taking out the garbage wished me a good day. Maybe he could teach his coworkers about how to run a business.

I had their pho special and noticed they did not rinse my pho noodles well because my soup was starchy and cloudy. But looking at other people's photos, their broth seems clear. Since my friend and I came in on a weekend, I assume they rushed my order. It eventually became hard to eat and broth is a little bland and lack the "pho" aura. I still haven't given up hope at this place yet since their other dishes look authentic. Will give this place another try but will not get the pho.

Gasmasters came to our house in January to fix our fireplace.  Charged $85 trip fee and told us that would be applied to the cost of the repair once they ordered the necessary part.  Months went by with multiple phone calls and emails made to Gasmasters checking on status, only for them to tell us in September that their parts person left and it was his fault that they never received the part.  They came out later in September, ignored the $85 prepayment from the January visit, and the original instructions that included a replacement remote control.  Another $85 trip charge was added plus the excessive repair charge.  The repairman had no information on the remote request until I asked him to go back to his January paperwork where it clearly stated new remote was needed.  They proceeded to come back a 3rd time and attempted to charge us ANOTHER $85 trip fee.  In between the last 2 visits, I talked to Richard to schedule the remote visit.  Expressed my concern that we were overcharged.  He said he would look in to it.  We scheduled the visit for the following week.  No one showed up.  I called and he had no recollection of our conversation and insisted no appointment was scheduled.  
BOTTOM LINE:  IF I CHARGE THEM FOR THE AMOUNT OF TIME I TOOK TO GET THEM TO DO THEIR JOBS AND PROVIDE GOOD CUSTOMER SERVICE, THEY WOULD BE PAYING ME!
I STRONGLY URGE PEOPLE TO NOT USE THIS COMPANY.

Nice spot for date night. Live music at 6pm on a Friday night. Fast service and great customer service. They have a dinner menu but they also have all day breakfast. The burgers seem to be really popular here. Only thing I would say are they are light on the seasoning.  The drinks are great because they are loaded with alcohol lol. I would definitely return.

Quick, cheap and good pho! Can't beat that. Sure there are a lot of phi places around the city that people like, but i think pho, like the cheesesteak, has become something where everyone has a go to place. This is mine. Typical Chinatown service (not saying much) but the food is good and that's really what you should be looking for when it comes to the restaurants in the area.

I am a guy who sticks out in these settings. That being said walking into these environments already prove to be an obstacle. The issue is beyond the weird glares... I recieved an especially condescending remark about my inability to read from the jonas brother look alike with the red  karate kid bandana rolled lazily on his forehead who stood with poor posture atthe register. I proceeded to carefully choose my breakfast selection and came up to the counter acknowledged his remark to which I recieved a glare and a number 6 slammed in front of me. I sat and waited for my order to be filled. I would like to say that the waiting and kitchen staff were cordial and welcoming. Unfortunately the prepubescent face they put in front of the register needs to check his privilege and poor sense of humor as it has lost you a customer

I wish there were laundry places like this everywhere!!! Clean! Free GOOD WiFi! Good prices! And the Dryers are stellar and are $1.50 for like 100min. 

Cool pop chill music playing the whole time, open 24/7 and there's a universal phone charging station. 

The best laundry experience if you have to go laundry!
Tashua is very attentive and super sweet! She patiently answered any questions or concerns I had about waxing services. My whole family goes to her for waxing.

Foods good, service is good, but variety in terms of whole wheat pasta is no longer a choice available for customers with diabetes. With the population increasingly having to contend with diabetes, it is a clear lack of understanding to not offer a better and more conscientious effort to help decrease the passive restrictions embedded into our culture that's killing us.

Please resume offering whole wheat pasta!!!

Wonderful yogurt, and wonderful service. What I really love about this place however is their frozen yogurt pies. They are to die for! During these COVID-19 times, the flavors are limited but there is always something wonderful on hand.
Order Togo food and wow I was disappointed. The soup looked like it was rushed with little bits here and there. Never going to order from this location again.
Stopped at three other laundromat prior to choosing this one. Nicest and cleanest in the area.
Derek was wonderful super attentive. Food was good salad was great as always. Also enjoyed my blue Hawaiian which Derek recommended.

Not only this branch, but the corporate executives in Phoenix, provide the absolute worst customer service one can imagine. On a real estate loan, their appraiser used the wrong peoperty; their check printer never did get my checks to me; their loan officer was 20 minutes late to a scheduled closing; and their follow up to correct the situation was horrendous!

Went on a Wednesday around noon, busy but not too many people. A lot of machines were out of order. The App was not working for me, so coming here was a complete waste of time. Every washer I tried to use the app said "washer is not responding". I noticed since the app works via Bluetooth if you were trying to use, say, 121 the app would pick up 131 so if you do come here to do your laundry make sure you're paying for the right machine. This place seems convenient, but if the app isn't working properly it's a total fail. Very disappointed in my experience. I ended up going to the Florida Express Laundry instead, which was far less busy & has plenty of washers varying in size.

I LOVED Ulele! Their drinks were awesome and the food was incredible. I loved the menu and how diverse it is. I get so tired of trying some place new and you open the menu and everything is so uninspiring. 
The Mojito was awesome! The oysters were excellent and I LOVED LOVED LOVED the scallops and I'm not a scallop person! 
The fried ice cream was incredible and done perfectly which isn't as common as it should be. 

Ill be back again for sure! I want to film my show here!

Attractive atmosphere, decent  food (nothing special) but prices are out of line.  $60 for two lunches, 2 iced teas, one small soup and tip - ridiculous!
Chicken fajitas portion was very modest and arrived with 3 tiny tortillas.  
It will be a while before I return to Teresa's.

The waitress/hostess was very rude. No customer service at all. I wanted to leave when we were ordering but decided to stay. That was a bad decision. She was on a personal phone call when she brought our food. And said we had to go for our drinks inside cause she esos to want to bring them out. Wtf? Do not come here.

Sundaze Yogurt has the perfect combination of great tasting frozen yogurt, warm and consistent service and offers a clean and delightful atmosphere.  Love the salted caramel.  It's my favorite place for yogurt in Tucson.

All of their bowls and smoothies are delicious. I eat the larger size as breakfast sometimes and it's sooo filling. I love that everything is vegan and you can basically customize everything for your bowl. All the girls working here are wonderful, always so friendly and helpful. The rewards program is basically buy 9 get 1 free- great deal compare to other places. My top 3 favorites smoothie/ juice/ bowl place in Tampa for sure.

Normally I love coming here! However I ordered a morning bowl yesterday and noticed it was missing half the ingredients on it, including the avocado they charged $1 extra for. When I came back the host was super nice about it, even offering to make a new one. I wish I remembered his name. My issue lies with the girl who was handling the food. She looked at the bowl and proceeded to argue with me saying that the  ingredients that were missing were definitely there. They weren't. She proceeded to keep coming back and forth between me and the kitchen staff telling me I was wrong. Why would I waste my own time driving back to correct my order that was very obviously missing HALF the ingredients that were listed on the menu. This experience left me with such a bad view of Goodness that I don't think I'll ever come back. I worked in restaurants for years and that is just unacceptable.

Pho Xe Lua is a great place if you want something good and cheap and fast at the same time. Def one of the best in Chinatown. Always try new things, especially the appetizers. You will be surprised. Pho (noodle soup) and broken rice platters are their known dishes. But don't forget to try their Rainbow Ice on their drinks menu. Just such a nice presentation and taste. 

The restaurant has not been remodeled for a while. But for the price of the food, I won't complain!

Three strikes against Cimarron. (1) Two years ago my cat went there for annual exam and shots and I had to get her myself from under their exam table. Despite my warnings that she acts feral when handled without me present, but I can calm her and make it work, they refused to let me be with her and took her to their back room. They then got her so upset she wouldn't alllow the exam and got away from them. Yes I had to go to the back room and get her myself from under a desk. I  chalked that up to bad cat behavior and kept with them for my new puppy last fall (Cats will go back to Cat Hospital who is farther away but excellent and doesn't have this issue with my cat.) 
(2) I paid for a full puppy package for my baby golden retriever in fall 2019- over $700 for the neuter, exams, vaccinations, wormings for one year. His neuter two months ago required an extra surgery for a non-descended testical so I chalked this up to the extra surgery... He was so sick after I brought him home - he had diarreah like water all over himself and all over the place for two solid days. I called the first day of it and they said "it happens sometimes."  It  was awful and I didn't think it was normal. I gave him no pain meds because it could worsen it, poor baby.  Then yesterday, strike three: (3) I called  because my (now 11 month old) golden retreiver  was lethargic, not eating,and salivating, obiously nauseaus and sick, so I called to bring him in and was told they had no appointments that day, but I could bring him the next day.(???)  I explained he was actually sick and in need of same-day exam, but to no avail, and  I even had to ask the gal to have the vet call me with advice.  I didn't get a call so in an hour I called again and she told me she had spoken to the vet who said, "that's not much to go on," and no mention of her calling me to go over it.  Upon stating my irritation I was told OK, I could drop him off and they would try to work him in during the afternoon. The lack of concern for their regular patient was the breaking point so made an appointment with VCA down the road -- Not even a patient there, but I told the gal his symptoms and she got me worked in by 2 and then their vet got on the phone with me and MADE room based on his age and symptoms. He got immediate blood work done to rule out organ failure and an exam and by 2 pm and was referred directly to emergency hosptial for an overnight stay for heat exhaustion, dehydration, and possible pneumonia or valley fever.  Also x rayed to rule out him swallowing a foreign object. Suffice it to say,  I won't go back to Cimarron.

I am a regular at Sundaze Yogurt. What a great small business. The owners are exceptional people and the staff they hire are great kids. The yogurt is fresh, not made from powder. I would highly recommend this yogurt shop. Buy local!

Just had breakfast at this cute spot for the first time. Amazing! We sat outside and enjoyed the breakfast burrito and the Ronald McGee sandwich. Both so fresh, light, and flavorful! Customer service was exceptional and we're excited to come back to try their wide variety of lunch and dinner options. The Açaí bowls also looked amazing!

Goodness is a local favorite breakfast spot. Great outdoor area, very friendly staff and super quick. Also if you like coffee and/or peanut utter the Daily Buzz is for you!! Also really like Healing Vines smoothie too. So many more things to try

First visit today, and was not impressed. We got the OG burrito and avo toast, which were both decently flavorful and yet obscenely overpriced.  My biggest gripe is the absolute and utter lack of an even basic understanding of customer service.  I ordered the beet juice, and it was delivered to our table quite full with a lid on it.  But no straw. My husband popped up to the counter to get one, and was told "straws are only for the smoothies, not the juices."  The thing is, it was BEET JUICE. And really full.  Taking the lid off would mean I would be wearing beet juice.  The food delivery girl was walking past our table, and I asked again for a straw.
Her, "Oh, we're trying to get away from those. But we do have reusable straws for sale by the register."
Me: ...
Her:...
Me: "So, are you telling me you are unable to provide me with a straw?"
Her: "We have straws, but those are for the smoothies."
Me: ...
Her: ....
Me:  May I have one?
Her: (exasperated sigh), turns without responding and comes back to hold out a smoothie straw.

Please note that all during this interaction, I am staring at cups full of plastic utensils at the pick up counter ten feet away.  So, Goodness, are you anti-plastic or aren't you? And how about a little common freaking sense and a modicum of customer service skills in your staff? Your POS asks for tips at check-out, and I can see why you would want them up front.

I'm typically a "if you can't say something nice" kind of yelper, but this really ticked me off. I gave you thirty six freaking dollars for a meal that would have cost us $25 at First Watch, and you made me fight to get a damn straw? Seriously?

The decor here is contemporary.  The chairs are a mix of wood and metal with farm house style tables.  At lunch they are usually full.  There are also outdoor tables with posts for umbrellas, parking in the strip mall is a problematic but look for parking in the back.  I love the healthy options although I've only had one meal here, and it was the Mediterranean quinoa which was tasty.  But my go to, especially if I'm in a hurry is the Daily buzz, which includes: House cold brew, peanut butter, chocolate, banana, agave, chia seeds, whole milk.  I like coconut milk better than almond milk and they have subbed that for me or added half almond or half coconut.  I like the ability to make changes to my food.  This is a staple for me!

I personally think most of the Vietnamese restaurants in Chinatown are not that good as I have tried them all. However, choo choo is the go-to and hands down the best one in this side of the Philadelphia.

The pho is good, although on the salty side. I get an extra large bowl which serves my cravings (I also chug a couple glasses of water an hour later). The spring rolls and summer rolls are very good as (along with lotus salad) are my staple appetizers to order. Bo kho, pork and rice platter and vermicelli dishes are good as well and I recommend them.

Service is fast and attentive. Overall, you'll be left satisfied!
Our waitress Donna was fantastic; helpful and knowledgeable !!! Great work !!   An ideal server and asset to the restaurant.

It is just okay 
If you crave for authentic viet foods, this is not gonna be your type

The service was not good.  We should have left the moment we walked into the smell of stale cigarette smoke.  I don't think it was in the dining area but coming more from the back. The (Lipton???) tea had something floating in it and when I went to wipe out the wet extra cup, it had tea in it that had never been cleaned out. I couldn't get myself to eat anything after that. The other 3 at the table said the food was less than desirable. Just do yourself a favor and eat at the many other local restaurants.

It has been three days since we had our first meal at Classic Spagetti and I have given a lot of thought to the experience prior to posting this review. We had a party of 20. When we arrived there were four people already at the tables. Each had drinks. Over the course of the next 15 minutes or so the balance of the party had arrived.
