We were there close to 30 minutes before our drink order was taken. Three people had appetizers delivered shortly after we arrived and we were never asked. The entire evening was extremely disorganized as far as the level of service. The hostess of the group had called in advance to make a reservation. So the management had time to staff. While we were there only two or three other tables were occupied. My husband and I ordered Spagetti Marinara. Thank goodness we travel with chilipitens. Otherwise the sauce was extremely bland. We have never eaten Italian food without it being accompanied by bread. No Bread was offered. One of the parties had ordered a steak and the server apologized for the delay. It had been overcooked and they prepared a second one. This experience can be the result of an inexperienced staff member who did the best she could on her own. However, the restaurant is owned by someone with experience. Disorganized service and mediocre food is not a good combination. One will often offset the other. On this night both were a fail.

If you're craving healthy, yummy food you can feel good about, look no further!
The food at Goodness is fresh and you can tell by the first bite that the ingredients are quality. 
The lemonade was so delicious and refreshing, I definitely recommend getting a  glass and can't wait to go  back and try the strawberry lemonade!
The bowls are also tasty, I would say the size is adequate for the price (I had some left after I ate, but it wasn't quite a whole meal worth left), but I see it being pricey especially if feeding a family!
I would definitely(and likely will) to try other bowls!
Also if you're a fan of the TV show The Office, you'll probably get a kick out of the names of some of their menu items! Overall, I really enjoyed Goodness and will likely be back!

I've been too some nice WaWa's and this one has potential, but the day I went, there was trash all over the sidewalk outside, the bathrooms weren't clean, and the area by the registers is congested and it's difficult to tell if you are in line or not. 

Big redeeming moment though when a worker/possibly the manager, jumped into action to get the registers caught up.

I'm here from out of town celebrating my son birthday and I can't believe the waitress here is so mean I don't know if she having a bad day but the host that sat us is also rude walk us to the table n stop and didn't even say nothing where we sitting at then didn't even give us a kids menu I'm not sure if I should just have my food Togo

The food deliver safety for the restaurant is an A grade. They have you order online and pay online without touching. The pickup also touch less because you roll down window of the passenger side for them to drop the food. The check in also touch less by said that you are here to pickup. 

The Carside pickup simply doesn't work. I have put my order in the restaurant at 1pm for 4:40pm pickup. I arrive and check in at 4:39. I was assigned a parking spot for pickup to wait for them to take the food to deliver to the car. I was wait there till 5:07 pm for deliver the food to my car. 28 minutes wait at partial shade area. Some car doesn't even have shade area. For taking so long to wait for the food I thought they must be cook the food when you check in. It was not. It is warm food and seem like seating at the kitchen. Obviously the my early put in order was cook on time but the communication from check in to food delivery to car was not coordinated. I also see an customer who missing a sauce and they take about 10 minutes to get the missing sauce to him. The execution is a F. 

With that said. Their grade could be D. But I give them C because the food still tasty.
I am giving them 3 stars, as I have been to few better places for Thai food in nyc and even in philly . These folks are average !

This is the best local bike shop in Tucson!  Brian's shop and team offer some of the best service and experience I've ever had.  Since discoverng, I buy all my gear and get all my servicing done by their expert technicians here.  Highly recommend.

BBQ lemongrass chicken can be hit or miss at most Vietnamese restaurants. This one was above average, really tasty. My boyfriend ordered the chicken wing appetizer, be careful the chicken was not fully cooked. Pho was good, average.
She did my eyebrows. Shaped and tinted them. She was wonderful, very professional, kind, Personable. I can't wait to go back and see what other services she offers. She's the bomb!!

We very recently had to have our dog put down here. He had an issue with his spine and spent days at cimmaron while they tried different things to save him. Although we didn't get the final outcome that we were hoping for, we are so grateful to everyone there for their kindness and compassion. From Rachel and Claire on the phone, to Leanne and Dr Bohnke when we were there saying our goodbyes; everyone was so caring and helpful to us. Thank you all for trying to save our pup and for making a heartbreaking decision a little bit easier.

I'm not a Pho expert. I do know that they make it better than I would. I usually grab the Veg Pho and I think that it is suitable. For 5 bucks a ton of broth, noodles, lime, basil, sprouts, mixed green veggies etc. I dislike the chewey rubbery tofu strips so I don't put them in my soup. Tiny dirty place, but it's Philly Chinatown no surprises there. I said 5 bucks.

Haven't been to Olive Garden in a bit so was really wanting to.  I should have stayed away....Dinner came out immediately after the soup and salad did, really I had maybe 2 bites of my salad and the dinner was there already.  It just sat there while I finished my salad and by that time the noodles were cold and stiff the lasagna was Wayover seasoned like super super salty almost like someone just dumped salt on it.  Good thing the salad wasn't bad because that was the only thing I was able to eat.  
    The waitress did come over to ask how everything was, but she asked while we were still having the salads (you know because the dinner came out at the same time). Didn't see her again until she was telling us how to pay for it.  

Definitely not going back food was just awful and I spent $70 for us to eat a fucking salad

My friends and I saw this place on yelp and had to check it out. The food was decent but didn't meet our expectations. We got the lobster poutine and burgers. The lobster poutine was pretty good but nothing special about it. The burgers were decent but again, nothing special about it. The service was pretty decent tho.

I used to think this place was just popular for its artsy/aesthetic healthy dishes and decorations, but wow this place is more than just pretty acai bowls! Everything I've tried here has been super tasty, fresh, and healthy. My favorite things to get are the Thai chicken bowl, kale Caesar salad wrap, pesto grilled cheese, original breakfast burrito, "new kid in town" breakfast burrito, and acai bowl. It's random but my mom, sister, and I all agree that they have the best breakfast burrito in Tucson. Not many places can make fresh and healthy food taste this good!

If I could give it a zero star I would! I feel like I should call the cops because I just got robbed for paying the amount I did for such garbage food. My wife got the veggie burger and she barely ate it because she has self respect and wouldn't lower her standards to such embarrassing food. I got the turkey burger, which I believe was under-cooked so that will be funny getting sick later... and fries which were so under-cooked that they might as well have given us whole potatoes!!! I am so ashamed that on my death bed I will always remember that this insult to my taste buds wasted 45 mins of my life that I will never get back. Thank you for slow, non-cooked, no-taste meal you somehow call a lunch.

#shuttheplacedown
This laundromat is state if the art. All machines are application based. No coins. Customer service is excellent, just send email through the app. You get prompt response.

We had to sit down at a dirty table and then clean it ourselves even though staff were standing around. Annoying loud music inside, went outside to escape the music. Waited outside so long for food I had to come back in because of the heat despite fans. When I finally got my turkey sandwich it was missing the cucumbers and avocado spread. Overpriced, uncomfortable atmosphere, bad experience.  My gfs Golden latte tasted super sour and was "premade" nothing in a golden latte should taste sour. Her side salad never came out which means I just paid $13.00 for a sandwich. Her sandwich was super spicy which would have been fine if they didn't give you tiny cups that you have to refill yourself for water. She got up probably 7 times to get water because the cups were so small. If I could I would give 0/5.

It really pains me to leave only one star for Olive Garden because it is one of my favorite restaurants. But my sister and I had a horrible experience this week at this location. 

First, it was lunch time, about 12:30 p.m. on a Friday and there was a line waiting to be seated. The hostess had to leave her post and wipe down tables for people to be seated. I have no idea where the busboy was. 

We finally got seated and got our menus. It just went downhill from there. 

2. Our salad plates were HOT like they just got out of the dishwasher and were not chilled like they should have been. 

3. We had to ask twice for our breadsticks. 

4. All the other tables around us were offered free samples of wine. We were never offered any.

5. My sister ordered a dinner sized meal but she was brought the lunch sized portion and had to send it back.  

6. When she did get her meal, there was no scampi sauce on it. The pasta was dry. She had to ask for more sauce and it was brought to her in a very small cup.

7. Not once did our waitress offer to clear away our used dishes and the plates piled up on our table. 

8. We were never offered refills on our drinks and had to ask for them

9. We took advantage of the $5 take home meal with purchase of an entree and we both ordered the stuffed fettuccini alfredo  But when we got home, we saw we were only given plain fettuccini. 

10. I don't know if they changed their recipes but my food's (the tour of italy) lasagna and chicken parmesan was highly over salted. I could not enjoy it as i usually have. The chicken was also overcooked and was totally dry. 

11. My sister always gets cappuccino with her dessert and it was on the menu, but our waitress said they did not have any. My sister was pretty disappointed. 

12. We waited and waited and waited for our waitress to come back to our table but she never did so we had to ask another waitress at another table for a take home box for my dessert. She brought it immediately

All in all, i will return to Olive garden but will probably not go to this location ever again. Bummer, because it's one of my faves.

6 years later, place is still great. My main measure of pho is the flavor of the broth and quality of the meat. The broth is Divine, may take the place of my 8 year favorite pho ha. 

This spot is on the fringe of Chinatown. Parking is always a problem which is why I don't go to Chinatown for pho. Other places with dedicated parking lots are available, but if you are on the area and don't feel like having Chinese food, then I would recommend it here

The Bar
I saw a bar on the outside on the main restaurant and inquired if I could purchase a cocktail. The blonde manager lady asked me if I was with the "party", which I assumed meant this may have been a separate open bar specifically for them. I said no, while the waitress standing next to me encouraged me to lie and say I was. I told her I wouldn't do that, and the blonde manager again asked me if I was with the party, and the waitress again told me to lie, and for the second time I told her I was not and would not. She then explained I could order a drink inside. I started by ordering a drink separately at the bar. The bartender asked me if I'd like a "off the menu" gin drink, so I said yes. It had a gin base and green chartreuse - way too much chartreuse. Tasted like floor cleaner. I told the bartender, and he immediately brought over simple syrup and doused it. Absolutely disgusting. 
The Music
The Frank Sinatra cover bad was absolutely atrocious, the worst live band I have ever heard. Many people in the restaurant were actually covering their ears because "Frank's" voice was so terrible. It was really appalling. 
The Meal
For dinner, the "center cut sirloin" was the toughest piece of meat I've ever had, and flavor was bland - I asked for it medium and it looked rare and extremely tough. The asparagus that came with it was also tough and undercooked. The accompanying french fries for both my steak and my wife's "lobster and shrimp salad sandwich" were not cooked through... They were limp and soggy. As I was telling one of the waitresses about the fries, she said they were already bringing out more fries. Why were these abominations even brought out in the first place? My wife's shrimp/lobster sandwich tasted like the shrimp was still frozen after four months of being in the freezer. Another family member had the pesto with crab meat in it - the crab meat was tough and disgusting, the whole dish was bland and flavorless. The floor had trash all over the place. When other guests arrived at both entrances of the restaurant, chaos ensued. Mostly, people waited with no one coming to seat them for a while, and staff walking by constantly. The location here is great, but the restaurant is being greatly mismanaged.

Needed dinner and did not want another Philly Cheesesteak so we decided to get pho! Pho is always a great option! First off, one thing I noticed was that this place offered indoor dining- they marked off some tables to create space between tables which is great but we opted to taking out anyway. We ordered a bun bo hue and a grilled pork/spring roll and shrimp vermicelli and the total came out to under $20. Def a tad cheaper than NY pho! We had to wait about 10 mins for our order so we walked around for snacks before coming back to pick it up. 
The orders felt heavy- they give a LOT of food. The bun bo hue noodles/bean sprouts/beef came in a take out container that was packed to the rim (no picture because we couldnt wait to eat) and the vermicelli was also packed! First, the bun bo hue is a little different from how I am used to eating it in NY. not bad, just different. The vermicelli was also pretty good. The grilled pork was soo good, it was pretty much the star of the night for me. Not sure what it is but it was reallly tasty I wished I got just a grilled pork vermicelli. Overall, a great meal!

this place is clean and the equipment is all new.  Cathy who works there is awesome and the wash dry fold is $1 per pound with 20% your first time.   One downside is no TV's but they have free wifi  so i watched my netflix which was fine.

We wanted to go to Pho 75 but since we stayed at the hotel close to Chinatown and this place seems to have good reviews and decided to give a go.  First they are Chinese not Vietnamese but nothing wrong with that because many Chinese comes from Vietnam and also we are from NYC so most of the Vietnamese restaurants are owned by Chinese.  Now that being said Philly has the best authentic Vietnamese food and that's one of the reason we like to have the authentic Vietnamese here.  So now we got that clear away here's my good impression.  Authenticity: 7, thé rest is 9.  Thé summer roll I ordered wasn't wrapped tight so it is loose and lumpy and hard to eat.  The spring rolls were big and not small.  Pho was decent.  Overall it is a 3/4 out of 5 for me.  So I won't be lazy next time and get ass to Pho 75.

I had heard good things about the restaurant and decided to go in for breakfast when meeting a new friend. The ambiance was laid back and the vibe was definitely on chill mode. 

I tried a more traditional breakfast of bacon, eggs, home fries, and toast. The bacon was perfectly crisped, the eggs were good and the home fries were good. The toast was served with a whipped butter, which I always enjoy. My friend had the french toast. The french toast was rich and flavorful. 

The prices were good and the food was good, while it was nothing outstanding, i enjoyed myself and would definitely give it another try.

I do not recommend getting Thai food at this place. The pad Thai I ordered came soggy and gross. The green curry broth was also horrible, it was gooey and not like how coconut milk should be like. 

I've been to this location before and ordered Vietnamese which was much better.
This place is super cute and delish!! Nicole is a kick ass server - Get in her section and you will be stoked! Happy Sunday brunch Funday!

Do not go if you are black!! They don't like black people here they have a dress code that clearly targets styles of clothing black guys wear! And there is a video circulating of the owner calling the black customers niggers!!! Do not support this place!!!

The takeout ordering was very easy! I ordered a smoothie and Aztec bowl online and picked it up with no problem. They have safety procedures in place and it wasn't at all busy. 

The food is always great, you really cant go wrong with anything!

I ordered a 24 oz ACAI bowl. It was delicious! I didn't give it a better raining because the cup was not even close to full. The photos posted on here are deceiving. I paid over $14 for a 24pz cup not a 16oz cup.

One thing comes to mind when someone mentions Olive Garden: SALT. The food is so salty, it's inedible. The only thing that would bring me back to this restaurant is if it suddenly became cool to have cankles from water retention.

Why is this chain so successful?

Dinner last night at what we now refer to as the "Salt Lick restaurant.  Why are the breadsticks so darn salty and why wreck a perfect piece of salmon by dumping salt on it? We also bought 2 entrees to go, will review that order tomorrow.  The salad was way overdressed so that was also not edible after a coupla bites. All in all not a restaurant we will try again.  If you need extra sodium this is the place for you...

I love this laundromat!  It is always very clean.  I have brought bedding here to be laundered.  Karen was very helpful to me.  When I picked up bedding everything was so clean, bright, smelled great, and folded perfectly.  She is so helpful to all the customers there.  She is constantly on the move making sure machines are in great running order!  I recommend this place to everyone I know!

This is one of my favorites in Tucson for breakfast (and for working. It almost workes as an office for me sometimes.) I drink coffee, do emails, and enjoy good food. The ingredients are advertised to be fresh and organic. I feel good eating here. The staff is friendly. I've tried different bowls, burritos, salads, and others and like them all. I plan on trying all menu items. It's a comfortable place and good food for me. Two recommendations for breakfast: original burrito and cacao warrior. The warrior is mixture of coconut, seeds, granola and berries providing a nice mixture of smooth almond milk texture with crunchiness. This morning the warrior is extra delicious!!

I'm happy with the veterinarians on staff, and very happy with the clinics hours of operations, you can't beat the hours for working pet parents, however, their customer service seriously lacks. When talking to the front desk person about my dogs prescription food and trying to explain I needed her to email it to me so I can upload it to the pharmacy that I chose for quicker service, she said she would "try" to email it and then said she had another call and had to go, cut me off. Wow!!! Not the first time, something like this has happened. It was a bit of an urgent situation, as it takes time to get this stuff processed and delivered and the vet office only had 11 cans in stock and told me it would take 2 weeks for them to get it. My dog has serious digestive issues from painful constipation to throwing up.  

Even more interesting, the vet office had no idea my dogs original prescription food was back in stock (several problems with prescription food due to the pandemic)

Improve your customer service please!

Got the spring rolls, beef carpaccio and vermicelli bowl.

The spring rolls were fresh but awkwardly wrapped. Now that we got that out of the way, the other two dishes were good! 

The bowl was made well and the noodles yummy. The beef carpaccio was tasty and sliced very well. 

Most vietnamese restaurants may mostly focus on pho or roles. I like that this restaurant offered more variety.

I've been a huge fan of this place for a while now, but today they really sealed my business! Outstanding customer service and friendly staff. Their açaí bowls are my favorite in town. I love coming here for a delicious treat, I really can't get enough! The mango jungle is to die for!!
Been coming to this place for 16 years. Always yummy and I love how they have different creamy flavors. Thank you!!

The service was very terrible. The was very snappy when asking about the drink we order even though she got the wrong order. And we found bugs in our food. When dealing with the issue the lady was rude and tried to insinuate that we had put bugs or lied about having bugs in our food when 5 people in our group found bugs in our food. She tried to solve it with a discount even though she just gave us a dollar back. I'm course with corona it adds steps to things but the way she handle it was rude and wasn't accommodating. It sad cause I definitely thought this was a spot for me and my friends since I been there a couple times in the past but the service and the way she treated us just made me never want to go their again

I really dislike giving bad reviews on establishments. My hope is that with this review maybe things will change. I am a huge fan of Armature works because of the variety of foods they offer and the environment. I decided to give SOHO juice a try after seeing they were new to Armature works. Another thing that compelled me to give them a try is their vegan options. 

Well, I've tried SOHO juice on two different occasions. The first time I tried the vegan chocolate cookie dough donut. Simply put, it was not appetizing. I paid $4 for the donut and it tasted pretty bad. It's hard to even explain the taste. It definitely wasn't worth the money. The taste was so off that I didn't even finish it. 

I recently decided to give SOHO juice a second try and gosh do I regret it. I purchased the Açaí bowl, which with tax costed me $13. At other establishments I've paid about $10 for açaí bowls so SOHO juice definitely has theirs priced pretty high. I was hoping the quality would measure up to the high price, sadly, it did not. The açaí bowl was watery and didn't taste good at all. According to the description there is supposed to be strawberries but none were chopped up and placed on the top of my bowl like the bananas. When I asked about this, I was told that the strawberries are blended in with the açaí mix. Also, there was no taste or hint of almond butter in my bowl which was also in the description. Honestly, the bowl tasted a little earthy almost like dirt. 

Sadly, even the customer service was poor. There were about 4 young girls behind the register and all of them were chatting and not even focused on properly making my bowl or ensuring I was satisfied with my experience. I can say without hesitation that I will not be back to SOHO juice. There are so many other establishments that have quality food, better prices and are more attentive to their customers.

I met a friend here for lunch for the first time today.  I got the Kale Citrus salad and a bottle of water, and she got some sort of steak quinoa bowl with a super delicious yogurt sauce on the side.

The place itself is cute, though when I was there all of the tables were dirty, and for the hour that I was there nobody came out to clean them.  So, after I ordered, I found the least dirty table and sat down to wait for my companion.

Ordering was fine.  The guy wasn't overly friendly, didn't even crack a smile when I walked up to the counter.  He wasn't rude, but he wasn't memorable, either.  

My salad was nearly identical to a salad I get for half the price at Trader Joe's.  It had butternut squash, cranberries, pumpkin seeds, brussel sprouts and a citrus dressing.  It was yummy, and while it wasn't super expensive as far as salads go, while i was eating it I kept thinking that I get the same salad, the same size, for a lot less.  Maybe I should have gotten something else.  Maybe I had different expectations since it did cost more.  I don't know.  

I'm totally willing to come back here.  They had some smoothies that looked delicious, and some of their other vegetarian fare looked like it would be worth a try.  I wasn't a huge fan after today, but I didn't hate my lunch.  It was a three star experience, "A-OK" as Yelp puts it.  Food that was ok, and service that was mediocre at best.
Dip duo: TERRIBLE ! taste like frozen pizza sauce..doesn't taste anything like a lasagna, would not recommend to anyone since it'll be a waste of time

My boyfriend and I go to Olive Garden all the time as it is my favorite place to eat of all time.  Though this experience was extra good and one to talk about.  Our server gave me three (surprisingly big) glasses of different types of wine to sample/taste before I chose which one I actually wanted to purchase.  Extra wine is always a plus.  Though it was not the wine that made me write this review it was the service.  Everyone including our server was very pleasant and courteous and made my dinner night a great one.  I would absolutely return to this location.  Thanks!
Awesome frozen yogurt! I love the Peanut. Butter and Cake Batter flavors. Great service as well!

This was my go-to Vietnamese restaurant for pho in Chinatown.  But, lately it seems like quality has depreciated a lot.  Price is reasonable but it is still low value if food is low grade.  Two stars for poor quality food and value, despite friendly service. 

Disappointment:
It is the worst of all emotions
Creeping in like a snake
Seizing your breath and tongue
A chill that raises the hair on your arms
Your stomach drops and your face 
Turns hot
Disappointment. 
It is not fleeting like anger
Or easily soothed like sadness
It's brother is bitterness and
It's sister is misery 
Leaving a stain that can only be cut out 
Disappointment.

OMGoodness soooo gooood! This was my first visit; loved the ordering process to make your own; the staff was helpful and I will definitely be back! Hope to visit all the locations-Armature Works is. so cool:)))

I previously rated them very high, but I had a very unpleasant experience last time I came here. I ordered "The Veggie" that is described as "garlic kale, butternut squash, roasted peppers, hummus, balsamic glaze, french roll." Well, my sandwich ONLY contained the French roll (which was soggy and not toasted) and roasted peppers. The kale was replaced with spinach without them informing me of the change. THAT WAS IT!! Soggy bread with some spinach and a little bit of red pepper! Where was my kale? What about my balsamic glaze? Where was my hummus? I do not enjoy writing bad reviews, but I just feel like I was so cheated. I paid $12 for such a crappy sandwich, and that's just not right. I wish I took a picture of it, but I was too disappointed to think about that at the time.

I GENUINELY CANNOT BELIEVE THESE REVIEWS ARE FOR THIS PLACE. Pete is a kind heart but THE SINGLE MOST UNPROFESSIONAL MECHANIC I HAVE EVER HAD THE DISPLEASURE OF WORKING WITH. Very much like the only other negative review, I brought my car in for a check engine light. He put it on the machine and said I needed a camshaft position sensor and a new motor mount and to bring it back the next day and he'd take a look at it. The day went by, I heard nothing, another day went by, I heard nothing, so I went over and he says "you got a lotta problems with your car. Bring it back next week and I'll fix it in one day." Once again, I dropped it off on Monday evening expecting it back Tuesday evening. I hear nothing. I call him up and he says "oh, um now you have a bad strut and a bad axle and they need to be replaced too, it will be ready tomorrow. I uber home and come back the next day and my car hasn't moved. Long story short, he tells me I can pick up my car at the end of the day 3 days later, I'm come to get it, he is GONE, never called to say the car was ready, his partner has to call him and he says, on the phone, "it's all set! ". I drive off with the car and all of the lights come on. I call him and try to explain what's going on and he tells me that he won't stand for my attitude. I continue anyway and he says it's because "aftermarket parts don't work on my vehicle" so he ordered a different one it will be in tomorrow. If you remember he said it was all set and that I could take it. I drop it off the next day for him to fix it, to no avail. My car is still in the EXACT CONDITION I DROVE IT ONTO THE LOT IN. Also, while my car was sitting it got a ticket that he took off of my car and never told me about. ALSO, he charged me 350 for "all of his labor!" I will never ever ever even walk by this place again! EVER!

This is probably the best pho in philly!! BBQ pork chops on the broken rice, shrimp summer roll, house special pho, salt & Pepper squid, curry shrimp. Oh my god so many good stuff. You guys really need to come in and check it out. Also don't be scared to order the raw beef steak, it's amazing.

Stubbled upon this place while visiting the historic sites in Philadelphia over the weekend.  The atmosphere was welcoming and the staff were very attentive and pleasant despite the restaurant being rather busy.  We ended up coming during a time when they were serving their brunch menu!  Yay!! The food was excellent!!! I got the Chop Chop without bacon and a blueberry muffin (which was grilled).  Yum! The salad was HUGE!  No way I could finish it and I felt bad because it was so good.

This is probably my favorite pho spot in chinatown and I come here quite often when I'm craving as it's much closer to me than little Saigon. The portions are great for the price and the pho is delicious. They also prepare it extremely quickly. 
I also am a fan of some of their appetizers such as the spring rolls and the summer rolls. Their peanut sauce is very good as well.
My friends have gotten some of their other dishes and have enjoyed them. I say that they weren't bad but I would probably stick to the pho.

It was cheat day so we splurged on FroYo! Happy we found this place driving by. The owners were working and seemed very kind and committed to their craft. The first few flavors were ok: peanut butter and mocha something so we moved on to vanilla and chocolate. No complaints on our end. I actually (surprisingly) enjoyed the sugar-free flavor they had and mixed it with my vanilla. With a plentiful scoop of caramel cups and brownie bites, I smiled until I saw the bottom of my cup.

Tasty food and nice atmosphere. Unfortunately though, they are just like most every other restaurant in that their alcoholic drinks are nearly all ice and very little drink. 

Their Seafood Alfredo was more like a lunch portion but with a dinner price. It was a pleasant meal though because Katie took great care of us.

My first time being in this restaurant the ambiance was nice for a south philly American restaurant. I ordered the lobster roll my servers name was Jenna, she was very polite, speedy service and also recommended the lobster roll cause I informed her I was a pescatarian! The food came in less then 10 mins I was pleased with the portions and the price. Will definitely eat there again and I recommend the server as well.

Oh for goodness' sake, lunch mid-town just got great. We left feeling delightfully satisfied, glowing and healthy. It could be the cacao warrior, a heavenly bowl packed with acai, berries, hazelnut milk, and nibs and seeds of all incarnations. We split a thick albacore tuna salad sandwich with olives, cuke and sweet pesto. Our smoothie,  the bikini blaster or some such amusing moniker, was meticulously prepared and probably fulfilled all nutrition needs for a week. My only complaint was the brain freeze I kept getting from sucking the fat straw too hard because it was so delicious. Finally, a guilt-free lunch option on Campbell!

To all looking for a place don't look here. The staff is very very Unorganized. I requested to be transferred to a one bedroom apt. they lost my transfer papers then trued to charge me for staying in my old apt. After 3 weeks I told them how I felt. The same day they served me a non renew lease paper. When I moved in 2019 Everything was brand new. I few days later I started see Roches. I had them coming out of my dishwasher. 
They sent the Exterminator an a few days later they were back. I advice no one to move here. If I could give them a no stars

Yummy tomato soup!! I like getting the grilled cheese/soup combo.

I tried a Thai Peanut rice bowl one time and it was pretty bland. A lot of food for the price, though. 

I tried a Big Melon juice also and it was good. Expensive for just a drink, but that's pretty typical. 

I wish it stayed open later.

Quick and friendly service! After walking the riverwalk, a smoothie was the perfect reward. They have some that you can order off the menu or create your own. I did the Floridian and loved it!! 

I saw a bunch of donuts/cupcakes that were all gluten free - some were CBD infused. I didn't try any (this time), but they looked delicious! Hopefully I can make it back to try one.

My son and I visited this afternoon.  It's a small place, but seems to be clean and organized.  We were promptly waited on.  Prices are reasonable and they seem to have a good variety of smoothies and yogurt.  They also offered pies, which I'd like to try.  My smoothie was quite good and I liked that you could choose the juice.  My son didn't enjoy his as much because he was told they had to put juice in it.  There isn't a juice that would taste good with peanut butter so they just added water.
I always come to Goodness for this Mango Jungle Bowl. Today the bowl was just gross the strawberries in the bowl were not fresh and the açaí was yucky.

Best service I've had in a while. There was a long wait but of course, it is Sunday & the food came after a reasonable time. My waitress(Olivia) made the experience worthwhile, as if we were her only customers.

Cockroaches in the pho!

I have been to this restaurant several times and always liked the food.   But I went again with some friends last night and guess what we found in one of our bowls of pho?  A cockroach.  Yes, you read it correctly.  There was a cockroach, dead and looking as though it had been there a while, floating in the pho.

We stopped eating and complained, of course.  What was most disturbing was that the waiter look unsurprised!  It was clearly not the first time this had happened.  And he offered to get us more pho.  Needless to say, we refused.  Obviously the entire pot was contaminated.  Although the manager/owner apologized, it was only after it became clear that other diners began to notice.  We didn't pay for the pho, any of it.  But they still charged us for the rest of the food we had already eaten (mostly apetizers).

Apparently pho is made in advance and sits around for a while to ferment.  The same pot is used for days.  So if the establishment is not careful about cleanliness, things can fall in the pot.

We will never go back.

Goodness Juice Bar is probably is just OOOkkkkaaayyy in my book and here's why.

They definitely are going for the hipster-trendy-healthy-LAesque kinda feel. The decor and vibe of the restaurant definitely achieves that goal. But I feel like the food definitely fell short. For such a high price tag (especially for Tucson, but to be honest I won't pay that much even if Goodness was in LA)

Healing vibe juice: $6.5 for the smaller size. It was so strong of ginger it was difficult to swallow. I'm a fan of ginger and have had ginger in lots of juices before, this one just tasted like your aunt's hangover cure. Temperature wise, the drink was luke-warm so it was pretty hard to down. Just meh.

I LOOOOVE acai bowls, and I've been craving it so much since I moved down to Tucson. Unfortunately, Goodness' bowls fell short of my expectations (again, for such a high price tag I expected better, the average acai bowl in Phoenix/ LA are usually $5 or 6 at most). The bowls were liquidy, not quite frozen-cold. 

Mango Jungle $8.75 (3.5/5): tastes pretty great, besides the fact that it was pretty melted/ soggy when served, I enjoyed the blend of sweet honey/ mild with the tart taste of mango. 
Pink dragon $8.75 (1/5) : I've hard real dragon fruit in Asia and this tasted nowhere near the real taste of dragonfruit. Again, the bowl was melted and soggy; just very disappointing.

Anyhow, I won't be back anytime soon. If anyone knows of a place with decent acai bowls, please let a sistah knows.

Like most other Indian restaurant, SERVICE is what this restaurant misses too. Food - good. Service - Horrible! You don't have to wait to be seated as an employee has to play candy crush on his mobile! And you don't have to wait for water to be served to you even after 15 minutes when there isn't customers there at the restaurant, because the employee wants to play candy crush!

I've eaten here at least 5 times but to this day I still don't remember the name because my friends and I call it "the choo choo place" because of the sign outside. I had to check the pictures on Yelp to be sure I was reviewing the correct place! I initially heard about this place a couple years ago through word of mouth; everybody kept saying it's the best pho in Chinatown and I have to agree. I'm pretty familiar with the restaurants in Chinatown since I've lived here for a few years. This place has the best broth and the most meat which are the two most important pho elements for me, a novice pho eater and appreciator. 

The portions are gigantic. I'm known to have a huge appetite, but not even my nearly-bottomless-pit of a stomach can't contain an entire bowl of pho from here. And what is insane to me is that you can get a pho feast for less than $7! 

Service is very fast, but it is always a little awkward when there's a couple minutes of delay between each dish and everyone is waiting for the last person to get their food. That seems to happen a lot when I come here.

I'm sorry I wouldn't even want to give this restaurant a 1 star review. Yes it was busy tonight - Sunday 6/2/19- but the fact that the Service was quite slow and daft as well. Do yourself a favor and do not order their version of breaded shrimp. It comes spicy or plain. Both are horrible. The waiter was very understanding and did offer to bring me the other choice when I chose the spicy option first, but when I received my bill I had three charges of the same dish, one was for the table next to me when one the waiter tried to bring me the same dish twice. When I asked for it to be removed off of my bill altogether it took over 25 minutes for the waiter to come by saying his manager was coming by with the revise check. After about 15 more minutes of waiting around for this manager I finally flag down the manager and explained or asked him where my check was and he was so confused as to why he had to bring the check. The level of incompetence in this restaurant is baffling. I understand for Sunday night they were busy but that doesn't excuse the fact that they blatantly ignored us the entire time and try to get us to pay for another persons food

I have worked with Mr. McGuire on a loan. There have been many challenges. I am a big advocate of working from home. However, for some things working online and not face-to-face is like trying to see a whole football field through a straw. Mr. McGuire has been patient, helpful and knowledgeable. He has never once sounded exasperated, although I'm sure that he has been.  Additionally, I went in to the branch and was warmly received. These are tough times for many, often customer service takes a hit. National Bank of Arizona is demonstrating a good work ethic. How refreshing!

They have some really good food, I always get the plant based breakfast burrito and it slaps. The poke bowl definitely needs to be revamped, not really filling or worth the money for the price. The biggest issue is the wait, they seem to have an issue with outputting online orders in time as well as in person dine in, and the employee that told me my order wasn't ready seemed annoyed at me for showing up. Seems to be a staffing issue rn like everywhere else, just frustrating to see employees have casual conversations while orders are backing up.

went last night to icandy...  the doorman said it was "theme" night... no "work boots" so I was not let in... they are not work boots but "tims"... if they have four floors does this apply to my shoes?  I was really looking forward to seeing this new club from the inside... icandy taste sour... I won't be going back.

Without a doubt, from top to bottom, this is a tragedy. 
1. Location: sketchy part of Stone, north of Speedway. Business is hard to find because their signage is so small and the building looks like an old El Taco.
2. Get a new hostess. We got there for early dinner and told her we had reservations and she said she couldn't find them. Really? This is mid-week and how many people were you expecting at 5:30 p.m.? Mind you, the restaurant is empty except for one table. She finally finds the res and while the rest of our party arrives and is getting out of their car and coming in, she decides to march us to the table. I told her, let's wait for the rest of the people, but she just keeps on walking. I stood my ground (the table was close) and again said, lets wait for everyone...crickets...she turns around when she gets there, looks at us and starts to walk back to the front desk and by that time the rest of the family is inside. We had 2 children in our party (4 & 10). Miss Thing then informs us they don't have any children's menus! She didn't know where they were...whatever...shortly, our waiter comes over and suddenly she YELLS across the room that she found ONE child's menu. He very quickly runs over to her and tells her not to yell across the room. She then comes over, without said menu, and proceeds to read off the items that she has written down. Oh my word...
3. Get a new chef. Now, on to the food...
The boys ordered mac and cheese. Completely flavorless! Not one grain of salt to be found in the dish, small shell macaroni cooked to death.
I ordered a rib eye steak with Bone marrow compound butter. Hey! looks like I found the salt for the mac and cheese! It's ALL in the compound butter! Completely inedible. Let's talk about the steak. They choose to serve the cheap, bone in (NOT a cowboy cut) rib eye barely a 1/2 in thick which we got to pay $34 for plus additional for the butter...did I mention that it was inedible? the steak had NO flavor...what a disaster. 
The creamed spinach side was also a casualty of the salt storm in the kitchen.
I have to mention, the wait staff is VERY attentive and super nice. They couldn't explain the problems so here comes the owner...
Asking how we "enjoyed" our meal we proceeded to tell him. When he told us they also own and run Saguaro Corners, it became clear what the problems are (see my review of Saguaro Corners):
there is no leadership in the kitchen or in the front of the house. They just go along running the place without a clue.
He was gracious enough to comp a lot of our bill but we'll never go back again.
There's a lot of good steak restaurants here so don't buy the hype of the Spaghetti Western to cover up bad food.

All of my kids love the FroYo at Sundaze. 
My puppy's also love the puppy cups! 

Great service and delicious FroYo. 
Family owned and operated!
The smell in this place is awful.  What is it?  Moldy carpets?  The food is mediocre and pricey,  will not be back!

One of the best breakfasts I've had.  We booked a reservation after a walk that my family and I were participating in.  From the first phone call to to the last cup
Of coffee we had the best experience.  The service was impeccable!  Thank you to all for accommodating our group.  We will definitely be coming back!!!

Had our company Christmas dinner at this place.  Different with some surprises.  Salmon and prime rib was really tasty.  The peach cobbler was truly amazing and a great way to end a pretty good meal.  The atmosphere is on the cozy side.  Will be back to try a few of the other dishes.

I really want to give this place a good review, but every time I try something new I regret it and wish I just got what I know is good...

So far I've tried their avocado toast, peanut butter toast, ribeye banh mi, poke, and the healing vibes juice. The only things I could ever finish was the peanut butter toast and juice. Everything else I have tried I just could not finish because it was not good... 

I had the ribeye banh mi today and it was pretty tasteless... the bread they used as well was not great quality. The poke that I tried in the past was not good quality fish either. As for their avocado toast, it was just not hitting the spot. 

I weirdly really love their peanut butter toast, but I wonder if that because it has the least amount of ingredients...

So unhappy with my experience. I love the food, hands down one of my favorite places, HOWEVER, the customer service that I received (and have been receiving from Stephanie on multiple occasions) was appalling. Stephanie was rude, unapologetic and frankly a deterrent as a customer.  Again, the food is delicious and always prepared in a timely fashion. After speaking with my friends (who also swear that this is one of their favorite places eat) agreed that Stephanie's customer service was far below what should even be expected from a Mc. Donalds employee, NOR is this first time we were taken back by her comments to us. If I were the manager of this store I would highly suggest employing a new front staff to work hands on with customers who love your food so much. Stephanie, as the first impression of your store has accumulated an extremely poor representation of your company.

My husband and I were happy with this bank for a while until we accidentally overdrafted our account by $10. We incurred over $150 in overdraft fees. We were never once notified of our balance. I believe in paying for our mistake, but to me, that is a little ridiculous. We paid We went to close our account and there was no customer service whatsoever. There was no customer retention or apologies.

Alright, I've been here a million times and I need to update my review to 5 stars. I love Goodness! Because, well, the food is full of... goodness.  I am used to going to a place and having to pick apart a menu to find a healthy option. Here, it's all good-for-you food.

I really like their smoothie bowls when I'm craving something sweet. None of that artificial tasting smoothie flavors and the presentation is beautiful.  The savory bowls and salads are fresh and generously portioned. Several of my friends love the grilled cheese and soup. I like that they also sell bottled kombucha and other drinks.  I think the prices are reasonable for the quality and quantity of food. They do give a small discount with a Cat card if you have one handy.

I do wish the dining area was larger, because it can be hard to find a spot (all open seating). The patio is also not shaded so it makes sitting outside a little less pleasant.

Overall, I really do like Goodness. It is frequently the lunch spot of choice for me and my friends.

Shared a OG breakfast burrito and a PB with my girlfriend and it was amazing! The food was delicious, the staff was very friendly, and the building was very trendy and clean. 

I would recommend this place to my family and friends.

I've come here for good Viet food for years. Always solid food at great prices! The spring rolls are so crispy and crunchy with great filling. I've been to a lot of Asian restaurants and I think Pho Xe Lua has the best.

One thing I was sad about is that they no longer serve alcoholic beverages (cocktails were so good!), but it is BYOB if you want a drink with your food on a weekend night.

Really delicious Vietnamese food. there's menu items you usually wouldn't see at most Vietnamese restaurants like snails and pork belly. There's also a shake/bubble tea bar where I got my soursop shake with boba from.

Would definitely go back when I visit Philly again.

I will NEVER eat at Olive Garden. I always try to give this restaurant a second, and third chance but every single time i am proven wrong. EVERY SINGLE TIME, IT IS THE WORST EXPERIENCE. No matter what location i go to, they will never win me over. They always have shitty service. The salad has always has too much vinegar-where my tongue always is cut. THEY ALWAYS serve my appetizer,salad, and entree at the exact same time. Even though i specifically stated the their staff I DO NOT WANT MY FOOD BROUGHT TO BE AT THE SAME TIME. I like to progress with my dinner, starting with appetizer then a salad and then my entree. Like any other normal human being.


Sorry, but you're not a family restaurant. You need to change your Restaurant motto until you can actually fulfill it!

Had the opportunity to try this hidden spot today. They serve breakfast all day which is a bonus. If you want something super healthy and fits in your diet then this appears to be the place to come. I went with the OG breakfast Burrito and it was delicious. It came with a sauce that I can't remember but was super tasty as well. The portions are a little small but I guess it's more healthy then filling. Or just the right amount portion wise. Everything seemed to be fresh and the service was fast. If you want healthy head here.

This is our neighborhood Olive Garden. I have been to this place many time when my kid is young. He loves the Chicken Alfredo here. This Olive Garden at New Tampa is better than the Brandon and Bush location. It provides more quantities of food than the other two locations. 

Tonight they have a promotion of 4 course meal from $14. The entree on the $14 is not attractive. As a result, my wife select the four course with Shrimp Alfredo entree $17.50. I have the rosemary garlic chicken that is not in the four course meal. The four course meal came with chicken meatball with tomato sauce. It is good. My meal came with a soup Zuppa Toscana.  I love this soup with fresh kale, Italian sausage and  slice potato. It is good when you dip your garlic bread and let it sit for a few second and allows the soup sock into the bread. Then you eat the socking bread. Yum. The rosemary garlic chicken is ok for it price. No wow factor. 

Today I am disappointed on the service. They are slow. It almost want me to give them two stars. Base on the past experience, I give them 3 stars. They could have been 4 stars, unfortunate they do not earn that tonight.
quick wait times, tasty food would recommend

This place is amazing, I have been visiting it since it opened years ago. The food is delicious the cuban pizzas, creams, but my favorite that I tried today was the 8oz Lobster $24. I got what I paid for it was enormous delicious. Best lobster i have ever tried in the US. They gave you free bread with oil and garlic toasted, was awesome. Cant recommend it more. The customer service was great and the staff was very friendly. My congratulations to the chef.

The dryer at the house went out, so it's just easier to come do all the laundry. Tried finding a place that wasn't so crowded and stumbled across this place. It's the new way of washing I guess you could say. You down load the app, enter the washer or dryer # and it charges to your credit card. No need for quarters. The big washers you can wash 4lbs for $5. The dryers are only $1.50 for 40 mins. It's nice and clean. They have charging stations for your phones, and free WiFi. They have a drop off to have your clothes done for you, just not sure how much that is.

Wholesome and healthy! Great gluten free options, perfect for breakfast and lunch or a quick on the go bite! We got the breakfast bowl and breakfast burrito with the Morning Buzz smoothie. The service was a tad slow but overall great aesthetic, atmosphere and food.

Pho Xe Lua is a little gem for sure.

Their pho amusingly comes in two sizes: large or extra large, and I hope that's warning enough for you to come very, very hungry!  The pho is really good, even though I don't remember the exact kind I got, it had pork meat in it (very tender) and so many soft rice noodles.  I couldn't finish mine and practically had to roll my round self out of the restaurant.

The first time I came, I had pho but the second time I had heard a lot of good things about their Tom Yum Soup, so I knew I had to get that this time around.  I also ordered the snails (ugh, so delicious.  Also so many!) and their banh cuon cha lua (steamed rice flour rolls with Vietnamese sausage).

The Tom Yum Soup isn't the best I've had, but it hit the spot - I was really hoping for a bit more of that tangy / sour taste.  The seafood they had in it was also alright too, it tasted not as fresh as I was hoping.  I think because I came with such a high bar, that's why I felt a little bit disappointed after eating it.  The rice flour rolls were also maybe not quite what we expected, but it was fun to try even if it wasn't one of our favorites (this was probably just due to personal preference). 

The snails though!! They are a must have!! Just give them a try - you eat them by sticking your toothpick into the shell to pin down the snail meat and drag it out of the shell.  The marinade they were cooked in is straight up addictive.  You will love it, trust me.  

My recommendation? Get the snails as an appetizer.  Get the pho.  Leave EXTREMELY satisfied.

This place is very efficient and the menu is actually pretty expansive which is always a plus in my book. We ordered the veggie lomein, spare rib tips, boneless bbq ribs and almond cookies and we were not disappointed.

Nice looking place but nothing we ordered was as good as it sounds on the menu.  Also we possibly had the least friendly waitress I've ever encountered and she barely did anything or spoke to us despite being her only table.  I would rate as a 2.5 if I could.


Edit:  Pauli's, we were there for lunch on 8/21.

What's not to like? Freshly made juices and a menu that boasts good quality and healthy choices. Goodness was a much needed addition to the food scene in town, no doubt about it. From Sammie's to wraps, power bowls and juice the menu is creative enough to keep healthy eating fun! I wish this place was closer to my place, I'd definitely make more regular appearances. Open up a spot Downtown! I recently tried the Thai Chicken rice bowl and it was delicious- packed with veggies, brown rice and the dressing comes on the side! My favorite juice is the Green Bully. A shoutout to Chef Pen, the master of all things healthy at Goodness. Sure, it's on the pricey side, but you get what you pay for and good quality is worth the extra. It's not that expensive people! Goodness is great for a quick lunch or take out. But there's plenty of seating indoors and out. I would like to see an improved trash system. I understand space is limited, so disposable ware is the way to go, but recycling bins would make a
Huge difference and would also result in a fifth estrella.

Place is cleaner but Pho broth is not the same under new management.  It doesn't have the deep bone broth taste.  Flavor is light still decent but no longer worth driving into the city for Pho. Anyone know where the old owners moved to?

This cute little shop is exactly what you'd want for a healthy delicious breakfast or lunch or even just a snack! They have many juice/smoothie options made fresh to order from local farms, tasty melt in your mouth sandwiches in the best way and savory soups to satisfy your hearts desires! It's a must stop and the only thing I wish would change about this place is that it's open later for those of us who can't swing by for breakfast or lunch!!
I stopped in for dinner the other night and it was very good. Also Gabby was wonderful!

I visited this place with my friend recently for lunch. I ordered a thai chicken bowl ($9) and my friend ordered the breakfast bowl. The ingredients are all fresh and healthy and it's a great place if you feel like eating out somewhere casual yet light. The portion sizes are relatively small, so I wouldn't take anyone here who has a huge appetite, because it can be pricey. I've heard great things about their juice, so I really want to come back to try them.

I used to order take out from here often. Recently ordered and the lady who picked up didn't speak English or Cantonese. I ordered a Bun Rieu, I don't know what number that is on the menu and she keep asking for a number. I eventually gave up and went order at the restaurant. I knew something wasn't right. I walked in and immediately noticed different faces and a different vibe.

Very disappointed that an old Chinatown institution like Choo Choo had sell out. Restaurant decor has changed, staff has changed, prices have gone up significantly and food quality noticeably dropped. 

Vietnamese Chinese family used to run this place and now, it's run by FJs. I'm sorry, but the authenticity and flavors are no longer there. 

I won't be coming back unless I absolutely have to. Another old and good restaurant is gone. RIP Choo Choo!
They allowed dine in, and the size and taste is absolutely wonderful. Will def try again.

I usually love goodness and make it a treat of mine. However today's experience lacked in what I was used to. We got a mango açaí bowl and avocado toast for $19.73 total. Usually I don't mind paying higher prices but today I did. The quality wasn't what I was used to. The açaí bowl was soupy and amateur and the avocado toast was more sprouts than anything. It looked like a thin green avocado paste on soggy bread versus fresh avocado.  Neither items had the look or the texture that I've had there before. Kind of upsetting when you spend more and don't receive the quality you wished for. Probably won't go back.

SO MUCH FOR PICKING UP SOUP FOR A SICK FRIEND !!! IL POST THE PICTURES... So dissapointed in this experience its not what i expect from olive garden. I ordered a boat of alfredo and breadsticks  which i should have recieved breadsticks regardless to go with the  THREE SOUPS I also bought. The boat of alfredo is half empty unless your an optomistic then lets say its half full regardless if i pay for it fill  it up i mean this isnt even half way full $3.49. Do not  order to go from here or even bother to call ahead and specify I called at 6:27 they said my order would not be ready till 7pm ITS SOUP for the love of God.  My chocolate candies were smashed and melted  on my plastic  wear idk who mad this worker mad but why did she take it out on me sheesh!

Woah - Olive Garden delivered for lunch (pickup at 1130am) + had enough leftovers for dinner.

Their Chicken Tortellini (lunch portion) included long strips of tender chicken (lots of it) & cheese tortellini, is it dried pasta? I don't know for sure that the pasta wasn't made in house - excellent nuggets filled with cheesiness in a bath of MORE CHEESE :) - a highly recommended dish!

The salad is OK - it includes Italian dressing and iceberg lettuce...very boring and lacks imagination.

Usually when I review a restaurant on Yelp, I don't mind doing it right then and there.  This time, though, there's enough that went wrong to wait until I got to an actual computer keyboard. 

We did a takeout order via Grubhub.  When I picked up the order and brought it back to the hotel where my friends and I were staying, we noticed that they were missing a dish.  I called the restaurant, they apologized, and said I could come back to get a fresh dish.  Then while en route, my friends told me that another dish was missing.  I called the restaurant, but they swore up and down that the chicken curry with potatoes was in the order.  I couldn't tell them enough about how there was nothing we had with a single potato.  Even when I arrived, they refused to make the dish that was missing.  

Grubhub refunded my money but my friend who ordered it had to do with roast pork from a nearby place that had it in the window.

Make sure you have what you ordered before you leave!

yay!! they are open for dine in and i was really happy because i used to come here all the time for my
pho cravings :) 

vermicelli: ooo this was really good! the texture of the veggies with the noodles and meat: tied together with fish sauce! super fresh and yummy, and the bbq pork is super flavorful  and tender. 

pho: idk why but it tasted different than how i remembered it! it was slightly less deep of a flavor today than normal, but still pretty good. it'll cure your pho craving on a cold day, but not necessarily the best pho spot in town.

Great food but a little pricey. We had the burgers with fries which was very delicious. We also had the chicken and waffles with bacon inside the waffles (first time I ever had one) which was also great. Service was slow despite only few customers  inside the establishment. It took forever for our orders to arrive and we were very hungry. Ambience is great and soothing. Amount of food was more than enough for two people for our two orders.
this is a sad, sad racist place. must be shut down, they are bad for philadelphia. bad for all of us, management is irrelevant
Pho Xe Lua is as good as ever. By the time I remember to take a photo, everything was almost gone.

We decided to check this place out this past weekend since we were looking for somewhere new to try. We used to live in the Franklin and were happy to see the space being utilized well. The atmosphere is simple and the windows give it a bright and open look.

We were seated right away and given menus. There is an all day menu and also a breakfast menu, which makes for a lot of options. I noticed that the prices on two of the breakfast menus we were given were different.. obviously they have increased their prices about 1-2 dollars in just the short time they've been open, which probably means they are doing well.

We started with tuna tacos, which came as an order of 3. We asked to add 1 more since we were a party of 4, but the server was confused and didn't understand what we meant.. so we just gave up and split the 3. Oh well. They were good with a crunchy shell, fresh tuna, and citrusy mango salsa. For our meals, I split the french onion soup and the chicken BLTA. The soup was good, though a little smaller than I imagined. Definitely on the less salty side, which I appreciated. The chicken sandwich was very tasty. I'm not usually one for grilled chicken sandwiches, but the chicken was tender and not dry. The fries were nice and crispy and paired well with their maple mustard sauce (ask for it on the side). Our friends enjoyed their meals as well. We didn't drink this time, but they do have a full bar.

There are a lot of options here and it's a nice change from the slew of cash only, BYO, difficult to get a reservation brunch spots in the area. I would definitely check it out again.

My favorite spot for a light healthy meal. Acai bowls, fresh juices, and burritos are always solid choices for quick recharging meals. Green Bully juice is not the tastiest drink (in fact some may say it borders on bitter medicine), but it will make you feel better because of the healthy ingredients and feel a bit broke because of its hefty tag (over 10 dollars after taxes). I'm a fan!

The best thing about this place is nobody's ever thought about steak and spaghetti. Clearly this place is living in 3017! The food I had was decent nothing to write home about the environment was a little old for my taste but at the end of the day they're bringing something unique and people are going to come to the restaurant for that reason. I recommend you try it just for yourself, I would say in full confidence that I would go back, no it's not my favorite place to eat in Tucson but it was definitely good enough for me to be back. 

Steak: 4 Stars 
Spaghetti: 2.5 Stars 
Meatballs: 3.5 Stars 
Service: 4 Stars 
Ambiance: 2 Stars

Found this spot by accident and made a mental note to try them out the next time I was craving neighborhood chinese food. 

Tonight was the night! Ordered fried dumplings, which appeared homemade. The flavors were good albeit a bit greasy for my liking. Next time I'll get them boiled and drown them in that delicious house dumpling sauce. That was the star. It had tang, spice and savory sweetness. Perfect combo to drown those morsels in.

Also ordered shrimp in lobster sauce and it was excellent. The shrimp were larger than I expected and the sauce with the pork fried rice was bomb.

This was pretty good quality at exceptional prices. I will definitely order again!

I was so excited to try this new restaurant after passing it daily and watching the parking lot get more and more packed with cars. I think the concept is great! We made a reservation for 6pm on a Saturday and when we arrived 4 minutes early we were almost scolded for arriving early and told we would have to wait...odd, there were plenty of tables available. Ok, no big deal they have a bar. The bar is well stocked and the bartender was the best part of the experience. He was friendly, knowledgeable and helped us get in drinks and an appetizer during their happy hour. 

We were soon seated at a small table, unfortunately my seat had a direct view of the kitchen and bus station so ambiance was sorely lacking. Poor lighting (everyone was using their flashlight phone feature to read the menu), unbalanced table, and my fluorescent kitchen view was not going to ruin the meal I expected from many of the reviews I read. So far the drinks and calamari were great and arrived quickly. 

Our waiter was very pleasant and took our order well before a table of 8 was seated next to us. We waited and waited for our soup to arrive while the table of 8 enjoyed their first course. By this time the  droning of the spaghetti western music from the lone tv in the main dining room really starts to get to you. The chaos from the kitchen and host are apparent as plates arrive at tables either incorrectly or randomly as some are without food at the same table. 

Our waiter assured us the chef will have our soup out next (it's been 25 minutes.) French onion soup is just okay--not baked with cheese as told by our waiter, but good flavor. Our entree was delivered to the table next to us as was the case all too often. Eventually the plates were redirected to our table. 

Both ordered the 16oz ribeye, spaghetti and 
meatballs. We are about an hour into our experience and the dining room was now full and loud. The flavor of the steak was really very good, however the steak was over-cooked, not medium at all, definitely well. The spaghetti had cooled off from its journey and the meatballs were grossly over-salted (and I'm accused of over salting when I cook). Both of us took one bite of the meatballs and pushed them to the side. 

I struggled to cut my well done ribeye and eventually gave up--at this point we both couldn't wait to leave. At no time did out waiter ask about temperature or flavor and honestly, I would have said "all good" just to get this meal over with. 

Expect to spend $100+ for two, with one drink each, one appetizer and two entrees...it's not cheap! I was very disappointed and hope they can turn it around. We agreed independently, not to return. There are far better places in Tucson to spend that kind of time and money.

I'd like to update my review as I just had a very impressive encounter/experience with the manager of Goodness. I was reached out to after posting my review and was asked how the wrong could be made right. We were welcomed back into the restaurant today and greeted with kindness and excellent hospitality by the manager. After apologizing he then proceeded to cover our meal. Once we were seated, we had a good chat about service and what he expects from his employees. I learned a bit more about what Goodness strives for in hospitality and what we received originally was not what is expected of Goodness employees. 

The food was wonderful and we enjoyed our visit. We will definitely go back again as we feel the wrong was made right and the food is yummy! Especially the homemade orange juice!

This place is the absolute worst. It's the pits. It's the Shelby of female names. If you enjoy rude door men and a cover to be able to dance or watch gross looking people dance in a shower then this is the place for you. 

The downstairs portion of the bar isn't that bad, so iCandy receives 1 star. You're not allowed to bring your drink upstairs and have to pay a cover to get up there. Once up there, you are not allowed to bring your drink to the dance floor, which, is completely covered in nasty smelling fog. Additionally, the stripper poles won't be used by the people who work there, but guests also are not allowed to use them. I was asked to not dance on both poles, yet no one else or the people working there were using them either, but I can't really blame them because of the tired music and tired looking lady-boys. 

Overall, I do not recommend going here. The only favorable thing I can think about is how polite the bartenders are. They are quick with a strong drink and easy to chat with.

Highly recommend Tashiology Skincare! I went in for a 60 min facial and a Brazilian wax. Tashua is incredibly kind and knowledgeable. She makes you feel welcomed and goes through everything she is using on you. I felt great after both appointments and will definitely be going back!

Phenomenal happy hour! And on top of that the food is to die for! Went for the first time on a whim looking for a good happy hour, Kept going back for more! They even had live music! Branched out from happy hour drinks into the food menu, it did not disappoint! Poutine is insane. Highly recommend any of the different types. (We tried them all)*don't judge*      
Staff  is so friendly and welcoming! Great service! Ally is wonderful! As well as the bartenders! Our glasses were never empty and they were present, helpful and took care of us the whole time! 

Can't wait to try their brunch!! *word on the street, it and the Bloody Marys are life changing. 
Highly recommend this place. It's family friendly too!

Classic pho joint here in Philly. Service was great. I was able to catch a waiters attention each time I needed to and the food came out quickly. The shrimp summer rolls were a little on the basic side; the sauce wasn't anything special and it could've used some more herbs in my opinion.

I ordered the classic pho bowl, 101, and realized half way into the bowl that I forgot to take a photo. The beef was very tender and the broth hit the spot; comfort food. Nothing fancy, just a bowl of pho and sometimes that's exactly what you need.

Pho Xe, Choo Choo, whatever your name is...hot damn this is some good pho! 
Meat, noodles, fixins and such were all standard, but the broth was some of the best I've ever had. And really, that's the most important part. 
6.50 for an XL bowl with rare beef. 
3.50 for a shrimp roll. 
Free hot tea on the table.
Win.
Don't be fooled by other pho places in Chinatown. Choo Choo is tops!

I thought the food here was pretty good. I ordered one of the appetizers for lunch, the tuna poke tacos. I thought they were quite tasty - four tacos in a fried wonton wrapper, with sashimi tuna chunks, a mango and red onion salsa, and a spicy mayo on the side for dipping. I wish I could end the review right here, but alas I'm giving this place a lower rating because the service is just comically BAD.

Server started off by coming for our drink order. I ordered a soda. Server disappears for 10 minutes, comes back to take food order, but didn't bring a drink. Order food, ask again for a soda. Food comes out, still no soda. It is a bit frustrating to have to ask 3 times to get a drink, strike one.

I'm used to the server coming back at some point in time and asking how the food is, and if they can get us anything. This happens pretty much universally at restaurants. Our server waited a bit long to do this. My husband eats fast, I eat a little slow. So by the time she comes over to ask how the food was, he was finished with his food. After asking me how my food was, to which I said very good, she starts throwing table trash on my plate and begins taking it away. I was confused as hell and said, "but I'm still eating?" Out of the four tacos I received, I still had one left on my plate. She made some offhand remark about how we "looked like we were in a hurry" but didn't apologize. I can't say I've ever been rushed out of a restaurant before simply because my husband eats faster than I do... strike two.

Apparently this restaurant uses handheld card scanners that they bring to your table, similar to Europe (although unlike Europe they stare at you directly as you enter how much you're going to tip them, instead of leaving the device with you - note to the wise: pay attention, these devices are scammy as hell when suggesting tip amounts. The smallest tip it suggested I leave was 7 bucks on a $30.80 order, which is 23% - use the custom entered tip option and NOT the fake suggested numbers). My meal at Sandler's ended by the server scanning my card and then dropping it on the floor, again with no apology, stating, "you're going to want to pick that up, it's by your foot." I guess it would be far too much to expect either an apology, or the server to pick up what she dropped. Oh well, strike three.

In some ways, some of what I say may sound a bit nitpicky, but you pay a premium to go to a restaurant and sit down, and if servers can't bring you what you order, nor make general pleasantries, they should probably not be servers. I've been to plenty of restaurants where something has been forgotten, and there's always some sort of apology involved, and that's understandable, it's human nature. Instead I got none of that here, I just got a look like I was being exceptionally burdensome for simply ordering something off the menu. Also, I can't think of the last time I've ever been rushed out of a restaurant, with the server trying to run away with my plate - with food still on it - without even having asked me if I was done. It is worth noting that this was at 3pm on a Sunday... hardly a busy hour. Then again, maybe the server was due on break after brunch was over, and my presence was disturbing that.

I think if I ever came back, it would surely be for takeout only.

FOOD: 5/5
SERVICE: 0/5
This place is awesome..great drink specials the staff is super friendly.gogogogogogog and have alot of fun

Excellent, dishes we're very well prepared, hot. I especially liked the 'ANGRY CHICKEN DIPP!' We got that one & 'SPINACHE & ARTICHOKE DIPP!' It was served with brushchetta breads. Wow the ANGRY CHICKEN DIPP was crazy good. Our server, KATE, KATEY working in the Bar area was more than helpful, funny kept us laughing & informed. Our Entre's were outstanding. We ordered the 'LASAGNE, shrimp & muscle saute'!!! 
 We both had not gone  to a Olive Garden in over 7 years due to qaulity & cost then. BUT!!! This was an amazing evening meal, well worth the 16 mile drive & Amazing service buy Katey at the 17011 Pal Point Drive Tampa restaurant!!! We give it a Hell Yeah. We will be back!!! Thank you Olive Garden & Katey & Staff. Amazing Food & Drink

My second favorite pho place in Philadelphia. Convenient location as some really great pho places are very much out of the way. I've gone here 6 times and enjoyed it every time and brought friends here. Very good price for what you're getting.

It has been several years since I have been to an Olive Garden, but my son wanted spaghetti for dinner, and I didn't want to cook. Not much has changed in the past few years at this location (perhaps the marquee). By the time we arrived, I wasn't sure what I wanted and really wasn't feeling all that hungry, so all I ordered was a bowl of soup and some water. I indicated that I might want something more a little later to our waiter; who appeared to be annoyed by this and did not seem to have anywhere near close to the desired personality for a service position (sarcastic/snarky). We felt as though we were interrupting him from more important matters.

My son ordered a bowl of spaghetti with plain marinara (which he loved) off the adult menu, and my friend ordered Braised Beef & Tortelloni, which I tried a few bites, and it was **fantastic**. The food was great and it served in a reasonable amount of time. However...

The older I get, the more I value customer service; it is a large part of my dining experience and a portion of what I am paying for when I choose to dine out. Our server was much younger than my friend and me, and it could just be generational differences; but we both felt our dining experience would have been much better if our server's boisterous/snarky personality were toned down just a tad while dealing with patrons.

Service was attentive.  House salad was way too large for the plate making it difficult to eat without spilling everywhere with a bland, bottled Italian dressing.  The shrimp scampi was a recipe never before encountered either by Italian relatives or at any other Italian restaurant -- wide pasta, cream sauce with tomatoes.  The calamari was served with a ketchup(?) based dipping sauce.  Probably never to return.

I love this place so much! I think it has the best pho In philly, I always stop by when I'm in town. 
The pho's soup is light but tasteful and the other foods are really good too. Personally I love the Xe Lua special pho. Though it has some meat pieces that may be a little challenging if you're not used to it. 
If you're coming alone then no worries, I always go alone and while I was there a lot of people came alone. Their service is quick so you can be in and out if you're in a hurry, but if you want to take your time then more than welcomed to take your time. 
One caution: if you're under $15 then it's cash only

Sad to say that our most recent dining experience at Sandler's was a steep decline from our previous experiences. Our group of 4 dined at 8 pm on a Saturday and it wasn't great. 

The awesome, high quality napkins were replaced by mediocre, normal quality napkins. This was my first sign that things must not be going well. 

The drink that I previously loved and thought was so high quality tasted like fruit juice. 

We got lobster poutine. This was not at all poutine but glorified cheese fries with huge hunks of lobster meat. There was no gravy. It was fries smothered in a cheese sauce with huge lobster claws. The fries themselves were good. The lobster tasted high quality and delicious but as far as poutines go, it was not a poutine. The lobster should have been smaller so you were getting lobster in most bites instead of having to eat a giant hunk of lobster after eating some fries. 

My fiancé said his burger was the worst burger he's had at a restaurant. It was undercooked, it had no flavor and it didn't have cheese even though he requested cheese.
