I got the lobster roll and it was just ok. I didn't care for the sauce. It was too mayonnaise-y. I wouldn't order it again. But then again, I probably won't be returning anyway. 

Our waitress was bizarre. She looked very unkempt. Her shirt was dirty and that's a turnoff. You want your servers to look fresh and to present themselves in a clean, professional manner. She said a lot of weird things throughout the experience. It was just odd. She was rushing us even though she claimed she wasn't. She forgot things we asked for. It just wasn't a good experience. 

I also didn't appreciate being locked into a tip on the device she gave me to sign for our credit card statement. So she's standing there waiting for me to sign and I have to select from the tip amounts being offered at the top and then hand it back to her. No thanks! 

I am very disappointed because I really liked this place but they went downhill pretty quickly and we won't be back as a result.

I've been coming to this laundromat for a few months now and it has gradually declined. At first it was very clean and all machines worked. Now the place is constantly dirty. I've been there while there is someone cleaning and the job that is done is terrible. The mop used smells like it has never been replaced. The machines are wiped down with what seems like a dirty rag which smells the same as the mop. Some of the washing machines do not work and some of the ones that do only are able to use warm or hot water. Half of the dryers do not work which is a huge inconvenience when there are more working washers than dryers. Based on my experience the last few times I've been here I will be looking for another laundromat. I highly recommend you look elsewhere unless you want to be inconvenienced.

I was really grateful to find this place after a friend recommended it. I have a bunch of food allergies, which makes eating out very challenging. The chef and the staff were really understanding and they carefully checked to make sure I was covered. I had a green curry (gluten free / soy free / garlic free). It was really clean and sat really well with me. Not too spicy. Great flavors. One of the things I really liked about it was that it was thicker than other green curries (cornflour thickened), so it wasn't thin or watery like this dish often is at other places. 

My boyfriend had the frog and it was really great too. It was his first time eating frog and he said that had made it super tasty. 

Very happy to find this place and would definitely eat here again.

Some of the best pho I've had that was perfect on a cold windy night. We came here for dinner on a Saturday and were seated right away. Ordering was quick and efficient and the food was out in minutes. I ordered 101. Special Pho, large size. The servings were huge and had a ton of meat, broth, and noodles. The broth was rich and flavorful, exactly what you want from a pho broth. I really liked the variety of meat, including steak, tendon, and tripe. The bowl was more than enough to fill me up. Highly recommend coming here for a no frills and solid meal!

I love the way the server took his time. You can tell he was genuinely nice and care about our needs. I had a salad as a starter with no croutons, cheese or the Italian dressing. Of course, since I'm vegan, I asked to have balsamic vinegar and olive oil. (: For my meal, I chose Whole Wheat Linguine, Marinera sauce and Garden Veggies. I made sure to tell him no dairy of any kind, which he understood completely. He was confused at the fact that I had sausage on my plate lol... I brought vegan sausage from home to make the meal more filling. So for all my Vegans out there bring your cheese and your cooked sausage to Olive Garden. Meals were delicious and server looked like prince charming. What more could I have asked for?

This is a corner restaurant in Philadelphia. It seems fairly new, and I think it is a decent place. You are able to book it through Yelp, which is a great!

Food 7.5/10
- Pretty decent. I highly recommend the Poutine fries to share with the table. We ordered the lobster poutine, and it was heavenly. No, seriously, it was GOOD. 
- As for the meals, the burgers look decent. I had their Bucatini Pasta and I added chicken (yes, you can do this). Very good pesto taste to it, but otherwise somewhat bland. This did get much better after adding some salt to it, but it wasn't as good as I had hoped it would be
- Full bar with a decent drink selection. Prices are appropriate

Environment 7/10
- Came at night and it was dark. Abundance of seating and they also have a nice glass rooms for a small party
- Nice bar area 
- Service was average

Overall: 7/10
Recommendation: Probably would come for the poutine. And will try something else next time besides the pasta.

I enjoyed the soup, until I found a string of plastic in it. The manager came out to apologize and justified plastic being in it. In response I smirked and said no worries with the thought of the meal being taken care of or something...however no charges were taken off the check and I was charged $3.49 for marinara sauce without knowledge of it costing anything. To top off the evening I didn't receive Andes mints with my check that was overpriced. Unfortunately I don't think I won't be going back to Olive Garden.

Can not understand in this electronic age why a restaurant chain like Olive Garden does not take any type of reservation or Call Ahead seating for a party of 5. It is listed in the Yelp listing but instead I was told, just come in and it is first come first serve. If the food wasn't so good, would go to another Italian restaurant which can properly service a group of 5 customers.

Terrible service. ordered $52 in food, came back 1 hour later and our order was still not prepared. Attendant lied about time elapsed, everyone is asleep at the wheel there. refunded on the spot. Will not be back.

Came in for a quick bite after the gym. Took a while deciding on what I wanted but I went with the daily buzz smoothie and the steak taco. Initially they got my taco order wrong, they served me a chicken taco and I had asked for steak but they corrected my order and did not charge me the difference (great job, I also noticed the lady ordering after me having a mistake with her order as well. Could've just been a busy day). The steak taco was absolutely delicious but very small. If you're super hungry I'd suggest you get about 4 but that'll run you $16 alone. The nice thing was that they do offer student and military discount 10% the smoothie was delicious. Definitely going to put this place on my list of regular spots to visit.

I've been going to Wawa to get gas and free air for my tires for a couple of years. I didn't know it was so organized, clean, and pretty darn efficient when it comes to food and beverages. I just happened to go inside a couple of times recently to place an order. You basically use their touch screen ordering system, get a ticket with your number, pay at the cashier, and then walk on over to the pick up area and wait for your number to be called. It's easy and quick. It didn't take long for my order even during the busy morning rush. The service was fantastic. The staff are friendly.

Now, I have to tell you about the food. I saw that they have some healthy breakfast sandwiches (some under 300 calories), and they have all kinds of coffee preparations. I got the cortadito with the option of almond milk. I know that sounds gross. My Puerto Rican mom wouldn't have been happy that I chose almond milk, but it was actually very good with the espresso. It was the sweetened almond milk. I didn't even have to put any sugar in it. It was prefect. I'd get it again. The breakfast sandwich was surprisingly good. 

Yes, it was my first time eating at a Wawa. I loved it! I will return since this is where I get my gas on the way home from the office. I want to try the chicken corn chowder that a friend recommended to me, and other menu items.

I go to Goodness when I want to eat out, don't mind spending a pretty penny, but still want to be healthy. 
Don't get me wrong though, I've had unhealthy options from here too. 

There is mostly always a line around lunch time and can I just say the parking is horrendous! Pro Tip: there is parking behind the restaurants. I've also sneakily parked at eegees but that was for a quick pick up that took 5 mins, tops. 

Their menu does have something for everyone. Plant based, carb eaters, and picky eaters. I personally loved their grilled cheese but only a cheat day. The salad I to go ordered below is was a delicious massive amount of veggies. I loved the overload of garlic.

I'm always looking for good vegan / vegetarian options, but I probably wouldn't have stopped here if I first had noted the July 2020 health score provided on the Yelp app. 

I was able to order right away when I walked in, and the lady working the register was very friendly. The checkout process is "touchless", except that they hand you a reusable number in spite of also taking your name. 

I ordered The Goods smoothie with almond milk in place of the coconut milk. It took about 5 minutes for it to come up, which was fine. They called my name from the counter (why did I have that number?), and I went on my way. 

The smoothie was tasty - nice and thick, not too sweet. A 16 oz. was just over $7. Goodness is out of the way for me, and I still can't quite get past the health score.

The place smelled nice, not strongly of animals or waste, which tells me they keep the place nice and clean in the back as well.  They saw my guinea pigs and were able to provide me tons of info on what is best for them.  The prices are about what you would expect, not dirt cheap but not overly priced either.  I will definitely take my babies here again!!
Today my family and i went to eat dinner and it was very disappointing the lasagna was over cooked and burned the service was bad as well

Good-bye 12th Air!! Oh wait. You're back. And your name is now iCandy. Great. But you have some changes. Thank you for no more neon green. But wait! Now the first floor looks like Taco Bell. That's awesome. I'm so happy. But I have to pay 5 dollars to leave Taco bell to go to the dance floor? 

Fine, but only if I can pay in Sacajawea coins. Okay, so you were pretty gracious about me paying in such an unorthodox manner.  How is upstairs? Wow, I'm back in 12th air. Seriously. 

2 stars since it's the only gay bar with some form of roofdeck, though I think I heard someone yell "My dick smells like citronella," no doubt due to the pungent candles.

Horrible service had a 5 pm reservation for a birthday dinner didn't get food until 6:30 entire party's food was wrong.... kitchen was backed up food was cold.  I still was missing my food by the time it came I didn't want it. Will never come here again.

The food here is great, I recommend the cloud 9. I usually get this once a week, and the manager knows exactly what I get. The service is excellent! I think her name is Helen? 
Best açaí place in Tampa.

This place is AMAZING you know whatever you are going to have is going to be made from good ingredients and made my great people. My friend took me there yesterday and now I just want to go back for breakfast and a power shake haha Defiantly my new spot!

This place recently opened right near my work so I decided to try it after work one day. The menu has a lot of good choices. I ordered the poke tacos with a mango salsa and they were very fresh and delicious. For my entree I ordered the lobster roll. Both were very good... will definitely dine there again.

Tashua is so friendly and professional. Been going to her for years for waxing and just got my first facial. She always explains the products, uses natural products and the facial was amazing. So relaxing. High recommend Tashiology skin care for waxing and facial services.

We call it choo chops because of the train I'm the window definitely a hidden gem in China town i love the food i have tried pho , as well as many Chinese and Asian dishes the flavor in the food and pho broth is the most flavorful i have ever tried Highly recommend

Thee best Chinese Food in the city, hands down! I've searched far and wide, and can find no other that even come close. The shrimp fried rice has shrimp in every bite, the general tso's chicken is crispy and cooked to perfection, the portions are hearty (two meals worth at least) and everything tastes freshly made. Definitely recommend if you are in the Mt. Airy/Chestnut Hill section of the city, or even if you aren't and are just in the mood for amazing Chinese cuisine.

I have to admit, I was highly surprised by how communicative and on top of everything they were. I am a small business and applied for the PPP loan, and throughout they were proactive, prompt, and got things done much faster than I'd anticipated. Granted, with the PPP loan they get paid for every loan approved, so it's in their best interest to get them done quickly. That said, I have nothing but good things to say about Aaron, Catalina, Amanda, and their team.
Used the take & bake menu. Very nice dinner for 6 got lasagna salad and sticks. Curb side service

I came here for dinner on a Saturday night with a group of 5 people.  We ordered a bunch of dishes: shrimp summer rolls, steamed mussels, beef pho, salted pepper 3 treasures (shrimp/scallop/squid), and bbq lemongrass chicken over rice.  If you order the beef pho, you get a choice of large or extra large.  You might as well get extra large since you only live once right.  The summer rolls were okay but the shrimp was small.  The spicy sauce on the mussels was not spicy, more on the sweet side.  The mussels were fresh though.  The extra large beef pho was huge and there's a generous portion of noodles/toppings.  The pho broth was flavorful and not too oily.  The salted pepper 3 treasures was crispy and fresh.  The bbq lemongrass chicken was juicy and tasty.  Service was fast and friendly.  This was one of my favorite places for pho.  I would definitely come back here if I'm ever in Philly.

My revisit was satisfied. They were running the $8.99 deal during the weekday 3 to 5 pm. I got the chicken piccata. The chicken is grilled. The sauce has piccata and lemon base. It is delicious. It come with slide zucchini top with bread crumbs. 

Even thought the price is reduced, the service is top notch. The food also is great quality. They did not reduce the quality since the price of the dish was cut more than 40%. I have to tip my hat to the restaurant for such good quality.

I'd give iCandy 4 stars for my night there, but heavy deduction is necessary when managers at the bar cut off your friend from drinking for NO REASON.  

My friend and I both had one drink each on arrival, then ordered a second round right before I stepped outside for a cigarette. I came back inside and my friend sitting at the bar tells me, "So apparently, I've been flagged and can't buy drinks anymore." I'm obviously BAFFLED by this because she literally had one vodka soda and barely sipped on the second one before security came over and told her she's been flagged by a manager and can't buy anymore drinks. On top of that, they took that second drink away from her (one that I BOUGHT for her, mind you) and wouldn't let her finish it. 

I ask the security (who was super sweet and was just following his boss' orders, I get it) to get the manager her because I want to know why she was flagged, and when he finally comes, he doesn't even speak to me: the manager just tells the security person "she's just been flagged and can drink anymore" and that's it.

I had a pretty damn good time at iCandy and my friend was a good sport about being flagged (which has never happened to any of us ever), but if your establishment is gonna flag someone, give a GOOD reason why you're flagging them for sitting at the bar, looking at Facebook while their other friend is outside for not even five minutes. Idiots.

I'm thinking that if you call an order in, you shouldn't have to wait 50 minutes, once you get there, to get your order.

Live and learn.

Nothing screams comfort than pho on a gloomy windy day. In need of something soupy and warm, we stumbled upon this restaurant. 

Of all the pho places, we chose here due to the amount of reviews. Upon walking in, the restaurant felt like a hole in the wall. Old, but gave warm vibes. Definitely a taste of home. The server attending to us was speedy, jumping from table to table. 

We ordered the Shrimp Summer Rolls ($5.25), Large Special Rice Noodle Soup ($9.75), and the Large Medium Rare Beef & Tripe Rice Noodle Soup ($9.75). The Shrimp Summer Rolls were served on separate plates (how cute). They were probably the worst I had due to how flimsy they were, but they still satisfy! Our pho were pretty much the same of course, but with different ingredients. I still prefer the Chinatown NYC pho better, but these were different, from the noodle texture to the broth. Their broth was on the sweeter side. Their beef was bomb though, as they were very tender and soft. 

Bowls were large, with even an option for extra large. You will definitely leave with a stuffed tummy here, in a good satisfying way.

Found a spot through yelp and was highly impressed. I'm very familiar with Vietnamese food and this hit home in a good way! I went there with my family of four and we ate so we couldn't eat anymore. The bill only came to $23 and the food was amazing! I highly recommend the lemongrass chicken, barbecue pork, and the spring rolls

It's awesome,friendly..but a few jerkoff staff memebers...like the bar back with the blond hair and tatts,you the the one who never smiles..douche.and what about the staff dude with the beard walks around with his finger up his azz...so unfriendly..

Food for the price you pay is definitely 5 star level but let me tell you about this one particular waiter.

One day I ordered some bun bo something with some tasty pork hock bits and there were these bones that I chewed on and left on the table.  Picture the table filled with pork bones with little bits of meat and tendon on them that I had enjoyed thoroughly.  At the end of my meal this one waiter came to clean up our table and literally grabbed all my half chewed wet nasty pork bones WITH HIS BARE HANDS so he didn't have to "waste" a napkin.  I WAS SHOOK.  

HOLY MOTHER THIS GUY GETS TEN STARS IN MY BOOK.  THAT IS THE BEST SERVICE I HAVE EVER RECEIVED IN AN AMERICAN RESTAURANT.
Food was great! Even better than the food was the service! Nicole D was super friendly, attentive and made our experience A+. I would definitely come back and highly recommend!!

The Pho was pretty average. They were generous with the amount of meat and noodles. But the broth was very light. Surprisingly enough, the smell of fish sauce was a bit overpowering when they first brought the bowl out. The old menu that was posted on Yelp made it seem incredibly cheap for what you can get in the Philly Chinatown. But they have increased their prices. Instead of $7/8 it's now pushing $11. It's pricy for what it is, but it's not the worst Pho I've ever had. The staff was attentive, which is nice, they didn't push you to finish super quickly. It's a bit odd however that there weren't a lot of people who went there. I saw most other people walk into the other restaurants in the area. The ambiance is a bit lacking. The owners clip and prepare a lot of the basil and things you put on the pre Pho plate out. In the restaurant area. I mean, it's nice to know it's fresh, but at the same time you're turning the dining area into the extension of the kitchen. Overall I'd give it a 3.4.

I used to love this place and how everything was made fresh. My recent Mediterranean plate was pre-made given to me cold right out of the fridge. The chicken and veggies were cold. The rice was not only cold but some pieces were so hard that it felt like I was biting rocks. Definitely not worth the price point either. As I was leaving at the back I also saw an employee on his phone with food gloves on and then go back in, touching the door handle and all  I sure hope he exchanged those gloves before dealing with food again.

Frustrated.  Checked from home, website offers "join that waitlist". Clicked on it.  Note said "there is currently no wait at this restaurant". But of course that is not true.  Told it's 20-30 minutes.  Went back to website still says "no wait". This is a problem.  Especially when you can't wait in the lobby in the AC because of Covid.  Don't offer it if you aren't going to use it.

Came by for dinner before a show at the Walnut. I got the hog burger with sweet potato fries and my partner got the turkey club with regular fries. Everything was delicious. Highly recommend before a show or if you're just in the area
absolutely fantastic! fast, painless, professional process and Tash makes you feel at ease!

Dirty machines. Almost no laundry mat in Tampa Keeps clean machines. Hair & dried soap. It really disgusting. You would think these people care about their business but it's almost like they don't want to hold no standard.

Worst restaurant ever had :( 
I order the spring rolls and fry rice. Taste really bad .Never come back again.
After a long flight home, there is nothing like refreshing healthy food from Goodness whether you are a vegetarian or an omnivore.

I am a tremendous fan of this venue!  I come here all the time for two main reasons:  1) LOW prices and 2) excellent selection.  The food out of here is authentic and is not of the take out style.  it is well-prepared and for as low as $5.50 you can enjoy a FULL meal.  I eat here all the time for lunch and get it to-go for dinner often as I work nights and do not have time to prepare dinner.  It is cheaper than Subway, McDonald's,  and fast food style Chinese take-out but it is a real meal and the portion size is more than enough to feed a 165 lb male as myself.  do yourself a favor and check it out.  You won't find any compromises on quality or portion size with the low prices here.

If you're looking for a quick place for Pho in Chinatown, Choo Choo's is the place to go. The pho here is refreshing and has a clean after taste with no oily residue, which is an added plus! 

The shrimp on sugar cane was delicious. The sugarcane was my favorite part. You just chew on the sugarcane and it is jam packed with flavorful broth from the shrimp and sugar.

The bbq pork over rice was beautifully seasoned and perfectly cooked. This was by far one of the best bbq pork over rice dishes I have had in the Philly area.

This place an it's employees are incompetent. I move in September of last year. When I moved in everything was brand new. After a few days I start seeing roches. They don't care about the tenants all they want is the money. If you value your things don't move in.

In search of a lighter snack, we journey for Pho. Incited by decent reviews, we happened upon Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai Restaurant. It wasn't that busy but it seemed to serve quite a few locals. We ordered spring rolls and Pho Ga (shredded chicken) and the food was prepared very quickly. The Pho was done just right but the spring rolls were over cooked. It was not unbearable but it could've been cooked a minute or two less. It is a nice spot to try but it would not be my first choice for Pho. 

With that being said, I would visit again. A second chance may lead to a more exciting experience.

Came here around 7pm on the eve of Lunar New Year so the streets of Chinatown were abuzz with various celebrations to welcome the new year. Not only was their service quick and  attentive on such a busy night but more importantly, their pho flavors delivered. The broth was flavorful and the beef was cooked just right. The bean sprouts were fresh and crunchy and the serving portion was quite generous. We also had the grilled chicken and pork combo with steamed egg and they were well-seasoned and tender. We also  had the spring rolls which came out sizzling hot (be careful  that you let it sit for a while before  you take a bite)! They were crispy and not greasy nor soggy. I loved the nuoc mam which came in a bigger than usual size dipping bowl! In addition, we tried the mango bubble tea and it was refreshing. When the bill came, it was also surprisingly very reasonable so what's not to like?

This is a follow up. My Chewy.com order went to Cimmaron today and after my post of disappointment in their lack of concern for my sick dog two days ago, and having to find someone else to see him.  they declined Chewy.com's request to fill his heartworm prescription. Told the pharmacy  he was no longer their patient and declined his refill on his heartworm medicine. Talk about no concern for the health of the animal. They don't care about his health at all. Everything is a bother to them. They denied him his medicine! Unbelievable. Stay away from this place for the health and welfare of your pet.

We came back for breakfast takeout. Ordered online stopped at cartel a few doors down for coffee and or order was ready on time.   We have to disagree with others  reviews on the avocado toast.  There was avocado spread on the toast with fresh avocado slices   Very fresh and flavorful.  Everything well package for an breakfast picnic
Loved the food!! Definitely the best Vietnamese restaurant in Philly!!! Had to come here twice during our visit to the city cause that's how good it was.

I've been here twice now in the last two months. And the service has always been really fast and the servers are very knowledgeable and courteous which is key. The establishment is also quite clean for a place this busy. The prices are good and the food is tasty. This place is great for groups. They have an area upstairs for additional seating. My favorite thing to get at Vietnamese restaurants is vermicelli with shrimp. It also comes with pork which is good too. 

I recommend checking this place out!

Wasn't sure what to expect since it is located underneath the Ben Franklin and near DiBrunos, so it may be delicious. But it's also close enough to touristy old city to be sort of overpriced and meh. Turns out it's the latter; I would totally go to Talulas instead for your soup/salad/sandwich needs. Although I was pleasantly surprised that my beet salad wasn't a total disaster, it did contain some yellow-y leaves of kale so clearly veggies aren't at the top of anyone's priority list. My friend got the veggie burger, and it looked sort of bland. He said it tasted just fine. The waitstaff was very nice, but they all seemed confused; 3 different people came up to us to seat us, but we actually didn't get seated until 10 minutes after that and when we got our check, the guy asked us who our waitress was. I had to try and physically describe her without seeming rude (I'm horrible at names and wouldn't have thought I would get asked what her name was at the end of my meal!)

Was 2 seconds away from walking out before even being seated. Every table in sight was dirty. Waited nearly 5 minutes to be sat. Hostess didn't make eye contact. We sit down and Ms. Rose graced us with her presence. All smiles and hospitality. Apologized for the tables as they just had a rush and everyone was playing catch up. From the moment she said hello until she said goodbye, she was pure hospitality. When asked a question about a drink, she politely had the bartender address us personally. I'm extremely pleased with her assistance. Thank you so much for your time tonight.

Hi my name is Lauren and I love gay bars..."Hi Lauren." 

There, I admitted it. It's not quite the revelation if you're friends with me, and as a straight girl who is known as FruitFly, I have frequented many of the city's offerings for the gay community. And when my gay friend tells me, "I went to your favorite place last night..." my reply is always, "ICandy!?!?!" 

This place has a great roof top deck, awesome specials, and (this seems random) clean bathrooms. The frozen drinks are awesome and REALLY strong. There's always great music and it needs to be said- great eye candy. Get it? Ok, I'll stop.

But seriously, this is a solid spot. Their happy hour is from 4-7 and isn't junk booze (or watered down). Head on over and enjoy the roof deck before it's too cold. If not enjoy one of their MANY rooms and dance floors.

This is one of my favorite pho spots, there is another one close by that I go to as well. The pho here is sooo good and it's a bit less expensive than the other place I visit. I bring everyone to eat pho here! Everyone I brought enjoyed it except one, (but she wasn't an adventurous eater). 

I can not wait to go back and get pho again. The smoothies they have are delicious and taste really fresh. I bought a mango smoothie and it was pretty awesome! This is definitely one of my go to spots because I haven't had a bad experience yet and I've come here to get pho many times!

The food was good and waitress nice.  Would have given 4 stars definitely for the food however there seemed to be a strong smell of mildew. I asked the waitress and she didn't smell it.  Almost like a stale carpet odor.  It got in the way of enjoying the dinner basically. Maybe it will be cleaned soon.

I've came here a few times and each time that I have came, I've been treated horribly by the servers. 

I've had a few bad incidents, but the one that stuck out to me the most was when I came here with a group of 8. Out of the 8, me and a friend decided to split a dish. So I asked the server for an extra plate and he knocked on the table with his knuckles 2 times. Just like this "KNOCK KNOCK" very loudly to show me that he already brought me an extra plate. RUDE! I could not enjoy the rest of my meal or my time there with my friends because I just felt very uncomfortable and unwanted at the restaurant. 

After this incident, I've never returned. And the food here is average anyway. Plus there's plenty of other places surrounding the area that serves the same cuisine and with better service. 

Do no waste your time coming here.

Olive Garden used to be such a good restaurant now it an ok restaurant. I feel like the vibe has died. Food is getting worse and worse like idk. The shrimp was very undercooked and the Spaghetti barely had any sauce. The fries are awful do not get those. However the breadsticks is the only reason i go. I know they are frozen but damn. Overall probably a 3/10.

"Give me your tired, your poor..."

Philadelphia, I love you, but your gay scene is so breathtakingly lacking you make Tampa look like Ibiza.

The name alone ... iCandy? Oy. Tired. And the logo ... brazenly dated. I just can't give you love. 

So, why is this place getting the crowds? Because there's nothing. else. going. on. In other words, it would be literally impossible to fail in a market with huge demand and zero competition. 

Please at least change your name so I can have the option to take friends here without disgracing embarassment. Please!!

Grade: i -minus.

Truly am a fan of the OG in Wesley Chapel. I understand that everyone has a bad night. And really that's not a problem. Rather than write a negative review I called today and talked to a manager, Bill. Now since everyone can have a bad night it's more of how things are handled by management and by the wait staff. I will say management did very well handling things when I called today.

I'll still be a "regular" no doubt.
Except for last night their food has always been great. And even last night the fried calamari was very good and tender. Like butter.

goodness is a really nice place to stop for a quick breakfast or juice! the price point is a little higher than i would have expected for the serving size we got, which is why i'm giving them 4 stars. 

i got the avocado toast, and the sourdough was absolutely perfect, the goat cheese, pickled onions, and avocado worked so well together. my partner got the salmon toast and she thought it was really good. i got the green bully juice and she got the healing vibes juice, both were good but i would probably try a different flavor next time just to switch it up. 

definitely recommend coming here if you're a big fan of juice, or just want a quick but nice breakfast or lunch!

I have gone to Cimmaron for about a decade now and I've seen multiple doctors but Dr Valdez is amazing. She understands I want an integrative approach and respects my decisions and helps me make the best decisions for me and my dogs. When my dog of 10 years passed away, they sent me a letter that everyone had signed to wish me condolences.

We've been going to goodness a long time, but lately our routines have strayed from the ordinary. With Goodness open, and social distancing still in place we thought it would be the perfect spot for a takeout picnic. We opted for our usuals, Breakfast Burritos and a shared Hot Tropic smoothie and took it to our neighborhood park to fuel us after a run with the dog. Burritos are so good with tofu/veggies subbed for protein, and my favorite part of this smoothie is the yummy little chucks of dates.

This little hole in the wall restaurant delivers! It's simple but to the point. The food is delicious, inexpensive, and big portions. The waiters listen and will actually make substitutions without any hassle. 
We came on a cold and rainy Philly afternoon hoping to find a delicious bowl of pho to warm our souls and we were not disappointed. We got the XL bowl of pho $8.95 (ours had different cuts of beef and meatballs). This bowl was definitely XL it fed two adults and we had leftovers. The broth was full of flavor and just perfectly cooked. They do not skimp on anything here. My favorite were the meatballs next time I'm getting extra of these.
We also got the shrimp summer roll for $3 you get two huge rolls per order. It was very fresh and satisfying. 
All around 5 stars. This place delivers what it promises at such a low price. Food is at your table in no time. And servers are attentive, I can't wait to go back and explore their menu!

Probably the best pho place in Chinatown. Made my bowl an XL because I'm a pig and it was definitely a lot of food. $7.50 for a large bowl of warm goodness on a winter day is unbeatable.  Although the pho places near the Italian market is still better, this is as good as it gets in center city east.

Our server wasn't that attentive though, didn't refill our water once. I need my cold water with warm foods!
They have great options for plant based meals and non vegan food too. The ribeye tacos were bomb. They also have really good smoothies, I recommend the Hot Tropic. Love this place!

I have been going to Tashiology Skincare for a year now and Tashua provides an experience like no other. She is absolutely amazing and makes the client feel incredibly comfortable, whether it is a Brazilian wax service or a facial. I always enjoy her company and my favorite days are when I get to see her. She is very knowledgeable about the services she provides and the products she is using. My skin is looking so much clearer and brighter since I started getting monthly facials with her.

Really unique restaurant with very fresh ingredients. Have been a few times and always get the Morning Bowl...not real sure what the sauce is but it's absolutely delicious! My daughter usually gets the acai bowls, she's had both the Cacao Warrior and the Mango Jungle and they both looked great. Staff is responsive when spoken to but not overly friendly, they kind of appear to be in their own world. Good food and there's an option to sit outside which once it cools off will be great!

My colleagues kept raving about the chicken and waffles (with bacon inside), I had to try it even I was on a diet. Oh my god.. this got to be the best chicken n waffle I've had! The chicken portion was great and the waffle was just perfect, come on it had bacon bits inside of it! Top It off with the syrup they gave, I almost cried because of happiness  anyway, it is not just the hype. It's definitely true, the service was A-M-A-Z-I-N-G! first time a hostess asked our group "Are you guys on lunch break and short on time?" they were going to adjust the service according to our break! The server was awesome! We also ordered the wings (Korean and buffalo) they were also good! I highly recommend this place! Will be coming back for more!
My food was super greasy and I couldn't eat it. They really need to ease up on the oil.

This place was great! They are available on Open Table. They are kind of small and the tables are relatively close together but we had a good spot. They have extremely high quality napkins which I truly appreciated. Weird, I know. 

I wasn't sure about our server at first but he was great! We appreciated his service. He had an apprentice of sorts and she was great as well. She appreciated my love of ketchup and she hooked me up with lots of extra ramekins upon my request. Anyone that reads my reviews knows I hate my ketchup being rationed. Lol! 

The drinks were excellent!!! They are honestly the most reasonably priced cocktails we've ever had at a nice restaurant and the best part was they used high quality ingredients and they were DELICIOUS! I had a version of a Kir Royale which is one of my favorite social sparklers and it was even better than the last bar that served me my favorite Kir Royale.  I couldn't even resist...I had two!!! 

My fiancé got a chicken sandwich which he didn't love. He said it was kind of dry and he wouldn't order it again. I got a cheeseburger with avocado which was so good! One of my favorite burgers at a restaurant. The fries were good! 

The bathrooms were clean. They looked modern but when closely inspected, you can see a lot of shabby work that could be improved. 

The restaurant is attached to the Ben Franklin Residences which has a very nice lobby area. 

They have a small but energetic bar scene. They don't stay open super late but they are a great spot for lunch or dinner or some early drinks. It gets kind of loud inside even when it isn't packed. 

We enjoyed Sandler's, I recommend it and we will definitely return!

I visited this location about three times now and had a decent experience both times... that's where the four stars are from! But recently we went here and the wait staff was WELL BELOW AVERAGE.
First and always foremost for me: OUT SIDE DINING IS SO LOVELY! When we went they were ofc doing landscaping so there was a weed eater and mower running but other than that- it's priceless!!!
We went this time and was told that the outdoor seating was unavailable...which is strange during a pandemic but okay? We waited about 15-20 minutes before being seated which we thought was really good for a Friday night! Our waiter was really terrible. He never offered soup or salad? We got out entrees before bread...bc we had to ask for it. We'd look for our waiter for refills and he was no where to be found.
Overall very tough experience but that's not our normal here.

We will be back

After pre and post renovation visits, I'm glad this place is finished being reconstructed.  The main floor is still as it was, while the 2nd and 3rd levels received a major face lift. Usually there's a cover to go on the 2nd and 3rd levels, but I assume due to the city seemingly being dead (surprising for a Saturday) you were free to roam. 

Good vibes, scantily clad dressed Jell-O shot(not enough liquor) servers, decent food selection, strong drinks and the prices are reasonable. 

Come one, come all.

Really enjoyed this place. Great place for lunch. Quick and healthy. I have the poke bowel and outside the tuna chunks being cut too large, super good. Friend had the grilled cheese and tomato soup. She said it was really good but did not that it seemed like the soup had a coconut cream in it. So note that. The bread looked tasty, maybe Barrio bread. Either way, will be going back.
Disgusting found a small spider in the soup tried to call waiter attention he didn't come after almost 5 min. Will not comeback.
Good restaurant, no complaints.  Crispy Thai chicken was good and so was the pho.
The açaí bowls are my favorite in Tucson. I always order them and they come quickly and perfectly!!! Classic. Cant go wrong.

This isn't my favorite pho place. They do have really delicious lemongrass chicken. I've had dirty cups with someone else's lipstick still on it and cutlery with old food stuck on it here before that's just put me off from visiting. It is also a little cramped inside. The pho itself is okay, not the most flavorful but you do get a huge portion for cheap.

I am so grateful for the staff at Cimarron Animal Hospital. My dog has high anxiety, is very aggressive when scared, and does not handle vet visits well- it's always a stressful time for us both. However, the staff took time to work with him, allowed me to assist in calming him down, and let me sit in a back room with him until his sedative kicked in before surgery. They did not get frustrated or upset with him at any point. They were so good with him and kind towards me. Other vets haven't been able to deal with him, so I am so glad to have found this place. He is recovering perfectly from dental surgery. I could not be happier with the services here.
Food was tasty. We had the vegetarian sandwich and the Thai bowl with chicken. But the wait time wasn't really worth it.

We have been fans of Sundaze for a long time (I'm frankly surprised I haven't reviewed until now).  The owners and their employees are polite, efficient and very service oriented.

Tasty FroYo (today we had vanilla and peach tart) and a zillion possible toppings!  We brought home pints of pistachio and mashmallow/rootbeer float!  You can even check their FB page to see what's on tap for the week!

In addition to the tastiness, I appreciated their COVID modifications- one family/party in the lobby at a time (its a small lobby); they will take orders and serve from the door if you are uncomfortable using the lobby, masked employees (which I feel like is getting a little harder to find these days), and bottles of hand sanitizer everywhere you look.  

They have sweet little tables outside so you don't have to drive away with melting FroYo in your lap.

I am so glad that Sundaze appears to be faring ok during this odd time- we will definitely be back (again and again and again).

So for a long time this wasn't on my list... I had tried it and had such a bad experience i never wanted to go back...but since all my friends LOVE this place i finally stepped back in...

i'm still not a fan of their pho or their crispy spring rolls topped w. crushed peanuts?! (i like the traditional ones made with rice paper) but their bo tai chanh (raw beef w. lime juice, fried shallots with fish sauce dip) is awesome!!!  So friggin GOOD. (think of it as viet style beef carpaccio)

Now the last time we went we decided to get family style dishes and they were all a hit!

snail with lemongrass & hot pepper: YUM!  you need to use toothpicks but well worth the work
salted baked soft shell crab: hmm looked/tasted deep fried to me! but it's a huge plate and it's GOOD!  super fried goodness (i've had this dish multiple times...YUM)
pan fried egg noodles with seafood: noodles were crispy, sauce was really good and went well w. the seafood, plus it had some veggies/mushrooms which is always nice

Add a side of rice and you had 3 happy and stuffed people.  We even had to pack leftovers.  Food looked and tasted so good the table next to us ended up asking what it all was so they could try it on their next visit.

bonus: cheap!!! 8.95 for the noodles, 13.95 for the softshell crab and 9.95 for the snails

This has been one of my favorite spots for affordable and BIG portions of pho! It's not the best or most delicious bowl in the city, but with how big the bowl is and how little they charge for that, it's hard to resist. An excellent choice if you're in the Chinatown area and you're craving a noodle soup or Viet-Thai in general!

I came in because I won a gift card to this establishment and I was pleasantly surprised by their menu. I have a friend who is vegan and it's always so hard to find places that accommodate our two differing food preferences. Really enjoyed that the food tasted like a home cooked meal vs something that came out of a package and heated. My friends and I will definitely visit again.
Unfortunately took them 25 mins to prepare my mobile order of a smoothie and burrito :/ wasn't busy either. Staff was nice though!

The very best in healthy great tasting food! Goodness has gone above- and beyond- in doing their part to keep our community, and their staff, as safe as possible during this hard time- all while providing excellent , friendly service. It's invaluable for our spirits to have a bit of normalcy- and I really appreciate that Goodness has been able to provide this . Please support  local restaurants when you can- especially ones like Goodness that serve amazing clean food .

I took my dog here after 3 days of vomiting and diarrhea. They gave him a shot for nausea, which helped, but all they knew to do about diarrhea is give him probiotics, which I had already tried (they also didn't bother to explain that the anti-diarrhea treatment they prescribed was nothing but probiotics; if they had bothered to explain, before charging me for that treatment, I could have saved $50 for something I had already been administering, which didn't help). 

They did a follow-up call, during which I explained that he now has a rectal prolapse due to (now on day 6 of) diarrhea, every 45-60 minutes, and all they could recommend was an ultrasound and more fluids. $400+ dollars down the drain.

Not a great experience for my birthday,  girl acted like she wanted to go home, didnt take our dirty dishes away till we got the bill, no happy birthday, cake or even a smile, sorry  bad experience on my day 7/11 me and my daughter..

Goodness Juice Bar has the pull of everything I love in food: fast, delicious, healthy and colorful!! It was on my list of places to visit in Tucson from the beginning, so with the first opportunity given, I drove straight to Goodness for indulge myself. 

I came in with Acai on my mind. Luckily I didn't hold up a line while making my difficult food decisions; I vacillated between the Mango Jungle bowl and the Pink Dragon, but the bee pollen and raw honey on the Mango bowl won me over.  I also decided I needed to try a Tofu Taco. 

You walk up to the ordering counter, sign says "Order Here" - easy. Give your order, then sit down and relax until your name is called at the "Pick Up" station. My order came out in waves: first the Acai bowl, then the Tofu Taco about 3 minutes later.

So I started in on the Acai bowl as soon as it was in front of me. And sadly, I found that this bowl was not excessively impressive. My favorite aspects were the bee pollen as well as the raw honey - they provided the most flavor in the bowl. The acai mixture was yummy, but the mango was slightly under-ripe, so not much "mango" came through. I still enjoyed this cold treat, however. I'd start with the Pink Dragon next time.

The Tofu Taco was delicious!!! It is on the A la Cart menu, and comes on a wheat tortilla. The tofu is also supplemented by a cabbage slaw, roasted red peppers, pumpkin seeds and an amazing cilantro cream sauce. One taco definitely wasn't enough (I wanted to eat at least 3 more) but I was heading back home for a bite with the family, so it was better that I didn't stuff myself.

If I lived in Tucson, I know that Goodness Juice bar would be a constant stop for me. I love how they serve healthy foods that also taste excellent. It's my favorite way of eating. Just while sitting in and enjoying my quick meal, I noted how busy this establishment gets! There was a constant stream of people, and a line even started to form while I watched, though it moved quickly. This will totally be a traditional stop for every time I visit Tucson.
They don't care about the tenants who pay their bills. They have a roach infestation in every building

I had a fabulous experience tonight for dinner. I picked a meal that qualified for a second meal for free. It was easy to follow their directions to park and get your food handed to you through the car window. I paid when I ordered so that was already taken care of. When I pulled into the parking lot, I was offered wine or sangria to add to my order. Now I'm sitting home and relaxing with a nice glass of sangria. That's how you do take out!!!!

We stopped by through a recommendation from a friend. Are we glad we did !

It's a small, quaint, and comfortable place. If any of you have been to Umi Star before, they've taken up that space now. Minimal decor, limited seating, but understandable considering the space. It's cute. Service is friendly, but also minimal? No greetings or anything. Eh.

The line starts to the left right after you walk through the doors (which we missed and had to walk around. Oops.) The menus follow the wall that you walk through to wait to order. 

We ordered from the Breakfast menu. The Burrito is AMAZING ! I don't exactly remember what was in it... Quinoa, chicken, fresh tasting something or another, all wrapped in a wheat (?) tortilla, and then put on the grill for a slightly crunchy finish. I was full after only eating half, along with my melons juice. But I swear I wanted to finish all of it. The bf ordered the Breakfast Sandwich. We loved the bread it comes on, and how fresh the ingredients tasted. Portions look small, but everything was very filling. I made him finish my burrito, which he did not object to... so that definitely topped him over a bit. He also ordered a juice, which I believe was the Hulk. He liked it. I did not. I'm not a big juicer, nor do I like parsley. It's a biased opinion in my case.

The location is definitely out of the way for us, but worth the trip when we can manage. $8 for each sandwich/burrito and $6 for each of our drinks. It's not the cheapest for breakfast-on-the-go type of food, but it seems worth it to us.

I was there on Sunday to watch the Eagles game. The restaurant is beautiful. I absolutely love the decor! The food was amazing, the drinks were even better. Gina was outstanding. She was constantly making sure we were good on drinks & clearing everything we weren't using. Lisa also came over multiple times to make sure we were enjoying everything, which I really appreciated. They genuinely care about guest experience. I already told multiple people to check this place out & I'll be back soon!

Poor food, no seasoning, not on time for pickup, and missing parts of salad, utensils, and napkins. 
Not even close to par of others in the chain. HUGE DISAPPOINTMENT. NOT RETURNING TO THIS LOCATION. FAILURE!

I love Soho juice co and most of their products.

I recently tried the Grandma's waffle with almond butter, bananas, and dates, and the Notella waffle with notella and strawberries. Both were amazing. Definitely recommend. 

The cashew cups and almond cups are amazing too. I also love their most of their juices. You can ask to try some if you're not sure what to get. 

I tried the Cookie Monster donut, it was ok, I wouldn't recommend it. I was going to order the bronut for my little sister but they said it's 18+ because it's CBD infused. 

Service is not great at this location, but amazing at their other locations.

Literally one of the best tacos and protein drinks I've ever had. So refreshing. So many vegetarian options and more. One a kind with an awesome vibe inside. Lots of nice seating and great musical ambiance.  I ordered the Goods protein drink and a Tofu Taco. More than fulfilling!

I have been less than frequent patron of La Giraldilla. Nevertheless it is an Excellent place to go eat. The attention from waitresses is superb as they all serve you well.

The food is very, very good, delicious, although I always ask for the same dish lol, (Bistecs salteado) other accompany friends agree with my assessment.

The restaurant is ample, familiar, theres live music at times. There is a terraza area for the outside eater or smokers I guess.

I recommend it.

Cheap, quick, delicious.

Nothing spectacular, but solidly decent all around. 

GET THE RAW BEEF DISH! raw beef+lime juice+peanuts+fish sauce = :))))

Pho, vermicelli bowls (bun) are safe. Was not a fan of the chicken curry, though.

I've been to this location twice, and I have to say, I'm impressed! When I got there a few days ago, I thought that I'd have to wait in a line because it was packed but low and behold, they have an upstairs seating area which blew my mind as it looks so small from the outside. 
I've been looking for a new Pho place to frequent after moving to Philly recently and this place truly delivers. The broth when the food first arrives is amazing. I didn't even have to add any siracha or other additions to make it taste better (even though I did later to suit my needs haha). 
While I've only ordered Pho here, I have to say that I will be back many more times to check out the rest of their menu. With the recent cold weather, it's the perfect place for a large bowl of Pho to warm you up. The thing I think I love about this place is that it's pretty reasonably priced for how much you get and the variety is endless. A regular size is enough for a large adult while an XL is huge! I will definitely be back soon!

Sunday brunch without a reservation and a large group is basically impossible in the heart of the city. Sandler's on 9th was so accommodating to our large group at just a moments notice and I was so impressed. I came with a group of 16 people on Sunday around 11am and the staff was so courteous and kind despite the fact that we had late arrivals. They seated us in an enclosed area so our large group was able to talk freely while still being heard. 

I got the chicken and waffles and they did not disappoint. Wow. Everyone was a fan of their meal, from the personalized omelets, to the elvis pancakes. Great location, great atmosphere, great staff. 

It took some time to ask for the smaller things like hot sauce and sour cream, but with such a large group - that's to be expected.

I ordered a kale citrus salad and there was no kale or avocado in it. It wouldn't have been a big deal but I paid 10bucks for it and they didn't say hey by the way half the stuff you paid for isn't even in there. They get worse every time I go.

GET A SECOND OPINION!!!! Dr Scott Goldsmith and his PA told my wife and I that surgery was the only option to realign her broken bones.  This was simply not true.  I took her to a hand surgeon for a second opinion, and found out that he can set the bone straight by hand! This was a very painful process, but the pain was something my wife was willing to Indore so that she does not have to live with a plate and screws in her wrist for the rest of her life.  Do not proceed with any surgery here prior to getting a second opinion!

This isn't my personal choice for a Vietnamese restaurant, but a friend wanted pho and she chose this so I went with it. 

For starters since we were a large group they placed us near the back but it was pretty uncomfortable, at least for me, because the servers would just stand there are stare at our table. But besides that let's get on with the rest of the review...

Food was decent prices, very inexpensive for a large amount of food. My sister ordered a "small dish" on the menu and it was pretty large. But besides the size of the food being good, the food itself was decent tasting. Nothing special, but it wasn't bad. 

The one thing that made this review bad was my other sister's dish had a piece of metal in it the size of the tip of your pinky.......I didn't know about it until we left the restaurant otherwise I would've complained about it and taken a picture as proof. I would've understood if it was a tiny piece of plastic, but a piece of metal??? That was really bad. 

I would personally never come back here due to the metal and due feeling slightly uncomfortable due to the staff. And if you REALLY want Vietnamese food drive a little further and out of Chinatown and you'll find pretty decent Viet restaurants out there. And honestly if I were in Chinatown Philly go eat Chinese food not Vietnamese there.

I thought it was pretty decent. This was my first time here today. Service was great and food came out super fast. 

We ordered cha gio (egg rolls) and goi cuon (rice paper spring rolls for apps. I thought the eggs rolls were too greasy as you can still see the oils on the plate. I thought the spring rolls were okay. The rice paper wraps were a bit over done and mushy. 

For our meals I got the pho ga (chicken). The broth was pretty good. It said on the menu shredded chicken and that was what I was expecting, but it wasn't. We also ordered pan fried noodles with chicken and veggies. We enjoyed that very much. Overall pretty good place in Chinatown.

Everything I've tried on the menu has been delicious. So full of flavor that you wouldn't know your actually eating really healthy meals. I love to go for breakfast. I have had the granola several times. You get your choice of almond milk or skim milk but really you can ask for any milk they have as a substitute. It is always topped with seasonal fruit. I love buying a bag of the granola to take home for the week as well. They don't have the granola bags on display but you can ask and they will grab you one and they are very affordable and a goof amount compared to other restaurants in town. I was a little nervous to try the breakfast burrito because its a little different then what your used to since it has quinoa and a wheat tortilla but it ended up being delicious. I have never been disappointed with anything I've ordered here. From the juices to entries everything is on point.

I've been coming to Pho Xe Lua for years, and I'll continue to do so. For what it's worth, the interior looks like it's trapped in a timewarp. It literally looks the same as it did the first time I stepped in.

$7 for two pork chops on rice? Yes, please.

Thanks to Amy L. for getting me to stop by "choo choo"[1], and suggesting I get the pork on rice.

[1] A lot of my friends call Pho Xe Lua that because of the neon train sign out front.

I can't say enough about Ulele. The menu is incentive, all locally sourced and absolutely delicious. Hard to choose from this menu. The drinks are amazing! Excellent US Wines (+a few Spanish wines, a nod to it's owners, Columbia), and house made beers. Servers are spot on! Great personality, extremely knowledgeable and pleasant. Excellent location on the water too.

Confession: I cheated on my typical pho place (pho ha) to try out this restaurant. Shame on me. While the location is way more convenient for me, the service, cleanliness, and food just fell short. We were seated in the upstairs part of the restaurant which is pretty disgusting compared to the downstairs. There are large bins full of dirty dishes just laying around everywhere. Not a good first impression. 

We looked over the menu but ended up with our typical meals: shrimp summer rolls to start and 2 bowls of steak pho. The service was not great- it was difficult to find our server to get tea and water. Also, we got the rolls at the same time as the huge bowls of pho, which was kind of annoying. The rolls were pretty good but nothing special. I started eating my HUGE bowl of pho (we got extra large thinking it was similar to the sizing at pho ha and they were way too big). The flavor was good.. and then I saw a bug floating around in my soup. Womp womp. We sent it back after we tracked down our server and I was given a new one very quickly, but the little appeal that the place had pretty much dwindled after this. They didn't take the pho off the bill or even apologize. Subpar customer service. 

I won't be back!

I have never been disappointed with a 4 star yelp review until today.  This brunch barely deserves 2 stars, but ambiance and the waitress deserve some credit!   My $16 omelet has barely any extra ingredients which I paid $1.50 per additional topping, it was thin and tasteless. The hash browns though I asked for well done, to me that means crispy and golden brown. These were embarrassing to look at tiny pieces of burn skin and bottom of the bag potatoes. It was the worst presentation of a very pricey omelet.  The kids pancakes were fine, nicely split in half but the tempura banana was soggy not crispy. 
Brunch is hard to mess up this bad.  Highly disappointed.

Stopped here on the way back to Orlando to grab a drink and use the restroom after a Buccaneers game. The place was pretty darn crowded, but it was probably because everyone else leaving the Bucs game had the same idea we did. LOL 

It is your typical Wawa. It's clean and convenient. Clean bathroom. Tons of snacks and drinks. Gas which is generally cheaper than other places in the area. 

Would have given another star if they would have had another register open. Line was way too long for a quick stop at a convenience store.

This used to be my favorite restaurant in town for healthy, balanced veggie-friendly food. They must have switched owners or something- because the menu is completely different now. All of their new menu items are overpriced- I paid $12 for their "veggie sandwich" which was basically chunks of kale with tiny pieces of squash and pepper on a cheap, store-bought white roll. Hardly worth the price tag. Not only that but we had to wait a long time just to order even though there was only one person in front of us. And we had to pay a 10% gratuity for using a card even though we didn't receive any service. Makes no sense to me- miss the old Goodness but luckily there are plenty of other great restaurants nearby that we will be patronizing instead.
I love this place :) the juice is made fresh. I really like the big melons one. They are all good though. The chicken caesar wrap is my favorite menu item and the tofu tacos are excellent too

Disappointed. Haven't tried the pho yet, which sounds good from their other reviews but from the dishes I ordered, I was not at all satisfied. I went craving some banh cuon with cha lua but I was told they only had it in appetizer form (not a full dish like what I thought from the pictures). Worried I wasn't going to make the $15 minimum for credit cards I went with my second favorite dish, mi xao gion, and an order of cha gio. Both were disappointing and tasteless. The cha gio were crunchy but didn't have any flavor on their own - practically needed to be drenched in fish sauce to be slightly tasty. The mi xao gion was equally bland - the sauce was just a tasteless brown sauce adding nothing to the fried noodles. I might come again to try the pho but not anytime soon given how disappointing the other dishes were. Not even sure if this place is Vietnamese because none of the waiters understood me. 

Mi xao gion

The first time I came here, I was told that we going to Choo Choo's for some pho - which I thought was a strange (but very cute!) name for a Vietnamese restaurant. Then I saw the little train on their sign and had a real "ohhhh" moment.

Reasonably-priced, hearty bowls of pho and speedy, no nonsense service is what makes Choo Choo's a place to come back to time and time again. Pho is easy to find in Philly, but Choo Choo's definitely serves up some of the best bowls in the area.

This place is great for a refreshing meal, however my peanut bowl was lacking some sauce, and slightly impractical to make into bite size portions. I would give the overall meal a 3/5 but the restaurant a 4/5.

Ok, so I was completely shocked to find out a 16oz smoothie was $9.  Y'all are out of your damn minds. Also, why are you asking us to tip you on top of that? I got this smoothie weeks ago and I'm still pissed about my $9.

Family restaurant with quick service.
Food was good and you are able to BYOB. Tried the fried rice and pho which was very good.

This place is amazing. The food is excellent. I was walking around Chinatown looking for a new place to eat as always. I found this place with great ratings so I stopped by. Was greeted promptly and was sat down right away. The menu have so many great options and the prices are amazing. Also the portion are amazingly big so come with a appetite. The staff are very friendly and always alert for your needs. I must say I will visit more often.

Wonderful food, so healthy and fresh.  The outdoor patio is lovely - covered and a nice option to eat outside.
We'll go back for sure.

Came in 40 minutes before closing and the lady in the front was very hesitant to take my order and only offered the to-go option. Felt unwelcome as a customer and the two other costumers waiting for their order publicly announced how rude the worker was. One of the men felt targeted then stated it was because of his race. Very uncomfortable environment she created. On top of that the food was dissatisfying and not as good as we've had it. She then closed the restaurant 20 minutes early.
Beer cooler locked, asked cashier to let me in. Said someone will be over. Waited 20 mins and nobody . First gas station I've ever been at that locks beer smh . Go to shell across the street.
Great, friendly service. Generous portions and very tasty. My party of four was very happy with our choices.

This review is about the Olive Garden at 17011 Palm Pointe Dr, Tampa, FL 33647. I love Italian food and consistently enjoy the food here. I've gone there many time with family from 2-6 people.  I also have gone as part of a group of 30 people three times.  I organize lunch out for the seniors in the park I live in.  I am always impressed with how attentive the staff is during these outings. For the most part we enjoyed our meals.  Of course there may have been one or two who weren't all that happy.  When I suggested that we go again this summer no one objected.  Any time I've ever gone I end up taking half my food home.  Can't eat it all after having a big salad and plenty of breadsticks. They wrapped up breadsticks for me and sent me home with extra sauce when I ask. The check comes with delicious Andes mints.

Sandwich bread is changed from regular ole wheat bread that you use at home to a wheat long sub bread :). 

Kafette with sugar is amazing! 3 bucks for a shot glass size of coffee but it's so smooth and tasty and packed with caffeine lol.

I always rotate between the pink dragon, the chicken n brie sandwich, and the kale citrus wrap (which was taken off the menu as a wrap but they can still make it at request)

I go here all the time and I love it! Their bowls are great and so is the avocado and salmon toasts. This place is healthy and fresh and they make great fresh pressed juices. I wish I took more pictures of the food I've had but I only have this one picture. I definitely recommend Goodness for breakfast lunch or brunch
The special noodle soup and the special vermicelli are all you need here for the first time. Thank you, thank you for bringing the taste of Vietnamese heaven to us.

I love coming here for pho. Their large bowl of pho is huge. They give a generous amount of noodles and toppings. It's probably one of my favorite pho places to go in Philly!  I usually love my pho with tendon and tripe. 

Other items I love ordering here is their salted chicken and fish fried rice. They make it so well. I also like the vermicelli noodle with the spring rolls, meat, and shrimp, also the raw beef appetizer with fish sauce. That is absolutely delicious. 

I believe the place changed owner as the last time I came to eat in, I don't see the usual servers but I would say the food was almost the same with the new owner.
Ate here for the first time recently, really enjoyed my experience. Quick and great service. I had the Asian Noodle salad. It was delightful! I will be back again.
Had a nice salad and husband had a turkey sandwich. The atmosphere is hipster industrial.  It's a fine place for a small bite, if that's all you want.  I would come here again.
Good soup, good price, nothing fancy. My go-to spot for Pho.

12th Air was one of my favorite bars ever because of hilariously quirky staff,and cheap large beers. 

The owners knocked down some walls, closed the awesome roof deck, and got new furniture and ICandy was born. Management also hired a troop of muscle-y dark haired men to serve shots and dance in panties on poles.

Went here on a Saturday night and it was ridiculously crowded. The dance floor is small and cramped. One plus is that there are about 5 separate bar areas so it doesn't take long to grab a drink. The roof deck wasn't open which really sucks, it was a great area to take a rest and talk to friends.

Also I didn't quite understand why every bar I went to had different prices on the same drinks and why the sizes differed. Overall really cheesy, I liked 12th Air better.

So at first go-around, I was pretty weirded out by the pre-juiced kale, parsley, et al... I'm used to ordering a juice by clarifying the amount of kale leaves, lemon wedges, and pretentiousness I want in my very large, very green juice. 

Juice control freak. No big. 

But, I'll tell you, by the second go-around, I relaxed about it. My juice concierge put me at ease. The selection of pre-juiced greens are great, so that you can add "just a little... whatever it is you want added".

I've tried three different juices from the menu and loved all three. Big Melons (hello, just named so they can say it over the loud speaker when the juice is ready? yah, i think so. LOL.), Commuter & Clean it Up. I would recommend all 3. 

 Also had the grilled cheese and the veggie teriyaki bowl. I would recommend both. 

The grilled cheese came with this out-of-this-world aioli, and sun dried tomatoes were the perfect addition. The teriyaki bowl had the teriyaki sauce on the rice & veggies, and also a little extra on the side. This was literally exactly what I needed. Not overly sauced, but as I wanted a little more towards the end, it was already there me. Goodness, goodness!

My response to everyone who says their portions are small: Yes, when raised to think that a big mac, super size fry and a 44 oz soda constitutes a reasonable lunch, then YES ... Absolutely their portions are small.

But comparison truly is the thief of joy. 

If you need to be uncomfortably full after you eat, for less than $8 - this is not your place.

But I don't. So I loved it. I will definitely be back.

sandler's on 9th is great. we recently hosted a work function (drinks and dinner) here, inclusive of 25 people and there were no issues. in fact all those who attended were very pleased - the food was excellent; drinks were delicious; and the staff was friendly and attentive. the planning process leading up the event was also great. 

highly recommend this place and we look forward to hosting our next event here. can't wait to get the nachos and the garlic shrimp pappardelle again (yum!).

Stopped by for dinner with my in-laws on a Sunday night. We ordered iced Vietnamese coffees, several varieties of pho, a bun rieu and 2 banh cuon. The banh cuon tasted like it was previously frozen and ultimately defrosted, but the other dishes were pretty good. I devoured my pho and finished my coffee and everyone else quite enjoyed their pho. My only comment is serving sizes are pretty generous. I have a big appetite for a woman and the large pho filled me up to the point where I was uncomfortable. My other half ordered the XL and finished it as well, but he was satiated after.

Food is great and it's located in a very convenient location. The staff is always pleasant and professional. We go there with family and we always have a blast, it is such a chill and nice place to dine, with a great menu that never strays away from what they are: a Italian restaurant. I tried their new chicken Alfredo bites and it was really good, something I would definitely eat again and my brother-in-law had their chicken Scampi. They also have wine and drafts and cocktails but also non alcoholic beverages and you can have endless soup and salad and I have to say their soups are great, packed with flavor and they feel fresh.

I'll be short and sweet (a first for me!) Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai or affectionately know as "Choo Choo" in Chinatown. is the biggest bang for your buck in Chinatown along with Tasty Place. 
The food is good and two people can feast on $20 bucks and I mean feast. 
I gotta give a shout out for their amazing fruit smoothies (Strawberry!!)
WOO WOO!! all aboard!

Hmm.. as I munch on my aztca bowl I can't help but think that I am eating a more expensive version of a chipotle bowl. The elements and flavors of steak, brown rice, salsa, and lettuce completely mirror a chipotle bowl.. and I can't help but feel that I just got ripped off. $12.00 for 3 thinly cut pieces of avocado, a scoop of brown rice, a handful of lettuce, poorly seasoned steak and a dash of pico de gallo doesn't make me too happy, especially since the portion size is very small. I was able to finish this bad boy off way too quickly, and to top it all off.. it tastes exactly like chipotle, oh and I am still hungry. I think next time I come I'll have to try their acai bowls or their salads or juices.. because sadly my first visit left me more than disappointed.

I'm disappointed that they closed the North location as Goodness has quickly become one of my favorite restaurants. Can't go wrong with breakfast (served all day) and their bowls and coffee are great too. I just tried the Hot Tropic smoothie and it was honestly the best smoothie I've had in my life. So glad to see the owners opening more restaurants around the city too!

Natural gas grill running! I purchased a Napoleon gas grill and it was installed by another company incorrectly, I had a very hard time and had multiple other companies come out that were a little to no help. STEPHEN from Gas masters came out and truly lived up to their name! The pricing was extremely reasonable and the work was done in about 30 minutes. Not sure about other peoples experiences but mine was fantastic!

Despite the restaurant being understaffed (food can be a long wait) the dishes are excellent.  I simply love their burger and their Daily Buzz Smoothie.  I show up weekly for them.  Their PB toast and Salmon toast are excellent as well, along with their grilled cheese and tomato soup.  This is one of my favorite places to eat.  I just wish they had more staff to run more efficiently.  Also, it would be nice if the service fee (tip) was optional or adjustable, and not just added to the bill.  I don't mind tipping the staff, but it feels a bit forced, and makes the bill more expensive if you aren't aware it's added in there.  All and all, I'll keep showing up for this yummy healthy food!
Looooooooovvvvvvveeeeeee their granola. That is by far my favorite granola in the whole wide world. Had a few other dishes but I wasn't a fan. Loved the berries with the granola. Get the granola!!!

We called:
1) pho xe lua (3/10). It tastes okay but there weren't a lot of meat and the broth tastes full of msg
2) oc gao xao xa ot (1/10) literally no flavor
3) cari de/lau de/goat or lamb curry (1/10) again absolutely no flavors. The vegetables and the meat didn't taste like they came from the same pot. It's almost like it was cooked separately and then dumped into the yellow curry.
4) mi xao gion (5/10) it was okay, definitely better than all the other dishes. The meat was cold while the noodles were hot.

We came from the DMV and had quite some expectations for the food at Philly, but it was rather disappointing. The customer service here was great though!

Being Vietnamese, I think I tend to be a bit strict when it comes to Vietnamese food. I've come here twice with friends from college and both times the food has alright, nothing to write home about but it hits the spot when you're craving Viet food. The restaurant is very much a no frills, no fuss place to get a quick meal.

We've gotten pho, bun bo hue (Vietnamese beef noodle soup, which is my favorite type of soup), and rice platters. The pho is pretty good, not the best pho I've ever had but hit the main points: savory broth, lots of noodles and meat, with a plate of all the accompanying vegetables you'd expect. The bowls are huge- the small size is "large" while the larger size is labeled "XL", and they don't lie! The "bun bo" was also satisfactory, not as good as my grandma's but it'll do in a pinch. There was a good amount of meat and pork legs, However, there was a ton of mushy lemongrass and other particles at the bottom that made the last couple spoonfuls of soup inedible. I think I must've gotten the last serving at the bottom of the pot they used to cook. While I didn't try the porkchop rice platter, it looked pretty standard.

The food is standard Vietnamese fare, but I have to admit the good prices (~7 for a pho or beef noodle soup) and large portions might keep me coming back.

I'd say this is one of the best pho places in Chinatown, but not Philly overall. The prices are remarkably cheap for the amount of food you get, be it a large bowl or pho or a bowl of bun. 

I'd come to Pho Xe Lua for a bowl of pho before swinging in Pho 75 or Vietnam Palace. It's just easier on the wallet and more food for your buck.

So I suppose if you're in the Chinatown area and in the mood for pho, swing down here. But if you're in south philly or otherwise, you know what to do: go to Washington Ave.

I love supporting local business and this is one place I will be supporting often.  I've been several times and have enjoyed everything ordered between myself and friends.  The Kale Caesar was crisp, light, and refreshing.  The Bistro Filet and Gorgonzola sandwich was so yummy, I could have eaten it again.  The Roasted Chicken and Brie sandwich was delightful (and I don't tend to like Brie).  The Thai Chicken was bowl licking worthy!  The staff are helpful and friendly, which always makes for a better dining experience.

This is the perfect place on a cold and rainy day. The portions are HUGE and the value is great. Service was fast as well. So happy I found this place.

I ordered #101, which is the basic rice noodle soup with medium rare beef and various fixings. One thing I really enjoyed was the tripe. It added a chewiness to the bites. Must add a bit of sriracha to the broth to give it a kick. Broth was so rich and they gave generous portions of beef.

I visited here during the pandemic and as unfortunate as that was they had a great table setup at the front entrance to serve customers and the service was wonderful as well as the product. I'll definitely be back! Thank you.

Found a spot through yelp and was highly impressed. I'm very for Milyer with Vietnamese food in this hit home in a good way! I went there with my family of four and we ate so we couldn't eat anymore. The bill only came to $23 and the food was amazing! I highly recommend the lemongrass chicken, barbecue pork, and the spring rolls

I cannot recall the name of the vet that I saw.....but here's the scenario.  We had a 17 year old dalmation (yep, 17 years old). Actually, he was my husband's ex-girlfriend's dog that we had been taking care of for over 2 years.  After time, she would not do what she was supposed to do to take care of "her dog."   His hip displasia was beginning to get worse and worse.  So, I took matters into my own hands and brought the dog to this vet.
The dog was well fed, excercised, bathed and all in all WELL taken care of.  The vet started of rude before even hearing the dog's issues.
