After she explained that it would cost upwards of $1000 to help the dog.  I explained that we did not have that amount of money and that the dogs owner refused to take care of him.  I had also explained that the dog was 17 and that the hip displasia could not be fixed and unfortunately his time was limited.  She basically called me a liar and said the dog was 14 (although, I knew for a fact the age of the dog).   But I asked her for pills to help ease his pain.  She told me that I was a bad owner and that I had no compassion for animals.  Are you kidding me?!?!?! I just spent over $200 on a dog that I had been taking care of for over 2 years that was not even mine.
To top things off, after the appointment, the elevator to go back downstairs would not work and I had to carry the dog down 2 flights of stairs.  They called me for a follow up and I explained why I would not be returning.  2 weeks later, they called me again, and a few weeks after that, they called me again.  Now, they have added me to their email list.

Do not go to this vet!     She falsified aspects on my dogs blood work in order to incur extensive unnecessary testing,  the costs would have been excessive.   The doctor and the assistant base their practice on scare tactics.   They threaten with cancer and then make me feel totally bad in order to charge for completely unnecessary tests.  She wanted to run extensive testing on "elevated" kidney levels however, with a second opinion, there was nothing wrong nor did the blood results show this elevated level in the kidneys.   All kidney results were within normal ranges yet she insisted on a multitude of expensive tests based on her false diagnosis.  She is a quack and will rob you blind all while pleading with your love foe your pet,   Do not go to this vet unless you have a lot of expendable money and want your beloved pet to undergo unnecessary, painful testing,

So we went to ICandy on Sunday, August 26th, 2018, for a Drag Brunch sponsored through Eventbrite. We decided to do the 3 course brunch for my future sister in laws bridal shower. This was really a waste of money, we did not get 3 courses we barely got one and the food was horrible. The performances were just as awful expect for the Drag Queen that impersonated JLo and Selena (she was actually very good). The only reason I gave it a 2 was because the bartender Liam was great and the drinks were very good. Other than that I do not recommend the Drag Brunch unless you want to see fake drag queens with hairy underarms and the gross food to match!

I had been dying to check this place out and who better to go with than our wonderful Yelp Philadelphia CM Michelle C?!

My lunch date and I popped in at noon on a Wednesday. The restaurant was moderately filled. We were quickly seated at a table for two close to the entrance to the restaurant (beware that there is a second entrance for take-out orders. If you're planning on dining in, use the entrance nearest Chestnut Street).

After all the "treating myself" I have been doing for the past couple weeks, I initially planned to choose something on the healthier side, however, all of that went out the window when I saw the menu. The burgers sounded delicious! How could I NOT get one? So, I ended up choosing the Hog which comes with Korean BBQ pork, bacon, angry onions and cheese. To make myself feel a little less guilty about the situation, I asked for a house salad instead of fries. 

The Hog burger was very good. The pork was flavorful, tender and juicy. The bacon was crispy, as were the deep fried slivered onions, and both were perfectly placed on top of the pork. The burger was huge and piled high. My only complaint was the bun. It wasn't well toasted and a bit soggy. Overall though, the burger was great and I was happy to take leftovers home with me (half of it to be exact - it is so big and filling!). 

The restaurant is quite spacious, clean and well maintained. There's a full bar over in one corner which I wouldn't mind sitting at next time so I can sip on a drink while enjoying my burger. 

I'm looking forward to my next visit and trying something else on the menu. Maybe next time, I'll even indulge in some fries!

Why can't NYC have better pho? Sigh.

Had to try the Vietnamese in Philly on my 24-hr trip here, so I dragged my poor boyfriend to this restaurant (Is there actually Thai on the menu? I didn't even bother to check) a mere 40 minutes before our bus was scheduled to leave - and after a feast at Reading Market, no less. That's how committed to noodle soup I am.

Place was bustling on a Saturday afternoon, and my order of the namesake pho xe lua (extra tendon, please and thank you) did not disappoint. A step above most of what's served in NYC, and at a cheaper price to boot. I somehow did not manage to inhale the entire bowl in 10 minutes, and my doggy bag had the noodles and soup packed separately.

I was, however, disappointed by the wait time (way too long) and table service (terrible, even for Chinatown).

The owner, Wendy, was very informative, inviting, and kept the free samples coming fast. In fact, I think I tried all 6 flavors but couldn't decide between ginger and turtle. It was seriously the hardest decision of my day. That's when Wendy suggested swirling the ginger and turtle together as another sample (for those counting at home, that's 7!). And if 7 wasn't already enough, I ordered a large bowl (YOLO!) which was filled and topped with a generous amount of cookie dough. The ginger was the winning flavor and is made from real ginger root. The texture was smooth, soft and the flavor was zesty and biting yet sweet. The flavor stuck on my palette well after I finished. It was so good that I ate it too fast and forgot to take a picture!

There are only 6 flavors but they are rotated about every week or so. It's nice that there are many non-fat and sugar free options but I would like to see a non-dairy option and fresh fruit toppings.

I'm glad I grabbed a frequent buyer punch card because I'll definitely be back.

I was in the area one afternoon, and wanted to try out a dining spot that I had never tried before. As I walked along Campbell. I spied a small dining spot that seemed to be full of people. Enter Goodness. 

It was a crisp December day, and I was craving something to warm my belly, and soothe my grinchy soul. Thankfully, they had an assortment of soups to choose from. I chose tomato soup. 

To pair it up, there were a variety of sandwiches available. What better to pair with tomato soup than grilled cheese? Yep, they had that too!

In fact, there is something for everybody here. Craving coffee, they've got it. Are you a vegetarian and in need of some sustenance? They also have salads and acai bowls!

The tomato soup was excellent. It was very thick and creamy, very unlike most tomato soups I have tried, and probably one of the best I've ever had. 

The grilled cheese was OK. It tasted a little strange and did not pair well with the tomato soup like I was expecting it to. 

Altogether, this place is pretty solid, though I'm not entirely sure if the food here is worth the money that you pay. It's still worth it if you are in the area and looking for a bit of a treat.

Ever since Covid they have changed pretty much everything on their menu. Smoothies are still good but we've had several breakfast items and salads since the change and they were all really bad. 

I see another reviewer mention the avocado toast and it was very accurate. It's slimy, sour green paste that doesn't even taste like avocado. I could image a fast food place serving nicer "avocado paste" than this. It was so slimy even my boyfriend who eats anything didn't want to finish it. So I took a bite, he took a bite, and we threw it out. 

I used to come here at least once a week and now after trying it 3 or 4 times since Covid we will not be coming back for food, but maybe for a smoothie every once in a while.

I really hope they go back to their old menu because the changes are not working for them. I'm very sad to have lost one of my favorite breakfast places. I hope they figure out something that works for them, but the changes to the previously great menu items (especially the breakfast items) are not it.

Found it on Yelp with high scores, and had lunch here with my friend. There were many types of pho on the menu, with different toppings. I had pho with well cooked beef and tribe, and my friend had pho with raw beef, well cooked beef and tribe. They offered large and extra large size to choose, and I think the large size is enough for girls. The pho was really yummy, and the soup was tasty too. We also had spring rolls. They were fried and cut into small pieces, very convenient for multiple people to share. Service was quick and good.

The pho here is delicious! I always get the Pho Tai Nam, but sub in the beef for chicken. 

The food is always fresh and the portions are huge! $5.95 for a large, $6.95 for an extra large. Such a great price for the amount of vegetables, meat, and broth you get. 

One of the best parts about this place is their incredibly fast service. Whenever my boyfriend and I have called in to place our order, our two entrees are ready for pick up within 10-15 minutes. Perfect for when you're hungry and need a quick and easy, but delicious, dinner!

Olive Garden to go is great!  Ordering online is a cinch and typically an order takes about 30 minutes. You pull into their designated curbside parking spots and once you check-in, within 5-10 minutes (they can be slow sometimes) your food is brought to the car and you're on your way. 

I haven't been here in a long time and i forgot how tasty the chicken scampi really is. Packed with flavor and leftovers for tomorrow. Win Win!

This place is really nice and spacious. However, I wasn't really impressed with the service or the food. We requested that things were brought out as they were finished (since we have little kids and we like to have our food hot). However, that did not happen and everything came out all at once. I don't mind when this happens when food is still hot, but things were not (except for about 2 dishes). Our server also disappeared on us for some time. Didn't check up on us at all and when we needed her, I couldn't find her to even wave her down.

Snyder's honey mustard and onion pretzel chicken - The chicken was moist, but I did not taste any of the snyder's breading on it. In fact, it was quite bland. 

Lobster poutine fries - these were decent (a lil salty at the end), but it did not have a lot of lobster in it like the photos the business owner posted on Yelp. It also was a tad on the luke warm side and the cheese was hardened when we received it. I felt if we received it when it was completed by the chef, we wouldn't have a difficult time pulling the fries apart because of the cheese

Kids mac n cheese - these were not cheesy nor saucy enough. My kids didn't really eat it.

Hog burger - probably my favorite item here. It was a nice size and was flavorful. Really enjoyed the crispy onions in them and there was plenty on the burger. I do wish it came with a little bit more pork though as I didn't really get to experience to Korean flavor to it.

Garlic Shrimp Pappardelle - this was a huge miss. Bland, pasta was dried out from sitting under a heat lamp, and the oil separation was just horrible.

Overall: I might give breakfast a chance, but I'm a tad afraid. We even skipped on desserts bc we weren't impressed with the meal.

Their cold brew coffee is great and so is the breakfast sandwich. The turkey sausage was nice and spicy and the bleu cheese was amazing and really added to the sandwich and it's also a much healthier choice than a bagel at Starbucks next door. It is kind of hidden in a strip mall, but the interior is really cute and modern.

Tashua is the best! I started coming to see her for brow lamination and I am always trying something new! She is so professional and sweet, it always makes my day seeing her! She always answers all my skin care questions! I couldn't recommend anyone else! Also Justin who helps with booking and scheduling is great!! I love seeing both of them!

I've had to bring my dog in several times because allergies are just a persistent menace and compared to the local national chain, I feel like my little family has gotten much more love and attention here than anywhere else. The weekend hours and the quick turnaround for a call back have been very helpful, making this place that much more dependable and overall excellent. 

The only reason there is a missing star on my rating is because of the limited use of the pet care plan/wellness plan. My pooches may not even need the the maximum number of visits but I'm still debating whether that cap is going to be a deal breaker ... the jury is still out on that one, but I definitely recommend this place!
Staff is super friendly and the food is amazing. You can tell everything is made fresh and I love that they have vegan options.

This restaurant gave my friends and I a HORRIBLE time! We walked in and the staff automatically took up straight upstairs, to the back corner, away from any and everyone else that could dine in. We ordered our food, and waited. The service was okay, the food had no seasoning in it, and when I received my food I had over 5 gnats in my dish! A few of my friends found gnats in there dishes as well. The way the manager was talking to my friends and me felt honestly anti-black. I was overly disgusted and honestly horrified. If you asked me for a recommendation, I'd give a 0 out of 10, would NEVER recommend!

Bohnke has a 200% mark up on all her procedures including routine and preventative work. Your money is better spent elsewhere. She takes advantage of her clients and isn't in the veterinary field because she cares. She's in it for the money.

clean, fast and big bowl of pho for a reasonable price. crunchy onions, some scallions, throw in bean sprouts and mint leaves, beef ready - the only way to go is here. if you want pho in philly, this place will serve you right. a favorite when i'm in philadelphia.

Just had a terrible experience I feel I need to share:
I got an egg white burrito to go. Burrito was wrapped in super flimsy piece of deli paper. When I opened the burrito it was super soggy, the tortilla was that wet-slimey way they get when there is too much juice. The deli paper was sticking to the whole outside of the tortilla. I finally got some off to take a bite. First bite was good (despite sogginess). Second bite sent an EXPLOSION of juices out of the back end. Luckily I was eating over the tiny paper bag they gave me. I could see how giant the puddle was. There was juices all over the table, my skirt, and hands, which leads me to my next complaint: NO NAPKINS.

I threw out 3/4 of a $10.50 burrito because It was a giant pile of mucky mess.
I'm still hungry.

My friend brought me here when I went down to Philly to visit him. I've had Pho in NY and NJ. Comparing them to this place, Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai is okay. My friend and I ordered beef pho and spring rolls for appetizers. Both were good. Nothing special. It is a big bowl of pho at a very good (cheap) price. So I cannot complain.
Went back again and again found the food very good and very consistent. If you're into vegan food you'll definitely like this place.
The best pho in Chinatown. The extra large bowl is huge, and so affordable. This will be my new go to pho.

Came here around 930pm (they closed at 10pm) on a Thursday. My friend and I were seated right away. We ordered and the food was out within what seemed like a few minutes.

The three dishes we got were very good (comparing it to homemade Vietnamese cooking as well as Boston's Vietnamese restaurant scene).  We got phó tai bo vien, bun dac biet, and banh cuon cha lua. 

Would come back again.

Put in a pick up order here that was supposed to be ready in 15 minutes and ready at 12:04 PM. At 12:57 PM it's finally ready.

I'm so irritated because my brother has been sitting in the store waiting and we chose this option because it was "fast".

I also ordered delivery here 2 days ago and my instructions weren't followed. Major slip in quality lately. The owner should show up and help his struggling team. One cashier and one cook doesn't cut it during the lunch rush sadly. 

Will start making scrambled eggs at home I guess and break out my vitamix.  ‍

I came here with my wife for lunch and had a very pleasant time, Chevy was amazing, he knew when to approach us to ask if we needed anything, he explained some of the dishes and he was on point even when the restaurant was slammed, I had their Zuppa Toscana which was absolutely delicious as always and my wife had their salad. For our main courses my wife had their create your pasta option with linguini pasta, mushroom cream and grilled chicken as the protein and she loved it. I had their chicken cheese piadina and it came with a pasta salad and it was really good and filling and again Chevy's service was great. Oh and yeah the restaurant was clean and in great conditions. I'll be looking forward for our next time eating at this restaurant.

I am no Pho aficionado - in fact, this was only my 3rd experience with the soupy, noodley concoction... but I am fairly certain I will not find anything quite like this anywhere else. 

The broth - oh my. So amazing! The noodles - plentiful and delicious. The service was very, very good.

No, it's not fancy. I don't go out to eat for fancy all the time. You can't beat a quality meal at an affordable price; and one where you don't have to make it yourself. Let's be honest. The quality of food is far more important than the ambiance. And, I would patronize this place even if I had to sit in a cardboard box to do it.

Before you go in, look for the choo choo train neon sign. That's the reason why the locals call this place the choo choo pho place. It's worthwhile to visit this place at least once.

One of my to-go pho spots in Chinatown. The broth is a bit sweeter than other places. They name their bowls large and extra-large, so it feels like you're getting a bargain - and you are.

The staff members are always friendly. The food comes out just as you expect the food to out.

I hadn't been to this location in a long while and it really has gone down hill. I swung in at 6 pm to grab something quick and easy for supper. The parking lot had trash strewn around everywhere and was full but inside was almost empty. I ordered my food and went to pay. My salad came out right away but the cheese quesadilla wasn't ready for sometime later bc they did all the food out of order. 
There were 3 men behind the food station and I watched them make 7 orders never changing their gloves. As they attempted to make my cheese quesadilla one of them kept reaching over and grabbing burgers out of the container and grease and juice kept falling right in my food. It was so disgusting and unsanitary I just left before my food was ordered. I will not return.

Thank GOODNESS we have Goodness Fresh Food and Juice Bar here in Tucson, AZ.

As a person that attempts at being healthy her fair share of the time, I find our options in Tucson are extremely limited. The few healthy options we seem to have are either underwhelming, lacking in flavor, or in super inconvenient locations. Goodness is absolutely NONE of these, and checks off all the necessary boxes.

Goodness is regularly changing up their menu and keeping it interesting, while maintaining a consistently delicious standard. The atmosphere is casual, but aesthetically pleasing (AKA SUPER CUTE), and the staff is always helpful.

I am a big fan of the Turkey Pesto sandwich, especially when toasted, and the BF loves the Azteca bowl (adds steak). We always mean to try new menu items, but we love these options so much, we always keep coming back for the same thing! I can't wait to try more options!

My only suggestion would be if they had an easy online ordering system to order, pick up, and have it ready when you arrive (OR PLEASE BE ON ONE OF THE FOOD DELIVERY SERVICES)! 

You really can't go wrong with eating here, as your body will thank you for it, and you will be craving it afterwards! Enjoy!

I learned I am the sign of a horse. 

Horses must be allowed to show their emotions. They are hotblooded, hot-tempered, and impatient,and they will gladly demonstrate. In love, Horses are quite vulnerable. They give up everything for the object of their affections. This causes them trouble since they are such impulsive creatures! They must learn to use caution. If one has a Horse in their house, you can bet the Horse receives most of the attention. Horses like being the hub and have everything revolving about them. In return, they work hard and share with everyone.

My mate should be a tiger! 

That's what I learned cause I was waiting so long to be waited on.  Seriously we waited a good 15 minutes before we were about to walk out and someone finally came over.  

Hmmm now what did I have the chicken or pork? Funny I couldn't tell the difference because when I tasted my friends plate it tasted the same.

Lobster Poutine - wear loose pants, order this, and thank me later. 

But in all seriousness, everything I have ordered from here on three different occasions has been stellar. I also love that they give a small discount to people who live at the Franklin Residence (balling hard is a lifestyle, but i appreciate a little discount like the rest of y'all).

This place was delicious and the food was ready quick which is great if you're in a rush. I ordered the clean it up juice and the Mediterranean bowl with tofu while my mom ordered the avocado toast and a black tea. Both dishes were flavorful and the juice and tea were very refreshing. The service was fast a friendly. I would definitely recommend this place to others and would come back again in the future to try some of their other food dishes and juices.

After months of deliberation, my partner-in-dine and I finally made it to the doorstep of Classic Spaghetti Western Steakhouse. We made a reservation on Open Table for New Year's day dinner. There weren't that many patrons when we got there at 5:30 pm. We chose to sit in a booth instead of at a table. The restaurant had a cozy ambiance with piped-in Spaghetti Western movie tunes to set the mood. The only thing I didn't like about the interior was that it was too dark where we were sitting. 

Our server was friendly but he was not very attentive or efficient. He was MIA most of the time. 

My partner-in-dine and I both ordered the same thing -- the 16-oz. ribeye steak with spaghetti...and two meatballs! It was a moment of insanity when we dared to order it, an hour-long fervent attempt to finish everything, and a lifetime memory of delirious and superhuman feasting. 

The ribeye was cooked to medium-rare perfection. It was succulent and soul-taming. The spaghetti tasted excellent. Our order also came with broccoli and cheese sauce.

Overall, we were very impressed with the food. We will be back, but not in the immediate future. It's not the fault of the restaurant at all. We just have to abstain from overindulgence of the gastronomic kind.

With a nice weekend trip to Philly, I was honestly craving for some Pho. While strolling down through Chintown, Pho Xe Lua peaked my interest. Being originally from California, I've definitely had some pho during my time so I'm coming in here with some expectations. Just walking in and doing a quick glance through, this place definitely looked like a legit pho restaurant. From the plastic utensils, the cheap tables, and authentic smell, these were green flags, and I was ready to go!

Now the prices here are pretty legit too. $5.95 for a regular bowl, and $6.95 for a truly large bowl. I mean, that bowl is gigantic, so if you're really really hungry, then opt for the large. I went ahead and ordered the usual #1 combination bowl of pho with all your typical fixings like tripe, brisket, tendon, etc. Now when my pho came and I took a sip of the broth, I was sadly underwhelmed. The broth was decent, but it didn't have a blast of flavor that I was expecting. To be honest, it was even a little on the bland side. To compound that, it was a little lukewarm, which isn't always the best with soup. As far as the toppings are concerned, they were all there, but there was like 1-2 pieces of each ingredient. I kind of expected there to be more meat, but I guess that comes with the large bowl? The noodles were spot on though. Nice and chewy and cooked to perfection. But even so, that's not enough to save the total package.

Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai, your name is so legit for a pho restaurant, but the pho is actually a little underwhelming. Perhaps you had an off day, or perhaps you just really like serving underwhelming pho. At least your prices are legit enough that I can't stay mad at you forever.

Wow!! I miss Wendy, this place has gone downhill!! Since she sold it. No One answers the phone.  Gone there twice at 11:00 
still closed. The last time the guy working was rude. Told me wasn't ready, had to wait.  It was after 11:00. So today gave them one more try. The chocolate yogurt was horrible. Doesn't even have a taste of chocolate.  Will not go they anymore.

The place have good prices and the food is very good. There is available parking and the service is good. The restaurant looks dirty and finishes are terrible. Pizza is great and so cheap, about $7 per personal pizza enough for 2. Fried rice is loaded for about $15 and vaca frita is great at about $13. Go check it out but do not expect a fancy dinner experience.

This is hands down one of the best pho we've had! We were visiting from New York and craving pho- the 106 pho was absolutely amazing and so filling. The broth was delicious and there was sooo much food in the large (they only do large or extra large). The summer shrimp rolls with peanut sauce were good. 

I left very satisfied and very full! The price was also very good!

First visit to this restaurant. Despite the western name of the place the interior is mostly finished in modern style,although the walls to feature paintings of famous western movie stars. Full service bar on site made a nice margarita, a decent sized wine menu is available. The menu does indeed present with a size able number of classic Italian American entrees and a decent amount of choices of steaks with appropriate sides. 

The calamari appetizer came of piping hot and tender. The spinach and basil manicotti I had was tasty, my wife's steak was properly cooked to her desired wellness, very tender and properly seasoned. All in all we enjoyed everything.

This place was easily affordable when I was a jobless high school student living on allowance. Yup. It's that cheap.

It was also always tasty, and quick.

My recommendations:

- Try the coconut or the lemongrass snails. They're very tasty, and have the texture of very tender (but not chewy) young squid.

- Get an extra large bowl of pho to split between 2 people. It's huge.

- Carpaccio! Served with lots of fresh basil, toasted garlic and onions, peanuts, and lime wedges to squeeze over the top.

- Nem nuong, Vietnamese grilled pork meatballs - not as good as Vietnam Palace's, but good enough to get.

- People love their "milkshakes" here. They're really just fruit smoothies, but they ARE tasty.

If you get every item I just mentioned, you fed four people for about 30 bucks, not including tip. Score!

Pro-tip: I don't really go here for atmosphere, but the place is an old standby that will always be an option for me. Start your night here with a starchy, meaty dinner, and then go drink yourself silly.

EDIT
I downgraded this to a 3 star because I can't put it on the same level as my actual favorite Vietnamese restaurant.

This is the best Pho I've had in Philly. Amazing broth, noodles were good and I like how the onions dissolve, rather than being stringy and getting stuck in my teeth. 

We got take out, so I haven't sat down here in probably ten years, but the broth stayed hot all the way home (15 min drive), so the take out is good.

Climb aboard the Phooooo Train! With the Pho train you pretty much get what you pay for. The Pho definitely isn't the best that you'll find. But it's inexpensive enough to make it just above sub par. and you can't go wrong with the fact that it hooks up cheap drinks with frilly umbrellas (or can you?).

It does dish out an interesting assortment of milkshakes (jackfruit!). And it hooks up a great assortment of soups and pad Thai's. But there are just factors like service, and consistent quality that makes it just fall short of being one of the the better Pho institutions of Philly.

I had the best lunch yesterday with my 1 year old daughter. Not so much because the food was spectacular, but because our server and service were! We decided to dine at Olive Garden because they had their famous endless soup, salad & breadsticks promotion going on. Can you believe you can get all of those items (unlimited amount) for $7.99!!?? 
Our server was Morgan H (redhead) and she was so sweet! Very prompt with service and bringing our bowls of soup and salad. I never had to wait too long for a refill. I tried 3 out of the 4 soups they serve. My favorites were the creamy based soups (zuppa Tuscany and their gnocchi and chicken). Olive Garden is a chain restaurant so I don't expect a home made taste to their food but the soup actually tasted like someone made it and not like it was popped out of a can. I did have to add a little salt & pepper for seasoning but other than that I really enjoyed their selections. 
Can we talk about how good their salad dressing is? Hands down my favorite dressing. My only complaint about their salad is I would prefer it with romaine lettuce instead of iceberg lettuce but the toppings and salad dressing make up for it. Of course I haven't forgotten to mention their breadsticks! Hot and fresh right out of the oven - what else could you ask for to go well with your hot bowl of soup!

I absolutely love this place! The atmosphere outside is just so cute and welcoming! I feel relaxed out there, and they have such great food options. They have a variety of healthy choices for people with all kinds of different taste buds. Great!

I am being generous with 3 stars. This place has the potential to be 5. I will come back again and hopefully they have the kinks worked out!

We ordered a TMB sandwich and a Kale Citrus salad to share. The sandwich came out first and the salad arrived 10 minutes later (and after other orders came out). 

The food quality is good and fresh but the service and speediness needs improvement.

I have and will always be a fan of soho juice co! They're açaí bowls and juices are the best in Tampa (at least I think so!). Recently tried their CBD infused cinnamon bun and it was delicious! It's DF, GF, soy free, basically free of it all. The only reason why I didn't give it 5 stars is because of the cost. In my opinion, even with it being CBD infused, it was overpriced.

Once getting there the line was outside the door. We went to the bar and waited 10 minutes to get menus. Staff stood around doing nothing. Tables were left uncleaned for 30 minutes at least.The salad was okay but my spaghetti was undercooked and plain with almost no marinara sauce with some exceptional meatballs. Service was terrible. Not coming here again. At least the mints were good.

I went to Cimarron Animal Hospitial because they allow pet parents to go into the exam room. My Dachshund needed most, if not all, of  his teeth extracted. Dr, Bohnke called me while my dog was under anesthesia and said it would cost $1800 for everything which I agreed to. My dog has had extractions before and I was less concerned about the bill than my dog's welfare. After the extractions, they handed me my dog, Patrick, in the parking lot and I did not notice he was in distress because he was still anesthetized. He bled and whimpered all night and his mouth was very swollen. I called and brought him in again the next morning and he saw another vet. They had to use laser to close the wound. Another $200. The bill for the surgical procedure was not available yet and they could not tell me how many teeth were extracted. At his follow-up visit the next week, they would not allow me into the exam room and told they would have to look at his mouth in the waiting room. The support staff was great but both doctors were awful.

A struggle between three stars and four stars because while very fresh and delicious, it's just simply not affordable. I know you get what you pay for, so I can't really fault them on that but every time I come here I wind up spending between $20-$40 for two people. My breakfast this time which consisted of a plant-based burrito and potatoes cost $20. The burrito was small but full of trending ingredients like JustEgg, whole wheat tortilla and quinoa. I call this the kitchen sink dilemma where a place throws too much into one item. I wish there was a "base" burrito for a cheaper price and if you wanted all the fancy ingredients you could add to it.  Vegan breakfast options are limited in Tucson and they're on the right tract, just not quit there yet. I was say the potatoes were DELICIOUS. I will happily make a breakfast of just them.

Goodness is incredible.  The Thai chicken quinoa bowl, and "the goods" smoothie are a treat for me and are my go to favorites.  There is so much flavor in the food and the freshness is unmatched. 

I am thrilled to find a progressive place like this in Tucson.  The only reason I didn't give it five stars was because of space!  There's not enough, which is a testament to how wonderful goodness is!!!!  At lunchtime it's slammed and the parking is awful.  

Keep it up guys, I hope this place stays open!

Located on a busy corner off Chestnut, sits Sandler's. My friends and I decided to come for lunch on a weekday and was met with subpar service and petite portion plates. Our hostess sat us quickly, but our waitress was quick to disappear throughout our dining experience. I would understand if the restaurant was busier, but to have to ask for takeout containers 3 separate times with 3 different employees working the floor is pretty inexcusable. The food itself was also underwhelming. The gimmick of putting the sandwich on a stick to dunk into the soup was unique but failed to save the dish. The portion was tiny and my friend had to get another dish. The avocado toast was also tiny and the bread was soggy. My girlfriend also asked them to fry the egg so it was not runny, but they failed to do that. I ended up getting the lobster fries, and while it was a heaping plate, the fries were completely soaked. The front house and the kitchen were both disappointments, and we won't be back.

I'm only giving this Olive Garden a 3 star rating for the following reasons ....
We asked to sit in a booth at the bar which we usually do on any other day , only 2 booth's were taken , 3 were available and no one was at the bar , however we were told no so we proceeded to the main dining room where at least 25 people were all crammed into one corner of the restaurant while the rest of the restaurant was open and there was no one sitting anywhere except crammed into this tiny corner so we asked can we sit over on the other side with less people and we were told no. My only issue is the restaurant thinks it's ok to stack people on top of one another and yes people are coughing, blowing noses, etc .. also the restaurant allowed the 2 people in the bar to bring in a dog in a stroller, not a service animal, a person who just wanted to bring their dog in to eat. I have no complaints with the food or the waitress but I do have a problem with how they are seating, especially when the staff is walking around with masks on do to Covid, it's apparently ok to stack 25 people on top of one another and allow a pet in the restaurant but you absolutely will not be allowed to sit anywhere that gives you a little distance. I also understand businesses are understaffed and I appreciate all the hard working people and like I said I have no issues with food or the waitress only the situation with seating.

I have to bump you back up to four stars, Choo Choo. 

It's criminal that I took a star away from you because I felt like you couldn't compete with my favorite Viet spot in Philly. Really, I shouldn't have been comparing you two in the first place. Because even though you have similar menus, you offer completely different things, and you are greater than the sum of your parts.

Also, even though you're not quite as pretty, every time I try a new ramen joint in this town, I find myself thinking about how much I'd rather be with you.

Stay cool, Choo Choo.

Hello there awesome new PHO spot.

Clearly, I am in a full blown exploration of the great city of brotherly love. So far the food has been good but this place just made my experience in this city that much better.
My co-worker and I were craving some delicious pho and had no idea where to go. But, when in doubt Yelp! 

Being that this spot is located in the heart of Chinatown, we knew we were in for a treat. When we first walked in, a gentlemen behind the counter greeted us. He was extremely friendly! Asked us where we're from, what we enjoyed to eat, and made suggestions. All while we waited for a table.
While we were waiting, we noticed their extremely large menu and the fact that it was PACKED! 
Granted we came during lunch time, but there was no empty seat in the house.

I stuck with my basic chicken pho (I know who gets that and not beef but don't judge me) and it was so deliciously yummy. I get scared/worried trying new Asian spots and I def will be sticking to this spot for my pho. My coworkers got bun which they raved about! 

All in all great spot. There is no going wrong with cheap good food.

iCandy is what can go wrong with a bar that has too many ideas - especially if those ideas are already being executed better at the bars they're trying to copy.

There's the "Tavern," which copies the name and vibe of Tavern on Camac to weaker results. There's the sports bar, which runs a distant third to Tabu and Westbury (mostly because those are real sports bars). There's brunch, which is miles behind Knock. And then there's the dancefloor, which charges the same amount as Woody's, has half the people, and charged me three different prices for the same drink - this all happened at the SAME bar.

What's hilarious is that every time they post an event, they feel the need to try to say something snarky about the "other bars" in the neighborhood. There's no need to trash someone else if you're able to bring it. Clearly, they haven't gotten the memo that it's not cool to take a swing at someone else every time you have an event.

There are a few things going for it if they can get it right - they have the deck that is the one thing they haven't copied, and a couple of good staff (mainly Charlotte, god bless the lesbians) among all the others who have no idea how to make anything that doesn't list the ingredients in the name. Good luck trying to get a good margarita. 

Maybe there is hope for them if they can just be themselves instead of trying to rip off ideas from everyone else.

After reading all the reviews and hearing such great things about this restaurant I was excited to give it a try. 

There was 5 of us in the party and we decided to go on a Sunday night. We didn't have reservations since it was about 7:30 and we felt that it wouldn't be busy. 

When we arrived there were 2 large parties and a few other tables seated around the restaurant. We waited a few minutes and I didn't see a single person who worked there. I finally saw someone and they were running food to a table. No one even acknowledged we were there. I walked around the restaurant and still nothing. After about 10 minutes someone comes up to the front and they walk right past us to another group that had come in about 5 to 10 minutes after us and they get seated.

I was pretty upset I didn't say anything since we had been waiting for a total of 16 minutes without someone saying a word to us. We ended up just leaving and going to a restaurant down the street that was able to seat us right away. 

I don't know if I plan to go ever again since there was not a single person who ever acknowledged we were even there.

This LOCALLY OWNED establishment has been a staple in my life for many years and frankly, I could not live without it!  Ok, so maybe I'm being a bit melodramatic, but my day ends with goodies from Sundaze.  Not only do I enjoy having a treat there, where the place is clean, the staff  professional and the atmosphere friendly, but I often take quarts/pints home to enjoy there as well.  I like that the owners have been in business for over 10 years, and especially that they are members of my community.  

You owe it to yourself to try Sundaze!  Whether you prefer a shake, a sundae, sugar free or fat free yogurt, you will find what you are looking for!  The selection of toppings is amazing, too!

Don't shop at a chain, "make-your-own" yogurt place!  Get the friendly personal attention from someone who lives in your town!  

Gotta go-I'm picking up Angel Food Cake and Chocolate Peanut Butter-YUM!

A friend of mine claimed that Xe Lua was the best pho in Chinatown, and my first bite was enough to win me over as well.

Moving to Philly from Seattle, pho was the one food I found myself craving over and over again. After eating here, I mentally made this my go-to restaurant. Clean restaurant, fast service, plenty of seating, hot and flavorful broth, big portion sizes, there is nothing Xe Lua falls short on.

This place is the best pho place I've been to here in Philly, and I strongly think that it'll continue to be for a long time! If you are craving pho and you're in the area, drop by for a quick bowl and you won't regret it!

I was staying with my brother in Chinatown and was craving some "bun bo hue". I did a search on yelp and this was the closes place and seeing the four stars, I was stoked! I didn't want to eat there so I called and ordered it to go. I should have hung up realizing this place was not legit when they didn't know what "bun bo hue" was from me speaking it. Despite my better judgment I went to pick it up and it was gross. There was no lemongrass smell to it (the foundation to this soup) at all. It seems like they used the pho broth and just poured it over a different kind of vermicelli and called it "bun bo hue".

We were craving Vietnamese for lunch and we decided to give this place a try. I ordered the Hu Tieu Mi Sate Bo Kho (rice noodle beef stew) it was OK. The beef itself was tender and good, however the sauce and overall flavor of the dish was alright, I was not a fan and I've had this dish before at other establishments. My BF ordered pho- the broth was very tasty even without any sauce. We both ordered Vietnamese iced coffee (I like mine very strong and flavorful), unfortunately here it was watery and lacked flavor- I did not even finish mine. The service was pretty quick however, they initially only brought out my coffee so we had to ask for another (despite having ordered two); additionally, my BF ordered an XL pho which turned out to just be a large (I realized this upon seeing bigger pho bowls as we were leaving).
Maybe ordering the wrong dish gave me a bad first impression, but if I were to ever return, I would only order pho.

Very friendly staff, nice environment with healthy, tasty food & beverage options.

Have been in a few times before, the breakfast burrito is great. I really liked the bite of salmon toast that I stole from my roommate. 

This time I came in for something light and the Acai Bowl was delicious. 

The Turmeric Shot was still Turmeric but I don't know who drinks that for the flavor anyways 

Fun spot, would recommend! 

I guess, I am currently recommending  :)

While strolling through Philly I found this place along my walk.  I came in on a Sunday and was able to enjoy the brunch.  I ordered the salmon burger and a French onion soup.  The French onion soup was very filling and not too cheesy.  I sat at the bar and the waiter was very attentive and had a great personality.  He made light jokes and helpful drink suggestions.  I got a raspberry mimosa to pair with my meal... what's brunch without a mimosa?

Fresh, clean food. Fresh, clean atmosphere. I love that the juices aren't sugared/ overly-fruited. My breakfast burrito this morning was awesome (the only thing I can think of to suggest is to maybe season the quinoa... a little cumin might go a long way). My boyfriend's breakfast sandwich was super good too, and our juices were such a great way to start the day. I love that everything is just simple and very well done. 
I will be back often.

Came here with a friend and we had burgers and split an app. I got the korean pork burger. Just FYI, the meat is on TOP of the burger so it's meat overload which is just my kind of burger. If you're looking for portions that are HUGE and prices that are great, this is a great place. Also split a bacon and brusselsprouts app. The brusselsprouts could have had slightly more flavor (felt a little bland even with the bacon), but texture was nice and roasted. Definitely would return to try their other stuff. Their brunch/breakfast menu looks great too.

Just visited and was impressed by how they got rid of their "to go containers" and upped their portion sizes. Prices still have not changed but I'm happy to pay if I  feel my $'s match what I'm getting as far as portion and my experience is concerned. Will definitely be coming back again. I was really impressed by how full I felt after my meal here and again I am extremely happy that they got rid of their dine in to-go containers which didn't make any sense to me. I'm still a little apprehensive of getting a sandwich though as my experience with those have been tainted in the past, but I can definitely feel good about ordering a bowl or a smoothie.

This place gets quite busy and makes finding a parking spot and navigating the parking lot very difficult. Staff is pleasant and helpful. Drinks are usually stocked well. The biggest draw back is it seems this locations menu for food options is quite limited. For example you can't get a hash brown in your breakfast burrito or even veggies. Only meat options.

This restaurant has only been open about 6 weeks. It has kind of a small parking lot. The location is in a good spot, and should get a lot of traffic. 

My husband and I went here tonight on date night, and we weren't real sure what to expect. We walked in the door and were greeted by a very nice hostess. She interacted with us as if we were old friends and that it wasn't just her job.  We only had to wait maybe a minute or two before our waiter promptly approached our table. Our waiter tonight was Colin, he was friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. 

The food -- the food was amazing. I ordered the spaghetti and meatballs and my husband had the New York strip with the loaded baked potato and cream of spinach. All of it had a wonderful flavoring to it. The steak melted in your mouth and was just amazing. My husband raved about his loaded baked potato. And I am usually skeptical about ordering spaghetti anywhere, I went ahead and took the leap to try it. I'm so glad that I did, it had a great flavor to it and was just delicious.

I had questioned about the meatballs as I had noticed some red in them and thought maybe they weren't cooked all the way through. Well I had just made it as a comment to the waiter he insisted on taking it back to show the chef, I really wasn't asking for that to happen. I had planned on just eating the spaghetti and not the meatballs. Colin went ahead and took the plate back to the chef after a couple minutes he returned with my plate. I was mistaken, it seems there were four or five meets combined in the very large meatballs. The red I was seeing was the pork that was used. I was a little embarrassed but relieved. My spaghetti and meatball dinner was to die for.

My overall opinion of this restaurant is that you must go and try it out. The wait staff and the hostess staff we're super nice and me the experience One in which I would want to return for. I can't say enough good things about the food, as I don't think there's enough adjectives haha. Also to top off your meal I would recommend the desert they have called the Pope's pillow. It was wonderful. My husband and I both agree that we will be returning back here again.

My friend and I stumbled upon Sandler's tonight for dinner totally accidentally after we found out the restaurant we originally intended to go to was closed due to renovations. The menu looked very good (American), so we ended up stopping in! 

I really liked the sound of all the cocktails they had on their drink menu, which were also reasonably priced ($8.34!). I picked the key west martini and it actually tasted like key lime pie! My friend ordered the citrus martini. 

I then ordered the chicken BLTA and my friend ordered the steak frites. My chicken BLTA was just fine. It was really dry and very under-seasoned, but I loved how there was avocado on it! If they could season the chicken better or add some type of sauce to the sandwich it'd be much better. But as it stands now, I'd definitely not order it again. 

My friend's steak frites looked really good! I tried the fries and they were very good, so I'd recommend that dish over the chicken sandwich. But overall, the menu has a lot of varieties of food to offer, so I'll probably be back. I also want to try breakfast. The sign outside says they serve breakfast all day, but I'm not sure if that's true.

I'm a HUGE fan of Sandler's and actually have this on my list of recommendations for those travelling to the city or locals looking for a good place to eat. 

Sandler's on 9th is a pretty big restaurant with a lot of seating. It's great for bigger dinner parties. I like how bright and welcoming it is inside. The large windows along the walls provide a lot of lighting. 

The menu is pretty extensive and has a lot of breakfast and all day options to choose from. 

The owner's daughter and staff were super friendly and gave me a great first impression. It was really nice getting to know the owner's daughter and hearing about the products they serve. The owner's daughter was helpful in deciding what I should eat. I got several plates. A mix of breakfast and dinner foods. I can honestly say, everything was outstanding and made with such care. The food was cooked perfectly and the presentation of the dishes pulled everything together. I was able to even overhear other tables around me and they were also really enjoying their food. I like that you can go here for brunch, lunch, or dinner, and if you go late at night, they still have breakfast dishes available to choose from. Again, I love this place and I'm really looking forward to coming back soon!

TGIF... Time to splurge on lunch.. Tastebuds had a hankering for some Pho.
Called in my order and it was pipping hot when I arrived to pick it up. I couldn't wait to eat. The cashier (whom may have been a manager) advised that he could add shrimp to the Pho in the future or modify any other dishes that I'd like to order

Arrived back at my office and couldn't wait to dig in and enjoy this relatively new favorite of mine, Pho Ga with shredded chicken.  Seasoned to perfection broth and side styrofoam container of bean sprouts, rice noodles, shredded chicken, jalapeno peppers, cilantro, scallions and lime. Purely deliciously. How could I possiblly eat this whole thing, I have no idea how I did it but I did.

Well seasoned broth which complimented the noodles authentically. The fresh lime and jalapenos just gave the Pho dish the added joy my stomach applauded.

Again soon Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai, I will be back.

I select no star rating but to post i had to select a star.

When I first entered this place i thought okay. Music is alright.

The bathrooms were dirty paper towels everywhere. It smelled like urine that has been sitting there for a long time. I noticed the entrance to the kitchen was right next to the bathroom. First thing i thought was, no way am i ordering food here. If the bathrooms are dirty and door handles are not cleaned what awaits in the kitchen. 

They serve the beer very nicely dresses up in a napkin. That is a nice touch.

I am scared to eat at this restaurant even if they clean up.  First impression is everything.  How clean are you?

I had a Thai peanut bowl with chicken for dinner here yesterday. It was good and quite filling. My friend's banh mi was also tasty. The bowl cost $10 plus a dollar service charge. All in all, I was satisfied with the food and the experience.

We ordered the BBQ pork and lemongrass chicken on rice as well as the Black pepper pork. The first dish was okay, there was barely any lemongrass flavor and it was quite salty. But the second dish was truly disgusting. As soon as I opened the box it smelled of dead rats (insert puke emoji). I thought I could eat it without inhaling but couldn't do it. It was pretty much the most disgusting smelling dish I have ever tasted in my life! I don't think I'll experiment and only stick to lemongrass chicken or Pho when it comes to Vietnamese food.

As someone who's part Vietnamese, I expected more from this place. My boyfriend and I frequent Pho Cali a lot (a few blocks down) but we decided to branch out to other Vietnamese restaurants for more expansive menu. It's apparent that a lot of people like this place since it's always packed, but I don't see what the hype is imo. The food is mediocre and the staff can be a bit annoying. The two times I've been here, I've always felt like I can't eat my food without feeling like I'm being watched. I prefer Pho Cali over this spot any day. The folks at Pho Cali never leer over us. Go to Pho Cali if you wanna feel like you're eating pho at your aunties house. Go to Pho Xe Lua Viet Thai if you like to follow the hype and be watched while you're eating your food. You can tell we didn't enjoy our experience here since I didn't take any pictures of my meal lol! The best thing about this place is the pho, the pork chop and rice was soooo underwhelming. There was no grill to the pork chop... like come on people, melanin matters!!! I need my jawn charred. Won't be returning here anymore.

I love this place, pho realz.

It's cheap, it's fast, and, most of all, it's delicious. I love this place so much that I used to go by myself after work to have a date with just me and my bowl of pho. Those were good times. And even now it is still a place I frequent with my friends often. 

I've never gotten any food other than pho here, but I've had friends who love the vermicelli bowls just as much as I love menu item 101. When I'm feeling less meaty, I go with 110. But regardless, it's all delicious.

Came here around lunch time.
We had to wait for a while before a waitress realized that we don't have anything: menu, drinks, or water in front of us.
Didn't realize the food would be comfort food rather than brunch.
My meal was carb filled but burger here is to die for!
Poutine was very disappointing... i do not recommend it.

Don't be deterred by the entryway - once inside Pho Xe Lua is a first rate pho spot in Philly's Chinatown. As is indicative of a good Viet spot, the seating area is casual, and the hand painted mural on the longest wall harkens back to rural Vietnam countryside of yesteryear.

The menu is straight forward - and though I failed to see a pho dac biet with everyyyythinggg that I like (tendon, tripe, beef balls), you can certainly add additional items. 

Alright, enough ground work - the broth is AMAZING. Truly exploding with umami, beefy flavor, and just the right amount of warmth from anise and other spices, and the sweetness level of the broth is perfection. Truly: perfection.

Waitstaff is friendly, casual, just right. I cannot wait to return.

Great coffee and friendly staff. I really like their holiday drinks and their bagel sandwiches. The place has a good amount of seating but it's usually busy. They have outdoor seating too. The decor is really cute. If purple is your fav color, this is the place to go.

I've been to goodness a few times now. It's a nice convenient location near work, so we often end up here. This time I had the Greek yogurt. It was pretty tasty and the fruits seemed fresh. Overall pleasant experience, chill environment and good food.

I just made a move from South Philly to Center City. Let me be dramatic for a second here: I feel so far away from the great pho along Washington. 

So boyfriend and I made a visit here to explore the pho options in my new neighborhood, in a vain attempt to fill this noodly hole in my heart. 

We'd heard lots of good things about this 'choo choo train' spot. Sadly, it didn't stack up. While Pho Xe Lua Viet is totally serviceable, it's nowhere close to the better bowls in the city (hat tip to Pho Cyclo and Pho 75.) 

The broth is a little bland, the noodles are gummy and sticky, and the cuts of meat are flavorless, dry, and too large. The springrolls were pretty good though! And it's always nice to be able to order a beer. 

Like I said, not bad, but think I'd rather take the longer walk south for better noodles.

Fantastic place! Staff could not be friendlier or more attentive. Ordered an appetizer and entree and thought I could finish it all in one setting!  I was wrong - the leftovers made a perfect late night meal. 

Had the beef in grape leaves for the app and don't recall the formal name of the entree but it was shrimp, pork meatballs, and BBQ pork with vermicelli.  Perfectly fresh and flavorful.  Now when I visit Chinatown again I won't have to wander aimlessly for what I'm looking for - I'll be making a beeline straight for here.

This has been my favorite pho place since my college days (10+ years ago). As a Philly area local, I've been around looking for noodle hotspots and to this day, this is still the default pho restaurant I take everyone to who's from out of town!

I've tried every pho bowl at least once, and really enjoyed medium rare steak. Well done steak is really chewy which I'm not keen on. I personally love tripe and flank, but if you enjoy tendon, you have that option too. And if you want more than 3 toppings, you can add more for an extra cost.

There is a $15 minimum for credit card, so bring cash if you're splitting the bill with a friend or know you'll be spending less.

Its my first time at Choo choo's, the resturant's popular nickname. When walking in, it's easy to suddenly feel just a bit overwhelmed: the smell of clearly Vietnamese cooking hits you and the sound of bustling customers are present. The bar is a bit over decorated but the dining area is simplistic and well designed. You're immediately seated and there's always space despite being popular.

The place is definitely popular, and the establishment is very legitimate in what they advertise themselves as: a Vietnamese and Thai resturant. (Though its mostly the Vietnamese part that I pay attention to.) The condiments are all there (best sign!), the prices are reasonable, and the food is done with clearly family recipes that one would definitely find in a Vietnamese home. The atmosphere is great, the decorations a bit tacky but tasteful. The music that they play is usually Asian, mostly Vietnamese and I had to smile at their selections because they were popular songs that my family listens to whenever we all get together to have a feast. The menu is in Northern Vietnamese but the dishes taste just a bit Southern. (This is a good thing, guys.)

I had gotten a rice dish, number 204: rice with BBQ pork, shredded pork, and steamed egg that had its usual lettuce, cucumber, carrot and radish side dish that would be present. While it reigned true to Vietnamese cooking (and trust me I was quite impressed that my date had picked out a place that reminded me of Vietnam so clearly), it was averagely sub par at most. It was good though, don't get me wrong. It's mostly personal preference and a bias of my grandmother's cooking, I'd suppose. Lettuce was a bit too hard, the nuoc mam is a bit sweet but not overly spicy (disappointing for me but perfect for people who've never had it before and do not mind a bit bit of sweetness in in their sauces), but the meat well prepared and seasoned properly. I enjoyed tearing through a dish such this that i haven't had in a long time. But I've had better.

The staff is productive, not too friendly but not rude: they come and then they go. Due to how's it usually busy and bustling, they are only there when you need them.  It'd best to to try to to get their attention when you're ready to order, don't sit there waiting.

The complimentary tea is great and well picked although their tea pot isn't well suited for people who aren't used to drinking tea, and at worse,  annoying to tea-drinkers such as myself when trying to pour as it spills when you finish pouring. (Ordering a drink would probably be best. If you're of age, try the bar seeing as I can't give a proper review of that.)

There's not much hassle about payment, you pay for your meal when you're done and leave the blackbook to an employee and then you're out on your way. They clean up once you're out so try not to leave too much of a mess but don't clean it up for them.

I wouldn't mind going back, perhaps to try their pho and see whether they know how to make a good broth or not. But I do recommend trying the place out if you ever need a good Vietnamese comfort or an adventurous mood for Thai, try here if you've got $10-$20 to spend if you're a party of two or more. (Don't forget to tip.)

Second visit here... and the although my sandwich is good.. its not amazing and certainly not worth the heavy $8.00 price tag. Keep in mind that beyond bread is literally right down the street, and they are known for their amazing filling sandwiches. I  am also bothered by the "to go" containers even though each time I have been here I have told them that I wanted to dine in. It seems like the price of the containers are factored into the cost of operation... and we the consumers seem to be paying the price. I also can't help but feel that Goodness's portion sizes are intentionally small here because they are also trying to push the additional sale of a smoothie to fill you up. I dunno, even though the ambiance is great here, the high prices + small portions are going to prevent me from coming back. I literally just finished my sandwich and I have a bad feeling that I am going to go hungry within the hour. Yelper Duy N. said food here is "definitely a healthy snack / small meal" and I think he couldn't be more right!

I got takeout from this place the other day and it left a lot to be desired.  The samosas were fine, but the saag was virtually inedible.  I understand that vegetarian meat is not going to have the exact same consistency as regular meat, but this was not even close.  It was like eating saag with pieces of a sponge.  Plus there were so many onions I could barely bite it without crunching.  Would not go back.

Food is very flavorful, but service is horrible. They are extremely slow, yet extremely sloppy. When I got there, I waited in line, and waited, and waited again. The lady in front of me asked if she was in the right spot to order a salad bc it wasn't going anywhere.

When I ordered, the guy scooped up some lettuce in the bowl and added the topping. Soo meek regarding some of the toppings. :-( Then the girl who put dressing on my salad made a complete mess while mixing it that it came out of the bowl. Then pouring it into the to-go container, she spilled even more. 

My company orders Cosi a lot for lunches and I love all their sandwiches and salads. Flatbread is also extremely delicious. Asian salmon salad is one of my favorites. It has this ginger sesame candy crisp this that just puts it over the top. Mmm!
Great overall experience. The fresh baked pita is delicious and the food tastes homemade by grandma. Lamb was tender, juicy and very flavorful. Portions are generous and service very attentive.

Wow the food is unbelievable. If you know good middle eastern cuisine, you'll love the authentic baba - humus - tabouli - falafel - stuffed grape leaves - shish kebob - fresh oven to table pita bread and your favorite BYOB fabulous! super clean - friendly accommodating atmosphere - pretty decor. It simply doesn't any better then this! Enjoy!!

If I were you, I'd pass on the food truck and opt to go to Greek Lady or Hummus instead. Albeit I've only tried their falafel salad, I was still disappointed at the amount of food and the price. (

Small portions + high price (for a lunch truck) + so-so taste = PASS.

A chichi Sammie shoppe whose idea was developed by a Kiwi violin maker in Italia, who then perfected his bread recipe in Paris--- et voila!!

Why not reviewed more? Very comfortable interior, like the tables, music, clean....take a number, and they will find you at your table. Choose between flatbreads or sandwiches (whose bread is, essentially, the flatbread sliced in half)....

My margherita sandwich utterly fresh. Fragrant basil and light, spongy mozzarella.

Never had a more stale sandwich. This was turkey and Brie 
They used to be so much better when they first opened. Cosi standards everywhere have dropped.

To be honest I just came in for a cinnamon roll and a  coffee but ended up getting the fruit tart, it was excellent.  The atmosphere was chill....oldies (think elvis) playing in the background. The staffing friendly enough but the service seemed a little slow as I watched customers getting their food delivered to their table.  I think if you are in absolutely no hurry this would be a great place to  have a coffee and a pastry. BONUS: I was able to get my fruit pastry and coffee for less than a large drink at Starbucks.

My girlfriend and I found this little gem on Groupon, and boy are we glad we did!  The food is excellent as well as the service.  It is also a BYOB, which we love,  I highly recommend their grilled salmon with feta, and my girlfriend enjoyed their vegeterian platter.

I have been here a few times on my travels to Philadelphia. When I am close by and have a hankering for some Lebanese food this is the place I go. The food and ingredients remind me of other authentic homemade Lebanese cuisine I had before. I am a fan of the chicken shawarma and their fattoush salad when it is prepared well. I highly recommend stopping by this eating establishment, you will not be disappointed.

Oh man, all you can eat Indian food for $8.95??? Awesome.

So, why only 3 stars? Well, I feel like it's my responsibility as a Yelp reviewer to try to set reasonable expectations for my fellow Yelpers. I think that if you go into this place thinking you're going to get a 3 star all-you-can-eat buffet for $8.95, you won't be disappointed.

To echo what others have said said, the food was tasty, but not mind blowing. Make it one of your regular spots - not where you take your new girlfriend to try to impress her with your foody-ness - and you'll be fine.
Awesome little breakfast/lunch spot. This place is special! Great selection of delectables and fun gifts!

On a rainy, lazy night, I decided to disregard the low star review because I REALLY wanted Indian and dint want to have to go far to get it. It was a Monday night, and that meant a lot of the places were closed. So I ordered some chicken tikka masala and some naan. 

This place was not good. I basically had 2 chunks of chicken, about a half breast sized each, so to enjoy i first had to cut up the meat. Chicken tikka is supposed to marinate in the yogurt sauce and absorb the flavors for a while before cooking, so the smaller chunks are likely going to be more flavorful, but instead I had to cut up my two half breasts of chicken before I could start eating. Indian food isn't likely going to have the highest quality meat, but this was unusually tough. The flavor of the sauce was okay, not spicy at all when I did request it spicy, and the reviews about the grease were spot on, there was a layer of grease on top of the sauce. 

Next time, I'll just wait till Tuesday.

The women who work the counter are surly. The gentleman, I believe his name is Bill, is extremely pleasant on the other hand. They are very unhelpful and do not have packing tape - should you need to seal a normal package bring your own.  Classic overpaid government employees. They normally only have one or two stamp selections. Better to order them online if you'd like something specific.

Lots of mixed reviews here. I was extremely skeptical and held off going into this location because of all of the mixed reviews. Until my brother brought me their delicious turkey bacon avocado sandwich for lunch one day in Yuma. I went in to this location yesterday and was blown away. The staff was super nice. The girl saw and helped me right away. It's pretty much a brand new building. The inside is super clean first of all. They have more than one restroom which is becoming harder and harder to find. They also have a REAL FIREPLACE! How awesome is that!? They offer gift wrapped baskets with their delicious baked goods and have a station set up to make them. They have a wall of fresh baked artisan loaves of bread. They have a cold box with juices, pastries and another baked good display case with even more amazing pastries and baked goods! I had their turkey bacon avocado salad with ranch and a soft roll. I made it a combo and got a small cream of broccoli soup and a berry pomegranate tea! Their drink options are amazing! You can get the regular fountain soft drinks like soda, lemonade, water etc or.... They have 3 teas they brew in house. Green tea,  organic black tea and the pomegranate berry that I chose. They are perfect! Unsweetened so grab sugar if you like sweet tea! It was smooth and fresh not bitter and old! They also have a hot drink option with two different kinds of roasts and decaf coffee and a station with half and half or whole milk and sugar. I got a key lime tart for dessert and it was delicious. Super flavorful and creamy filling with a perfect crust! I will definitely be back and plan on making this a regular stop in the winter for my soup, baked goods and hot chocolate, chai tea or coffee. I highly recommend it! Not sure what went wrong for everyone else but I loved it!

Today was my 1st and last trip to Kneaders.  My brother and I both ordered the French Dip and if Jaime o.  thinks this is a good sandwich I don't know what a bad sandwich would be.  It came with parmesan chips and a pickle and cookie.  I won't complain about the cookie but we did not get a pickle and the chips were not parmesan chips and they were stale.  The bread was good but there were 2 little tasteless pieces of meat the grocery story roast beef is much better.  It covered about 1/2 the bread the au jus was cold.  Never again.

The decor is charming. That aside, the food was not that great. Half way through my chicken pesto panini, I thought I had been served the wrong order...no chicken. I peeled the bread apart to find a tiny piece of chicken. The artichoke soup was good. I'll stick to Panera or Beyond Bread...

Jenn is the owner and she is very experienced in hair and also models so she is up to date on looks you may love trying out!  She will tell you if something is not going to go well and she along with all the stylists spend time to council/ chit chat about what's to come of your style.
Todd is actually a calculating mad man on your hair...he takes longer because he cares a lot about your hair, I am sure he likes you just fine but seriously he cares more about your hair. 
Alise is always friendly, she works hard for the salon and her clients = Happy boss! 
Some of the women have been there for a long time and keep busy with regulars from the hood but they always welcome walk ins too and that is the kind of option I need!

visited this morning, went inside to order. I ordered an egg and cheese sandwich (overly greasy and croissant was falling apart) and an iced carmel macchiato (which was then given to me hot instead of iced. the young lady at the register quickly fixed the coffee mistake) but it took 15 min for me to get a sub par egg and cheese sandwich. I had high hopes since the one in phx is amazing. the cinnamon bread is the best. I will give them one more chance here in tucson before my final decision is made.

This is the best food cart on UPenn's campus and the best (most authentic) middle eastern food I have had in Philly. 

EVERYTHING on the menu tastes great. My favorite is the kefta sandwich with everything on it... SOO GOOD. 

I actually eat here almost every day and I get a different thing every day of the week and ALWAYS love it.

I had 2 samosas take out yesterday & it wasn't cooked properly. Potato inside was only half cooked! Samosa looked very dark and the skin of it was so thick. I mean hey the place is call San-samosa.. Their samosa should be perfect at least.
Awesome restaurant. Everything was delicious. Very friendly staff. We ordered the seafood Sayadieh and the Lamb combo. They were both delicious.

I was in a pinch and needed someone to do my hair that day. They got me in quickly. My stylist was Trish. She's amazing. Very friendly. Made the experience like I go there all the time. She even stayed later and rearranged someone to pick up her family to finish doing my hair.
Great food, good prices, speedy service! The sourdough pancakes are absolutely amazing

First time here and couldn't be happier with the restaurant the staff is more than friendly Ghasan was the owner and he made the experience that much better if you're looking for middle eastern cuisine in the city there is no better place

Far too long since my last visit. 

Here it is, the food here is VERY GOOD. It's FRESH, Authentic, and not overpriced.. just right. I  cannot stress enough how good the food is, whether you dine in.. or order your food to-go (which they do). We eat Mediterranean / Middle Eastern food all the time.. Cedar's is top notch in Philadelphia.

The setting is intimate, even romantic for a date.. we also saw a group friends celebrating a birthday. It's a BYOB, and close to other bars in Headhouse if you want to make a night out of it.

I HIGHLY recommend going here now.

The middle eastern food here is really good, but a little on the small side for the price at a food truck: $5-6 for a pita wrap that won't completely fill you up. This is okay, but if you're a fat kid like me you could just as easily go to a Chinese cart and pay $3.50 or $4 for a huge platter or to Tacos Don Memo for a delicious $7 monster burrito that you may not be able to finish. 

That said, the food here IS quite delicious (try chicken kebab with feta in a pita sandwich), relatively healthy, and worth the extra cash once in a while, especially when you're not starving (or if you happen to eat like a bird/be on a diet).

I work Close to this new restaurant so I was happy to have a change of some place to eat unfortunately I won't be going back I had the French dip sandwich nice big piece of bread one thin sliced beef that was overcooked and dried up too bad it would be nice to have some great restaurants close by this just isn't one of them

Well meters has a great name is a beautifully clean facility looks more like an gift shop with a couple of pastries. I'll bet their lunches are better than their breakfast because we had to leave ours on the table and exit. It's not impressive and we found it to be unimpressive. It's been awhile since I've had to do that to a place but somebody had to be the winner at the bottom of the list. I suggest the lunch maybe better breakfast forget it

This place deserves ZERO stars.  I just moved to the area and I have been trying to get them to deliver my 2 day express delivery for over a week.  They "left" a notice and then LOST my package.  When they finally recovered it a week later they said they would re-deliver because since my license is not my new address I am not allowed to pick it up.  Then then re-delivered it at 4:30 and "left" another notice.  I did not receive a notice either time.  I am beyond frustrated.  I am NEVER sending a package to my house again.  I have yet to receive my package and I cannot argue another day with Aisha the employee who answers my phone calls.

My first time here, not impressed.  After being greeted by the surly register lady we went to get coffee only to find all three urns empty.  I reported this to said surly register lady, who was not too worried about it.  An employee finally came to replace the coffee and literally stepped in front of me to fill his coffee up before me ... seriously!?!  The "omelet" was dry and had the consistency of scrambled pancakes, which was better than the burnt toast.  Sitting back watching the interactions of the employees and customers makes me wonder why none ... literally none ... of the employees are smiling.  Well, the guy who got his coffee filled up was pretty happy.  At least he enjoys his job!  Don't bother folks!!

I came into Tucson from so cal and I needed vape juice and I found this spot. Super friendly staff and very knowledgeable! And their juices are out of control and made to order! That's a first to me and I thought it was really cool. But I definitely recommend this spot for any of your vaping needs especially if you want to try a lot of good juices!

Disappointing!  That's the best word I can use to describe what has become of Charleys.  I took my wife there for a a nice dinner, my wife is allergic to gluten and didn't think it would be an issue which it was,  I wanted to order agratin potatoes and they told me they couldn't do them without gluten; that made no sense since the key ingredients are potatoes, cheese and cream lol. When it came to desert, they had one option for her and they were out of it lol. In contrast, we went to Flemmings last night and enjoyed our delicious steaks with there version of the Agrautine potatoes, mushrooms, and chocolate lava cake ( yes app gluten free).  It just seems like Charley's is still caught in the past!  For a quality High end steak house, I recommend Flemmings.

This station has gone WAY downhill since the 2 people who worked there several years retired. The main lady, with the pony tail and wrinkled skin, is EXTREMELY rude and non caring towards customers. They are always under staffed and take forever to help or do anything for customers, even though we all pay their salaries.
The whole place had a strong smell of bacon. Not pleasant when you just want to enjoy a pastry in the afternoon. Service was very slow and the fruit tart was not tasty. Very disappointing
Very average fare. Unless you are right in the neighborhood and desperately in need of Indian food, you can avoid it.

If you are a lover of Panera/Paradise Bakery type foods, Kneaders is the spot for you to try! Ever since it opened in Tucson, I have been a handful of times and have never been disappointed with food or service. 

My favorite items are either the Turkey Bacon Avocado Sandwich or Roast Beef Dip. Both are huge and so filling! You can't go wrong ordering one of these sandwiches. It's GOOD food-- not greasy, slimy fast food. Your body will actually be happy eating this!

Pastry items here are also a must try! Usually I say no to extra sides or desserts at restaurants, but adding a pastry to your meal is necessary for any sweet tooth.
