From the simple sugar cookie to brownies to bread pudding, Kneaders offers a little bit of everything. My all time favorite is the Salted Carmel Cheesecake. This puts the Cheesecake Factory to shame!! Kneaders cheesecake is soft and airy, but still has the strong cheesecake taste. 

What makes Kneaders above and beyond any cafe sandwich/soup type shop is their service. Everyone is so kind and willing to help explain anything on the menu. The service alone could keep me coming back! 

The only reason I gave 4 instead of 5 stars is simply because of the menu. Don't come here expecting a hardy 12oz steak. This is a perfect lunch or light dinner place.

Kim did a fantastic job on my hair.  She was friendly and competent.  I had a nice scalp massage with shampoo.  She cut it into a brand new style cutting off 5-6"!  I was very specific in my requests with photo examples.  She asked before any new section if I wanted that much off and was willing to cut longer and then take more off if needed.  As she blew it out, we talked about highlights.  I'd never done it but she had the time.  I decided to go for it!!!  I'm so pleased!  My husband loves it.  A fellow I see almost daily at our community gate did not recognize me!  Thank you, Kim!  I am a new woman!

i have had more issues with this post office than i have collectively had with all of the post offices that have managed mail delivery over my lifetime. because you can't choose the post office that delivers your mail, i won't go into all of the specifics, but suffice it to say, i'll be glad when i move to a different geographical area.

i will give kudos to bill, the saturday front counter worker, who is great. he's really efficient and super nice.

First of all: What is this place called? I've seen New Samosa and San Samosa an equal number of times.

Now that that's off my chest, I can get into the curried meat of my review. I've been to this place a couple of times, and have no plans to go back. The worst aspect of this place is the service. I would seriously rather give a generous tip to Satan than give any tip here. My worst experience was when I got charged way more than the menu price for the buffet. I did learn that there's no sense in reasoning with the management here, as they claimed they were allowed to charge the higher price because the menus they set down on my table were "old." I actually found the credit card company MUCH easier to deal with when I disputed the charge. IMAGINE THAT!

I will say that the food didn't taste too poorly. I especially enjoyed the curried chicken and desserts. Unfortunately, no food (no matter how tasty) can eliminate the bad taste left in your mouth when you get ripped off.

We ordered delivery from here and 45 minutes later when it came, one item was missing from our order and the other dish was completely wrong. When I called back to let them know of their mistake, I struggled on the phone because the person barely spoke any English. When the correct food finally came, it was bland and flavorless. I will definitely NOT be ordering from here again.

don't buy groupons for this this place. The lamb kabobs came as 2 tiny skewers with a total of 4 small pieces of lamb. grape leaves were missing filling, regular coffee tastes like ****. and owners are just crooks, they add 20% tip (while groupon does not mention it) to entire amount. i saw people without coupons calculating tips. so between them cutting down on portion sizes and adding 20% for tips, plus tax on entire amount, not on $35 pre fix dinner, you will be spending more than if you did not gave groupon. Food is not that great

Cosi always provides fast pleasant service.. I come often for their fresh salads that you customize and there is a good selection of salad dressings.. Great for a quick lunch. Flat bread pizza's are delicious and a nice selection of toppings.

I'm a gluten free vegetarian and I recently went to Cedars for dinner after a friend recommended it. I'm so glad I went! I went with a friend, who happens to be vegan, and we found plenty of options! We left absolutely stuffed. We selected several appetizers including the tzatziki, cabbage leaves, mjadra (which are cooked lentils), cauliflower, and falafel. They even let us create our own salad since we both had some dietary restrictions. Everything was so flavorful and delicious! I'm so glad this is in my neighborhood. I loved our server and the owner. This place was recently renovated and had their grand re-opening. It's very chic - I love what they did. I will definitely be back again soon!

I'm all for Indian Buffets and have tried my fair share in Philadelphia. What I cannot stand though is the blatant use of frozen vegetables in what I generally consider the healthiest dishes. Packed with sodium and bland flavor, the food I had at Samosa was sub par. The samosas themselves are probably the best dish because they're not swimming in oil. The salad bar may also be a good option, but this is not what I would consider authentic Indian food nor is it even that tasty.

Everytime I eat here I just get the all-you-can-eat buffet.  My absolute favorite is the vegetarian korma.  The sauce is creamy, nutty, and savory.  I love to eat it over the coconut rice.  Of course the samosas are quite delicious.

My experience with the dessert buffet was not so good.  I got some kind of cake, it tasted like it had been sitting out for awhile and gotten a bit stale.  There was also some kind of mango thing that was so bland and uninteresting that I only took a bite of it.

You go to places like this and you never know what you're going to get.  The reviews seem to yo-yo, but we caught them on a good night.  It's a solid four stars, but the slightly outdated interior and the automatic 25% tip on the Groupon made me think about dropping one.  The BYOB aspect sealed the deal.

The caviar appetizer is unlike anything I've ever had, and it was absolutely delicious.  It's like a whipped, fluffy cream with caviar mixed in.  It's not overpowering and has a wonderfully delicate flavor with a nice hit of acidity.  The grilled octopus appetizer is decent, but not nearly as good as the one at Zorbas, which is outlandishly good.  

Both our entrees were very good.  I had mixed seafood dish, which was light and nicely portioned.  My partner had the lamb kabobs, which were great, but they could have given you a third for the price.

The desserts are fine, but not all that impressive, and certainly not worth the price.

Came for the grand opening and had the free French toast. 1-1/4" thick! With caramel syrup and sweetened (tasted like maple) whipped cream and strawberries. It was delicious! They use their Cinnamon Chunk bread to make the French toast. So yummy to have the flavor permeate the whole slice. But you get two of these behemoths and it WILL be filling. Really, they are large.

I also ordered a slice of their Raspberry Creme pie--only $2.99! Again, delicious! I can't wait to go back to try their lunch menu. Chicken White Curry soup? I'm so there.

Great pizza!  Just like the New York Pizza under the Brooklyn  bridge!  I stood in line an hour and half in NY to have the exact same pizza, I cant believe we actually have a location here in Tampa.

I highly recommend ordering the pizza's as they come, they just make each pie with perfection.

A very clean atmosphere...suitable for dinner, not just a little lunch or grab and go establishment.

My wife & I dropped in to sample some appetizers for a light lunch and were pleasantly pleased.  The service was attentive & friendly.

We ordered:  (see pictures at the top)

Dolmades - The rice-stuffed grape leaves were served warm with lemon...perfectly seasoned.

Foul Moudamas  - This is a blend of cooked fava beans, lemon and garlic. The beans had been cooked to a semi-soft consistency and made a rich broth. I'd never tried this before and was pleasantly surprised.

Kibbi - I'd never had kibbi prepared this way...cinammon spiced ground meat, pinenuts & bulgar all encased in a wheat crust and fried...think of it as a Scotch Egg but with Mediterranean filling instead of egg & sausage.

Falafel - A simple well crisped patty of beans, served with pickle, tomato & a tahini sauce...this went great with the pita bread they serve at the table...we rolled them up and had mini-falafel sandwiches.

I'm not sure if the prices are reasonable or not for the entrees, but I'd keep coming back for the appetizers, which comprise about half the menu...they even have a meze tasting that is nothing but a cavalcade of apps...might be the next thing we try.
This has got to be the worst medical experience I have ever had. I come from a medical family but I have never been treated as rudely, dismissively, and ignorantly as I was by Dr Lawrence.

Just spent the Past 6 days in Tucson, AZ ate breakfast at Kneaders every single morning except for Sunday however if they were open on Sunday I would've eaten there!!! Staff and management are very friendly! Food was delicious every single day!! My personal favorite is their Sausage, egg & cheese on a croissant & all you can eat French toast!!! I highly recommend you try it!!! It will not disappoint!
This restaurant is a good introduction to Lebanese and Mediterranean food!  Looking to try something different while in South Street? This is a great choice!

This was an amazing experience. Alot of bold flavors and a great staff the owner was hands on and very engaging. We ordered what I believe was called the Mezza, for 35$ dollars you basically eat everything this place has to offer and to top it off it's a BYOB and parking was pretty easy. No Doubt I'd be back again also ask for the toum..

im in here 3-4 times a month for the Margerita pizza. the staff is really cool about things, which is nice when you compare it to the RUDE ppl at there old city establishment. And for rittenhouse its great to have a real person to chat with. The lemonade has me hooked!!! and as a stone cold soda- fanatic....that means something. I really enjoy the salads here, i can adjust them 200 ways and not be judged. Tip though, dont go around 2:15 pm, the line is impossible. other then that the place is loaded with outlets for plugging in and there wifi is some of the best in the region. Price wise- this is real food, not fast food. but it wont drain your saving account either. i pay 9.34 for my pizza and
After experiencing other offices, now I know that the services provided by this group was mediocre.
We stopped in to get out of the Philadelphia sheet, and we're happy to find some outstanding iced coffee, iced tea, and salads. Also, I was happy to see that the bathrooms are all clean, thanks!

Fluffy, flaky, crispy croissant sandwiches where the ham and eggs aren't just thrown on top but folded together. Real eggs, real ham, and real cheese!!! The only reason for one less star is because the employee at the register was curt and short, not very friendly. They also have several breads and pastries to sample at the register. The lemon poppyseed bread, the but bread, and the almond pastry are awesome!!! Restrooms are clean and stocked.

Just had another great meal here. The pita is made to order and comes out looking like fluffy fresh pillows. They are so good we always order more. All of the grilled meats are great, especially the lamb. The appetizers are great too. We really like the Greek salad, tabouli, cabbage salad, and of course the hummus. The staff is also incredibly warm and friendly. We've been here over a dozen times and never had a bad meal. This is a real neighborhood gem.

Just got takeout here, one of my favorite local spots off of Headhouse. Great falafel and grape leaves. The interior, as mentioned in other reviews, is a little dated, but I think that adds to the charm. Not sure why this place isn't rated higher. Also, doesn't hit the wallet hard. BYOB if dining in.

It was a warmish Saturday night in January and after spending 5+ minutes  waiting to just put our name down at a nearby Italian restaurant, my famished, vegetarian friend and I stumbled upon this restaurant.  The fact that it was empty was an appeal at that point.  We didn't do the buffet and I had no desire to venture over to the fake meat entrees - we both got a harmless, and tasty vegetable entree.  The Naan was good and the tomato soup I had was tart and had a lot of cilantro - yum!  Since I'm not a huge eater of Indian food I can't speak to its "in the realm of other Indian foodness" - nor can I speak to its comparison to its previous incarnation.  I also honestly don't even remember the music being played - I guess my dinner companion was just more interesting :)  It was all fine by me...

This place would get zero starts if it weren't for the great guy that works at the counter. Except for him, everything stinks. The hours are horrible. They routinely lose my packages. There are always crazy people in here. They should get one of those machines in which you can mail a package without waiting in line.

I was excited for this new restaurant to open. First, we walk in and a bunch of the tables were dirty. It is definitely a cute-looking place, Italian themed, but the dirty tables, were frustrating but that's an easy fix. Second, three out of the five of us got our food in 15 minutes and the rest of the two (one being a little kid) had to wait 20 minutes extra to get theirs. The kid's sandwich was easy too. We had to sit and watch everyone behind us get their food before us which was a letdown. When they finally did get their orders, they were wrong. Don't get me wrong, cute place and the bread was good. I will wait a long while before coming back, when maybe they will get the kinks worked out. It's a new restaurant, so I think it will get better. On the plus side, the manager offered us some free pastries! His name was Andrew and he was very kind! Thanks Andrew! This shows good customer service. THE PASTRIES WERE YUMMY. This review will be updated soon once they get it all worked out. Contrary to popular belief, a restaurant takes a while to get the kinks worked out and it running smoothly. A lot of people don't get that! Show some grace for the new restaurants in town, Tucson. I'm just happy this place isn't ghetto like some restaurants are around town. :)

Amazing food and service, came in with a large party and felt like we owned the place. The service was quick and attentive, the food was amazing and we paired great red wine (byob) with every course. Rami took great care of all of us and was very polite and professional. I'm planning on coming back next week if not sooner.

It's a national chain, so the lunch items taste accordingly- average at best. I got the Turkey Cranberry croissant. It was good but the ratio of turkey to croissant was off. Very little turkey. The croissant was good and I tried the pumpkin muffin top, which were both very good. They have a great selection of baked goods that all look delicious. My biggest issue with this place is its overwhelming gift shop atmosphere. They have all sorts of crap for sale in the dining room like aprons, cookbooks, candles, etc. and none of it is unique. I already know you want my money; don't overwhelm me with yard sale quality junk while I eat just to reiterate that point.

I just want mail like every other person in my neighborhood. I should not have to call the post master general to get normal mail delivery. I'm not looking for packages, live animals or hazardous material, just the simple little envelopes that you put a stamp on and send. For whatever reason, my mail comes when someone feels like delivering it. I mean, really, who does that? I will tell you who, the USPS located on Gray Ferry Ave, that's who! smh

this place is good if you want a simple, healthy, good dinner. i had the grilled chicken combo, which included hummus and tabouli, both of which were right on. we got a big basket of pita with our meals that was fine, and some mint iced tea that was great. skip the lebanese coffee, it's nothing fancy, and go for american coffee to end your meal. the place is clean and the staff is super pretty and nice. our dinner ran about $20/person (entree, tea, coffee) and i'd say it's worth it if you're in the south street area and want something a better than the usual.

Been here several times. Always a pleasant experience. The food is always great. The portions are filling (never enough for left overs). Price is medium fare. The chocolate mousse is superb they have any). Would surely go again!

I only have 30 minutes for my lunch break and I decided to grab Kneaders because they have a drive through and I was craving soup. Wow am I glad I did! The women at the drive though was so nice and I didn't feel rushed at all. She helped me decide on which soup to get and which bread to choose. I ordered the chicken noodle with sourdough bread and green/pomegranate tea. It was out in a matter of minutes. I really do appreciate good customer service so when I receive it I like to give credit. Everything was fresh homemade and ohhhh so good! I will defiantly be back soon!

My husband and I had dinner at Kneaders last night. He got the Club Sandwich and still hasn't stopped talking about how good it was. We are pleased that the portions are so generous that we can bring some home for lunch the next day. I appreciated that there wasn't any fuss about me asking for a substitute cheese on my delicious turkey cranberry croissant. We also ordered an off the regular menu Caprese salad. It was over the top. I have eaten countless Caprese salads. Never before have I had one sitting on romaine lettuce leaves with crumbled bacon to top it off.

We also got a lemon blueberry loaf of sweet bread to being home. It was amazing and we are still enjoying it. We will definitely be back. Thank you for bringing Kneaders to Tucson!!!

All I can say about this place: YUCK! It should never be called "Super Buffet", rather "Mini Buffet". There is nothing either about this place warranting to be called "Sushi" when the selection of sushi is limited to 4 types of rolls!
The cleaning "island" is in the middle of the restaurant and we saw an opened box of Theraflu and an opened sore throat candies laying among the dirty dishes. Someone sick was working and passing germs to all of us....wow just wow!!
The premises seem dirty and the outside, parking lot and building, neglected. 
I will not return to this buffet again!

After traveling to the Middle East three times in the past two years, I find myself frequently craving authentic Middle Eastern food.  For a food truck where you can get a meal in under $7, this is about as close as it gets.  My favorites are the Kefta, Falafel and Babaganouj.  Their combo platters allow you to pick and choose pretty much any combination of your favorite ME foods.  Definitely one of my favorites in the area.

The biggest upside to this place is their more than generous portions for a pretty cheap price. However, food was pretty average and it definitely wasn't my favorite. But if you're looking for a food truck that will fill you up, this isnt a bad place to go!

Somebody point me in the direction of something spectacular, please! I'm getting tired of writing these "meh/grrr" reviews. And I really wanted to like Samosa. Or New Samosa. Or whatever the heck they're called. I mean, they're a vegetarian Indian place that also does "vegetarian gourmet sandwiches" AND they make Dosas. And being the Dosa Daria that I am I cannot help but make sure I try every place in Philly that makes them. Now that I have visited Samosa I believe I have hit every Dosa-making Indian place within Philadelphia proper (if I haven't somebody please tell me and I will gladly correct the situation)!

Now I must insert a caveat here: I got here about 45 minutes before the place was slated to close. There was another couple there, mid-meal, there was me and a friend of mine, and there was a dude loading up a take-away container at the buffet. No one came over to take our order, so we actually had to go over and ask for what we wanted at the counter (this began the general theme of the staff being preoccupied with closing the place up rather than assuring our dining needs were taken care of). 

My friend got the Paneer and it was just ok. I got a Masala Dosa. I actually got to have an informative conversation with a woman who seemed like the owner or manager of the place about the nature of Dosas and why they could not fold it into a triangle the way I like it. Her explanation made sense theoretically, I just thought it was weird that other place I have been that make Masala Dosas never had an issue folding it into a triangle for me. But maybe there's more to that. Anyhow, I happily accepted the tube version as we all know it's not about the shape, it's about the way you ... uh... the way you...put it in your mouth. Well, mostly. 

I just have to say it was one of the most ...unique Dosas I've had. It was smaller than what I'm used to, and it had a slightly different texture to than what I normally experience with Dosa. The potatoes were differently spiced than I'm used to and were kind of bland. I don't  usually feel bloated halfway through a Dosa but this time I definitely did. I was also disappointed by the lack of spice and the relatively flavorless chutneys and Sambhar (the soup that accompanies Dosa). I think this may have been a case of them doing too much -- I mean North Indian, South Indian, and Gourmet Sandwiches. Please, stop somewhere, and just specialize. You want to be solely vegetarian? Ok, well, South Indian food is traditionally vegetarian, why not just be the only solely South Indian restaurant in Philadelphia and make Dosa and Uttapam that just knock people's socks off? I will personally bring everyone I know to eat there at least once if anyone makes such a place in Philly. Really, I will. I'm almost ready to do it myself...except for lack capital, skill, and the desire to run a restaurant.

So anyway, I will not be returning to Samosa myself, but I wouldn't write it off completely, especially if you're a vegetarian. Their buffet looks like its a good deal, and it looks you can get some of it to go in one of those three-sectioned trash-the-planet Styrofoam containers. Also, their sandwiches are probably worth trying. Definitely a good place to go for take-out as the service leaves something to be desired. It's not exactly a pleasant dining atmosphere either, kind has a run-down feeling to it. Though they do have a couple of tables outside, so it might be a nice place to come sit in the summer time and crack open a bottle of wine. Just make sure you get the buffet so you don't have to deal with the service. 

I'm sure there's a lot of food here that is awesome that I just didn't get to try, so I encourage you to give this place a shot, just be forewarned that the South Indian cuisine isn't up to par, and neither is the decor or service. So get it to go and go eat!
great service, food is ok, coupon policy is horrible, they add their own tax and gratuity. ended up paying way more than expected.

Pluses:
WAS all-vegetarian
Buffet
Location

Minuses:
NOW serves chicken, lamb, and seafood
Got rid of vegan ice cream
Quality was always meh...

They lost my certified package and gave me a number to call which never connected even though I called multiple times during their business hours. They insist they sent it back even though the sender never got the package back.  They are refusing to even try to look in the back in case it was misplaced. I got scolded for not coming earlier, which might be fair if this location were not open only within my working hours, and only open for a limited time on Saturdays.

Very unsatisfying. 

The falafel and hummus were good but slightly over priced, at least for the amount of food you received.

The lentil soup was one drop away from sucking on a lemon rind. 

The salad was sitting in a pool of dressing the "Do you want some lettuce with that dressing way". The dressing would have actually been delicious used in moderation AKA about 80% less dressing.

In general there was WAYYY too much lemon in everything.

The atmosphere of the place is nice enough and the staff was friendly but in general the amount of food we got for the amount of money spent was quite out of balance. 

$40 later, we left hungry, slightly sick from lemon acid and unsatisfied.

If you are a hungry vegetarian, go here.
With a wide variety of dishes, samosas, killer chutneys, and a carrot dessert that leaves me jumping for joy, Samosa (once called New Samosa, now called San Samosa) is definitely worth checking out.
Some days are better than others.  Yesterday I noticed a sort of homogenization of flavors on my plate which was a little bit on the boring side and disappointing side- but this is not typical of them.  Generally Samosa's dishes don't pack the heat that the dishes do traditionally, but with so many options - a couple are sure to really please.   
My non-vegetarian boyfriend (think meat with a side of more meat) loves this place more than I do.  It got him hooked on Indian food.  It's a good transition for those that have never experienced such food.  It's also mad cheap.  Go for the lunch buffet!

A favorite place for me! Great cuts, color and style. 
Walking in for the simple things usually works out perfectly and scheduling more involved work has always been timely and reliable. 
 I love all all the people here ~
Did they change the bread recipe? The sandwich I just got is soft and flat and not crispy...it's just sad. I'm sad.

This is the best post office I have used in Philly. Nice, efficient and helpful people -- which is invaluable to me! The post office on Chestnut St by 20th or so is closer to me at work, but the lines are long, the staff there is really slow and disengaged -- so I really appreciate the Grey's Ferry staff. Any season that I go, they are great.
This was my second time at Split Endz and they really know how to make you feel welcome! Thanks to Trish for such an amazing experience

This is how my visit went yesterday:

I got there extra early so I can insist I do not have a copay for preventative care on my PPO. The receptionist says "But you're at a doctor's office. People pay copays." I pay it but remind her that Drexel always sends me a check and a letter weeks later reminding me that I did not have a copay. I then sit in the waiting room for my 10:40 appointment.

I am called to the back at around 12:00 where the nurse checks my blood pressure and pauses. She then checks it again and yells "high blood pressure!" and leaves the room. The wait for the doctor is short-- maybe only 5 minutes-- but during that time, I look to the computer and see the entire health history, medication, and reason for the current visit of the last patient that was in the room! I mean, I'm not a professional or anything, but that seems to be a HIPAA violation. the doctor was very nice and professional, but her performance still couldn't warrant me to give more than one star for this place. The doctor heard the nurse yell about my blood pressure, checked it herself, and said it was fine and must have been an error.

I then was asked to give blood and a urine sample. I waited for 15 minutes until my favorite blood pressure nurse came in to draw my blood. I then counted as she stuck me with the needle ten (10) times. She said she was "trying to find a vein" and swore to me she was in it. I then ever-so-patiently asked her to do my other arm where there is an enormous vein. She did all of this without wearing gloves. The urine sample was fun too! There was nowhere to hang my coat, so I was forced to put it on the ground. There was also no soap nor paper towels. 

I left to find that I got a parking ticket for being at my spot more than two hours. I also woke up this morning to find a huge rash on my arm where I was stuck so many times.

On another occasion, I had poison ivy and called for a phone prescription, as I get it every year and had scripts from them for it from last year. I figured it wouldn't be a problem, since I still had the almost-empty creams from last summer. They refused to let me talk to the doctor and every voice mail I left was never returned. The desk girl said the doctor just doesn't check her messages at times. She told me to go to the ER, and when I say "she", I am saying the desk person. With her years of qualified experience as a doctor-turned-office-assistant, she made the decision to tell me to go to the ER for poison ivy. Think about how stupid that is. 

Please don't ever go here. Seriously, please... It is like this every time I am in there.
Delicious food! We ordered baba ganouj which was delicious. The gyro and chicken shawarma were also very flavorful. Will definitely go back !

I had a bad sore throat and was very low of energy. Since this was the closest place I decided to go here. They took me in without an appointment. The receptionist was very friendly and helpful. I was diagnosed with strep throat within 20 minutes of walking in. The medicine they gave me left me feeling like my old self by night time. I highly recommend this office,

I've taken my vehicle to Mike's on 4 or 5 occasions and have always left satisfied. It's family owned & operated and they do a tremendous job. The prices are more than fair & the service is quick & excellent.

I used to frequent this Cosi a lot because it was attached to my building and it was convenient.  But even then the food was plentiful and the employees was pleasant, especially the guy who used to do the salads.  Very personable, not sure if there was a changed in management; but it doesn't seem that way any longer.    I will check it out during active lunch to see if the lunch bunch is better.

Im frequent here because its attached to my building, so Cosi is very convenient. 

For breakfast, I love the scrambled egg and Spinach wrap, that is actually very good, and only $4.29 and a 0.99 coffee, I get away with a good breakfast for only $5 bucks. This is my go-to.  However, the coffee tastes terrible, I don't know what type of coffee beans they use, but I think they are switching them soon. 

For lunch, the melts are decent, the soup is OK, but for the portion size you get, I think its a tad overpriced. I never waste time on salads here, it's usually full of lettuce and hardly any toppings. If you get a combo meal, you're spending over $10 for lunch. However, I do use the reward card, which is nice, to buy 10 meals and get the 11th free. That helps me to keep coming back. 

The service is spotty... sometimes the people behind the counter are so friendly and happy! And sometimes not. But oh well, they still make the food quick and I guess that's what matters most. Oh, I also like the caloric content on the menus. Helps me make smarter decisions.

This place has a Hazelnut bread that is so delicious. My favorite part is when they have the 50%off. I always end up buying more stuff then I need. They have the Best caramel cheesecake and I am not a cheesecake person but this is one of my favorite. And their Hot coco is yummy. Love this place.

Came back from a year long deployment and discovered this new sandwich shop. Always get the Cordon Blue. Simple ingredients, fresh bread and some tasty baked goods if you are craving a sweet tooth. 
Just a personal preference for me but i love the fact that they have bread samples at the register. Just adds a nice touch.
Not gonna lie though, i feel bad for the other sandwich shop 50 feet away. Don't think they will stand a chance against this place.

More like House of Yum.

I got the Shwarma (aka Gyro) platter and it was delish.

It's always great when you can roll up to a street truck, get your meal fast, and pay bottom dollar.

The rice, which was a combo of two kinds, which I can't entirely describe, but it was good.

I also like the humus and salad that came with it.

All very yummy.
Been here several times over the years and have taken slices to go.  Everything has always been delicious. Love the free cannoli when you check in also!
I got a haircut here last time I was in town and it was great! I just noticed they closed, does anyone know where these talented ladies work now??

Very happy with my experience at Split Endz. I have thick and curly hair so I'm very nervous about new salons and stylists. However, it's been a year since I've moved to Tucson and it was about time I got a hair cut. I also wanted to dye/highlight my hair, and because of previous reviews, I decided to give Split Endz a try.

First impression was that the salon was clean and the staff was friendly. I had my appointment with Trish and I really appreciated how easy it was to talk to her about how I wanted my hair to look. 
She did a great job, especially considering how much hair I have and all the time it took to process the color and give it a cut. She knew a lot about styling curly hair so that made me feel less nervous. 
I would give the cut and color 4/5 stars, but what adds the final star to this review is Trish herself. I had to come back in 2 more times to finish my cut and color (I don't think I've mentioned enough how thick my hair is) and that was only after Trish insisted that I come back in for finishing touches. Most stylists would call it a day after the appointment, but not Trish. She made sure I was satisfied with my cut and color and made the overall experience enjoyable. Professional, sweet and did a great job. Will definitely be returning!

Spacious, friendly baristas, plenty of tables.

Almond milk au lait was delicious.

However, seats next to the window in the middle of winter are very cold. I don't see any outlets around me, so not the most ideal place to study on a cold day (try Starbucks across the street).

Cool decor and vibe - would be a nice place to meet a friend for a conversation.

Why is the phone line always busy?  What's that about?  It's 2012, people.  Let's get with it.

They are nice though.  Helpful.  But meh, it's by no means exceptional.
The best lebanese restaurant in the city. Delicious food and very friendly service! I would recommend it to all my friends and family.
Not open till 10 PM.  Drove up to the drive through at 9:10 pm, no person to take my order.  Pulled  up to the window  and was ignored.  Honked my horn and was still ignored.

This is one best store go .. The staff was so cool about answer my question, he wasn't try hurry me up with anything like that  plus they let kid in if u have kids they will let them in not like Freedom smoke shop... Now gojng to them to buy all stuff

We love this place for its wonderful customer service and the owners are very sweet and kind.  ;) God bless them and all the staff here!  Always feel the love here when we visit.  Nice spot! =) #ManaiaLeMeaAi:)

Talking about the confused interiors of this place doesn't matter, because the chicken shawarma is the best in Philadelphia. 

* Perfect Pita
* warm grape leaves
* simple salads


Wait staff is slightly mob cover-up vibe, in a should you know something or be here type of way. It's good though, enjoy it. 

Exterior sign is designed by David Lynch?

I'm ashamed I've been in the neighborhood for quite sometime without trying Cedars. I've probably walked in front of the weathered and dimly lit store front 100 times. However, once you walk through the doors, you enter into a welcoming, cozy, candle lit byob. We tried a number of cold and hot appetizers and the lamb shishkabob for the main course. Everything was wonderful. The waiters were very attentive and kind. I will definitely add Cedars to the rotation of great restaurants I dine in the queen village/society hill/olde city area.
Love the atmosphere and these guys are so friendly.  The food is amazing.  Best rice and kebabs I ever had and I'm picky!!  Can't wait to come here again.  Oh yeah their hummus is to die for!
The chunky cinnamon french toast was amazing!! Very reasonable prices. Nice atmosphere. I wish San Antonio had a Kneaders!! We would go all the time! Love all the homemade bread items!

I used to go so often.  everything was vegetarian, rather bland... but it was all about face time with Ravi.  New owner no so charismatic.   um, and NOW THEY SERVE MEAT!  WTF.   so yeah, i will pretty much go to any other place in the city instead.  a part of me died as i typed this.
Sandwich was okay, establishment was clean. What made the experience stand out was how kind the employees were. Unsure how frequently I will be back (I think the sandwiches are a bit pricey).

We came here for a quick lunch and it was a great option.

Pros:
+ Plenty of vegetarian options - yes they do have real sandwiches that are more than just lettuce and a slice of tomato between two slices of bread
+ Huge variety
+ Healthy options - Turkey artichoke is my favorite!!!!

Cons:
- The prices are a little expensive for just a sandwich, but the quality of the sandwich is definitely worth it!

Philly is not known for its middle eastern food but this is one of the best that Philly has to offer.  

Service is pleasant the restaurant looks updated on the inside.  The mixed grill platter is perfect and just what you need for a middle east fix.

I've been here a couple of times and will go back many more.  

If you're trying to decide where to go... you just found the place.  I think you'll be happy if you want an ethnic treat that is relatively nice on the inside and good for many occasions. This place is pretty quiet.
Was a little pricey but the food was good and the pastries where delicious. Would for sure go back and love the drive thru

Stopped in here on a whim and tried the buffet. I think there were two things I really liked but don't know what they're called. One is yellow and is basically carrots and peas in a semi-spicy sauce and the other was the sweet carrots with almond slivers. Yum! I could've gorged myself on those two things alone. The naan was just okay, the curried goat was riddled with bones. That being said, I still left stuffed. 

The service was pretty good and the overall price was pretty cheap.

Side Note: Personally, I'm partial to The Palace's buffet, which has spicier and more plentiful options and is available from 11 AM - 3 PM. I wouldn't revisit this place knowing that The Palace at the Ben is right down the street (9th and Chestnut) unless they were closed and I was DYING for Indian food. Even then, I bet I could find a decent curry in Chinatown....

I had an awful experience last night. I was with a group of students on a predetermined trip so we had no choice but to stay for dinner. My students freaked out when they saw a mouse in the kitchen. The food was so bad I couldn't even eat it. The bread was hard and chewy and there was way too much mayo. It was dirty and disgusting. I went hungry rather than eat that garbage.

I like this Cosi location.  While recently pregnant, I would go in once or twice a week for a bagel and ice tea.  The staff was very accomodating (easy on the cream cheese and always asked for a tea without lemon) and was always friendly.

I usually just got a drink and a bagel - which were pretty decent (why is CC Philly lacking in GOOD bagel places).  Salads are good too and made to order.  They are a touch on the pricey side, but comparable to other similarly located lite fare places.

What amazes me was that I went back 4 months later (post maternity leave and had a hankering for a bagel) and the girl behind the ordering counter remembered me - even asking how I was and how was my baby!  I was floored!  

So if you are looking for some basics - soup, sandwiches and salads - this is not a bad place to go in the CC area.

I have been brining my samsonite bags here for years.  Its the only samsonite luggage repair authorized center in the entire southeast.  They do an excellent job and if the bag is under warranty its free!

There is always something not quite right about a visit here. The wait is always too long, the doctors too hasty. The magazines are limited. And it always bugs me to get weighed in more or less public. The one positive is a good location and that some of the staff are very friendly. Generally blah.

I love chineese buffet b/c you get to sample everything and go back for seconds so for me ITS ALL GOOD. I started off (as always) with hot & sour soup topped  it off with the fried noodles. The soup was great and the noodles were fresh, some that want to pass off the lil round noodles you can get from the grocery those will not do yuck!  Then on  to the main course;  the chicken and broccoli, sweet and sour chicken, Mongolian chicken along with  general tso chicken were good.  The crab rangoons and spring rolls were really good and not stale.I choose for dessert, they had several usual flavors but the coconut was the flavor of the year. pleasant surprise. The place was really clean ... I mean really clean! The wait staff was friendly and did not keep coming to the table to pick up dirty dishes. I know that cleaning up the dirty dishes is a good thing but some places seem to be like vultures perched to swoop them up just before you are done. I will be going back  but dont trust me go see for your self I bet you will be back,

Cedars is a great little place suited for a romantic dinner or a family meal. I have been here for both and have always left happy. If you are adventurous, you should try the Kibbeh Naya. The staff are very friendly and the food is excellent. Be sure to try some Lebanese wine too!

I have been to this restaurant twice and both times I've left so happy!  First visit I had turkey artichoke panini, it was delicious.  We dined in and the insidebis clean and charming with plenty of tables.  The service was great.  The second time I used the drive thru and ordered the BBQ southwest chicken salad, it was SO good!  To top it off they have green tea, which I prefer.  Only thing they could do to make it better is carry stevia packets to sweeten the teas.  This is my new favorite drive thru and restaurant.

I went through the drive-thru to get my sandwich. I had the cranberry turkey sandwich on a croissant which came with a very small salad. They have a decent variety of offerings. I'd go back to try something else. The croissant was good and the turkey was real turkey. The taste was ok. The salad was limp and in a small cup. Could have done without that. They were selling elephant cookies to benefit childhood cancer research which is a nice thing to do. The cookie was delicious so I suspect their bakery goods might be very good. The sandwich was fine-just nothing special. I'd go back to try something else. I didn't go inside the restaurant. They do have some outside seating. They are located just south of the Quik Mart.

This restaurant is run down and dirty but the parking is sort of decent if you arrive around 11 in the morning.  Expect to see a moderate rush of customers around 12.

You get what you pay for here.  It's cheap eating.  They have a nicely sized buffet, with a huge variety of rice, noodles, chicken, beef and just about anything you expect to find in a Chinese restaurant. Yes, even donuts.

The food here not the best tasting.  Their bourbon chicken looks very fatty and their white rice tasted as if it was sitting on the warmer for a couple of days.

In fairness, the waitresses and staff are very friendly.  I can't say that I would recommend this restaurant.
My friend and I went here this afternoon and it is awesome service and cleanest shop . So many flavors different at this location.  Staff is friendly and helpful.

Main reason not to go-They charged two of us an $8 BYO fee without telling us until the end. We each had one beer. That was bullshit. Then when we went to pay, the lady should have handed me $5 in change but instead she said "so I'll keep this for tip". So rude! We went with a restaurant.com coupon and I am glad we did because the food was lousy. I will never be going back there again and I suggest you don't either. Go to Tiffin at 7th and Girard. They are the best in the city!

I went here with a few friends and we all agreed that this place was very good. They had a lot of vegetarian choices which was really nice. It wasn't too expensive. The service was good, although there weren't too many people in there at the time. Most importantly all the food tasted really good.

A great spot for lunch in the City. There is a guy named Will who works behind the counter and always has a smile on his face and an upbeat attitude.  Refreshing to see someone who takes pride in his job.

I rarely give out one stars, but this was honestly one of the worst food truck experiences I've ever had.

Firstly, the wait took forever. My friend and I were the only people there and no one came to pick up food for the 20 minutes we waited on the sidewalk. I'm sure it doesn't take that long to put together two lunches.

Secondly, the food itself was very disappointing. The platter was actually a little cold. The rice had no flavor to it. And to top if off, they put raw onions on top of everything. Like, a lot. I had to take them all off in order to taste what little taste the food had. The grape leaves were also disappointing. All I tasted was the bitterness of the leaf and the rice. Finally, to think I paid $6 for that meal. Definitely not going back.

If you want MIddle Eastern/Mediterranean food, stop by Hummus or Greek Lady down the block. Well worth the walk and the few extra bucks.

Found it tucked on a side street away from the main square. We got the baba ghanouj appetizer ($7ish), shish kabab ($8ish) and chicken kabab ($8ish) sandwiches. Delicious, authentic, quick and kind service. If the cost was just a little lower for the portion size, it would have been perfect but still fair pricing for the neighborhood.
Stay away!!! Horrible, incompetent office management when it comes to billing and insurance.

Uhhh bought a travelzoo coupon that was rather misleading. We didn't get to pick our dessert or wine.  We got the hummus for appetizer which was not something I'd ask for again, the pita bread was hard and chewy. Our entrees were ok I got the kafta which was the highlight.  Our tax and tip was calculated incorrectly (tip was over 20%),i made our waitress correct this for us.  I don't plan on going here again, id rather spend my money at kanella for better meals

Do you like coffee? YES! 
Do you like chocolate? YES! 

Try their Cafe Mocha! You'll love it. 

When you first walk in you'll be overwhelmed by the yummy looking pastries/sweets by the cash counter; try their cookies! Their customer service is excellent. All the employees are friendly and answers any questions you may have about the menu. I really love their sausage/egg croissant! It's so delicious and a decent portion. My husband is a die-hard "Chicken-Cranberry Salad" lover. He's always order it when we go! 

They also sell cute little knick knacks! Similar to items that you would see on Pinterest. On the other side, there's wrapping paper/tape. Y'know...just in case ;) 

Give them a try!

my roommate bought the travelzoo deal, $40 for 2 apps, 2 entrees, bottle of wine and desert.  It was not as good as it sounds!! The pita was dry for the hummus. The spinach pie was ok. The baklava was the only option for dessert, which I was excited about, but the baklava had no nuts!! I have never had baklava without nuts!! worst part they charged us $25 for tax and tip!!! that is insane. never going back again!

I agree with all other reviews. Do not entrust your healthcare with these people.  They do not care about you as a patient at all.  I wait at least 30 minutes to be seen and then I am rushed though.  I recently called with a bad respiratory infection and was told that my Dr was on vacation. When I asked to speak with or to have an appointment with the on call physician, I am told that someone will call me.  I've now been waiting 31 hours and after numerous calls I was told to just go to the ER. Why the hell would I go to an ER when I am supposed to be a patient of this office???
Very good food. We had the Maza dinner (several small courses) and we really enjoyed it. Cute little place with nice decor. A South Street tradition.

I only go here when everything else is closed or I'm sick of eating at the 2-3 other comparable takeout spots that are within a block of my office. Being as I have to punch out for meals, I purposefully try and limit my lunches to as little time as possible. The number of spots I can hit in a 15 minute roundtrip is decidedly small. When all the others are closed or wondering why I'm back again so soon, I go to Cosi.

But enough about me, you all want to hear about the undersized portions at supersized prices. The vaunted "bread" is really an oversized cracker. Cosi bread is to real bread what the Monkees were to the Beatles: a commercial grade imitation without the substance or flavor of the original. The salads are the same ones you can get anywhere that sells salads, only slightly smaller. Their house soup is warmed over V8 cut with half & half.

The service is B- fast food level. I refuse to enter any Cosi during lunchtime. The frenetic disorganization is enough to fray my nerves before I order, nevermind during the interminable pileup at the end of the queue while you wait for your food. Best time to go is near closing, when the staff has few distractions and can take an order and get it out the door in a reasonable timeframe.

But hey, they have baby carrots.

I've heard of this place and have wanted to try it for ages. I was not disappointed when I was finally able to eat here! We received excellent service and food, and I enjoyed the atmosphere this restaurant provides. It feels like a small, country home. Some of the knick knacks are even available for purchase, which isn't something you see very often.

First, the menu is diverse enough that anyone could get a sandwich, salad, or soup here. They also have several combinations you can add on, including sides, drinks, and a pastry (my favorite combo). I ordered the sandwich that comes with pesto and spinach on a panini. It was grilled perfectly and arrived as I had ordered it (I left the artichokes off). The bread was crisp but not difficult to eat.

Our food arrived incredibly quickly. My friend and I had barely sat down with our drinks when a server was bringing out our food. They had packed up our pastries on the side as it was a lot of food in one sitting, which was a nice touch. I ordered BBQ chips, but since my sandwich automatically came with the Parmesan, they gave me both (when they really didn't have to).

Ah, the pastries. The case was incredibly tempting. I tried the Chocolate Dome Cake, which was a layer of chocolate cake, mousse, and then surrounded by chocolate with a dollop of whipped cream on top. Heavenly. It was lighter than I expected, which I didn't mind at all after such a great sandwich.

There were also breads and lots of other goodies available. When I have an incredible desire for chocolate and carbs, this place will be my go to. I wish there was one a little closer to me, but this location is excellent.
Closed. Got worse and worse and eventually closed this month. There's a new Mexican place there now; hopefully it's better! :)
Staff was so friendly and knowledgeable. They had a great selection on flavors and let us sample a few the pineapple was amazing. We left with the Melon Blast and will be back for more!

It was a sad day finding out that the owner of Samosa was sick. I used to go there for lunch 3 times a week. So they closed the doors of the place, and put a sign on the window saying they would return. This sign stayed there for a while. 

Well, almost a year later the NEW Samosa opens. They change the cuisine, and changed the decor. Overall I did not enjoy the food at the new place. The place had a weird funk to the air, and the food was mediocre at best. 

This place won't be seeing me anytime soon.

I went to the Cosi next to my office this morning around 10:30 am to purchase a piece of the whole wheat flat bread.  I frequent this Cosi often and would consider myself a loyal customer.  When I asked the woman behind the counter for a piece of the flat bread she said they didn't have any, despite the fact she was standing behind an entire counter of made and cut pieces of flat bread.  When I asked if I could purchase one of the many pieces on the counter in front of me she told me I could not.  I have never been to a food establishment where I was told I was not allowed to purchase a food item that was made and prepared.  As a loyal customer I was disappointed and shocked that a business would refuse to sell an item for no apparent reason.
Leanna always does a wonderful job with my highlights and cut! I love this salon! Everyone is always so friendly and so much fun to be around :)

Love their bread pudding and salted caramel cheesecake!! The food was good too! Loved their chicken and ham sandwich! However, I thought their going guava smoothie and white chocolate and berries smoothie sucked! Also, the service was so slow!

this is the only city where i have received rude behavior with the employees at usps, the attitude & service is despicable! every time i have to go into this location i cringe praying that this will be a smooth and good experience. 

this never happens! the women behind the desk middle aged short hair/African American should look for a new job if you're that unhappy. 

these are some examples..
1.smile

2.ask : what can i help you with today!?

3.be proficient & pro active

4. ask " is there anything else i can help you with? do you need stamps today?"

5. do not rush or push customers out of the way so you can go home on time during closing. its the busiest time of year (Christmas) you should have expected ms. cranky, i hate the world! 

just a few ways to create a warm friendly experience for your customers, remember you have a job!!!! i guarantee someone out there can do it better then you and would be grateful!   

i give this one star only because it's open for half ass business. 

ps. usps you should start recruiting...fasttttt

I went there twice, it is definitely one of the worst restaurants in the area.  Small meal, average food,  expensive. There r much better options in the city, With a better taste. Don't Waste your MONEY.

My husband and I have been coming to Cedar's for years, and we continue to be amazed by the quality of the food. We've never had anything that wasn't absolutely delicious. If you're into Middle Eastern and Lebanese food, or want to dine at a place where the food won't disappoint, this is hands down the best place in Philly.

We tend to order lots of small plates to share. The baba ghannouj, kibbi and stuffed grape leaves are my favorites, while my husband loves the kibbi nayeh, falafel and hommus. Kibbi nayeh is raw meat and may not be for all tastes buds, but if you're into this we highly recommend it. We've also tried the tzatziki, labni, cabbage leaves, tabouli and some of the kebob entrees and everything is delicious. Recently, they've made their pita bread even better and they now serve a homemade version that comes out warm and delightful. I'm getting hungry from writing this review!!

For dessert, we'd always had the baklava and it's great. Recently, though, we tried the Kanafi and it's just unbelievable. All desserts are homemade, and the Kanafi is takes-you-back-to-childhood good. 

We think the owners did a great job with the recent rennovations. The place looks great, the staff is some of the friendliest in Philadelphia, and the food is superb!
I have been here twice and have loved it both times. The breakfast sandwiches and chunky french toast are delicious and I love the chicken artichoke sandwich. The inside is also super cute and clean.

I wish I could give this place a zero for stars. As I was eating my salad, I found a dead fly just sitting in it! I brought it to the front counter and they asked me if I wanted something else. So, I figured I would go with a sandwich. GUESS WHAT? I found a strand of hair in my sandwich. Never again going to this place. I feel sick just thinking about it now.

I gave this office one star but now that I am thinking about it I wonder if that is too generous! I was thrilled to find a medical group in my neighborhood that accepted my insurance but my enthusiasm was short lived. My beloved primary care doc had a baby and left her practice leaving me scrambling for a replacement. So hoping for a suitable replacement I made an appt here with a lady doctor and went to my appointment only to leave with a feeling of disappointment. Not only did the doctor leave me feeling underwhelmed I was sure she was watching the seconds hand on her watch when she was examining me. 
The girls at the front desk didn't seem to understand this was a work environment and I was a witness to some bickering not usually seen in a doctor's office.
I would not return here as I found a doctor who acted in a professional manner and actually answered my questions like they were not a problem for her!
Roasted chicken is amazing, Hummus is on point, and the baklava ain't too bad either. We'll definitely be back soon!!

Little to no wait, friendly front desk staff, knowledgeable doctors... Yay! As the previously reviewer said, checkout does get a little backed up, but they're so helpful you really don't mind. Everything seems so clean and well-run, and overall it's a good experience if you have to be at a doctor's office.

Despite the fact that the place looks like it hasn't updated its interior since the 1950's, Cedars serves a pretty tasty Lebanese fare. 

We asked for "Lebanese alcohol," and the server recommended wine. We weren't looking for wine, and a after a quick wiki, we knew we wanted Arak. Surely they did have Arak, just not on the menu. It was the first time I had Arak so I don't have any frame of reference, but it's pretty effing strong. I sipped a shot glass equivalent throughout the meal. 

We got (in pictures): 

Kibbi for starters, pretty delicious. 

Salmon with Fries - I'm not a fan of the thick layer or creamy sauce on a nicely grilled piece of fish, but in case ambivalent. The sauce was good. 

Lamb with Hummus and Tabbouleh - My main complaint is that 3 small pieces pep kebab stick didn't justify the price tag. The lamb it self was nicely charred on the outside, and tender inside. Hummus and Tabbouleh, refreshing as always.  

Capped the meal with Turkish coffee and baklava.

I was advised to try out this place by a friend. We went after church, I wanted an inexpensive option for lunch after hearing the Word. We landed at China Pearl. 

We were seated right away when we entered, the hostess and server were very professional. The food selection was basic Chinese buffet fare but it was very tasty. I sampled several items, the shrimp, stuffed mushrooms, string beans, and chicken were all well made. The sushi was fresh, made right next to the display table by a chef. The deserts are good, nothing special but very good for the price. The servers are attentive and quick with drink refills. 

All in all this is a great bargain. It is very affordable and a good way to fill up if you are in the carrollwood area looking for a buffet meal without breaking your wallet.

We went with our neighbors - she of Lebanese descent - and couldn't have been happier. We enjoyed the fixed-price meal, which included stuffed grape leaves, stuffed cabbage leaves, kibbi, hommus, baba ghannouj, tzatziki, pita, shish kebob, and more. Everything was very fresh, piping hot, and delicious. Our friend said it was just like her grandmother used to make. We were at Zahav just last week, and Cedars was better, in our opinion. The dining room was clean, felt modern, quiet, and comfortable with a choice of sitting on chairs or on benches along the wall with plenty of pillows to lean against. It's a BYOB, but we didn't know that and didn't have a bottle with us - no problem, they bought it for us from next door. Service was friendly and attentive. We'll definitely return!

We stopped into Cedars on a low key Friday night and found the service to be lovely, and the place to be warm and cute. At Middle-Eastern restaurants, I usually leave wishing I had just ordered a bunch of appetizers instead of one app and an entry so that is exactly what I did this time around. Items we ordered ran the gamut from fresh and delightful to below average (the pita was straight up dry and stiff). Oh well, maybe it was an off night but I've had consistently better middle eastern food at many other places around Philly.

The fresh pita is melt in your mouth fantastic. The food was fantastic, and the service great. It is a nice little breath of fresh air right off of South St. Recommended for that authentic Middle Eastern experience.

I went to Club Vapor to purchase some e-juice for a friend of mine. Since I don't smoke, I didn't really know what I was looking at or purchasing. The man at the counter was SO helpful and allowed me to try some of the juice without nicotine which was great considering I don't smoke. Thank you Club Vapor!

My review is for the Fit Bar and for the Fit2Run.com store. First I absolutely LOVE this place. The Fit Bar has delicious healthy food choices and the physical store is paradise and the on-line store is great too. They carry the latest in great work out apparel, shoes & accessories. I have gotten into a running, Pilates and, spinning routine and... my 50 year old knees need to have the best shoe fit and product. Thanks to the very well trained staff I am delighted with my purchases. I would not buy my shoes anywhere else.

Been here a couple times, its always so so.  Today i spent 25 mins in the drive thru with one car a head of me, who i heard order just a salad and extra bread.  I was thankful when the car behind me backed out for waiting too long, so i could back out as well! Im sorry but its a sandwich shop....why should anything take over 5- 10 mins to prepare!

Are you kiddin me??
Why are the reviews so bad for this place?
I did the all you can eat during which they bring so much food as you like. I loved every single item and the dessert as well.
With tax and tip I ended up with a 45$ bill which is way more than I expected. That's why I am giving it 4 stars!

I had a long lunch break, so I decided to give this place a shot after driving by it several times. 

Boy, am I glad I had that long lunch break! To be fair, it was during busy lunch hour time, but there was a line and then after ordering it took quite awhile to come out. Not to mention, the counter staff wasn't the friendliest - kind of felt like they were there for a paycheck and doing the bare minimum when it came to customer service. No greeting, no thank you, call my name, hold the bag towards me and rush back off to the back without a word. Anyway.

I ordered the harvest veggie panini (a hot sandwich) which included eggplant, portabella mushrooms, roasted peppers, zucchini, onions, with ricotta and parmesan cheese. Also, looking at all the amazing looking pastries in the bakery case while I stood in line, I caved in and ordered the key lime tart. My total, for sandwich, tart, and a small drink came to about $16, which is way more than I usually spend for lunch.

The sandwich: the messiest sandwich I have ever eaten. Veggies in their lemon sauce fell out all over the place, juices flowed down my hand and onto my arm, the bread became somewhat soggy. The flavor wasn't there. I'll be honest. I usually don't put cheese on my sandwiches because the cheese tends to overpower the taste of everything else. I thought I'd give this a shot as I'm sure they'd made sure the flavors complimented each other. Boy, was I just further reminded and reinforced in my habit - the ricotta and parmesan overpowered everything and the whole sandwich came out bland. I ended up picking the veggies out of the bread, but it didn't help much. I was disappointed, since the sandwich itself was almost $9.

The key lime tart: Omg. This tart itself made up for the whole thing. It's the only reason this review is 3 stars and not 2. This tart made my whole day. It was amazing. 

I'll probably come back for the pastries as this seems to be their strong suit. I might try another sandwich or maybe one of the many soups they have available. Maybe then things will be a little different.

Stopped in here on the way home to pick up some sweets for dessert. We have stopped in before and have found the staff to always be friendly and that was the case tonight.  Fair warning, generally at night (like tonight) they start running low on some of their more popular sweets.  We went into it know this, so we were not disappointed.  The food is always yummy, but tonight they did not get our order right.  Once we got home we realized they gave us a muffin top instead of the croissant we had ordered for our daughter.  Trust me, she will still eat because it look really yummy, but we were a little disappointed they pulled the wrong treat.

Great food, the lamb chops were good...the filet mignon was overcooked a bit but acceptable...the duck was interesting...the best dish was actually the calamri salad and the chocolate pagoda was the best dessert.

The buddha was interesting, with his/her tiny head, they must've found it in Chinatown around the corner, I'm sure some folks will find it offensive.

The worst part was that all the African American patrons seemed to be seated near the bar or back towards the restrooms, while only white and asian patrons were visible on the main dining floor.  Coincidence?  I sure hope so.  The manager should be sensitive to this sort of perception and I certainly hope they work on that.

Horrible experience, didn't expect staff to try kicking my family and I out at closing time in the middle of our meal. When we refused after cashier told us they had to deep clean she finally moved on to the next customer and proceeded kicking them out rudely instead of telling everyone nicely to take their time and that they were closing. Very poor customer service. I wouldn't recommend eating at this location.

What?! I usually never give a restaurant five stars - usually the food is fine and the service is fine and there is nothing ostensibly wrong, so 80% seems like a good grade.

Valanni has earned its five stars.

A friend and I split four tapas: baked brie (with apples and cranberries), the three spreads with pita, spanikopita, and the truffle mushroom arancini.

We sat and ate wordlessly for the first half of the meal, punctuated only by statements such as "this is stupid good" or pure monosyllabic sounds of satisfaction ("mmmmmm!"). We also walked out completely full.

Service and decor are on point - urban chic vibe and clean typeface on the menu. But it's really the quality of the dishes that blows this place away. Everything was so perfectly balanced and enjoyable to the point of absurdity.

Only downside: most bougie crowd that I have ever seen. Housewives with body waves and too much makeup and fake tans, about one decade away from being obsolete. Play along! Bring a guy who knows how to rock a sweater over a button down and a pair of khakis. Pea coats for everybody!

Just kidding, we are so excited to go back. Absolutely worth the price and the 5-star rating!

My friend and I ordered the lamb platter and the chicken platter. The woman who works here is a complete sweetheart, so huge points for that! Our meals had two types of rice, and I love rice, so that was a plus! The salad that went with it was also pretty fresh. I thought the chicken was alright. It tasted a bit dry to me, but there was lots of chicken. My friend enjoyed his lamb plate, so overall, good deal and decent taste.

My husband and I both vape and we were victim to the Freedom people.. These people are friendly and knowledgeable.  The owners remember us every time we walk in.  I used to buy some juice at other places and end up throwing some away because it ruined. They have awesome flavors, and are written where you can see them without having to look thru a book and are more than willing to let you try what you want and as much as you want.  You don't have to do extra flavor because it is quality. The store is always clean and they are very sanitary, They listen to you and make you feel very valued. I would drive past a lot of vapor stores to get to this one. If you have any doubt give them a shot and you will be pleasantly surprised. We will be forever customers!!!

My family and I had a great experience today. My son decided to cut his long curly hair. We went in because it was cose to our house. Leanna took him right away, looked at the picture that he picked for his hair, and talked to him about it. She was very friendly, and no one seemed to mind that my 2 year old was running wild around the salon. I really appreciated that. My family and I will definitely be using salon and recommending it! My sons hair looks great, I am happy and so is he!

This is a worse version of Panera. Panera sucks. Honestly, that's probably all you really need to know right there, but I will of course elaborate...

We had seen this place pop up and were somewhat excited to give them a try. Wound up in the area randomly and were hungry for breakfast, but wanted it on the go. Kneaders has a drive-thru so we figured it was worth a try. 

I went with the reuben panini, and my wife got the harvest vegetable sandwich. We both got chocolate croissants and I got a large iced tea, she had a coffee with cream. The best items were the croissants. Not the best I've ever had but they were nice. They were light and crispy on the outside, the chocolate had a nice flavor. In descending order, I think my wife's sandwich was the second best item, but it was a little odd. The roasted vegetables were good, and the bread was good, but there was a cheese on it that you would think and expect to be cream cheese that turns out to be ricotta. And its not like super high-grade ricotta either. It made the sandwich weird. From there, the food is a drastic drop off in flavor and quality. My reuben was thin, soggy, and one of the worst sandwiches I've had in a long time. I thought this was supposed to be a panini...You know, like crispy on the outside? No. It was complete mushy awfulness. Both of our sandwiches came with potato chips that were not cooked all the way through, so they were crispy on the outside and soft once you bit into them. Terrible. My wife's coffee was clearly burnt and my iced tea had no ice.

The only vaguely redeeming factor to this place was that the people working there were very nice. And the croissants were good. Apart from that, everything was just awful. This is not a chain that is going to survive in Tucson, I'd like to think we have higher standards.

This location is horrible. First of all, the person who delivers the mail on my street CONSTANTLY marks whatever he wants on the tracking number. I've had to call their godforsaken office many times to track my packages. There is never an apology but always an excuse. They really need extended hours since most of us that work cannot make it 9-5 Monday through Friday. Aside from a few jam packed hours on sat morning, you don't have much of a chance to pick up packages. Oh, and don't even think about friendliness, efficiency, or any other hallmark of a good organization/business.

Wow!
So, I was kind of in the mood for low key, I didn't want to do myself up and go to one of our regular spots. I walked passed Cedars yesterday like I have many times and decided that was where I wanted to go for dinner. So when my boyfriend got home I announced there was a bottle of wine in the fridge and we're going to try a new BYOB.
We were greeted very warmly by our server who promptly opened our wine and told us about the specials. He was extremely helpful with the menu, so helpful that everything sounded good and we ordered way too much!
We started out with the hummus appetizer which was deliciously smooth and perfectly warm. That came with piping hot pita bread fresh out of the oven. I know this because it was still puffy when he brought out two huge pieces. :) yum!
We also started with the grilled octopus..we were hesitant because it was $16 but another couple had told us it was totally worth it. It comes prepared in sauteed veggies, onions, peppers and cherry tomatoes. Normally I'm not a  huge onion and pepper fan but I seriously could not stop eating these onions! The octopus was tender and cooked perfectly.
I ordered the seafood rice..unfortunately I don't remember what it was actually called. But it was DELICIOUS!!! A giant portion of rice with mixed seafood, scallops, shrimp and salmon. So giant I took the majority of it for lunch AND shared it with a co-worker. He assured me he was going to visit Cedars with his wife soon.
My boyfriend opted for the lamb kabobs and they were also delicious. I loved that you could get veggies and hummus as a side or rice and veggies. I asked for a small side of tzatzki because who doesn't love lamb with tzatzki! Comes with three giant kabobs and those leftovers will be my dinner tonight!
The owner or manager (I'm not sure) came around and made small talk with us and was very friendly. The service was great, our server came around filling our wine glasses and checking on us regularly. 
Great casual spot for a delicious meal! I can't wait to try more!

The food is really good and the staff has always been pleasant. I think the desserts I have tried were just okay, but my girlfriend really enjoyed the desserts she has tried specifically the key lime pie. 

I would highly recommend this place.

A Tampa institution that lives up to - and perhaps exceeds - its reputation. Ambience was really cool, from the main entrance all the way to the dessert room. Food was delicious and surprisingly affordable (for a renowned steakhouse, at least). Guided tour of the kitchen and heralded wine cellar was a nice cap to a memorable dining experience.

Decent food, bad service.

The people working the counter never want to make any of the speciality drinks and often claim ignorance like all they are there to do is claim money for the buffet (if they are even there). The buffet is decent but you have to put up with horrible service. It's like a dive bar for curry.

I'm a bit biased because I always give the benefit of the doubt to the all-vegetarian establishment, but I had a pretty good dinner here. The vegetarian options at a "normal" (i.e., not-all-vegetarian) Indian buffet are often hit-or-miss, so it's nice to have a full veggie buffet. It's not a place to take anyone you want to impress like a date, your parents, or your accountant, but it's nice-enough and cheap-enough, so maybe at least your accountant will appreciate it.

It's a post office. 

Essentially it fulfills its intended purpose. 

I do wish there were more counter staff during busier times, and dually wish the staff on call were friendlier. But it's fine. They've always been cordial.

Aside from that the parking lot sucks but I don't feel like that is the post offices fault.
Dined there last evening with a friend. Very gracious service from Ramy (sp?), very good food.

The New Samosa is definitely an improvement over the "old" samosa, let me tell you, which closed down a few years ago. The New Samosa is a decent place to grab some decent Indian buffet for lunch--vegetarian and non-vegetarian. For me, it's good grub for a filling lunch hour meal. While dinner is served here as well, it's not the kind of place I would choose to go "out" for Indian food for dinner. They did just recently make some interior improvements that have helped elevate the ambiance a bit.
Went to Kneaders which I love but came home with a salad that included 3 raspberries and 4 tiny pieces of chicken, small enough that I had to hunt for them! There was more onion in it...

Excellent breads, cinnamon rolls and French toast. It's a favorite treat to buy their bread to make our own French toast but it's better in store. I've been to this specific one several times and each time it has been very clean with friendly and knowledgable staff. A great place to meet up with friends and chat over yummy food! Great for any meal of the day.

This is a really great place to try, especially if you are a vegetarian.

The dining room is grand and it feels like you are in a mansion. I love their kabobs (get the lamb) and grilled meatballs. Oh, not to mention this is a totally affordable place to grab dinner with your friends.

I wanted to like this place, I really did. It replaced the sad Drinker's West (which was honestly the most depressing bar on campus). I loved the décor and feel upon walking in, and the tables are so big and perfect for welcoming groups of friends for late night drinks and snacks, but the food really does fall flat.

[ vibe ]
Dark metal tables that look like they were made from the sides of boxcars or old machinery. Magnetic menu holders were a nice touch and fun to play with. The tables are large and low with benches and I could easily imagine a group of 10-12 people sitting comfortable around one, and they are very conducive to conversation. 

Strings of bulbs across the ceiling. Nice clean individual bathrooms. No complaints here.

[ food ]
The dinner menu sounded great in theory, but the food was rather underwhelming when it arrived. Pierogies were fine but nothing worth remembering, as was the grilled cheese.

What really killed the deal was the mac and cheese that we ordered - flat, tasteless, and we were pretty sure that it was made with Velveeta. If the place were slightly fancier we would have sent it back. Wawa mac and cheese tastes better and costs less.

[ conclusion ]
Willing to come back here one more time to try brunch or drinks, but a rather underwhelming first experience. Don't get the mac and cheese.

This place is barely OK to go to. I am an Indian and my default food craving setting is set to Indian. Went to this place after a year and it is still as bad. Don't know what the hell do they serve in the name of Indian food. 

The best part is their Samosas are pathetic. You'd expect a good samosa at a place that is called Samosa. But no sir! 

Sadly, there are hardly any good Indian restaurants in Philly and this is one of the crappy one.

I have to agree with the other reviewer who had the Travelzoo coupon. We paid $39 for the coupon too, which was to include 2 apps, 2 entrees, 2 desserts and a bottle of wine. The app we chose was the sampler plate and we thought it was fine, though at $14, a bit price-y. There were a couple of spreads and some rolled grape leaves plus feta and olives on shredded lettuce. It was attractive but since it was expensive it was equal to 2 apps. They let us pick whatever entree we wanted. One of us had the moussaka, which was fine.  The other had the salmon, which was tasteless and had a cotton-y texture. It was seriously bad and it didn't even seem fresh, there was that vague ammonia smell that is a sign that fish has been out of water too darn long. I was kind of excited about dessert because I saw they had chocolate mousse on the menu but no one gave us a chance to even choose the dessert. The waiter just came out and plopped two dishes on the table. Well, the waiter should have been embarassed because on the plaste were  two of the teensiest slices of baklava. I'm not kidding, they were just a little longer and wider than your average Marlboro 100 cigarette and so thin that there was room only for phyllo dough, no filling.
