It was ridiculous and they charged us $4 for each for a pretzel stick of what was basically puff pastry. The wine by the way was a Barefoot Cabernet. I think Barefoot is about a $7 bottle at my local liquor store. They marked it up to $35. When the bill came they charged us about $8 for tax and tacked on for themselves a whopping tip. Between the cost of the Travelzoo coupon and the $26.50 they added this dinner cost about $66 bucks. Worst meal in recent history, no bargain at all. I will never recommend it to anyone or go back there myself. Total rip.

"Ahem.  Yes.  Thank you for coming to the Cosi employee training seminar.

We at Cosi realize two things.  We have great bread.  Great bread that that we can shove a small amount of ingredients into and people will still be happy.  Good for us.  

But more importantly, we've learned something far more crucial.  That our bread is good enough that we can skimp on hiring employees who have a full brain.  That's right, you.  Our assembly line is so simple and easy that a monkey could do it, which we would do if the health department didn't have a problem with it.  Trust me, those little monkeys have small hands that would be great for packing our bread, but no, they will not budge on that. As a result, we've hired you.  Thank you for being one step above a monkey.

Monkeys aside, let's get down to business.

First of all, let me make sure that each and every one of you have tattoos on your arm.  This is a strict requirement. (looks around)  Oh, you, little old lady.  I see that you don't have one yet.  Might I suggest a fallen family member as a tribute?  Pet name?  Random words?  Okay.  We'll fix you up.

Secondly, let me make this abundantly clear, you are to treat the customer with a humorous amount of apathy and disdain.  Do not smile or look directly at the customer.  Might I suggest staring out into space while shoveling items into our delicious flat bread?  Also, when speaking, do so quietly and with a drawl.  Like this, 'keeeeyaaan I heaaaaaaalp eyyyyoooou?"  

People, I need you to channel your inner sloth.  We didn't hire you to move fast or react.  Just stand there with no hair net on and kind of zone out.  If there's a line somewhere else in the shop, be sure to just stare at it.  Stare and stare and stare.  Customers might be staring at you because they're wasting their lunch hour waiting in a line but, like I said before, do not stare back!

Alright people.  Even though half of you have quit in the time I spent giving this speech, I know that each one of you will give some of the worst customer service this city has seen!  Go get 'em!"

Really great food, mediocre to indifferent service.

I am not sure if the service is typically this way, or if it's because we went there with a Groupon.  

The overall experience is as follows:

-We were seated in a horrible spot,  where the staff and customers bumped into my chair every time they tried to pass.   My friend was scrunched with his stomach against the table (and he's a skinny dude).

-We asked to substitute the wine with something of equal value - NO.

-We asked to be seated elsewhere - NO. 

-We got 4 stuffed cabbage leaves, when the menu said 6.

-We had no choice of dessert.

-We were asked to pay a gratuity of 20% based on the restaurant's esimate value of our meal, which was not what we ate, and not the tip we would have left it were up to us.

It's unfortunate, because I thought the food was very good, and would have recommended this place and returned myself, if it the experience was more pleasant.

Called for a same day appointment a couple hours before my lunch and was able to get in with Kim. It was my first time going to this salon and I'm very pleased! Not only did Kim get me in and out on my lunch hour she did an amazing job cutting and styling my hair quickly. I typically avoid going to salons because I admit I always end up disappointed they cut my hair to short, uneven, ect. Kim listened to what I wanted and nailed it, I plan to try and come back and see her very few months and might try getting highlights with her. Thank you Kim!

New Samosa is a very misunderstood and underrated restaurant in Philly.  It deserved much better than the ratings it's getting.

We don't get to the Philly area much, but we were lucky to go to New Samosa when it was all vegetarian.  Alas.. to compete, now it serves meat too..  oh well.  The last of the 'all vegetarian' Indian restauarnt is now.. not that..

This place is like an enigma.  Everything is low-priced, fresh and delicious.  The lowest price buffet of Indian food.  While it can't replace our fave Palace of Asia for the most fantastic taste-- it is what it is:  inexpensive, tasty healthy and fresh Indian food at amazing prices!   And yet, lo and behold, because it's simple and low-priced, most people do not get it.

New Samosa actually serves the type of Indian food which Indians actually serve at their home for daily meals:  lower spice; high freshness (contrary to the myth, no... most Indians do not overspice and overgrease their homemade daily meals the way Indian restaurants do).    For those, who think Indian must mean 10 pounds of tandoor spice, this place may be too healthy for you.  For for those who want fresh, healthy and simple Indian items, this is it:  FRESH AUTHENTIC HOMEMADE SIMPLE INDIAN FOOD

Apple cinnamon bread pudding is flavorful, cinnamony, moist, & accompanied by vanilla creme.
I'd like some raisins in there - but many folks may not.
As of this date, it's about $4.99 for a fairly big square - 4 inch X 4 inch or larger.
Companion ordered breakfast sandwich on croissant & raved about it.
One register with samples located there.
Friendly.

LOVE this place. Good food, good prices and small crowds equal good spot.

Its small and quaint. Food is very good, and staff is quick and helpful. 
Have had numerous items on the menu, from their skewers, gyros, lamb, dolmades, and eastern coffee. 

It seems to be a mix of greek, turkish, middle-eastern cuisine. Very good bang for your buck. Good date spot, as its candle-lit, decent music, open for conversation and away from the typical crowds in Old City or nearby south street.

There are a lot of really nice ppl in this office, but good luck getting a timely appointment. After a couple years with them I've become so frustrated at the unavailability - ESP WHEN YOU NEED IT MOST - I had to update my review. No, I don't want an appointment a month from now, I'd like to see the doctor this week.

This place is good.  Not mind-blowing, not even excellent, but it's an all-you-can-eat Indian buffet with a low price.  I've had better Indian food, I've had much, much worse.

I do really like that they have ice cream, as well as a buffet.  Today I sat outside with a friend, ate my fill, chatted for an hour, and went back in for dessert.  It's worth noting that I've also had better ice cream, but this was just...so...there!

Overall, it was a fantastic time. The good was top notch BBQ; My 2 friends and I got the "Sampler". There was enough food for 5 total meals, it was absurd. I recommend the Truffle Mac and Cheese and essentially any of the meat items. We all enjoyed the Brisket, the Pulled Pork, and the Ribs. The guys there couldn't have been nicer and more accommodating.  If it weren't a half hr drive away, I'd make it a regular place to frequent.

Why do I bother going back to Kneaders during lunch? When this location first opened both the food and service was amazing! However it has gone downhill. If it was not for the raspberry bread pudding I would probably go next door. Today I went through the drive through and ordered hot raspberry bread pudding. Of course I did not check the bag and drove off. Once I got to work I noticed that I was given significantly less(1/2 the amount) than usual, the bread pudding and sauce was also very cold. The portion provided was definitely not worth $3.99. I am pretty disappointed and probably won't be back.

My Sunday stroll around South Street made me stumble into this little gem! (You like that alliteration?) Friend and I weren't as hungry, but we decided to check it out anyway. Decor is a bit outdated, with several praises and awards going back to 1991 and 1996, but hey, the chairs were comfortable! It also seemed that there were some regulars there which is a good sign.

We ordered the Kibbi (three mini hot pockets filled with ground meat) and Shish Taouk (grilled chicken and veggie skewers with rice) to share, and they were delish! However, the pita bread that came to us before our dinner came was meh. Warm, yes, but very chewy.  I really liked the skewers, and the rice was cooked to perfection. The yogurt sauce that comes with the dish delivers, and I smothered that all over everything. 

Some added pluses is that it's a BYO and accept card. If Fez isn't open yet, go to Cedars!

Hindsight being 20/20, I'm thinking July 3rd might not have been the best day to do a University City food truck tour. I'm fairly certain I only had about 1/4 of the choices that are normally available. 

However... Absolutely no lines whatsoever at 1:30, so it has its upsides. 

I tried this truck first because I happened to park near it and I like Halal food. A $5 plate of lamb gyro with rice, lentils, white sauce, that comes with a bottle of water was a great deal and I downed it happily. 

But it was very basic food. I did get the feeling that on a day where other trucks are around that I could have done better.

The lunch buffets just aren't as good as they were when I first tried them.  Great deal for the price though, definitely try it out if you get the chance, though your naan may get a bit smushed in that container they give you.

Have yet to actually dine-in here.

Stopped by here tonight off a recommendation. Seems like many people like it, I must've hit them on an off night. The restaurant was empty, that's not usually a good sign. I order the garlic chicken, it was ok, the chicken itself was over cooked, no veggies come with their entres. The potatoes in the batata harra were raw in the middle, the hummus had way too much lemon in it. To add insult to injury the food was way overpriced for what it was. I didn't think it was worth the visit and most likely will not be back.

Great experience! The staff are real people, good people who really try to meet you halfway- I was surprised how quickly they fit me in as a new patient. Once there, everyone was friendly & polite. Dr. Lawrence is thorough and I feel confident with the medical direction I'm receiving. She was quick to direct me to get a specialized test, just to ensure nothing serious was afoot.

Small quaint environment, pleasantly decorated 
Horrible parking!
Breakfast classics, great smoothies, wonderful bread choices, Gormet sandwiches, salads, soups and a nice classic style bakery. 
I had the chicken pesto panini with mozzarella it was OK, slightly on the bland side, would recommend switching the bread to something other than the French bread that is offered... Jalapeño maybe?
My partner had a kinda of build your own Cafe sandwich that he says was good. 
We're going to try one of the eclectic salads on our next visit that won't be on a weekend... 
My only complaint was the human element pertaining to the staff... Not very outwardly friendly, they all seemed to need a nap and as we had stated when we walked in, it's was our first time there.  They could have up sold me on what Kneaders is all about because the concept is not original, there is a Beyond Bread down the street that is local with a very similar ambiance with much better seating and ample parking. 
Overall it was not a bad experience and we will be back...

I've eaten here 5 times, once with a large group and the staff couldn't have been more accomodating if they'd tried, pushing tables together and moving things around.  The food isn't gourmet nor does it claim to be...just good old-fashioned Lebanese cooking at an amazing price point.  Love the moussaka, love the kibbe, love it all really.  Very cozy atmosphere, kindof like eating at a Lebanese neighbor's house.  I highly recommend it, and a great spot to go on a date too.

I would like to start off stating that my wife and I have been coming here since it has opened and have always enjoyed the friendly staff, clean facility, and good food.  It pains me to say that the service and food has gone down significantly over our last three visits all in the second half of 2017.  The last visit on a Saturday evening, we were the only people in line entering at 6:58pm half of the restaurant had the chairs on the table and was closed off, blocked by more chairs from all sides.  We almost left assuming they had closed early.  It wasn't until we approached the counter we could see others eating in the restaurant,so already knowing our order waiting for any staff member to take our order.  Finally having to flag someone down to order, we sat in the crowded half of the restaurant that was still open.  I needed a high chair for my daughter which I had to break down the chair barrier to retrieve.  At this point we are frustrated and checked the stores hours only to find nearly 2 hours prior to closing that all of the staff was gearing up for their Saturday night rather than helping customers.  After the food arrived my sandwich was nearly half the size of my wife's which was on the same bread, coincidently the smallest portion I have ever received from this establishment and I order the same thing every time we come here.  The restroom was also closed, and staff nowhere to be seen in order to open it.  Finally after 8:00pm all pastries are half off and a line has formed to take advantage of the deal, only no one is being helped because staff is cleaning the kitchen so they can leave.  After hearing two other customers in line complaining about the wait to order, I decided to write this review.  I am sad to say that since the corner bakery opened right next door this location seems to no longer provide the exceptional service they once did in years past.

I have MAJOR nut allergies and this place always goes WAY above and beyond to make sure none of the food I eat will kill me. :)

The food and service are both excellent, and beautiful atmosphere. Hope this place stays around. 

Extra kudos to Joseph for taking the time to check lots of different ways to make sure my lunch is nut-free.

It has been 10 years since I left Philly and was dying to have cosi's this weekend. This location was not what I expected. The sandwich was good and the staff was very pleasant. The other location was a little more relaxing.

Love this place however hopeful for some improvements. Came in Dec 23rd night asking to make a gift basket and none of the staff appeared to want to step on a managers toes and offer anything. From what I could tell the employees went and found a manager who told them I could come back and pick something up the next day. The girls were nice but leadership appeared to be lacking that night. We are now back again for lunch and my hubby gets a French dip with like 3 slices of meat. Love the atmosphere but hopeful for improvements!
I tried the Mezza, great trial run. All food was delicious and got to experience a number of the restaurants flavors.

Blehhhhhhh!! This was the biggest disappointment. I went here for dinner one night because I was desperate for indian food in center city. We got the dinner buffet, which was first of all far too overpriced to begin with. But the food, no matte what the price, THE FOOD WAS JUST PLAIN BAD. It wasn't flavorful and everything tasted exactly the same. I was expecting chicken tikka masala and I ended up eating chicken in a red, slightly spiced goo. It's like they decided to open an indian restaurant, and never learned how to cook.

I have been very disappointed by the quality of care at this clinic. The staff are not very friendly and it is hard to get the doctor to spend any quality time with you. I have seen three different doctors in four visits (not by choice) and each time I felt that the doctor asked minimal questions and gave me generic answers to my questions. I have switched clinics and am happier already.

Want a midly overpriced sandwich or salad with a huge side of explicit rudeness and complete absense of customer service?

Run, don't walk to this center city Cosi location for a lunchtime experience that is like no other.  Prepare to be ignored, then barked at and insulted! Come one, come all!  Also, you'll be thrilled to wait in line not once but twice as you order your items,and then proceed to pay for this lovely dining abuse.

But seriously, if you've got time to spare for lunch, avoid this Cosi location at all costs.  Seems like the downtrodden manager (a poor fella in a dress shirt that jumps behind the register or hands out those measly carrots or lackluster Cosi chips, who is clearly exasperated with his life and his minions) is the only one who knows what's going on and tries to run the show (but miserably fails).  

Even in this economy, is this really the best kind of staff Cosi could come up with?  Is this Cosi that hard up for good employees that they could only manage to hire the most unhappy and disaffected people to stuff bread and toss salads?  

Even after the lunch rush, when there is no one in line to order and in the face of  "Hello, how are you? May I please have [insert food choice here]" coming from the customer (and not the Cosi employee!) - one is met, stonefaced with nary a reply.  Fabulous, no?  Why must we accept this kind of service as normal around here? Most importantly, why does Cosi?

I have been going to Jen and her stylists for several years. They are all welcoming and friendly. Professional without all of the $$hype.  I am so happy with their excellent service and abilities, especially with color.  I have such trust in all of their stylists, because I am notorious for asking for last minute appointments and I have never been disappointed with the results. Love this salon!

The food here is good, but we have a serious complaint about their coupon policy. It ended up costing us considerably more to eat there with a so-called discount coupon than if we had just ordered on our own. First of all, they don't allow you to order the more expensive appetizer dishes using the coupon. Second, they include a bottle of wine, which, for two couples, means two bottles. This was not the problem. The problem was that the final bill includes tip and tax for what the total would have been without the coupon, which therefore includes a bottle of wine we would not have ordered. We also would not have ordered the dessert. We will not return. What they gained in the short term, they lost in terms of future customers.

This place is underrated. I am not a huge fan. The food here is as good or bad as any other Indian restaurant in the city and they have three desserts in the buffet which is great. Also one thing I noticed that was better than other restaurants was that they serve real basmati rice and better gulab jamuns than any other place. Their food doesn't make your stomach a run as the spices are not too much.

UPDATE -  I think they have become crappier now. How can one make DAL that does not taste good! Come here to find out....
I love this place soooo much. Its a little pricey, but you get a lot of food. The only catch, is the drive-thru SUCKS. ALL LOCATIONS are SUPER slow in drive thru.

This post office is great!!!!Bill and the other guy with the tattoos get u in and out. They know what they are doing and are quick too. They are respectful and always keep me laughng when I walk in. The lady that usually be up there with bill is something else. If they could replace her with the other guy that would be better.

Delicious pulled turkey sandwiches. Awesome desserts. And amazing customer service. 
They're seasonal cupcakes are yummy. My favorite dessert is their chocolate dome. Although, their sugar cookies are killer too. I love how they make European style bread daily. It's hard to find bread with a few ingredients- and many of the kneaders bread are made with three ingredients- flour, water, and salt. I can't wait for the new store to open off of Craycroft- because it's closer to me.

Try the three cheese cauliflower soup, and Asiago cheese bread! Service was friendly, soup was GREAT (and hot!), and the bread was fresh! It's affordable and not too loud. Nice atmosphere with big band music playing.

Excellent breads, cinnamon rolls and French toast. It's a favorite treat to buy their bread to make our own French toast but it's better in store. I've been to this specific one several times and each time it has been very clean with friendly and knowledgable staff. A great place to meet up with friends and chat over yummy food! Great for any meal of the day.

Not impressed. The veggies were clearly canned and tasted like mush. 

Will not go back!
They have the best Middle Eastern food. Never had a bad meal there. Everything tastes great.

I used to go to Samosa all the time years ago and now that I'm working downtown again, I expect to get there more often. I went a few months ago when they had more Caribbean offerings mixed in with the Indian offerings and thought it was pretty good then. I was there yesterday and now it's back to being all Indian and now they have a little gelato bar too (which I didn't try...darn them for making their buffet so good that I had no room for gelato ;).)

The food yesterday was good as usual. There was a good spicy eggplant dish that I kept going back for more of and the desserts were good too (though it would have been nice to have gulab jamin there instead of only in the gelato bar).

Turkey Bacon Avocado Salad. Delicious as always: freshly roasted turkey, and croutons. My go-to lunch at the office.

The drive through had speedy service today, even with 3 cars in line ahead of me. My order was correct and served with a smile.

I'm not sure why this place has an average rating of 2.0.
I had a wonderful experience with everyone at the office. Dr. Kuzma was also very helpful.

Hmmm, a long wait despite being the only one in front of the truck. The price is right for a tasty mid-day meal, but I immediately wished I'd gone for more falafel and less chicken. The chicken ended up dry and tasted sort of like it'd been sitting out for some time, while the falafel balls were juicy and flavorful. I think it ended up being like, $5.75 for a meal that was big enough (two sides of different kinds of rice, chicken, salad, hummus, and falafel) for lunch and dinner. 

The service was questionable. The woman who was working the truck was on the phone the entire time, and communicated to me mostly through gestures and whispered words. I would maybe go back, but will try the other nearby trucks first before making that decision.

They used to have great bagels. Now they're the same pre-ordered bagel you can get anywhere. It seems to be only this Cosi, because the one in Old City has the squagels typical of Cosi. 

Combined with the terrible service, there's really no reason to go here anymore.

I can't speak to the prices, because I was a guest here (at a wedding rehearsal dinner) but the food is delicious and the staff are attentive and lovely!  It felt like being at a dinner in someone's home.  We had dolmades, kibbe (for the meat-eaters), falafel, mujadara (lentils with rice and onions), labneh (soft cheese, almost yogurty in texture), baba ganoush and hummus and pita,  and finally skewers of grilled chicken and lamb.  There was also some Lebanese wine on offer that was tasty and unusual.  I'm looking forward to visiting again!

I was apprehensive about ordering from here given the reviews, but I was craving Indian food and didn't want to leave the house or pay $16 per entree. For around $35 we received good sized portions of meat samosas, chana masala, butter chicken, naan, and masala tea. Apart from the tea (which almost tasted like coffee), I was pretty happy with most everything. The garlic naan was okay but too doughy for my tastes. I also tried the peshwari naan because it sounded interesting, but the cherries seemed to be maraschinos and I couldn't taste the coconut at all. I think we ended up throwing half of it out.

Not sure if I'd dine in, but I'll probably order from here again. I figure as long as I stick with the basics I won't be disappointed.

Tried to order a pie and staff was extremely rude.  They wouldn't take an order because it was the day before Easter????? They claimed it was first come first serve.  They close at 9 pm, when I called at 3 to see if they had a chocolate pie, they said they were out of pies for the day!!  It obvious why parking lot is always empty!! Don't waste ur time here!

Have been using them for 2 years now and never a problem. Always explains what the problems are . Has saved me money many times. Mike and his wife, Liz his daughter and mechanic are always there and willing to help. Few times living close by I was given a ride home. Great shop !!

My brother and I ordered vegetarian lamb curry, vegetarian tikka masala, veggie pakora, samosas. ($36) The "pakora" were soggy pieces of greasy cauliflower. Inedible. The samosas were burnt and lacked flavor. We moved on to the curry, to discover after consuming a piece that we were given real lamb! I repeated several times on the phone that we wanted the soy lamb, and even referenced menu numbers. The woman who took our order even called back to confirm what I had said. I returned for a refund, and was treated rudely by the unapologetic man at the counter. His only statement after I commented on his rudeness was that he didn't take the order. San Samosa's food is bland and greasy, and the customer service abominable. Plenty of better options for indian in center city, NOT RECOMMENDED!!!

I'm giving Kneaders 5 stars for food and 3 for staff/cleanliness. This is my daughter's favorite place to eat and she loves the combo choices. Overall, it has a bakery, deli, gift shop feel and is a pretty cool place. The food is unbelievably good and has always been very fast yet fresh. They clearly use fresh ingredients and the breads all appear to be baked fresh...not 100% on that though. They have a rotating selection of pastries and soups and a pretty large assortment of sandwiches and salads. Only small criticism would be that more often than not, we need to give our tables a fresh wipe down...have seen others taking part in the same and the staff taking orders are very aloof and not really engaged with the dialogue--what I'd expect from a fast food chain.  Overall, the food will keep us coming back however.

Place is kinda similar to what was left of the restaurant business in Baghdad, first of all I want to clarify that we had a groupon. It said appetizers for 2, dinner for 2, and desert for 2 for 35$. Sounds like a good deal right ? NOOOO they charged us 5$ for a coca cola in a can and 5$ for a ice tea, plus added 25 $ tax to our bill and added his own gratuity to our bill as well. Then they insisted that we pay in cash sisnce we had a groupon, as they don't want to let groupon see that they are adding on additional charges that are not in the agreement. Now here is the worst part, the food was terrible, I mean terrible, They served my food on a pre-sectioned plate, the kind that you give to kindergarteners. I'm so not surprised and the kebabs, they were 90% girlled tomatoes and peppers, basically it was a veggie kebab with a side order or 2 or 3 chicken cubes. The bread wasn't worty of even being called bread, I think they bought that shit from mecca market and just threw it in the microwave . you can go to wah gi wah or some indian , paki , or Turkish place if you want good bread and kebabs.. The dinner winded up costing us 75$ and I swear you can make better food at home. The place is a scam and I have already reported them to groupon but now my last task has been accomplished , and that was to warn the public about these clowns and their treasure of garbage they call cedar's restaurant !

I am new to town as a travel nurse and decided to try Split Endz based on the Yelp reviews and the $75 for $100 coupon. So glad I did! My cut and color appointment was with Tricia who was amazing. I haven't trusted somebody to color my hair in over a year, and she nailed it. I wanted a sandy blonde that was close to my natural color and it is spot on. I couldn't be happier. Also, I had some money left over from my $100 coupon and they gave me a gift certificate to use the rest of it in the store. Definitely recommend and will go back before I leave in December.

Yelp reviews landed me in Cedars while I was on a trip to Philly and staying a block away.  From the website the limited days and hours they operate got me thinking it was very exclusive and perhaps a snob factor was included at no extra charge.  I was glad to find it was just your typical restaurant.  My called in take out order was ready within 10 minutes and very reasonable for the money.  The garlic chicken and spinach pie were were more than enough for dinner.  The spinach pie is a must try item.  It is a very simple concept of cooked spinach put into a pita bread shell but with a little lemon juice on it; wow.  If I ever stay near here on a future trip I will probably go back just for the spinach pie.
Great work and price I very fair! I get my eyebrows threaded here and they do a great job in men. I also take my mom here and she loves it too!
The food is cold and nasty the people are nice... I went twice and had same experience and will never go back...
Always enjoy Indian Buffets. Every time I pass this restaurant, it is never busy. The servers were friendly.
Located in my office building and good place to have lunch (especially in cold weather). My pick: Hot roasted veggie + tomato basil

Austin did a really nice job on my tat, was VERY pleased. Friend of mine had one done here too and it's awesome. Very reasonable prices too. If I get another one this is where I'll head to. I also plan to recommend this place to freiends.
Great middle eastern cuisine with a cozy and quiet atmosphere,  I eat here often and it never disappoints.
The lunch special is really good if you are in a hurry. The buffet is nice, with a decent selection. The music isn't bad either.

I bought a Groupon for this salon, usually I will research the salon first but I did not. My appointment was with Kelly. First impression, salon was beautiful! Bright, modern and most importantly CLEAN! Although I had a Groupon, I wasn't treated as such. If you Groupon, you know what I mean. She was wonderful and chit chatted like we were old friends. Wonderful experience and I told her I'd be back. I was looking for a new stylist, she was it. 

I called to make another appointment with Kelly and was told she no longer there. I hung up, disappointed. But I called back..... This salon was friendly, clean and upbeat. I had a good feeling that all of the stylists there were up to par as well. I made an appointment with Todd, I'm fuzzy with names. But I believe the only male there and from Canada. 

He got me in two days later for a partial highlight and cut. OUTSTANDING!  Hands down one of the best cuts I've had to date. Not only was he warm and personable, but I could tell he loved being a hair dresser.  I told him not to bother styling bc I had to shower before work. Normally a stylist would say, sweet! I'm done!  Not Todd. He still blowed and styled to make sure the cut and color was perfect. Kudos!


I work for a major wholesaler and am constantly stopped and asked who does my hair. Needless to say I'll be back. Thanks Todd and the great team at Split Endz

We just had Sunday dinner at this spot over the weekend.  We had never been here before, but purchased a half-price Groupon.  I Pita bread was definitely dry and stiff.  The service was great, maybe because we were the only customers there at the time.  The food was pretty good, though the portions were too small, especially the dessert portions.  Here's the kicker though, the Groupon price was what it should've been, however, they charged us tax (which would've been fine if it wasn't 10% tax!) and included a 25% gratuity! It wasn't the worst experience we've had, but we won't be going back.

I definitely prefer this place over its next door neighbor, the Corner Cafe or whatever it is. This place has the cutest desserts, the portion sizes are more than enough, and the service is quick and pleasant. Kneaders is the perfect lunch destination with ample soup, salad, and sandwich options.

Bllllllllllaaaaaaaannnnnndd.  

In a word, this describes their lunch buffet food.  Indian food?  Bland?  With a genre of food that utilizes curry, how could it be bland?  Some how, they do it.  Limited selection due to the vegetarian aspect and you have some surprisingly, yes, bland food.  

On top of it, the service was a little preoccupied with something else besides ringing me up at the register.  Booo!
This place is a hidden gem.  Phenomenal food matched with an intimate atmosphere.  The grilled chicken and rice is amazing.
Overpriced mediocre food. Spent $15 on a sandwich I could have made at home. I would not recommend this place.

It gets JAMMED here during lunch but don't let the long lines fool you. Great process from start to finish and they move you along with efficiency. 

I had half a sandwich a chicken/pesto mix with a bowl of soup. I get it it's summer in Philly and I ordered tomato soup. I don't care as it's DELISH! 

A medium lemonade rocked it. Easy in easy out. I miss COSI so much as they closed the Columbus, OH locations. :(

What a perfect place for a party!  We recently celebrated my daughter's graduation and had a wonderful evening.  The staff could not have been more welcoming and accommodating. The restaurant is not usually open on Tuesdays, but they opened specially for us so that we could mark this special occasion.  The food was delicious and plentiful.  We loved all the appetizers, including the hummus, baba ganoush, falafel, lentil rice, cauliflower, stuffed cabbage and grape leaves.  But the highlight was definitely the lamb and chicken kebabs.  And, best of all, our gluten free daughter and guest could eat almost all the dishes.  We highly recommend Cedars, and look forwarded to returning soon.

This is my go to spot when I want a tasty salad.  I usually get the cobb no bacon and add dried cranberries. 

Yum!

Today i tried ordering ahead and my order was perfect and was ready when promised.    So glad I don't need to wait on the line anymore :)    It does get busy during the week at lunchtime.

When I want a lunch that is filling, delicious, and ethnic tasting, I go to this food truck located near the corner of 38th and Walnut Street.  Everything is homemade and prepared fresh daily.

For the price, this food truck can't be beat.  I normally get the grilled chicken with grape leaves platter for my lunch.  With this comes a full sized pita bread, tabbouleh, hummus, Tzatziki, yellow rice and lentil rice.  You have the option of onions and hot sauce.  This is all for $5.25.

They have a grill in the truck to heat up whatever you order.

I can't do the menu justice here, but they have vegetarian and meat dishes and many small items which you can purchase.  Prices range from $1.00 to $5.25.

They cater and will take orders over the phone for fast pick-up.  They run from 11 AM to around 5 PM, M-F (even though their menu is listed as 8 PM).  In one order, if you order 9 platters, the 10th is free!

I'm giving them 2 stars because I love Cosi and their food in general.  I prefer their breakfast food to Dunkin Donuts, but I'll choose DD every time because the service at this Cosi is painfully slow as I'm trying to get to work.  I'll get there with 10-15 minutes to spare, have maybe one customer ahead of me, and have to walk out before anyone even takes my order.  Most times there is only one guy taking orders.  Just a hint, when a customer has been waiting, don't take time to yell across to your co-worker to find out how her night was until you've helped your customer.

I told the manager at my former local Cosi that he needs to come up to Philly and get these employees working more efficiently.

if you liked the "old" samosa, just avoid this place at all costs. myself? i had loved the cheap buffet, great food, snazzy vibe of the old joint. so i was doubly sad when i went to the "new" version.

the way it is now? oh, man...rock hard naan, greasy & soggy samosas, and pasta?? what the fuck? pasta? yuck. i'd rather just cook at home, thanks.
Felt a little rushed by the doc and she didn't diagnose anything, just passed me onto specialists even for a nose infection.  Takes forever to get an appointment.

Run for the hills. 

I went here with my boyfriend who was born & raised in Tampa and the last time he made an appearance at China Pearl was when he was 13 years old. 
 
He told me this great story about their food and how they used to have unlimited crab legs and how "delicious" it was. 

So we went and I wanted to walk out the moment I set foot inside, but my boyfriend is an odd one that once he walks in regardless of the situation we are going to eat there. 

This establishment is a horror show and no longer is the China Pearl he once knew. 

The food is lukewarm, the sushi is alarming and should not be touched with a ten foot pole, the ambience is depressing as you stare at the surrounding delusional people eating the bland, weirdly flavored food, and going up for second helpings.

On top of all that there is a sign on the buffet that says "If you need your food heated up ask your server"

That right there should have been a dead giveaway, but I still proceeded to try the food that whispered "We've been out here since this morning, we're still good, I promise. Just try us."

Nothing, Nothing, NOTHING, except for the water, Mountain Dew mix, and the waitresses being on top of their refill game was good. 

I am not too depressed for my wallet loss since it was ~10 dollars to eat there, but to those who are considering this save your time and your intestines and go somewhere else.

I was in Tucson visiting my cousin and I needed a blowout. She recommended this salon, but Todd in particular. 

I walked in to a nicely appointed salon. It looked upscale and was very clean. I was greeted by Todd and he led me over to wash my hair. I wish that he had looked at my hair before so he would have an idea of how I liked it, but whatever. 

To start the shampoo he used smelled really good. I asked what brand and oddly he didn't tell me. Oh well, moving on. I was checking into Yelp as he was washing my hair and that apparently annoyed him. He kept taking two fingers and pushing my forehead back to wash my hair. Let me tell you, the difference between where my head was and where he wanted it was negligible. It's not like he was cutting it, he was washing it. He was obviously having a hard time because the angle of my face while using my phone was not to his liking. He pushed my head back THREE times. I almost got really bent, but it was my cousin's salon so I didn't want to have an aneurism right there in the place she goes to so I'll just Yelp it.

He took me over to his chair and I wasn't paying any attention. Before I knew it he had finished drying it and was dragging a flat iron out and about to put it on my hair. I never use flat irons, I don't like the severe look that it produces (very, very flat, straight up against my head) and I'm not fond of the heat because my hair already has so many strikes against it (curly, porous, dry, colored, etc). I also told him when I got there that I wanted my hair smooth with a slight curl on the end (under). None of that happened. I don't really appreciate someone styling my hair the way they want to. I would have appreciated if he had asked me how I wanted it. I DID say blowout, NOT flat iron. Sorry, but it pissed me off. 

While we work out how to do my hair he's talking to me like I haven't been coloring my hair red for 20 years. I understand being helpful, but I felt like he was treating me like a child. None of his helpful hints were that helpful. 

I felt really uncomfortable around him, he doesn't have a customer oriented approach and he seems really unapproachable. 

The only reason I gave it two stars, was because the blow out was super cheap and the salon was nice.

Also, what is with a name for a salon that describes what you DON'T want your hair to have? Weird.

The wait for this place is very long. The line is long but dont be decieved. It is probably because the lady cranks out food slowly so the line just does not decrease. The line is not long because this place is delicious.

The woman is very nice if you go during closing time. She will offer extra hummus or give you larger portions if you come during closing time. The food is ok. It is not good, but it is not bad either. Just typical middle eastern food cart.

The falafels were sort of dry and they were not flavorful. They were just a little salty. The hummus is not very memorable either. It was a little more lemony and has less of a tahini taste to it than other though. The hummus is better than the babaganoush here so if you are debating, get the hummus instead.

That being said if you really do want this type of food, walking a little bit more for to Hummus is better even if you have to pay a little more. The quality is so much better than this food truck.

I stopped in for lunch today and am glad I did! Second time here and tried the chicken salad croissant sandwich with a little side salad. It was very good and the croissant was baked to perfection! The chicken is chunky which I like and it has a nice flavor to it. Topped with water chestnuts to give it just a little crunch to it. Lots of great choices and I see they also serve breakfast. I'll be back soon. Fast, courteous service.

This byo has very good Lebanese food.  The pita bread is baked fresh.  The falafels are well seasoned and cooked perfectly.  The shwarma and kabobs are cooked very well.  The lamb was tender.  Also, the rice was not overcooked or dry.  They recently renovated the place as well, so it looks modern and clean.   I highly recommend this spot!

I went to the newly refurbished cedars last night after a long hiatus.  We were encouraged to order the mezes platter which all eight of us did.  Be warned - it is a mountain of food but a terrific way to try almost all the appetizers.  Everything was delicious but a special call out of the home cooked pita, the babaganoush, and my husband loved the chicken shish kebab.

Incredibly friendly staff and they let us watch the pita being made which puffs up instantly in the oven.  This restaurant is a great option for casual dining with interesting and tasty food.

I've driven past this place twice a day for months, and have tried eating here several times on Sunday mornings. Something about a Sunday morning makes baked goods and coffee sound much better. Alas if you don't know already Kneader's is full blood Mormon, and closed every Sunday a la Chick Fil A. 

Finally made it in on a Saturday and we're greeted with visual overload. Menu layout reminds me of Panera Bread and all the tables are granite and mahogany. They really went for it. 
But what you notice first is the smorgasbord of baked goods on the other side of the sneeze guard: eclairs, cheesecakes, coffee cakes, cookies, fruit tarts... it's all a bit distracting. 

We went with the all you can eat French Toast, which is the solid choice when you want to maximize food-to-dollar-spent ratio. Bear with me as I get a little weird: I didn't care all that much for the food. I don't like bread much (I know, just stay with me) and was hoping for a more eggy or sweet flavor profile. A good way to describe this is "airy," very bread-focused. It came beautifully presented with sliced strawberries, whipped butter and homemade syrup. The price? $5.50. For all you can eat. All day, every day (but not Sundays...)

So there it is. A 5 star review for a place where I consider the food kind of meh. I'll be back to check out their soups and desserts, and I still recommend you start with the French Toast. Unless you're a weirdo and don't like bread. 

Don't let this place go out of business folks.

The "NEW" samosa recently opened and you'll know it by the flags they've been flying across the sidewalk on Walnut and the flourescent signs that advertise ridiculously cheap lunch and dinner buffets.

The food is all veggie and on the higher end of decent.  You don't even notice you're missing meat b/c you're too busy listening to the hip hop and pop Indian music they play.

There was nothing bad about the food at Samosa's, but there was nothing that good about it either.  It's typical Indian buffet fare, nothing that will knock your socks off.  The restaurant was uncomfortably hot though, and due to the selection of items in the buffet, the price should have been knocked down a few bucks to $7.99.  All in all, it was decent but unremarkable and probably not something I'm going to crave and want to come back for.
I guess I paid for a full soup instead of half? I come here a lot during lunch time, just for the convenient location

I usually get the lunch buffet here to go during my break from work, since  it is much quicker to be in and out of here than other popular spots that serve lunch on Walnut. 

I enjoy the food, but it is upsetting that the lunch buffet that was once $5 is now $8. I know that they serve meat now, and didn't previously, but I assume that many of their customers are vegetarian still, and are not getting any sort of bonus with the extra three dollars they are paying.

I also don't think that adding meat and adding ice cream to their menu got them a larger customer base, since it is usually pretty empty in there.

I had the country lentil soup and it was alright, nothing crazy. The flatbread that came with it was pretty good though. I liked the ambiance, and the staff was friendly, especially the cashier girl, she was a sweetheart.

I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here, but it sure beats micky d's down the street. Overall i had a good experience.

Like the 4 stars proclaim... 'Yay! I'm a fan.' I work relatively close (5 blocks or so) and come here for lunch on occasion. The food is decent, not spectacular... but better than many of the reviews also. I used to come with vegetarian peeps from time to time and was a fan of it then.

But... now they serve meat... so I am much more partial to it now. West Indian food is pretty much a staple in my diet, so when I strolled into Samosa I was very pleased to see curry goat on the buffet. At $7.99 for the lunch buffet it's a good deal. At $7.99 for all-you-can-eat curry goat... it's a great deal. They had curry chicken as well today... pretty solid. The tandori chicken is somewhat dry, but again... it's all about the curry goat for me... I'd give it 5 stars if I were only voting on that.

I have never had a problem with the service here... never bad, never exceptional.

Oh, and one more thing... the somosa's were outstanding today as well.

Overall solid food at a decent bang for your buck. But... if your jonesin' some curry goat... skip a platter at your West Indian spot and eat as much as you can here.

Best Lebanese food. Wish it was in my neighborhood, i'd be here everyday!
Can't  beat $8.00 for lunch. It cost mor to eat at a shitty fast food restaurant.

We used a half price groupon and still the bill was way too high for what we got. The food is good but portions are very small, not worth the price. I have had just as good food in order and sit-down or take out type of place for a lot cheaper and more generous portions. Mint tea was very good though :)

I've been to this place a few times, but it's been a while.  I was hoping it would still be as good as I remember.

We were seated inside.  The decor is exactly what you'd expect for a Middle Eastern restaurant... its a bit 'off' but upscale, clean, and very nice.  Just not what I'd call 'stylish'.

We were seated by the window which in my eyes is always a plus.  We had a restaurant.com $25 voucher and you have to order 2 Maza's.  I'm a vegetarian, and my boyfriend is quite the opposite... so I was a bit concerned that I'd get the typical veggieburger treatment.

Not in the least!  They just kept bringing out plates and plates of food- fallafel, hummus, baba ganoush, these fried meat-ball things that my boyfried was gaga over, bean salad, taboulli, a veggie and rice dish (my boyfriend got lamb and chicken shish kabobs), by the time we left, we were literally about to fall over.  EVERYTHING was worth a) the price we paid, and b) the space it took up in my stomach.  The pace was a bit quick, but our waitress recognized us stalling a bit, and told the kitchen to slow it down without us even having to say anything.... so obviously the service rocked.

BEST PART- this place is a BYO so grab a bottle of wine or a growler of beer and enjoy.  

We walked out with a $40 bill, some leftovers, and a big smile on our faces.  I wouldn't recommend the Maza if you're headed out afterwards, as you'll fall asleep, but I recommend Cedars for every meal you'll ever eat.  Its delicious, reasonably priced, conveniently located, the service is great, etc.  A true gem right off of South Street.
They were out of one-cent stamps yesterday and frequently do not have a great selection of stamps.

I recently ate here for lunch with 2 friends one Saturday afternoon. For $6.99 for the buffet- I was super happy. They had all of the traditional Indian foods you'd see at any other Indian buffet and they also include a nice salad bar, iced tea, and selection of desserts. However, if you're vegetarian... be warned! They just made it a meat-friendly place. All-in-all I was very satisfied and I will be back there next time I'm in the area.

How I heard of this place: Flora recommended hitting up the Chinese buffet on our way back from two hours of sun and swimming at Clearwater beach. It sounded like this was one of Carl & Flora's go-to restaurants; even Chris recognized the newly renovated interior.

Type of cuisine: Chinese, sushi, American. Everything from General Tso's chicken to Crab Rangoon, gyoza to fried plantains, boiled dumplings and fried chicken to crinkle-cut fries, fish sticks and won ton soup. Two large buffets of meats and vegetables, and one smaller buffet for the sushi, fruit (limited to watermelon) and desserts: cake, ice cream, coconut macaroons, chocolate pudding, fried sesame balls with red bean paste and Asian-style donuts tossed in sugar.

Ambiance: The red and yellow exterior, from signage to roof to outside walls with green accents surround an almost completely windowless, one-story building. The entryway opens up onto a small foyer with a brown, wooden shelving unit ornamented with Chinese artwork and a gold, waving cat figure. A small, jade elephant holds sprouting bamboo on its back, as patrons make their way into the restaurant. The large, open, newly renovated seating area, offers chair and booth seating around thickly laminated wooden tables, some in a deep burgundy, others in lighter cream colors. Waist-height walls are built to separate spaces one from the other, creating more intimate settings where larger parties can maintain boundaries. Red-cushioned and backed chairs with green legs or red faux-leather booth benches sit next to the tables, which are set far enough apart to allow for ease of getting up and sitting back down with new plates of food, piled high. Staff are always readily available, but inconspicuous, which gives the impression of empty plates mysteriously disappearing as you are taking your last bite or are at the buffet for your second, third or fourth helping. The music of Michael Jackson and Mariah Carey can be heard overhead, set to elevator-themes creating a light lounge feel.

What I ordered: The four of us eating at China Pearl enjoyed the buffet. I sampled nearly one of everything: Crab Rangoon, General Tso's Chicken, Sesame Chicken, Bourbon Chicken, Sweet & Sour Pork, Broccoli & Beef, chow mein, rice noodles with spring onions and egg, a chicken nugget, grilled potatoes, fried bananas, mushrooms, green beans, broccoli, stuffed mushrooms, Pepper chicken, teriyaki chicken, and then I made my way to the dessert bar. I had two Sesame Balls, one and a half donuts, tasted the coconut macaroon, a bite of white cake with a thin layer of cream & strawberry preserves, and a spoon of chocolate pudding.

What I loved: Of the main entrees, I most enjoyed the Pepper Chicken. One of my dining companions agreed, with General Tso's getting our third dining companions rave review. Our fourth diner enjoyed the fried chicken and desserts! I always like the sesame balls and this occasion was no different. But the thick, fried dough(nut) was delicious and warranted a full one to myself, rather than solely the first, shared donut.

Why I loved it: I loved that the food was served in smaller dishes so that it could be freshly topped in less time than many buffets I have visited. The space was clean, quiet and open. Our dishes were picked up quickly, inviting us to return to the buffets for more...and more...

Cost: Average

I absolutely love the salads here as the tomato basil soup, but I swear they are cheap on their ingredients. Most often when I order a salad, they dont even include a full scoop of the ingredient (and the scoop is smaller than an average ice cream scoop). Only one time that I have been here have i gotten full scoops and oh, it sure was a delicious salad.

I agree worh Annie S. I had a great experience here. Evertyone was friendly and courteous, and Dr. Kuzma couldn't have been nicer. I am a complete wreck about having bloodwork done, and was put completely at ease, and had no idea I was stuck until it was over. Sure, I had to wait a bit before being seen, but no longer than any other doctor's office I've visited.

I've been to this location twice and have no complaints. It was my first time trying Cosi, and I really like the food. Both times I've been during lunch hours and it hasn't been crazy busy. Ive tried the turkey avocado sandwich and the turkey club. Both really good. The bread is great - it's like a flatbread type thing. And you can watch them make it/make adjustments. Important: The mojito lemonade is amazing!! Definitely worth trying. One downside from today: I always take my food to go and my chips were missing from my bag when I got back to my office. I should have checked before I left the store, but the person checking me out asked if I wanted chips or carrots, so I just assumed he put it in. Other than that, I'll be back. It's down the street from my job and they have good sandwiches for lunch.

The reason I go to lunch buffets is usually because of time constraints. Doing outside sales I am often in a time crunch.   I can duck in, eat real quick, and get back about my business. That's what caused me to stop here. Expectations are not high for these kind of places but here is an expectation of some quality.
The good: In spite of the fixtures being worn the place was clean. The wait staff was professional. Most of the food seemed to be fresh.
The bad: Most of the food being fresh doesn't mean all of the food. Several item were obviously old including the sushi (which I was afraid to try) rice and some entree's. I was there around 11:30 on a Monday and got the idea on some items they were left over from Sunday dinner. 
The Ugly: The food wasn't nasty but was mostly just tasteless. I tried several items trying to find something I'd enjoy, never did. You can get nourished here but that's about it.
I believe in second chances on dining so if I was in the area and in the mood for Chinese I might give them another try. Just to make sure it wasn't a bad day but I won't go out of my way to go there. There's several eateries in the area which offer much better dining.

Being Indian I usually don't like to talk bad about Indian places but if you have the word samosa in your name, shouldn't you have some good samosas?!?! I got fooled. Sigh.

Naan was a little dry but saag paneer took care of that. I felt there wasn't enough paneer, but then again I'm a paneer-holic. 

There are better Indian options in the area but for a quick bite without going across town, drop by this place. Just don't go in expecting alot.
Amazing food, great ambience, super friendly staff. The food is incredibly authentic. The lamb is amazing. Highly recommend.

Good cheap center city Indian eats. The buffet was extensive, wellstocked and seemed fresh. The owner is this cute little Guyanese-Indian lady who is super nice. A great way to get your Indian food fix. Not a super fancy place, ambiance is pretty minimalist.

Hello everyone, I am a physician visiting San Samosa Restaurant for the 1st time and would like to extend my gratitude for the delicious dinner I had yesterday and today. I am in the Philadelphia region for a  Diabetic conference and was pretty skeptical about trying out Indian food ( I love the food my wife prepares back home) however a fellow colleague heard of this restaurant and we decided to give it a try. I must say it was so amazing and with a great low price that we returned for a second night tonight!
 I had the dinner buffet the 1st night which allowed me to indulge in various traditional Indian dishes including my all time favorite Saag Paneer. Tonight I decided to try a masala dosa from the menu and that too was savory and crisp, cooked to perfection and must I add it was so big it extended beyond the large platter it was served on. I'm here for several days more and am eager to spread the word so others can experience such tasty home-style Indian food. My wife will definitely be happy to know I'll be fed so well while here on my trip!

Luckily I had a Groupon, or I would have felt guilty spending more money to come here.  For dinner at 8PM on a Wed night, we were the only ones in here.  The waiter was extremely nice and attentive which is the main reason I'm giving this place 2 stars instead of 1.  Unfortunately, the food just wasn't very good.

For apps we got the Taramasalta which was overwhelmingly salty and the pita it came with tasted kind of stale.  We also got the grilled octopus which came over a salad dressed w/ a balsamic dressing.  The octopus tasted like rubber.  I've actually have never had such bad octopus before.  

Entrees: The lamb kabobs came as 2 tiny skewers with a total of 4 small pieces of lamb.  The lamb was also so overcooked and totally stuck to the metal skewers that I could barely get it off.  The rice it came with, however, was pretty good.  We also got this salmon entree with some kind of tahini cream sauce over it which was the only redeeming aspect of the meal.  It was pretty good, although the salmon was undercooked and we had to send it back once.

The baklava was also pretty good for dessert.  All in all, I probably won't come back here again.

I was very worried after reading the reviews, I was a bit leery coming here. The sign outside says the place is San Samosa.

The buffet is a bit run down (you know how food gets a skin on top from drying out). Some of the descriptions were a bit sketchy too. But like any buffet, I pulled up a chair and sampled just about everything. They don't use a lot of care in preparation, as I got a few bites of cartilage in the Tikka Masala. The veggie dishes were a bit dried out.

The food was edible, even the Tikka tasted good. If I lived in the neighborhood, I probably wouldn't be a regular here.

Called at 9:33 for a restuarant that closes at 10. The, what sounded like the owner, mumbled an incoherent response why they were closing early. I asked for a clarification and he hung up. That service is lifespan-reducingly terrible..

I visited this terrible and tax fraud place on 5th september 2011( labor day at 8:30 pm) . I and my husband got a combo for 39$ from travel zoo. I have filed a tax fraud to IRS for this restraunt. I want to inform everybody please do not visit this place if possible. We were charged randomly 7$ as tax and 18$ as SERVICE CHARGE. Total of 25$ ( the receipt was not valid, as they randomly wrote on loose piece of paper and handed to us and strictly told us to pay by cash. I want to make sure you guy are aware before visiting this place. They were many student around the area, so I think they do not care as food was cheap.. I want to make sure we all fight against this. PLEASE DO NOT VISIT THIS PLACE. Moreover I ordered SPANAKOPITA ( spinach and cheese in puff pastry) which was microwaved. Food quality was worst and even 2 serves were total improffesional wearing some crazy clothes with hair loose open and not washed properly. Please do not visit. Please contact through email to ask more about it.

I've been here several times to get piercings done and Katie is great. She takes her time and really makes sure you like and approve of where she intends to pierce you. The prices are fair and she has always done a great job. Would recommend to a friend.

An OK place.

The wine by the glass is expensive for it's terroir.

Best to order just the standard appetizers b/c you get the same sides on any dinner plate.

Skip the deserts, they were dry and very hard. The coffee will need 3-4 sugars and keep you up all night.

We had a great and very satisfying meal here on a whim and we do not regret it. The Shawarma was very well spiced and quite satisfying. The arnabeet, a new dish to us, from their hors d'oeuvre sampler was particularly outstanding. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. We will be returning.

I made the trek here on the recommendation of a co-worker. The food quality was fine - slightly better than average Middle Eastern food - and, theoretically good value for money - ASSUMING YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR. 

I ordered a kefta and grape leaves platter, and was certainly charged for one. But, when I opened up my container of food, there was NO kefta. Kind of a big mistake since it's the centerpiece of the platter. All I was left with was basically a Styrofoam container full of rice and a tiny mound of hummus. It was no fun having to face the rest of the workday 6 dollars short and with a growling stomach.

Can't attribute this error to them being too busy - I was one of two people in line. Maybe they were having a bad day and it was my bad luck to catch them at that time, but I won't be going back.
I really wanted to like this place.  But it's just not good. The chicken is over-cooked and chewy, the salads are warm and wilted, and nothing has much taste.

Okay y all I was in tuson for a few day and I had ran out of my vape juice . So I had at this other place we are not going too name . Cause they just total sucked ass. But I found this place from my great Yelp app and you great people . I went too the vape and I swear nothing but cool people.  They listen to what I was looking for toke the time too find the juice i would like . Tryed them out . Well I would give this shop a 100 stars cause the too workers where great .  So I got 3 t0 50 mls bottle and a 1o . And a new mod set up cause I just had fallen in love with my little alien. Best smoke shop for a vapeing in the area .  Thanks guys.

My husband and I loved this restaurant. The food is to die for:hubby said it was the best shish kebab he's had in a long time and I loved the vegetarian choices - I chose an eggplant and vegetable dish. We also enjoyed the baklava, which was just right. We used a restaurant.com coupon and because the prices are so unbelievably reasonable for the food you get, we couldn't get the bill up to $50, so they kindly prorated the discount. It's a nice location near Headhouse Square in the Society Hill area. Very attractive place. I would definitely recommend this.

That staff were super friendly. There were many breakfast options to pick from. For my first time. So glad to see so many healthy options. Clean, quite , food was amazing. I look forward to my next visit.

Great restaurant! Great food! So happy to finally get such a delightful restraint! All of the pastries and cookies are tasty; My husband craves the, "all you can eat French toast" I have never had a bad experience at Kneaders! We did go opening night and it was jam packed! I can't wait to go back when it isn't quite as busy;)

I used to love Samosa when I lived in Center City.  The owner was so nice and friendly and would sometimes sit down to chat with you.  I was sad to hear that he was having health problems and that they had to close their doors.  

When they re-opened I was anxious to come back, but alas, it was a dissappointment.  The food was at best "mediocre".   The prices have gone up (except take-out is super cheap) and the quality has gone down.  Not sure if I'll be back.

I left a prior review about Kim after my first ever experience with highlights.  It was my first time seeing Kim.  I was impressed.   I now have seen her for the 4th time I believe.  I have come to trust her judgment like none other.  And I am not one to trust a hair dresser easily with my hair!  She's a natural talent.  She really listens to what you want and goes beyond expectations!  Thank you again, Kim!

The decorum is nice and the atmosphere is relaxing. They offer a wide variety of soups, sandwiches and pastries.  I had the Reuben sandwich and my wife had the Orange Citris salad. Both entries were less than satisfactory. Their Reuben isn't as good as Beyond Bread's.

This wonderful Palestinian stand single-handedly fills in a good portion of the shocking dearth of Arabic food in the Philadelphia area. Hanan is a sweetheart, and her falafel and baba ghannouj are always delicious  and homemade. I think it's fair to say that this is the best falafel I've had in the U.S. (outside of someone's house, that is). It's also wonderfully cheap, which is great for us college-student types. As a vegetarian, I haven't tried any of the meat options, but my dad had some chicken shawarma and said it was very tasty as well. 

In this era of "pita pocket" and "pita pit" feaux-Arabic food stops in mall food courts, it's always hugely exciting to find fresh Arabic food made the right way. Oh, and in the spirit of keeping it authentic, for God's sake (and your own) don't dilute the flavor of the food with gobs of hot sauce.

I went to Cedars tonight with some friends for my friends bday. One word: Unbelievable! The service was amazing, the food was mouth watering and Ghassan, I believe the owner, was a delight and took photos of our group and went above and beyond. We shared several apps from the hummus, spanakopita, calamari, cabbage, and falafels to name a few and all dishes were prepared to order, fresh and so tasty!!!! I have been here at least four times and I will be back again! Keep up the great work!!!

Great ambience, love the food, cool decor. This place has extremely long waits in the summer time, especially during center city sips. I usually get a good waiter/waitress that is easy going and helpful, however, the last time I was there the waitress didn't show up.

In any case, besides the waiting time, this place is definitely a go to spot.

This is the only Middle Eastern place to go. 
Best Chicken Shawarma in Philadelphia. 
Their fresh Pita will put anyone else to shame. 

Great people, and all around.
Probably the worst buffet I have ever eaten at, everything was cold and was obviously sitting a while before I ate it......people were nice.

This place is devastatingly close to my work, so I'm going to be a regular regardless, but they're nothing to write home about.  I love Cosi's "Lighter Side" TBM and the Tomato Aurora Basil soup, and its a bit overpriced in my opinion, but still a lot of food for less than $10.

Here's what to expect:  You walk in, and there are two lines.  You get in the left line if the only things you want are soups or salads, or you get in the line on the right if you want sandwiches or anything else.  Unless its a drink; theres a separate line for that, too.  In the sandwich, etc. line, there is somebody standing there writing down your order.  If you want a hot sandwich, the guy hands the sandwich people a ticket and you go stand in line to pay then wait around awkwardly by the door and somebody will eventually bring you your sandwich.  If you want a cold sandwich (such as the tbm mentioned above), you get handed a ticket which you hand to the sandwich people and stand there awkwardly until somebody hands you a sandwich; then you stand in line to pay.  So yes, line waiting and awkward standing seem to come standard.  

I've only ordered to-go thus far.  Although there appears to be an upstairs, I have yet to find the stairs.  The downstairs seating is limited.

Its a decent spot for lunch, as long as your expectations are too high.

I stopped by this truck after my dog's appointment at UPenn's veterinary hospital. While driving, I saw a bunch of trucks, but being the hummus-addict I am, I had to go try this one.

I ordered a falafel & hummus ($4.50). It was ok. They were a bit stingy on everything except the pita they wrapped it in. The taste itself wasn't bad.

I'll try a different truck next time I'm in this neck of the woods.

1 star...if that...Absolutely the worst experience here. I have to mention how ridiculous they handle their online "coupons"--just very dumb. The coupon says 25% off tattoos & piercings...tattoos AND piercings and he's going to say "it's only for tattoos..." When clearly the coupon says...tattoos AND piercings ...25% off..-_- anyways now on to the rest of it...last year the girl who pierced our noses did an excellent job. Over the course of the year the wife's came out so we decided to get hers re-pierced in the same spot as the first one was. So the piercer Austin Knger(that's how it looks like it's spelled on the card) gets the wife and the result is atrocious. It doesn't even sit on the nose properly and he had NO CLUE what she was talking about when he said "all done. Check it out" she was trying to explain how the bar is too big and isn't bent into her nose properly. He said its "too allow for swelling " but no. It's just plain an simple eff'd up. It's been about 6hrs since she got it done and has had to reposition it more like 50+ times only for it to stick out the top of her nose  again and jab the other side of her nostril. Plain and simple ...horrible job. Will not be back
the reason for the low star is that i bought a  tank here they call the C-5 broke on me the next day im hoping to stop by after work to see if they can help me fix it or show me what im doing wrong .

Really good food, very friendly and helpful staff, quiet atmosphere.  We loved it.  We had a coupon and were told we had to pay cash because of that which was sort of weird but other than that, had an excellent meal.

Try the cheese kanafeh for dessert!

Great food! I enjoyed the arnabeet (fried cauliflower) and baba ghanoush on the cedars combo platter. Vegetarian options excellent. Friendly server.

I was happily surprised on this visit to find they have new chairs!! The previous chairs were too plush, oversized and dominated the dining area. The newer chairs are much better and makes for a more pleasant dining atmosphere.
BLT sandwich was amazing. Workers are fine but they could been more calm down. They could provide extra like free wifi and more portions. System could use some work to run it better.
A coworker just came back to work from Samosa to tell me the same woman tried to rip her off AGAIN.  Ridiculous.
Had breakfast, food was fresh and delicious, quickly served, nice people. The decor available for purchase is unusual and cool. We'll be coming back

I've lived in many cities and had to deal with a lot of post offices and this branch on Grays Ferry Road will surely ruin your day if you have to deal with them. I've had countless packages that they have said they tried to deliver, yet there was never a pink slip in my mailbox. The times I have gone into the branch they're so busy doing everything but helping customers that they make it seem like you are a nuisance. Oh and forget about mail delivery, you better hope that you don't have a substitute carrier because the mail will almost definitely be delivered to the right number address but wrong street. I'm at the point with this branch that I will pay extra to have FedEx or UPS deliver packages instead if deal with the nightmare that is the Grays Ferry Branch.

I've seen drexel family medicine for years because they were convenient. For many years I said the physicians had terrible bedside manor, but otherwise I had pleasant experiences with the staff and appreciated having all of my care organized under one roof. A year ago a resident misdiagnosed a potential cancer scare as a pulled muscle before the attending came in and said I needed and ultrasound immediately. I still didn't leave the practice. Then I showed up for a physical which I scheduled months ago and even though they didn't have me on the schedule, I was calm and understanding. When they weren't able to find an alternate appointment time that fit with my schedule I grew irritated but didn't raise my voice and was told (by the staff) to stop being rude. 3 staff people (receptionist, office manager and a tech) stood in the window and said "don't even bother with her" like we were getting in a fight in the school cafeteria. Needless to say, I finally hit the wall and will not be going back to drexel family medicine.

Burgers are over cooked. Chicken wings were from anorexic chickens, they were skimpy on the hummus, but they are kosher. I ordered from there because they are kosher, close and fast food. But the service and the food aren't that great, not to mention a little steep on the prices.

Excellent food! This is truly a hidden treasure. The hummus is top notch. The mixed grill with tabbouleh is fresh and delicious. The variety of menu options feels much more unique than your typical Mediterranean restaurant. I will definitely be coming back again.

Love Love Love all the delicious pastries!!
Gave 4 stars , because of the portion size = amount charged for a sandwich  (croissant) and the dessert prices are a bit steep. However,  everything is delicious and the service was excellent! Keep it up!

Finding a reliable mechanic is not easy. Like anything else, you need to shop around. Big corporations and even dealerships work off of commission. They will tell you something needs to be fixed just to make money. Mike definitely listed off the dozens of repairs I needed, but he proceeded to assure me that all I needed for it to run were two specific parts. The repairs he did quote me on seemed a bit high, so I called around for other opinions. It turned out that it was a fair price after all. Although Mike never actually did any repairs for me because I decided to trade my car in, he could not have been more patient and respectful to me when I know I had been an absolute pain for several days.

i actually really enjoyed the lunch time all you can eat buffet...three times.  some items are definite misses, but i always find a couple hits (last time i enjoyed the korma and saag paneer). these two definitely were not bland! lots of variety, and you gotta love the all you can eat fried goodies. granted sometimes the food is luke-warm, but considering the price (6 bucks) i don't mind. 

btw the only other indian food i've eaten in philly is tiffin and i was definitely not a fan...

Pretty tasty and a good deal.   

Samosa has the usual vegetarian dishes, plus a few you don't see too often.  They aren't overly fancy dishes, it's just honest, good Indian food.

And as you'd expect, the samosas are very addictive and worth a visit all on their own.

I have eaten at Cedars a few times now and I cannot say that I was disappointed with anything. The staff is gracious and attentive, the decor is awesome and the food is delicious. I have gone alone and with groups of people. My sister requests Cedars every time she visits. The falafel is tasty and crisp and the grape leaves are superb. Even my finicky boyfriend who is terrified of food he cannot pronounce is comfortable at this restaurant. Lebanese is my favorite cuisine and I really enough this place. A few of the reviews question the prices but I don't find them to be outrageous for a casual sit down meal in the city. Sure it would be great if it were cheaper but the price doesn't keep me away. Worth a visit.

We got to try Kneaders and we loved it! The food was so delicious even my picky children enjoyed it. They have great sandwiches, soups, and salads. Their desserts were so delicious. We love the food and the service was just as great. They were fast, efficient, and welcoming. Looking forward to trying more things on their menu.

POSITIVES:
+ There's a drive-thru window!!  So if you're craving a fancier sandwich/soup/etc  (so you don't have to get a Grinder at the other place!) or your kid fell asleep on the drive and you don't wanna wake him and need food, this place could be a savior!
+  It's not bad but it's not anything I crave.   To me, its similar to Panera bread.  I had the French dip sandwich and a mango smoothie -- both were a.ok.
+ If you need to shop, they have seriously cute kitchen/garden/gift shop items in the center that you can conveniently grab and pay for along with your meal

NEGATIVES:
-Finding cute things to shop for when you really just need to grab a meal and quit shopping!

I have come three times for a visit with Dr. Kuzma and have always waited at least an hr before I actually see her. Not to mention that I am always called to the back about a half an hr after my appt time, so in total, give yourself about an hour and a half wait time.

Not only do I wait a long time, I am always incredibly rushed by Dr. Kuzma. She checked my lungs and barely wait for me to inhale, let alone begin my exhale, before she moved to a new spot on my lungs. She did not palpate my lymph nodes at all (and I was here for a physical), she barely tested my reflexes. 

I then asked for some titers as I am about to start school and need some immunization history. She said that she had ordered them, but it has been two weeks ( I have called twice about this problem with no answers) and apparently the lab did not request for these titers, even though they are listed on my chart. I have learned to always request a print out of what happened during my visit so that when I call I can give a detailed and exact description of what happened. 

After this, I am definitely finding a new primary care doctor. Dr. Kuzma cares more about being your friend than your doctor, and that is not why I come to the doctor.

Friends don't let friends eat at Samosa. 

Our service was pretty bad.  The food was worse.  

Long gone were the faux meat items that drew me here in the first place.  The tandoori chicken was fried and sitting in heavy grease, the bathrooms looked like a set from requiem for a dream and the manager overcharged us for drinks that never made it to our table.

Do your gastrointestinal tract a favor and satisfy your Indian buffet craving elsewhere.

I started to look for a place to get a hair cut . I never go to salons I tried  some barbers around town but I  was never really happy with my haircut, that I would go home and try to fix it or buy a hat on my way home. My wife suggested her place and todd who works there really knows, what's up. Yeah the place is worth it , they do a great job on my wife's hair and mine.
