I went a second time and can confirm that the first time was not a freak accident of nature and that the food here is actually stupid good.

We kept making sounds about how good the food was and I'm fairly certain the couple in the other corner was judging the daylights out of us. Oh well, screw them. :D

Additional stuff was tried:

-Sriracha calamari - waaaah so good
-Shiitake Polenta - spot on
-Chickpea frites - also spot on, served with a great spicy tomato sauce

-Fried goat cheese

Okay, so this one is fun enough to deserve its own paragraph. The waiter comes, pours some sort of ethanol on top, flambées it in front of you for your enjoyment, and the squeezes lemon juice. Served with pita. Quite ridiculously delicious.

-Brussel sprouts - if you have a kid who doesn't like vegetables, we've found the solution right here
-Grilled shrimp and octopus

We used the Yelp check-in to get free red and white sangrias (you need to order 2 tapas per free drink). They were excellent and not too sweet.

If you haven't been here already, hurry up!

Really was craving soup and a good sandwich. Upon walking in the place looks like it will provide good food. However, after paying almost $40 for two sandwich combos and two brownies they were most definitely not worth the price or time wasted getting there. Really disappointed with quality.

I can't agree more with the reviews here.  The 6 times I've been here, I've waited at least 30 minutes per visit in the waiting room, up to an hour.  This isn't even including the extra half hour wait after a nurse has taken vitals, but before the doctor arrives.
Once the doctor arrives, I know I'm about 3 minutes from being done, as that is the average time I've spent with a doctor here.  I know their time is valuable, but they need to understand that after waiting an hour to see them, nothing could make a patient angrier than feeling like the doctor is rushed/annoyed to see them.
Time to find some new docs...

I tried the French dip sandwich twice. I'm a sucker for quality bread. Having said that they really skimp on the meat. It's about the same amount you get on an Arby's jr. Roast beef. So I can't recommend this sandwich, but the place is inviting, the staff is friendly, and I have tried their salted Carmel cheesecake and red velvet bunt cake and those are deee-lish!

I find the ordering ahead feature on their website to be very useful - my order is ready in 15 minutes - no waiting online. The Greek salad and Italian Wedding soup are my favorites, although I haven't had the sandwiches lately. I have found the people to be friendly and eager to please - maybe they've made some new hires since the unfavorable reviews?

Used to see Leanna, she cuts and colors hair great but it always seemed like she put more of her own touches than my own that I requested. Switched to Jenn and no complaints. She can cut and color hair, makes recommendations, has a personality which is great for passing time while glued to a chair, nothing else I could as for.

The food and the baked goods are quite tasty; however, today's register attendee lacked warmth and was not very helpful in assisting us with our order.  In fact, it could be said that she would be better off working at the DMV.

The food here is delicious and authentic. My roommate's parents (who are very Lebanese) brought us here and described the food as "fantastic." 
We got the hummus, baba ghannouj,  foul moudamas, and fatush salad for an appetizer. The flavors were nuanced and unique. Everything was served with fresh pita. For entrees we ordered shish taouk, moussaka, shawarma, the shish kebob combo, and the kafta kebob combo. Service was great, and very personal. Ended up giving us a free dessert.

Not sure why I ever come here for lunch. The flat bread is a winner but service truly sucks. The people here are way too rude for my liking. You get a choice of greasy chips or dried baby carrots to go with your meal.

This place deserves less than one star. They should NEVER be called super buffer. It's a joke! Nothing is super there. If you are looking for sushi, never go there, it was old and only like  3 kinds. Yuck. 
Inside looked dirty too, window frames looked so dirty. I wish i had never gone there.  It's disgusting.

I came here for a quick lunch and was sorely disappointed. I have cooked better chicken curry. It was underspiced and when that is just wrong especially when you are talking about Indian food. I also wish there was more variety. Maybe there's more during dinner time.

I love meat, and I make fun of my vegetarian friends...but damn, this place is good! They were smart in not telling me that it was vegetarian until I was in line getting the food.

I'll definitely come back again.
I've been going to see Greg H. here now for over a year. His work with the single needle is incredible, excellent black and grey work! Highly recommend him.

Food is not bad but What a bad service...! After our pricy meals (4 couples) We ordered a small pastry: "Tres leches" $3.99 a very dry item, we returned for another item, we got another one for 2.99 and as my wife was about to start to eat it and the girl came to tell us: we have to charge you for that... we told her but the other one was a bad or not good and she said "yes but you already start the other pastry... so in front of our friends we have to give our pastry back. We paid 3.99 we returned, we got the second one (cheaper) and they want to charge us even more... I went to the counter then to ask for our first pastry and they give us the second at no charge...

If you're ever on 38th between Walnut and Spruce, you can't miss this van painted in hues of pink, yellow, and green. Unknowingly from the outside, a whole bonafide Middle Eastern kitchen is housed within this sixties-esque food truck.

Hanan's an allright place for a snack, but not so great for a meal. Their falafel sandwiches with feta, hummus, baba ghanoush, etc. are always made fresh, but never truly fill you up, unless you get two. Chicken sandwiches are also pretty good here. The platters are also made on the spot, but I always feel that they mainly consist of rice & veggies while lacking in kebab. But, perhaps, I'm simply a glutton used to the giant portions of our modern-day restaurants.

A good place though for vegetarian eaters because they have a very wide range of options. It's inexpensive and orders are almost always filled within 10 minutes of ordering.

This place is Amazing! Every time we drive through AZ we make sure to stop in. I love this Kneaders because the restaurant is always so clean. The staff is always friendly and attentive and they offer up great suggestions if I'm undecided on what to get! I always have a great experience when I stop in. Fast, friendly service as well as tasty food!

I could not have asked for a better restaurant to have my 27th birthday party. I made the reservation almost a month in advance, forgot to call the restaurant to confirm the day of, and walked in to see my table for 8 people perfectly set up and waiting. Since I had never experienced this restaurant before, as well as neither as my friends, I was a little nervous to have chosen it for my birthday celebration. I could not have been happier with my decision. We received some of the best service I've ever had from Rom (sp?), who was unbelievably attentive, professional, and so friendly. The food was absolutely delicious, everyone got something different with lots of plates to share. The kibbeh and falafel were amazing, and my platter of chicken, hummus, and tabbouleh was perfect! I am 100% coming back, and I advise anyone reading this to do the same! Wonderful food, exceptional service, affordable prices, and BYOB! It doesn't get much better than that.

I really like this bakery cafe.  Delicious sandwiches made to order with filling soups for sides.  I try not to indulge in the tempting desserts too often as I am diabetic.  Sometimes we share an item.

This place isn't bad - but I am looking for more than "not bad" when I spend my hard-earned money. Refused to sell us a slice of the Irish Soda Bread so we bought the meal that came with it - which was stew. The stew looked NOTHING like the picture promoting it - was bland and mushy. The soda bread was good - they advertised it as coming with jam - and it did - about one half a teaspoon. I went up and asked for more - was given one more half a teaspoon. Very stingy. This place is similar to a Panera only Panera has more options and is a better bet in my opinion.

I've been going to this post office for the past two years and I think they are quite decent, in particular for Philly standards. In addition to picking up my mail, I use it frequently to send packages and the workers have watched me bumble through not knowing which tape goes with what kind of mail and always helped me figure it out.
They don't have easy jobs and some of the customers in there can be pretty rough, so fact that they are still friendly most of the time leaves me impressed.

Yeah, the parking does suck and there often isn't a spot, but this post office deserves credit where it's due!

Like everyone else, I was skeptical of eating here, even after I scored a $25 restaurant.com gift card.  Last night, a bunch of us were hungry, and our go-to Minar Palace was closing, so we popped into San Samosa (as their signage still says).

After we sat, the lone server asked if we wanted the buffet or menus.  I asked how much the buffet was, and she said "hold on, let me ask," and disappeared.  Weird.  At $10.95, why not - so we stuffed our bellies with plates of mediocre, flavorless, spice-free food... and I'm no spice nut!

We had to spend $35, so we ended up getting ginger beers, "made with fresh ginger," as their menu proclaims.  Do yourself a favor, and do not get this ginger beer.  Someone thought it tasted like Windex, others thought it was just too sugary, or fake.

Oh!  The best part was the server left, so we had to pay some guy working there.  He refused to take our phone copy of the gift card, even though it clearly says "show this to your server!" saying he needed a print out for their "records" (they ended up taking it after we duked it out).

Does it bother anyone else when restaurants haven't hit their closing time yet, but start cleaning up the place to shoo you out?  We were still "enjoying" our ginger beers, when they started turning all the chairs upside down on the tables... also, I feel like this is unsanitary and gross.

Thanks but no thanks!

It isn't the most amazing meal you will ever eat, but it's tasty food at a reasonable price. There are plenty of vegetarian choices, excellent appetizers, and rich but small desserts so you can have something sweet without trying to find room in your stomach for a ginormous slice of cake.

The staff is friendly and warm, service is pretty fast, and I've always been satisfied.

Bought the turkey bacon avocado salad today and there was literally 2 tablespoons of turkey and about 1 tablespoon of bacon. I was in drive through and didn't realize till I got home. This was disappointing . Love Kneaders but will reconsider going  in the future

SO glad I did not look at reviews before going into this doctors office! I had my first visit there today & LOVED the place, waited less than 10 minutes to be seen, and had extremely personable & attentive staff. 

While in the waiting room, I had a hilarious conversation involving the other 2 people waiting & the receptionist. After waiting less than 10 minutes I was taken back by a friendly nurse who was quick & efficient. 

Waited no more than five minutes before seeing Dr. Kuzma. She was GREAT! Probably the best doctor I've met in terms of "bedside manner" & did an excellent job of providing thoughtful advice. 

Only negative = the receptionist I talked to when making my appointment was a little rude & didn't tell me about the necessary blood work that I would need to do.. Which required fasting. This meant I had to make another appointment. Kind of excited to go back & see everyone, though!

Got the craving for some curry and saag paneer at lunch so I wandered on up to Samosa for some quick to-go grub.  Walking into the small, plain restaurant, you can clock it for what it is; cheap bland Indian.  My brain told me to leave but unfortunately my hunger compelled me to stay.  Yes it's cheap but I can't really call it a bargain as you're getting what you pay for, certainly not bang for your buck.  Here, little money gets you: little flavor, limited buffet selections, and samosas with an ever-hardening outer layer generated by hours under the heat lamp.  Good Indian food possesses a powerful profile of flavors, and sometimes some nice heat; none of that here.

Staff, when rarely around, not really helpful or pleasant; one guy in line at the buffet asked for a new set of tongs as he had fumbled them and caught them with his hand (on the part that grabs the food).  The waiter decided not to fetch a fresh pair and that was my cue to leave.  Unfortunately, not too many great Indian spots in the area and Samosa brings up the bottom of the list.  Hell; they're name is Samosa and their samosas were damn weak.  I've had better from the freezer.

We were there 4.17.13.  Everything we had was superb.

Appetizers: Cabbage Rolls and Kibbi
Entrees:  Salmon with Feta Cheese and Olives/Lamb Kebob Combo
Desserts:  Baklava

I had the Lentil Soup too.  It was light and very tasty.

Our waiter was Tony.  He was most helpful, not annoying, and very attentive to our needs.

We will definitely will be back here again.

Hungry hungry hungry.. Waited 20 min to get my food, that's ok because I wasn't in a hurry. Ate my sandwich (that was ok) ate my chicken noodle soup noticed not one piece of chicken, more carrots than anything else. Good taste but no chicken. Unfortunate because I like be this place.

Do not go to this tire kingdom! I heard Chris and Renzo telling their staff to go back and find more wrong with my car. I only came in for two tires and they tried to sell me $600 worth of extra unnecessary work. It's obvious that they treat their staff like crap. These guys work on commission and they make more money by selling unnecessary work. Be very leery of taking your car there

A cheap Indian restaurant with horrible food. Honestly, i am surprised about the crowd which like their food. They keep their price low, possibly because they serve the leftovers from previous day. And they are dumb enough not to heat it before serving. A restaurant spoiling the credibility of Indian cuisine.

Much more disappointment is their concept to charge you more as service, which infact is nil. Samosa was a biggest mistake.

The only positive of the restaurant is its location. Wish there was a good food at this amazing location.

I would strongly recommend to avoid this restaurant.

I love Bern's!  I went there for my birthday when I was new to Tampa in the early 1990's.  It is my favorite choice for any special occasion, especially the Server Drew.  He is always full of stories!  What I love is the menu is ALL INCLUSIVE- no paying extra for a potato, veggie, salad, cheese toast, onion soup and onion straws.  They have their own farm to grow their own food, and you can tour the kitchen and everything will be explained.  In all these years I have only have ONE time where the steak wasn't truly amazing.... LOVE IT!  And the dessert room upstairs has rooms for two, 4, 6 or even a larger party, all private!  All homemade.... YUM.

We stopped by Kneeders on Friday January 12.  No one working the counter--had to wait.  Requested gluten free for my wife and they had none.  I ordered something for my self and a coffee.  All coffee urns were empty.  I mentioned it to the one guy behind the counter and while he acknowledge my statement did nothing to fill the pots.

We left without coffee (which I had paid for) and apparently no gluten free anything.
Something is definitely wrong with the staff training and why are there no gluten free foods?  We will not be back.

Felt scammed!

We purchased the travelzoo deal for these guys: $39 for 2 apps, 2 entrees, bottle of wine and desert.  Sounds pretty good but found out it is kind of a scam.

The food was decent, the service was friendly, the ambiance felt like a buffet restaurant.  The deal we were promised however only said that tax and tip were not included.  The staff changed the prices of the dishes we ordered to increase their tip.  $70+ dollars worth of food suddenly had a bill of $92, plus $8 of tax (do you pay tax on the menu price of the food or the value of the voucher - this I really don't know), for a $100 total and thus a perfect $20 tip for a two person dinner.  Forced 20% tip is a little high, especially since 50% of the meal cost was one bottle of wine.  

I like the food, but I liked it for $40, not $70.  While it was still pretty cheap, the tricky behavior left a bad taste in our mouths.

The pierces here are not well trained! Not only did my piercing reject, but I was lied to about the kind of jewelry that was put in. While my piercing looked like it was going to reject I came back in to talk to the piercer and she said it was fine! I don't recommend getting anything pierced here!

Delicious authentic Lebanese food. A little restaurant with a soft ambiance tucked away off of South Street. 

I'm not sure if it's because of the location or something else but it's always been empty when I've gone here. I'm not complaining, just a bit curious. The staff is extremely accommodating and it's always a relaxing meal here.

This is one of my new favorite BYOB places in Philly with its chic interior, friendly staff, delicious food and unbelievable price point.  Don't walk, but run to try this restaurant!!!!

Seven friends and I enjoyed doing the mezza, which at $30/person is a ridiculous bargain.  Since none of us had been here before, the mezza allowed us to try soooooooooooo many different Lebanese dishes and determine our favorites.  As we worked our way through the endless variety of incredible hot and cold appetizers, we had to keep reminding ourselves to leave room for the lamb and chicken kebobs.  Everyone in the group had a different favorite (e.g., stuffed grape leaves, roasted cauliflower, hummus, baba ghanouj, cooked lentils), but everyone agreed that everything tasted fresh and amazing.  We could not finish everything because of the generous portions, so the staff offered to wrap up anything that we couldn't finish to enjoy as leftovers at home.  Luckily did find a little room in our stomachs to enjoy the delicious Baklava (the bite-sized portions were perfect because everyone felt like they could squeeze in a bite but could not have ate anymore).

Always satisfied when I come here! My go to is the turkey bacon avocado sandwich (no bacon) make it a combo with the Greek salad on the side. All for around $13 which is a good deal for a giant sandwich and side w/ a drink. I love that the Greek salad is traditional Greek salad and not just lettuce with Greek dressing disguised as "Greek salad." Everything I order is always made perfectly and decent sized portions. I will always choose Kneaders over Panera bread because they give you more food for your money and they have more options in my opinion! I always go through the drivethru and my food is always out very fast and accurate. Love coming here! (They also have plenty of food options for vegetarians as well if you are on a no meat diet)

Don't waste your money. Just went here about 2 weeks ago and everything was disgusting looking. They don't season their food well. The food was cold. I was scared to death to touch the sushi. Temperatures are off. We were scared before we ate, but we were sooo hungry and just wanted to try the food. We ate half a plate of food and left. I told the dyke lady how terrible everything was and she didn't even offer to give a discount. She just asked me eactly what was bad. I told her everything was and she just said sorry and gave me the total of $25. Had to go down the street to Burger Monger right after to get decent meal. I wouldn't take my dog here to eat. 
We should have known when we entered during dinner time and only 2 other tables were filled.

The Little Donut is a great spot, they have a great selection of sandwiches and donuts. I got the bacon and Gouda sandwich which was amazing. Also got the 12 pack of donuts they were delicious. This place is affordable and just overall great! A must try especially for breakfast.

Service is quick and courteous. I came in for a flat tire fix and they also did an overall check up on my car to let me know if there's anything else I should have fixed while I'm there. 

Waiting area is clean and well kept. They have a vending machine and coffee available for you to enjoy while you wait.

If you know what you need done, you can buy the parts and bring them here to have them properly installed. This can save you a good bit of money and time.

After waiting 10 minutes in the drive-thru I recieved my pumpkin cheesecake, and my moms berry cheescake slices. My moms strawberry on the top had mold on it, and my cheesecake was in pieces. I called the restaurant, and was told to speak with a manager-the manager had the lady tell me they would call me back. This was 4 days ago...So I emailed the company and let them know what happened, and they told me pretty much "sorry this happened, we will let the manager know"...not only is the food, and he presentaton of it horrible. So is their customer service. I drove 40 minutes to try it because so many people on my FB told me it was great. I will never suggest this place to anyone. Customer service didn't even ask for the pictures of what they gave me. They obviously don't care.

Not very good at all! I love Cosi's, usually. Food not hot, staff not knowledgeable about what comes as part of menu items. I always get the tomato-basil soup and it comes with bread. It's a hearty lunch on a day like today (chilly in Philly). I had to ask for bread and he just automatically wrapped up the plain bread without asking what kind I wanted. The bread was not warm and the soup was barely warm.  Very disappointed on my first trip for the season.

I've been to this place three times and each time was very different. I would have to say the first time I went was the best. It was my birthday and it was packed but not too packed and there's was just the right amount of girls. We had a great time that night. The girls were very laid back and friendly and made sure we had a good time. I got a lot of attention to because it was my birthday so that was a plus. The second time we went was for my girlfriend's birthday and it was very slow. They only had 5 or 6 girls that night. It was almost shocking because the first time we went was so great and a lot of fun. We still made our own fun. Even though there weren't many girls they still made their rounds and did the best they could. The third time honestly is what turned me away from this place. It was a Monday night and we had been hearing how packed they get on Mondays. It was supposed to be their best night. So we tried it out and honestly NEVER AGAIN will I go on a Monday night if I go back. It was too packed and hard to watch the girls because people were standing in front of each other. They had many different types of girls but only certain ones (the ratchet ones) got on stage. They made all the money because it seems they knew about 80% of the people there. If anyone else got on stage they maybe made 7 or 8 dollars. It was pretty divided. They had a concert on stage which wasn't very entertaining either. I honestly don't recall seeing any of the girls I saw the first 2 times I went either. I liked the other girls way more. They were friendly and knew how to mingle, whereas these girls wouldn't even go near you if they didn't know you. I know I could go any other day and I probably wouldn't have this problem but that night really turned me off of this place. I was really disappointed. Even with us going on a really slow night, I still had this club 5 stars in my mind because we still had a good time. After last time....nope

"Hi, Welcome.  I will be right with you."  
learn it.  
I went into Kneaders today with my kids to get some treats to bring home, and we stood there and waited until I realized that no one was going to wait on us.  Even though the worker came right on the other side of the counter, literally 3 feet away from us at least 6 times, she totally ignored us.  Even though we like your sugar cookies, it doesn't help if no one will sell them to us..

So we went next door to Corner Bakery and Cafe, where omg, we were greeted with a smile when we came to the counter.

I never write reviews but this place was phenomenal! I had the tomato basil soup with a baguette, a green salad & the pomegranate berry iced tea. The soup was perfection and a very good portion. The baguette was an ample amount and it was some of the most delicious bread I've had! The green salad came with lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, homemade croutons, cheese, and your choice of dressing. It was nothing special but still very tasty and the tea was refreshing! I also ordered a pumpkin chocolate chip cookie which was to die for. Not only was the food delicious, the customer service was great & they had free samples of a salted caramel & praline cupcake and some different types of bread near the register. I highly recommend Kneaders, it knocks Panera out by a long shot.

I can honestly say they have the best coffee I have ever tasted. Very delicious. It's also refillable. The staff was pleasant and told us to take as many samples of the pumpkin bread we wanted since we were one of the last customers. We ordered cinnamon rolls and they were big, gooey slices that did not disappoint. Will definitely come here again.

BEWARE!!! The woman who works the cash register WILL rip you off!  She's tried doing it to me, and I've seen her do it to multiple people. (Specifically, she will charge you the take in price for the buffet when you're doing take out, which is $3 less)  CHECK the prices before you pay!

However, I'm actually surprised to see all the bad reviews about the food - I actually think the food is pretty great (hence the 3 stars).  Maybe because I come here for lunch, before its been sitting out all day...

Never eating here again. I just found a piece of wood in my soup - possibly something used to stir the soup. The manager was super nice and gave me money back no problem - but it doesn't seem like a safe place to get soup anymore. Maybe revisit your food preparation safety policies?
We went to cosi in Washington on 15th and e street the people were very friendly and food was fresh and delicious so much better than the one in Philly thanks

Delicious steakhouse with great prices. The desert room and restaurant tour is also a GREAT experience, but the deserts and coffee are not the best. Still a must go restaurant when in Tampa. Reservations required.

Excellent food and a great value! Service staff was friendly and polite and very helpful. Unfortunately I didn't get the name of the person who took my order, but he was extremely helpful and knew the menu well. I would highly recommend this restaurant to my friend's and family. I couldn't eat the whole meal because of the size of the sandwich ,but I will enjoy the sandwich in the morning!

Great shop. I was there this past weekend for their Friday the 13th tattoo special, and they were all truly awesome. Nice staff, very attentive, non-judgmental, super down to earth. I got a beautiful beetle from Austin, who has an extremely light touch and is great with line detail. I wanted to get one of the pieces that Mitch was doing, but as he had a client at that moment, he offered to let me come back the next day and he did it at the same price- extremely fast and painless- I was in and out the door again in less than an hour.

I'll definitely be going back to bug these guys for more work in the near future. Highly recommend.

This place is really bad. 
The lunch price and student discount make it fair. The service is also really friendly and makes you root for it, but come on, the food is awful!

I was happy they had all the Gulab Jamun in the world, but everything else was really ill conceived. The naan was basically white bread shaped like naan as if it were play-doh. Awful. 
The rice was super under cooked and sharp. 
The tikka masala and other dishes were meh, but just really would avoid this place unless I were really craving Indian and poor.

GO TO NEW DELHI in UCITY! Amazing buffet for the same price.

The hours of operation have changed -nearly 2 years ago- and they are open 7 am-9 pm Monday through Saturday and are closed on Sunday. Staff and management are super friendly at the Wilmot location.

Not open until 10 pm as listed on Yelp and Apple Maps!. Hopefully one day this will be corrected.

Enjoy some delicious Japanese food in the wonderful ambiance of the new Mercado San Augustine (MSA) Annex!! The food was very good! (We enjoyed the Ramen, Tuna Mayo/Pork Belly Rice Balls, and Seaweed Salad) And again, you can't beat the ambiance here! The restaurant serves food outside to the beautiful/new outdoor MSA Annex, and it's also a great place to bring the kids vs. a traditional restaurant. You can even order wine and beer from Eastbound (they have quite the selection on tap right next door to Kuka) and enjoy some alcohol with your food at your table if you feel inclined. We will definitely be regulars here!

This was the first kneaders in our area so I was super excited to try it and unfortunately I don't think we will return. First we walked in and went straight for the bathroom to wash our hands. The door handle wouldn't turn so we assumed someone was in there. We went to order and they ran out of menus so we could only order off the wall hangings which don't give a very descriptive picture of what you're ordering. Even the guy at the register didn't seem to have answers to what was in certain salads. I ordered the potato soup in a sourdough bowl and this is how it came. Am I supposed to scoop out the inside of the bread and put my soup in it? They cut the top off so why didn't they put my soup in the bread bowl? I'm confused. I asked the lady who brought our food if there was only one bathroom and she said "no there's two stalls on there but the door handle gets jammed". So I asked her to show me. She opened the door for me but why wouldn't they put a note up? Tape the door so it wouldn't stick? I don't understand. There was at least 3 ladies waiting to use the restroom. Also I went thru 3 cups because they all leaked out the bottom. They said this has been happening over the last few weeks. What if someone takes this to go and it leaks in their car or on their clothes? This place seems poorly managed. The food is okay, nothing special. The bread was good but not good enough to bring me back here. Sorry guys. I wished we had a better experience here.

The main perk of this Cosi is the fact that it's in my office building. Don't think I'd be coming back as often as I do if that wasn't the case. The flow or customers from ordering to paying gets a little confusing and the lines can get long at lunch time. I wish the sides (chips and carrots) were larger, but at the end of the day, I can get a good sandwich or salad right downstairs.

The main perk of this Cosi is the fact that it's in my office building. Don't think I'd be coming back as often as I do if that wasn't the case. The flow or customers from ordering to paying gets a little confusing and the lines can get long at lunch time. I wish the sides (chips and carrots) were larger and they often run out of them, but at the end of the day, I can get a sandwich or salad right downstairs. I have not come in a while thought since I've reduced my meat-eating. There aren't the most options in that regard.
First timer to a strip club and I'm glad I pick this place! Good first experience girls are beautiful and friendly.

A friend recommended that I go see Jenn back in 2007, and I have never gone anywhere else since. The salon itself has a great look & their team is truly a family.

Jenn is a master colorist & has always taken the time to get it right. This is saying a lot because I have a ridiculous amount of hair! She never rushes & always does a beautiful job styling it at the end. 

Every time I leave the salon feeling like a million bucks & get tons of compliments on my hair. I would highly recommend this salon to anyone looking for a great stylist.

A vegetarian Indian buffet? I thought I'd be in heaven. I got a little above purgatory, but nowhere near the pearly gates.

There were surely a lot of options. But the food, overall, was just so-so. A lot of it was on the not-so-warm-anymore side. Which was disappointing. Everything was just kind of, eh. The curry dishes had no unique punch to them.

My favorite dish was the soy-chicken tiki masala. The sauce was tasty.

The iced tea also had some good spices in it and was yum.

Everything else. I've had better. But they get 3 stars because there was just sooo much veg food. And it was one of the only restaurants we could find in the area that was still open at 9pm on a Friday night.

If I lived in the area, I might return. But I'd probably check out other Indian options first to compare local choices before coming back.

FYI: They also have a lot of random other veg foods, and such, like veg cheese "steak" and veggie burgers. Didn't try those. Plus, they have ice cream and milkshakes.

I have come here almost every single morning for their omelets. It includes - nice size omelet, fries (or oatmeal, and toast--- all for $5! Other than that, the sandwiches are amazing and full of value. The staff is attentive and moves quickly and efficiently. This is easily my favorite "grab and go place".

The Roasted Red Pepper Gouda soup was very tasty except for the occasional burst of burnt taste. Really it was a tomato soup with Red Pepper and Gouda. The twice baked Almond Croissant has a filling that seemed like a combination of vanilla pudding and almond paste so we got a hint of almond only.  
This place is not handicap friendly as people have to stand in line to order. The booths are wood and very hard. Drop in and get your bakery goods and take them out.

Tried this place for the first time last weekend for brunch with my Mom. 
We both really enjoyed the food & the chocolate eclare was TO DIE FOR!!! :)
Very nice granite counter tops & very cute decor! Even the service was  very friendly, knowledgable & even made some useful suggestions! Will definitely be coming back :)
Super friendly staff. Clean lobby.  Good food. Good value. The chocolate mousse dome cake is moist, rich, delicious, and reasonably priced.

The belt on my dress is leaving lines on my stomach right now, thanks to Hanan.

I went to PennFoodTrucks.com to find this gem and have been there twice...both times I've gotten the grilled chicken platter for $5.50.  I noticed I got less chicken today than I had before, but it's still a lot of food.  I'd have to say there is about a cup and a half of two different kinds of rice - yellow & lentil, a little pool of hummus, and a little mound of tabbouleh - and chicken on top of the rice.  If there was more, I'd eat it, and my belt would break.  

There was no line, I guess because there are some mixed reviews, but then again I only go here when I am RAGING with hunger.  Also today, it still tasted good, but the hummus was a bit on the liquidy side.  Prob need to add some more chick peas to the food processor.

Love Kneaders!  It's a fantastic brunch place with delicious pastries and sandwiches.  I always go for the turkey avocado on a croissant.  
The down side is 1. Not open Sundays..  For being a brunch place I find it odd. 2. There is a guy there who I am assuming is a manager.. He tends to be short and borderline rude. Everytime I walk in I try and avoid him.. If he is a manager I hope he treats his staff better than the customers.  3. While the food is scrumptious,  it's somewhat expensive.. We spend about $45 every time we go.

I am from India and have been in USA for almost 20 years. I mostly travel for my job and first thing I look is for Indian resturant in the city where ever I visit. This is by far the WORST ever food I have tasted.
Its a insult to Indian buffet. The buffet does not even come close to say "OK".
The only one star is for the hottie who sits at the cash counter. I dont really think the owners really bother if the customers are happy or not. they are least concerned.
The appetizers have no taste, the veges like cucumbers, carrots are stale and stink. The rest of the food on the buffet is either over cooked or repeated cooked(from lunch to buffet and again from buffet to lunch)
The desserts are cold cold cold. no taste at all.
Lastly, the cutlery is so pathetic, you cannot differentiate between clean and unclean ones. If you still dare to go there, I will suggest pick the plastic ones :-)

There's a lot of good options on the menu. I've been here once before and tried a breakfast croissant which was good. I came today and was disappointed. The oatmeal was dry and cold, they only have half and half creamer for the coffee, the fruit did not look fresh. I ordered a caramel macchiato and half the cup was filled with caramel. Despite all of this, their Greek omelette was delicious. So I give them that.
Got a really great cut and a little splash of color here.  Highly recommend.
The food is the real deal served by friendly staff. Great baba  ganouj and falafel. The kibbe nayeh was wonderful.j

Pros: Food was tasty and high quality ingredients. Nice selection of sandwiches, salads, soups, breakfast and baked goods. Friendly staff. Flavored and regular non-sweet iced teas. Pastries, baked goods, pies. Gift items, DIY gift wrap station. Sandwich bread was soft and easy to eat (no tough Beyond Bread-like crust on their white sourdough). Potato salad was good. They have a drive through. Similar pricing to Beyond Bread.

Cons: insanely busy during lunch rush. Standing room only with customers who placed orders with no place to sit. Should have opened 3rd cash register as there was a customer with a lengthy problem/ return and another picking up a catering order. They did not allow me to substitute bacon for roast beef on the Club so I omitted roast beef and paid extra for bacon. Soup came with two large foccacia wedges but no butter. Will not dine in at lunch time.

We have been blessed with a Kneaders Bakery being built just a couple blocks away from our home a couple of years ago.  We usually just hit it up on a lazy Sunday morning for a couple eclairs and a brownie or 4!
Well the other day, in our time of pandemonium.....my wife read a Facebook add that mentioned that their loaves of bread were only $1.99.  Now I'm not sure what the normal price of this wonderful bread is, but whatever it is, we're gonna be paying it!  This is some of the best bread ever and for the price, let alone that all stores are currently out of....well, EVERYTHING....it's a great deal!   
What made the experience even that much more pleasant, was the incredibly nice young lady, Lorena.   In a time like this, when nerves and moods are at an all time low, this girl just couldn't be in a better mood and more helpful.  It's employees like these, that make businesses run flawlessly.   So Mr. Kneader, if you're looking for an "employee of the year" candidate ....you KNEADN'T LOOK ANY further!   Lorena is your woman!

We tried the buffet, which had plenty of the standards you'd expect at an Indiant buffet. The chicken curry had decent curry flavor and tender chunks of meat. The tandoor chicken also had a fair amount of seasoning but was a bit dry.

Watch out for bay leaves, bark, cardamom berries and other flavor adders in the heat trays that you might not want to ingest. Despite this, the food as a whole seamed to lack that "pop" that I look for in good Indian food. The spice could definitely stand to be kicked up a notch.

I'd consider ice cream for desert if they offered more exotic varieties (like cardamom), but no such luck. Overall a fulfilling meal at a good price, but there definitely are better options available.

We purchased a queen "Kings Down" mattress from Vern N at R&S Mattress.  It was delivered in a timely fashion.  The two gentlemen who delivered the mattress brought it right in the house and placed it on the guest bed.  I slept on it for a few nights, and discovered it was firm on one side and soft on the other.  I called Vern.  He was embarrassed to admit that he neglected to tell us that about that particular mattress.  We stopped back at the store, and Vern gave us a good deal on a new queen BB (Brooklyn Bedding) mattress.  Within days, the new mattress was delivered and the "Kings Down" returned.  I have slept on the new mattress for about a month and all seems well.  Nothing but good to say about Vern N at R&S Mattress on Oracle.

Disappointing experience on a weekday night. I have good memories of this restaurant from years ago. I think it's gone downhill.
Restaurant was almost deserted.
Appetizers were not especially flavorful. Fresh pita was a highlight.
Lamb shish-kebab was overcooked, veggies the same. Rice had no flavor.
Will not rush back.

I have used Mike's Garage for three years. They provide honest diagnostics, provide reasonable quotes, and quickly fix your car. I trust Liz and Mike; they take the time to explain the problems to you. I will always go to them. They have saved me a lot of money compared to dealership mechanics.

How can a place called "Samosa" not have authentic samosas?  I walked in thinking I'd have the lunch buffet, but after looking over their selection (pretty standard fare-- good amount of meat and vegetable options), I thought maybe next time (the food wasn't extra appealing to me and my friend did not want to eat Indian, but I needed a "hit" lol).  So, I ended up ordering vegetable samosas.  Needless to say, I was kind of disappointed.  They didn't make their own dough for the samosas, instead of the thick, hand-made type, they used that thin, phyllo pastry kind of dough (makes for a very crunchy and crumbly shell) and the inside tasted like curried mashed potatoes-- very creamy... ew and weird.  However, the flavor was good.

Ultimately I was disappointed with my samosa experience, but their buffet looked like they had a lot of options, so I think this place is just, OK.

I went here for an early dinner- about 4:30- with a google offer that basically just saved me $4.  Figured it was worth it to try out an Indian place near work that I'd never been to.  I was the only one in the place, aside from who I can only assume was the manager? owner?  Even the waiter arrived after I had started eating.  They allowed me to eat buffet despite the fact the offer specifically said the buffet was not included.  I guess without a waiter on hand, it was easier for the manager guy to just let me at it, much to my delight.  

I enjoyed everything I tasted!  I'm a big spice fan and everything was a little tame for my tastes, though not lacking in flavor.  The veg samosas were especially delicious in my opinion.  Nothing was dried out or cold, though the naan may have been sitting out just a little longer than it should have.  The buffet is set up dessert first, which is odd in my opinion, but the puddings (rice and mango) were excellent.  

As others have said, this is not a place to go for stellar customer service.  While I was happy to get more than I expected based on my google offer, I think it was out of lack of effort rather than special treatment.  They didn't even ask if I wanted anything to drink besides the pitcher of water they left on my table.   But for a quick Indian fix on a low budget, this is definitely a worthwhile place in my opinion.

Not impressed with this location. It took a while for our order to be taken, the ice machine was out of ice, the majority of tables were dirty, and the food had the tiniest portion sizes. I ordered the chicken salad croissant and there was barely enough chicken salad to cover the croissant. Will not be back to this location.
I walked in and walked right back out . There was a line of people and I saw 1 person working . The place didn't have a lot of pastries like I was expecting I thought it would be just like a bakery

My wife and I had a great experience with R&S.  We arrived close to closing time, but our salesperson Alex stayed at least an hour past closing to make sure we found the right mattress.  He spent a lot of time with us and gave us some good advice on choosing the right mattress.  I honestly felt that he was trying to find the best mattress for us, rather than selling us the best mattress for his sales commission.  If you go into the store, I highly recommend working with him.  When the mattress was delivered, the drivers called twice beforehand to update me on the schedule.  They arrived on time and were quick and courteous.  It was an excellent experience.  I would (and plan to) shop there again.

BYOB. Low key. Delicious food. 
Love love love this place. It has become one of our favorite places to go for consistently good food. As a Greek/Armenian/American family we are picky about our Mediterranean food, but this place is the real deal. They are warm, welcoming and fill your belly with delicious food. Some of our favorites include the baba ganoush, falafel, cauliflower, dolmas and many of the chicken dishes. I saw a plate of octopus pass me by last time that I am looking forward to trying on our next visit. Wonderful hidden gem.

I have now eaten at Cedar's twice.  Both times the food has been delicious and the staff are so nice.  You really do feel like welcome and taken care of.  We even had a voucher that they graciously accepted it.

Decent bakery chain restaurant. Lots of soup, salad and sandwich options. Combo options give drink with another food item.  Small gift shop. Indoor and outdoor seating. Closed Sunday. Needs better cleaning because counters, steel trash and glass displays are all  smeared. 

Good food, warm, tasty
If I wanted a loaf of bread for lunch I would of bought that. French dip, where's the meat and did you put it in the microwave?

This is a great place!  So many food and dessert options.  We recently stopped by for cinnamon rolls and grabbed a couple desserts for that evening.  We also sampled bread and a spread.  They also have a gift shop.  The shop always cute holiday items and various take home food items.  Prices are reasonable and the locations are always clean.

I ordered takeout via www.DiningIn.com, and the delivery was late, so perhaps you should take this review with a grain of salt, given that the food was just barely warm by the time it got here. But then, a lot of the reviews on here mention the pleasant ambiance of the restaurant, so perhaps my review, devoid of the actual experience of the brick'n'mortar restaurant, might actually be more accurate, as I'm focusing solely on the food.

The first impression when I opened my takeout bag was the strong smell of fish. That apparently was coming from my order of grilled calamari. I had never before experienced a fishy smell from calamari though, so that was a put-off. And the eating of the calamari wasn't much better than the smelling of it -- it was rubbery and undercooked. The rest of my order consisted of baba ganouj and a falafal sandwich. The baba was overly acidic, most likely due to too much lemon in the recipe. If you're making baba ganouj for grocery store sales, and you need it to have a long shelf-life, I could understand using extra lemon as a preservative. But if you're a restaurant, there's no reason to use so much lemon, unless you're making a huge batch at a time that's lasting you for a whole week or more. But if you're a restaurant that's doing that, you should stop doing that. Just make a small batch at a time. The overly acidic taste of your baba ganouj is overwhelming the eggplant flavor, and therefore ruining the baba ganouj.

The "pita" bread that came with the baba ganouj (and I put pita in quotes because it's unlike any pita I've ever had before) was quite bizarre. it was an extremely thin, very flat bread, more like a lightly-cooked tortilla than an actual piece of bread. And as soon as it lost its warmness, it also lost its moisture, and thus became dry.

The falafal sandwich was very bland. Neither the falafals themselves, nor the dressing or vegetables (oddly, sliced tomatoes and pickles), much less the "pita" wrapping, offered any interesting flavors.

Perhaps I didn't order Cedars' specialty dishes. Perhaps the delivery took so long that all the flavors blew out the deliveryman's car windows. Perhaps the wonderful ambiance of the actual restaurant would have lulled me into thinking everything was delicious. I, though, will never know, as there are much better Middle Eastern restaurants in Philadelphia that I know I can rely on for good, flavorful, quality food.

This place is an ABSOLUTE must try for anyone who appreciates good mediterranean / Lebanese food out there! To say that the food is delicious is an UNDERSTATEMENT. This beautifully decorated, cozy restaurant not only boasts meals that are fit for the Gods with flavor profiles unlike any other, coupled with unparalleled  hospitality and customer service by the owner, Yassan and his nephew, Elias, your dining experience would be made magical whether you're there on a casual dinner night, celebrating a special birthday, or simply to go out with a group of friends and enjoy a delicious mind blowing meal together!

I would highly recommend doing the mezza ($30 a person, WELL WELL WORTH your money) which is a traditional lebanese feast serving a wide variety of the most popular hot and cold appetizers and mixed kebobs! Truly, a MUST MUST TRY to know what homemade, food with no frills taste like.

Check out our public food album link: https://www.facebook.com/media/set/?set=a.10105003403755662.1073742199.10139157&type=1&l=e00c379a7f

We started off with a feast of the kibbi (cracked wheat pockets stuffed with ground lamb, perfectly seasoned with onions and pine nuts), labni (low fat creamy yogurt topped with crushed mint) and the PITA bread ZOMG!!! hot and fresh from the oven, perfectly salted and it comes steaming HOT to pair with almost anything from hummus to baba ghanouj (roasted eggplant & tahini). The cabbage leaves and stuffed grape leaves were equally delightful. 

Now, here's my favorite: a simple but absolutely delicious side: Mjadra: cooked lentils, seasoned rice topped with perfectly caramelized onions. Together with their hot and fresh falafels, easily one of the best in the city, these glorious balls of chickpeas and fave beans paired with tahini sauce will BLOW your mind!

Their entrees from their kebob (grilled meat) platters: Shish Taouk (grilled chicken skewers), kafta (grilled lamb with onion, parsley and spice) and Laham Mishwi (skewered lamb kebob) over a simply yet absolutely delicious bed of perfectly cooked rice & angel hair strands = a MEAT lover's dream!

KANAFI: is all you need to say for dessert! and Baklava. I won't ruin the surprise for you. Just try it :)

I cannot vouch for the authenticity of this restaurant any more. A restaurant that was established in 1986 with absolutely no frills but just delicious home cooked meals! When you're done with fufu fifi meals, come enjoy a delicious traditional treat at Cedars! and say hi to Yassan the owner and Elias his nephew! Tell him Laura sends her best!

oh and this is a BYOB!

PS. Fun fact: Cedar is the national tree of lebanon and is a centerpiece of the Lebanese flag.

We all know the stereotype of the Irish - Drink, drink, drink.  Fight.  Rinse.  Repeat.  It seems the staff at Finnigan's Wake takes this to the next level;  they actually just aspire to be the biggest assholes in a 2-mile radius (success!).

If you are a bro and looking for a good place to release all that testosterone, give it a go.  Otherwise, take heed, my friends.

Have I had better Indian food? Most certainly. Have I had better Indian buffet? Oh yes sirree. But New Samosa does work in a pitch.

On July 4th, me and my friend wanted to go out for lunch and a lot of restaurants closed for the day. As we were walking down Walnut Street for IHOP, we walked by New Samosa, saw the price and decided to eat there instead. It was a tad late but we waltz in and decided that there's enough food before sitting down to eat. Sorry, I can't help my Asian tendencies when I'm around buffets. 

There seems to be only one waiter for the whole hall and we decided not to wait for him and decided on an empty table and headed for the buffet. Their samosa was crisp and plump, filled with curried potatoes and peas. The chicken tandoori is also yummy as can be, it's smoky, savory with a nice tang. The goat beriyani also tasted very good, though when we get there all we got was sauce and bones. Other than that everything else did not stand out. There's vegetable korma, saag paneer, chicken tikka masala and all but they were ok. 

Service was non-existent, but it was $7.95 for lunch buffet. Not other restaurants in the neighborhood could match that price with the same gut-busting feel and truly good Indian food are at least 15 blocks away.
Doing my shift as mgr Sunday funday cold beer and great music and of course the wonderful lady's of Tampa come on down we will leave the light on
I had a sandwich it's was a very cold one I asked hem too hear it up and they sad they are not able to heat up cold chicken sandwich I went to Panera  bread after and they treated me with respect

We tried this place out for the first time last week.  Not having any idea what to expect, as I sat munching my Chicken Pesto Panini it made me think of Panera...but better than Panera.  The place was pristine and all dressed up for the holidays.  They had this whole section where they were selling stuff - reminded me of Panera meets Cracker Barrell but smashed into a small space?  The merchandise was kind of weird sitting in the middle of the store.

Anyway, we did really enjoy the counter service which was incredibly friendly, and the food came out quick.  My Chicken Pesto Pinini was great, and came with homemade chips.  The hubs ordered the French Dip along with the White Cheddar Pablano soup (very good) in a bread bowl.  

Not sure if I would say I am a fan yet... definitely would choose this place over Panera.

I stop by  after work and told them i was having problems with my new tank the c-5 the clerk listen  as I tried to explain what i thought was wrong with my new tank. He check it out and told that he could fix it by adjusting some parts but he decide to give a new tank. I bought some  e-juice and they filled up my tank and ask me to try it out, there's nothing better than a new tank. I just started vaping so I haven't decide to buy a expansive tank because the disposable ones work fine for me. I definitely have to go back sometime to try check out the e-juice bar

My husband and I came here for the first time last week. We have returned three time since. We are so happy to finally get a good alternative to Beyond Bread and Panera for salads and sandwiches. Kneader's is delicious. I love the Caeser Salad and my husband has ordered several delicious soups. The place is really busy already which is great because we want them to stick around for a long time. Thumbs up!
This truck food is different from the surrounding ones with much better quality. More authentic middle eastern. The lady is very nice indeed. She really deserves the five stars.

DO NOT COME HERE!!! I brought my car and explained the noise it was making and i left feeling confident in the work they were going to do on my car. They assured me nothing was wrong and my car would make it back to New York in my long upcoming drive. I left feeling confident in the worker i spoke with. Fast forward 2 days as i was driving home i heard this awful new noise coming from my car.  Sure enough i get out and check my tire and 3 of the screws attaching my tire we're completely stripped and if i continued driving my tire would have blown off.  Tire kingdom when rotating my tire tightened it too much and the tire stripped.  Clearly their mechanics are inexperienced in a simple tire rotation.  This place is very very unreliable, do not go there!

Food is fine, but if you're running a restaurant catering to lunch for office workers, you need to figure out how to manage a line better.  Not sure who can fix this there (manager or if it's just bad corporate policy), but there have to be other stores that are doing a better job.  Is there a separate line for soup or isn't there? Are people taking orders while people wait or aren't they? figure it out and stop having employees behind the counter who can't help people because there are other customers in the way.

I've been here after the reopening, and I thought the food was pretty good. It's your typical Indian buffet, but everything overall was tasty.
The decor is kind of bland, and they place this really weird popish-Indian music the whole time.
Service is kind of lacking, our watier seemed indifferent to us.

TERRIBLE customer service.  They don't answer their phone.  THen, when they eventually do answer their phone, they put you on hold for hours!  Ridiculous!  HORRIBLE!  If only we had a choice of postal offices, I would switch!

I love this salon. I've seen Leanna twice and have recommended her to several friends/family. 

I had her put purple highlights (lowlights?!) on the bottom layer of my hair, close to my neck. She called them "peek a boos". This is definitely not a common service, so I was a little nervous going into it, being able to explain what I wanted exactly, etc. She listened, asked questions, and I ended up with exactly what I wanted. The shade of purple was vivid and exactly what I wanted. 

I came back a few months later to get it redone, that's how happy I was. I also got a cut at that time, which I was also happy with. 

I've recommended Leanna to several friends (one of whom got the same color service), and my husband and brother have also been to see Todd for cuts. Everyone I know who has been to Split Endz has been happy with their service. 

The prices are the BEST! Super competitive. Go, you won't be disappointed.

I wouldn't call Cedars a "destination restaurant" -- I can't remember one single time we've left the house expressly with Cedars in mind, or absolutely craving their hummus or grape leaves or chicken kebobs. But we've ended up there a half-dozen or so times over the last couple of years and I can definitely say I've never regretted it. The aforementioned food items are consistently good -- not best-ever or in any way life-changing, but reliably well-prepared. Really just simple, standard, earthy Middle Eastern fare, unfussy and nicely presented, with a nice balance of all the usual lemony, garlicky, cumin-y, herby flavors. Very mellow ambience, and rarely more than a couple of tables occupied whenever we've been there, so the service has typically been prompt and attentive. 

If Cedars ever closed, it wouldn't break my heart, but on more than a few occasions it's provided a perfectly fine spur-of-the-moment meal when we've been in that neighborhood and were feeling a bit indecisive about where to grab dinner. If that's your only expectation upon walking in, you probably won't leave unsatisfied. Prices are absolutely reasonable and we've never left hungry after a shared appetizer or two, entrees, and pita bread.

This post office is highly incompetent when it comes to communicating and tracking packages. When I called all throughout the week that my package was supposed to be delivered they assured me it was in route. When the final day came and my package did not arrive I called them to see what the issue was. They had no idea where my package was and did not know what to do... Now i'm down 2 packages and they are down a customer.
At least UPS tracks their packages.
The breakfast croissant is my favorite... until Sunday morning when I am craving it and realize I can't have it because their closed, then I'm very sad. :)

Went here with some friends for dinner who were big fans of the place. The restaurant is in the back of the store, and there is a table or two that you can eat at.
The food is pretty cheap and they give large portions, but I wouldn't say I was too blown away by my tacos. They were decent, but pretty much tasted like tacos I've had before.
I know people rave about this place, but I have had better Mexican food elsewhere.
Love this place! I've been eating here since as long as I can remember. Great food great service. Everything's fresh and you can actually taste the handmade quality in their food!

If you've walked around the streets of Philly, it's likely that you've run into one of Cosi's many outposts. Years ago when I was in college in Chicago (think a decade or so), I stopped by Cosi to try their s'mores - basically a set up where you can make your own s'mores on a table-side fire pit. Apparently they still have that and have branched out to pizzas, sandwiches, and salads.

So for a recent work-day lunch, the GF and I met up at the Cosi on 17th and Market, replete with its own roaring pizza oven! This outpost has two levels with plenty of seating for the work crowd.

Signature Salad ($7.99)
Mixed greens tossed with red grapes, pears, pistachios, dried cranberries, gorgonzola and tossed in balsamic vinaigrette.

The GF went with one of their fresh salads. This one had a nice funk from the blue cheese. The pears and red grapes were refreshing, while the dried cranberries offered some tang. The pistachios provided that necessary textural element. The GF opted for light balsamic rather than the sherry vinaigrette, which allowed the vinegary tang of the balsamic to brighten up the dish.The accompanying bread was nicely grilled and satisfying.

Steakhouse Gorgonzola Melt ($7.99)
Tender beef medallions, Gorgonzola, caramelized red onions & bleu cheese spread.

Of course, I did not opt for a salad. I went with the steakhouse gorgonzola melt, which was surprisingly good. While the beef was closer to medium-well, it still had a nicely tender and juicy. 

The caramelized onions added heft to the dish, with the funky gorgonzola and blue cheese spread adding coma-induing salty creaminess. Perfect for returning to work.

The sandwich came with Cosi branded kettle chips, which were not at all salty, nor were they greasy.

Chicken Margherita Flatbread Pizza ($13.99)
Grilled chicken, fresh mozzarella, basil and tomato 

I mentioned a pizza oven earlier in this post. So naturally, I had to try Cosi's pizza as well. Rather than go for the individual portion ($7.69), I went for the 'shareable' portion, of which the GF had one piece (I ate most of the rest and took the rest home for dinner if you really need to know - I am an admitted glutton). You get the choice of regular or thin crust on Cosi's flatbread pizzas. 

This is not the best 'artisanal' flatbread pizza I've had, but for what is essentially a chain, this gets the job done. After the bread is baked in the oven, juicy chunks of chicken were spread atop cheesy mozzarella and tart tomato sauce. Then the pizza gets put through a salamander grill to get it toasted and melted. Fresh basil was then liberally distributed all over this monstrosity. This was a lot of above-average pizza for the price. Really surprising.

Overall, Cosi gets the job done for a work-day lunch. The prices are on par with anything you'll find in Center City. They offer salads, sandwiches, and pizza. Pretty standard fare for lunch, but they elevated it to a level that's above what you typically find.

R&S MATTRESS LIQUIDATORS IS BY FAR THE BEST PLACE TO PURCHASE A MATTRESS, MATTRESS PROTECTOR OR PILLOWS. I NEEDED A MATTRESS OF QUALITY BUT NOT TOO EXPENSIVE AND I MUST SAY R&S was wonderful with making that happen for me. If you want deals and great customer service come on in. My sales guy Vern was extremely knowledgeable and I felt really cared for since it was my first time purchasing a mattress. I couldn't be happier with my luxurious inexpensive queen sized bed. You'll be happy too.

Had the dinner buffet.
Had a bowel malfunction an hour later.
Goat curry was full of bone chips.
This place is horrible.  SLOW.  got my order wrong.  highly inefficient.  i'm no fan of cosi, but this place is horrible even by cosi standards.  avoid at all costs!

They have some of the best kefta (lean hamburger) I've ever had, and I've been to the Middle East and have lived in Michigan, which has fantastic Middle Eastern food. The pitas are actually pretty lame (a little too chewy for me) and almost drive this review down to four stars, but the saving grace is the not-hot-but-super-tasty hot sauce and the mild feta cheese that is a perfect compliment to the spiced kefta.  

Their hummus is of the liquid-y sauce-type variety (as opposed to the thicker hummus that can be found at more Israeli-style places like Hummus and Mama's Vegetarian), which isn't my favorite, so I usually stick with the feta and kefta wrap with hot sauce. All in all, this is probably my second favorite lunch truck in the University City area (behind Tacos Don Memo).

What a disappointment today. I have been here before and it was great, but today was a disaster. The loaded potato soup was absolutely destroyed and tasted awful, not even edible. The chocolate cream pie should not have been served, the taste was shockingly awful, the worst I've ever had. Not sure I'll ever be back. My fountain drink was good though.

I came with my crew of 5 which consisted of Egyptian natives who knew a thing or two about middle eastern cuisine. In the end, all of them had been pleasantly surpised of how good the food was. 

The entrance and dining area is very clean- a few 4 or more top tables accented with tea lites and standard place settings. We sat in the far end with a comfy backsplash of a couch with additional chairs- a nice little arrangement for close seating. I recommend coming with a group to appreciate the coziness- but it's also appropriate for romantic dates as well. 

As a side note, if you're coming here to get drunk and experience loud music- skip over to the bars around the block- because this place is quite the opposite. They don't have a huge liquer collection but it might have been intended to be that way so that there would be more concentration on the food.

In a nutshell, our meals were excellent. Their serving portions were perfect and because the servers were from the arab culture that promotes generosity, they didn't skimp on providing us with more food and excellent service. They continually brought us repeated baskets of pita bread for our dipping pleasure of each other's dishes as we joyously sampled the falafel, grapeleaves, hummus and other goodies which had wonderful mediterranean appeal. I personally had the shwarma sandwich- a good choice but I'm eager to try another item on their menu when I return. 

And if the food wasn't enough to woo you- the prices for them were even better. Everything was moderately priced and accurately represent the food and ambiance. Good food, good service, good times. 

In close, the whole experience was nothing short of the true and authentic middle-eastern theme you'd come to expect from this restaurant.  I look forward to coming back.

everything tastes like garlic here, even their ripoff "sanstone" ice cream. plus, this restaurant has gone through too many iterations: vegetarian, then they were serving "italian" for a while, now they serve lamb and other meats too. pick a specialty and stick with it! and lay off the freaking garlic!

three good stars. this place could be great, the atmosphere is nice and persiany but a little bit cramped. my advice to the owners is to expand the beer and wine list and the vegetarian food section of the menu, they only had the regular crap beers and lager. the food was good, i got the feeling that alot of the veggies in my dish were fresh outta the can. good grape leaves, good hummus, really good grilled octopus and really good falafel,  they almost got another star for that alone! it does seem like it would be a good place to go with six or so people because you'd get to sit at one of the big tables, the 4 top tables have a mysteriously huge base, go, see what i mean! keep reaching for those stars, cedars.
Had to update after dealing with headches post-visit re: insurance.  I don't know how these people made it through medicial school, nursing school, or... any school.

If i could give this location 0 stars, i would. The employees are rude, seem miserable to be there, and never make the sandwiches consistently. The floor is never clean, no matter what time of the day it is. The food that should be kept cold at all times seems a little too warm. 

I stopped going there about a week ago, and JUST found out they were shut down from a health inspection TODAY. They legally cannot open for a minimum of 48 hours, and they will need ALL the time they can get. Needless to say, i don't think i'd give this location another opportunity and will go elsewhere.
Was referred to Club Vapor by a coworker. Nice lounge area with very nice "bar" area to sample flavors. Huge variety of flavors. Price of juice is about the same as other places. Will visit again.
Food is pretty meh. The pakoras were actually pretty fantastic though. Kind of dingy on the inside. The positive thing is that it's pretty cheap.

I have been to a lot of sushi places in Philly and this is one of my favorites. Great sushi, love the specials, great service, BYOB is a plus, and serves there own alcohol, I love the vibe and ambiance. There prices are definitely reasonable for a nice sit down sushi restaurant.

Really cute, lots of little odds and ends. Not too big of a menu... Staff was friendly, knew their stuff. Got food Togo. 

Got turkey bacon avocado sandwiches. Good, nothing really special though.

Bonus points for organic black tea.

Cookies and mousse were really good.

Sometimes I don't want to have to go far for coffee or a latte so I find myself at Cosi.  The staff is usually pretty friendly and if you get a bagel with your drink, there is some sort of deal that makes the pair cheaper.  

Even if they are square, the bagels are still pretty decent.

I agree with many other reviewers that the food isn't as fresh-tasting as it could be. In all fairness, I showed up at 4pm on a Tuesday, so perhaps it's fresher earlier in the day.

It's not the best Indian food I've had. Nevertheless, the buffet selection is decent and most items are vegetarian (everything is clearly labeled). The staff is also friendly and courteous.

My first time here and it was not too busy, the tables were dirty and when we walked up to the counter to order I said hi and did not receive a smile or a greeting. Hopefully the food is still good  I work in customer service and I know that is not how you greet people walking in. Also when the woman who brought us our food asked if we needed anything else, my grandmother asked if she could get her a fork and the lady just said it's self serve instead of having true customer service and just grabbing one. Ummm okay?

I had already anticipated the ubiquitous pink slip in my mailbox when I arrived home from work. I had been waiting for a week for this package whose arrival time my mind had played forward and back, again and again. It was a rare lull in my 7-day, 60 hour workweek, and I snatched the pink paper blindly while running to my car. I drove, it rained, traffic parted to guide me to my destination, doors flew open and welcomed me in. After reaching the beginning of new life at the end of a gray, shuffling line, I handed the folded card to the clerk who greeted me with warm antipathy. She returned moments later with a medium brown box and passed it off to me. "Have a good day, Sean". Only my name's not Sean. My name is not Sean Williamson, and that is not my address. I correct the malevolent clerk and send her reeling back to the purgatory of cardboard architecture- "My address is 1238; the name is Theresa." She traced the same path as first.

"This says Theresa."
"Yes, that's my mother's name."
"Then you need her ID."
"She doesn't even live at this address. I have no way of getting that."
"Then we'll send someone out with another slip in the morning."
"So if I have the slip, I can just walk out with the package with no further hassle?"
"That's right"
"Can I have Sean's package back?"

Virtue becomes her. The same government cog who had previously pilfered an innocent man's mail with little coaxing was now ordering me back into the lobby where I had waited with patience that in hindsight paints my face shameful. How could I be so naive? There is no happy ending for me. The scales of justice weigh heavy with iniquity.
Came on a Monday which I thought was a good night but it was pretty dead. The dancers were A1 tho

First stop in Phili for some breakfast. Had Western Sesame Bagel and coffee. The Bagel has only a few Sesame seeds, so watch out when our Bagel will be picked.  There is no sweet cream cheese available. The coffee, even the fresh brewed one wasn't hot and tasty. The guys from Costi were very friendly.
Do Not Go There!!Bought $600 in Tires cause $600 worth of damage for no reason to `my car!! problem not resolved.

[ overall ]
You don't come here for the food, you come here for the feeling of being "healthy". Mediocre salads that leave you feeling ripped off ($11+) and hungry an hour later. Filled with see-and-be-seen Lululemon types walking in from Pottruck. The conversations you overhear will lower your faith in humanity.

To be fair, maybe the last two gripes only apply to the Penn location, but come on. Just because I'm vegetarian doesn't mean I want to pay $11 for a bowl of rabbit food.

[ vibe and service ]
Think Whole Foods crossed with Lululemon. Staff are friendly enough and work pretty quickly. No complaints here.

[ conclusion ]
Just not worth it when there are so many better, healthy options that also actually taste like food (Hai Street, Hummus, Herban). Take a pass.
Cool vape store for all your vape needs. Awesome e-juices, friendly staff and a very nice selection of many different batteries, atomizers, tips an anything vape related.

If I could give this place 10 stars, I would. 

It really doesn't take much for me to give a five-star review - all a place has to do is NOT screw up on anything (food is good, service is good, décor is good, pricing is commensurate with value received). I don't require the place to go above and beyond.

Reed's goes above and beyond. This is THE perfect small business, run with love and pride.

[ intro ]
Upon entering, Kat and Reed George will personally greet you, ask for your name, and ask if you've ever been here before. They do this with the most genuine warmth and love that I have ever experienced from two strangers. I literally feel like I'm being welcomed home.

[ food ]
I arrived around brunch time (12:30pm) and told George that I am vegetarian, and asked for a breakfast recommendation. He told me about his favourite vegetarian "sausage" (made with soy protein) and offered to cook it into an egg and "sausage" breakfast sandwich on a bagel. Kat also went into the back and grabbed a veggie breakfast burrito and read all the ingredients out to me in case I wanted a different choice, but I went with George's rec.

The sandwich was fantastic, and the best-tasting veggie "sausage" I have ever had. I also ordered a hash brown which was a standard frozen thing, but still quite yummy. Kat brought ketchup and pepper packets and some plastic cutlery.

I'll have to come back for dessert, but the smell of the waffles that the table next to us ordered was simply incredible.

They have a wide selection of high-quality coffees, teas, and espressos, all well done.

[ service ]
Kat and George personally bring food and drinks to each table, and you pay at the end when you leave.

You feel so incredibly at home here.

[ vibe ]
Clean and well-maintained, sunny, and lovely decorations (neat paintings, framed quotes on the wall, old lanterns, a lovely mix of brown-earthy-classy things.

Lots of outlets and wifi for getting work done. Perfect for earnest conversations.

[ conclusion ]
The perfect example of what happens when a small business is run and cared for with love and pride. The walk from Penn is a little long, which might be why nobody knows about this place, and to be honest I don't mind - it's unspoiled by the pretense of places like Starbucks or Hubbub. A earnest and lovable get-away off-campus that lovingly captures what so many businesses lack.
I don't know who wrote that this place opens at 9 AM, but I've definitely never seen it open before 12.

DO NOT GO TO THIS TIRE KINGDOM!

I recently went in for an oil change appointment in which I was told if I came in at 9am ( the minute they open) I would be in and out within an hour. 

INSTEAD, 4 hours later I get a call saying my car is finally ready. When I arrived there were more issues an questions than there was before I dropped my car off. They didn't reset any of my service lights, as typically done. My check engine light, which gets reset after every oil change, was still left on after I asked for them fix it. 

Chris Parker, the store manager, was the most unhelpful and rude person I've ever dealt with at any tire kingdom I have gone too and I have been a customer for 7 years! He tried covering up for all their mishaps and talked very aggressively towards me. He was still unable to solve my problems even after I pointed out their errors. I end up leaving and having to go to the tire kingdom on Fowler that has never done me wrong !  


Lastly, my car had 3 others lights on that They never even asked to inspect and instead were going to let me drive off with an unsafe car! Do not go here if you want good service or to be treated kindly. I promise you Chris Parker will make you feel like you're only good for your money and you can tell his staff are afraid of him.

Why the complaints is beyond me. I've never had a bad meal here and I've been buying lunch and dinner here for more than 5 years.  My favorites are the Shanghai salad with that fabulous ginger dressing and the turkey and Brie sandwiches.  Service is quick and the staff is friendly.  Prices are reasonable for the location and I love my perks such as free entrees and beverages.

Arrived on Saturday night with my wife. They charged us $20 cash apiece.  Included a drink.  Got inside and sign inside said couples free.  Asked why we were charged when leaving 10 mins later and the excuse was they did no know we were together.   This despite the rings and and not asking us like most reputable places would ask.

Last weekend, my fiancé and I had our engagement party here. We rented the whole place out and had about 35 people. The servers setup the tables perfectly and placed water and wine glasses at every seat. They had a laptop connected to the speaker system, which allowed me to hook up a playlist I made on Spotify.  The servers set up two tables in the front of the restaurant, one for alcohol (it's byo) and one for our photos and cake. The set up was so  beautiful. It could not have looked nicer. They left the center area of the restaurant open to allow people to mingle before taking their seats. It was a very ideal setup.
