The chicken salad and the third burger were passable. Needless to say, it was disappointing to get raw burgers after waiting so long. My guests were not impressed.

We ordered take out from them today. Was told it would be 20 minutes. Went to get the food at the time they told us to, then we waited for another 25 minutes for the food. They were totally unapologetic, like this is normal or something. Customer service is terrible. Completely unacceptable. We will not be back- it's absolutely not worth it.
I had brunch there this morning I had a sandwich that was spectacularly good with eggs and cheese and and I have a huge Cubano latte that was just wonderful

Not sure what all the bad reviews are about. This is the best japanese restaurant I've been to *in philadelphia* so far.  I've had plenty of japanese food in San Francisco, Tokyo, NYC, etc. and Shiroi Hana is way better than Zama, Fuji Mountain, etc. This place kind of reminds me of Ise in NY. All the same type of appetizers and entrees.

I have loved every burger I've tried here and always want to bear hug the chef.  I never tire of the fries dipped in aioli sauce. I like that it's a casual, no frills place.  I can't believe they serve vegan food here too.  I love the mac & cheese, although I didn't used to.  My husband and I would sit there eating this mac & cheese complaining how it's too peppery, but not be able to stop eating it.  WTF?  Now, we crave the stuff.  Pretty cool if you ask me.  Great milkshakes too.

I've become quite fond of ground beef and all of it's many incarnations. Meatloaf to meatballs, tacos to lasagna, it's versatility knows no limits. Heck, even though Hamburger Helper tastes just fine by itself , we all know that it's the beef that we crave. Clara Peller knew this and I'm sure you do too. 

Of all it's incarnations, what beef aspires most to become is a Hamburger. I'd go as far as to say, that if a country had to pick a single icon to represent them, America would choose a burger. Fuck Apple Pie!  ( on second thought, knowing my audience, some of you may actually try that).

I've made it my goal to try as many burgers as I can and have already torn through this city, like Wimpy on a bender. The name Sketch had been tossed around frequently, whenever I mentioned my quest. I simply had to try it, but Sketch was playing hard to get. The first time I intended to go, they were closed for a spring vacation. Other times we were nearby, sustenance was found in other places chosen by haters.

Finally, on a recent North Bowl outing, the stars aligned and we all agreed to get our burgers on. As with any worthwhile quest, the journey was difficult. We attempted to walk from North Bowl to Sketch, which isn't too terrible but between the sleety, cold weather, to the darkness it proved difficult. We ended up overshooting it by a few blocks because we were deep in conversation. During the day, this would have been impossible, as the facade of Sketch is as gaudy as a Pastel pimp but We eventually made it inside of the establishment.

It was much smaller inside, than it's reputation led me to believe. I was pretty hungry by this point and was happy that the menu was simple. I chose the onion burger ( it wasn't a burger made out of onions as someone from my table led me to believe, but a beef burger with sauteed onions pressed in) and we decided to share regular and sweet potato fries.

As we waited for our food, it was clear that the name Sketch is not just a name. There was paper and drawing implements on the table and many doodles posted on the walls. We had fun "sketching" eachother and examining other peoples work on the walls. Sketch has a Trader Joes vibe. Kind of a friendly hippy dippy atmosphere that really works for a burger joint. 

The fries came first and they were among the best fries I've ever eaten. The dipping sauce was also a gem. We had made the decision to share and I was beginning to take on a Gollum-like greed towards them counting how many others were taking, searching the table for a sharp knife. Luckily, the burgers arrived, squelching my murderous feelings.

What a burger! Sketch holds it's own among the best burgers I've had. Luckily, I wasn't planning on kissing anyone that evening because there was an entire fried onion patty on that sandwich. Super tasty! 

I sat in the booth afterwards, completely satisfied and feeling like Jughead from the Archie comics. Our server had been excellent ; funny, knowledgable, available.there were interesting homemade dessert options that tempted us but I was content to simply ride out the meat coma I had been placed in.

Overall, I'd have to say that Sketch does ground beef proud. I not only had it my way, but I was lovin' it. I can say with confidence tray the little shop on Girard has the Beef.

this local eatery is about 2 blocks from my favourite intErnational turmeric flavored hangout. the burgers at sketch are large and delish with my fav the truffle burger(yeah it's an acquired taste) with the chili cheese fries, share the fries or "itis" will set in quick. it was worth the ride to bumpy girard ave. order roll  scooped for less messy eat
daym.....im super excited i finally got to try this place. top notch burgers and friendly service. unique interior.

I want to be a fan, but they're on and off. When they're on they're really on, and if they're not, well, be prepared to eat burnt stuff. The last time I was over there, they burned the onions on my burger. The fries were still really good and the burger was really wet and drippy. 
For the most part it was  ok.

Excellent burger for reasonable pricing, sketch also makes their own fresh fries which you can feel in every bite. The tables are filled with paper, crayons and markers which leads to unlimited fun and opportunity to display your art. The staff was very friendly. Would of been 5 stars if only it wasn't freezing while I nipped on my burger and created my masterpiece. If visiting sketch while it's cold out prepare to be chilly. Besides that wonderful experience and definitely would go back.

Shiroi Hana, as many have commented, has beautiful interior with a calming, comfortable ambiance. It is memorable for the way it is minimally decorated and extremely clean. 

The food:

Gyoza: liked the flavor of the filling, but the wrapper wasn't crisp/light

Tempura: beautiful presentation with light batter. Very well-done and great portion/variety.

Tonkatsu - Lightly breaded and tender cutlet. For its price, you get two cutlets worth of katsu, and I think the real treat is the katsu sauce with kewpie mayonnaise. Really lovely.

Sashimi regular- For $25, you get a 12-piece sashimi dinner. Extremely fresh fish, and I love the shredded daikon beneath. The salmon and the yellowtail were exceptional. Filling alongside salad and rice. 

Hamachi don- Again, beautifully fresh hamachi don presented on rice with black sesame. (Chirashi must also be wonderful)

I am looking forward to trying more of their traditional dishes, and I was very taken with their service. Absolutely a gem in Philly.

-

Edit: Surprised with my second visit. Had the chicken teriyaki, which was terribly overcooked chicken breast with a very thin dressing as the "teriyaki sauce." Not moist or flavorful at all. Also, the agedashi wasn't very good, either. Tough tofu and the flavor was a little off.

High quality sushi. Nice list of quality sakes. Fast but not pushy service. Very relaxed and quiet inside. I generally don't take pictures of food but this is one time that I wish I had as the presentations were also really nice.

Very good! After a friend of mine deemed Sketch one of his favorite burgers in Philly, I had to try it. He was on the money... Very good! I had the turkey burger with avocado and horseradish cheddar, it was very good! They season the patty which works very well! The staff were extremely friendly as well! I got it 3 hours ago and I'm still full! Try it!

I heard so many good things about this place so I decided to give it a shot. Got here before the school rush, so it didn't take long for the food. Tried the regular beef burger and grilled chicken sandwich. Enormous, so it'll be worth your money and it seemed like they used fresh ingredients and buns. I enjoyed the burgers and a random conversation with a septa worker. Waiting to be more adventurous burgers next time.
Great food I love the Teri chicken and bang shrimp. Good portions and great staff. It's truly one of my favorite restaurants here in Tucson.

Ok ok, I went to the Luau at Snow Peas... 3 stars. Only because the rice was obviously snow peas, dry boring white rice... When Solid Grindz uses sticky... And they don't have katsu there either... So I will not be going back for that, but doesn't change my die hard love for solid grindz.

Ever been to a place and then find yourself trying to go back? This is that place for me. I never get around to it due to the universe getting between me and the burgers "I'm always talking about at work". MUST find time to come back! My only regret is being on a diet last time I went. I ended up splitting a burger with a friend... And I didn't want to split or share anything after the first bite! Ugh...

This was the second time we rented from Alamo at PHL.  We prepaid everything.  When we got to the airport the shuttle came sort of quickly (could have been faster, but it is a busy airport).  When we got to the lot, I wasn't sure what to do.  A VERY helpful Alamo representative came right out and after looking at the paperwork (pre-printed before the trip) told us to pick a car in our class and load up.  We stopped at the guard house and told the lady about a couple of scratches and dings.  She notated it and off we went.  I stopped in Cherry Hill and filled up.  At drop off I told the VERY nice lady the car had a slight cigarette smell and she took off almost a hundred bucks from the bill (credited my account in about two days).  Will NEVER NEVER NEVER look anywhere else but Alamo, especially at PHL.

I came to Macayo's last week after proclaiming to my boyfriend that I wanted chips and salsa with my dinner that night.  He got a very serious look on his face, simply said "Spinach queso dip.", and we were off.

I have not been to Macayo's in years, not since I was about 11 or 12.  And I remembered it being pretty yummy.  So we ordered up some of this spinach queso dip, and I will just say it was not for me.  My boyfriend was giddy as a school girl over it, and he loved it, but for me it was really thick and I needed to put some of the salsa on it to be able to swallow it.  I guess it's just a difference of opinion.

Now let me tell you about our service.  Macayo's manager or owners, are you reading this part?  Our servers name was Evan, and he was freaking awesome.  Seriously.  Some of the best service I have had in a long time.  He was kind, helpful, enthusiastic (but not over-the-top or annoying), funny and quick to refill our drinks.  He even offered us to-go iced teas.  Don't let this guy go.  

I got the fish tacos.  Also really, really good.  I got the marinated ones instead of the fried ones, and my goodness!  They were tasty and flavorful!  I was not expecting that since, you know, it's here, in Tucson, where there is no ocean.

I am glad to have rediscovered Macayo's.

A cool, unpretentious burger place in the fishtown area of the city (which is kind of getting big these days). Burgers are monstrous and pretty tasty, though you generally cannot move afterwards. I'm a fan of the cyclops burger - burger with an egg - but you will find a few options for everyone - including vegetarians. 

There are few other good burger places in the area, but I would probably hit up sketch because it is laid back and the staff is nice.
Can't wait to try everything they can cook!! Loved the bison bacon burger with horseradish cheddar cheese and avocado, put me in a euphoric food coma!!- super friendly staff and cool atmosphere too!

Shiroi Hana is an above-par neighborhood sushi spot. The ambience is calm & quiet in a fairly casual & clean space.  The menu covers all the bases with your basic appetizers, simple fresh sushi, creative rolls, and some cooked entrees, as well as daily specials. The service was good and our food came out quickly. 

We started off with wine - while it wasn't the best white wine I've ever had, the pour was big, and the more I drank it the better it tasted ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
My mom and I started with two salads - seaweed & house. The SEAWEED SALAD was good, with a touch of acidity from a lemon slice! The HOUSE SALAD used a spring mix and had a tasty ginger dressing. 

We also had a couple of sushi rolls and one of the specials. I forget the name of the special we had, but it was our favorite thing we ordered! If there's a special with a description containing "crispy rice" and "spicy" - get it and thank me later. The dish comes with two planks of thin and crispy rice with a chewy interior, topped with spicy tuna, jalapeno slices, roe, and a sauce. It had the perfect combination of textures and flavors, and I love anything with a spice! My SALMON AVOCADO ROLL was very fresh, and had the perfect amount of rice. I forget which rolls my mom ordered, but she enjoyed hers as well.

With so many Japanese restaurants, Shiroi Hana isn't a place I'd go out of my way for or choose over another more favorable spot, but I wouldn't hesitate going here when in the area!

Stopping in for a burger for lunch with a couple friends I was surprised to find a totally empty burger place, at least with such variety, in such a location.  Walking in your eye jumps to the walls covered in crayon drawings of ideal burgers, jokes, etc. made by previous customers. I know because my friend was rather excited that his was still up by the register. That being said, I was told to get the kobe beef burger and to give my reaction in comparison to 500°, Marathon Grill, PYT, DiBruno Bros., and Squareburger. My companions ordered the same, two well-done, and I being the snob that I am ordered mine medium rare. Now let it be known that I'm not one to complain, I'm always the guy that eats his food in silence, good or bad, you got one shot.

That being said, the burgers arrived burnt to a crisp, almost an insult to well-done. and in addition to that, the harissa aioli that was to adorn my burger was on my friend's sandwich, which he wiped off. Eating my hockey puck, I found the only saving grace were the fries, which tasted to me as though they had been partially cooked earlier and refried to order. I'm all for pommes frites, but I don't think that's quite what they were aiming for. They weren't bad but not what I had hoped for, the availability of dipping sauces saved it (good fries don't need condiments!).

Don't think I'll be returning anytime soon. Maybe if I need a soda...or shade.
This place is very very good.  Bring your appetite as the burgers are big.  Both my daughter and I had the onion burger and thought they were as good as anywhere and the fries were excellent.

Strange experience with the delivery guy(s). I got the knock on the door and opened it to one guy standing there without the pizza in normal clothing and then this other guy with his shirt unbuttoned down to the last button handed me my pizza. I'm talking chest/ chest hair out, shirt almost completely unbuttoned. Not exactly the most appetizing experience. The pizza ended up being just warm but not hot and felt room temperature about a minute after opening. 

Pretty strange experience. Keep your delivery guys in check WP. It's nice to have things stay professional.

Macayos was always my families go to restaurant . Unfortunately the last two experiences have changed that now.I get the minimum wage hike is impacting businesses but when your prices increase and the service declines , it's inexcusable. The waiter made an error and our burritos were made enchilada style . Thank you for scraping off most of the sauce but you could still taste the red sauce ......
 The military discount was a nice treat but now it's only on veteran specific holidays . That discount usually went to the waiter-waitresses tip and would bring us back more often.  The food is starting to decline as well.I don't have an issue with with paying my fair due but the restaurant is on a decline and I hope it goes back to how it used to be .

Chocolate chip cherry cookie with salt flakes was to die for. The stout and smoked popcorn was also ridiculously good. Other things were just ok like the Guinness cake and the pear hand pie (crust was nice and flaky though) so overall I would go back definitely get those first two things and then try some more

Food and staff are amazing. I used to live in Fishtown and this was a favorite stop for dinner or lunch. Their specials are always delicious as well. I will go back whenever I visit and always recommend to others.

Best microwave dinner I've had in a while. Ordered a chimichanga and it was fried, put on a plate with the leftover rice and beans then microwaved. It was ok tasting but the chimichanga was soggy from being nuked and the rice and beans were dry. 

Positives:
Great service
Spinach queso
Salsa

This place is my favorite spot for sushi. I usually get take out but I've come here with friends a few times. 

If you come here to sit down it's a small restaurant but usually very quiet. The staff is great and the sushi is my favorite of the city they have a great selection. 

The only reason I give them 4 stars and not 5 is because their hours annoy me. They are closed in the middle of the day and that's usually when I want sushi.

This place was perfect for a Saturday afternoon with a toddler.  Family friendly, quick, and delicious.  Excellent burgers, perfect milk shakes, yummy seasoned fries with your choice of dipping sauces.

I am always in search of my next favorite burger, and this might just be it.  What I liked most of all- the staff, they were all SO kind, friendly, and accommodating.  Will definitely be going back.

Come with an empty stomach- these burgers are big.

Shiroi Hana is a tasty and aesthetically pleasing restaurant. The food is very fresh and flavorful. I do not enjoy a lot of Philly's Japanese restaurants but this place is pretty exceptional. The staff are attentive and accommodating. The place is very clean and decorated beautifully. The cream, pale yellow, and brown décor is very inviting and soothing. I love coming here in the cold weather and getting settled in with a hot hand towel and a cold Sapporo. 

The sushi portions are quite large and they are generous with the sashimi. The udon is tasty and the teriyaki and chirashi dishes are not half bad. I knock a star off because I do think it is overpriced. I have had a few rolls that were mediocre and there are much cheaper Japanese places out there with a higher quality of food. Overall, Shiroi Hana is a pleasant restaurant and worth checking out.

I am a raw fish fanatic, and am always willing to drop the extra money for quality sushi, but this restaurant is definitely NOT the place to do it.

My boyfriend and I ordered edamame for starters, and three specialty rolls. The edamame was dried out from being over-microwaved, and the rolls were the smallest/dullest $15 rolls I have ever seen in my life. 

The ambiance is really nice for a sushi restaurant, which is why I gave it two stars instead of one, but it's definitely not worth the low-grade fish, stingy portions, and lack of plate presentation.

We were so dissatisfied with this place that my boyfriend and I went to another sushi joint the next day. We spent half the amount, and got twice the amount of food WITH better quality. Sure, I had to sacrifice the nice lighting and table cloth at the other place, but my stomach and I left a hell of a lot happier.
Consistently excellent and fresh. By far the best sushi in Center City.

While not a culinary tour de force, Solid Grindz is pretty much exactly what the name would imply. 

The first comparison that'll come up is with Mama's Hawaiian BBQ, and they're pretty comparable. Solid Grindz has a bit more expansive of a menu though, but they're both worth trying out. 

I got a 3 entrée plate with Shrimp, Chicken, and Pork, along with some beans and Tuna Macaroni Salad. I figured that the Tuna Mac Salad would have actual Tuna in it, but I didn't notice any actual fish... but it definitely had a canned tuna flavor. I don't know if I'd call that a positive or a negative, I'll leave that up to you. The Teriyaki Chicken, oddly, seemed to be straight from Panda Express. It's not a bad thing, but while it was filling and tasty, was not necessarily revolutionary. The Bang Shrimp wasn't spicy, but it was a breaded shrimp with a good tropical flavor to it. Probably the highlight of the entire experience, although there were no low points either. The Kalua Pork they offer is cooked with cabbage and other vegetables, and is pretty solid. Their Island Beans are in essence, baked beans with some peppers. 

I will say that I had to stand there for a few minutes waiting to order, being ignored by the cashier. They did have a few orders to bring out but it would have been nice to be acknowledged. 

Overall, this was 14 dollars with a drink included. It was a BIG meal and definitely filling and not a bad price at all. The shrimp was the best part, but while nothing was truly a home run, it was all certainly good. Solid Grindz is exactly that, solid. Not an all star establishment, but a solid restaurant making good food at a reasonable price.
Best burgers in Philly! Check out my full review here! :) http://goodyummyeats.wordpress.com/2013/09/10/sketch-burger-the-best-burgers-in-philly/

I'm giving this place 4 stars instead of 5 mainly based on our last visit. We have been to this location twice and the most recent visit the service wasn't very impressive. Here is some backgroud. We recently moved here from Las Vegas where they also have Macayo's (same exact company). So we found out on our first visit that they do things a little different at Macayo's out here. Which is fine, it's still very good. They have a different menu, different salsa, more selection of sides, different side of baja sauce (they serve it cold as opposed to being put under the broiler like were used to).
So my husband's absolute favorite salsa is the "smooth" salsa that they serve along with a "chunky" salsa (my favorite) at their Vegas locations. So the first time we visited this Tucson location they just brought out "chunky". So my husband politely asked our server if they had a "smooth" variety of salsa he could have instead. Our server said "yeah" and brought out smooth for him which he was very pleased with. That first visit was great, our server was on the ball and very accommodating. Now our most recent visit which was just a few days ago. We had a different server who brings out just "chunky" salsa. My husband again kindly asks if he can get the "smooth" salsa. The waiter jokes with him "Yeah, You want me to strain it through my fingers to get all the chunks out". We don't know if he was just trying to be funny or if we was just being facetious because he never did bring out smooth salsa, which my husband was very annoyed about. Other than that our server was fine but we both look forward to the salsa and chips when we go to Macayo's and that kind of put a damper on our dining experience. Especially for my husband. 
Also on our first visit I ordered the calabacitas which were amazing! They were slightly caramelized, salted/seasoned well, tasted like it may had been cooked with some butter. They were very very tasty! On our second visit I ordered calabacitas again and they were not the same. They tasted fine but were not caramelized, and definitely not salted/seasoned. Not nearly as much flavor as the first time I had them. Not liking the inconsistency going on there. 

Besides those two issues with the smooth salsa and calabacitas everything was great.

This place needs a complete overhaul. We went to Macayo's because a family member we were dining with wanted to go there. Ughhhhh...bad Tex-Mex and chit chatting with distant family members? Shoot me now.

The food was subpar, every single one of our orders was wrong and the service was slow to boot. That is the restaurant death hat-trick folks. 

Just say NO to bad "Mexican" food.

Stumbled upon this place by accident and decided to give it a try. Candidly I was heading to Jimmy Johns in the same shopping area but saw their sign and stopped in here instead.  Location isn't great and that's a shame, but they more than make up for it in service and quality.  They greeted me when I came in, I told them it was my first visit so they gave me the low down: homemade bread/rolls which to me is a major plus, lots of variety, and  they offer hot pressed subs. The menu is diverse and eclectic, it was very difficult to decide what to get.  

The two nice ladies working the counter couldn't have been more friendly and helpful.  The sub was inexpensive (compared to their overpriced competitors) and they don't skimp on the ingredients.  Very healthy 6" sandwich.  Great experience, I will definitely be back as it is my new 'go to' sandwich joint in Tucson. 

Cheers!
Went in today for lunch and I was super impressed. Everything tasted amazing. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Definitely going back.

I started coming to Macayo's in 1999, and I think tks is a great restaurant. I recommend it to friends visiting Tucson for a good quality mask at a great price. My favorite meal is the chimichanga de Macayo. I always start with a cheese crisp. I also always leave with left overs which keep very well for a second meal.

Yum! Around the corner from my house, it's filling (huge burgers), and I'm envious of the mac and cheese. It's sooooo good. I've so far had the regular burger and the turkey burger. You also get a choice of sauce for the burger, and I chose chipotle. Choose chipotle!

They also have a special board, and my b/f got some fish tacos (fried fish). They were okay, but I like unfried fish in my tacos. I can't remember what else I've had here, but their baked goods look insane too! I wonder if they're open in the morning for those...

We've always gotten takeout, but sitting in would be cute. The place is full of sketches (duh) and kitschy decor. There are 3-4 booths and some other tables. I like the counter by the window. Very decent. Thumbs up, and all that!
The first thing that struck me about this place wasn't the food, but the amazing service I received from the minute I walked in. The delicious food is the cherry on top!

All of the food I've had here has been absolutely delicious and the staff have always been excellent. The restaurant itself has a bit of a hipster feel to it which I kind of like, but may leave something to be desired for some. Appearances aside, this place is fantastic!

The best burgers you'll probably ever have. Definitely order truffle butter on your burger, you'll thank me later. They also have great Belgian-cut fries that come with your choice of dipping sauce. The space itself is really small (I'd say only about 20-25 customers can fit) so you may have to find the right time of day to go, but its not one of those line-out-the-door places. All in all, Sketch is a Fishtown staple and a Philadelphia gem, and every time a friend of mine visits Philly for the first time I take them here.

I have always had good sushi here.  I've been here for lunch with a colleague, for dinner with my six year-old son, dinner with just adults, and a big party (upstairs there are more tables and you can have a private party up there).  The service is quick.  If you want a leisurely, cool, funky night out - don't come here for that.  If you want great sushi, interesting rolls, and fresh sashimi - come for the food.  When I came with my son (who LOVES sushi), the waitress was very nice to us and accommodating.  This is a kind of place where you will see some business dinners, small groups of friends, dates, and a few kids.
Amazing fries, great burgers! BYOB? Even better. A must visit in Fishtown. The Cyclops Burger and aioli sauce are the best.

Just a quick review

I've been to Philly twice and both times I had to get some Sausage to bring back home.  Love Martins!!

The Buffalo Chicken is quite tasty!  Actually every flavor I've tried has been great - Italian Hot - Garlic - Provolone - Sweet... mmmm mmm!

I'm pretty picky with burgers and Sketch totally delivers.  The beef is what stands out to me.  Great flavor and freshness.  Not too salty but not flavorless. Also not oily.  The burgers sit extremely well in my belly.  No drama.  

Best of all is the incredibly friendly service.  It's great to get a smile and cheerful personality.  It makes a difference and shows that they care about what they are doing. Burger temps are accurate which is great.  If you can't get that right..,.

Anyway.  I work in the city so it takes a lot to bring me back down on my free time and sketch burger is often a reason to make the drive.   There are always people here which is another sign of good food.

This place was referred to me as "the best burger in Philadelphia" and so far, I must agree.

I had a truffle burger, rare and without cheese and it was GOOD. Perhaps one of the best hamburgers I've ever eaten. The waitress was reluctant to put it down on the table when she brought it out, she kinda wanted to eat it herself (and told me as much).

The fries were also good. I could not finish them, due to the immensity and nature of the burger I ate with them. I suggest two people per cone.

Will definitely bring others here for the tasty experience.

I LOVE THIS PLACE.  Staff is friendly, please is clean, sanitary and great atmosphere.   I would give an additional star it would be great if they served wine!  *Joking...no really they need to serve wine.

I used to get just my pedicure here and then took a leap of faith when my original eyebrow person was not available at another store....they ended up perfect.  I got gel nails manicure for the first time and they were great..2 weeks later still intact.   I have been to most all of the staff in there and they are consistent but now I mostly deal with 1 staff member.  I would highly suggest trying this place, you will not be disappointed.

Did take out just before closing.  Tuna, salmon and double eel.  Unbelievable.  Glad I took a walk around the block of the hotel.  The tuna and salmon were very high grade.  Reasonable prices as well!

Great menu terrible service. I have been there a few times and they always seem overwhelmed regardless if there are other people waiting on orders or not. There is also always a very long wait over 10 minutes for a drink. They had a sign on the door that they would open at 7 due to the heat, at 715 the doors were still not open, even though the woman inside saw me waiting that entire time. I love supporting local business, but it's hard to support one that doesn't provide great service.

I've been trying for months to actually go here, and last night was the first time they were actually open.  Mostly worth the wait.  

The burgers are kind of huge.  Delicious, but gut busting.  I don't think much would be lost making the burgers more reasonably sized. The vegan burger was really good--had a texture similar to a well done meat burger, but was a bit flavorless.  Good thing for the sauce and additions!  As a vegetarian, I'd rather have this burger than one down the street at the burger place on the Piazza.

Fries?  Outstanding.  Seriously.  They had sweet potato fries as a special and, well, yum.  Possibly the best sweet potato fries I've ever had.  The standard fries were also delicious.

Cookie for dessert was taken on the road, because I just didn't have room.  It was pretty good--kind of greasy, but deliciously indulgent. 

My dining companions got shakes, so it's no wonder they had no room for dessert. 

Price was very reasonable,

Went here last night w/ the BF. It's a little weird being in love with a meat-eater, but I'm trying to get used to it. He seemed to really enjoy his burger, but this is my [vegan] review, not his.

Great atmosphere, really fun, I love any opportunity to use crayons! LOVED the fries. Had the seitan sandwich & well, I kind of hated it. I also kind of hated their BBQ sauce.

Nevertheless, I'd go back for the fries alone, and I'd give the veggie burger a chance...as well as the vegan chocolate shake (duh).

If I really like the veggie burger, I'll update my review. But awesome fries alone can't carry any more than 3 stars.

Pros:
-Great burgers
-Great food in general
-Cool theme!

Cons:
-Doesn't accept cards, ATM inside
-It's slightly out of the way for most people
-Fairly small.

We had dinner here Saturday night. It wasn't crowded and the friendly server helped us choose a sake that we were very happy with. The fish is fine, nothing special. In general,  bland -- even the spicy tuna hand roll -- and overpriced. (When a meal is great, I never mind the price. If I'm not impressed, I notice it!) The sashimi deluxe was just lops of tuna, salmon, and yellowtail. When we ordered mackerel for some variety, the sushi chef handed us more salmon.  Overall, eh. You can find better.

Biggest patty I've ever seen and ohhhhhhhhh so juicy. Could've used some more salt in the meat but I know a lot of people don't like seasoned beef so I won't hold it against them. Fries were delish too. I'd definitely recommend. Visiting Philly and was pleasantly surprise

I really like their burgers here, like.. a lot. I've never gotten anything other than the Truffle butter burger + mushrooms + swish cheese. They actually cook the burger however you order it, it's always perfectly medium when I order. It's juicy, truffly, and you just can't go wrong there with a solid burger.
My friends have raved about the Dr. Pepper Pulled Pork and also the Cyclops burger. I just can't say no to truffle.
The sweet potato fries were also perfectly crispy and nice and tender on the outside.
The burger will run you between $8-11 most likely depending on type / toppings you get . 
2 burgers + sweet potato fries + 2 sodas ran us to a $29 bill.

Friendly staff as well. And I love all the sketch drawings on the walls!
Solid burger, not worth the wait.  Seated immediately, waited 30 mins just for fries then another 20 minutes for a burger that took me 5 minutes to eat. Ridiculously slow wait staff as well.

Hands down my favorite burger in Philadelphia, I always get the same thing but my god why would I change.
I get the truffle burger, angus beef cooked in truffle butter, with truffle seasoning topped with mushrooms.  I add a fried egg, thick cut bacon and some advocado.  Mmmmmm, so good.  But the fries could take center stage on their own.  Handcut, fried till every bite is ultra crispy and then dip them into sketchs spicy garlic aioli sauce.  Omg soooo good!
And when your done drop the 2-3 bucks on a fresh cookie. Add a soda and your looking at spending $20.

Not to shabby, if I say so myself!

I went here over the weekend (6/4/11) and ended up walking away with one of the worst face-to-face customer service experiences I've ever had. Things started out ok. I ordered 1 half-pound steak and one half-pound pork chop. Then, the elderly gentleman who waited on me attempted several times to get me to purchase a larger quantity of meat. First it was another steak, then, after I declined, another pork chop. After I rebuffed his second attempt, he became visibly annoyed, and implied that my "small" meat purchase was somehow un-American. I don't want to use Yelp to make any big social-political statements, but maybe that's exactly the problem with America and our current obesity epidemic. Anyway, I definitely won't be going back to this stand again, nor would I encourage anyone else to patronize a food vendor with such a backward outlook on nutrition.

The service here is good.  We were acknowledged as soon as we walked in the door and they were ready to take our order right away.  We ordered a large pizza with pineapples, wings half BBQ half Buffalo and garlic knots.  The only thing that was good was the garlic knots and the sauce they gave with it was delicious, you could tell it was made in house.  But the pizza was a soggy mess.  A puddle of liquid in the center when they delivered it to our table, the girl even apologized for the liquid in the middle and the wings were so overcooked they were barely edible.  Limp pizza slices and no flavor, very very thin crust and just a mushy mess.  I do not recommend this place.  I think if I went back it would only be for the garlic knots.

Oh. My. God. This is the best burger that I've ever had in my entire life. 

I've been hearing a lot about this place, but haven't been to check it out myself. I'm so glad that I now have first-hand knowledge about the awesomeness that is Sketch. 

I went with three friends, and we all got something different...then switched plates so we could each try everything. I got the burger with truffle butter and mushrooms, and I cannot say enough good things about it. It was absolutely mouthwatering. Another friend got a Kobe beef burger with avocado and bacon, which was also amazing. It had a garlicky aioli sauce on it that our server (I think the owner?) said was homemade. Delicious! 

The third person in our party ordered the pulled pork sandwich. It was sweet, with a little bit of kick, and juicy...not dry at all. As much as I love the burgers, the next time I come in (and there will be a next time), that's what I'm ordering. Finally, another friend ordered a couple of different empanadas from their specials board. They had a few different varieties available, and everything we tried was yumtastic.

Lots of people love the fries, and I'm no exception. I'm so glad that I found this spot, and will make it a regular Philly visit. Oh, and the staff and servers were awesome...very helpful and friendly. Wins all around!!
Some of the best Hawaiian cuisine I've ever had! Good food and great service! Would defiantly recommend it to anyone!
Great place. I can't not get a burger every time I come here. The fries are awesome. Everyone here is kind and helpful.

Usually a decent place for quick sushi but after the customer service we received after take-out today,  I would not recommend anyone to pay a visit. After receiving poor quality fish and skin on a roll we called and was told "I checked it over and everything looked fine. " I'm not sure which is worse,  knowingly serving us less than acceptable fish or arguing that it was correct. Poor form!!  Not worth the visit!!

Yo! My fav fav favorite sushi place at PA! Fresh sashimi ever! The presentation of the sushi is perfect. I like the best is the spider roll. Love the little tail. Oops.. The taste of wasabi is still in my mouth. Deliciousss.. Service here is fast and clean too. Price is reasonable. Dude, give it a try!

I had to wonder where the sauce was for my pizza! I lifted the cheese and didn't see any. The toppings didn't go to the edge, so I felt like I was just getting crust, and it was dry and chewy. We didn't have this problem at the Carrollwood location.

I'm going to keep this short.

The burgers are overrated. I ordered mine medium rare because I like 'em juicy, and what I got was medium well. The first few bites I was fooled into thinking it was delicious but as I continued to chow down, I started feeling like I was duped. I almost had dry mouth. Ugh! Not even the freshness of the lettuce and tomato could help that poor, bland wannabe burger.

Needless to say, I was disappointed. I was really in the mood for a delicious burger and based upon the good things I'd heard about theirs, I thought for sure this would be a four or five star experience. Wah, wah, I'm crying now.

While I won't go back to Sketch for a burger, I will go back for their phenomenal milkshakes. Those babies are super thick and mighty tasty. Best milkshake I've had in a long time, possibly even in my entire life. (They really are that good. I'm not exaggerating.)

Oh, the green chili cheese fries are quite scrumptious, too, but overpriced for the amount you get. The plain fries, on the other hand, just fail. We're talking FAIL Blog fail. Maybe Sketch was having a bad day?

Overall, the milkshake is Sketch's saving grace. Now that I think about it, maybe my review is biased because I prefer milkshakes to cheeseburgers. Hmm ... just maybe.

PS. What's with the little signs all over the place basically asking you to tip your server? Um, what server? You order at the register and the woman brings your food to the table when it's ready. That does not a server make. I think they should decide what they're going for here. If I'm going to tip someone, I shouldn't have to order and pay at the register, as well as clean off my table afterward. Hmm ... a little sketchy, no?
I was really disappointed with the food. It was bland, and you could taste the bitterness of the old oil used to fry the food.

okok, so im writing from the vegan's perspective. 

I have heard lots of great things from people about their meat and other nonvegan food but I am vegan, so:

I get very excited when places are vegan friendly and even will pay the extra money in order to enjoy a vegan coffee milkshake, because how often does that happen? not often at all. I loved sketch, and never stopped recommending it to people.

BUT I have finally had it. Too many times I have gone into this vegan friendly joint to be served something that i thought was vegan with non vegan items on it. For example, I order a vegan burger, its served on a nonvegan bun, or they change their sauces from mostly all vegan to only two that are and not mention it. So I find out when im re-reading the menu while i wait for my boyfriend to finish. 

I am no longer going to spend 22 bucks on a grain based burger (THAT TASTES DIFFERENTLY EVERYTIME) french fries, and a milkshake. I was a sucker a few times, but no longer.

I haven't had Belgian fries like this in a long while.  They are really crispy on the outside and hot and fluffy on the inside.   They come  before your burger and really hot.  My only criticism of them is that they aren't long enough.  You end up fishing in the basket for fry pieces which is really annoying.   I still ate most of them.  For $2 with a sauce for a small order, it's a bargain.

I got the beef burger.   Extremely huge burger, I wish there was a mini version or a 6oz one instead.   Half a pound of burger is a lot.  I asked for it medium and it was slightly over medium, but I can be really picky about burger temperature.   A little annoying, but still a good burger.  Also, the cheese was really gooey and kinda slid off the burger and then the burger began to fall apart.   The caramelized onions were cooked down a lot, but you could tell they were prepared well in advance and was cold.  

All things considered, I'll be back and please the the Harissa aioli on the fries, it was great!

I'm a bit of a burger snob.  Maybe it's specificity that I search for, but this place didn't really impress me.  The burgers are monsterous and messy (though I got mine mid-rare and a fried egg) but it seemed like it was almost an inch thick and served in a paper tray.  There weren't a whole lot of tastes and textures, but it wasn't a "bad" burger either.  I think that the burgers at Abbaye or Standard Tap are better than this place.  The Belgian Fries are pretty decent (though nothing like Pommes Frites in NYC) and the sauces (I only tried two) are also pretty good and lardy.  

It's got a quaint interior, colorful, small.. but it's very comfortable.. complete with paper and markers to "sketch" your own drawing.  Get it now?  The employees and servers are really nice.  

Worth a visit, but I wasn't completely sold.

We found this place extremely randomly, we were on our way to the Sugar House, and happened to see this place on the way.

Those fries. Those Belgian cut french fries. a large order for only $3. I'm loving this place. Fancypants restaurants also put these "pommes frites" in a cone with mayonnaise and charge like $12. not the case at sketch.

My husband got the Dr.Pepper pulled pork sandwich, ( i tried a bite..or 3) it was awesome, came on a nice soft bun. Just delicious.  I wanted a burger really bad because they all sounded so good, but i knew I wouldn't be able to eat something that big so I opted for the hot dog, which was delicious and came on nice baguette bread. The highlight though was definitely those fries, and the garlic aoili it came with. 

I am a compulsive doodler, so it was great that we could sit and draw little pictures until our food came as well.

I can't wait to go back.
Because of the menu, location, and yelp cred I could definitely see myself being a regular here.... if the burgers were three or four dollars cheaper.

Best Hawaiian place in Tucson!!!!!!!!

Definitely recommend to anyone who wants a taste from the island!

Not only are the burgers delicious but the staff is super accomodating, they have a fun dog walking around the restaurant and the milkshakes are to die for!!

I got the vegan burger with mushrooms and onions (i am not a vegan but wanted to try something different) It was amazing and the french fries made the meal!! Can't wait to go back and try something new
I've tried eating here 3 times and have yet to be able to try it. Everytime I've gone its been closed when though it's their normal business hours.

One of The Best Burgers that I've had in a while, Awesome! My Kobe Burger was Tender and Juicy through every bite, paired with Fresh Toppings(Lettuce, Tomato and Pickles)and Great Cheese Selections-It's a match made in Heaven. The French Fries were "The Bomb"! We ordered the Cheese Fries, Parmesan Truffle Fries and Regular Fries. They were All Great and with Their House-Made Sauces We were in French Fry Heaven! We Loved every minute of Our Eating Experience! We plan to return soon!

Their business hours are not 5pm.. it is 5:30pm! It is abit later then other restaurants, but 30min was so worth it!

I ordered Sashimi plater. They presented 3 pieces per fish and there were 4 different fishes.(total 12 sashimi) When I saw the dish, I was bit disappointed about the amount/varieties compare to the price, but it was so worth it! It was fresh (of course) and the thickness of the sashimi were pretty decent, so it full me up very quickly.

I am very look forward to visit this place again. Very good service or course!!!
Sketch is a great find.  Love the enthusiasm of the owner Phyllis.   She's truly a Foodie and it shows in every way.  You must try her homemade desserts as well as her great sandwiches and fries.

We are just passing through Tucson and saw an ad for this restaurant.  Looked good so we gave it a try.  Wonderful meat!!! My wife had the brisket while I had the pork ribs.  Each meal came with beans, coleslaw and potato salad, each great in its own right. My wife got so much brisket, she couldn't finish it and we took back to the hotel.  I got three nice sized ribs with lots of meat with a really nice char on them.  Sauce was really good addition price was just $13 for each meal and a coke ran $2.00.
Great deal on a great meal. Wish we were staying longer in town.

Terrific food, my favorites are the Smashed onion Burger, the Falafel, the sweet potato fries with Garlic Aoli sauce and there yummy desserts. Also the server is awesome, music is great and the atmosphere is fun. I love the sketches on the walls.

I don't understand the bad reviews! They make their own vegan burgers which is pretty awesome. Plus they're creative with toppings and sides. Decor leaves a little to be desired, but I can look past that for delicious food.

Tried this place out last night. I had the kobe burger and it was grilled to perfection..very, very good! I'm giving them only four stars because I also had the fries which were nothing to write home about. But I would definitely have the burger again.
Best burger in the city. They REALLY need to start accepting credit cards and delivery...even grubhub or postmates. I would order WAY more if they offered delivery services.

I only come here for their desserts, which by the way are to die for ~ especially the carrot cake and chocolate layered cake.  The staff is fun and very personable and always a joy to see.  I haven't tried their bread, but it always seems to fly off the shelf when I'm there.

OK, I'm very disappointed that I have to write a less than stellar review of a neighborhood venture. I just cant look past the fast that I paid over $12 dollars for a burger that I ended up throwing away.

I decided to check it out one night while my wife was at work and I had the house to myself. Seeing all the positive feedback Sketch has been receiving and the fact that I live one street away had already formed a good opinion in my mind with out actually eating anything yet.

I ordered the Kobe burger with pepperjack cheese and aioli sauce. I believe the total came to just below $13. 

First of all, that instantly takes it out of the family friendly category for me. I can't fathom spending $39.00 before drinks and tips for my wife and son, but then again, I'm middle class. Seems like there are many new to the hood, where this isn't an issue, I'm envious of you.

Now I took my burger to go. I'm sitting at home, unwrapping the large sandwich, looking forward to my first bite. That's when I encounter my first problem and probably a personal preference, but it was an issue for me. The cheese was sliced way too thick. I had two quarter inch thick for a total of one half inch thick slice of cheese. They didn't melt at all and I like my cheese to some what melt. Maybe others like it this way, if that were my only problem, I'd give Sketch better review and make sure I tell the food prep person to slice thinner.

My main issue and this is the deal sealer is that the burger was so salty it was gross. I could feel the salt crystals on my teeth when biting down. It was the nastiest taste. My best guess is that the slat shaker lid fell off when making this, I cant see how else this could happen. i was able to eat about a quarter or so before the taste was so bad I tossed it.

If any of the Sketch people see this, please ditch the salt, leave it up to the individual eater to put salt/pepper on their own burger. I'm sure this was just a aberration since I didn't see anything in other reviews saying this, but it was enough for me.

We used to go every Sat. night for probably 10 plus years.. we loved the atmosphere and the margaritas were the best I had found in Tucson..It's such a shame that the portion size decreased the price increased and the margaritas were like a frozen slushy...the only thing that kept us going back was our server Rich...he was wonderful, but even he wasn't enough to keep us coming back..so sorry to see our tradition go by the wayside, I know things change and prices increase, but not to such a drastic point..If you are still working there Rich, know we miss you.
Cool customer artwork on the walls and great food. The place is super small but service was quick and burgers, fries and shakes are delicious.

Had a pretty great experience overall but enough nitpicking to knock it down to 3 stars. This tiny restaurant has a sparse yet intimate feel. First gripe is the wine selection or lack thereof. I think they had like 4. My second gripe was the miso soup; I have never before had miso soup that I disliked before although of course some are better than others. Theirs had a strange, mysterious fishy taste. My final gripe was the lack of exciting dishes on the menu for non sushi lovers. I settled on chicken teryaki. On the upside the chicken teriyaki was very tasty and too plentiful for me to finish. They offered white or brown multigrain rice so I chose the latter. I'm not sure what kind of rice it was as it was a purplish shade but it was very tasty. Our server was wonderful; attentive but unobtrusive. The experience was lovely but I'd be much more likely to return if I liked sushi!

Sketch is one of my favorite burger joints in Philly. Way better than PYT hands down. Their smashed onion burger with green goddess sauce.. WOW. The burgers are always moist and juicy!  I also love that they make vegan treats. Their sweets always look so delicious, but I'm usually too stuffed to thing about more food after I shove down a burger and some sweet potato fries. 

Only complaint is the service is spotty. Sometimes is can be really slow. It's also cash only which can be annoying when you forget to get cash out prior to going.

I love their Hawaiian food. We really enjoy the bang shrimp, the teriyaki chicken, chicken Katsu and kahlua pork. I really like their tuna Mac salad side. Good portions. Unique, fresh food. Great atmosphere and friendly staff. They recently changed locations and the setting is much nicer now. I started eating it as just a food truck and now 2 locations later I'm still a huge fan. I highly recommend.

Good prices. Veggie burger with chipotle sauce is amazing! The seitan special was really salty- which was unpleasant so ask for no salt! The sweet potato fries are amazing- I didn't really like the table service tonight- I miss the old fashioned way order at the register and then they bring you food- but I guess that way you didn't have to tip so they now make more money

Their sausages are always fresh and delicious, and the prices are reasonable. The people who work behind the counter are friendly and quickly fill orders. I try to visit often because they have a rotating list of specials. I love that they have lots of turkey and chicken alternatives.

Sketch WTF!?
I've been coming to your business for awhile & have noticed a steady decline - especially since the new owner of the business.

Taking the falafel off the menu?!! So sad, it was by far the best item on the menu. The veggie burger is just meh at best.

We have ordered take-out & items have been missing from our order.... including the top of a bun to the burgers. Items have also recently been cold. 

Not sure how I'm feeling about Sketch lately. :/

Food was decent. Service was  horrible. Drink order was taken promptly. I had eaten about half the chips by the time the order was taken. Food took a long time to arrive. Took about 10 to 15 to eat but I waited and extra 20 or more to get my check. I finally just stood up and walked to the cashier. Cashier had to find my server. I can understand this type of service if the place is busy but there was only one other table in the area I was seated at and a handful of tables being used in the other side of the restaurant. So my lunch hour took 1.5 hours because of the poor service. 
I think the servers should ask customers during the week at lunch time if they are in a hurry due to lunch breaks so that they know not to lolly gag throughout the day.
The seitan sandwich I had tonight was really, really good.  Their seitan sandwiches have come a long way from when they first opened.

Hands-down the best chimichangas in town! Macayo's is a family favorite we have been going to for years. Sometimes the service leaves room for improvement but the food makes up for it! Try their frozen margaritas and soups!

They have a special that includes 2 large 
Slices of pizza and a drink for 6 dollars.
Many types of pizza to choose from.
They also heat the slices.
It's perfect! 
I enjoy there pizza and eat there often.

We came searching for dessert, and left anything but satisfied. The following statement is not an exaggeration: the flan was frozen solid, as you can see from the photo.  That would be great...if I was looking for flan ice cream. To sum it up: epic fail. :(

I've only ever gotten ground turkey, ground beef, and various different types of sausages, chicken spinach and cheese, straight chicken, chorizo, and they are all very very good. 

If you need or want some fresh meat, then get your craving satisfied by martins quality meats, they know how to wrap it up right!

Unfortunately, we did not love this place and there are much better burgers elsewhere in the city...

Pros:
Quick, friendly, and efficient service
Cold toppings (lettuce, tomato, onion and pickles were fresh, cold and tasty)
Buns were fresh and sauces were pretty good
Fun decor with drawings of patrons on the wall - great for kids!

Cons:
Sirloin burgers did not have any flavor on their own - so cheese and sauce are necessary 
Ordered the sweet potato fries and they were mostly burnt and basically inedible
Average milkshakes (not a ton of flavor) - bit pricey at $6 a pop

It seems others enjoyed the Kobe and Truffle burgers more so if I went back I'd be inclined to try one of those, but other than a huge fairly cheap burger, there's not much to praise here in terms of taste.

First of all, I want to say I've been going to Macayo's Del Este ever since I've lived in Tucson, or since 1997. I can honestly say it was hands-down my favorite restaurant ever. I brought family there when they visited from out of state, friends, etc. A close friend of mine and I have every single Bob and Cha Cha mug in every imaginable color (even a few of the new "smaller" mugs which I was dismayed to see as they are considerably smaller than the older ones). The prickly pear margarita (frozen) was to die for. Every weekend, we looked forward to our prickly pear. We even suffered through the "no more prickly pear margarita refills at a reduced price" fiasco (though we had to argue just a wee bit with the waiters over paying full price even though we had the Bob and Cha Cha mugs with us)!  Over the past year, nearly every time we've gone it's taken a long time to get our order or even be waited on in the first place despite there being LOTS of empty tables all around us. To top it off, the last few times we have been to Macayo's, the prickly pear margarita was NOT prickly pear. Just white froth with hardly any pink to it at all. We went one more time JUST to be sure and nope, it was the same. Sad to say, I just don't think we will be back. I will have to settle for keeping my Bob and Cha Cha mugs on display until the day when I find the time to learn how to make my own frozen prickly pear margaritas!
This guy is a jack**s. He is like an old stereotypical used car sales man. It was really not a good shopping experience. I would actually ask anyone reading this to shop else where.

Last year when I was here with my granddaughter visiting my son and his wife and son we had dinner here and it was so good that when my granddaughter and I were discussing things we'd like to do when we came this year visiting this restaurant was at the top of our list! Once again we were not disappointed.  We had a variety of dishes including the enchilada sampler, the Bahamas burrito, the build your own combo and the child's plate with tacos, toastadas, and chimichongas. Everything was generously portioned and delicious. Our server Jared exceeded our expectations with his attention to detail and prompt care. He was warm,friendly, and knowledgeable about the food and beverages. My only suggestion concerned the drink special they had. It was a watermelon and jalapeño Margarita. It was a good drink but lacking both the expected watermelon and jalapeño flavors. I feel if you are going to advertise a flavor profile it should be first and foremost and this was a great lime drink with no watermelon or jalapeño flavor.  We'll probably go again before we head back to Florida and we'll definitely be back when we come back next year.

Bf brought me here after he saw this place on some food show. It's a good find. Based on the reviews, we tried the green chili cheese fries. They were good. Seasoned well. We shared a veggie empanada. That came with this tasty green dipping sauce. I ordered the vegan burger with hot mustard. Really good. My bf got the beef burger w wasabi sauce. He liked it a lot. We saw some really cool artwork on the walls too. Staff was friendly and attentive.

Huge burgers and all of them are delicious. If ordering the cyclops burger, ask the egg to be cooked enough that the yolk won't explode all over when you in that first bite. And the sweet potato fries are the best. Get them and share because again the burger is gonna fill you up. Only thong is that this place is small and a max of 4 per table can fit but that shouldn't make this any less of a place for good food. Haven't tried the milkshakes but they look good and a prettty large order too.

My husband ordered pizza, spaghetti, and mozzarella sticks I'm pregnant and I've been craving New York style pizza and pasta. The food was completely mediocre and I'm very unsatisfied. The pizza did not taste fresh and tasted like they just heated it up. It was obviously NOT made to order. It was very very dry and bland. The pasta had no flavor. I could have gotten better results at home.  If you want pizza that taste good don't come here because you will end up VERY disappointed.

Best veggie burger in Fishtown. That's saying something: best veggie burger in a hipster enclave where the veggie burger is of equal importance to the meat version. Tons of topping options - truffle butter, for example.

I was impressed all around. A very good restaurant. My date and I walked in around 8:45 on Valentines Friday night and they were able to seat us without reservations within a few minutes. The service was quick and no fuss--not overly friendly but not rude either. 
The food was very authentic, fresh and tender. The salad ginger dressing had a little more lemon than most sushi restaurants but it was refreshing rather than overpowering. It was also nice to see that on a busy night the chef was prepared and did not have to water down the miso soup.  The Shiroi Hana special had very tender chicken with perfectly cooked and breaded tempura. 
The sushi specials were again fresh with very tasty and hearty cuts of fish.  The sashimi was perfectly sized (a mistake of a lot of sushi restaurants is that they make such big pieces that it's no longer bite size).  The green tea ice cream was creamy, tasty, refreshing and a perfect way to end the evening. I will be going back next time I'm in the area.

The burger was HUGE and tasty however there could have been a bit more flavor- maybe it was because I only got the beef burger. The fries with cheese were amazing and the waitstaff was awesome! I loved the idea of drawing sketches. 
My only complaints were I wish you did not have to pay extra for cheese on your burger and I wish the place was bigger - which can't be changed. But it was clearly popular and more seating is needed! 
I'll be back if I'm in the area again!

Yummy food and great service!  i ordered the Sonoran Sampler and it was definitely enough for 2 people.  Our Waitress Esther was awesome as well.  Enjoyed this place and would definitely come back.  There are a ton of Mexican places around town but this one came highly recommended by one of my colleagues while I was in town for a business trip! +10 for yummy points!

Cute place to grab some sushi.  Their food is always good and sushi is fresh.They also deliver and are fast and always get everything right.  I love sushi and live near there so I get the deliver quite a lot.  Overall, they are great.

I checked out sketch burger about a month ago because I'm seriously into burgers. Like SERIOUSLY into burgers. I heard a lot of good things from friends in the city. We walked in and placed our orders and got some sodas out of the reach in fridge they have there. Cash only place which I didn't mind and they also have an ATM in the dining area in case you forget cash. Now let's go on to the food. The fries came out first and they were absolutely fantastic. I was impressed and I was excited for the burger. I ordered a bacon cheeseburger medium. Well upon the burger coming out it looked delicious. I took a bite and much to my dismay the burger was cooked completely well done. Now I'm not sure how you can be known as a burger joint and not cook the burgers at the temperature people ask for. Maybe the cooks had a bad day or something but this was a super disappointing trip for me. Maybe I'll give it another try and hopefully they will cook my burger properly.

Tender sushi-excellent service. This is a little gem of a place. They have their own soy sauce, it is tasty.  They have room for larger parties in their upstairs with a bar. Everything was arranged thoughtfully for sharing a love sushi platter.  The banana tempura dessert was perfect. Only misstep is miso does not stay hot because of plastic bowl and ginger salad is on spring mix, which is not my preference and they drowned it in dressing. Ask for light dressing.
Best sushi in philly here. The place is kind of small so seating can be hard however take out is very good. Not an overly priced japenese restaurant  like some other places.

Being allergic to gluten makes having a Philly cheesesteak challenging.. luckily Westshore Pizza who offers gluten free pizza made the best Philly cheesesteak for me! Order it in the GF pizza crust with no sauce. It was amazing. So nice to be able to eat delicious normal food:)
Great little lunch spot . This is going to a popular spot due to lack of options in south Tucson. They have great tasting subs slightly better than subway .

Okay, Sketch is a super dangerous place to go to satisfy the munchies. The food looks and is so delicious, but it is also plentiful. Almost too plentiful. 

Against good judgement, I consumed an entire vegan burger that was about the side of my head and half of an order of french fries. My boyfriend had a sirloin burger that was "perfectly cooked" (medium). My burger was brown and crispy around the edges and flavorful. The patty extended about an inch all the way around the bun, but I was okay with that. It was massive. That's what she said.

The only downer - we called our order in ahead of time, asking for our respective sauces on the side, since the last time we brought burgers home from here, my burger was too saucy (I know, hard to believe). We got home and there were no sauces! But it wasn't so bad - we both sauced up on our own with a little ketchup and the burgers wound up perfect. Delicious. 

I ate my burger sometime in the six o'clock hour. I went to bed several hours later, still super full. Maybe the chocolate chip cookies I made for dessert, or the absent-minded snacking I continued to do for the rest of the night had something to do with it. But I'm going to go ahead and blame it on the Sketch.

To counteract this and the massive helping of free goodies at yesterday's Yelp event, I am eating a giant bowl of fruit.

Hands down the best burgers in Philly and more. I have been going to Sketch for about a year now and never had a bad meal. To the reviewers that complain about the price for the quality you can not get a better price. Also the place is cool just to hang out and chill. This is one of the best kept secrets in the city but I do not think it will stay that way

I went for dinner with friends on Saturday night. It wasn't too busy but the service was pretty slow. Took like 10 minutes to order our food. I got the $33 set dinner with miso, salad, box sushi, and ice cream. The salad was pretty average. It tasted fine but I wasn't that impressed because the dressing was just OK. The box sushi was quite small and not filling for something that should be $33. You get four pieces of sushi and six small pieces of one roll, and it comes with tempura, seaweed salad, and teriyaki chicken. The sushi wasn't in a good presentation and tasted just average. The portions were overall small and the teriyaki did not have a good glaze. It seemed like our was just baked chicken with sauce glaze on it. 

Overall I would be happy if this meal cost $20 or a little more because that's about the quality and quantity you get, but it was not worth it.

Sketch Burgers definitely lives up to the hype.

My journey began with me narrowly missing the location, but finding a primo parking spot right down the block. The building/eatery is unassuming and was faintly hidden behind some trees, adding to the mystery as we walked in.

The decor was cool and simple, foreshadowing the feel you get from their amazing food.

My gf and I both ordered the vegan bean burger, asked for it to be well done, and added our own spin with additional toppings. Also got the Belgian fries and the brownie w ice cream, and they too were phenomenal.

The burger patty tasted fresh with that made from scratch texture to it. The green goddess sauce added a perfect spice to it, and I will def be choosing that sauce again when I return. 

Overall, this place made it to my top 2 list for burgers. Its only competition lies with the veggie boom burger from UBurger in Boston.... But it's an epic tie. Can't wait to come here again!

I love this place! This is eatery is great for a person who is on the go and don't have time to maintain a balanced diet. All the food is tasty! I literally don't go anywhere else to buy breakfast or lunch and if I know I don't have time for dinner I grab that too!

I am obsessed with burgers. In fact, I'm defrosting one right now so I can eat it for lunch. After hearing all the commotion about Sketch, I decided I had to try one on for size. I wanted to start out simple, so I said, "just a cheeseburger with sauteed onions, lettuce, and tomato." 20 minutes later, I'm racing home, burger aromas overwhelming my car, Giles in the backseat threatening to steal my meat with one swift move...we arrive. Up the stairs, I hit the living room and unwrap my burger. Mushrooms ooze out the sides, bacon sticks out at all ends, bleu cheese encrusts the top of my meat, sauteed onions...

Let's just say this wasn't the burger I ordered, but it's probably best that it came home with me. Clearly, the actual owner of my mistake-burger was on mission: death by burger. I attempted to eat it, but found it nearly impossible to take a satisfactory bite. I could only fit half the thing in my mouth. 

For those of you who prefer size to compactness, this might be the place for you. I prefer the burger and toppings to be tightly hugged by the bread. Think: 5 Guys, In n Out, Shake Shack type places. 

I'm not knocking the mistake they made by giving me the wrong burger, I'm just saying their burger-style isn't my cup o'tea. Still, I'm willing to give it another try.

Sketch is one of my favorite places to grab a bite in fishtown. The service and food here are great and the specials keep me coming back for more.  I usually get the Kobe burger with a fried egg and bacon. If it's not that ill pick one of the many daily specials they have here. 
Also don't forget to try the shakes and homemade desserts here. Green ice cream floats are bomb

I love this quirky burger shop so much. Such a good find in fishtown. There is seating outside for a nice day (beware of crackheads, remember you're in fishtown). Or you could get served inside and look at the great sketches taped up all over the walls. My boyfriend and I have gotten the cyclops burger and cheese fries. The cyclops burger is huge and good. The ingredients that are on the burger are what make the burger so great. Otherwise the actual burger itself is a little dry and not so juicy (maybe because it's so huge OR maybe because they over cooked my medium into a well burger). As for the cheese fries -- THEY ARE THE REAL HERO HERE. I think they put crack in their cheese. And the order is huge so you really only need 1 order for 4 people. My bf and I decided to reheat the fries in the oven. They were still so good we were even eating the burnt pieces lol.

Looking around all the Japanese restaurants in Philadelphia, the first restaurant which flashes in my mind is Shiroi Hana. It is suited in Center City at 222 South 15th Street near City Hall. There are a variety of transportation choices to arrive at this restaurant. Although the restaurant looks small, the inside environment is cozy and comfortable. 
  
     I have been to this restaurant twice. The food there always looks colorful and tastes good. Because of my interest in raw fish, I never forget to order a fish over rice dish for each meal. I tried the Salmon Don the first time and the Chirashi the second time. The Salmon Don is a bowl of sliced salmon with a bed of sushi rice, and the Chirashi is a bowl of sliced toro, uni, yellow tail and salmon with a bed of sushi rice. All the slices of fish are really fresh and will let you feel as though the fish is still alive on your tongue. Each bowl of rice includes almost 12 slices of fish. It is enough for us to eat one bowl of fish rice as a dinner.

     Of course, many other delicious dishes are provided every day by Shiroi Hana. We chose the sushi plate the first time. It is called the Sushi Deluxe, which is a plate of 10 pcs of sushi with spicy tuna rolls. The slices of fish are out of this world and the rice is a little bit sour because of the sushi vinegar. Customers can add mustard and ginger slices in it if they like. I ordered iced tea and my friend ordered the hot tea for drink. The iced tea is a cup of black tea with a slice of lemon and a can of sugar. I think the iced tea is too diluted so that I even cannot get the smell of black tea. My friend told me that the hot tea is good. It is mixed Chinese green tea with Japanese green tea. My friend likes it very much. It is worth mentioning the tempura in this restaurant. The shrimp tempura and the soft shell crab tempura is fantastic. Especially the tempura sauce, it is almost the same as the sauce, which is provided in Japan!  

     To tell the truth, the service in Shiroi Hana is better than any other restaurants I have ever been to in Phily. Waiters and waitresses all know Japanese and they always talk to Japanese guests choice by Japanese. Every ten minutes, they will come to every table and ask guests if they have needs. They are polite, friendly and well trained.

     In addition, the first floor of the restaurant is small but beautiful. People can choose either to sit beside the cook, choice the process of making sushi or to sit in sofa, waiting for the delicious food. People also can go upstairs to several small rooms for private conversations by reserving in advance. The restroom there is clean and sweet-scented. You must have a good experience there with an amazing dinner.
Derrick P. said on yelp website, "This place is definitely solid. Fish is very fresh and a straightforward atmosphere with quick service. Huge fan of their salmon avocado and sashimi rolls." I really agree with his opinion and recommend people to have a meal there too. 

     All in all, Shiro Hana is really a good restaurant to have a try!

So we took a chance on the sushi place with decent reviews, a liquor license, and. 5 mile from our hotel.  The place was small (but aren't most sushi bars) but not cramped.  True staff seemed pleasant.  Their downfall was the ADD they all seem to suffer from.  Error #1 everyone around us got the hot towel treatment.  While that may seem trivial, when you don't get it,  you miss it. Don't lie...you know I'm right. #2 if I say I ordered sashimi and you bring me sushi, don't tell me I'm wrong when it was you who was distracted by the number of tables sat while taking our order. Error #3 host:when a kid asks you for training chopsticks don't say"go ask your waitress" while you sit idle.

I'm not a big teriyaki fan, but I loved eating their beef teriyaki rice plate, which is priced around $20. The sushi here is pretty good (but not the best) and I fell in love with their beef teriyaki because they used thinly sliced rib-eye. They give you decent sized portions and the meat was tender with just the right flavoring.

I love this Museum and try to get down to Tucson at least twice a year to go visit. 

Unless you're acclimated to Tucson summers, it's better to go here during the winter months.  Actually, that's the case even if you are acclimated to AZ summers.  There are quite a few drinking fountains and a few shaded areas, but it can get a bit brutal during the summer months.

Admission is very reasonable for what you get, especially since they've been adding exhibits on over the year.  You can also pay a buck and get a field guide where you stamp the animals' footprints throughout the park.  It's a silly little fun side project as you're going through.  

The volunteers who work here are amazing!  They're very knowledgeable and friendly, and will answer all of your questions with the patience of a saint.

It's a great place for little kids, teens, and adults.  Make sure you take your stroller for the tiny guys, because it is a LOT of walking.  Unless you want to end up carrying them, pack wisely.

Depending on your pace, it's a couple-hour walkthrough.  You really get to experience how beautiful the Arizona desert can be.  Make sure you bring your camera because there are some spectacular sights.  Hardcore photographers will have a field day!

I actually enjoy the Sonora Desert museum more than the Phoenix Zoo.  It's more reasonably priced, with fewer people and better ambiance.

Not too much to say... stopped in for a quick sushi dinner.  The sushi was pretty good and service was friendly.  Nothing too spectacular but I do remember feeling like the rolls were bigger than normal.  I'll take it!

We haven't been in here for years.  Not many people eating which in years past it would be packed.  We order off  the special menu.  Food was outstanding.  Sonora Enchiladas and Shrimp Fajitas. A shear delight.  Service was top notch.  Thanks Tony.

Came here during a quick burger run on Friday night with my sister while visiting her in Philly. Maybe our expectations were too high for a good burger but it wasn't what it was chalked up to be. It's not in the nicest area and they only have a few tables. The servers are really nice but the actual service is super slow. The burger is thick but it really takes a long time to come out from the kitchen. We got the mushroom truffle burger with green goddess sauce on the side. We shared the burger because we were doing a mini burger crawl and heading to PYT afterwards. The burger was just okay, still juicy despite the thickness and being overcooked for a medium temperature. The sauce was the star of the plate though. We took the rest of ours home to use on chicken, fish, etc to cook during the weekend hah. Overall - unmemorable.

Just had dinner here, after not having been for a couple of years. 

Baja Burro still hits the spot, with it's spicy cream sauce! Wife had a carne asada chimi with some kind of cheese sauce, which was also really tasty. The star tonight was the green corn tamale bites, served with the Baja sauce. We decided we could probably make a meal out of those! 

Another highlight was our server/bartender, Cole. Really nice, and attentive.

Unfortunately, it was not very busy, for being peak dinner time. I hope they stick around. Come support a Tucson institution!

This is a must eat...feed your inner fat kid. Always a generous portion of food, great price, and awesome owners!! 
#followthepig 
I'm not sure I can narrrow down my favorite menu item, everything is tasty!!

I have been coming to sketch for over a year and I absolutely love this place! 

It's BYOB! wohoo

They offer a salad for your burger rather than a bun and as a diabetic, i am very very happy about that. 

A week ago was my boyfriends birthday and since we both adore Sketch I decided to plan a surprise dinner there. It was a success!
