Not only did Sketch take my reservation of 12 people, took my order for 18 cupcakes with the words "Happy Birthday" but they put candles on the cupcakes and made them half reg. and half vegan!

Everyone loved it and the service is superb! Love you Sketch and love the good people that work there!

I've been going to Shiroi Hana for about four years now and have never been disappointed. There have been times when I would go here once or twice a week. Not only does Shiroi Hana have fresh sushi and unique rolls that I haven't seen in other sushi restaurants in Philly (I highly recommend the Island Roll; it's my personal favorite), but it offers an array of Japanese-style chicken, steak, and cooked fish which is great when you have less adventurous members of your party who aren't crazy about the idea of raw fish. In addition to the normal menu, they have included an insert for a special "spicy" menu for the past few months. I have tried everything on it and love it all.

From a price perspective, Shiroi Hana is a bit more expensive than small sushi bars. However, it is less expensive than other ultra modern, swankier sushi places like Raw and Zama. That being said, Shiroi Hana's ambiance is somewhere in between, so I'd say it has a pretty casual vibe that can be dressed up or down. Dinner guests are usually a combination of locals from the neighborhood and also business people staying nearby or theater-goers.

I LOVE SKETCH. I'll say it again: I LOVE SKETCH. Their food is AMAZING. It's not always the healthiest, but it is SO good. The burgers are great, they have a ton of vegan/vegetarian options, I'm in love with their fries, and their mac and cheese is ridiculously awesome. They're great for take-out too (no delivery). The service is sometimes slow, but always worth it. Plus, you can make your own drawing to hang out the wall. Seriously. I love Sketch.

This place is the tits! Michelle is super cool and awesome. I mean who doesn't like delicious burgers and drawing. But for real though, burgers here are great. Big, but don't fall apart all messed up like some other places. If you commit, it's definitely eatable without getting everything all over yourself. 

They also have way cool drawings by patrons who have come before. Def SnapChat worthy. Just try and draw something as cool. 

Intimate without being stuffy, with great burgers and fresh specials you won't find many other places.

One of my favorites for sure! very cool place and the food is amazing! Chef Rene knows what he's doing and knows what people want. The menu is perfect and has so much variety so there is something for everyone! They even have vegan items!

Stopped by with 4 adults and a toddler Saturday night and were seated quickly. I think I've been here before but did not recognize the interior, so maybe not.

Tried the carnitas plate myself and was satisfied. The portion size was good and the meat was juicy. Rice was surprisingly less dry than I had anticipated. Beans were beans.

Wife had the appetizer combo plate. Most was stock catered style Mexican snack fare, but the little fried tamale balls (masa + meat + chile + fry) were interesting. They did not hold up very well as leftovers, however.

Kid had a bean burrito and grapes. It was a bean burrito and grapes.

All told, we were satisfied. The service was good, the food was good. The price was a bit higher than the quality warranted, but not onerously so.

Very simple but excellent quality.  You don't have to spend a fortune (like Budakon) to prove quality.  Loved it...loved it...loved it.  Parking right next door or numerous parking lots around the area.  Close to Rittenhouse Square if you want to walk after dinner.
Also, Good Dog is right next door if you want to hang at the bar with friends after dinner...

I used to live in Philly and never went here as I was vegan at the time.  Vegan no moar!  I now live a block from the Reading Terminal Market and am currently doing the slow carb thing, which suggests 30g protein at breakfast...I don't eat eggs, so, sausage?  Super pleased to find an array of breakfast sausages for $3.59/lb (excepting the beef breakfast sausages which were $4.59/lb).  Turkey sage is the bomb.

I generally buy my meat grass fed/organic but it's difficult to find turkey/pork that ways, especially breakfast sausage.  And forget about it being a price I can afford.  I do have affordable sources for grass-fed beef and organic chicken but in a pinch, Martin's is a great source, it looked very, very fresh, maybe $3-4/lb ground beef.  Def stock up on their specials (I got 3lb roasted red pepper sausage for $10).
Order in, our order was quick and very good, we order one special two slice of white pizza and my husband ordered one slice and a Philly cheese steak.

Although I get to Martin's less often these days, a trip is as cherished as ever.  Martin's sausage is some of my absolute favorite, and I have in particularly never found a better andouille sausage even close, other than in New Orleans itself.  Other favorites of mine in the sausage ranks inlcude their pepper and onion, and any of the breakfast links.

Of course, the steaks, veal, short ribs...everything else is readily available.  Everything is masterfully prepared, as fresh as it gets, and with friendly and fast service to boot.

Charming little place in Fishtown..  The walls are filled with sketches made by the patrons. And they give you supplies to make your own drawing. And good food great atmosphere. I tried the farro salad with mixed veggies which was a generous portion and was very delectable. I would go there again for sure. They have a really good black bean burger. Yummers! 

Definitely try their sweet goodies too I tried the salty nut and pecan pie bar. And some of my friends got the little hearts and the dark chocolate truffle. Very very tasty.

I loved the cool, fun atmosphere of this restaurant. There were probably hundreds of patron artwork plastered on the walls of this place, which gave it an unique vibe. My boyfriend used to live in PA and when we visited, he insisted on bringing me to the best burger he's ever had. I got the American Kobe Burger with Pepper Jack and an egg. My boyfriend got the Truffle Butter Burger. Both were cooked on point and the patty was very juicy. Although the burgers looked really plain, it was actually full of flavor. We also got a side of fries that came with marissa aioli. They were thick cut and not too greasy. 

The restaurant is a little hard to find and parking isn't great. However, you'll forget all about it once you try their burgers!

The Kalua Pork & cabbage and chicken katsu is out of this world!!!! So so good! The Kalbi was ok, the marinade is not as good as Mama's, same feeling about the Terri chicken. Other than that, excited to be able to eat Hawaiian foods in Tucson! Will be back again!

I'm not usually one to write a place off because of bad service, but this place is the exception.

To start, the girl behind the counter was confused about taking our order, didn't understand simple questions about the menu.  I was expecting to wait a little bit for the food, but our wait was excessive.  Let me also preface this by saying, my group was only 1 of 3 groups of people in the place.

They gave part of our order to the wrong table, then blamed it on the other customer.  The people that came in about 5 minutes after us, got their food way before us.

I was with a group of 3 people, they then brought 2 of 3 burgers, and seemed to totally forget we ordered another and fries.  Our server came over, not once, not twice, but three times asking, "what are you guys missing?"  

I must say, the food was very good, which makes me feel bad about writing this negative review.  The milkshakes were great, and I love that you can get a vegan one (i'm lactose-intolerant).  The burger was awesome, very filling.  But $40 for 3 people having burgers is kind of ridiculous as well.

Oh, and even better, when we went to pay, the cashier, who took our order and brought it out to us, had to again ask us what we had.  I should have told her i had just a coffee.  

To sum it up, if you want an expensive, tasty burger, want to wait a long time for it, and feel like putting up with horrible service, then this is the place for you.  There are plenty of other local places, like Memphis Taproom, that make even better burgers, that come with fries, for almost half the price, with spectacular service.
This place keeps my ADD butt busy. Sketching eating drinking. I love this shop of BurgerBliss

"I'm building the most ridiculously sloppy burger possible!  Why?... because the beard is officially gone, fuck napkins" is how my most recent conversation started with one of the employees here!  Ohhh believe me, she made sure it was as sloppy as it was delicious.  
  A great selection of meats, cheeses, sauces and fixins', build your baby as you see fit & you will not be disappointed.  While you wait for your creation, grab some chalk, paper, markers, or crayons and create another masterpiece on the construction paper at the tables & add it to the collage that is the interior walls.  Where the hell was this place when i was 6, all Friendly's ever gave me was a 2 pack of crayons and a shitty place mat.  
  I have eaten here countless times, & am yet to be disappointed.  Anyone that has ever accompanied me here has left at least a half a pound heavier in need of a lounge chair contemplating the idea of becoming bulimic.  Hell it was that good I wanna taste it again!

A burger joint for people who like to sketch!

The place itself is nothing to write home about.  In fact, I think they paper the wall with all of those sketches to hide the fact that the inside of the restaurant is in fact, a little sketchy looking.

That aside!  If you like burgers and are, like my fiance,  in a constant quest to find the best burger in town, then you should definitely check out this Fishtown spot.  I got the "cyclops burger" with provolone, bacon, and a fried egg on top.  Ooey-gooey, meaty goodness!

+     Fantastic, juicy burgers
+     Fun, witty Sketches of things like the Heisenburger
+/-   Good spot for hipster watching if you're into that
-      For a burger joint, I was surprised by the long-ish wait for our food
-      CASH ONLY (annoying)

Some friends have been telling us we HAVE to go and we finally got to try Sketch's burgers.

I'd say it lived up to the hype. The burger was juicy and delicious. A little rarer than I prefer but that's my fault.. they cook burgers exactly to how you ask which I'm not used to so I usually ask for "medium rare" in order to get "medium" and Sketch actually gave me "medium rare" so that's really a pro for them. 

The decor was fun and it was nice having something to do (doodling!) while waiting for our food.

The fries were incredible.. I'm dying to try them with cheese next.
The chocolate croissants are amazing, an actually better than the ones I had in France. The coffee is some of the best as well. The bread is pretty good.

I've been wanting to try a Sketch burger for a long time. I've heard many good things about this place. I finally got to check it out the other week, and all good things I've heard turned out to be true.

I had the American kobe beef burger, and it was pretty awesome. I'd say the 2nd best burger I've ever tasted. (Bridget Foy's is my number one!) I asked for fries with a side of cheese, but the waitress told me that they have good sauces and she REALLY wanted me to try their sauces instead. (Ok, whatever lady).... she gave me a chipotle sauce, and some other kind of garlic sauce which was pretty good. I also asked for the mac n cheese( I was super hungry that day), but the waitress told me NO! She said that the mac n cheese is a meal in itself and that I should come back another day and order that by itself. Haha. this lady was pretty ballsy. but she was also super nice and friendly soo it's cool. I will just have to come back again one day to try out this mac n cheese that I've heard so much about.

I've also heard that on certain days they serve ostrich burgers and buffalo burgers which iI wouldn't want to try but I find it pretty interesting. 

All in all, Sketch is a cute little burger place, and I will defintely be back!

really big fan of the creativity going on in the restaurant. Burger was cooked to perfection, however they lose a star because i once overheard the owner talking to what seemed to be a family member saying that they accept cash only so they can make extra money on your service fee at the ATM inside... not a fan of your loophole antics to take my money. ITS 2018! buy a Square for heaven sake.

This place is exactly what you want from a burger place. If I am ever craving a juicy burger, I come here. Sketch burger has a great variety of traditional and eclectic choices. Even though I don't need to worry about it, they have a pretty good selection of vegetarian selection (including the seitan cheesesteak which my brother tells me is delicious). I also highly recommend the green chile cheese fries. They alone keep me coming back!

I've been making the rounds in Philly for sushi lately, and this place has become my perennial favorite. I've taken two dates here and also come with my dad, and the minimal, quiet, clean atmosphere seemed to fit both situations. Price-wise, it's no steal, but it's fair and not inflated by trendy cache.

The fish is the freshest I have had and sashimi cuts are generous and uniform. If you're more into rolls, try the eponymous Shiroi Hana roll or the rainbow roll. I am a sushi/sashimi purest, and could not tell you what the appetizers or wine selection were like, two complaints I've noticed in other reviews, which may be fair for all I know. I personally can't waste valuable stomach real estate on anything but the sushi, save a little miso and some sake. I do recall the seaweed salad was a big hit with my date. Not my bag.

Everything here from the decor, to the service, to the presentation, does a wonderful job doing exactly what it should and then getting out of the way so that the sushi sits center stage. It's a couple more bucks than your corner sushi joint, but even on a budget I have always considered it money well spent.

I needed a repair on my Singer sewing machine.  I knew what the problem was but could not find the part I needed anywhere on line, so I took it here for service.  This place is knowledgeable, friendly, and professional.  I called back for an estimate in 2 days and they gave me a detailed list of what parts and service were needed.  It was exactly what I expected had to repaired/replaced and the price was very reasonable.  They gave me a 90 guarantee and remembered me when I picked it up.  This place is awesome!  There are few reliable sewing machine repair stores and I am so happy that I found this one!! I recommend it to anyone who has a machine problem or is looking for a new machine (they sell as well).  These guys are great!

After scouring the area for the best local food our feet could carry us to and by that of course i mean using yelp, we came across sketch burger. It had four stars at the time and after our experience i could say its a true 4-5 star. If your looking for a large delicious burger with thick and crunchy fries this is the place. The dining area is small and cozy but your quickly distracted with all the customer own drawn decor. The walls are lined with cartoons and sketches ranging from amateur to prodigy either way all worth a laugh while waiting for your food. The food comes out quickly and the burger choices are minimal but people often overlook the flavor and worth of just a good burger. Can customize your burger with cheese and sauce options and the LTO toppings are hearty. Be sure to check out the menu on the wall because its different than there menu at the table. The chili was a silent front runner especially in the winter. They have can and bottle type soda drinks that are self served but they only accept cash. They had an ATM in the building but it was out of service when we went but there is one a block down. Overall a good experience.

The address is wrong. They have recently moved. 

The outside of the building is deceiving to what awaits you inside. The food is ordered at a counter but delivered to your table. Had the shredded pork, island salad, and island beans. Reminded me of some of the better meals I had when I visited Oahu in 2015. I will definitely make this a place to eat when I return. 

YUM!
The staff is awesome and friendly. The best Hawaiian grinds in Tucson hands down. The portions are generous and tasty not bland.

Can be amazing but not consistently enough for a higher review. When it's good, it's the best burger you'll find anywhere in the greater Philadelphia area. It's just only that good about 1 of every 3 times. If you dine in you'll get your fries 20 minutes before your burger which doesn't work for people like me that want to eat them together. That being said the fries are fantastic and pair really well with the sauces offered. As far as consistency, I often get food from here for my girlfriend and I and we can order the same burger cooked to the same wellness and they won't resemble each other at all. The last time we got food from here, a few days ago, the burgers were unrecognizable as being from sketch and far from the best we've had there. We keep coming back on the chance we'll catch them at their best which is an overwhelmingly satisfying experience, but for the price we're let down more often than not.

UPDATED 9/7/18

This place used to be hit or miss, now it's just miss. I completely regret going back at this point. At $40 for 3 underwhelming burgers and some semi raw fries it almost feels like they stole the money right off of my dresser.

Fantastic in all ways. The service is exceptionally nice and pleasant. The smashed onion burger was great - same for the fries and dipping sauce. Love the down home feel to the place. Can't wait to go back and try the shakes.

Well..... I've eaten here before and can't quite remember the food but I've returned because of the dessert. After a not so good dinner me, my bff and her sis was craving a warm dessert and she thought of Macayo's. The chocolate mini chimis are an explosion of yummy goodness in your mouth. SOOOOOO good. We also tried the cinnamon apple filled enchilada for the first time and oh em gee this was just as amazing. All served with a scoop of ice cream on the side :) We love being fatties!

THE SUBS THAT DREAMS ARE MADE OF.  Yes, his was literally the best sub I've ever eaten, EVER.  I typically find one thing I like at a restaurant and stick with it, however The Experience (sandwich name- doesn't seem to be on the online menu, but available in the store) was so damn AMAZEBALLS that I am inspired to try every single sub on the menu. Seriously, do not miss this!  And while you are there, make sure to try a solo pickle!  I don't know how they made a pickle so good, but it would turn a pickle hater into a pickle lover!  See you soon Planet Sub!

4.5 Stars.
I declare Shiroi Hana as my official GO-TO Japanese restaurant!  

This place is the real deal.  You can tell by the menu that they're serious about this cuisine and authenticity...and it's also worth noting that their online menu does not list everything that is available.

All the food was absolutely fresh and delicious.  The actual restaurant itself was pretty, and service was above and beyond.  

Whether you're having date night, dinner with padres, or a meal with friends... choosing Shiroi Hana would be a no-brainer.

I wish I could have Phyllis cook for me all the time!  The best pulled pork i have ever head, an amazing burger, and daily specials, including new empenadas that will blow your mind.  I spend way too many nights eating there, but I never complain cause it's always something new and always something delicious.

Hands down the best burger in all of Philadelphia and the best burger I have ever eaten in my life. I have been here so many times and am always impressed by the quality of meat and how juicy the burger is. Also you have to try the sweet potato fries with the garlic aioli. That is money right there. I recommend try the truffle butter burger and you will never eat at another burger place again.  I wish I could rate past 5!!!!

Love, love, love the sushi & sake martini!  We were so busy enjoying the casual but on-point service, oysters, sushi, and conversation that we forgot too snap a few photos.  There will definitely be a next time! 
If not a fan of sushi there is a full menu of fresh and mindfully prepared options. But do have sushi. 
Outstanding!

Great beef burgers.  Great vegan burgers.  Great fries.  Great sauces.  Excellent baked goods.  The milk shakes are a bit pricey but delicious.  Overall, an excellent meal.  The decor is fun and funky with church pew seating and lots of customer's sketches hanging on the walls.  We prefer to take our food to-go as the seating area is somewhat awkward and small...and we have a toddler who wants to run around.

I stopped by here for the first time on Saturday with a friend to watch the Kensington Kinetic Sculpture Derby go by on Girard Ave.  I've heard great things about this place but had never ventured there.

Hands down, the best burger I've ever had in Philly!  Also, a shout-out to the fries; I don't know what they season them with but they were perfect!  They even included malt vinegar on the table, which I love, but I didn't use it or ketchup or any sauce on them.  As for the burger, I ordered the cyclops (bacon and fried egg) which was cooked to a perfect medium with just the right amount of pink in the center for me.  The burger was extremely juicy and made a giant mess on my hands and serving dish which to me is a sign of an awesome burger!  The messier, the better!  Also, the milkshakes were also quite delicious!

The sketching-while-you-wait is a whimsical touch too.  As many have mentioned prior, the walls of this joint are filled with other people's artwork.  It gives the place a cozy, artsy feel.  The wait staff was very friendly as well.

2 burgers, a large fry to share and 2 milkshakes came to about $30....a great Saturday lunch which kept me full the rest of the day.  Thanks guys!!!
Ok.  This has gotten ridiculous.  I discovered a penny at the bottom of the shake cup.  Pretty gross.  Down to 0 stars.

Sketch offers burgers of epic proportions. I find it unfair that they don't have small cots to pass out on after you've ingested your weight in burger. 

BURGERS: The burgers themselves are great. Cooked the way you want them, and with many creative options. I usually go for Onion smashed Kobe burger. Also, if you're feeling extra gluttonous, try to the truffle butter burger. Your body will hate you, but it has so much flavor. They come with lettuce, tomato, and 1 sauce. Everything else is extra, so choose wisely young padawans.

CRAYONS: Now the best part, you're seated at table equipped with crayons and construction paper! The whole place is decorated with their patrons artwork. A really fun interactive way to keep customers distracted from their hunger pains.

SERVICE: The servers are always very friendly, never a bad experience.

If you're looking for a place to gain a little weight for the winter and have some fun, this is your place! Get those creative juices going!

This burger is one of the best I've ever had! I got the classic burger done medium with sweet potato fries  my bf got the same, except he got normal fries. The burgers are so juicy and cooked to perfection. They also have huge portions for good prices. The menu has a lot to choose from and they also have Lotsa specials. It's a small casual place, and it is Byob so bring some beers to go with your burger! I do recommend the regular fries over sweet potato though, I couldn't keep my hands off them"

1 hour ago, i went that restaurant and i totally got annoying!! I found hair in the California roll and i talked to my server! Actually i thought apology is mandatory in this case, But they just took away my food which was included hair and just provided new one! They didn't say any SORRY!! It simply doesn't make sense. 
I really disappointed that restaurant also i didn't wanna eat anymore, so i asked my check and they just include my California roll that had trouble! It was really rude and they have to apologize about that part!! I absolutely DO NOT recommend this restaurant

This place is awesome.  Try the Dr. Pepper pulled pork sandwich if you're looking for something different than a burger (though they are Sketch's specialty).  Other great options include the chili cheese fries which are fantastic and the shakes which aren't too bad either.  They also have a lot of vegan options which is a plus!

I've only had a milkshake but oh my word it was good. Vegan pistachio milkshake was maybe the best shake I ever had. And the crayons, construction paper and markers at the table made us feel like kids.
The pizza is good! The service was also super friendly and personal! We had a nice conversation with what seemed to be a manager and she was cool! Enjoyed the food and the prices were just right too!

This place is called Martin's Quality Meats & Sausage... not because the sausage isn't quality but because it's in a category of its own. If I ever become a connoisseur I'm gonna say I got my start with Martin's...

So here's a little breakdown of what I've tried... I mix and match these in my different dishes.

garlic - I consider this one to be a staple. It has a great flavor and isn't particularly offensive to anyone. I usually fry up Martin's sausage in batches of 3 or 5. So I'd be using 2/3 garlic or 3/5 garlic. I think these are better skewed towards lunch or dinner and sandwiches specifically. They add a nice punch to other meats (bacon, chicken, ground beef/turkey).

banger - For me, this is the other staple and I think it's a better pick for breakfast. I'm not Irish and I can't speak to "bangers and mash" as I've only tried it once, but these go great with french toast and apples... or anything sweet. Also, it's a good choice for a first timer.

red pepper and onion - Don't be fooled by the name... the red pepper is really about the vegetable inside. If you can't handle spice, this isn't one to shy away from as it's actually pretty tame. These are a great substitute (chopped) for when I don't have actual fresh vegetables and I often mix these with the staples on my dishes that are a type more Italian.

chorizo - I didn't care too much for these. I'm probably biased and spoiled on the Mexican restaurants along Washington Ave (w/ explosive heat and flavor). But I will say that these are about even with a couple of Latin (non-Mexican) restaurants I've been to. They're spicy, but not dangerous. If you'd like an introduction to chorizo, sure give them a try.

andouille - I have a specialty sandwich that I make and I offered one to a friend... he started coughing right away, but it was a good cough. Like... yo man this joint is SPICY! Yep, this is the one... if you're about that spice. It'll open your nose up. Andouille partners up well with the garlic. It has the **POW** that the chorizo is lacking... not to mention it's my favorite. You may not want to drink coffee with these because that acidity will really magnify the spice.

sage and basil (I think) - I'm a fan of a basil so I couldn't go wrong with these. Just like with the red pepper and onion, they're a great substitute for actual fresh vegetables (in a dish of course). I like these with a little lime/lemon juice and spice.

apple - This variety of apple was too tart... was it grannysmith...? ...golden delicious? Either way, I was expecting a sweeter flavor and it just wasn't there. Also, it's a bit harder to get a good cut on these once they're done. Other than that, they're fine. They'd probably make cool h'orderves.

Overall, I think there are 2 types of fresh sausage... and I base this on consistency. The tighter pack vs the looser pack. Martin's has a tighter pack which is easier to get a sharp cut and great for making sandwiches. The looser pack is like Whole Foods where the insides will spillover when you cut them or casing will pop more easily when frying. That kind is bad for sandwiches but good for... say... pasta.

Sketch Burger is awesome and nails it for a local delicious burger joint! The burgers are absolutely mouth watering, fries are phenomenal and the service is great. A must try and a burger go-to in Philly.

The burger, fries and even the fried Cauliflower was good. Would of gave it 5 stars but it kind of looks dumpy and the bathroom was kind of grungy, however the sketches on the wall are pretty cool. Service was pretty good too. The food was so good, it made u forget about your surroundings! I will definitely be back here to eat!!!!

This place is THE REAL DEAL! Drive past the other Hawaiian BBQ place in Tucson and get here with your appetite! Family owned and it feels like it! These folks started as a food truck. The teriyaki chicken is beyond delicious! And the rest of the menu had plenty of choices for everyone. You can tell they cook what they know well. It's soooo good!
OK, been back too many times to count and the over salting problem is fixed. Still way to expensive to take the family, but good burgers.

I'm reserving the 5-star for another go at this place, but on the first go around, the burger was amazing. I got the Cyclops Burger [burger, cheese, bacon, and an egg] and the homeboy picked up a Kobe Burger.

BANGIN', these burgers were off the hizzeeeeeeee. Luckily, there weren't many people in the joint, so we were able to relax and take in the decor and scope the place out. As a spaceman, this is a cool place to hang out and eat, the random ass images all over the walls were of an eclectic mix to say the least.

The burgers? Great. We both got 'em medium, and his Kobe was a fair bit bloodier than mine, but damn if it wasn't delicious. We skipped on the fries, and for good reason; these things were big. Fat ass patty o' meat on a greasy ass bun done-the-fuck-right. PYT around the corner? I don't care, I'm coming here...

Fuck it, it's getting 5-stars. Can't wait to go back.

Had a wonderful dinner there last night.  Both food and service were truly exceptional. After sharing a delicious lobster tail tempura, two of us shared the Ume Dinner Special after being advised that two of them would be too much food. It was a very large bento assortment of chicken teriyaki, shrimp and veggie tempura, seaweed salad & sushi. It  came with miso soup, salad & ice cream.

The place is adorable. Bright and clean. Cozy, but with plenty of seating. Sketches of hamburgers drawn by customers are hanging up all over the walls.

The service is super friendly and really helpful. I went in with Burger Club Philly, 20 of us took the little place by storm and the servers didn't get stressed or overwhelmed or rude. 

I got a rare cheddar cheeseburger with fried onions and wasabi sauce. It was probably the juiciest burger I've ever eaten. Really really delicious! Just super messy. I think the meat was too big or something. It was all sliding all over the place and coming out of the roll. Hardly something to complain about. It was worth the messy fight!

Also, this place is a BYO!

I came 5 minutes before closing time and I'm so glad they still served me! Although, they did tell us right away that they were only doing take out orders. Still, since my friend drove us all the way from Temple campus, we were happy to take out.

I got the smashed onion burger (no cheese, harissa aioli), whereas my friend ordered the Dr. Pepper Pulled Pork. My burger was extra oniony and huge! Satisfying patty. I regretted the harissa aioli, since I had been eyeing the green goddess sauce for ages... but still delicious nonetheless. My friend's pulled pork was also delicious, but I was put off by his dish because it was lacking in anything green. Are you supposed to eat pulled pork sans lettuce? Not sure.

Anyway, I'm totally a fan. The place is adorable, with all the drawings customers put up on the walls. The burgers are substantial, full bodied, and delicious. Parking outside was no hassle, the wait was fine, and the servers friendly.

I went to sketch burger this past summer and had a great experience so I was excited to return! However, I was extremely disappointed. First, the service was very poor. Wait staff was inattentive and unhelpful. We arrived at 7:30pm (the place is open until 9pm) and were told they were all out of regular fries. We asked how the sweet potato fries were and our waiter responded "well, the regular fries are better". Not helpful considering we could not order them. It took a long time to order our food and even longer to get the bill at the end. The waiter also forgot my friend's regular milkshake.
Sketch burger has also cut down it's vegan options. One of the things I was excited to order upon returning was a vegan milkshake, but they no longer have them on the menu. I decided to just order the vegan burger with green goddess dressing, but was informed they were also out of the dressing! 
The burger I had tasted average, but considering there are so many better places to eat in Philly with better food, better service, and more options, I will NOT be returning.

The standard for sushi is simple...are the fish fresh?  This was my first time eating at Shiroi Hana and I was not disappointed.  I had the mixed three option, to which I chose the #1, 2, 4.  The fish was very fresh and tasted great.  The piece of fish was decently large and the amount of rice was small.  No complaints there.  

The price at $15 for 8 pieces of nigiri and 2 hand rolls was not so bad considering the price of each individual nigiri was mainly $3 or more.  This was during lunch so I'm not sure if they have this for dinner also.  Once I added a scallop, toro, and uni nigiri, well let's just say the price tag sky rocketed.

Service was fast and friendly.  I would not mind coming back.  However if I was in the mood to really indulge on sushi, I would probably not come here.  I mainly eat nigiri and the price here is ridiculous.  There are definitely places with fresh fish at a cheaper price tag.

Great burgers! This is probably one of my favorite burger joints in the whole city.The regular mix burger is always juicy, and served with great fixings. My wife, normally a shy eater, decided to try the Cyclops burger and loved it. The burger was a perfect medium, and the egg was a perfectly cooked bit of artery hardening decadence piled on top.

I had the kobe beef burger with bacon. The kobe was definitely juicier and tastier than the regular mix, and the bacon was tender and lay on top of perfectly melted cheddar. The chipolte sauce was a tasty compliment,

My daughters shake was rich and creamy, with a generous amount of delicious ice cream (I wish I could remember the dairy they use). The fries were hand cut, fresh, hot, and delicious with a choice of sauces...we had the aioli and wasabi sauces..delicious.

The only noticeable issue was the bun. On this visit they were slightly dry and crumbly, though on other visits they've been fresh and soft. Not sure what happened there, and hope its not a recurring issue.

I'm struggling a bit after seeing all of the positive feedback this place gets.  All of the glowing-ness of 4 or 5 stars makes me think that folks need to normalize their excitement.  At this point, I know that I'm doing more to review the reviewers  but I'm having trouble understanding.  

My thoughts:  Decent bun.  No one should charge for raw onions on a burger.  You get three automatic sides:  lettuce, tomato, onions.  At minimum, those three are provided.  The burger itself would've been average, and by that I mean, backyard-burger-on-the-4th-of-July average, had it not been overcooked.  I like my burgers rare and I got medium.  Its something burger joints should get right.  We had the Belgium fries which were tasty, if not a little over-seasoned.  The fries could also benefit from being cut a little thinner.  A few were cool in the middle.

The brightest point here were the empanadas.  The bean and cheese pockets were cooked perfectly.  Golden-brown and flaky.  The interior of the bean and cheese was tasty and had a great spicy bite to it.

All of this said, my biggest issue was the dog.  Yes, a dog came in with one of the waitresses and roamed the room freely.  It was a very nice and seemingly obedient dog, but unless I'm in my buddies back yard on the 4th, I don't want a dog wandering around my table.  There was no attempt by the staff to corral the dog or send him away.  He made several customers visibly and obviously uncomfortable, especially after spelunking underneath their table.  The dog smelled like he is kept outside.  Next time you eat a burger, you should try to pair the taste of well cooked beef with the smell of a musty dog.  Its gross.  Its probably not the reason the health department forbids it, but it should be one of the many others.

Apart from the dog, this place is heavily over-rated.  If you must, get the empanadas to go.  Hopefully the dog hasn't nosed through the line.

My wife recently tried this out and loved it.  Food, ingredients and seasonings are all fresh.  You still need to prepare and cook!  But eliminate pushing carts through busy grocery store aisles, standing in line at the butcher and deli counter, reading the labels on a variety of seasonings and coming up with a menu all together and you've just cut down hours upon hours from the entire cooking experience.  So, you can just get to the fun stuff which cooking is...fun!  Food tasted great btw, and the menu is pretty inventive and changes monthly.  We will be going back for couples night.  Oh, it's social, too!  Go with friends and you can catch up on the gossip while being productive.  Kill two birds...

With so much great Mexican food in Tucson, it is amazing that a place like Macayos can actually have a dedicated following.  Service is lukewarm, the enchilada sauce is like ketchup, and the salsa is too spicy - with a weird flavor too.  This is the kind of Mexican food one might expect in Fargo, North Dakota, not Tucson.  Skip this place for something better like Poco and Moms or Guadalajara Grill.

I LOVE SKETCH!!! as far as burgers go, this place is KING, from burgers better than ANYWHERE Ive ever been to amazing fries with awesome sauces the smashed onion burger is great, the kobe beef burger is really something special. but my personal favriote, the cyclops burger, bacon egg and cheese on a burger amazing.

Now this is a burger joint... for meat eaters and vegans alike. 

My eyes immediately locked on the American Kobe Burger so the SO and I both went for it w/cheddar cheese cooked med. rare.  It did take a while but that's fine for a small place like this.  When it came out, it was a monster. It had to be at least an 8oz burger cooked good enough (a little on the rare side but I don't mind). I'm guessing it wasn't 100% american kobe beef but you could definitely taste the difference from a normal beef burger. The bun could use some work. I don't like mine as dense and dough-y as this was.

The fries were good, Belgian frites style. The harissa aioli was very very addicting. It's the perfect sauce to complement the fries and the juicy burger. 

I'd go to Philly for that burger again over any of the overhyped cheesesteak joints.

I tried the vegan burger, it tasted great.  I had it with the truffle butter, (cause I'm not actually vegan) and avocado.  The fries were really tasty, too.

The downsides were that the patty fell apart a lot as I ate it and that it gave me crazy gas, haha.
This place was good but a little on the pricey side. The menu was what you'd expect for a sushi spot. Give it a try if you're in the neighborhood.

An authentic Japanese restaurant.  Got the Hardcore sushi and it was great.    Also ordered the Daifuku mochi that was also good.   I would highly recommend this place if you are looking for a real Japanese run restaurant.

This place will be a major disappointment if you are a fan of fresh, authentic sushi. Sushi chefs looked bored and upset when I sat down at the sushi bar. Showed no interest in engaging in conversation. Would not help at all when I asked about recommendations, what was fresh. I ordered the "hard-core sushi" combination with salad and miso soup. Miso soup fine, salad with ginger dressing too heavy on the greens.  Fish were all served at luke-warm temperature. Mixture of fresh and previously frozen fish. Snow crab sushi had a piece of shell left in it. Didn't have any problems with tendons left in the fish, but the chefs clearly had minimal training in the art of fish cutting. Quality of fish is maybe 3 out of five and that is being generous. Overpriced for what you get.

Sketch is probably the right name for this experience, that I wanted badly to feel but didn't. Hungover and needing the revitalizing hot beef and cheese injection experience, I was led astray into the sobering grunge of Fishtown in midday sun and felt worse for the wear pretty much across the board.  The place is going for laid-back neighborhood vibe, but finishes a note too swarthy. 

Pros
-Dipping sauce... it's just mayo in a variety of disguise but still delicious.
-Old dog on the floor.
-Crayons

Cons
-A burger too far - some inventions are too good to mess with. You don't need to reinvent the wheel, you can't build a better mousetrap. Same with burgers. Sketch got too high concept on the 'smashed onion burger' for example, and I paid the price with his huge mess. Unwieldy and over-complicated, it seemed all I could taste was cheese and burnt onion. Maybe that's someone's thing. Not mine.
-Cheese - I never thought I'd say this, generally being a big fan, but when your entire enormous patty is covered in a half-inch thick layer of congealing pepperjack, it's a little off-putting.
-Milkshake-down - big, undifferentiated soft-serve with a pump of coffee syrup for like $6.

This is one of the only Japanese restaurants in the city that is actually owned by Japanese.  Unfortunately the sushi chefs have as much personality as my left toe, but the fish quality here is excellent.  Also, one of the only restaurants other than Raw and Morimoto that carries Mirugai all the time.
Sushi beginners may want to stay away, as this place is far from a bargain.  Due to the fact that I eat a lot more sushi than a normal patron, I would say to expect a bill ranging from $50-200.
Friendly service. Was expecting to taste the best burger ever since they were featured on the travel channel but it was at best "ok".

Best Teriyaki Chicken in the area.  The best is at the food truck on Davis-Monthan, but the brick and mortar location isn't far off in quality and taste.  Prices are reasonable for the quantity received.

Oh Toro is THE best part of the tuna and they served it FROZEN. No REAL sushi place serves it FROZEN. Also a friend ordered oh toro sushi, while the rest of us ordered sashimi. The amount of meat was such a huge difference for the same cost. Definitely get sashimi if you're going to pay market price and if you're going to try out this place.

I ordered a Sapporo Light, she still brought me the wrong one after I said it twice AND pointed it out on the menu.

Excellent place for lunch! I had the Kahlua Pulled Pork. So good! Huge portion. Came with mixed vegetables and rice. My husband got the Teriyaki Chicken. It was so tender & lots of flavor. The prices are reasonable. 

The employees are super nice & didn't mind explaining the menu. 

Definitely worth a visit!

Wow.....great steaks. First time at the market, and happened upon this place. Their meat looked good, so I'd thought I'd try some strip steaks. Glad I did....they were tremendous. I was surprised how much better the steaks were compared to the high end supermarkets.  I haven't tried their sausage yet, but will do so soon.  The guys behind the counter were friendly and very helpful... Told me where to go for the best fresh pasta in Philly.  I will have to make the hour plus trek to  the Martins on a regular basis....summer....grilling....steaks.....Martin's .....could'nt  be better......
The overall experience is great! Everytime i go i get a black & white shake, they are to die for. Their burgers are really good also. I like how they have all the drawings hungup on their walls.

Absolutely delicious!!! My family and I went here the night before the Philadelphia marathon to have sushi for dinner and it exceeded our expectations. My wife and I eat sushi once a week and we are very selective. The fish was very fresh and I would recommend this place to friends and family without hesitation.

I always wanted to try this place and I am glad I did. As soon as I walked in I was given a friendly greeting and the waitress complimented my shirt ( she seems to like punk). That is always nice when someone goes out of their way to make you feel welcomed.

She took my order promptly and my food came out fast. I just ordered the sirloin burger and fries. The burger was huge, meaty, and juicy. The fries were thick and the chipotle sauce went well with them. 

The atmosphere was fun as well with a ton of sketches on their wall from patrons. I know most of my carnivore friends will love this place. I will definitely return here when I am around the neighborhood
I had the cyclops burger and the sweet potato fries! Both were awesome and the sweet potato fries are the best ever, with their chipotle mayo! Service is awesome too!

This place is ok if you want a grungy atmosphere  with  mediocre and overpriced food. I had the KOBE burger made medium well and it was boring. The fries are huge and flavorless and the same goes for the mediocre peanut butter/chocolate shake I ordered. At one point, while I was prepping my burger, the guy walked over, and without notice GRABBED my cheap paper tray and said "that's not your burger. . .this is". So, I wonder what I ate in the first place. Four burgers, three shakes, and two orders of fries wound up totaling  over 100 dollars. you decide. I will leave this place to loser hipsters who think they're cool by going here.

I love Sketch, I'll be the first to admit it, but I have come to learn the hard way that the human body has only enough blood either to function normally, or to digest a Sketch burger, not both. I frequently find myself engaging in the act of self-immolation that is eating a Sketch burger with all the fixins' and tackling an order of fries. Time and time again I hear my heart (and its surrounding arteries) scream, "NO!" but my stomach and brain stifle its cries and eat the monster burger anyway, only to pass out for the rest of the day.

Sketch burgers are real show-stoppers and should only be attempted by the seasoned professional or the serious masochist. I recommend not eating for the entire day and going on an empty stomach. You won't regret it.

the burger menu, decor, service, and spirit were great. But the taste of the burger meat was  definitely lacking. I ordered the cyclops burger with the aioli sauce and wasabi sauce. Also the burger was WAY TOOO  GREASY!

Friday night dinner date and it was cozy and not a lot of ppl. Kind of dark but it wasn't bad especially for date night. Food was excellent and the margarita definitely had a kick! Had the tamale plate and it was a big! The wife had the burrito. That's her favorite and she never gets anything else lol. Waitress did her job well and didn't bother us too much or too little. Food came out rather quickly

This has been bookmarked for awhile and I finally had the chance to go. We went at an off time around 4:15 pm to beat rush hour traffic and not having to worry about parking. There is only street parking no parking lot. 

It's on the smaller side for a restaurant and they have about 8 tables to sit out and a few to able to sit outside. I love that they have beautiful "sketches" on the wall from other restaurant patrons before. Some of the art work is truly amazing. I especially loved all the ones with cats. There's a specials board with apps and special burgers. We decided to try the special of loaded cheese fries that came with fried onions, bacon and jalapeños. It was amazing, I could have ate the whole order to myself! I also decided to try the burger special of the "Nashville Spicy Burger" it came with pepper jack cheese, jalapeños. The burger was delicious and you could see how fresh and juicy it was. Everything our party ordered looked amazing and everyone was very happy with their meal. The servers Rachel and Michelle were very attentive. 

They offer milkshakes and desserts, if your still hungry. 

The best part is that it's a BYOB. I highly recommend trying this place if you love burgers. It's worth the drive!

Wow! One of the best meals I have ever eaten. The Dr. Pepper pulled pork was amazing and the burgers were good too. I also liked the dipping sauces for the fries. Service was wonderful and fast. The drawings on the wall were a nice touch.

Good Burger (Not Mind Blowing) but good.  Alot of flavor..alot of grease. sometimes grease is good. But it's been a few hours and I still taste it. I do have to say the employees that were working were very sociable and the concept is very original. My daughter and I drew up a couple pictures and the gentleman working the floor was awesome he was very polite and gave her scotch tape to put them on the wall. Now the reason I was so mean and I gave this place 4 stars is this hipster strapper who can benefit from a stick of Old Spice gave my one year old son a dirty look because he accidently touched his arm, see I'm a family man now. But a few years ago I would of choked him with his own dreadlocks but today Id rather enjoy a Sunday burger and fries with the wife and kids.. Then to top it off behind me some other wasted embryo wearing his sister's jeans was obnoxiously making some crap play list "drowning out some solid ass James Brown that was playing in this fine establishment".that was reason alone for me to want to flip my table over. So with that said draw a burger on some loose leaf at the crib and bring it in when you go pick up your take out. And make sure you get the loaded fries.

mmm delicious!

I just got back from having dinner here.  Slightly pricey, but definitely really good.  I ordered the dragon roll and the salmon steak (cooked to medium).  Everything was so yummy.  I feel like I ate a meal for 3 people all by myself, cause I didn't want anything to go to waste.  If I lived in philly, I'd prob frequent this restaurant a bit more often.

Sketch is an inviting, colorful Fishtown burger joint. True to its name, every table comes stocked with crayons and paper, allowing patrons to sketch fan art to be hung on the restaurant's walls. Their site even features a sketch of the month.

It's a clever concept.

This establishment offers unique burger options, such as the Cyclops, which comes with bacon and eggs, and the Truffle Butter, which is exactly what it sounds like. Each burger is also served with your choice of sauce (chipotle, wasabi, tahini, etc.)

The burgers are flavorful and very juicy -- which is to say that they're incredibly messy. The food is generously portioned as well. However, the hand-cut Belgian fries are the true show stopper. You could make a meal out of this side dish alone.

If you happen to be a vegan who misses some of the guilty pleasures in life, I have to imagine this is the only place where you can get a vegan-friendly milkshake and burger.

Sketch has one of the better burgers in the city but it is a notch below the elite five-star status of other Philadelphia area burger places because the bread brings it down. Apparently, they use LeBus buns, but it did not taste like any of the LeBus breads I've had in the past. In an otherwise great meal, this was the only letdown.

The ONLY negative thing about this place is that they do not accept credit cards. Boo. The BEST thing about this place... the FOOD!! All of it is freaking delicious! The Dr. Pepper pulled pork/brisket (not sure what meat) is TO DIE FOR!!!! As is their milkshakes.  sooooo goooood!!

After waiting 45 minutes for our food to arrive, it came out cold. They claimed it "just came up," but the chips in the tortilla soup were completely soggy, and the refried beans had formed a crust on top. To their credit, they did promptly remake the food (had it to us in 5 minutes), and the chips in the soup were still crisp. Unfortunately the food for our toddler did not arrive with the rest of the meal. It arrived 20 minutes later. Food service 101: don't make the kids wait. It was clear the server forgot to put in the order.  I won't be back.

Crazy good burgers!  Had mine with salsa verde and cheese.   My sons had theirs with bacon/cheese and my wife had one with avocado and truffle butter.   Fries were really good and the dipping sauces were great.   Milkshakes were over the top good and had plenty of flavor choices.  Would be five stars if they gave you a pickle or slaw.   Food is a delight and could use something to cut the richness.  

Parking on Girard is tough but keep looking, the burger is worth the search.   Staff was awesome and helpful, reflecting the character of the neighborhood.   Bring cash to pay - they do have an ATM.  

Lastly, enjoy the sketches and get your sketching on.  The pics are worth the trip and add great character to the trip.

My girlfriend and I have been coming here for years but she had a lousy experience here today. One of the things we always do is get their excellent Cheese Fries with some of the Dr.  Pepper Pulled Pork on top. They charge us a bit extra for it-- $3 or $4 bucks but it is worth it. 

Today, the cashier (whom she didn't recognize) rang up the same item as $15-- the price of Cheese Fries plus a Pulled Pork Sandwich. When asked about it, the cashier insisted it had to be done that way. Our past experience indicates it doesn't have to be done that way. 

I hope that the management can address this issue, otherwise they have lost some long term repeat customers. (Frankly, they should just put the pulled pork as a fries topping on the menu.)

Also, the food here is good, but the real secret is the baked goods. They are fantastic.
One of the best burgers you will ever have. Also, their green chili cheese fries are to die for.

After living in San José CA and having access to Japantown and now having visited Japan,  Shiroi Hana is the place that delivers the real deal.   Excellent atmosphere and ambiance with superb food!  I highly recommend for lovers of Japanese cuisine!

The only thing I'd recommend from this place is the TUNA TARTAR.  Yummy avocado, tasty seasoning, and most importantly - fresh tasting, melts in your mouth, tuna.  After trying this appetizer, I was super duper excited to try the rolls.  I loooovvveeee sushi so I have very high expectations for every place I try, considering how pricey this type of food is.  Anyway, onto the rolls.  Overall, the PRESENTATION of the food was excellent and  quite artistic.  But.....my bf and I tried:

Spider roll - this is my all time favorite roll, next to anything spicy tuna.  So this roll HERE...was a huge let down.  It wasn't hot or crunchy or flavorful.  It was just whatever and had a strange sweet flavor.  They give you this semi-salty dip to go with it but man, that doesn't make it any better.  

Spicy tuna roll - GUEH! It wasn't spicy nor did it taste like tuna. And what's with the weird sauce on top?! Is that supposed to be their version of eel sauce or something? I'm confused.  

Rainbow roll - another disappointment.  The tuna was kinda dry..and the yellowtail was oddly flaky yet chewy at the same time.  The salmon was alright though.  

Crunchy roll - this was by far the worst.  What made this roll "crunchy" was the fact that they sprinkled a tiny bit of tempura over the roll.  What a ripoff!  An expensive roll that can't even live up to its name! D: I couldn't even taste the shrimp either...

Based on what I got here, I would not come back and order it again all for 70 bucks.  I've seriously had better.  Quality and quantity.  

A plus is that the service here is very good.  Everyone's very polite and it's like they wait on you, hand and foot.  They literally stand by your side and make sure you have everything you need, etc.  

Again, I think I'm just gonna try other things on the menu besides the sushi if I ever come back.  Hopefully they're as good as the tartar.

TRUFFLE Burger..... nuff said.

well. wait.... I'd give it 5 stars if it weren't for the flourescent lights but yea. truffle burger. mmmmmm.

EDIT for subsequent visit:
Last visit they turned OFF the flourescent lights and put some warm incandescent lamps around. Very Cozy! Burgers are still out of this world. 5 Stars

Pretty solid food truck, prices are competitive and they will give you enough food to feed a small village. Pulled pork has lots of flavor and appropriate texture, and teriyaki chicken is perfectly marinated and charred.The biggest downside is the sides -- white rice is just too plain, and tuna mac isn't that great. Overall, highly recommend, but next time I would ask for Hawaiian rolls to replace the sides.
Their pizza is great, their cheesesteak is awesome. What more can I say? I've been going here for years now and I have no real complaints about the place.

A family member gave my 90 year old mom a gift certificate, so she could get some homemade frozen dinners & not cook.
The store is very clean & fairly well laid out. This is not a new concept.
They have the various stations for people to run in & put together a good meal or several. The selection is listed, all the ingredients you need to prepare dish have been misen placed for your convenience & aluminum to go containers are also in reach.
The concept started many years ago, I believe with blue apron. I can appreciate the concept of making 1 or more meals to take home to eat or freeze, but I have some problems with the concept also.
Actually you have no idea of the actual quality of the food you are using. There was staff visible & no other customers, but no personable interactions, explanations or  assistance. When I asked a question I recieved a curt, short respose, that's it.
Going to the prepared frozen meals, they are not just your meat & potatoes. It is foodie oriented, with most dishes, my mom having never hear of, picky eaters.... beware.
The sizes in my opinion are greatly exaggerated. If it is to feed 3-4 people, on the entrees, they are not including hard working men & women, that are truly hungry when they get home. They have "petite " selections, but after thoroughly searching the freezer section I found 1 entree.
Besides entrees, they offer sides, appetizers & desserts that are frozen. 
The jury is out on the prices, since I do not agree with their stated serving size. I tasted an initial meal of bolagnasie, from the first offering my mom got, it was good, but nothing special.
Due to the food choices this is definitely not the answer for our aging population. I see it geared to the millennial's. Yup, it's tastier than most store bought frozen meals, but at what price & not knowing all the ingredients. The store bought  items must list all ingredients, but again you have no true idea of the quality of ingredients, that is a personal problem for me.
I really know the store should take classes in customer relations & attitude. If my mom had gone without me, there is no doubt she would have left empty handed. This is definitely not a place for me, but maybe you guys think differently

What's a girl to do? I will keep cooking larger portions, freezing them & delivering them, on my visits.

I wanted to try Sketch because I passed by here once, but didn't have time try it out. After reading the reviews I was optimistic. So I get there just as it starts raining and I walk back as far as customers are allowed. Then I was told to have a seat and check out the specials.

I got a BBQ, bacon, bleu cheese burger (beef) and a small order of frites. At the time, the owner (I suppose) was doing it all. Someone else eventually showed up to help out. For me, here's the dealbreaker... and many places have this same problem. The drinks! I had the choice between 16-20oz bottles of tea, soda, or whatever, OR $5-ish milkshakes. 

Given the size of the food portions these overpriced bottles don't cut it. The owner said they don't have space for fountains. Fair enough. I got a cookies and cream milkshake (as much as I didn't want to... but it would last longer) and it was hard getting the food down... really. The bill is tallied up after rather than before. No harm there, but for this kind of place it seemed awkward. I saw other customers come in order and then grab a drink to have it later added to the bill. With everything being $2 or more it felt like a trap. I seriously bring a drink with me to places like this. I know my consumption. One of those bottles would be gone after getting halfway through the frites.

So what about the food? Everyone is right about the harissa aioli... it's great. I think the brioche buns are baked in-house because I've never seen them this big. The frites were hand-cut (right?) but a little thick for my taste and the milkshake didn't help. The shake wasn't bad. I would have liked it smoother. And the burger itself was righteous (although my BBQ sauce was sparse), but for the overall price of the meal ($18+tip) I can't hang. The decor really turned me off from the price. I'd spend this kind of money in Rittenhouse, but here I felt like I was at summer camp. And I'm actually an artist so I thought I'd like the whole "sketch" idea. Overall, I just wanted to try this place at least one time and I have and now that's that. I could certainly nitpick a few more things, but you get the idea. The owner is friendly and accommodating. I suspect she has loyal foodies on her side, but for the average Joe I just can't see it.

Execellent variety and taste.  We had a one year old, and the staff was extremely accommodating and friendly.  We loved the decor and the ability for our son to color helped to subside our hunger.  We can't recommend the food or the device enough. We will definitely be back!
Great burger atmosphere with greetings all over their walls. The fries were excellent but the burger patty imo was too soft and the bread was too large. Excellent service though.

They have the best burgers in Fishtown!Definitely worth to go! Fast cook, decent price, and huge size of burgers! You can choose all kinds of meats or vegetables that you would love to put in your burgers. In addition, it is a really cute store. You can draw anything you want and put on the wall for the restaurant decorations. Down side is that it is cash only.

Been going to Martin's for over 15 years.  My go to place for meat.

Prices are good, but more importantly the quality is great!  Every time I buy meat at Trader Joes, I always wish I had just had the time to go get it fresh.

My favorite is the Sirloin and the Lamb Shoulder chops.  The key with Lamb is that it is 'domestic' (corn fed) rather than New Zealand (grass fed and therefore gamey).

I can't really say much else, it is a great value.  You could pay more for prime, but why bother when their meat just tastes good.

This is just concerning their Baguette. They consistently bake the best I've ever eaten. It's better than any Baguette in France for that matter. 

It's a shame the little outpost on Germantown Ave. is now closed, but it's apparently going to become available now in the new store that has taken over the location. 

Here's a little tip though, the Chestnut Hill Cheese Shop and the Weaver's Way Cooperative both sell Metropolitan's Baguette, and it's actually cheaper to buy it from Weaver's Way. Also, you can pick up some really good cheeses at these other places to accompany Metro's best Baguette ever.

I was highly disappointed since we drove out of the way to come here. My cousins from New York came down and had a list of places they wanted to try after watching the foodnetwork/travel channel. 

It is located in the fishtown section of Philadelphia. Parking was a little tough since it's street parking in a mainly residential and yes it was the day after thanksgiving which doesn't help. We found the place to be charming with a hipster vibe. The staff was friendly. It was empty when we came in but since the place is relatively small seating about 24 people, our family took up half of the seatings. I did like the atmosphere filled with sketches done by customers (hence their name)

The food. We ordered 2 orders of regular fries, 1 sweet potato fries and a truffle fries. The fries were handcut it seems and all of them fries were undercooked and some pieces were raw. The truffle fries does not taste like truffle fries at all. At these prices or any prices that was disappointing. I had the lamb burger which was the special of the day, it $13 compared to their other burgers at $8-$10. It came with a fennel slaw. I asked for it medium when asked how I wanted it. Fries would be extra so I passed on it. The burger came with the buns toasted but when touched, it was cold!!! The lamb burger was over cooked and dry. All of our burgers were over cooked and the buns were all cold while showing signs of being toasted.  

We didn't even bother ordering any shakes! We just drove 15-20 minutes to the nifty fifty's on Grant Avenue and the boulevard to get our shakes. Will be writing a review for that soon.

Won't be coming back.

HOLY COW, the burgers here are amazzzzziiiinnnnngggg!

I had been meaning to make it to Sketch for a while now since I moved to Northern Liberties and I am so glad my boyfriend agreed to let me take him here for his birthday last week.  The menu here is short and sweet, but everything sounded great to it took me a little while to finally decide upon what to have.

I finally made the decision on the smashed onion burger (the onions are literally smashed under the patty on the griddle to cook) with horseradish cheddar cheese. My burger came out cooked perfectly and was so tasty, yet not overly greasy. I also had the delicious green chile cheese fries, which are completely necessary to get when you come here.

What really stole the show was the lamb burger. It is not on Sketch's every day menu, but if you like lamb and you ever see it on the specials board, do yourself a favor and order it. It was seasoned perfectly and had a great yogurt sauce on it to level out the spice.

Last but not least, we had AWESOME service. Our waitress was so pleasant and gave us honest recommendations on what toppings go best on certain burgers. She really made the night special when she overheard it was my boyfriend's birthday and gave him a little cake on the house! 

I only have one tiny complaint about this place and it is the lighting. Eating under fluorescent lights just makes me feel uncomfortable. 

All in all, I will be back without a doubt!

Those stars are for the fun little bar game at the end of the bar that I spent about 45 minutes entertained by (with my two underage cousins), and the pretty bomb margarita.  The food was wicked bad.  My pores are still excreting salt trying to bring my body back to a natural balance.  Food was cold, food took ages, two people got left out for a while, food was icky, everything was salted 8 miles beyond reasonable. . .Good thing I don't hang out in Tucson looking for bad Mexican food much.

The burgers are HUGEEEE. 

I love the concept of being able to sketch while waiting for the food. The restaurant is decorated with drawings, but it's really small. 

The fries are soooo good! Definitely get the fries. They are the best fries I have ever had! The burger will definitely fill you up and is really good. 

The burgers and fries are a little pricey, but worth trying.

I am ecstatic to have finally found a place in Philly that has GREAT burgers and fries!! I went with the family on Saturday and hubby and I were back in the very next day for take out. I had their Truffle Burger and fries with aioli sauce and it was absolutely delicious. I would have tried one of their milkshakes; however, I was stuffed. The ambiance was beyond inviting and colorful, as there are hundreds of "sketches" from previous customers. Each table has sheets of construction paper, colored chalk and crayons so you can create a work of art, which gets tacked up on the wall or decopaged onto their tables. My son looked at me with embarrassment as I playfully took to creating my work of art, which I'm hoping will be posted up. At our 2nd visit, hubby and I brought in our dog (they are dog friendly) and they gave her a thick cut slice of cooked bacon (on the house) as we waited for our take out order. Her pup review is 2 paws up and we will definitely be returning.

I decided to try this place although I saw the poor reviews. Most of the reviews were based off customer service and not taste and quality of the pizza. I wanted pizza and I was in town so I gave it a shot. I liked it! Pepperoni was good, garlic knots were good and the sausage pizza was good for my daughter.

Give it a shot...see for yourself.

Underwhelming experience. I wasn't expecting fancy by any means, but the burger itself did not deliver in my opinion. I got the truffle butter burger, a vanilla milkshake and a small order of fries with chipotle sauce. 

I asked for my burger to be cooked medium rare. It came out medium - medium well, and tasted more dried out than juicy. The truffle was hardly detectable save for the mushrooms thrown in on the bottom. The Le Bus bun is good but doesn't save the burger. The fries were actually my favorite part of the meal. Thick cut and crispy on the outside and they go well with the chipotle sauce.

The place itself is a small, unpretentious Fishtown joint. There is no table service, order inside and grab a table. I understand the concept of "sketch" but the inside felt dingy and a little grimy. It has fluorescent lighting which doesn't help the cause. Of note, it is cash only, but they do have an ATM inside.

Probably wouldn't come back, I can get a better burger elsewhere.

3.5.

I got the Cyclops burger, which consisted of a humungo patty (medium rare), humungo/thick piece of bacon and egg (runny yolk, of course!). It was delicious. The meat...might has well been a decent size steak, it was that big. It was quite greasy, more greasy than your typical burger, and the bacon and the yolk probably made it worse. Nonetheless, pure guilty pleasure.

The green chili cheese fries did not live up to the hype. Too much cheese and non-crispy fries= soggy mess. I was fishing around for the fries around the border that wasn't drowned in the cheese.

Final note, one of my pet peeves is when the restaurant menus are sticky. Or if the tables are. In this case, both were, and that's kinda gross.

It took over an hour for takeout, there were three mess-ups with our order and I still think the prices for some stuff are a little ridiculous...but I really liked my vegan burger. I'd skip the truffle butter as a topping, barely detected it, and I wish I'd opted for avocado.  My mushrooms were also on the scant side. If you're going to charge astronomical prices for toppings make them count please. 

My guess is this place needs more employees, especially on a Friday night.  The three employees were working as hard as they could to fill the massive amount of orders coming in and they were clearly overwhelmed.  We ended up missing one of our cheese fries, which luckily we caught before we left, but it added about 10 minutes to our wait time and I am not exaggerating in the slightest when I say it took one hour.  For takeout. For burgers and fries. 

My burger was wrapped upside down and really loose, the two seitan sandwiches were miss marked and one had a different type of cheese than requested plus mushrooms that weren't requested.  Lucky for me, the mistakes weren't near my food and my burger was delish.  So my complaint is for you management/owners--hire some more peeps and fix your scheduling issues. Until then, see you on weekdays. 

 
Oh and they take cards now, which maybe they have for a while, whatever.
I ordered Zeppoles and got six of them for over $4. And to top it off they were garlic knots with powdered sugar on them. Just sad and lazy. This was my icing to never go back.

We having been going to Macayo's for many, many years.  Besides the yummy house margaritas, I have also become a full blown Baja Sauce addict, lol.. Over the years I have ordered nearly everything off the menu and I have NEVER had a bad meal.  My current favorite is the shredded beef Baja chimichanga, oh and the green corn tamales, not to forget the spinach enchiladas and the....  Hmmm, everything is good!!

This was my first time at sketch burger, and I was so excited to try it because I heard so many good things. I guess my first mistake was going at 7:45 pm on a Sunday night. The place was filthy. There was dirt on the walls, food all over the benches, and nothing appeared to have been wiped down all weekend. We started off with an order of regular and sweet potato fries, which were very good. However, I ordered a beef burger with mushrooms, bacon, and cheese. The mushrooms were cold, not even lukewarm but cold. The bacon was barely cooked, and my burger had 0 taste. Needless to say I was incredibly disappointed and I'll never go back. And to top it off it was so expensive.

I'll be the slight downer in this litany of praise.

I've been to Sketch a few times and though the atmosphere & service is pleasantly quirky and the menu & specials are unique, the burgers themselves leave a bit to be desired.  Maybe I'm not as adventurous as the menu suggests I should be - I get the sirloin burger with cheddar, avocado & bacon (no sauce).  However, even the most basic burger should be delicious.  There is never enough seasoning to the meat, which is I suppose why a sauce is recommended.  I also wish the lettuce were a better quality served in big luscious pieces as opposed to just shredded flavourless iceberg.

The portions are indeed huge (sometimes not a good thing - I dislike having to figure out how to bite into it) and you get your money's worth in that respect, but they never ever sit well in my stomach.  I had one over two hours ago and it's just a brick in there making me feel gross.

The shakes are really good, but I'd suggest getting one to go and not having it with the burger because either one, the other or both won't get finished in that sitting (maybe I just have a small stomach, who knows).

I'll end with this - a block away is a place where I get the exact same order of a burger (minus avocado, but plus tasty pickles) that is always perfect and digests beautifully.  Try Kraftwork's burger - you might not return to Sketch.

Probably the worse burger in Philly. Seriously!
Started with the fries (which were great by the way) being served 10 minutes before the burger. That means you're either finishing the fries before you get the burger, wait until you get the burger and eat cold fries OR get another order of fries when the burger arrives.
I ordered my burger cooked medium and it came well done and dry, the mushrooms on it tasted like the griddle hasn't been cleaned for a few days, the meat had no flavor at all and over all was extremely greasy.

As a burger lover, I honestly don't understand the hype around this place. 

Never again.

I wanted to like this place based on the great reviews.  First of all I stepped in and since it was the first time I had ever been I had no idea you needed to go to the back to place your order.  Someone should be close to the door seating people instead of in the kitchen.  

I ordered a cyclops burger and I must say this is something I could have made at home.  The burger was on the dry side inspite of me ordering it medium.  The portion was fairly large, but I had to stop eating it due to the lack of flavor. The bacon was undercooked and still had a large piece of fat on it.  

If I were rating this place solely on the cheese fries it would easily be a 5 star review, but everything else was meh including the tacky decor. 

I don't know what the deal is with restaurants in Philly being cash only, but it is very annoying.  For the prices that I paid at this place they should at least accept debit cards.

So they advertise all day every  happy hour, but the catch is its only in the bar! I order the carna asada queso chimichanga. It tasted amazing but didnt have much meat. For desert the mini chocolate chimis with vanilla ice cream super good!

Stopped in here over the weekend. I had seen this place on TV some time ago and made a mental note to stop in as some point. Well, that time was last Sunday(7/9). The place wasn't very busy. There was a couple eating outside and no one was inside, which was fine with me. The menu has several burger options and a variety of sauces. BTW, the garlic aioli is AMAZING. I think I need to come back just to try the other sauces. I had the truffle butter burger add bacon, cheddar and the usual accoutrements(lettuce, tomato, onion and pickle). No joke! This is one of the best burgers in Philly. I usually do mustard and ketchup on my burger, but I ate this one condiment free. It didn't need any condiments. A couple other burgers caught my eye(Cyclops and Kobe), so between the burger options and the sauces, I will be back.
The bang shrimp is awesome along with the pulled pork, just topped Mamas. Can't wait to try the poke!

I was disappointed when I went here shortly after moving to town. There's barely seating and there was one server running around like she was trying to do everything, but no one was helping her. It was actually kind of strange how she looked so busy with only a few tables in the whole place.

I was ready to love this place when I first saw the menu online, but my burger was overcooked and kind of boring, there was wayyyy too much lettuce and the cookie I bought tasted like refrigerator. The wait was also a bit longer than I expected in such a small place.  My boyfriend was pretty happy with his burger and the cheese fries were pretty good, if a bit too salty. They were friendly enough... well, the one person who interacted with anyone, even though there were a few people in the back. I wouldn't bother going back though.

Today was my first visit to Sketch. It was lunch with my two daughters and a friend. I love the look of the place with the drawings all over the walls and tables and the mix of chairs and what look like church pews. We all ordered burgers and fries. The waitress was very nice. The fries came first and they were hot, crispy and seasoned well. The green goddess sauce was tasty. The burgers were big and juicy. It was a good burger. I can't say it's the best in the city but I intend on going back to sample other menu items. I would recommend people who haven't been here to give it a try.
It's a good classic Japanese restaurant. The sushi is always fresh. It is more expensive than most

I just love this place and I always bring out-of-town friends to it. It's pricey, but you get what you pay for. I also like the idea that there are a few standard menu items and everything else rotates based on what they have and/or have dreamed up. You definitely need to call or drop in to see what they have on any given day. 

As a vegetarian/most of the time vegan, it's hard to find "comfort food" that meets my dietary and ethical standards.
