The hand-made veggie burger here is second-to-none and they always have slamming vegan specials. There is a daily  seitan special and there are often vegan soups, chilis, and empanadas. The sweet potato fries are amazing and should be purchased whenever they are available. 

This is really a sort of once a month/ every once-in-a-while thing for me, even though I live around the corner, because I usually end up dropping $20 or so on whatever they have to offer. Nonetheless, travellers should keep this in mind when they are hitting up a show in Philly - it's right off I-95!

SUMMARY
Best bubble tea and sushi place on campus with smart management. I don't understand why people don't come here more often - probably because it's new and the location is a bit out of the way (next to Kiwi). It's about time that Penn got a decent sushi place - Mizu is okay but too small and there's never any room to sit. This place is fantastic - great food, great decor, friendly servers, fast service, and amazing value for the sushi you get.

FOOD - SUSHI
Sushi is fresh, high quality, and pretty much the best you could possibly wish for at the dinner pricing of $14 for 3 rolls. Never settle for the boxed stuff at Houston again. Some people are all uppity about their sushi but I personally can't tell the difference between this and the $45 places like Fuji Mountain.

FOOD - BUBBLE TEA
Bubble tea here is definitely the best on campus. $2.50 for a small with tapioca boba, which is usually more than enough if you get it with food (I never finish mine).  They use real ingredients (i.e. the red bean tea actually contains red bean purée and is not from a powdered mix like Carina). Beijing isn't even worth mentioning. :p

SERVICE
Waiters are friendly, professional, and fast. Food usually comes within 10 minutes of ordering. No complaints. You can sit down or order takeout sushi/bubble tea from the bar at the front - no difference in service speed.

DECOR/FEEL
Really big, plenty of seating, have never had to wait for a table even during busy lunch/dinner times. Menus are beautiful and typo-free. Large tables with comfy chairs/booths, bamboo dividers, faux-stone on the walls (well done though, not tacky) and a soft blue light which lends a nice feel. Plates are large and artsy, food is nicely arranged without going overboard. Would not feel embarassed taking a friend here at all despite the great prices (sub-$20 for a meal with bubble tea), whereas Mizu feels a little more dumpy/hole-in-the-wall.

BUSINESS/MANAGEMENT ATTITUDE
Experienced two great customer service judgement calls here which have made me a loyal fan. The first time, a friend misunderstood the dinner combo and ordered five different rolls, thinking that the dinner combo would allow her to pick five different types of sushi. Seeing as the rolls would be $7-8 each when ordered separately, this would have amounted to $35-40 on the bill in addition to the other stuff she ordered. When she explained her mistake, management agreed to take the rolls off the bill and let her redo her order.

Second example was when I was accidentally given the wrong order and started eating because I was hungry/distracted by conversation. Two pieces in I realized it wasn't what I had ordered - server took the whole thing back, was very apologetic, brought the correct order immediately, and didn't charge me extra. Very impressed.

I love a good burger, I mean who doesn't? So when I found this place on Yelp with good reviews and delicious sounding burgers that are all less than $10 I was very excited to try it. The inside has a very cool, hipster vibe with all the sketches done by customers hanging all over the walls and the 90s-esque diner style booths. There isn't very much seating in there, maybe enough for 20-30 people total, but we got a table right away. We shared an order of regular hand cut french fries which were good, nothing special though. I ordered the cyclops burger with the garlic aioli sauce on it. Our burgers came out quickly and hot off the grill. Mine was cooked perfectly along with the fried egg on top of it (yum). The garlic aioli was the star of the show though, sooooo good.
I definitely recommend this place for anyone looking for a chill, low-key burger dinner that is relatively cheap.
Awesome place. Best burger in Philadelphia as far as I am concerned. Village Whiskey might be slightly better, but much more expensive. I recommend without reservations.

I came here last night with my boyfriend and we have both been up all night with severe food poisoning. Avoid this place unless you want diarrhea and vomiting all night and day.  I should send them my hospital bill. Do not go here!

meh burger ok nothing great, big yes great and full of flavor not so much, I had the beef burger with bbq sauce, bacon, grilled onions and cheddar cheese and it was just ok, with out the toppings it would have been rather unremarkable. the place is very small and hipster paint and little sketch covered walls only slightly mask the run down feel. def felt out of place not wearing skinny jeans. I would say its more of a take out place w/ the option to eat in, esp since they don't even have any fountain drinks, just bottles and cans. prob wont go back, would rather go to the place down the street, better food and full bar!

I'm always on the lookout for a better sushi spot, but when it's all said and done I always come back. Try as I might to find a new sushi restaurant, I never find anything quite good enough to dethrone Shiroi Hana.

It's not that there's anything wrong with this place - the fish is always fresh, the miso is delicious, the udon's warm and inviting. The place is consistently good, but I guess I'm just searching for greatness. I don't even know what I'm looking for in particular. I always leave satisfied, but wanting something more.

It's a nice place with a great atmosphere, but nothing stands out. 3*

Customer service is excellent. The server is incredibly attentive. 4*

I only tried the sushi and it doesn't stand out. The taste is just so-so. I personally think that the sushi is a bit dry. 3*

I was visiting Philadelphia over the weekend and my friend recommended here. I immediately enjoyed the laid back vibe of the place, and the food was delicious. From the different sauces to add to your burger, to the fries that were just amazing, I wish we had one of these in Orlando! I ordered avocados as a topping for an extra $1.50 I think, and they pretty much put a whole avocado on the burger, definitely worth the add on price. 
My only issue I had were the drinks, after we order the waitress just asked us to get up and pick out what drinks we wanted, as they seemed to only have teas, and bottled drinks, besides their milkshakes. That was a little bit of a turn off for me, as I felt they could have just mentioned what they had instead of making us walk towards the register. Minor detail, but I think it could have been a more efficient way to deal with drinks.
Overall friendly service, fun atmosphere, and I will be back next time.

Finally! I found some place where I want to be a 'regular'- and I am!

If you don't have the time or money to travel to Tokyo, just stop by Shiroi Hana. Grab some sake or a Japanese beer, enjoy the relaxing, modern, warm interior, and prepare to have some of the best sushi in the city. Their cooked dishes are also fantastic- the seafood teriyaki, in particular. Honestly, the white sticky rice with teriyaki sauce poured over it is heaven. I know, but just try it. The service is also wonderful. We have one waiter in particular who we really like... attentive, friendly, and unobtrusive. 

Definitely give this place a try. It'll be your new favorite Asian spot in Philly!

I've been eating solid grindz since they were just posted up at the base. They are good, however, their food has been mediocre my last 3 trips. I got the chicken katsu plate and it was over cooked. Portions have gotten smaller on the rice and mac salad. But if I had to choose between solid grindz and mamas hawaiian bbq, I'd definitely pick solid grindz for the price.

My husband and I went to Macayo's for dinner.  We waited almost 10 minutes before anyone came to greet or seat us.  My husband told the hostess that we were just about ready to leave - she just smiled.   The food was fair.  The service was not good.  The waiter took our drink order and I tried to order a Happy Hour drink - those prices were only good in bar.  So I decided I'd drink water.  It took forever for the waiter to give us our bill - even close to "tip time" the service was very bad.  We'll never return to this restaurant again.  There are way too many good restaurants in Tucson, but this is not one of them.

Well Below standard! This is for the location in the Chestnut Hill Marketplace.

Although the pastries were nicely displayed and looked wonderful, each of the three things I purchased were real disappointments. This is why I am reviewing them here.

First I'll mention that the salesperson was kind, positive and professional. As for the products--I purchased three basics: a brownie, a cookie and a croissant. The brownie was a 'midnight brownie.' It had no flavor whatsoever. I love many types of chocolate but this recipe was missing something.

The cookie was an oatmeal pecan one with raisins. Again, surprisingly disappointing. It was horribly sweet ( and I like sweet) and had no texture--and again no flavor.  Worst oatmeal cookie of all time, and I've had loads as they're my husband's favorite.

The 'almond' croissant was the most shocking of all. It was so tough that I had to literally TUG a bite off with my teeth. It was also sliced in half with old, oily, badly flavored spread inside! This 'filling' tasted like old butter with a tiny bit of almond flavoring spread unevenly. I love almond croissants and have enjoyed many here and abroad. This one was disgusting. If I didn't live too far away I would have returned  to this location and asked for a refund.

This was my first--and will be my only--visit to the Metropolitan Bakery. The products resembled a novice baker's experiments rather than the staples of a well-established business.

my friend and I went there before an evening show at the academy of music, cos i've been craving for sushi for about two weeks and this family style restaurant is AWESOME! 

appetizer: 
edamame - boiled green soy beans. haven't had this for ages. my mom used to make this during summer and we would just snack on it while watching movies or chatting, or both. 
fried oyster - w/ house sauce. awesome! 

entreé: 
chirashi - sorted raw fish over sushi rice with sesame, fish eggs, and seaweed tucked in between. 
vegetable teriyaki - my friend is not a raw food lover and he thinks it's more secure to order cooked stuff...and it's good! esp the tofu and the black mushroom! yum! 

their entreé comes with either soup or salad and both of us had miso soup. they cut the chives in heart shape! soooooo sweet! our server was very friendly too. 

will come back and try sushi love. 

I'm taking one star off cos the warm towels we got before the dinner...one of them had a stain looked like blood. the server apologized and brought another one upon my friend's request. hope that won't happen again!

Vegans beware. My husband and I went to Sketch when they first opened years ago and enjoyed their friendly service, quirky atmosphere, decent (though never great) vegan burgers, delicious fries and plentiful vegan seitan and dessert options. We went last week when my pregnancy had me craving a greasy burger and fries. I really enjoy their seitan specials and milkshakes and saw that is all listed on their website, paper and blackboard menu. 

When we asked for these options, the server said they were no longer available even though they are splashed all over their various menus. Ok. We'll just get the burgers. The buns have egg wash. Ok, regular rolls. We didn't make a big deal out of this to her but perhaps we looked disappointed because she went on for FIVE MINUTES about how vegan options are more expensive (ok, but you charge $7 for a vegan shake so...), the desserts rot more quickly (huh?), no one wanted vegan options (I see a lot of yelp reviews to the contrary but I understand not all customers are on yelp) and they had no room for vegan options. At this point I had to say that many nonveg restaurants in Philly offer great vegan options so it was disappointing that sketch was going backwards instead of forward in this regard. She said that most of their customers didn't want anything vegan. 

The fries are still good but other than that and the burger (without a bun!) there are no veg options here anymore.

Additionally, I call Sketch Sketchy because cleanliness levels are not up to par. The tables are sticky and smell of wet rags. Oh well.  

I understand that Sketch has never been a vegan restaurant and that businesses need to make decisions based on costs. But after years of offering these options and getting support from vegans, it seems odd to me to just remove these items from the menu seemingly overnight and to so aggressively and negatively speak about a way of eating that more and more people are embracing.
The interesting thing about Sketch burger is that you can draw pictures of anything and tape it anywhere in the building. The burgers are ok nothing amazing and out of this world!

Delicious burgers!  The only reason I'm not giving this place 5 stars is the wait seriously is ridiculous.  We called our take out order in, they said it would be 45 mins. Fine, no problem.  We get there after 45 mins and had to wait another 20.  If they just would have said an hour in the first place it would have been fine.  Waiting in the cold restaurant where there's really no place to stand and wait sucks.
Vegan shakes the size of a small country. SO good. Have yet to eat here, but will be back for sure.

Ate here once and loved the sushi! I ordered a delicious squid appetizer and my boyfriend got chicken teriyaki because he doesn't like sushi. Too bad the price is out of our range to eat here more often but if I could afford it, I would totally make this a regular stop. 

The seating area seems really small so we were fortunate to visit when it wasn't peak time (not sure when that is, maybe weekends). I only noticed it because it was right across from Applebees.

Was excited to try it out but could not have been worse of an experience.  Got a Cyclops Burger and it was sucked dry over cooked and a crust of burnt meat on one side.  Also go green Chile fries that were a bit sour and fries tasted burnt.  

They did offer for me to come back after I called but I was already home.

Reasonable prices, fresh sushi, and very amazing, mostly traditional Japanese food. Great atmosphere inside, but a little difficult to spot or find. Service is fantastic and everyone is extremely pleasant. Green tea and green tea ice cream here is the best in Philadelphia!

I work right at 15th and Locust so I'm taunted by Shiroi Hana when I walk home each night. I've heard from several people it's the best Japanese in CC so I've been patiently waiting to try it. I finally made it in for lunch the other day and was very impressed. The service was speedy, the decor was chic, and the prices for lunch were totally affordable. 

I had the Mix 3 Special for $15, which included 8 pieces of nigiri, 6 pieces of sashimi, and soup/salad. The fish was fresh and the sashimi was cut quite generously. My husband had the Mixed Tempura bento for $10, which included 3 pieces of gyoza, cali roll, and salad. When he took his first bite he said, "finally, real tempura."

I've already decided that SH is too pricey for dinner, and since I'm from Cali I refuse to pay that much for Japanese food based on principle. But for lunch it's an awesome deal and I'll definitely be back. If you live/work/just happen to be in the area M-F from 12-2:15p, check it out. You won't be disappointed!

How they manage to serve the best Hawaiian food and the best pad Thai we ever tried!!?? 

We will be back for sure!!

Sketch Burger is going to be my downfall!  My boyfriend recently moved right next door to the joint and I am fearful we will be eating there more than at home.  The burgers are good; the Cyclops is definitely my favorite and the fries!  AMAZING.  And, the milkshakes...

Knocking off a star because my burger was a bit greasy for my taste, but in the end it was still tasty. The fries were very good. Yummy pastries, too. The vibe of the restaurant is very fun, and I enjoyed looking at the sketches on the walls!

Decided to go outside of my normal area for lunch today and happened upon Sketch. I was drawn in by the funky look and the interesting menu made me stay. I wish I had had enough time to stay and eat there but I took my lunch to go. I got the fried chicken sandwich with fries. I was torn between that and the cheddar scallion buttermilk biscuits with pulled pork. The fried chicken was great but the bread was meh. Wasn't necessary. I ate the chicken by itself. Crispy, flavorful, and tender! Fries were also good, more rustic with a nice seasoning. I will definitely go back...that Milky Way milkshake has my name on it! Loved all the drawings on the wall, too.

BUYER BEWARE...  I stopped in during a frequent business trip to Center City after reading the excellent reviews on Yelp, rather than going to some of my tried-and-true options in Philadelphia because it was closer to my hotel.  I should have known something wrong was going on when I was the only person in the restaurant at 9pm.  I ordered several pieces of sushi and a simple side salad, as I found the rolls to be somewhat unnecessary modifications to the staples (e.g. who puts crab stick in a Philadphia roll?).

After receiving my salad, I quickly realized there were multiple dead insects on the lettuce including a dead ladybug directly on top.  I don't know if they store the greens outside, didn't wash them at all, were completely careless, or all three, but it was probably the most disgusting thing I've seen in a sushi restaurant where raw food preparation necessitates a certain heightened sense of cleanliness.  I quickly pointed this out to the waitress, who was the only person on the floor.  She took the salad away without any apology, correction, or offer.

At that point, I was tempted to walk out but stayed to try the lackluster fish that was barely a half step above grocery store grade that was delivered with a friendly "we're closing in 10 minutes, please eat quickly."  Thankfully, they didn't charge for the salad, but I will certainly not be making a return visit.

Better picks - for the same prices, go witb Zama or Vics for a far superior experience.  For an amazing deal with better fish than Hana, try the all-you-can-eat sushi at Aki - service there can be slow during rush hours, but it's clean and delicious.

Just got back from my ~20th time at Sketch Burger. We showed up a half an hour before close, and they were gracious enough to seat us, even with our large bottle of wine. The owner talked to us at length about our options, and let us take our time. The hospitality is unmatched: laid-back, kind, and helpful.

This place not only has great food and a great atmosphere, but it has something else -- something intangible -- that makes it truly great. I've had conversations with the owner and with the resident baker about their recipes, what they recommend, and their Sketch garden. They're always willing to talk shop with me, the amateur baker, and I'm always grateful.

Every single one of their baked goods that I've tried has inspired me. Inspired. Their meat is always cooked to perfection, but even if you're not vegan/vegetarian, you will love their veg options. It's not about exclusion here; it's about good food, and that's it.

Sketch is a way of life. I subscribe to that way of life, and you should, too.

This place has seen better times. I've been going here on and off for a year or so now and when I first went here, I loved it! But as time went on, they've forgotten how to cook burgers per your request and the personalities that work here are too much to handle. The last time I called to order, for instance, the lady was acting like she was having a psychotic episode (no joke) and was very rude. Hence, I'll probably not be returning, even though it is so close by to me. I REALLY wanted to like this place. Bummer.
No lie, their sweet potato fries are way too addictive and I still have dreams about this burger. Delivery takes a little too long but the food completely makes up for it!

A few days ago, I was craving a burger and I remember a few friends mentioned this place to me.  

Approx. $10 gets you an 8oz kobe beef burger (cheese is a buck extra).  Heaven.  

$5 gets you a milkshake.  At first, I thought $5 for a milkshake was a bit steep, however, when its served to you, you are left thinking, "did they just give me a pint of ice cream?!"  The shake is certainly worth sharing.  

I plan on returning here the next time Im in the area.
Been coming to Macayo's for years. Love their Baja Chimis, Spinach Queso, and Baja Tamales. Richard is the best waiter, very attentive and helpful.

The butchers are friendly and easy to work with.  Quality and selection of meat and sausage is superior.  If these guys were closer I'd be a weekly regular.  As it stands I'll have to keep making special trips.
As i walked I to this place, no one greeted me. A server was chasing a customer about not tipping her enough (15%). Ok I don't know how feel about that, so I left without dining

Without exaggeration I can not remember ever having a better burger in my life. The kind of burger that makes you say, "If I opened a burger joint I would make mine just like this".

If it is actually possible, the fries may have even out shined the burgers! Previous reviews mention closing at 9pm and no fries. We were served by three of the sweetest ladies ever just after 9:30 and the labor intensive basket of fried potato greatness hit our table shortly after ordering. No long wait for anything. 

To know: Main thing to know is that the burgers are huge. Big patties on big delicious buns, almost like a chala (sp), with fat ingredients...they put half an avocado on my girlfriends burger! Holy guac-a-Moly! So yes, awkwardly huge and drip down your arm delicious! Smash it down, and go to town!

Ok, in my post burger bliss (is it possible for men to have after-glow) I am rambling. So let me just share one last thing. I want to share an example of food "love". The owner is neither vegan nor vegetarian, yet she painstakingly spends hours a day preparing items to serve both lifestyles. If she is going to spend that much time rolling brown rice and lord knows what else into something she believes even a meat eater would love, well then you know she put's the love in every other item on the menu too.

One final personal note: If the horse faced hipster, retread valley girl, shoving 10lbs of shit in a 5lb bag, loud mouth bitch that couldn't stop talking about all the band guys numbers she has and utters the phrase "Philadel-phia Taa too Cun-vention" every third sentence is reading this. Shut the fuck up already! You are not cool, you are not original. The only difference between you and the most annoying of sorority girls is 3 jars of ranch dressing and your gas station shades vs. her designer sunglasses. The only reason those dorks were with you is because they heard you gave it away like Christ gave away loaves and fishes.

I've only been here once on a whim because I was having a serious burger craving. My first impression was that it was a little pricey for a burger joint but the burger I had here was to die for! Seriously AMAZING. I had the smashed onion burger with bacon and cheese. Whoa. My mouth is watering just thinking about it. I had their seasoned fries which were fine, not great but they were good enough. I will definitely be going back again and again!

This place is so white washed it's not even funny.  I ordered a jarritos, which was on the beverage menu, and the waitress looked at my like I was crazy.  Speaking of the staff, they were very far from friendly.

The food was OK but really plain and American-ish.

This place would not have been my choice nor would it be again.

Contrary to popular beliefs, Philly DOES make some great beef between buns that AREN'T called cheesesteaks. So if you're not from here, it's worth making the trek to Fishtown to check out this hip establishment called Sketch.

So, creativity is the name of the game of this restaurant. And one burger they drew up is called the Cyclops Burger ($9) that has a fried egg and bacons in it. This burger is a must order! The Beef patty, bacons, and fried egg is a sinful combination. Absolute gluttony. I especially liked the sweet bun (LeBus Bakery) on the burger. I thought the meat was good quality, juicy and cooked right. 

The real standout was the hand cut Belgian style sweet potato fries though. They melt in your mouth on the inside and just plain crispy awesomeness on the outside. It was love at first bite. Dipped with their special homemade chipotle sauce, heaven. 

Overall, service was friendly and decent. Coming back soon!

Visited around 7 on a cold saturday night.

Decor is pretty nice. Very tiny. Just a small crowded room. Lots of wood.

Service was poor. After being seated we waited sometime before being asked about drinks, and later a salad we ordered was never served. (We didn't bother fixing it and just had it removed.) However, it was nice to get hot towels.

Food  was fairly average. and a bit pricey, as sushi tends to be.

After an OPI binge at a beauty supply store, a friend and I decided to stop by here for even more indulgence. I have had this place bookmarked since it opened, so it feels great to cross it off my list. 

First off, this place is tiny. Luckily we were there at like 3 pm on a weekday, so there was only one other party seated. I love the customer-generated art decorating the walls. It is amazing what some people can create with standard crayons, no? I drew an ocean scene while we waited for our order, cause that's basically all I can draw.

I ordered a medium-rare burger with cheddar, chipotle, lettuce, tomato, and grilled onions. Plus, my friend and I split an order of fries and a strawberry shake. And, to top it all off, I grabbed a Boylan's birch beer from the drink case. I firmly believe that birch beer is a gift from the gods and is far to difficult to find these days, so I was happy to get my fix.

So the burger is served on a brioche-y bun (half-brioche? does that exist?) and was so large it was rather unwieldy. If you can finish one of these bad boys in a single sitting, you go girl. The patty was cooked slightly beyond my desired level of doneness, luckily the toppings were great. I kind of feel like they rely too heavily on the additional ingredients here, the meat could benefit from  a little more seasoning and a slightly higher fat content. Still, it was far from a bad burger. The fries were fresh cut with the skin still on , perfectly crisp, and my favorite thickness. The garlic aioli that came with it was pretty delicious as well.

On the way out, I ordered a burger for Chad- medium-rare, chipotle aioli, pepper jack cheese, avocado, and chiles. Now that was a glorious burger, let me tell you. That combination is what I would recommend to anyone who comes here, it is perfectly spicy, fatty and flavorful.

Perfect for a lunch meeting! 
Good menu selection and fish quality
It's family owned so the service is fine
Prices are within range but not exactly low
I am a frequent costumer and will continue to support their good business

Solid sushi dinner. Great service- friendly and quick. Spicy tuna roll, shrimp tempura roll, island roll (salmon and mango) and dragon roll- all good quality and fresh. Also had fried banana dessert. Could have used a little more honey and a touch of salt, but pretty good.
Would definitely come back.

A-mazing!  I ordered the smashed onion burger and the green chili cheese fries along with a peanut butter milkshake.  everything was delicious!! my husband picked up the food so i can't comment on the ambiance but the food was fantastic, especially the green chili cheese fries.  probably the best i've ever had.  the sauce we got was really flavorful as well but i'm not sure which one it was.  i would absolutely go back there again.  their burgers are delicious and juicy and the portion sizes are huge.

I'm probably the wrong person to be reviewing a burger joint.  Not a vegetarian by any stretch of the imagination, I just don't really like ground beef in a... chunk.  Meatballs?  Nah, I prefer the beef crumbled into my tomato sauce.  Meatloaf?  Um, it's a LOAF of MEAT.  Just, ew.  And I feel the same way about burgers.  Crumble up the meat and call it a sloppy joe, and I'm all about it, but in solid form, it kinda grosses me out.

Yet, I still continue to order burgers because I am convinced that one day I will have a burger that is so juicy, so flavorful, so succulent, that I will be reformed.

On this visit to Sketch, we started with an order of fries while we perused the menu.  In minutes, we were served a cone of fresh cut, piping hot fries with a side of aioli.  They were pretty amazing, and despite the fact that the large order got us an entire golden pound, we polished them off quickly and contemplated ordering a more to go with our burgers. 

We exercised a moment of restraint and figured that the burgers we were about to eat would (should) be enough food.

I went with the smashed onion burger because I thought it would be least burger-like, flattened out over a bed of grilled onions, topped with bleu cheese, tomato and lettuce.  I will admit, I did really like the first couple of bites.  It was hot and greasy, and the bun was soft, and the cheese was melty and the onions were grilled to perfection, sweet and slightly charred.  But then the beef just overwhelmed me a little and all I wanted to do was remove it from the bun and eat a topping sandwich.

My friend ordered the black bean veggie burger with pepperjack cheese.  She was a little disappointed, citing lack of flavor in both the burger and the cheese.  Her boyfriend went with the classic sirloin burger with cheddar cheese.  He said it was good, but that's about all I got out of him.

There were several non-burger items on the menu that I'd really like to go back and try.  Really, I should have stuck with them to start with, given my... history with burgers.  Still, I'll go back for the fries alone, and next time I'll try a shake, too.

surprisingly good for philly's business district! when i studied at penn, i had to venture out quite a bit to eat a decent chirashi (sagami anyone?) wish i had known about this place. the decor is elegant. service matched the decor and value for the food, though i couldn't figure out if she was japanese or ... i have something for being served by waiter/waitress from the same region as the cuisine i'm savoring.

This is by far my favorite Hawaiian food!  I have tried just about everything in the menu and it's sooooo good!  This place does not disappoint and I love the spam masubi.  Check it out.  You'll love it

Got some Queso for $8 that tasted exactly like a melted block of Velveeta. 
It then took 15 minutes for him to come and refill  drinks the first time even though he circled our table 3 times and 25 minutes the second time
Chips were nothing but crumbs.
Prices are outrageous. $16 for a chimichanga? It was good though. Really good. I don't suggest the Queso on top due to it tasting like grocery store cheese.
Steak Cortez is really good.
The kids really loved there kids combo and taco plates, too.
The Carne Asada burrito was decent not very full of meat. Had to add rice and beans just to get it to be somewhat stuffed. 
The food was good but I'd probably rarely ever come here.

First the good news about this place: Burger was cooked perfectly and fries were crispy and delicious. Great service, although I could do without the dog roaming the dining room. 

Now the bad: They charge you $1 for cheese and $1 for onions, fried or raw. Even though I found this a bit pricey for onions, I ordered the fried. I got a slab of fried onions that was as thick as the burger itself. I don't think anyone needs this many onions. Please, charge me .50 and give me half as many next time. Then, there must have been 5 slabs of thick cheese on there which totally over-powered the burger.. Another gripe I had is that pickles were not on the topping menu. Pickles and burgers go together like peanut butter and jelly! Oh and the shakes are a rip off too, at $5 a pop. Pretty pricey for Fishtown. 

I think with a little work this place could become a destination, but for me it is just not there yet.

Not too many places have me running home to write a YELP review, but Sketch did it to me.  I have not had a burger this good since, well, maybe Rouge 10 years ago... and this was better.   Hubby and I both got a Cheeseburger with Pepperjack Cheese which arrived with fresh shredded lettuce and tomato.  The fries are thick hand cut Belgian fries which are delish.  Hubby was so happy he even drew a burger with the complimentary crayons and construction paper supplied at each table...great for kids.   We stuck with the basics this time around but will definitely be back to try the Kobe burger and Turkey Burger and Sweet Potato Fries.  I did try the Green Goddess dressing on the side with my burger and fries which was an explosion of fresh mint & cilantro, again delish.  Totally stuffed but a sucker for a cupcake, I decided to get 2 for the road.  Not expecting much...you can't do great burgers and cupcakes...c'mon!...boy! was I wrong! One bite of this cupcake and I had hubby turning the car around so I could go back and buy 6 more! I am so glad I made the trip today...great burgers...great fries and amazing cupcakes...any one of these babies would have been worth the trip.  Kudos also to the friendly staff.  Looking forward to my next Sketch burger.

Great service, beautiful environment, quieter and not as hectic as the usual sushi lunch special rush in other locations. It is a bit pricier than other spots in the city, but the quality and experience is better too. The pick 3 special gave me a full plate of sushi, sashimi, and 2 handrolls, and soup or salad for $17. Overall great lunch value and a nice calm place in the middle of the city

This place is undeniably tasty. I can give it only two star rating:

Prices. The prices for this joint are far higher than they should be. Especially for add-ons like onions and mushrooms. $1 each? Really? We're on Girard Ave in Fishtown.

Fries. They are thick cut, but bland, even with green chilies.

Shakes. Meh. What was that scene from Pulp Fiction?

"Vincent Vega: Did you just order a five dollar shake?
Mrs. Mia Wallace: Ummhh.
Vincent Vega: That's a shake . . . that's milk and ice cream.
Mrs. Mia Wallace: Last I heard.
Vincent Vega: That's five dollars? You don't put bourbon in it or nothin'?
Buddy Holly: No.
Vincent Vega: Just checking."

I don't know if it was worth five dollars. It was alright, though.

And as much as I love animals, I am pretty certain that it's some health code violation to allow your pooches to just hang out in the restaurant with you, whether you own the restaurant or not.

Overall, meh. The vegan burger was good, just a little too salty. 

If you're looking for a vegan burger joint, this is your place. I don't think I'll be returning, though.

his place blew me away. The burgers are nothing like I've ever had; it was perfectly prepared. We had an order of the fries and the BBQ pork sandwich, which were also very well balanced dishes. Anyone who takes food seriously should be visiting this place.
Food is really good. Prices are decent. The best part, they offer military discount. Tuna Mac is a must try.

WHAT HAPPENED TO MACAYOS?????

although Yelp said it's my first time being at Macayos, I've been eating here since  forever.
They no longer have a  lunch menu. The menu has really scales down. 
On a positive note, I still love their chips and salsa...I can just eat that as my meal.
PRO:  they do offer military discount! .

However today, when I showed the server  my military ID and he thanked me for my service. I didn't realize that he did not take the discount off after I paid. 

I would still go for HH

I wasn't really expecting to get good sushi in Philly, but damn.  This place was good.  I got the sashimi dinner, which was a little pricey, at $25 for 18 pieces of sashimi.  But every little bit was fantastic.  There were four pieces of mackerel (which I usually dislike due to its excessive fishiness - I know, I know, how can sushi NOT be fishy? -  but was pleasantly surprised at the quality of these slices), five large slices of good quality tuna, three slices of salmon, four big slices of octopus, three slices of hamachi, and two slices of toro.  I was in heaven. And I just did the math, and that was way more than 18 pieces.

I love you Shiroi Hana!

This place is pretty authentic Mexican. The food is delish, the decor is lousy, soccer on the tv, attentive waiters... come on, you gotta love this place! I brought my husband here after he had been saying for forever that he was craving real Mexican food. (He's so used to eating from taco trucks in L.A.) This hit the spot for him and we've been back lots of times since.

They have a bread mixer and it says the bread is homemade, also says they have home
Made gluten free (Bona Dea) bread.  They also have Roman Wraps, big deli pickles. Butternut squash soup. was sweet (but cold - maybe it was supposed to be?).  Kids subs were good ( we had ham and cheese and pizza ) the come with drink and chips ( or pickle or potato salad).  The Green Turkey sub was good.

Wow, this place has gone downhill since my last visit. I should have known something was off when we walked in for lunch (7/5/18) and it didn't smell very good. A restaurant that doesn't smell good is a bad sign. Another bad sign, half of the menu was blacked out. I had planned to order wings but when I asked they said they were no longer selling them. I ordered the pork rib plate and it was a super small portion of super small ribs. The women's restroom didn't seem to be air conditioned and it really smelled dirty, the trash was overflowing. All of this made for a pretty unpleasant lunch. Next time I will go somewhere else.

Used to live in Tucson and loved Macayos.  Have been back twice on visits to the city and have been disappointed both times.   Most recent was this past Thurs, party of 4 and none of our meals of the standard we used to expect. Most tasted as if the meat had gone off.  Will not be back.

My lady friend and I went for dinner at this CASH ONLY establishment at around 5:30 before attending a comedy show.  I heard that this place was pretty awesome and you could draw at the table.  Well, I'm sold.  Sounded like a cute date spot.

The ambiance leaves much to be desired (only reason aside from being cash only for the 4 stars).  Sketch is located in a transitioning neighborhood.  It felt very hipstery, but the food was first class.  Definitely blew me away.  I highly recommend the spicy lamb burger special, if available, and the Kobe burger.  Amazingnessity.  Tasted the turkey burger and was surprised at how meaty it was.

A special note: doneness.  I ordered my burger medium.  It came in a little rare.  Another gent complained about the doneness also.  With that said, I recommend ordering your burger one level more done than you normally would to ensure doneness.  So instead of medium, I'd get a medium well.  See how that turns out.

Other than that, prepare to be amazed.
A great romantic location for a date with my gf. Delicious, fresh sushi ; good service & atmosphere.

Amazing! I love sketch... we eat there at least once a month. Totally addicted to the Dr. Pepper pulled pork sandwich and green chili cheese fries. The baked goods are out of this world too.... the coconut macaroons will change your life....

The best burger Ive had, and Ive had a lot ( A few places in Paris came close). The Kobe truffle burger is amazing! So tender and flavorful. The fries are good as well and come with the option of multiple different sauces. Ive gotten a few out of town friends hooked on this place and they bring it up whenever we talk. I would never have found this place if I hadnt moved to Nolib. Prefer not to eat in the tiny spot though, little ambiance, but great food.

HANDS DOWN  the best burger I've ever had in my life. Even when I reheated half my leftover burger in the nuker the next morning it was one of the best. I got a simple plain burger with horsradish cheddar cheese, lettuce and tomato.

My roommate found this place by smell while he was out jogging one morning, and demanded we go here for lunch. I'm so thankful he insisted on how great this place smelled! We split some fries - the sauces are as amazing as the burgers, btw. We tried the chipotle, wasabi, and garlic and loved them all.

We also loved looking at all the drawings on the walls. There are some really good and really funny ones.

I had dinner in this place. I ordered Veggie Teriyaki, Udon noodle and avocado rolls, all of which were presented well. The Udon soup is so great, I had a lot since it is so warm. Staff are nice and considerate in this place. I'll definitely go back to this place when I'm around.
This place is the truth. Burgers are juicy and buns are sweet and toasted, the pulled pork is delicious and I recommend subbing bbq sauce on the sammy. Also the the fries the fries are amazing

Sketch burger is everything if you're trying to stuff your face with a tasty burger. I've only had their veggie burgers, but hot damn,  are they good. Love the add on options and their expansive soda selections. If you come here, don't forget to grab a cookie too. Best cookie I've ever had.

Came with four friends, two of whom are vegetarian. We were all very impressed. I had the veggie burger with harissa, and it certainly ranks up there on my lifetime list of best meatless patties. (If I really think about it, probably the closest competitor would be the Czech veggie burger at Korzo Haus in Alphabet City). By way of description, hyperbole tends to get at the truth: "the sheer number of elemental flavors combined in their burgers trumps human comprehension!" 

Also I liked that this was a very informal establishment with no frills - and no huge crowds, either. Just a place to sit and enjoy an imaginatively concocted burger.

Really disappointed they don't have vegan ice cream anymore... They had such great vegan milkshakes! Went in there looking- and they "no longer have that"...:( boo...giving two because at least they still have one vegan thing...right?:/

The best place in Fishtown - and has been since long before the neighborhood became cool. You can get any kind of burger with any kind of toppings and sauces that you can dream of. Plus the milkshakes and baked goods (including lots of vegan options!) are to die for.

The place is small and super casual. People are always absurdly friendly. Plus you get paper and crayons to create your own masterpiece which you can hang on the walls. Pictures that I put up years ago are still there. It makes it feel like the lovely neighborhood establishment that it really is.

So the first time I came here it kinda sucked...the server was less than attentive and took forever to come over and seemed totally irritated when you asked her for anything. However, my bro is a big fan of this place so I gave it a 2nd shot and it was great! The owner was there the 2nd time. She had the best personality! 
The place is super cute inside and the food kicks ass...so as long as you dont mind tossing the coin to see if you get the awesome owner or her bad attitude server, I would def recommend going here.

This place has awesome burgers, great fries, and the selection of sauces is really great. As mentioned already, the harissa aioli is awesome and my burger was perfectly cooked at a lunch rush hour.

 My only complaint would be the price. My two co workers and I ordered lunch and it was more than 3 dollars for 3 cheese burgers and fries.
The style is closer to what I've known growing up in Southeastern Arizona and Southwestern New Mexico.  Great enchilada sauce, good value.
Best burgers around yes they are! great fries tioo,the vegan shake is great its just real pricy to go there

My experience at this store has been so unbelievably positive that one year after my purchase I am still so happy with it, and with their continued customer care, that I had to write a review. I bought the vac at the Dresher location. The gentlemen who helped me was so knowledgable and no nonsense. He sold me a Simplicity, and it's been a dream. I have two dogs, hardwood floors and tons of rugs. It gets All. The. Hair. Period. On top of that I thought I broke it at one point so I took it in to the Andorra location and the guy informed me that it was just a clog and unclogged it for me. Then he referred to my vac model as a "bear of a machine" and said never in his career has he seen one of these things die. Meanwhile there were like 30 Dysons there waiting for repair work... Then I got a postcard wishing my vac a happy birthday and a free tune up! I love them. They have inspired me to seek out independently owned business like this for my household furniture and appliance needs. Regarding the one star reviews, I have a feeling their no nonsense attitudes can rub people the wrong way. They are just seasoned experts in their field and they probably get sick of people's BS and their propensity to shop at big box stores over theirs.

I've been to Japan a few times, for long enough to have unreasonable expectations from Japanese food restaurants and be super conceited about it so everyone hates me.

But Shiroi Hana is really a shining example of what an American Japanese food restaurant should be.  There were enough hints of authenticity to please me.  The flavors are strong, the fish is fresh, the miso was delicious.  I walked away satisfied, not longing for Tokyo fare (any more than usual).  And the $9 house sake really, really messed me up.

I've eaten take-out from here as well, and made the mistake of ordering the "Special" rolls -- it's a personal thing, but I can't stand sushi pieces that ridiculously large.  So I stick to the basics.  The nigiri pieces are almost too generous with the fish-to-rice ratio, but I've still been able to eat them in one bite (as opposed to the awkward "Sushi debris all over your plate and table and face" results from the supersized rolls).  Very good stuff.

Oh my vegan black bean burger.  That thing was huge!  Seriously, the biggest veggie burger I have ever seen.  I had mine with mushrooms and fried onions.  Delish!  They also have vegan cheese, 2 different seitan options and vegan desserts.  Thank you, Sketch!!

Hubby had the kobe burger and said it was awesome!

I've seriously never had a bad dish from this place!  Their maki rolls are delicious and they offer a great variety of sushi and shashimi.  The Rolls Royce Roll is one of my favs, as is the shrimp shumai!

I'm a sushi fanatic, and so is my bf (thank the LORD!), and our favorite thing to do on a weekend night is order in sushi and watch a Flyers game (if there's one on - otherwise, movie night!!). We had somehow overlooked Shiroi Hana amongst all the ones in our neighborhood, so we decided to try a new place for fun.

They don't have a massive list like some places, but there is a fairly decent amount of roll choices, mostly the usual suspects of course. I called, ordered (one of the few sushi places open on a Sunday night - phew!), and 20 minutes later zipped over to pick up our order. The interior is surprisingly nice and tasteful (surprising because I rarely expect it), and pretty full considering it was a Sunday. I'm a sucker for interesting sounding special rolls and ended up ordering:

Island Roll (Crunchy spicy salmon roll inside w/ fresh mango, salmon and wasabi tobiko on top): I enjoyed this roll - hey, anything with mango is awesome, Gotta love those omega-3's too.

Passion Roll (White tuna, scallion, ginger, tempura flakes, shiso flakes and jalapeno spicy mayo): this one was weird. Seriously. And I know that the culprits were the ginger and shiso flakes. I need to remember: DO NOT ORDER SUSHI THAT HAS GINGER AS PART OF THE ROLL. There's a reason why its served pickled on the side. And the shiso flake addition just made things even more confusing. If they took those two elements out this could be a tasty roll. But it wasn't.

Unakyu Roll (Eel, cucumber, sesame seeds): Good, but a hard roll to f-up. Clearly they're good with the basics, and the fish is fresh so they must really make those standard rolls shine.

Spicy Scallop Roll (Cooked scallop, spicy mayo, scallions): I'm of the opinion that scallop sushi should always be raw; if you offer it cooked, its probably not going to be all that great and this was one of those ugh rolls. It just....wasn't mouth-wateringly silky smooth good. Their spicy sauce has a real kick to it (possibly to cover things up though) and was definitely trying to take over.

I'll have to just try out the standard rolls before making a final decision, but it was a little bit of a disappointing first experience. There were so many good reviews of this place I had some high hopes (always nice to find additional awesome sushi places), but this just kinda fell short.
This place used to have 4 stars for me but now they don't have vegan ice cream for milkshakes. The fries were overcooked and it is always cold in here.
Had few rolls and they were average. The fish was fresh, but the rolls seem to be lacking of flavors. A bit pricy too

I'm usually praising this place but we decided to try the dos diablos enchiladas today.  First bite into the pork enchilada was a chunk of fat.  Third bite into it another big chunk of fat.  Yeah I know there is fat in pork but having large chunks makes me want to puke.  Tried the red chili meat about half way through found fat.  Wife's plate was the same way.  We filed a salsa container 3/4 of the way with the fat from the enchiladas.  Showed the server she took it to what I'm guessing is the assistant manager. He came by apologized and said that's typical with pork.  So will think twice before coming here again.  Seems the quality of food is going down year after year.  They need to bring back the manager that was here for years. He ran a tight restaurant with fewer purple and quality food.

Whenever I travel to Philly I stock up on Martin's sausages. They have a huge variety of meats and fillers. They make great meals, Italian, Mexican, Polish any style of cooking they are great!!! I wish they shipped. I'm on my last pack, so sad.

3.5 stars

The fish is fresh, the chirashi was quite good and the ambiance is really nice / quiet, but I didn't find it particularly special or a must-visit the next time we're craving sushi. Good spot for a date night or smaller group dinner (4 max).

It does not get much better than Sketch. We went to Sketch for the first time the other day and had a few burgers, some green chili cheese fries and the Korean wings. Hands down, the best burger I have had in Philly. Moist, cooked to request, great toppings but the best part is that this place is BYOB!!
Fine food, but for some reason my Salmon and the meal in general was very oily.. maybe that is how it was supposed it be, but very delicious indeed.

Excellent location in old city.  Rather than the $40 valet at the Monaco, I parked here overnight for $25. Saved me a few bucks!  It's literally right around the corner from the hotel. 

Steep ramps, tight parking, but definitely doable.  (have a pretty long car...)  Attendant very friendly.
The food was fine... Not bad but not remarkable either. There was no music so we heard the entire conversation of the table next to us.  Cute decor.
Close at 9:00 called at 8:29 took the last order for the day what your still open for 31 more min good burger but it's bin going down hill
Great Mexican food and even better Margaritas but sadly they are closing for good on January 15th

My  most regular stop in the Terminal. A few links from here plus some broccoli or green beans from Iovines is a great weekday meal. I always go for chicken sausage to keep it healthier; I've gotten the chicken & apple and the buffalo chicken a million times. The prices are lower than almost anywhere and the staff is so friendly. I cook them covered in a pan with a tiny bit of water to steam through, then cut in half lengthwise and pan fry for a little on both sides to brown it up.

I ordered two burgers from them tonight via uber eats. My food was "being prepared" for two hours. Two hours?! For a burger?! When my order finally arrived I only got one burger and the restaurant closed. The one burger I did get was completely raw on the inside and had a hair in it. So a two hour wait for food I couldn't eat. Absolutely horrible experience. I had eaten in the restaurant once before after hearing rave reviews. I wasn't blown away, if anything it made me depressed that this is considered Philly's best burger. I thought I'd give it another try. I will never eat here again. Completely awful experience
Yummy vegetarian selections-a nice surprise for the Girard avenue burger themed bars. Love coming here with my kid. Definitely fun.

Sketch is a place that one could drive or walk by and think that it's not that special...it is!

Just about every time I go in I'm greeted by the same very friendly (and cute) person. She lets you know that drinks are available in the cooler by the register and to have a look at the menu and specials on the blackboard. I don't stray from the big attraction here...the awesome burger!

My go-to is an all beef burger cooked medium rare with mayo, American cheese, lettuce tomato, onion, jalapeños, and avocado served on a very fresh brioche like bun. The burger is huge...I mean literally...I struggle to get my mouth around it but am oh so happy when I do. Juicy and perfectly cooked I'm glad they have plenty of napkins on the table. 

What's a great burger without fries? Sketch nails this as well. I switch it up between the regular and the sweet potato fries...when I'm feeling really decadent I get the cheese fries (awesome).

If for some reason you have a tapeworm and are still hungry, try one of the many baked goods they offer for desert. Come hungry and bring cash. A bank's ATM is next door if needed.

Yum. Made to order burgers. I had the smashed onion burger and it was delish, as were the hand cut fries with wasabi mayo and horseradish sauce. Washed it down with a Boylan's diet root beer. Awesome restaurant. Easy to get to. Loved the fact that you can sketch at the table (materials at your fingertips) and they will hang it up, if you wish. Will definitely go back.

This may be it. We had our anniversary dinner here, two year anniversary on moving to Philly!

We had the sushi lover and the sashimi deluxe. both were very good. Fish was fresh, and well presented. Only complaint is that the wasabe is not very strong. Other than that I have no complaint. 

Waiter was attentive and helpful. Deco is nice and clean.
Delicious food, great service! The margaritas were delicious and the atmosphere was very festive! Thumbs up!!!

There isn't much I can add that hasn't been said about this cute little hipster burger bodega. The one thing I can tell you that I hadn't seen in reviews, there are actually (2) 400 blocks of Girard Street East & West. I did not know this and we were over on WEST Girard; this place is on EAST Girard. Googlemap it of course, had I done that I would have transported us here in one fell swoop, instead of ASSuming that 4th & Girard means the 4th & Girard you know. HA! ... Before you say, DUH, you should know that most blocks in Philly arent like this, FYI!

So now about the food: this is DEF a MAN's burger place! IMy dad & fincy both love love LOVED it. My fincy who is not from Philly was actually like, "this is the burger place I have been seeking when I say I want a burger!" ........ So if it's a  big fat honkin' burger you seek, Sketch is for you. The burgers were actually too big for me--and a little on the greasy side--which I think is from butter added to the meat(?) BUT it was my papa's birthday and he (and the fincy) were both beaming so I was happy :)

I didn't find it overly expensive like many other reviews said. It was $52 for the 4 of us: 4 burgers done up righteously; an of large sweet potato fries and lan order of large regular fries for the table; and 4 drinks. 

Loved the waitress/cashier; she was very upbeat and def added to fun factor. Worth a go to see if it is your burger utopia.
Fun place great food. Had the cyclops and wasabi fries. Be warned that the fermented lemonade is VERY fermented.
NOONE IS BETTER THEN TRAM! This salon is very comfortable and clean and the workers are friendly. I never left the salon unsatisfied. I always look forward to my next visit with Tram

Food is solid but absolutely TERRIBLE service. They made us wait over an hour and served multiple tables before us. They then promised the food was still coming out just to say "oh we thought you didn't want to eat now". WTF?

I had Chirashi, and it was amazing. Granted, it was not too cheap ($29), but worth the money. Fish was fresh and nicely prepared. The atmosphere was also very good and the lady who served us was friendly. I would definitely go back there.
Always good food, great selection of pizzas for the $6 lunch special. Sausage and pepperoni always a favorite.

Saw this mentioned on Philly's top food critic's IG account so decided to give it a try. This is a small place but has a very fun atmosphere and welcoming staff. The walls are covered in burger-themed artistic renderings that previous patrons have left and provide great entertainment. The real stand-out is the food.  The burgers are huge and totally customizable. We had the truffle mushroom burger and the smashed onion burger with green goddess sauce. All of the options are great and the price is very reasonable. The burgers were cooked perfectly and the green goddess sauce was herbaceous and well spiced. My only recommendation for the burgers was they needed a bit more salt. The fries are also good and a small is certainly enough for 2 people to share. Overall, this was a fun and casual burger spot...just FYI, it's cash only.

Oh Sketch, you're so trendy and so hyped. I secretly kind of wanted to hate you.

The truth is, I didn't. Actually, I loved everything about Sketch. I loved the crayons and construction paper at the tables. I mean, come on guys, that didn't take you back to the good 'ol days when your parents would take you to Friendly's and shove crayons in your face so they could have 5 minutes of uninterrupted adult conversation? AND you get to have your drawing hung up on the wall? Super cool.

Anyway, the food. WOW. I had the smashed onion burger with pepper jack cheese, bacon and green goddess sauce. It was so surprisingly awesome. The burger was noticeably well seasoned. I like salt on my food. I don't like bland things. This was perfect, and by perfect I mean only a few extra shakes shy of being oversalted. Flavor is your friend, people! The green goddess sauce was the best I'd had, really fresh and bright. The smashed onions on the bottom were awesome. Some were caramelized and some still had a little crunch. It was a great contrast of flavors and textures and it really added to the overall enjoyment of this burger.

I like my burger medium rare but not raw, so I followed some of the advice from other reviews and ordered my burger medium. It was cooked perfectly, bright pink and juicy. Not only was this a huge burger, but it was quite messy. Luckily, there are already napkins on the table so we didn't have to worry about asking for any extras. 

I also had the fries with the harissa aioli for dipping. I am going to run out to the store right now and buy some harissa so I can make that aioli at home and dip everything in it from now on. Yeah, it was that good. I also tried Hubby's shake and it was pretty tasty. 

The service was quick and attentive and our server was friendly. Everything was prompt but she was not overbearing. Sketch was so delicious that I'm not even ashamed to love something that's so painfully trendy. Hopefully this was just the beginning of a long, meaty love affair.

Wow, I can't believe anyone dislikes this place.  The neighborhood stinks, the restaurant is closed on random days, the hipster crowd is blasé...

But the burger--the burger is AWESOME.  Order a Kobe burger medium rare and add harissa aioli and you'll be set.  The fries are perfect too.  In between steak fries and shoestring fries in size, they come out perfectly cooked and tasty.  I can't speak for the shake (yet), but I'll think about it for the next time.

Gotta love a good sushi place. The Vegetarian roll is to die for. Whenever I go to a new sushi place, I always try the Spider roll. Shiroi Hana makes an amazing spider roll; very flavorful and a little warm... perfect.

I have been here twice to try out the burgers.  They are absolutely delicious.  The meat is an extremely fresh patty that is cooked very well.  In my opinion, the best sauce topping is the garlic aioli.  The fries are very fresh as well.  It is nice that they usually come out in the beginning so you can munch on them before your burger arrives.

While you are waiting, they have a bunch of construction paper / markers / crayons for you to draw some artwork.  There are some really original and creative artists that make burger art.

Service is pretty good.  They are friendly and helpful.  The seating area is rather small, so if you go during lunch / dinner rushes, you may be waiting for a table to open up.

Since my new boss is from Japan I have become an official sushi snob!
One major issue is they use toooooooo much rice, thats not the real way.  Need more fish less rice.  I have to say though, the fish itself was fresh which is good.  It was a bit pricey for the size of the rolls though.  I got a rainbow roll that looked like it hadn't fully matured yet! I think i devoured it in 2 gulps.  The sushimi salad is great lots of fresh pieces of fish in there which made up for the rainbow row.  But over all for that and tea I spent a total of 35 bucks for lunch! not worth it for the small portions and the amount of rice they fill you up on.

If your just looking for a place for a quick bit while walking around stop in, but if you are looking for some serious sushi go to BLUEFIN!

******IM SHAMELESS******
Bluefin
1017 Germantown Pike
Plymouth Meeting, PA 19462
Phone: (610) 277-3917 
Price: $ Hours: Mon-Thu 11:30am-2pm-5:30pm-10pm, Fri 11:30am-2pm, 5:30pm -11pm, Sat 5:30pm -11pm

Delicious!! Had the seitan special and it was amazing. The fries were fresh and savory with a yummy dipping sauce. If you are feeling artistic while waiting there are crayons and paper for you to add your artistic vision to their wall.

Best burgers around.  Utterly amazing.

I order the burger with wasabi sauce and horseraddish cheddar cheese every time I'm there.  It's the perfect combo and just soooooooo good.  

I honestly don't order burgers out anywhere else because it's just not worth it.  

I have had the Dr. Pepper Pulled Pork once and it was amazing... but I can't help but to go back to the burger every time I'm there.  

The Green Chili Cheese Fries are also really good (and big enough to share with a group of 4.)  

Milkshakes are outstanding.  

I can't say enough good things about this place.

I know it's a chain but I judge a Mexican food place in large part by their salsa and chips.  We went on the recommendation of a friend.  We still like her but, Sorry folks, this place was a bust.  The food was very average....much better Mexican restaurants in Tucson.  Skip it and go to Molinitos, Blanco or el Charro to name a few.

First timer this afternoon. Ordered cheeseburger medium with wasabi mayo and a small fries with wasabi mayo dipping sauce. No sauce for either burger or fries, burger was under cooked and worst of all... no top bun! WTF! I'm not paying $10.75 for half a burger.
This is my favorite sushi restaurant in Philadelphia. They have the best spicy crunchy tuna roll.

I lived in Hawaii for 7 years and have a serious soft spot for plate lunch and spam musabi and you can't beat this one!! I had the kalua pork and my husband had the chicken. Don't miss out on the Mac salad! It's the best!!!
Good quality meats and sausages at a reasonable price.  They have quite a large selection of sausages, usually about 20-30 different types.

oh. em. gee.  sketch burgers are so enormous.  you look at it and think i can NEVER eat all that.  and the order of cheese fries is so delicious and flavorful (not your regular frozen fries, these are thick like steak frites). 
then you look down at your plate and the burger and fries are gone. maybe you unbutton your pants too, you heifer. 
i would definitely come back here on a weeknight, because we had to get takeout,  since the entire restaurant (note: 5 tables) was full.  it was probably better that way, so that no one had to see the savage beasts we became as we polished off those burgers.

My family use to order from the Westshore pizza location on Lambright 2 times a week, Until today. I will NEVER order form here again.

On Saturday we had a couple friends over and placed an order for 12 wings and a Pepperoni pizza. I placed it at 7:30pm.

9:15 came and I called to check on my order. They told me it was "out for delivery" 

(I only live 3 miles away)

9:45- Still nothing. I call. Was told it was "out for delivery"

15 minutes go by and finally the food arrives. 10pm

I pay and go inside, we are all starving. I open the box and the food is ICE COLD. Both the pizza and wings are completely cold. Like they had been sitting for HOURS.

I call the location thinking since we order all the time that they will take care of this since we are loyal customers. 

I was told since I had a "bite" of the pizza there was nothing they could do. Finally they offered to remake our food and deliver it. At this point its almost 10:15. We were all starving and didn't want to eat dinner at midnight. I asked her if we could just get a credit on our account for our next order. First she said no and then she said "no problem" that she would "add a note" to the account. I asked for her name and she said "Jessica"

Flash forward to today: we call to place a replacement order. What a surprise. No note. So they said there was nothing they can do. No compassion or trying to make a wrong situation right, they were just cold (kind of like my food was)

I call back to speak to the manager "Debbie" and she straight up calls me a liar and says she "looked at the time stamps" The convo ended by me telling her I would make sure everyone knows how they do business and her hanging up on me.

VERY VERY VERY RUDE people here. Seriously awful. I cannot believe this is how businesses treat their LOYAL customers these days.

White pizza okay. Cheese pizza ordered w pepperoni, had no pepperoni . When I called and explained pepperoni was missing, she said to bring it back so they could see there's no pepperoni . 
Why would I lie about pepperoni ?! 
I told her no, I would not drive all the way back in 6 o clock traffic, she pretty much said oh well too bad. No other help or suggestion, other than show us the pizza. 

Acting as if I were making up a story made me angrier than no pepperoni . 
There are way too many pizza places out for way less money!!, to have crappy customer service skills!!

Turkey burger with Avacado and Chipotle!
Dr. Pepper-marinated pulled pork!
Cheeseburger with sauteed onions!

These heavenly meat dishes will not disappoint - they are huge and filling!  Our leftovers kept us fed for the rest of the week.  And based on the Decor, you might think this joint was plucked straight out of NYC's East Village.

Definitely a cool spot.

Note: In my last review I gave this place a hard time on account of their prices, but after a couple more tries I can say without reservation - it's worth it.

Maybe one of the most solid burger joints in the city. Unpretentious good eats with a chill atmosphere. The ladies who work this place are genuinely good-natured and possibly more excited about the burger you're about to eat than you are. Took a date here -- she had the truffle butter burger, I went with the smashed onion. As other reviewers have mentioned, the green chili cheese fries are a must. Those fries are so crispy, they masterfully stood up against the cheesy spicy goodness. WMGK was playing over the radio. Something is totally perfect about hearing Led Zeppelin as you're consuming burgers amid a backdrop of hand-drawn art.

My only complaint: wish they'd expand the soda choices and include Pennsylvania Dutch Birch Beer. Will definitely return.

Best shoe repair in town!  Prices are very reasonable.  Lee has repaired heels and soles on my shoes for years.  I trust him with high end Italian made shoes.  He also does shoe shines and shoe repairs.    I've tried others and they are either too expensive or just poor workmanship.  You gave to give him a shot!

Time crunched and needing a jumbo mortgage... Tom V. handled everything in a perfectly orderly, predictable and quality manner. I also could not realistically find a better rate. I am a happy customer, pleasantly surprised by the lack of glitches, and easily recommend Tom at iMortgage.

The directions are wrong, so watch that close.  It is still worth going.  The beef ribs are excellent and so was the teriyaki chicken.  The employees were extremely friendly and the place was clean.  You can't ask for anything else.

I come to sketch every Saturday with brother and it is one of my go-to burger places. The staff is extremely friendly, to the point where they know my order by heart (because I'm in so often!!) the burgers are super juicy and delicious. The restaurant has a pretty cool atmosphere, very hipster because of the amazing drawings on the walls. Hence the name, SKETCH burger. You're provided with crayons and markers and paper to draw while you wait for your food. Kids aren't the only ones who are able to express their artistic ability. Definitely check out this burger joint!! The truffle butter burger is TO DIE FOR! And you haven't tried the cyclops burger..you're missing out. Beef with bacon, egg, and cheese? Yum!!

Sketch is a down-to-earth burger joint that delivers a casual and laid-back experience. Sure the ambiance may not be filled with over the top fancy decor. But hell, it's an experience that's reminiscences of growing up -- where you're reminded that all you need is a sheet of paper and a box of crayons.

The food is definitely a good bang for the buck. The variety of choices are solid. The staff is cool and genuine. And the whole place just sit's well in my stomach and worth a sketch. I mean shot.

A nice Japanese restaurant with sushi bar that seemed a bit empty even for a weekday night. I came with a large group upon a friend's recommendation.

The service was relatively quick for our size and different orders. I ordered a Rainbow Roll. Although they serve "American style" rolls, the focus still remains on the fish. I asked to replace the imitation crab in my roll with snow crab, and they were happy to do so at an extra cost.

While I have no particular complaints except that the rolls seem smaller than average (or maybe I was just really hungry), there was no wow factor. 3 stars.

Monster burgers, super juicy and always cooked perfect. Harissa aioli is awesome. 
Great for eat in, but usually get it to go. 

Thick shakes and thick cut fries- cooked to order. 

Hard to drive thru Fishtown without considering a stop. 

Beats PYT and 500 degrees in my opinion on service and quality.
Hair in my sushi!!!!  My sushi rolls which were avocado rolls had pieces of hair in them. So disgusting. I wouldn't eat here as I question their cleanliness.

I feel like I could write the same review here as I did for Sumo Sushi. They're both sushi places in the same area, and I feel as though they are interchangeable. Both have pretty good sushi, relative to the area, and are slightly higher priced than comparable area restaurants. I happened to be walking by Shiroi instead of Sumo, so I popped in here for takeout. They had quick service and a comfortable waiting area, which bodes well if you'd want to dine in, but I was heading home after an evening meeting. I stuck to my traditional sushi order (think something along the lines of spicy tuna, alaska, california, etc) and it was all pretty good.

Like Sumo, both places are a better deal for lunch than dinner. More specials!

No. i don't know what to say other than, no. My girlfriend and I once traveled 8,000 miles coast to coast eating just about anything, so perhaps our experience at Sketch was incidental. That notwithstanding, they do not not live up to the HYPE.

I'm sorry to have to use case like a douche-bag, but this is a serious problem with small entrepreneurial endeavors in the fishtown/kensington region; cult of personality! For you see, Northern Liberties got over itself and grew up, a couple years ago. Agreeing to allow only pricey, yet established restauranteurs the privilege of serving the public, and the ability to charge prices that are necessary to keeping in line with better-than-average health and service quality.

Full disclosure: I've been dish washing cooking, serving and managing  since I was 16, all over the country. And I'm not into making grand determinations based on one lousy encounter but I will say this, what was served to me as a mid-rare burger DOES NOT reflect the kind of food I want to find at an establishment which receives above-average ratings!
 We could not finish it. We we're not asked about the 3/4 of a burger which was left glaring on the plate, but received a bill. This after an eight minute wait, form the outset! 

SOMEONE is content with resting on their laurels.

oh and the fries were room temp & guess what, the special-fancy sauce 
is ranch mixed with ____. ..or ancho or mayo or vegano....

Their tarts are good. However, the service is substandard. The older lady  who was working behind the counter appeared very unfriendly and almost as if she didn't want to be there in first place. I am hesitate to go back there again.

The food was pretty good but what pushed it to a 4 was the service. Our server, Aaron, was fantastic. He was one of the better ones we have had in a long time. Defiantly ask for his section.

Give them a try.
The Cyclops is the best! If you want to go out for a burger and milkshake, this is the place! Everything about it is great. Great deserts and home made cookies.

Delicious as always!! So glad they have a permanent location! Katsu Chicken , bang bang shrimp and chicken terayki was perfect as always! Unfortunately they were out of spam, so guess we will be back later this week so the MIL can get some :)

Best burger I ever had...stopped there on my way to Flyers Stanley Cup game with my son...I had the truffle butter burger...I've been dreaming about it since...I think I've eaten in every high end restaurant in the city and this is the best thing I've ever eaten

On Father's Day, my family and I were looking for a nice sushi restaurant that has quiet and spacious ambience. I remembered that I had a wonderful experience with my friend who took me there last time, so I took my family there. 

The service was very good. The waitress was very attentitive and cordial. They give hot towels to clean the hands!

We ordered hardcore sushi plate, crazy roll, Japanese steak, and individual sushi (mackerel, squid, fluke). They were all delicious.  The rice was perfectly seasoned and the steak sauce was not to sweet or salty.

I highly recommend the place and will return.

My boyfriend and I ate just shortly before meeting up with our friends here for dinner and decided to order 1 burger to share. Good thing we did because these burgers are HUGE! Make sure you come here on an empty stomach and be prepared to fall into a deep food coma afterwards!

We got the American Kobe cheeseburger with bbq sauce, simple but still delicious. I got a bite of my friend's truffle burger which was amazing! The fries were pretty good, esp with the aioli dipping sauce.  Definitely coming back!

The service wasn't great, but it also wasn't bad. Just not very welcoming or friendly and I felt hurried despite them being pretty empty. 

BUT the food was amaaaaaaazing...hence the 5 stars. I got the truffle burger (medium) with bacon and a fried egg with fries and some delicious sauce. Really just too good for words. It was a lot to finish but I didn't let that stop me. I'm looking forward to coming back to Philly just for this burger. Under $20 for the meal including a bottled soda.

***Update*** Being the glutton that I am, I went back the next day (today) and had a far different experience. The service was about the same but this time my order was messed up because of waitress error and the food didn't taste the same at all. Except the fries. Those were perfect again. In any case I'm not nearly as happy about the food this time around as I was before. Wouldn't go out of my way to come back.

Sketch definitely makes my top 5 favorite burger list in Philly. The vibe is what you'd expect from a burger joint in Fishtown: small and casual/laid back scene. The menu provides a bunch of topping combinations, but everything is customizable. The stars in my book are anything on the kobe burger, or doused with truffle oil. Careful when adding your own toppings though, as this can quickly rack up the bill. Fries are also served separately, but large enough for sharing and served with (homemade?) sauces. The food isn't the fastest, but not to worry, just grab a crayon and sketch away! But once you do get your food, all worries will melt away. Every sandwich I've had has been extremely flavorful, not to mention ooey gooey deliciousness. And if you've managed to save room for dessert, Sketch has awesome ice cream flavors and milkshakes, including vegan options. 

If you haven't been to Sketch yet, what are you waiting for?!
Def make a good burger, that I cannot complain about. The staff is ok although the woman who took my order seemed to be in a rush and was rather rude.

they use these weird puffy, kind of greasy buns that taste amazing, and overall the burger was really really good. it was a little more expensive than it should have been (especially with the whole "tip your server" thing that was mentioned in another review), but i enjoyed it. maybe they should include fries for that price. i didn't try the fries, but i was full after that burger without them.

one of my favorite parts is that they have crayons and paper, so i enjoyed doodling while i was waiting for my food. the walls are sort of like your parents' refrigerator, so a bunch of the drawings get posted. it's neat.

Am I the only one who doesn't like the idea of a dog roaming the kitchen area of restaurant?  I am not sure if it belonged to one of the proprietors or was just a visiting dog, but I guess at least it was a short-hair dog.  If it had really bothered me, I would not have eaten.  If the food had been great, I probably would not even mention the dog.
