Anyhow, I went with some friends to grab a burger.  My friend had heard this place was good.  We walked in and were directed to the rear to give our orders.  I got the burger with chipotle sauce and bleu cheese, on the recommendation of the cashier.  We also got some chili cheese fries.  

The burger was good, but it was not great.  I have had bleu cheese burgers before, and this one tasted much too salty.  I am assuming this was due to the specific cheese used; and, yes, I know bleu cheese is always salty, but this particular brand overpowered the burger.  Also, there was very little chipotle sauce on the burger.  I certainly do not want it overly slathered with the stuff, but at least put enough so that every bite gets the taste of chipotle.  The chili cheese fries were pretty good, so no complaint on those.  The staff as friendly and helpful, and they may have just had an off day, but I thought their food could have been much better.  There are places that do the burgers much better.

Not your average burger joint.  This place can do a hell of a lot between a bun.  Beef, chicken, pulled pork, turkey, kobe beef, lamb, vegan, there is literally something for everyone here.  Lots of topping options and even more sauce options.  The combinations are nearly endless.  I did the standard beef burger, but added truffle butter, bacon, grilled onions and some aoli.  The burger was enormous and incredibly moist.  I probably didn't need the aoli with all the flavor the bacon, onions, and truffle butter packed, but it certainly didn't hurt anything.  Friends got the lamb and turkey burgers and loved those as well.  Burger prices are decent, but when you start adding toppings the prices go up quick.

The star here, surprisingly, isn't even the burger somehow, it's the fries!  Specifically the green chili cheese fries.  Those things were mind blowing.  We ordered a small order of the regular fries with aoli and they were outstanding, but when our server brought over the green chili cheese fries 2 minutes later, we soon forgot about the other fries and went on a feeding frenzy.  We finally had to go back to the regular fries when we finished all of the others and needed something to dip into the green chili and cheese.  So damn good.  Everyone around us was ordering them.  There's no secret, these are a homerun.

Also loved the self-serve homemade dessert bar.  The blonde bombshell was a perfect end to an already memorable meal.  They can definitely be shared too.

Definitely the funky feel you'd expect in Fishtown.  Sketch will not disappoint if you're looking for some heart-warming American grub with a little twist and not looking to spend a ton of money.

My wife and I have loved Shiroi Hana for years.  We were regulars for a few years, but moved away for a little while.  When we came back to Phila, it was like seeing an old friend again.  The staff is always friendly, service is always good.  I what sets this place apart for me is the fact that they not only have fresh fish, but they know how to prepare it.  There is nothing more disappointing than when you order Tempura, just for it to have the texture of fried chicken.  Great place to frequent.

Pros:
-quality sushi
-fair price
-intimate by contrast to many crowded/dark/noisy Center City spots

Cons:
-service is slow (on a Saturday at 6 pm, took 45 min to be served sushi)
-be careful that they bill you correctly

The interior is quiet and softly lit. There is a sushi bar and tables to seat groups of 2-4. The tables were a little too close together for my taste, but still better than many other restaurants in the area. If you have a party of 10-15, you can reserve a cool table on the upper level, with cushioned benches set into the ground surrounding a central table--I'd love to try this sometime!

We ordered the Sushi Love ($60), which is 16 pcs assorted nigiri (pieces of fish on rice, two pieces of each fish), one "rock and roll" feat. shrimp tempura, one salmon avocado roll, and one spider roll of fried soft-shell crab (really just 4 large pieces with plenty of extra crab). We liked that the sushi was set up symmetrically, so that we could both sample each fish at the same time, matching one for one-- a synchronized sushi flight! Everything tasted fresh, but our favorite pieces were the tuna, unagi (cooked eel), and fried crab.  It also came with a choice of soup or miso salad, one per person.

However, we had to wait over 45 minutes for our meal, which is surprising, given that sushi generally does not require a large deal of cooking...It seemed like take-out orders were prioritized. Then they rang up the wrong bill, which was fine-- but only because we caught their mistake.

These guys take their burgers seriously. This is my favorite burger place, and I rarely get to go.  Every time I've ordered a medium rare burger, it always comes out perfect. 

The truffle mushroom burger is my go-to, and it is delightful. Juicy, pungent truffle Aroma and taste. If you like truffle, it's a must try.

The hand cut fries are good, and comes with a choice of sauce. I always opt for the spicy aoiila, which is like a mayo based sauce. 

Service can be a bit slow because they are serious about cooking a burger, so expect a wait!  Order ahead for takeout to avoid the line!  In either case, well worth the wait.

These burgers are delicious. Probably one of the best I've had in Philly. Also, the people who work here are really nice, though the waitress we had was perhaps a tad overenthusiastic. Better than apathetic, I suppose. 

And crayons + construction paper? Yes please.
Solid breads and pastries. Their croissants are light and flaky but not too heavy. Their breads have a good crust and flavorful interior. I only wish I lived closer.

Despite having explored other options in the market, Martin's remains my go-to butcher for beef, pork, and sausages. They don't possess the sheer quantity of beef nearby Guinta's does, but in my experience the meat is fresher and, most importantly, cut to your desired size (within reason) upon request. Ditto for the pork, I got a beautiful 7 pound shoulder pared down to a far more manageable 4 pounds without issue or increased cost.

The sausage selection places Martin's on an entirely different level than the other meat purveyors at Reading. The sheer variety is mesmerizing, so look to the specials board to narrow your choices. Something on sale will most likely satisfy your palette. The only variety of sausage I've disliked is the chorizo (not seasoned enough), all the others (particularly the many riffs on Italian pork sausage and spicy lamb merguez) satisfy immensely.

The stand's fresh poultry leaves something to be desired, but there's always Godshall's for that. There's also a substantial selection of decent quality lamb, but I prefer Border Spring's relatively local sourcing and slightly cheaper prices for that meat. If in need of beef, pork, or meat in tube form, look no further than Martin's for helpful service, reasonable pricing, and an appropriately vast selection.

Tom helped me on a very complex refinancing:  I had just moved back to the U.S. after five years in China, and am self-employed, so we had to go through issues like overseas assets (and statements that had to be translated from Chinese to English), a variable income (my income is based primarily on investment returns, and those can fluctuate dramatically from year to year), and a host of other issues.

Still, Tom got things done and I was very pleased with the end results and his customer service.  Tom even uncovered over $2,000 that we were owed from our escrow company because of a mistake they made in charging me for property taxes prior to me closing on my home.

I found Tom through the great Yelp reviews he had, and I'm very happy to add another five-star rating to Tom and iMortgage.

This spot is my all time favorite burger place! You can call in for takeout or they have tables inside. Check out all the artwork on the walls. My favorites and must-haves : cyclops burger (which has bacon and a sunny side egg) and the onion smashed burger! Pretty good sized. Also get fries (kinda weird they serve it in a brown lunch bag but it works ) with the aoli sauce for dipping. Milkshakes are really good too here.

We have always liked Macayo's. We don't get to the "city" very often and we also like trying different restaurants, so it's been a while since we have eaten hear. Service was great, Angela, our waitress very kind. The food service was fairly quick and our meal were also very tasty. BUT since we haven't been here in a while the menu changed and so did se of the way they make and put meals together. That is where we were disappointed. I know things change, se of it was a little much. When I order a green chili burro that's what I expect, not everything but the kitchen sink wrapped in s tortilla. We always enjoy the salsa (hot and mild) and the thin crispy tortilla chips.

Sketch Burger is so delicious! Can be expensive, but worth it in my opinion. Customer drawn burger related sketches line the walls inside-great conversation starters if you're on a date. Cash only, which is a bummer. Only a few outdoor tables (that need some repair/TLC) Something for everyone at this cute burger joint!

I'm unsure, but I'd swear this place changed hands in the last year or so.  I used to love this location, but the service and what they now serve has drastically changed.  I used to enjoy the Baja Chimi, but the meat doesn't have the same flavor, it now tastes like it came out of a can and the rice is crunchy.  The wait staff needs some training for sure, you can go thru your whole meal and they won't refill your glass.  

It's a shame, it used to be good place to go and I used to look forward to dining there.  No longer worth the money.

If you're looking for a chill spot and a good burger, this is your place. The burgers are big and DELICIOUS. cool gimmick- There are paper and markers and crayons at your table to "sketch" pics and the entire inside of the place is plastered with people's sketches. Pretty cool.  But the burgers are delish and the choices of burges and cheeses are unique!

I want to start by saying that I order Westshore Pizza a lot, but from a different location. 

Tonight we ordered to side salads, two meat lasagnes, a chicken part, and a cheese steak deluxe (cheese, shroom, green peppers, and onion).  This order was for delivery.  

The cheese steak was very flavorful.  It was also moist without being a soggy mess.  The lasagna was covered in so much sauce the dish was delivered as a bolognese soup, completely lacking the texture of a well baked dinner.

The salads were mostly onion, gross.

The chicken part was not delivered, so I had to wait another 30 minutes to eat myself.  By then the chicken was dry and the noodles had doubled in size and were soggy.

when i worked in chestnut hill, i would visit metropolitan every so often for their prune danish...it was freaking phenomenal, and large enough to split with someone 

i do remember that they would sell day-old breads at a discount, which comes in handy if you are planning on making french toast or bread pudding

4.5 stars

Burgers so good I'd eat one off the SEPTA rail floor... now that is FUNKY good stuff baby!

Seriously though... 3 second, 5 second, 10 second rule. If this massive juicy burger slipped through my hands mid bite I'd have no problems or regrets picking it right off the floor and shoving it right back into this hypoglycemic mouth. That's how much I enjoy my SKETCH BURGERS!

I'm usually the type of girl who does her burgers with "no bun" but this burger is worth being bad for. Go bun or go home! The bun completes this tasty masterpiece.

- Amazing Truffle Mushroom Butter Burger 
- Crispy Fun Fries that have loads of dip options
- Affordable prices and hearty portions
- Laid back, fun, back to your child hood, doodle your tush off and post it on the fridge for mom vibe

- sadly, not a fan of the mac and cheese...not cheesy enough for me and too much pepper. 

The menu list goes on and on... tons of tasty options and it's just a laid back, simple, paper plate and plastic fork spot

I went on a Thursday afternoon....right when it opened. The burger superwoman/cook/host lady was awesome and I'll be making this place my go to dive burger spot.

Go ahead..call me nasty for eating a dirty burger off the ground. I will gladly except that nickname for these burgers. :)

I really wish I could give this place more stars because they make delicious food. The burgers are the perfect size and are clearly hand formed patties. The fries are hot and crispy, and I love that you can get several different sauces. I loved the aioli- it was spicy but not too spicy. If you really love spice, get the hot mustard. However, the service left so much to be desired. There was one waitress for everyone so she was on the run the whole time. I had to go up to the cash register to get more water because I couldn't catch her. I recommend getting everything you need the first time the waitress comes, otherwise you'll be waiting forever.

I read the reviews before I went but know people that have gone and liked this place so against my better judgment we went. VERY dissatisfied and disappointed. We sat out on the patio and enjoyed looking at a table with dirty dishes and it stayed like that he entire time we were there. My husband even make a comment to our waitress who was MIA most of the time and she shrugged it off. There was one other person on the patio. There were 2 tables that were cleared but covered in food and salsa. Ok so back to our waitress. Another server took our drink orders and our food order. Our waitress brought our margarita flights out. I asked which was which and she told me in a very irritated manner almost as if I should have known. She came out once to see how our food was and to collect payment for the check. The man who delivered our food brought our check. Never knew her name because as I said she didn't do anything except deliver drinks and collect the check. Overall the margaritas tasted like watered down drinks. Food wasn't that great and service was atrocious. I will NEVER be back. I only gave it a 1 because that is the lowest score you're able to provide.

this place is two blocks from my favorite intErnational eatery in the city truffle burger was a gem. yeah i know its an acquired taste. the chili cheese fries was a delight but for sharing  to avoid "itis" within minutes and you will appreciate the international graffiti sketches for the love of burgers. the unique flavours will keep me going back for more

Came from Boston MA
All the food was outstanding and the atmosphere for this restaurant was perfect. 
Will come again 
Highly recommended

~BRIDAL DIET CHEAT DAY~

What was worth it:
The fries- piping hot potatoey goodness. 
Harissa aioli- a new classic.
Horseradish cheddar- because duh.

What wasn't:
The bun- I know it's le bus, but it was too big and made the burger hard to eat.
The beef- did not taste high quality and was cooked unevenly.

The service was pleasant. I'll be back to try other menu items after August 29.

I really enjoy sketch burger for its low key, fun atmosphere (byob), and amazing burgers. You can get the kobe beef, regular beef, or a veggie patty with a bunch of different sauces and toppings as options. My friends and I have tried all of them and really enjoyed them. The kobe beef is rich, so I would get it sometimes but not always. The truffle burger is also pretty bomb. They also have french fries you can try with the sauces as well. 

Pro tip, if you come here on your birthday your friends pretty much have to draw you a card.

Best burger joint in the city, and I always go big with the Kobe burger. However, previously Sketch made these delicious gourmet chili's that were unbelievable. Now the only Chili they serve is a thick chili to go over chili fries. How I long for those delicious chili's. But all in all, the burger's and the hand cut fries they serve with gourmet dipping sauces are outstanding!

Absolutely the best sausage on the planet! However, make sure you get it fresh at the Reading Terminal, and not the prepackaged ones that you can find in various grocery stores around the city. The Boudin Blanc and chicken feta versions are particularly unique and amazing, but even the regular Italian sausage is unbeatable! If you love sausage, you have to go to Martin's!!!

Oh hey, you took the vegan shakes off the menu, and a few other vegan options too. Thanks a lot, Sketch. What's that you say? You still have a veggie burger on the menu? Sorry, I can get one of those pretty much ANYWHERE. Smell ya later.

Looks like your hole in the wall burger joint but don't let this narrow restaurant steer you away. They are vegan friendly. Where else can you enjoy a vegan milkshake with your omnivore friends that enjoy their own milkshakes as well. Come here with an empty stomach because you will leave full! Veggie burger was yummy and they have a interesting list of sauces you can have with your burger. My friend and fiancé enjoyed their burgers very much they still raved about it after we left the restaurant! The interior of the restaurant is fun and hip as if you eat here it will always make a good table conversation piece. They even have crayons and paper at the table you can create your pics to add to their wall of art.  If they could improve..they should mention what's gluten free on their menu.

You can't go wrong with this place this is one of my favorite Hawaiian places that I've ever been to. The service is always great the sauces, the chicken, and pulled pork is all phenomenal. I have yet to have anything go wrong at this place. Definitely the best Hawaiian in Tucson and probably anywhere. I would like to see some imported Hawaiian drinks but other than that I can't complain about anything.
Pretty impressed. Was skeptical about it but turned out delicious! Had the red chili burro. Good sized and the chips and salsa were great! decent prices as well.
I wish I had a photo to upload.  OMG my friend shined me onto this place.  It's now on my 10 ten list of yummyness

I always try to hit the International Wildlife Museum after going to the Sonora Desert Museum.  It's my family's two-fer when we drive down to Tucson from Phoenix.  We try to go here at least once a year.

My family and I refer to this as the Stuffed Animal Museum because this place is chock full of taxidermied animals that have been donated over the years.  If you have an aversion to hunting or taxidermy, stay home.  Seriously.

The admission price is very reasonable.  The exhibits are really interesting, particularly the prehistoric room.  Some of the animals are just awesome (in the literal sense) in size: the mammoth and the elk, for example.

It's a great outing that all ages can enjoy.  Unless you hate hunting and taxidermy, that is.
HUGE VEGAN MILKSHAKES. Pretty good burg as well. Rotating seitan special--not as good as the burg. Fills up at lunch time, but def worth the wait.

Love the freshness of the fish here at Shiroi Hana! I've stopped by here twice now and the quality of sushi and freshness of fish did not disappoint. There Miso soup is delicious, as well as the spicy tuna roll and the other standard rolls. I have not tried many of their specialty rolls but look forward to trying some on my next visit. The sashimi is wonderful. And don't forget to grab some hot sake when you visit. It is much smoother than most other places I've been to, and I really enjoyed it. They also have delivery from here and take out if you are interested. However, this is a nice place to sit down and relax for dinner after walking throughout the city.

I write yelp reviews of my negative and positive experience. I never thought that the places I write about it review them. However this restaurant apparently does. A manager replied to my yelp review and told me to reach out. So, I did. Both managers I spoke with through email was absolutely amazing. I was definitely not trying to score a free meal. I'm not even a fan of going out to eat very often. However they offered for all 7 of us that went to dinner. It was really amazing. We went tonight (Friday. March 31st) our waiter was absolutely amazing. One of the best waiters I've ever had. His name is Henry. Definitely ask for him! We had a few other courteous waitresses that checked on us too. I never got to meet the managers unforutatenly but if you read this, please know I appreciate your courtesy. The food was also 1000x times better, too. I will be coming back next time we're able to go out and are craving mexican food. We may have not paid for anything but I did still leave a generous tip! Well deserved.

Steak Cortez and chicken chimichanga are the way to go by the way.

I'm so glad a colleague told me to try this place! My boyfriend and I grabbed a quick dinner here while visiting Philly the other night. It's not super visible from the street, so we probably would have missed it otherwise. I had the smashed onion burger and a black & white shake, and both were good. The onion burger was really different! We also split an order of fries. The best part was the decor - sketches cover literally every available inch of wall space. Staff was awesome and totally willing to turn down the AC when we asked. I'll definitely be back.

I finally  got to sketch. It has been on my radar for over a year but when I drive by it is always crowded and there is nowhere to park.  The place is divey in a nice way.
Very friendly and a good neighborhood crowd.  Tiny space with a grill/cook and a waitress.  Both were cool and really helpful.  The menu is mainly burger-centric with homemade Empanadas and bakery items.  I opted for the beef burger with swiss and bacon.  It was a generous size patty, really flavorful and at least 8 oz or more on a brioche roll with lettuce and tomato cooked perfect medium rare.  May be the best burger I have had in the city.  Forget Rouge and Village Whiskey...Seriously who would have thought.  Empanadas were hominy and bean and cheese and jamaican beef patties which were delicious.  I took out a sampler of most of the baked goods.  cookies were really good chocolate chip and brownies were great as well as the red velvet whoopee pies...clever. I am dreaming of that burger.  I will be back real soon!

Super good burgers.  You can feel the love that went into all of their food.  Their fries are hand cut and out of this world.  I love how you can just walk up to the cooler and get your own drinks.  Went there during a busy time, and the food took quite awhile, but well worth the wait.  I love how they have special sauces that you can choose from.
best casual sushi spot in philly.  i agree with the other reviews - not as cheap at other spots but consistently fresh, delicious, and good service,   great corporate lunch place.

First this restaurant is definitely 3.5 stars, but I'll round up because the food was good. 

Pluses: the food was excellent. Had a great Arizona Sunset margarita (in a huge glass) and tried the tour de Macayo for my entree. My best friend got the combo plate with an enchilada and a beef taco. She's a picky eater, including not liking a lot of different sauces, and she cleaned her plate. She actually finished her dinner before I did, something that never happens when we eat out. That earned it high marks. 

Cons: so so slow. After a long day of driving and then a few hours exploring Old Tucson, I just wanted to eat and go. It didn't seem exceptionally busy so I'm not trying to be harsh, but there was a point where the couple eating at the table behind us had gotten their food, eaten and left before we'd seen any of ours. Maybe the long day added to my irritation, but I felt it took far too long to get out entrees.

The best thing about Shiroi Hana besides the food has to be the atmosphere. It feels more mature than and reserved and yet modern, than your increasingly common hip multicolored contemporary sushi restaurant.
The staff are very friendly and clearly well knit and the patrons are more likely to be 30+ and enjoy a quieter environment without top 40's blasting in their ears.

My gf and I came here a number of times while we resided in Philly and every time we ordered the Sushi Love. This restaurant essentially introduced me to good consistent sashimi. A+ for the spicy tuna rolls. The miso soup was very nice, basic style, yet very tasty in flavor. mmm mmm.
Prices are comparable with the wider sushi community in Philly if not a little bit on the higher side.
Come here for a nice calm evening of good sushi.

Best burger that I've had in a long time! My son wanted a great burger for his birthday dinner and they didn't disappoint. The service was great and the atmosphere was artsy and fun. I had the turkey burger, my son had the beef burger, and my husband had the cyclop burger. We all agreed that they were awesome and the fries were also amazing. I'd definitely return whenever I'm in the area.

We happened  upon this place while staying at an Airbnb around the corner. I had the burger with diced onions and my husband had the regular burger. They were both very good, very juicy and cooked how we asked. We shared an order of fries and had a lot left over. Service was great too. Artwork was a great touch.

What were we waiting for?  Finally, we have tried Dinner Done in Carrollwood, and it was fantastic.  I recommend the Grab and Go if you don't have time to cook your own meal.   With a brand new baby and no extra time to prepare a meal, this was the PERFECT solution for a small dinner party.  My guests raved about the delicious steak and asked how to make the mushroom sauce.  I gave them directions to Dinner Done!  LOL.

I used to like this place but things have gone seriously downhill even since my last post. The burgers I've received are soggy and disgusting. I keep coming back out of convenience... I need to stop. Last time I got a cheeseburger and fries and it cost me $16?! My bun was so soggy and the meat was not good. I pretty much threw the whole meal out. What a waste. They used to use tasty meat. Now it tastes cheap. Won't be going here anymore :/

The best burgers in Philly, without a doubt!!! I have been here many times, and never had anything I didn't really enjoy. I usually get a burger, medium rare, with bleu cheese. Really good. The fries are awesome. The sauces are all good. I really like the wasabi one.

I've also had their Dr. Pepper pulled pork. Phenomenal. And they have good cheap desserts.

Ambiance:
Sketch Burger is definitely memorable - as the name implies its walls are pasted with the creative and sometimes offensive sketches left behind by its patrons. There are markers and paper available at each table if you'd like to make your own. I love coming here and having a laugh at all of the different pictures as I enjoy my burger. 

Food:
The burgers here are damn good. There are a few different patty's to choose from - I'm a fan of the Kobe Burger. You then get to pick your sauce - I like the Aioli and the Curry Ketchup - and which type of cheese and other toppings you'd like. They have your standard burger fare as well as some more inventive options so there's something for every taste. The fries here are very good and come with a selection of sauces - recommend the Sweet Potato fries or the Cheese fries. This is my go to spot for burgers. 

Drinks: 
This place is BYOB!

Service:
Service is low-key and friendly. No complaints - the staff are knowledgeable about the menu and happy to make recommendations. 

Value: 
Depending on what you order your meal can be pricey but it's definitely worth it for all the fixins.

Very unique dining experience! Great food, great atmosphere, straight-forward menu. Just a warning: they're cash only and have limited seating inside. I had a delicious turkey burger and the best sweet potato fries I've ever had. They have veg options as well!

Perfect. Every single time. I absolutely love coming here. They had a food truck on base that was always slammed & the hours were a little crazy for obvious reasons but now they've got a shop which is great. Brought my fam from HI & they loved it. Said it reminded them of home.

This place has so much personality but no flavor. Man I really wanted to like this place. But it just doesn't live up to the hype. I've had so many people recommend this place to me that I was excited to try it out. I love the layout of Sketch. The art on the wall is funny and I'm sure I could eat there 100 times and find something new. But I wouldn't want to eat here that many times.

I went with some friends and we all ordered some burgers, fries, and shakes.  My one buddy got a Dr. Pepper pork sandwich. We tried a bit of each others and the consensus was,"Meh". The burger just lacked flavor. Sure there were a lot of different toppings to get, and we all tried to mix it up but nothing was standing out. I know some people may have their own magical combinations but it's not the customers job to find out what they should and should not get. The fries weren't anything special. I liked my shake. The meal was pricey for the quality, and this is coming from a guy who paid $26 bucks for a burger in the past.

The service was so good that it get's it's own special line right here.

My buddy tried Sketch and loved it but he said he hasn't had a good burger since his first. I've asked some of the people who recommended Sketch to me what other burger joints have they tried and liked and they told me they haven't really tried other places. I've been to about a dozen restaurants in the city that are known for their burger so I have some perspective. Sketch doesn't fall into the same league. If someone suggests Sketch, try it. But maybe find out if they have tried some other places as well. Trust me, there are much better burgers in Philadelphia.

Came here for lunch, food was decent, the service was pretty good too.  I got a few different rolls, nothing really extraordinary.  The miso soup hit the spot.  I have a suspicion their drinks are a little watered down, though.  They take Discover, and don't seem to mind splitting checks and stuff.  Lots of seating options.

I'm a huge burger guy.  I had to get down here and give it a try.  I'm going to get the bad out of way, and why Sketch lost a star right off the bat.  Then I'll move on to my review.  I have a few issues with this place.  It's extremely dark, only having narrow storefront, and the lighting is pretty bad.  It's also extremely dirty. I sat in a booth towards the rear of the restaurant.  The walls and surfaces in general were filthy.  This place really needs to be cleaned badly.

We entered, were seated, and greeted by all three people working.  They were very friendly and helpful.  The staff is excellent and really make you feel at home. One odd thing is that they take you order, like a regular restaurant; but send you back to the cooler in the kitchen area to get your drink.  The sketches on the wall are very entertaining, and there's plenty of art supplies to keep you busy while waiting for your burger.  This aspect would also likely keep the rowdiest kids occupied for the duration of their stay.

I ordered a sirloin burger, medium rare.  It came out cooked perfectly.  The lettuce and tomato were fresh.  I added the harrisa aeoli, which wad a slightly pungent garlic taste.  Next time I think I'll try the chipotle sauce.  I also added a slice of American Cheese for a $1.50.  It's a slice of American Cheese, a $1.50, really?  The patty was a really nice size, and they aren not skimping on meat here.  It was although overshadowed by the size of the bun, which was decent.  Overall, this is a very solid burger.  They would benefit hugely from downsizing that bun.  

We also ordered both regular and sweet potato fries.  Both types of fries may have actually topped the burgers.  I'm not usually a big fan of fries, but both types of fries were excellent.  They're also served with your choice of sauce. Next time I will trying the green chili cheese fries, that looked amazing the table next to me.   

I'm definitely coming back here.  If they clean up a bit, I'm definitely adding a star.  Although, he food is good enough for me to deal with the grit.

Having started on a dairy-sugar-legume/soy-grain-alcohol purge diet, I knew that eating out at restaurants would be a challenge.  But I have been to 2 other restaurants in the past couple of weeks that were able to accommodate my "without..." requests fairly easily and with flair and flavor.  Not so Shiroi Hana.  My first thought was to order the sashimi roll with a seaweed salad.  But when I asked if the salad could be made without soy or sugar, I was informed that it was a pre-packaged mix that already had sugar in it!  What?!! Not from scratch?  Ok, so then I asked if they could just give me a couple of the veggie fillings as a side dish from the veggie rolls...just without the rice.  But no, the "chefs" apparently don't "do" that.  They offered a pile of steamed veggies that was ok, just not all that interesting.  The sashimi roll probably could have served as a veggie side in itself, since there was approximately a 1:1 ratio of filling to cucumber.  They didn't even take all the skin off the cucumber on 2 of the rolls...just try to bite through that without the whole piece falling apart; there was a good inch or so of solid skin on both.  And not much flavor in that sashimi roll either.  I guess they rely pretty heavily on people's use of soy sauce, wasabi, and ginger.  They never even brought the salt I asked for with the veggies (which, by the way, they charged me $8 for!)  Overall, not a particularly satisfying lunch, and for that, the cost was $23 before tax & tip.

Mixed review.  The food was tasty, but room temperature, at best.  Our waiter started out very friendly but apparently one of the other waiters overheard us lamenting how long it was taking to be waited on, get our drinks and length of time before our waiter came back to check for refills.  They had a large party come in but our party of approx. 16 was there long before the larger party of about 30.

Now for the positive side:  My daughter complained to the manager about the slow service, food not being hot and our waiter being inattentive.  The young lady who was apparently the manager was beyond nice.  She not only discounted the bill and the service suddenly got better, but even went next door to the 7-11 to get some milk for my great granddaughter's bottle, since they had run out of milk.

The manager was very pleasant, professional and handled the situation in an excellent manner.

If I owned a restaurant -- large or small, she would be an excellent choice for manager.  No, I'm not related to her and had never met her till going to the restaurant last night.

To date, these are the best wings I have found in Tampa.  Quality chicken, cooked the way you ask and great sauce flavors.  My favorite are the Garlic, Hot wings.  They have fresh slivers of Garlic with the hot sauce.  My only complaint is they can't get the amount of sauce correct.  The mild and the medium wings have very little sauce and the hot wings are "drowning" in sauce.  If you don't like your wings that way you may be disappointed and I would ask for "light" sauce which still comes heavy.  The service has always been good and it is fairly inexpensive.

I brought my vacuum cleaner in for a new plug.  No problem.  $20.00.  Less than 3 months later one of the prongs of the plug became loose.  Then a week later the plug became detached from the cord. They wanted to charge me  $65.00 to replace the cord!  They said they don't guarantee plugs.  Clearly the plug they used was defective and they should replace it at no charge.  The owner tried to claim that I caused the damage by yanking the cord sideways.   Not true.  The owner needs to work on his people skills.

PROS:
Burgers are so F-ing goooooood!  Big and juicy and lovely. I've been here twice in the past month - first trying a beef burger and then another day trying the Bison Burger. Obvi the beef is better, but the bison is healthier and tastier than the turkey (which I was also tempted to try).

The fries are Belgian-cut and a touch on the thicker side, perfectly seasoned and paired with a few different sauce options (+$). The Jalapeño Cheddar is amazeballs but the Chipotle Aioli is really by fave.

It's a BYOB but there are also several bottled beverages from which to choose. I always go diet cream soda.

There are a selection of homemade cookies and brownies displayed in jars that are for sale. Do it!

CONS:
It's a small place, maybe 7 tables inside. Cash only, but there's an ATM inside, and a Bank of America next door. They do not recycle - c'mon friends, it's the little things we can do!

If you're veg(an) - get the seitan bbq sammich, you wont be disappointed! lots of seitan and lots of delicious sauce on a nice big roll. has outdoor seating too, which is a plus in the warmer weather. writing this review made me hungry.

Came in here yesterday to pick up some lunch. I had the vegan burger with cheddar cheese. It was huge, and tasted great. There are quite a few sauces to choose from, and I wish I had tried one. I'll have to try the vegan bbq sauce next time. 

My boyfriend got the spicy lamb burger that was on special, and he said it was amazing. We also split cheese fries which were very good. They gave a large amount which was perfect for sharing. 

This place also has milkshakes and a ton of desserts that I will have to try next time. 

I would definitely recommend this place if you are in Fishtown, and will be going back to try something else!

We had my daughter's going away party catered by them and they did a lovely job. The food was fresh and tasty and everyone just loved it. The staff made us feel like we were their biggest clients even though we were just a small party. 

We'll be using them again!

This bakery is really a pleasure, with a well selected range of  products that are just about all top-notch or nearly so. Even though the breads and other baked goods are not prepared on site, they don't seem to suffer for it - except maybe the baguettes. Some of these breads, in particular the signature "pain au levain", could stand shoulder-to-shoulder with any breads anywhere. Other highlights include the olive loaf, the country white and the chocolate cherry bread, though the last of these is not always consistent. 

Crust... the crusts of Metropolitan's breads are in a different class than many of its competitors. At their best, they have that quality of being a bit like Christmas glass on top of a thin layer of leather. Crusts tend not to last long, so it's best to get the breads early in the day. I cut and freeze the bread immediately, and this preserves the quality quite well. It can then be restored simply by toasting. 

Crumb... the crumb (that is to say the insides) of Metropolitan breads are generally dense and moist. You can make a sandwich out of this bread and it will hold together. It's definitely not "air bread". Many are part sourdough. This kind of bread, sliced and toasted and cut into little squares is a perfect base for a ripe creamy cheese.

There is a refrigerated section with specialty butters and cheeses and spreads. This is the priciest part of the shop, but the products are good, in my experience.

Among the highlights here are their pastries and cakes.  At the top of the list are the canelés, a specialty of Bordeaux. Don't be put off by their burnt appearance. In fact, the darkest ones are the best. These delights consist of a crackly caramelized shell around a rich, yellow bread-pudding-like interior that is subtly flavored with vanilla and rum, and it seems, a bit of lemon zest. Many of the other pastries are also excellent, such as the mixed berry danish, the cream cheese brownies, oatmeal cookies and the carrot cake. The fig bars can be a bit dry and unsatisfying.

They also have very good prepared sandwiches and the vegetable focaccia is a treat.

The handsome, tall painted glass sign outside the shop tells that this bakery took inspiration from the bakeries of Paris, and breads say so as well. It's about as close as you can get in these parts to a real Parisian boulangerie. Thank you, Metropolitan!
3.5 stars! Sushi here was great. I had take out. The restaurant looked inviting. Service was great. Sushi tasted fresh and the prices were decent.

You can't spell "hype" without Shiroi Hana!
--------------
Before I begin, I have to apologize to Stephanie Y (3/31/10) - she was spot on with her review of this place!  

Either I'm a sushi snob, or too many people have unrefined palates. Or both.
After reading so many good reviews about this place, we decided to come here for dinner.
We split an order of the hard core sushi combo, tempura, and a spider roll. 

- Tempura: fried very well.  Dipping sauce had a touch of ginger.
- Spider roll: average.  Too much lettuce, which in my opinion has no role in ...a role. 
- Hard core sushi combo: they ran out of surf clam, and so I asked to substitute for an additional piece of uni.  The uni was VERY DISAPPOINTING, and had obviously been sitting out for too long.  It was half melted before it arrived, and it had no creamy, "umami" sweetness (it tasted salty, which reflects BAD uni).  The overall fish quality was mediocre, and MUCH better fish can be had at 3rd & Chestnut, 2nd & South, etc etc...  Let's not even mention the poor wrapping job on the salmon roe sushi (see my pic)

It got the second star only because of doting service. 

I bet the reason why this place gets massive grade inflation is that people review their the cooked items.  I thought this was a sushi restaurant, not a Yakitori restaurant?!

The name is appropriate: quality and even more important than that, consistency. My personal favorite are the sausages with the cheese in them. Why? Because there's cheese, I don't think I need to say more on that. Their prices are extremely reasonable and they run sales all the time on various sausages or meats. They also have great bacon too. The employees are very friendly and extremely patient because it can be a little overwhelming, given the variety of sausages. As if that's a bad thing! During the summer, this will definitely be a stop for me to pick up meats to barbecues and tailgates so they can ooh, ahh, then nom and ask "where'd you get these?". There's a $10 minimum on credit cards.

the most amazing food on girard ave ,,,,,everything is fresh and super tasty , burgers speciality dishes ,and fabulous fabulous homemade baked goods !!!!    prices are great too !  and the staff is fantastic !!!!  the owner , always has a big smile on her face , this place is super popular , and with good reason ,,,,,,the best burgers in the city ,,,great environment to bring children !!!!!

I had an excellent shopping experience here for a new vacuum. The price was better than anything I found online and he threw in extra tools. Not only did I get a great price, but I was shown how to use all of the attachments which helped once I got it home. I really recommend this store, this was my first time there and I will tell everyone I know to avoid best buy, target, etc and get your vacuum here. It's cheaper and supports a local business.

Believe the hype! Great burgers. Great price. The Dr Pepper pulled pork (essentially a traditional Mexican carnitas) is killer. Nice place to bring the kids, a real fun experience. Good selection of desserts.Seating can be a little tight to say the least. Parking is a bear.

Food: 4.5
Decor: 3
Ambiance: 3.5
Service: 3.5
Value: 4

Very good burger in a unique and accessible atmosphere.

This is a real gem, with excellent, super-friendly service and always fresh, well-prepared sushi and sashimi (having lived in Japan, I know this is quality without fluff). Calm "zen-like" ambiance that is way better than most other Philly restaurants in that you can actually have a conversation with your dining companion! Our go-to place before weekend concert (and the service is quick especially if you let them know your time issue).

Horrible experience with delivery at this location ordered several times in hope that it would get better but last night was 3 strikes your out for us. Took almost 2 hours and when pizza finally arrived it wasn't even hot!! We decided we would not be ordering anymore from here

The food here is very good, and the seafood, in particular, is quite fresh.  The Hard-core Sashimi combo is excellent and includes uni, scallop, and toro, along with a  salmon and avocado roll.  Great if you want a variety of tastes.  The teriyaki here is delicious as well, and the udon is warm, flavorful, and satisfying.  Definitely one of my fav places in the city for sushi.

The food is amazing. They have the best vegan burger in Philadelphia. That being said, the service has truly declined. We have been eating here since it's opening and were always happy with the service. Recently, we attempted to eat here on a Friday. We attempted to call ahead and order food. They would not allow us to order. We arrived and it was crowded. A very rude and abrupt cashier with blue hair asked us if we were eating in or carrying out. We answered eating in as she walked away from us she muttered 35 minutes. She then did not return to the counter. I had to yell across to her to ask if we could carry out. She then told us 45 minutes to carry out. I could understand her lack of manning the counter if she was helping out in the kitchen, but she was not. She was rude and brusque.
Amazing dogs and sliders!  Been in need of a spot like this in Tampa!
They make a great tuna roll with cucumber-no rice!  Service is excellent and sushi is yummy.

I don't understand why this is everyone's favorite burger place... I've definitely had better burger! The place looks pretty cool with customer's artwork all over the wall but to be honest, it's a little small and "dirty" in my opinion.

Hands down the best burger I've ever had. Kobe beef, and the sweet potato fries are nothing short of a miracle. I will be back every time I visit my sister in law. Place is a bit small, but the staff really makes it work. Plan for a wait depending on what time you get there.

Chile rellenos in the Tucson Area rated according to the Homeland Security Advisory System with three word descriptors.

Macayo's: better than expected. Yellow

See photos.

Used to love this place but I don't know what happened. Burger was ordered medium and came out well done, with quite a bit of char. Needed to add salt, even though I had bacon on it. Fries were mostly limp, and the "mayo" sauce was very watery. Staff was very friendly, I'll give them that.

"Mmm, mmm, mmm, that is a tasty burger!"

I met up with a few fellow bloggers for a maiden voyage to Sketch.  As we sat in our booth, we each cracked a high life (I know, classy) and proceeded to devour the sweet potato fries with the chipotle aioli.  The fries were very tasty and crispy, yes it can be done.

My burger arrived and was presented simply in a paper box.  I went for the ground beef, cheddar and grilled onions.  The brioche bun rounded out what was a really solid burger.  The burger itself was just below the "too big to eat" point which annoys me sometimes.  In the Philadelphia burger space, lots of people are going bigger which does not necessarily mean better.  Give me a burger that I can fit in my mouth already.

Anyway, it's a fun spot and the decor is definitely not like anything I've seen anywhere else.  I even thought about making something for them but I'm just not that talented.

I'll just stick to eating their burgers.

Me and my friend debated where to go and eat, and he has this software on his IPhone called  urbanspoon that picked that restaurant. We went not expecting anything special. We were greeted and sat, the aura is very minimalistic (very Japanese indeed) and created a nice calm harmony and made the restaurant seem wider and cozier.
The food by far exceeded my expectations: FRESH, well cooked, well presented, did I say delicious too :) It is a restaurant week in Philly so they had a special dinner package for $35 and boy, let me say that it was a lot food. Dessert was sublime...
The service was great: my friend ordered hot tea and the owner,I think, kept refilling and checking in on us nonstop. I surprised her with knowledge of Japanese which I think made her day!
The ultimately best joint to take your friends, out-of-town visitors, dates or lovers there: it will never let you down nor disappoint you.
the couple next table mentioned they had been coming there for a while and just love it!
Both hands and legs up :)
Great Hawaian inspired food. Kaluah pulled pork, moco loco, and the list goes on. Excellent food for a very inexpensive price.

What a cool place!
Granted, it was wedged in a weird spot on Girard, but once you walk in you smell the delicious burgers cooking and you see alllll the art work from other customers! 
Our waitress greeted us quickly, explained to us the menu, the specials, and where drinks were located. 

I ordered the Cyclops burger with no cheese and all the garden. It was delicious! That bacon. So. Good. 
It took a little longer than expected but they only had one cook making all the food so I wasn't too surprised. 
Also the fries!!!!! They were fresh and abundant. Totally worth the extra cost and the sauce we got was a great addition. 
All around, great experience, plenty of food, and fun art to look at!

Good but I prefer a smaller patties over the thick patty and large, heavy bun needed to maintain it.  I felt full after a couple bites. Ordered it cooked medium which was rightly done, but if it was medium-well or well it would probably be pretty dry. Good flavor though and the harissa sauce is really good.

I am so sad to give 2 stars! Sketch was my fav but there isn't really anything there for me now except a veggie burger. When it was a Mecca of vegan friendly treats I would go all the time. I stopped in for fries the other day and I couldn't believe everything was gone! And a sign staying "regular" ice cream flavors mocked me and just an awkward empty space where the vegan flavors were. I'm hoping to update this review one day with great news they brought the veg stuff back.

I'm on a journey to find Phillys best vegetarian burger and this was a place that was on my list.  I stopped in this very small hole in the wall with tons of character.  There was only one server who was taking care of the dine-in guests as well as the take out orders and register.  After ordering it took about 15 minutes for my order.  The burger was a nice hearty flavorful veggie burger.  I could barely finish it all.  I also ordered fries and there were a ton of fries.  I enjoyed the selection of sauces.  This is definitely in my top #5 veggie burgers.  I will definitely be back.

Average quality sushi at above average prices run by a well below average manager. If you are in the mood for expensive sushi, go somewhere nicer. If you are in the mood for average sushi go somewhere cheeper. Either way, avoid Shiroi Hana.

Metropolitan bakery was the only reason I attended church without complaint as a kid. The bribery became something of a ritual, as every Sunday morning (gotta get there early! It's gutted pretty quickly, especially on weekends) my mom'd get a latte and a millet muffin, my brother'd get a lemon bar or a slice of flourless chocolate cake, sister'd get a rosemary & olive oil foccacia and a Yoohoo, and I'd get a plum tomato & pesto foccacia with an Orangina. I've also had their gingerbread (regrettably seasonal-- only in Winter in my experience) and it is an amazing holiday treat-- moist and tender. I love their croissants, and lust over their chocolate croissants, but savory always triumphs over sweet in the life of me. Plum. Tomato. Pesto. FOCCACIA.

Not your daily bakery because it's not cheap, but an easily justified sporadic treat!

This place is absolutely amazing. I started going to the Terminal about 9 months ago and decided to check out Martin's because I was looking for bratwurst similar to what I got back home. I was blown away by the huge selection of meats and sausages and have not been disappointed by anything I've gotten here. The prices are definitely in line with the supermarkets and usually even a little cheaper, and the quality seems to be way better. They've got some tasty flat iron and tenderloin steaks, and I've absolutely loved all of varieties of sausages I've tried. I'm a little disappointed when they don't have the chicken andouille, but the turkey is almost as good. Any time I'm in the area for anything, I always check to see if they've got anything new to try out. The staff is always super friendly and very knowledgeable. Highly recommended!
This place used to be great now it's just an okay at best burger, long wait, good fries. I used to really like this place but won't be back.

The burgers were good and juicy and the atmosphere was fun but the service can be better. The waiter had an attitude and my friends and I felt rushed and uncomfortable with her when ordering and paying for our food.

Very friendly and personable customer service! Prices can't be beat and neither can the selection. They have everything from center cut pork chops to any type of sausage you can imagine. My favorite is the buffalo sausage...yum!

As with any place in Reading Terminal, the best time to go is right when the market opens. Beat the crowds and tourists and have first-pick of all the meats!
Best burgers I've ever had.  It doesn't matter what kind you order they're all yummy.  The fries are great too just straight up no wiz.  Sketch may be what I miss the most about Philly when we move.

Service is great, but can't say the same about the food. 

From the looks of it, this is a Chinese owned Japanese restaurant. I've only had the chirashi bowl and the udon lunch set. 

The chirashi bowl, which I had for dinner, is pretty filling. I can't remember the price, but I remember thinking it was expensive. The fish did not taste very fresh to me and I've definitely had better chirashi bowls in my lifetime. However, it's also not the worst. I wouldn't ever order it again, but it may taste okay for people who have less sensitive stomachs than I. 

The udon lunch set comes with a California roll. My entire meal came out to be $16 with tax and tip, which again, I felt was not worth it considering how easy it is to make (what I assumed was packaged) udon and how small the roll was. The udon is not soft and tasted like packaged udon that had been sitting in the freezer for months and is also very very bland. The soup is also VERY bland, although I actually found that part to be refreshing. The California roll was hastily made. It tasted like a typical California roll, so not much to comment on that except that it tasted like it had a little too much sodium. 

On a positive note, the service was great. The people who worked here were very nice and concerned that I did not enjoy my dish. I wish that the food was as good as the service, but it did not match up.

I had dinner at Shiroi Hana's sushi bar lat night and it was excellent.  The quality of the sashimi could only be better if the restaurant was located on a boat and the portions of sushi, sashimi, and maki were all generous.  Even better, no one judged me for eating an absurd amount of food.

Despite the huge conference nearby at the convention center (but I guess there's always one of those), there was plenty of room in the restaurant.  The only complaint I have is that Mirugai wasn't on the menu but that's true at most sushi restaurants so I can't hold it against them.  I'd love to come back to Shiroi Hana a few more times and see if they're consistently this good.

I ordered the chicken enchilada. ..but unfortunately it only had 3 tiny pieces of chicken. Grandma had the combination platter and it was okay. I really wanted a better authentic tasting plate for Tucson but it was lacking in flavor...however the staff was exceptional!!
Great Japanese food in center city.  Very unpretentious.  While food off the grill is good, I think the Sushi is the reason to go here.   Reasonably priced.

I came with friends to Posh Nails yesterday. I was well pleased with the salon as well as the wide range of polish choices. Salon is very upscale and professional. Come visit if you are in the South Philly area.

Love, love, love Sketch ... which was/is a welcome addition to the Fishtown strip of pizza & cheese steak places! Wished it had been in business when I lived in the neighborhood.

In my experience the service has always been attentive and friendly. Menu is varied, different and caters to vegans as well as meat-eaters. We've NEVER been disappointed w/ the food. Pulled port, mac & cheese, fish tacos and salmon burgers .... all YUMMY!

My only 'beef' is that while the concept is 'cool' ..... I'm overstimulated by the decor. But, all in all it's great. I'd give it 4.5 stars if it were possible.

We'll be back!!!!!

Worst experience ever. Walked in at 6pm and left out at 7pm with no food. Three tables were empty as I walked in: while waiting for one veggie bean burger two of those empty tables now full with 7 people total being served. The waiter would not make eye contact with me during the entire time waiting. He came over once and said, "your bugger will be ready in a few mins."  Those few mins turned into 30mins! I will NEVER GO BACK! Pls don't waste your time at this location. 

FYI -- I decided to make my own judgement call after reading a few bad reviews. If you decide to waste about two hours of your life... good luck.

The moment I walked in, I was already uncomfortable. It's that unquantifiable uneasiness that I you can't explain. I was even hesitant to mention it in my review.

The sushi was of so-so quality, halfway between what you pick up at a cheap grocery store and the better grade sushi houses in the area. The only great piece I had was the o-toro. Oh, and the rice crumbled the moment I picked up the piece. Probably an isolated incident, the rice was a little better the second and third time around. Dessert was an equally strange mix of flavors. 

Bah, read faye b's review...I don't like reliving bad meals =( Service was off, atmosphere was off, price was...well, off? I'll give it a shot another time, but two stars as of my last meal.

Got the hankering to make some french toast last Sunday but didn't have any bread so we headed on down to this little bakery towards the top of the hill.  I've picked up a couple of unimpressive loaves from the Flourtown farmer's market so my hopes weren't high but their shop offered plenty considering the small size of the storefront.  Needless to say, the quality was much better than found at the farmer's market (cut out the middle man); the white loaf was superb and their veggie focaccia really went down well.  They also offered a smattering of fresh goodies; cheeses, fresh pasta, hummus; not exactly what I expected from a small local bakery.

Keep in mind that nothing is baked on site so you won't find loaves still warm from the oven but their goods are still plenty fresh; I wavered on the four stars but that loaf did make some damn-fine french toast and the service there was excellent.

Welcome to Good Burger, home of the good burger, can I take your ooorder?

Sketch is a quaint establishment in the Fishtown area. They provide paper & art supplies in the form of colored pencils, markers, crayons & whatnot. Patrons are welcome to doodle (or sketch) away their heart's delight. As you wait for your scrumptious sandwich, take a gander at what has preceded you. 

As for the burger itself, they offer a substantial array of choices to dress your burger. You can choose from your cheese, sauce, & toppings. Notable toppings include bacon, avocado, & (my personal favorite) truffle butter. Luckily for me, they had a bison burger on special when Acelyn B & I paid visit. Top it with bacon, truffle butter, and provolone cheese. YUMMMM. The sweet potato fries were savory in their dry seasonings. 

Service was friendly. & so were the patrons. When Acelyn B & I walked in, two gentlemen offered their table to us. They accurately read our timid nature in avoiding any conflict as we didn't want to disrupt the cake display on the hightops by the window. Very nice people all around.

Oh yeah. Cash only. Don't forget the cash, folks.
Great burgers. Amazing belgian french fries with dips. Crayons at tables to draw your next masterpiece. The only negative is the price but you pay for quality.

Definitely one of the best burger joint in Philadelphia. Get ready for a juicy, kind of greasy but in a good way, thick, home made, made to order satisfying burger. You can do beef, turkey, chicken, vegetarian, vegan and so forth. They have so many options from toppings, cheeses, whatever, they have it all. 

The place is definitely a hole in a wall but it has improved inside. I think the place is pretty clean and who cares? Hole in wall places are usually the best place to eat! 

The fries are absolutely to die for, it's crunchy, flavorful and the sauces on the side just makes them 110% better. The staff is very friendly so it's just a really great experience and if you love to draw maybe yours will be good enough to make unto the wall!

They have probably the best "veggie burger" that I've ever eaten.  You will not leave hungry!  I think it's also impossible to leave Sketch in a bad mood.  If you don't like playing with crayons then you don't belong here.  We once arrived close to closing and were still served a full meal with milkshakes with zero attitude.  Didn't think existed in Philly!

Taco Bus is the shit. I love it. Crave it. The fish tacos are amazing, as is the ceviche. I will find a reason to fly back down to Tampa very, very soon.  Just to eat at the bus again..oh yeah, and to visit my son at USF!

Macayo's has my favorite chili relleno ever...so much so that when my husband and I come to Tucson to visit his mother, we eat at Macayo's. I recommend getting the basic one though (instead of the 3-relleno combo) if you want a no-frills, tasty chili relleno. I just now tried the 3-relleno combo and only ended up finishing the basic cheese one. Also, while I was excited to try the fried ice cream, it was kind of sickening.

It was ok. I was super pumped for what I thought was going to be an awesome burger but it fell short. We tried the truffle, smashed onion and a bacon cheeseburger. I was happy to hear they offer rare burgers...a rarity. I opted for medium rare and unfortunately they mixed up my burger with someone else's in our party that asked for medium. Overall it was tasty but a little too greasy and the meat to bun ratio was off...grease soaked through my bun causing me to eat a mushy burger without a bun. The best burger in the group was the plain old bacon cheeseburger....so I recommend if you go here to skip the fancy topping and sauces and keep it simple.

3.5 stars.

I went here last Saturday night after I decided this place over Ekta. Parking was a little bit of a pain but I guess that's because i wasn't familiar with the neighborhood and there was some sort of neighborhood game/festival going on nearby.  
 
I ordered a turkey burger with bacon, avocado and pepper jack cheese. I also got a shake as well(Moooooooooooo).  The servers were very pleasant and attentive. It was a little bit of a different set up in that you pay for your food upfront and then they cook and bring it out to you. I"m not normally a big fan of this because in my previous experiences, this kind of pay setup means that they have no motivation as far as good service. But au contrair mon frer, the service was excellent.

The burger did take a little while to come out, but I knew that because 1. the reviews commented on it, 2. They upfront told me and 3. There's a little sign somewhere there that says it takes time.  The burger was really big and had plenty of tomato, lettuce and avocado on it. The bacon was cooked juuuuust right, nice and crispy but not too greasy.  The sandwich was really hot, I mean steaming hot ouchity hot. I had to put it down after a bite or two. The cook actually came out after two or three minutes and asked me if everything was ok. I said yeah, I was just letting the burger cool because it was really hot. She was relieved to hear that.  So I ate my cheeseballs while I waited and read a little.  

The cheeseballs were fun, but I kind of felt like I got the short end of the picnic stick. I'd also like to have fries. I wonder if maybe fryers or oil are in short supply. Or whether they are trying to be different based on a no-fry policy.  I'd settle for some pan fries or wedge fries. Something potatoey.

Once the burger cooled down I ate it. This was not your average turkey burger. This had some great spices and flavor to it.  And it was big. Ok, now my mouth is watering again, dangit.

The shake was the weak link here for me. It was very flavorful, but as previously pointed out, a little too milky. I"d prefer something somewhat thicker. Oh yeah and no water either. Gotta buy in bottles. I hate that here. Drives me frickin crazy.

Overall, I enjoyed my visit to Sketch. Good service, good food and a good attitude. When I was done, the cook said "Do you want me to cook you another one?" I wish I had had room enough to say yes. But there's always next time......I"m thinking Kobe beef. Mmmmm japanese cow......

Holy Moses, smell the roses. I'm still full from dinner last night at Sketch, yet I'm obsessively planning how I can get back over there later for another burger. I will be 900 lbs. by the end of the year if I keep my current eating schedule up!

My bff and I were in search of food last night, and I remembered how great the reviews were for Sketch. We drove over, got a spot right outside and were pleased to walk into such a bright and well-decorated place. It's small - three booths and and L-shaped counter with stools - but mighty. The smell of the burgers smacks you in the face as soon as you step inside, and it will make you very, very happy (they're going to be open for lunch, too, starting on Monday). 

I went with the beef burger with American cheese, tomato and Harissa Aioli. All I can say is that it's probably the best burger I've had in Philly. The roll was perfection and the size of the meal was humungo. The burger was so good that it didn't need ketchup or mayo or anything else. They even have milkshakes on the menu, but since I had already had one earlier in the day, I decided to save it for next time (oh, there will be a next time very soon).

Instead of french fries you'll be treated to a bag of Andy Kapp Hot Fries. I didn't know they even made those anymore! It takes a while for the burger to come out (they're makin' them fresh in the back) but it's worth the wait. You even get to "Sketch" on the tableside chalkboards while you anticipate the sweet, sweet meaty goodness that is about to come your way. 

Anyone want to pick me up and drive me to Fishtown? If I don't get another Sketch burger soon I may die*.

*OK, maybe I won't die because of not getting a burger. That's just me being dramatic. But I might cry. Or eat my computer. Or something...

Seating outside is very uncomfortable, they could at least cushion the metal seats. I went during brunch and ordered the smoked salmon dish, it took a very long time for it to come out. When it finally arrived, it had a lovely side of hair on it. Potatoes also looked like they were bad before being cooked. Very disappointed with this place.

Any place that serves a truffle butter burger is A-OK in my book.  The service was friendly and I love all the sketches along the wall.  I have tried three different burgers so far (this place remains my monthly cheat day) and I have not be disappointed.  I took my boyfriend here and he can't stop talking about it, I found out that he often brings co-workers here for lunch.  This place is amazing and I really hope they never change.

Sober modern decor (neither bling bling nor generic Asian). Good shrimp shumai. 
But the rest was pretty bad. Greasy gyoza, subquality fish (some fishy, some mushy). Service was cold and could not understand plain English. 
Definitely not coming back.

Don't even get me started on their green chili cheese fries. There culdn't possibly be anyone who loves french fries more than I do. I try them from every place that serves them so I know french fries and these are some of the best I've ever had the enormous pleasure of eating. Even without the yummy cheese and delicious green chili's, the fries alone are perfection!

5 guys who?!?! Hands down..best burger I ever had and yes better than 5 guys (whom I used to be a big fan off).  Some of my co-workers told me about this place and because of the location, I was a little indecisive at first but man am i happy i went there.  I got the cyclops burger and it had to be the best burger I ever had not to mention it was huge.  I got full half way through my sandwich.  The fries are really good too but try not to eat alot of it otherwise you won't be able to finish your burger.

Slow, pricey, and greasy.  I really wanted to like this spot, but quantity doesn't equal quality.

The burgers really are huge and the toppings are generous.  The problem is they aren't especially flavorful, or combined in proportions that compliment each other.  I had a beefburger with grilled onions, mushrooms, and Swiss cheese, and the onions overwhelmed everything else - which is saying something as the burger was easily a 1/3 pound of meat.  Our side of fries was generous but tasteless, too, requiring seasoning.  Lastly, the shake was made with melted ice cream, so it wasn't very thick at all.   These were all rookie mistakes. 

All told, two sandwiches, a side of fries, and two drinks set us back $25.  If you really want a burger, make your own at home as you probably can do just as well Sketch.

This place has changed my life! I hate to cook and my children and I were suffering for it. Wonderful freezer to oven meals that are fun to put together! Music, wine, lots of help. OR you can have it delivered to your house OR pick up the pre made meals they keep in stock. The menu items are adult but kid friendly enough to please both crowds. Leave out the ingredients you don't like. One or two times a month the delivery fee is dropped to $5! This place is a no brainer for any working human being wanting fresh, delicious food and variety without the mess.

Awesome Sushi at a great price.  This is my go to restaurant and I eat there or order in a few times a week.  The food is always great and delivery is always quick.  You cant beat it.  Try the tuna club for a real treat.

White pizza okay. Cheese pizza ordered w pepperoni, had no pepperoni . When I called and explained pepperoni was missing, she said to bring it back so they could see there's no pepperoni . 
Why would I lie about pepperoni ?! 
I told her no, I would not drive all the way back in 6 o clock traffic, she pretty much said oh well too bad. No other help or suggestion, other than show us the pizza. 

Acting as if I were making up a story made me angrier than no pepperoni . 
There are way too many pizza places out for way less money!!, to have crappy customer service skills!!

Love Solid Grindz food. No longer have to settle for soso Hawaiian food in Tucson. Only problem is, after a grand opening, they decided to only serve the military base.  While I think it's great to support the troops, I don't know why they don't spend any time off base.  I was happy to see this last week they announced some time at UofA then changed their mind.  That wasn't cool.  As much as I loved the food from the grand opening, I am likely to not return even when they return to serve the civilians.  Quality of food is the only reason this is a 3 star and not a 1.

Before going to Sketch, I heard a lot of talk about the place.  The general consensus was that they have good burgers, good shakes, and are bit pricey.  I have wanted to check this place out ever since I heard they serve up Kobe-style burgers.  Kobe cows are fed a beer a day, receive daily massages, and are raised and killed humanly.  This is all done under the pretense that happy cows taste better.

Sketch is a tiny joint with three booths and a small bar running along the wall.  It's painted with bright colors and has chalk boards along the walls (hence the name).  You order at the counter and the servers bring out each item as soon as it's ready.  It's a really fun way to enjoy the meal, although it was a bit awkward with my burger coming out first, and the fifth and last burger coming out about ten minutes later.  I still think it's the best way to operate though.  It also helps that ever single person working at Sketch is incredibly nice and seems like they're having a great time.  Despite the small size, the atmosphere is great.

Even though Sketch is establishing itself as a burger joint, the menu is quite varied.  In addition to their regular fare, they have rotating specials that include a salad, pulled pork, brisket and more.  Sketch is also vegan friendly, and is willing to whip up a vegan shake or burger on request, and they looked delicious.  Further, Sketch was right up my alley with fresh and locally sourced ingredients brought in daily.  They are really striving to do everything correctly to create the most excellent burger.

I am constantly on the search for the best burger in Philadelphia, and I think I may have found it.  I went with the Kobe beef, but I'm honestly not sure if I would be able to taste the difference between that and their regular burger.  Next time I'll have to do a taste test.  Everything, from my burger, to the shake, and the fries was so full of flavor.

Here's my note on the prices.  Burgers are about $6, the Kobe burgers are $9.60.  Cheese is $1 extra.  A huge order of fries is $3, and shakes are $4.50.  While that does sound a bit pricey, all of these are large enough that almost any normal person could fill up on half of the portion.  Then, splitting a burger, shake and fries could be less than $20.  Even if you want to eat the massive portions, the quality easily makes up for the price.

Bottom Line: I wrote so much more than usual because this is the most exciting new place I've been in a while.  The are serious contenders for the best burger in town, and being within walking distance of my house makes this place just that much better.  I highly recommend this place for anyone, and with all of the veg options, you really have no excuse not to go.  (Unless you hate fun and/or delicious things.)  Enjoy.

The only reason this doesn't get five stars is the prices.
It's pretty expensive for a burger here but it's REALLY good.
I think the portion of fries as an appetizer is a smart idea because trust me, their burgers are HUGE.

I had a standard beef sirloin, medium-well with cheddar cheese and their homemade BBQ sauce. It came out to be $10 or so.

The location is very close to the Front & Girard station on the Market-Frankford 'EL' if you are using SEPTA. It is also accessible via the Girard Avenue trolley.

The wait for the food was around 10-20 minutes. It varies because of the amount of customers and whatnot.

Looking to get a milkshake the next time I go, considering they had a slew of flavors.

Just recently tried this place. Very laid back earthy staff, bohemian decor, with sketches all around created by various customers. I didn't have a burger on this first visit, but I tried the veggie kielbasa with bbq sauce on a roll. It was very tasty. My friend was really digging her cheeseburger empanada. My order of sweet potato fries was just so so. I didn't like the thick cut of the fries, and they were a bit underdone. I liked my friend's order of the Belgian fries much better.

The best part of the meal, dessert. The have a pretty big selection from ice cream, brownies, cookies, tarts, cupcakes, and shakes. I had a scoop of coconut ice cream over a warm brownie. Was yumtastic. Next visit I will try the truffle burger and will take a sketch artist.

Okay wow. If you like burgers you must check out this place. I've told several people about this place in person - that's how good it is. I am still drooling thinking about this burger. 

I got the cyclops burger cooked medium with an over-easy egg, bacon, cheddar, lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles, and chipotle sauce. It was the kind of burger where I didn't reach for anything additional, and so juicy! 

There's a lot of really cool options - Kobe beef burger, Pulled pork cooked in Dr. Pepper, Truffle Butter Burger - in addition to your usual suspects (turkey burger and vegan bean burger). They have a good variety of sauces too, and all of their fries come with a choice of two sauces. 

It is pretty small inside, but on nice days they have outdoor seating. They brought free bottled water for all seven of us which was so nice! Really adds to that neighborhood feel with all of the art inside.

The place is cash only but there's an ATM.

Went there today for lunch with my husband.  He had the salmon bento box and enjoyed it.  I had two orders of salmon skin rolls, delicious.  It is not a good a maybe Zama on a good Zama day but we'll definitely come back for the nice host and frequent refill of our tea.

Damn, this place is wonderful. The burgers are juicy, the fries are spot on, and their diverse array of sauces are delicious. It's also really cool that they have daily specials and set vegan/vegetarian options because I can grab my carnivore AND vegetarian friends to have a field day. While a bit pricey, definitely worth every penny.

Situated in the center of Reading, Martin's is a local favorite. I've been visiting the counter for the last 4 years and the quality is always superb. There's something incredibly serendipitous to watch fresh protein being packaged in brown wax paper. You might have to wait a little while in line, especially if you go on the weekend, but it's absolutely worth the wait. The guys behind the counter are always friendly and ready to help!

On top of selling cuts of meat, they specialize in specialty sausages. My go-to purchases are the spicy turkey Italian sausage and the Andouille sausage. They are great on their own or as additions in soups!

3 things:

1. Smashed onion burger (chipotle sauce, fried egg, provolone cheese, & avocado)
2. Green chili cheese fries
3. Black & White malted milkshake

The massive burger is mind-blowingly amazing, & the fries are nothing like I'd ever had before! Be warned that the portions are gigantic, enough for 2 people to share. Another thing loved about Sketch is the decor, which was filled with pictures drawn by customers. They even provide construction paper and crayons for you to draw while you wait for your food. The food does take long to come out, but I guess it's cos the burger is so gigantic. Prices are a little steep, cos every time I've gone, me & my sister have ordered 2 burgers, 2 drinks, & an order of fries which came to around $32 without tip. But if you're looking for a great indulgence, this is it!
Great burgers with lots of choices of toppings. Excellent fries. Two words TRUFFLE BURGER!
I lived in Hawaii for four and 1/2 years. This food takes me back to the wonderful days on Oahu.  I highly recommend the Teri chicken and Chicken Katsu.

I was quite disappointed by this place.
