It started off on a good note, with them bringing oshibori to the table, along with the menus. Our waitress brought out an appetizer of mushy "grilled" veggies in some watered down teriyaki sauce.

Er? I was hoping our sushi would be better. We placed our order (salmon, yellowtail, and otoro sushi, a spider roll, and kumos). At one point I asked our waitress what roll she recommended and she said, "I don't know; I don't eat raw fish," but she rattled off a few from the menu. Did she actually try them, I don't know.

The oysters came, all 5 of them, in spoons, heavily seasoned with soy sauce. They took away the experience of sucking the oyster off the shell, AND covered up the taste with soy sauce?? 

Our sushi came a few minutes after. I picked up the first piece of salmon nigiri and the rice fell apart. Side note: the rice is supposed to be put together such that it doesn't fall apart when you pick it up but falls apart once it touches your tongue.

The salmon tasted okay. Now on to the yellowtail. The rice stayed intact, but the fish wasn't as fresh as I was used to. 

I tried a piece of the spider roll and that was fine as well.

The o-toro was the highlight of the meal. The fish was large (and it better have been for EIGHT DOLLARS) and melted in my mouth. Yum! If I had a bottomless bank account this is what I would have splurged on.

We ordered another set of the salmon, yellowtail, (the duo by which we judge sushi places), and o-toro. No rice mishaps this time either, so I'm thinking it was just the first piece. Bad first impression though. This batch was solid.

We ordered dessert just for the heck of it-- banana tempura with mango sorbet. I don't know about you, but I prefer my fried banana with a milder ice cream like vanilla or vanilla bean. Mango sorbet was just weird with it...oh, and the two random Pocky and honeydew melon! 

Dessert was fine...until I felt something hard in my mouth. At first I thought it was the stem from the cherry, but when I pulled it out, it was plastic! You know those plastic rings they have to hold the price tags onto a shirt? It was something like that. WTF?

Well, that killed it for me. Mediocre sushi, mediocre service, very high prices, and a plastic thing in my ice cream.

I think I may have waited too long to try Sketch.  Earlier reviews rave and recent reviews seem to describe my experience pretty well.  The place is really cute, with customer sketches all over the walls, a few booths and a counter set up along the wall.  I wanted to sketch while I waited as a sign suggested but I couldn't find the paper and writing instruments.  Oh well, they're missing out on a really poorly executed squirrel drawing, not me. 

The menu is pretty extensive burger wise and the non-burger specials board was also considerable.  I opted for a burger (the vegan kind) since I had read they are quite delicious.  There are a slew of toppings to ponder, all will run you $1.  Some of them really don't seem $1 worthy.  I mean I get why cheese, avocado or bacon costs $1 but onions and mushrooms?  Maybe it's just easier that way,  I don't know.  I do know that it deterred me from going crazy with the toppings since my vegan burger was already $7.  I topped it with avocado and the included in price aioli.  I also splurged on a regular order of french fries.  These babies are boasted as hand cut.  I usually love that since that's how Momma used to make them but these were just okay, a little too thick, which would have been fine but they weren't cooked long enough based on their cut. 

The actual vegan burger was really tasty, it was served on yummy, although a bit too big for the burger square bun.  It consisted of lots of lentils, beans and other healthy yum-yums.  I couldn't figure out if it was coming from the bun, the burger or the aioli but something had a cinnamon or nutmeg flavor that was too overwhelming and did not have any business in my lunch.  All in all I'd say I enjoyed my meal, but please note I was reallllly hungry.   

I will go back but I think I'll try the big salad or one of the seitan specials.  Any neighborhood joint that serves veg food is worth another shot.  They also sell baked goods and vegan ice cream, which is nice.

So I was turned off of Hawaiian BBQ because of the other popular place in town which in no way tasted like the real deal. Solid Grindz delivers! Katsu, Teriyaki Chicken, Musubi, & their rice is delicious. Fresh, filling and linguisa!!!!! I will go back again and again and sending my friends! Definitely worth a try!

I honestly don't understand all the positive reviews. My food was good but it wasn't amazing in anyway and it was quite expensive.
They had one girl working the counter, waiting the tables and answering the phone taking phone orders. This was on a Friday afternoon at lunch time.
The inside is very small and you have to get your own napkins, condiments, etc.
My burger was slightly overcooked.
I was next in line for a table and they gave that to two old dudes that walked in after me, she even told them they were second in line.

 I just don't see what the all the hoopla is about.
I would also like to add, there is a 'type' of crowd here, everyone dresses similarly, I wouldn't say 'hipster', but def. young, well with the exception of some older people who have money.

I'm very particular about Chirashi, and I have to say the chirashi here is filling and fresh. Definitely loved it compared to other japanese restaurants I've been around in philadelphia. Also, it is much easier to come to this location than Sagami, which I would have to drive to. Definitely would come back for fresh sashimi.

So I'm hoping maybe because it was late at or night or just an off day but for the amount I payed for the burgers I got, I was really unfortunately disappointed... I wouldn't have payed close to that amount for what I got had I known.. I normally am really good with burgers, not too picky. But this night's order was really unpleasant and not dirty or anything but tasted old... Like maybe it was made a while ago and was reheated or something... It looked delicious and was on time though and from what I've heard, they usually are good but as for today, I'm not a happy girl... This was a really disappointing experience though. Next chance I can, I'll be trying the shakes. Hopefully it won't be the same this time , my partner was especially unhappy with his, even though he had the Kobe beef burger.. He didn't even finish It in the end..

I was so excited to try this place after hearing all about it. Our cheese fries and milkshake came out first and were delicious! Unfortunately, it ended there. I got the cyclops burger, and while it wasn't bad, it wasn't anything special. I'd probably come back for fries and a shake, but I'd get a better burger elsewhere.

This is one of of favorite stands in reading terminal. Delicious, gourmet sausages at reasonable prices.

Most stuff is around $4/Lb.  I highly recommend the Italian stuffed with provolone and broccoli rabe.

I was in the area and was super hungry. Decided to try out planet sub after looking at their menu online. I walked in and right away I was greeted by the most pleasant two women. Soooo nice. They asked if it was my first time there and I told her yes, she suggested this sandwich to me called "The Experience" and oh my gosh, best choice ever. I'm not one to try new things but I'm so glad I did.
Yes it is a little pricey, but you're paying for the quality of your food.

This place was amazing! Right from the start! The customer service was in point. She was super friendly and very patient with us. Especially sense it was our first time there and we ask a lot of questions. The wait was nothing. And they were slammed! Great staff. We got a plate with two Meats on it. Got chicken katsu and teriyaki chicken. Both of them outstanding! Thank you guys for the most amazing experience. Keep up the great work!
I've been coming here more often now that I can get Hawaiian rolls instead of the tuna mac. Excellent option for lunch,

Sketch Burger is a little on the expensive side, and since we ordered delivery through diningin the menu prices were roughly a dollar higher automatically. However, it was DELICIOUS and we will order for lunch again. All the sandwiches had a choice of special sauces, although only one person chose one. I got the Dr Pepper Pulled Pork sandwich. It was jam packed full of meat and whatever the sauce is had a nice little kick to it. Everyone in our office chose something different. Turkey Burger with horseradish cheddar and avocado. She said it was not overly seasoned and very good. Smashed Onion burger with horseradish cheddar and chipotle sauce. He said the onions were just sauteed and placed first on the bun, so they made the bun very greasy. Otherwise he really enjoyed it. Beef burger with american cheese. At first he was skeptical, because he did not want "sauce" on his burger. However, the sauce ended up being the cheese melted into a sauce-texture. He ate his burger without the bun, because the buns are very heavy and extra filling. The fries were mediocre, not great but also not bad. They came in a paper bag, which is good so they did not get too soggy on the drive. We were all stuffed after our lunch and ready for a nap.

Sushi Heaven is here. Casual, yet delicious and without the pretension that makes it impossible to get a table at some of the other sushi spots in town. Understated, yet elegant surroundings make this a choice spot for a first date or a business dinner, and the sushi is divine .

We were staying at the Hyatt Bellevue nearby and found this place on Yelp.  Everything we ordered was great.  Price was very reasonable especially coming from Los Angeles.  We tried the lobster tail tempura skewer, naked tuna, triple spicy double tuna roll, California rolls, and tuna sushi.  Sushi was fresh.  Everything was great.  Service was good.  We thoroughly enjoyed our whole experience.  Would definitely come back if staying at the Hyatt in the future.

Really nice Hawaiian food, probably the best in town. Their shrimp and mac salad are a go-to. Nice selection of sauces as well. Location is informal, nothing to rave about but just fine for a fast meal.
Space is cozy and kid friendly. Service was super friendly and attentive. Food was delicious. Try the falafel and fries. We will definitely go back.

Very enjoyable experience. The venue is small, so if you're going to visit, they take reservations--make one. The service is top notch. The quality is superior, and for their location, their prices are very reasonable.  We were in and out, but not rushed. Would definitely visit again.
Hands down, the best sausage I've ever had. Make sure to get it from the source, rather than pay as much as double elsewhere! (I'm looking at you, DiBruno's!)

Hands down the best burger I've had in Philadelphia. I order their Kobe Burger with Cheddar every time. They pile the cheese on and the bun is always soft and fresh. As for the beef... It's the juiciest most flavorful burger I've ever had. It is always cooked perfectly to order, and is amazingly well put together. 

I would recommend this to anyone who wants what burgers are supposed to be.
Terrible store. I second the reviewer who called this guy a stereotypical used car salesman.   Avoid at all costs.

Delicious food, simple menu, great looking baked goods out for dessert . . . I feel bad for the person who didn't enjoy the decor. The idea of Sketch Burger is that it's a small restaurant where the walls (and tabletops) are covered by sketches that you make as you eat. I personally loved this idea, and the more I looked around at the work of those who had eaten and sketched there, the more I liked what I saw. There is some serious creativity on display, with some great humor as well. This place is a bit pricey, but I definitely enjoyed eating here.
I love Sushi.  Shiroi Hana is OK. There's nothing wrong with it at all and the prices are about average.  It's getting an extra star though for being well slick looking inside.

Macayos may not be the Mexican food I grew up on but it is delicious! Chips and salsa are complimentary. Their salsa and chips are soooo good. The first time we went our son couldn't get enough. He was just under a year  old and wouldn't touch anything spicy but he was  literally drinking out of the salsa bowl!!Their rolled taquitos appetizer is a meal in itself! The chicken is even full of flavor whereas most other restaurant flauta or rolled taco filling can be flavorless but not these! They are extra crisp and fun of flavor the sauce they add on top makes it over the top! We also love their chicken tortilla soup! Shredded chicken, tomatoes, green chilies avocado, cheese and tortilla strips on top! The spinach con queso dip is also a must have! Their chimis are absolutely the best! I regret not trying their carne asada chimi for so long. I thought no way would it be good since it isn't a spot that I consider authentic but I was super impressed! The carne asada in the chimi is really good quality steak! Not chewy at all and perfectly seasoned! They fill the chimi with Pico and top with their spinach con queso (that I love just not on my chimi) I always ask for red sauce and cheese like a classic red enchilada because even though I love the spinach con queso I prefer it as a dip with their fresh chips. It has so much flavor it would drown out all the other deliciousness in the chimi! Anything we've ordered from here has always been delicious. They recently added some new Chiles rellenos that I can't wait to try! When I do I will post pics and weigh in because  Chile rellenos are my favorite!! Highly recommend this restaurant, it's a great place to hang out with family or just to have a nihht out with the girls/guys for drinks and apps! Pretty sure they have happy hour and app specials too! Be sure to ask your server!

My family and I came here instead of waiting at another local restaurant and the food was really great. I would recommend the green chili tamales with the Baja sauce. That Baja stuff is to die for. My husband had the carne asada chimi, which had an amazing cheese sauce over it. The kids menu featured items all under $5 and they were really great portions! Our servers name was Lori. I would recommend you sit in her section if at all possible. She was very attentive and sweet. This restaurant also had a great patio, which we would've used but it was a touch to windy that day. We will be back!
It's an unassuming sushi restaurant in the heart of Philly. The house Shiroi Hana roll was super tasty. Definitely worth coming back for more sushi.

Very solid and very interesting burger joint in Fishtown. They've got kobe beef and smashed onion, but I'd reccomend the regular sirloin cut. Got a beautiful burger from there a week or two ago, advacado, pepperjack cheese, chipotle sauce, onions. Shit was scrumptious! 

Sides sound delicious too, but I can't stray from the burger and fries when I go. Nice music, nice decor, crayons and shit for the kiddies. 

Only negative... a bit pricey. That burger above I spoke of, cheese fries, and a coke came to 16 bucks for one person. C'mon now.
This was my favorite Mexican restaurant when visiting Tucson.  I try to go at least once every time I'm in town.  This past year seems to have gone downhill a little.  I'd still recommend them!

Incredible sushi!  Especially enjoyed the double eel roll and SST hand roll.  Food is incredible.  Beer options could be better, and would be nice to have an unfiltered sake option without having to buy a whole bottle.  But still highly recommend.

If you're a vegan in Philly, you need to know about Sketch!  We moved here last summer, and we wanted to know: where is the best veggie burger?  Where is some great vegan ice cream?  We've been in search of both for months, with lots of disappointment.  The weird ice cream flavors and consistency at Little Baby's really turned us off, and we've had some "homemade veggie burgers" at joints in the city that were seriously weird--mushy, lumpy, ew.  

Sketch was a pleasant surprise.  The food is awesome--great vegan black bean burger or seitan sandwich, with vegan long roll--and the service is great.  Our server was sweet and cheerful and attentive.  We got to draw pictures while we ate.  And the VEGAN MILKSHAKES WERE THE BOMB.  They came in regular flavors (chocolate, vanilla, cookies n cream, mint chocolate chip, peanut butter, etc)--with lots of choices.  We will definitely be back.  Awesome.

Another thoughtfully run establishment by the matriarch of Canvas Coffee Company, located just across the street, as fate would have it!  Phyllis' creations have proven delish at Canvas, so I thought it my duty to check this place out as soon as it opened.

Where Canvas has found a wonderful niche in this Port Fishington community of business men/women, artists, musicians, tightly tapered jean wearing scads of patrons, Sketch is something new...and satisfying.  

By walking through the brightly checkered doorway, you'd think at first glance that it was simply a down home burger and shake shop.  But it's vegan friendly folks, with choices for the carnivore, veggie goer, and vegan palate.  It boasts a unpretentious menu, with the standard choices of Kobe beef, turkey, boneless chicken breast, and smashed onion.  But where it hits the mark for drool worthiness is the freshness and quality of meats.  All the ingredients are freshly made and never frozen.  There are also plenty of homemade sauces, toppings, and cheeses to help make your samich a signature one.  

Then there are the shakes...woo!  Definitely worth the calories, y'all.  And again, there are vegan options for the cow lovers.  I myself, partake in the real milk jawns, and they are pretty damn tasty.

This is a fairly straight forward concept for an eatery, but if it's hearty food that you crave, then your belly will be thanking you after a meal here.  I had the special tonight, which was a tangy saitan sandwich.  By saying that the roll was packed to the gills with innards is an understatement.  You get a lot of what you order.  That sandwich was busting with a whole lotta veggie-lover's meat.  Juicy and seasoned well.  I recommend Sketch to anyone looking for a good burger, and is willing to try it with a twist.  

I'll definitely be back for more!

i think the yelpers are dead on.  if anything epitomizes a four-star place it is sketch.  the food is above average i would say.  the decor is damn cute and makes me want to linger for hours.  service is super-friendly - great little addition to the neighborhood and an owner that is not afraid of color for sure!!!  you'll see what i mean when you walk in there.

First off, I want to say that in my experience, the service was really good here.  Everything was quick and the waitress was helpful and friendly.  I ordered a turkey burger while my boyfriend got the smashed onion burger.  

        The fries came out first, and they were really good.  Fresh, hot, and nice and crispy.  Real french fries.  My turkey burger looked good, but neither my boyfriend or I liked the strange taste it had.  It must have been whatever they seasoned it with.  Oh well.  My boyfriend enjoyed his smashed onion burger though.  We both agreed that the bun it was one was nice.  

      I like the crayons and chalk and the cheesy pictures on the walls.  Some of the drawings were pretty decent, and we were amused while waiting the short time for our food.  

    I would try Sketch again, but this time I think I'd opt for the veggie burger.  My only big complaint is the prices.  It seems a bit high.  I agree with some of the earlier reviews about charging $1 for bacon or cheese $1 for onions or mushrooms, isn't really a fair trade.  You can really run up your bill by putting stuff on your burger.  Also, I always order water because that's what I drink.  I feel bottled water is silly and a waste of money when we live in a country with safe, good tasting tap water.  Here the drinks are only bottled, so I had to get one, which was a bit annoying.

Sketch is one of those places where I am ok with  taking in a magnanimous amount of calories. It's just that good. Even if the food was terrible I would still give this place a thumbs up because the staff there are so ridiculously nice. Definitely go here ,especially if you can get down with a good vegan burger ( which I can). Do it you will love it!

Burger to the face!

I am not much of a carnivore but the cyclops burger certainly makes me thankful we kill cows. Fried egg, horseradish cheddar cheese, and plenty of vegan BBQ sauce makes for an excellent savory meal. 

Green chili cheese fries...nom nom nom. Just get them and thank me later. 

Oh, if you suck at drawing, please try to get your sketches on the wall. Mine are terrible and if the overall quality can just keep decreasing, then maybe mine will get on some day. 

The only gripe is that they need to clean the place a bit more. The tables were pretty sticky on two separate visits here and the waiter needs to wash his hands! 

Otherwise, good food, and a great joint to take some carnivores, perhaps even your dog can share a table with you. Dig in!

I can't speak for the burgers, but I can sing at the top of my lungs for the Dr. Pepper Pulled Pork.

I never realized that heaven could be found piled high on a biscuit, but it can be and IT IS!

Every Thursday my friends and I get together for Fat Kids' Thursday where we gorge on all the sinful things you shouldn't the other 6 days of the week and based on YELP reviews, we went here.

Holy Balls of Awesome. This was a true Fat Kid's delight complete with fresh handcut fries and Green Goddess dressing for a diptastic adventure. 

The only downside for me is that I'm a South Phillyist and this was quite a hike, but we ordered when we got there and everything was done in 20 minutes. We were there for dinner 'rush' which was more of a mild meander, so you should be fine during high traffic times.

We have one Veggie in our group who died over the terriyaki seitan. The sandwich was the size of her head and completely awesome. 

TL;DR - There is nothing sketchy about this place. It is the perfect illustration of deliciousness and adventure with short wait times and lots of Veggie selections.

This is my second time here at Solid Grindz. I would like to say that their customer service is on point! The workers are very kind, the restaurant itself is also clean. The jams they play makes the atmosphere relaxing. Now let me talk about their food. DE-LI-CIOUS!  I've tried many of their dishes and it's good. The portion is big so I hope you brought your A game since you will be leaving stuffed and satisfied. Also who could resist some good spam masubi. I have not tried their pho yet, but when I do, I'll be back with another review. Enjoy your eats here!

Hands down as they ahould be awarded for
best burger in town.   I just didnt like the parking situation.  Their burgwrs ate huge and fries arent needed to fill you up!
Went there today for the first time. A little pricey, but worth it. We didn't have to wait long at all. Me and my husband walked in and sat right away.

Went during lunch time and it was pretty quiet. Ordered a special roll (salmon salsa?) and a salmon sashimi. They were good but not great, and for the price, especially at lunch, thought it wasn't a great value. The lunch specials are the very boring standard ones, so for ordering the same thing, seems better to go at dinner. Food was fast, waitress was good, so no real complaints
Being raised around Hawaiian food as a kid, this place definitely hits the spot.  The bang shrimp with their secret sauce is unbelievable.  Highly recommend this place over Mama's.

Great Hawaiian food.  I had the spam musubi, which was a great comb of sweet and salty.  The shrimp pad Thai had the right amount of spicy for a non spice consumer like myself.  My nose is running as I write the this.  Also had the chicken teriyaki, which was only slightly burnt.

Excellent.  Writing a review so that I can easily find this place next time I'm in Philly.

Favorite was the spicy tuna handroll.  Was not mushy...had fresh tuna with a small amount of spicy mayo.  

Also, loved the Saki Martini.  Refreshing and tasty (b/c I'm not a saki fan)/

Sushi craving satisfied. But is this place more of a lunch location?

Don't be fooled... the hours say that it's open starting at 5PM on Fridays, but it doesn't open until 5:30. My manfriend and I went there last Friday night at 5:35 and nobody was there. In fact, the host had to check his watch to make sure it was time to open. It was oddly quiet the whole time we were there.

Our server was incredibly friendly, and she didn't even flinch when I had no idea what the towels were for that she brought out upon our arrival. For those of you that don't know--the damp towels are for wiping off your hands if you wish. In the summer they are served cold, and in the winter they are served warm. Pretty neat.

The sushi we ordered was definitely delicious. We got a California Roll, the Island Roll, the Rolls Royce, and a Spider Roll. The balance on each was very well executed. The Spider Roll was particularly interesting... it tasted like they cooked the soft-shell crab in some sort of broth before it was tempura'd. Super interesting and tasty. The Island Roll had this delicious wasabi tobiko on it, and the mango didn't overpower the salmon at all.

The fish was incredibly fresh and everything was presented well. Everything cost as much as I expected it to. Sushi is never a cheap trip, but the manfriend and I made it out the door for $20 per person. Not bad!

Cool, retro, hip burger joint on Girard with a colorful interior and customer-drawn pictures on the wall.

While the booths are roomy, the space insight is a bit tight, as you walk through an aisle between tables/booths, and to the back, where the server's counter is.  I wasn't sure if we had to order at the counter or if we just sit and the waiter would take our order (fyi, it's the latter).

We sat at the booth and I think there was only guy running the whole show that night, and it was relatively busy, but he did a good job and kept a great attitude.  We decided to split three things:

Veggie Burger - honestly, terrible. I've had a lot of veggie burgers in my day, and while their 12 grain black bean burger is unique and homemade, it was extremely dry, too fat/lumpy for the bread/sandwich, and carelessly put together.  We split the burger, and not sure if this is how they normally come because he cut it in half for us, but all of the fixings came on the side, and the bread and cheese ended up sticking to the patty and we couldn't take either bread off without making a complete mess to add on the toppings (lettuce, tomato, onion, pickle).  It ended up being a complete mess.  Even with the sauces, which are OK at best, the dryness of the burger didn't taste good.

Cheese Fries - fries are decent, and they're cut thicker than normal (not steak), and lightly seasoned.  The cheese itself was a weird texture...I think it's hard to get cheese fries right because of the texture cheese becomes when it goes from hot to cold (which happens too quickly).

Peanut Butter Milkshake - if there's one thing they do well, it's their milkshakes...this one was great!  Not super thick or chunky, and there was a nice blend and balance of peanut butter.  We wanted cookies n cream, but they were out.

Overall, I think the prices for the burgers are good, but their fries and milkshakes are overpriced.

I have seen Sketch come up on three of the best burger in Philadelphia lists (and all pretty high up) so we decided to head over to give it a try . Sketch is on Frankford Ave. in the Northern Liberties/Fishtown area of the city. We were able to find parking across the street on Frankford Ave.

The restaurant is pretty small, there is one table out front and seating for about 20 inside. Sketch is a cool, clean and  funky place.The decor is simple and very casual with plain bench type tables. The walls are decorated by hamburger art drawn by the patrons. Specials are on the wall on a chalk board. There were a ton of hipsters there on the Saturday we chose. Its all good to me as variety makes the world go round. I am amazed how much this section of the city is changing and all of the new building.

Back to Sketch, everything is made to order and on a busy Saturday evening, there were 4 people working including the cooks. Our waitress was great and very efficient. She would constantly let people know how long the wait was for booth take out and eat in.  The take out was up to 45 minutes by the time we left, but that didn't seem to daunt customers. Be patient at Sketch, you will be rewarded.

We had the Cyclops, the Onion burger and the Lamb burger special plus Belgian style fries and Sweet potato fries. The fries came out first and the Belgian fries were probably the best I have ever had. They were hot, and crispy with great seasoning. Sketch gives choices of unique dipping sauces also for the fries. My Cyclops was really good, the burger was perfect and the bacon and egg were also tasty. The bun was great too and not soggy at all. The Lamb burger had great seasoning with a hint of mint and the onion burger was very good too. Sketch is definitely up there with best burgers in the city. The prices are reasonable especially compared to Village Whiskey, Rogue. etc. for burgers. They had some nice looking home made desserts but I surrendered after the burger and fries. We were in food coma.

Sketch is CASH only so bring hard currency.

We waited around 45min still no food. Someone came to apologize for the wait, fine that's cool. A few minutes later still no food and they offered free milk shakes, myself and a buddy are lactose intolerant. We asked if we can get half off the burgers to make up for the wait and was given a full refund. 1 hour into this thinking we're going to get a meal still for waiting over1 god damn hour. What kind of business refuses to take care of their customers after their incompetency. Word? your manager refuses to serve us since we're given a full refund?  This place is CHALK
Bigger burger than you'd ever imagine.  Looking forward to coming back and trying something else.  I had the special, beef burger with fried green tomatoes and L,T and comeback sauce.

We had my daughters Graduation party here and I am so glad we did! We had nothing but stellar service from the manager & staff. 

Before booking the party I called several restaurants. What stood out to me about about Macayos is when my husband and I went to speak to Jim the manager, he was very accommodating! He told us if we can vision it, they will do their best to make it happen. Alot of other restaurants I called their customer service wasn't even close to our experience at Macayos. 

We invited over 40 guests and did the plated dinner menu and got to choose 5 items on our menu. Which I was impressed compared to other restaurants where they didnt have as many. The food was delicious and the portion sizes were much more than we expected. 

I have to give a shout out to the wait staff.  We didn't have to wait long for food and drinks and they were so awesome! My husband was very impressed with the mgr. He kept checking up on us to make sure everything was going well from the air temperature to making sure everyone was happy.  I want to add that they even let us bring in our own Mariachis! 

All of our guests had a wonderful time and we had a very memorable evening.  Thank you Macayos!

People are going to think I'm a lying chauvinist but they are fools who speak nonsense and I'll cuff them about their ears with nary a second thought.

Sketch is my local burger place and it is the greatest.  The folk-art drawings adorning the walls are wonderful and fascinating and the burgers are the best on the East Coast.  The People are great artists; they make lovable, whimsical sketches of great beauty even though the crayons and markers provided are sub-par.  I guess it's part of the challenge.

Let me tell you what's not sub-par.  These are great burgers and it's easy to get one for as little as $6.95 but definitely under $10.  Unless you get the Kobe in which case you are a wealthy, richie-rich plutocrat who probably wipes her bum with Franklins and money is no object.  Even so, it'll be under $12 for a reeeeally fancy hamburger.  I am also pleased that they don't use those stupid sweet cotton buns that you would get at McDonald-BKing-Wendy's.

The tiny shoebox of an establishment is bursting with talent and juicyburgers.  Planet Earth is filled with mediocrity but not at Sketch.

Been a Terminal customer for many years and the good folks at Martins 
always have a great selection of quality meats. From the renowned links to the NY strips .
When grilling with friends  , I'm always asked .. Where did you get these ?

Oh my sketchburger.

This is a small place in Fishtown that really packs deliciousness inside a burger.

Today a friend and I got a cyclops burger (essentially a glorified bacon cheeseburger with an egg on top) and a Dr. Pepper Pulled Pork Burger. 

You get to choose your own cheese and egg prep

Also SWEET POTATO FRIES! 1 pound of sweet potato fries in any sauce you want.

I've been here multiple times and the Kobe beef burger is also great.

but dont forget the fries.

They were both really good and the taste still lingers as I write this review at home.

Its cash only now so bring some cash! unless you want to use the ATM machine.

I'm really not a fan of this place.  My friends love it, though.  I strongly dislike the vegan burger.  My friends loved this green chile cheese, which sounded extremely unappealing to me, and then I saw it(scary).  The green chile cheese is super thick cheese sauce with green chunks in it.  I should give them two stars for their huge array of burgers/shakes( vegan and non)and lovely staff, but..... ok I will change it from one.  Nope, just changed my mind again...the bill was outrageous.

The best veggie burger in the city is from Memphis tap, as I recall.
if you want a mouthgasm eat these burgers. best god damn thing ever. and the fries. and the shakes.

Big, messy, GLORIOUS veggie burgers (actually vegan!) that make missing eating meat a thing of the past. Add some of their delicious salty fries (served in a cool cone-thing with two sides of sauce), crayons, and goofy puns all over the walls, and this is one of the greatest places ever. You can get milkshakes either vegan or regular, and astoundingly both are delicious. 

The only negative I can think of is that they charge you for onion on your burger (?) and they only bring you water if you ask, but it's definitely worth it.

I'll give respect to any place that cooks their fries properly. If making french fries was as simple and cutting them up and dropping them in some frying oil, we'd all be making awesome fries at home. They are cut, soaked, and then blanched. And then they're fried to order. Delicious! And they furnish you with rich dipping sauces to add a little more unhealthy goodness to your meal. 

Speaking of unhealthy, this was a giant burger! I had the smashed onion burger with horseradish cheddar. I ordered it medium rare and it came out perfectly medium rare. I could tell it was a nice juicy burger because it ruined my brand new Flyers shirt. But I consider that acceptable collateral damage. 

I've noticed a couple of common complaints. One of them pertains to wait times. I agree it was a bit poky, but the fact remains that it takes a while to cook a giant burger. Go throw one on the grill and see if you can have it ready in 5 minutes without turning it into a charcoal briquette. Another has to do with accurate doneness of the burger. I can't speak to that. Mine was perfect, but things happen when burgers are cooked to order. The final one related to the burger 'not being seasoned enough'. This is a point of contention, but I personally feel the flavor of the meat has to speak for itself. If you're putting anything in there aside from salt and pepper, you're making a meatloaf. Just saying. 

Anyway, it was a delicious and (probably too) hearty meal! 

Go get a sketch burger!

This place is so cool! The walls are covered in creative customer artwork all dedicated to burgers. My fav is the turkey burger with mushrooms and bbq sauce and the fries are deliciously potato filled :-P

Maybe it was because we came in so late, but i dont get what the big deal is.  I like shake shack alot more.  The restaurant is really cute and small and i like that they post up original art done by their patrons.

The atmosphere at this place is homey and fun. You can grab your own drink from the fridge and sit down to "sketch" a drawing to add to the covered walls. It's a small establishment with charm and good food. I love the fries and trying new sauces to dip them in. It is cash only, which I don't mind especially as they have an ATM.

Amazing. Some of the best Japanese food I've ever had, and I eat A LOT of Japanese food. I ordered the age tofu to start and it was PERFECT. The presentation was spectacular and the actual tofu was lightly breaded and had an excellent sauce underneath. For the main course I ordered the teriyaki salmon lunch box. It came with these Japanese dumplings that I would risk my life for, a nice salad with a ginger dressing, a california roll which was not the best I've had but certainly not the worst, and of course, the teriyaki salmon. The box that it came in was very nice and had little paintings on the side and everything fit nicely. The salmon was unlike any salmon I've had before. The fish just melted in your mouth. As for the dumplings as I said before, I would risk my life over having another one of these. The salad was a nice break from the saucy food and the sushi was so-so. And the bill for 2 was only $32! All in all 6/5

Great lunch special! I ordered the udon soup special for take-out, which comes with a California roll. The soup was a large portion and very tasty. The California roll was extremely fresh. And only $10! I've walked by this place a million times but have never gone in. The inside was very cozy and decorated beautifully. I'll be back to dine-in soon!

Let me start by saying that I love burgers and have tried almost every burger in the area suck as Sketch, PYT, dog and bull, red robin, Kraftwork and more. Dog and bull is still my favorite but this place is solid. Great burgers and fries without all the crazy BS fancy burgers at PYT that come with a high cost. I would absolutely come back here for a delicious treat. The cyclops burger was fantastic! Great for kids but not big groups as I think the place can only fit about 20 total.
Great eats with great flavored meats!! Bring a friend or bring the entire family, just bring your appetite!
I've only had the terayki chicken there because it is delicious. The portion sizes are generous. You'll have enough to each more later. The staff is very friendly and the prices are right.

Good sushi for what you are paying for. It also has very chic decor and very quiet ambient which would make a great date spot.

My boyfriend and I stopped by for dinner on a Wednesday night. We started with some seaweed salad. They gave us a good amount of salad, considering how much it would cost in supermarket. I got Shiroi Hana roll and Rock 'n roll. I loved the Rock 'n roll. Two rolls are definitely enough for one person. 

To finish up our dinner, we got the tempura green tea ice cream. It took a while for them to bring it up but it's totally worth it. It was probably the best fried ice cream I have ever had! It's a solid ice cream ball in the middle which is surrounded by a light fried coat. Nom nom nom...

I cannot wait to go back there to get the tempura ice cream again!

I love this place so much.  Yes, it can be a bit expensive, but it's very much worth it.  I tried the ELK burger this weekend and it was awesome!  The vegan milkshakes are also great, seeing as I'm completely lactose intolerant.

One of my top 3 burger joints in all of Philadelphia. No need to go to those over-priced, fancy gastropubs to get quality burgers. You can get a juicy, perfectly cooked burger of choice for ~$10. Put on your sauce and cheese of choice, and egg if you desire, and enjoy a piece of heaven. 

This place also houses the best sweet potato fries I've ever had. Their regular fries are amazing as well. 

I'm glad I don't live in fishtown because I'd be obese from eating here every day.

The food is soooooo good and will leave you stuffed for days!
You gotta try the green chili cheese fries.

Going down hill.  When my family first tried this place it was awesome.  The prices were always on the hefty side.  It's hard to pay about 30 bucks for 2 burgers a fries but we figured to hell with it because its good food.  Then more and more it became not worth the price.  I always get the same thing.  Cyclops burger cooked medium.  They really need to figure out their timing.  Maybe twice has my burger been cooked to medium.  It's either completely cooked or raw. I just ordered food from here a few days ago for pickup.  I got the cyclops burger, and a bacon cheese burger both cooked to medium.  One burger was on the medium side, the other was raw.  It doesn't make sense to have one be raw in the same order.  The bacon on both burgers were under cooked.  It was rubbery.  My cyclops burger also had no egg.  That's what makes it a cyclops burger.  

Also, to the owners, I recommend you let people who are coming in for a pick up to pay while they wait.  Anytime I come for pick up I can't pay until my food is finished and then my food is stuck just sitting on the counter because I haven't paid yet and now I'm waiting in the line of other people paying or placing orders.  By the time I pay, my food has been sitting there for 10 minutes or more.  Then by the time I get home, the food is almost cold and the fries are soft from steaming in the bag.  We have come back multiple times hoping for the off chance it's good again but we just can't bring ourselves to keep throwing away over 30 bucks on food that just ends up being disappointing.

Meh... a cool, but tiny, burger joint with difficult parking and a bit of a wait. 

I split a green chili cheese fries with a friend. If it was based purely on this I'd have given them a 4 or a 5. These were flavorful with a strong chili flavor, a must have.

The burger... that was a bit underwhelming. I ordered the truffle butter burger which came with onions and a stingy swipe of truffle butter. The waitress recommended chopped onions so I added that as well. I had the meat prepared medium rare and it came out perfectly cooked. Unfortunately, it was pretty flavorless.

The butter had a bit of the truffle flavor, but there wasn't quite enough in there. The bun was good and chewy and the meat was cooked well, but I didn't really get much flavor from my mess of a burger. I was a fan of the consistency and how moist it was, but there was no strong fat or grilled flavor from the meat. 

My dining companion ordered a $5 milky way milk shake which was pretty delicious. I had two spoonfulls of that decadent gluttony.

I didn't like eating Japanese food; I don't think that's delicious. Half years ago, it was the first time for my girl friend and I to ate at Shiroi Hana. I didn't like this restaurant, but they were very different between the outside and inside. You will think this is a small bar, but this is very warm inside. I was felt comfortable by the yellow lights; these wooden chairs and desks made me fell like home, it's very good for date; some mirrors would make you fell here is bigger. This place wasn't good at decoration, but they still make you comfortable. 
First of all I want to introduce their food. I ordered a lot, but I didn't order a lot one time, I can't pay for that. They were not expensive but it's also not that kind of cheap. I ordered some sashimi, a roll, a unadom, and a beef sukiyaki and green tea ice cream. Let me introduce the yellow tail roll first. It's my first time to eat yellow tail. This was very delicious. The fresh yellow tail with vegetable and good rice was the food very hard to be found in Philly. The unadom was a kind of ell over rice. I love ell very much. This is only one thing what I love in Japanese food. I had to say this will never make you upset. This ell looked very good; when they were over the rice what I can say is awesome. However the beef sukiyaki was not good. It just liked a soup and that's it. Please don't order that, it's not cheap. Next one is the main point - the sashimi. I ordered some salmon, octopus, red snappers, tunas and shrimps. All of them were very delicious and fresh. Expect red snappers was tasted not good enough, it's too fat. Let's begin with salmons. These salmons were fresh, but they were not the best. The others were very awesome. By the way they have two kinds of shrimp, one of them is sweet shrimp, this was small shrimp and not fresh; the other one was bottom shrimp, this was very good and fresh. I won't forgive that, if I have chance.  
  

And then we ordered something more. This was a nice try. I mean this one surprise us. We want to try something more so we ordered black cod. This is a kind of fish, which lives in South Pole. They have a fat. Shiroi Hana's chef smoked it but they still keep this fish's original flavor. What I can see is if they don't char that, this will be very good. In the end I advise you ordered the green tea ice cream that will surprise you.
Second, I will talk about the service. I have to say their service is so so. Sometimes the service was very good. However sometimes I just wanted to leave. When an old Japanese woman services you, you are very lucky. If she doesn't service you, I have to say, "Please don't be angry." 
That's all the reason I think you should go to Shiori Hana.
This is delicious food with good size portions for a great price, and you can't lose when they're always playing reggae over the speaker system!

As you can probably tell when you walk into the restaurant, Sketch is a place with character. This was equally true for the woman who took our order and served us our food. Service was wonderful and she was super friendly.

I thought that the burger was meh. Sure, it's big, but I thought the meat was actually a bit dry. The fries on the other hand, and the different sauces, are pretty good.

This review is for the S.S. Franklin Fountain at the Spruce St. Harbor Park.

Product: 3/5
Service: 1/5

Ice cream was okay. I tasted the peanut butter/vanilla, vanilla bean, and mango sorbet (although this seemed to really annoy the woman helping me). Her service alone made me never want to come back to S.S. Franklin Fountain. 

But then...add the ridiculously long wait, post-order (for ice cream) and the sick, sniffling, nose wiping ice cream handler...ick...and we've hit a new low.

Other people around me also waiting way too long for ice cream post-order, were just as disgusted as I was with this sniffling mess of an ice scream server.

Not impressed.

I spend time in Hawaii so it is nice to get a taste of it here in Tucson.  I went with a group of friends.  You order at the counter and they bring your meal to you.   I had the pulled pork, a dish I often have in Hawaii and I found it to be quite good.  They have some Asian dishes as well and a couple of people had the pad thai and thought it was very good.  Everyone in our group seemed to really like their meal.  You can order Hawaiian rolls with your meal for an additional price if you wish but mine wasn't real fresh.  The portions are large and prices are reasonable.  It's a casual place-a bit difficult to find-I drove past it and so did a couple of others.  It's a green building and if you watch for it, you will find it-it is just after 22nd on the west side of Craycroft.

Finally, a good (and affordable) sushi restaurant in Philly. The ikura was excellent, as was the sunonomo.

Also, I really appreciated that the chefs spoke Japanese. 

Gochisosama deshita!

Dr Pepper pulled pork???
SOLD!
Add a coconut/strawberry milkshake up in there and I'm good.

Shake = large, coconutty, good
Sandwich = Nice! Not overpowering but good sauce, fatty/juicy meat, just enough sauce (kinda), yummy bun but not enough for all that meat!, had to save HALF!
Fries w aoili = fries were just okay, aoili--slightly spicy aftertaste

Loved all the drawings everywhere on construction paper! There were some super creative ones!

Think I'd try the truffle butter burger during my next visit.

We had dinner here during Labor Day weekend and enjoyed it. I ordered the Hardcore Sushi and my dinner mates had various a la carte sushi, ume (chicken teriyaki bento box), the sake don (salmon sashimi over seasoned rice), and seared tuna & avocado dish. We also had some fried ice cream and mochi ice cream for dessert. 

All of the food was quite good and the fish tasted fresh. The major problem was that the food took a really long time to come. I'm generally not too fussy about service, but the order took forever. We had to tell the server several times to bring food for the kids first because they were getting really hungry and cranky. As the food dribbled in, we all waited for the last person to get his food, which was roughly 50 minutes. By that time, most of our hot food (soup, teriyaki, etc.) had gotten luke warm or cold. 

The restaurant didn't seem to be especially busy; there were a few open tables. And we had read other Yelp reviews saying that service was efficient. So we were mystified by the long wait.

All in all, the food was pretty good and the service was a bit lackluster, though the server was very apologetic. I would certainly come again to give them another chance.

I really like their fries dipped in the harissa aioli.  I love the harissa aioli.  As for the burgers, they are huge and darn delicious, though I can rarely finish one if I order fries. I usually get the smashed onion burger, with the aioli, bacon, and horseradish cheddar, no lettuce and tomato.  I've ordered with lettuce and tomato before and I feel like it makes the already huge and kinda messy burger a little too messy and hard to eat.  I also ordered without bacon once and I found the burger to be a little meh, but it may have just been an off night or something.  Or maybe bacon really does make everything better, I'm not going to test that theory by ordering without bacon again.  The only real problem I've had with the place has been getting a burger cooked how I like it.  I like my burgers medium rare.  They seem to have a hard time achieving that.  Most times I've gotten a burger that has been quite rare, a little too rare.  I've attempted ordering medium, thinking maybe that would do the trick, but then it's been too cooked.  The burgers are still tasty either way, but I'd love to order and get a true medium rare burger.  In addition to the burger and fries, I've also ordered the mac and cheese on several occasions and the Dr. Pepper pulled pork sandwich once.  The mac and cheese is peppery, I happen to like black pepper on everything, so this works for me; cheesy, peppery, and yummy.  I like it best when it's cooled a little and the cheese sauce has more of a creamy texture.  The Dr. Pepper pulled pork was good as well, but maybe a little too sweet for me.  I'm really not a sweet person though, so I think that's just me.  I think it would have been awesome with some type of slaw on it.  The pork was great, even if I did find the sauce too sweet for me, the buns they use are awesome, the option of some slaw might make the sandwich for me.  Sadly, I have yet to try one of their shakes, but I plan to fix that soon!

Really good fresh sushi, great location, and nice atmosphere...good date spot.  The staff was really nice and friendly, with pretty prompt service.  Favorite rolls were Shiroi-hana roll and sashimi roll.  A bit expensive, but definitely worth it.

Was looking for a good sushi spot near Rittenhouse Square and found one just a few blocks from my noon meeting. Shiroi Hana is a nice cozy low key lunch spot with a friendly staff and a chill environment. I ordered the Island Roll first which has one of my favorite combos: salmon and mango! Its the perfect fresh pairing in/on a roll in my opinion. Next I had the Seaweed Sal-sa which was an awesome unique creation: three pieces of sashimi (tuna, salmon & yellowtail) wrapped around seaweed and topped with masago and jalapeño. It was great and presented very well. I finished it off with my go to dessert, the tempura green tea ice cream and it was awesome as well. All around thumbs up and would definitely go back again and again!
We only buy our meats here.  My Irish wife got them to make bangers and they are spot on!  Top quality meats from some of the friendliest folks at the Reading Terminal!

I've come here a few times.  I've found the service to be okay most of the time.  The food is good; but just a smidge better than a taco shop. The decor is super bright and fun.

I appreciate that it's a Tucson staple.  Their margaritas are great.  

My critique is the dust.  You look up at the sun art in the dinning room and theirs dust from the vents.  If you're going to draw attention to a point with neat lighting, make sure it's clean.

My husband and I love his sub shop. We recently moved to Tucson and we tried it out as keep coming back! My husband is a big eater, but he gets filled up on just the half. My husband is a really tough cookie to please (I've cried a lot in the past! Lol) but he keeps saying "this is really so good!" He likes it better than any sandwich place. We've tried many on the menu and can't pick which is our favorite!! You've got to try it!! 

Also, the owner had been here each time. He personally makes the sandwiches and brings it to us. He also stops by to make sure we like it! I really like this place and will definitely continue to come back. 

Always fresh and hot!!

I tried the shrimp and the beef it was good( a little sweet) however I got extremely sick for two days straight. Achey and other food serious poison symptoms I'd rather not describe in detail. The staff was wonderful but the overall vibe to the restauraunt wasn't my cup of tea. Will not return. The only reason I left three stars is because the girl behind the counter was a sweetheart.

you guys never seize to amaze me!! great toppings.  fries are awesome.  the cheese for the fries could have been a little better but everything else was amazing!!! I said the second money sign because of the amount of toppings one might want.  Kobe burger was incredible.

Great food and a wonderful staff!

My wife and I were visiting Tuscon and looking for a place to eat that would serve us a little later at night. We came in to eat around 9:55 PM, 5 minutes before closing, but Macayo's was more than willing to seat us and provide us with a meal. We ordered Patron margaritas (and got a cheese crisp on the house), which were DELICIOUS. We also ordered some combination plates and enchiladas, which were also fantastic.

The next day I realized I had left my credit card at the restaurant. I called them as early as possible and they were more than willing to look for my card and then mail it to my home in San Francisco. Thank you to Marissa and Robert for helping me and providing us with a great meal and beyond the call of duty service.

If you're in Fishtown, you need to eat here at least once.  The menu selections are always creative and delicious, and I have yet to eat here and be disappointed.  Their dessert options are also pretty great!

You should know, this food delicious. I showed up with coworkers and I had never eaten there. As is par for the course, I go to the front counter and ask,"Whats the go-to first time meal?" No hesitation, the lady at the counter says,"get the two meat plate with Teriyaki Chicken and Kalua Pulled Pork." So I got it with brown rice and a Hawaiian roll. It was amazing; juicy, flavorful, and a hefty portion.

If you love yourself even a little bit, get in your car and drive there right now. You're welcome, tastebuds.

I went here after Vic Sushi Bar, so unfortunately I can't give it 5 stars due to the prices being a little higher than Vic.  It was still really good though!

It chic inside with tons of seating (I didn't even realize the gigantic area upstairs with another bar until I had to use the restroom).

The seafood in the rolls was some of the most fresh and delicious I've had in a while, and the giant heaping quadrants of fried ice cream drizzled in chocolate sauce definitely didn't disappoint.

I'd definitely come back here for a nice, low-key dinner with a group of people, but there's other places with way cheaper sushi in the city.

Fantastic food.  Mongolian 'beef' dish was amazing. I'm a meat eater who is trying to expand my horizons. The food here is very convincing...

Bathrooms sketchy though. Clean them!!!!!!

Don't order from this location.  They will take your order, then 1 hour fifteen minutes later not deliver it and when you call say they are backed up and can't deliver it to your house.  Order anywhere but here.  We spoke to Mgr Naomi who talked to owner Debbie and they said sorry-it's our problem they can't deliver the pizzas.

finally got to check out this this new option of dining in the Fishtown area.  I am stoked to have a vegetarian friendly "burger joint".  Originally I was going to try the vegan burger but was enticed to try the seitan special.  Served on a yummy roll with the cheese puffs on the side.  it was super yummy!  I also somehow squeezed in a chocolate ($4.50) shake.  also delish.... but a bit pricey.

anyway, this is the place to go if you are a vegetarian seeking the hearty fill of a meaty sandwich.  I don't eat much meat nor do i crave it usually but  i think it would delight even the meatiest of meat eaters.  :)

i wouldn't recommend you to eat here every night unless you like to truly load on the calories... it is not a super health food place but it is definitely a great place when you have that "burger & cheese puff" craving. (truth be told, i could live without the cheese puffs, but i give them and A for trying and for breaking up the monotony.)  

the ambiance is great too.  simple, dim & fun (chalkboards are cool!).  the staff is wonderful as well!

'Dis place broke da mouf! Good food, friendly service, reasonable prices. I wish they served laulau! I haven't been there since they moved to the new location, but I really enjoyed the food. Family-owned, local business - money stays local.

Udon is my Japanese comfort food of choice.  It's how I rank a Japanese joint.  These guys do it pretty well! Personally though, I think they'd do better if they didn't strive to be a fancy modern restaurant, their space is better suited to be a hole in the wall gem.

Great quality sausages and meats for a decent price. They had chicken, hamburgers and such. The beef bacon is da bomb!!!

We were traveling back to Virginia and they got us an ice pack for our order. Service is top notch and we cannot wait to get track there. Great place!!!

After living in California all my life this is the best Mexican food I've had in Tucson. It's always consistent. I recommend the shredded beef crunchy taco and chicken enchilada combination plate. The taco is very good!! The enchilada is quite delicious also but I order mine easy on the sauce. Service is good and the food comes out quick.
Awesome food I had a Cyclops burger fantastic and the belgian fries great must try for all those in the mood for a great burger
Very good sushi.  Very good fried ice cream.  Excellent service. Very nice decor.  A little pricey.  I would definitely go back.

My daughter is an Owl at Temple University.  She knows I enjoy a good burger so she took me the Sketch Burger.  This place is in Fishtown.  The place is pretty eclectic, apparently you can draw things and it may get put on the wall.  So we ordered burgers and fries. The fries were amazing!  My burger was juicy and fresh.  I would have preferred a little more salt, but is was good.  The fries were definitely the star!  
They have novelty sodas and good juices and teas as well. Make sure you bring cash! Or you can use their ATM machine.

Upstairs is quiet for groups.  Went there on a Wednesday night, they held our reservation though we were late.  Sashimi was fresh and tasty, especially the snapper and tuna.  Sushi in both rolls and nigiti forms was well made and prompt.  Japanese beers included a good weisbier from Hitachi,; sake was also available both cold and warm. as well as the usual Sapporp, Asahi, etc.  All in all we had a good time, nice service.  Only one negative--like most American sushiya, they serve the soup before, rather than with or after, the entrees as it is in Japan.

Martin's is a veritable sausage fest; in a good way!
Fantastic sausage selection. 
Friendly and patient butchers.  
It doesn't matter whether you are buying 1 pound of one kind or 1 pound of 10 different kinds. They are happy help you. 
We drive from central New Jersey just to load up on their sausage.

We love this place, we are from out of town and do a lot of research on restaurants ahead because I am Gluten Free. We LOVE this place. They have Fresh Baked Gluten Free Bread! My sub was fresh and delicious. I appreciate the effort it takes to bake GF bread daily and consider it a treat as other restaurants rely heavily on ready made breads from GF bread bakers which are okay but not fresh baked. Give this place a try!
My daughters favorite restaurant. She loves the hand rolls and special rolls. Nice BYOB. Hard to park in the area though. Other than that great place. Come check out this little gem!

Delicious, fresh, high-quality sushi. Great for a low-key dinner date or for takeout/delivery. Slightly more expensive than places like Fuji, but definitely higher quality fish.  People are friendly, efficient and professional. Highly recommend!

The best sub and sandwich place inside of the Market Place Area suitable for anyone! They offer some of most extensive vegan and vegetarian options in the zip code. Subs run around $9 for whole subs but they do have daily specials on weekdays. Like $6 veggie whole sub Thursdays. Incredible friendly and helpful staff. My coworkers love the meat options. Definitely recommend this place for any situation. Can't wait until they start stocking tempeh!

Just ate here on a hungover whim and boy was it the bomb.  A friend mentioned wanting to try this place and we did just that.  With hardly enough time to sit and eat we decided to call in for takeout.  Once we arrived there was a parking spot right out front and so we decided to eat in.  I got the Kobe burger with chipotle and some kind of horseradish cheese and fries that came with a side of Aioli to dip.  The fries were decent and the burger was decadent. The roll was perfect the meat was tender and juicy and delicious and the size was large, I couldn't even finish it.  And it was so good I decided to bring home the leftover to tear into as soon as I can make some room in this belly.  I recommend.

Me and a coworker ate here for the first time.  We each got the two meat plate.  Teriyaki chicken, Kalua Pork, and beef ribs.  Pork and chicken were great and good quantity.  Ribs were a little tough and I'd recommend several hours on a slow cook.  Salad was actually cabbage but the dressing was good.  Beans were pretty good as well.  The place does get busy so you might want to go early.

We were in the area and were looking for a local restaurant to try out, so glad we stopped here for dinner. Haven't had a Hawaiian treat in quite some time. We ordered the chicken with a side of salad.  The chicken was great and the sauce they provided was even better, but the salad was nothing special that you wouldn't find anywhere else and they use the same Hawaiian bread rolls you get at the grocery store. Overall great location for some authentic Hawaiian food.

Updating to 5 stars. Service and food quality has been consistent every time!
My go-to spot for island food.

Meat eaters and vegans alike can enjoy this cozy eatery of sorts.  

It should be noted that this place is cash only, but they do have an atm for the people who might forget sometimes *clears throat*.

I fancy their green goddess sauce as it compliments almost anything on the menu except maybe their amazing milkshakes.

Tried this spot a few months back and was disappointed with the lack of seasoning. Bland flavors on what otherwise taste like fresh ingredients and could have been great.

Duck burger with apple was on special, tried that with the cyclops that both were underwelming. Same with the fried Mac n cheese balls/bombs. 

It's as if they want to convince you that you don't need any salt because they highlight fresh ingredients. Instead it fails misreably making you crave a seasoned burger, despite being masked by the fun sketching concept and colorful walls. 

Concept and attentive staff merit- 2 stars.

I love Sketch!!!

-BEST BURGERS IN PHILLY BUT TRY SOMETHING ELSE TOO!!!!!!!

Everything is homemade and fresh like her Soups, Dumplings, Seitan, Mac & Cheese, Desserts , etc etc etc etc etc
One of my fave spots when visiting Philly. Minimal in terms of ambiance and location/size. Great sushi. Efficient service. Yummy saki. Solid!

There are several reasons that this place has a leg up on your run of the mill sushi joint.  (1) They serve alcohol, so you don't have to remember to BYOB.  (2) It's clean (no sticky tables and floors) and (3) nicely appointed with minimalist décor.  (4) They take credit cards, not cash only.  Seaweed salad and dumplings to start were good, standard fare - hard to mess up, and they were delicious as expected.  The sushi itself was fresh and pretty generously portioned.  It may be a touch more expensive than your corner sushi joint, but you are getting what you pay for with the whole experience.  It's a good in-between option if you're in the mood for a nicer sushi restaurant - don't get me wrong, it's no Morimoto, but it's perfect for a quiet meal, a date or a quick cure for your sushi craving.

We ended up here by accident; showed up at Genji for lunch on a Saturday and found out they aren't OPEN for lunch on a Saturday.  The ladies next door at the Fox Bookstore recommended this place for the two tourists - one from San Francisco, who eats Japanese food all the time and knows what's good, and one from Montreal who rarely gets any and knows very little, but would happily eat it seven days a week. 

Yesterday we unfortunately ended up at Misoro [shudder] and boy, did this place reclaim our faith as to the ability of Philadelphians to Yelp correctly (HOW that pit gets the same number of stars as Shiroi Hana, I have NO idea!).

The fish was so fresh I'd think they were catching it in a pond in the kitchen

The dishes were prepared with artistry.

The tastes were subtle and beautiful.

The service was not bad.

My only major complaint was the Tuna "sandwich" roll, but that could just have been me - it was too big to eat in one bite, but couldn't easily be bitten through and just made a mess.

Best Hawaiian we've had in Tucson!  And better than so many we've tried elsewhere!  Yummy mochiko chicken, and teriyaki.   Musubi were delicious and perfectly seasoned, our favorite.  Service super friendly! We can't wait to come back!  We only wish the location was closer to us!

Jim the manager is the best!!  He always makes sure to find by and make sure everything is ok. However, I used to give this place 5 stars, but after taking my son and some friends here, I changed it.  My sons friend ordered chicken fingers. O. M. G. The worst! They, I guess we're cooked, but so hard you couldn't eat them. The tostadas, the tortilla was so wet from the lettuce and tomatoes, that is was soggy. You couldn't even pick it up.  The frozen ice cream, is smaller then a small scoop at Baskin-Robbins. So not impressed anymore. Food taste was bad.

Good but expensive

I stopped in here for lunch on Friday. They serve lunch specials until 2pm (but if you walk in at 1:55 you're outta luck). Ordered the pork cutlets bento box which was pretty good, however the sauce for the pork was wierdly tart (I prefer mine sweet). Also had the tuna nigiri which was very fresh.

Why only 3 stars then? After ordering the bento box (~10) (which didn't come with rice (2) ), tea (1), and 2 pieces of nigiri (3 each) , my bill was around 25 after tax and tip. Talk about nickeling and diming you.

This place is great! I got "the experience" sub and my husband got the "planet sub" sub. I originally got the big size to eat half then give my husband got left overs but after just a few bites, decided I'm eating the whole sub myself! They make the bread fresh and you can really tell! The people there are so so friendly and the food is fantastic. Highly recommend trying them out.l
Ordered takeout. The burgers are a filling size and the taste is delicious. You can't go wrong with any burger. Everything is fresh. The portion of fresh fries could be bigger- only issue.

Just okay. There was only one server and one cook so everything took a while. It took us about 10 min to pay because the one worker was busy. He also ended up not knowing what we got.  Not a huge deal but a bit unorganized overall. The food was decent. We got truffle fries and loaded fries which were tasty but a little too soft for me. The burger was just okay. Seasoning just was not there. Lastly, it was an expensive meal. We each paid about $20 for a burger, shared fries and a drink. They charge extra for cheese and most toppings. Overall just a decent experience. I wouldn't go out of my way to come back.

I always ate at this place's food truck on base whenever i got the chance. Way better than "that other" Hawaiian BBQ joint here in town. Then i found out they opened up a place off base and just had to go! The food is still absolutely delicious and now with an expanded menu!!! New menu items are also proving to be a hit.

I actually found this place because I was looking for a recent article listing two other joints' competition for "Best Burger in Philly". Instead of finding the article, I found Yelp, listing Sketch as #1 in the city, so I took it upon myself to find out how good they were.

First thing I noticed was the family atmosphere. It was almost like being in a friend's kitchen for a meal. I was greeted warmly by both the female who took my order (based on conversations I overheard, I think she might be the owner) and the gentleman cooking.

As far as the food goes, the fries were incredible, and though I'm not a fan of dipping sauses, I tried what the lady said was its most popular, and I was pleasantly surprised. That was the first time in my life I was tempted NOT to put ketchup on my fries.

The burger was absolutely huge, and the mean was incredibly tasty and juicy. That thing definitely had to be over a half pound! For the quality and size of the burger, in my opinion, it is WAY underpriced!

Sketch will definitely be part of my weekly "rotation", and next time I stop in I have to try the shakes, which I heard were outstanding as well.

GREAT FOOD, GREAT PEOPLE, GREAT  PRICE....This place is a MUST for burger lovers!

My boyfriend introduced me to Planet Sub in Chandler when we were visiting his parents. I had no idea they were opening one here in Tucson until I saw a Groupon for the place. I bought three of them! I hope they will open a location on the Northwest side or more central; the location is not convenient for me. I hope they do well; it seems that area is growing up with Dave and Buster's and the new theater.

My boyfriend likes the meatball grinder and the beefeater. I have always ordered the green turkey; it has turkey, bacon, tomatoes, cream cheese, sprouts, salsa, and guacamole. The subs are served on house-made wheat bread, which is soft and fresh-tasting. You can also order your sandwich on gluten-free bread or in a tortilla or lettuce wrap. This would be a great place for people with dietary restrictions, and they have a good selection of vegetarian options as well.

A half-size of any sandwich is plenty for me, or I will order a full size and save half of it for later. I'd expect to pay about $10-12 per person, depending on if you get a side or a drink. I just ordered the sandwich and got water, but they have bottled drinks as well as a Coke Freestyle machine. They offer chips, cookies, and pickles for sides. I read they also have soup on the menu, which changes daily, but I didn't take notice of it on my visit.

There were two guys working when I was in. They were both very friendly, and the place was clean.

I have walked by here probably a thousand times, and I'm glad to have finally tried it! It's a quiet little sushi spot - love the minimalist decor and booth seating. Our server was friendly and attentive. I got a glass of the house white wine - nice glass & reasonably priced. The 16oz Sapporos the guys purchased were well worth the price. 

I wasn't a huge fan of the edamame - not enough salt for me! My small house salad was a nice starter and the standard ginger dressing was just right. I got the Rock 'n Roll & the Island roll. Island was my favorite with the thinly sliced mango on top. It had a great kick! 

We had a 20% off coupon for the Cherry Blossom Festival, but the prices were fair and I will add this to our list of great Philly sushi spots!

The food I ordered was great the service however was terrible at least by second shift. By that I mean there was a Barmaid that was very bias to which customers she served the regulars got all her attention, she stayed down at the same end of he Bar most of the time I believe her name was sandy short, breasty,Blonde haired girl who you could tell she used as her tipping catcher with the old men she giggled at the whole time instead of serving the rest of us their. She had to be called every time I needed a new drink, never asked if I needed anything she tried to charge me regular prices on a Happy Hour night for my drinks and she was rude during the whole time by not coming down the end where we were also paying. For a first time impression she sucked and so did her service. Pool table gets taken over by the regulars so get there early if you wanna play on them. And don't GO while she's working lousy service you will go dry waiting on a drink from her.

one of the best sushi places i've ever been too. definitely a little more pricey but if you're gonna spend money on raw fish why not make sure it's good quality? you definitely get what you pay for and the staff is super nice! recommend this place to anyone who is a sushi lover! also their hibachi menu is off the charts, recommend their salmon teriyaki as well!! 10/10

Service was great, food was good, price was overall pretty fair. The menu is quite extensive and offers a huge selection of mexican food and a nice selection of items in the Cantina for adult type beverages. This location was clean and the only thing I wasn't pleased with was the oarking lot is set up very strange, however it wasn't horrible. Will return to this location.

Good service but the sushi rolls are not worth the money. They have too much rice. I ordered one with cucumber, smoked salmon and avocado and the cucumber tasted funky (I don't think it was ready to be cut!) and the smoked salmon was over cooked and hard. The bagel roll was mainly rice.

I'm soooo sad!!
It's been awhile since I visited Solid Grindz. They were still in their previous location, which I adored! The bright green polka dot building suited them somehow.
Yesterday I brought a newly transplanted to Tucson friend to try out one of my favorite good eats establishments...and I wound up completely embarrassed. 
We both ordered the Teriyaki chicken, which is raved about, and when it came to our table it was cold. Cold as in the same temperature as our tuna mac salad. Cold as in no where close to the 165° the health department requires food to be kept at to serve. Not only was it cold, but it had not char to it as I remembered it having, and it had a disconcerting amount of connective tissue and skin with it.
The tuna mac salad was great, as always, but the chicken was a deal breaker.
We happened to get there when an influx of service members from Davis-monthan arrived as well, but I'm assuming they moved to the new location to accommodate more patrons? If that's the case, the kitchen also needs to be brought up to speed.
I don't think I'll be returning. I'll catch my Hawaiian BBQ fix when next I visit Phoenix.

Went here for lunch. Love the feel of the place. It is a bit cold in the dining room if you are eating in.

Food: we ordered the Kobe burger and the bacon chicken salad also sweet potato fries with garlic aoli and cheese fries. The fries were both amazing as well as the Kobe burger. The chicken salad was simply okay. Overall I will be back but for a burger next time

They say you know it when you see it. Talent that is. 

When melted cheese and succulent bacon covers and smothers your delicately rugged, hand-cut french fries, this, my friends, is french fry nirvana...and way all pommes frites were meant to live and die. 

Finally, to be prepared within 8 minutes of you ordering it...that's talent. Respek.

Sketch has burgers for vegans and for meat-eaters. Their french fries are awesome! When you order fries, they grab a potato and slice it up, so it is fresh and delicious, the way potato SHOULD be eaten, with the skin on.

They also have melt in your mouth sweets and my favorite is the chocolate covered macaroon.   Mmmmmmmm, chocolate...........Mmmmmmmmm coconut. 

I have tried several of their sandwiches and burgers, and they are just too oily and lacking in flavor.  I have the admit, the first few times I went there, it was good...but then it became progressively worse.  I love their fries and I love their macaroons, but that's about it.
They were out of chicken during lunch, said it would be another 20 min ... So I had the ribs.  They were ok.  The Teri sauce was good though.

Ok, so an update. The wife and I got back together. But it didnt last long. This place is still terrible. 

After much talking and exercise, my wife took me back after I got fat from eating these burgers. All was right in the world.

We went here for dinner on Friday night. I got the smashed onion burger and she got the Mac and Cheese. We shared an order of Cheese Fries. The burger which I order medium, was actually cooked medium! Most places dont know how to cook a decent burger. 

We finished up our dinner and went home. My lady wasnt feeling well and left to go to CVS. She comes home and I find out she was cheating on me! Yep. Thats right. The signs were right in front of me. She has some white stuff in the corner of her mouth and on her dress.....thats right. Cheese. She had went back out to get more of Sketch's amazing Cheese Fries! I tried to confront Sketch, but they pretended they weren't home. 

This place is horrible. Their food is so god damn good, it ruins families and tears people apart!

Not authentic mexican food.

I think the 1st sentence alone should be enough for anyone to read.

*poor service
*order always incorrect
*overpriced for quality food

First let me say that we've been loyal Macayo's customers for over fifty years. My wife remembers going there as a little girl as a 'Sunday after church' treat. The food is wonderful.
