The green corn tamales with Baja sauce are to die for. My wife loves their chili rellenos and I always loved the green chili burritos. I was so thrilled a few years ago when they put their original chimichanga back on the menu. Wonderful! Service has always been accommodating and efficient. It has been our go to place for our forty years of marriage. When our boys were little they loved Sunday because it meant lunch at Macayo's and we have fond memories of them ordering 'a cheese enchilada' from their high chair. We've been regulars both when we lived in Phoenix and now for many years in Tucson. We even stop on occasion to order eighty to one hundred dollars worth of food to take home and nosh on and take to work, etc.

That is why I'm so disappointed with the current menu changes. I was laid up recently with neck surgery and my wife, to avoid cooking, stopped by to do a big order as we have in the past and was told that the green corn tamales and chili rellenos were no longer on the Mex and Match menu, but could be ordered as separate meals for ten dollars for one item only. She asked several more questions and was told that she could only order two item meals on the Mix and Match menu (unlike the three items they used to let us buy at an additional price). Frustrated, she finally just walked out and spent $87 at another Mexican food restaurant closer to our house.

We stopped in today and scoured the menu. The Mex and Match menu is in deed limited to only tacos, enchiladas, and tostadas. No more tamales. No more rellenos. A few years ago they had cut the meat filled burritos from that menu but now even the bean burrito is gone. I groused about the menu changes and the server agreed to sub in a green corn tamale with Baja sauce. That was nice. The food was excellent, but with just the two items we didn't have much of a leftover box to have for breakfast tomorrow. The server's explanation that they were simplifying things in order to maintain quality didn't make much sense to me since the items are still available as stand alone meals. 

I hate the menu change. I can make a tostada at home. I can't make a green corn tamale with Baja sauce at home. Well, I can and I have, but it is not as easy as slapping beans and cheese on a crispy tortilla. I understand that food costs drive these decisions as well as the number of sales. I wouldn't mind if they had the Mex and Match menu as is with another column that, if ordered from, increases the price by a few bucks. Unique items like rellenos, tamales, and meat filled burritos could fill that column. 

We'll probably be back, but we are far less likely to keep it as a regular place. I'm probably just a grumpy old man, but it is so sad when favorite things disappear. The food is great, the service is great, and the atmosphere is great. My issue is with whoever made the menu changes. That person should be fed to the parrots...

I've heard about Sketch through several friends and was really jonesing for a burger one afternoon.  Hopped in my ride, went down to F-town and got me a big ass cheeseburger and fries.  Burger tasted like heaven topped with angel wings.  Fries weren't the best.  No fountain sodas sold here either, just bottles.

Last night I dropped in for a drink. As I was sitting there a black man walked in sat near me. Minding his business. A lady across the seemed to know him. She was saying something to him. He was making features as he could hear her. Her boyfriend sitting next to her .I assumed by the way he was talking he worked there. He was screaming to the black man to be nice. The black said what did I do. I boyfriend ran over screaming . I told you to be nice. I thought he was going smack this black man. The bartender just stood there. Not opening her mouth to defuse the issue. I told her this has never changed .  As I walked out door the boy friend was screaming at me. I felt sorry for this black man who had to endure this embarrassing situation. This place is still a dump.
Great subs! Really fresh ingredients and fresh bread, baked twice a day. I look forward to going back and trying more of their menu. The employees are very friendly too.
So delicious!  I've been a few times, and I always order the patty melt.  It's amazing.  Also, the service is friendly and accommodating.  Will be back soon

There's a 3-star review on this place? Atrocious! Why is this place empty at 10pm on a Thursday night? I guess Sansom is kind of far unless you live in Kings Court, but are we Penn students really all so bougie that we can`t be bothered to trek more than 2 blocks for a late-night happy hour? Come on, it's only two doors down from Mad Mex!

If you've never tried the late night 10pm happy hour here you are missing out on a hidden gem. $3 fishbowls, $4 house wines (cabernet or chardonnay, both decent), and $3 beer/cider. 

But what really kills it is the food selection. Everything on the menu is amazing, and you can't beat $1 oysters. $5 appetizers are 100% on point:

- best calamari on campus, IMHO
- 2 large crab arancini balls with marinana sauce
- 5 balls of lobster mac and cheese
- orange sesame shrimp - if you get nothing else, get this. Simply amazing!
- tater tots with cheese and crab

SERVICE
--------------

The people here are fantastic and so full of character. The door people will make fun comments if your ID is from an interesting place. Todd was our server for a friend's farewell event and he is sassy as hell, in the best possible way. What a guy. He saw me accidentally drop a tater tot into my fishbowl and gave me crap for it, which I totally deserved.

On another note, excellent business judgement - one of my friends knocked over and broke his glass and the staff immediately came to remove the broken pieces without any hint of irritation. They also replaced his drink free of charge, gave us a new plate of calamari in case some of the glass shards had fallen in, and followed up with a witty quip ("Gosh, he dresses well but you can't take him anywhere, huh?"). Very impressed. They also gave us a fishbowl on the house!

DECOR, AMBIANCE
----------------------------

Decor is much classier than Baby Blues or Mad Mex or anything else close by. Nice nautical theme - pictures of ship blueprints on the way to the bathroom, etc. Definitely feels like a restaurant during the day, and transforms nicely into a late-night without the ratchetness of Smokes. 100% classy.

OVERALL
--------------

Definitely an underrated gem on campus - maybe people just don't know about the late-night deals, as I certainly did not until senior year. Food is 100% on point, drink specials are reasonable, service staff are fantastic, beautiful ambiance.

The only shame is that there aren't more people here for the late-night! On the other hand, that makes it a great place to have a conversation where the music and background noise isn't so loud that you can't hear each other.

Stop by after 10pm and see what you've been missing out on!

i love this place and i haven't even had a burger here yet. i came in yesterday afternoon, when i was tooling around on my bike and getting hungry. i was feeling healthy, so i wasn't prepared to eat an enormous and amazing-looking burger, as tempted as i was by all the gorgeous options. i ordered one of the specials instead, the grilled eggplant salad, and it was delicious. smoky but bright, with mint and cilantro in the dressing. the woman who served me was clearly the owner, and she was incredibly friendly and in high spirits. even as i was eating the salad i was planning my trip to come back for burgers. i can't wait.

Parking is horrendous, but even with that it is worth going to.  I have figured out the times when I can get one of the two handicapped spots.

The food is decently priced for the portion size.  The add on option is well worth it.  I like the bang bang shrimp and also the other shrimp dish they have.  The chicken katsu is really good as well as the teriyaki.  It comes with two sides, I always get tuna Mac and rice.  Both are very good.  My only complaint is the tuna Mac gets heated with the hot food next to it.  When I take it to go, that doesn't help.  I would prefer it packed separate so it's cold and if eaten at the place, separated some how.  It is a small pet peeve of mine and really not a huge deal.

They have a counter with the sauces which are very good.  They also have the little to go containers so you can easily take the sauce home.

I go to this place about once a month and really enjoy it.

Alright, here goes.  5 stars, Sketch.

I'm not on the 'let's try every burger in the city' mealplan, but I've eaten my fair share of burgers, trust me.  I was not let down by the massive offering I consumed at Sketch.  Okay fine, the three that I've consumed in the last three weeks.

I've always been here for lunch, so it was never crowded.  I've also never been in a rush, so I can't give you much input in terms of the wait and what not.

My first order was the beef burger, harissa aioli, grilled onions, and a fried egg.  Excellent choice of toppings by me, thank you very much.  Flavor of the meat = excellent.  Bun = a little greasy, but still good.  Size = giant.  Sauces/toppings = elevate this burger to the next level.  And price, I think it ended up being about 9 for this, plus a few extra bucks for fries.

The second time I got the spicy mustard on the beef burger with onions.  Way too spicy for me (I took the sauce off the roll)...but I think if you're a fan of spice, you'll love this.

The fries are also great.  Always come out hot and fresh, and you can choose any of the dipping sauces for your fries.

Just don't ask for ketchup.  We were chastized for asking for it hahah.  The chef/owner (I presume?) with the curly dark hair told us not to ruin her burger by putting ketchup on it.  She did give us ketchup with the fries.  But honestly I thought it was hilarious that she was mad at us for asking for ketchup, so I think that was actually a positive.  Love a place with some grit and character.

Go here, get a burger.  Enjoy it.  Don't waste your money for a $20 burger at another fancy place unless you're able to accept that you paid a few extra dollars for a more upscale dining experience.

So Sketch, hats off to you - a job well done.  Or medium...you shouldn't be allowed to eat beef if you ask for it well-done :)

Any restaurant that provides crayons, markers, and construction paper to adults judgment-free wins automatic Gina points. I didn't draw anything myself because I was too busy being transfixed by everyone else's drawings, but I had the option to, and that is what matters. Even the tabletops are covered in drawings (but with protective covering so they can just wipe the tables off if you make a mess). 

I got the regular old beef burger and a chocolate milkshake, and both were amazing. The lettuce and tomato on the burger were crisp and fresh, the patty was thick and juicy and perfectly seasoned, and even the bun was tasty. I often have a problem with the bun-to-meat ratio of hamburgers, but I am happy to say that Sketch does not have an excessive bread issue. I'm not at all picky about how my meat is cooked, so I usually just say "medium" and am happy with whatever I'm given, but I must say this was a perfectly-cooked burger. Now, the milkshake. Many milkshakes I've had taste like milkshake, not like ice cream. I'm not sure how else to describe it, other than there is a distinctly un-ice-cream-like flavor that marks it as a milkshake and not melted ice cream. This milkshake tasted just like melted chocolate ice cream, but melted chocolate ice cream that is still cold, and that makes it amazing.

I will definitely go back, and next time, I will draw!

[ overall ]
A beautifully designed flyer left in a Huntsman Hall classroom salvaged an otherwise boring math class. Great colour balance, elegant design, 10% off coupon code? Must be worth a try. And boy it was. I LOVE it when new businesses have not just a great marketing team, but also have their operational sh*t together too.

Vegans and vegetarians on Penn campus rejoice - no longer do you need to suffer the mediocre, overpriced rabbit food and basic, brain-numbing conversation at Sweetgreen. HipCityVeg lost its novelty after a while and isn't actually all that healthy with all the fried junk. The holy grail of vegetarian delivery appears to have arrived in West Philly.

Whoever is running this joint - you kick ASS.

[ experience ]
Though there is no app (yet), the Herban website was consciously designed to be elegant and mobile-friendly. A pleasant, straightforward ordering experience, Facebook or Google sign-in for quick registration, an email confirmation seconds later, and live order status updates.

The kitchen opens at 4:30pm and as we learn in OPIM101, there will be a wait time for the first orders of the day going through the system. On Tuesday it happened to be one hour, which was fine.

My food arrived promptly at 5:30pm, delivered by a pleasant and friendly lady with a really cool bike. Full points here.

[ food ]
And here is where Herban really shines - there is a very small intersection between healthy, delicious, and affordable, and Herban somehow manages to occupy this sweet spot. As far as I know, there is nowhere else on campus that you can get a delicious, healthy, freshly prepared meal that will fill you up delivered to your door for $10.

I'm vegetarian but I'm sure the meat options here will be just as fantastic. I got:

- the vegan skillet with kale and tomato sauce. If you have a friend who tells you that tofu tastes terrible, to which you respond by rolling your eyes and saying "tofu tastes like whatever you cook it to taste like", try throwing this at them. Very yummy.

- sweet potato mash - mixed with coconut milk and sesame. Also delicious.

- quinoa and cheese - satisfying like mac and cheese, but so much better for you!

[ conclusion ]
Proof that eating healthy and / or being vegetarian doesn't mean you have to put up with eating some bullshit salad at Sweetgreen or some hipster hole in the wall.

Kudos to these guys for finding a killer business model. I have a feeling they'll be picking up repeat customers all over the place and will need a bigger kitchen very, very soon.

The only good thing about this casino is that it is so close to Center City.
Otherwise, the people who play here look pretty shaddy, There are not a lot of gaming tables and it is not often that the blackjack tables are less than $25 per hand.

Originally I assumed they were open until 8:30 when the mall closed. I went at 8:00 pm and they were closed. So I called the establishment to find out their hours of operation. They informed me that they were open until 8 pm. I went the next time at 7:30 pm, and they were closed. Although they do great work, their inconsistency makes it difficult to pick up your items.

So I looked on yelp and foursquare for a good burger place close to Port Richmond (BF lives there....and this place came up numerous times....
After looking at the pics and reading the reviews I decided to try it out....

Walked in and it's a messy/trendy little dive and the owner was the waitress/cashier and cook.

For 8.50$ I had the best burger I have ever eaten in my entire life.....Well....it was in the top 3....and I'm a burger freak.

The burger had the bacon, fried egg and cheese on it....and she didn't give me weird looks when I asked her to just leave the bun off of it.
It was clearly a burger made by hand...and the bacon was ungodly amazing...

I can't wait to eat here again.

BEST BURGER IN TOWN!

Best Shake, Best Sietan, Best Brioche Bun, and the BEST homemade Brownies I have ever had!

The owner is super nice, Max is a great cook!

If you haven't had a Sketch Burger I highly recommend getting one. Many options to choose from and great prices!

Sirloin Beef Burger $6.95
American Kobe Burger $9.99
Turkey Burger $8.00
Vegan Bean Burger $8.00
Smashed Onion Burger $7.95
Cyclops Burger $8.95
Truffle Butter Burger $8.95
Dr. Pepper pulled pork $7.50
Grilled Chicken Breast $6.99

Check out their website for more items
http://www.sketch-burger.com/index.html

Excellent food is always good.  They recently changed the lighting .... not sure why, feel like I'm in a hospital.  I did enjoy the Nacho's and other items with my kids.   Definitely love the Salsa and the tacos as well as the Red Chili Burritos.  It does have a heavy garlic taste ... but my mouth is watering after thinking of the experience.
Service was excellent, everyone is very nice. The subs are a good size for a low price and they're delicious!

Best Hawaiian food in town!  This is the only Hawaiian restaurant in Tucson where I've seen tuna mac - one of my favs!!  The bang shrimp was crunchy with great flavor, and the teriyaki chicken was just right!  You order at the cashier and pick your sides.  I had the combo with 2 mains and 2 sides, it all went down pretty easy!  A large part of their clientele are Air Force as they are situated so close to the base, and they started as a food truck on the base.  The surroundings are pretty non-descript and casual, and of course Hawaiian music plays in the background for ambiance!
I thoroughly enjoyed the sushi here! I ordered takeout, the sushi was fresh, my order was on time and the the people who greeted me were friendly. No complaints and would order again!

Disappointed again. Given that the first time we went to this place was in November of 2008, we decided to give it another chance since a few of our friends wanted to take advantage of the Subaru Cherry Blossom Festival's promo on 20% off select Japanese places around the city (ends tomorrow, April 1).

Boy, I should have trusted my instincts. I really don't understand the hype about this place, aside from the nice decor and attentive service. Fish quality stayed the same (mediocre). Nigiri was small (and are they really charging $3 a piece for something that small?!). The amount of wasabi they put on the nigiri was enough to totally overpower the taste of the fish. 

A group of us ordered the Sushi Lover platter, and surprisingly, the rolls were the best part. The nigiri was just off and nothing to be wowed over. The o-toro, which I enjoyed last time, was COLD. Like...almost frozen in the middle cold. WTF? Don't charge $8 per piece and serve it semi-frozen!

Then came the issue with the bill. Nowhere on the flier does it say you had to print it out for the discount to be honored. Our waitress even gave us a line: "Oh, you need to bring it in because there's a bar code we need to scan." So my husband ran back to our place a couple blocks away and printed it out. Guess what? There was no bar code.

I don't think I'll be back to this place. I've lived in Japan and know good sushi, but this place does not even come close.

We had excellent service and very good sushi here. The value is good-- lots of sushi for two for $60 after tip. Some highlights: spider roll, dragon roll, octopus app. More than anything, the service was extremely welcoming and friendly.
I was here last a week ago for Veterans day and the food at this place was very fresh and tasty. I would definitely come back. Also their banana tempura with ice cream was awesome.

I HATE the decor, theme etc....crayons and such ? -  so messy and hap- hazzard.  

- But - 

I  LOVE the veggie buger - so thumbs up. Though over-priced a bit.
Great Burgers.  Mac and Cheese equally good. When in Philly get to Fishtown

Cyclops burger and beef burger are big and beautiful . So filling. Wished I had enough room for the fries which were also amazing! Sweet potato fries are even better the NEXT DAY which is rare for fries! Recommend getting it fresh. Picking it up does allow it to congeal. Still good just don't order the large fries as well!

Sketch immediately became my favorite burger in Philly a few years ago when, while driving down Girard, I saw a bright neon sign and decided to find out what it was. They were massive mounds of beef, covered in really great sauces on delightfully soft buns. Impossible to eat without making a mess. The owner also seems very serious about using fresh, quality ingredients and being pretty eco-friendly. I love that.

Over time, it seems like the quality has slightly declined but it's still pretty great. The burgers aren't quite as big or as tender as they were a couple of years ago, but they're still really, really good. The Dr Pepper pulled pork sandwich is one of the best things there. I've yet to meet someone who doesn't love it after trying it. Apparently they sell it by the pound, too, which sounds pretty great for a party.

Lately, I've been trying the vegetarian options on the menu. The bbq seitan sliders that were on special a while ago were pretty awesome. The vegan chili I recently had was delicious, and the fries (both regular hand-cut and sweet potato) are just perfection. I actually just stop here for fries sometimes. There's a variety of really, really great dipping sauces. The aioli is my favorite.

The baked goods are always imaginative and look so tempting. I love that they always have several vegan options for those crazies.

It's a pretty tiny place, but has some cute booth seating and drawing materials. Seems to have a talented customer base, judging by the artwork on the walls.
There can be a wait during peak times when the tiny kitchen is working really hard, so calling ahead is never a bad idea.

Waffle fries and sliders as part of the regular menu would definitely get me back here more often!

Right next to Dipinto Guitars this place is a nice little joint to get a burger. However my only time there I didnt get a burger. I got the Mac n Cheese special and a side order of Garlic Mashed Potatoes. Some yummy food here folks! The serving was so huge that I could only eat a litle more than half, and ate the rest for dinner. Next time I'm in need of a tasty burger I know where to go!! Oh yea they have a chalkboard  and chalk if you feel creative while waiting.

Discovered this spot a few years back and still stop in for a good burger from time to time. Food is quality and appetizing. Only thing is, place is rather small and sometimes you might not get a seat and if you don't want to wait, take out is the next option. Recommended.
Great food for the price. Even after the family was stuffed there was left-overs. Great tasting food. I will be back for more!

My wife and I decided to eat Mexican Food on the east side while we were shopping.  We saw Macayo's and we had thought we should try it due to our sentimental side and eating our first lunch together at the North side location.  The waitress was pleasant, but seemed to forget about us and she looked really busy working multiple tables.  I had ordered a Mexican Beer (which they did not have in stock) so I ordered a dos equis draft lager.  A BOTTLE of dos equis was brought to me.  The chips were a store bought "authentic" chips and the salsa was a glorified ketchup.  I had ordered the Tres Enchiladas platter and my wife ordered the Baja Chicken Quesadilla,  First the enchiladas:  The tortillas were thin, corn, tortillas that seemed like they were store bought that roughly turned to mush as you cut into them.  The flavor of the enchilada sauce was not bad, and the cheese enchilada used yellow cheese.  Beans and rice that came on the side were nothing spectacular.  Overall the enchiladas were not bad, it is just that I might get a more enjoyable and cheaper meal with the same quality as Taco Bell or Del Taco.  My wife enjoyed the quesadilla, but again it was nothing spectacular.  Macayo's is a restaurant that you would take your midwestern friend who has never experienced any "Meheeecan" Culture.  The flavors are truly catered to a more Anglo palate.  There are truly much better Mexican restaurants if you are willing to look around and give a chance.
They had some big parties so we had to wait awhile, but all in all the service was good and so was the food.  I really love their chicken taco's. They are always very nice to their customers.

the best burgers in Philly! I love this place. it's a little dive-y looking but don't let that fool you. they know how to do it. they have a selection of sauces you can add to your burgers, amazing. the 'green goddess' is one of my faves. and the green chili cheese fries?! yum!

One of the best restaurants I have been to, in every aspect of the eating out experience - food, service, decor...

We arrived (without reservation) and were seated almost instantly on a Saturday evening - it was really busy, too. We were able to order quickly and had some soft shell crab rolls, king crab roll, tuna sashimi and the seafood teriyaki. The sushi and sashimi was really fresh and presented to look so appetising and pretty. The seafood teriyaki comes with rice and miso soup - this is the best miso soup I've ever had. All too often, miso soup has too much soy sauce added, but this one is perfect. The seafood teriyaki contains prawns, scallops and lobster - the prawns really make this dish. 

It was really very busy in the restaurant. A group of 3 came in after us. My hubby offered to swap since we were sitting at a 4 person table
and didn't need quite so much space. The restaurant manager was very kind and gave us some ice cream mochi on the house, as a thank you - really great ice cream mochi! 

Absentmindedly I left my gloves in the restaurant. But the staff had managed to find them and put them aside for me! So... I had a very happy experience at Shiroi Hana! I will go back every time I visit Philadelphia!

I've been here a few times & I don't usually leave reviews but I wanted to leave a review because the other night me & my sister wanted to come here to pick up something to eat, I was craving the grilled Teriyaki Chicken  but when I looked up the hours, I realized they were already closed because it says they close at 7:30pm which I didn't know... (this was a few nights ago). We still wanted to get some Hawaiian food so we decided to try Mama's Hawaiian Bar-B-Q. When we got our food, I could  tell it was different from the food we got at Solid Grindz. Not saying it wasn't good, but it wasn't as good as Solid Grindz...I think the only thing better was they give you a little bit more rice. But that's it....the customer service was really good, don't get me wrong. The people working there were really nice but I will be sticking with Solid Grindz from now on. I used to live in Hawai'i when my family was stationed out there on Hickam from 2005-2009.  so when I moved to Tucson 6 months ago, I was so happy when I found out they have Hawaiian food out here. I can tell you that this place is just as good as L&L in Hawai'i. This is definately one of the BEST in town ! & they also offer a military discount. My favorites on the menu are the Grilled Teriyaki, Chicken Katsu & their Spam musubis. If you've never tried Hawaiian food this is the place to go! :)

Burgers are extremely big and can definitely fill you up, add Fries and you're extremely full. They have a nice selection and the flavor is great. The Truffle Burger is probably my favorite and be careful with the Aioli sauce as it's PACKED with garlic. The few downsides are that it's cash only and it's definitely not a fast food burger place as it usually takes a good 25-40 minutes. All in all a great place to get a burger if you have cash and some time.

I really liked this place! I had been meaning to go for a while, and I had tried a few times before but couldn't find parking, so I'm glad I finally got to make it. The vegan black bean burger was great. It was a little dry so it needed the BBQ sauce. I wish there were more vegan sauce options. And a vegan cheese. The fries were awesome and the employees were really nice.

My husband dropped in here last week and picked up our food to bring home. He got me the kahlua pork plate with a side of white rice and their tuna macaroni salad. My husband got the bang shrimp with a side of rice and 2 hawaiin rolls. The Bang shrimp was very tasty. It tasted like it had a deep fried coating on it and then tossed with a sweet sauce. It didn't need any dipping sauces to compliment it. My kahlua pork was mixed with cabbage and didn't have a lot of flavour until I added teryiaki sauce. The rice was sticky which was perfect and the macaroni salad tasted homemade. Overall this place ranks up there with Mamas Hawaiin BBQ.

I'm giving two stars rather than one because the waitstaff was friendly and accommodating.  Otherwise, Stats on 17th was a one-star experience from beginning to end.  We reserved a table for a large party to watch the Eagles game and ordered food in the first quarter that didn't arrive until nearly the end of the fourth quarter.  And the food itself was salty, dry and generally not good.  The waitress apologized for the kitchen's disorganization, which was clearly not her fault.  

I think this place needs to make sure it's better prepared for large crowds if it continues to tout itself as the place to be for watching the big game.

Martin is the man.... the meat and sausage man!  Don't even bother going to the other stalls in Reading Terminal Market for sausage -- just go straight to Martin.

There's a wide variety of sausages (and other meats!) to be had here.  The chorizo, garlic sausage, apple sausage and chicken feta are fabulous.  Really, you can't go wrong with any flavor.

And if you are looking for a particular cut of meat, talk to Martin!  My husband was in search of a whole rabbit for a stew and Martin totally hooked him up (just be sure to give him at least a day's notice to obtain it!).
Had my first sub here yesterday, wow & awesome!  Bread is unique and very tasty.  Got the "experience" sub and it was super yummy.  Customer service was outstanding.  Highly recommend.

Let me preface this review by saying I typically dislike burgers. . . 

However, i totally enjoyed my turkey burger from Sketch.  I added avocado and green goddess sauce, making this burger a delightful eating experience!  The fries only added to this yummy experience.  

This is a small hole in the wall in Fishtown, where the walls are adorned with customer's drawings and that houses about 10 tables.  Diners can choose beef, turkey or veggie patties then top those with the toppings of choice (cheese, veggies, sauces, etc)  Fries, onion rings and salads can join your burgers.

There are homemade desserts in jars and baskets on display as well.  Designed for eat in or to take out and all looked awesome.  I can't judge on taste because I had zero room after my burger.  

The next time I have a hankering for a (turkey) burger I will definitely make my way back to Sketch.
Highly recommend the Medusa Roll. This restaurant has the best sushi in all of Philly. Dare I say the best sushi I've ever had in my life! Service is good as well.

I must've driven past Sketch a zillion time, each time intrigued by what wonders await beyond the hot pink and neon green facade. I decided to grab dinner there one night on my way to work, upon my boyfriend's roomate's (bother's sister's cousin's parakeet's) recommendation. Mind you, if youve ever had a burger craving in Philly, you know Fishtown is the burger Mecca. So if Sketch was worth recommending, it must've been bangin'!

So I called in my order...as I was parking...obnoxious, I know. But I figured I'd just sit and scope out all the cool sketches on the wall. Doodle art galore! I opted for a good ol' fashion burger with Bleu cheese, mushrooms and onions (my go-to burger toppings) and a side of green chili cheese fries. (though I'm told the Kobe beef burger is what the clouds in heaven are made of). I remember thinking that $9.5 for a burger that doesnt come with sides from a place that looks like an 80's carry out pizza joint was a bit steep. 

Butttt then after only waiting a few minutes, my order was hot and ready. The  cashier was very sweet and smiled the entire time. I thanked her and ran on my way. 
 
All in all, it was a messy burger. But thats often the sign of a good, juicy burger. Toppings flying everywhere, juice running down my hands....it was a massacre. The burger was outstanding, though still not my favorite in the area. I'm curious to try their other burgers. Truffle burger anyone?! Om nom nom.

The end.


Oh wait, you thought I forgot about the fries, didn't you?! Don't be silly. A good fry is a measure of a good restaurant. While these are more like steak fries, which are not my personal style, they were deliciously seasoned! The cheese sauce was tasty, didn't have that plasticy aftertaste some cheese sauces have. The green chilies were a nice touch but next time I think I'll just order cheese fries and smother them in sriracha. But be warned, that order of fries fed 5 hungry skinny girls at my job...you know, model types that could eat a whole herd of cows and still have room for desert? So I highly recommend the fries as a stand alone munchy. 

Happy sketching!

This place sucks! Horrible service, half-cooked food and rude employees that give you that "I'm in a stuck-up, vegan food joint" attitude. Avoid the seitan at all costs!!!! Sweet potato fries are also horrible.. Avoid the hype, save your hard earned money.
Ordered the pulled pork plate with mac salad and rice. DELICIOUS! Never doing that Mamas place again when I'm in the mood for GOOD Hawaian food.

Shiroi Hana doesn't hold a candle to places like Tomoe or Kanoyama in NYC, but by Philly standards, I'm actually pretty pleased with this find (thanks yelp).  

First off, it's like the only decent sushi place in Rittenhouse that's actually open on Sunday.  

Second, the fish here is actually fresh.  Rolls (so far I've had the spicy tuna and an eel/avo) are good - nothing to write home about, but definitely standard (thereby not disappointing).  If anything, they throw in a tad too much rice, but I'll deal with that.  

Seaweed salad is also good if uninventive - it's literally straight from some Costco-size pre-packaged container, but again, that's Ok.  I've definitely lowered standards since moving to the hood.

I'm happy to have found a solid sushi joint in the area.  The restaurant itself has great atmosphere, but SH is also very accomodating to take-out orders (Sunday Sushi in the Park is my new tradition).  

For those complaining about the prices: don't ever go for sushi in New York.  As a recent transplant, I think the $6-7 rolls at SH are a DEAL.

What a great little place to enjoy a fresh, tasty Japanese meal.   I prefer a la carte sushi and sashimi over their rolls, but I seriously never ate anything there that didn't leave me happy and content.  I think this is a perfect place to go to for a high-quality but efficiently served lunch.

I got to be honest, i didn't have a great first time impression of the White Flower.  There are so many other great Sushi restaurants ... and I just feel that this spot hasn't stepped up their game in both the quality, quantity of service.  They are just... average.  It's almost like... if you are walking by on the way to the car from work.. and you've got the munchies... stop on in.  But, to plan an exciting, spectacular events at the White Flower... ummm... i'd think again.

I ate here today and I got some kind of Italian type sandwich. It was amazing. I was really skeptical because they have a really poor selection of sides and the potato salad is from a container I think. But they did not fail on the most important part-the sandwich. It was huge and the bread was really fresh  and you could tell. The prices were also really cheap. My daughter kids meal, a ginormous sandwich, chips and potato salad was around $15. I liked it a lot and would come back.

Wait wait wait....I can get a burger with a fried egg on it!? The Cyclopes burger is amazing. As soon as you bite into it, you can just taste that it isn't a frozen meat patty, but a pound of fresh ground meat. Cooked to your liking, the burger is served to you piping hot.
Order the fries. Why? They taste like potato's....they don't taste like frozen deep fried spuds. They are amazing hand cut awesomeness.
The staff is extremely friendly as well. 
The price is a tad steep, but what do you expect for a meal that will leave you stuffed and satisfied. Its easily overlooked. 
This is defiantly my new spot for burgers.

Lots of people I know have had terrible experiences at various Macayo's locations--Ive never experienced it for myself until my visit there last night.

For anyone unacquainted with what Macayo's is, its what I call Gringo Mexican Food. Really delicious "mexican" food that really only vaguely resembles food that actually originates in Mexico, but is friendly to people who dont like spicy food, or people who don't know any better. I love my real mexican food, but every once in a while, I go gringo for a night.

My experience here was bad for one reason: my server. Terrible. Just terrible. The man had a whopping 3 tables to take care of, and he was REALLY struggling to keep up with that. I dont think Ive ever seen such a lazy or inattentive server before.

When I first was seated, the table just behind me was just getting their food and they immediately sent it back because it had apparently been sitting so long it was now cold. They asked him to reheat their food. That should have been the tip-off for me to request to be seated elsewhere, but alas I did no such thing. It took an unusually long time for my table to receive chips and salsa and for someone to come take a drink order.

One thing I will never go to Macayo's without ordering is their spinach con queso dip. Yeah, I know it probably arrives in the kitchen premade in some giant plastic bag or something, but I don't care--its delicious. Its also very good when its hot, which mine was not. At around the time it arrived at my table, I noticed that a couple who was seated at least 10 minutes after me but in a different section had already received their meals and Im just now getting my appetizer...and its cold. Great.

I had ordered a chicken chimichanga enchilada style and a cheese enchilada as the main course. It took quite a long time to come out, and when it did, it was clear to me it had also been sitting for a long time. The chimi was no longer crispy and hot, it was soggy and luke-warm. The enchilada sauce had been sitting long enough to develop a skin over the top. At this point, I just wanted my experience here to be over, so I didnt send anything back and just ate what had arrived and got the hell out of there as quick as possible. The food as always was tasty, though.

One thing I will say is worth coming here for is the chips and salsa. The salsa is really very tasty, and I like the texture too. The chips are super thin and salted well...very good. I did order a pint of salsa (with chips) to go before leaving.

The location on the northwest side is much MUCH better with regards to service than this one. I dont think Ill be returning here very soon.

Found this place by accident, thanks to Yelp.

Excellent subs!  Probably one of the best Italians I've had other than Santoros.

Excellent counter lady.  Very patient while we decided what to order.  She made suggestions and went into great detail on what was in each choice.  The service here was superior and really made the place.

Very reasonable prices considering the size of the sub and the quality and abundance of the ingredients.  Very happy we found this place!

Solid establishment with great food and friendly service. We had the pulled pork and the 3 combination plate. Pulled pork was perfectly cooked with the right spices. Macaroni was just like I remember in Honolulu. The 3 plate combination was equally exceptional with authentic Hawaiian taste. 

From other reviews, they started as a food truck and recently moved into a building location. The place looked clean but we had to move tables since some of the tables and booths were a bit shaky - maybe tighten up the screws and bolts? The facility is massive for a food truck transition, however I hope they can stay open. Great addition to the Tucson food scene!

Authentic Hawaiian food. Clean dining area. Friendly service!

This is my new favorite place at Reading Terminal.   I purchased skirt steak for dinner and bacon and sausage for Sunday breakfast.  All fabulous.   The sausage is special...and that was just the regular old country links.  There's a whole counter to try.  It's worth the train ride into the city.

Oh Sketch, how you disappointed me today.

We arrived for lunch, hungry as ever. The place was relatively busy, so a long wait was inevitable. I proceeded to order the American Kobe Burger with Swiss (as the waiter expressed that it was his favorite burger) and my girlfriend ordered the Onion Smashed Burger. We also ordered their fries, along with their amazing aioli sauce.

So, we begin to wait. A long wait, which I didn't mind too much, especially if the burger was to die for. 

Then the fries came and they were really delicious. They were thickly cut and fried to a perfect crisp. The complementing harrisa aioli sauce was so tasty. 

Cue another waiting period, a long waiting period. I will cut them some slack since it was lunch, and it didn't seem like many people were working at the time (about 2 or 3).

The burgers came out, and we were really excited. At first glance, the burgers looked amazing and big enough to share. We all know looks aren't everything, so the tasting began. My burger was not medium rare, like I had asked for, but was more medium with each side almost burnt to a crunchy crisp. I didn't want to send it back, since the wait was longer than I could have handled for them to re-fire me a burger. Taste-wise, it was not anything special. The charred taste was all I could really tell.

The sad news came when my girlfriend asked me to take a look at her burger after taking a couple of bites. It was still raw inside (she had ordered medium rare as well). Ew, we like rare meat, but raw is a no-go. We sent it back and got it off our check. 

Sadly, my experience was not that great. I gave them two stars for the atmosphere and concept of the place. A small, cozy hole in the wall for people to come in and enjoy (sub-par) burgers, fries, and milkshakes. There are cool doodles hanging around the place, which just gives them a certain charm. The menu was designed very well. To all the design geeks, the use of Archer went well with the feeling the restaurant wanted to portray; soft and friendly. 

The end.

I kept hearing almost weekly from my bf's bro about how great this place is and after reading a review of Sketch on a hamburger today (http://aht.seriouseats.com/archives/2011/01/sketch-burger-review-philadelphia-pa.html) I finally made it in for an early dinner. I was really surprised when we walked in...not at all what I expected it to look like! It's a little dive-y but cozy, also we were the only people in there which surprised me. We sat down and our waitress came over and told us to check out the specials and the menu. My boyfriend and I both decided to go all out with the Kobe burger, hey why not? I got mine with horseradish cheddar and my bf got his with bacon and American. We also got a large order of fries (make sure you get the aioli dipping sauce, it's free).

No fountain soda here-- just a very random selection of small bottles in a fridge. So we grab 2 and sit down. Our fries come out in about 5 minutes and they were excellent; thick cut, crispy & sort of Belgian style, with lots of flavor. I would kill for the recipe for the aioli dipping sauce - I couldn't get enough. We couldn't stop eating them and I was worried I wouldn't be able to even touch my burger. Soon after our burgers came out...My burger was cooked perfectly medium and very juicy, however there was soo much juice I had a bloody pool in the bottom of my container so the bottom bun was totally saturated and was a mushy mess but what can ya do?  Either way, it was a good burger, BUT it wasn't what I expected for the Kobe beef patty. My bf and I agreed it tasted like any other beef burger I've had in a decent restaurant. 

I only have one complaint and that was the price...
Our total came out to $30 without tip for 2 burgers, 1 order of fries, & 2 sodas.

The Kobe burger is $9.50 (YIKES!) and that is just the burger with lettuce and tomato...if you want cheese add $1 and any other toppings add another $1 for each. I would definitely get the regular sirloin ($6.50) next time...no need to upgrade to the Kobe.

A side note...
Later on I was looking at the postcard menu I took with me and noticed it said American Kobe...so it's not the real Kobe beef I originally thought I was getting. Not that it's a huge issue or that I'm an expert on the topic, but should that still carry the high price and the name? I think American Wagyu is the correct term, but now I'm just being a huge food snob. :)

I visit Tucson twice a year and always make Macayo's one of my stops.  You have to get the cheese crisp!  My wife and I always have to get a cheese crisp and love them so much that I keep trying to get our small town Mexican restaurant back in Illinois to start making them.  The food is always good.  It has had a makeover since our last visit and looks very clean.  Our young waitress was very good and pleasant.  You won't be disappointed with a meal from here.  I really have no complaints other than it is always busy when we go there.  They have 1/2 off cheese crisp during happy hour if you sit in the bar area or patio.  The bar area is vey nice.  I've included a picture.  The dining area is divided into two areas making it feel more intimate than if they had one very big area.  I will be back tis summer!!!

Awesome burgers. Awesome milkshakes.

Can be tough to go here with a group because of the relatively limited menu. Specials tend to come and go which is cool because you know they just made it, but its a pain when someone wanted a non-burger item and you promised they would have one and then they didn't. 

You get to draw while you wait for your order.

DELICIOUS burgers...I'm not sure if it's my favorite spot in the city but its probably pretty close to being so. 
The joint is covered with local art, as in customer art. I was in awe of the artistic ability that has walked through these doors. It's pretty distracting ! It reminds me of my days at Friendly's where we had coloring pages and they sold ice cream. The difference is, Sketch has good food (I didn't know better as an ignorant child).
I got the cyclops burger which I highly recommend to bacon and egg lovers. I got it medium rare with chipotle sauce and pepper jack cheese. It was everything savory, meaty, and greasy to fulfill and satisfy my appetite. I also shared the green chili cheese fries which were amazing ! You could actually taste the green chili, true to their title.
Unfortunately it's cash only which really stinks. Also the service is good, but slow. It took a long time to order, and a long time for the food to come. However, it's worth it. Don't come here if you're on a time restraint, but come if you're in for deliciousness!

What more can I say about a burger joint that has pork cooked in root beer?  Aside from the fact that I've had horrendous gas the past two days (which is clearly a sign of "good eats"), I was happy to hear that my once favorite café has turned into an awesome burger place!  

There's still more on the menu for me to try, but as per usual, the staff is awesome, the food is unique and the decore is similar but brighter than Canvas.  If you're in the area, don't take this suggestion lightly - GO TO SKETCH FOR FOOD.

I am hooked! I have been looking for a healthier option in this area food wise and this place didn't disappoint! I love they way that they treated me when I was there greeted me when I walked in and checked in with me well I was eating and said bye to me as I left. Their food is so good I honestly think this place will see me at least 2 if not 3 times a week.
Sandwich was delicious, melt in your mouth good.  Staff was very friendly and restaurant was clean.  Multiple televisions with the NFL games were on.  I highly recommend.

Got two lbs of exceptionally tasty meatballs for about $11 here. My partner was craving spaghetti and meatballs and told me that it was one of the best meals I'd ever made. Thanks, Martin's, for making me look so good! Any time I am at Reading Terminal or even the neighborhood, I will stop by. The sausage variety is abundant and so reasonably priced as well!

Sketch is the only restaurant where the deep-fryer is flourless enough for me to eat the fries without having a gluten attack. This is a blessing. An order of small fries is only $2. All the sauces are GF as well.

The first time I went here, I had spent all day making a cake for my birthday party and didn't have time to make dinner as well. When I told the waitress it was my birthday, she gave me a free GF nut cookie, which was delicious. 

On the other hand...A smashed onion burger and small fries, plus 20% tip, cost me $12.30. And that just feels like a lot of money.

Now I would like to start out this review with 2 facts: 1 I (used to) love their food and 2: I know the owner/manager is a bit of B. Like I have met and spoke to her a couple times and that's the vibe I get. ie:when asking about milkshake flavors (which are not listed on their website; i get a sigh and long response)
I am not currently rating their food, just the huge attitude I have gotten from this one woman.

anyways I have had issues trying to order take out from them before, the only issue being that   the wait time has been estimated to be 1 hour to 2 hours. this could be at 3 pm on a sunday.  Fine I get it. you're busy.
but tonight I ordered around 8.  were told 30 mins. My husband went to pick it up and was told it would be another 25, they were a little busy inside. he waited outside in the very comfortable 55 degree weather. I finally met up with him at the new revised time
 No one had come to check on him, apologize, update him or even see if he was still waiting outside.
I know this because at 8:55 I called, asking saying my husband was waiting for food that was supposed to be ready, she goes sarcastically I might add "NATHAN??? NATHAN?...oooh it looks like he stepped out(because you told him to) do you want me to relay a message?"
at this point I know you didn't look or care, because hes been gone for 5 minutes and is walking with me, I just called to see what lie you would come up with.

so i told her we weren't paying for the food. shes like "great okay!"

whoever this lady is, if shes a little busy or inconvenienced does Not care if you have to wait. does not apologize. and no fucks are given. if I am calling to check on a effing burger and pulled pork an HOUR later, and its STILL not ready, you haven't even started, and you enjoy making people wait for their food for no apparent reason at all..


never ordering here again, or recommending it to anyone again.


burger places are a dime a dozen. come off it. so are people with your attitude.

Ate here last night on the recommendation of a couple of friends. Just moved to the area so it's always nice to have a good burger place to head to when you're craving. 

Well I immediately became a fan! I was wondering why the place was named sketch but my question was quickly answered as soon as I opened up the door. There's a colorful mixture of paper covering the walls with sketches drawn on them from patrons that go in...very cool idea/concept and super cheap. Also, the font on the chalkboard, and simple illustrations of milkshakes, etc. was a big win. 

The food was amazing as well. My wife and I both had a burger. I had the cyclops....which is probably one of the best burgers I've had in a while, and my wife had a make your own. The roll they use is amazing, and both our burgers were cooked perfectly. They def. don't short on the quality of anything there. The burgers were oooozing with juiciness. I went through at least 4 napkins which was a good thing. The fries with the aioli are amazing too.

The only reason I give this place 4 stars is because its kind of grimy. The "sketches" do a pretty good job of disguising the cleanliness but the place could use a good clean up. And that rug going up to the second level on the walkway is gross. time to invest $20 and get a new one dooods.

Other than that amazing...well be back again and again

Ordered take-out during a Saturday evening rush. I write to convey the following:

Sketch made the finest burger I have ever eaten. My husband bought the vegan burger; I bought the conventional Sirloin. The chef cooked both to perfection.

Also: the expediter/greeter/receptionist told us the order would take 25 minutes. We parked in front of the shop at the 24-minute mark. When we walked through the door, an employee bagged our meal.

We are grateful.

This place was perfect. Quiet (but not like you didn't feel comfortable talking to others), fresh food and the service was great. Atmosphere is great with dim lighting and the prices were very reasonable. Would highly recommend!

I'm no connoisseur of Hawaiian style plate meals...but with some company of a few fellow yelpers...was schooled on all the delicious eats! I ordered the two meat combo plate with Teriyaki chicken, Katsu chicken, tuna mac salad and rice- yum! It was a ton of food and super tasty indeed. We also ordered the Spam Musubi which was one of my favorites. This is a family run place that started as a food truck. Super casual, order at the counter and fair prices too!

Amazingly inventive hamburgers on the menu and equally inventive are the sketches on the wall(all created by customers!). 

Food was top notch, one of juiciest patties I've ever had. 

About the name, they literally provide you with crayons and paper to make art lol. I gave the thing a shot but my drawing was so bad it did not make it on to the wall. Still, 10/10 would go back again!

I had a pleasant experience at planet sub. For my first visit I had nice customer service provided to me by ceci. And let's not forget the food. There are plenty of menu options and what I chose was delicious. Very good alternative to the usual competitors.

I haven't been to Shiroi in a very long time - their other restaurant Doma is closer to home and is now our go-to place - but Shiroi never disappoints me.

We are even planning a big party here in April.

Love the spicy tuna hand roll here, house-made tamago, ohitashi.

Sublime!  Fresh and yummy.

I first ate at Shiroi Hana about two and a half years ago when my brother started college in Philly. My family is always up for some good sushi, and Shiroi Hana was within walking distance from Hotel Sofitel in Rittenhouse Sq, where we were staying. I just went back for a second time this weekend, and it didn't disappoint. The restaurant is nice and bright, and there is an upstairs section that has a tatami mat seating area, but both times I have been there, the second floor was not in use. Maybe they only open it up for private parties - but the bathrooms are upstairs so anyone who's dining can check it out. I had the sashimi special - fresh selection but not enough variety - and we also had some age tofu, always a favorite. The only thing that put me off was that they charge for green tea - I'm just used to having that served for free at pretty much any sushi place I go, but I guess I will fork over $1.50, not a big deal. It's not the best sushi I've had, but Shiroi Hana consistently delivers on good quality sushi with great service.

If you come for lunch, make sure you've got time to spare. I've been here twice, both times I've waited at least ten minutes to order, and then another 20-30 minutes for the food to be ready. The burgers are incredible - massive, well-spiced patties - and they offer a wide range of sauces and toppings. But if you're in a hurry, call ahead.

My go-to sushi place when I'm in Philly! Always very good, never disappointed, nice and calm atmosphere but tonight we waited 40mins between miso soup and entrees...way to long! I asked a waitress (our waiter disappeared) what was going on, she asked and brung finally our order. Something went wrong and despite the fact that the quality is still perfect and those things can happen we would appreciated a commercial gesture but instead we finished our dinner and we left without even having a goodbye. I will come back because it's good, fair price and I'm sure it won't happen again but if it does for another table I just hope they will work on their service.
Love this place! The burgers are the absolute best. Great concept. Definitely a repeat customer.

At first i wasn't sure about this place.   Then i realized it was the food truck so i was all in.  Well, i don't know if it was because I came around 6 and they were done cooking food. I got my food to go.  I instantly realized that they had microwaved my wings.  They were good but you can tell they weren't fresh which i guess is fine. Then I had the teriyaki chicken which was okay as well.  Would I eat there again?  I don't know.  I wasn't all that impressed with it.

Delicious burgers!! I loved it! I got the cyclops and my boyfriend got the smashed onion burger and a chocolate shake, and we shared a large fries with the aioli and wasabi mayo!! Everything was delicious especially with the truffle butter!! Go if you love burgers!!
I stopped in and had to walk out, there was no air conditioning. It was hotter inside the business than outside.
Love, love love!!! Food is fantastic.very friendly. I usually get the chicken  Katsu, macaroni  salad and white rice.  But everything  is great. Always ask for chili sauce:)

This place is horrible the tech was really rude to me and rush me to pick a color and got made when I changed my mind and I ask them to square my nails Bc I got a over later and they where all different sizes please don't  go here they are beyond horrible waste of money

This place is great if you need your current vacuum repaired! I haven't had my Dyson cleaned in years and took it there recently and they replaced all the prices that needed it, cleaned out the hose, and the entire vacuum for about 1/3 the price of a good vacuum cleaner. The gentleman in the store is very knowledgeable and kind. Highly recommend!

I've eaten here 3 times.  Obviously, it was good enough that I went back but each time I wonder if I should be concerned about the cleanliness.  The beverage cooler looks like it is crawling with bacteria and so do the employees (eek! sorry but it's true).  I'm not afraid of a messy burger though-and these babies ARE messy.  The buns are so soft that if you get anything liquidy on them (sauces etc...), be prepared for your last few bites of burger and bun to be pretty mushy. I do like that they offer different types of sauces-besides BBQ, hot sauce etc... like green goddess.
Grown-up or not, I appreciate the crayons ('crowns') and construction paper and like giggling at other people's pictures hanging on the walls-a great distraction from staring at the cook who is cooking my burger!

Wow. Is there a way to give negative stars? After I received my order (cheesesteak hoagie& cheese hoagie) that turned out to be potati salad and garlic bread, I was told all woulde be made right. Next round had ketchup (???). 

Gave them a second chance (everyine can have a bad day). Soggy fries, stale bread, wrong stuff on sandwich. 

Done.

I tried sketch once a long time ago and recently went back. I kind of forgot about it for a while. Not sure why because the food is good. They have homemade vegan burgers, slammin french fries, and vegan milkshakes too (although the shakes are $7 so i opted-out). They also have seitan entrees and miscellaneous vegan / vegetarian specials. They also serve meat, so you can go there with your omnivore friends. I love the concept of this place and it's fun to look around at all of the drawings that people post on the walls while you wait for your food. Best vegan burger in Fishtown (and beyond) ! :-P
best burger i've had in phila, hands down.  and an adorable little place.  oh, and delicious milk shakes.

Excellent and filling Hawaiian plated meal for a reasonable price.  Portions are large and everything I tried was very good. I tried the shrimp, pulled pork, and mac salad  The pulled pork was a touch on the salty side for me but not terribly so. I also tend to like my food a little lighter on the seasoning. You order the food cafeteria style and then sit wherever you would like.  Even so, the service as very friendly, and one of the owners came over to check to see how we were doing. This was my first plated Hawaiian meal experience so I am certainly no expert, but it was delicious and I plan on coming back!

This burger joint is solid. The place is creative in having scrap papers for you to doodle (or genuinely create art). The walls are full of drawing from just fun to some serious art work. The place is small but enough seating for friends. 

The food was surprising delicious. I have not heard of the place and had zero expectations so, just came blind. 

The fries which cheese (wiz) was very good. Fries were flavorful and cheese just added to what was already good. 

The burger... I was surprised from the first bite. I got the truffle butter burger and holy moly, the juiciness and flavor of the patty was delictable. The buns too were firm and filling but not too overwhelming. You can eat the burger as is without any toppings and it would still be delicious.

You can keep your Subway's, Firehouse, PJ's, East Coast Super, Eegees, or any other sub place you can think of; I'll take Planet Sub over all of them.

I go at least once a week during lunch and have not been disappointed yet.  I usually go with the Dagwood or Super Hero and they are both better than any sub I've had in Tucson.  Full disclosure, I've only ordered cold subs, except once.  I can vouch for The Cuban  as a hot sandwich, how can you go wrong with pork, mustard, and pickles.

If you like the ingredients of the sandwich, I dont see how you can go wrong, just order it the way you like it, hot or cold.  Be ready for a friendly teasing if you order a cold sandwich.

Last but not least, the unsung hero is the bread.  Makes all the difference in the world to me.  Also, if you dont stop by on Wednesday, youre missing an opportunity to try a great sub at a reduced price.

The fish has tasted very flavorful and fresh both times I have been here.  I've tried a couple of the special rolls and have not been disappointed.  The cuts of fish seem to be more generous here than in some other sushi places I have tried.

(to the tune of "We Got the Beat" by The Go-Go's)

See the people coming off 12th Street
Getting in lines, wond'rin' what to eat...
They don't know, where they want to go
So they just get in lines.... 

(They need some meat) x3
Yeah, they need some meat!

Ditch the grocery store, don't be a fool,
Quality and great prices keep it cool
Buy in bulk, and get yourself a deal
Hardly ever any line....

(You need this meat) x3
YEAH, you need this meat!

Martin's Sausages make me wanna dance....
Bangers, chorizo, bratwurst, feeling fance...(y)
Eat so much, wear some stretchy pants
Just get yourself in line!

(They've got your meats) x3
YEAH, they got it!

Martin's is really the only place I get sausage any more. I love to just roll up with no list in hand and let the meat masters be my guide. They stuff their sausages with everyone from herbs to spices, cheese to garlic, and blend it all so well. I typically get a variety and cook them at home with veggies, in casseroles or breakfast dishes, or as a topping on pizzas. The prices are never more than $5/lb for like... any sausages, and they mix up what's on sale each week with some sausages $3.59/lb (or less when you buy in bulk!) 

Friendliest staff, most helpful folks, and they move fast so even if there IS a line (which is rare), you're in and out quickly.

Credit Card minimum is $10 I believe, so bring cash if you're cooking for one or two OR stock up!

We were looking for something new to try and decided to look up Hawaiian food. We saw this location had good stars. It was good food. The sauce on my Kalua pulled pork was good. I really did like the tuna Mac salad. The lady taking our order at the register seemed like she would rather be anywhere else so that was off putting. It was a long drive from our place to get to it and I can say I wouldn't go that far for it again. My boyfriends chicken was a bit dry and nothing too special. Maybe if your in the area and want a quick bite that isn't fast food it would be good.

I'm from the olde Eastern Block and I know my sausage. 
I found links and flavours that rival the best in Berlin or Budapest. 

Not to mention, they were incredibly patient with me when I ordered 6 different, one pound helpings to sample their stuff (if I had been behind the counter I would have smacked the customer across the head with a 'buffalo-chicken-blue-cheese' after the third or the fourth order).

Over the course of two weeks, I called them 5 times asking if they had any of their freshly made gluten free bread (so exciting for someone who can't eat gluten!) -- they said no each time. Twice they said they would make it tomorrow morning and to check back in, but both times they failed to follow through. At one point they were completely out of all bread and selling only lettuce wraps - this is a SANDWICH SHOP, people! By the fifth time I told them I would stop trying. :( They seem to be quite a disorganized and unreliable establishment.

I went Yelping around for a new place to try within walking distance of my house and stumbled upon Sketch and it's great reviews.  I can't believe it took me so long to discover this place! I'm pretty much always in the mood for a good veggie burger and some fries and Sketch fit the bill. I grabbed a couple of beers (byob!) and the boyfriend & I headed over around 8pm on Friday night. 

I was a liiiiitle put off by the big ole fly buzzing around our table (plus some smaller fruit flies), but I waved them away and got over it.  We started out with the green chili cheese fries and ohhh my god, the trip to Sketch was worth it for the fries alone.  They were perfect.  Not a too-soggy or too-crispy one in the bunch.  They were thick enough to stand up to the cheese & chili but not too starchy or potato-y.  The green chilies added just enough of a kick without being too spicy. 

The vegan burger was pretty good, though not the best I've had.  It was full of beans & lentils and had good flavor, but the veggie patty fell apart when I picked it up.  This is a pet peeve of mine!!  I went with wasabi as my choice of sauce and found it to be too mild; I needed a little spice. 

I was stuffed beyond capacity after the fries & the burger, so the milkshake will have to wait till next time. I'll definitely return to this divey burger joint.

Awesome atmosphere for a chill afternoon lunch. The staff was smiling and very attentive on taking your order and getting the pizzas started. 

Tries the BBQ Chicken and enjoyed it very much. Try their white tomato pizza well done for that extra crisp and fresh taste of tomato and cheese. Let me know how it goes!

I was actually very surprised. Some friends wanted to meet here. Normally we would have passed based on their low reviews. This place was actually good. The service was good. Employees were nice. It's pretty much self serve. They have a soda machine that you get your own drink. They deliver your food and beer, or at least they did in our case. They had pizzas made so you can order by the slice. Thin pizza, NY style. The pizza and garlic knots we got was good. Domestic draft pitchers were cheap. This is not a one or 2 star place. Give it a try.

Recommended hole in the wall here in Philly. Not a huge menu selection but the sandwich was really good. Did expect more of a selection in regards to burgers, but if in the area again I'd definitely come back again. Good service as well.

I was expecting a lot from Sketch Burger and I wanted to love it, so I was pretty bummed out when I didn't. What I expected was cheeseburger greatness, and possibly even nirvana. What I got instead involved ingredients of high quality that were badly prepared. That's doubly frustrating. Sketch totally had all of the parts and stuff but yet, somehow, the stars didn't align. At least, not this time.

I will say I dig their vibe. The space is covered wall-to-wall in customer-produced art (hence the name). The interior has a bright, zany hipness and includes spacious wooden booths. Our server was friendly. We were looking forward to a lovely burger meal in the Fishtown area, and I recommended this place based on bookmarking it years ago and wanting to try it since forever.

We started out with truffle fries. Great fucking potatoes, man. The finished fry product, though? They were way too soft and undercooked. We managed to finish them all but keep in mind we were both really high! My stomach felt like a bottomless pit and I just kept chomping away.

Anyway, onto the burgers. We both ordered CYO bacon cheeseburgers. Her, cheddar and aioli, medium-well. Me, horseradish cheddar and aioli, medium. I definitely ended up with a medium-well burger! The buns, either brioche or challah (I suspect?) were stale. The bacon was undercooked but would've been bomb if cooked properly and not cold!

I get the distinct impression that these guys have what it takes to achieve burger stardom and *possibly* just fell off on this particular night. We were the only ones in there when we first plopped down. I would perhaps give them another go if I happened to be in the area, but I wouldn't go out of my way.

PS - Suspicion confirmed! I just saw how Kathleen L.'s French fries from literally one day ago look basically perfect!

! Oh my goodness , talk about good eats! Had a great lunch here with son Mark & my husband , Solid Grindz Hawaiian BBQ On Craycroft.
The teriyaki chicken is beyond amazing as are the Island beans & Island salad..& we got to meet the warm & friendly cook/ owner ! The entire staff is awesome. A definite " going back" HIGHLY RECOMENDED.

They used to have the best burgers in the city, but the quality has gone down.  When I ate there my Kobe burger was way over done and slightly burnt instead of being the medium rare temperature I ordered.  Still a decent burger and a fun atmosphere, but sketch is not what it used to be.

Oh Solid Grindz, you never disappoint me. I love coming here! The new location is great too! Everything on the menu is so delicious and mouthwatering. Bang shrimp, teri chicken, tuna mac salad with white rice and sauce is AMAZING!! I recently tried their Poke as well... SO GOOD! You can't go wrong with this place. The staff is also so friendly and welcoming! Definitely a must.

Best burger joint in the world!! Cyclops burger is my favorite!! Parking can be a drag because it's all street parking.  Price is not bad at all!! Also had a cherry vanilla shake!  The bomb!! Love this place!! They need to bring one business to Hawaii!!
Didn't quite get the look I was going for. However they still turned out okay. The staff is always nice. And there is available parking which is a plus.

The Sweet Potato Fries were amazing. Banging burgers too of course! They had a special available of fried green tomatoes and they were very good. 

The burger I had was topped with truffle butter and I added cheese. It was amazing and you can ask for sauce on the side. 

Cash only. Get creative and draw to add something to their walls.

I was born & raised in Hawaii so hawaiian food is comfort food for me.  I had the chicken katsu & bang shrimp. Chicken katsu not too bad just wish the chicken pieces were a little thicker. The bang shrimp was okay probably won't get it again. The spam musubis were okay still think 7-11 has better. Probably will go back to try the spicy ahi.

Real cool local spot. My friends friend is the grill master which actually lived up to the hype. Menu has a lot of crazy options which is rare for a burger spot. The name of the place was concerning until I realized it was because you can draw a picture and they'll hang it up. Get whatever kind of burger you want but you have to get the sweet potato fries. All the employees were really friendly.

UPDATE 6 Feb 2018: it's been a few months since I've eaten here and decided to go....Well, they're definitely back in my top 5 places to eat in Tucson. Chicken Katsu plate with mac salad and rice was on point. Plus they sell spam musubi (spam sushi)?!?  Portions are generous and the atmosphere is great. Island music in the background makes you feel comfortable. Go check it out and see for yourself!

I've been eating solid grindz since they were just posted up at the base. They are good, however, their food has been mediocre my last 3 trips. I got the chicken katsu plate and it was over cooked. Portions have gotten smaller on the rice and mac salad. But if I had to choose between solid grindz and mamas hawaiian bbq, I'd definitely pick solid grindz for the price.

This burger Joint, is a great local place, very eclectic , No frills-Love them. I came here with a high school friend who has frequented this place handful of times. He loved it. So I thought I 'd give it a try, since Marcello & Jessica E. had given good reviews. We were able to find parking right outside, no one inside-yet. The place had pictures/drawings of burgers, etc from customers who had visited it -posted them all over the place, guess if you won, get a free burger or something. My friend said, "Here, your the art person, draw." I didn't want to. Wanted to eat.We placed our order ,I got a shake. Yummy. I got the sirloin burger with aoli sauce, bacon-OMG!! Huge burger, is it better then others nearby, Ahh yes!!! Hands down-it was. I like that they had little of variety then just burgers, tuna ahi sandwich, turkey , vegan , all kinds sides, it was nice for people who didn't want beef. I ended drawing a picture, course when we went up to the cashier, the lady was getting confused because my friend was trying to say he drew mine, & I drew this crappy -ass pic ..don't know what the hell his was-in his eyes, lousy interpretation of me. It was whack!!! I Take pride in my art, he wanted to pass it off as his, write his # , & contact info in it ??! WTF??! Joke or not, wasn't feeling it. Whatever. 
All in all..I will go back..great place, good food, local place, just food done right!!!

We've been to Dinner Done many times over the years and it's a great help for busy people who want to prepare their own meals. I imagine it would be especially great for working moms.

One thing we love is their Valentine's Day menu. They pre-prepare everything and you just pick it up (fresh, not frozen) to cook at home. They make it really simple and include EVERYTHING (even butter for the rolls and chopped parsley for garnish). You end up with very few dirty dishes and have a great time at home without fighting the crowds and paying too much for some stupid prix fixe menu. Our only complaint is that the menu is the same each year.

HUGE burgers. I got the truffle butter burger which was decadent, no additional sauce needed, and very messy to eat. My friend got the kobe burger and we shared fries with the aioli sauce. I was full for the rest of the day. Great burger spot, cash only.
I love Shiroi Hana. The interior is lovely and understated. The food always a step above, fresh and good size portions. The staff exceptional.
used to be good but now the bread is soggy the last 3 times in a row. my wife's turkey had a funky smell to it and that was the final straw. i'd give it zero stars if it were possible!
Fantastic Spinach, Ricotta and Tomato pizza! It didn't last long in our household. Actually, I couldn't even wait until we got home to munch on it. ''Twas a messy ride home.  Very VERY tasty.

I had a fantastic experience here. I was a little hesitant at the initial price of the meals. $100 for 4 meals, sounds a bit high. In actuality you are able to split the meals into two making at least 8 meals at that price that will feed 2-3 people. These meals are made with good cuts of meats, fresh herbs, and high quality ingredients. I went with a group of girls as an event. They served us appetizers, wine, and soft drinks beforehand. As a bonus to the group event they gave us a dessert to prepare free of charge. I was a little overwhelmed to make the meals, but the instructions and food are all prepped to easily put the meals together. I've had a chance to try each meal I prepared, and they are all unique and nothing I would normally prep at home. Bourbon chicken, chicken herb stuffed pastries, flank steak, and broccoli cheddar stuffed chicken. They all come with labels, so anyone can cook them the day of. I even gifted a meal to a friend who just had a baby.  The only meal we didn't love was the bourbon chicken. Mostly because it had too much fresh garlic. In the future I will watch how much I add. Some of the meals come with a rice side but most are stand alone. You can purchase sides for a very good price. Large helpings for around $5. I bought the Asian green beans and twice baked mash potatoes. The dessert was a delicious chocolate puff pastry. I made it when the in-laws were visiting and they were impressed! I will definitely be coming back before my second baby is born to stock the freezer. Excited to see what will be on the menu!

I want to start by saying the service is amazing, they greet you at the door and make sure your enjoying the food! If your looking for great food at a great price then Planet is for you. I ordered the Experience sub and was surprised about how amazing my experience was! I love spicy sandwiches and this one is by far the best I've tried! This sub was packed with chicken and jalapeños which made it fantastic. They have a wonderful menu of all sorts of exciting subs to try. Can't wait to try there gluten free bread next time. The bread is made fresh daily and they also have wonderful cookies made fresh also. If your looking for new sub shop that delivers great hot and cold sandwiches then you need to check this one out. I'll be coming back very soon. Thank you Planet Sub!!

I love the infectious buzz that takes over the hood when a new restaurant opens.  There's been plenty of that this summer in the NoLibs / Fishtown areas!  One of the newest arrivals (just a few blocks north of "world famous" Johnny Brenda's) is Sketch.  

I'm a pretty critical burgerer (or is that burgeree?) if I do say so myself.  There are a number of establishments claiming "best burger" and each year publications name another in the line of heirs to the Burger Thrown.  Ironically, I don't believe the masked burger crusader himself has ever once taken his rightful seat upon the hill top of Burger Land.  With that said, there have been only a handful of burgers that have reached their pinnacle in my Top Five, and today friends, I introduce you to my number three!

As I pushed opened the slightly stuck door to Sketch at about 10 PM on a Monday night, I am greeted by whom I assume to be the owner.  It can be a turn off to me when a new business owner is super happy to see you and super attentive but I was made more comfortable by her calm and cool composure.  Clearly this lovely lady is well aware that simply her fine-burger-goodness would gallantly speak for itself!  I placed my order for a pepper-jack cheese burger with aioli sauce and bacon.
