We haven't participated in the cooking experience of what Dinner Done offers. With a newborn in the house, I don't foresee us having time to do that anytime soon, but maybe someday!

The only negative to Dinner Done is that I enjoy the meals so much that I end up eating well beyond a "healthy" portion every night. The portions are listed as for "2-3 people, depending on hunger," so what happens every night is that I end up eating at least two portions worth, because what's left after we both eat never seems to be quite enough to save for leftovers. 

Just a heads up - these meals usually end up taking about an hour to cook + defrosting time. But it's still a heck of a lot more convenient than cooking everything from scratch!

title: Kind Of Stiff Compared To Most Duct Tape
text:
I have some issues with things that need tightening by wrapping duct tape around them. One example is a cane. As you use them, the bottom needs to be tightened after wear. I got this colorful duct tape for a fun twist.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes with two rolls in plastic wrap with a plastic divider. That is good because sometimes the edges of rolls of tape can stick together.

TEXTURE
This is a stiffer duct tape. It does not bend as easily and it almost appears not to be as sticky. It does have fibers woven into it for strength.

DOES IT WORK?
This works pretty well, although it seemed to be stiffer than any others I have. Once I got it into place, it seems to stay put okay. I am not sure it will stay put as well as the other tape I used before that.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is pretty, but it is stiffer and not quite as sticky as I would have liked, but it works okay so far.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS, although if it does not stay put like it should long term, I will adjust this rating.

title: Mislabeled?
text:
After a lot of headaches with this filament I'm not convinced that it is even actually PETG. I have my machine and slicer pretty dialed in for PETG I have used from other brands. When I tried using this I went with the same profile that I usually use and 240°C. Terrible blobs and stringing and after a few attempts a clogged nozzle. I tried to lower the temperature, then lowered it again and again.

At this point I am at 200°C (like PLA) and it is still extruding. It cracks and breaks (like PLA) instead of bending like PETG. And it pops off of the glass bed easily (like PLA) instead of being extremely stuck and needing to be fiddled with to remove it. It still looks bad and has blobs of crap all over the place though.

If I wanted PLA I would have ordered that. I also notice that contrary to the label on the spool that suggests 230-260°C the item description on amazon says "220+/- 5°C" for whatever that's worth.

It also maintains optimal levels of moisture, so the wound doesn’t dry out too much, nor is it overly wet. The antimicrobial properties also help keep it clean. It also offers a little bit of padding for better protection. Great product!

title: Practice Makes Perfect, Yes, Glue Is Sticky!
text:
Recently purchased this because I needed to attach 20 enlarged photos (16" x 20" and 20" x 30") to foam core. After reading some of the reviews I was a little apprehensive but followed the directions and it ended up working out pretty well. I will agree with one reviewer who said that this adhesive is not really positionable, but other than that, it works better than aerosol spray in my opinion. With practice, you will develop a workflow in using this product successfully. There are some tools that you will absolutely need and might require a trip to the hardware store Those are:
1) An exacto knife; I ended up using the Stanley yellow and black one that uses 25mm blades. Cost about $5.
2) A cutting surface; I ended up using two smooth pine wood shelves laid out on the kitchen table
3) A metal yard stick, preferably longer than what you are cutting. You need this to run the knife against to cut a straight line.

The main issue here is that you will get glue on your fingers or thumb doing this and following the instructions, and if you touch one of the pictures with the glue, it basically ruins the picture and is very difficult to get off. I actually destroyed one picture trying to get the glue off and made the problem worse. But that is operator error, not the fault of the glue. For example, when you begin step 1, and unroll the tape, non-stick side down and sticky side up, your thumb or finger is going to touch the sticky side, no question about it. But if that happens, you can rub your fingers together and get the glue off that way or go wash your hands and get it off that way. But either way, you need to get the glue off your fingers. What I found helpful during the first step was getting a small piece of tape and taping down the loose end of the roll, so it would stay put and not curl up. That makes it easier to set your picture down and line it up with the sticky side of the roll.

So after you've unrolled the roll, sticky side up, you tape down the loose end, then being as careful and precise as you can, you put the backside of the photo against the sticky side. If you can just get one side lined up, you should be okay. At this point, the picture, is somewhat repositionable.

Then you take your metal ruler and lay it across the top part of your picture, and cut the roll. So now the roll of mounting adhesive can be put away. Then you take the Release Paper, that comes with product, and lay it with the Teflon or non-stick paper facing up. Then you turn your photo over, and place it on that paper. And on the back side of your photo, which is now facing up, you have the sticky paper stuck to the back of the photo and the back of the sticky paper is a non-stick Teflon type material.

It is at this point that you take the squeegee that comes with the roll and get all the air bubbles out and smooth the surface flat. Once the surface has been smoothed out, and this is a key point, you need to get a clean rag and press really hard across the backside again, making sure you apply a lot of pressure. If you use a lot of pressure, when you remove the sticky paper, most of the glue will transfer to the backside of the photo.

So after you have rubbed the backside of the photo, you grab the sticky paper and slowly pull it off. When you do, if you applied enough pressure, 70-80% or more of the glue will transfer to the back of the photo.

One thing to mention about the glue is that it is very sticky and stringy. It is sticky like a mouse or roach glue trap but stringy too if you touch it. Again, if at any point in any of this, you get glue on your fingers, STOP and go wash it off.

Once the glue has been transferred to the back of the photo, all you have to do is place the photo on whatever it is you want to mount it to. This part is probably the hardest because you are trying to pick the picture up without getting glue on your fingers and lining it up with the mounting board.

Here it is best to just try and line up at least one edge the best you can or a corner. But you have to be as precise as you can because once the picture goes down, it binds very easily and is not really positionable.

However, the good news here is that if you are off by a 1/4 inch or even more, you can always trim the entire thing to even up the edges.

Once the picture is in place, then you put the release paper over the picture and again squeegee out the bubbles. And you can again get a soft cloth and apply pressure uniformly across the surface to ensure a good bond.

With several of the pictures, my alignment wasn't perfect, but with the metal ruler and a sharp knife, I was able to even up the edges and make every single picture look great.

The greatest thing about this product is it is virtually odorless and it does bind very well.

title: Works, but may not be weatherproof enough because there is no seal for the shaft.
text:
Installation went fine. It's a simple device. It was unclear whether the hex nut was supposed to go on the front side or the back side of the panel I mounted it to. I put the nut on the outside so it would tighten to the switch behind the panel. The rubber tip screws off and is part of a round type nut. My guess is that you could leave it off if you did not need the button to be weatherproof. However, for those that want the switch to be weatherproof, you will need to install it. However, you cannot tighten it unless you use pliers that will bugger up the steel. Furthermore, there should be a gasket or seal so the weatherproof rubber steel part will seal to the body of the panel and not leak past the shaft. I used a garden hose seal to seal it.

The button worked on my tractor as a glow plug switch because my model tractor does not turn on the glow plugs until you crank the engine over. That causes it to turn over a lot and sputter when it starts. This button allows me to heat the glow plugs before I crank the engine. It is working so far. I used a switch like this from an auto parts store last year and it didn't last a year before water corroded it. I hope this brand does better.

title: First I was going to...
text: Write a horrid review!  Read through the instructions twice and I said "lets do this."  Followed the directions to a T and had massive bubbles.  I had so many bubbles that I wasn't going to send it to anyone because of the embarrassment factor.  So I thought it was the resin or me.  I couldn't be sure.  I saw someone's post (in the Q &A section) that said to warm it up.  So I warmed one part up and left the other part.  Still bubbles.  Now I was going out of my mind.  I was going to come here and give it one star and be done with it.  So yesterday morning I got very stubborn (and mad) and decided to try it again.  I heated both parts up to just over room temp.  Then I poured them both into a third cup.  I decided instead of the instructions (which said to stir it vigorously) I would stir it slowly for 4-5 minutes.  So slow I go.  Some bubbles, but that's okay.  I'll just use the fire to get rid of them.  So I tint my resin cups and cross my fingers (still intent to do a bad review).  Lo and behold, I had absolutely no bubbles.  Slow and Steady did win the race.  Now I have bubble free art work (mostly animals, pen holder for a desk, etc) that I'm not embarrassed about sending.  I will be buying more when I'm out because I found the "trick" to bubble problems.  I am happy with the end results.  It took time for me, but it is totally worth it. title: Works well for my purposes
text:
So far, so good. This tape worked for my purposes. What did I get this for? Well years ago I discovered that to seal up window ACs that you wish to leave in the window over the winter the best way to do that was with duct tape. I tried everything before that - plastic bags, pillowcases, even bought covers made for air conditioners. So then I start to take them out of the window every year. Which is a pain in the butt and then have to store them and then have to put them back in. Again a pain in the butt. Nothing works as well as duct tape, I promise you if you want to leave them in.

So since that is what I got this tape for and that is what I used it for - I cannot really comment on anything else. What I can tell you is that it’s not as sticky as some other duck tapes. It also feels a bit thicker than some other duct tapes. When I dropped the roll still holding the tape, the tape unfurled all the way to the floor. So usually with duct tape when you kind of let go of the roll your hand can still hold it by just holding on to the tape and you have to actually really kind of tug at the tape to get it loose to use. So that’s the only thing I noticed that it was extremely easy to unfurl this tape from the role.

I can’t really tell much else because I just did it but it was easy to work with. I’ll let you know if it holds well through the wind and the dampness and whatever else and if not I will come back and update this review. But again the only thing I can really comment on is what I used it for.

title: Not a wire gauge for any wire in any wire system, this is a gauge for sheet steel.
text:
The description on this ad is fraudulent. You cannot use this tool to identify wire. Bought this to try and identify some unknown wire I had on hand. This is not made to identify wire gauge in any wire thickness standard (AWG, SAE, SWG, etc.). Pretty easy thing to look up. However this is correct for measuring the thickness of sheet steel. So I guess I'll keep it.

The diameter of copper wire varies based on the number of strands. So a solid conductor of one gauge can be smaller in diameter than a high strand count version of a lower gauge (higher numerically). So you can't really even make a wire gauge tool like this. I ended up just measuring the diameter of one strand and counting the number of strands. Strand number and diameter can be looked up to figure out the wire gauge.

title: Thinner prints are wonderfully translucent
text:
I got this pack of small spools because I only needed a small quantity of translucent material. I am printing small, thin objects like windows and lamp shades where translucency is important and this filament performed well. It is PETG, not PLA, so be sure to check your print settings, and the spools are not the standard 'full sized' spool - these are more of a sample sized, which for me, was ideal.

I made a couple of thin prints with this material - about 6 flat discs for windows in a model, and two larger, concave domes for other windows, and they turned out very well. The flat prints look like stained glass - totally clear and evenly colored. The domes, which required some support material due to the bridge distance in the centers, also turned out well, but not as clear as the flat prints (just as expected.) The thicker the material the less translucent it will be, but even with thicker prints, there is a wonderful level of light transmission.

I would buy this same pack again if I ran out of any given color. I am very pleased with it's performance. These are individually vacuum sealed with desiccant, as typical, and were print-ready right out of the package. It's simple to dry filament, but as a test, I printed straight from the box and got great results.

title: Good size, and very absorbent
text:
We use these in combination with ABD pads and/or a gauze wrap roll (curly) to absorb moisture from a weeping leg wound. They are soft, non-irritating, and absorb a significant amount of liquid to help keep the wound dry and sanitary to aid healing. They also effectively cushion the sensitive area around the wound.

Note that they also have NO adhesive component, so you'll need tape, a compression wrap, a curly like we use, or some other method to hold it in place. Depending on the quantity of exudate, these can be left in place for a day or two, or more, which is good because they are rather expensive. For our purposes we can cut them down to smaller sizes, which is fortunate because we have to change them fairly often.

A good product that works as represented, but like many such medical products, it's not inexpensive!

title: Work well for a basic absorbent wound covering
text:
These are a decently absorbent pad for covering a weeping wound, and absorb fairly well, holding a reasonable amount of exudate before leaking. They are not non-stick, and require a little care and saline solution to free them from the tender wound, nor do they contain silver or any other bacteria-inhibiting compound, but they are sterile, reasonably priced, and probably best used for daily bandage changes.

As stated, they have no built in adhesive border and so must be covered with some other type of bandage or gauze wrap to hold them in place.

A good option if a basic, non-adhesive, highly absorbent 4" bandage pad fills your needs.

These are NOT water proof, but can be made waterproof by the addition of liquid tape or electronic grade silicone (I am using liquid tape - just dipping the entire assembly with wires into the liquid and letting it dry).

text:
Initial Review Feb 11, 2023

I started a long detailed review but in the end there are too many things wrong with this vacuum. The bottom line is the actual robot seems to function as designed (vacuum only - we didn't try the mop feature), but the software that guides the robot around to clean just fails in so many ways.

We have a VIOMI V3 Max Robot Vacuum that is 1/3 the price but does not have the self empty feature. The VIOMI can clean our whole area in about 45 minutes. It is smart in how it creates and follows a pattern. It performs quite well and is fascinating to watch as it cleans. Not having the self empty feature isn't a big issue because our floors and carpets are normally pretty clean. We selected this Obode to be used for the second half of our house. Rather than deal with two maps we decided to have two robots.

This Obode takes 2 1/2 hours to clean the same area because it follows such an inefficient path. It will begin cleaning a room but the pattern it follows may actually have it leave that room for another before the first is clean. Ultimately it appears to clean the whole area as requested, but the pattern is so erratic it is hard to know if it did indeed cover everything.

The Obode doesn't seem to know where its own base is while cleaning. It tries to climb over the foot of the home base when is should very well know where it is.

The Obode had trouble with throw rugs. Rather than transitioning from the hard kitchen floor to the throw rug in front of the refrigerator it caught the edge of the rug and rolled it up. It eventually got itself untangled from the throw rug but it had trouble with all 5 throw rugs (the older robot vacuum never had this behavior).

Setup was easy.

The Android app also has issues. The robot had made one large room from out kitchen through to the living room. When I used the app to try to split the large room into two smaller rooms there was no button to push to actually cause the map split to occur.

I think the Obode could be vastly improved by updating the software. I will hang onto it for a while to see if the company develops updated software.

I'm very surprised by the other positive reviews. Perhaps there is something wrong with the one I have.

I do not recommend this robot.

title: CC3D has become my go-to for PETG filament
text:
Most of the things I make are custom functional items: An axehead edge cover, mounting supports for repair projects, parts hangers, tool jigs, project boxes, and mechanical parts. 3D design and printing lets me accomplish project goals.

When durability or outdoor use is in play, not the final product's surface finish, I always turn to PETG. And, since CC3D's PETG is the least expensive filament in my collection and delivers prints just as good as any other PETG I've used, I've started using it for printing almost everything that doesn't require post-processing to a smooth finish.

CC3D PETG is just as tough and easy to work with on my Ender 3 S1, which I outfitted with a titanium metal heat break and filament dryer, and I've never needed to change my CCD filament profiles when moving from one roll to the next. For large (for me) prints, I start my jobs in the evening, make sure the first few layers set up correctly, come back a couple of hours later to check for warping and other problems, then just let it run overnight and grab my print in the morning. Because it's cheaper than any other filament I use, I can print and refine designs to my heart's content without stressing about cost.

Things to know about working with PETG:
First, PETG filament absorbs water from the air like crazy, and that affects print quality. Pack your filament in a ziplock with a silica gel water absorbent to keep it dry between uses and get a filament dryer if you you run into print quality problems after your first few prints. My printer is in my basement workshop where the air is more humid; using a dryer made a huge difference. I just load my filament in the dryer with its silica gel pack in the center hole; it keeps the filament dry while printing.

Check your bed level (and make sure your bed is heating evenly) if you run into print adhesion failures. Better yet, get or upgrade to a printer with a "touch" sensor.

Fine-tune your print temperatures and speeds to work with your PETG. I use the "Test your 3D printer! v2" design by ctrlV on Thingiverse to do this. Start with the CC3D's suggested settings, then spend time fine-tuning them to get the best print possible on your printer. There are YouTube videos that will show you how to do this. Save the settings to a CC3D PETG filament profile and use that profile for future prints.

All PETG products like to string when the print head moves from one print surface to another. Use your slicer's "avoid crossing perimeters" and "wipe" settings to keep stringing to a minimum.

title: Whatever It is, It Isn't PETG! Never Seen Anything Like This
text:
I have the blue PETG from this company, which I purchased first. It was absolutely impressive, so I ordered the orange thinking it would be at least close. Oh no, this is galaxies apart from the blue. I have no idea what in the world this stuff is, but I know it ISN'T PETG.

I print a lot...A LOT. Probably burn through 6-10 rolls per week at minimum and it's 100% PETG. I will run every roll with the exception of a couple of manufacturers through my modified Jayo (Sunlu) fila-dryer at 53c for 6-10 hours with dessicant in the box to make certain that it's free of moisture and clean to print. Once dried, I then run a slicer flow calibration to make sure my flow is correct and I will do a couple test prints to make sure the squish is on point for each spool, even if it's the same brand/color. Not all lots are created equal, so I want to be sure my stuff is dialed before diving in and running 20+ hour prints.

With that said, I have run through half this 1kg spool trying my hardest to get it to print clean. Not possible. I have tried so many temps, speeds, flow etc. Tried it at 230c with 1.75mm/s retraction at 40mm/s retract speed, which I have only seen one other brand of PETG print that cool, mind you I am using an Ender 5 Pro with Micro Swiss Direct Drive and Hot End with a MS Hardened Steel .04 nozzle. Didn't like that. Tried several various temps and speeds from 230c to 252c, and reatraction all over the board as well as general print speeds from 75mm/s down to 40mm/s. Nothing at all yielded clean prints.

You can see by the pix attached, it has serious issues just staying together. I am half tempted to try it down at like 210c like PLA and see if it takes that. Nah, back this nonsense goes and I will get some reliable other material. I can't have business slowed down due to something that isn't what it claims, and it just isn't a PETG of any quality, if it's PETG at all. Other reviews have said very similar things, so I wouldn't be surprised if it is PLA that is mislabeled and it's just cooking the material. Either way, I won't waste another minute on it and I sure won't waste any money on it either. Sometimes you find a diamond in the rough with low priced PETG filaments, this one is just a lump of coal.

title: This model 70XL versus the NR3XL
text:
This is definitely the model you want for typical household use. Much better than the Wilkins NR3XL.

I've been running a 1" Wilkins NR3XL (their most basic model) pressure reducing valve on my residential water main line for about 4 years. I was always frustrated by the pressure dropoff with the most basic flow demands. To throw out some numbers, my incoming pressure is around 100 PSI, and I set the outgoing pressure to 60 PSI. If I turned on the kitchen sink faucet, I got a pressure drop of 20 PSI (to 40PSI). With a second demand, such as a toilet flush, the pressure dropped by over 30PSI (to about 30 PSI). I commonly had a working PSI of about 25 to 40 PSI under typical load.

I did some research and read that this model has much better flow capacity (i.e. less pressure dropoff under demand). I installed it and took new pressure measurements under load. Running the kitchen sink faucet now produces a dropoff of 3 PSI. Add flushing a toilet and running the bathroom sink and the total dropoff is still under 10 PSI. I now rarely see the working pressure go under 50 PSI. The pressure is much less variable now.

title: Certainly positionalbe, very very sticky.  Leaves string of adhesive when lifing item off
text:
I ordered this adhesive to use in cardmaking - to adhere layers of cardstock together. My hope was that the 'positional' element would allow me the opportunity to adjust the layers if they weren't perfectly positioned. Then use the scraper to make a permanent bond.

My experience so far is that it sort of works. First I cut a strip of the adhesive covered paper backing about .5 : wide. I placed that on the back of my A2 sized card, centered it, then pressed it down. It does make a permanent mount and I was able to adjust it slightly as long as I hadn't pressed too firmly. The problem with this technique is that the adhesive easily pulls away from the back sheet and develops sticky strings when it does so. those have to be managed somehow. It also made the scissors very sticky.

The next attempt was to unroll just a few inches of the adhesive, place it on a self-healing mat, and cut a strip with a rotary cutter. That didn't work at all, as the rotary cutter quickly got gummed up with the adhesive and the adhesive got on the self-healing mat - and it's still there. I haven't tried an adhesive remover yet, and that might take it off.

Then I tried placing the top layer of cardstock along the edge of the adhesive, trying to roughly get about .5 inch of adhesive on the edges of the back of the cardstock. Again, the strands of adhesive pull up off the backing and make a mess.

My last use was to use the adhesive as it is designed to be used - by placing the whole A2 sized pieces of cardstock on the adhesive, and use the backing sheet to adhere the whole things. Works fine, but again those strings of sticky adhesive make a mess.

After these experiments, I have to believe those who use this for mounting photos or artwork must also experience the 'sticky strings' phenomena, so I don't believe it's just my unorthodox attmpts to use it in a way not previously endorsed by 3M.

As this is a significant investment, I'm not going to discard this. I've thought about chilling it - would that tame the strings? But I don't know if refrigeration would cause other problems such as making the backing paper moist and/or affecting adhesive properties. I suppose I might cut a small piece off and try it. . .

Between discovering this item on Amazon and ordering it I pondered how to use it as it seemed like it might be a very affordable and effective answer to the cardstock layering dilemma, allowing me to adjust the position easily. I'm not giving up because if I can figure this out, I can seem so many uses for it. I'll report back with progress.

title: I like this better than my Roomba
text:
We have 12 cats in house, along with 2 regular vacuums, a hand vac, and a Roomba. Now, the roomba does a decent job of cleaning, but the biggest drawback is all the cat toys it eats. So, I started up this unit and let it do its initial run to map my 3200 sf house. Right off the bat, I noticed that it did NOT run over the cat's food and water stations, which sit on a low silicone mat. Then it took to mapping the rest of the kitchen, the utility and the family room. It successfully mapped out every piece of furniture as well as items that were sitting on the floor. It picked up every single bit of cat hair and litter and moved on. So, I wondered to myself, what happens if it hits a table and knocks a cat toy or something into its own path? I tossed a cat toy into its path...a place it had already mapped. It came within 3 inches of it, stopped, then circled it. It came back twice to make sure it was still there and on the second pass I picked it up. The vacuum was confused. It circled, looking for the cat toy, and then it moved on. It successfully transitioned to the carpet, made it over the transition from vinyl to tile flooring that the roomba can never seem to handle. On to the living room. It spotted and avoided every single thing in its path, seeking a way to vacuum around it and moving on. The cats were horrified and stayed a safe distance away. One got bold. He moved in to paw at the vacuum and it stopped, turning this way and that, trying to figure out why this object was moving. I guess it finally determined that the thing was alive and should be avoided, so it started out and went at the thing at regular (ramming?) speed. The cat never went near it again. My high-end roomba bangs into things and fails to avoid anything under about 6 inches square. This vacuum detects literally everything and avoids it. No crashing into tables and knocking things down. No shipped spots. I'm going to say straight up that I like this one better.

On to floor scrubbing. I followed all the instructions and it performed the same way as it had before, avoiding all objects and overlapping its paths so as to cover the entire floor. Vacuumed and then mopped, the floor in the kitchen was looking good. Bonus points for the self-emptying feature. More bonus points for it going to recharge when needed. The only con I saw was that this requires a small bag. I don't like emptying bags or even dealing with them. Finding replacements can often be costly and difficult. But over all, I like this unit far better than any mops or vacuums I've ever owned. It's a keeper and I think my new favorite weapon in the war against cat hair.

title: Didn't like it
text:
I bought this PETG filament to print accessories and parts for my 1/10th scale rock crawler because I read that PETG was stronger than PLA. My results with it did not bear this out. I found that my Identical PLA printed components were much stronger than the same printed with this PETG. I tried different print temps from 200 to 235 degrees, but none were as strong as the PLA part. (All parts were printed with 100% infill).
I am disappointed and will stick with PLA.

title: A sweet upgrade for my Ender 5!
text:
I have two Ender 5's and had recently upgraded my newer one with the Creality Silent board. I was so impressed with how quiet the printer is that I immediately ordered another one for my older Ender 5. Both boards worked flawlessy and have made my printers so quiet that all I hear now are the cooling fans on the power supply and the hot end. I used to worry about keeping my wife awake when printing at night but that worry is now gone.
When doing the swap, take pictures first before starting, then remove the hot-glue that helps hold tight the wires and plugs on your printer's original board. I used and X-Acto knife and that worked well. Once you have the glue off, start removing the old plugs and wires ONE at a TIME and plug them into the new board. Take your time and you'll be done in about 10 minutes. It is not difficult.
Glad I did this upgrade with these Creality 1.1.5 Silent boards!

title: Great Screw assortment for working on 1/10 scale RC trucks!
text:
I wanted to do some upgrades to my Redcat Racing Gen 8 Rock Crawler and knew I would need a lot of small metric screws so I ordered this kit from vigrue. There are many uses for small screws in the M2, M3 and M4 size so this assortment handled my needs nicely. I hate digging through a box or jar of small hardware looking for just the right screws or nuts, so having this on hand makes the task of working on your truck much more satisfying.
I would buy this kit again as it had all the hardware I needed and the different sizes were all bagged individually and placed in the marked compartments of the handy and well made plastic kit box. It is easy to keep things sorted properly. Bonus!

title: A cheap, durable Extruder upgrade from Creality.
text: I've seen pictures of extruder handles with grooves worn into them but my biggest fear was breaking the handle on the Extruder feed which would have caused several days of downtime. title: Handy expoxy putty, works well  for my  modelling applications
text:
I use this two part putty to fill in seams and holes in my 3D prints and to repair broken parts. It is easy to work with, just cut off a strip with the amount you need, knead it until the color is uniform, then apply and shape it where needed. It sticks well to plastic and forms well. It takes a little longer to harden than I expected from the directions, but it does harden up fully after a day or so. I like that it sands easily so I can get the right shape and finish I need for my model. It doesn't cure rock-hard so that you couldn't finish it. Another plus is that this stuff does not shrink. what you put on is what you get.
This putty works well for me and I'm glad I came across it as other modelling putties I tried were awful.

title: Should have been a great 3D printer but flawed execution made me send it back!
text:
I really wanted to love this printer. I was looking for a dual extruder printer after having become very comfortable with my Creality Ender 5. The Hictop D3 Hero arrived quickly and was well packed. Assembly was pretty simple and I was looking forward to some nice prints. I levelled the bed, adjusted the second extruder to match the first and prepared to print the two color dragon from the supplied SD card. Unfortunately the Hictop printer would not read the card. I solved this by copying the files from the card onto my computer, reformatted the SD card and copied the files back.
The card could then be read and the sample dragon printed out beautifully.

I then tried to print a 2.5" to 3.5" hard drive adapter. This should have been simple, it was a large, flat object with good adhesion potential. Unfortunately it got knocked off shortly into the print. This happened for the next few prints as well.
I rechecked the bed level for both extruders, and tried again. No luck. Suspecting the bed, I got my straightedge out and discovered the bed was warped badly in the front right corner. I sent an email to hictop_usa support hoping they would resolve the issue.

I tried adjusting the clamps that held down the glass bed so that they minimized the warp so that I could continue testing and was able to print objects that weren't too large.
I then set up an Octoprint server so I wouldn't have to keep flipping SD cards in and out of the machine. I have an Octoprint server set up on my Creality Ender 5 and it is awesome, especially using The Spaghettie Detective plugin.

I had a bit of trouble getting the Octoprint server to connect to the Hictop. I had to run Octoprint in safe mode to reliably connect. I tried several prints but was never able to successfully print from Octoprint. The printer would stop at some random point in the print every time. I again emailed Hictop about the problem, hoping for resolution.

I then tried the two color Panda print again, this time printing from the SD card since there appeared to be a severe communications issue when printing via Octoprint.
The print started out nicely, but I noticed after a few hours that there was a huge layer shift that started about half way up the print. The shift was about a full inch (see the photo) .

I cancelled the ruined print and gave up on the Hictop, still not having heard a reply to either of my emails.
I began the return with Amazon (Yay, Amazon and your return policy!) Took the printer apart, packed it back up in the original packaging and returned it.
I had high hopes for the printer, but they weren't matched by the product. To be honest, I know there are some people on the Hictop Facebook forum who are getting great results and reliable prints, but with the lack of support response I got, I was not going to take the chance of blowing through my return window with Amazon.
It's been another week and still no reply from Hictop Support to my original requests for support. I had hoped that perhaps they would respond to my issues and maybe I would try another Hictop D3 Hero, but I think I will be more satisfied with another Ender 5. I know their support (Comgrow) is good.

title: Really cleans that cruddy jewelry.
text:
I searched through the Ultrasonic cleaner reviews on Amazon and decided that this had the most/best reviews and was a good price. The unit arrived promptly, thanks to Prime, and I loaded it up with hot water, dish soap and dirty jewelry. It took a couple of goes at 4 minutes each, but did the job. I really bought it to clean the jewelry that I make after buffing. It really gets loaded with silver dust, buff fiber and polishing compound. You can see the black just boil off the piece when you turn on the cleaner. I like that it has several different run time cycles to choose from. It is small, quiet and works great! Just be sure to use hot water, and a little soap or cleaner. I see some people actually use alcohol in it for really dirty stuff.
I'm going to get a lot of use out of this unit.

title: Great replacement bearings.
text:
I ordered these to replace the bearings that came with the Marathon 11x4.00-5" Flat Free Tire on Whee that I had ordered for my Troy-Bilt Mustang 42" Zero Turn Mower. The wheels are great, but they require cutting or grinding down the hub to fit on the narrower Troy-Bilt front wheel assembly.
I didn't quite get them right and had to knock the bearings out for more grinding and ended up damaging them.

These replacements came quickly and were economically priced. I pulled the seals on them, as some other reviewers suggested, and added more quality grease to the bearings and then put the seals back in place.

The bearings turn easily and will hopefully last a long time. I made sure not to abuse them putting them back in (after I'd ground the hubs down further) and with the grease top-off i did, they should be nicely lubricated.

So far, my mower is running nicely with the new bearings.

title: Cure that awful noise in your mixer with this excellent white grease.
text:
When my wife's KitchenAid mixer started making noises I knew it was time for a lube job. This grease is synthetic and works across a wide range of temperatures, but most important is that it is FOOD GRADE for use in kitchen appliances. It is also WHITE so it won't leave greasy marks on your appliances either. Please note however, as metal wears and oxidizes, it can transfer to the grease and turn it darker or black. In that case, wipe everything clean, re-grease and you should be good to go again for quite a while.

So, I cleaned out the old grease in my wife's mixer, re-greased it with the Super Lube and now life is quiet again.

There is enough grease in this can to do the mixer several times, so should the noise come back down the road, I'm ready.

title: Great little temperature controller, excellent value!
text: This little temperature controller is amazing for the small price.  I'm using it to control the temperature of a fodder sprouting station that I use to create fodder to feed animals on our homestead. I wired the controller up to an extension cord that supplies power to a small heater that blows warm air into the fodder unit.  The heater is cheap and has no thermostat, but the Inkbird unit handles it marvelously!  The unit is easy to connect and program, and also has a relay for cooling, should I ever need it. For the small price, this Inkbird digital Temperature controller really solved my problem.  I love the digital display, it lets me monitor the temperature inside my fodder unit, and verify that all is well. The included temperature probe was longer than I expected and was easy to connect and mount, and is very responsive.  I wouldn't hesitate to buy another of these units should the need to control temperature arise.

title: good non adhesive ag+ dressing
text: I take care of a family member with a chronic would so we go through dressings all the time I used to use meplilex ag but it's gotten even more expensive than it already was so I'm always looking for cheaper alternatives. This dressing isn't adhesive so you'll need some method of attaching it I used paper medical tape and that worked fine. The wound it is protecting has a lot of drainage so depending on how it felt it was changed about every other day it does have an ag+ rating so it will fight against colonization which is critical for any chronic wound this feature also means that the amount of time you can use this will depend on how much drainage you have. Speaking of drainage the dressing held a good amount of drainage it's a little hard to tell how much drainage the dressing has absorbed once it's on because the back has that typical bandage silicone cover on top of the actual pad so you have to ask the patient how wet it feels or partially remove it to check on it luckily the dressing is not adhesive so this isn't hard to do.  Overall this is a good ag+ dressing it's non adhesive but that can be a positive or a negative depending on your needs, If you need to treat a chronic wound this is a good option it meets all of the critical requirements in my opinion for chronic wound care and is priced competitively especially considering the size of the dressing.

After a thorough cleaning of the printhead, the third clog was 7 hours into an 8-hour print. I gave two stars instead of one because that first spool was fine, maybe you'll get a good one.
EDIT: The company reached out to me and sent a replacement spool, I haven't had a chance to try that 3rd spool yet but I bumped the rating up a star for now because of their response. The next time I need to print using black PLA I will give it a try.

How I review:
When I review a product said product automatically starts with four stars as I rarely will purchase anything below four stars. I then add and/subtract stars based on certain criteria as listed below.
1. If an item is exactly what I expected and nothing more it will receive a four star rating
2. If an item surpasses my expectations it will gain a star (5 Stars)
3. If an item goes slightly below my expectations it will lose a star (3 Stars)
4. If the instructions for the product (if needed) are poorly written (hard to understand due to language issues or grammar) or just too hard to follow it will lose a star no matter if the product meets or exceed my expectations
5. If a product is significantly below my expectations I will deduct two stars
6. It will be rare that I would give a product one star since I buy mostly items that have a 4+ rating but in rare instances there may be a good reason that even a four star product receives a one star rating from me. It could be because of customer service issues from the company but whatever the case is I will clearly explain my reason for giving a product only one star

title: Very easy to use PERFECT waffle iron, Properly break it in and you will LOVE it.

Preheated to Green light at max setting, Repeated a couple of times to function check, Burned off any factory coating and season plates. This thing probably got assembled and never has been fired up before setting on my counter. Let it cool to touch. Wiped down plates. Set control at mid point. Frist batch of waffles tossed just because. They looked fine, but were just a test. No sticking. No problems moved control to higher, darker setting.

Perfect waffles, No fuss. No spray. No sticking. Pre heat closed. Green light, Ladle in waffle batter. Close and wait till Green light comes back on.
Repeat until you run out of batter or you have made all the waffles you desire.

Same Machine, same file still in the machine, I put some green Inland PLA+ like the Gold Mushroom in the pics (This stuff is the best PLA+ you will find) and it's printing beautifully right away as usual with nothing changing but a different PLA. SO I would say that is a pretty good acid test. 4 scenarios with exactly the same everything, the only difference is the PLA. You tell me what more I can try. I'll never buy this crap again. I'll never buy anything but Inland PLA+ from now on. I told myself not to get this crap but my wife thought it looked cool, and the reviews seemed good. Well I bench tested to set up the firmware and DWIN_SET. Software seemed to load, Display loaded fine. Now I have a display but if I touch anything it locks up and I have to power it off. I tried it on my Ender Pro 3 that has a working touchscreen and same thing. I load the old firmware for the the off brand touchscreen and BAM works perfectly. So either this is a bad unit or the software doesn't work because I am obviously doing it correctly or I could not have gotten my old touch screen works right away again perfectly. SO I would suggest staying away from this product. Also seems that you loose many features because the firmware sucks.

title: Vibration Town
text: Put them on my Ender 3 Pro. Easy to attach and have nice jumper cables. Right away I noticed a vibrating noise when I had it go "Home". The motors worked fine however they were moving in a way that cause a vibration. I did 3 prints and it never changed. It's rather annoying since the printer is so quiet with the new MB. I noticed no difference in print quality from without them. I was surprised because you can physically feel the vibration in the chassis. So maybe I did something wrong but it doesn't matter with direction you hook them up. From my point of view it was a waste of time and money. Perhaps you may have different results.

title: Jaw Dropping
text: I got scared when I first got it installed it because some guy kept screaming "Oh My God", and then I realized it was me. It really is jaw dropping. The leveling is off the chart cool. It adds so many more features it's like getting a new main board. For the price it's really a no brainer. Getting rid of the piece of crap rotary encoder on the old screen makes it worth it alone. Just make sure you get the files from the link on the product description. First take the back off the new touch screen and make sure you have a non conductive spot you can place it while flashing it. The it's a bit tricky because the sd card slot is upside down at the crook of the mounting plate and I had to use needle nose to get it in and out. WHY!!! Anyway, put the card in with the "FOLDER" of the  DWIN_SET you downloaded. Turn on you will get the text on the screen showing it updated. Turn off. Now put the Main Board bin file in the sd card slot on the printer this time and fire it up. It takes about a minute so don't get excited, give it a second. Then the screen comes up looks great. I accidentally put the new regular bin file in the first time and it worked but it was in Chinese and I freaked out, then I check my files and realized what I did, re flashed the board with the new bin file I downloaded from the product description and it was in English and worked great. All I can say is your going to want to get this unit, it is a "Have to Have" in my opinion.

title: One Bad Spool of Filament! Well it was until I dried it out...
text:
Looked really nice. Spent an entire day thinking my printer was off. I have never experienced anything like this before. ZERO adhesion to the bed or itself. Changed to my my brand and instantly had beautiful prints. I would say that is a pretty solid acid test.
Update:
After 2 days of a good vacuum sealed heated dry out I gave it another test before I sent it back. To my amazement it prints exceptionally well. It must have gotten some moisture in it somewhere. So is you have this problem just dry it out before you send it back because it's pretty darn nice PLA.

I would like to apologize to YSF for making a snap judgment before attempting to dry it.

title: Has amazing cleaning power! The app could use some work, but it cleans wonderfully.
text:
First off: The cleaning on this thing is wonderful. It vacuums incredibly well. The mopping seems to do a good job too. You can create rooms where it won't mop at all, such as carpeting or rugs, and I believe it automatically senses carpet as well. The vacuuming power is amazing! It's definitely one of the strongest ones I've ever come across. In terms of cleaning ability, this thing gets a solid 5 stars.

One huge thing is I do wish there was a way to make the machine go back to the dock and empty out the dust tray while it's cleaning. I live off of a main road in a decently sized city, so there is a lot of dust and debris that gets in. I have to manually stop the machine, tell it to go back to the charging base (where it automatically empties) and then restart the cleaning again to get it to do what I want. A setting that would allow it to empty itself out and return to cleaning the room it was in would be *wonderful*.

I'm only giving this product 4 stars because of the software. I've run into some issues with the scheduled cleaning, where I have it in my correct time zone to clean at 1600 (4 PM), but it'll start cleaning at 0500 instead... It's very odd, and I've tried to fix it and sync the time zones multiple times, but it doesn't work. The mapping system is wonderful, but I did have some trouble trying to create room zones with the app's tool. It's a line you drag across the doorway/section you want to be separate from another room. With enough attempts it finally went through, but I was having some issues with it at first. To be fair, though, the customer support was happy to help, and they got back to me in a timely manner.

I've been very happy with this machine. I think the $510 sale price point is a much more fair price than the $600 price point, but I do think both are reasonable.

title: Nice PETG once it is dried.
text:
Purchased this and it was delivered on August 21st. Was tried a few days ago and it was very blobby and stringy. Normally I do not have that problem. Since that is a symptom of moisture in PETG the printing was stopped and the filament was dried for 4 hours at 150F. After that the prints came out perfect so the filament appears to have been sent damp. It was in a vacuum sealed bag with a desiccant package.

I like the color, it is almost silky appearing and the green is a very nice color. Parts come out strong and no delamination or other problems were noted. Just a problem with it initially being wet.

If you are experiencing blobbing and excessive strings and normally do not have that problem try drying this filament out if you bought some. The wetness will not keep me purchasing more as I do like the appearance of the finished prints and will dry any I pick up before printing with it,

title: 40 grit flap discs with plastic insert
text:
These flap discs have a bit of a different design to them than normal grinding/sanding discs. The center is a raised plastic that I was worried may become loose or wear down before the sandpaper did but I have had absolutely no issues at all. The disc sticks down a bit away from the tool which keeps the disc clear of hitting anything. I was able to tighten up the collet as much as I would on any other disc and they never came loose during use.

The quality of the flap disc paper is good. These are all 40 grit so good for heavy rust and paint removal. I use 40 grit a lot and they do tend to wear out quick when working on older materials with a lot of build up. I haven't noticed these wear any faster than other brands, including more expensive discs I've used. I would never pay more for "brand name" flap discs after using these and other lower cost discs from Amazon. The quality is great for the price and the 13,000 RPM limit of these discs is will over the 9,000 RPM of my entry level electric and pneumatic grinders. Great discs for home use but professionals may be happy with these as well. The quality is much nicer than I was expecting at this price of around 1.60 per disc.

title: Excellent for dog post surgery
text: Our GSD had a weird lump removed from his leg, and the resulting wound was about the size of a half-dollar coin. We needed dressings at home to protect the wound while it healed, and the vet advised against using typical dry bandaids or gauze and tape as the wound would dry out which would significantly slow down healing. I remembered having ordered these, and I am very glad I did as these dressings were the perfect solution. Not only did they absorb exudate quickly and completely, our dog's wound was kept clean and properly moist for optimum healing. We did change his bandage every day for the first few days as instructed, but then would leave these on for two or three days at a time before changing out. The area around his wound hand been shaved, but the adhesive on these bandages was gentle enough not to cause any irritation. The squares stayed on decently well considering they couldn't adhere to bare skin and the area of the wound was right below his hind 'knee'. By the end of two weeks and this box of bandages, our dog's leg was completely healed. There wasn't even the usual crusty scab on the wound which was great. This meant he wouldn't lick the spot trying to relieve any itching or discomfort caused by the scab flaking off or the skin around it being dry and itchy. I ended up buying another box to have on hand after my mom's hip surgery. Once again these bandages did a fanatic job healing her surgical wound. We still have a few left, but I will be ordering more as well as other offerings from this company.

text:

An email to the support email address never got answered and all I got on Amazon answers was short answers that really did not help.

My main concerns are that this deals with Butane, which is highly flammmable. I also want to make wax with a purity that doesn't contain traces of Butane. To do this, I need a vac pump and purge chamber. But you would never know this from buying the unit as there was no documentation included at all. And they don't answer their support phone.

Physically, the extractor is very well built. This unit should last a long time. This unit would have gotten 5 stars if they had better support and documentation.
