title: Great price for fiberglass if you need small pieces or long piece if you don't require a super flat surface..
text: For the price, It's great even unbeatable. There is creases everywhere so it would not be good for a long flat surfaec but for my subwoofer enclose, this was perfect!

title: very sticky
text:
I use more duct tape than anyone I know, so I feel I'm a bit of an expert.
This duct tape is of decent quality as far as I can tell.
Something else I like about it is that it comes with a division between the two rolls so that they don't stick together like I've seen some other rolls do in the past.
It rips fairly easily so you can still use it if you don't have scissors handy.
It is very sticky which is another good thing.

The only nit I see is that sometimes when you rip a piece off, it will leave a string. If you have a habit of using scissors to cut it, then you don't have to worry about it, since it won't happen.

title: Works really well
text: I used this to print ear savers for a couple friends on my Anycubic i3 MEGA.  It printed as well or slightly better than other PETG’s I’ve tried.  I still get more stringing than PLA or ABS. But it’s more flexible than PLA and I don’t need to worry about curling like ABS.  The trade off is definitely worth it.

title: Good idea but difficult to deliver
text: To get this to print welly, many things need to go right, including things you can't control, including the filament winding onto the spool and whether any twisting is introduced. However, I've gotten "banding" of color on every print. This is true while using a bowden tube and a direct drive extruder. Good idea, but not sure how to avoid this issue. 3/5 because it still printed well.

title: Good glass, plastioc OK
text: Glass is perfect, plastic base fit and finish is poor.

title: Great value.  Great price.
text: This is a great kit for prototyping and contains every value you would need in a single turn trimmer resistor.  Leads are fully plated and straight.  The materials are equivalent to consumer level quality which again is great for prototyping.  Total resistance tolerance on a random sample was about 10% per part.  I've used several already in a couple of projects and made at least 50 turns per unit with no affect on accuracy or noise.  It's very nice to get a divided parts box with a label indicating where the values are.  So I think this kit is a great value for the price.

title: Not worth trying
text:
I tried every nozzle temp and bed temp I could. Glass bed, spring steel, polypropylene and standard ender beds. This stuff was just awful.

Stringy, gloopy mess.

I have 4 printers and have gone through, literally hundreds of rolls of PLA, PET, PETG, Nylon and ABS. I have all metal hotends and dual gear extruders. This honestly was the worst stuff I have tried. I threw away half the roll.

title: Five Stars
text: Perfect for what I was doing. Used in with my fish pond.

title: Incredible Value
text: These switches are amazing! They're very smooth stock, and have a very bouncy feel to them. I actually prefer these to Gateron Pro Yellows, as they feel less mushy.

title: Works Well
text: I have animals that I'm allergic to, so I use these so I don't break out when I clean their enclosure. They work well, even grabbing hay with them, they still resist punctures. They've got a bit of a matte texture too, which makes grabbing things easier.

title: Very nice PETG, prints very well,
text:
This is a very well priced nice working PETG.
Does have the very fine stinging that is common to PETG, but it prints very well on my DIY printer at at 250C (My printer has to run hotter than most)

title: One of the best PETG filaments i've used so far.
text:
This roll printed realy well. I had no problems that were not printer or settings related.
Once I had it dialed in , it printed great. I will be purchasing more.

title: Overall decent
text: These are not the easiest to fold and assemble. Though they aren't super hard either. The lower back seam is just a little tricky to get to fold the right direction. They aren't the sturdiest of bakery boxes, but not the flimsiest by far. As long as you don't overfill they should be fine.

title: Prints great with just the right amount of squish.
text:
Prints great even with a bowden setup like in my Ender3v2.

Layers bond well to each other, and the first layer holds perfectly to my hairsprayed smooth PEI sheet (unheated for this material).

Printed the tire in the photo with 10% gyroid infill and it squishes just like a 'real' tire would.

Surface finish is fantastic, especially for the sidewalls. A little scuff on the tread surfaces and they'll look just like the real thing.

I also have a combo pack of 500g black and white. The white prints great just like the black, but has a REALLY good squish, best of the TPUs I've tried.

title: Decent for the price
text: It's decent petg filament, thigh it prints and feels more like pla. Not as flexible as some other the petg I have used, but still decent. Overall decent, but I wouldn't buy unless you just want some decent and cheap filament for running test prints

title: Prints nice and nice color
text: Prints nice and nice bright color. I would buy it again. No problems at all.

title: Good product
text: The tape is just what I expected and it came right on time

title: No adhesive, nicely cushioned
text:
I've been using foam dressings instead of bandaids because of a skin allergy to the bandaid's sticky adhesive material. These 4x4 are a good size for larger wounds or sores, and are nicely cushioned. They can but cut down to size. Very comfortable for days of usage, nicely packaged, each foam dressing is individually packed. Note that each foam dressing does NOT come with a built-in adhesive, as a result, you must use your own. For example, I use 3M micropore tape to keep it in place.

**10/12/2022 UPDATE** I've had a case of cellulitis and these foam dressings have been a GODSEND. They don't stick to the wound like gauze or adhesive dressings or bandaids do. The foam provides a very comfortable cushion. Although they lack adhesive, just use surgical tape. In fact, these have been so helpful that I'm buying another box.

title: Great larger style dressing pads!
text: These are great for larger wounds or cuts. Easily paired with some medical tape and keep the wound clean and absorbs any oozing or bleeding that may occur.

title: Good color, sturdy prints.
text: I have been trying a lot of filament lately. This stuff has been a little finicky for me. It seems strong but has a narrow temp range for me. I like the color. It's bright and just different enough from other colors that I can tell the brand apart. Was at a great price so I would probably buy it again.

title: Contact
text: Working very well. Using for a direct starter button on a 11 horse  500cc Briggs engine on a pressure washer. Now I see a Moroso one for less money though. Bah Humbug.

title: Used to connect porch swing chain to 1/2 inch eye hook in rafter.
text: Very strong and well made.  Able to connect porch swing chain to 1/2 inch eye hook in rafter.  Was able to hold my wife and my weight in swing. (500-550lbs tested.)

title: Naga is great affordable filament
text: This red PETG is no different than the other NAGA filaments I use. It has become one of my go to brands for consistent quality and great price, much cheaper than most brands. I haven't received a tangled roll from them yet and they are always vacuum sealed when they reach me. Their color range and filament types are growing every time I get online to look for more.

title: good upgrade kit for most bed slinger printers
text: This is a good kit with the MK8 nozzles and silicone spacers that most bed slingers can benefit from. The red wheels are just a bonus and in my opinion don't improve anything but looks. But this kit is the same price as a pack of the silicone spacers I got a couple of years ago for my first printer so great value overall.

title: Can easily burn them
text:
Cannot confirm if it is actually 4:1 but it does the trick. ok selection of sizes for the kit but the lengths could be longer. I use a small torch instead of a heat gun so you have to be careful not to burn them as it takes a little longer to get the adhesive lined tubes to heat up enough. Take your time and don't hold the heat in one spot too long.

Overall, can recommend as it did the LED wiring cleanup I was doing on my truck an easy job.

title: Not a huge fan of this brands silk
text:
I use Naga PLA+ for most of my PLA printing as it is very inexpensive for its capabilities and color selections. Had hopes for the silk to mirror that but I am not really impressed. regardless of the flow and temp I haven't gotten really good layer adhesion like I know I can get. It is great for anything but decorative, which lets face it, really is all the silks are good for.

The price for this silk though is great when comparing it to some of the other well established manufacturers out there so you can't go wrong there. Plus the silk green is sort of a unique offering.

title: serves its purpose
text: I got these to create small UV lights to go inside my resin prints to cure the inside that my curing chamber doesn't get to. Does the trick once you get a small power source.

title: Who in the heck doesn't need 200 springs
text:
I do quite a bit of crafting and 3d printing. That is about the only reason I can find a reason for using these. The price is well worth the few I will end up using, but who doesn't need to have a very small, but packed full, bit of springs.

These will come in handy for a good long time.

title: Greatful for NAGA
text:
NAGA has brought reliable and repeatable results to printing. Competes with the likes of Sunlu or Duramic for PLA+ but has become my go to for TPU.

Lost a star for lack of colors but hopeful they will grow the pallet soon. As usual with TPU, it is particular with temps and retraction and speed and even moisture so it will take some tuning for your particulars. Waste 50g doing your calibration prints and get it right before jumping into the bigger prints.

title: Very good assortment
text:
I get kits like this frequently to refill smaller hardware bins and this one does not disappoint. It does not have a huge amount of any one size but better than most in this price range. This one is keeping my stock up longer than most kits and seems to be of actual stainless unlike some of these cheap kits.

Comes with tweezers to help and very cheap wrenches (don't torque down on them) but useable for most applications.

title: Overpriced for PETG
text:
Does what any other PETG I run does. Solid prints at the expected temp ranges and holds up strength wise. But I if you can get similar results at 20% less why would you not.

I got the least amount of stringing at 235 and no issues on adhesion on PEI about 70 on the typical cheap ender machine.

lost the 1 star from 5 for what you gotta spend on it.

title: Good spares
text: Good nozzles to keep for spare. Took out of the foam and added more to the plastic container as there was tons of wasted space with the foam in there. How well the hardened nozzles hold up, time will tell.

title: My absolute favorite filament.
text:
For prints you wont be painting, this is my absolute favorite. I don't like much of the dual and tri extrusion filaments because they are mostly silks and I am tired of those and they print poorly compared to plain old PLA or PLA+. This being matte really made a huge difference there. Such a great looking color combination.

Temp tower came in looking great at a wide range of temps and stringing almost non existent. That disappeared with some tuning of retraction. Roll was wound well and sealed out of the box. Sits in my roughly 40% humidity print room without issue so far.

title: Awesome filament
text:
This stuff is probably my favorite dual color except it being silk. I wouldn't call it black and red though, which is why it lost the star. The pictures are accurate though, it is a pink and grey dual color roll and that still makes it beautiful in my book.

My temp tower from 230 to 190 was all the same with ever so slightly different color saturation at lower vs higher temps but 205 looked best to me. Stringing was non existent. Came well sealed and wound well on the roll. Good price for dual color silks

title: The absolute best thing for creality printers
text:
What a great thing to finally bring klipper to the masses. I was just getting started with klipper and it is daunting to say the least. Took a lot of reading and rereading, at least for me, until I was comfortable trying it. Then along comes the Sonic Pad and it does all the hard work for you.

I have this connected to my 5 S1 and my 3 Max neo. I couldn't get it connected to my 3rd max neo so not sure if it had to do with the multiple printers with same specs or what. Gave up for a while but will attempt again when I have the time to mess with it.

Cannot say enough how much this has made my printing more enjoyable. Even if it is for the simple fact it can replace up to 4 raspberry Pi's for remote upload/printing. Looking forward to learning more and seeing if I can get it working with some of my non ender printers.

title: Not very matte if you ask me
text: This prints find and is wound decent. Came well vacuum sealed and being the variety pack, it was packaged well. But I don't see this as being very matte in sheen. The colors sorta appear to be matte like but there is still some shine to the print. I know that can change with the temperature but at least for me that didn't seem to make a difference, at least not in the range of temps this printed cleanly at.

title: My best printer
text:
This turned into my best printer. It was number 9 in my collection and it is by far the best one. I tend to wait until it is free to print the majority of stuff. Its fast and clean.

When I first got it I had more layer adhesion for the first 2-3 mm of print but a firmware update with the sonic pad and I was good to go. Seems a semi common issue so just flash the firmware to most recent and get to printing.

This is probably one of my only printers I can say is absolutely a beginner friendly setup. easy to assemble and very intuitive. Needed the least amount of adjusting and tweaking out of all of my Creality machines. I am thinking of selling off my other printers that have the same or similar build plate size and replacing with a couple more of these.

Paired with the sonic pad it does best but even without it is great and worth it.

title: No Glow
text:
didn't get any glow out of this filament. Even when blasted with my resin curing UV flashlight it barely glowed. Bit of a waste as the color is useless for anything unless I am going to paint.

Wound well and printed easy so it has that going for it at least.

title: Cannot get it to glow
text: This is basically just an off-white filament for me, no glow to it whatsoever. Aside from that it prints like any other PLA for me. Temp and retraction towers match the majority of PLA's I run so no need for extra filament profile. Will probably keep this on hand for when I run parts to paint but not for the benefit of glow in the dark.

title: Always worth having a spare on hand
text: I have a couple of these now because I like to have a spare. This one actually went into a machine I am modifying but its a bit of a Frankenstein's monster. Good thing about these creality hotends, they are basically universal and easy to get setup with all the gantry mounts available.

title: Good TPU
text: I have had a couple of other TPU's that just like this one, are tough to get dialed in but once you figure it out then these are a lot of fun. I used this one for making timing belts for some of my 3d printed gadgets. One oddity with this one is it prints much cooler than most of my TPU. This one likes 190 while the rest are 210-225. I only have one of my direct drive printers I use TPU for so I cannot say it changes with machine yet or how it does in a bowden setup.

title: Handy for a dryer but
text:
This is great, like many of the available dryers out there, for making sure your hydrophobic filaments are good and dry. This one gives you the option of drying 2 rolls which is great if you are running a couple of printers side by side or in my case, a dual extruder single hotend setup.

the down side is that if you need to swap one of the rolls, it is difficult not to disturb the feeding of the other roll. So don't count on being able to swap mid print. Because of this I will use this as a dryer not feeding my printers.

title: Not great
text:
Got this to make lithophane globes/ornaments. Very hard to get dialed in and seems to be very particular with the settings which I haven't gotten to my liking yet. Ended up having to go back to my usual white to get done by Christmas, which printed right away without issue.

Now that I have some more time I will go back and try again. The color is also more of an opaque (picture watered down milk) when printing thin walls like needed for lithophanes.

title: Great gift bags
text: I added a sticker that I printed to these gift bags. They work great for small goodies to give out.

title: Very cool filament
text:
Very easy printing filament. Unique color/glitter and will make some really cool models I have planned.

Temp towers printed consistent across 25 degrees without much in the way of stringing or quality loss. Failed once they hit 190 on my machine which is lower than most of my filaments anyways. 215 seemed to be the sweet spot for me. Good layer adhesion across all those temps too.

This is my first Stronghero filament but they have some really unique combinations and will definitely be getting some more.

title: Finally some durable minis
text:
I stumbled on this by chance and wanted to give it a go. I don't do a ton of miniatures but have been getting into it more lately. One issue I had was the fragility of detailed models with weapons that were easy to break. This stuff seems to have solved that issue.

I am still trying to get it dialed in and have had more failed prints than good ones but I think once I get it dialed in it will be my go to. I am excited to try mixing this with my usual resin just to give it a bit of durability also.

title: Good easy printing filament
text:
Filament was not quite vacuum sealed but whether it unsealed during shipment or from the factory is unknown. While it hasn't jammed or gotten tangled it also isn't wound great. I don't expect any issues from the winding but if that changes I will update my review.

What this filament does excel at is the printing. Very forgiving in temp ranges, I could barely tell a difference between 195 and 215 on my temp tower. Even above or below that did ok but you could see the quality slightly drop. Great layer adhesion across the entire temp tower though. Was hard pressed to break it with pliers and it withstood more than I would have expected it to.

title: Nice filament for the price
text:
Printed the usual calibration prints and honestly am able to use the same settings I use for PLA plus. Temp towers from 220 down to 190 show almost no difference between temps. I even sped up my print by almost double and got same results with just a slightly lower quality print.

Roll came well packaged and vacuum sealed which is common now but the winding is perfect as well.

Color selection is lacking so far but for an inexpensive PLA, they have the basics. I will certainly be using them again

title: Good price for a PLA
text:
Printed well in the usual calibration prints. For me temps between 190 and 200c were indistinguishable as far as layer adhesion and print quality. Anything above that and stringing started showing up.

Came packaged halfway decent in a box and then vacuum sealed. Winding wasn't near as neat as depicted in the pictures. I haven't had a tangle but it wouldn't surprise me if it did.

This brand has a halfway decent selection of colors but nothing unique. There are better filaments out there and cheaper, if you buy bulk. If you are only buying a roll or two though, this isn't a bad price. If you are content with an unknown brand.

title: Do not waste your time
text:
I have been 3d printing for a few years now and have 6 or 7 printers running (depending on if I have any taken apart at the time) most days. I don't run a farm, I just really like the hobby and tinkering with them and changing parts and upgrading and all that.

The last couple of years 3d printers have become a more mainstream thing. They have come down in price drastically and made it affordable for most people to get into the hobby. With that comes company's like this that do the bare minimum. That may be a bit harsh but taking components like the direct drive and silent stepper drivers on a decent (though I am not familiar with the brand) main board, they pairing it with motion motors that I am not sure are actually stepper motors and no user interface.

Assembly is easy, though the assembly video flys through so quick you have to pause and rewatch a few times. Leveling (tramming) is a nightmare on this thing because you cannot easily reach the bed leveling nuts. Then the worst part of this thing, the controls.. The play button is pretty much the only thing you have to touch, which grabs the most recent gcode you put on the card. In the case of what comes with it is a tiny rocket. Printed fine. Then I found the calibration cat on the card as well but had to delete the rocket for the printer to even see that the cat was there to print. It printed ok but there is lots to improve on the overhangs.

So you have to slice a file and put it on the card. Nothing new there but then you are stuck being only able to print that one thing until you either add a new file or delete that one. So there is no option to slice a bunch of stuff and print one thing after another. A screen user interface that allows at least scrolling through files and settings is a must.

Now I received this for an honest review. And my honest opinion is this is not a $100 dollar printer. This is a $50 dollar printer at best. I wouldn't consider this a beginner friendly printer either because if I hadn't already known what I do about printers I would have given up pretty quick getting this thing going.

This will sit on my shelf until I find a project I can take it apart for, or maybe fire it up once a month when my daughter wants a trinket that my other printers are too tied up for.

title: Seems to work
text: This seems to be working, but I think I need more to completely cover the flowers. I will update this review in a few weeks.

title: I think this is my favorite now
text:
This is my first "matte" filament and I was blown away. I have about 75 rolls of filament sitting on my shelves and this one is now my favorite when it comes to color. I print a lot of black and white for my tests or prototyping but for fun toys or decorative stuff, this one beats the rest easy.

I think the matte does a great job of hiding the layer lines that even the best tuning can't always get rid of. This is also my first roll of eSUN, but won't be my last. Roll came vacuum sealed tight and rolled neatly so there is no worry of tangling.

title: Great hotend swap
text:
I have a few of these now and love them. I am constantly playing with my printers to see what I can get out of them and having a reliable hotend capable of higher temps and having all metal in the heat zone gives you the opportunity to push it.

This kit comes with the heater cartridge but no thermistor so keep that in mind. You will never be able to just swap a component like this and get good results without proper tuning so keep that in mind.

title: Tough to dial in but unique TPU
text:
As with most TPU, it is hard to dial in but slow is critical. It seems a little harder than other 95A I have but I also didn't print thin. The color change is so gradual you almost need a large or dense model to make use of it.

Overall it is a fun filament to play with or have on the shelf for one of those lightbulb idea moments. It is much pricier than others that are comparable quality though.

title: Love this hotend setup
text:
I have a couple of these now and am very happy with the results I get. I am a tinkerer so I am always playing with my printers and pushing their capabilities and having a reliable hotend capable of higher temps and having all metal in the heat zone gives you the opportunity to push it.

These are great for an easy swap on most enders but there are so many adapters out there and it is easy to make your own to fit your printers needs anyways.

Not sure why it comes with the heater cartridge and not the thermistor but those are cheap and plentiful too. As with any swap, run through the tuning processes to get the best results. You will never be able to just swap a component like this and get good results without proper tuning.

title: Has become my go to PLA
text:
It came well sealed on a cardboard roll and it is wound really nicely. It also seemed to succeed in a couple temp towers at differing speeds but at a wide range of temps, my towers go from 190 to 230 and aside from some extra stringing at higher temps and poor layer adhesion at the lowest temp, it held up. No failed prints in the subsequent prints made.

The color is a nice green, and they are starting to offer a wider selection of colors

Good printing PLA and would recommend.

title: Its CA glue
text:
This is glue. It sticks 2 things together that were not previously stuck together. If you spray the glue with the activator it sticks things together faster than if you had not sprayed it.

Joking aside this stuff works pretty well. A good size bottle compared to other brands of comparable price point. It doesn't say it in the description but I would consider this close to the medium starbond, maybe a tad in between medium and thin.

So far it hasn't let me down, thumbs up

title: Better than manual pump
text:
So far the bags seem to hold the vacuum after a couple of weeks so that's a big plus. Cannot say that for all vacuum bags I have gotten before. The battery pump is much better than having to manually pump the bags but that's me being spoiled.

Overall works well and am happy to have gotten this kit. Will be buying more bags when I get my next batch of filament.

title: Absolute garbage glass build plate
text:
I have been printing for a few years and have 6 other printers of different makes and styles. Most being FDM bed slingers. My favorite part of this hobby is tinkering with the machine and getting the best results the hardware can provide.

To start with this one, easy to assemble and comes with a good amount of preloaded files to get you started checking your assembly. I used to print only on glass build plates and would always give them the nod over flexible build plates just because of the adhesion. But I could not get anything to stick to this glass build plate not matter how I tweaked my z-offset and how much squish I gave it. Even to the point I was almost clogging the extruder I was so close to the glass. It would lay out a decent skirt but the second it made its next trip around and touched the previous line it picked it up and dragged it around. This is using the preloaded files so not my own poorly sliced files. I ended up having to use glue stick to get the first print. I am not a fan of that because of the residue and eventual buildup you have to clean up. I got a flex plate and chucked the glass plate and have not had a single failed print since. Far better successful print percentage than any of my other printers. It is also my quietest and fastest stock printer, by a large margin there.

One of the only things I am not a huge fan of is the touch screen. I like that you can pick it up and use it like a tablet but you have to press too hard for it to be very useable when its sat in its tray. That's pretty minor though.

So this is my first dual extruder machine and I thought I wouldn't like the dual extruder into a single hotend but I was wrong, this has become my favorite printer to try and print dual colors and get it tuned to really not bleed colors together. That's down to slicer settings but I am really enjoying learning that bit.

The laser has been hard to get to work right. I can get decent results out of the preloaded files but when trying to make my own laser files, I haven't succeeded yet. But again I am enjoying the troubleshooting and trying part of this machine.

Overall I am not sure I would consider this a beginner printer. It is easy to put together and get started but even as a semi experienced 3d printer, I struggled to get anything useable at first. There is a good group of folks online to reach out for help but seems everyone has had a few issues to start out. If you are getting this to use the laser primarily then don't waste your time. For the price of the machine you can do much better there. But as a dual extruder machine, I thoroughly love this one and am impressed.

title: You need to get vacuum pump oil
text:
Aside from this coming out of the box having leaked the little oil it had all over the unit and box, this thing is perfect for my needs. I got this to degas resins after mixing before pouring and intend to try things like stabilizing wood and even rapid pickling.

It doesn't come with the oil you need to run the pump so be prepared to order that before you can get started but this goes together easily, is quiet and efficient.

title: Not fully functional without the turntable
text:
Got this to supplement my 3d printing addiction. I wanted to be able to scan little crafts and items my kids like and recreate them with my printers. The software works simply enough but the turn table will not connect up. Says it needs a firmware update but when you click the update it says I am not connected to the internet. Tried over and over and even the support email contact was not able to help. They in fact acted like I did not understand how to use a computer and connect to the internet. I get they need to be precise and speak simple (even with a language barrier) to help those that may need those steps, but they didn't listen to my troubleshooting steps that I repeated to them multiple times. They certainly don't need to be condescending.

In the end I made my own turn table so I could at least get to testing the scanner. The small bust they send to test with came out wonderful and I started to get excited. Tried to scan a few other things using the exact same settings and method and cannot get a useable file. Tried different color objects (white works best) along with tweaking one setting at a time and still have not had any success. I will keep trying when time permits but for the price of this thing, I would expect a much better set up and usability. Had I not received this for free to review, I would be returning it for a refund.

I will certainly come back and update this review if I am able to get the turntable working or find the cause of frustration to be my own fault and not the scanners complexity.

title: Great way to keep your hands clean
text: These gloves are perfect when you’re working with resin. It’s the great way to keep your hands clean because resin can be extremely messy.

title: Very good resin
text: I like this resin, it comes out crystal clear and doesn’t have a lot of bubbles.

title: Cool gradient color change but little if any "glow"
text:
If you are after a glow in the dark then pass this by. It barely glows if I shine my UV light on it and not at all if it sits in my normal house lights.

The gradient color change is pretty good though and unique in the colors but is that worth the price asked? I don't think so. I wouldn't pay more than normal PLA prices for this honestly.

title: Prints well and good skin tone colored filament, assuming you want us white folk skin tone.
text:
This prints pretty easily, haven't had any issues printing at normal settings for PLA+ (215 and 60) which is my go to filament of different brands. A little on the shiny side for my liking but serves its purpose for making some knick knacks my daughter wants for her dolls.

Not many colors like this in other brands that I have found so if you are in the market for skin tone this is a good one.

title: Not really 2mm ID
text:
Measured with calipers, I get 2.12 mm ID. not end of the world and it will work but it will add slop in the retractions. It also doesn't feel as slick as normal PTFE tubing. Usually I have to use a small piece of sand paper to grip tubing when inserting into the fittings at the extruder or hot end but this stuff I don't, makes me wonder if it is legitimately PTFE. It is also much more see through than other PTFE which I sort of like but the rest of the negatives make me worry about a clog because it has more friction and more room to move before retractions and extractions do their job.

The cutter is useful though.

title: This one surprised me!
text:
I have been printing for a few years and have 7 printers as of this review, all of the DIY sub $1000 style that are in abundance on Amazon. They all required a bit of trouble shooting or tweaking to get going properly, but this one needed nothing but hooking up power and the bowden tube. Good clear instructions to get it going, and quite a few sample files to print right away.

Pros
1. Ready to print 5 minutes out of the box
2. Compact. This thing takes up little room on my desk and even less on my shelves of printers. Haven't measured but its only a bout a cubic foot in space including a small roll of filament on the side.
3. Auto bed leveling. I am amazed that there are still printers that come without this, but the fact that a small desktop printer on a smaller build plate size is a nice surprise
4. Fast. I am not sure what the speeds are that the sample files were sliced at but that little print head was whipping around fast than my larger tuned printers and laying down some plastic cleanly
5. Flexible build plate. granted it is just a thin magnet sheet with masking tape for adhesion but it does work well
6. Slicer. They provide a dedicated slicer program so you don't have to attempt to make a cura profile for this. I may do so just so I don't have to use multiple slicers, but the already set up one for the Tina 2 is nice to have. It is simple and pretty intuitive but I have only sliced a few things so far.

Cons
1. Small build plate. 100x120x100 is tiny. They aren't hiding this so it's not a surprise but you don't have much room. There aren't many things I usually print that would fit on this.
2. Loud. It doesn't have silent stepper drivers so this thing has got the classic robot noises when its going
3. No parts cooling. Build size means you will likely have some pretty quick layer times, and without part cooling you are going to get curling and bad looking overhangs. This is evident even in the sample files to print which are usually tuned to perfection from the manufacturer.
4. Hard to access components. This may not be an issue but because I am used to the type of printer that you need to change parts or remove a hot end for cleaning a clog or something, then having access is needed. Because of the semi-enclosed build of this printer, I looks like doing that may be pretty difficult. But then again maybe this printer wont need the tweaking as often.

Over all I think this is a fun and very easy printer to get going with. I think I will give it to my son to play with and see if he gets interested in printing as I have. The fact it doesn't need much to get going may help someone new get into the hobby with less headache.

title: Pretty and Unique colors
text:
These are like many silk filaments, finicky and need to be dialed in just right to get quality prints. But once you do then you have some pretty cool unique colors to play with. I recently got a small desktop 3d printer that cannot support a full 1kg roll of filament but these 250g rolls fit like it was made for it.

Came well packaged and vacuum sealed as you would expect. Rolls are wound cleanly so it looks like I shouldn't have any issues with winding or feeding problems. Good adhesion and strength seems a bit stronger than most silks I have used. Still would not use for structural prints but to each their own.

Overall a cool set of silks for a good price.

title: Really fun filament
text:
I really enjoy these new tri-color filaments. As with any silk filament, you really have to dial in the temp and retraction or it will look horrible, because issues are extra obvious with silk filament. Same goes with layer adhesion and silk filaments, not as strong as even regular PLA.

Vases are my favorite things to print with these because they are decorative, would not use this for anything that needs strength.

title: Cool color effects and fun to find files worth printing in this
text:
Hard to dial in temp and retraction to avoid stringy or blobs. Ran a few temp towers and retraction tests based off my usual PLA settings and they were a bit finicky. Roll came well sealed and vacuumed but still required to run from a dryer to all but get rid of the strings and blobs. Also layer adhesion is not great. It is basically similar to other silks in this manner.

I prefer the tri color to the dual color as it seems to keep the color consistency much better. The dual colors you get the shift if you cant keep the filament lined up just right going into the hotend but the tri color seems to not have that issue.

title: Hand saver for sure
text:
I just recently got into painting my 3d prints and part of that is having to shake up tiny bottles of airbrush paint. This saves a good bit of time having to shake and shake and shake some more. It is quicker but maybe not a ton, it is more for saving the arm and hand cramps you get from it. I like that its a simple press down to shake and release to stop.

It came with a bag of mixing balls to put in the paint but I have not used them yet as I want to test them to make sure they wont leach anything into the paint first. Not like I am a professional and would know the difference yet but call it peace of mind.

title: Not sure this is PLA+
text:
Had my first (printing for about 3 years) major clog that what at first I thought was the fault of this filament. Huge glob of filament completely encasing my head block. Was able to salvage the hotend and only lost the silicone sock and fan shroud. After rebuilding and ensuring all was tight as it should be, did a few tests and it printed as expected. perhaps not quite as good build plate adhesion as the same filament in a different color but still useable. Why i think it may just be PLA is that it prints at PLA temps vs another roll of this same stuff in another color which prints at my usual 215 for PLA+. This roll of purple prints at 200 happily.

The color isn't as brilliant as I would think from the pictures. It's just a run of the mill purple with a very slight translucence you can only see with 2 walls or less.

title: Really good color
text:
Was in need of a decent gold that wasn't "silk" and stumbled on this. Hadn't heard of the brand before but figured I would give them a shot. Did not disappoint at all. Couple quick calibration prints to tune the temp (215 and 60, 60mm/s) and I was off. This actually had little difference between 200 and 230 in my setup but just barely noticeable improvement at the 215 for me.

Came vacuum sealed and hasn't shown any evidence of moisture or stringing. Will likely give them a shot with other colors in their list.

title: Suitable replacement
text: This works as intended and fits the sprite extruder. Simple swap out part but use thermal paste and follow usual methods of heating hotend components before tightening everything down and you should be good to go.

title: Decent with some part swapping
text:
The one I received was in fact "all metal" but I think I would consider it more of a hybrid. It does require PTFE tubing but the tubing stops in the heat break and is separated from the backside of the nozzle by about 13mm. This is not direct drive but suitable for the hotend mounted extruders that do the same as the micro Swiss or Ender DD mods.

The heater block itself allows for different types of thermistors but if you aren't using a cartridge type then you leave that space open which may effect the heaters efficiency. I haven't tested that so I cannot say for sure, just a hunch.

Overall this is a suitable V6 clone if you get some decent cooling to keep heat creep at bay.

title: Why do they put the hole for the filament in the middle?
text:
It does what it is supposed to do. It doesn't display the humidity or temperature which is obnoxious but it dry's out my PC and TPU just fine. My roll of PC has sat out for a couple of months in my home in Florida (humid) and when I started a 24 hour print, you could see the stringing and globs but as the print went along and the dryer was working, you could see the print improve at about the 3 hour mark and the remainder was just about perfect.

I will end up drilling a hole a couple of inches higher than it is. for the filament path. A full roll of filament has to make a bit of a sharp turn to make its way out of the existing hole and that causes drag and more effort for my extruder than is needed. The only time the existing hole will work without drag is when there is almost nothing left on my roll.

title: Good quality for the price
text: I am surprised to find PLA+ for less than 20 a roll. I am building a Mando armor suit for my son for Halloween and this stuff has done great so far. Prints just as easy as my go to brand that I may be giving up for the NAGA. I will test the durability though as I do enjoy my go to brand because of its toughness.

title: Door is absolute garbage
text:
As a dryer it does it's job. There is no temp indicator so you have to assume the knob is doing its job. The humidity sensor is a nice addition and I like that there are multiple locations you can run the filament out of. But that is where the good stops in my opinion.

The spool holder isn't the roller style but a center holder which is on the larger size. I have a couple of rolls that just barely fit over it with room to allow it to roll. But the absolute worst of this design is the door. It is so snug that the worthless toggle string opener thing cannot be utilized with one hand. I have to hold the thing down to the bench or pick it up to open it and it feels like it breaks every time have to do it cause it gives way all of a sudden. Why not stick with the tried and true flip open top.

title: Siraya Tech is the go to resin for quality parts.
text: I will use the cheap stuff for prototyping and mass prints but when I want the best quality and for the final parts I use Siraya Tech. But even the Form is priced very competitively and may be my go to for all printing given its ease and quality.

title: Cool carbon fiber finish on print
text:
Like any other flexible built plate out there but this one comes with the carbon fiber layer for the smooth sheet which leaves the print with a cool carbon fiber look to its underside. not quite as smooth as others so it is a little more difficult to get good adhesion without really dialing in the first layer but have not had to use any adhesive to assist yet.

Also like the silicone handle covers. though they are a bit of a pain to install straight they do help when you have the bed temp jacked up and go to quickly snatch the print off.

title: Another 'New' Creality printer that in reality is the same as previous...
text:
...just with the upgrades everyone is already doing to the ender 3 max.

This, like many of the moderately priced printers out there, you will need adjusting to get really good quality prints. This may only be considered beginner friendly if you plan to learn how to adjust the printer to improve its quality. Out of the box, the gantry isn't level to the frame by a couple of millimeters. not a show stopper but annoying. All of the concentric nuts on the wheels needed adjusting as they were either so loose the bed was wabbly or so tight you almost couldn't move it manually with the motors off. this goes for the x y and z.

Got the critical stuff out of the way but I will say a couple of things I like about the Max Neo. They put the metal extruder, which is necessary as the Creality plastic ones are crap and always break eventually. They added CR touch. Some folks like them (I personally do on my printers) but others hate them. I find them useful if you get the firmware right. Adding them after the fact is more difficult than the manufacturer doing it as you have a better chance of the firmware working correctly with it. Last upgrade is the dual z, which isn't needed but I like it. It does make it harder to get rid of z binding though.

title: what's not to love about TPU, except it is very difficult to dial in
text:
This is my first go at TPU. I have tried flexible PLA and loved that stuff so I had to give this a go. Started off with temp tower and usual calibration prints and as expected got massive amounts of stringing. I have only been able to successfully print calibration prints that do not utilize retractions as my direct drive extruder jams up on the retractions. I will keep tweaking but so far this stuff is a lot of fun. My kids are amazed that you can print "squishy stuff"

Always do a temp tower though. My printer likes this stuff at 215c which is even below the recommended temps.

title: Very specific colors and not a huge gradient between shades
text:
Based on the dozens of other multicolor filaments I expected different. Can't fault the manufacturer as I don't see claims that didn't deliver. These are just very specific color combinations that I don't see myself using and the transitions are slow enough and faint enough to not be useful for me.

That said there were no issues with the filament itself that I found. Ran the usual calibrations and found that were stringy regardless of temp so a quick dry in the dehydrator seemed to help a bit. Once that was done then it printed as expected.

title: Stiffer less flexible but more durable
text: These seem to have less flex than gloves I had been using but also seem to take less holes also. I don't typically care for black but for what I use them for it doesn't matter. Price is also slightly less than the ones I typically use so I believe I will be switching to these now.

title: Yet another Creality variant of the same basic printer.
text:
I received this for free for an honest review.

As many have said, it is just another Ender 3 with a couple of upgrades that a most users wanted to see. I am tired of Creality doing this and blowing it up as the newest and best thing.

I have a couple years experience printing and this is my 6th of this style, but I am no expert. I like to tweak and tune and upgrade, like better hotends and mainboards and firmware, so this one does a little of that already.

This, like many of the moderately priced printers out there, you will need adjusting to get really good quality prints. This may only be considered beginner friendly if you plan to learn how to adjust the printer to improve its quality. Out of the box, the gantry isn't level to the frame by a couple of millimeters. not a show stopper but annoying. All of the concentric nuts on the wheels needed adjusting as they were either so loose the bed was wabbly or so tight you almost couldn't move it manually with the motors off. this goes for the x y and z.

Got the critical stuff out of the way but I will say a couple of things I like about the Max Neo. They put the metal extruder, which is necessary as the Creality plastic ones are crap and always break eventually. They added CR touch. Some folks like them (I personally do on my printers) but others hate them. I find them useful if you get the firmware right. Adding them after the fact is more difficult than the manufacturer doing it as you have a better chance of the firmware working correctly with it. Last upgrade is the dual z, which isn't needed but I like it. It does make it harder to get rid of z binding though.

I wouldn't personally buy this at this price if I hadn't received this for free.

title: Made a massive difference
text:
I primarily print smaller items and hated having to raise the print and angle it with supports and a raft, just so I could get my part off the build plate. This is especially useful for flat items that before i would either damage the edge trying to scrape it off or have to lift and get artifacts from supports left behind and have to be sanded away (yes that can be reduced somewhat with tuning, but whos got time for that?).

I bought 2 as I wanted the second flex plate to be able to start another print while I was able to start post processing the first print. Installation was a snap and I have had no case of the magnet sheet coming away from the build plate. I did not clamp it at all, I aligned it and pressed it on and started a print. It has sat with resin on it for a week or two at a time if I don't clean it without issue and has gone through dozens of washes in an IPA bath without coming lose from build plate.

Will 100% buy more for replacement build plates or on my next resin printers.

title: Works as intended
text:
This is the printer if you intend to leave as stock (at least as of this review 7/26/21). Understandably this will change with time but there are no firmware like Jyers or Alex's as of yet, though they are working on this from what I read. Even Voxelab isn't offering firmware to accept BL Touch yet. For the price I should have bought another Ender 3 v2 (similar price during sales). That said I am on the fence if it is worth keeping or sending back. Worse case I keep it for spare parts for my Ender 3 v2 as it is a clone on the bits and pieces side of things.

Initially I got about 5 prints out of it before the knob started getting very sticky during turning and clicking would stick a bit making multiple unintended selections and locking up the printer, requiring a power cycle. An email to support, and over the weekend mind you, and within 5 hours I received a response. They asked for the usual purchase verification along with a couple of minor troubleshooting tips (basic and already tried) but quickly realized it was lost cause and sent me a new screen board. Received it within a week (impressive given it came from china) and aside from having to flash the firmware myself once it was received, I was back in business. I then spent a few days with jamming left and right and after lots of usual trouble shooting I narrowed it down to the filament. But big bonus for the support from Voxelab. I cannot compare support with Creality as I haven't had any equipment problems from them (I was getting the same jams on my Ender 3 v2 with that filament that jammed the Aquila x2).

Overall I am not upset given the price point of this printer. Worth 4 stars so far mostly for the support. Otherwise the lack of firmware upgrades or ABL support and given I immediately had to replace the screen would have gotten 3 stars at best.

If you are on the fence, grab it when it is on sale and enjoy its capability as is. It will improve with time if it picks up popularity as much as the regular Aquila has.

title: It Works
text:
The product description stated "Included libraries and example code for both SD and RTC mean you can get going quickly". There was nothing included, no instructions, website direction, etc. There is ZERO seller or manufacturer support for this product. As someone stated this is a knockoff of an obsolete Adafruit shield and Adafruit instructions and libraries worked for this shield..

The contacts are flimsy. My recommendation would be to buy a cheap $8 Uno knockoff for this. Plug it in and leave it in for a dedicated datalogger. The contacts are not intended for interface cycling.

The battery holder is less than adequate. 1220 is not a common size even in a large city such as Houston, Tx. I was unable to find a 1220 cell locally so I had to order them. Once received I discovered the cell is easily jarred loose from the socket. Mine has already popped out twice during transport. I will replace the cell holder when time allows.

With all this said I still give it four stars due to price. You get what you pay for and then some here. With the Adafruit library and instructions you can be developing in no time. You can build a versatile, multi-channel, time stamped data logger for under $20 with this shield and a cheap Uno clone. Sure, it was assembled with inexpensive components but it's available for a third of Adafruits asking price when they were available.

After using this for some time I noticed the RTC is slow. I realized it is relying on a resonator rather than a crystal. I lowered my rating to three stars.

title: Hardware good - Software bad
text:
Initial Review Feb 11, 2023

I started a long detailed review but in the end there are too many things wrong with this vacuum. The bottom line is the actual robot seems to function as designed (vacuum only - we didn't try the mop feature), but the software that guides the robot around to clean just fails in so many ways.

We have a VIOMI V3 Max Robot Vacuum that is 1/3 the price but does not have the self empty feature. The VIOMI can clean our whole area in about 45 minutes. It is smart in how it creates and follows a pattern. It performs quite well and is fascinating to watch as it cleans. Not having the self empty feature isn't a big issue because our floors and carpets are normally pretty clean. We selected this Obode to be used for the second half of our house. Rather than deal with two maps we decided to have two robots.

This Obode takes 2 1/2 hours to clean the same area because it follows such an inefficient path. It will begin cleaning a room but the pattern it follows may actually have it leave that room for another before the first is clean. Ultimately it appears to clean the whole area as requested, but the pattern is so erratic it is hard to know if it did indeed cover everything.

The Obode doesn't seem to know where its own base is while cleaning. It tries to climb over the foot of the home base when is should very well know where it is.

The Obode had trouble with throw rugs. Rather than transitioning from the hard kitchen floor to the throw rug in front of the refrigerator it caught the edge of the rug and rolled it up. It eventually got itself untangled from the throw rug but it had trouble with all 5 throw rugs (the older robot vacuum never had this behavior).

Setup was easy.

The Android app also has issues. The robot had made one large room from out kitchen through to the living room. When I used the app to try to split the large room into two smaller rooms there was no button to push to actually cause the map split to occur.

I think the Obode could be vastly improved by updating the software. I will hang onto it for a while to see if the company develops updated software.

I'm very surprised by the other positive reviews. Perhaps there is something wrong with the one I have.

I do not recommend this robot.

title: Failed attempt at making dichromatic filament
text:
Looks like this company was attempting to produce dichromatic filament - 2 colors based split down the middle the filament such that you're always printing both colors. The appears of the finished product changes color based on the angle you are viewing. It'll shift from one color to the other as you rotate the product. This filament does do that - BUT they did not keep the color sides consistent. It reverses several times on the roll.

After purchasing I received an email from the seller."...The dual color filament you bought is a new arrival product. So we need to make a survey.
We would like to know if it works fine when you print with it.
If there is any problem, please contact us directly.
We'd like to address any issues or concerns you have...."
I contacted them after printing a Voron calibration cube and told them about the color shifts. Their response was the part was "too small". In actuality, a smaller part would be less likely to experience the reversing of the colors.

My advice - spend a little more and get your dichromatic filament from a name brand supplier. I gave them a chance but won't be buying more.

title: Prints great, but had some potential contamination issues.
text:
Overall my experience has been great, but once I got about 1/3 of the way into the spool, I started experiencing some sputtering and bubbling that usually means some sort of contamination in the filament. I stopped what I was doing and ran a few pulls and passes with cleaning filament and thoroughly cleaned the whole nozzle area and path.

I reloaded and tried again, this time with a spiral print just to confirm that I wasn't dealing with a retraction or ooze issue. I got about 1m in and *sputter*, another bubble of something and a pile of crap right in the middle of the print. My printer and spool are in an enclosure, so it's not environmental. It's definitely something in or on the filament itself. I continued to print a bunch of smaller items and the issue seems to have cleared after about a dozen meters.

There's no obvious defects in the filament that I could see and it seems to have been isolated to a specific area of the spool (so far). Luckily I'm doing a lot of small prints, so it's just a minor inconvenience. I have a lot of supports as well, so some of the sputters are getting caught in non-critical places.

I don't know that I'd trust this for large prints, but the ease of printing and the color and quality of the results (overall) will keep me using it for small parts.

title: Certainly positionalbe, very very sticky.  Leaves string of adhesive when lifing item off
text:
I ordered this adhesive to use in cardmaking - to adhere layers of cardstock together. My hope was that the 'positional' element would allow me the opportunity to adjust the layers if they weren't perfectly positioned. Then use the scraper to make a permanent bond.

My experience so far is that it sort of works. First I cut a strip of the adhesive covered paper backing about .5 : wide. I placed that on the back of my A2 sized card, centered it, then pressed it down. It does make a permanent mount and I was able to adjust it slightly as long as I hadn't pressed too firmly. The problem with this technique is that the adhesive easily pulls away from the back sheet and develops sticky strings when it does so. those have to be managed somehow. It also made the scissors very sticky.

The next attempt was to unroll just a few inches of the adhesive, place it on a self-healing mat, and cut a strip with a rotary cutter. That didn't work at all, as the rotary cutter quickly got gummed up with the adhesive and the adhesive got on the self-healing mat - and it's still there. I haven't tried an adhesive remover yet, and that might take it off.

Then I tried placing the top layer of cardstock along the edge of the adhesive, trying to roughly get about .5 inch of adhesive on the edges of the back of the cardstock. Again, the strands of adhesive pull up off the backing and make a mess.

My last use was to use the adhesive as it is designed to be used - by placing the whole A2 sized pieces of cardstock on the adhesive, and use the backing sheet to adhere the whole things. Works fine, but again those strings of sticky adhesive make a mess.

After these experiments, I have to believe those who use this for mounting photos or artwork must also experience the 'sticky strings' phenomena, so I don't believe it's just my unorthodox attmpts to use it in a way not previously endorsed by 3M.

As this is a significant investment, I'm not going to discard this. I've thought about chilling it - would that tame the strings? But I don't know if refrigeration would cause other problems such as making the backing paper moist and/or affecting adhesive properties. I suppose I might cut a small piece off and try it. . .

Between discovering this item on Amazon and ordering it I pondered how to use it as it seemed like it might be a very affordable and effective answer to the cardstock layering dilemma, allowing me to adjust the position easily. I'm not giving up because if I can figure this out, I can seem so many uses for it. I'll report back with progress.

title: Not bad for the price
text:
UPDATE: This review is for the carbon fiber PETG filament. Other reviews not related to this particular filament are now appearing due to a listing change with other filament options. This confusing practice of grouping reviews of different products should be stopped.

I found this filament at a great price and Matter Hackers was out of their carbon fiber PETG so I gave this a go without the help of other reviews. I've been getting good prints out of it.

I'm using a .6mm hardened steel nozzle as they recommend.
I found that I needed to use the higher end of their temperature range to prevent clogging. 245C
I'm also using a 0.3 to 0.4 layer height to keep the viscous goo flowing.
There is some stringing but that is expected and not a big deal to clean up.
Hairspray or gluestick on your build surface at 70C sticks fine.

The parts are nice and stiff and I think the glass transition point will work for my needs. The layer adhesion is good but not great. I think lowering the part cooling fan speed might help that.

All and all, with some tuning I think it's a deal. Keep the temps high and please report back your findings. This is a new product and IEMAI checked in with me to see how it was printing. I appreciate that.

text:
[[VIDEOID:96c81342620c7ec9c97c78d6e4318ea8]] Wanted to try some of this dual color change filament that’s been the new “thing” lately, but the name brands were easily 30-40$ a kg, and seeing as I get my normal and silk PLA for 15-20$ that’s a bit much.

title: Cheap but awesome
text:
Stock ender 3 beds (flex bed) wear pretty quick with a lot of printing. While they can be cleaned and reused for a decent while, wanted something I didn’t have to worry about, and would last, but also didn’t want to spend 40$ Or more on just a bed surface.

This thing is great! For less than 20ish bucks, you can’t go wrong. I have had absolutely zero issues. The magnetic sheet is actually very strong, had a few where it would barely stay due to weak magnetism. I was so impressed I actually bought another one for my other ender to replace my glass bed. Adhesion is phenomenal with pla and petg, and when prints are finished, as the bed cools, parts literally just pop off. Don’t even need to remove the bed and flex it, just give it a minute and viola, no curling, no warping, no hassle.

Be aware tho, BOTH sides are textured. It’s not like others where one is smooth and one is rough. I’ve read a few people have scraped one side w a putty knife or something and smoothed it because they like that finish better. As I acquire more printers, My first “upgrade” will always be this bed.

Getting proper adhesion can be a huge pain and frustrating (as with any brand petg) but once I dialed in my temps (recommended 230-250/60-80, ended up at 265/75) and baby steps on the Z axis, it’s some solid filament. Finish is actually better than I expected and as far as “clear” filaments, this stuff is actually probably the cleanest I’ve used. So far, enjoying it, and depending how the rest of this roll goes, will probably order a few more! This may replace overture as my go-to petg

title: Amazing tiny tuner!  Serious players need this!
text:
This thing is amazing. Never have I been excited by a guitar tuner until now. I love it and I haven't even figured out all of the various options this thing offers.

The standard tuning mode and the polytune feature are nice, but I generally use it only on the chromatic/strobe mode. I've heard it can also tune to 432hz and do other tricks as well. I tune to either E standard or Eb standard and it works great for that. I really love the strobe mode for the accuracy. I use the "bars" in strobe mode to get it close and then can use the strobe lines to get it as close to perfect as my hardware can manage.

I also appreciate that it stays in my chosen mode when I unplug the board and go to a gig. Pressing the little button by the power input can be fiddly while on the board, but I only need to press it when I'm toying with it at home. It's always gig-ready on the last settings I used.

The foot switch is great. There is no click. It just moves up and down smoothly, and a light tap turns it on/off. Same switch as my mini Ditto looper by TC.

I use the buffer for now. I have flipped the buffer switch a few times, but can't tell much difference in the sound when the tuner is off one way or the other. Maybe it will be more apparent to me in time. I use about 30ft of cable in my rig altogether, so I like the idea of a buffer at the start of the board. I have not used the "always on" mode.

I started with a heavy, ancient tuning pedal which looked similar to a boss pedal. It was awesomely accurate, but half broken and stuck in always-on mode, so I couldn't mute my sound while tuning. I upgraded to a donner deluxe mini tuning pedal, which is a nice size, but turned out to not be very accurate at all. It would get me close enough to be able to play, but I was never totally happy with my tuning with that pedal.

So eventually, I did my research and decided this was the best option for a mini tuner with guaranteed accuracy. And I was right. This guy almost never shows a string as being properly in tune and it's very easy to jump past that marking showing you as in tune. That is great in my opinion, as it means it is accurate. And I can absolutely hear a difference. My chords sparkle again and I'm in love with the sounds I get from this rig now.

The display is also nice and bright and easy to read from a distance.

My guitarist friends freak out when I let them tune my guitar and show them all the stuff this thing can do. It really is awesome and I'm glad I made the investment.

If you are a bedroom player, it may not be worth it, but if you are recording or playing live shows often, I absolutely recommend this tuner. It is about as good as any tuner can get and also in a tiny package. These are slowly replacing the old trusty Boss tuners as the industry standard.

This tuner is the most expensive pedal on my pedalboard and I am totally okay with that. I should have bought one of these years ago.

title: OK for the money, but not great.
text:
This Behringer DD400 delay unit has a lot of great features. I particularly like the stereo outputs which allow the user to send the delayed signal to a separate amplifier for a dramatic stereo effect. The extra-long 1300 millisecond delay is great for Pink Floyd/David Gilmour style solos. The shorter delay settings allow for rockabilly slap back effects, although I hardly ever play in that style, so it doesn't matter that much to me.

Here's where it gets weird: I tested the unit using a vintage Fender tube amp for the primary signal and a Vox Valvestate amp for the delayed signal. As long as I played loudly, everything worked quite well. However, when I set the guitar down for a moment, I started hearing voices. Yes, voices! The delay unit was picking up radio frequency interference a la Jimi Hendrix at Berkeley. I have no idea HOW it was doing this, but I could clearly hear some sort of radio transmission like CB or family band radio. The interference went away after a few minutes.

As for design, I don't buy the "German innovation" advertising line from Behringer. This is obviously a cheap Chinese copy of the legendary Boss DD-7 which costs four times as much. If you want really good quality, buy the Boss unit! If you can get buy on a fairly cheap delay unit that talks to you from time to time, the Behringer is ok.

The clarinet played fine out of the box (I've played clarinet/sax/keys for decades, so I am an experienced player). So far, so good. Doesn't require more air pressure than any other clarinet, produces sounds at low registers easily. Just goes to show, sometimes quality doesn't have to cost a bundle.

I'm very pleased with this at the price, and am glad I bought it -- highly recommended for a first-time beginners' instrument, as it plays fine and is in tune (often the budget instruments are woefully out of tune; this one is reasonably in-tune, and key action and playability is fine).

UPDATE Jan 2012: I liked this clarinet so much I bought a second "backup" one; it's very, very well made and in the months since I bought it, my family likes it a lot. Just goes to show you can get a decent instrument at a great price (though that's rare, most low priced instruments aren't any good. This one is). Highly recommended clarinet, this one's a winner.

title: A nice, compact, 2+ channel battery-powered mixer with USB in/output for your audio kit!
text:
When I ordered this, it was the only small, battery-powered, self contained mixer with USB input/output that I could find under $100 (heck this one is under $50!). I expected to use it just for teleconference audio mixing until I got a fancier JK Audio RemoteMix 3. I found myself constantly using this little mixer in testing and setup of one-time demonstrations as well as using it in our Podcasting 101 workshop. If this didn't have a few quirks and had better documentation, I would give it 5 stars.

Yes, one can find a bit more durable knobs on higher priced units which drive the price way over $150, but most of these fine laptop/tablet/smartphone attachable mixer/audio interfaces do not work as standalone mixers.

Here is a summary of the usual pros and cons, starting with the pros:
+ compact and solidly built internals
+ integrated Lithium Ion battery pack
+ extremely clean audio - which isn't always true from the inexpensive mixers of this class
+ very welcome two band equalization, especially in the field when there are very noisy input channels
+ usable stereo crossover mixing control on both the main mic/line input and the secondary RCA or USB input
+ additional line in for external digital recorder (originally designed for tape! Is anyone still using a small input like this for tape!)

Cons:
- would prefer to have one more 1/4" TRS or 3.5mm TRS connector instead of RCA jack pair
- control knobs can come off, as can the RCA jack shield; both easily repairable with a drop of glue, but annoying
- Li Ion battery pack is not easily removable for swapping
- quirky controls, especially the way USB audio is input to the mixer
- documentation could be a bit better written

In summary: a great battery powered two input mixer with USB input/output interface to keep around when you need an extra 2 channels to add to your audio mix!

title: Tascam DR-60DmkII nice enhancement over DR-60D and big jump up from DR-40, BP-6AA is essential!
text:
The Tascam DR-60DmkII includes enhanced pre-amps that are good enough not to not introduce any measurable noise on battery power with a quiet room and a Pyle podium mic that requires High mic gain setting. However using a USB to 5v adapter (not the Tascam adapter) did introduce noise. For this reason, I am using a BP-6AA identical to the one used on a Tascam DR-40 recorder installed in a church recording system. Though we can run the DR-40 or this DR-60DmkII off external USB port power, noise levels are typically much lower using the BP-6AA which I'll review separately. With such a low noise recorder, and with the BP-6AA using tripod mounts to attach to the top or base of the recorder, no brainer upgrade from 2+ yr old Tascam DR-40!

Here are our usual pros and cons:

Pros:
+ lower noise, higher gain pre-amps than prior model DR-60D
+ safety track record feature is a lifesaver when initial gain settings are too high! (DR-40 has this feature, too)
+ consistent menus and operation to prior generations of Tascam DR series including when power or computer is externally attached via USB port
+ available BP-6AA external battery pack gives reasonable life for rechargeable NiMH batteries, but see below...
+ Broadcast Wave File (BWF) support - can be a lifesaver when merging audio and video from different recorders. To effectively use, you should keep the clock set correctly.

Cons:
- drains batteries rapidly compared to comparable Zoom or lower end Tascam DR series recorders
- no integral MP3 compression, implying you shouldn't use compression with such a high end recorder! I'd like to make that decision!!
- there should be a Li Ion external equivalent bolt-on like the BP-6AA instead of lower capacity and bulkier BP-6AA with NiMH batteries!
- might want to think twice about putting a relatively heavy DSLR on top of recorder as shown in photos! This puts a lot of strain on the tripod mount in the bottom of recorder; just don't do it if a BP-6AA is used!
- menus can be a bit confusing for the uninitiated and this generation manual is not as helpful as prior generations. Look for YouTube tutorials!

I was going to put a small shotgun mic on top with a 1/4" to 5/8" adapter, but realized the DR-60DmkII + BP-6AA underneath + mic on top is not very stable. Better to use either a two-in-one bar tripod adapter or multiple tripods adjacent to one another. If a BP-6AA pack is mounted on top with nothing mounted on top of BP-6AA, then BP-6AA batteries may be changed without impacting setup. The DR-60DmkII batteries are accessible, but it isn't easy to pop them in the rear while the whole setup is sitting upright.

Edited 07-31: Beware of open box items marketed as "new". I received one from a vendor sold as new that showed a bit of wear on the rear battery cover and underside. However, the style of packaging for this Tascam makes it difficult to tell whether this is a new, returned, or open box item!

I have seen some "unboxing" videos on YouTube and this is the first Tascam DR series I've purchased that doesn't come in a sealed box with a plastic protector for the display and a sealed (at least taped) poly bag holding the recorder. I have seen this style of packaging on "professional" gear before. So how are we as consumers to tell whether an item is an "open box" or return? TEAC/Tascam saved perhaps a few pennies but it would be great to go back to providing a screen protector and tape the poly bags!

+ 9V phantom power works on all podium mics tried
+ base actually works with other podium mics!
+ nice positive action on mic pre-amp button
+ good quality speech audio from pre-amp/mic combination

Cons:
- red LED just under mic tip can be a distraction in some uses
- does not accept phantom power presented to XLR connector
- because of above, must constantly check the battery
- the base failed very soon after the warranty expired. The mic does function in AT8666 type podium base which is how it is being used now!

Product changes required for broader use:
* add a way to disable or mask the red LED under the mic tip
* allow phantom power from the XLR connector to be passed through to the mic connector
* add a low battery indicator

title: Sounds great, simple, ideal for beginner -- UPDATE after >1 year of ownership
text:
Overall: In my opinion, this is the best beginner amp, offering the highest value for money. I'm sure it's great for experienced guitarists as well.
Pros: 12" speaker (great bass response), very simple to use, can layer on multiple high quality effects, can play at 0.5 watt setting (perfect for midnight practice), memory settings, USB connection. Most importantly, sounds great.
Cons: No built-in tuner as on the Yamaha practice amps.

This is an incredible amp. There's a lot of hype on YouTube with reviewers extolling the virtues of the the Katana series, and I believe it's justified. I started my electric guitar journey with a Fender Champion 20 amp, which was half the price of the Katana 50. While not complex, it was always a bit loud, cumbersome to use effects, switch amp "styles" and the overdrive sound was lacking. The Katana 50 appears to be equally complex in terms of number of dials, but it has proper EQ settings, very easy-to-choose amp "styles" (eg. clean, crunch, etc), a 12" speaker that booms with the bass and really makes the sound so much richer, as well as 3 types of effects you can layer together. Finally it has an internal memory to store your preferences as well as a USB connection for recording and firmware updates. Most importantly for me, adjusting volume to play at night is a huge plus, as the amp can go down to 0.5 W.

As a beginner this amp sounds amazing for the price and is very simple to use. Clean and crunch are fantastic, and overdrive sounds pretty good. Addings effects like delay and reverb is very easy. Overall, highly recommend.

-------

I've had this amp for over a year now, and I think I like it even more. It is truly a great amp for any level of guitarist. Also, just updated the firmware to version 3. Cleans are still great and dirty channel is awesome. There are plenty of onboard effects to play with so you don't need to mess around with pedals (eg. multiple types of reverb with 3 accessible at any time from the front buttons). The memory setting are dead easy and it has the added benefit of being customizable from the computer. If you need a single do-it-all amp, this is still the one to go for.

My wish list: I would definitely upgrade my Katana 50 for a newer version of the amp if it came with a built-in tuner and little digital display to show me which effects were currently engaged.
