title: Best wireless "gaming" mouse, but cheaply made?
text:
First off, don't spend your money for this if you're not a serious gamer. You don't need the responsiveness, without the feel of a wire. This is a very good product at the end of the day, but you should understand it comes with a few cons. Let's get into it and tell you why this 3 star product is the best "gaming" mouse on the market (right handed only review).

+ Design is simple and comfortable with your hands (layout). No awkward accidental hits die to weirdly placed buttons.
+ Looks fantastic, and the RBG plays into the fun factor.
+ Materials feel nice against your skin. Grippy, yet soft.
+ Weight is excellent. I like using the heaviest 'coin' insert.
+ Response time is as fast as the quickest wired mice. Enough said.
+ Sensor accuracy is bar none the best. I've tried it all. This doesn't skip. I can't make it skip or stutter. This is rare, as I can make anything else skip pretty easily with flick type shots or 180 spins. Final Mouse, Rival, Sensei, all lack here.. Make sure you get the PMW3366 sensor, not the older SKU.
+ Software is easy enough to use and configure to your specific wants. Full macro control.
+ No cord snag, which is very nice for fast competitive gaming, especially FPS.
+ Charge life is excellent, with or without RBG cycling.

Now I know you're confused why 3 stars after all these glowing points. Read the second negative, and it's why this product isn't a 5/5 stars. To me, it's a big flaw.
- Weighted coin insert not included in the newest sensor revision. I use mine from the old mouse, which broke. For a mouse so expensive... Really Logitech?
- Mouse wheel is atrocious. It comes a little stiff that you can press down, and it won't scroll also. But the wheel gets "broken in" very quickly and then becomes an utter mess. Depending on what you use Mouse3 for, it can really impact you negatively. I've gone through many of these mice, and they are all the same. I press Mouse3 in (middle button) and it's a damn challenge to not scroll with it to. Want to use the scroll function? Try to go 1 tick, but it goes multiple because it's so loose and flimsy. This one button is the death of me. The best mouse on the market with a disastrous flaw. This mouse wheel is one of the worst I've had ever tested, which is strange. The best mouse wheel I've tested is still the old school Logitech G400s. I guess now days they try to save costs in something they think is over looked. Sad cause the rest of the mouse seems premium.

It's still not great, but with this mouse it's so much better!

So I got this for gaming on my Xbox series S. title: Great Sequel to the South Park Video Game Franchise
text:
Following South Park The Stick of Truth‘s success, where Trey Parker and Matt Stone, creators of the show South Park, had complete creative control, the game needed a sequel. One with equal quality as in the first one, while pushing through new creativity & content. And for that they released two great games. First, South Park‘s Phone Destroyer, which I shall review eventually, then The Fractured But Whole, which covers an important current in American Cinema today.

Super Heroes movie franchises.

Movies praised for their high special effects and for connecting families multi-age audiences, but criticised for their bombastic formulas, their unsubtle/moralising/preachy SJW messages, and commercialistic opportunism. Which has been denounced in certain Marvel Comics films like Captain Marvel. Although this criticism has been mostly absent from the DC franchise as movies like Wonder Woman have tried to focus on their stories and not on a political agenda. Although if one criticism still remains strong, it is the commercial business behind these super hero films.

Which is what the storyline in Fractured But Whole tries to satirise. In a game where the New Kid, after his adventures in Stick Of Truth and Phone Destroyers, participates in the Super Hero adventures within the South Park Community. Developping an identity as The Farting Vigilante. Discovering the rival camps between the “Coon and Friends” and “Freddom Pals” teams as they attempt to launch their specific movie franchises. And fighting crime around South Park as many South Park cats have disappeared. And behind this drama hides an evil antagonist who exploits others as puppets; in his games of money and power.

So through this game, Trey Parker and Matt Stone entertain us with a hilarious story that further explores South Park’s mentality and satirises Super Hero culture. Always subtly, never trying to overpreach a message. While introducing new characters from the latest seasons. Such as PC Principal and his SJW tactics that players can use to defend themselves during fights. Like they can also summon special individuals who can attack enemies; though they do not completely vanquish them like in Stick of Truth, nor are they usable only once per day. Instead, they can be summoned at a specific number of times during the entire game, or if certain items are crafted.

Indeed, another function offered in Fractured But Whole is “Crafting”. Where you conceive items strengthening your powers, defend you in fights, heal you, or even design costumes for your Super Hero Identity. Ability which grows the more you craft items and collect junk during fights, and while you walk around levels or purchase items in stores.

In sum, a creative customisation that integrates itself into the story. And it is nice how the game’s cinematics retranspose on your character your costume design. As it makes the game more personalised, following your creative and design interests.

For the gameplay, players still move around a South Park environment that corresponds to the one on TV, as if we were interacting in an actual episode of the show. Though for the fights, the game levels are different. Not using a RPG turn based attacks mode, but a board game platform like in Super Robot Taisen and Fire Emblem, with players moving and attacking like Chess figures. So every move can either help you or hamper your battle. Furthermore, your attacks may be infinite and not rely on Power Points, but the way you interact in the fight can have an impact on your victory or defeat.

So in its game content, South Park Fractured But Whole offers a new interaction mode with the characters and their environments. While presenting an interesting storyline that details more about the New Kid and his family, whose turmoils reach a critical tension as both parents argue constantly regarding their son and his Super abilities; while refusing any dialogue with him about their past. Which makes me wonder what does the father do for a living? Let’s hope another South Park game answers that question one day. Just like they introduce further DLC contents as interesting as the ones we have. Indeed, the game presents as first DLC level a Vampire story set in the actual Casa Bonita restaurant, popular in Denver and worldwide thanks to South Park who did an episode about it. Through this level, an adorable way to discover the culture of this restaurant whose attractions look fascinating and worthy to visit one day. A level that also offers an awesome tribute to a legendary pop culture figure, which delighted that artist’s fans a lot.

Then, as second DLC Level, a Friday the 13 like tribute on the horror movie genre, set at Lake Tardicaca and featuring Mint Berry Crunch, a super hero whom I wish could have had a presence as well in the game’s Cthulhian side-story as Mint Berry Crunch first appeared in a South Park episode satirising HP Lovecraft’s classics.

Still, the completion of these DLC levels allow you to add Mint Berry Crunch into your super hero team for your main storyline, alongside another character I will not name, but whom fans like a lot as she becomes playable during the Casa Bonita adventure and into your main story.

Finally, there is the customizable Virtual Reality fights of Professor Timothy, allowing you to revisit past antagonists or new ones in particular battle situations, Obtaining bonuses and certain items as victory results.

For the soundtrack of Fractured But Whole, Jamie Dunlap and Scott Nickoley did fantastic compositions. Melodies and tunes that follow the musicography of the South Park show. Employing original tunes from the show, but also new tracks. Grandiose melodies that show how the artists behind South Park have always been attentive to their projects’ music. Which makes sense as they were behind the successful Book of Mormon musical.

For the voice actors, the same original cast records voices. And if you enjoy the show in different languages, you can also obtain a French and Spanish dub. Though regarding the French voice work, I wish it had the original French dubbers like Christophe Lemoine as Cartman for their performances were unique, to a point some francophone fans preferred listening to the show in French rather than English. Whereas for this game, the voices we have here are unmemorable.

Nevertheless, South Park Fractured But Whole is a must if you are a fan of the show, but also enjoy playing unconventional video games that make you question your surroundings, while never trying to preach an unsubtle message. Which too many USA entertainment films/shows attempt today, but do so quite badly and people don’t embark into their agenda.

title: "They can't see me. Good. Let's keep it that way." - Batman
text:
In 2011, the second chapter of the Batman Arkham Series, Arkham City, appeared in stores. To great success as the public enjoyed it, alongside its upgraded version released for the XBox One and Playstation 4. With enhanced graphics that made the game more beautiful, and Arkham more decadent. Showcasing further how corrupt Gotham City is. Which this game further presents as it follows what happened in Arkham Asylum.

Indeed, after the explosive attempt of the Joker to hijack Arkham Asylum, its director, Quincy Sharp, has decided to launch his Arkham City Project which Batman uncovered during the first game. An attempt to convert a portion of Gotham City into a Gettho like prison that would jail all the criminals of Gotham City. Infringing those prisoners’ human rights and all those who denounce and condemn Quincy Sharp, now Mayor. Which is what happens to Bruce Wayne as Arkham’s soldiers ruin his election campaign and jail him inside Arkham City. A location which Professor Hugo Strange governs. Where he reveals to Bruce that he knows he is Batman. So during this night, the Dark Knight will fight his way through this Maximum Security neighbourhood, survive its criminals, and try to stop Hugo Strange and his Protocol 10. Project that would endanger the lives of many prisoners. Whether they are guilty or innocent.

So it is during this night that Batman experiences those events. Encounters reuniting him with figures from the first game like Victor Zsaz, Poison Ivy, Killer Croc, the Joker, and Harley Quinn, but also other antagonists we know in the comics, but never confronted in the first game. Calendar Man, Two-Face, The Penguin, Mister Freeze, the Mad Hatter, Deadshot, and Rhas al Ghul among them. But the one I enjoyed the most was Hugo Strange. Indeed, before the Joker ever appeared in the 1940s, Strange was the first major villain Batman had to deal with in the Comics. In storylines involving monstrous creatures and gritty situations. So it was nice to see in this game a past figure that represented much of that age’s uncensored culture. Alongside an attempt to show the series’s villains as psychotic goons. Who kill their obstacles and and employ controversial tactics for their agenda. In evil ways that display the rottenness of Gotham’s community.

Indeed, during this game, we explore various urban locations whose architecture presents the evil, corrupt, and despotic climate of Gotham City. Whose massive buildings structures reference architecture and statues linked to the Nazi aesthetic culture of Albert Speer and Arno Breker. Which Tim Burton referenced also many times within his Batman movies through his vision of Gotham City. Furthermore, the decaying streets and ruins of Arkham City show Gotham as a living organism that has fallen into disarray. With churches and factories turned into refugees for doctors and security guards. And famous locations like the Iceberg Lounge or the Amusement Park now headquarters for the Joker and the Penguin.

So the artists show to us a Gotham City that is as much a character as the people that inhabit it. A micro-organism that lives according to the actions of its citizens; but still exists thanks to figures like Batman. Though we always feel this will not last. That whatever good the Dark Knight and Robin do, Gotham’s evil is immortal.

And speaking of Robin, how great we get to see him interact with the Batman in this game. As a secondary non-playable figure in the main story, but playable in the DLC content. In special missions he did with the Batman after the main story, and also before those events. Same thing for Catwoman and Nightwing; though for Dick Grayson, he is only available in DLC special levels. A bit sad as he is a valuable character, the first Robin figure and first partner of Batman. Then again, as he works in Bludhaven city now, this absence is understandable.

On another note, it is wonderful how the DLC content offer us Brawl and Stealth missions set within the Wayne Manor. It allows us to discover the property of Bruce Wayne; Its various corners and rooms. Though I’d wish we could have a virtual exploration of those rooms; outside of a Stealth setting, which does not allow us to explore further that residence.

Indeed, Arkham City‘s artists have taken their time modelling and designing Gotham, its buildings, and accessories. Employing delicate lighting to create specific mood in certain locations. To better present the antagonists’ disturbing personalities, and the creepy history behind Gotham. As a place of secrets whose evil exists for centuries; tainting its community’s heart. And that the upgraded versions of this game have enhanced the textures and designs means we can better appreciate the artistic quality of Batman Arkham City.

In its Gameplay, the game is an adventurous open-city universe where players have to fight brawls with numerous criminals, travel over many buildings, and accomplish puzzles offering them trophies and clues as to where to locate the Arkham employees the Riddler kidnaps. A sub-quest that takes much time and patience, but is rewarding for its participants. For it not only involves Catwoman also, but it presents new facts about the history of Gotham’s criminals. How they evolved, how they became bandits, and how they reacted to certain incidents in the Arkham series. Before Arkham City’s storyline began.

For the voice actors, the cast is excellent. As always, Kevin Conroy (Batman) and Mark Hammill (Joker) have a superb chemistry to their roles and their performances are always a delight to listen to. Even more wonderful is how the actors performed their scenes together. Which is great as it allows the work to be reactive to each other’s talent rather than an individual record of voices which some productions do, making more difficult the connections between everybody’s words; necessitating further re-recordings.

As for the soundtrack, Nick Arundel and Ron Fish returned for the adventure. Doing beautiful tracks like its Main Theme, but also This Court Is Now In Session. My favourite music composition of them all. Displaying the grandiose nature of a brawl where the forces of good and evil would collide. And in this entire soundtrack, a portrayal of Gotham’s nightmare. A town always at the border of falling into an abyss.

In sum, this game, alongside the entire Arkham Series, enriches further the folklore of Batman’s mythology, but also of Gotham City which now becomes an incredible character. With a History that no other games ever presented before.

A must to play in every gamer’s household, but also for any Batman fan.

title: Only dreams are the wings of the heart that  no one can steal - MAKE UP (Pegasus Fantasy song)
text:
Among Shonen Jump‘ mangas, Saint Seiya has had quite an international success. Especially in France where it was broadcasted as Les Chevaliers du Zodiaque on Club Dorothée, TF1’s main children/teen broadcast programs of cartoons and anime. And thanks to that success, various tie-in products appeared. Figurines, Lego toys, Music CDs, and video games. Such as Saint Seiya Soldiers’ Soul.

Offered for Playstation 3, Playstation 4, and PC, this game is a Fighting Adventure product that allows its players to relive the arcs of Masami Kurumada’s classic. From the Sanctuary Saga to Asgard’s Apocalypse, then the Poseidon Polemic, and finally Hades’s Homecoming. Many adventures for the Goddess Athena’s Bronze knights; ready to defend her and save the world. Against other deities linked to the Greek and Nordic Mythologies. Which makes Saint Seiya a neat introduction to Europe’s folklore. To reincarnations of deities and mythological figures like Orpheus, Minos, Poseidon, Odin, Hades, and other omnipotent legends.

In its story mode, players can revisit all the encounters Seiya and his comrades experience during their adventures. Including key moments from the original manga. Allowing non-fans to learn more about the storylines set within these arcs. Discover the strengths and flaws of Masami Kurumada’s storytelling. Which are similar also in the manga and 1980s anime release.

Indeed, the series Saint Seiya presents a great universe where mythological figures still exist within our reality and continue to help our world in times of paranormal crisis. Where other mythological figures (Hades, Odin, Poseidon, etc.) and their soldiers try to assault Athena and her knights who fight back; or try to endanger our planet for selfish reasons. Of the chivalrous who come to the rescue, they wear gorgeous armours ranked according to their chivalry class (Bronze for the weakest, Silver for the sturdiest, and Gold for the legendarily). Each knight representing a constellation in the sky and using their Cosmos to gather energy to accomplish powerful attacks. And among the most popular ones are Seiya (who represents Pegasus), Shun (who represents Andromeda), Ikki (who represents the Phoenix), Hyoga (who represents the Swan), and Shiryu (who represents the Dragon). Each having specific personalities and interaction dynamics with one another. Giving off nice moments to all who discover their stories.

But in its flaws, the series reproduces repetitive story structures. For each arc, the same situation. Which is the Goddess Athena getting cursed or jailed under a curse or using her power under a time constraint which a powerful nemesis has put her into. While Seiya and his friends must rescue her quickly before she passes away or the world is cursed. And in its fights, the series repeats a lot its story; where the Bronze knights encounter an enemy whom they first fight with their attacks, but are quickly punched back by the adversary in a critical situation. Until the knights, in dire distress, summon their inner strength and expand it at a level that allows them to vanquish their opponent. And some knights like Shiryu tend to repeat the same patterns, either by removing their armour to fight more boldly, getting blind or non-blind when a deus ex machina cures him. In Shun’s case, his refusal to fight forces his brother Ikki to rescue him many times. And this kind of narrative actions happens several times for many battles. Which makes you astonished at how a series like Saint Seiya, for its grand settings and characters, presents such redundancy. Especially as the knights’ armours weaken fast and are replaced by superior versions that are still crushed down into pieces and replaced by stronger ones.

So it can be a bit disappointing to see the same story narratives displayed four times into different settings. And I think this repetition is part of the reason why the original Saint Seiya manga was cancelled after the Hades arc. Because the series did not escape its creative bubble and did not push itself forward with its narration. Had it done so, then it would have gotten the conclusion it eventually got several years later. As such, I wish that Masami Kurumada had worked alongside another co-writer as well, helping him find more diverse situations and resolutions than the ones he presented. That would have given to the story the cosmic truth it never got to present entirely. With situations that could have involved either the human world, or a unity between mythological figures and cruel human beings.

Nevertheless, for all its repetitive flaws, Saint Seiya‘s storyline remains quite a great adventure for its actions, emotional story, cultural settings, and incredible artwork Masami Kurumada presented. Though for those who might not have read the manga, they might be confused by certain plotholes in the game’s adaptation as at one moment Shiryu propulses himself and a Golden Knight into the Cosmos and we don’t learn how Shiryu escaped that lethal setting to participate in the Asgard chapter. Nor do we learn, in the Hades`s Arc how he recuperated his sight after losing it too many times before. So to those who might not have read the manga series or seen the anime, take this game as an introduction to the lore and story world of Saint Seiya. As an appetiser of something richer than what is shown here.

Regarding its gameplay, the fighting dynamics occur on a 360 degrees 3D stage. Either a temple linked to a specific knight, an Asgard landscape, an undersea palace with rooms and corridors, or, for the Hades level, an underground castle that leads to the Inferno and other dimensions. All of them beautiful stages superbly modelled and rendered with great textures.

For each fight, the characters can kick, punch, and perform combos set to their favourite moves. Including throw attacks linked to the knights’ super powers. For its energy bars, you have an endurance bar and a Seventh level one that can make your knight obtain a superior level of Cosmic energy. Allowing you to crush massive blows and attacks on your enemies. Giving forth incredible animation sequences where the characters pull their attacks. All of them well animated and impressive. Though I did notice how, for these moments, the brightness of the images is dimmed down severely, hurting the impact of those animation scenes. Was that decision due to concerns of epileptic seizures caused every since the Pokemon controversy; with its Porygon episode that gave massive epileptic attacks to its viewers? Who knows. Either way, this decision does affect the impact of those animations and does not give them the full quality they deserve.

In its animation and character designs, the work is excellent. The models are detailed, their armours impressive, and their animation poses very well worked. Although for several characters, I did notice their mouth animations being at times not animated properly and several times some characters’ hair tips shaking a little bit for no reason at all. Probable because those parts were not perfectly rigged by the artists. Nothing alarming, but you do notice this during certain scenes if you play the game on a big screen.

As for the music, the composer did for the game a great job. Using electronic music that fits perfectly with the great moments of the story. And it is wonderful that within the game you can obtain the tunes of the music so you can listen to them again and again. Either while studying or while reading the original manga itself. As for the voice actors, their performances were excellent; perfectly fit for each character in the game.

Regarding its other features, you can obtain various armours for your characters, but also other Bronze knights that were absent in the story mode, such as Jabu, knight of the Unicorn. Bronze knights that you can play as or against not in the story mode, or during the Fighting Match section of the game. Furthermore, there is even a mode where you can fight online with upgraded characters set according to key phrases you obtain during the game, strengthening them for your online matches with other players.

In conclusion, Saint Seiya Soldiers’ Soul game remains a pretty good game experience for fans of the Shonen Jump magazine and of Masami Kurumada’s classic.

Worth playing for its fighting matches and concepts and for reliving crucial moments of the manga series.

title: "Take a look inside your banana cave. You're in for a big surprise!" - Cranky Kong
text:
With the early 1990s Nintendo brand, people knew of the Super Mario Bros, Kirby, and The Legend of Zelda figures. But in 1994, a new protagonist entered that gallery. Or should I say a descendant of a Nintendo Legend.

Donkey Kong, grandson of Cranky Kong; latter who was the Kong in the Donkey Kong arcade game where Mario was trying to rescue Pauline from Cranky who had kidnapped her.

Though in this game, Mario does not appear at all. Instead, the whole story happens on the Kong Island. Set miles and miles away from human civilisation. A haven where they do have to deal with unpleasant individuals like King K Rool. Ruler of a crocodile tribe who decided to steal Donkey Kong’s Banana Hoard one night. While Donkey was asleep and his best friend Diddy Kong was guarding his fruit cave.

So for this game, first part of a trilogy called Donkey Kong Country, it is up to Donkey and Diddy to find where those fruits are. Indeed the thieves, while carrying their robbery, left a trail of bananas that goes through Donkey Kong’s Island. An island that is itself a character in the game.

An island which, while we explore, conceals secrets and history linked to the protagonists and antagonists. Temples with various crocodile statues, a factory whose pollution contaminates the jungle and ecosystem. Tribes of beavers living inside huts. Enough locations that make you realise how there is a history and a culture inside that game. How the War between the two tribes has been going on for a long time and that the crocodile clan has been trying to re-appropriate a location they seem to have abandoned for centuries and which the Kongs had appropriated years before King K Rool reappeared. And of that king, he stands among a massive figure for characters to remember of this adventure.

Alongside other companions such as Funky Kong, whose travel agency can help Donkey and Diddy travel through the island in his planes. Or Candy Kong; Donkey’s girlfriend whose barrels can help you save your games. Even Cranky Kong gets to be part of the adventure. Giving you advice and ideas how to uncover the secrets of Donkey’s levels. Locations that are another argument to continue playing Donkey Kong Country again and again as their uncovery increases a percentage in your game slot’s exploration. A replay factor that would be employed again in the next two chapters. Though in a different form of discovery for them.

As for the gameplay of Donkey Kong Country, people can change between Donkey Kong and Diddy Kong; depending on whether or not you find the DK barrels that contain those two. And for each character, you only get a chance to play with them. If you get hit by an enemy, you lose a companion and you have to rely on your second protagonist (if he is with you to continue your game. If you lose them both, you lose a life. So this absence of energy bar enriches this Rare Production quite an exigent difficulty, like in Commander Keen. Like the bosses who can be tough figures to fight. Some of them Godzillaesque entities.

About the graphic design, Rare did a stellar job. For each map, a clear trail that displays portions of the Kong Island. And in each level, a landscape that oozes a personality and energy. More flagrant through the soundtracks of Robin Beanland, Eveline Fischer, and David Wise. Three figures whose musics are perfect. Each track respecting and honouring the mysteriousness of that universe and its characters. A mix of Jazz, hip hop, electronic music, and rock that still amazes me. For its freshness in encouraging players to play the game and discover the people of that classical series. Which new generations have rediscovered on the Wii and Nintendo 3DS stores.

A game that deserves all its success to its talented team, which contains names like Chris Sutherland who voiced the characters, Tim Stamper who directed the game and is known for his work on the difficult Battletoads franchise, and Gregg Mayles, who worked on the game design and story with Dan Owsen and Tim Stamper. All of them part of the reason why Donkey Kong is a popular figure in the video game and pop cultures.

title: My favourite Super Nes video game
text:
In 1994 and 1995, Nintendo released a video game called Earthbound. Sequel to Mother — the first chapter in Shigesato Itoi’s Mother trilogy — that Super Nintendo adventure follows the trials of four children against a diabolical Alien named Giygas. An entity from the first game that has returned from his planet, more powerful and diabolical than before, and who will conquer Earth in the Future. Though a prophecy predicts how a kid called Ness — alongside his friends the medium Paula, the intelligent inventor Jeff, and Poo the Prince of Dalaam — would vanquish Giygas thanks to their psychic powers and their courage. From this revelation, Ness enters an epic journey that catapults him from his hometown Onett to worldwide locations. Hoping to find the weapons, teammates, and powers necessary to vanquish Giygas.

Of the game, the creator of the Mother series — Shigesato Itoi — wrote and directed it. And through a clever and structured narrative, he presents a world where paranormal phenomenons are part of the Earth’s folklore as it is brainwashed by Alien PSI entities. Turning animals, people, machine, and objects into vicious enemies. Some of them spies for Giygas, such as a certain character close to Ness, though I won’t reveal who it is. Is it a family member, a friend, or a neighbour? That is for you to find out during your playing of this excellent game that offers some pretty philosophical dialogues and situations for Ness and his friends.

For more than a fight against the Earth, it makes each teammate grow up into incredible persons normal circumstances would not have allowed them to experience. And at the end of Earthbound, their melancholy and sadness affect players as well as they have grown alongside those four comrades; through this game that touches so many issues and realities about our lives.

In its game design, Earthbound‘s visuals made me think of a Playmobil universe. With its characters as figurines you would find in a toy shop. Which reinforces further the childhood aspect of this series. A world and its people/architecture/settings seen through the eyes of children. Which made this Role-Playing Game a more accessible entry for kids who discovered the game in 1995; like me when I played Earthbound in 1996 at 11 years old. A world much closer in its visuals to what you would find in the Pokemon games, which makes sense since some artists involved on the Mother series would work on the first Pokemon release. As for its fighting platform, the concepts of seeing the antagonist through the eyes of the main characters and of interpreting the attacks through psychedelic flashes reinforces the experimental nature of Earthbound and how the world we see is influenced by the characters’ perspective. Even cooler are references to Twin Peaks with the music group The Runaway Five and the Twoson bar’s colour design they perform which is reminiscent of the Black Lodge in that show.

As for its gameplay, we have a RPG that allows us to fight against enemies not with swords or lances, but with baseball bats, frying pans, ray guns, and martial art techniques; alongside psychic powers some characters can display. For the character of Ness, this PSI knowledge — alongside his appearance similar to Ninten, the character of the first Mother video game — makes you wonder if Ness is the son of that character. Especially as his mother is a bit similar to the female protagonist of the First Earthbound game.

As for the music Hirokazu Tanaka composed, this soundtrack is another crucial pillar behind the success of Earthbound. For each city and location, a soundtrack set to the personality of the region. At some instances, nods to tunes from the first game. Like for instance the Pollyanna song in Ness’s house. A track that Catherine Wardwick even sang a song for the CD release of Earthbound‘s soundtrack that fans adore.

As for its original compositions, tunes like the towns of Onett, Twoson, Threed, and Summers each present the region’s personality. For instance Summers, a superficial and materialistic Beach Resort. Very relaxing, though you can identify airs of phoney appearances in the area. Similar to what you’d see in superficial cities like Cannes or Nice. As for Threed, we have music a haunted town with airs close to George Romero’s Night of the Living Dead who, when liberated thanks to Ness and his friends, expresses a freedom and relief that forewarns of beautiful reconstruction for that cursed community. Though the most beautiful music moments are portions of a crucial Melody that will help you vanquish Giygas and which are located at specific landmark locations; alongside touching moments for the characters. Whether it is in the Magicant or when Buzz Buzz Fly speaks about the Prophecy to Ness, or even the final showdown with Giygas himself.

As for the symbolical interpretations behind the antagonist and the state we find him in Earthbound, so different from how he was in Mother, I think it is due to the incredible powers his people gave him during the events of Mother. Indeed, I think that because of the psychological attacks he endured from Ninten and his friends, his spirit has derailed and when he returned to his planet, he slaughtered his entire population and, through gaining their abilities, knowledge, and wisdom, he became what we see of him in the final fight. A form I will not describe, but stunned everyone who played the game.

Finally, to conclude the review of this great game I encourage you all to play and which is available to purchase on the Nintendo Online Store for the 3DS console, I think it is deplorable that the series’ release has been so neglected in Europe and North America. If for sure we have had the release of the first game on Wii U, which I hope shall occur for the Switch, the third and final chapter of the series Mother 3, has never been released outside of Japan. And the numerous letters/petitions from fans were such that it became a joke among the video game community, got quoted in the Robot Chicken series, became an irritant for people at Nintendo of America, and a frequent frustration for gamers as characters of Mother 3 are mentioned in the Super Smash Bros series. Which is hypocritical as Nintendo of America is not afraid of releasing a Brawl game that features characters of that final chapter, but refuses to release Mother 3 for unspecified reasons. Some of which could be explainable in these videos down below. All of them shameful censorship.

But more than that, I think that had it not been for the mediocre commercials Nintendo did for the Earthbound games back in 1995, I am sure the game would have had better sales figures for the series which would have encouraged the American and European releases to present the third and final chapter.

Again, I hope and pray that people of Nintendo will eventually release Mother 3 in worldwide markets. For if they did, then it would show them as a company connected to its audiences’ concerns and needs. As people who care about their games, in the same way, we wish older releases like Illusion of Gaia or Secret of Evermore would be available to play again either on Nintendo 3DS or on the Switch.

title: A rainbow of Characters and Spirits that just shower you with Multiple adventures!
text:
Since the Nintendo 64‘s release, the video game company Nintendo has released a Fighting Game Series called Super Smash Bros. Games where Nintendo characters such as Mario, Luigi, Samus Aran, Ness, Link, Zelda, Pikachu, and many others would enjoy brawl matches between themselves. And since the amazing Super Smash Bros Brawl game on the Wii, more characters from other consoles and Nintendo games have joined the fighters ranks. Solid Snake, Pokemon Trainer, Lucario, Greninja; though among my two favourites are Shulk of Xenoblade Chronicles and Bayonetta from the series Bayonetta.

In this game made for the Nintendo Switch, Super Smash bros Ultimate offer many game content for fans and newcomers. Online brawls, Smash matches with eight players, Mob Smash, Tourneys, Special Smash with twisted obstacles, online matches with worldwide participants, challenges, and story modes. And for that latter aspect, players get a great jackpot. A storyline called World of Light, with all heroes fighting off two armies of darkness and light led by formidable opponents. A game where we explore two worlds. One of Light, another of Darkness. Where we reassemble characters together and advance through fights that allow us to collect spirits linked to popular Nintendo series, but also obscure/neglected ones like Eternal Darkness and Hotel Dusk. Two universes I love, alongside those of Mother whose first and third games really deserve a proper release on Nintendo 3DS or on the Switch. Just like these other classics that need more attention from the public.

So for this World of Light storyline, we get a wide exploration and battle on major platforms linked to many games universes we love. But on the downside, I wish that the game director and producers could have offered us cinematics between the characters. Sequences that would happen either before/after the fights, or in between spirits and the playable characters they are friends with. That would have brought us back to the beauty of Super Smash Bros Brawl‘s story mode on Wii. As we saw in that Wii game emotional connections between the characters that were absent in the Switch. Connections revealing the complicity and rivalry amongst the crew. So if there ever were a new game in the Smash Bros series, I hope we will get cinematic moments between characters in the game story mode. More than funny or epic photos we can obtain if we accomplish certain achievements.

As for the Classic Mode, an individual storyline for each character; fights set according to certain persons related to his/her life. Either another playable character, or a Major Spirit Opponent (ex: Dracula if we fight as Simon or Richter Belmont). A storyline that concludes with a nice hunt for points through the end credits. Culminating with a funny picture. Though again, I’d wish interactive cinematics would have been offered for these adventures.

Apart from these narrative gameplays, fans of game designs will enjoy creating their own stages in the Stage Builder and sharing them online, just like they will love training their own Amiibo figures they have purchased in stores. Another great initiative for fans of Mii players are their chance to design their Mii’s suit. Wearing costumes from all series (Super Mario, Fire Emblem, Legend of Zelda, etc.)

Now for the gameplay of Super Smash Bros, the camera angles are the same as in all Smash games. Wide angles that cover the entire stage, which may be cumbersome or confusing for certain gamers. So those who’d prefer their brawl matches with much closer angles may find it cumbersome to play a Smash bros game series and might want to pass.

As for the music, Masahiro Sakurai, Yoshino Aoki and Hideki Sakamoto composed a nice range of melodies for the game. Making it grandious, epic. And the addition of tunes from the games mentionned in that console are another great chance for fans to discover of relisten to their tracks.

In sum, Super Smash Bros Ultimate is a wonderful chapter in that Nintendo game series and a must if you own a Nintendo Switch.

And with the upcoming new characters like Banjo Kazooie and those from Dragon Quest, fans of those two series will be sure to enjoy this fighting-brawl game.

title: A placid island hiding secrets not meant for the faint-hearted
text:
Many might have heard the name H P Lovecraft, but ignore his stories such as Call of Cthulhu. For those who might not know, he is a crucial novelist whose novellas, novels, and poetries gained success after he passed away; revolutionised the Horror genre by diving into the psychological fears of humanity. For instance, the demons that haunt the heart and also the monsters that create such nightmares.

And in the novella The Call of Cthulhu, an intellectual discovers that cults all over the World are attempting to summon back into this world the Demon Cthulhu. A tall 100 Metres High Demon who shall wreak havoc all over the World if he is summoned. As such, a legendary story that influenced many stories presented to the public. Movies, novels, board games, RPGs, and video games. Some of them inspired by the H P Lovecraft lore such as Eternal Darkness, and others more faithful to the writer’s literature.

Such as this game.

Call of Cthulhu. Directed by Jeremie Monedero and Justin Villiers. Written by Mark Morrisson, Maximillien Lutz, Fabrice Collin, and Pla-Victoria Jaqmart.

Where Edward Pierce, a Private Investigator struggling with his World War One traumas and alcohol issues, receives a new client. A businessman called Mr. Hawkins who wants him to find the whereabouts of his daughter Sarah Hawkins, a talented painter who supposedly died in a fire down DarkWater Island, where she used to live with her husband and son, but whom he believes that she is still alive. So following this strange request, and a sinister nightmare involving a strange cult he received before this client appearance, the Detective heads to this Island and discovers in it an sea of corruption. On its surface through a shady businesswoman crook called Cat and her team of thief, and underneath its houses as a strange Cult hides behind closed doors and secret passageways. Harbouring monsters, demons, and a diabolical project that could endanger the World.

During your investigation, all done through a First Person Point-Of-View, you can explore locations around Darkwater Island and discover their secrets. Some of them answering the truth about Sarah Hawkins, but also the region’s dangers. Including horrors that can damage your sanity. Indeed, according to what you uncover, your psychological health may take a toll and it will affect your gameplay and the story’s resolution. For four different endings can happen. Some of them obtained only if you do certain actions. All of that through a horror game that fuses both detective work and stealth that can make you gain points which will allow you to uncover more secrets.

Now starting with Call of Cthulhu‘s good points, the story is well written, the dialogues are excellent, the plot is wonderful, and the characters well developed. Latter which reveal what we need as much through their talk than in their mysteries. Some of which you can uncover fully if you obtain the proper perks to unlock their truth. Regarding the main character Edward Pierce, I adored him and found his personal fight and quest of truth very convincing, especially as the barriers of reality are shattering through the secrets he uncovers. I also liked how the game can make you collaborate with teammates. Faithful new friends who can follow you when you play Edward Pierce, but also play through their skins, such as Dr Mary Colden, who makes you realize another reality of the DarkWater folklore. In this case, the island’s hospital. And through the levels you meet, each object uncover can help you elucidate the folklore of the island, but also educate you the history/culture of the time period.

For instance, in the Hawkins Manor, you can find various cultural treasures through music on the radio at the start of the game, but also books such as Moby Dick, Frankenstein, 20 000 Leagues Under The Sea, Rip Van Winkle, and The Wizard Of Oz. Making a subtle but wonderful publicity for these classics that gamers can read after/while playing the game. Which makes me wish that the game had offered either ebook versions of those classics, or physical copies with covers made specifically for that Call of Cthulhu game occasion.

As for the music from Markus Schmidt, an excellent soundtrack that I wish we could listen either on Itunes or Spotify. Even excerpts of the mysterious ambience in Call of Cthulhu would be enjoyable as the soundwork is an influential power in the game’s horror nature. Sound effects that can pressure the players in their gameplay, either distort them or terrify them so much they just want to lower the volume. Latter detail a crucial evidence that the horror in this story works.

And let’s speak of all the voice actors who worked on the Game. People who through the Side UK voice acting studio. From Anthony Howell as the tormented, but charming/attractive Edward Pierce, Emerald O’Hanrahan as the wise and thoughtful Dr. Marie Colden, Antony Byrn as the faithful and friendly Officer Bradley, Gerald Kyd as the shattered Art Collector Francis Sanders whose life met the path of Sarah Hawkins, whom Christina Cole plays admirably, everyone did a superb job with their voice work. Kudos to the Side Uk Studio for assembling and producing in their offices such a great team of artists.

In its visuals, the work is wonderful. The character designs are convincing, their animations and facial features are powerful and convincing. As for the lighting around Darkwater and its green/blue monochromatic palette in some locations, I adored it as it brought me back to Batman Arkham Asylum whose atmosphere was influenced by HP Lovecraft. Back to the character designs and animations, I have noticed in some cinematics that some characters are more detailed visually than in the gameplay. Which might annoy some players who’d expect a constant visual nature. About the cinematography, both the First Player view and the third person point of view in the main cutscenes offer a good camera; As for the editing, everything is well filmed and well edited and the suspense of scenes is quite satisfying for fans who wonder what will happen next to Edward Pierce. If he will resist or fall to the darkness.

Now as for the game’s weak points, I do think that the stealth nature is still awkward as it happens in the First Point of View, and the few ways you can move around really does not make it a very ergonomic aspect of it. indeed, those levels, especially in the Asylum, got on my nerve as they were not as pleasant to go through and enjoy as it is difficult to see either where to go or how to check out if those security guards/monsters are moving and will catch you. And as for the one level where you have to physically fight off some monsters, the gun visor is still sketchy as sometimes it doesn’t shoot the target properly. So those two details are elements that may hamper the pleasure of some gamers.

Nevertheless, whatever flaws the game has, I encourage players to discover Call of Cthulhu for it honours important American Literature folklore, but also presents a great horror video game. One that deals on a psychological nature on its players. That reminds us that the most frightening horrors aren’t really the monsters, but the fears in our minds.

title: An Official Storyline Worthy Of Jojo's Bizarre Adventure. And My Favourite Playstation 4 Video Game.
text:
Since 1986, Jojo’s Bizarre Adventure has presented its saga in the Shonen Jump Magazine, then in the Ultra Jump edition since 2003 with the Steel Ball Run Saga. And since the anime releases broadcasted from 2012, the series has gained a worldwide popularity and reception. Both with the public and critics.

Indeed, that series displays an emotional and powerful adventure about the JoeStar Dynasty and the conflicts they have with a crook named Dio. A Heathcliff-like psychopath whose crave for power makes him evolve into a powerful vampire who dreams to eradicate humanity. With his new Undead powers, then his Stand abilities, which his descendants/rivals inherit/obtain as well, Dio and the Joestars enter a war that travels many historical periods/countries/generations. In appearance, an adventure of magic, hidden powers, and heroes trying to save the world. But in reality, an ode to humanity and its ability to survive through willpower and human strength. Whatever tragedies and fallen allies/friends occur on the road of life.

And in this game, that family lives through another storyline. An official one presented by Hirohiko Araki himself, which is wonderful as this makes it a certifiable narrative of the Joestar family. A story where the various eras of the series unite together due to an army of former enemies/brainwashed allies who are trying to unite a Holy Corpse whose powers could destroy many universes.

Of the story, which happens over many days, we witness the Joestars’ trials in uniting the corpse, but also reuniting with friends who had passed away. And for fans of the games, this is a moving moment as it allows those people and their friends to speak together and trying to make amends over the flaws that they had in the past. Through subtle dialogues, but also various side-missions certain individuals can perform. And all of that through many funny and sharp dialogues the characters have between themselves. A mix of comedy and action that respects the manga/anime series narrative. All thanks to Hirohiko Araki’s presence. Indeed, the dialogues/scenes/emotions are always precise and faithful to each individual and the banters certain pairings add much to the chemistry/rivalry between them. Due to that, we get beautiful moments between Joseph Joestar and his son Josuke Higashitaka, Iggy and Polnareff, Lisa Lisa and Jonathan Joestar, and Jolyne with her father Jotaro Kujo. On another note, it is interesting how we get to encounter the alternate reality of the Joestar family; through the Steel Ball Run and the Jojolion runs. Especially as the Jojolion sagaa is incomplete. Which makes me wonder how things would have been different had that branch already been completed in the magazine Ultra Jump. Would we have had more individuals joining the fight? more narrative opportunities? Who knows. Either way, the storytelling in this game is satisfactory, which is refreshing considering that several tie-in games have disappointing plots. Therefore, just for the story, this game is a worthy purchase for the PS4.

In its game designs, Eyes of Heaven happens on stages set within each parts of the series. Using the original stage designs of the Brawl game All Star Battle alongside those conceived for Eyes of Heaven. Though it makes me sad that we don’t get to explore and fight inside all of those All Star Battle levels. Indeed, several of them would have fit perfectly with the narrative of the story, like Dio’s Mansions, Rome Streets, and the house of Yoshikage Kira’s father. And although some of them appear in crucial cinematic, their lack of exploration is a small criticism that l had to say. Of my wish to rediscover again those levels through Eyes of Heaven‘s gameplay. Especially when some of them had superb Finishing moments in All Star Battle. Moments that reminisced iconic scenes of the manga series. And through the few Finishing ones that appeared in the game (three I think) were great, I wish there could have been more. One for each stage offered.

About the gameplay, Eyes of Heaven is both Battle-oriented and Adventure like. Travelling through stages set in different eras where the characters, in battle moments, fight in an exploration-way around the levels. So different from the Brawling nature of All Star Battle; which didn’t allow players to dive deeper into the mood of this surreal manga series, especially for locations like Morioh town, the Naples Train Station, the Rocky Mountain Village, and Air Supplena Island. And in terms of visuals, what an amazing level of work the artists pulled out. For the Morioh town levels, the artists used Fauvists colours for the sky; warm palettes which go well with the art references in Hirohiko Araki’s Art who was influenced a lot by Gauguin, Matisse, and De Staël.

Of the characters, the range of playable people consist of either three or two persons for the first, seventh and eight arcs, while for the second/third/fourth/fifth arcs, more than five characters appear in the adventure. And for each, the character designers reused the models used in All Star Battle, but also honed them according to the Anime series; giving them colours more accurate to them, and even added in new costume designs as well. In sum, gorgeous 3D models accompanied by the voice actors of the original anime series. For instance the late Unshou Ishizuka, whom the anime community misses dearly.

And speaking of the voice acting community, what an incredible team of actors were involved in the game. Each of them gave excellent performances that follow the storyline and the people`s emotions. As such, this game is a great masterclass for fans of anime and voice actors as to how to perform emotional stories through the voice. Which I insist seriously as some actors have tried that kind of performance in animation or video games, and their work was disappointing.

As for the music, what an amazing soundtrack from Chikayo Okuda. Involved in other project like the Hack Series, but also the excellent Asura’s Wrath, this musician gave in Eyes of Heaven a music that respects the surreal/action atmosphere of the story, but also the various musical references in the series; such as 1970s UK Rock, Heavy Metal, Rock musicians like Prince, Pop Music, and punk. And what a great idea from the game’s makers to present that soundtrack in a gallery section. Of my favourite tunes, I loved the Morioh Theme, the Mountain Village One, the Alternate Higashitaka house, and various battle themes available in the game. Another favourite tune was an oppressive and apocalyptic theme that used cellos and which was absent from the gallery mode. Which is sad because it recaptures the dramatic tension of the series. A tune that I wish and hope people behind the video game series will get to include into Eyes of heaven's Gallery in a game update.

Speaking of the PS4share option, it is awesome how people can share excerpts of the game on Twitter, Facebook, and YouTube. Through that Playstation 4 functionality, players can present online portions of Eyes of Heaven that give the game a great publicity for the game, but also allows fans to connect together and display their favourite moments. Though I have to warn everyone that at the second third of the game’s story mode, all PS4share options are blocked; to make sure that no spoilers come out of the story. A strategy attempt that I quite agree with, though anybody going on YouTube can see that some players who did playthroughs of Eyes of Heaven have managed to show those non-shareable moments as well through their video recording softwares. Either way, my PS4 warning is a fact that I wanted to speak of to anybody who wanted to purchase the game.

Alongside that story mode exists also battle modes players can do between each other. Either online or at home, as they can play against each other, or let the CPU play with himself against two teams and perform for fans a match of which they have no control for. Of the online matches, it is sad how there aren’t that many players anymore. Indeed, it’s as if after a couple of years, people have dropped that game aspect and have either left Eyes of Heaven for another game to play, or prefer to participate only into the story mode. Therefore, to any fan of the game who is reading this review, I encourage them to play online as well. For the more players are present online, the more chance people will get to enjoy these online matches occasions.

As for the availability of the game, people can purchase it both ways. Either as a physical copy, if you live in Europe Japan or other regions. But if you live in North America, the best way is through the digital editions available on the PS4 store as you can obtain there extra side missions and special playable characters like Saga 4’s Jotaro Kujo.

In sum, Jojo’s Bizarre Adventure; Eyes of Heaven is not only my favourite video game release of a popular anime/manga series, it is also my favourite Playstation 4 game as well. A great addition to anyone’s video game library.

title: With powers beyond human and elf understanding...With more popularity appeal than John Lennon himself...behold...Sir Douchebag!
text:
Released after years of developments and rewrites, a suspended release, Activision's legal issues, Ubisoft's release, and a Black Friday trilogy promoting the human-elf war in an awesome three-parter, here is the video game South Park fans have been waiting.

South Park The Stick of Truth. Entirely developed, conceived, written, and performed by the show's creators, Trey Parker and Matt Stone, their show's production team, and Obsidian Entertainment.

Set over a course of three days, you play a new kid who has moved into South Park under strange circumstances his parents wanted to escape and preserve their son from. Powers that end up in the hands of the South Park fourth graders who are busy playing their Elf and Wizard game, started after the Black Friday debacle and its heretic resolution.
At the game's beginning, four classes are offered to you: Warrior, Mage, Rogue, and Jew. Each presenting specific abilities and attributes one can obtain through experience or by making friends with the South Park community, either through sub-quests, discussions, or main quests you complete for them, situations as crazy as the town itself; but also clever social commentary on the video game medium (ex:Bioshock audiophones, DLC, reused ideas, etc.) and on our world's injustices (ex: germanophobia, phony media statements even in the face of truth, cultural barriers within Canada, etc).
Of the gameplay, everything occurs in a two-dimensional environment similar to the TV show, which mixes both cut scenes the South Park studio animated, and a game environment where the character fights against his enemies in a traditional RPG battleground. While loading screens serve as transitions from certain environments (houses, sewers, country, etc.) and also to pass from the free-walking environment to the battleground you and your guest character get to play against enemies. Though the walking environment can offer you props that allow you to bypass enemy fights in clever ways and gain experience points. An awesome idea from the show's creators as it makes the game more alive and real.
Through the entire game, Parker and Stone succeeded in recreating the town's major buildings and made multiple references and jokes to popular characters in the show; Past show elements like the Chinpokomons, Crab People, Lemmiwinks, Mr. Hankey and his dysfunctional family, Critter Christmas, and Jesus. Some you get to summon as Espers, and others you meet only once like the Aliens, but whose interaction with brings forth a serious impact to the storyline. Storyline in which the creators will not release any DLC extra levels, though they have offered in the game enough achievements to encourage players to replay twice or thrice or anytime you'd want to for the game really offers much to play and laugh with.

As for the Grand Wizard set, the game comes with a hand drawn map of South Park by Cartman, a large plastic figurine of him, and DLC costumes for your character. Indeed, Ubisoft has developed a nice collection set for any video game and/or South Park fan, though I'd wish they could have offered more choices of large figurines. Either Butters or Princess Kenny, whose popularity grew enormously due to the Black Friday Trilogy.

In conclusion, although this game's loading screens can sometimes load more longer than necessary, this game is the first South Park video game I have adored in its entirety and I encourage anyone to buy it. Not only that it is also an awesome love letter and tribute to the Earthbound video game, which Trey Parker and Matt Stone have admitted being enormous fans of, especially of its surreal and unique gameplay with children that fight against something adults have no control on.

title: "Safe and sound in its shell, the precious pearl is the slave of the currents." - Important quote employed in this video game
text:
Released in 2003 as the Irak War and its propaganda intoxicated worldwide medias, especially in America where government leaders encouraged soldiers and Americans to be patriotic and defend their country; or else society would label them as anti-Americans, "Beyond Good and Evil" came out during this troubling war frenzy and terrorist witch-hunt.

Although the game had started its production years before that political turmoil, its storyline took a stronger and more serious actuality as events in our reality unfolded.
A story involving Jade, a freelance photographer-reporter who takes care of orphan children whose parents were victims of the Domz. Aliens that have declared War through the galaxy and started to attack Hyllis, Jade's planet. Soon after the game starts, Jade receives a new reporting contract that develops into something more political. A deal that asks her to go through borders beyond what the press is propagandizing to the Hyllians; into the Alpha Sections quarters, a military division that is supposed to defend them. Uncovering a truth that hurts and which she must expose to the population, along with who are the real heroes and allies in the Domz War. Ending with a twist that reveals another secret.

Although the game is in English, it can be played in many languages. In particular French, which I decided to use as the game was done in France and because it also offered an excellent voice casting of people I recognized in French cartoons and Anime adaptations (ex: Cybersix, Macross Plus). In her work, Emma de Caunes, who plays Jade, is perfect as her voice offers the maturity and emotion the character deserves.

Done by the creator of Rayman, this video game offers mature and very moving storytelling where players feel like watching a clever tv series/movie that is not gratuitous. A story that asks questions about the War, but also tackles and condemns medias like CNN, Fox, BFMTV, LCN, CTV, CBS, ABC, Fox, and others who propagate rubbish during troubling time periods. Making money out of our fears and collaborating with those whom they shouldn't be doing business with. As such, this game is a smart product that makes gamers think and question. Which is nice as most video games unfortunately don't offer that opportunity and are mostly offered as punching bags to decompress on.

In its visuals, the characters' design is like a cartoon and wonderful to look at, especially in its mechanical designs as some wonderful machines are used by the main characters. As for the monsters, their frightening aspect is quite convincing for players who start the first time and want to replay it again. In its gameplay, the game is adventure-action-stealth, which means that some situations require stealth moving through guarded locations. Puzzle environments that one must use clever strategies to pass through enemies and security devices. Beyond Good and Evil also offers mini-games where players can photograph different species around Hyllis, collecting specific key items I will not name, items that can, and must, be collected in other non-linear stealth levels around the capital. Ones that if played accordingly go along with the plot's development.

As for Christophe Heral's soundtrack, I found it quite memorable in its mix of genres (orchestral, hip-hop, oriental,etc) and I wish they could have released it as an album.

In conclusion, this underperformed, but critically lauded, game is now reoffered to us in a Download opportunity (PC, XBOX, and Playstation) as its original release gave less sales than expected. Maybe because of its political content in a very tense time period, or because Beyond Good and Evil was released during the 2003 Christmas holidays, time period where players preferred to buy the latest franchise games, like a certain Prince of Persia: the Sands of Time that Ubisoft had released simultaneously with Beyond Good and Evil, overshadowing Jade's story and becoming the game of the year.
But stealing from Beyond Good and Evil part of the success this game deserved and still deserves. For instance, its sequel that is still in production, according to what I've heard and read.

title: "A hundred years from now, someone like me will love someone like you,and there will be no Templars to tear them apart."-Anders
text:
Years ago, I played the first Dragon Age, but never finished it. For many reasons. One, because the game engine seemed too much outdated for what the game could and should have offered; for I thought it would play out something much closer to the technological quality Mass Effect 2 offered.
Two, because the main character was still an unvoiced one and the dialogue choices were again too similar to what Jade Empire had offered; short summaries lacking the emotional and rich phrases Mass Effect's actors and writers had pulled. Not to say that a non-voiced hero is necessarily bad. Think of what "South Park: the Stick of Truth" pulled with Sir Douchebag. But after Mass Effect's full voiced hero opportunities, I felt Dragon Age should have offered a voice to its hero.
And three, I stopped playing Dragon Age Origins because I felt the game repeated the usual "Chosen-hero-trying-to-save-his-world-from-a-Lord-of-The-Rings-like-enemy-or-army-and-bla-bla-bla". A concept that stories like these tend to repeat all the time, trying to be the next Tolkien and it tired me too much. So I pulled the first game away and focused on others.

Of course, I heard they had released a second Dragon Age due to the first game's success, but I didn't play with it for years. Until I accidentally saw video walkthroughs on YouTube of the game. And what I saw convinced me to give this series a try. Not through the first game, but Dragon Age 2. Which is not a sequel but an "inquel" that starts in the first game to evolve into a side story; where a Fereldan named Garrett Hawke, his dog, his mother, and his sister Bethany/brother Carver took refuge into the city-state of Kirkwall, where they would evolve from living in the city's slum to reclaim their family's name. Meanwhile, allies join them and Hawke gets involved into incidents that will have a major impact years later, for the game lasts over seven years. A story retold through the Jacques-the-Fatalist-like narrations of Varric, a dwarf who was in Hawke's team of friends. And who witnessed how Hawke evolved into Kirkwall's Champion and involved himself into Kirkwall's politics.

So this concept interested me more as we would see a character's evolutions through seven years of his life, divided into three acts. His dilemmas, his friendships, and his family's secrets (through DLC contents). But also love; including, and that makes me so happy, homosexual relationships.
Which too many video games or media content tend to not present for various fears. Or if some medias and video games do, it's to present sexual minorities under such homophobic presentations that it can offend and hurt the LGBT community, even discourage people who are "still in-the-closet" to come out to their relatives and society.
But in Dragon Age, Bioware's writers, like in Mass Effect, have set an example for sexual minorities' representation. Indeed, apart from one secondary character with nasty prejudices, nobody in Thedas freaks out because someone comes out of the closet and admits that he, or she, has a crush on someone of the same sex and wants to date that person. And nobody, nobody gives an ovation to someone if he/she proclaims himself/herself to be heterosexual when asked about his/her sexual orientation. It is a world where sexual minorities aren't labelled as sexual perverts and freaks, but as people with real feelings of love.
In conclusion, I find that game's presentation of sexual minorities much better and a million times more dignifying than what some TV channels (Gay-aimed or not), gay associations, and some media people in the gay community promote (ex: Queer as Folk, scandal talk shows like Jenny Jones and Maury Povich and Jerry Springer, Queer Eye for the Straight Guy, certain gay porn movies, etc.). Programs that, unlike Bioware's games, are promoting dangerous homophobic prejudices about the LGBT community.

Regarding the gameplay, the game is an action-RPG, meaning that the RPG is done in an action style environment. Which I found quite appropriate for the game as it changes from the classical Final Fantasy gameplay SquareSoft pulled for years. And which personally, I wish they could have done the Harry Potter games as Action-RPG like Dragon Age.
As for the game's visual designs, they are excellent. Indeed, the city-metropolis of Kirkwall offers a very gothic architecture, quite like what you see in Fritz Lang's Metropolis, which foreshadows the game will present injustices in Kirkwall's classes, populations, and societies. As for the characters designs, they are not as customizable as the other Bioware games, but they can be enhanced inside a certain location. But personally, I preferred keeping my characters like how they first came to me. Especially Hawke, as I found him quite cool and gorgeous.

If there are some flaws to the game, it would be that some environment designs tend to repeat themselves (caves, underground cities, mansions, and temples) and I wish they could have put more variations. Two, that although the game is and remains playable as how Bioware wished it to be, some bugs might still occur in the game. Now, many of them were corrected through updates, but still, those who'd like to be aware of them can look at the Dragon Age 2 Wiki. Where, for each quests and levels, they describe a nice list of what bugs may occur.

As a whole, I encourage anyone who loves RPG or well-written stories to purchase this wonderful game that I feel one should play as one read a novel, through various dive-ins to let the story and its characters penetrate you. A game that has motivated me to take a look back at the first part.

title: Red Dead Redemption's father
text:
Before I begin this review, I would like to warn players that this game only works on the Original XBox console released in 2001. If you try it on the Xbox 360, it will only work for a third of the game where suddenly, everything freezes. I just wish that Rockstar could rerelease this game as a game on demand like they did for Red Dead Redemption, its sequel happening in the 20th century.

Now for Read Dead Revolver, released in 2004, this third-person shooter is an awesome hommage to the elements and figures of this legendary movie genre. It is the tale of a bounty hunter called Red Harlow who, after the murder of his parents when he was in his teens, goes on the search of his parents' murderers. During this adventure, he will have to fight ordinary outlaws, bounties, and psychotic criminals while uncovering a big conspiracy surrounding his parents' death. At the same time, it is a game where the player gets to use not only Red Harlow, but other characters such as Annie Stoakes, Jack Swift, Shadow Wolf, and other fascinating characters. Each of those charecters are used in distinct levels which are all introduced with a stylish animation featuring each character doing moves in front of a silhouetted background, a visual treat that I found excellent. As much as the slow-motion shooting feature that was first used in Max Payne and that other western games like Gun, Call of Juarez, and Red Dead Redemption have also used.

Of the story, I found it as explosive and entertaining to watch that I just wanted to keep playing this game over and over again, even when the game was finished. Why, I loved so much the characters that I wish that they could have introduced Red Harlow in its sequel's storyline.

Visually, the game's models might seem dated and simple compared to other games released at the time like Halo, however that aspect didn't matter to me since the models looked pretty much like those in Gun Theft Auto and Bully, and also because I felt the game's real concern was to make the most memorable spaghetti western tribute in a video game. First in Red Harlow's Clint Eastwood designs, then to the movies' grainy image quality, in its villains and the towns that they fight which look exactly like the movie sets in those movies, and in the soundtrack which used important music from Spaghetti Western composers such as Ennio Morricone (A Sky full of Stars for a Roof, Stark System), Piero Piccioni (Minnesota Clay), Francesco de Masi (Seven Dollars on the Red, Ranch of the Ruthless,etc.), Bruno Nicola (Django Shoots First, Dead Men Ride,etc.) and other composers that each have contributed to the Spaghetti Western movie genre. Personnally, I was disappointed that they didn't release a special feature in the game, or a CD soundtrack, with all the tracks used in the game and that we could be listening again and again. It would have been a treat to the game players, but also to the fans of those movies.

As such, Red Dead Revolver is a game that should have had the same recognition that Red Dead Redemption got in 2010-2011.

title: "And at the end of Fear...Oblivion!!!" - Jonathan Crane (alias Scarecrow) in Batman Arkham City
text:
Although I do not read the recent Batman Comic books for they keep juggling around the continuity of their storyline so much that it becomes confusing, I have however nothing but respect for Paul Dini's interpretation of the Batman myth. Indeed, with the excellent scripts he did with his "Batman the Animated Series", "Gotham Girls", "Justice League", "Superman", and "Batman Beyond", Paul Dini has revealed, like Tim Burton did with his excellent movies, the troubled personality of Batman, his contradictions, and the darkness that surrounds Gotham, its citizens and its criminals. And once again, Paul Dini offers another excellent work with his "Arkham" Series, in which we are once again reunited with Kevin Conroy as Batman, Mark Hamill as the Joker, and Arleen Sorkin as Harley Quinn. In this first game, which entirely happens in the Arkham Asylum grounds, Batman tries to stop a riot that the Joker initiates after the Dark Knight brings him back to the Asylum for his murder attempt on the Mayor. Not only that, Batman has to fight off the Riddler's enigmas, along with Poison Ivy, Zsaz, Bane, Killer Croc, and Scarecrow, my personal favourite, along with a new enemy whose presence will be dramatic in the sequel Arkham City.

After playing Arkham Asylum, I have only praise for this excellent video game. First of all, the voice acting of all the actors is perfect, not only in the game but also in the audio interviews that players can uncover. It was a clever idea to use those interviews since it allows us to learn other details about the characters. Indeed, the writing in those scenes is so good that I felt the Batman villains were like real people and their psychology is very powerful as we see some of them reveal how twisted they were. For instance, I loved Zsaz's interactions with Doctor Cassidy and I too wondered what happened to her, until I got to play the game further and read afterwards a special prelude Arkham Asylum comic book. Apart from the storyline, the game offers the possibility to play Challenge Levels, which include Fighting and Infiltration maps that can offer Ranked results when playing online. It is not necessary to play those sections to complete the story, but they are a great addition that will add further replay value to the game. For the gameplay, I loved how they used the Unreal game engine, which was the same one that the Bioshock game used, since the textures and model designs gave me the same amazement that I felt when I played Bioshock. For the gadgets, I adore the grappling hook, the Bat glide, but also the various batarangs such as the sonic Batarang which allows you to attract enemies and knock them out with a shockwave. Not only that, I love how you can use those gadgets in the exploration levels and in the fights. On a last note, I really love the tension of some of the levels, most of all the fight with Bane, but also the ones with the Scarecrow, which mix both surrealism and realism gameplay and I hope we will get to see him again in any sequels that Paul Dini and Rockstar would want to do.

To conclude, this game is an excellent example that you can make an excellent super hero video game with both a great script and awesome level designs; a story that offers something more to the fans who think that they've seen it all with the Dark Knight.

title: "That's why this game got an M rating" - Terror Mask
text:
In this 21st century remake of the Splatterhouse series, this video game combines various story elements from the three original 1980s video games and presents a storyline occurring in the year 2010. For this story, Rick and Jennifer - instead of entering by accident the West Manor like in the first game - are instead invited to the manor as Doctor West, an eminent teacher at the Arkham University, invites Jennifer to do an interview with him for the school paper. As Rick follows her, both for a following date and as a bodyguard, we see their date turn from a simple academic business to a diabolical nightmare composed of twelve levels, whose designs were haunting and corresponded to the tension I found in the original games.

Of the storyline, I liked how the game's makers interspersed several flashbacks in the storyline. To me, this strategy allows us to dive straight into the characters' nightmare, and forces us to venture through the game if we want to understand how Rick got to wear the Terror Mask. Not only that, finding the complete photos of Jennifer in the game, along with doing the levels on various difficulty levels, allows us to find out how the Manor was built, but also how Rick and Jennifer's relationship went over the years.

Of the voice actors, I loved Josh Keaton, Richard Doyle, and Shanelle Gray's excellent performances. But I loved and adored the twisted interactions between the Mask and Rick. And for that I am glad that the game makers cast Jim Cummings (DarkWing Duck) as the Mask. Good work from the writer Gordon Rennie, and to Howard Drossin, whose soundtrack was the perfect companion to this gory horror game.

As for the gameplay, it is set in a 3D environment, but it also offers level sections presented in side-scrolling camera angles. This was fun to do as it reminded me of the original games, which you can play if you want to see the complete storyline from the trilogy. Personally, I think it is agood thing they put the original games in this remake for I heard that there won't be any sequels to this 2010 remake since Splatterhouse didn't do enough sales to allow a sequel. This is sad for the game ends on a cliffhanger just like in the Evil Dead movies that Sam Raimi did.

Maybe what didn't help to the game's reception were the long loading times between levels, the difficulty to manipulate the camera, and the very sensible or unresponsive controls if you wanted to do certain moves.
